title: 清秀佳人
author: L. M. Montgomery 露西·莫德·蒙哥馬利
description: 《Anne of Green Gables》(1908):紅髮孤女安妮來到綠色屋頂之家,用想像力和真心改變了整個阿文利小鎮,是英語學習者最愛的成長小說。

chapters.title: Ch. I Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised 第一章:雷切爾·林德太太吃了一驚

passages.original: CH MRS.
passages.vernacular: 太太
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太太

passages.original: Rachel Lynde lived just where the Avonlea main road dipped down into a little hollow, fringed with alders and ladies’ eardrops and traversed by a brook that had its source away back in the woods of the old Cuthbert place; it was reputed to be an intricate, headlong brook in its earlier course through those woods, with dark secrets of pool and cascade; but by the time it reached Lynde’s Hollow it was a quiet, well-conducted little stream, for not even a brook could run past Mrs. Rachel Lynde’s door without due regard for decency and decorum; it probably was conscious that Mrs. Rachel was sitting at her window, keeping a sharp eye on everything that passed, from brooks and children up, and that if she noticed anything odd or out of place she would never rest until she had ferreted out the whys and wherefores thereof.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾·林德就住喺阿文利大路剛好陷進一個小窪地嘅地方,四周長住赤楊同鈴蘭,一條小溪穿過窪地,溪水嘅源頭遠喺老卡思伯特家嗰片樹林嘅深處;據講呢條溪喺流經樹林嘅上游時,曲折湍急,藏住深潭同瀑布嘅黑暗祕密;不過等佢流到林德窪地嘅時候,已成咗一條安靜、規規矩矩嘅小溪,因為就連一條小溪,從雷切爾·林德太太嘅門前流過,都唔能夠不顧體面同規矩;佢大概都意識到,雷切爾太太正坐喺窗前,從小溪到細路,對路過嘅一切都盯得緊緊嘅,而且只要佢發現乜嘢奇怪或不對勁嘅事,不把前因後果查個水落石出,佢係絕唔肯罷休嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾·林德就住在阿文利大路剛好陷進一個小窪地的地方,四周長著赤楊和鈴蘭,一條小溪穿過窪地,溪水的源頭遠在老卡思伯特家那片樹林的深處;據說這條溪在流經樹林的上游時,曲折湍急,藏著深潭和瀑布的黑暗祕密;可是等它流到林德窪地的時候,已成了一條安靜、規規矩矩的小溪,因為就連一條小溪,從雷切爾·林德太太的門前流過,也不能不顧體面和規矩;它大概也意識到,雷切爾太太正坐在窗前,從小溪到孩子,對路過的一切都盯得緊緊的,而且只要她發現什麼奇怪或不對勁的事,不把前因後果查個水落石出,她是絕不肯罷休的。

passages.original: There are plenty of people, in Avonlea and out of it, who can attend closely to their neighbors’ business by dint of neglecting their own; but Mrs. Rachel Lynde was one of those capable creatures who can manage their own concerns and those of other folks into the bargain.
passages.vernacular: 喺阿文利內外,有不少人專靠忽略自己嘅事,嚟緊盯住鄰居嘅事;可雷切爾·林德太太卻係嗰種能幹嘅人,既能料理自己嘅事,仲能順便料理別人嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在阿文利內外,有不少人專靠忽略自己的事,來緊盯著鄰居的事;可雷切爾·林德太太卻是那種能幹的人,既能料理自己的事,還能順便料理別人的事。

passages.original: She was a notable housewife; her work was always done and well done; she “ran” the Sewing Circle, helped run the Sunday-school, and was the strongest prop of the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個出色嘅主婦;活兒總是做完喇,而且做得好;佢「主持」縫紉會,幫住主持主日學校,係教會互助會同海外傳教輔助會最有力嘅支柱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個出色的主婦;活兒總是做完了,而且做得好;她「主持」縫紉會,幫著主持主日學校,是教會互助會和海外傳教輔助會最有力的支柱。

passages.original: Yet with all this Mrs. Rachel found abundant time to sit for hours at her kitchen window, knitting “cotton warp” quilts--she had knitted sixteen of them, as Avonlea housekeepers were wont to tell in awed voices--and keeping a sharp eye on the main road that crossed the hollow and wound up the steep red hill beyond.
passages.vernacular: 然而即便咁樣,雷切爾太太定係有足夠嘅時間,一坐就係幾個鐘頭,坐喺廚房窗前織「棉線」被子——佢已經織咗十六條,阿文利嘅主婦哋談起嚟總是帶住敬畏嘅口氣——同時緊盯住橫穿窪地、蜿蜒爬上對面陡峭紅山坡嘅嗰條大路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而即便這樣,雷切爾太太還是有足夠的時間,一坐就是幾個鐘頭,坐在廚房窗前織「棉線」被子——她已經織了十六條,阿文利的主婦們談起來總是帶著敬畏的口氣——同時緊盯著橫穿窪地、蜿蜒爬上對面陡峭紅山坡的那條大路。

passages.original: Since Avonlea occupied a little triangular peninsula jutting out into the Gulf of St. Lawrence, with water on two sides of it, anybody who went out of it or into it had to pass over that hill road and so run the unseen gauntlet of Mrs. Rachel’s all-seeing eye.
passages.vernacular: 由於阿文利佔據嘅係一個伸進聖勞倫斯灣嘅三角形小半島,兩面環水,所以凡是出入阿文利嘅人,都得走過嗰條山路,從而經過雷切爾太太嗰雙無所唔見嘅眼睛嘅無形夾道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 由於阿文利佔據的是一個伸進聖勞倫斯灣的三角形小半島,兩面環水,所以凡是出入阿文利的人,都得走過那條山路,從而經過雷切爾太太那雙無所不見的眼睛的無形夾道。

passages.original: She was sitting there one afternoon in early June.
passages.vernacular: 六月初嘅一個下午,佢正坐喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 六月初的一個下午,她正坐在那裡。

passages.original: The sun was coming in at the window warm and bright; the orchard on the slope below the house was in a bridal flush of pinky-white bloom, hummed over by a myriad of bees.
passages.vernacular: 陽光暖洋洋、亮晃晃地照進窗嚟;房子下面山坡上嘅果園,開滿咗新娘般泛住紅暈嘅粉白花朵,無數嘅蜜蜂喺上面嗡嗡作響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 陽光暖洋洋、亮晃晃地照進窗來;房子下面山坡上的果園,開滿了新娘般泛著紅暈的粉白花朵,無數的蜜蜂在上面嗡嗡作響。

passages.original: Thomas Lynde--a meek little man whom Avonlea people called “Rachel Lynde’s husband”--was sowing his late turnip seed on the hill field beyond the barn; and Matthew Cuthbert ought to have been sowing his on the big red brook field away over by Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 托馬斯·林德——一個溫順嘅小個子男人,阿文利人都叫佢「雷切爾·林德嘅丈夫」——正在穀倉後面嘅山坡地裡播種佢嘅晚蘿蔔種子;而馬修·卡思伯特本該喺綠色屋頂嗰邊遠處嘅大紅溪地裡播佢嘅種子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 托馬斯·林德——一個溫順的小個子男人,阿文利人都叫他「雷切爾·林德的丈夫」——正在穀倉後面的山坡地裡播種他的晚蘿蔔種子;而馬修·卡思伯特本該在綠色屋頂那邊遠處的大紅溪地裡播他的種子。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel knew that he ought because she had heard him tell Peter Morrison the evening before in William J. Blair’s store over at Carmody that he meant to sow his turnip seed the next afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太知道佢該咁做,因為前一天晚上佢聽見佢喺卡莫迪嘅威廉·J·布萊爾店裡對彼得·莫里森講,佢打算第二天下午播蘿蔔種子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太知道他該這麼做,因為前一天晚上她聽見他在卡莫迪的威廉·J·布萊爾店裡對彼得·莫里森說,他打算第二天下午播蘿蔔種子。

passages.original: Peter had asked him, of course, for Matthew Cuthbert had never been known to volunteer information about anything in his whole life.
passages.vernacular: 當然係彼得問佢嘅,因為馬修·卡思伯特呢輩子從來冇主動講過任何事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然是彼得問他的,因為馬修·卡思伯特這輩子從來沒有主動說過任何事。

passages.original: And yet here was Matthew Cuthbert, at half-past three on the afternoon of a busy day, placidly driving over the hollow and up the hill; moreover, he wore a white collar and his best suit of clothes, which was plain proof that he was going out of Avonlea; and he had the buggy and the sorrel mare, which betokened that he was going a considerable distance.
passages.vernacular: 不過眼下,馬修·卡思伯特卻喺忙碌嘅一天下午三點半,安安穩穩地趕住車經過窪地,上咗山坡;而且佢仲穿住白領子同最好嘅一套衣服,呢明擺住係要出阿文利;佢仲趕住輕便馬車,套住栗色母馬,呢表明佢要去嘅地方相當遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是眼下,馬修·卡思伯特卻在忙碌的一天下午三點半,安安穩穩地趕著車經過窪地,上了山坡;而且他還穿著白領子和最好的一套衣服,這明擺著是要出阿文利;他還趕著輕便馬車,套著栗色母馬,這表明他要去的地方相當遠。

passages.original: Now, where was Matthew Cuthbert going and why was he going there?
passages.vernacular: 咁,馬修·卡思伯特要去邊度,點解要去呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,馬修·卡思伯特要去哪裡,為什麼要去呢?

passages.original: Had it been any other man in Avonlea, Mrs. Rachel, deftly putting this and that together, might have given a pretty good guess as to both questions.
passages.vernacular: 如果換作阿文利嘅其他任何男人,雷切爾太太把呢件事同嗰件事巧妙地一湊,呢兩個問題大概都能猜個八九不離十。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果換作阿文利的其他任何男人,雷切爾太太把這件事和那件事巧妙地一湊,這兩個問題大概都能猜個八九不離十。

passages.original: But Matthew so rarely went from home that it must be something pressing and unusual which was taking him; he was the shyest man alive and hated to have to go among strangers or to any place where he might have to talk.
passages.vernacular: 不過馬修好少離家,所以拉佢出門嘅一定係乜嘢緊迫而不尋常嘅事;佢係世上最害羞嘅人,最討厭到陌生人中間去,或者去任何要佢開口講話嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是馬修很少離家,所以拉他出門的一定是什麼緊迫而不尋常的事;他是世上最害羞的人,最討厭到陌生人中間去,或者去任何要他開口說話的地方。

passages.original: Matthew, dressed up with a white collar and driving in a buggy, was something that didn’t happen often.
passages.vernacular: 馬修穿住白領子,趕住輕便馬車,呢可唔係常見嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修穿著白領子,趕著輕便馬車,這可不是常見的事。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel, ponder as she might, could make nothing of it and her afternoon’s enjoyment was spoiled.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太苦思冥想,卻點都琢磨不透,下午嘅興致全畀攪喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太苦思冥想,卻怎麼也琢磨不透,下午的興致全給攪了。

passages.original: “I’ll just step over to Green Gables after tea and find out from Marilla where he’s gone and why,” the worthy woman finally concluded.
passages.vernacular: 「食完茶點我就到綠色屋頂去一趟,問問瑪麗拉佢去咗邊兒、點解去,」呢位賢惠嘅婦人終於作出咗決定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吃完茶點我就到綠色屋頂去一趟,問問瑪麗拉他去了哪兒、為什麼去,」這位賢惠的婦人終於作出了決定。

passages.original: “He doesn’t generally go to town this time of year and he never visits; if he’d run out of turnip seed he wouldn’t dress up and take the buggy to go for more; he wasn’t driving fast enough to be going for a doctor.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個時節佢一般不進城,而且佢從不串門;要係蘿蔔種子用完喇,佢都唔會穿戴整齊趕住馬車去買;佢趕車嘅速度都不像係去請醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個時節他一般不進城,而且他從不串門;要是蘿蔔種子用完了,他也不會穿戴整齊趕著馬車去買;他趕車的速度也不像是去請醫生。

passages.original: Yet something must have happened since last night to start him off.
passages.vernacular: 不過從琴晚到而家,一定出咗乜嘢事,才讓佢出門嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是從昨晚到現在,一定出了什麼事,才讓他出門的。

passages.original: I’m clean puzzled, that’s what, and I won’t know a minute’s peace of mind or conscience until I know what has taken Matthew Cuthbert out of Avonlea today.”
passages.vernacular: 我簡直一頭霧水,就係咁樣,不弄明白今日係乜嘢事把馬修·卡思伯特帶出咗阿文利,我心裡一分鐘都唔會安寧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我簡直一頭霧水,就是這樣,不弄明白今天是什麼事把馬修·卡思伯特帶出了阿文利,我心裡一分鐘也不會安寧。」

passages.original: Accordingly after tea Mrs. Rachel set out; she had not far to go; the big, rambling, orchard-embowered house where the Cuthberts lived was a scant quarter of a mile up the road from Lynde’s Hollow.
passages.vernacular: 於是飲完茶後,雷切爾太太就出發喇;佢要走嘅路不遠;卡思伯特一家住嘅嗰座寬大、凌亂、掩映喺果樹叢中嘅房子,離林德窪地沿住大路上去,只有唔到四分之一英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是喝完茶後,雷切爾太太就出發了;她要走的路不遠;卡思伯特一家住的那座寬大、凌亂、掩映在果樹叢中的房子,離林德窪地沿著大路上去,只有不到四分之一英里。

passages.original: To be sure, the long lane made it a good deal further.
passages.vernacular: 不過,嗰條長長嘅小巷讓路程遠咗許多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,那條長長的小巷讓路程遠了許多。

passages.original: Matthew Cuthbert’s father, as shy and silent as his son after him, had got as far away as he possibly could from his fellow men without actually retreating into the woods when he founded his homestead.
passages.vernacular: 馬修·卡思伯特嘅父親,像佢兒子後來嗰樣害羞沉默,當年建造家園嘅時候,幾乎係躲到咗離同胞最遠嘅地方,只差冇退進樹林裡去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修·卡思伯特的父親,像他兒子後來那樣害羞沉默,當年建造家園的時候,幾乎是躲到了離同胞最遠的地方,只差沒退進樹林裡去。

passages.original: Green Gables was built at the furthest edge of his cleared land and there it was to this day, barely visible from the main road along which all the other Avonlea houses were so sociably situated.
passages.vernacular: 綠色屋頂就建喺佢開墾嘅土地嘅最邊緣,直到今日佢仲喺嗰度,從大路上幾乎睇唔見,而阿文利所有其他房屋,都咁合群地沿住大路坐落住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 綠色屋頂就建在他開墾的土地的最邊緣,直到今天它還在那裡,從大路上幾乎看不見,而阿文利所有其他房屋,都那麼合群地沿著大路坐落著。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel Lynde did not call living in such a place living at all.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾·林德太太覺得,住喺嗰樣嘅地方根本算不上生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾·林德太太覺得,住在那樣的地方根本算不上生活。

passages.original: “It’s just staying, that’s what,” she said as she stepped along the deep-rutted, grassy lane bordered with wild rose bushes.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰只係待住,就係咁樣,」佢沿住車轍好深、長滿野草、兩旁係野玫瑰叢嘅小巷走住,講道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那只是待著,就是這樣,」她沿著車轍很深、長滿野草、兩旁是野玫瑰叢的小巷走著,說道。

passages.original: “It’s no wonder Matthew and Marilla are both a little odd, living away back here by themselves.
passages.vernacular: 「難怪馬修同瑪麗拉都有點古怪,喺呢遠遠嘅地方自己守住過日子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「難怪馬修和瑪麗拉都有點古怪,在這遠遠的地方自己守著過日子。

passages.original: Trees aren’t much company, though dear knows if they were there’d be enough of them.
passages.vernacular: 樹木算不上乜嘢伴兒,不過天曉得,要係算嘅話,呢度倒係夠多嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樹木算不上什麼伴兒,不過天曉得,要是算的話,這裡倒是夠多的。

passages.original: I’d ruther look at people.
passages.vernacular: 我寧可睇睇人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧可看看人。

passages.original: To be sure, they seem contented enough; but then, I suppose, they’re used to it.
passages.vernacular: 講實話,佢哋睇上去倒挺滿足;不過我想,嗰個係佢哋習慣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說實話,他們看上去倒挺滿足;不過我想,那是他們習慣了。

passages.original: A body can get used to anything, even to being hanged, as the Irishman said.”
passages.vernacular: 一個人乜嘢都能習慣,連被絞死都能習慣,就像嗰個愛爾蘭人講嘅嗰樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個人什麼都能習慣,連被絞死也能習慣,就像那個愛爾蘭人說的那樣。」

passages.original: With this Mrs. Rachel stepped out of the lane into the backyard of Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 講住,雷切爾太太從小巷走進咗綠色屋頂嘅後院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說著,雷切爾太太從小巷走進了綠色屋頂的後院。

passages.original: Very green and neat and precise was that yard, set about on one side with great patriarchal willows and on the other with prim Lombardies.
passages.vernacular: 嗰院子好綠、好整潔、一絲不苟,一邊栽住高大嘅、古老嘅柳樹,另一邊栽住規規矩矩嘅倫巴第楊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那院子非常綠、非常整潔、一絲不苟,一邊栽著高大的、古老的柳樹,另一邊栽著規規矩矩的倫巴第楊。

passages.original: Not a stray stick nor stone was to be seen, for Mrs. Rachel would have seen it if there had been.
passages.vernacular: 睇唔到一根散落嘅枯枝,都睇唔到一塊石頭,因為只要有,雷切爾太太就一定能睇見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看不到一根散落的枯枝,也看不到一塊石頭,因為只要有,雷切爾太太就一定能看見。

passages.original: Privately she was of the opinion that Marilla Cuthbert swept that yard over as often as she swept her house.
passages.vernacular: 佢私下裡認為,瑪麗拉·卡思伯特掃院子嘅次數,一定同掃房子一樣勤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她私下裡認為,瑪麗拉·卡思伯特掃院子的次數,一定和掃房子一樣勤。

passages.original: One could have eaten a meal off the ground without overbrimming the proverbial peck of dirt.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰地上食飯,都唔會食進俗話所講嘅一配克嘅塵土。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那地上吃飯,也不會吃進俗話所說的一配克的塵土。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel rapped smartly at the kitchen door and stepped in when bidden to do so.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太輕快地敲咗敲廚房門,聽見喊佢進去,就走咗進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太輕快地敲了敲廚房門,聽見喊她進去,就走了進去。

passages.original: The kitchen at Green Gables was a cheerful apartment--or would have been cheerful if it had not been so painfully clean as to give it something of the appearance of an unused parlor.
passages.vernacular: 綠色屋頂嘅廚房係個令人愉快嘅房間——要唔係佢乾淨得讓人難受,幾乎像間冇人用嘅客廳嘅話,本來係會令人愉快嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 綠色屋頂的廚房是個令人愉快的房間——要不是它乾淨得讓人難受,幾乎像間沒人用的客廳的話,本來是會令人愉快的。

passages.original: Its windows looked east and west; through the west one, looking out on the back yard, came a flood of mellow June sunlight; but the east one, whence you got a glimpse of the bloom white cherry-trees in the left orchard and nodding, slender birches down in the hollow by the brook, was greened over by a tangle of vines.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅窗戶朝東同朝西;透過朝西嘅窗戶,可以睇到後院,柔和嘅六月陽光傾瀉進嚟;不過朝東嘅窗戶,從嗰兒可以瞥見左邊果園裡盛開嘅白色櫻桃樹,同下面小溪邊窪地裡搖曳嘅纖細白樺,卻被一片亂糟糟嘅藤蔓遮成咗綠色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的窗戶朝東和朝西;透過朝西的窗戶,可以看到後院,柔和的六月陽光傾瀉進來;可是朝東的窗戶,從那兒可以瞥見左邊果園裡盛開的白色櫻桃樹,和下面小溪邊窪地裡搖曳的纖細白樺,卻被一片亂糟糟的藤蔓遮成了綠色。

passages.original: Here sat Marilla Cuthbert, when she sat at all, always slightly distrustful of sunshine, which seemed to her too dancing and irresponsible a thing for a world which was meant to be taken seriously; and here she sat now, knitting, and the table behind her was laid for supper.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉·卡思伯特要坐嘅時候,總是坐喺呢度,對陽光總有點不信任,喺佢睇來,陽光太愛跳舞、太不負責任喇,不適合一個本該認真對待嘅世界;此刻佢都坐喺呢度織毛線,身後嘅桌子已經擺好咗晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉·卡思伯特要坐的時候,總是坐在這裡,對陽光總有點不信任,在她看來,陽光太愛跳舞、太不負責任了,不適合一個本該認真對待的世界;此刻她也坐在這裡織毛線,身後的桌子已經擺好了晚飯。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel, before she had fairly closed the door, had taken a mental note of everything that was on that table.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太門仲冇完全關上,就已經喺心裡把桌上嘅每樣嘢都記咗一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太門還沒完全關上,就已經在心裡把桌上的每樣東西都記了一遍。

passages.original: There were three plates laid, so that Marilla must be expecting some one home with Matthew to tea; but the dishes were everyday dishes and there was only crab-apple preserves and one kind of cake, so that the expected company could not be any particular company.
passages.vernacular: 擺咗三副碟子,所以瑪麗拉一定喺等人同馬修一起回嚟飲茶;不過碟子都係平日嘅碟子,食嘅只有野蘋果蜜餞同一種蛋糕,所以要嚟嘅客人唔可能係乜嘢特別嘅客人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 擺了三副碟子,所以瑪麗拉一定在等人和馬修一起回來喝茶;不過碟子都是平日的碟子,吃的只有野蘋果蜜餞和一種蛋糕,所以要來的客人不可能是什麼特別的客人。

passages.original: Yet what of Matthew’s white collar and the sorrel mare?
passages.vernacular: 不過,馬修嘅白領子同嗰匹栗色母馬又係點回事呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是,馬修的白領子和那匹栗色母馬又是怎麼回事呢?

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel was getting fairly dizzy with this unusual mystery about quiet, unmysterious Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太被呢個發生喺安靜、毫無神祕色彩嘅綠色屋頂嘅不尋常嘅謎團,弄得頭都暈喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太被這個發生在安靜、毫無神祕色彩的綠色屋頂的不尋常的謎團,弄得頭都暈了。

passages.original: “Good evening, Rachel,” Marilla said briskly.
passages.vernacular: 「晚上好,雷切爾,」瑪麗拉爽快地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「晚上好,雷切爾,」瑪麗拉爽快地說。

passages.original: “This is a real fine evening, isn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 「今晚天氣真不錯,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚天氣真不錯,是不是?

passages.original: Won’t you sit down?
passages.vernacular: 你不坐一會兒嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不坐一會兒嗎?

passages.original: How are all your folks?”
passages.vernacular: 你家裡人都好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你家裡人都好嗎?」

passages.original: Something that for lack of any other name might be called friendship existed and always had existed between Marilla Cuthbert and Mrs. Rachel, in spite of--or perhaps because of--their dissimilarity.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉·卡思伯特同雷切爾太太之間存在住,而且一直存在住某種,因為缺少別嘅名字,只好稱之為友誼嘅嘢,儘管——或許正因為——佢哋截然不同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉·卡思伯特和雷切爾太太之間存在著,而且一直存在著某種,因為缺少別的名字,只好稱之為友誼的東西,儘管——或許正因為——她們截然不同。

passages.original: Marilla was a tall, thin woman, with angles and without curves; her dark hair showed some gray streaks and was always twisted up in a hard little knot behind with two wire hairpins stuck aggressively through it.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉係個高個子嘅瘦女人,有稜有角,冇曲線;佢烏黑嘅頭髮裡夾住幾縷灰白,總是喺腦後盤成一個硬邦邦嘅小髻,仲用兩根鐵絲髮夾氣勢洶洶地插住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉是個高個子的瘦女人,有稜有角,沒有曲線;她烏黑的頭髮裡夾著幾縷灰白,總是在腦後盤成一個硬邦邦的小髻,還用兩根鐵絲髮夾氣勢洶洶地插著。

passages.original: She looked like a woman of narrow experience and rigid conscience, which she was; but there was a saving something about her mouth which, if it had been ever so slightly developed, might have been considered indicative of a sense of humor.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇上去像個閱歷狹窄、良心嚴苛嘅女人,佢都的確係;但佢嘅嘴上有某種可取之處,如果稍稍再發展啲,或許就可以被睇作係幽默感嘅標誌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看上去像個閱歷狹窄、良心嚴苛的女人,她也的確是;但她的嘴上有某種可取之處,如果稍稍再發展一點,或許就可以被看作是幽默感的標誌。

passages.original: “We’re all pretty well,” said Mrs. Rachel.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋都挺好嘅,」雷切爾太太講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們都挺好的,」雷切爾太太說。

passages.original: “I was kind of afraid you weren’t, though, when I saw Matthew starting off today.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我今日睇見馬修出門嘅時候,有點擔心你哋不好呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過我今天看見馬修出門的時候,有點擔心你們不好呢。

passages.original: I thought maybe he was going to the doctor’s.”
passages.vernacular: 我想佢可能係去睇醫生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他可能是去看醫生。」

passages.original: Marilla’s lips twitched understandingly.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉嘅嘴唇會意地抽動咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉的嘴唇會意地抽動了一下。

passages.original: She had expected Mrs. Rachel up; she had known that the sight of Matthew jaunting off so unaccountably would be too much for her neighbor’s curiosity.
passages.vernacular: 佢早就料到雷切爾太太會嚟;佢知道馬修嗰樣莫名其妙地出門,睇喺鄰居眼裡,佢嘅好奇心一定忍不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她早就料到雷切爾太太會來;她知道馬修那樣莫名其妙地出門,看在鄰居眼裡,她的好奇心一定忍不住。

passages.original: “Oh, no, I’m quite well although I had a bad headache yesterday,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不,我挺好嘅,不過尋日頭疼得厲害,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不,我挺好的,不過昨天頭疼得厲害,」她說。

passages.original: “Matthew went to Bright River.
passages.vernacular: 「馬修去咗明河。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修去了明河。

passages.original: We’re getting a little boy from an orphan asylum in Nova Scotia and he’s coming on the train tonight.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋從新斯科舍嘅孤兒院領一個小男孩,佢今晚坐火車嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們從新斯科舍的孤兒院領一個小男孩,他今晚坐火車來。」

passages.original: If Marilla had said that Matthew had gone to Bright River to meet a kangaroo from Australia Mrs. Rachel could not have been more astonished.
passages.vernacular: 就算瑪麗拉講馬修去明河接一隻從澳大利亞嚟嘅袋鼠,雷切爾太太都唔會更食驚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就算瑪麗拉說馬修去明河接一隻從澳大利亞來的袋鼠,雷切爾太太也不會更吃驚了。

passages.original: She was actually stricken dumb for five seconds.
passages.vernacular: 佢竟然啞口無言咗五秒鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她竟然啞口無言了五秒鐘。

passages.original: It was unsupposable that Marilla was making fun of her, but Mrs. Rachel was almost forced to suppose it.
passages.vernacular: 唔能夠想像瑪麗拉係喺攞佢開玩笑,可雷切爾太太幾乎唔得不咁想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不能想像瑪麗拉是在拿她開玩笑,可雷切爾太太幾乎不得不這麼想。

passages.original: “Are you in earnest, Marilla?” she demanded when voice returned to her.
passages.vernacular: 「你係認真嘅嗎,瑪麗拉?」等聲音恢復喇,佢質問道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是認真的嗎,瑪麗拉?」等聲音恢復了,她質問道。

passages.original: “Yes, of course,” said Marilla, as if getting boys from orphan asylums in Nova Scotia were part of the usual spring work on any well-regulated Avonlea farm instead of being an unheard of innovation.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,當然,」瑪麗拉講,好像從新斯科舍嘅孤兒院領男孩,係任何一個管理有方嘅阿文利農場春季嘅例行工作,而唔係乜嘢聞所未聞嘅創新似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,當然,」瑪麗拉說,好像從新斯科舍的孤兒院領男孩,是任何一個管理有方的阿文利農場春季的例行工作,而不是什麼聞所未聞的創新似的。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel felt that she had received a severe mental jolt.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太覺得自己嘅頭腦受到咗劇烈嘅震動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太覺得自己的頭腦受到了劇烈的震動。

passages.original: She thought in exclamation points.
passages.vernacular: 佢腦子裡想嘅全係驚嘆號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她腦子裡想的全是驚嘆號。

passages.original: A boy!
passages.vernacular: 一個男孩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個男孩!

passages.original: Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert of all people adopting a boy!
passages.vernacular: 偏偏係瑪麗拉同馬修·卡思伯特領養一個男孩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 偏偏是瑪麗拉和馬修·卡思伯特領養一個男孩!

passages.original: From an orphan asylum!
passages.vernacular: 定係從孤兒院!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是從孤兒院!

passages.original: Well, the world was certainly turning upside down!
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,呢世界真係要顛倒過嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,這世界真是要顛倒過來了!

passages.original: She would be surprised at nothing after this!
passages.vernacular: 呢以後佢乜嘢都唔會食驚喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這以後她什麼都不會吃驚了!

passages.original: Nothing!
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢都唔會喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼都不會了!

passages.original: “What on earth put such a notion into your head?” she demanded disapprovingly.
passages.vernacular: 「到底係乜嘢讓你哋有咗呢種想法?」佢不以為然地質問道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「到底是什麼讓你們有了這種想法?」她不以為然地質問道。

passages.original: This had been done without her advice being asked, and must perforce be disapproved.
passages.vernacular: 呢件事冇徵求佢嘅意見就辦喇,所以必定要反對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這件事沒有徵求她的意見就辦了,所以必定要反對。

passages.original: “Well, we’ve been thinking about it for some time--all winter in fact,” returned Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我哋想呢件事已經有些日子喇——其實整個冬天都喺想,」瑪麗拉回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我們想這件事已經有些日子了——其實整個冬天都在想,」瑪麗拉回答。

passages.original: “Mrs. Alexander Spencer was up here one day before Christmas and she said she was going to get a little girl from the asylum over in Hopeton in the spring.
passages.vernacular: 「聖誕節前有一天,亞歷山大·斯潘塞太太嚟過我哋呢兒,佢講春天要從霍普頓嘅孤兒院領一個小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聖誕節前有一天,亞歷山大·斯潘塞太太來過我們這兒,她說春天要從霍普頓的孤兒院領一個小女孩。

passages.original: Her cousin lives there and Mrs. Spencer has visited her and knows all about it.
passages.vernacular: 佢表親住喺嗰兒,斯潘塞太太去睇過佢,對嗰兒嘅情況瞭如指掌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她表親住在那兒,斯潘塞太太去看過她,對那兒的情況瞭如指掌。

passages.original: So Matthew and I have talked it over off and on ever since.
passages.vernacular: 所以馬修同我從嗰以後就時不時地商量呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以馬修和我從那以後就時不時地商量這件事。

passages.original: We thought we’d get a boy.
passages.vernacular: 我哋想領一個男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們想領一個男孩。

passages.original: Matthew is getting up in years, you know--he’s sixty--and he isn’t so spry as he once was.
passages.vernacular: 馬修年紀越嚟越大喇,你知道——佢六十喇——不像從前嗰樣靈活喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修年紀越來越大了,你知道——他六十了——不像從前那樣靈活了。

passages.original: His heart troubles him a good deal.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅心臟都常常出毛病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的心臟也常常出毛病。

passages.original: And you know how desperate hard it’s got to be to get hired help.
passages.vernacular: 你都知道,而家雇人幫忙有幾咁難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你也知道,現在雇人幫忙有多麼難。

passages.original: There’s never anybody to be had but those stupid, half-grown little French boys; and as soon as you do get one broke into your ways and taught something he’s up and off to the lobster canneries or the States.
passages.vernacular: 能雇到嘅總是嗰啲愚笨嘅、半大不小嘅法國小子;而且剛把佢調教得合你嘅規矩、教會點本事,佢就跑去龍蝦罐頭廠或者去美國喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 能雇到的總是那些愚笨的、半大不小的法國小子;而且剛把他調教得合你的規矩、教會點本事,他就跑去龍蝦罐頭廠或者去美國了。

passages.original: At first Matthew suggested getting a Home boy.
passages.vernacular: 起初馬修提議領一個『家園男孩』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初馬修提議領一個『家園男孩』。

passages.original: But I said ‘no’ flat to that.
passages.vernacular: 但我一口回絕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我一口回絕了。

passages.original: ‘They may be all right--I’m not saying they’re not--but no London street Arabs for me,’ I said.
passages.vernacular: 『佢哋或者不錯——我唔係講佢哋不好——但我可唔好倫敦街頭嘅流浪兒,』我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『他們也許不錯——我不是說他們不好——但我可不要倫敦街頭的流浪兒,』我說。

passages.original: ‘Give me a native born at least.
passages.vernacular: 『至少畀我一個本地生嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『至少給我一個本地生的。

passages.original: There’ll be a risk, no matter who we get.
passages.vernacular: 不管領邊個回嚟,總歸有風險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管領誰回來,總歸有風險。

passages.original: But I’ll feel easier in my mind and sleep sounder at nights if we get a born Canadian.’
passages.vernacular: 但如果領一個土生土長嘅加攞大人,我心裡會踏實些,晚上都瞓得安穩些。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果領一個土生土長的加拿大人,我心裡會踏實些,晚上也睡得安穩些。』

passages.original: So in the end we decided to ask Mrs. Spencer to pick us out one when she went over to get her little girl.
passages.vernacular: 所以最後我哋決定,請斯潘塞太太去領佢嘅小女孩時,順便畀我哋挑一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以最後我們決定,請斯潘塞太太去領她的小女孩時,順便給我們挑一個。

passages.original: We heard last week she was going, so we sent her word by Richard Spencer’s folks at Carmody to bring us a smart, likely boy of about ten or eleven.
passages.vernacular: 上星期我哋聽講佢要去喇,就托理查德·斯潘塞家嘅人從卡莫迪捎話畀佢,讓佢畀我哋帶一個聰明、有出息、十嚟歲或十一歲嘅男孩嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上星期我們聽說她要去了,就托理查德·斯潘塞家的人從卡莫迪捎話給她,讓她給我們帶一個聰明、有出息、十來歲或十一歲的男孩來。

passages.original: We decided that would be the best age--old enough to be of some use in doing chores right off and young enough to be trained up proper.
passages.vernacular: 我哋認為嗰個係最合適嘅年紀——大到能即刻幫住幹些雜活,又小到可以好好調教。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們認為那是最合適的年紀——大到能馬上幫著幹些雜活,又小到可以好好調教。

passages.original: We mean to give him a good home and schooling.
passages.vernacular: 我哋打算畀佢一個好家同好嘅教育。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們打算給他一個好家和好的教育。

passages.original: We had a telegram from Mrs. Alexander Spencer today--the mail-man brought it from the station--saying they were coming on the five-thirty train tonight.
passages.vernacular: 今日我哋收到亞歷山大·斯潘塞太太嘅一封電報——郵差從車站帶嚟嘅——講佢哋坐今晚五點半嘅火車嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天我們收到亞歷山大·斯潘塞太太的一封電報——郵差從車站帶來的——說他們坐今晚五點半的火車來。

passages.original: So Matthew went to Bright River to meet him.
passages.vernacular: 所以馬修去明河接佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以馬修去明河接他了。

passages.original: Mrs. Spencer will drop him off there.
passages.vernacular: 斯潘塞太太會喺嗰兒讓佢下車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯潘塞太太會在那兒讓他下車。

passages.original: Of course she goes on to White Sands station herself.”
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢自己繼續坐到白沙站。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,她自己繼續坐到白沙站。」

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel prided herself on always speaking her mind; she proceeded to speak it now, having adjusted her mental attitude to this amazing piece of news.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太以總是直言不諱自傲;佢調整好自己對呢個驚人消息嘅心態後,而家就講開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太以總是直言不諱自傲;她調整好自己對這個驚人消息的心態後,現在就說開了。

passages.original: “Well, Marilla, I’ll just tell you plain that I think you’re doing a mighty foolish thing--a risky thing, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,瑪麗拉,我直講咗吧,我覺得你哋喺做一件好愚蠢嘅事——一件冒險嘅事,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,瑪麗拉,我直說了吧,我覺得你們在做一件非常愚蠢的事——一件冒險的事,就是這樣。

passages.original: You don’t know what you’re getting.
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道你領回嚟嘅係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道你領回來的是什麼。

passages.original: You’re bringing a strange child into your house and home and you don’t know a single thing about him nor what his disposition is like nor what sort of parents he had nor how he’s likely to turn out.
passages.vernacular: 你把一個陌生嘅細路領進你嘅房子、你嘅家,你對佢一無所知,唔知道佢嘅性情點樣,唔知道佢有乜嘢樣嘅父母,都唔知道佢將來可能變成乜嘢樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把一個陌生的孩子領進你的房子、你的家,你對他一無所知,不知道他的性情怎麼樣,不知道他有什麼樣的父母,也不知道他將來可能變成什麼樣。

passages.original: Why, it was only last week I read in the paper how a man and his wife up west of the Island took a boy out of an orphan asylum and he set fire to the house at night--set it on purpose, Marilla--and nearly burnt them to a crisp in their beds.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,就喺上星期,我喺報紙上讀到,島西邊有一對夫婦從孤兒院領咗個男孩,嗰細路夜裡放火燒咗房子——係故意放嘅,瑪麗拉——差點把佢哋喺床上燒成焦炭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,就在上星期,我在報紙上讀到,島西邊有一對夫婦從孤兒院領了個男孩,那孩子夜裡放火燒了房子——是故意放的,瑪麗拉——差點把他們在床上燒成焦炭。

passages.original: And I know another case where an adopted boy used to suck the eggs--they couldn’t break him of it.
passages.vernacular: 我仲知道另一個例子,一個領養嘅男孩老鍾意偷吸雞蛋——點都改不掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還知道另一個例子,一個領養的男孩老喜歡偷吸雞蛋——怎麼也改不掉。

passages.original: If you had asked my advice in the matter--which you didn’t do, Marilla--I’d have said for mercy’s sake not to think of such a thing, that’s what.”
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋事先徵求我嘅意見——可你哋冇,瑪麗拉——我會講,睇喺老天嘅份上,別想呢種事,就係咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們事先徵求我的意見——可你們沒有,瑪麗拉——我會說,看在老天的份上,別想這種事,就是這樣。」

passages.original: This Job’s comforting seemed neither to offend nor to alarm Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 呢番約伯式嘅安慰似乎既冇冒犯瑪麗拉,都冇嚇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這番約伯式的安慰似乎既沒有冒犯瑪麗拉,也沒有嚇著她。

passages.original: She knitted steadily on.
passages.vernacular: 佢繼續穩穩地織住毛線。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她繼續穩穩地織著毛線。

passages.original: “I don’t deny there’s something in what you say, Rachel.
passages.vernacular: 「我不否認你講嘅有些道理,雷切爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不否認你說的有些道理,雷切爾。

passages.original: I’ve had some qualms myself.
passages.vernacular: 我自己都有過啲疑慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己也有過一些疑慮。

passages.original: But Matthew was terrible set on it.
passages.vernacular: 但馬修特別執意要咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但馬修特別執意要這樣做。

passages.original: I could see that, so I gave in.
passages.vernacular: 我睇得出嚟,所以我就讓步喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看得出來,所以我就讓步了。

passages.original: It’s so seldom Matthew sets his mind on anything that when he does I always feel it’s my duty to give in.
passages.vernacular: 馬修好少對乜嘢事攞定主意,所以佢一攞定主意,我總覺得我有責任讓步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修很少對什麼事拿定主意,所以他一拿定主意,我總覺得我有責任讓步。

passages.original: And as for the risk, there’s risks in pretty near everything a body does in this world.
passages.vernacular: 至於風險,人在世上做嘅幾乎每件事都有風險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於風險,人在世上做的幾乎每件事都有風險。

passages.original: There’s risks in people’s having children of their own if it comes to that--they don’t always turn out well.
passages.vernacular: 講到底,人哋自己生細路都有風險——細路都不一定都有出息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說到底,人們自己生孩子也有風險——孩子也不一定都有出息。

passages.original: And then Nova Scotia is right close to the Island.
passages.vernacular: 再講新斯科舍離咱哋島好近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再說新斯科舍離咱們島很近。

passages.original: It isn’t as if we were getting him from England or the States.
passages.vernacular: 又唔係從英國或美國領養佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又不是從英國或美國領養他。

passages.original: He can’t be much different from ourselves.”
passages.vernacular: 佢唔會同我哋有多大差別嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不會和我們有多大差別的。」

passages.original: “Well, I hope it will turn out all right,” said Mrs. Rachel in a tone that plainly indicated her painful doubts.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,但願一切順利,」雷切爾太太講,語氣明顯地表露咗佢沉重嘅疑慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,但願一切順利,」雷切爾太太說,語氣明顯地表露了她沉重的疑慮。

passages.original: “Only don’t say I didn’t warn you if he burns Green Gables down or puts strychnine in the well--I heard of a case over in New Brunswick where an orphan asylum child did that and the whole family died in fearful agonies.
passages.vernacular: 「只係,要係佢把綠色屋頂燒喇,或者往井裡下馬錢子毒藥,可唔好講我冇警告過你——我聽講新不倫瑞克有個孤兒院嘅細路就咁幹過,全家人都死得慘不忍睹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是,要是他把綠色屋頂燒了,或者往井裡下馬錢子毒藥,可別說我沒警告過你——我聽說新不倫瑞克有個孤兒院的孩子就這麼幹過,全家人都死得慘不忍睹。

passages.original: Only, it was a girl in that instance.”
passages.vernacular: 不過,嗰次係個女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,那次是個女孩。」

passages.original: “Well, we’re not getting a girl,” said Marilla, as if poisoning wells were a purely feminine accomplishment and not to be dreaded in the case of a boy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我哋領嘅又唔係女孩,」瑪麗拉講,好像往井裡下毒純粹係女人嘅本事,男孩就唔使害怕似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我們領的又不是女孩,」瑪麗拉說,好像往井裡下毒純粹是女人的本事,男孩就不必害怕似的。

passages.original: “I’d never dream of taking a girl to bring up.
passages.vernacular: 「我做夢都唔會想到領個女孩嚟教養。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我做夢也不會想到領個女孩來教養。

passages.original: I wonder at Mrs. Alexander Spencer for doing it.
passages.vernacular: 我真奇怪斯潘塞太太點會咁做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真奇怪斯潘塞太太怎麼會這麼做。

passages.original: But there, she wouldn’t shrink from adopting a whole orphan asylum if she took it into her head.”
passages.vernacular: 不過話講回嚟,佢要係一時心血嚟潮,連整個孤兒院都敢領養嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過話說回來,她要是一時心血來潮,連整個孤兒院都敢領養的。」

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel would have liked to stay until Matthew came home with his imported orphan.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太本想留下嚟等馬修帶住佢嗰個進口嘅孤兒回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太本想留下來等馬修帶著他那個進口的孤兒回來。

passages.original: But reflecting that it would be a good two hours at least before his arrival she concluded to go up the road to Robert Bell’s and tell the news.
passages.vernacular: 但想到佢至少仲要兩個鐘頭才能到,佢決定定係到羅伯特·貝爾家去,把呢消息告訴佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但想到他至少還要兩個鐘頭才能到,她決定還是到羅伯特·貝爾家去,把這消息告訴他們。

passages.original: It would certainly make a sensation second to none, and Mrs. Rachel dearly loved to make a sensation.
passages.vernacular: 呢肯定會引起一場無同倫比嘅轟動,而雷切爾太太最愛製造轟動喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這肯定會引起一場無與倫比的轟動,而雷切爾太太最愛製造轟動了。

passages.original: So she took herself away, somewhat to Marilla’s relief, for the latter felt her doubts and fears reviving under the influence of Mrs. Rachel’s pessimism.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢走喇,呢多少讓瑪麗拉鬆咗口氣,因為喺雷切爾太太悲觀情緒嘅影響下,瑪麗拉感到自己嘅疑慮同擔憂又復甦喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是她走了,這多少讓瑪麗拉鬆了口氣,因為在雷切爾太太悲觀情緒的影響下,瑪麗拉感到自己的疑慮和擔憂又復甦了。

passages.original: “Well, of all things that ever were or will be!” ejaculated Mrs. Rachel when she was safely out in the lane.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,天下竟有呢種事!」雷切爾太太安全走到小巷時,大聲講道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,天下竟有這種事!」雷切爾太太安全走到小巷時,大聲說道。

passages.original: “It does really seem as if I must be dreaming.
passages.vernacular: 「簡直像係喺做夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「簡直像是在做夢。

passages.original: Well, I’m sorry for that poor young one and no mistake.
passages.vernacular: 哎,我真替嗰可憐嘅小傢伙難過,啲不假。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,我真替那可憐的小傢伙難過,一點不假。

passages.original: Matthew and Marilla don’t know anything about children and they’ll expect him to be wiser and steadier than his own grandfather, if so be’s he ever had a grandfather, which is doubtful.
passages.vernacular: 馬修同瑪麗拉對細路一竅不通,佢哋會指望佢比佢自己嘅爺爺仲聰明仲穩重,如果佢有過爺爺嘅話,呢仲難講呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修和瑪麗拉對孩子一竅不通,他們會指望他比他自己的爺爺還聰明還穩重,如果他有過爺爺的話,這還難說呢。

passages.original: It seems uncanny to think of a child at Green Gables somehow; there’s never been one there, for Matthew and Marilla were grown up when the new house was built--if they ever were children, which is hard to believe when one looks at them.
passages.vernacular: 唔知點嘅,想到綠色屋頂裡有個細路,就覺得怪怪嘅;嗰度從來冇過細路,因為蓋新房子嘅時候,馬修同瑪麗拉已經長大喇——假如佢哋都曾係細路嘅話,睇住佢哋,真叫人難以相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知怎麼的,想到綠色屋頂裡有個孩子,就覺得怪怪的;那裡從來沒有過孩子,因為蓋新房子的時候,馬修和瑪麗拉已經長大了——假如他們也曾是孩子的話,看著他們,真叫人難以相信。

passages.original: I wouldn’t be in that orphan’s shoes for anything.
passages.vernacular: 我講乜嘢都唔願站喺嗰孤兒嘅位置上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說什麼也不願站在那孤兒的位置上。

passages.original: My, but I pity him, that’s what.”
passages.vernacular: 天呀,我真可憐佢,就係咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,我真可憐他,就是這樣。」

passages.original: So said Mrs. Rachel to the wild rose bushes out of the fulness of her heart; but if she could have seen the child who was waiting patiently at the Bright River station at that very moment her pity would have been still deeper and more profound.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太把滿腔嘅心裡話都對野玫瑰叢講喇;不過,如果佢能睇見此刻正耐心地喺明河車站等住嘅嗰個細路,佢嘅憐憫一定會更深更切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太把滿腔的心裡話都對野玫瑰叢說了;可是,如果她能看見此刻正耐心地在明河車站等著的那個孩子,她的憐憫一定會更深更切。

chapters.title: Ch. II Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised 第二章:馬修·卡思伯特吃了一驚

passages.original: CH MATTHEW Cuthbert and the sorrel mare jogged comfortably over the eight miles to Bright River.
passages.vernacular: 馬修·卡思伯特同嗰匹栗色母馬,舒舒服服地小跑過咗去明河嘅八英里路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修·卡思伯特和那匹栗色母馬,舒舒服服地小跑過了去明河的八英里路。

passages.original: It was a pretty road, running along between snug farmsteads, with now and again a bit of balsamy fir wood to drive through or a hollow where wild plums hung out their filmy bloom.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一條漂亮嘅路,沿住舒適嘅農舍旁邊延伸,不時要穿過一小片散發住香脂味嘅冷杉林,或係經過一個野李花飄住輕紗般花朵嘅窪地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一條漂亮的路,沿著舒適的農舍旁邊延伸,不時要穿過一小片散發著香脂味的冷杉林,或是經過一個野李花飄著輕紗般花朵的窪地。

passages.original: The air was sweet with the breath of many apple orchards and the meadows sloped away in the distance to horizon mists of pearl and purple; while
passages.vernacular: 空氣中瀰漫住許多蘋果園嘅甜香,遠處嘅草地向地平線上珍珠色同紫色嘅薄霧緩緩傾斜;而
passages.vernacularMandarin: 空氣中瀰漫著許多蘋果園的甜香,遠處的草地向地平線上珍珠色和紫色的薄霧緩緩傾斜;而

passages.original: “The little birds sang as if it were The one day of summer in all the year.”
passages.vernacular: 「小鳥唱得歡,彷彿呢個係一年當中唯一嘅夏日。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小鳥唱得歡,彷彿這是一年當中唯一的夏日。」

passages.original: Matthew enjoyed the drive after his own fashion, except during the moments when he met women and had to nod to them--for in Prince Edward Island you are supposed to nod to all and sundry you meet on the road whether you know them or not.
passages.vernacular: 馬修按自己嘅方式享受住呢趟旅程,只有遇見女人必須點頭致意嘅時候才例外——因為喺愛德華王子島,你遇見路上嘅每一個人,無論認識不認識,都得點頭打招呼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修按自己的方式享受著這趟旅程,只有遇見女人必須點頭致意的時候才例外——因為在愛德華王子島,你遇見路上的每一個人,無論認識不認識,都得點頭打招呼。

passages.original: Matthew dreaded all women except Marilla and Mrs. Rachel; he had an uncomfortable feeling that the mysterious creatures were secretly laughing at him.
passages.vernacular: 馬修害怕所有嘅女人,除咗瑪麗拉同雷切爾太太;佢有種不舒服嘅感覺,覺得呢啲神祕嘅生物暗地裡喺笑話佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修害怕所有的女人,除了瑪麗拉和雷切爾太太;他有種不舒服的感覺,覺得這些神祕的生物暗地裡在笑話他。

passages.original: He may have been quite right in thinking so, for he was an odd-looking personage, with an ungainly figure and long iron-gray hair that touched his stooping shoulders, and a full, soft brown beard which he had worn ever since he was twenty.
passages.vernacular: 佢咁想或者好對,因為佢係個長相古怪嘅人,身材笨拙,灰鐵色嘅長髮垂到彎曲嘅肩膀上,仲有一把濃密柔軟嘅棕色鬍子,二十歲起就一直留住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他這麼想也許很對,因為他是個長相古怪的人,身材笨拙,灰鐵色的長髮垂到彎曲的肩膀上,還有一把濃密柔軟的棕色鬍子,二十歲起就一直留著。

passages.original: In fact, he had looked at twenty very much as he looked at sixty, lacking a little of the grayness.
passages.vernacular: 事實上,佢二十歲時嘅樣子同六十歲時差不多,只係少咗啲灰白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實上,他二十歲時的樣子和六十歲時差不多,只是少了一點灰白。

passages.original: When he reached Bright River there was no sign of any train; he thought he was too early, so he tied his horse in the yard of the small Bright River hotel and went over to the station house.
passages.vernacular: 到咗明河,卻冇火車嘅蹤影;佢以為自己嚟早喇,就把馬拴喺明河小旅館嘅院子裡,走向車站大樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到了明河,卻沒有火車的蹤影;他以為自己來早了,就把馬拴在明河小旅館的院子裡,走向車站大樓。

passages.original: The long platform was almost deserted; the only living creature in sight being a girl who was sitting on a pile of shingles at the extreme end.
passages.vernacular: 長長嘅月臺上幾乎冇人;視線中唯一嘅生物,係一個坐喺最遠端一堆木瓦上嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 長長的月臺上幾乎沒有人;視線中唯一的生物,是一個坐在最遠端一堆木瓦上的女孩。

passages.original: Matthew, barely noting that it was a girl, sidled past her as quickly as possible without looking at her.
passages.vernacular: 馬修幾乎冇留意嗰個係個女孩,盡量快地從佢身旁溜咗過去,睇都冇睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修幾乎沒留意那是個女孩,盡量快地從她身旁溜了過去,看都沒看她。

passages.original: Had he looked he could hardly have failed to notice the tense rigidity and expectation of her attitude and expression.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢睇喇,就唔可能不注意到佢嗰緊繃、僵直、滿懷期待嘅姿態同神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他看了,就不可能不注意到她那緊繃、僵直、滿懷期待的姿態和神情。

passages.original: She was sitting there waiting for something or somebody and, since sitting and waiting was the only thing to do just then, she sat and waited with all her might and main.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐喺嗰度等住乜嘢嘢或者乜嘢人,而且既然此刻只有坐住等呢一件事可做,佢就拼盡全力地坐住等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她坐在那裡等著什麼東西或者什麼人,而且既然此刻只有坐著等這一件事可做,她就拼盡全力地坐著等。

passages.original: Matthew encountered the stationmaster locking up the ticket office preparatory to going home for supper, and asked him if the five-thirty train would soon be along.
passages.vernacular: 馬修遇見站長正在鎖售票處,準備回家食晚飯,就問佢五點半嘅火車係唔係快到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修遇見站長正在鎖售票處,準備回家吃晚飯,就問他五點半的火車是不是快到了。

passages.original: “The five-thirty train has been in and gone half an hour ago,” answered that brisk official.
passages.vernacular: 「五點半嘅火車半小時前就進站又開走喇,」嗰位乾脆利落嘅官員回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「五點半的火車半小時前就進站又開走了,」那位乾脆利落的官員回答。

passages.original: “But there was a passenger dropped off for you--a little girl.
passages.vernacular: 「不過有個乘客畀你哋留下喇——一個小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過有個乘客給你們留下了——一個小女孩。

passages.original: She’s sitting out there on the shingles.
passages.vernacular: 佢就坐喺嗰邊木瓦堆上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她就坐在那邊木瓦堆上。

passages.original: I asked her to go into the ladies’ waiting room, but she informed me gravely that she preferred to stay outside.
passages.vernacular: 我請佢到女候車室去,可佢一本正經地告訴我,佢寧願待喺外面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我請她到女候車室去,可她一本正經地告訴我,她寧願待在外面。

passages.original: ‘There was more scope for imagination,’ she said.
passages.vernacular: 『嗰度有更多想像嘅空間,』佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『那裡有更多想像的空間,』她說。

passages.original: She’s a case, I should say.”
passages.vernacular: 我睇佢不過個奇人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看她可是個奇人。」

passages.original: “I’m not expecting a girl,” said Matthew blankly.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇喺等女孩,」馬修茫然地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒有在等女孩,」馬修茫然地說。

passages.original: “It’s a boy I’ve come for.
passages.vernacular: 「我係嚟接一個男孩嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是來接一個男孩的。

passages.original: He should be here.
passages.vernacular: 佢應該喺呢兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他應該在這兒。

passages.original: Mrs. Alexander Spencer was to bring him over from Nova Scotia for me.”
passages.vernacular: 亞歷山大·斯潘塞太太應該從新斯科舍畀我帶佢過嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 亞歷山大·斯潘塞太太應該從新斯科舍給我帶他過來。」

passages.original: The stationmaster whistled.
passages.vernacular: 站長吹咗聲口哨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站長吹了聲口哨。

passages.original: “Guess there’s some mistake,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇係出咗乜嘢差錯,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看是出了什麼差錯,」他說。

passages.original: “Mrs. Spencer came off the train with that girl and gave her into my charge.
passages.vernacular: 「斯潘塞太太同嗰個女孩一起下嘅車,把佢交畀咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「斯潘塞太太和那個女孩一起下的車,把她交給了我。

passages.original: Said you and your sister were adopting her from an orphan asylum and that you would be along for her presently.
passages.vernacular: 講你同你妹妹要從孤兒院領養佢,你好快就會嚟接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說你和你妹妹要從孤兒院領養她,你很快就會來接她。

passages.original: That’s all I know about it--and I haven’t got any more orphans concealed hereabouts.”
passages.vernacular: 我就知道咁多——我呢一帶可冇藏住別嘅孤兒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就知道這麼多——我這一帶可沒藏著別的孤兒。」

passages.original: “I don’t understand,” said Matthew helplessly, wishing that Marilla was at hand to cope with the situation.
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白,」馬修無助地講,真希望瑪麗拉喺身邊嚟應付呢種局面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白,」馬修無助地說,真希望瑪麗拉在身邊來應付這種局面。

passages.original: “Well, you’d better question the girl,” said the stationmaster carelessly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你最好去問問嗰個女孩,」站長隨意地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你最好去問問那個女孩,」站長隨意地說。

passages.original: “I dare say she’ll be able to explain--she’s got a tongue of her own, that’s certain.
passages.vernacular: 「我敢講佢能解釋清楚——佢有一張自己嘅嘴,呢個係肯定嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢說她能解釋清楚——她有一張自己的嘴,這是肯定的。

passages.original: Maybe they were out of boys of the brand you wanted.”
passages.vernacular: 或者佢哋嗰度冇你要嘅嗰種牌子嘅男孩喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許他們那裡沒有你要的那種牌子的男孩了。」

passages.original: He walked jauntily away, being hungry, and the unfortunate Matthew was left to do that which was harder for him than bearding a lion in its den--walk up to a girl--a strange girl--an orphan girl--and demand of her why she wasn’t a boy.
passages.vernacular: 佢因為餓喇,輕快地走開喇,不幸嘅馬修被留下去做一件對佢來講比虎穴捋鬚更難嘅事——走向一個女孩——一個陌生嘅女孩——一個孤兒女孩——仲要質問佢點解唔係個男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他因為餓了,輕快地走開了,不幸的馬修被留下去做一件對他來說比虎穴捋鬚更難的事——走向一個女孩——一個陌生的女孩——一個孤兒女孩——還要質問她為什麼不是個男孩。

passages.original: Matthew groaned in spirit as he turned about and shuffled gently down the platform towards her.
passages.vernacular: 馬修心裡呻吟咗一聲,轉過身,慢吞吞地朝佢走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修心裡呻吟了一聲,轉過身,慢吞吞地朝她走去。

passages.original: She had been watching him ever since he had passed her and she had her eyes on him now.
passages.vernacular: 自從佢走過佢身邊,佢就一直喺睇住佢,呢陣佢嘅眼睛仲盯喺佢身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從他走過她身邊,她就一直在看著他,這時她的眼睛還盯在他身上。

passages.original: Matthew was not looking at her and would not have seen what she was really like if he had been, but an ordinary observer would have seen this: A child of about eleven, garbed in a very short, very tight, very ugly dress of yellowish-gray wincey.
passages.vernacular: 馬修冇睇佢,即使睇咗都睇不出佢到底係個乜嘢樣嘅人,但係一個普通嘅觀察者會睇到呢啲:一個大約十一歲嘅細路,穿住一件又短、又緊、又難睇嘅淡黃灰色棉毛混紡裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修沒有看她,即使看了也看不出她到底是個什麼樣的人,但是一個普通的觀察者會看到這些:一個大約十一歲的孩子,穿著一件又短、又緊、又難看的淡黃灰色棉毛混紡裙子。

passages.original: She wore a faded brown sailor hat and beneath the hat, extending down her back, were two braids of very thick, decidedly red hair.
passages.vernacular: 佢戴住一頂褪色嘅棕色水手帽,帽子下面,垂到背後嘅係兩根好粗嘅、紅得毫不含糊嘅辮子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她戴著一頂褪色的棕色水手帽,帽子下面,垂到背後的是兩根非常粗的、紅得毫不含糊的辮子。

passages.original: Her face was small, white and thin, also much freckled; her mouth was large and so were her eyes, which looked green in some lights and moods and gray in others.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉又小又白又瘦,仲長滿咗雀斑;嘴好大,眼睛都好大,喺某些光線同情緒下睇上去係綠色,喺另啲時候則係灰色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉又小又白又瘦,還長滿了雀斑;嘴很大,眼睛也很大,在某些光線和情緒下看上去是綠色,在另一些時候則是灰色。

passages.original: So far, the ordinary observer; an extraordinary observer might have seen that the chin was very pointed and pronounced; that the big eyes were full of spirit and vivacity; that the mouth was sweet-lipped and expressive; that the forehead was broad and full; in short, our discerning extraordinary observer might have concluded that no commonplace soul inhabited the body of this stray woman-child of whom shy Matthew Cuthbert was so ludicrously afraid.
passages.vernacular: 普通嘅觀察者就睇到呢啲;一位不普通嘅觀察者或者會睇到,嗰下巴好尖,好突出;嗰雙大眼睛充滿咗精神同活力;嗰嘴唇甜美而富於表情;嗰前額寬闊飽滿;總之,我哋呢位有洞察力嘅不普通觀察者或者會斷定,呢個被害羞嘅馬修·卡思伯特如此荒唐地害怕住嘅流浪女孩身上,棲居嘅絕唔係一個平庸嘅靈魂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 普通的觀察者就看到這些;一位不普通的觀察者也許會看到,那下巴非常尖,非常突出;那雙大眼睛充滿了精神和活力;那嘴唇甜美而富於表情;那前額寬闊飽滿;總之,我們這位有洞察力的不普通觀察者也許會斷定,這個被害羞的馬修·卡思伯特如此荒唐地害怕著的流浪女孩身上,棲居的絕不是一個平庸的靈魂。

passages.original: Matthew, however, was spared the ordeal of speaking first, for as soon as she concluded that he was coming to her she stood up, grasping with one thin brown hand the handle of a shabby, old-fashioned carpet-bag; the other she held out to him.
passages.vernacular: 然而,馬修唔使經受先開口嘅折磨,因為佢一斷定佢係朝佢走嚟嘅,就站咗起嚟,一隻瘦瘦嘅棕色小手攥住一隻破舊、老式嘅毯子布手提袋嘅提手;另一隻手向佢伸咗過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,馬修不必經受先開口的折磨,因為她一斷定他是朝她走來的,就站了起來,一隻瘦瘦的棕色小手攥著一隻破舊、老式的毯子布手提袋的提手;另一隻手向他伸了過來。

passages.original: “I suppose you are Mr. Matthew Cuthbert of Green Gables?” she said in a peculiarly clear, sweet voice.
passages.vernacular: 「我想,您就係綠色屋頂嘅馬修·卡思伯特先生吧?」佢用一種特別清脆甜美嘅聲音講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想,您就是綠色屋頂的馬修·卡思伯特先生吧?」她用一種特別清脆甜美的聲音說。

passages.original: “I’m very glad to see you.
passages.vernacular: 「見到您我真高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「見到您我真高興。

passages.original: I was beginning to be afraid you weren’t coming for me and I was imagining all the things that might have happened to prevent you.
passages.vernacular: 我頭先開始害怕您不嚟接我喇,仲喺想像可能發生嘅各種事,阻止咗您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我剛才開始害怕您不來接我了,還在想像可能發生的各種事,阻止了您。

passages.original: I had made up my mind that if you didn’t come for me tonight I’d go down the track to that big wild cherry-tree at the bend, and climb up into it to stay all night.
passages.vernacular: 我已經打定主意,如果您今晚不嚟接我,我就順住鐵軌走到轉彎處嗰棵大野櫻桃樹嗰兒,爬到樹上去過夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經打定主意,如果您今晚不來接我,我就順著鐵軌走到轉彎處那棵大野櫻桃樹那兒,爬到樹上去過夜。

passages.original: I wouldn’t be a bit afraid, and it would be lovely to sleep in a wild cherry-tree all white with bloom in the moonshine, don’t you think?
passages.vernacular: 我啲兒都唔會害怕,而且瞓喺月光下開滿咗白花嘅野櫻桃樹上,一定好美妙,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一點兒也不會害怕,而且睡在月光下開滿了白花的野櫻桃樹上,一定很美妙,您說呢?

passages.original: You could imagine you were dwelling in marble halls, couldn’t you?
passages.vernacular: 您可以想像自己住喺大理石嘅殿堂裡,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您可以想像自己住在大理石的殿堂裡,是不是?

passages.original: And I was quite sure you would come for me in the morning, if you didn’t tonight.”
passages.vernacular: 而且我好確信,如果今晚您不嚟,聽日朝早您一定會嚟接我嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我很確信,如果今晚您不來,明天早上您一定會來接我的。」

passages.original: Matthew had taken the scrawny little hand awkwardly in his; then and there he decided what to do.
passages.vernacular: 馬修笨拙地握住咗嗰隻瘦小嘅手;當時當地佢就決定該點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修笨拙地握住了那隻瘦小的手;當時當地他就決定該怎麼辦。

passages.original: He could not tell this child with the glowing eyes that there had been a mistake; he would take her home and let Marilla do that.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔能夠告訴呢個眼睛閃閃發亮嘅細路,出咗差錯;佢要把佢領回家,讓瑪麗拉去講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不能告訴這個眼睛閃閃發亮的孩子,出了差錯;他要把她領回家,讓瑪麗拉去說。

passages.original: She couldn’t be left at Bright River anyhow, no matter what mistake had been made, so all questions and explanations might as well be deferred until he was safely back at Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 不管出咗乜嘢差錯,反正唔能夠把佢丟喺明河,所以所有嘅問題和解釋,不如等佢安全回到綠色屋頂再講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管出了什麼差錯,反正不能把她丟在明河,所以所有的問題和解釋,不如等他安全回到綠色屋頂再說。

passages.original: “I’m sorry I was late,” he said shyly.
passages.vernacular: 「對不起,我嚟晚喇,」佢害羞地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對不起,我來晚了,」他害羞地說。

passages.original: “Come along.
passages.vernacular: 「走吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「走吧。

passages.original: The horse is over in the yard.
passages.vernacular: 馬喺院子嗰邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬在院子那邊。

passages.original: Give me your bag.”
passages.vernacular: 把你嘅包畀我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你的包給我。」

passages.original: “Oh, I can carry it,” the child responded cheerfully.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我自己能攞,」細路高興地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我自己能拿,」孩子高興地回答。

passages.original: “It isn’t heavy.
passages.vernacular: 「不重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不重。

passages.original: I’ve got all my worldly goods in it, but it isn’t heavy.
passages.vernacular: 我所有嘅家當都喺裡面,但不重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我所有的家當都在裡面,但不重。

passages.original: And if it isn’t carried in just a certain way the handle pulls out--so I’d better keep it because I know the exact knack of it.
passages.vernacular: 而且如果唔使某種特定嘅方法攞,提手就會脫落——所以最好定係我自己攞,因為我知道其中的確切竅門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且如果不用某種特定的方法拿,提手就會脫落——所以最好還是我自己拿,因為我知道其中的確切竅門。

passages.original: It’s an extremely old carpet-bag.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個極其老嘅毯子布提包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個極其老的毯子布提包。

passages.original: Oh, I’m very glad you’ve come, even if it would have been nice to sleep in a wild cherry-tree.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我好高興您嚟喇,儘管瞓喺野櫻桃樹上都會好美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我很高興您來了,儘管睡在野櫻桃樹上也會很美。

passages.original: We’ve got to drive a long piece, haven’t we?
passages.vernacular: 我哋要趕好長一段路,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要趕很長一段路,是不是?

passages.original: Mrs. Spencer said it was eight miles.
passages.vernacular: 斯潘塞太太講係八英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯潘塞太太說是八英里。

passages.original: I’m glad because I love driving.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興,因為我愛坐車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興,因為我愛坐車。

passages.original: Oh, it seems so wonderful that I’m going to live with you and belong to you.
passages.vernacular: 哦,想到我要跟您一起生活,屬於您,真係太美妙喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,想到我要跟您一起生活,屬於您,真是太美妙了。

passages.original: I’ve never belonged to anybody--not really.
passages.vernacular: 我從來冇屬於過任何人——唔係真正屬於過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從來沒有屬於過任何人——不是真正屬於過。

passages.original: But the asylum was the worst.
passages.vernacular: 可孤兒院係最糟糕嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可孤兒院是最糟糕的。

passages.original: I’ve only been in it four months, but that was enough.
passages.vernacular: 我只喺裡面待咗四個月,但嗰已經夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只在裡面待了四個月,但那已經夠了。

passages.original: I don’t suppose you ever were an orphan in an asylum, so you can’t possibly understand what it is like.
passages.vernacular: 我想您從來冇當過孤兒院裡嘅孤兒,所以唔可能明白嗰個係乜嘢樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想您從來沒當過孤兒院裡的孤兒,所以不可能明白那是什麼樣子。

passages.original: It’s worse than anything you could imagine.
passages.vernacular: 嗰比你能想像嘅任何事都更糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那比你能想像的任何事都更糟。

passages.original: Mrs. Spencer said it was wicked of me to talk like that, but I didn’t mean to be wicked.
passages.vernacular: 斯潘塞太太講我嗰樣講話係不好嘅,但我並唔係故意要不好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯潘塞太太說我那樣說話是不好的,但我並不是故意要不好。

passages.original: It’s so easy to be wicked without knowing it, isn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 唔知不覺地就變壞喇,呢太容易喇,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知不覺地就變壞了,這太容易了,是不是?

passages.original: They were good, you know--the asylum people.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋係好人,您知道——孤兒院嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們是好人,您知道——孤兒院的人。

passages.original: But there is so little scope for the imagination in an asylum--only just in the other orphans.
passages.vernacular: 但係孤兒院裡想像嘅餘地太少喇——只有喺別嘅孤兒身上才有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是孤兒院裡想像的餘地太少了——只有在別的孤兒身上才有。

passages.original: It was pretty interesting to imagine things about them--to imagine that perhaps the girl who sat next to you was really the daughter of a belted earl, who had been stolen away from her parents in her infancy by a cruel nurse who died before she could confess.
passages.vernacular: 想像佢哋嘅事挺有意思嘅——想像坐喺你旁邊嘅嗰個女孩或者真係某位佩帶綬帶嘅伯爵嘅女兒,喺襁褓中被一個殘忍嘅保姆從父母身邊偷走喇,嗰保姆仲冇嚟得及坦白就死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想像他們的事挺有意思的——想像坐在你旁邊的那個女孩也許真是某位佩帶綬帶的伯爵的女兒,在襁褓中被一個殘忍的保姆從父母身邊偷走了,那保姆還沒來得及坦白就死了。

passages.original: I used to lie awake at nights and imagine things like that, because I didn’t have time in the day.
passages.vernacular: 我以前夜裡躺住瞓不住,就想像呢類事情,因為白天冇時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以前夜裡躺著睡不著,就想像這類事情,因為白天沒時間。

passages.original: I guess that’s why I’m so thin--I am dreadful thin, ain’t I?
passages.vernacular: 我想呢個就係我咁瘦嘅原因——我瘦得可怕,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想這就是我這麼瘦的原因——我瘦得可怕,是不是?

passages.original: There isn’t a pick on my bones.
passages.vernacular: 骨頭上啲肉都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 骨頭上一點肉都沒有。

passages.original: I do love to imagine I’m nice and plump, with dimples in my elbows.”
passages.vernacular: 我真鍾意想像自己又白又胖,胳膊肘上有小酒窩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真喜歡想像自己又白又胖,胳膊肘上有小酒窩。」

passages.original: With this Matthew’s companion stopped talking, partly because she was out of breath and partly because they had reached the buggy.
passages.vernacular: 講到呢度,馬修嘅同伴停止咗講話,一半係因為佢喘不過氣嚟,一半係因為佢哋已經走到咗馬車旁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說到這裡,馬修的同伴停止了說話,一半是因為她喘不過氣來,一半是因為他們已經走到了馬車旁。

passages.original: Not another word did she say until they had left the village and were driving down a steep little hill, the road part of which had been cut so deeply into the soft soil that the banks, fringed with blooming wild cherry-trees and slim white birches, were several feet above their heads.
passages.vernacular: 直到佢哋離開村子,沿住一條陡峭嘅小坡往下走,嗰一段路被深深地切進鬆軟嘅土裡,兩邊長住盛開嘅野櫻桃樹同纖細白樺嘅堤岸比佢哋嘅頭頂高出好幾英尺,佢才再都冇講過一句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到他們離開村子,沿著一條陡峭的小坡往下走,那一段路被深深地切進鬆軟的土裡,兩邊長著盛開的野櫻桃樹和纖細白樺的堤岸比他們的頭頂高出好幾英尺,她才再也沒說過一句話。

passages.original: The child put out her hand and broke off a branch of wild plum that brushed against the side of the buggy.
passages.vernacular: 細路伸出手,折下一根擦過馬車側面嘅野李樹枝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子伸出手,折下一根擦過馬車側面的野李樹枝。

passages.original: “Isn’t that beautiful?
passages.vernacular: 「嗰不美嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那不美嗎?

passages.original: What did that tree, leaning out from the bank, all white and lacy, make you think of?” she asked.
passages.vernacular: 嗰棵從堤岸上探出身嚟、全身雪白又像蕾絲一樣嘅樹,讓您想起乜嘢?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那棵從堤岸上探出身來、全身雪白又像蕾絲一樣的樹,讓您想起什麼?」她問。

passages.original: “Well now, I dunno,” said Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個嘛,我唔知道,」馬修講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這個嘛,我不知道,」馬修說。

passages.original: “Why, a bride, of course--a bride all in white with a lovely misty veil.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,當然係新娘啦——穿住一身白、披住可愛嘅朦朧面紗嘅新娘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,當然是新娘啦——穿著一身白、披著可愛的朦朧面紗的新娘。

passages.original: I’ve never seen one, but I can imagine what she would look like.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過新娘,但我能想像佢係乜嘢模樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過新娘,但我能想像她是什麼模樣。

passages.original: I don’t ever expect to be a bride myself.
passages.vernacular: 我自己從冇指望能做新娘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己從沒指望能做新娘。

passages.original: I’m so homely nobody will ever want to marry me--unless it might be a foreign missionary.
passages.vernacular: 我長得咁醜,冇人會想娶我——除非係個去國外嘅傳教士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我長得這麼醜,沒人會想娶我——除非是個去國外的傳教士。

passages.original: I suppose a foreign missionary mightn’t be very particular.
passages.vernacular: 我想去國外嘅傳教士或者唔會太挑剔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想去國外的傳教士也許不會太挑剔。

passages.original: But I do hope that some day I shall have a white dress.
passages.vernacular: 不過我真希望有一天我能有一件白衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我真希望有一天我能有一件白衣服。

passages.original: That is my highest ideal of earthly bliss.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係我心目中塵世幸福嘅最高理想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是我心目中塵世幸福的最高理想。

passages.original: I just love pretty clothes.
passages.vernacular: 我就係愛漂亮嘅衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是愛漂亮的衣服。

passages.original: And I’ve never had a pretty dress in my life that I can remember--but of course it’s all the more to look forward to, isn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 而我記憶中從來冇過一件漂亮嘅衣服——不過當然咁樣就更有盼頭喇,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我記憶中從來沒有過一件漂亮的衣服——不過當然這樣就更有盼頭了,是不是?

passages.original: And then I can imagine that I’m dressed gorgeously.
passages.vernacular: 然後我就可以想像自己穿住華麗嘅衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我就可以想像自己穿著華麗的衣服。

passages.original: This morning when I left the asylum I felt so ashamed because I had to wear this horrid old wincey dress.
passages.vernacular: 今日朝早我離開孤兒院嘅時候,覺得好羞愧,因為我得穿呢件難睇嘅舊毛混紡裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天早上我離開孤兒院的時候,覺得很羞愧,因為我得穿這件難看的舊毛混紡裙子。

passages.original: All the orphans had to wear them, you know.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅孤兒都得穿呢種,您知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的孤兒都得穿這種,您知道。

passages.original: A merchant in Hopeton last winter donated three hundred yards of wincey to the asylum.
passages.vernacular: 去年冬天霍普頓有個商人畀孤兒院捐咗三百碼呢種料子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去年冬天霍普頓有個商人給孤兒院捐了三百碼這種料子。

passages.original: Some people said it was because he couldn’t sell it, but I’d rather believe that it was out of the kindness of his heart, wouldn’t you?
passages.vernacular: 有人講嗰個係因為佢賣不出去,但我寧願相信嗰個係出於佢嘅好心,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人說那是因為他賣不出去,但我寧願相信那是出於他的好心,您說呢?

passages.original: When we got on the train I felt as if everybody must be looking at me and pitying me.
passages.vernacular: 我哋上火車嘅時候,我覺得人人都一定喺睇住我、可憐我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們上火車的時候,我覺得人人都一定在看著我、可憐我。

passages.original: But I just went to work and imagined that I had on the most beautiful pale blue silk dress--because when you are imagining you might as well imagine something worth while--and a big hat all flowers and nodding plumes, and a gold watch, and kid gloves and boots.
passages.vernacular: 不過我就開始想像我穿住最美麗嘅淡藍色綢緞裙子——因為既然係想像,不如想像點值得嘅嘢——仲戴住一頂全係花同搖曳羽毛嘅大帽子,有一塊金錶,仲有小山羊皮手套同靴子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我就開始想像我穿著最美麗的淡藍色綢緞裙子——因為既然是想像,不如想像點值得的東西——還戴著一頂全是花和搖曳羽毛的大帽子,有一塊金錶,還有小山羊皮手套和靴子。

passages.original: I felt cheered up right away and I enjoyed my trip to the Island with all my might.
passages.vernacular: 我即刻就高興起嚟,盡情地享受咗我去島上嘅旅程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我馬上就高興起來,盡情地享受了我去島上的旅程。

passages.original: I wasn’t a bit sick coming over in the boat.
passages.vernacular: 我坐船過嚟嘅時候啲都不暈船。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我坐船過來的時候一點也不暈船。

passages.original: Neither was Mrs. Spencer, although she generally is.
passages.vernacular: 斯潘塞太太都冇暈,儘管佢一般都會暈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯潘塞太太也沒暈,儘管她一般都會暈。

passages.original: She said she hadn’t time to get sick, watching to see that I didn’t fall overboard.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢冇工夫暈船,因為要睇住我別掉到海裡去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她沒工夫暈船,因為要看著我別掉到海裡去。

passages.original: She said she never saw the beat of me for prowling about.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢從冇見過比我更愛到處亂逛嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她從沒見過比我更愛到處亂逛的人。

passages.original: But if it kept her from being seasick it’s a mercy I did prowl, isn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 不過要係呢讓佢冇暈船,嗰我亂逛倒係萬幸喇,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過要是這讓她沒有暈船,那我亂逛倒是萬幸了,是不是?

passages.original: And I wanted to see everything that was to be seen on that boat, because I didn’t know whether I’d ever have another opportunity.
passages.vernacular: 而且我想睇遍嗰條船上所有能睇嘅嘢,因為我唔知道以後仲有冇機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我想看遍那條船上所有能看的東西,因為我不知道以後還有沒有機會。

passages.original: Oh, there are a lot more cherry-trees all in bloom!
passages.vernacular: 哦,又有好多開滿花嘅櫻桃樹!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,又有好多開滿花的櫻桃樹!

passages.original: This Island is the bloomiest place.
passages.vernacular: 呢座島係最繁花似錦嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這座島是最繁花似錦的地方。

passages.original: I just love it already, and I’m so glad I’m going to live here.
passages.vernacular: 我已經愛上佢喇,我太高興能住喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經愛上它了,我太高興能住在這裡。

passages.original: I’ve always heard that Prince Edward Island was the prettiest place in the world, and I used to imagine I was living here, but I never really expected I would.
passages.vernacular: 我一直聽講愛德華王子島係世上最美嘅地方,我以前常想像自己住喺呢度,但我從冇真嘅指望過會成真。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直聽說愛德華王子島是世上最美的地方,我以前常想像自己住在這裡,但我從沒真的指望過會成真。

passages.original: It’s delightful when your imaginations come true, isn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 想像成真係幾咁令人愉快啊,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想像成真是多麼令人愉快啊,是不是?

passages.original: But those red roads are so funny.
passages.vernacular: 不過嗰啲紅色嘅路真有趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過那些紅色的路真有趣。

passages.original: When we got into the train at Charlottetown and the red roads began to flash past I asked Mrs. Spencer what made them red and she said she didn’t know and for pity’s sake not to ask her any more questions.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺夏洛特敦上火車,紅色嘅路開始閃過窗外嘅時候,我問斯潘塞太太係乜嘢讓佢哋變紅嘅,佢講佢唔知道,仲講睇喺老天嘅份上唔好再問佢問題喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在夏洛特敦上火車,紅色的路開始閃過窗外的時候,我問斯潘塞太太是什麼讓它們變紅的,她說她不知道,還說看在老天的份上別再問她問題了。

passages.original: She said I must have asked her a thousand already.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我已經問咗佢上千個喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我已經問了她上千個了。

passages.original: I suppose I had, too, but how are you going to find out about things if you don’t ask questions?
passages.vernacular: 我想我確實問喇,但係你不問問題,點能弄明白事情呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我確實問了,但是你不問問題,怎麼能弄明白事情呢?

passages.original: And what does make the roads red?”
passages.vernacular: 嗰到底係乜嘢讓路變紅嘅呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那到底是什麼讓路變紅的呢?」

passages.original: “Well now, I dunno,” said Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個嘛,我唔知道,」馬修講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這個嘛,我不知道,」馬修說。

passages.original: “Well, that is one of the things to find out sometime.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,嗰個係有一天要弄明白嘅事情之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,那是有一天要弄明白的事情之一。

passages.original: Isn’t it splendid to think of all the things there are to find out about?
passages.vernacular: 想想有咁多事情有待弄明白,係唔係太棒喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想想有那麼多事情有待弄明白,是不是太棒了?

passages.original: It just makes me feel glad to be alive--it’s such an interesting world.
passages.vernacular: 呢讓我覺得活住真高興——呢個係個幾咁有趣嘅世界啊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這讓我覺得活著真高興——這是個多麼有趣的世界啊。

passages.original: It wouldn’t be half so interesting if we knew all about everything, would it?
passages.vernacular: 要係我哋乜嘢都知道,就連一半有趣都冇喇,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是我們什麼都知道,就連一半有趣都沒有了,是不是?

passages.original: There’d be no scope for imagination then, would there?
passages.vernacular: 嗰樣就冇想像嘅餘地喇,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那樣就沒有想像的餘地了,是不是?

passages.original: But am I talking too much?
passages.vernacular: 不過我係唔係話講得太多喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我是不是話說得太多了?

passages.original: People are always telling me I do.
passages.vernacular: 人哋總是講我話多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們總是說我話多。

passages.original: Would you rather I didn’t talk?
passages.vernacular: 您係唔係寧願我不講話?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您是不是寧願我不說話?

passages.original: If you say so I’ll stop.
passages.vernacular: 如果您講讓我唔好講喇,我就不講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您說讓我別說了,我就不說。

passages.original: I can stop when I make up my mind to it, although it’s difficult.”
passages.vernacular: 只要我打定咗主意,我就能停下嚟,雖然好難。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要我打定了主意,我就能停下來,雖然很難。」

passages.original: Matthew, much to his own surprise, was enjoying himself.
passages.vernacular: 馬修自己都好驚訝,佢居然好開心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修自己都很驚訝,他居然很開心。

passages.original: Like most quiet folks he liked talkative people when they were willing to do the talking themselves and did not expect him to keep up his end of it.
passages.vernacular: 像大多數安靜嘅人一樣,佢鍾意健談嘅人,只要佢哋肯自己講,而不指望佢嚟接話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像大多數安靜的人一樣,他喜歡健談的人,只要他們肯自己說,而不指望他來接話。

passages.original: But he had never expected to enjoy the society of a little girl.
passages.vernacular: 但佢從來冇想到自己會鍾意一個小女孩嘅陪伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他從來沒想到自己會喜歡一個小女孩的陪伴。

passages.original: Women were bad enough in all conscience, but little girls were worse.
passages.vernacular: 女人已經夠糟糕嘅喇,可小女孩更糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女人已經夠糟糕的了,可小女孩更糟。

passages.original: He detested the way they had of sidling past him timidly, with sidewise glances, as if they expected him to gobble them up at a mouthful if they ventured to say a word.
passages.vernacular: 佢討厭佢哋從佢身邊怯生生地溜過去、斜住眼睛瞟嘅樣子,好像佢哋要係敢講一句話,佢就會一口把佢哋吞掉似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他討厭她們從他身邊怯生生地溜過去、斜著眼睛瞟的樣子,好像他們要是敢說一句話,他就會一口把她們吞掉似的。

passages.original: That was the Avonlea type of well-bred little girl.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個就係阿文利嗰種教養良好嘅小女孩嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就是阿文利那種教養良好的小女孩的樣子。

passages.original: But this freckled witch was very different, and although he found it rather difficult for his slower intelligence to keep up with her brisk mental processes he thought that he “kind of liked her chatter.”
passages.vernacular: 不過呢個長滿雀斑嘅小精靈完全不同,雖然佢覺得自己遲鈍嘅頭腦好難跟上佢敏捷嘅思路,但佢覺得自己「有點鍾意佢嘅嘮叨」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是這個長滿雀斑的小精靈完全不同,雖然他覺得自己遲鈍的頭腦很難跟上她敏捷的思路,但他覺得自己「有點喜歡她的嘮叨」。

passages.original: So he said as shyly as usual:
passages.vernacular: 所以佢像往常一樣害羞地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他像往常一樣害羞地說:

passages.original: “Oh, you can talk as much as you like.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你想講多少就講多少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你想說多少就說多少。

passages.original: I don’t mind.”
passages.vernacular: 我不介意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不介意。」

passages.original: “Oh, I’m so glad.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我太高興喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我太高興了。

passages.original: I know you and I are going to get along together fine.
passages.vernacular: 我知道您同我會相處得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道您和我會相處得很好。

passages.original: It’s such a relief to talk when one wants to and not be told that children should be seen and not heard.
passages.vernacular: 能想講就講,而不被人講小細路只該睇不該出聲,真係一種解脫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 能想說就說,而不被人說小孩子只該看不該出聲,真是一種解脫。

passages.original: I’ve had that said to me a million times if I have once.
passages.vernacular: 呢句話我被人講過不下一百萬次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這句話我被人說過不下一百萬次。

passages.original: And people laugh at me because I use big words.
passages.vernacular: 而且人哋笑我用大詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且人們笑我用大詞。

passages.original: But if you have big ideas you have to use big words to express them, haven’t you?”
passages.vernacular: 不過如果你有大想法,你就得用大詞嚟表達,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是如果你有大想法,你就得用大詞來表達,是不是?」

passages.original: “Well now, that seems reasonable,” said Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢聽起嚟有道理,」馬修講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這聽起來有道理,」馬修說。

passages.original: “Mrs. Spencer said that my tongue must be hung in the middle.
passages.vernacular: 「斯潘塞太太講我嘅舌頭一定係掛喺中間嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「斯潘塞太太說我的舌頭一定是掛在中間的。

passages.original: But it isn’t--it’s firmly fastened at one end.
passages.vernacular: 但唔係——佢牢牢地固定喺一頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但不是——它牢牢地固定在一頭。

passages.original: Mrs. Spencer said your place was named Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 斯潘塞太太講您嘅地方叫綠色屋頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯潘塞太太說您的地方叫綠色屋頂。

passages.original: I asked her all about it.
passages.vernacular: 我向佢問咗個清清楚楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向她問了個清清楚楚。

passages.original: And she said there were trees all around it.
passages.vernacular: 佢講周圍全係樹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說周圍全是樹。

passages.original: I was gladder than ever.
passages.vernacular: 我就更高興喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就更高興了。

passages.original: I just love trees.
passages.vernacular: 我就係愛樹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是愛樹。

passages.original: And there weren’t any at all about the asylum, only a few poor weeny-teeny things out in front with little whitewashed cagey things about them.
passages.vernacular: 孤兒院周圍根本冇樹,只有前面幾棵可憐嘅瘦小嘅嘢,周圍圍住刷白嘅小籠子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孤兒院周圍根本沒有樹,只有前面幾棵可憐的瘦小的東西,周圍圍著刷白的小籠子。

passages.original: They just looked like orphans themselves, those trees did.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲樹睇上去簡直就像孤兒一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些樹看上去簡直就像孤兒一樣。

passages.original: It used to make me want to cry to look at them.
passages.vernacular: 睇住佢哋我常常想哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看著它們我常常想哭。

passages.original: I used to say to them, ‘Oh, you poor little things!
passages.vernacular: 我常對佢哋講:『哦,你哋呢啲可憐嘅小嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我常對它們說:『哦,你們這些可憐的小東西!

passages.original: If you were out in a great big woods with other trees all around you and little mosses and June bells growing over your roots and a brook not far away and birds singing in your branches, you could grow, couldn’t you?
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋係喺一片大森林裡,周圍都係別嘅樹,根上長住小小嘅青苔同六月鈴,不遠處有條小溪,枝頭有鳥兒歌唱,你哋就能長大喇,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們是在一片大森林裡,周圍都是別的樹,根上長著小小的青苔和六月鈴,不遠處有條小溪,枝頭有鳥兒歌唱,你們就能長大了,是不是?

passages.original: But you can’t where you are.
passages.vernacular: 不過喺你哋而家呢個地方就不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是在你們現在這個地方就不行。

passages.original: I know just exactly how you feel, little trees.’
passages.vernacular: 我清清楚楚地知道你哋嘅感受,小樹哋。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我清清楚楚地知道你們的感受,小樹們。』

passages.original: I felt sorry to leave them behind this morning.
passages.vernacular: 今日朝早離開佢哋,我好難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天早上離開它們,我很難過。

passages.original: You do get so attached to things like that, don’t you?
passages.vernacular: 你就係會對咁樣嘅嘢產生感情,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你就是會對這樣的東西產生感情,是不是?

passages.original: Is there a brook anywhere near Green Gables?
passages.vernacular: 綠色屋頂附近有小溪嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 綠色屋頂附近有小溪嗎?

passages.original: I forgot to ask Mrs. Spencer that.”
passages.vernacular: 我忘咗問斯潘塞太太呢啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忘了問斯潘塞太太這一點。」

passages.original: “Well now, yes, there’s one right below the house.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,有嘅,就喺房子下面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,有的,就在房子下面。」

passages.original: “Fancy.
passages.vernacular: 「真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真好。

passages.original: It’s always been one of my dreams to live near a brook.
passages.vernacular: 住喺小溪附近一直係我嘅夢想之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住在小溪附近一直是我的夢想之一。

passages.original: I never expected I would, though.
passages.vernacular: 不過我從冇指望過能實現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我從沒指望過能實現。

passages.original: Dreams don’t often come true, do they?
passages.vernacular: 夢想不常成真,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夢想不常成真,是不是?

passages.original: Wouldn’t it be nice if they did?
passages.vernacular: 要係能成真,唔係好好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是能成真,不是很好嗎?

passages.original: But just now I feel pretty nearly perfectly happy.
passages.vernacular: 不過而家我覺得自己幾乎係完全幸福喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過現在我覺得自己幾乎是完全幸福了。

passages.original: I can’t feel exactly perfectly happy because--well, what color would you call this?”
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠感到完全完全幸福,因為——嗯,您講呢個係乜嘢顏色?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能感到完全完全幸福,因為——嗯,您說這是什麼顏色?」

passages.original: She twitched one of her long glossy braids over her thin shoulder and held it up before Matthew’s eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢把一根長長嘅有光澤嘅辮子從佢瘦削嘅肩頭甩過嚟,舉到馬修眼前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把一根長長的有光澤的辮子從她瘦削的肩頭甩過來,舉到馬修眼前。

passages.original: Matthew was not used to deciding on the tints of ladies’ tresses, but in this case there couldn’t be much doubt.
passages.vernacular: 馬修不習慣判斷女士哋頭髮嘅色調,但喺呢件事上唔會有多大疑問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修不習慣判斷女士們頭髮的色調,但在這件事上不會有多大疑問。

passages.original: “It’s red, ain’t it?” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「係紅色嘅,對不對?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是紅色的,對不對?」他說。

passages.original: The girl let the braid drop back with a sigh that seemed to come from her very toes and to exhale forth all the sorrows of the ages.
passages.vernacular: 女孩讓辮子垂咗下去,發出一聲嘆息,嗰聲音似乎來自佢嘅腳趾,呼出咗千百年嚟所有嘅憂傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩讓辮子垂了下去,發出一聲嘆息,那聲音似乎來自她的腳趾,呼出了千百年來所有的憂傷。

passages.original: “Yes, it’s red,” she said resignedly.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係紅色嘅,」佢認命地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是紅色的,」她認命地說。

passages.original: “Now you see why I can’t be perfectly happy.
passages.vernacular: 「而家您明白點解我唔能夠完全幸福咗吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在您明白為什麼我不能完全幸福了吧。

passages.original: Nobody could who has red hair.
passages.vernacular: 邊個長住紅頭髮都唔可能完全幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰長著紅頭髮也不可能完全幸福。

passages.original: I don’t mind the other things so much--the freckles and the green eyes and my skinniness.
passages.vernacular: 別嘅事我不太在乎——雀斑、綠眼睛,仲有我嘅瘦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別的事我不太在乎——雀斑、綠眼睛,還有我的瘦。

passages.original: I can imagine them away.
passages.vernacular: 我可以把佢哋想像掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以把它們想像掉。

passages.original: I can imagine that I have a beautiful rose-leaf complexion and lovely starry violet eyes.
passages.vernacular: 我可以想像我有玫瑰花瓣般美麗嘅膚色同可愛嘅星星般嘅紫羅蘭色眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以想像我有玫瑰花瓣般美麗的膚色和可愛的星星般的紫羅蘭色眼睛。

passages.original: But I cannot imagine that red hair away.
passages.vernacular: 不過我冇法把紅頭髮想像掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我沒法把紅頭髮想像掉。

passages.original: I do my best.
passages.vernacular: 我盡咗最大努力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我盡了最大努力。

passages.original: I think to myself, ‘Now my hair is a glorious black, black as the raven’s wing.’
passages.vernacular: 我對自己講:『而家我嘅頭髮係光彩奪目的黑色,像烏鴉翅膀一樣黑。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對自己說:『現在我的頭髮是光彩奪目的黑色,像烏鴉翅膀一樣黑。』

passages.original: But all the time I know it is just plain red and it breaks my heart.
passages.vernacular: 不過我心裡一直知道佢不過係普普通通嘅紅色,呢讓我心都碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我心裡一直知道它不過是普普通通的紅色,這讓我心都碎了。

passages.original: It will be my lifelong sorrow.
passages.vernacular: 呢將係我終生嘅悲哀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這將是我終生的悲哀。

passages.original: I read of a girl once in a novel who had a lifelong sorrow but it wasn’t red hair.
passages.vernacular: 我曾喺一本小講裡讀到一個女孩,佢都有終生嘅悲哀,但唔係紅頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我曾在一本小說裡讀到一個女孩,她也有終生的悲哀,但不是紅頭髮。

passages.original: Her hair was pure gold rippling back from her alabaster brow.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅頭髮係純金色嘅,從雪花石膏般嘅額頭向後瀉下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的頭髮是純金色的,從雪花石膏般的額頭向後瀉下。

passages.original: What is an alabaster brow?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢係雪花石膏般嘅額頭?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼是雪花石膏般的額頭?

passages.original: I never could find out.
passages.vernacular: 我一直冇弄明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直沒弄明白。

passages.original: Can you tell me?”
passages.vernacular: 您能告訴我嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您能告訴我嗎?」

passages.original: “Well now, I’m afraid I can’t,” said Matthew, who was getting a little dizzy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,恐怕我講不上嚟,」馬修講,佢有點頭暈喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,恐怕我說不上來,」馬修說,他有點頭暈了。

passages.original: He felt as he had once felt in his rash youth when another boy had enticed him on the merry-go-round at a picnic.
passages.vernacular: 佢感覺就像佢年輕冒失時,曾被另一個男孩喺野餐會上哄去坐旋轉木馬時嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他感覺就像他年輕冒失時,曾被另一個男孩在野餐會上哄去坐旋轉木馬時那樣。

passages.original: “Well, whatever it was it must have been something nice because she was divinely beautiful.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,不管嗰個係乜嘢,一定係好美嘅嘢,因為佢美得像神一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,不管那是什麼,一定是很美的東西,因為她美得像神一樣。

passages.original: Have you ever imagined what it must feel like to be divinely beautiful?”
passages.vernacular: 您有冇想過美得像神一樣係乜嘢感覺?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您有沒有想過美得像神一樣是什麼感覺?」

passages.original: “Well now, no, I haven’t,” confessed Matthew ingenuously.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個嘛,冇,」馬修老實地承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這個嘛,沒有,」馬修老實地承認。

passages.original: “I have, often.
passages.vernacular: 「我常常想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我常常想。

passages.original: Which would you rather be if you had the choice--divinely beautiful or dazzlingly clever or angelically good?”
passages.vernacular: 如果可以選擇,您寧願做邊個——美得像神一樣,定係聰明得令人眼花,定係好得像天使?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果可以選擇,您寧願做哪個——美得像神一樣,還是聰明得令人眼花,還是好得像天使?」

passages.original: “Well now, I--I don’t know exactly.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個嘛,我——我講不準。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這個嘛,我——我說不準。」

passages.original: “Neither do I. I can never decide.
passages.vernacular: 「我都係。我永遠決定不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是。我永遠決定不了。

passages.original: But it doesn’t make much real difference for it isn’t likely I’ll ever be either.
passages.vernacular: 但呢其實冇多大關係,因為我不大可能成為其中任何一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這其實沒多大關係,因為我不大可能成為其中任何一個。

passages.original: It’s certain I’ll never be angelically good.
passages.vernacular: 可以肯定,我永遠唔會好得像天使。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可以肯定,我永遠不會好得像天使。

passages.original: Mrs. Spencer says--oh, Mr. Cuthbert!
passages.vernacular: 斯潘塞太太講——哦,卡思伯特先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯潘塞太太說——哦,卡思伯特先生!

passages.original: Oh, Mr. Cuthbert!!
passages.vernacular: 哦,卡思伯特先生!!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,卡思伯特先生!!

passages.original: Oh, Mr. Cuthbert!!!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,卡思伯特先生!!!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,卡思伯特先生!!!」

passages.original: That was not what Mrs. Spencer had said; neither had the child tumbled out of the buggy nor had Matthew done anything astonishing.
passages.vernacular: 斯潘塞太太並冇講嗰樣嘅話;細路都冇從馬車上摔下去,馬修都冇做乜嘢驚人嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯潘塞太太並沒有說那樣的話;孩子也沒有從馬車上摔下去,馬修也沒有做什麼驚人的事。

passages.original: They had simply rounded a curve in the road and found themselves in the “Avenue.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋只係轉過咗路上嘅一個彎,發現自己進入咗「林蔭道」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們只是轉過了路上的一個彎,發現自己進入了「林蔭道」。

passages.original: The “Avenue,” so called by the Newbridge people, was a stretch of road four or five hundred yards long, completely arched over with huge, wide-spreading apple-trees, planted years ago by an eccentric old farmer.
passages.vernacular: 「林蔭道」,係新橋嘅人咁叫嘅,係一段四五百碼長嘅路,上面完全被巨大嘅、枝杈伸展嘅蘋果樹拱成咗頂,嗰啲樹係多年前一位古怪嘅老農夫栽嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「林蔭道」,是新橋的人這麼叫的,是一段四五百碼長的路,上面完全被巨大的、枝杈伸展的蘋果樹拱成了頂,那些樹是多年前一位古怪的老農夫栽的。

passages.original: Overhead was one long canopy of snowy fragrant bloom.
passages.vernacular: 頭頂係一整片雪白芬芳嘅花朵形成嘅華蓋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭頂是一整片雪白芬芳的花朵形成的華蓋。

passages.original: Below the boughs the air was full of a purple twilight and far ahead a glimpse of painted sunset sky shone like a great rose window at the end of a cathedral aisle.
passages.vernacular: 枝杈下面嘅空氣中瀰漫住紫色嘅暮色,遠處一抹彩繪般嘅夕陽天空,像大教堂走廊盡頭嘅一扇巨大嘅玫瑰花窗一樣閃耀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 枝杈下面的空氣中瀰漫著紫色的暮色,遠處一抹彩繪般的夕陽天空,像大教堂走廊盡頭的一扇巨大的玫瑰花窗一樣閃耀。

passages.original: Its beauty seemed to strike the child dumb.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅美似乎讓細路啞口無言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的美似乎讓孩子啞口無言。

passages.original: She leaned back in the buggy, her thin hands clasped before her, her face lifted rapturously to the white splendor above.
passages.vernacular: 佢靠喺馬車裡,瘦小嘅雙手交握喺胸前,臉狂喜地仰向上方白色嘅華美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她靠在馬車裡,瘦小的雙手交握在胸前,臉狂喜地仰向上方白色的華美。

passages.original: Even when they had passed out and were driving down the long slope to Newbridge she never moved or spoke.
passages.vernacular: 即使佢哋已經走出去,沿住長長嘅斜坡往新橋駛去,佢都冇動,冇講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使他們已經走出去,沿著長長的斜坡往新橋駛去,她也沒有動,沒有說話。

passages.original: Still with rapt face she gazed afar into the sunset west, with eyes that saw visions trooping splendidly across that glowing background.
passages.vernacular: 佢仍帶住入迷嘅神情凝望住遠處嘅夕陽西天,眼睛睇到咗幻象,喺嗰片璀璨嘅背景上華麗地列隊而過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她仍帶著入迷的神情凝望著遠處的夕陽西天,眼睛看到了幻象,在那片璀璨的背景上華麗地列隊而過。

passages.original: Through Newbridge, a bustling little village where dogs barked at them and small boys hooted and curious faces peered from the windows, they drove, still in silence.
passages.vernacular: 穿過新橋,呢個熱鬧嘅小村子,狗朝佢哋吠叫,小男孩哋起鬨,好奇嘅臉從窗戶裡探出嚟,佢哋駛過,仍然沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 穿過新橋,這個熱鬧的小村子,狗朝他們吠叫,小男孩們起鬨,好奇的臉從窗戶裡探出來,他們駛過,仍然沉默。

passages.original: When three more miles had dropped away behind them the child had not spoken.
passages.vernacular: 又走過三英里後,細路定係冇講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又走過三英里後,孩子還是沒說話。

passages.original: She could keep silence, it was evident, as energetically as she could talk.
passages.vernacular: 顯然,佢能夠像講話一樣有力地保持沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 顯然,她能夠像說話一樣有力地保持沉默。

passages.original: “I guess you’re feeling pretty tired and hungry,” Matthew ventured to say at last, accounting for her long visitation of dumbness with the only reason he could think of.
