passages.vernacular: 「我想你一定又累又餓喇,」馬修終於冒險講道,用佢所能想到嘅唯一理由嚟解釋佢長時間嘅啞口無言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你一定又累又餓了,」馬修終於冒險說道,用他所能想到的唯一理由來解釋她長時間的啞口無言。

passages.original: “But we haven’t very far to go now--only another mile.”
passages.vernacular: 「不過我哋都冇多遠喇——只有一英里喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過我們也沒多遠了——只有一英里了。」

passages.original: She came out of her reverie with a deep sigh and looked at him with the dreamy gaze of a soul that had been wondering afar, star-led.
passages.vernacular: 佢深深嘆咗口氣,從沉思中走咗出嚟,睇住佢,目光像一個被星星引領、神遊遠方嘅靈魂嗰樣夢幻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她深深嘆了口氣,從沉思中走了出來,看著他,目光像一個被星星引領、神遊遠方的靈魂那樣夢幻。

passages.original: “Oh, Mr. Cuthbert,” she whispered, “that place we came through--that white place--what was it?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,卡思伯特先生,」佢低聲講,「我哋剛穿過嘅嗰個地方——嗰個白色嘅地方——嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,卡思伯特先生,」她低聲說,「我們剛穿過的那個地方——那個白色的地方——那是什麼?」

passages.original: “Well now, you must mean the Avenue,” said Matthew after a few moments’ profound reflection.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個嘛,你一定係指林蔭道,」馬修喺深思咗片刻之後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這個嘛,你一定是指林蔭道,」馬修在深思了片刻之後說。

passages.original: “It is a kind of pretty place.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係個挺漂亮嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是個挺漂亮的地方。」

passages.original: “Pretty?
passages.vernacular: 「漂亮?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「漂亮?

passages.original: Oh, pretty doesn’t seem the right word to use.
passages.vernacular: 哦,漂亮好像唔係合適嘅詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,漂亮好像不是合適的詞。

passages.original: Nor beautiful, either.
passages.vernacular: 美麗都唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美麗也不是。

passages.original: They don’t go far enough.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都唔夠用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們都不夠用。

passages.original: Oh, it was wonderful--wonderful.
passages.vernacular: 哦,太奇妙喇——太奇妙喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,太奇妙了——太奇妙了。

passages.original: It’s the first thing I ever saw that couldn’t be improved upon by imagination.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我見過嘅第一樣唔能夠用想像力嚟改進嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我見過的第一樣不能用想像力來改進的東西。

passages.original: It just satisfied me here”--she put one hand on her breast--“it made a queer funny ache and yet it was a pleasant ache.
passages.vernacular: 佢就喺呢度讓我滿足喇」——佢把一隻手放喺胸口——「佢讓我有種奇怪嘅有趣嘅疼痛,但嗰又係一種愉快嘅疼痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它就在這裡讓我滿足了」——她把一隻手放在胸口——「它讓我有種奇怪的有趣的疼痛,但那又是一種愉快的疼痛。

passages.original: Did you ever have an ache like that, Mr. Cuthbert?”
passages.vernacular: 您有冇過咁樣嘅疼痛,卡思伯特先生?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您有沒有過這樣的疼痛,卡思伯特先生?」

passages.original: “Well now, I just can’t recollect that I ever had.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個嘛,我想不起嚟我有過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這個嘛,我想不起來我有過。」

passages.original: “I have it lots of times--whenever I see anything royally beautiful.
passages.vernacular: 「我常有——每當睇到任何帝王般美嘅嘢嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我常有——每當看到任何帝王般美的東西的時候。

passages.original: But they shouldn’t call that lovely place the Avenue.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋不該把嗰個可愛嘅地方叫林蔭道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們不該把那個可愛的地方叫林蔭道。

passages.original: There is no meaning in a name like that.
passages.vernacular: 呢種名字冇意義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種名字沒有意義。

passages.original: They should call it--let me see--the White Way of Delight.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋應該叫佢——讓我想想——歡樂白路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們應該叫它——讓我想想——歡樂白路。

passages.original: Isn’t that a nice imaginative name?
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係個好有想像力嘅好名字嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是個很有想像力的好名字嗎?

passages.original: When I don’t like the name of a place or a person I always imagine a new one and always think of them so.
passages.vernacular: 當我不鍾意一個地方或一個人嘅名字時,我總是想像一個新嘅,然後就始終嗰樣想佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我不喜歡一個地方或一個人的名字時,我總是想像一個新的,然後就始終那樣想他們。

passages.original: There was a girl at the asylum whose name was Hepzibah Jenkins, but I always imagined her as Rosalia DeVere.
passages.vernacular: 孤兒院裡有個女孩叫赫普齊巴·詹金斯,但我總是把佢想像成羅莎莉婭·德維爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孤兒院裡有個女孩叫赫普齊巴·詹金斯,但我總是把她想像成羅莎莉婭·德維爾。

passages.original: Other people may call that place the Avenue, but I shall always call it the White Way of Delight.
passages.vernacular: 別人可以管嗰個地方叫林蔭道,但我永遠叫佢歡樂白路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別人可以管那個地方叫林蔭道,但我永遠叫它歡樂白路。

passages.original: Have we really only another mile to go before we get home?
passages.vernacular: 我哋真嘅只剩一英里就到家咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們真的只剩一英里就到家了嗎?

passages.original: I’m glad and I’m sorry.
passages.vernacular: 我既高興又難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我既高興又難過。

passages.original: I’m sorry because this drive has been so pleasant and I’m always sorry when pleasant things end.
passages.vernacular: 我難過係因為呢趟路程咁愉快,而愉快嘅事情結束時我總是難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我難過是因為這趟路程那麼愉快,而愉快的事情結束時我總是難過。

passages.original: Something still pleasanter may come after, but you can never be sure.
passages.vernacular: 後面或者會有更愉快嘅事,但你永遠唔能夠肯定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後面也許會有更愉快的事,但你永遠不能肯定。

passages.original: And it’s so often the case that it isn’t pleasanter.
passages.vernacular: 而且常常並不更愉快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且常常並不更愉快。

passages.original: That has been my experience anyhow.
passages.vernacular: 至少我嘅經驗係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少我的經驗是這樣。

passages.original: But I’m glad to think of getting home.
passages.vernacular: 但係想到回家我好高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是想到回家我很高興。

passages.original: You see, I’ve never had a real home since I can remember.
passages.vernacular: 您瞧,我記事以來從冇過一個真正嘅家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您瞧,我記事以來從沒有過一個真正的家。

passages.original: It gives me that pleasant ache again just to think of coming to a really truly home.
passages.vernacular: 光係想到要到一個真真正正嘅家,就讓我又有咗嗰種愉快嘅疼痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 光是想到要到一個真真正正的家,就讓我又有了那種愉快的疼痛。

passages.original: Oh, isn’t that pretty!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,嗰多美啊!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,那多美啊!」

passages.original: They had driven over the crest of a hill.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋剛駛上一座山頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們剛駛上一座山頭。

passages.original: Below them was a pond, looking almost like a river so long and winding was it.
passages.vernacular: 下面係一個池塘,睇上去幾乎像條河,又長又彎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下面是一個池塘,看上去幾乎像條河,又長又彎。

passages.original: A bridge spanned it midway and from there to its lower end, where an amber-hued belt of sand-hills shut it in from the dark blue gulf beyond, the water was a glory of many shifting hues--the most spiritual shadings of crocus and rose and ethereal green, with other elusive tintings for which no name has ever been found.
passages.vernacular: 橋橫跨喺池塘中間,從嗰度到池塘嘅下游,嗰兒一帶琥珀色嘅沙丘把佢同外面深藍色嘅海灣隔開,水面係一片光彩奪目的變幻色彩——番紅花色、玫瑰色同空靈嘅綠色最富靈性嘅色調,仲有其他難以捉摸、從冇人為之命過名嘅色澤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 橋橫跨在池塘中間,從那裡到池塘的下游,那兒一帶琥珀色的沙丘把它與外面深藍色的海灣隔開,水面是一片光彩奪目的變幻色彩——番紅花色、玫瑰色和空靈的綠色最富靈性的色調,還有其他難以捉摸、從沒人為之命過名的色澤。

passages.original: Above the bridge the pond ran up into fringing groves of fir and maple and lay all darkly translucent in their wavering shadows.
passages.vernacular: 橋嘅上游,池塘延伸進杉樹同楓樹環繞嘅林子,喺佢哋搖曳嘅樹影裡,水色深沉而半透明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 橋的上游,池塘延伸進杉樹和楓樹環繞的林子,在它們搖曳的樹影裡,水色深沉而半透明。

passages.original: Here and there a wild plum leaned out from the bank like a white-clad girl tiptoeing to her own reflection.
passages.vernacular: 呢度嗰度,有棵野李樹從堤岸探出身嚟,像一個穿白衣嘅女孩踮住腳尖睇自己嘅倒影。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡那裡,有棵野李樹從堤岸探出身來,像一個穿白衣的女孩踮著腳尖看自己的倒影。

passages.original: From the marsh at the head of the pond came the clear, mournfully-sweet chorus of the frogs.
passages.vernacular: 從池塘上游嘅沼澤傳嚟青蛙清脆而淒婉甜美嘅大合唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從池塘上游的沼澤傳來青蛙清脆而淒婉甜美的大合唱。

passages.original: There was a little gray house peering around a white apple orchard on a slope beyond and, although it was not yet quite dark, a light was shining from one of its windows.
passages.vernacular: 喺對面山坡上,一座灰色嘅小房子從一片白色嘅蘋果園後面探出頭嚟,雖然天仲冇完全黑,有一扇窗戶裡已經亮住燈光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在對面山坡上,一座灰色的小房子從一片白色的蘋果園後面探出頭來,雖然天還沒完全黑,有一扇窗戶裡已經亮著燈光。

passages.original: “That’s Barry’s pond,” said Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係巴里池塘,」馬修講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是巴里池塘,」馬修說。

passages.original: “Oh, I don’t like that name, either.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,呢個名字我都不鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,這個名字我也不喜歡。

passages.original: I shall call it--let me see--the Lake of Shining Waters.
passages.vernacular: 我要叫佢——讓我想想——閃亮湖水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要叫它——讓我想想——閃亮湖水。

passages.original: Yes, that is the right name for it.
passages.vernacular: 對,呢才係佢嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,這才是它的名字。

passages.original: I know because of the thrill.
passages.vernacular: 我知道,因為我有咗嗰種激動嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道,因為我有了那種激動的感覺。

passages.original: When I hit on a name that suits exactly it gives me a thrill.
passages.vernacular: 當我想到一個完全合適嘅名字時,就會讓我心頭一顫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我想到一個完全合適的名字時,就會讓我心頭一顫。

passages.original: Do things ever give you a thrill?”
passages.vernacular: 有乜嘢嘢會讓您心頭一顫嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有什麼東西會讓您心頭一顫嗎?」

passages.original: Matthew ruminated.
passages.vernacular: 馬修思索住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修思索著。

passages.original: “Well now, yes.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個嘛,有嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這個嘛,有的。

passages.original: It always kind of gives me a thrill to see them ugly white grubs that spade up in the cucumber beds.
passages.vernacular: 我睇到黃瓜地裡翻出嚟嘅嗰啲難睇嘅白色蠐螬,總是會心裡發顫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看到黃瓜地裡翻出來的那些難看的白色蠐螬,總是會心裡發顫。

passages.original: I hate the look of them.”
passages.vernacular: 我討厭佢哋嘅樣子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我討厭它們的樣子。」

passages.original: “Oh, I don’t think that can be exactly the same kind of a thrill.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我想嗰唔可能係完全同一種激動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我想那不可能是完全同一種激動。

passages.original: Do you think it can?
passages.vernacular: 您覺得可能嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您覺得可能嗎?

passages.original: There doesn’t seem to be much connection between grubs and lakes of shining waters, does there?
passages.vernacular: 蠐螬同閃亮湖水之間好像冇多大關係,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蠐螬和閃亮湖水之間好像沒有多大關係,是不是?

passages.original: But why do other people call it Barry’s pond?”
passages.vernacular: 不過別人點解叫佢巴里池塘呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過別人為什麼叫它巴里池塘呢?」

passages.original: “I reckon because Mr. Barry lives up there in that house.
passages.vernacular: 「我猜係因為巴里先生住喺嗰邊嗰座房子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我猜是因為巴里先生住在那邊那座房子裡。

passages.original: Orchard Slope’s the name of his place.
passages.vernacular: 佢嗰地方叫果園坡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他那地方叫果園坡。

passages.original: If it wasn’t for that big bush behind it you could see Green Gables from here.
passages.vernacular: 要唔係後面嗰片大灌木叢擋住,從呢兒就能睇到綠色屋頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是後面那片大灌木叢擋著,從這兒就能看到綠色屋頂。

passages.original: But we have to go over the bridge and round by the road, so it’s near half a mile further.”
passages.vernacular: 但我哋得過橋,再繞大路走,所以仲要多走近半英里。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們得過橋,再繞大路走,所以還要多走近半英里。」

passages.original: “Has Mr. Barry any little girls?
passages.vernacular: 「巴里先生有小女兒嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴里先生有小女兒嗎?

passages.original: Well, not so very little either--about my size.”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,都唔係太小——大概同我差不多大。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,也不是太小——大概和我差不多大。」

passages.original: “He’s got one about eleven.
passages.vernacular: 「佢有一個,大約十一歲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他有一個,大約十一歲。

passages.original: Her name is Diana.”
passages.vernacular: 佢叫黛安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她叫黛安娜。」

passages.original: “Oh!” with a long indrawing of breath.
passages.vernacular: 「哦!」深深地吸咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!」深深地吸了口氣。

passages.original: “What a perfectly lovely name!”
passages.vernacular: 「幾咁美麗嘅名字啊!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多麼美麗的名字啊!」

passages.original: “Well now, I dunno.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個嘛,我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這個嘛,我不知道。

passages.original: There’s something dreadful heathenish about it, seems to me.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得呢名字有點可怕地帶住異教味兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得這名字有點可怕地帶著異教味兒。

passages.original: I’d ruther Jane or Mary or some sensible name like that.
passages.vernacular: 我寧願叫簡或者瑪麗,或者像嗰樣有理智嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願叫簡或者瑪麗,或者像那樣有理智的名字。

passages.original: But when Diana was born there was a schoolmaster boarding there and they gave him the naming of her and he called her Diana.”
passages.vernacular: 不過黛安娜出生嘅時候,嗰兒正好有個教書先生寄宿,佢哋就讓佢畀佢取名,佢就叫佢黛安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是黛安娜出生的時候,那兒正好有個教書先生寄宿,他們就讓他給她取名,他就叫她黛安娜。」

passages.original: “I wish there had been a schoolmaster like that around when I was born, then.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我出生嘅時候要係都有咁樣一位教書先生喺旁邊就好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我出生的時候要是也有這樣一位教書先生在旁邊就好了。

passages.original: Oh, here we are at the bridge.
passages.vernacular: 哦,到橋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,到橋了。

passages.original: I’m going to shut my eyes tight.
passages.vernacular: 我要把眼睛閉得緊緊嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把眼睛閉得緊緊的。

passages.original: I’m always afraid going over bridges.
passages.vernacular: 我過橋總是害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我過橋總是害怕。

passages.original: I can’t help imagining that perhaps, just as we get to the middle, they’ll crumple up like a jack-knife and nip us.
passages.vernacular: 我忍不住想像,或者我哋剛走到橋中間,橋就會像摺刀一樣摺起嚟,把我哋夾住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忍不住想像,也許我們剛走到橋中間,橋就會像摺刀一樣摺起來,把我們夾住。

passages.original: So I shut my eyes.
passages.vernacular: 所以我就閉上眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我就閉上眼睛。

passages.original: But I always have to open them for all when I think we’re getting near the middle.
passages.vernacular: 但係只要我覺得快到中間喇,我總是不顧一切地睜開眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是只要我覺得快到中間了,我總是不顧一切地睜開眼睛。

passages.original: Because, you see, if the bridge did crumple up I’d want to see it crumple.
passages.vernacular: 因為,您瞧,要係橋真嘅摺起嚟,我想睇住佢摺起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為,您瞧,要是橋真的摺起來,我想看著它摺起來。

passages.original: What a jolly rumble it makes!
passages.vernacular: 佢發出嘅隆隆聲多有趣啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它發出的隆隆聲多有趣啊!

passages.original: I always like the rumble part of it.
passages.vernacular: 我總是鍾意隆隆聲嗰一部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我總是喜歡隆隆聲那一部分。

passages.original: Isn’t it splendid there are so many things to like in this world?
passages.vernacular: 呢世上有咁多可鍾意嘅嘢,唔係太棒咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這世上有這麼多可喜歡的東西,不是太棒了嗎?

passages.original: There, we’re over.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,我哋過橋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,我們過橋了。

passages.original: Now I’ll look back.
passages.vernacular: 而家我要回頭睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我要回頭看。

passages.original: Good night, dear Lake of Shining Waters.
passages.vernacular: 晚安,親愛嘅閃亮湖水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安,親愛的閃亮湖水。

passages.original: I always say good night to the things I love, just as I would to people.
passages.vernacular: 我總是對我愛嘅嘢道晚安,就像對人一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我總是對我愛的東西道晚安,就像對人一樣。

passages.original: I think they like it.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得佢哋鍾意咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得它們喜歡這樣。

passages.original: That water looks as if it was smiling at me.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰水睇上去好像喺對我微笑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那水看上去好像在對我微笑。」

passages.original: When they had driven up the further hill and around a corner Matthew said:
passages.vernacular: 等佢哋駛上更遠嘅山坡,拐過一個彎時,馬修講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等他們駛上更遠的山坡,拐過一個彎時,馬修說:

passages.original: “We’re pretty near home now.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋快到家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們快到家了。

passages.original: That’s Green Gables over--”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個就係綠色屋頂,就喺嗰邊——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就是綠色屋頂,就在那邊——」

passages.original: “Oh, don’t tell me,” she interrupted breathlessly, catching at his partially raised arm and shutting her eyes that she might not see his gesture.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,別告訴我,」佢氣喘吁吁地打斷咗佢,一把抓住佢舉起一半嘅手臂,閉上眼睛,免得睇見佢嘅手勢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,別告訴我,」她氣喘吁吁地打斷了他,一把抓住他舉起一半的手臂,閉上眼睛,免得看見他的手勢。

passages.original: “Let me guess.
passages.vernacular: 「讓我猜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我猜。

passages.original: I’m sure I’ll guess right.”
passages.vernacular: 我肯定能猜對。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我肯定能猜對。」

passages.original: She opened her eyes and looked about her.
passages.vernacular: 佢睜開眼睛,環顧四周。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她睜開眼睛,環顧四周。

passages.original: They were on the crest of a hill.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺一座山頂上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在一座山頂上。

passages.original: The sun had set some time since, but the landscape was still clear in the mellow afterlight.
passages.vernacular: 太陽已經落山好一會兒喇,但喺柔和嘅餘暉中風景仍然清晰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽已經落山好一會兒了,但在柔和的餘暉中風景仍然清晰。

passages.original: To the west a dark church spire rose up against a marigold sky.
passages.vernacular: 西邊,一座黑色嘅教堂尖塔聳立喺金盞花色嘅天空下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 西邊,一座黑色的教堂尖塔聳立在金盞花色的天空下。

passages.original: Below was a little valley and beyond a long, gently-rising slope with snug farmsteads scattered along it.
passages.vernacular: 下面係一個小山谷,遠處係一道長長嘅緩緩上升嘅山坡,舒適嘅農舍散落其上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下面是一個小山谷,遠處是一道長長的緩緩上升的山坡,舒適的農舍散落其上。

passages.original: From one to another the child’s eyes darted, eager and wistful.
passages.vernacular: 細路嘅目光從一座房子跳到另一座,熱切而渴望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子的目光從一座房子跳到另一座,熱切而渴望。

passages.original: At last they lingered on one away to the left, far back from the road, dimly white with blossoming trees in the twilight of the surrounding woods.
passages.vernacular: 最後,目光停喺左邊遠處嘅一座房子上,佢遠離大路,喺周圍樹林嘅暮色中,被盛開嘅樹朵映得隱隱泛白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後,目光停在左邊遠處的一座房子上,它遠離大路,在周圍樹林的暮色中,被盛開的樹朵映得隱隱泛白。

passages.original: Over it, in the stainless southwest sky, a great crystal-white star was shining like a lamp of guidance and promise.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢上方,無瑕嘅西南天空中,一顆巨大嘅水晶般潔白嘅星星像一盞指引同承諾嘅明燈,閃耀住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在它上方,無瑕的西南天空中,一顆巨大的水晶般潔白的星星像一盞指引和承諾的明燈,閃耀著。

passages.original: “That’s it, isn’t it?” she said, pointing.
passages.vernacular: 「就係嗰兒,係唔係?」佢指住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是那兒,是不是?」她指著說。

passages.original: Matthew slapped the reins on the sorrel’s back delightedly.
passages.vernacular: 馬修高興地用韁繩拍咗拍栗色馬嘅背。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修高興地用韁繩拍了拍栗色馬的背。

passages.original: “Well now, you’ve guessed it!
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個嘛,你猜對喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這個嘛,你猜對了!

passages.original: But I reckon Mrs. Spencer described it so’s you could tell.”
passages.vernacular: 不過我想係斯潘塞太太描述得讓你能認出嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我想是斯潘塞太太描述得讓你能認出來。」

passages.original: “No, she didn’t--really she didn’t.
passages.vernacular: 「不,佢冇——真嘅冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,她沒有——真的沒有。

passages.original: All she said might just as well have been about most of those other places.
passages.vernacular: 佢所講嘅一切,大可以用嚟形容嗰啲別嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她所說的一切,大可以用來形容那些別的地方。

passages.original: I hadn’t any real idea what it looked like.
passages.vernacular: 我根本唔知道佢到底係乜嘢樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我根本不知道它到底是什麼樣子。

passages.original: But just as soon as I saw it I felt it was home.
passages.vernacular: 可我一睇見佢,就覺得嗰個係家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可我一看見它,就覺得那是家。

passages.original: Oh, it seems as if I must be in a dream.
passages.vernacular: 哦,好像我一定係喺做夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,好像我一定是在做夢。

passages.original: Do you know, my arm must be black and blue from the elbow up, for I’ve pinched myself so many times today.
passages.vernacular: 您知道嗎,我嘅手臂從胳膊肘往上一定都青紫喇,因為今日我掐咗自己咁多次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道嗎,我的手臂從胳膊肘往上一定都青紫了,因為今天我掐了自己那麼多次。

passages.original: Every little while a horrible sickening feeling would come over me and I’d be so afraid it was all a dream.
passages.vernacular: 每隔一會兒,一種可怕嘅、令人噁心嘅感覺就會襲嚟,我就好害怕呢一切只係一場夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每隔一會兒,一種可怕的、令人噁心的感覺就會襲來,我就非常害怕這一切只是一場夢。

passages.original: Then I’d pinch myself to see if it was real--until suddenly I remembered that even supposing it was only a dream I’d better go on dreaming as long as I could; so I stopped pinching.
passages.vernacular: 然後我就掐掐自己,睇係唔係真嘅——直到忽然想起,即使呢只係一場夢,我都最好盡可能長久地做下去;於是我就不掐喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我就掐掐自己,看是不是真的——直到忽然想起,即使這只是一場夢,我也最好盡可能長久地做下去;於是我就不掐了。

passages.original: But it is real and we’re nearly home.”
passages.vernacular: 可呢個係真嘅,我哋快到家喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可這是真的,我們快到家了。」

passages.original: With a sigh of rapture she relapsed into silence.
passages.vernacular: 佢心醉神迷地嘆咗口氣,又陷入咗沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她心醉神迷地嘆了口氣,又陷入了沉默。

passages.original: Matthew stirred uneasily.
passages.vernacular: 馬修不安地動咗動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修不安地動了動。

passages.original: He felt glad that it would be Marilla and not he who would have to tell this waif of the world that the home she longed for was not to be hers after all.
passages.vernacular: 佢好慶幸,要向呢個世界嘅流浪兒講明佢渴望嘅家終究不屬於佢嘅,將係瑪麗拉,而唔係佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很慶幸,要向這個世界的流浪兒說明她渴望的家終究不屬於她的,將是瑪麗拉,而不是他。

passages.original: They drove over Lynde’s Hollow, where it was already quite dark, but not so dark that Mrs. Rachel could not see them from her window vantage, and up the hill and into the long lane of Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋駛過林德窪地,嗰度已經好黑喇,但仲冇黑到雷切爾太太從佢嘅窗口有利位置睇唔見佢哋;然後上山,進咗綠色屋頂嘅長長小巷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們駛過林德窪地,那裡已經很黑了,但還沒黑到雷切爾太太從她的窗口有利位置看不見他們;然後上山,進了綠色屋頂的長長小巷。

passages.original: By the time they arrived at the house Matthew was shrinking from the approaching revelation with an energy he did not understand.
passages.vernacular: 等佢哋到達房子時,馬修正以一種佢自己都不明白嘅力度,逃避住即將到來嘅揭曉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等他們到達房子時,馬修正以一種他自己也不明白的力度,逃避著即將到來的揭曉。

passages.original: It was not of Marilla or himself he was thinking or of the trouble this mistake was probably going to make for them, but of the child’s disappointment.
passages.vernacular: 佢想嘅唔係瑪麗拉或佢自己,都唔係呢個錯誤可能畀佢哋帶嚟嘅麻煩,而係細路嘅失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想的不是瑪麗拉或他自己,也不是這個錯誤可能給他們帶來的麻煩,而是孩子的失望。

passages.original: When he thought of that rapt light being quenched in her eyes he had an uncomfortable feeling that he was going to assist at murdering something--much the same feeling that came over him when he had to kill a lamb or calf or any other innocent little creature.
passages.vernacular: 一想到佢眼中嗰狂喜嘅光芒將被熄滅,佢就有一種好不舒服嘅感覺,覺得自己好像要參與謀殺乜嘢嘢——就像佢唔得不殺一隻羔羊或牛犢或任何別嘅無辜小生靈時嘅嗰種感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一想到她眼中那狂喜的光芒將被熄滅,他就有一種很不舒服的感覺,覺得自己好像要參與謀殺什麼東西——就像他不得不殺一隻羔羊或牛犢或任何別的無辜小生靈時的那種感覺。

passages.original: The yard was quite dark as they turned into it and the poplar leaves were rustling silkily all round it.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋拐進院子時,院子裡一片漆黑,周圍嘅白楊樹葉子喺絲絲沙沙地響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們拐進院子時,院子裡一片漆黑,周圍的白楊樹葉子在絲絲沙沙地響。

passages.original: “Listen to the trees talking in their sleep,” she whispered, as he lifted her to the ground.
passages.vernacular: 「聽,樹喺瞓夢中講話呢,」佢把佢抱下地時,佢低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽,樹在睡夢中說話呢,」他把她抱下地時,她低聲說。

passages.original: “What nice dreams they must have!”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋一定做住幾咁美好嘅夢啊!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們一定做著多麼美好的夢啊!」

passages.original: Then, holding tightly to the carpet-bag which contained “all her worldly goods,” she followed him into the house.
passages.vernacular: 然後,佢緊緊抓住嗰隻裝住「佢所有家當」嘅毯子布提包,跟住佢走進咗屋裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,她緊緊抓著那隻裝著「她所有家當」的毯子布提包,跟著他走進了屋裡。

chapters.title: Ch. III Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised 第三章:瑪麗拉·卡思伯特吃了一驚

passages.original: CH MARILLA came briskly forward as Matthew opened the door.
passages.vernacular: 馬修一開門,瑪麗拉就快步迎咗上嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修一開門,瑪麗拉就快步迎了上來。

passages.original: But when her eyes fell on the odd little figure in the stiff, ugly dress, with the long braids of red hair and the eager, luminous eyes, she stopped short in amazement.
passages.vernacular: 不過,當佢嘅目光落喺嗰個穿住硬邦邦、難睇裙子嘅古怪小身影上,睇見佢嗰兩根長長嘅紅辮子同嗰雙熱切明亮嘅眼睛時,佢驚愕地停住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是,當她的目光落在那個穿著硬邦邦、難看裙子的古怪小身影上,看見她那兩根長長的紅辮子和那雙熱切明亮的眼睛時,她驚愕地停住了。

passages.original: “Matthew Cuthbert, who’s that?” she ejaculated.
passages.vernacular: 「馬修·卡思伯特,呢個係邊個?」佢脫口而出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修·卡思伯特,這是誰?」她脫口而出。

passages.original: “Where is the boy?”
passages.vernacular: 「男孩呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「男孩呢?」

passages.original: “There wasn’t any boy,” said Matthew wretchedly.
passages.vernacular: 「冇男孩,」馬修沮喪地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有男孩,」馬修沮喪地說。

passages.original: “There was only her.”
passages.vernacular: 「只有佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只有她。」

passages.original: He nodded at the child, remembering that he had never even asked her name.
passages.vernacular: 佢朝細路點咗點頭,呢才想起自己連佢嘅名字都冇問過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他朝孩子點了點頭,這才想起自己連她的名字都沒問過。

passages.original: “No boy!
passages.vernacular: 「冇男孩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有男孩!

passages.original: But there must have been a boy,” insisted Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 不過一定有個男孩,」瑪麗拉堅持道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是一定有個男孩,」瑪麗拉堅持道。

passages.original: “We sent word to Mrs. Spencer to bring a boy.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋托人捎話畀斯潘塞太太,讓佢帶一個男孩嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們托人捎話給斯潘塞太太,讓她帶一個男孩來。」

passages.original: “Well, she didn’t.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢冇帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,她沒帶。

passages.original: She brought her.
passages.vernacular: 佢帶嚟嘅係佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她帶來的是她。

passages.original: I asked the stationmaster.
passages.vernacular: 我問過站長喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我問過站長了。

passages.original: And I had to bring her home.
passages.vernacular: 我只好把佢帶回家嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只好把她帶回家來。

passages.original: She couldn’t be left there, no matter where the mistake had come in.”
passages.vernacular: 不管差錯出喺邊度,總唔能夠把佢留喺嗰兒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管差錯出在哪裡,總不能把她留在那兒。」

passages.original: “Well, this is a pretty piece of business!” ejaculated Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,呢可真係件好事!」瑪麗拉大聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,這可真是件好事!」瑪麗拉大聲說。

passages.original: During this dialogue the child had remained silent, her eyes roving from one to the other, all the animation fading out of her face.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢場對話期間,細路一直沉默住,眼睛喺兩人之間嚟回轉動,臉上所有嘅生氣都消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這場對話期間,孩子一直沉默著,眼睛在兩人之間來回轉動,臉上所有的生氣都消失了。

passages.original: Suddenly she seemed to grasp the full meaning of what had been said.
passages.vernacular: 突然佢好像明白咗頭先講嘅話嘅全部意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然她好像明白了剛才說的話的全部意思。

passages.original: Dropping her precious carpet-bag she sprang forward a step and clasped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 佢扔下佢嗰寶貝毯子布提包,向前跳咗一步,雙手緊握。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她扔下她那寶貝毯子布提包,向前跳了一步,雙手緊握。

passages.original: “You don’t want me!” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋唔好我!」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們不要我!」她喊道。

passages.original: “You don’t want me because I’m not a boy!
passages.vernacular: 「你哋唔好我,因為我唔係男孩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們不要我,因為我不是男孩!

passages.original: I might have expected it.
passages.vernacular: 我早該想到嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我早該想到的。

passages.original: Nobody ever did want me.
passages.vernacular: 從來冇人真嘅要過我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從來沒有人真的要過我。

passages.original: I might have known it was all too beautiful to last.
passages.vernacular: 我早該知道,呢一切太美好喇,唔可能長久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我早該知道,這一切太美好了,不可能長久。

passages.original: I might have known nobody really did want me.
passages.vernacular: 我早該知道,冇人真嘅要我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我早該知道,沒有人真的要我。

passages.original: Oh, what shall I do?
passages.vernacular: 哦,我該點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我該怎麼辦?

passages.original: I’m going to burst into tears!”
passages.vernacular: 我要哭出嚟喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要哭出來了!」

passages.original: Burst into tears she did.
passages.vernacular: 佢真嘅哭咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她真的哭了出來。

passages.original: Sitting down on a chair by the table, flinging her arms out upon it, and burying her face in them, she proceeded to cry stormily.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺桌邊嘅一把椅子上坐下,把胳膊伸到桌上,把臉埋喺臂彎裡,放聲痛哭起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在桌邊的一把椅子上坐下,把胳膊伸到桌上,把臉埋在臂彎裡,放聲痛哭起來。

passages.original: Marilla and Matthew looked at each other deprecatingly across the stove.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉同馬修隔住爐子面面相覷,滿臉不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉和馬修隔著爐子面面相覷,滿臉不安。

passages.original: Neither of them knew what to say or do.
passages.vernacular: 兩個人都唔知道該講乜嘢、該做乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個人都不知道該說什麼、該做什麼。

passages.original: Finally Marilla stepped lamely into the breach.
passages.vernacular: 最後瑪麗拉笨拙地出嚟打圓場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後瑪麗拉笨拙地出來打圓場。

passages.original: “Well, well, there’s no need to cry so about it.”
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,用不住為呢個哭成咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,用不著為這個哭成這樣。」

passages.original: “Yes, there is need!”
passages.vernacular: 「有必要!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有必要!」

passages.original: The child raised her head quickly, revealing a tear-stained face and trembling lips.
passages.vernacular: 細路猛地抬起頭嚟,露出淚痕斑斑嘅臉同顫抖嘅嘴唇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子猛地抬起頭來,露出淚痕斑斑的臉和顫抖的嘴唇。

passages.original: “You would cry, too, if you were an orphan and had come to a place you thought was going to be home and found that they didn’t want you because you weren’t a boy.
passages.vernacular: 「如果您係個孤兒,嚟到一個您以為會成為家嘅地方,卻發現佢哋唔好您,只係因為您唔係男孩,您都會哭嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果您是個孤兒,來到一個您以為會成為家的地方,卻發現他們不要您,只是因為您不是男孩,您也會哭的。

passages.original: Oh, this is the most tragical thing that ever happened to me!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,呢個係我遇到過嘅最悲慘嘅事!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,這是我遇到過的最悲慘的事!」

passages.original: Something like a reluctant smile, rather rusty from long disuse, mellowed Marilla’s grim expression.
passages.vernacular: 一絲勉強嘅笑意,因久不使用而顯得有些生疏,柔和咗瑪麗拉嚴厲嘅表情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一絲勉強的笑意,因久不使用而顯得有些生疏,柔和了瑪麗拉嚴厲的表情。

passages.original: “Well, don’t cry any more.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,唔好再哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,別再哭了。

passages.original: We’re not going to turn you out-of-doors tonight.
passages.vernacular: 我哋今晚唔會把你趕出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們今晚不會把你趕出去。

passages.original: You’ll have to stay here until we investigate this affair.
passages.vernacular: 你得待喺呢兒,等我哋把呢件事調查清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你得待在這兒,等我們把這件事調查清楚。

passages.original: What’s your name?”
passages.vernacular: 你叫乜嘢名字?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你叫什麼名字?」

passages.original: The child hesitated for a moment.
passages.vernacular: 細路猶豫咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子猶豫了一會兒。

passages.original: “Will you please call me Cordelia?” she said eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「您能叫我科黛莉亞嗎?」佢急切地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您能叫我科黛莉亞嗎?」她急切地說。

passages.original: “Call you Cordelia?
passages.vernacular: 「叫你科黛莉亞?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「叫你科黛莉亞?

passages.original: Is that your name?”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係你嘅名字嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是你的名字嗎?」

passages.original: “No-o-o, it’s not exactly my name, but I would love to be called Cordelia.
passages.vernacular: 「不——不,不完全係我嘅名字,但我好想被叫做科黛莉亞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不——不,不完全是我的名字,但我很想被叫做科黛莉亞。

passages.original: It’s such a perfectly elegant name.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個極其高雅嘅名字。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個極其高雅的名字。」

passages.original: “I don’t know what on earth you mean.
passages.vernacular: 「我真不明白你係乜嘢意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真不明白你是什麼意思。

passages.original: If Cordelia isn’t your name, what is?”
passages.vernacular: 如果科黛莉亞唔係你嘅名字,嗰你叫乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果科黛莉亞不是你的名字,那你叫什麼?」

passages.original: “Anne Shirley,” reluctantly faltered forth the owner of that name, “but, oh, please do call me Cordelia.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,」呢個名字嘅主人勉強吞吞吐吐地講,「不過,哦,請叫我科黛莉亞吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,」這個名字的主人勉強吞吞吐吐地說,「可是,哦,請叫我科黛莉亞吧。

passages.original: It can’t matter much to you what you call me if I’m only going to be here a little while, can it?
passages.vernacular: 既然我只會喺呢度待一小會兒,您叫我乜嘢對您來講冇多大關係,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然我只會在這裡待一小會兒,您叫我什麼對您來說沒多大關係,是不是?

passages.original: And Anne is such an unromantic name.”
passages.vernacular: 而且安妮係個好冇浪漫色彩嘅名字。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且安妮是個很沒有浪漫色彩的名字。」

passages.original: “Unromantic fiddlesticks!” said the unsympathetic Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢浪漫不浪漫嘅鬼話!」毫不同情嘅瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼浪漫不浪漫的鬼話!」毫不同情的瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “Anne is a real good plain sensible name.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮係個挺好嘅、樸素、實在嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮是個挺好的、樸素、實在的名字。

passages.original: You’ve no need to be ashamed of it.”
passages.vernacular: 你冇理由為佢感到羞愧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒有理由為它感到羞愧。」

passages.original: “Oh, I’m not ashamed of it,” explained Anne, “only I like Cordelia better.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我並不為佢感到羞愧,」安妮解釋道,「只係我更鍾意科黛莉亞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我並不為它感到羞愧,」安妮解釋道,「只是我更喜歡科黛莉亞。

passages.original: I’ve always imagined that my name was Cordelia--at least, I always have of late years.
passages.vernacular: 我一直想像我嘅名字叫科黛莉亞——至少最近幾年一直係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直想像我的名字叫科黛莉亞——至少最近幾年一直是這樣。

passages.original: When I was young I used to imagine it was Geraldine, but I like Cordelia better now.
passages.vernacular: 小時候我常想像佢叫傑拉爾丁,但而家我更鍾意科黛莉亞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小時候我常想像它叫傑拉爾丁,但現在我更喜歡科黛莉亞。

passages.original: But if you call me Anne please call me Anne spelled with an E.”
passages.vernacular: 不過如果您非叫我安妮,請叫我末尾帶E嘅嗰個Anne。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過如果您非叫我安妮,請叫我末尾帶E的那個Anne。」

passages.original: “What difference does it make how it’s spelled?” asked Marilla with another rusty smile as she picked up the teapot.
passages.vernacular: 「點拼寫有乜嘢區別?」瑪麗拉問,又露出一個生疏嘅笑容,一邊攞起茶壺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼拼寫有什麼區別?」瑪麗拉問,又露出一個生疏的笑容,一邊拿起茶壺。

passages.original: “Oh, it makes such a difference.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,區別可大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,區別可大了。

passages.original: It looks so much nicer.
passages.vernacular: 睇起嚟好睇多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看起來好看多了。

passages.original: When you hear a name pronounced can’t you always see it in your mind, just as if it was printed out?
passages.vernacular: 當你聽到一個名字被念出嚟嘅時候,你唔係總能喺腦子裡睇到佢,就像印出嚟嘅一樣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你聽到一個名字被念出來的時候,你不是總能在腦子裡看到它,就像印出來的一樣嗎?

passages.original: I can; and A-n-n looks dreadful, but A-n-n-e looks so much more distinguished.
passages.vernacular: 我能;A-n-n睇起嚟好難睇,而A-n-n-e睇起嚟高貴多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能;A-n-n看起來很難看,而A-n-n-e看起來高貴多了。

passages.original: If you’ll only call me Anne spelled with an E I shall try to reconcile myself to not being called Cordelia.”
passages.vernacular: 只要您肯叫我末尾帶E嘅Anne,我就會努力讓自己接受不被叫做科黛莉亞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要您肯叫我末尾帶E的Anne,我就會努力讓自己接受不被叫做科黛莉亞。」

passages.original: “Very well, then, Anne spelled with an E, can you tell us how this mistake came to be made?
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,咁,末尾帶E嘅安妮,你能告訴我哋呢個差錯係點出嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,那麼,末尾帶E的安妮,你能告訴我們這個差錯是怎麼出的嗎?

passages.original: We sent word to Mrs. Spencer to bring us a boy.
passages.vernacular: 我哋捎話畀斯潘塞太太,讓佢畀我哋帶一個男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們捎話給斯潘塞太太,讓她給我們帶一個男孩。

passages.original: Were there no boys at the asylum?”
passages.vernacular: 孤兒院裡冇男孩嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孤兒院裡沒有男孩嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, there was an abundance of them.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,有,有好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,有,有很多。

passages.original: But Mrs. Spencer said distinctly that you wanted a girl about eleven years old.
passages.vernacular: 不過斯潘塞太太明確地講您哋要一個十一歲左右嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是斯潘塞太太明確地說您們要一個十一歲左右的女孩。

passages.original: And the matron said she thought I would do.
passages.vernacular: 而院長太太講佢覺得我合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而院長太太說她覺得我合適。

passages.original: You don’t know how delighted I was.
passages.vernacular: 您唔知道我有多高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不知道我有多高興。

passages.original: I couldn’t sleep all last night for joy.
passages.vernacular: 琴晚我高興得整夜冇瞓住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨晚我高興得整夜沒睡著。

passages.original: Oh,” she added reproachfully, turning to Matthew, “why didn’t you tell me at the station that you didn’t want me and leave me there?
passages.vernacular: 哦,」佢轉向馬修,責備地補充道,「您點解不喺車站告訴我您哋唔好我,把我留喺嗰度呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,」她轉向馬修,責備地補充道,「您為什麼不在車站告訴我您們不要我,把我留在那裡呢?

passages.original: If I hadn’t seen the White Way of Delight and the Lake of Shining Waters it wouldn’t be so hard.”
passages.vernacular: 如果我冇睇到歡樂白路同閃亮湖水,就唔會咁難受喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我沒有看到歡樂白路和閃亮湖水,就不會這麼難受了。」

passages.original: “What on earth does she mean?” demanded Marilla, staring at Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「佢到底喺講乜嘢?」瑪麗拉盯住馬修問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她到底在說什麼?」瑪麗拉盯著馬修問。

passages.original: “She--she’s just referring to some conversation we had on the road,” said Matthew hastily.
passages.vernacular: 「佢——佢只係喺講我哋喺路上聊嘅啲話,」馬修連忙講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她——她只是在說我們在路上聊的一些話,」馬修連忙說。

passages.original: “I’m going out to put the mare in, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我去把馬安頓好,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我去把馬安頓好,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Have tea ready when I come back.”
passages.vernacular: 我回嚟時把茶準備好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我回來時把茶準備好。」

passages.original: “Did Mrs. Spencer bring anybody over besides you?” continued Marilla when Matthew had gone out.
passages.vernacular: 「除咗你,斯潘塞太太仲帶咗別嘅人過嚟嗎?」馬修出去後,瑪麗拉接住問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「除了你,斯潘塞太太還帶了別的人過來嗎?」馬修出去後,瑪麗拉接著問。

passages.original: “She brought Lily Jones for herself.
passages.vernacular: 「佢畀自己領咗莉莉·瓊斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她給自己領了莉莉·瓊斯。

passages.original: Lily is only five years old and she is very beautiful and had nut-brown hair.
passages.vernacular: 莉莉才五歲,長得好漂亮,有一頭堅果棕色嘅頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 莉莉才五歲,長得非常漂亮,有一頭堅果棕色的頭髮。

passages.original: If I was very beautiful and had nut-brown hair would you keep me?”
passages.vernacular: 如果我長得好漂亮,有一頭堅果棕色嘅頭髮,您會留下我嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我長得非常漂亮,有一頭堅果棕色的頭髮,您會留下我嗎?」

passages.original: “No. We want a boy to help Matthew on the farm.
passages.vernacular: 「唔會。我哋要嘅係一個男孩,幫馬修幹農活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會。我們要的是一個男孩,幫馬修幹農活。

passages.original: A girl would be of no use to us.
passages.vernacular: 女孩對我哋冇用處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩對我們沒有用處。

passages.original: Take off your hat.
passages.vernacular: 把帽子摘下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把帽子摘下來。

passages.original: I’ll lay it and your bag on the hall table.”
passages.vernacular: 我把佢同你嘅包放喺門廳嘅桌上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把它和你的包放在門廳的桌上。」

passages.original: Anne took off her hat meekly.
passages.vernacular: 安妮順從地摘下帽子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮順從地摘下帽子。

passages.original: Matthew came back presently and they sat down to supper.
passages.vernacular: 馬修不久就回嚟喇,佢哋坐下食晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修不久就回來了,他們坐下吃晚飯。

passages.original: But Anne could not eat.
passages.vernacular: 不過安妮食不下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是安妮吃不下。

passages.original: In vain she nibbled at the bread and butter and pecked at the crab-apple preserve out of the little scalloped glass dish by her plate.
passages.vernacular: 佢徒勞地小口啃住麵包同黃油,從盤子旁邊嘅扇形小玻璃碟裡啄咗點野蘋果蜜餞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她徒勞地小口啃著麵包和黃油,從盤子旁邊的扇形小玻璃碟裡啄了點野蘋果蜜餞。

passages.original: She did not really make any headway at all.
passages.vernacular: 佢其實啲都冇食進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她其實一點也沒吃進去。

passages.original: “You’re not eating anything,” said Marilla sharply, eying her as if it were a serious shortcoming.
passages.vernacular: 「你乜嘢都冇食,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地講,睇住佢,好像嗰個係個嚴重嘅缺點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你什麼也沒吃,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地說,看著她,好像那是個嚴重的缺點。

passages.original: Anne sighed.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮嘆了口氣。

passages.original: “I can’t.
passages.vernacular: 「我食不下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我吃不下。

passages.original: I’m in the depths of despair.
passages.vernacular: 我處喺絕望嘅深淵裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我處在絕望的深淵裡。

passages.original: Can you eat when you are in the depths of despair?”
passages.vernacular: 您處喺絕望嘅深淵時仲食得下嘢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您處在絕望的深淵時還吃得下東西嗎?」

passages.original: “I’ve never been in the depths of despair, so I can’t say,” responded Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇處喺過絕望嘅深淵,所以我講不上嚟,」瑪麗拉回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒處在過絕望的深淵,所以我說不上來,」瑪麗拉回答。

passages.original: “Weren’t you?
passages.vernacular: 「冇嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有嗎?

passages.original: Well, did you ever try to imagine you were in the depths of despair?”
passages.vernacular: 咁,您有冇試過想像自己處喺絕望嘅深淵?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,您有沒有試過想像自己處在絕望的深淵?」

passages.original: “No, I didn’t.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,我冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,我沒有。」

passages.original: “Then I don’t think you can understand what it’s like.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我想您唔可能明白嗰個係乜嘢滋味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我想您不可能明白那是什麼滋味。

passages.original: It’s a very uncomfortable feeling indeed.
passages.vernacular: 嗰確實係一種好不舒服嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那確實是一種非常不舒服的感覺。

passages.original: When you try to eat a lump comes right up in your throat and you can’t swallow anything, not even if it was a chocolate caramel.
passages.vernacular: 您想食嘢嘅時候,喉嚨裡就會堵上一個硬塊,乜嘢都咽不下去,即使係巧克力焦糖都不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您想吃東西的時候,喉嚨裡就會堵上一個硬塊,什麼也咽不下去,即使是巧克力焦糖也不行。

passages.original: I had one chocolate caramel once two years ago and it was simply delicious.
passages.vernacular: 兩年前我食過一次巧克力焦糖,簡直太美味喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩年前我吃過一次巧克力焦糖,簡直太美味了。

passages.original: I’ve often dreamed since then that I had a lot of chocolate caramels, but I always wake up just when I’m going to eat them.
passages.vernacular: 從嗰以後我常夢見自己有好多好多巧克力焦糖,不過我總是喺剛要食嘅時候醒嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那以後我常夢見自己有很多很多巧克力焦糖,可是我總是在剛要吃的時候醒來。

passages.original: I do hope you won’t be offended because I can’t eat.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望您唔好因為我食不下而生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望您不要因為我吃不下而生氣。

passages.original: Everything is extremely nice, but still I cannot eat.”
passages.vernacular: 每樣嘢都好好,可我定係食不下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每樣東西都非常好,可我還是吃不下。」

passages.original: “I guess she’s tired,” said Matthew, who hadn’t spoken since his return from the barn.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇佢係累喇,」馬修講,佢從穀倉回嚟以後一直冇講過話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看她是累了,」馬修說,他從穀倉回來以後一直沒說過話。

passages.original: “Best put her to bed, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 「最好讓佢上床瞓覺,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最好讓她上床睡覺,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: Marilla had been wondering where Anne should be put to bed.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉一直喺琢磨該讓安妮瞓喺邊兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉一直在琢磨該讓安妮睡在哪兒。

passages.original: She had prepared a couch in the kitchen chamber for the desired and expected boy.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺廚房閣樓上畀期望中、等待中嘅男孩鋪咗一張臥榻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在廚房閣樓上給期望中、等待中的男孩鋪了一張臥榻。

passages.original: But, although it was neat and clean, it did not seem quite the thing to put a girl there somehow.
passages.vernacular: 但係,雖然嗰度整潔乾淨,唔知怎嘅,讓一個女孩瞓喺嗰兒似乎不太合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,雖然那裡整潔乾淨,不知怎的,讓一個女孩睡在那兒似乎不太合適。

passages.original: But the spare room was out of the question for such a stray waif, so there remained only the east gable room.
passages.vernacular: 而備用客房對咁樣一個流浪兒來講係唔可能嘅,所以只剩下東山牆房間喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而備用客房對這樣一個流浪兒來說是不可能的,所以只剩下東山牆房間了。

passages.original: Marilla lighted a candle and told Anne to follow her, which Anne spiritlessly did, taking her hat and carpet-bag from the hall table as she passed.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉點亮一支蠟燭,讓安妮跟佢嚟,安妮無精打采地跟住,走過門廳時從桌上攞起佢嘅帽子同毯子布提包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉點亮一支蠟燭,讓安妮跟她來,安妮無精打采地跟著,走過門廳時從桌上拿起她的帽子和毯子布提包。

passages.original: The hall was fearsomely clean; the little gable chamber in which she presently found herself seemed still cleaner.
passages.vernacular: 門廳乾淨得令人生畏;佢隨即走進嘅嗰間山牆小屋似乎更乾淨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 門廳乾淨得令人生畏;她隨即走進的那間山牆小屋似乎更乾淨。

passages.original: Marilla set the candle on a three-legged, three-cornered table and turned down the bedclothes.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉把蠟燭放喺一張三條腿、三個角嘅桌子上,掀開咗被子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉把蠟燭放在一張三條腿、三個角的桌子上,掀開了被子。

passages.original: “I suppose you have a nightgown?” she questioned.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你有瞓衣吧?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你有睡衣吧?」她問。

passages.original: Anne nodded.
passages.vernacular: 安妮點點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮點點頭。

passages.original: “Yes, I have two.
passages.vernacular: 「有,我有兩件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有,我有兩件。

passages.original: The matron of the asylum made them for me.
passages.vernacular: 孤兒院嘅院長太太畀我做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孤兒院的院長太太給我做的。

passages.original: They’re fearfully skimpy.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋窄得要命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們窄得要命。

passages.original: There is never enough to go around in an asylum, so things are always skimpy--at least in a poor asylum like ours.
passages.vernacular: 孤兒院裡嘅嘢從來唔夠分,所以乜嘢嘢總是窄小嘅——至少喺像我哋咁樣一所窮孤兒院係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孤兒院裡的東西從來不夠分,所以什麼東西總是窄小的——至少在像我們這樣一所窮孤兒院是這樣。

passages.original: I hate skimpy night-dresses.
passages.vernacular: 我討厭窄小嘅瞓衣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我討厭窄小的睡衣。

passages.original: But one can dream just as well in them as in lovely trailing ones, with frills around the neck, that’s one consolation.”
passages.vernacular: 不過穿住佢哋做夢,都同穿住脖子上帶花邊嘅漂亮拖地瞓衣一樣好,呢個係一種安慰。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過穿著它們做夢,也和穿著脖子上帶花邊的漂亮拖地睡衣一樣好,這是一種安慰。」

passages.original: “Well, undress as quick as you can and go to bed.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,趕緊脫衣服上床吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,趕緊脫衣服上床吧。

passages.original: I’ll come back in a few minutes for the candle.
passages.vernacular: 我過幾分鐘回嚟攞蠟燭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我過幾分鐘回來拿蠟燭。

passages.original: I daren’t trust you to put it out yourself.
passages.vernacular: 我唔敢相信你會自己把佢吹滅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不敢相信你會自己把它吹滅。

passages.original: You’d likely set the place on fire.”
passages.vernacular: 你好可能把呢地方點住喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你很可能把這地方點著了。」

passages.original: When Marilla had gone Anne looked around her wistfully.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉走後,安妮悵然地環顧四周。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉走後,安妮悵然地環顧四周。

passages.original: The whitewashed walls were so painfully bare and staring that she thought they must ache over their own bareness.
passages.vernacular: 刷白嘅牆壁光禿禿地瞪住人,讓人難受,佢覺得佢哋一定為自己嘅光禿而痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 刷白的牆壁光禿禿地瞪著人,讓人難受,她覺得它們一定為自己的光禿而痛苦。

passages.original: The floor was bare, too, except for a round braided mat in the middle such as Anne had never seen before.
passages.vernacular: 地板都係光禿禿嘅,只有中間有一塊圓形嘅編織墊子,係安妮從冇見過嘅嗰種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 地板也是光禿禿的,只有中間有一塊圓形的編織墊子,是安妮從沒見過的那種。

passages.original: In one corner was the bed, a high, old-fashioned one, with four dark, low-turned posts.
passages.vernacular: 一個角落裡係床,一張高高嘅老式床,有四根深色嘅低矮車製嘅床柱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個角落裡是床,一張高高的老式床,有四根深色的低矮車製的床柱。

passages.original: In the other corner was the aforesaid three-cornered table adorned with a fat, red velvet pincushion hard enough to turn the point of the most adventurous pin.
passages.vernacular: 另一個角落裡係前面講到嘅三角桌,上面擺住一個胖胖嘅紅絲絨針墊,硬得能頂彎最勇敢嘅針尖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一個角落裡是前面說到的三角桌,上面擺著一個胖胖的紅絲絨針墊,硬得能頂彎最勇敢的針尖。

passages.original: Above it hung a little six-by-eight mirror.
passages.vernacular: 桌子上方掛住一面六寸乘八寸嘅小鏡子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桌子上方掛著一面六寸乘八寸的小鏡子。

passages.original: Midway between table and bed was the window, with an icy white muslin frill over it, and opposite it was the wash-stand.
passages.vernacular: 桌子同床之間係窗子,窗上有一圈冰冷嘅白紗花邊,對面係洗臉架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桌子與床之間是窗子,窗上有一圈冰冷的白紗花邊,對面是洗臉架。

passages.original: The whole apartment was of a rigidity not to be described in words, but which sent a shiver to the very marrow of Anne’s bones.
passages.vernacular: 整個房間有一種無法用言語形容嘅僵硬,令安妮從骨髓裡打咗個寒顫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個房間有一種無法用言語形容的僵硬,令安妮從骨髓裡打了個寒顫。

passages.original: With a sob she hastily discarded her garments, put on the skimpy nightgown and sprang into bed where she burrowed face downward into the pillow and pulled the clothes over her head.
passages.vernacular: 佢抽噎住匆匆脫掉衣服,穿上嗰件窄小嘅瞓衣,跳上床,把臉朝下埋進枕頭,把被子拉過頭頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她抽噎著匆匆脫掉衣服,穿上那件窄小的睡衣,跳上床,把臉朝下埋進枕頭,把被子拉過頭頂。

passages.original: When Marilla came up for the light various skimpy articles of raiment scattered most untidily over the floor and a certain tempestuous appearance of the bed were the only indications of any presence save her own.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉上嚟攞燈時,地板上亂七八糟地散落住幾件窄小嘅衣物,床上有一種狂風暴雨過後嘅樣子,除咗佢自己之外,呢個就係屋裡有人存在嘅唯一跡象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉上來拿燈時,地板上亂七八糟地散落著幾件窄小的衣物,床上有一種狂風暴雨過後的樣子,除了她自己之外,這就是屋裡有人存在的唯一跡象。

passages.original: She deliberately picked up Anne’s clothes, placed them neatly on a prim yellow chair, and then, taking up the candle, went over to the bed.
passages.vernacular: 佢不慌不忙地撿起安妮嘅衣服,整齊地放喺一把古板嘅黃椅子上,然後攞起蠟燭,走到床邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不慌不忙地撿起安妮的衣服,整齊地放在一把古板的黃椅子上,然後拿起蠟燭,走到床邊。

passages.original: “Good night,” she said, a little awkwardly, but not unkindly.
passages.vernacular: 「晚安,」佢講,有點笨拙,但並不冷淡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「晚安,」她說,有點笨拙,但並不冷淡。

passages.original: Anne’s white face and big eyes appeared over the bedclothes with a startling suddenness.
passages.vernacular: 安妮蒼白嘅臉同大眼睛突然從被子上冒咗出嚟,令人食驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮蒼白的臉和大眼睛突然從被子上冒了出來,令人吃驚。

passages.original: “How can you call it a good night when you know it must be the very worst night I’ve ever had?” she said reproachfully.
passages.vernacular: 「您明知呢一定係我度過嘅最糟糕嘅一夜,點仲能講晚安呢?」佢責備地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您明知這一定是我度過的最糟糕的一夜,怎麼還能說晚安呢?」她責備地說。

passages.original: Then she dived down into invisibility again.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢又鑽下去,唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她又鑽下去,不見了。

passages.original: Marilla went slowly down to the kitchen and proceeded to wash the supper dishes.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉慢慢走下樓到廚房,動手洗晚飯用嘅碗碟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉慢慢走下樓到廚房,動手洗晚飯用的碗碟。

passages.original: Matthew was smoking--a sure sign of perturbation of mind.
passages.vernacular: 馬修喺抽煙——呢個係心神不寧的確切跡象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修在抽煙——這是心神不寧的確切跡象。

passages.original: He seldom smoked, for Marilla set her face against it as a filthy habit; but at certain times and seasons he felt driven to it and then Marilla winked at the practice, realizing that a mere man must have some vent for his emotions.
passages.vernacular: 佢好少抽煙,因為瑪麗拉反對呢個係個骯髒嘅習慣;但喺某些時候,佢覺得非抽不可,呢陣瑪麗拉就睜一隻眼閉一隻眼,明白一個大男人總得有個發洩情緒嘅出口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很少抽煙,因為瑪麗拉反對這是個骯髒的習慣;但在某些時候,他覺得非抽不可,這時瑪麗拉就睜一隻眼閉一隻眼,明白一個大男人總得有個發洩情緒的出口。

passages.original: “Well, this is a pretty kettle of fish,” she said wrathfully.
passages.vernacular: 「哼,呢真係個大麻煩,」佢憤憤地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,這真是個大麻煩,」她憤憤地說。

passages.original: “This is what comes of sending word instead of going ourselves.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個就係不親自去、只捎話嘅下場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就是不親自去、只捎話的下場。

passages.original: Richard Spencer’s folks have twisted that message somehow.
passages.vernacular: 理查德·斯潘塞家嘅人把嗰口信弄岔喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 理查德·斯潘塞家的人把那口信弄岔了。

passages.original: One of us will have to drive over and see Mrs. Spencer tomorrow, that’s certain.
passages.vernacular: 聽日我哋兩個人中得有一個趕車去見斯潘塞太太,呢個係肯定嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天我們兩個人中得有一個趕車去見斯潘塞太太,這是肯定的。

passages.original: This girl will have to be sent back to the asylum.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個女孩得送回孤兒院去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個女孩得送回孤兒院去。」

passages.original: “Yes, I suppose so,” said Matthew reluctantly.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我想係咁樣,」馬修不情願地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我想是這樣,」馬修不情願地說。

passages.original: “You suppose so!
passages.vernacular: 「你想係咁樣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想是這樣!

passages.original: Don’t you know it?”
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道嗎?」

passages.original: “Well now, she’s a real nice little thing, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢係個挺好嘅小傢伙,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,她是個挺好的小傢伙,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: It’s kind of a pity to send her back when she’s so set on staying here.”
passages.vernacular: 佢咁一心想留喺呢兒,把佢送回去有點可惜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她這麼一心想留在這兒,把她送回去有點可惜。」

passages.original: “Matthew Cuthbert, you don’t mean to say you think we ought to keep her!”
passages.vernacular: 「馬修·卡思伯特,你唔會係講你認為我哋該留下佢吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修·卡思伯特,你不會是說你認為我們該留下她吧!」

passages.original: Marilla’s astonishment could not have been greater if Matthew had expressed a predilection for standing on his head.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉嘅震驚程度,就係馬修表示鍾意倒立,都唔會更大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉的震驚程度,就是馬修表示喜歡倒立,也不會更大了。

passages.original: “Well, now, no, I suppose not--not exactly,” stammered Matthew, uncomfortably driven into a corner for his precise meaning.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個嘛,不,我想不——不完全係,」馬修結結巴巴地講,不舒服地被逼到角落裡要講明佢確切嘅意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這個嘛,不,我想不——不完全是,」馬修結結巴巴地說,不舒服地被逼到角落裡要說明他確切的意思。

passages.original: “I suppose--we could hardly be expected to keep her.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想——我哋唔能夠指望留下佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想——我們不能指望留下她。」

passages.original: “I should say not.
passages.vernacular: 「我都咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也這麼說。

passages.original: What good would she be to us?”
passages.vernacular: 佢對我哋有乜嘢用?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她對我們有什麼用?」

passages.original: “We might be some good to her,” said Matthew suddenly and unexpectedly.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋或者對佢有些用,」馬修忽然出人意料地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們也許對她有些用,」馬修忽然出人意料地說。

passages.original: “Matthew Cuthbert, I believe that child has bewitched you!
passages.vernacular: 「馬修·卡思伯特,我睇呢細路把你迷住喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修·卡思伯特,我看這孩子把你迷住了!

passages.original: I can see as plain as plain that you want to keep her.”
passages.vernacular: 我清清楚楚地睇出你想留下佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我清清楚楚地看出你想留下她。」

passages.original: “Well now, she’s a real interesting little thing,” persisted Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢係個真有趣嘅小傢伙,」馬修堅持講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,她是個真有趣的小傢伙,」馬修堅持說。

passages.original: “You should have heard her talk coming from the station.”
passages.vernacular: 「你真該聽聽佢從車站回嚟路上講嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真該聽聽她從車站回來路上說的話。」

passages.original: “Oh, she can talk fast enough.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢講起話嚟夠快嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,她說起話來夠快的。

passages.original: I saw that at once.
passages.vernacular: 我一眼就睇出嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一眼就看出來了。

passages.original: It’s nothing in her favor, either.
passages.vernacular: 呢都唔係佢嘅優點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這也不是她的優點。

passages.original: I don’t like children who have so much to say.
passages.vernacular: 我不鍾意話咁多嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不喜歡話這麼多的孩子。

passages.original: I don’t want an orphan girl and if I did she isn’t the style I’d pick out.
passages.vernacular: 我唔想要孤兒女孩,即使要,佢都唔係我會挑嘅嗰種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不想要孤兒女孩,即使要,她也不是我會挑的那種。

passages.original: There’s something I don’t understand about her.
passages.vernacular: 佢身上有些嘢我不明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她身上有些東西我不明白。

passages.original: No, she’s got to be despatched straightway back to where she came from.”
passages.vernacular: 不行,佢得即刻被打發回原來嘅地方去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不行,她得立刻被打發回原來的地方去。」

passages.original: “I could hire a French boy to help me,” said Matthew, “and she’d be company for you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我可以雇一個法國小子嚟幫我,」馬修講,「而佢可以畀你做伴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可以雇一個法國小子來幫我,」馬修說,「而她可以給你做伴。」

passages.original: “I’m not suffering for company,” said Marilla shortly.
passages.vernacular: 「我不缺伴兒,」瑪麗拉簡短地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不缺伴兒,」瑪麗拉簡短地說。

passages.original: “And I’m not going to keep her.”
passages.vernacular: 「而且我不打算留下佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且我不打算留下她。」

passages.original: “Well now, it’s just as you say, of course, Marilla,” said Matthew rising and putting his pipe away.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,當然隨你講咗算,瑪麗拉,」馬修站起嚟,把煙斗收起來講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,當然隨你說了算,瑪麗拉,」馬修站起來,把煙斗收起來說。

passages.original: “I’m going to bed.”
passages.vernacular: 「我去瞓喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我去睡了。」

passages.original: To bed went Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 馬修去瞓喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修去睡了。

passages.original: And to bed, when she had put her dishes away, went Marilla, frowning most resolutely.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉把碗碟收好後,都去瞓喇,眉頭皺得好堅決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉把碗碟收好後,也去睡了,眉頭皺得十分堅決。

passages.original: And up-stairs, in the east gable, a lonely, heart-hungry, friendless child cried herself to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 而喺樓上,喺東山牆房間裡,一個孤單嘅、渴望愛嘅、冇朋友嘅細路哭住瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而在樓上,在東山牆房間裡,一個孤單的、渴望愛的、沒有朋友的孩子哭著睡著了。

chapters.title: Ch. IV Morning at Green Gables 第四章:綠色屋頂的早晨

passages.original: CH IT was broad daylight when Anne awoke and sat up in bed, staring confusedly at the window through which a flood of cheery sunshine was pouring and outside of which something white and feathery waved across glimpses of blue sky.
passages.vernacular: 安妮醒嚟坐喺床上時,天已大亮,佢迷惑地望住窗戶,一片明朗嘅陽光傾瀉進嚟,窗外有乜嘢白色嘅、羽毛似嘅嘢,喺一角角藍天前搖曳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮醒來坐在床上時,天已大亮,她迷惑地望著窗戶,一片明朗的陽光傾瀉進來,窗外有什麼白色的、羽毛似的東西,在一角角藍天前搖曳。

passages.original: For a moment she could not remember where she was.
passages.vernacular: 有咁一會兒,佢想不起自己喺邊度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有那麼一會兒,她想不起自己在哪裡。

passages.original: First came a delightful thrill, as of something very pleasant; then a horrible remembrance.
passages.vernacular: 首先湧上嚟一陣愉快嘅顫慄,像係有乜嘢好愉快嘅事;然後係可怕嘅記憶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先湧上來一陣愉快的顫慄,像是有什麼非常愉快的事;然後是可怕的記憶。

passages.original: This was Green Gables and they didn’t want her because she wasn’t a boy!
passages.vernacular: 呢個係綠色屋頂,而佢哋唔好佢,因為佢唔係男孩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是綠色屋頂,而他們不要她,因為她不是男孩!

passages.original: But it was morning and, yes, it was a cherry-tree in full bloom outside of her window.
passages.vernacular: 不過而家係早晨,而且,冇錯,窗外係一棵盛開嘅櫻桃樹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是現在是早晨,而且,沒錯,窗外是一棵盛開的櫻桃樹。

passages.original: With a bound she was out of bed and across the floor.
passages.vernacular: 佢一躍下床,跑過地板。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一躍下床,跑過地板。

passages.original: She pushed up the sash--it went up stiffly and creakily, as if it hadn’t been opened for a long time, which was the case; and it stuck so tight that nothing was needed to hold it up.
passages.vernacular: 佢推起窗框——佢僵硬吱嘎地升咗上去,好像好久冇打開過喇,確實如此;而且佢卡得好緊,乜嘢都唔使撐住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她推起窗框——它僵硬吱嘎地升了上去,好像很久沒打開過了,確實如此;而且它卡得非常緊,什麼也不用撐著。

passages.original: Anne dropped on her knees and gazed out into the June morning, her eyes glistening with delight.
passages.vernacular: 安妮跪下嚟,望住六月嘅早晨,眼睛閃耀住喜悅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮跪下來,望著六月的早晨,眼睛閃耀著喜悅。

passages.original: Oh, wasn’t it beautiful?
passages.vernacular: 哦,多美啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,多美啊!

passages.original: Wasn’t it a lovely place?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係幾咁可愛嘅地方啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是多麼可愛的地方啊!

passages.original: Suppose she wasn’t really going to stay here!
passages.vernacular: 假如佢其實唔會喺呢度留下嚟呢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假如她其實不會在這裡留下來呢!

passages.original: She would imagine she was.
passages.vernacular: 佢就想像佢會留下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她就想像她會留下。

passages.original: There was scope for imagination here.
passages.vernacular: 呢度有想像嘅餘地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有想像的餘地。

passages.original: A huge cherry-tree grew outside, so close that its boughs tapped against the house, and it was so thick-set with blossoms that hardly a leaf was to be seen.
passages.vernacular: 窗外長住一棵巨大嘅櫻桃樹,離得咁近,樹枝都敲到房子上喇,花開得咁稠密,幾乎睇唔到葉子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窗外長著一棵巨大的櫻桃樹,離得那麼近,樹枝都敲到房子上了,花開得那麼稠密,幾乎看不到葉子。

passages.original: On both sides of the house was a big orchard, one of apple-trees and one of cherry-trees, also showered over with blossoms; and their grass was all sprinkled with dandelions.
passages.vernacular: 房子兩邊都係大果園,一個係蘋果樹,一個係櫻桃樹,同樣開滿咗花;草地上到處灑滿咗蒲公英。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房子兩邊都是大果園,一個是蘋果樹,一個是櫻桃樹,同樣開滿了花;草地上到處灑滿了蒲公英。

passages.original: In the garden below were lilac-trees purple with flowers, and their dizzily sweet fragrance drifted up to the window on the morning wind.
passages.vernacular: 下面嘅花園裡,丁香樹開滿咗紫色嘅花,醉人嘅甜香隨住晨風飄上窗嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下面的花園裡,丁香樹開滿了紫色的花,醉人的甜香隨著晨風飄上窗來。

passages.original: Below the garden a green field lush with clover sloped down to the hollow where the brook ran and where scores of white birches grew, upspringing airily out of an undergrowth suggestive of delightful possibilities in ferns and mosses and woodsy things generally.
passages.vernacular: 花園下面,係一片長滿三葉草嘅綠色田野,向下傾斜到小溪流過嘅窪地,嗰度長住幾十棵白樺,從暗示住各種蕨類、青苔同一般林中事物嘅奇妙可能嘅灌木叢裡輕盈地竄起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 花園下面,是一片長滿三葉草的綠色田野,向下傾斜到小溪流過的窪地,那裡長著幾十棵白樺,從暗示著各種蕨類、青苔和一般林中事物的奇妙可能的灌木叢裡輕盈地竄起。

passages.original: Beyond it was a hill, green and feathery with spruce and fir; there was a gap in it where the gray gable end of the little house she had seen from the other side of the Lake of Shining Waters was visible.
passages.vernacular: 越過去係一座山,綠茸茸嘅,長滿咗雲杉同冷杉;山中有一道缺口,透過佢,可以睇到佢從閃亮湖水嘅另一邊睇見過嘅嗰座小房子嘅灰色山牆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 越過去是一座山,綠茸茸的,長滿了雲杉和冷杉;山中有一道缺口,透過它,可以看到她從閃亮湖水的另一邊看見過的那座小房子的灰色山牆。

passages.original: Off to the left were the big barns and beyond them, away down over green, low-sloping fields, was a sparkling blue glimpse of sea.
passages.vernacular: 左邊係大穀倉,穀倉嗰邊,往下越過低緩傾斜嘅綠色田野,遠處閃爍住一抹藍色嘅海。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 左邊是大穀倉,穀倉那邊,往下越過低緩傾斜的綠色田野,遠處閃爍著一抹藍色的海。

passages.original: Anne’s beauty-loving eyes lingered on it all, taking everything greedily in.
passages.vernacular: 安妮愛美嘅眼睛流連喺呢一切之上,貪婪地吸收住一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮愛美的眼睛流連在這一切之上,貪婪地吸收著一切。

passages.original: She had looked on so many unlovely places in her life, poor child; but this was as lovely as anything she had ever dreamed.
passages.vernacular: 佢呢輩子見過太多不美嘅地方,可憐嘅細路;可呢度同佢曾夢想嘅任何地方一樣美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她這輩子見過太多不美的地方,可憐的孩子;可這裡和她曾夢想的任何地方一樣美。

passages.original: She knelt there, lost to everything but the loveliness around her, until she was startled by a hand on her shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 佢跪喺嗰度,除咗周圍嘅美景乜嘢都忘喇,直到肩膀上被一隻手一碰,才嚇咗一跳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她跪在那裡,除了周圍的美景什麼都忘了,直到肩膀上被一隻手一碰,才嚇了一跳。

passages.original: Marilla had come in unheard by the small dreamer.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉進嚟時,呢個小夢想家根本冇聽見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉進來時,這個小夢想家根本沒聽見。

passages.original: “It’s time you were dressed,” she said curtly.
passages.vernacular: 「該穿衣服喇,」佢簡短地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「該穿衣服了,」她簡短地說。

passages.original: Marilla really did not know how to talk to the child, and her uncomfortable ignorance made her crisp and curt when she did not mean to be.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉實在唔知道點跟呢細路講話,佢嗰種不舒服嘅無知讓佢喺唔想生硬嘅時候都變得乾脆而生硬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉實在不知道怎麼跟這孩子說話,她那種不舒服的無知讓她在不想生硬的時候也變得乾脆而生硬。

passages.original: Anne stood up and drew a long breath.
passages.vernacular: 安妮站起嚟,深深地吸咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮站起來,深深地吸了口氣。

passages.original: “Oh, isn’t it wonderful?” she said, waving her hand comprehensively at the good world outside.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,呢唔係太奇妙咗嗎?」佢講,向外面美好嘅世界廣泛地揮咗揮手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,這不是太奇妙了嗎?」她說,向外面美好的世界廣泛地揮了揮手。

passages.original: “It’s a big tree,” said Marilla, “and it blooms great, but the fruit don’t amount to much never--small and wormy.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係棵大樹,」瑪麗拉講,「花開得好旺,不過果子從來不點樣——又小又長蟲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是棵大樹,」瑪麗拉說,「花開得很旺,可是果子從來不怎麼樣——又小又長蟲。」

passages.original: “Oh, I don’t mean just the tree; of course it’s lovely--yes, it’s radiantly lovely--it blooms as if it meant it--but I meant everything, the garden and the orchard and the brook and the woods, the whole big dear world.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我講嘅不只係嗰棵樹;當然佢好可愛——係嘅,佢光彩奪目地可愛——佢開起花嚟好像係真心實意嘅——可我係指一切,花園、果園、小溪、樹林,整個可愛嘅大世界。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我說的不只是那棵樹;當然它很可愛——是的,它光彩奪目地可愛——它開起花來好像是真心實意的——可我是指一切,花園、果園、小溪、樹林,整個可愛的大世界。

passages.original: Don’t you feel as if you just loved the world on a morning like this?
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅早晨,您不覺得自己簡直愛呢個世界嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的早晨,您不覺得自己簡直愛這個世界嗎?

passages.original: And I can hear the brook laughing all the way up here.
passages.vernacular: 我喺呢兒就能聽到小溪喺笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在這兒就能聽到小溪在笑。

passages.original: Have you ever noticed what cheerful things brooks are?
passages.vernacular: 您有冇注意過小溪係幾咁快活嘅嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您有沒有注意過小溪是多麼快活的東西?

passages.original: They’re always laughing.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋總是喺笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們總是在笑。

passages.original: Even in winter-time I’ve heard them under the ice.
passages.vernacular: 即使喺冬天我都聽到過佢哋喺冰下面笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使在冬天我也聽到過它們在冰下面笑。

passages.original: I’m so glad there’s a brook near Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 我太高興綠色屋頂附近有一條小溪喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興綠色屋頂附近有一條小溪了。

passages.original: Perhaps you think it doesn’t make any difference to me when you’re not going to keep me, but it does.
passages.vernacular: 或者您覺得既然你哋不打算留下我,呢對我就冇乜嘢區別,不過有嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許您覺得既然你們不打算留下我,這對我就沒有什麼區別,可是有的。

passages.original: I shall always like to remember that there is a brook at Green Gables even if I never see it again.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠會鍾意記得綠色屋頂有一條小溪,即使我再都見唔到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠會喜歡記得綠色屋頂有一條小溪,即使我再也見不到它。

passages.original: If there wasn’t a brook I’d be haunted by the uncomfortable feeling that there ought to be one.
passages.vernacular: 如果冇小溪,我會被一種不舒服嘅感覺困擾,覺得本該有一條才對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果沒有小溪,我會被一種不舒服的感覺困擾,覺得本該有一條才對。

passages.original: I’m not in the depths of despair this morning.
passages.vernacular: 今日早晨我不喺絕望嘅深淵裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天早晨我不在絕望的深淵裡。

passages.original: I never can be in the morning.
passages.vernacular: 早晨我永遠唔可能喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨我永遠不可能在。

passages.original: Isn’t it a splendid thing that there are mornings?
passages.vernacular: 有早晨,呢唔係件美妙嘅事嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有早晨,這不是件美妙的事嗎?

passages.original: But I feel very sad.
passages.vernacular: 不過我感到好傷心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我感到很傷心。

passages.original: I’ve just been imagining that it was really me you wanted after all and that I was to stay here for ever and ever.
passages.vernacular: 我頭先一直喺想像,其實你哋終究定係要我嘅,我要永遠永遠留喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我剛才一直在想像,其實你們終究還是要我的,我要永遠永遠留在這裡。

passages.original: It was a great comfort while it lasted.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰持續嘅時候,嗰個係好大嘅安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那持續的時候,那是很大的安慰。

passages.original: But the worst of imagining things is that the time comes when you have to stop and that hurts.”
passages.vernacular: 但想像事情最糟糕嘅係,總有必須停下嚟嘅時候,嗰會好痛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但想像事情最糟糕的是,總有必須停下來的時候,那會很痛。」

passages.original: “You’d better get dressed and come down-stairs and never mind your imaginings,” said Marilla as soon as she could get a word in edgewise.
passages.vernacular: 「你最好穿好衣服下樓嚟,別管你嗰啲想像喇,」瑪麗拉一能插上話就講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你最好穿好衣服下樓來,別管你那些想像了,」瑪麗拉一能插上話就說。

passages.original: “Breakfast is waiting.
passages.vernacular: 「早飯喺等住呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「早飯在等著呢。

passages.original: Wash your face and comb your hair.
passages.vernacular: 洗洗臉,梳梳頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 洗洗臉,梳梳頭髮。

passages.original: Leave the window up and turn your bedclothes back over the foot of the bed.
passages.vernacular: 窗子開住,被子翻過嚟搭喺床尾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窗子開著,被子翻過來搭在床尾。

passages.original: Be as smart as you can.”
passages.vernacular: 儘量利索點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘量利索點。」

passages.original: Anne could evidently be smart to some purpose for she was down-stairs in ten minutes’ time, with her clothes neatly on, her hair brushed and braided, her face washed, and a comfortable consciousness pervading her soul that she had fulfilled all Marilla’s requirements.
passages.vernacular: 安妮顯然能利索得好有效果,因為佢好鐘後就下樓喇,衣服穿得整整齊齊,頭髮梳好編咗辮子,臉都洗喇,心裡有一種舒坦嘅意識,覺得自己已經滿足咗瑪麗拉所有嘅要求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮顯然能利索得很有效果,因為她十分鐘後就下樓了,衣服穿得整整齊齊,頭髮梳好編了辮子,臉也洗了,心裡有一種舒坦的意識,覺得自己已經滿足了瑪麗拉所有的要求。

passages.original: As a matter of fact, however, she had forgotten to turn back the bedclothes.
passages.vernacular: 然而事實上,佢忘咗把被子翻過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而事實上,她忘了把被子翻過來。

passages.original: “I’m pretty hungry this morning,” she announced as she slipped into the chair Marilla placed for her.
passages.vernacular: 「今日早晨我餓極喇,」佢宣布道,一邊滑進瑪麗拉替佢擺好嘅椅子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今天早晨我餓極了,」她宣布道,一邊滑進瑪麗拉替她擺好的椅子裡。

passages.original: “The world doesn’t seem such a howling wilderness as it did last night.
passages.vernacular: 「世界睇上去不像琴晚嗰樣係片荒涼嘅曠野喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「世界看上去不像昨晚那樣是片荒涼的曠野了。

passages.original: I’m so glad it’s a sunshiny morning.
passages.vernacular: 我太高興呢個係個陽光燦爛嘅早晨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興這是個陽光燦爛的早晨。

passages.original: But I like rainy mornings real well, too.
passages.vernacular: 不過我都好鍾意下雨嘅早晨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我也很喜歡下雨的早晨。

passages.original: All sorts of mornings are interesting, don’t you think?
passages.vernacular: 各種早晨都有趣,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 各種早晨都有趣,您說呢?

passages.original: You don’t know what’s going to happen through the day, and there’s so much scope for imagination.
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道一天裡會發生乜嘢事,而且有咁多想像嘅餘地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道一天裡會發生什麼事,而且有那麼多想像的餘地。

passages.original: But I’m glad it’s not rainy today because it’s easier to be cheerful and bear up under affliction on a sunshiny day.
passages.vernacular: 不過我好高興今日不下雨,因為喺陽光明媚嘅日子裡,更容易保持快樂、忍受苦難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我很高興今天不下雨,因為在陽光明媚的日子裡,更容易保持快樂、忍受苦難。

passages.original: I feel that I have a good deal to bear up under.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我有許多要忍受嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我有許多要忍受的事。

passages.original: It’s all very well to read about sorrows and imagine yourself living through them heroically, but it’s not so nice when you really come to have them, is it?”
passages.vernacular: 讀到悲傷嘅事,想像自己英雄般地熬過佢哋,呢固然好好,不過真嘅碰上咗就不咁美妙喇,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讀到悲傷的事,想像自己英雄般地熬過它們,這固然很好,可是真的碰上了就不那麼美妙了,是不是?」

passages.original: “For pity’s sake hold your tongue,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「睇喺老天嘅份上,閉上嘴吧,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看在老天的份上,閉上嘴吧,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “You talk entirely too much for a little girl.”
passages.vernacular: 「你對一個小女孩來講話太多喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你對一個小女孩來說話太多了。」

passages.original: Thereupon Anne held her tongue so obediently and thoroughly that her continued silence made Marilla rather nervous, as if in the presence of something not exactly natural.
passages.vernacular: 於是安妮聽話地、徹底地閉上咗嘴,佢持續嘅沉默倒讓瑪麗拉相當緊張,好像面對住乜嘢不太自然嘅嘢似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是安妮聽話地、徹底地閉上了嘴,她持續的沉默倒讓瑪麗拉相當緊張,好像面對著什麼不太自然的東西似的。

passages.original: Matthew also held his tongue,--but this was natural,--so that the meal was a very silent one.
passages.vernacular: 馬修都閉口不言——但呢個係好自然嘅——所以呢頓飯食得好安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修也閉口不言——但這是很自然的——所以這頓飯吃得非常安靜。

passages.original: As it progressed Anne became more and more abstracted, eating mechanically, with her big eyes fixed unswervingly and unseeingly on the sky outside the window.
passages.vernacular: 飯食到一半,安妮越嚟越心不喺焉,機械地食住,大眼睛直勾勾地、茫然地盯住窗外嘅天空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 飯吃到一半,安妮越來越心不在焉,機械地吃著,大眼睛直勾勾地、茫然地盯著窗外的天空。

passages.original: This made Marilla more nervous than ever; she had an uncomfortable feeling that while this odd child’s body might be there at the table her spirit was far away in some remote airy cloudland, borne aloft on the wings of imagination.
passages.vernacular: 呢讓瑪麗拉更緊張喇;佢有種不舒服嘅感覺,覺得雖然呢個古怪細路嘅身體或者喺桌邊,佢嘅靈魂卻遠喺某個遙遠嘅空中雲國,乘著想像嘅翅膀翱翔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這讓瑪麗拉更緊張了;她有種不舒服的感覺,覺得雖然這個古怪孩子的身體也許在桌邊,她的靈魂卻遠在某個遙遠的空中雲國,乘著想像的翅膀翱翔。

passages.original: Who would want such a child about the place?
passages.vernacular: 邊個會想要咁樣嘅細路待喺家裡呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰會想要這樣的孩子待在家裡呢?

passages.original: Yet Matthew wished to keep her, of all unaccountable things!
passages.vernacular: 不過馬修竟然想留下佢,呢個係幾咁不可理喻嘅事!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是馬修竟然想留下她,這是多麼不可理喻的事!

passages.original: Marilla felt that he wanted it just as much this morning as he had the night before, and that he would go on wanting it.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉覺得,佢今日早晨同琴晚一樣想留下佢,而且會一直想下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉覺得,他今天早晨和昨晚一樣想留下她,而且會一直想下去。

passages.original: That was Matthew’s way--take a whim into his head and cling to it with the most amazing silent persistency--a persistency ten times more potent and effectual in its very silence than if he had talked it out.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係馬修嘅作風——腦子裡冒出一個念頭,就用驚人嘅沉默嘅堅持咬住不放——呢種堅持,喺沉默中嘅威力,比講出嚟要強十倍,有效十倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是馬修的作風——腦子裡冒出一個念頭,就用驚人的沉默的堅持咬住不放——這種堅持,在沉默中的威力,比說出來要強十倍,有效十倍。

passages.original: When the meal was ended Anne came out of her reverie and offered to wash the dishes.
passages.vernacular: 飯後,安妮從沉思中回過神嚟,提出要洗碗碟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 飯後,安妮從沉思中回過神來,提出要洗碗碟。

passages.original: “Can you wash dishes right?” asked Marilla distrustfully.
passages.vernacular: 「你會好好洗碗嗎?」瑪麗拉不信任地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會好好洗碗嗎?」瑪麗拉不信任地問。

passages.original: “Pretty well.
passages.vernacular: 「仲不錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還不錯。

passages.original: I’m better at looking after children, though.
passages.vernacular: 不過我更擅長照睇細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我更擅長照看孩子。

passages.original: I’ve had so much experience at that.
passages.vernacular: 我喺呢方面經驗太多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在這方面經驗太多了。

passages.original: It’s such a pity you haven’t any here for me to look after.”
passages.vernacular: 真可惜您呢兒冇細路讓我照睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真可惜您這兒沒有孩子讓我照看。」

passages.original: “I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present.
passages.vernacular: 「我不覺得我仲想要比而家更多嘅細路嚟照睇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不覺得我還想要比現在更多的孩子來照看了。

passages.original: You’re problem enough in all conscience.
passages.vernacular: 你一個人就夠成問題嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一個人就夠成問題的了。

passages.original: What’s to be done with you I don’t know.
passages.vernacular: 攞你點算,我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿你怎麼辦,我不知道。

passages.original: Matthew is a most ridiculous man.”
passages.vernacular: 馬修真係個荒唐嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修真是個荒唐的人。」

passages.original: “I think he’s lovely,” said Anne reproachfully.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得佢好可愛,」安妮責備地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得他很可愛,」安妮責備地說。

passages.original: “He is so very sympathetic.
passages.vernacular: 「佢好富有同情心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他非常富有同情心。

passages.original: He didn’t mind how much I talked--he seemed to like it.
passages.vernacular: 我講咗多少話佢都不介意——佢好像仲鍾意聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說了多少話他都不介意——他好像還喜歡聽。

passages.original: I felt that he was a kindred spirit as soon as ever I saw him.”
passages.vernacular: 我一睇見佢,就覺得佢係個志同道合嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一看見他,就覺得他是個志同道合的人。」

passages.original: “You’re both queer enough, if that’s what you mean by kindred spirits,” said Marilla with a sniff.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋倆都夠古怪嘅,如果你講嘅志同道合就係呢個意思嘅話,」瑪麗拉哼咗一聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們倆都夠古怪的,如果你說的志同道合就是這個意思的話,」瑪麗拉哼了一聲說。

passages.original: “Yes, you may wash the dishes.
passages.vernacular: 「對,你可以洗碗碟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,你可以洗碗碟。

passages.original: Take plenty of hot water, and be sure you dry them well.
passages.vernacular: 多用熱水,一定要擦乾淨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多用熱水,一定要擦乾淨。

passages.original: I’ve got enough to attend to this morning for I’ll have to drive over to White Sands in the afternoon and see Mrs. Spencer.
passages.vernacular: 今日早晨我有好多事要處理,因為下午我得趕車去白沙睇斯潘塞太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天早晨我有很多事要處理,因為下午我得趕車去白沙看斯潘塞太太。

passages.original: You’ll come with me and we’ll settle what’s to be done with you.
passages.vernacular: 你跟我一起去,我哋嚟決定點處置你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你跟我一起去,我們來決定怎麼處置你。

passages.original: After you’ve finished the dishes go up-stairs and make your bed.”
passages.vernacular: 洗完碗碟後上樓去鋪床。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 洗完碗碟後上樓去鋪床。」

passages.original: Anne washed the dishes deftly enough, as Marilla, who kept a sharp eye on the process, discerned.
passages.vernacular: 安妮洗碗碟洗得相當熟練,呢個係一直緊盯住整個過程嘅瑪麗拉睇出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮洗碗碟洗得相當熟練,這是一直緊盯著整個過程的瑪麗拉看出來的。

passages.original: Later on she made her bed less successfully, for she had never learned the art of wrestling with a feather tick.
passages.vernacular: 後來佢鋪床就冇咁成功喇,因為佢從冇學過如何跟羽絨褥子搏鬥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後來她鋪床就沒那麼成功了,因為她從沒學過如何跟羽絨褥子搏鬥。

passages.original: But it was done somehow and smoothed down; and then Marilla, to get rid of her, told her she might go out-of-doors and amuse herself until dinnertime.
passages.vernacular: 但總算弄好喇,撫平喇;然後瑪麗拉為了打發佢走,告訴佢可以到外面去玩,直到食午飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但總算弄好了,撫平了;然後瑪麗拉為了打發她走,告訴她可以到外面去玩,直到吃午飯。

passages.original: Anne flew to the door, face alight, eyes glowing.
passages.vernacular: 安妮飛向門口,臉龐發亮,眼睛閃耀住光芒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮飛向門口,臉龐發亮,眼睛閃耀著光芒。

passages.original: On the very threshold she stopped short, wheeled about, came back and sat down by the table, light and glow as effectually blotted out as if some one had clapped an extinguisher on her.
passages.vernacular: 就喺門檻上,佢猛地停住,轉過身,走回嚟,喺桌邊坐下,臉上嘅光彩被徹底熄滅喇,就像有人用滅燭罩把佢扣住咗似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在門檻上,她猛地停住,轉過身,走回來,在桌邊坐下,臉上的光彩被徹底熄滅了,就像有人用滅燭罩把它扣住了似的。

passages.original: “What’s the matter now?” demanded Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「而家又點喇?」瑪麗拉問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在又怎麼了?」瑪麗拉問。

passages.original: “I don’t dare go out,” said Anne, in the tone of a martyr relinquishing all earthly joys.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔敢出去,」安妮講,語氣像一個放棄咗所有塵世歡樂嘅殉道者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不敢出去,」安妮說,語氣像一個放棄了所有塵世歡樂的殉道者。

passages.original: “If I can’t stay here there is no use in my loving Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 「如果我唔能夠留喺呢度,嗰愛上綠色屋頂就冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我不能留在這裡,那愛上綠色屋頂就沒有用。

passages.original: And if I go out there and get acquainted with all those trees and flowers and the orchard and the brook I’ll not be able to help loving it.
passages.vernacular: 而且如果我到外面去,同所有嗰啲樹同花、果園同小溪混熟喇,我就忍不住會愛上佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且如果我到外面去,和所有那些樹和花、果園和小溪混熟了,我就忍不住會愛上它。

passages.original: It’s hard enough now, so I won’t make it any harder.
passages.vernacular: 而家已經夠難嘅喇,所以我唔好讓佢更難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在已經夠難的了,所以我不要讓它更難。

passages.original: I want to go out so much--everything seems to be calling to me, ‘Anne, Anne, come out to us.
passages.vernacular: 我好想出去——似乎一切都喺呼喚我:『安妮,安妮,出嚟找我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我非常想出去——似乎一切都在呼喚我:『安妮,安妮,出來找我們。

passages.original: Anne, Anne, we want a playmate’--but it’s better not.
passages.vernacular: 安妮,安妮,我哋想要個玩伴』——但最好定係唔好去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮,安妮,我們想要個玩伴』——但最好還是別去。

passages.original: There is no use in loving things if you have to be torn from them, is there?
passages.vernacular: 如果愛上嘅嘢最終要被硬生生拆開,嗰愛佢哋就冇用,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果愛上的東西最終要被硬生生拆開,那愛它們就沒有用,是不是?

passages.original: And it’s so hard to keep from loving things, isn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 而且好難不去愛嘢,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且很難不去愛東西,是不是?

passages.original: That was why I was so glad when I thought I was going to live here.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係我以為我要住喺呢兒時咁高興嘅原因。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是我以為我要住在這兒時那麼高興的原因。

passages.original: I thought I’d have so many things to love and nothing to hinder me.
passages.vernacular: 我以為我會有咁多嘢可以愛,而且冇乜嘢會阻礙我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以為我會有那麼多東西可以愛,而且沒有什麼會阻礙我。

passages.original: But that brief dream is over.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰個短暫嘅夢結束喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那個短暫的夢結束了。

passages.original: I am resigned to my fate now, so I don’t think I’ll go out for fear I’ll get unresigned again.
passages.vernacular: 我而家已經順從咗命運,所以我想我不出去喇,免得又不順從起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在已經順從了命運,所以我想我不出去了,免得又不順從起來。

passages.original: What is the name of that geranium on the window-sill, please?”
passages.vernacular: 請問窗臺上嘅嗰盆天竺葵叫乜嘢名字?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請問窗臺上的那盆天竺葵叫什麼名字?」

passages.original: “That’s the apple-scented geranium.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係蘋果香天竺葵。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是蘋果香天竺葵。」

passages.original: “Oh, I don’t mean that sort of a name.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我唔係指嗰種名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我不是指那種名字。

passages.original: I mean just a name you gave it yourself.
passages.vernacular: 我係指您自己畀佢起嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是指您自己給它起的名字。

passages.original: Didn’t you give it a name?
passages.vernacular: 您冇畀佢起名字嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您沒給它起名字嗎?

passages.original: May I give it one then?
passages.vernacular: 嗰我可以畀佢起一個嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我可以給它起一個嗎?

passages.original: May I call it--let me see--Bonny would do--may I call it Bonny while I’m here?
passages.vernacular: 我可以叫佢——讓我想想——邦妮就挺好——我喺呢兒嘅時候可以叫佢邦妮嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以叫它——讓我想想——邦妮就挺好——我在這兒的時候可以叫它邦妮嗎?

passages.original: Oh, do let me!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,就讓我叫吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,就讓我叫吧!」

passages.original: “Goodness, I don’t care.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,我不在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,我不在乎。

passages.original: But where on earth is the sense of naming a geranium?”
passages.vernacular: 不過畀天竺葵起名字到底有乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過給天竺葵起名字到底有什麼意思?」

passages.original: “Oh, I like things to have handles even if they are only geraniums.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我鍾意嘢有個把手,即使佢哋只係天竺葵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我喜歡東西有個把手,即使它們只是天竺葵。

passages.original: It makes them seem more like people.
passages.vernacular: 呢讓佢哋更像人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這讓它們更像人。
