passages.original: How do you know but that it hurts a geranium’s feelings just to be called a geranium and nothing else?
passages.vernacular: 您點知道只被叫做天竺葵而不叫別嘅,唔會傷天竺葵嘅感情呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您怎麼知道只被叫做天竺葵而不叫別的,不會傷天竺葵的感情呢?

passages.original: You wouldn’t like to be called nothing but a woman all the time.
passages.vernacular: 您都唔願意一直只被叫做女人吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您也不願意一直只被叫做女人吧。

passages.original: Yes, I shall call it Bonny.
passages.vernacular: 對,我要叫佢邦妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,我要叫它邦妮。

passages.original: I named that cherry-tree outside my bedroom window this morning.
passages.vernacular: 今日早晨我畀臥室窗外嘅嗰棵櫻桃樹起咗名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天早晨我給臥室窗外的那棵櫻桃樹起了名字。

passages.original: I called it Snow Queen because it was so white.
passages.vernacular: 我叫佢雪之女王,因為佢咁白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫它雪之女王,因為它那麼白。

passages.original: Of course, it won’t always be in blossom, but one can imagine that it is, can’t one?”
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢唔會總是開住花,但可以想像佢開住,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,它不會總是開著花,但可以想像它開著,是不是?」

passages.original: “I never in all my life saw or heard anything to equal her,” muttered Marilla, beating a retreat down to the cellar after potatoes.
passages.vernacular: 「我呢輩子從冇見過、都冇聽講過有邊個能同佢相比,」瑪麗拉嘟囔住,撤退到地窖去攞土豆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我這輩子從沒見過、也沒聽說過有誰能和她相比,」瑪麗拉嘟囔著,撤退到地窖去拿土豆。

passages.original: “She is kind of interesting, as Matthew says.
passages.vernacular: 「佢確實有點有趣,像馬修講嘅嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她確實有點有趣,像馬修說的那樣。

passages.original: I can feel already that I’m wondering what on earth she’ll say next.
passages.vernacular: 我已經感覺到,我正在納悶佢接下嚟會講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經感覺到,我正在納悶她接下來會說什麼。

passages.original: She’ll be casting a spell over me, too.
passages.vernacular: 佢都會對我施魔法嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也會對我施魔法的。

passages.original: She’s cast it over Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 佢已經對馬修施咗魔法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她已經對馬修施了魔法。

passages.original: That look he gave me when he went out said everything he said or hinted last night over again.
passages.vernacular: 佢出去時畀我嘅嗰一眼,把佢琴晚講嘅、暗示嘅全都又講咗一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他出去時給我的那一眼,把他昨晚說的、暗示的全都又說了一遍。

passages.original: I wish he was like other men and would talk things out.
passages.vernacular: 我希望佢像別嘅男人嗰樣,有話講出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望他像別的男人那樣,有話說出來。

passages.original: A body could answer back then and argue him into reason.
passages.vernacular: 嗰樣我哋仲能頂嘴,同佢爭辯講道理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那樣我們還能頂嘴,和他爭辯講道理。

passages.original: But what’s to be done with a man who just looks?”
passages.vernacular: 不過對一個光睇住你嘅男人,你能攞佢點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是對一個光看著你的男人,你能拿他怎麼辦?」

passages.original: Anne had relapsed into reverie, with her chin in her hands and her eyes on the sky, when Marilla returned from her cellar pilgrimage.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉從地窖朝聖歸嚟時,安妮又陷入咗沉思,下巴托喺手裡,眼睛望住天空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉從地窖朝聖歸來時,安妮又陷入了沉思,下巴托在手裡,眼睛望著天空。

passages.original: There Marilla left her until the early dinner was on the table.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉把佢留喺嗰兒,直到早午飯擺上桌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉把她留在那兒,直到早午飯擺上桌。

passages.original: “I suppose I can have the mare and buggy this afternoon, Matthew?” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「馬修,我想我今日下午可以用母馬同輕便馬車吧?」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修,我想我今天下午可以用母馬和輕便馬車吧?」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: Matthew nodded and looked wistfully at Anne.
passages.vernacular: 馬修點點頭,惆悵地睇住安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修點點頭,惆悵地看著安妮。

passages.original: Marilla intercepted the look and said grimly:
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉截住咗呢個眼神,嚴厲地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉截住了這個眼神,嚴厲地說:

passages.original: “I’m going to drive over to White Sands and settle this thing.
passages.vernacular: 「我要趕車去白沙把呢件事解決喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要趕車去白沙把這件事解決了。

passages.original: I’ll take Anne with me and Mrs. Spencer will probably make arrangements to send her back to Nova Scotia at once.
passages.vernacular: 我帶安妮一起去,斯潘塞太太大概會即刻安排把佢送回新斯科舍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我帶安妮一起去,斯潘塞太太大概會馬上安排把她送回新斯科舍。

passages.original: I’ll set your tea out for you and I’ll be home in time to milk the cows.”
passages.vernacular: 我把你嘅茶擺好,我會及時回家擠牛奶。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把你的茶擺好,我會及時回家擠牛奶。」

passages.original: Still Matthew said nothing and Marilla had a sense of having wasted words and breath.
passages.vernacular: 馬修定係乜嘢都冇講,瑪麗拉有種白費口舌同力氣嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修還是什麼也沒說,瑪麗拉有種白費口舌和力氣的感覺。

passages.original: There is nothing more aggravating than a man who won’t talk back--unless it is a woman who won’t.
passages.vernacular: 冇乜嘢比一個唔肯回嘴嘅男人更氣人嘅喇——除非係一個唔肯回嘴嘅女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有什麼比一個不肯回嘴的男人更氣人的了——除非是一個不肯回嘴的女人。

passages.original: Matthew hitched the sorrel into the buggy in due time and Marilla and Anne set off.
passages.vernacular: 馬修及時把栗色馬套上輕便馬車,瑪麗拉同安妮出發喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修及時把栗色馬套上輕便馬車,瑪麗拉和安妮出發了。

passages.original: Matthew opened the yard gate for them and as they drove slowly through, he said, to nobody in particular as it seemed:
passages.vernacular: 馬修為佢哋打開院門,佢哋慢慢駛過時,佢講,似乎唔係對任何人講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修為他們打開院門,他們慢慢駛過時,他說,似乎不是對任何人說:

passages.original: “Little Jerry Buote from the Creek was here this morning, and I told him I guessed I’d hire him for the summer.”
passages.vernacular: 「溪邊嘅小傑里·布特今日朝早嚟過,我告訴佢我想我會雇佢幹一個夏天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溪邊的小傑里·布特今天早上來過,我告訴他我想我會雇他幹一個夏天。」

passages.original: Marilla made no reply, but she hit the unlucky sorrel such a vicious clip with the whip that the fat mare, unused to such treatment, whizzed indignantly down the lane at an alarming pace.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉冇回答,但佢狠狠地畀嗰匹倒霉嘅栗色馬抽咗一鞭,呢匹胖母馬冇受過咁樣嘅對待,氣呼呼地以驚人嘅速度沿住小巷飛馳而下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉沒有回答,但她狠狠地給那匹倒霉的栗色馬抽了一鞭,這匹胖母馬沒受過這樣的對待,氣呼呼地以驚人的速度沿著小巷飛馳而下。

passages.original: Marilla looked back once as the buggy bounced along and saw that aggravating Matthew leaning over the gate, looking wistfully after them.
passages.vernacular: 馬車顛簸住前行時,瑪麗拉回頭睇咗一眼,睇見嗰個氣人嘅馬修靠喺大門上,惆悵地目送住佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬車顛簸著前行時,瑪麗拉回頭看了一眼,看見那個氣人的馬修靠在大門上,惆悵地目送著他們。

chapters.title: Ch. V Anne's History 第五章:安妮的身世

passages.original: CH DO you know,” said Anne confidentially, “I’ve made up my mind to enjoy this drive.
passages.vernacular: 「你知道嗎,」安妮悄悄地講,「我已經打定主意要享受呢趟旅程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道嗎,」安妮悄悄地說,「我已經打定主意要享受這趟旅程。

passages.original: It’s been my experience that you can nearly always enjoy things if you make up your mind firmly that you will.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅經驗係,只要你堅決打定主意要享受,你幾乎總能享受到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的經驗是,只要你堅決打定主意要享受,你幾乎總能享受到。

passages.original: Of course, you must make it up firmly.
passages.vernacular: 當然,你必須堅決打定主意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,你必須堅決打定主意。

passages.original: I am not going to think about going back to the asylum while we’re having our drive.
passages.vernacular: 喺我哋趕路嘅時候,我不打算去想回孤兒院嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我們趕路的時候,我不打算去想回孤兒院的事。

passages.original: I’m just going to think about the drive.
passages.vernacular: 我只想住趕路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只想著趕路。

passages.original: Oh, look, there’s one little early wild rose out!
passages.vernacular: 哦,睇,有一朵早開嘅小野玫瑰!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,看,有一朵早開的小野玫瑰!

passages.original: Isn’t it lovely?
passages.vernacular: 不可愛嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不可愛嗎?

passages.original: Don’t you think it must be glad to be a rose?
passages.vernacular: 您不覺得佢做一朵玫瑰一定好高興嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不覺得它做一朵玫瑰一定很高興嗎?

passages.original: Wouldn’t it be nice if roses could talk?
passages.vernacular: 要係玫瑰能講話唔係好好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是玫瑰能說話不是很好嗎?

passages.original: I’m sure they could tell us such lovely things.
passages.vernacular: 我敢肯定佢哋能告訴我哋咁多可愛嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢肯定它們能告訴我們那麼多可愛的事。

passages.original: And isn’t pink the most bewitching color in the world?
passages.vernacular: 粉紅色唔係世上最迷人嘅顏色嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 粉紅色不是世上最迷人的顏色嗎?

passages.original: I love it, but I can’t wear it.
passages.vernacular: 我愛佢,可我唔能夠穿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛它,可我不能穿。

passages.original: Redheaded people can’t wear pink, not even in imagination.
passages.vernacular: 紅頭髮嘅人唔能夠穿粉紅色,連想像里都不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紅頭髮的人不能穿粉紅色,連想像里也不行。

passages.original: Did you ever know of anybody whose hair was red when she was young, but got to be another color when she grew up?”
passages.vernacular: 您有冇聽講過邊個小時候頭髮係紅嘅,長大後變成咗別嘅顏色?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您有沒有聽說過誰小時候頭髮是紅的,長大後變成了別的顏色?」

passages.original: “No, I don’t know as I ever did,” said Marilla mercilessly, “and I shouldn’t think it likely to happen in your case either.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,我想我從冇聽講過,」瑪麗拉毫不留情地講,「而且我覺得呢種事喺你身上都不大可能發生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,我想我從沒聽說過,」瑪麗拉毫不留情地說,「而且我覺得這種事在你身上也不大可能發生。」

passages.original: Anne sighed.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮嘆了口氣。

passages.original: “Well, that is another hope gone.
passages.vernacular: 「唉,又一個希望破滅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「唉,又一個希望破滅了。

passages.original: ‘My life is a perfect graveyard of buried hopes.’
passages.vernacular: 『我嘅生命係一座埋葬住希望嘅完美墳場。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『我的生命是一座埋葬著希望的完美墳場。』

passages.original: That’s a sentence I read in a book once, and I say it over to comfort myself whenever I’m disappointed in anything.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我喺一本書裡讀到嘅一句話,每當我喺任何事上失望時,就把佢念出嚟安慰自己。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我在一本書裡讀到的一句話,每當我在任何事上失望時,就把它念出來安慰自己。」

passages.original: “I don’t see where the comforting comes in myself,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我自己睇不出呢有乜嘢安慰,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我自己看不出這有什麼安慰,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “Why, because it sounds so nice and romantic, just as if I were a heroine in a book, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,因為佢聽起嚟咁美好、咁浪漫,好像我係書中嘅女主角,您知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,因為它聽起來那麼美好、那麼浪漫,好像我是書中的女主角,您知道。

passages.original: I am so fond of romantic things, and a graveyard full of buried hopes is about as romantic a thing as one can imagine, isn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 我特別鍾意浪漫嘅嘢,而一座埋葬住希望嘅墳場,簡直係人能想像到嘅最浪漫嘅嘢喇,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我特別喜歡浪漫的東西,而一座埋葬著希望的墳場,簡直是人能想像到的最浪漫的東西了,是不是?

passages.original: I’m rather glad I have one.
passages.vernacular: 我挺高興自己有一座。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我挺高興自己有一座。

passages.original: Are we going across the Lake of Shining Waters today?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋今日要過閃亮湖水嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們今天要過閃亮湖水嗎?」

passages.original: “We’re not going over Barry’s pond, if that’s what you mean by your Lake of Shining Waters.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋不走巴里池塘,如果你講嘅閃亮湖水係指嗰個嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們不走巴里池塘,如果你說的閃亮湖水是指那個的話。

passages.original: We’re going by the shore road.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋走海岸路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們走海岸路。」

passages.original: “Shore road sounds nice,” said Anne dreamily.
passages.vernacular: 「海岸路聽起嚟挺美嘅,」安妮夢幻般地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「海岸路聽起來挺美的,」安妮夢幻般地說。

passages.original: “Is it as nice as it sounds?
passages.vernacular: 「佢像聽起嚟咁美嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它像聽起來那麼美嗎?

passages.original: Just when you said ‘shore road’ I saw it in a picture in my mind, as quick as that!
passages.vernacular: 您一講『海岸路』,我腦子裡就一下子睇到咗一幅畫!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您一說『海岸路』,我腦子裡就一下子看到了一幅畫!

passages.original: And White Sands is a pretty name, too; but I don’t like it as well as Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 白沙都係個好聽嘅名字,但我不像鍾意阿文利嗰樣鍾意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白沙也是個好聽的名字,但我不像喜歡阿文利那樣喜歡它。

passages.original: Avonlea is a lovely name.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利係個可愛嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利是個可愛的名字。

passages.original: It just sounds like music.
passages.vernacular: 聽起嚟就像音樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽起來就像音樂。

passages.original: How far is it to White Sands?”
passages.vernacular: 到白沙有多遠?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到白沙有多遠?」

passages.original: “It’s five miles; and as you’re evidently bent on talking you might as well talk to some purpose by telling me what you know about yourself.”
passages.vernacular: 「五英里;既然你顯然一心想講話,不如講些有用嘅,告訴我你自己嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「五英里;既然你顯然一心想說話,不如說些有用的,告訴我你自己的事。」

passages.original: “Oh, what I know about myself isn’t really worth telling,” said Anne eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我自己嘅事真嘅不值得講,」安妮急切地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我自己的事真的不值得說,」安妮急切地說。

passages.original: “If you’ll only let me tell you what I imagine about myself you’ll think it ever so much more interesting.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果您讓我講講我對自己嘅想像,您會覺得有趣得多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果您讓我說說我對自己的想像,您會覺得有趣得多。」

passages.original: “No, I don’t want any of your imaginings.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我唔好你嘅乜嘢想像。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我不要你的什麼想像。

passages.original: Just you stick to bald facts.
passages.vernacular: 你就只講乾巴巴嘅事實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你就只說乾巴巴的事實。

passages.original: Begin at the beginning.
passages.vernacular: 從頭講起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從頭說起。

passages.original: Where were you born and how old are you?”
passages.vernacular: 你喺邊兒出生,今年多大?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在哪兒出生,今年多大?」

passages.original: “I was eleven last March,” said Anne, resigning herself to bald facts with a little sigh.
passages.vernacular: 「今年三月我滿十一歲,」安妮講,輕輕嘆咗口氣,順從咗乾巴巴嘅事實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今年三月我滿十一歲,」安妮說,輕輕嘆了口氣,順從了乾巴巴的事實。

passages.original: “And I was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
passages.vernacular: 「我出生喺新斯科舍嘅博林布羅克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我出生在新斯科舍的博林布羅克。

passages.original: My father’s name was Walter Shirley, and he was a teacher in the Bolingbroke High School.
passages.vernacular: 我父親叫沃爾特·雪莉,係博林布羅克中學嘅老師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父親叫沃爾特·雪莉,是博林布羅克中學的老師。

passages.original: My mother’s name was Bertha Shirley.
passages.vernacular: 我母親叫伯莎·雪莉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我母親叫伯莎·雪莉。

passages.original: Aren’t Walter and Bertha lovely names?
passages.vernacular: 沃爾特同伯莎唔係好可愛嘅名字嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沃爾特和伯莎不是很可愛的名字嗎?

passages.original: I’m so glad my parents had nice names.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興我父母有好聽嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興我父母有好聽的名字。

passages.original: It would be a real disgrace to have a father named--well, say Jedediah, wouldn’t it?”
passages.vernacular: 如果有個父親叫——嗯,比如講叫傑迪代亞,嗰可真係丟臉,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果有個父親叫——嗯,比如說叫傑迪代亞,那可真是丟臉,是不是?」

passages.original: “I guess it doesn’t matter what a person’s name is as long as he behaves himself,” said Marilla, feeling herself called upon to inculcate a good and useful moral.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇只要一個人行為端正,叫乜嘢名字都冇關係,」瑪麗拉講,覺得自己有責任灌輸一條有益嘅好道理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看只要一個人行為端正,叫什麼名字都沒關係,」瑪麗拉說,覺得自己有責任灌輸一條有益的好道理。

passages.original: “Well, I don’t know.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不知道。」

passages.original: Anne looked thoughtful.
passages.vernacular: 安妮若有所思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮若有所思。

passages.original: “I read in a book once that a rose by any other name would smell as sweet, but I’ve never been able to believe it.
passages.vernacular: 「我喺一本書裡讀到過,玫瑰換個名字,聞起嚟都一樣香,不過我一直冇法相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在一本書裡讀到過,玫瑰換個名字,聞起來也一樣香,可是我一直沒法相信。

passages.original: I don’t believe a rose would be as nice if it was called a thistle or a skunk cabbage.
passages.vernacular: 我不相信玫瑰要係叫薊或者臭菘,仲會一樣美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不相信玫瑰要是叫薊或者臭菘,還會一樣美。

passages.original: I suppose my father could have been a good man even if he had been called Jedediah; but I’m sure it would have been a cross.
passages.vernacular: 我想我父親即使叫傑迪代亞,都可能係個好人;但我敢肯定嗰個係個十字架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我父親即使叫傑迪代亞,也可能是個好人;但我敢肯定那是個十字架。

passages.original: Well, my mother was a teacher in the High School, too, but when she married father she gave up teaching, of course.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我母親都係中學嘅老師,不過當然,佢嫁畀父親後就不教書喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我母親也是中學的老師,不過當然,她嫁給父親後就不教書了。

passages.original: A husband was enough responsibility.
passages.vernacular: 丈夫就係夠重嘅責任喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 丈夫就是夠重的責任了。

passages.original: Mrs. Thomas said that they were a pair of babies and as poor as church mice.
passages.vernacular: 托馬斯太太講佢哋係一對傻細路,窮得像教堂裡嘅老鼠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 托馬斯太太說他們是一對傻孩子,窮得像教堂裡的老鼠。

passages.original: They went to live in a weeny-teeny little yellow house in Bolingbroke.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋搬到博林布羅克一座小小嘅黃色房子裡住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們搬到博林布羅克一座小小的黃色房子裡住。

passages.original: I’ve never seen that house, but I’ve imagined it thousands of times.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過嗰座房子,不過我想像過佢成千上萬次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過那座房子,可是我想像過它成千上萬次。

passages.original: I think it must have had honeysuckle over the parlor window and lilacs in the front yard and lilies of the valley just inside the gate.
passages.vernacular: 我想客廳窗戶上一定爬住忍冬,前院有丁香,大門裡面有鈴蘭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想客廳窗戶上一定爬著忍冬,前院有丁香,大門裡面有鈴蘭。

passages.original: Yes, and muslin curtains in all the windows.
passages.vernacular: 對,而且所有窗戶上都掛住細棉布窗簾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,而且所有窗戶上都掛著細棉布窗簾。

passages.original: Muslin curtains give a house such an air.
passages.vernacular: 細棉布窗簾畀房子帶嚟一種氣派。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 細棉布窗簾給房子帶來一種氣派。

passages.original: I was born in that house.
passages.vernacular: 我就出生喺嗰座房子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就出生在那座房子裡。

passages.original: Mrs. Thomas said I was the homeliest baby she ever saw, I was so scrawny and tiny and nothing but eyes, but that mother thought I was perfectly beautiful.
passages.vernacular: 托馬斯太太講我係佢見過嘅最難睇嘅嬰兒,又瘦又小,只剩下一雙眼睛,不過母親覺得我完美無瑕地漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 托馬斯太太說我是她見過的最難看的嬰兒,又瘦又小,只剩下一雙眼睛,可是母親覺得我完美無瑕地漂亮。

passages.original: I should think a mother would be a better judge than a poor woman who came in to scrub, wouldn’t you?
passages.vernacular: 我想母親應該比一個嚟打掃嘅窮女人更有眼光,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想母親應該比一個來打掃的窮女人更有眼光,您說呢?

passages.original: I’m glad she was satisfied with me anyhow; I would feel so sad if I thought I was a disappointment to her--because she didn’t live very long after that, you see.
passages.vernacular: 無論如何我好高興佢對我滿意;如果我認為我讓佢失望喇,我會好難過——因為您瞧,喺嗰之後佢冇活多久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何我很高興她對我滿意;如果我認為我讓她失望了,我會很難過——因為您瞧,在那之後她沒活多久。

passages.original: She died of fever when I was just three months old.
passages.vernacular: 我剛三個月大嘅時候,佢就死於發燒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我剛三個月大的時候,她就死於發燒。

passages.original: I do wish she’d lived long enough for me to remember calling her mother.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望佢活得足夠長,讓我能記得叫佢媽媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望她活得足夠長,讓我能記得叫她媽媽。

passages.original: I think it would be so sweet to say ‘mother,’ don’t you?
passages.vernacular: 我覺得講『媽媽』一定好甜蜜,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得說『媽媽』一定很甜蜜,您說呢?

passages.original: And father died four days afterwards from fever too.
passages.vernacular: 四天後父親都死於發燒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四天後父親也死於發燒。

passages.original: That left me an orphan and folks were at their wits’ end, so Mrs. Thomas said, what to do with me.
passages.vernacular: 呢就留下我一個孤兒,大家唔知道攞我點算,托馬斯太太係咁講嘅,簡直無計可施。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就留下我一個孤兒,大家不知道拿我怎麼辦,托馬斯太太是這麼說的,簡直無計可施。

passages.original: You see, nobody wanted me even then.
passages.vernacular: 您瞧,即使嗰時都冇人要我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您瞧,即使那時也沒人要我。

passages.original: It seems to be my fate.
passages.vernacular: 呢似乎係我嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這似乎是我的命運。

passages.original: Father and mother had both come from places far away and it was well known they hadn’t any relatives living.
passages.vernacular: 父親同母親都來自好遠嘅地方,眾所周知,佢哋冇活住嘅親戚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 父親和母親都來自很遠的地方,眾所周知,他們沒有活著的親戚。

passages.original: Finally Mrs. Thomas said she’d take me, though she was poor and had a drunken husband.
passages.vernacular: 最後托馬斯太太講佢嚟收留我,儘管佢好窮,丈夫又係個酒鬼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後托馬斯太太說她來收留我,儘管她很窮,丈夫又是個酒鬼。

passages.original: She brought me up by hand.
passages.vernacular: 佢把我一手帶大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把我一手帶大。

passages.original: Do you know if there is anything in being brought up by hand that ought to make people who are brought up that way better than other people?
passages.vernacular: 您知道被一手帶大係唔係有乜嘢嘢,應該讓咁樣被帶大嘅人比別人更好?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道被一手帶大是不是有什麼東西,應該讓這樣被帶大的人比別人更好?

passages.original: Because whenever I was naughty Mrs. Thomas would ask me how I could be such a bad girl when she had brought me up by hand--reproachful-like.
passages.vernacular: 因為每當我淘氣嘅時候,托馬斯太太就會責怪地問我,佢把我一手帶大,我點能咁壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為每當我淘氣的時候,托馬斯太太就會責怪地問我,她把我一手帶大,我怎麼能這麼壞。

passages.original: “Mr. and Mrs. Thomas moved away from Bolingbroke to Marysville, and I lived with them until I was eight years old.
passages.vernacular: 「托馬斯夫婦從博林布羅克搬到咗馬里斯維爾,我同佢哋一起生活到八歲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「托馬斯夫婦從博林布羅克搬到了馬里斯維爾,我和他們一起生活到八歲。

passages.original: I helped look after the Thomas children--there were four of them younger than me--and I can tell you they took a lot of looking after.
passages.vernacular: 我幫住照睇托馬斯家嘅細路——有四個比我小嘅——我告訴您,佢哋需要好多照睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我幫著照看托馬斯家的孩子——有四個比我小的——我告訴您,他們需要很多照看。

passages.original: Then Mr. Thomas was killed falling under a train and his mother offered to take Mrs. Thomas and the children, but she didn’t want me.
passages.vernacular: 後來托馬斯先生被火車軋死喇,佢母親提出要接托馬斯太太同細路哋,但唔好我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後來托馬斯先生被火車軋死了,他母親提出要接托馬斯太太和孩子們,但不要我。

passages.original: Mrs. Thomas was at her wits’ end, so she said, what to do with me.
passages.vernacular: 托馬斯太太對點安置我,簡直唔知所措,佢係咁講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 托馬斯太太對怎麼安置我,簡直不知所措,她是這麼說的。

passages.original: Then Mrs. Hammond from up the river came down and said she’d take me, seeing I was handy with children, and I went up the river to live with her in a little clearing among the stumps.
passages.vernacular: 然後河上游嘅哈蒙德太太下嚟喇,講佢睇我對細路好喺行,就收留我,我就沿河而上去跟佢生活,住喺樹樁間一小塊開闢嘅空地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後河上游的哈蒙德太太下來了,說她看我對孩子很在行,就收留我,我就沿河而上去跟她生活,住在樹樁間一小塊開闢的空地上。

passages.original: It was a very lonesome place.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個好孤寂嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個非常孤寂的地方。

passages.original: I’m sure I could never have lived there if I hadn’t had an imagination.
passages.vernacular: 我敢肯定,要係我冇想像力,我絕對唔可能喺嗰兒生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢肯定,要是我沒有想像力,我絕對不可能在那兒生活。

passages.original: Mr. Hammond worked a little sawmill up there, and Mrs. Hammond had eight children.
passages.vernacular: 哈蒙德先生喺嗰度經營一家小鋸木廠,哈蒙德太太有八個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈蒙德先生在那裡經營一家小鋸木廠,哈蒙德太太有八個孩子。

passages.original: She had twins three times.
passages.vernacular: 佢生過三次雙胞胎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她生過三次雙胞胎。

passages.original: I like babies in moderation, but twins three times in succession is too much.
passages.vernacular: 我適度地鍾意嬰兒,但接連三次雙胞胎就太多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我適度地喜歡嬰兒,但接連三次雙胞胎就太多了。

passages.original: I told Mrs. Hammond so firmly, when the last pair came.
passages.vernacular: 最後一對雙胞胎出生時,我堅決地咁對哈蒙德太太講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後一對雙胞胎出生時,我堅決地這麼對哈蒙德太太說了。

passages.original: I used to get so dreadfully tired carrying them about.
passages.vernacular: 我抱住佢哋到處轉,累得要命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我抱著他們到處轉,累得要命。

passages.original: “I lived up river with Mrs. Hammond over two years, and then Mr. Hammond died and Mrs. Hammond broke up housekeeping.
passages.vernacular: 「我同哈蒙德太太喺河上游住咗兩年多,然後哈蒙德先生去世喇,哈蒙德太太都唔再持家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我和哈蒙德太太在河上游住了兩年多,然後哈蒙德先生去世了,哈蒙德太太也不再持家了。

passages.original: She divided her children among her relatives and went to the States.
passages.vernacular: 佢把細路哋分畀親戚,自己去咗美國。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把孩子們分給親戚,自己去了美國。

passages.original: I had to go to the asylum at Hopeton, because nobody would take me.
passages.vernacular: 我只好去霍普頓嘅孤兒院,因為冇人肯收留我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只好去霍普頓的孤兒院,因為沒人肯收留我。

passages.original: They didn’t want me at the asylum, either; they said they were overcrowded as it was.
passages.vernacular: 孤兒院都唔想要我;佢哋講已經夠擠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孤兒院也不想要我;他們說已經夠擠了。

passages.original: But they had to take me and I was there four months until Mrs. Spencer came.”
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋定係唔得不收下我,我喺嗰兒待咗四個月,直到斯潘塞太太嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們還是不得不收下我,我在那兒待了四個月,直到斯潘塞太太來。」

passages.original: Anne finished up with another sigh, of relief this time.
passages.vernacular: 安妮又嘆咗一口氣結束喇,呢次係鬆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮又嘆了一口氣結束了,這次是鬆了口氣。

passages.original: Evidently she did not like talking about her experiences in a world that had not wanted her.
passages.vernacular: 顯然佢不鍾意談論自己喺一個唔好佢嘅世界裡嘅經歷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 顯然她不喜歡談論自己在一個不要她的世界裡的經歷。

passages.original: “Did you ever go to school?” demanded Marilla, turning the sorrel mare down the shore road.
passages.vernacular: 「你上過學嗎?」瑪麗拉問,一邊把栗色馬拐上海岸路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你上過學嗎?」瑪麗拉問,一邊把栗色馬拐上海岸路。

passages.original: “Not a great deal.
passages.vernacular: 「不太多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不太多。

passages.original: I went a little the last year I stayed with Mrs. Thomas.
passages.vernacular: 我喺托馬斯太太家嘅最後一年上過啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在托馬斯太太家的最後一年上過一點。

passages.original: When I went up river we were so far from a school that I couldn’t walk it in winter and there was vacation in summer, so I could only go in the spring and fall.
passages.vernacular: 搬到河上游後,我哋離學校太遠,冬天走不喇,夏天又放假,所以我只能春天同秋天去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 搬到河上游後,我們離學校太遠,冬天走不了,夏天又放假,所以我只能春天和秋天去。

passages.original: But of course I went while I was at the asylum.
passages.vernacular: 不過當然我喺孤兒院時上過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過當然我在孤兒院時上過。

passages.original: I can read pretty well and I know ever so many pieces of poetry off by heart--‘The Battle of Hohenlinden’ and ‘Edinburgh after Flodden,’ and ‘Bingen on the Rhine,’ and lots of the ‘Lady of the Lake’ and most of ‘The Seasons,’ by James Thompson.
passages.vernacular: 我讀得相當好,仲能背誦好多詩——《霍恩林登之戰》、《弗洛登之後嘅愛丁堡》、《萊茵河畔嘅賓根》,仲有許多《湖上夫人》,以及詹姆斯·湯姆森嘅大部分《四季》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讀得相當好,還能背誦好多詩——《霍恩林登之戰》、《弗洛登之後的愛丁堡》、《萊茵河畔的賓根》,還有許多《湖上夫人》,以及詹姆斯·湯姆森的大部分《四季》。

passages.original: Don’t you just love poetry that gives you a crinkly feeling up and down your back?
passages.vernacular: 您不鍾意嗰種讓你脊背上下起雞皮疙瘩嘅詩嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不喜歡那種讓你脊背上下起雞皮疙瘩的詩嗎?

passages.original: There is a piece in the Fifth Reader--‘The Downfall of Poland’--that is just full of thrills.
passages.vernacular: 第五讀本裡有一篇——《波蘭嘅覆亡》——簡直充滿咗震顫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第五讀本裡有一篇——《波蘭的覆亡》——簡直充滿了震顫。

passages.original: Of course, I wasn’t in the Fifth Reader--I was only in the Fourth--but the big girls used to lend me theirs to read.”
passages.vernacular: 當然,我唔係讀第五讀本嘅——我只讀第四讀本——但大啲嘅女孩常借佢哋嘅畀我睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,我不是讀第五讀本的——我只讀第四讀本——但大一點的女孩常借她們的給我看。」

passages.original: “Were those women--Mrs. Thomas and Mrs. Hammond--good to you?” asked Marilla, looking at Anne out of the corner of her eye.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰啲女人——托馬斯太太同哈蒙德太太——對你好嗎?」瑪麗拉用眼角餘光睇住安妮問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那些女人——托馬斯太太和哈蒙德太太——對你好嗎?」瑪麗拉用眼角餘光看著安妮問。

passages.original: “O-o-o-h,” faltered Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦——哦——哦,」安妮支吾住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦——哦——哦,」安妮支吾著。

passages.original: Her sensitive little face suddenly flushed scarlet and embarrassment sat on her brow.
passages.vernacular: 佢敏感嘅小臉突然漲得通紅,窘迫浮而家佢嘅眉間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她敏感的小臉突然漲得通紅,窘迫浮現在她的眉間。

passages.original: “Oh, they meant to be--I know they meant to be just as good and kind as possible.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢哋想要對我好——我知道佢哋想要盡可能地善良友好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,她們想要對我好——我知道她們想要盡可能地善良友好。

passages.original: And when people mean to be good to you, you don’t mind very much when they’re not quite--always.
passages.vernacular: 而且當人哋想要對你好時,即使佢哋唔係——總是——做得到,你都唔會太介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且當人們想要對你好時,即使她們不是——總是——做得到,你也不會太介意。

passages.original: They had a good deal to worry them, you know.
passages.vernacular: 您知道,佢哋有好多煩心事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道,她們有很多煩心事。

passages.original: It’s very trying to have a drunken husband, you see; and it must be very trying to have twins three times in succession, don’t you think?
passages.vernacular: 有個酒鬼丈夫係好難受嘅;而接連三次生雙胞胎一定都好難受,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有個酒鬼丈夫是非常難受的;而接連三次生雙胞胎一定也很難受,您說呢?

passages.original: But I feel sure they meant to be good to me.”
passages.vernacular: 但我肯定佢哋係想對我好嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我肯定她們是想對我好的。」

passages.original: Marilla asked no more questions.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉冇再問乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉沒有再問什麼。

passages.original: Anne gave herself up to a silent rapture over the shore road and Marilla guided the sorrel abstractedly while she pondered deeply.
passages.vernacular: 安妮沉浸喺對海岸路嘅無聲狂喜中,瑪麗拉心不喺焉地駕馭住栗色馬,同時喺深深地思索。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮沉浸在對海岸路的無聲狂喜中,瑪麗拉心不在焉地駕馭著栗色馬,同時在深深地思索。

passages.original: Pity was suddenly stirring in her heart for the child.
passages.vernacular: 憐憫之情突然喺佢心中湧動,係對呢細路嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憐憫之情突然在她心中湧動,是對這孩子的。

passages.original: What a starved, unloved life she had had--a life of drudgery and poverty and neglect; for Marilla was shrewd enough to read between the lines of Anne’s history and divine the truth.
passages.vernacular: 佢過嘅係點樣一種缺衣少食、無人疼愛嘅生活啊——一種苦役、貧窮同被忽視嘅生活;因為瑪麗拉足夠精明,能從安妮嘅敘述字裡行間睇出真相。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她過的是怎樣一種缺衣少食、無人疼愛的生活啊——一種苦役、貧窮和被忽視的生活;因為瑪麗拉足夠精明,能從安妮的敘述字裡行間看出真相。

passages.original: No wonder she had been so delighted at the prospect of a real home.
passages.vernacular: 難怪佢對有一個真正嘅家嘅前景咁高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難怪她對有一個真正的家的前景那麼高興。

passages.original: It was a pity she had to be sent back.
passages.vernacular: 真可惜佢得被送回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真可惜她得被送回去。

passages.original: What if she, Marilla, should indulge Matthew’s unaccountable whim and let her stay?
passages.vernacular: 如果佢,瑪麗拉,縱容馬修嗰莫名其妙嘅念頭,讓佢留下呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她,瑪麗拉,縱容馬修那莫名其妙的念頭,讓她留下呢?

passages.original: He was set on it; and the child seemed a nice, teachable little thing.
passages.vernacular: 佢執意如此;而呢細路睇上去都係個挺好嘅、可教嘅小嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他執意如此;而這孩子看上去也是個挺好的、可教的小東西。

passages.original: “She’s got too much to say,” thought Marilla, “but she might be trained out of that.
passages.vernacular: 「佢話太多喇,」瑪麗拉想,「不過呢個係可以調教掉嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她話太多了,」瑪麗拉想,「不過這是可以調教掉的。

passages.original: And there’s nothing rude or slangy in what she does say.
passages.vernacular: 而且佢講嘅話裡冇粗魯或粗俗嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且她說的話裡沒有粗魯或粗俗的東西。

passages.original: She’s ladylike.
passages.vernacular: 佢像個淑女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她像個淑女。

passages.original: It’s likely her people were nice folks.”
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅家人好可能係好人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的家人很可能是好人。」

passages.original: The shore road was “woodsy and wild and lonesome.”
passages.vernacular: 海岸路「林木蔥鬱、荒野、孤寂」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海岸路「林木蔥鬱、荒野、孤寂」。

passages.original: On the right hand, scrub firs, their spirits quite unbroken by long years of tussle with the gulf winds, grew thickly.
passages.vernacular: 右邊,矮小嘅冷杉,精神絲毫冇被多年同海灣風嘅搏鬥所挫敗,長得密密麻麻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 右邊,矮小的冷杉,精神絲毫沒有被多年與海灣風的搏鬥所挫敗,長得密密麻麻。

passages.original: On the left were the steep red sandstone cliffs, so near the track in places that a mare of less steadiness than the sorrel might have tried the nerves of the people behind her.
passages.vernacular: 左邊係陡峭嘅紅色砂岩懸崖,有些地方離車道咁近,要係換咗一匹冇栗色馬咁穩當嘅母馬,可能會考驗後面人嘅神經。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 左邊是陡峭的紅色砂岩懸崖,有些地方離車道那麼近,要是換了一匹沒有栗色馬那麼穩當的母馬,可能會考驗後面人的神經。

passages.original: Down at the base of the cliffs were heaps of surf-worn rocks or little sandy coves inlaid with pebbles as with ocean jewels; beyond lay the sea, shimmering and blue, and over it soared the gulls, their pinions flashing silvery in the sunlight.
passages.vernacular: 懸崖腳下係一堆堆被浪花磨蝕嘅岩石,或係鑲嵌住鵝卵石像海洋寶石一樣嘅小沙灣;遠處係閃爍住嘅蔚藍色大海,海鷗喺上空翱翔,翅膀喺陽光下閃住銀光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懸崖腳下是一堆堆被浪花磨蝕的岩石,或是鑲嵌著鵝卵石像海洋寶石一樣的小沙灣;遠處是閃爍著的蔚藍色大海,海鷗在上空翱翔,翅膀在陽光下閃著銀光。

passages.original: “Isn’t the sea wonderful?” said Anne, rousing from a long, wide-eyed silence.
passages.vernacular: 「大海唔係好奇妙嗎?」安妮從長長嘅、睜大眼睛嘅沉默中醒過來講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「大海不是很奇妙嗎?」安妮從長長的、睜大眼睛的沉默中醒過來說。

passages.original: “Once, when I lived in Marysville, Mr. Thomas hired an express wagon and took us all to spend the day at the shore ten miles away.
passages.vernacular: 「有一次,我住喺馬里斯維爾嘅時候,托馬斯先生租咗一輛快運馬車,帶我哋大家去十英里外嘅海邊度過一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一次,我住在馬里斯維爾的時候,托馬斯先生租了一輛快運馬車,帶我們大家去十英里外的海邊度過一天。

passages.original: I enjoyed every moment of that day, even if I had to look after the children all the time.
passages.vernacular: 嗰一天嘅每一刻我都享受,即使我一直得照睇細路哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那一天的每一刻我都享受,即使我一直得照看孩子們。

passages.original: I lived it over in happy dreams for years.
passages.vernacular: 多年嚟,我喺快樂嘅夢裡重溫咗嗰一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多年來,我在快樂的夢裡重溫了那一天。

passages.original: But this shore is nicer than the Marysville shore.
passages.vernacular: 但呢片海岸比馬里斯維爾嘅海岸更美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這片海岸比馬里斯維爾的海岸更美。

passages.original: Aren’t those gulls splendid?
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲海鷗唔係好壯觀嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些海鷗不是很壯觀嗎?

passages.original: Would you like to be a gull?
passages.vernacular: 您想做海鷗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您想做海鷗嗎?

passages.original: I think I would--that is, if I couldn’t be a human girl.
passages.vernacular: 我想我會——都就係講,如果我唔能夠做個人類女孩嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我會——也就是說,如果我不能做個人類女孩的話。

passages.original: Don’t you think it would be nice to wake up at sunrise and swoop down over the water and away out over that lovely blue all day; and then at night to fly back to one’s nest?
passages.vernacular: 您不覺得日出時醒嚟,俯衝下水面,整天飛翔喺嗰可愛嘅藍色之上,然後晚上飛回自己嘅巢,多美好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不覺得日出時醒來,俯衝下水面,整天飛翔在那可愛的藍色之上,然後晚上飛回自己的巢,多美好嗎?

passages.original: Oh, I can just imagine myself doing it.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我能想像自己咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我能想像自己這樣做。

passages.original: What big house is that just ahead, please?”
passages.vernacular: 請問前面嗰座大房子係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請問前面那座大房子是什麼?」

passages.original: “That’s the White Sands Hotel.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係白沙旅館。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是白沙旅館。

passages.original: Mr. Kirke runs it, but the season hasn’t begun yet.
passages.vernacular: 柯克先生經營嘅,不過旺季仲冇開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 柯克先生經營的,不過旺季還沒開始。

passages.original: There are heaps of Americans come there for the summer.
passages.vernacular: 夏天有好多美國人嚟嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏天有很多美國人來那兒。

passages.original: They think this shore is just about right.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋覺得呢片海岸正合適。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們覺得這片海岸正合適。」

passages.original: “I was afraid it might be Mrs. Spencer’s place,” said Anne mournfully.
passages.vernacular: 「我怕嗰可能係斯潘塞太太嘅家,」安妮悲傷地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我怕那可能是斯潘塞太太的家,」安妮悲傷地說。

passages.original: “I don’t want to get there.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔想到嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不想到那兒。

passages.original: Somehow, it will seem like the end of everything.”
passages.vernacular: 唔知怎嘅,嗰好像會係一切嘅終結。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知怎的,那好像會是一切的終結。」

chapters.title: Ch. VI Marilla Makes Up Her Mind 第六章:瑪麗拉拿定主意

passages.original: CH GET there they did, however, in due season.
passages.vernacular: 不過,到咗該到嘅時候,佢哋定係到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,到了該到的時候,他們還是到了。

passages.original: Mrs. Spencer lived in a big yellow house at White Sands Cove, and she came to the door with surprise and welcome mingled on her benevolent face.
passages.vernacular: 斯潘塞太太住喺白沙灣嘅一座大黃房子裡,佢嚟到門口,慈祥嘅臉上驚訝同歡迎交織喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯潘塞太太住在白沙灣的一座大黃房子裡,她來到門口,慈祥的臉上驚訝和歡迎交織在一起。

passages.original: “Dear, dear,” she exclaimed, “you’re the last folks I was looking for today, but I’m real glad to see you.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀呀,」佢驚呼道,「你哋係我今日最冇想到會嚟嘅人,不過我真高興見到你哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀呀,」她驚呼道,「你們是我今天最沒想到會來的人,不過我真高興見到你們。

passages.original: You’ll put your horse in?
passages.vernacular: 你哋把馬安頓好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們把馬安頓好嗎?

passages.original: And how are you, Anne?”
passages.vernacular: 你好嗎,安妮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你好嗎,安妮?」

passages.original: “I’m as well as can be expected, thank you,” said Anne smilelessly.
passages.vernacular: 「我仲算好,謝謝您,」安妮毫無笑意地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我還算好,謝謝您,」安妮毫無笑意地說。

passages.original: A blight seemed to have descended on her.
passages.vernacular: 一種枯萎似乎降臨喺佢身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一種枯萎似乎降臨在她身上。

passages.original: “I suppose we’ll stay a little while to rest the mare,” said Marilla, “but I promised Matthew I’d be home early.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我哋得待一會兒讓母馬歇歇,」瑪麗拉講,「不過我答應馬修要早點回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我們得待一會兒讓母馬歇歇,」瑪麗拉說,「不過我答應馬修要早點回去。

passages.original: The fact is, Mrs. Spencer, there’s been a queer mistake somewhere, and I’ve come over to see where it is.
passages.vernacular: 事情係咁樣嘅,斯潘塞太太,邊度出咗個古怪嘅差錯,我係嚟睇睇問題出喺邊兒嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事情是這樣的,斯潘塞太太,哪裡出了個古怪的差錯,我是來看看問題出在哪兒的。

passages.original: We sent word, Matthew and I, for you to bring us a boy from the asylum.
passages.vernacular: 馬修同我托人捎話,讓你從孤兒院畀我哋帶一個男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修和我托人捎話,讓你從孤兒院給我們帶一個男孩。

passages.original: We told your brother Robert to tell you we wanted a boy ten or eleven years old.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋讓你哥哥羅伯特告訴你,我哋要一個十歲或十一歲嘅男孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們讓你哥哥羅伯特告訴你,我們要一個十歲或十一歲的男孩。」

passages.original: “Marilla Cuthbert, you don’t say so!” said Mrs. Spencer in distress.
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉·卡思伯特,你唔係講真嘅吧!」斯潘塞太太苦惱地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉·卡思伯特,你不是說真的吧!」斯潘塞太太苦惱地說。

passages.original: “Why, Robert sent word down by his daughter Nancy and she said you wanted a girl--didn’t she, Flora Jane?” appealing to her daughter who had come out to the steps.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,羅伯特係讓佢女兒南希捎嘅話,佢講你哋要一個女孩——佢係咁講嘅吧,弗洛拉·簡?」佢求助於走到臺階上嘅女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,羅伯特是讓他女兒南希捎的話,她說你們要一個女孩——她是這麼說的吧,弗洛拉·簡?」她求助於走到臺階上的女兒。

passages.original: “She certainly did, Miss Cuthbert,” corroborated Flora Jane earnestly.
passages.vernacular: 「佢確實係咁講嘅,卡思伯特小姐,」弗洛拉·簡認真地證實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她確實是這麼說的,卡思伯特小姐,」弗洛拉·簡認真地證實。

passages.original: “I’m dreadful sorry,” said Mrs. Spencer.
passages.vernacular: 「我好抱歉,」斯潘塞太太講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我非常抱歉,」斯潘塞太太說。

passages.original: “It’s too bad; but it certainly wasn’t my fault, you see, Miss Cuthbert.
passages.vernacular: 「太糟糕喇;但呢確實唔係我嘅過錯,您瞧,卡思伯特小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太糟糕了;但這確實不是我的過錯,您瞧,卡思伯特小姐。

passages.original: I did the best I could and I thought I was following your instructions.
passages.vernacular: 我盡咗最大努力,我以為係遵照咗你哋嘅指示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我盡了最大努力,我以為是遵照了你們的指示。

passages.original: Nancy is a terrible flighty thing.
passages.vernacular: 南希係個極其輕浮嘅丫頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希是個極其輕浮的丫頭。

passages.original: I’ve often had to scold her well for her heedlessness.”
passages.vernacular: 我常常得好好責罵佢嘅粗心大意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我常常得好好責罵她的粗心大意。」

passages.original: “It was our own fault,” said Marilla resignedly.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我哋自己嘅錯,」瑪麗拉認命地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我們自己的錯,」瑪麗拉認命地說。

passages.original: “We should have come to you ourselves and not left an important message to be passed along by word of mouth in that fashion.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋應該親自去找你,而不該把咁重要嘅口信,就嗰樣靠口傳話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們應該親自去找你,而不該把這麼重要的口信,就那樣靠口傳話。

passages.original: Anyhow, the mistake has been made and the only thing to do now is to set it right.
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,差錯已經出喇,而家唯一要做嘅就係把佢糾正過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,差錯已經出了,現在唯一要做的就是把它糾正過來。

passages.original: Can we send the child back to the asylum?
passages.vernacular: 我哋能把細路送回孤兒院嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們能把孩子送回孤兒院嗎?

passages.original: I suppose they’ll take her back, won’t they?”
passages.vernacular: 我想佢哋會收回佢嘅,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他們會收回她的,是不是?」

passages.original: “I suppose so,” said Mrs. Spencer thoughtfully, “but I don’t think it will be necessary to send her back.
passages.vernacular: 「我想係嘅,」斯潘塞太太若有所思地講,「不過我覺得冇必要送佢回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是的,」斯潘塞太太若有所思地說,「不過我覺得沒必要送她回去。

passages.original: Mrs. Peter Blewett was up here yesterday, and she was saying to me how much she wished she’d sent by me for a little girl to help her.
passages.vernacular: 彼得·布萊維特太太尋日嚟過呢兒,佢跟我講,佢幾咁希望托我畀佢領一個小女孩嚟幫忙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得·布萊維特太太昨天來過這兒,她跟我說,她多麼希望托我給她領一個小女孩來幫忙。

passages.original: Mrs. Peter has a large family, you know, and she finds it hard to get help.
passages.vernacular: 你知道,彼得太太家細路多,佢覺得找幫手好難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,彼得太太家孩子多,她覺得找幫手很難。

passages.original: Anne will be the very girl for her.
passages.vernacular: 安妮正好係佢要嘅嗰種女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮正好是她要的那種女孩。

passages.original: I call it positively providential.”
passages.vernacular: 我講呢簡直係天意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說這簡直是天意。」

passages.original: Marilla did not look as if she thought Providence had much to do with the matter.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉睇上去並不覺得天意跟呢件事有多大關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉看上去並不覺得天意跟這件事有多大關係。

passages.original: Here was an unexpectedly good chance to get this unwelcome orphan off her hands, and she did not even feel grateful for it.
passages.vernacular: 眼前有個意外嘅好機會,可以把呢個不受歡迎嘅孤兒從佢手上甩掉,佢卻連啲感激都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 眼前有個意外的好機會,可以把這個不受歡迎的孤兒從她手上甩掉,她卻連一點感激都沒有。

passages.original: She knew Mrs. Peter Blewett only by sight as a small, shrewish-faced woman without an ounce of superfluous flesh on her bones.
passages.vernacular: 佢只係遠遠見過彼得·布萊維特太太,知道佢係個小個子,臉上帶住潑辣相,身上冇一盎司多餘嘅肉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她只是遠遠見過彼得·布萊維特太太,知道她是個小個子,臉上帶著潑辣相,身上沒有一盎司多餘的肉。

passages.original: But she had heard of her.
passages.vernacular: 但佢聽講過佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她聽說過她。

passages.original: “A terrible worker and driver,” Mrs. Peter was said to be; and discharged servant girls told fearsome tales of her temper and stinginess, and her family of pert, quarrelsome children.
passages.vernacular: 據講彼得太太係個「可怕嘅幹活能手同監工」;被辭退嘅女僕哋講起佢嘅壞脾氣同吝嗇,講起佢嗰一家子冇規矩、愛吵架嘅細路,講得令人害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據說彼得太太是個「可怕的幹活能手和監工」;被辭退的女僕們講起她的壞脾氣和吝嗇,講起她那一家子沒規矩、愛吵架的孩子,說得令人害怕。

passages.original: Marilla felt a qualm of conscience at the thought of handing Anne over to her tender mercies.
passages.vernacular: 一想到要把安妮交到佢嘅「仁慈」手裡,瑪麗拉感到良心不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一想到要把安妮交到她的「仁慈」手裡,瑪麗拉感到良心不安。

passages.original: “Well, I’ll go in and we’ll talk the matter over,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,我進去,我哋商量商量呢件事,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,我進去,我們商量商量這件事,」她說。

passages.original: “And if there isn’t Mrs. Peter coming up the lane this blessed minute!” exclaimed Mrs. Spencer, bustling her guests through the hall into the parlor, where a deadly chill struck on them as if the air had been strained so long through dark green, closely drawn blinds that it had lost every particle of warmth it had ever possessed.
passages.vernacular: 「瞧,彼得太太正好呢會兒上咗巷子!」斯潘塞太太叫道,一邊忙住把客人領過門廳進入客廳,一股死一般嘅寒氣向佢哋襲嚟,好像空氣被濾過太久嗰深綠色、緊拉嘅百葉窗,已經失去咗佢曾有過嘅每一絲暖意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瞧,彼得太太正好這會兒上了巷子!」斯潘塞太太叫道,一邊忙著把客人領過門廳進入客廳,一股死一般的寒氣向他們襲來,好像空氣被濾過太久那深綠色、緊拉的百葉窗,已經失去了它曾有過的每一絲暖意。

passages.original: “That is real lucky, for we can settle the matter right away.
passages.vernacular: 「真係太巧喇,咁樣我哋可以即刻把事情談妥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真是太巧了,這樣我們可以馬上把事情談妥。

passages.original: Take the armchair, Miss Cuthbert.
passages.vernacular: 坐扶手椅吧,卡思伯特小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 坐扶手椅吧,卡思伯特小姐。

passages.original: Anne, you sit here on the ottoman and don’t wriggle.
passages.vernacular: 安妮,你坐呢個腳凳,別扭嚟扭去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮,你坐這個腳凳,別扭來扭去。

passages.original: Let me take your hats.
passages.vernacular: 我嚟攞你哋嘅帽子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我來拿你們的帽子。

passages.original: Flora Jane, go out and put the kettle on.
passages.vernacular: 弗洛拉·簡,去把水壺燒上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗洛拉·簡,去把水壺燒上。

passages.original: Good afternoon, Mrs. Blewett.
passages.vernacular: 下午好,布萊維特太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下午好,布萊維特太太。

passages.original: We were just saying how fortunate it was you happened along.
passages.vernacular: 我哋頭先仲喺講,你嚟得幾咁湊巧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們剛才還在說,你來得多麼湊巧。

passages.original: Let me introduce you two ladies.
passages.vernacular: 讓我畀你哋兩位介紹一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我給你們兩位介紹一下。

passages.original: Mrs. Blewett, Miss Cuthbert.
passages.vernacular: 布萊維特太太,卡思伯特小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布萊維特太太,卡思伯特小姐。

passages.original: Please excuse me for just a moment.
passages.vernacular: 請原諒我離開一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒我離開一會兒。

passages.original: I forgot to tell Flora Jane to take the buns out of the oven.”
passages.vernacular: 我忘咗叫弗洛拉·簡把圓麵包從烤箱裡攞出嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忘了叫弗洛拉·簡把圓麵包從烤箱裡拿出來。」

passages.original: Mrs. Spencer whisked away, after pulling up the blinds.
passages.vernacular: 斯潘塞太太把百葉窗拉起嚟後,一陣風似嘅走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯潘塞太太把百葉窗拉起來後,一陣風似的走了。

passages.original: Anne, sitting mutely on the ottoman, with her hands clasped tightly in her lap, stared at Mrs. Blewett as one fascinated.
passages.vernacular: 安妮默默地坐喺腳凳上,雙手緊緊握喺膝上,住咗迷似嘅盯住布萊維特太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮默默地坐在腳凳上,雙手緊緊握在膝上,著了迷似的盯著布萊維特太太。

passages.original: Was she to be given into the keeping of this sharp-faced, sharp-eyed woman?
passages.vernacular: 佢要被交到呢個臉尖眼尖嘅女人手裡嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她要被交到這個臉尖眼尖的女人手裡嗎?

passages.original: She felt a lump coming up in her throat and her eyes smarted painfully.
passages.vernacular: 佢感到喉嚨裡有個硬塊喺上湧,眼睛痛得發酸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她感到喉嚨裡有個硬塊在上湧,眼睛痛得發酸。

passages.original: She was beginning to be afraid she couldn’t keep the tears back when Mrs. Spencer returned, flushed and beaming, quite capable of taking any and every difficulty, physical, mental or spiritual, into consideration and settling it out of hand.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始怕自己忍不住眼淚時,斯潘塞太太回嚟喇,滿臉通紅,笑容滿面,完全有能力把任何困難,無論係身體上嘅、心理上嘅定係精神上嘅,都考慮進去並當場解決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她開始怕自己忍不住眼淚時,斯潘塞太太回來了,滿臉通紅,笑容滿面,完全有能力把任何困難,無論是身體上的、心理上的還是精神上的,都考慮進去並當場解決。

passages.original: “It seems there’s been a mistake about this little girl, Mrs. Blewett,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「布萊維特太太,睇來呢個小女孩嘅事出咗點差錯,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「布萊維特太太,看來這個小女孩的事出了點差錯,」她說。

passages.original: “I was under the impression that Mr. and Miss Cuthbert wanted a little girl to adopt.
passages.vernacular: 「我原以為卡思伯特先生同小姐想收養一個小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我原以為卡思伯特先生和小姐想收養一個小女孩。

passages.original: I was certainly told so.
passages.vernacular: 我確實係咁聽講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確實是這麼聽說的。

passages.original: But it seems it was a boy they wanted.
passages.vernacular: 但係睇來佢哋要嘅係個男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是看來他們要的是個男孩。

passages.original: So if you’re still of the same mind you were yesterday, I think she’ll be just the thing for you.”
passages.vernacular: 所以如果你定係尋日嘅想法,我覺得佢正合適你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以如果你還是昨天的想法,我覺得她正合適你。」

passages.original: Mrs. Blewett darted her eyes over Anne from head to foot.
passages.vernacular: 布萊維特太太嘅目光從頭到腳掃咗安妮一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布萊維特太太的目光從頭到腳掃了安妮一遍。

passages.original: “How old are you and what’s your name?” she demanded.
passages.vernacular: 「你多大喇,叫乜嘢名字?」佢質問道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你多大了,叫什麼名字?」她質問道。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley,” faltered the shrinking child, not daring to make any stipulations regarding the spelling thereof, “and I’m eleven years old.”
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,」瑟縮嘅細路吞吞吐吐地講,唔敢對拼寫提出任何條件,「我十一歲喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,」瑟縮的孩子吞吞吐吐地說,不敢對拼寫提出任何條件,「我十一歲了。」

passages.original: “Humph!
You don’t look as if there was much to you.
passages.vernacular: 你睇上去冇多少肉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看上去沒多少肉。

passages.original: But you’re wiry.
passages.vernacular: 不過你好結實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過你很結實。

passages.original: I don’t know but the wiry ones are the best after all.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道係唔係結實嘅終究係最好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道是不是結實的終究是最好的。

passages.original: Well, if I take you you’ll have to be a good girl, you know--good and smart and respectful.
passages.vernacular: 好吧,如果我領你去,你得做個好細路,你知道——乖巧、能幹、有禮貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,如果我領你去,你得做個好孩子,你知道——乖巧、能幹、有禮貌。

passages.original: I’ll expect you to earn your keep, and no mistake about that.
passages.vernacular: 我指望你掙你嘅飯錢,呢啲唔會有錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我指望你掙你的飯錢,這一點不會有錯。

passages.original: Yes, I suppose I might as well take her off your hands, Miss Cuthbert.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,我想我不妨把佢從你手上接過嚟,卡思伯特小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,我想我不妨把她從你手上接過來,卡思伯特小姐。

passages.original: The baby’s awful fractious, and I’m clean worn out attending to him.
passages.vernacular: 嬰兒特別愛鬧,我照顧佢累壞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嬰兒特別愛鬧,我照顧他累壞了。

passages.original: If you like I can take her right home now.”
passages.vernacular: 如果你願意,我而家就可以把佢帶回家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你願意,我現在就可以把她帶回家。」

passages.original: Marilla looked at Anne and softened at sight of the child’s pale face with its look of mute misery--the misery of a helpless little creature who finds itself once more caught in the trap from which it had escaped.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉睇住安妮,睇到細路蒼白嘅臉上嗰種默默悲慘嘅神情,心軟喇——嗰個係一個無助嘅小生靈發現自己再次落入曾經逃脫過嘅陷阱嘅悲慘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉看著安妮,看到孩子蒼白的臉上那種默默悲慘的神情,心軟了——那是一個無助的小生靈發現自己再次落入曾經逃脫過的陷阱的悲慘。

passages.original: Marilla felt an uncomfortable conviction that, if she denied the appeal of that look, it would haunt her to her dying day.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉有種不舒服的確信:如果佢拒絕嗰眼神嘅懇求,佢會一直纏住佢到死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉有種不舒服的確信:如果她拒絕那眼神的懇求,它會一直纏著她到死。

passages.original: Moreover, she did not fancy Mrs. Blewett.
passages.vernacular: 而且,佢不鍾意布萊維特太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,她不喜歡布萊維特太太。

passages.original: To hand a sensitive, “highstrung” child over to such a woman!
passages.vernacular: 把一個敏感、「神經緊張」嘅細路交畀咁樣一個女人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把一個敏感、「神經緊張」的孩子交給這樣一個女人!

passages.original: No, she could not take the responsibility of doing that!
passages.vernacular: 不,佢唔能夠擔呢個責任!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,她不能擔這個責任!

passages.original: “Well, I don’t know,” she said slowly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔知道,」佢慢慢地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不知道,」她慢慢地說。

passages.original: “I didn’t say that Matthew and I had absolutely decided that we wouldn’t keep her.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇講馬修同我已經完全決定不留下佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒說馬修和我已經完全決定不留下她。

passages.original: In fact, I may say that Matthew is disposed to keep her.
passages.vernacular: 事實上,我可以講馬修傾向於留下佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實上,我可以說馬修傾向於留下她。

passages.original: I just came over to find out how the mistake had occurred.
passages.vernacular: 我只係過嚟弄清差錯係點出嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是過來弄清差錯是怎麼出的。

passages.original: I think I’d better take her home again and talk it over with Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 我想我最好定係把佢帶回去,跟馬修商量商量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我最好還是把她帶回去,跟馬修商量商量。

passages.original: I feel that I oughtn’t to decide on anything without consulting him.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得不跟佢商量,我不該決定任何事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得不跟他商量,我不該決定任何事。

passages.original: If we make up our mind not to keep her we’ll bring or send her over to you tomorrow night.
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋決定不留下佢,聽日晚上就把佢送到你嗰兒去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們決定不留下她,明天晚上就把她送到你那兒去。

passages.original: If we don’t you may know that she is going to stay with us.
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋不送,你就知道佢會同我哋住喺一起喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們不送,你就知道她會和我們住在一起了。

passages.original: Will that suit you, Mrs. Blewett?”
passages.vernacular: 咁樣合適嗎,布萊維特太太?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣合適嗎,布萊維特太太?」

passages.original: “I suppose it’ll have to,” said Mrs. Blewett ungraciously.
passages.vernacular: 「我想只能咁樣喇,」布萊維特太太不客氣地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想只能這樣了,」布萊維特太太不客氣地說。

passages.original: During Marilla’s speech a sunrise had been dawning on Anne’s face.
passages.vernacular: 喺瑪麗拉講話期間,一輪旭日喺安妮嘅臉上冉冉升起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在瑪麗拉說話期間,一輪旭日在安妮的臉上冉冉升起。

passages.original: First the look of despair faded out; then came a faint flush of hope; her eyes grew deep and bright as morning stars.
passages.vernacular: 先係絕望嘅神情褪去;然後係一抹淡淡嘅希望嘅紅暈;佢嘅眼睛變得像晨星一樣深邃明亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先是絕望的神情褪去;然後是一抹淡淡的希望的紅暈;她的眼睛變得像晨星一樣深邃明亮。

passages.original: The child was quite transfigured; and, a moment later, when Mrs. Spencer and Mrs. Blewett went out in quest of a recipe the latter had come to borrow, she sprang up and flew across the room to Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 細路整個人都煥然一新喇;一會兒後,斯潘塞太太同布萊維特太太出去找後者嚟借嘅一個食譜時,佢跳起嚟,飛奔過房間嚟到瑪麗拉身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子整個人都煥然一新了;一會兒後,斯潘塞太太和布萊維特太太出去找後者來借的一個食譜時,她跳起來,飛奔過房間來到瑪麗拉身邊。

passages.original: “Oh, Miss Cuthbert, did you really say that perhaps you would let me stay at Green Gables?” she said, in a breathless whisper, as if speaking aloud might shatter the glorious possibility.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,卡思伯特小姐,您真嘅講咗或者會讓我留喺綠色屋頂嗎?」佢氣喘吁吁地低聲問,好像大聲講出嚟就會粉碎嗰光輝嘅可能似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,卡思伯特小姐,您真的說了也許會讓我留在綠色屋頂嗎?」她氣喘吁吁地低聲問,好像大聲說出來就會粉碎那光輝的可能似的。

passages.original: “Did you really say it?
passages.vernacular: 「您真嘅講咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您真的說了嗎?

passages.original: Or did I only imagine that you did?”
passages.vernacular: 定係只係我自己想像您講喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是只是我自己想像您說了?」

passages.original: “I think you’d better learn to control that imagination of yours, Anne, if you can’t distinguish between what is real and what isn’t,” said Marilla crossly.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇你最好學會控制你嗰種想像,安妮,如果你分不清乜嘢係真嘅、乜嘢唔係嘅話,」瑪麗拉生氣地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看你最好學會控制你那種想像,安妮,如果你分不清什麼是真的、什麼不是的話,」瑪麗拉生氣地說。

passages.original: “Yes, you did hear me say just that and no more.
passages.vernacular: 「對,你確實聽我講咗咁多,冇更多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,你確實聽我說了這麼多,沒有更多了。

passages.original: It isn’t decided yet and perhaps we will conclude to let Mrs. Blewett take you after all.
passages.vernacular: 仲冇決定呢,或者我哋終究定係會讓布萊維特太太領走你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還沒決定呢,也許我們終究還是會讓布萊維特太太領走你。

passages.original: She certainly needs you much more than I do.”
passages.vernacular: 佢肯定比我更需要你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她肯定比我更需要你。」

passages.original: “I’d rather go back to the asylum than go to live with her,” said Anne passionately.
passages.vernacular: 「我寧願回孤兒院都唔好跟佢去住,」安妮激烈地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我寧願回孤兒院也不要跟她去住,」安妮激烈地說。

passages.original: “She looks exactly like a--like a gimlet.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢睇上去簡直像一個——像一把手搖鑽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她看上去簡直像一個——像一把手搖鑽。」

passages.original: Marilla smothered a smile under the conviction that Anne must be reproved for such a speech.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉把笑容憋咗回去,因為佢確信必須訓斥安妮呢番話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉把笑容憋了回去,因為她確信必須訓斥安妮這番話。

passages.original: “A little girl like you should be ashamed of talking so about a lady and a stranger,” she said severely.
passages.vernacular: 「像你咁樣嘅小女孩,咁樣議論一位女士,而且係個陌生人,應該感到羞愧,」佢嚴厲地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「像你這樣的小女孩,這樣議論一位女士,而且是個陌生人,應該感到羞愧,」她嚴厲地說。

passages.original: “Go back and sit down quietly and hold your tongue and behave as a good girl should.”
passages.vernacular: 「回去安靜地坐下,閉上嘴,做個好女孩該有嘅樣子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「回去安靜地坐下,閉上嘴,做個好女孩該有的樣子。」

passages.original: “I’ll try to do and be anything you want me, if you’ll only keep me,” said Anne, returning meekly to her ottoman.
passages.vernacular: 「只要您留下我,您要我做乜嘢、成點解樣,我都努力做到,」安妮講,溫順地回到佢嘅腳凳上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只要您留下我,您要我做什麼、成為什麼樣,我都努力做到,」安妮說,溫順地回到她的腳凳上。

passages.original: When they arrived back at Green Gables that evening Matthew met them in the lane.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上佢哋回到綠色屋頂時,馬修喺小巷裡迎接佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上他們回到綠色屋頂時,馬修在小巷裡迎接他們。

passages.original: Marilla from afar had noted him prowling along it and guessed his motive.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉遠遠就睇到佢喺嗰度溜達,猜到咗佢嘅動機。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉遠遠就看到他在那裡溜達,猜到了他的動機。

passages.original: She was prepared for the relief she read in his face when he saw that she had at least brought Anne back with her.
passages.vernacular: 當佢睇到佢至少把安妮帶回嚟喇,臉上露出咗如釋重負嘅神色,佢對此早有準備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他看到她至少把安妮帶回來了,臉上露出了如釋重負的神色,她對此早有準備。

passages.original: But she said nothing, to him, relative to the affair, until they were both out in the yard behind the barn milking the cows.
passages.vernacular: 但佢冇對佢講關於呢件事嘅任何話,直到佢哋都喺穀倉後面嘅院子裡擠牛奶時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她沒對他說關於這件事的任何話,直到他們都在穀倉後面的院子裡擠牛奶時。

passages.original: Then she briefly told him Anne’s history and the result of the interview with Mrs. Spencer.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢簡要地告訴佢安妮嘅經歷,以及同斯潘塞太太會面嘅結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她簡要地告訴他安妮的經歷,以及與斯潘塞太太會面的結果。

passages.original: “I wouldn’t give a dog I liked to that Blewett woman,” said Matthew with unusual vim.
passages.vernacular: 「我就係對我鍾意嘅狗,都唔會把佢交畀嗰個布萊維特女人,」馬修帶住少有嘅勁頭講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就是對我喜歡的狗,也不會把它交給那個布萊維特女人,」馬修帶著少有的勁頭說。

passages.original: “I don’t fancy her style myself,” admitted Marilla, “but it’s that or keeping her ourselves, Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「我自己都不鍾意佢嘅作風,」瑪麗拉承認,「但要麼係佢,要麼係我哋自己留下,馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我自己也不喜歡她的作風,」瑪麗拉承認,「但要麼是她,要麼是我們自己留下,馬修。

passages.original: And, since you seem to want her, I suppose I’m willing--or have to be.
passages.vernacular: 既然你似乎想要佢,我想我都願意——或者講唔得唔願意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然你似乎想要她,我想我也願意——或者說不得不願意。

passages.original: I’ve been thinking over the idea until I’ve got kind of used to it.
passages.vernacular: 我一直喺琢磨呢個主意,直到有點習慣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直在琢磨這個主意,直到有點習慣了。

passages.original: It seems a sort of duty.
passages.vernacular: 呢似乎係一種責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這似乎是一種責任。

passages.original: I’ve never brought up a child, especially a girl, and I dare say I’ll make a terrible mess of it.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇帶過細路,尤其係女孩,我敢講我會弄得一團糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒帶過孩子,尤其是女孩,我敢說我會弄得一團糟。

passages.original: But I’ll do my best.
passages.vernacular: 但我會盡力而為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我會盡力而為。

passages.original: So far as I’m concerned, Matthew, she may stay.”
passages.vernacular: 就我而言,馬修,佢可以留下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就我而言,馬修,她可以留下。」

passages.original: Matthew’s shy face was a glow of delight.
passages.vernacular: 馬修害羞嘅臉上洋溢住喜悅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修害羞的臉上洋溢著喜悅。

passages.original: “Well now, I reckoned you’d come to see it in that light, Marilla,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我就想到你會咁睇嘅,瑪麗拉,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我就想到你會這麼看的,瑪麗拉,」他說。

passages.original: “She’s such an interesting little thing.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係個咁有趣嘅小傢伙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是個那麼有趣的小傢伙。」

passages.original: “It’d be more to the point if you could say she was a useful little thing,” retorted Marilla, “but I’ll make it my business to see she’s trained to be that.
passages.vernacular: 「要係你能講佢係個有用嘅小傢伙,嗰就更切題喇,」瑪麗拉反駁,「不過我會負責讓佢被調教成有用嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要是你能說她是個有用的小傢伙,那就更切題了,」瑪麗拉反駁,「不過我會負責讓她被調教成有用的。

passages.original: And mind, Matthew, you’re not to go interfering with my methods.
passages.vernacular: 仲有,注意,馬修,你不許插手干涉我嘅方法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,注意,馬修,你不許插手干涉我的方法。

passages.original: Perhaps an old maid doesn’t know much about bringing up a child, but I guess she knows more than an old bachelor.
passages.vernacular: 或者一個老處女不太懂得點帶細路,但我想佢懂得比老光棍多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許一個老處女不太懂得怎麼帶孩子,但我想她懂得比老光棍多。

passages.original: So you just leave me to manage her.
passages.vernacular: 所以你就讓我嚟管佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你就讓我來管她。

passages.original: When I fail it’ll be time enough to put your oar in.”
passages.vernacular: 等我失敗喇,你再插手都嚟得及。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我失敗了,你再插手也來得及。」

passages.original: “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,瑪麗拉,你想點做就點做,」馬修安撫地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,瑪麗拉,你想怎麼做就怎麼做,」馬修安撫地說。

passages.original: “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her.
passages.vernacular: 「只係要盡量對佢好、對佢和藹,又不寵壞佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是要盡量對她好、對她和藹,又不寵壞她。

passages.original: I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”
passages.vernacular: 我覺得佢係嗰種,只要讓佢愛上你,你就能點樣都行嘅細路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得她是那種,只要讓她愛上你,你就能怎麼樣都行的孩子。」

passages.original: Marilla sniffed, to express her contempt for Matthew’s opinions concerning anything feminine, and walked off to the dairy with the pails.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉哼咗一聲,表示佢對馬修關於一切女性事物嘅意見嘅輕蔑,然後提住桶走去咗奶房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉哼了一聲,表示她對馬修關於一切女性事物的意見的輕蔑,然後提著桶走去了奶房。

passages.original: “I won’t tell her tonight that she can stay,” she reflected, as she strained the milk into the creamers.
passages.vernacular: 「今晚我不告訴佢佢可以留下嚟,」佢一邊把牛奶濾進乳脂盆,一邊思量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚我不告訴她她可以留下來,」她一邊把牛奶濾進乳脂盆,一邊思量。

passages.original: “She’d be so excited that she wouldn’t sleep a wink.
passages.vernacular: 「佢會興奮得一夜瞓不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她會興奮得一夜睡不著。

passages.original: Marilla Cuthbert, you’re fairly in for it.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉·卡思伯特,你呢下係結結實實地陷進去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉·卡思伯特,你這下是結結實實地陷進去了。

passages.original: Did you ever suppose you’d see the day when you’d be adopting an orphan girl?
passages.vernacular: 你可曾想過會有咁一天,你要收養一個孤兒女孩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可曾想過會有這麼一天,你要收養一個孤兒女孩?

passages.original: It’s surprising enough; but not so surprising as that Matthew should be at the bottom of it, him that always seemed to have such a mortal dread of little girls.
passages.vernacular: 呢已經夠令人食驚喇;但更讓人食驚嘅係,背後嘅人竟然係馬修,佢向來似乎對小女孩有一種致命嘅恐懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這已經夠令人吃驚了;但更讓人吃驚的是,背後的人竟然是馬修,他向來似乎對小女孩有一種致命的恐懼。

passages.original: Anyhow, we’ve decided on the experiment and goodness only knows what will come of it.”
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,我哋已經決定做呢個試驗,天曉得會有乜嘢結果。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,我們已經決定做這個試驗,天曉得會有什麼結果。」

chapters.title: Ch. VII Anne Says Her Prayers 第七章:安妮做禱告

passages.original: CH WHEN Marilla took Anne up to bed that night she said stiffly:
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上瑪麗拉帶安妮上床時,佢僵硬地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上瑪麗拉帶安妮上床時,她僵硬地說:

passages.original: “Now, Anne, I noticed last night that you threw your clothes all about the floor when you took them off.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,安妮,我琴晚注意到你脫衣服時,把衣服扔得滿地都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,安妮,我昨晚注意到你脫衣服時,把衣服扔得滿地都是。

passages.original: That is a very untidy habit, and I can’t allow it at all.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個好不整潔嘅習慣,我決不允許。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個很不整潔的習慣,我決不允許。

passages.original: As soon as you take off any article of clothing fold it neatly and place it on the chair.
passages.vernacular: 你一脫下任何衣物,就要整整齊齊地疊好放喺椅子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一脫下任何衣物,就要整整齊齊地疊好放在椅子上。

passages.original: I haven’t any use at all for little girls who aren’t neat.”
passages.vernacular: 我對不愛整潔嘅小女孩啲用處都冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對不愛整潔的小女孩一點用處都沒有。」

passages.original: “I was so harrowed up in my mind last night that I didn’t think about my clothes at all,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「琴晚我心裡太痛苦喇,完全冇想到我嘅衣服,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「昨晚我心裡太痛苦了,完全沒想到我的衣服,」安妮說。

passages.original: “I’ll fold them nicely tonight.
passages.vernacular: 「今晚我會把佢哋疊得好好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚我會把它們疊得好好的。

passages.original: They always made us do that at the asylum.
passages.vernacular: 喺孤兒院佢哋總是讓我哋咁做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在孤兒院他們總是讓我們這麼做。

passages.original: Half the time, though, I’d forget, I’d be in such a hurry to get into bed nice and quiet and imagine things.”
passages.vernacular: 不過有一半時間我都會忘記,因為我急住要安安靜靜地上床去想像嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過有一半時間我都會忘記,因為我急著要安安靜靜地上床去想像東西。」

passages.original: “You’ll have to remember a little better if you stay here,” admonished Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你留喺呢度,就得記得更牢些,」瑪麗拉告誡道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你留在這裡,就得記得更牢些,」瑪麗拉告誡道。

passages.original: “There, that looks something like.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,呢仲有點樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,這還有點樣子。

passages.original: Say your prayers now and get into bed.”
passages.vernacular: 而家做禱告,上床吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在做禱告,上床吧。」

passages.original: “I never say any prayers,” announced Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我從不做禱告,」安妮宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從不做禱告,」安妮宣布。

passages.original: Marilla looked horrified astonishment.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉露出驚駭嘅神色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉露出驚駭的神色。

passages.original: “Why, Anne, what do you mean?
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,安妮,你呢個係乜嘢意思?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,安妮,你這是什麼意思?

passages.original: Were you never taught to say your prayers?
passages.vernacular: 難道從來冇人教過你做禱告嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難道從來沒人教過你做禱告嗎?

passages.original: God always wants little girls to say their prayers.
passages.vernacular: 上帝總是希望小女孩做禱告嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上帝總是希望小女孩做禱告的。

passages.original: Don’t you know who God is, Anne?”
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道上帝係邊個嗎,安妮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道上帝是誰嗎,安妮?」

passages.original: “‘God is a spirit, infinite, eternal and unchangeable, in His being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth,’” responded Anne promptly and glibly.
passages.vernacular: 「『上帝係靈,祂嘅本體、智慧、能力、聖潔、公義、良善、真實,都係無限、永恆、不變嘅,』」安妮即刻流利地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『上帝是靈,祂的本體、智慧、能力、聖潔、公義、良善、真實,都是無限、永恆、不變的,』」安妮立刻流利地回答。

passages.original: Marilla looked rather relieved.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉睇上去鬆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉看上去鬆了口氣。

passages.original: “So you do know something then, thank goodness!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你定係知道啲嘅,謝天謝地!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你還是知道一些的,謝天謝地!

passages.original: You’re not quite a heathen.
passages.vernacular: 你不完全係個異教徒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不完全是個異教徒。

passages.original: Where did you learn that?”
passages.vernacular: 你係喺邊兒學嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是在哪兒學的?」

passages.original: “Oh, at the asylum Sunday-school.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,喺孤兒院嘅主日學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,在孤兒院的主日學校。

passages.original: They made us learn the whole catechism.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋讓我哋背整本教理問答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們讓我們背整本教理問答。

passages.original: I liked it pretty well.
passages.vernacular: 我挺鍾意嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我挺喜歡的。

passages.original: There’s something splendid about some of the words.
passages.vernacular: 有些詞句有一種壯麗嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些詞句有一種壯麗的東西。

passages.original: ‘Infinite, eternal and unchangeable.’
passages.vernacular: 『無限、永恆、不變。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『無限、永恆、不變。』

passages.original: Isn’t that grand?
passages.vernacular: 幾咁雄偉啊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多麼雄偉啊?

passages.original: It has such a roll to it--just like a big organ playing.
passages.vernacular: 佢有一種韻律——就像大管風琴喺演奏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它有一種韻律——就像大管風琴在演奏。

passages.original: You couldn’t quite call it poetry, I suppose, but it sounds a lot like it, doesn’t it?”
passages.vernacular: 我想唔能夠完全叫佢詩,但聽起嚟好像,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想不能完全叫它詩,但聽起來很像,是不是?」

passages.original: “We’re not talking about poetry, Anne--we are talking about saying your prayers.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋唔係喺談詩,安妮——我哋係喺談做禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們不是在談詩,安妮——我們是在談做禱告。

passages.original: Don’t you know it’s a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night?
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道每天晚上不做禱告係好邪惡嘅事嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道每天晚上不做禱告是很邪惡的事嗎?

passages.original: I’m afraid you are a very bad little girl.”
passages.vernacular: 我怕你係個好壞嘅小女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕你是個很壞的小女孩。」

passages.original: “You’d find it easier to be bad than good if you had red hair,” said Anne reproachfully.
passages.vernacular: 「如果您有一頭紅髮,您會發現做壞比做好容易得多,」安妮責備地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果您有一頭紅髮,您會發現做壞比做好容易得多,」安妮責備地說。

passages.original: “People who haven’t red hair don’t know what trouble is.
passages.vernacular: 「冇紅頭髮嘅人唔知道乜嘢叫煩惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有紅頭髮的人不知道什麼叫煩惱。

passages.original: Mrs. Thomas told me that God made my hair red on purpose, and I’ve never cared about Him since.
passages.vernacular: 托馬斯太太告訴我,上帝係故意把我嘅頭髮造成紅色嘅,從嗰以後我就再都不在乎祂喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 托馬斯太太告訴我,上帝是故意把我的頭髮造成紅色的,從那以後我就再也不在乎祂了。

passages.original: And anyhow I’d always be too tired at night to bother saying prayers.
passages.vernacular: 而且不管點樣,晚上我總是太累喇,懶得去做禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且不管怎樣,晚上我總是太累了,懶得去做禱告。

passages.original: People who have to look after twins can’t be expected to say their prayers.
passages.vernacular: 要照睇雙胞胎嘅人,唔能夠指望佢做禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要照看雙胞胎的人,不能指望她做禱告。

passages.original: Now, do you honestly think they can?”
passages.vernacular: 而家,您真嘅認為佢哋能嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,您真的認為她們能嗎?」

passages.original: Marilla decided that Anne’s religious training must be begun at once.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉決定必須即刻開始對安妮進行宗教訓練。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉決定必須馬上開始對安妮進行宗教訓練。

passages.original: Plainly there was no time to be lost.
passages.vernacular: 顯然一刻都唔能夠耽擱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 顯然一刻也不能耽擱。

passages.original: “You must say your prayers while you are under my roof, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 「只要你仲喺我嘅屋簷下,就必須做禱告,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只要你還在我的屋簷下,就必須做禱告,安妮。」

passages.original: “Why, of course, if you want me to,” assented Anne cheerfully.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,當然,如果您想要我咁樣嘅話,」安妮高興地答應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,當然,如果您想要我這樣的話,」安妮高興地答應。

passages.original: “I’d do anything to oblige you.
passages.vernacular: 「我願意做任何事嚟討您歡心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我願意做任何事來討您歡心。

passages.original: But you’ll have to tell me what to say for this once.
passages.vernacular: 不過呢一次您得告訴我講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過這一次您得告訴我說什麼。

passages.original: After I get into bed I’ll imagine out a real nice prayer to say always.
passages.vernacular: 等我上咗床,我會想出一篇真正好嘅禱告詞,以後一直用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我上了床,我會想出一篇真正好的禱告詞,以後一直用。

passages.original: I believe that it will be quite interesting, now that I come to think of it.”
passages.vernacular: 而家我想想,我覺得嗰會好有趣嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我想想,我覺得那會很有趣的。」

passages.original: “You must kneel down,” said Marilla in embarrassment.
passages.vernacular: 「你得跪下嚟,」瑪麗拉窘迫地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你得跪下來,」瑪麗拉窘迫地說。

passages.original: Anne knelt at Marilla’s knee and looked up gravely.
passages.vernacular: 安妮跪喺瑪麗拉嘅膝邊,莊重地抬頭望住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮跪在瑪麗拉的膝邊,莊重地抬頭望著她。

passages.original: “Why must people kneel down to pray?
passages.vernacular: 「點解禱告時要跪下?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼禱告時要跪下?

passages.original: If I really wanted to pray I’ll tell you what I’d do.
passages.vernacular: 如果我真想禱告,我告訴您我會點做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我真想禱告,我告訴您我會怎麼做。

passages.original: I’d go out into a great big field all alone or into the deep, deep woods, and I’d look up into the sky--up--up--up--into that lovely blue sky that looks as if there was no end to its blueness.
passages.vernacular: 我會一個人走到一片大大嘅田野裡,或者走進深深、深深嘅樹林,仰望天空——向上——向上——向上——望進嗰可愛嘅藍天,佢睇上去藍得冇盡頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會一個人走到一片大大的田野裡,或者走進深深、深深的樹林,仰望天空——向上——向上——向上——望進那可愛的藍天,它看上去藍得沒有盡頭。

passages.original: And then I’d just feel a prayer.
passages.vernacular: 然後我就會感受到一個禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我就會感受到一個禱告。

passages.original: Well, I’m ready.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,我準備好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,我準備好了。

passages.original: What am I to say?”
passages.vernacular: 我該講乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我該說什麼?」

passages.original: Marilla felt more embarrassed than ever.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉比以往任何時候都窘迫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉比以往任何時候都窘迫。

passages.original: She had intended to teach Anne the childish classic, “Now I lay me down to sleep.”
passages.vernacular: 佢本打算教安妮嗰首細路哋嘅經典禱詞:「而家我躺下瞓覺。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她本打算教安妮那首孩子們的經典禱詞:「現在我躺下睡覺。」

passages.original: But she had, as I have told you, the glimmerings of a sense of humor--which is simply another name for a sense of the fitness of things; and it suddenly occurred to her that that simple little prayer, sacred to white-robed childhood lisping at motherly knees, was entirely unsuited to this freckled witch of a girl who knew and cared nothing about God’s love, since she had never had it translated to her through the medium of human love.
passages.vernacular: 但係,就像我告訴過你嘅,佢有一絲幽默感嘅微光——嗰不過係對事物係咪相稱嘅感覺嘅另一種講法;佢突然想到,嗰首簡單嘅小禱詞,係屬於身穿白袍、喺母親膝邊咿呀學語嘅童年嘅聖物,完全不適合呢個長滿雀斑嘅小精靈般嘅女孩,佢對上帝嘅愛一無所知,都不在乎,因為從來冇人通過人間嘅愛向佢轉述過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,就像我告訴過你的,她有一絲幽默感的微光——那不過是對事物是否相稱的感覺的另一種說法;她突然想到,那首簡單的小禱詞,是屬於身穿白袍、在母親膝邊咿呀學語的童年的聖物,完全不適合這個長滿雀斑的小精靈般的女孩,她對上帝的愛一無所知,也不在乎,因為從來沒有人通過人間的愛向她轉述過。

passages.original: “You’re old enough to pray for yourself, Anne,” she said finally.
passages.vernacular: 「你已經夠大喇,可以自己禱告喇,安妮,」佢最後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你已經夠大了,可以自己禱告了,安妮,」她最後說。

passages.original: “Just thank God for your blessings and ask Him humbly for the things you want.”
passages.vernacular: 「只要感謝上帝賜畀你嘅福分,謙卑地向祂求你想要嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只要感謝上帝賜給你的福分,謙卑地向祂求你想要的東西。」

passages.original: “Well, I’ll do my best,” promised Anne, burying her face in Marilla’s lap.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,我盡力,」安妮許諾,把臉埋進瑪麗拉嘅膝蓋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,我盡力,」安妮許諾,把臉埋進瑪麗拉的膝蓋。

passages.original: “Gracious heavenly Father--that’s the way the ministers say it in church, so I suppose it’s all right in private prayer, isn’t it?” she interjected, lifting her head for a moment.
passages.vernacular: 「仁慈嘅天父——牧師哋喺教堂裡就係咁講嘅,所以我想私下禱告都冇問題,係唔係?」佢抬起頭嚟插咗一句。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「仁慈的天父——牧師們在教堂裡就是這麼說的,所以我想私下禱告也沒問題,是不是?」她抬起頭來插了一句。

passages.original: “Gracious heavenly Father, I thank Thee for the White Way of Delight and the Lake of Shining Waters and Bonny and the Snow Queen.
passages.vernacular: 「仁慈嘅天父,我感謝祢賜畀我歡樂白路同閃亮湖水,賜畀我邦妮同雪之女王。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「仁慈的天父,我感謝祢賜給我歡樂白路和閃亮湖水,賜給我邦妮和雪之女王。

passages.original: I’m really extremely grateful for them.
passages.vernacular: 我真嘅萬分感激佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真的萬分感激它們。

passages.original: And that’s all the blessings I can think of just now to thank Thee for.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係我此刻能想到嘅所有要感謝祢嘅福分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是我此刻能想到的所有要感謝祢的福分。

passages.original: As for the things I want, they’re so numerous that it would take a great deal of time to name them all, so I will only mention the two most important.
passages.vernacular: 至於我想要嘅嘢,佢哋太多喇,要一一列出得花好多時間,所以我只提最重要嘅兩樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於我想要的東西,它們太多了,要一一列出得花很多時間,所以我只提最重要的兩樣。

passages.original: Please let me stay at Green Gables; and please let me be good-looking when I grow up.
passages.vernacular: 請讓我留喺綠色屋頂;請讓我長大後好睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請讓我留在綠色屋頂;請讓我長大後好看。

passages.original: I remain,
passages.vernacular: 謹此,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謹此,

passages.original: “Yours respectfully, Anne Shirley.
passages.vernacular: 「您恭敬嘅,安妮·雪莉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您恭敬的,安妮·雪莉。

passages.original: “There, did I do all right?” she asked eagerly, getting up.
passages.vernacular: 「點樣,我做得對嗎?」佢站起身,急切地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼樣,我做得對嗎?」她站起身,急切地問。

passages.original: “I could have made it much more flowery if I’d had a little more time to think it over.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果我有多啲時間考慮,我本可以把佢講得華麗得多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我有多一點時間考慮,我本可以把它說得華麗得多。」

passages.original: Poor Marilla was only preserved from complete collapse by remembering that it was not irreverence, but simply spiritual ignorance on the part of Anne that was responsible for this extraordinary petition.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅瑪麗拉,全靠想到呢唔係出於不敬,而係安妮喺精神上無知才導致咗呢個非凡嘅祈求,才冇徹底崩潰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的瑪麗拉,全靠想到這不是出於不敬,而是安妮在精神上無知才導致了這個非凡的祈求,才沒有徹底崩潰。

passages.original: She tucked the child up in bed, mentally vowing that she should be taught a prayer the very next day, and was leaving the room with the light when Anne called her back.
passages.vernacular: 佢把細路喺床上掖好,心裡發誓第二天就要教佢一首禱詞,攞住燈正要離開房間,安妮又叫住咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把孩子在床上掖好,心裡發誓第二天就要教她一首禱詞,拿著燈正要離開房間,安妮又叫住了她。

passages.original: “I’ve just thought of it now.
passages.vernacular: 「我啱啱想到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我剛剛想到。

passages.original: I should have said ‘Amen’ in place of ‘yours respectfully,’ shouldn’t I?--the way the ministers do.
passages.vernacular: 我應該講『阿哋』,而唔係『您恭敬嘅』,係唔係?——就像牧師哋嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我應該說『阿們』,而不是『您恭敬的』,是不是?——就像牧師們那樣。

passages.original: I’d forgotten it, but I felt a prayer should be finished off in some way, so I put in the other.
passages.vernacular: 我忘喇,不過我覺得禱告應該以某種方式結束,所以我就加咗另一種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忘了,不過我覺得禱告應該以某種方式結束,所以我就加了另一種。

passages.original: Do you suppose it will make any difference?”
passages.vernacular: 您覺得會有乜嘢區別嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您覺得會有什麼區別嗎?」

passages.original: “I--I don’t suppose it will,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我想唔會有,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我想不會有,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “Go to sleep now like a good child.
passages.vernacular: 「而家像個好細路嗰樣瞓覺吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在像個好孩子那樣睡覺吧。

passages.original: Good night.”
passages.vernacular: 晚安。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安。」

passages.original: “I can say good night tonight with a clear conscience,” said Anne, cuddling luxuriously down among her pillows.
passages.vernacular: 「今晚我可以問心無愧地講晚安喇,」安妮講,舒服地蜷縮進枕頭裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚我可以問心無愧地說晚安了,」安妮說,舒服地蜷縮進枕頭裡。

passages.original: Marilla retreated to the kitchen, set the candle firmly on the table, and glared at Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉退到廚房,把蠟燭重重地放喺桌上,瞪住馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉退到廚房,把蠟燭重重地放在桌上,瞪著馬修。

passages.original: “Matthew Cuthbert, it’s about time somebody adopted that child and taught her something.
passages.vernacular: 「馬修·卡思伯特,係時候有人收養嗰細路,教佢點嘢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修·卡思伯特,是時候有人收養那孩子,教她點東西了。

passages.original: She’s next door to a perfect heathen.
passages.vernacular: 佢差不多係個地地道道嘅異教徒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她差不多是個地地道道的異教徒了。

passages.original: Will you believe that she never said a prayer in her life till tonight?
passages.vernacular: 你相信嗎?佢到今晚為止一輩子冇做過一次禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你相信嗎?她到今晚為止一輩子沒做過一次禱告。

passages.original: I’ll send to the manse tomorrow and borrow the Peep of the Day series, that’s what I’ll do.
passages.vernacular: 聽日我派人到牧師住宅去借《黎明一瞥》叢書,就咁辦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天我派人到牧師住宅去借《黎明一瞥》叢書,就這麼辦。

passages.original: And she shall go to Sunday-school just as soon as I can get some suitable clothes made for her.
passages.vernacular: 仲有,一等我畀佢做好合適嘅衣服,佢就得去主日學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,一等我給她做好合適的衣服,她就得去主日學校。

passages.original: I foresee that I shall have my hands full.
passages.vernacular: 我預見我會忙得不可開交。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我預見我會忙得不可開交。

passages.original: Well, well, we can’t get through this world without our share of trouble.
passages.vernacular: 唉,唉,我哋邊個都唔能夠喺呢個世界上不經歷一份麻煩就過一輩子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,唉,我們誰也不能在這個世界上不經歷一份麻煩就過一輩子。

passages.original: I’ve had a pretty easy life of it so far, but my time has come at last and I suppose I’ll just have to make the best of it.”
passages.vernacular: 到目前為止,我嘅日子過得挺輕鬆,但我嘅時辰終於到喇,我想我只好盡力而為喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到目前為止,我的日子過得挺輕鬆,但我的時辰終於到了,我想我只好盡力而為了。」

chapters.title: Ch. VIII Anne's Bringing-up Is Begun 第八章:安妮的教養開始了

passages.original: CH FOR reasons best known to herself, Marilla did not tell Anne that she was to stay at Green Gables until the next afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 出於佢自己最清楚嘅原因,瑪麗拉直到第二天下午才告訴安妮佢可以留喺綠色屋頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 出於她自己最清楚的原因,瑪麗拉直到第二天下午才告訴安妮她可以留在綠色屋頂。

passages.original: During the forenoon she kept the child busy with various tasks and watched over her with a keen eye while she did them.
passages.vernacular: 整個上午,佢讓細路忙於各種活兒,一邊用敏銳嘅目光盯住佢做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個上午,她讓孩子忙於各種活兒,一邊用敏銳的目光盯著她做。

passages.original: By noon she had concluded that Anne was smart and obedient, willing to work and quick to learn; her most serious shortcoming seemed to be a tendency to fall into daydreams in the middle of a task and forget all about it until such time as she was sharply recalled to earth by a reprimand or a catastrophe.
passages.vernacular: 到中午,佢得出結論,安妮聰明、順從,肯幹活、學得快;佢最嚴重嘅缺點似乎係容易喺做事中途陷入白日夢,把事情忘得一乾二淨,直到被一聲訓斥或一場災難猛地喚回人間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到中午,她得出結論,安妮聰明、順從,肯幹活、學得快;她最嚴重的缺點似乎是容易在做事中途陷入白日夢,把事情忘得一乾二淨,直到被一聲訓斥或一場災難猛地喚回人間。

passages.original: When Anne had finished washing the dinner dishes she suddenly confronted Marilla with the air and expression of one desperately determined to learn the worst.
passages.vernacular: 安妮洗完午飯嘅碗碟後,突然帶住一副孤注一擲、非要知道最壞結果嘅神態同表情面對瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮洗完午飯的碗碟後,突然帶著一副孤注一擲、非要知道最壞結果的神態和表情面對瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Her thin little body trembled from head to foot; her face flushed and her eyes dilated until they were almost black; she clasped her hands tightly and said in an imploring voice:
passages.vernacular: 佢瘦小嘅身子從頭到腳都喺顫抖;臉漲得通紅,眼睛放大到幾乎全黑;佢緊緊地絞住雙手,用懇求嘅聲音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她瘦小的身子從頭到腳都在顫抖;臉漲得通紅,眼睛放大到幾乎全黑;她緊緊地絞著雙手,用懇求的聲音說:

passages.original: “Oh, please, Miss Cuthbert, won’t you tell me if you are going to send me away or not?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,求求您,卡思伯特小姐,您能唔能夠告訴我,您係唔係要把我送走?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,求求您,卡思伯特小姐,您能不能告訴我,您是不是要把我送走?
