passages.original: I’ve tried to be patient all the morning, but I really feel that I cannot bear not knowing any longer.
passages.vernacular: 我整個上午都努力耐心等待,但我真覺得再都忍受不了唔知道嘅滋味喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我整個上午都努力耐心等待,但我真覺得再也忍受不了不知道的滋味了。

passages.original: It’s a dreadful feeling.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一種可怕嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一種可怕的感覺。

passages.original: Please tell me.”
passages.vernacular: 請告訴我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請告訴我。」

passages.original: “You haven’t scalded the dishcloth in clean hot water as I told you to do,” said Marilla immovably.
passages.vernacular: 「你冇像我叫你做嘅嗰樣,用乾淨嘅熱水燙洗抹布,」瑪麗拉紋絲不動地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你沒有像我叫你做的那樣,用乾淨的熱水燙洗抹布,」瑪麗拉紋絲不動地說。

passages.original: “Just go and do it before you ask any more questions, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 「先去把佢做咗再問別嘅問題,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「先去把它做了再問別的問題,安妮。」

passages.original: Anne went and attended to the dishcloth.
passages.vernacular: 安妮去料理咗抹布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮去料理了抹布。

passages.original: Then she returned to Marilla and fastened imploring eyes on the latter’s face.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢回到瑪麗拉身邊,把懇求嘅目光固定喺佢嘅臉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她回到瑪麗拉身邊,把懇求的目光固定在她的臉上。

passages.original: “Well,” said Marilla, unable to find any excuse for deferring her explanation longer, “I suppose I might as well tell you.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」瑪麗拉講,再都找唔到理由推遲佢嘅解釋喇,「我想我不妨告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」瑪麗拉說,再也找不到理由推遲她的解釋了,「我想我不妨告訴你。

passages.original: Matthew and I have decided to keep you--that is, if you will try to be a good little girl and show yourself grateful.
passages.vernacular: 馬修同我已決定留下你——都就係講,只要你努力做個好女孩,表現出感激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修和我已決定留下你——也就是說,只要你努力做個好女孩,表現出感激。

passages.original: Why, child, whatever is the matter?”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,細路,到底點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,孩子,到底怎麼了?」

passages.original: “I’m crying,” said Anne in a tone of bewilderment.
passages.vernacular: 「我喺哭,」安妮用困惑嘅語氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在哭,」安妮用困惑的語氣說。

passages.original: “I can’t think why.
passages.vernacular: 「我想不通點解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想不通為什麼。

passages.original: I’m glad as glad can be.
passages.vernacular: 我高興得唔能夠再高興喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我高興得不能再高興了。

passages.original: Oh, glad doesn’t seem the right word at all.
passages.vernacular: 哦,高興似乎啲都唔係合適嘅詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,高興似乎一點也不是合適的詞。

passages.original: I was glad about the White Way and the cherry blossoms--but this!
passages.vernacular: 我為歡樂白路同櫻桃花高興過——不過呢個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為歡樂白路和櫻桃花高興過——可是這個!

passages.original: Oh, it’s something more than glad.
passages.vernacular: 哦,呢個係比高興更多嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,這是比高興更多的東西。

passages.original: I’m so happy.
passages.vernacular: 我太幸福喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太幸福了。

passages.original: I’ll try to be so good.
passages.vernacular: 我會努力做得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會努力做得很好。

passages.original: It will be uphill work, I expect, for Mrs. Thomas often told me I was desperately wicked.
passages.vernacular: 我想嗰會係件食力嘅事,因為托馬斯太太常講我壞得不可救藥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想那會是件吃力的事,因為托馬斯太太常說我壞得不可救藥。

passages.original: However, I’ll do my very best.
passages.vernacular: 不過,我會盡我最大嘅努力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,我會盡我最大的努力。

passages.original: But can you tell me why I’m crying?”
passages.vernacular: 但您能告訴我我點解喺哭嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但您能告訴我我為什麼在哭嗎?」

passages.original: “I suppose it’s because you’re all excited and worked up,” said Marilla disapprovingly.
passages.vernacular: 「我想係因為你太興奮、太激動喇,」瑪麗拉不以為然地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是因為你太興奮、太激動了,」瑪麗拉不以為然地說。

passages.original: “Sit down on that chair and try to calm yourself.
passages.vernacular: 「坐喺嗰把椅子上,試住讓自己平靜下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「坐在那把椅子上,試著讓自己平靜下來。

passages.original: I’m afraid you both cry and laugh far too easily.
passages.vernacular: 我怕你又哭又笑,實在太容易喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕你又哭又笑,實在太容易了。

passages.original: Yes, you can stay here and we will try to do right by you.
passages.vernacular: 對,你可以留喺呢兒,我哋會努力善待你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,你可以留在這兒,我們會努力善待你。

passages.original: You must go to school; but it’s only a fortnight till vacation so it isn’t worth while for you to start before it opens again in September.”
passages.vernacular: 你得去上學;不過離放假只有兩個星期喇,所以不值得喺九月重新開學前就開始。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你得去上學;不過離放假只有兩個星期了,所以不值得在九月重新開學前就開始。」

passages.original: “What am I to call you?” asked Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我該點稱呼您?」安妮問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我該怎麼稱呼您?」安妮問。

passages.original: “Shall I always say Miss Cuthbert?
passages.vernacular: 「我一直叫您卡思伯特小姐嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一直叫您卡思伯特小姐嗎?

passages.original: Can I call you Aunt Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 我能叫您瑪麗拉姨媽嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能叫您瑪麗拉姨媽嗎?」

passages.original: “No; you’ll call me just plain Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「不行;你就叫我瑪麗拉,簡簡單單嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不行;你就叫我瑪麗拉,簡簡單單的。

passages.original: I’m not used to being called Miss Cuthbert and it would make me nervous.”
passages.vernacular: 我不習慣被叫卡思伯特小姐,嗰會讓我緊張。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不習慣被叫卡思伯特小姐,那會讓我緊張。」

passages.original: “It sounds awfully disrespectful to just say Marilla,” protested Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「光叫瑪麗拉聽起嚟太不尊敬喇,」安妮抗議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「光叫瑪麗拉聽起來太不尊敬了,」安妮抗議。

passages.original: “I guess there’ll be nothing disrespectful in it if you’re careful to speak respectfully.
passages.vernacular: 「我想,只要你小心地恭恭敬敬講話,就冇乜嘢不尊敬嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想,只要你小心地恭恭敬敬說話,就沒有什麼不尊敬的。

passages.original: Everybody, young and old, in Avonlea calls me Marilla except the minister.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利無論老少,除咗牧師,人人都叫我瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利無論老少,除了牧師,人人都叫我瑪麗拉。

passages.original: He says Miss Cuthbert--when he thinks of it.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講卡思伯特小姐——當佢想得起嚟嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說卡思伯特小姐——當他想得起來的時候。」

passages.original: “I’d love to call you Aunt Marilla,” said Anne wistfully.
passages.vernacular: 「我真想叫您瑪麗拉姨媽,」安妮悵然地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真想叫您瑪麗拉姨媽,」安妮悵然地說。

passages.original: “I’ve never had an aunt or any relation at all--not even a grandmother.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇過姨媽,或者任何親戚——連祖母都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒有過姨媽,或者任何親戚——連祖母也沒有。

passages.original: It would make me feel as if I really belonged to you.
passages.vernacular: 嗰會讓我覺得我真嘅屬於您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那會讓我覺得我真的屬於您。

passages.original: Can’t I call you Aunt Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠叫您瑪麗拉姨媽嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能叫您瑪麗拉姨媽嗎?」

passages.original: “No. I’m not your aunt and I don’t believe in calling people names that don’t belong to them.”
passages.vernacular: 「不行。我唔係你姨媽,而且我不贊成稱呼人家不屬於佢哋嘅稱呼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不行。我不是你姨媽,而且我不贊成稱呼人家不屬於他們的稱呼。」

passages.original: “But we could imagine you were my aunt.”
passages.vernacular: 「不過我哋可以想像您係我嘅姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我們可以想像您是我的姨媽。」

passages.original: “I couldn’t,” said Marilla grimly.
passages.vernacular: 「我做唔到,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我做不到,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地說。

passages.original: “Do you never imagine things different from what they really are?” asked Anne wide-eyed.
passages.vernacular: 「您從來不把事情想像得同佢哋實際嘅不同嗎?」安妮睜大眼睛問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您從來不把事情想像得和它們實際的不同嗎?」安妮睜大眼睛問。

passages.original: “No.”
“Oh!”
Anne drew a long breath.
passages.vernacular: 安妮深深吸咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮深深吸了口氣。

passages.original: “Oh, Miss--Marilla, how much you miss!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,卡思伯特小姐——瑪麗拉,您錯過咗多少嘢啊!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,卡思伯特小姐——瑪麗拉,您錯過了多少東西啊!」

passages.original: “I don’t believe in imagining things different from what they really are,” retorted Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我不贊成把事情想像得同佢哋實際嘅不同,」瑪麗拉反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不贊成把事情想像得和它們實際的不同,」瑪麗拉反駁。

passages.original: “When the Lord puts us in certain circumstances He doesn’t mean for us to imagine them away.
passages.vernacular: 「當主把我哋置於某種境遇時,祂唔係要我哋把佢哋想像掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當主把我們置於某種境遇時,祂不是要我們把它們想像掉。

passages.original: And that reminds me.
passages.vernacular: 呢讓我想起嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這讓我想起來了。

passages.original: Go into the sitting room, Anne--be sure your feet are clean and don’t let any flies in--and bring me out the illustrated card that’s on the mantelpiece.
passages.vernacular: 到起居室去,安妮——要確保腳係乾淨嘅,唔好畀蒼蠅飛進嚟——把壁爐架上嗰張帶插圖嘅卡片畀我攞出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到起居室去,安妮——要確保腳是乾淨的,別讓蒼蠅飛進來——把壁爐架上那張帶插圖的卡片給我拿出來。

passages.original: The Lord’s Prayer is on it and you’ll devote your spare time this afternoon to learning it off by heart.
passages.vernacular: 上面有主禱文,今日下午你要把空閒時間都用嚟把佢背下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面有主禱文,今天下午你要把空閒時間都用來把它背下來。

passages.original: There’s to be no more of such praying as I heard last night.”
passages.vernacular: 不許再像我琴晚聽到嘅嗰樣禱告喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不許再像我昨晚聽到的那樣禱告了。」

passages.original: “I suppose I was very awkward,” said Anne apologetically, “but then, you see, I’d never had any practice.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我當時好笨拙,」安妮道歉地講,「不過,您瞧,我以前從冇練習過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我當時很笨拙,」安妮道歉地說,「不過,您瞧,我以前從沒練習過。

passages.original: You couldn’t really expect a person to pray very well the first time she tried, could you?
passages.vernacular: 您總唔能夠指望一個人第一次試就禱告得好好,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您總不能指望一個人第一次試就禱告得很好,是不是?

passages.original: I thought out a splendid prayer after I went to bed, just as I promised you I would.
passages.vernacular: 我上床後想出咗一篇絕妙嘅禱詞,正如我答應您嘅嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我上床後想出了一篇絕妙的禱詞,正如我答應您的那樣。

passages.original: It was nearly as long as a minister’s and so poetical.
passages.vernacular: 佢幾乎同牧師嘅一樣長,而且咁富有詩意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它幾乎和牧師的一樣長,而且那麼富有詩意。

passages.original: But would you believe it?
passages.vernacular: 不過您信嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是您信嗎?

passages.original: I couldn’t remember one word when I woke up this morning.
passages.vernacular: 今日早晨醒嚟時,我一個字都記不起嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天早晨醒來時,我一個字也記不起來了。

passages.original: And I’m afraid I’ll never be able to think out another one as good.
passages.vernacular: 我怕我再都想不出另一篇同樣好嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕我再也想不出另一篇同樣好的了。

passages.original: Somehow, things never are so good when they’re thought out a second time.
passages.vernacular: 唔知怎嘅,事情第二次想出嚟,永遠不如第一次好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知怎的,事情第二次想出來,永遠不如第一次好。

passages.original: Have you ever noticed that?”
passages.vernacular: 您有冇注意到呢啲?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您有沒有注意到這一點?」

passages.original: “Here is something for you to notice, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「呢度有件事你該注意,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡有件事你該注意,安妮。

passages.original: When I tell you to do a thing I want you to obey me at once and not stand stock-still and discourse about it.
passages.vernacular: 當我叫你做一件事時,我要你即刻服從我,而唔係呆呆地站住大發議論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我叫你做一件事時,我要你立刻服從我,而不是呆呆地站著大發議論。

passages.original: Just you go and do as I bid you.”
passages.vernacular: 你就去照我吩咐嘅做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你就去照我吩咐的做。」

passages.original: Anne promptly departed for the sitting-room across the hall; she failed to return; after waiting ten minutes Marilla laid down her knitting and marched after her with a grim expression.
passages.vernacular: 安妮即刻動身去咗門廳對面嘅起居室;佢冇回嚟;等咗好鐘後,瑪麗拉放下毛線活,帶住嚴厲嘅表情大步跟咗過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮立刻動身去了門廳對面的起居室;她沒回來;等了十分鐘後,瑪麗拉放下毛線活,帶著嚴厲的表情大步跟了過去。

passages.original: She found Anne standing motionless before a picture hanging on the wall between the two windows, with her eyes astar with dreams.
passages.vernacular: 佢發現安妮一動不動地站喺掛喺兩扇窗之間牆上嘅一幅畫前,眼睛裡閃爍住夢想嘅星光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她發現安妮一動不動地站在掛在兩扇窗之間牆上的一幅畫前,眼睛裡閃爍著夢想的星光。

passages.original: The white and green light strained through apple-trees and clustering vines outside fell over the rapt little figure with a half-unearthly radiance.
passages.vernacular: 透過外面蘋果樹同簇生藤蔓濾進嚟嘅白綠色光線,灑喺嗰出神嘅小身影上,帶住一種半超凡嘅光輝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 透過外面蘋果樹和簇生藤蔓濾進來的白綠色光線,灑在那出神的小身影上,帶著一種半超凡的光輝。

passages.original: “Anne, whatever are you thinking of?” demanded Marilla sharply.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,你到底喺想乜嘢?」瑪麗拉厲聲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,你到底在想什麼?」瑪麗拉厲聲問。

passages.original: Anne came back to earth with a start.
passages.vernacular: 安妮猛地回到人間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮猛地回到人間。

passages.original: “That,” she said, pointing to the picture--a rather vivid chromo entitled, “Christ Blessing Little Children”--“and I was just imagining I was one of them--that I was the little girl in the blue dress, standing off by herself in the corner as if she didn’t belong to anybody, like me.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個,」佢指住嗰幅畫講——一幅相當鮮豔嘅彩色石印畫,名為《基督祝福小細路》——「我頭先喺想像我係佢哋中嘅一個——我係嗰個穿藍裙子嘅小女孩,獨自站喺角落裡,好像不屬於任何人,像我一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那個,」她指著那幅畫說——一幅相當鮮豔的彩色石印畫,名為《基督祝福小孩子》——「我剛才在想像我是他們中的一個——我是那個穿藍裙子的小女孩,獨自站在角落裡,好像不屬於任何人,像我一樣。

passages.original: She looks lonely and sad, don’t you think?
passages.vernacular: 佢睇上去孤獨又悲傷,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看上去孤獨又悲傷,您說呢?

passages.original: I guess she hadn’t any father or mother of her own.
passages.vernacular: 我猜佢冇自己嘅父親或母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我猜她沒有自己的父親或母親。

passages.original: But she wanted to be blessed, too, so she just crept shyly up on the outside of the crowd, hoping nobody would notice her--except Him.
passages.vernacular: 但佢都想被祝福,所以佢就羞怯地爬到人群外圍,希望冇人注意到佢——除咗祂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她也想被祝福,所以她就羞怯地爬到人群外圍,希望沒人注意到她——除了祂。

passages.original: I’m sure I know just how she felt.
passages.vernacular: 我確信我清楚佢嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信我清楚她的感覺。

passages.original: Her heart must have beat and her hands must have got cold, like mine did when I asked you if I could stay.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅心一定喺跳,佢嘅手一定變冷喇,就像我問您我能唔能夠留下時嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的心一定在跳,她的手一定變冷了,就像我問您我能不能留下時那樣。

passages.original: She was afraid He mightn’t notice her.
passages.vernacular: 佢害怕祂可能唔會注意到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她害怕祂可能不會注意到她。

passages.original: But it’s likely He did, don’t you think?
passages.vernacular: 但祂好可能注意到喇,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但祂很可能注意到了,您說呢?

passages.original: I’ve been trying to imagine it all out--her edging a little nearer all the time until she was quite close to Him; and then He would look at her and put His hand on her hair and oh, such a thrill of joy as would run over her!
passages.vernacular: 我一直喺試住把呢一切都想像出嚟——佢一直啲啲往近處挪,直到緊挨住祂;然後祂會睇住佢,把手放喺佢嘅頭髮上,哦,嗰將有一陣幾咁喜悅嘅顫慄傳遍佢全身啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直在試著把這一切都想像出來——她一直一點一點往近處挪,直到緊挨著祂;然後祂會看著她,把手放在她的頭髮上,哦,那將有一陣多麼喜悅的顫慄傳遍她全身啊!

passages.original: But I wish the artist hadn’t painted Him so sorrowful-looking.
passages.vernacular: 但我真希望畫家冇把祂畫得咁憂傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我真希望畫家沒有把祂畫得那麼憂傷。

passages.original: All His pictures are like that, if you’ve noticed.
passages.vernacular: 如果您留意過嘅話,祂所有嘅畫像都係咁樣嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您留意過的話,祂所有的畫像都是這樣的。

passages.original: But I don’t believe He could really have looked so sad or the children would have been afraid of Him.”
passages.vernacular: 但我不相信祂真嘅會睇起嚟咁悲傷,否則細路哋就會怕祂喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不相信祂真的會看起來那麼悲傷,否則孩子們就會怕祂了。」

passages.original: “Anne,” said Marilla, wondering why she had not broken into this speech long before, “you shouldn’t talk that way.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,」瑪麗拉講,納悶自己點解冇早點打斷呢番話,「你唔應該該嗰樣講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,」瑪麗拉說,納悶自己為什麼沒有早點打斷這番話,「你不應該那樣說話。

passages.original: It’s irreverent--positively irreverent.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係不敬——絕對嘅不敬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是不敬——絕對的不敬。」

passages.original: Anne’s eyes marveled.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅眼睛裡滿係驚奇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的眼睛裡滿是驚奇。

passages.original: “Why, I felt just as reverent as could be.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我感覺係無比敬畏嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我感覺是無比敬畏的。

passages.original: I’m sure I didn’t mean to be irreverent.”
passages.vernacular: 我確信我唔係有意不敬嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信我不是有意不敬的。」

passages.original: “Well, I don’t suppose you did--but it doesn’t sound right to talk so familiarly about such things.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想你唔係故意嘅——但咁樣親昵地談論呢類事情,聽起嚟不對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想你不是故意的——但這樣親昵地談論這類事情,聽起來不對。

passages.original: And another thing, Anne, when I send you after something you’re to bring it at once and not fall into mooning and imagining before pictures.
passages.vernacular: 仲有一件事,安妮,我派你去攞乜嘢嘢嘅時候,你得即刻攞嚟,而唔係對住畫發呆、胡思亂想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有一件事,安妮,我派你去拿什麼東西的時候,你得立刻拿來,而不是對著畫發呆、胡思亂想。

passages.original: Remember that.
passages.vernacular: 記住呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 記住這個。

passages.original: Take that card and come right to the kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 攞住嗰張卡片,直接到廚房嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿著那張卡片,直接到廚房來。

passages.original: Now, sit down in the corner and learn that prayer off by heart.”
passages.vernacular: 而家,坐到角落裡,把嗰篇禱文背下嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,坐到角落裡,把那篇禱文背下來。」

passages.original: Anne set the card up against the jugful of apple blossoms she had brought in to decorate the dinner table--Marilla had eyed that decoration askance, but had said nothing--propped her chin on her hands, and fell to studying it intently for several silent minutes.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把卡片靠喺佢帶進嚟裝飾午餐桌嘅嗰罐蘋果花上——瑪麗拉曾斜眼睇過嗰件裝飾,但乜嘢都冇講——用雙手托住下巴,默默地專注地研讀咗幾分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把卡片靠在她帶進來裝飾午餐桌的那罐蘋果花上——瑪麗拉曾斜眼看過那件裝飾,但什麼也沒說——用雙手托著下巴,默默地專注地研讀了幾分鐘。

passages.original: “I like this,” she announced at length.
passages.vernacular: 「我鍾意呢個,」佢終於宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我喜歡這個,」她終於宣布。

passages.original: “It’s beautiful.
passages.vernacular: 「真美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真美。

passages.original: I’ve heard it before--I heard the superintendent of the asylum Sunday-school say it over once.
passages.vernacular: 我以前聽過——我聽孤兒院主日學校嘅校長念過一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以前聽過——我聽孤兒院主日學校的校長念過一遍。

passages.original: But I didn’t like it then.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰時我不鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那時我不喜歡。

passages.original: He had such a cracked voice and he prayed it so mournfully.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅聲音咁嘶啞,念得咁悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的聲音那麼嘶啞,念得那麼悲傷。

passages.original: I really felt sure he thought praying was a disagreeable duty.
passages.vernacular: 我真覺得佢認為禱告係一件討厭嘅義務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真覺得他認為禱告是一件討厭的義務。

passages.original: This isn’t poetry, but it makes me feel just the same way poetry does.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係詩,但佢畀我嘅感覺同詩畀我嘅一模一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是詩,但它給我的感覺和詩給我的一模一樣。

passages.original: ‘Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name.’
passages.vernacular: 『我哋喺天上嘅父,願人都尊祢嘅名為聖。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『我們在天上的父,願人都尊祢的名為聖。』

passages.original: That is just like a line of music.
passages.vernacular: 呢簡直像一句音樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這簡直像一句音樂。

passages.original: Oh, I’m so glad you thought of making me learn this, Miss--Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我太高興您想到讓我學呢個,卡思伯特小姐——瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我太高興您想到讓我學這個,卡思伯特小姐——瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: “Well, learn it and hold your tongue,” said Marilla shortly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就學吧,閉上嘴,」瑪麗拉簡短地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就學吧,閉上嘴,」瑪麗拉簡短地說。

passages.original: Anne tipped the vase of apple blossoms near enough to bestow a soft kiss on a pink-cupped bud, and then studied diligently for some moments longer.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把嗰瓶蘋果花傾過去,足以畀一朵粉紅杯狀嘅花蕾一個輕柔嘅吻,然後又勤奮地學咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把那瓶蘋果花傾過去,足以給一朵粉紅杯狀的花蕾一個輕柔的吻,然後又勤奮地學了一會兒。

passages.original: “Marilla,” she demanded presently, “do you think that I shall ever have a bosom friend in Avonlea?”
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉,」佢不久後問,「您覺得我喺阿文利會有一個知心朋友嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉,」她不久後問,「您覺得我在阿文利會有一個知心朋友嗎?」

passages.original: “A--a what kind of friend?”
passages.vernacular: 「一個——邊種朋友?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個——哪種朋友?」

passages.original: “A bosom friend--an intimate friend, you know--a really kindred spirit to whom I can confide my inmost soul.
passages.vernacular: 「知心朋友——親密嘅朋友,您知道——一個真正志同道合、我能向佢傾訴我內心深處嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「知心朋友——親密的朋友,您知道——一個真正志同道合、我能向她傾訴我內心深處的朋友。

passages.original: I’ve dreamed of meeting her all my life.
passages.vernacular: 我一輩子都夢想住遇見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一輩子都夢想著遇見她。

passages.original: I never really supposed I would, but so many of my loveliest dreams have come true all at once that perhaps this one will, too.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇真嘅指望過,但我咁多最可愛嘅夢想一下子都實現喇,或者呢個都會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒真的指望過,但我那麼多最可愛的夢想一下子都實現了,也許這個也會。

passages.original: Do you think it’s possible?”
passages.vernacular: 您覺得有可能嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您覺得有可能嗎?」

passages.original: “Diana Barry lives over at Orchard Slope and she’s about your age.
passages.vernacular: 「黛安娜·巴里住喺果園坡,年紀跟你差不多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黛安娜·巴里住在果園坡,年紀跟你差不多。

passages.original: She’s a very nice little girl, and perhaps she will be a playmate for you when she comes home.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個好好嘅小女孩,或者等佢回家,會成為你嘅玩伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個很好的小女孩,也許等她回家,會成為你的玩伴。

passages.original: She’s visiting her aunt over at Carmody just now.
passages.vernacular: 佢眼下喺卡莫迪佢姨媽嗰兒做客。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她眼下在卡莫迪她姨媽那兒做客。

passages.original: You’ll have to be careful how you behave yourself, though.
passages.vernacular: 不過你得小心你嘅言行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過你得小心你的言行。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry is a very particular woman.
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太係個好挑剔嘅女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太是個很挑剔的女人。

passages.original: She won’t let Diana play with any little girl who isn’t nice and good.”
passages.vernacular: 佢唔會讓黛安娜跟任何不好不乖嘅小女孩玩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不會讓黛安娜跟任何不好不乖的小女孩玩。」

passages.original: Anne looked at Marilla through the apple blossoms, her eyes aglow with interest.
passages.vernacular: 安妮透過蘋果花睇住瑪麗拉,眼睛閃耀住興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮透過蘋果花看著瑪麗拉,眼睛閃耀著興趣。

passages.original: “What is Diana like?
passages.vernacular: 「黛安娜係乜嘢樣嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黛安娜是什麼樣的?

passages.original: Her hair isn’t red, is it?
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅頭髮唔係紅嘅,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的頭髮不是紅的,是不是?

passages.original: Oh, I hope not.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我希望唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我希望不是。

passages.original: It’s bad enough to have red hair myself, but I positively couldn’t endure it in a bosom friend.”
passages.vernacular: 我自己有紅頭髮已經夠糟嘅喇,但我絕對無法忍受知心朋友都咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己有紅頭髮已經夠糟的了,但我絕對無法忍受知心朋友也這樣。」

passages.original: “Diana is a very pretty little girl.
passages.vernacular: 「黛安娜係個好漂亮嘅小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黛安娜是個非常漂亮的小女孩。

passages.original: She has black eyes and hair and rosy cheeks.
passages.vernacular: 佢有黑眼睛、黑頭髮同紅潤嘅臉頰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有黑眼睛、黑頭髮和紅潤的臉頰。

passages.original: And she is good and smart, which is better than being pretty.”
passages.vernacular: 而且佢又乖又聰明,呢比漂亮仲好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且她又乖又聰明,這比漂亮還好。」

passages.original: Marilla was as fond of morals as the Duchess in Wonderland, and was firmly convinced that one should be tacked on to every remark made to a child who was being brought up.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉像仙境中嘅公爵夫人一樣鍾意訓誡,而且堅信對一個正在被教養嘅細路講嘅每句話後面,都應該附上一句訓誡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉像仙境中的公爵夫人一樣喜歡訓誡,而且堅信對一個正在被教養的孩子說的每句話後面,都應該附上一句訓誡。

passages.original: But Anne waved the moral inconsequently aside and seized only on the delightful possibilities before it.
passages.vernacular: 但安妮漫不經心地把訓誡揮到一邊,只抓住咗佢前面嗰令人愉快嘅可能性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安妮漫不經心地把訓誡揮到一邊,只抓住了它前面那令人愉快的可能性。

passages.original: “Oh, I’m so glad she’s pretty.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我太高興佢漂亮喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我太高興她漂亮了。

passages.original: Next to being beautiful oneself--and that’s impossible in my case--it would be best to have a beautiful bosom friend.
passages.vernacular: 除咗自己美麗——喺我呢情況嗰個係唔可能嘅——最好嘅就係有一個美麗嘅知心朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了自己美麗——在我這情況那是不可能的——最好的就是有一個美麗的知心朋友。

passages.original: When I lived with Mrs. Thomas she had a bookcase in her sitting room with glass doors.
passages.vernacular: 我同托馬斯太太住喺一起嘅時候,佢嘅起居室裡有一個帶玻璃門嘅書櫃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我和托馬斯太太住在一起的時候,她的起居室裡有一個帶玻璃門的書櫃。

passages.original: There weren’t any books in it; Mrs. Thomas kept her best china and her preserves there--when she had any preserves to keep.
passages.vernacular: 裡面冇書;托馬斯太太把佢最好嘅瓷器同佢嘅蜜餞放喺裡面——當佢有蜜餞要放嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 裡面沒有書;托馬斯太太把她最好的瓷器和她的蜜餞放在裡面——當她有蜜餞要放的時候。

passages.original: One of the doors was broken.
passages.vernacular: 其中一扇門係壞嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中一扇門是壞的。

passages.original: Mr. Thomas smashed it one night when he was slightly intoxicated.
passages.vernacular: 托馬斯先生有天夜裡飲得有點醉,把佢砸碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 托馬斯先生有天夜裡喝得有點醉,把它砸碎了。

passages.original: But the other was whole and I used to pretend that my reflection in it was another little girl who lived in it.
passages.vernacular: 但另一扇係完整嘅,我常假裝我喺裡面嘅倒影係另一個住喺裡面嘅小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但另一扇是完整的,我常假裝我在裡面的倒影是另一個住在裡面的小女孩。

passages.original: I called her Katie Maurice, and we were very intimate.
passages.vernacular: 我叫佢凱蒂·莫里斯,我哋好親密。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫她凱蒂·莫里斯,我們非常親密。

passages.original: I used to talk to her by the hour, especially on Sunday, and tell her everything.
passages.vernacular: 我常常一連幾個鐘頭跟佢講話,特別係星期天,乜嘢都告訴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我常常一連幾個鐘頭跟她說話,特別是星期天,什麼都告訴她。

passages.original: Katie was the comfort and consolation of my life.
passages.vernacular: 凱蒂係我生活中嘅安慰同慰藉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱蒂是我生活中的安慰和慰藉。

passages.original: We used to pretend that the bookcase was enchanted and that if I only knew the spell I could open the door and step right into the room where Katie Maurice lived, instead of into Mrs. Thomas’ shelves of preserves and china.
passages.vernacular: 我哋常假裝呢個書櫃係被施咗魔法嘅,如果我知道咒語,我就能打開門,一步走進凱蒂·莫里斯住嘅房間,而唔係托馬斯太太嗰一架蜜餞同瓷器。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們常假裝這個書櫃是被施了魔法的,如果我知道咒語,我就能打開門,一步走進凱蒂·莫里斯住的房間,而不是托馬斯太太那一架蜜餞和瓷器。

passages.original: And then Katie Maurice would have taken me by the hand and led me out into a wonderful place, all flowers and sunshine and fairies, and we would have lived there happy for ever after.
passages.vernacular: 然後凱蒂·莫里斯就會拉住我嘅手,領我走進一個美妙嘅地方,到處係鮮花、陽光同仙女,我哋會喺嗰度幸福地生活直到永遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後凱蒂·莫里斯就會拉著我的手,領我走進一個美妙的地方,到處是鮮花、陽光和仙女,我們會在那裡幸福地生活直到永遠。

passages.original: When I went to live with Mrs. Hammond it just broke my heart to leave Katie Maurice.
passages.vernacular: 我去同哈蒙德太太住嘅時候,離開凱蒂·莫里斯,真嘅讓我心都碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去和哈蒙德太太住的時候,離開凱蒂·莫里斯,真的讓我心都碎了。

passages.original: She felt it dreadfully, too, I know she did, for she was crying when she kissed me good-bye through the bookcase door.
passages.vernacular: 佢都一定感到好難過,我知道佢難過,因為佢隔住書櫃門吻我告別時喺哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也一定感到非常難過,我知道她難過,因為她隔著書櫃門吻我告別時在哭。

passages.original: There was no bookcase at Mrs. Hammond’s.
passages.vernacular: 哈蒙德太太家冇書櫃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈蒙德太太家沒有書櫃。

passages.original: But just up the river a little way from the house there was a long green little valley, and the loveliest echo lived there.
passages.vernacular: 但離房子沿河上游不遠嘅地方,有一條綠色嘅長長小山谷,嗰度住最可愛嘅回聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但離房子沿河上游不遠的地方,有一條綠色的長長小山谷,那裡住著最可愛的回聲。

passages.original: It echoed back every word you said, even if you didn’t talk a bit loud.
passages.vernacular: 你講嘅每個字佢都回應,即使你講得啲都不大聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說的每個字它都回應,即使你說得一點也不大聲。

passages.original: So I imagined that it was a little girl called Violetta and we were great friends and I loved her almost as well as I loved Katie Maurice--not quite, but almost, you know.
passages.vernacular: 所以我想像佢係一個叫維奧萊塔嘅小女孩,我哋係好朋友,我愛佢幾乎同愛凱蒂·莫里斯一樣——不完全,但幾乎,您知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我想像它是一個叫維奧萊塔的小女孩,我們是好朋友,我愛她幾乎和愛凱蒂·莫里斯一樣——不完全,但幾乎,您知道。

passages.original: The night before I went to the asylum I said good-bye to Violetta, and oh, her good-bye came back to me in such sad, sad tones.
passages.vernacular: 去孤兒院嘅前一晚,我跟維奧萊塔道咗別,哦,佢嘅告別回應畀我嘅聲音咁悲傷、悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去孤兒院的前一晚,我跟維奧萊塔道了別,哦,她的告別回應給我的聲音那麼悲傷、悲傷。

passages.original: I had become so attached to her that I hadn’t the heart to imagine a bosom friend at the asylum, even if there had been any scope for imagination there.”
passages.vernacular: 我對佢係咁依戀,所以喺孤兒院我冇心思再想像一個知心朋友,儘管嗰兒都冇乜嘢想像嘅餘地。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對她是那麼依戀,所以在孤兒院我沒有心思再想像一個知心朋友,儘管那兒也沒有什麼想像的餘地。」

passages.original: “I think it’s just as well there wasn’t,” said Marilla drily.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇冇都好,」瑪麗拉冷冷地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看沒有也好,」瑪麗拉冷冷地說。

passages.original: “I don’t approve of such goings-on.
passages.vernacular: 「我不贊成呢種行為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不贊成這種行為。

passages.original: You seem to half believe your own imaginations.
passages.vernacular: 你似乎有一半相信自己嘅想像。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你似乎有一半相信自己的想像。

passages.original: It will be well for you to have a real live friend to put such nonsense out of your head.
passages.vernacular: 有一個真正活生生嘅朋友,把呢種胡思亂想從你腦子裡趕走,對你有好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一個真正活生生的朋友,把這種胡思亂想從你腦子裡趕走,對你有好處。

passages.original: But don’t let Mrs. Barry hear you talking about your Katie Maurices and your Violettas or she’ll think you tell stories.”
passages.vernacular: 但唔好畀巴里太太聽到你談你嘅凱蒂·莫里斯同維奧萊塔,否則佢會認為你喺編故事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但別讓巴里太太聽到你談你的凱蒂·莫里斯和維奧萊塔,否則她會認為你在編故事。」

passages.original: “Oh, I won’t.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我不會。

passages.original: I couldn’t talk of them to everybody--their memories are too sacred for that.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠跟每個人談佢哋——佢哋嘅記憶太神聖喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能跟每個人談她們——她們的記憶太神聖了。

passages.original: But I thought I’d like to have you know about them.
passages.vernacular: 但我想讓您知道佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我想讓您知道她們。

passages.original: Oh, look, here’s a big bee just tumbled out of an apple blossom.
passages.vernacular: 哦,睇,一隻大蜜蜂剛從一朵蘋果花裡滾咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,看,一隻大蜜蜂剛從一朵蘋果花裡滾了出來。

passages.original: Just think what a lovely place to live--in an apple blossom!
passages.vernacular: 想想睇,住喺蘋果花裡,多可愛嘅地方啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想想看,住在蘋果花裡,多可愛的地方啊!

passages.original: Fancy going to sleep in it when the wind was rocking it.
passages.vernacular: 想像喺風搖住佢嘅時候瞓喺裡面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想像在風搖著它的時候睡在裡面。

passages.original: If I wasn’t a human girl I think I’d like to be a bee and live among the flowers.”
passages.vernacular: 如果我唔係人類女孩,我想我會想做一隻蜜蜂,住喺花叢中。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我不是人類女孩,我想我會想做一隻蜜蜂,住在花叢中。」

passages.original: “Yesterday you wanted to be a sea-gull,” sniffed Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「尋日你仲想做海鷗呢,」瑪麗拉嗤之以鼻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「昨天你還想做海鷗呢,」瑪麗拉嗤之以鼻。

passages.original: “I think you are very fickle minded.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇你呢人三心二意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看你這人三心二意。

passages.original: I told you to learn that prayer and not talk.
passages.vernacular: 我讓你背嗰篇禱文,唔係讓你講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讓你背那篇禱文,不是讓你說話。

passages.original: But it seems impossible for you to stop talking if you’ve got anybody that will listen to you.
passages.vernacular: 但係只要有邊個肯聽你,你似乎就唔可能停止講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是只要有誰肯聽你,你似乎就不可能停止說話。

passages.original: So go up to your room and learn it.”
passages.vernacular: 所以回你房間去背吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以回你房間去背吧。」

passages.original: “Oh, I know it pretty nearly all now--all but just the last line.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我而家差不多全會喇——只剩最後一行喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我現在差不多全會了——只剩最後一行了。」

passages.original: “Well, never mind, do as I tell you.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,別管喇,照我講嘅做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,別管了,照我說的做。

passages.original: Go to your room and finish learning it well, and stay there until I call you down to help me get tea.”
passages.vernacular: 回你房間去把佢背熟,待喺嗰度,直到我叫你下嚟幫我準備茶點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回你房間去把它背熟,待在那裡,直到我叫你下來幫我準備茶點。」

passages.original: “Can I take the apple blossoms with me for company?” pleaded Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我能把蘋果花帶到房間裡作伴嗎?」安妮懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我能把蘋果花帶到房間裡作伴嗎?」安妮懇求道。

passages.original: “No; you don’t want your room cluttered up with flowers.
passages.vernacular: 「不行;你唔想你嘅房間被花弄得雜亂不堪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不行;你不想你的房間被花弄得雜亂不堪。

passages.original: You should have left them on the tree in the first place.”
passages.vernacular: 你一開始就該把佢哋留喺樹上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一開始就該把它們留在樹上。」

passages.original: “I did feel a little that way, too,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我都有點咁覺得,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也有點那麼覺得,」安妮說。

passages.original: “I kind of felt I shouldn’t shorten their lovely lives by picking them--I wouldn’t want to be picked if I were an apple blossom.
passages.vernacular: 「我有點覺得不該摘下佢哋縮短佢哋可愛嘅生命——如果我係一朵蘋果花,我唔願意被摘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有點覺得不該摘下它們縮短它們可愛的生命——如果我是一朵蘋果花,我不願意被摘。

passages.original: But the temptation was irresistible.
passages.vernacular: 但誘惑無法抗拒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但誘惑無法抗拒。

passages.original: What do you do when you meet with an irresistible temptation?”
passages.vernacular: 當您遇到無法抗拒嘅誘惑時,您點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當您遇到無法抗拒的誘惑時,您怎麼辦?」

passages.original: “Anne, did you hear me tell you to go to your room?”
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,你聽見我叫你回房間咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,你聽見我叫你回房間了嗎?」

passages.original: Anne sighed, retreated to the east gable, and sat down in a chair by the window.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘆咗口氣,退到東山牆房間,坐喺窗邊嘅一把椅子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮嘆了口氣,退到東山牆房間,坐在窗邊的一把椅子上。

passages.original: “There--I know this prayer.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇——我會背呢篇禱文喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了——我會背這篇禱文了。

passages.original: I learned that last sentence coming upstairs.
passages.vernacular: 上樓嘅時候我學會咗最後一句。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上樓的時候我學會了最後一句。

passages.original: Now I’m going to imagine things into this room so that they’ll always stay imagined.
passages.vernacular: 而家我要把啲嘢想像進呢個房間,讓佢哋永遠留喺想像裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我要把一些東西想像進這個房間,讓它們永遠留在想像裡。

passages.original: The floor is covered with a white velvet carpet with pink roses all over it and there are pink silk curtains at the windows.
passages.vernacular: 地板上鋪住白色天鵝絨地毯,上面滿係粉紅玫瑰,窗上掛住粉紅絲綢窗簾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 地板上鋪著白色天鵝絨地毯,上面滿是粉紅玫瑰,窗上掛著粉紅絲綢窗簾。

passages.original: The walls are hung with gold and silver brocade tapestry.
passages.vernacular: 牆上掛住金銀錦緞掛毯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牆上掛著金銀錦緞掛毯。

passages.original: The furniture is mahogany.
passages.vernacular: 傢俱係桃花心木嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傢俱是桃花心木的。

passages.original: I never saw any mahogany, but it does sound so luxurious.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過桃花心木,但聽起嚟真奢華。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過桃花心木,但聽起來真奢華。

passages.original: This is a couch all heaped with gorgeous silken cushions, pink and blue and crimson and gold, and I am reclining gracefully on it.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一張沙發,堆滿咗華麗嘅絲綢墊子,粉紅嘅、藍嘅、深紅嘅、金色嘅,我優雅地斜倚喺上面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一張沙發,堆滿了華麗的絲綢墊子,粉紅的、藍的、深紅的、金色的,我優雅地斜倚在上面。

passages.original: I can see my reflection in that splendid big mirror hanging on the wall.
passages.vernacular: 我可以喺掛喺牆上嘅嗰面壯觀嘅大鏡子裡睇到自己嘅倒影。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以在掛在牆上的那面壯觀的大鏡子裡看到自己的倒影。

passages.original: I am tall and regal, clad in a gown of trailing white lace, with a pearl cross on my breast and pearls in my hair.
passages.vernacular: 我身材高挑,儀態高貴,身穿一件拖地嘅白色蕾絲長裙,胸前掛住一個珍珠十字架,頭髮上綴住珍珠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我身材高挑,儀態高貴,身穿一件拖地的白色蕾絲長裙,胸前掛著一個珍珠十字架,頭髮上綴著珍珠。

passages.original: My hair is of midnight darkness and my skin is a clear ivory pallor.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅頭髮像午夜般漆黑,皮膚係潔淨嘅象牙般蒼白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的頭髮像午夜般漆黑,皮膚是潔淨的象牙般蒼白。

passages.original: My name is the Lady Cordelia Fitzgerald.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅名字係科黛莉亞·菲茨傑拉德夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的名字是科黛莉亞·菲茨傑拉德夫人。

passages.original: No, it isn’t--I can’t make that seem real.”
passages.vernacular: 不,唔係——我冇法讓佢顯得真實。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,不是——我沒法讓它顯得真實。」

passages.original: She danced up to the little looking-glass and peered into it.
passages.vernacular: 佢舞動住跳到小鏡子前,向裡窺望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她舞動著跳到小鏡子前,向裡窺望。

passages.original: Her pointed freckled face and solemn gray eyes peered back at her.
passages.vernacular: 一張尖尖嘅、長滿雀斑嘅臉同一雙嚴肅嘅灰眼睛回望住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一張尖尖的、長滿雀斑的臉和一雙嚴肅的灰眼睛回望著她。

passages.original: “You’re only Anne of Green Gables,” she said earnestly, “and I see you, just as you are looking now, whenever I try to imagine I’m the Lady Cordelia.
passages.vernacular: 「你不過係綠色屋頂嘅安妮,」佢認真地講,「每當我試圖想像我係科黛莉亞夫人時,我睇到嘅就係而家呢個樣子嘅你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不過是綠色屋頂的安妮,」她認真地說,「每當我試圖想像我是科黛莉亞夫人時,我看到的就是現在這個樣子的你。

passages.original: But it’s a million times nicer to be Anne of Green Gables than Anne of nowhere in particular, isn’t it?”
passages.vernacular: 但係做綠色屋頂嘅安妮,比做一個無處可歸嘅安妮,要好一百萬倍,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是做綠色屋頂的安妮,比做一個無處可歸的安妮,要好一百萬倍,是不是?」

passages.original: She bent forward, kissed her reflection affectionately, and betook herself to the open window.
passages.vernacular: 佢俯身向前,深情地吻咗吻自己嘅倒影,然後走到敞開嘅窗前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她俯身向前,深情地吻了吻自己的倒影,然後走到敞開的窗前。

passages.original: “Dear Snow Queen, good afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅雪之女王,下午好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的雪之女王,下午好。

passages.original: And good afternoon, dear birches down in the hollow.
passages.vernacular: 仲有窪地裡親愛嘅白樺哋,下午好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有窪地裡親愛的白樺們,下午好。

passages.original: And good afternoon, dear gray house up on the hill.
passages.vernacular: 仲有山上親愛嘅灰房子,下午好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有山上親愛的灰房子,下午好。

passages.original: I wonder if Diana is to be my bosom friend.
passages.vernacular: 我想知道黛安娜係唔係我嘅知心朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想知道黛安娜是不是我的知心朋友。

passages.original: I hope she will, and I shall love her very much.
passages.vernacular: 我希望係,我會好愛佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望是,我會非常愛她。

passages.original: But I must never quite forget Katie Maurice and Violetta.
passages.vernacular: 但我決唔能夠完全忘記凱蒂·莫里斯同維奧萊塔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我決不能完全忘記凱蒂·莫里斯和維奧萊塔。

passages.original: They would feel so hurt if I did and I’d hate to hurt anybody’s feelings, even a little bookcase girl’s or a little echo girl’s.
passages.vernacular: 如果我嗰樣做,佢哋會幾咁受傷,我唔想傷害任何人嘅感情,即使係一個小書櫃女孩或一個小回聲女孩嘅感情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我那樣做,她們會多麼受傷,我不想傷害任何人的感情,即使是一個小書櫃女孩或一個小回聲女孩的感情。

passages.original: I must be careful to remember them and send them a kiss every day.”
passages.vernacular: 我必須小心地記住佢哋,每天畀佢哋送一個吻。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須小心地記著她們,每天給她們送一個吻。」

passages.original: Anne blew a couple of airy kisses from her fingertips past the cherry blossoms and then, with her chin in her hands, drifted luxuriously out on a sea of daydreams.
passages.vernacular: 安妮從指尖朝櫻花吹咗兩個輕飄飄嘅吻,然後,下巴託喺手裡,舒服地漂進咗白日夢嘅海洋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮從指尖朝櫻花吹了兩個輕飄飄的吻,然後,下巴託在手裡,舒服地漂進了白日夢的海洋。

chapters.title: Ch. IX Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified 第九章:雷切爾·林德太太驚駭萬分

passages.original: CH ANNE had been a fortnight at Green Gables before Mrs. Lynde arrived to inspect her.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺綠色屋頂住咗兩個星期,林德太太才嚟查睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在綠色屋頂住了兩個星期,林德太太才來查看她。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel, to do her justice, was not to blame for this.
passages.vernacular: 講句公道話,呢唔能夠怪雷切爾太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說句公道話,這不能怪雷切爾太太。

passages.original: A severe and unseasonable attack of grippe had confined that good lady to her house ever since the occasion of her last visit to Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 自從上次拜訪綠色屋頂以來,一場嚴重而不合時令嘅流感,就把呢位好太太關喺咗家裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從上次拜訪綠色屋頂以來,一場嚴重而不合時令的流感,就把這位好太太關在了家裡。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel was not often sick and had a well-defined contempt for people who were; but grippe, she asserted, was like no other illness on earth and could only be interpreted as one of the special visitations of Providence.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太好少生病,而且對生病嘅人有住明確嘅蔑視;可佢斷言,流感跟世上任何其他疾病都不同,只能理解為上天特別嘅降罰之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太很少生病,而且對生病的人有著明確的蔑視;可她斷言,流感跟世上任何其他疾病都不同,只能理解為上天特別的降罰之一。

passages.original: As soon as her doctor allowed her to put her foot out-of-doors she hurried up to Green Gables, bursting with curiosity to see Matthew and Marilla’s orphan, concerning whom all sorts of stories and suppositions had gone abroad in Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 醫生一准許佢出門,佢就急忙趕到綠色屋頂,急得要命地想見見馬修同瑪麗拉嘅孤兒,關於佢,阿文利已經傳開咗各種各樣嘅故事同猜測。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生一准許她出門,她就急忙趕到綠色屋頂,急得要命地想見見馬修和瑪麗拉的孤兒,關於她,阿文利已經傳開了各種各樣的故事和猜測。

passages.original: Anne had made good use of every waking moment of that fortnight.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把嗰兩個星期裡每一個醒住嘅時刻都利用得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把那兩個星期裡每一個醒著的時刻都利用得很好。

passages.original: Already she was acquainted with every tree and shrub about the place.
passages.vernacular: 佢已經熟悉咗周圍每一棵樹同每一叢灌木。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她已經熟悉了周圍每一棵樹和每一叢灌木。

passages.original: She had discovered that a lane opened out below the apple orchard and ran up through a belt of woodland; and she had explored it to its furthest end in all its delicious vagaries of brook and bridge, fir coppice and wild cherry arch, corners thick with fern, and branching byways of maple and mountain ash.
passages.vernacular: 佢發現蘋果園下面有一條小路,穿過一帶林地蜿蜒向上;佢一直探索到小路最遠嘅盡頭,探索咗佢所有迷人嘅曲折:小溪同小橋、冷杉叢林同野櫻桃拱門、長滿蕨類嘅拐角,以及楓樹同花楸樹嘅岔路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她發現蘋果園下面有一條小路,穿過一帶林地蜿蜒向上;她一直探索到小路最遠的盡頭,探索了它所有迷人的曲折:小溪和小橋、冷杉叢林和野櫻桃拱門、長滿蕨類的拐角,以及楓樹和花楸樹的岔路。

passages.original: She had made friends with the spring down in the hollow--that wonderful deep, clear icy-cold spring; it was set about with smooth red sandstones and rimmed in by great palm-like clumps of water fern; and beyond it was a log bridge over the brook.
passages.vernacular: 佢同窪地裡嘅泉水成咗朋友——嗰眼奇妙嘅、深邃、清澈、冰涼嘅泉;佢四周圍住光滑嘅紅砂岩,邊緣環繞住像棕櫚一樣嘅大叢水蕨;泉水嗰邊有一座橫跨小溪嘅原木橋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她和窪地裡的泉水成了朋友——那眼奇妙的、深邃、清澈、冰涼的泉;它四周圍著光滑的紅砂岩,邊緣環繞著像棕櫚一樣的大叢水蕨;泉水那邊有一座橫跨小溪的原木橋。

passages.original: That bridge led Anne’s dancing feet up over a wooded hill beyond, where perpetual twilight reigned under the straight, thick-growing firs and spruces; the only flowers there were myriads of delicate “June bells,” those shyest and sweetest of woodland blooms, and a few pale, aerial starflowers, like the spirits of last year’s blossoms.
passages.vernacular: 嗰座橋把安妮跳舞般嘅腳步領上咗對面一座樹木蔥蘢嘅山丘,嗰度直直生長嘅茂密冷杉同雲杉下,永遠係暮色蒼茫;嗰度唯一嘅花,係無數嬌嫩嘅「六月鈴」,嗰最羞怯、最甜美嘅林間花朵,仲有幾朵蒼白、空靈嘅星花,像去年花朵嘅魂魄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那座橋把安妮跳舞般的腳步領上了對面一座樹木蔥蘢的山丘,那裡直直生長的茂密冷杉和雲杉下,永遠是暮色蒼茫;那裡唯一的花,是無數嬌嫩的「六月鈴」,那最羞怯、最甜美的林間花朵,還有幾朵蒼白、空靈的星花,像去年花朵的魂魄。

passages.original: Gossamers glimmered like threads of silver among the trees and the fir boughs and tassels seemed to utter friendly speech.
passages.vernacular: 游絲像銀線一樣喺樹間閃爍,冷杉嘅枝條同流蘇似乎喺講住友好嘅話語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 游絲像銀線一樣在樹間閃爍,冷杉的枝條和流蘇似乎在說著友好的話語。

passages.original: All these raptured voyages of exploration were made in the odd half hours which she was allowed for play, and Anne talked Matthew and Marilla half-deaf over her discoveries.
passages.vernacular: 所有呢啲心醉神迷嘅探險,都係喺允許佢玩耍嘅零碎半小時裡完成嘅,安妮把佢嘅發現講得馬修同瑪麗拉耳朵都快聾喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有這些心醉神迷的探險,都是在允許她玩耍的零碎半小時裡完成的,安妮把她的發現說得馬修和瑪麗拉耳朵都快聾了。

passages.original: Not that Matthew complained, to be sure; he listened to it all with a wordless smile of enjoyment on his face; Marilla permitted the “chatter” until she found herself becoming too interested in it, whereupon she always promptly quenched Anne by a curt command to hold her tongue.
passages.vernacular: 當然,馬修冇抱怨;佢帶住無言嘅享受嘅微笑聽住呢一切;瑪麗拉容許呢種「嘮叨」,直到佢發覺自己對佢太感興趣喇,於是佢總是即刻用一句簡短嘅命令讓安妮閉嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,馬修沒有抱怨;他帶著無言的享受的微笑聽著這一切;瑪麗拉容許這種「嘮叨」,直到她發覺自己對它太感興趣了,於是她總是立刻用一句簡短的命令讓安妮閉嘴。

passages.original: Anne was out in the orchard when Mrs. Rachel came, wandering at her own sweet will through the lush, tremulous grasses splashed with ruddy evening sunshine; so that good lady had an excellent chance to talk her illness fully over, describing every ache and pulse beat with such evident enjoyment that Marilla thought even grippe must bring its compensations.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太嚟嘅時候,安妮正在果園裡,隨心所欲地漫遊喺被暮色殷紅嘅陽光濺染嘅、茂盛顫動嘅草叢中;所以呢位好太太有極好嘅機會把佢嘅病徹底談個透,描述每一次疼痛同每一下脈搏,顯然津津有味,以至於瑪麗拉覺得連流感都一定有佢嘅補償。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太來的時候,安妮正在果園裡,隨心所欲地漫遊在被暮色殷紅的陽光濺染的、茂盛顫動的草叢中;所以這位好太太有極好的機會把她的病徹底談個透,描述每一次疼痛和每一下脈搏,顯然津津有味,以至於瑪麗拉覺得連流感也一定有它的補償。

passages.original: When details were exhausted Mrs. Rachel introduced the real reason of her call.
passages.vernacular: 等細節講完喇,雷切爾太太才提出此行嘅真正原因。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等細節說完了,雷切爾太太才提出此行的真正原因。

passages.original: “I’ve been hearing some surprising things about you and Matthew.”
passages.vernacular: 「我聽到啲關於你同馬修嘅驚人消息。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我聽到一些關於你和馬修的驚人消息。」

passages.original: “I don’t suppose you are any more surprised than I am myself,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你唔會比我自己更食驚,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你不會比我自己更吃驚,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “I’m getting over my surprise now.”
passages.vernacular: 「我而家已經緩過驚嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在已經緩過驚來了。」

passages.original: “It was too bad there was such a mistake,” said Mrs. Rachel sympathetically.
passages.vernacular: 「出咗咁樣嘅差錯真糟糕,」雷切爾太太同情地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「出了這樣的差錯真糟糕,」雷切爾太太同情地說。

passages.original: “Couldn’t you have sent her back?”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋就唔能夠把佢送回去嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們就不能把她送回去嗎?」

passages.original: “I suppose we could, but we decided not to.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我哋可以,但我哋決定不送。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我們可以,但我們決定不送。

passages.original: Matthew took a fancy to her.
passages.vernacular: 馬修鍾意上佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修喜歡上她了。

passages.original: And I must say I like her myself--although I admit she has her faults.
passages.vernacular: 我必須講,我自己都鍾意佢——儘管我承認佢有缺點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須說,我自己也喜歡她——儘管我承認她有缺點。

passages.original: The house seems a different place already.
passages.vernacular: 呢座房子似乎已經變咗個樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這座房子似乎已經變了個樣子。

passages.original: She’s a real bright little thing.”
passages.vernacular: 佢係個真聰明伶俐嘅小傢伙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個真聰明伶俐的小傢伙。」

passages.original: Marilla said more than she had intended to say when she began, for she read disapproval in Mrs. Rachel’s expression.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉講得比佢開始時打算講嘅要多,因為佢從雷切爾太太嘅表情裡讀出咗不贊成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉說得比她開始時打算說的要多,因為她從雷切爾太太的表情裡讀出了不贊成。

passages.original: “It’s a great responsibility you’ve taken on yourself,” said that lady gloomily, “especially when you’ve never had any experience with children.
passages.vernacular: 「你畀自己擔上咗好大嘅責任,」嗰位太太陰鬱地講,「尤其係你從冇過帶細路嘅經驗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你給自己擔上了很大的責任,」那位太太陰鬱地說,「尤其是你從沒有過帶孩子的經驗。

passages.original: You don’t know much about her or her real disposition, I suppose, and there’s no guessing how a child like that will turn out.
passages.vernacular: 我想你對佢同佢真正嘅性情了解不多,而且冇法猜咁樣嘅細路會變成乜嘢樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你對她和她真正的性情了解不多,而且沒法猜這樣的孩子會變成什麼樣。

passages.original: But I don’t want to discourage you I’m sure, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 不過我當然唔想讓你灰心,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我當然不想讓你灰心,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: “I’m not feeling discouraged,” was Marilla’s dry response, “when I make up my mind to do a thing it stays made up.
passages.vernacular: 「我不覺得灰心,」瑪麗拉乾巴巴地回答,「我打定主意要做嘅事,就係打定喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不覺得灰心,」瑪麗拉乾巴巴地回答,「我打定主意要做的事,就是打定了。

passages.original: I suppose you’d like to see Anne.
passages.vernacular: 我想你想見見安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你想見見安妮。

passages.original: I’ll call her in.”
passages.vernacular: 我叫佢進嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫她進來。」

passages.original: Anne came running in presently, her face sparkling with the delight of her orchard rovings; but, abashed at finding the delight herself in the unexpected presence of a stranger, she halted confusedly inside the door.
passages.vernacular: 安妮不一會兒就跑咗進嚟,臉上因果園漫遊嘅喜悅而閃閃發光;但發現自己嘅喜悅喺一個陌生人意外在場時,佢窘迫地喺門內慌亂地停住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮不一會兒就跑了進來,臉上因果園漫遊的喜悅而閃閃發光;但發現自己的喜悅在一個陌生人意外在場時,她窘迫地在門內慌亂地停住了。

passages.original: She certainly was an odd-looking little creature in the short tight wincey dress she had worn from the asylum, below which her thin legs seemed ungracefully long.
passages.vernacular: 佢穿住從孤兒院穿嚟嘅嗰件又短又緊嘅棉毛混紡裙,下面佢嗰細瘦嘅腿顯得難睇地長,確實係個樣子古怪嘅小嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她穿著從孤兒院穿來的那件又短又緊的棉毛混紡裙,下面她那細瘦的腿顯得難看地長,確實是個樣子古怪的小東西。

passages.original: Her freckles were more numerous and obtrusive than ever; the wind had ruffled her hatless hair into over-brilliant disorder; it had never looked redder than at that moment.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅雀斑比以往任何時候都更多更顯眼;風把佢冇戴帽子嘅頭髮吹得亂得過分地耀眼;嗰頭髮從冇比此刻更紅過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的雀斑比以往任何時候都更多更顯眼;風把她沒戴帽子的頭髮吹得亂得過分地耀眼;那頭髮從沒有比此刻更紅過。

passages.original: “Well, they didn’t pick you for your looks, that’s sure and certain,” was Mrs. Rachel Lynde’s emphatic comment.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢哋挑你可唔係因為你嘅長相,呢個係肯定嘅,」雷切爾·林德太太斬釘截鐵地評論道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,他們挑你可不是因為你的長相,這是肯定的,」雷切爾·林德太太斬釘截鐵地評論道。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel was one of those delightful and popular people who pride themselves on speaking their mind without fear or favor.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太係嗰種令人愉快又受歡迎嘅人,以不畏懼、不偏袒地直言不諱而自豪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太是那種令人愉快又受歡迎的人,以不畏懼、不偏袒地直言不諱而自豪。

passages.original: “She’s terrible skinny and homely, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「佢瘦得可怕,又難睇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她瘦得可怕,又難看,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Come here, child, and let me have a look at you.
passages.vernacular: 過嚟,細路,讓我睇睇你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過來,孩子,讓我看看你。

passages.original: Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles?
passages.vernacular: 天呀,有邊個見過咁多嘅雀斑?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,有誰見過這麼多的雀斑?

passages.original: And hair as red as carrots!
passages.vernacular: 仲有嗰頭紅得像胡蘿蔔一樣嘅頭髮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有那頭紅得像胡蘿蔔一樣的頭髮!

passages.original: Come here, child, I say.”
passages.vernacular: 過嚟,細路,我講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過來,孩子,我說。」

passages.original: Anne “came there,” but not exactly as Mrs. Rachel expected.
passages.vernacular: 安妮「過嚟」喇,但並不完全係雷切爾太太所期望嘅嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮「過來」了,但並不完全是雷切爾太太所期望的那樣。

passages.original: With one bound she crossed the kitchen floor and stood before Mrs. Rachel, her face scarlet with anger, her lips quivering, and her whole slender form trembling from head to foot.
passages.vernacular: 佢一躍就穿過廚房地板,站喺雷切爾太太面前,臉氣得通紅,嘴唇顫抖,整個纖細嘅身子從頭到腳喺發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一躍就穿過廚房地板,站在雷切爾太太面前,臉氣得通紅,嘴唇顫抖,整個纖細的身子從頭到腳在發抖。

passages.original: “I hate you,” she cried in a choked voice, stamping her foot on the floor.
passages.vernacular: 「我恨你,」佢用哽住嘅聲音喊道,一邊喺地板上跺腳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我恨你,」她用哽住的聲音喊道,一邊在地板上跺腳。

passages.original: “I hate you--I hate you--I hate you--” a louder stamp with each assertion of hatred.
passages.vernacular: 「我恨你——我恨你——我恨你——」每重複一遍恨,就跺一腳,一次比一次響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我恨你——我恨你——我恨你——」每重複一遍恨,就跺一腳,一次比一次響。

passages.original: “How dare you call me skinny and ugly?
passages.vernacular: 「你點敢講我瘦、講我醜?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼敢說我瘦、說我醜?

passages.original: How dare you say I’m freckled and redheaded?
passages.vernacular: 你點敢講我長雀斑、紅頭髮?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼敢說我長雀斑、紅頭髮?

passages.original: You are a rude, impolite, unfeeling woman!”
passages.vernacular: 你係個粗魯、冇禮貌、冇心肝嘅女人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是個粗魯、沒禮貌、沒心肝的女人!」

passages.original: “Anne!” exclaimed Marilla in consternation.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮!」瑪麗拉驚慌地叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮!」瑪麗拉驚慌地叫道。

passages.original: But Anne continued to face Mrs. Rachel undauntedly, head up, eyes blazing, hands clenched, passionate indignation exhaling from her like an atmosphere.
passages.vernacular: 但安妮繼續無畏地面對雷切爾太太,頭昂住,眼睛冒火,雙手緊握,熱烈嘅憤慨像大氣一樣從佢身上散發出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安妮繼續無畏地面對雷切爾太太,頭昂著,眼睛冒火,雙手緊握,熱烈的憤慨像大氣一樣從她身上散發出來。

passages.original: “How dare you say such things about me?” she repeated vehemently.
passages.vernacular: 「你點敢講我咁樣嘅話?」佢激烈地重複。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼敢說我這樣的話?」她激烈地重複。

passages.original: “How would you like to have such things said about you?
passages.vernacular: 「要係有人咁樣講你,你會鍾意嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要是有人這樣說你,你會喜歡嗎?

passages.original: How would you like to be told that you are fat and clumsy and probably hadn’t a spark of imagination in you?
passages.vernacular: 要係有人講你又胖又笨,而且大概連一丁點兒想像力都冇,你會鍾意嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是有人說你又胖又笨,而且大概連一丁點兒想像力都沒有,你會喜歡嗎?

passages.original: I don’t care if I do hurt your feelings by saying so!
passages.vernacular: 就算我咁講傷咗你嘅感情,我都不在乎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就算我這麼說傷了你的感情,我也不在乎!

passages.original: I hope I hurt them.
passages.vernacular: 我希望傷咗佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望傷了它們。

passages.original: You have hurt mine worse than they were ever hurt before even by Mrs. Thomas’ intoxicated husband.
passages.vernacular: 你傷我感情,比以前任何時候都傷得更深,連托馬斯太太嗰個醉酒嘅丈夫都冇傷我咁深。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你傷我感情,比以前任何時候都傷得更深,連托馬斯太太那個醉酒的丈夫都沒傷我這麼深。

passages.original: And I’ll never forgive you for it, never, never!”
passages.vernacular: 我永遠唔會原諒你,永遠,永遠唔會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠不會原諒你,永遠,永遠不會!」

passages.original: Stamp!
passages.vernacular: 跺腳!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跺腳!

passages.original: Stamp!
passages.vernacular: 跺腳!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跺腳!

passages.original: “Did anybody ever see such a temper!” exclaimed the horrified Mrs. Rachel.
passages.vernacular: 「有邊個見過咁樣嘅脾氣!」嚇壞咗嘅雷切爾太太叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有誰見過這樣的脾氣!」嚇壞了的雷切爾太太叫道。

passages.original: “Anne go to your room and stay there until I come up,” said Marilla, recovering her powers of speech with difficulty.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,回你嘅房間去,待喺嗰兒,等我上去,」瑪麗拉費力地恢復咗講話嘅能力,講道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,回你的房間去,待在那兒,等我上去,」瑪麗拉費力地恢復了說話的能力,說道。

passages.original: Anne, bursting into tears, rushed to the hall door, slammed it until the tins on the porch wall outside rattled in sympathy, and fled through the hall and up the stairs like a whirlwind.
passages.vernacular: 安妮哭住衝到門廳嘅門口,砰地把門摔上,外面門廊牆上嘅錫器都隨之震響,佢像旋風一樣衝過門廳,跑上樓梯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮哭著衝到門廳的門口,砰地把門摔上,外面門廊牆上的錫器都隨之震響,她像旋風一樣衝過門廳,跑上樓梯。

passages.original: A subdued slam above told that the door of the east gable had been shut with equal vehemence.
passages.vernacular: 樓上傳嚟一聲悶悶嘅砰響,講明東山牆房間嘅門都被同樣猛烈地關上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樓上傳來一聲悶悶的砰響,說明東山牆房間的門也被同樣猛烈地關上了。

passages.original: “Well, I don’t envy you your job bringing that up, Marilla,” said Mrs. Rachel with unspeakable solemnity.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我可不羨慕你要養大呢個細路嘅差事,瑪麗拉,」雷切爾太太帶住難以言表嘅莊重講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我可不羨慕你要養大這個孩子的差事,瑪麗拉,」雷切爾太太帶著難以言表的莊重說。

passages.original: Marilla opened her lips to say she knew not what of apology or deprecation.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉張開嘴想講佢唔知道係道歉定係辯解嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉張開嘴想說她不知道是道歉還是辯解的話。

passages.original: What she did say was a surprise to herself then and ever afterwards.
passages.vernacular: 而佢真正講出口嘅,當時、以及此後一直讓佢自己都感到驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而她真正說出口的,當時、以及此後一直讓她自己都感到驚訝。

passages.original: “You shouldn’t have twitted her about her looks, Rachel.”
passages.vernacular: 「你不該嘲笑佢嘅長相,雷切爾。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不該嘲笑她的長相,雷切爾。」

passages.original: “Marilla Cuthbert, you don’t mean to say that you are upholding her in such a terrible display of temper as we’ve just seen?” demanded Mrs. Rachel indignantly.
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉·卡思伯特,你唔係講你喺袒護佢頭先嗰樣可怕嘅發脾氣吧?」雷切爾太太憤慨地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉·卡思伯特,你不是說你在袒護她剛才那樣可怕的發脾氣吧?」雷切爾太太憤慨地問。

passages.original: “No,” said Marilla slowly, “I’m not trying to excuse her.
passages.vernacular: 「不,」瑪麗拉慢慢地講,「我唔係想為佢開脫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」瑪麗拉慢慢地說,「我不是想為她開脫。

passages.original: She’s been very naughty and I’ll have to give her a talking to about it.
passages.vernacular: 佢好淘氣,我得為此好好訓佢一頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她很淘氣,我得為此好好訓她一頓。

passages.original: But we must make allowances for her.
passages.vernacular: 但我哋必須體諒佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們必須體諒她。

passages.original: She’s never been taught what is right.
passages.vernacular: 從冇人教過佢乜嘢係對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從沒有人教過她什麼是對的。

passages.original: And you were too hard on her, Rachel.”
passages.vernacular: 而你對佢太苛刻喇,雷切爾。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而你對她太苛刻了,雷切爾。」

passages.original: Marilla could not help tacking on that last sentence, although she was again surprised at herself for doing it.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉忍不住加上最後嗰一句,雖然佢再次對自己咁樣做感到驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉忍不住加上最後那一句,雖然她再次對自己這樣做感到驚訝。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel got up with an air of offended dignity.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太帶住受咗冒犯嘅尊嚴站咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太帶著受了冒犯的尊嚴站了起來。

passages.original: “Well, I see that I’ll have to be very careful what I say after this, Marilla, since the fine feelings of orphans, brought from goodness knows where, have to be considered before anything else.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我睇今後我講話得好小心喇,瑪麗拉,因為得先考慮天曉得從邊兒領嚟嘅孤兒嘅細膩感情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我看今後我說話得非常小心了,瑪麗拉,因為得先考慮天曉得從哪兒領來的孤兒的細膩感情。

passages.original: Oh, no, I’m not vexed--don’t worry yourself.
passages.vernacular: 哦,不,我冇生氣——別為我擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,不,我沒生氣——別為我擔心。

passages.original: I’m too sorry for you to leave any room for anger in my mind.
passages.vernacular: 我太為你難過喇,心裡冇餘地留畀憤怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太為你難過了,心裡沒有餘地留給憤怒。

passages.original: You’ll have your own troubles with that child.
passages.vernacular: 你同嗰細路會有你自己嘅麻煩嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你和那孩子會有你自己的麻煩的。

passages.original: But if you’ll take my advice--which I suppose you won’t do, although I’ve brought up ten children and buried two--you’ll do that ‘talking to’ you mention with a fair-sized birch switch.
passages.vernacular: 但如果你肯聽我嘅勸告——我想你係唔會聽嘅,雖然我養大咗十個細路,埋葬咗兩個——你就用一根大小合適嘅樺樹條嚟做你講嘅嗰個『訓話』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果你肯聽我的勸告——我想你是不會聽的,雖然我養大了十個孩子,埋葬了兩個——你就用一根大小合適的樺樹條來做你說的那個『訓話』。

passages.original: I should think that would be the most effective language for that kind of a child.
passages.vernacular: 我想對嗰種細路來講,嗰個係最有效嘅語言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想對那種孩子來說,那是最有效的語言。

passages.original: Her temper matches her hair I guess.
passages.vernacular: 我猜佢嘅脾氣同佢嘅頭髮一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我猜她的脾氣和她的頭髮一樣。

passages.original: Well, good evening, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,晚安,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,晚安,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I hope you’ll come down to see me often as usual.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你像往常一樣常嚟睇我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你像往常一樣常來看我。

passages.original: But you can’t expect me to visit here again in a hurry, if I’m liable to be flown at and insulted in such a fashion.
passages.vernacular: 但你唔能夠指望我好快再嚟呢兒做客,如果我隨時可能被撲過嚟、被嗰樣侮辱嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你不能指望我很快再來這兒做客,如果我隨時可能被撲過來、被那樣侮辱的話。

passages.original: It’s something new in my experience.”
passages.vernacular: 呢喺我嘅經歷中定係頭一遭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這在我的經歷中還是頭一遭。」

passages.original: Whereat Mrs. Rachel swept out and away--if a fat woman who always waddled could be said to sweep away--and Marilla with a very solemn face betook herself to the east gable.
passages.vernacular: 講完雷切爾太太揚長而去——如果一個總是搖搖擺擺走路嘅胖女人都算得上揚長而去嘅話——瑪麗拉帶住好嚴肅嘅神情走向東山牆房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說完雷切爾太太揚長而去——如果一個總是搖搖擺擺走路的胖女人也算得上揚長而去的話——瑪麗拉帶著十分嚴肅的神情走向東山牆房間。

passages.original: On the way upstairs she pondered uneasily as to what she ought to do.
passages.vernacular: 上樓嘅路上,佢不安地思索住自己該點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上樓的路上,她不安地思索著自己該怎麼辦。

passages.original: She felt no little dismay over the scene that had just been enacted.
passages.vernacular: 啱啱上演嘅嗰一幕讓佢好係驚慌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 剛剛上演的那一幕讓她很是驚慌。

passages.original: How unfortunate that Anne should have displayed such temper before Mrs. Rachel Lynde, of all people!
passages.vernacular: 真不幸,安妮偏偏喺雷切爾·林德太太面前顯露出咁樣嘅脾氣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真不幸,安妮偏偏在雷切爾·林德太太面前顯露出這樣的脾氣!

passages.original: Then Marilla suddenly became aware of an uncomfortable and rebuking consciousness that she felt more humiliation over this than sorrow over the discovery of such a serious defect in Anne’s disposition.
passages.vernacular: 然後瑪麗拉忽然意識到一種不舒服嘅、帶責備嘅感覺:比起發現安妮性情有如此嚴重缺陷嘅悲傷,佢為此感到嘅羞辱更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後瑪麗拉忽然意識到一種不舒服的、帶責備的感覺:比起發現安妮性情有如此嚴重缺陷的悲傷,她為此感到的羞辱更多。

passages.original: And how was she to punish her?
passages.vernacular: 而佢該點懲罰佢呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而她該怎麼懲罰她呢?

passages.original: The amiable suggestion of the birch switch--to the efficiency of which all of Mrs. Rachel’s own children could have borne smarting testimony--did not appeal to Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 樺樹條呢個親切嘅建議——雷切爾太太自己嘅細路哋都可以痛苦地證明佢嘅效力——並不吸引瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樺樹條這個親切的建議——雷切爾太太自己的孩子們都可以痛苦地證明它的效力——並不吸引瑪麗拉。

passages.original: She did not believe she could whip a child.
passages.vernacular: 佢不相信自己能鞭打一個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不相信自己能鞭打一個孩子。

passages.original: No, some other method of punishment must be found to bring Anne to a proper realization of the enormity of her offense.
passages.vernacular: 不,必須找到某種別嘅懲罰方法,讓安妮正確地認識到佢嘅過錯有多嚴重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,必須找到某種別的懲罰方法,讓安妮正確地認識到她的過錯有多嚴重。

passages.original: Marilla found Anne face downward on her bed, crying bitterly, quite oblivious of muddy boots on a clean counterpane.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉發現安妮臉朝下趴喺床上,哭得好傷心,全然冇注意到泥靴子踩喺乾淨嘅床罩上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉發現安妮臉朝下趴在床上,哭得很傷心,全然沒注意到泥靴子踩在乾淨的床罩上。

passages.original: “Anne,” she said not ungently.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,」佢講,語氣並不嚴厲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,」她說,語氣並不嚴厲。

passages.original: No answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答。

passages.original: “Anne,” with greater severity, “get off that bed this minute and listen to what I have to say to you.”
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,」佢更嚴厲地講,「即刻從床上下嚟,聽我跟你講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,」她更嚴厲地說,「立刻從床上下來,聽我跟你說。」

passages.original: Anne squirmed off the bed and sat rigidly on a chair beside it, her face swollen and tear-stained and her eyes fixed stubbornly on the floor.
passages.vernacular: 安妮扭動住下咗床,僵直地坐喺床邊嘅椅子上,臉腫住,滿係淚痕,眼睛頑固地盯住地板。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮扭動著下了床,僵直地坐在床邊的椅子上,臉腫著,滿是淚痕,眼睛頑固地盯著地板。

passages.original: “This is a nice way for you to behave.
passages.vernacular: 「你呢個樣子可真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你這個樣子可真好。

passages.original: Anne!
passages.vernacular: 安妮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮!

passages.original: Aren’t you ashamed of yourself?”
passages.vernacular: 你不為自己感到羞愧嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不為自己感到羞愧嗎?」

passages.original: “She hadn’t any right to call me ugly and redheaded,” retorted Anne, evasive and defiant.
passages.vernacular: 「佢冇權利講我醜、講我紅頭髮,」安妮反駁,閃爍其詞又帶住挑釁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她沒有權利說我醜、說我紅頭髮,」安妮反駁,閃爍其詞又帶著挑釁。

passages.original: “You hadn’t any right to fly into such a fury and talk the way you did to her, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「你都冇權利發咁大嘅火,嗰樣跟佢講話,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你也沒有權利發這麼大的火,那樣跟她說話,安妮。

passages.original: I was ashamed of you--thoroughly ashamed of you.
passages.vernacular: 我為你感到羞愧——徹頭徹尾地羞愧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為你感到羞愧——徹頭徹尾地羞愧。

passages.original: I wanted you to behave nicely to Mrs. Lynde, and instead of that you have disgraced me.
passages.vernacular: 我想讓你對林德太太好好表現,可你卻讓我丟咗臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想讓你對林德太太好好表現,可你卻讓我丟了臉。

passages.original: I’m sure I don’t know why you should lose your temper like that just because Mrs. Lynde said you were red-haired and homely.
passages.vernacular: 我真不明白,你點解僅僅因為林德太太講你紅頭髮、難睇,就要嗰樣發脾氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真不明白,你為什麼僅僅因為林德太太說你紅頭髮、難看,就要那樣發脾氣。

passages.original: You say it yourself often enough.”
passages.vernacular: 你自己都經常咁講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你自己也經常這麼說。」

passages.original: “Oh, but there’s such a difference between saying a thing yourself and hearing other people say it,” wailed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不過自己講一件事,同聽別人講,係大不一樣嘅,」安妮哀號道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可是自己說一件事,和聽別人說,是大不一樣的,」安妮哀號道。

passages.original: “You may know a thing is so, but you can’t help hoping other people don’t quite think it is.
passages.vernacular: 「你可能知道一件事係咁樣,但定係忍不住希望別人不完全咁認為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你可能知道一件事是這樣,但還是忍不住希望別人不完全這麼認為。

passages.original: I suppose you think I have an awful temper, but I couldn’t help it.
passages.vernacular: 我想您覺得我嘅脾氣壞透喇,但我控制不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想您覺得我的脾氣壞透了,但我控制不住。

passages.original: When she said those things something just rose right up in me and choked me.
passages.vernacular: 佢講嗰啲話嘅時候,有乜嘢嘢一下子湧上嚟,堵住咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說那些話的時候,有什麼東西一下子湧上來,堵住了我。

passages.original: I had to fly out at her.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔得不朝佢發作。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不得不朝她發作。」

passages.original: “Well, you made a fine exhibition of yourself I must say.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我必須講,你把自己出盡咗洋相。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我必須說,你把自己出盡了洋相。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde will have a nice story to tell about you everywhere--and she’ll tell it, too.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太到處都有關於你嘅好故事可講喇——而且佢會講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太到處都有關於你的好故事可講了——而且她會講的。

passages.original: It was a dreadful thing for you to lose your temper like that, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 你嗰樣發脾氣係件可怕嘅事,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你那樣發脾氣是件可怕的事,安妮。」

passages.original: “Just imagine how you would feel if somebody told you to your face that you were skinny and ugly,” pleaded Anne tearfully.
passages.vernacular: 「你想像一下,如果有人當面講您又瘦又醜,您會點樣,」安妮含淚懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想像一下,如果有人當面說您又瘦又醜,您會怎麼樣,」安妮含淚懇求道。

passages.original: An old remembrance suddenly rose up before Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 一個陳舊嘅記憶突然喺瑪麗拉眼前浮現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個陳舊的記憶突然在瑪麗拉眼前浮現。

passages.original: She had been a very small child when she had heard one aunt say of her to another, “What a pity she is such a dark, homely little thing.”
passages.vernacular: 佢定係個好小嘅細路嘅時候,聽見一位姨媽對另一位講起佢:「真可惜,佢係個咁黑、咁難睇嘅小嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她還是個很小的孩子的時候,聽見一位姨媽對另一位說起她:「真可惜,她是個這麼黑、這麼難看的小東西。」

passages.original: Marilla was every day of fifty before the sting had gone out of that memory.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉直到五十歲,嗰段記憶嘅刺痛才消失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉直到五十歲,那段記憶的刺痛才消失。

passages.original: “I don’t say that I think Mrs. Lynde was exactly right in saying what she did to you, Anne,” she admitted in a softer tone.
passages.vernacular: 「我並唔係講我認為林德太太對你講嗰啲話完全對,安妮,」佢用更柔和嘅語氣承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我並不是說我認為林德太太對你說那些話完全對,安妮,」她用更柔和的語氣承認。

passages.original: “Rachel is too outspoken.
passages.vernacular: 「雷切爾太直率喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「雷切爾太直率了。

passages.original: But that is no excuse for such behavior on your part.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰唔係你嗰樣行為嘅藉口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那不是你那樣行為的藉口。

passages.original: She was a stranger and an elderly person and my visitor--all three very good reasons why you should have been respectful to her.
passages.vernacular: 佢係陌生人、係長輩,又係我嘅客人——呢三條都係你應該對佢恭敬嘅極好嘅理由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是陌生人、是長輩,又是我的客人——這三條都是你應該對她恭敬的極好的理由。

passages.original: You were rude and saucy and”--Marilla had a saving inspiration of punishment--“you must go to her and tell her you are very sorry for your bad temper and ask her to forgive you.”
passages.vernacular: 你當時粗魯、無禮,而且——」瑪麗拉靈機一動想到一個懲罰,「你必須去找佢,告訴佢你為自己嘅壞脾氣感到好抱歉,請求佢原諒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你當時粗魯、無禮,而且——」瑪麗拉靈機一動想到一個懲罰,「你必須去找她,告訴她你為自己的壞脾氣感到非常抱歉,請求她原諒。」

passages.original: “I can never do that,” said Anne determinedly and darkly.
passages.vernacular: 「我永遠做唔到,」安妮堅決而陰沉地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我永遠做不到,」安妮堅決而陰沉地說。

passages.original: “You can punish me in any way you like, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「您可以用任何您鍾意嘅方式懲罰我,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您可以用任何您喜歡的方式懲罰我,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: You can shut me up in a dark, damp dungeon inhabited by snakes and toads and feed me only on bread and water and I shall not complain.
passages.vernacular: 您可以把我關進一個住滿蛇同蟾蜍嘅黑暗潮濕嘅地牢,只畀我麵包同水,我都唔會抱怨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您可以把我關進一個住滿蛇和蟾蜍的黑暗潮濕的地牢,只給我麵包和水,我也不會抱怨。

passages.original: But I cannot ask Mrs. Lynde to forgive me.”
passages.vernacular: 但我唔能夠請求林德太太原諒我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不能請求林德太太原諒我。」

passages.original: “We’re not in the habit of shutting people up in dark damp dungeons,” said Marilla drily, “especially as they’re rather scarce in Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋冇把人關進黑暗潮濕地牢嘅習慣,」瑪麗拉冷冷地講,「尤其係呢種地牢喺阿文利相當稀少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們沒有把人關進黑暗潮濕地牢的習慣,」瑪麗拉冷冷地說,「尤其是這種地牢在阿文利相當稀少。

passages.original: But apologize to Mrs. Lynde you must and shall and you’ll stay here in your room until you can tell me you’re willing to do it.”
passages.vernacular: 但你必須,而且一定要向林德太太道歉,喺你肯告訴我你願意去之前,你就待喺呢個房間裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你必須,而且一定要向林德太太道歉,在你肯告訴我你願意去之前,你就待在這個房間裡。」

passages.original: “I shall have to stay here forever then,” said Anne mournfully, “because I can’t tell Mrs. Lynde I’m sorry I said those things to her.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我只好永遠待喺呢兒喇,」安妮悲哀地講,「因為我唔能夠告訴林德太太我為對佢講咗嗰啲話而抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我只好永遠待在這兒了,」安妮悲哀地說,「因為我不能告訴林德太太我為對她說了那些話而抱歉。

passages.original: How can I?
passages.vernacular: 我點能?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怎麼能?

passages.original: I’m not sorry.
passages.vernacular: 我並不抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我並不抱歉。

passages.original: I’m sorry I’ve vexed you; but I’m glad I told her just what I did.
passages.vernacular: 我好抱歉惹您生氣喇;但我好高興我就係嗰樣對佢講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很抱歉惹您生氣了;但我很高興我就是那樣對她說了。

passages.original: It was a great satisfaction.
passages.vernacular: 嗰讓我極其滿足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那讓我極其滿足。

passages.original: I can’t say I’m sorry when I’m not, can I?
passages.vernacular: 我不抱歉嘅時候,唔能夠講我抱歉,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不抱歉的時候,不能說我抱歉,是不是?

passages.original: I can’t even imagine I’m sorry.”
passages.vernacular: 我連想像自己抱歉都做唔到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我連想像自己抱歉都做不到。」

passages.original: “Perhaps your imagination will be in better working order by the morning,” said Marilla, rising to depart.
passages.vernacular: 「或者到聽日朝早,你嘅想像力會運轉得好啲,」瑪麗拉講住站起嚟準備離開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許到明天早上,你的想像力會運轉得好一些,」瑪麗拉說著站起來準備離開。

passages.original: “You’ll have the night to think over your conduct in and come to a better frame of mind.
passages.vernacular: 「你有一整夜嚟想想你嘅行為,改變想法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有一整夜來想想你的行為,改變想法。

passages.original: You said you would try to be a very good girl if we kept you at Green Gables, but I must say it hasn’t seemed very much like it this evening.”
passages.vernacular: 你講過如果我哋讓你留喺綠色屋頂,你會努力做個好乖嘅女孩,但我必須講,今日晚上睇起嚟可不點像。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說過如果我們讓你留在綠色屋頂,你會努力做個很乖的女孩,但我必須說,今天晚上看起來可不怎麼像。」

passages.original: Leaving this Parthian shaft to rankle in Anne’s stormy bosom, Marilla descended to the kitchen, grievously troubled in mind and vexed in soul.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉留下呢支回馬箭喺安妮波濤洶湧嘅胸中發酵,走下廚房,心中痛苦煩惱,靈魂不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉留下這支回馬箭在安妮波濤洶湧的胸中發酵,走下廚房,心中痛苦煩惱,靈魂不安。

passages.original: She was as angry with herself as with Anne, because, whenever she recalled Mrs. Rachel’s dumbfounded countenance her lips twitched with amusement and she felt a most reprehensible desire to laugh.
passages.vernacular: 佢對自己同對安妮一樣生氣,因為每當佢回想起雷切爾太太目瞪口呆嘅臉,佢嘅嘴唇就因覺得好笑而抽動,佢有咗一種最該責備嘅想笑嘅衝動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她對自己和對安妮一樣生氣,因為每當她回想起雷切爾太太目瞪口呆的臉,她的嘴唇就因覺得好笑而抽動,她有了一種最該責備的想笑的衝動。

chapters.title: Ch. X Anne's Apology 第十章:安妮的道歉

passages.original: CH MARILLA said nothing to Matthew about the affair that evening; but when Anne proved still refractory the next morning an explanation had to be made to account for her absence from the breakfast table.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,瑪麗拉冇對馬修提呢件事;但第二天朝早安妮定係唔肯認錯,就得有個解釋來講明佢點解不喺早餐桌上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,瑪麗拉沒有對馬修提這件事;但第二天早上安妮還是不肯認錯,就得有個解釋來說明她為什麼不在早餐桌上。

passages.original: Marilla told Matthew the whole story, taking pains to impress him with a due sense of the enormity of Anne’s behavior.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉把整件事告訴咗馬修,竭力讓佢充分意識到安妮行為嘅嚴重性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉把整件事告訴了馬修,竭力讓他充分意識到安妮行為的嚴重性。

passages.original: “It’s a good thing Rachel Lynde got a calling down; she’s a meddlesome old gossip,” was Matthew’s consolatory rejoinder.
passages.vernacular: 「雷切爾·林德挨咗一頓訓斥係好事;佢係個愛管閒事嘅老長舌婦,」呢個係馬修安慰式嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「雷切爾·林德挨了一頓訓斥是好事;她是個愛管閒事的老長舌婦,」這是馬修安慰式的回答。

passages.original: “Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you.
passages.vernacular: 「馬修·卡思伯特,我對你真係食驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修·卡思伯特,我對你真是吃驚。

passages.original: You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part!
passages.vernacular: 你知道安妮嘅行為好可怕,可你仲袒護佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道安妮的行為很可怕,可你還袒護她!

passages.original: I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!”
passages.vernacular: 我想你接下嚟就要講佢根本不該受罰喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你接下來就要說她根本不該受罰了!」

passages.original: “Well now--no--not exactly,” said Matthew uneasily.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯——不——不完全係,」馬修不安地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯——不——不完全是,」馬修不安地說。

passages.original: “I reckon she ought to be punished a little.
passages.vernacular: 「我想佢該受啲懲罰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想她該受一點懲罰。

passages.original: But don’t be too hard on her, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 但別對佢太苛刻,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但別對她太苛刻,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Recollect she hasn’t ever had anyone to teach her right.
passages.vernacular: 記住佢從來冇人教佢乜嘢係對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 記著她從來沒有人教她什麼是對的。

passages.original: You’re--you’re going to give her something to eat, aren’t you?”
passages.vernacular: 你——你會畀佢嘢食嘅,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你——你會給她東西吃的,是不是?」

passages.original: “When did you ever hear of me starving people into good behavior?” demanded Marilla indignantly.
passages.vernacular: 「你乜嘢時候聽講過我用餓肚子逼人學乖?」瑪麗拉憤憤地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你什麼時候聽說過我用餓肚子逼人學乖?」瑪麗拉憤憤地問。

passages.original: “She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself.
passages.vernacular: 「佢會按時食飯,我親自畀佢端上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她會按時吃飯,我親自給她端上去。

passages.original: But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew.”
passages.vernacular: 但佢得待喺上面,直到佢願意向林德太太道歉,呢個係定咗嘅,馬修。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她得待在上面,直到她願意向林德太太道歉,這是定了的,馬修。」

passages.original: Breakfast, dinner, and supper were very silent meals--for Anne still remained obdurate.
passages.vernacular: 早飯、午飯同晚飯都好安靜——因為安妮仍然固執。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早飯、午飯和晚飯都非常安靜——因為安妮仍然固執。

passages.original: After each meal Marilla carried a well-filled tray to the east gable and brought it down later on not noticeably depleted.
passages.vernacular: 每頓飯後,瑪麗拉都把裝得滿滿嘅托盤端到東山牆房間,後來再端下嚟時並冇明顯減少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每頓飯後,瑪麗拉都把裝得滿滿的托盤端到東山牆房間,後來再端下來時並沒有明顯減少。

passages.original: Matthew eyed its last descent with a troubled eye.
passages.vernacular: 馬修用憂慮嘅眼神目送佢最後一次下樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修用憂慮的眼神目送它最後一次下樓。

passages.original: Had Anne eaten anything at all?
passages.vernacular: 安妮到底有冇食過嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮到底有沒有吃過東西?

passages.original: When Marilla went out that evening to bring the cows from the back pasture, Matthew, who had been hanging about the barns and watching, slipped into the house with the air of a burglar and crept upstairs.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天傍晚瑪麗拉出去把牛從後面嘅牧場趕回嚟時,一直喺穀倉附近徘徊張望嘅馬修,像個竊賊似嘅溜進屋裡,悄悄上咗樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天傍晚瑪麗拉出去把牛從後面的牧場趕回來時,一直在穀倉附近徘徊張望的馬修,像個竊賊似的溜進屋裡,悄悄上了樓。

passages.original: As a general thing Matthew gravitated between the kitchen and the little bedroom off the hall where he slept; once in a while he ventured uncomfortably into the parlor or sitting room when the minister came to tea.
passages.vernacular: 一般來講,馬修喺廚房同門廳旁佢瞓嘅小臥室之間活動;偶爾牧師嚟飲茶時,佢都不自在地硬住頭皮進客廳或起居室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一般來說,馬修在廚房和門廳旁他睡的小臥室之間活動;偶爾牧師來喝茶時,他也不自在地硬著頭皮進客廳或起居室。

passages.original: But he had never been upstairs in his own house since the spring he helped Marilla paper the spare bedroom, and that was four years ago.
passages.vernacular: 但自從春天幫瑪麗拉糊備用臥室牆紙以來,佢喺自己嘅房子裡就再冇上過樓,嗰個係四年前嘅事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但自從春天幫瑪麗拉糊備用臥室牆紙以來,他在自己的房子裡就再沒上過樓,那是四年前的事了。

passages.original: He tiptoed along the hall and stood for several minutes outside the door of the east gable before he summoned courage to tap on it with his fingers and then open the door to peep in.
passages.vernacular: 佢踮住腳尖走過門廳,喺東山牆房間嘅門外站咗好幾分鐘,才鼓起勇氣用手指輕輕敲門,然後把門推開,探頭睇咗睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他踮著腳尖走過門廳,在東山牆房間的門外站了好幾分鐘,才鼓起勇氣用手指輕輕敲門,然後把門推開,探頭看了看。

passages.original: Anne was sitting on the yellow chair by the window gazing mournfully out into the garden.
passages.vernacular: 安妮坐喺窗邊嗰把黃椅子上,悲傷地望住窗外嘅花園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮坐在窗邊那把黃椅子上,悲傷地望著窗外的花園。

passages.original: Very small and unhappy she looked, and Matthew’s heart smote him.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇起嚟咁小,咁不快樂,馬修嘅心被刺痛喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看起來那麼小,那麼不快樂,馬修的心被刺痛了。

passages.original: He softly closed the door and tiptoed over to her.
passages.vernacular: 佢輕輕關上門,踮住腳走到佢身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他輕輕關上門,踮著腳走到她身邊。

passages.original: “Anne,” he whispered, as if afraid of being overheard, “how are you making it, Anne?”
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,」佢低聲講,好像怕被人聽見,「你點樣,安妮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,」他低聲說,好像怕被人聽見,「你怎麼樣,安妮?」

passages.original: Anne smiled wanly.
passages.vernacular: 安妮無力地笑咗笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮無力地笑了笑。

passages.original: “Pretty well.
passages.vernacular: 「仲不錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還不錯。

passages.original: I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time.
passages.vernacular: 我想像咗好多嘢,呢有助於打發時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想像了很多東西,這有助於打發時間。

passages.original: Of course, it’s rather lonesome.
passages.vernacular: 當然,有點孤單。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,有點孤單。

passages.original: But then, I may as well get used to that.”
passages.vernacular: 不過,我不妨習慣佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,我不妨習慣它。」

passages.original: Anne smiled again, bravely facing the long years of solitary imprisonment before her.
passages.vernacular: 安妮又笑咗笑,勇敢地面對眼前漫長歲月嘅獨自囚禁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮又笑了笑,勇敢地面對眼前漫長歲月的獨自囚禁。

passages.original: Matthew recollected that he must say what he had come to say without loss of time, lest Marilla return prematurely.
passages.vernacular: 馬修想起必須趕緊講佢嚟要講嘅話,免得瑪麗拉過早回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修想起必須趕緊說他來要說的話,免得瑪麗拉過早回來。

passages.original: “Well now, Anne, don’t you think you’d better do it and have it over with?” he whispered.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,安妮,你不覺得最好定係去做喇,把呢事了結咗嗎?」佢低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,安妮,你不覺得最好還是去做了,把這事了結了嗎?」他低聲說。

passages.original: “It’ll have to be done sooner or later, you know, for Marilla’s a dreadful determined woman--dreadful determined, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「你知道,遲早都得做嘅,因為瑪麗拉係個好堅決嘅人——好堅決,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道,遲早都得做的,因為瑪麗拉是個非常堅決的人——非常堅決,安妮。

passages.original: Do it right off, I say, and have it over.”
passages.vernacular: 我講,即刻就做,了結佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說,馬上就做,了結它。」

passages.original: “Do you mean apologize to Mrs. Lynde?”
passages.vernacular: 「您係講向林德太太道歉嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您是說向林德太太道歉嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes--apologize--that’s the very word,” said Matthew eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「對——道歉——就係呢個詞,」馬修急切地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對——道歉——就是這個詞,」馬修急切地說。

passages.original: “Just smooth it over so to speak.
passages.vernacular: 「就係講把事情擺平。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是說把事情擺平。

passages.original: That’s what I was trying to get at.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係我想講嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是我想說的。」

passages.original: “I suppose I could do it to oblige you,” said Anne thoughtfully.
passages.vernacular: 「我想為了您,我可以做,」安妮若有所思地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想為了您,我可以做,」安妮若有所思地說。

passages.original: “It would be true enough to say I am sorry, because I am sorry now.
passages.vernacular: 「講我抱歉都夠真實嘅,因為我而家確實抱歉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說我抱歉也夠真實的,因為我現在確實抱歉了。

passages.original: I wasn’t a bit sorry last night.
passages.vernacular: 琴晚我啲都不抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨晚我一點也不抱歉。

passages.original: I was mad clear through, and I stayed mad all night.
passages.vernacular: 我氣瘋喇,通宵都氣住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我氣瘋了,通宵都氣著。

passages.original: I know I did because I woke up three times and I was just furious every time.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我氣咗一夜,因為我醒咗三次,每次都怒不可遏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我氣了一夜,因為我醒了三次,每次都怒不可遏。

passages.original: But this morning it was over.
passages.vernacular: 但今日早晨,氣過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但今天早晨,氣過去了。

passages.original: I wasn’t in a temper anymore--and it left a dreadful sort of goneness, too.
passages.vernacular: 我唔再發脾氣喇——佢仲留下一種可怕嘅空蕩蕩嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不再發脾氣了——它還留下一種可怕的空蕩蕩的感覺。

passages.original: I felt so ashamed of myself.
passages.vernacular: 我為自己感到好羞愧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為自己感到非常羞愧。

passages.original: But I just couldn’t think of going and telling Mrs. Lynde so.
passages.vernacular: 但係我就係唔能夠想像去告訴林德太太呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是我就是不能想像去告訴林德太太這一點。

passages.original: It would be so humiliating.
passages.vernacular: 嗰太丟人喇。
