passages.vernacularMandarin: 那太丟人了。

passages.original: I made up my mind I’d stay shut up here forever rather than do that.
passages.vernacular: 我打定主意寧願永遠關喺呢度都不咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我打定主意寧願永遠關在這裡也不這樣做。

passages.original: But still--I’d do anything for you--if you really want me to--”
passages.vernacular: 但係定係——我願意為您做任何事——如果您真嘅想要我咁樣——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是還是——我願意為您做任何事——如果您真的想要我這樣——」

passages.original: “Well now, of course I do.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,當然我想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,當然我想。

passages.original: It’s terrible lonesome downstairs without you.
passages.vernacular: 冇你,樓下可孤單得好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有你,樓下可孤單得很。

passages.original: Just go and smooth things over--that’s a good girl.”
passages.vernacular: 去把事情擺平吧——呢才係好細路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去把事情擺平吧——這才是好孩子。」

passages.original: “Very well,” said Anne resignedly.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」安妮認命地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」安妮認命地說。

passages.original: “I’ll tell Marilla as soon as she comes in I’ve repented.”
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉一進嚟,我就告訴佢我悔改喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉一進來,我就告訴她我悔改了。」

passages.original: “That’s right--that’s right, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「對——對,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對——對,安妮。

passages.original: But don’t tell Marilla I said anything about it.
passages.vernacular: 但別告訴瑪麗拉我講過呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但別告訴瑪麗拉我說過這件事。

passages.original: She might think I was putting my oar in and I promised not to do that.”
passages.vernacular: 佢可能認為我喺插手,而我答應過佢不插手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她可能認為我在插手,而我答應過她不插手。」

passages.original: “Wild horses won’t drag the secret from me,” promised Anne solemnly.
passages.vernacular: 「就係野馬都拖不走我呢個祕密,」安妮鄭重地許諾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是野馬也拖不走我這個祕密,」安妮鄭重地許諾。

passages.original: “How would wild horses drag a secret from a person anyhow?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過野馬點能從一個人嗰度拖出祕密嚟呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過野馬怎麼能從一個人那裡拖出祕密來呢?」

passages.original: But Matthew was gone, scared at his own success.
passages.vernacular: 不過馬修已經走喇,被自己嘅成功嚇壞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是馬修已經走了,被自己的成功嚇壞了。

passages.original: He fled hastily to the remotest corner of the horse pasture lest Marilla should suspect what he had been up to.
passages.vernacular: 佢匆匆逃到馬場最遠嘅角落,免得瑪麗拉懷疑佢做咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他匆匆逃到馬場最遠的角落,免得瑪麗拉懷疑他做了什麼。

passages.original: Marilla herself, upon her return to the house, was agreeably surprised to hear a plaintive voice calling, “Marilla” over the banisters.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉自己回到屋裡,驚喜地聽到一個哀怨嘅聲音喺樓梯欄杆上方喊住「瑪麗拉」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉自己回到屋裡,驚喜地聽到一個哀怨的聲音在樓梯欄杆上方喊著「瑪麗拉」。

passages.original: “Well?” she said, going into the hall.
passages.vernacular: 「點?」佢走進門廳講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼?」她走進門廳說。

passages.original: “I’m sorry I lost my temper and said rude things, and I’m willing to go and tell Mrs. Lynde so.”
passages.vernacular: 「我好抱歉我發咗脾氣,講咗粗魯嘅話,我願意去告訴林德太太。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很抱歉我發了脾氣,說了粗魯的話,我願意去告訴林德太太。」

passages.original: “Very well.”
passages.vernacular: 「好好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好。」

passages.original: Marilla’s crispness gave no sign of her relief.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉嘅乾脆冇流露出絲毫如釋重負。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉的乾脆沒有流露出絲毫如釋重負。

passages.original: She had been wondering what under the canopy she should do if Anne did not give in.
passages.vernacular: 佢一直喺琢磨,如果安妮唔肯讓步,佢到底該點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一直在琢磨,如果安妮不肯讓步,她到底該怎麼辦。

passages.original: “I’ll take you down after milking.”
passages.vernacular: 「擠完奶我帶你下去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「擠完奶我帶你下去。」

passages.original: Accordingly, after milking, behold Marilla and Anne walking down the lane, the former erect and triumphant, the latter drooping and dejected.
passages.vernacular: 於是擠完奶後,只見瑪麗拉同安妮沿住小巷走下去,前者挺直身子、得意洋洋,後者垂頭喪氣、沮喪不堪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是擠完奶後,只見瑪麗拉和安妮沿著小巷走下去,前者挺直身子、得意洋洋,後者垂頭喪氣、沮喪不堪。

passages.original: But halfway down Anne’s dejection vanished as if by enchantment.
passages.vernacular: 不過走到一半,安妮嘅沮喪像施咗魔法似嘅消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是走到一半,安妮的沮喪像施了魔法似的消失了。

passages.original: She lifted her head and stepped lightly along, her eyes fixed on the sunset sky and an air of subdued exhilaration about her.
passages.vernacular: 佢抬起頭,輕快地走住,眼睛盯住夕陽天空,有一種壓抑住嘅興奮嘅神氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她抬起頭,輕快地走著,眼睛盯著夕陽天空,有一種壓抑著的興奮的神氣。

passages.original: Marilla beheld the change disapprovingly.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉不以為然地睇住呢個變化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉不以為然地看著這個變化。

passages.original: This was no meek penitent such as it behooved her to take into the presence of the offended Mrs. Lynde.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係一個本該帶到被冒犯嘅林德太太面前嘅溫順嘅悔罪者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是一個本該帶到被冒犯的林德太太面前的溫順的悔罪者。

passages.original: “What are you thinking of, Anne?” she asked sharply.
passages.vernacular: 「你喺想乜嘢,安妮?」佢厲聲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你在想什麼,安妮?」她厲聲問。

passages.original: “I’m imagining out what I must say to Mrs. Lynde,” answered Anne dreamily.
passages.vernacular: 「我喺想像我該對林德太太講乜嘢,」安妮夢幻般地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在想像我該對林德太太說什麼,」安妮夢幻般地回答。

passages.original: This was satisfactory--or should have been so.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係令人滿意嘅——或者講本該令人滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是令人滿意的——或者說本該令人滿意。

passages.original: But Marilla could not rid herself of the notion that something in her scheme of punishment was going askew.
passages.vernacular: 但瑪麗拉無法擺脫一個念頭:佢嘅懲罰計劃中有乜嘢地方出咗偏差。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但瑪麗拉無法擺脫一個念頭:她的懲罰計劃中有什麼地方出了偏差。

passages.original: Anne had no business to look so rapt and radiant.
passages.vernacular: 安妮冇資格睇上去咁出神、咁容光煥發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮沒有資格看上去這麼出神、這麼容光煥發。

passages.original: Rapt and radiant Anne continued until they were in the very presence of Mrs. Lynde, who was sitting knitting by her kitchen window.
passages.vernacular: 出神、容光煥發嘅安妮一直持續到佢哋嚟到正坐喺廚房窗前織毛線嘅林德太太面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 出神、容光煥發的安妮一直持續到她們來到正坐在廚房窗前織毛線的林德太太面前。

passages.original: Then the radiance vanished.
passages.vernacular: 然後嗰光輝消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後那光輝消失了。

passages.original: Mournful penitence appeared on every feature.
passages.vernacular: 悲傷嘅悔恨出而家佢每一個表情上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 悲傷的悔恨出現在她每一個表情上。

passages.original: Before a word was spoken Anne suddenly went down on her knees before the astonished Mrs. Rachel and held out her hands beseechingly.
passages.vernacular: 冇等邊個開口,安妮突然喺驚呆咗嘅雷切爾太太面前跪下,懇求地伸出雙手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒等誰開口,安妮突然在驚呆了的雷切爾太太面前跪下,懇求地伸出雙手。

passages.original: “Oh, Mrs. Lynde, I am so extremely sorry,” she said with a quiver in her voice.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,林德太太,我好好抱歉,」佢講,聲音裡帶住顫抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,林德太太,我非常非常抱歉,」她說,聲音裡帶著顫抖。

passages.original: “I could never express all my sorrow, no, not if I used up a whole dictionary.
passages.vernacular: 「我永遠無法表達我所有嘅悲傷,不,即使我用盡一整本字典都不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我永遠無法表達我所有的悲傷,不,即使我用盡一整本字典也不行。

passages.original: You must just imagine it.
passages.vernacular: 您只能想像。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您只能想像。

passages.original: I behaved terribly to you--and I’ve disgraced the dear friends, Matthew and Marilla, who have let me stay at Green Gables although I’m not a boy.
passages.vernacular: 我對您嘅舉止太可怕喇——而且我讓親愛嘅朋友馬修同瑪麗拉丟咗臉,佢哋讓我留喺綠色屋頂,儘管我唔係男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對您的舉止太可怕了——而且我讓親愛的朋友馬修和瑪麗拉丟了臉,他們讓我留在綠色屋頂,儘管我不是男孩。

passages.original: I’m a dreadfully wicked and ungrateful girl, and I deserve to be punished and cast out by respectable people forever.
passages.vernacular: 我係個好邪惡、忘恩負義嘅女孩,我應該受到懲罰,永遠被體面嘅人拋棄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是個非常邪惡、忘恩負義的女孩,我應該受到懲罰,永遠被體面的人拋棄。

passages.original: It was very wicked of me to fly into a temper because you told me the truth.
passages.vernacular: 因為您告訴咗我實話就發脾氣,呢太邪惡喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為您告訴了我實話就發脾氣,這太邪惡了。

passages.original: It was the truth; every word you said was true.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係實話;您講嘅每一個字都係實話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是實話;您說的每一個字都是實話。

passages.original: My hair is red and I’m freckled and skinny and ugly.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅頭髮係紅嘅,我長雀斑,又瘦又醜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的頭髮是紅的,我長雀斑,又瘦又醜。

passages.original: What I said to you was true, too, but I shouldn’t have said it.
passages.vernacular: 我對您講嘅話都係實話,但我不該講出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對您說的話也是實話,但我不該說出來。

passages.original: Oh, Mrs. Lynde, please, please, forgive me.
passages.vernacular: 哦,林德太太,求求您,求求您原諒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,林德太太,求求您,求求您原諒我。

passages.original: If you refuse it will be a lifelong sorrow on a poor little orphan girl, would you, even if she had a dreadful temper?
passages.vernacular: 如果您拒絕,呢會成為一個可憐嘅孤兒女孩終身嘅悲痛,您會嗎,即使佢嘅脾氣好壞?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您拒絕,這會成為一個可憐的孤兒女孩終身的悲痛,您會嗎,即使她的脾氣很壞?

passages.original: Oh, I am sure you wouldn’t.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我肯定您唔會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我肯定您不會的。

passages.original: Please say you forgive me, Mrs. Lynde.”
passages.vernacular: 請講您原諒我,林德太太。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請說您原諒我,林德太太。」

passages.original: Anne clasped her hands together, bowed her head, and waited for the word of judgment.
passages.vernacular: 安妮雙手合十,低下頭,等待判決嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮雙手合十,低下頭,等待判決的話。

passages.original: There was no mistaking her sincerity--it breathed in every tone of her voice.
passages.vernacular: 毫無疑問佢係真誠嘅——佢喺佢聲音嘅每一個音調裡呼吸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 毫無疑問她是真誠的——它在她聲音的每一個音調裡呼吸。

passages.original: Both Marilla and Mrs. Lynde recognized its unmistakable ring.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉同林德太太都認出咗嗰明確無誤嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉和林德太太都認出了那明確無誤的聲音。

passages.original: But the former understood in dismay that Anne was actually enjoying her valley of humiliation--was reveling in the thoroughness of her abasement.
passages.vernacular: 但係前者驚慌地明白喇,安妮其實在享受佢嘅屈辱谷——喺佢徹底嘅屈服中縱情狂歡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是前者驚慌地明白了,安妮其實在享受她的屈辱谷——在她徹底的屈服中縱情狂歡。

passages.original: Where was the wholesome punishment upon which she, Marilla, had plumed herself?
passages.vernacular: 佢,瑪麗拉,自以為得意嘅有益嘅懲罰邊度去喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她,瑪麗拉,自以為得意的有益的懲罰哪裡去了?

passages.original: Anne had turned it into a species of positive pleasure.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把佢變成咗一種實實在喺嘅快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把它變成了一種實實在在的快樂。

passages.original: Good Mrs. Lynde, not being overburdened with perception, did not see this.
passages.vernacular: 善良嘅林德太太冇過分敏銳嘅洞察力,冇睇出呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 善良的林德太太沒有過分敏銳的洞察力,沒看出這一點。

passages.original: She only perceived that Anne had made a very thorough apology and all resentment vanished from her kindly, if somewhat officious, heart.
passages.vernacular: 佢只覺得安妮做咗好徹底嘅道歉,所有嘅怨恨從佢和善、雖然有些愛管閒事嘅心裡消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她只覺得安妮做了非常徹底的道歉,所有的怨恨從她和善、雖然有些愛管閒事的心裡消失了。

passages.original: “There, there, get up, child,” she said heartily.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,起嚟,細路,」佢熱情地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,起來,孩子,」她熱情地說。

passages.original: “Of course I forgive you.
passages.vernacular: 「我當然原諒你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我當然原諒你。

passages.original: I guess I was a little too hard on you, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 我想不管點樣,我對你係有點太苛刻喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想不管怎樣,我對你是有點太苛刻了。

passages.original: But I’m such an outspoken person.
passages.vernacular: 不過我呢人就係直嚟直去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我這人就是直來直去。

passages.original: You just mustn’t mind me, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 你別在意我就係喇,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你別在意我就是了,就是這樣。

passages.original: It can’t be denied your hair is terrible red; but I knew a girl once--went to school with her, in fact--whose hair was every mite as red as yours when she was young, but when she grew up it darkened to a real handsome auburn.
passages.vernacular: 不可否認你嘅頭髮紅得好厲害;可我認識一個女孩——事實上同佢一起上過學——佢小時候頭髮跟你嘅一樣紅得啲不差,但等佢長大喇,佢就變深成咗真正漂亮嘅赤褐色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不可否認你的頭髮紅得很厲害;可我認識一個女孩——事實上和她一起上過學——她小時候頭髮跟你的一樣紅得一點不差,但等她長大了,它就變深成了真正漂亮的赤褐色。

passages.original: I wouldn’t be a mite surprised if yours did, too--not a mite.”
passages.vernacular: 要係你嘅都咁樣,我啲都唔會食驚——啲兒都不。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是你的也這樣,我一點都不會吃驚——一點兒也不。」

passages.original: “Oh, Mrs. Lynde!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,林德太太!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,林德太太!」

passages.original: Anne drew a long breath as she rose to her feet.
passages.vernacular: 安妮站起嚟時深深吸咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮站起來時深深吸了口氣。

passages.original: “You have given me a hope.
passages.vernacular: 「您畀咗我一個希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您給了我一個希望。

passages.original: I shall always feel that you are a benefactor.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠覺得您係我嘅恩人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠覺得您是我的恩人。

passages.original: Oh, I could endure anything if I only thought my hair would be a handsome auburn when I grew up.
passages.vernacular: 哦,只要我想到我長大後頭髮會係漂亮嘅赤褐色,我乜嘢都能忍受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,只要我想到我長大後頭髮會是漂亮的赤褐色,我什麼都能忍受。

passages.original: It would be so much easier to be good if one’s hair was a handsome auburn, don’t you think?
passages.vernacular: 如果一個人嘅頭髮係漂亮嘅赤褐色,要做個好人就容易多喇,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果一個人的頭髮是漂亮的赤褐色,要做個好人就容易多了,您說呢?

passages.original: And now may I go out into your garden and sit on that bench under the apple-trees while you and Marilla are talking?
passages.vernacular: 而家,喺您同瑪麗拉講話嘅時候,我可以到您嘅花園裡去,坐喺蘋果樹下嘅長凳上嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,在您和瑪麗拉說話的時候,我可以到您的花園裡去,坐在蘋果樹下的長凳上嗎?

passages.original: There is so much more scope for imagination out there.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰兒有更多想像嘅餘地。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那兒有更多想像的餘地。」

passages.original: “Laws, yes, run along, child.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,行,去吧,細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,行,去吧,孩子。

passages.original: And you can pick a bouquet of them white June lilies over in the corner if you like.”
passages.vernacular: 你要係鍾意,可以喺角落裡摘一束嗰啲白色嘅六月百合。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要是喜歡,可以在角落裡摘一束那些白色的六月百合。」

passages.original: As the door closed behind Anne, Mrs. Lynde got briskly up to light a lamp.
passages.vernacular: 門喺安妮身後關上時,林德太太輕快地站起嚟去點燈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 門在安妮身後關上時,林德太太輕快地站起來去點燈。

passages.original: “She’s a real odd little thing.
passages.vernacular: 「佢真係個古怪嘅小嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她真是個古怪的小東西。

passages.original: Take this chair, Marilla; it’s easier than the one you’ve got; I just keep that for the hired boy to sit on.
passages.vernacular: 坐呢把椅子吧,瑪麗拉;比你嗰把舒服;我嗰把只係留畀雇嚟嘅小伙子坐嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 坐這把椅子吧,瑪麗拉;比你那把舒服;我那把只是留給雇來的小伙子坐的。

passages.original: Yes, she certainly is an odd child, but there is something kind of taking about her after all.
passages.vernacular: 係啊,佢確實係個古怪嘅細路,但終究有啲迷人嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是啊,她確實是個古怪的孩子,但終究有一點迷人的地方。

passages.original: I don’t feel so surprised at you and Matthew keeping her as I did--nor so sorry for you, either.
passages.vernacular: 我不像先前嗰樣對你同馬修留下佢感到食驚喇——都不咁為你難過喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不像先前那樣對你和馬修留下她感到吃驚了——也不那麼為你難過了。

passages.original: She may turn out all right.
passages.vernacular: 佢或者會變好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也許會變好的。

passages.original: Of course, she has a queer way of expressing herself--a little too--well, too kind of forcible, you know; but she’ll likely get over that now that she’s come to live among civilized folks.
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢表達自己嘅方式好奇怪——有點太——嗯,太有點強勁,你知道;不過既然佢而家嚟到文明人中間生活,佢好可能會改掉嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,她表達自己的方式很奇怪——有點太——嗯,太有點強勁,你知道;不過既然她現在來到文明人中間生活,她很可能會改掉的。

passages.original: And then, her temper’s pretty quick, I guess; but there’s one comfort, a child that has a quick temper, just blaze up and cool down, ain’t never likely to be sly or deceitful.
passages.vernacular: 仲有,佢嘅脾氣挺急嘅,我猜;不過有啲安慰,脾氣急嘅細路,一下子發火,一下子又冷靜下嚟,絕唔可能係陰險或欺騙嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,她的脾氣挺急的,我猜;不過有一點安慰,脾氣急的孩子,一下子發火,一下子又冷靜下來,絕不可能是陰險或欺騙的。

passages.original: Preserve me from a sly child, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 千萬唔好畀我碰上陰險嘅細路,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 千萬別讓我碰上陰險的孩子,就是這樣。

passages.original: On the whole, Marilla, I kind of like her.”
passages.vernacular: 總嘅來講,瑪麗拉,我有點鍾意佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總的來說,瑪麗拉,我有點喜歡她。」

passages.original: When Marilla went home Anne came out of the fragrant twilight of the orchard with a sheaf of white narcissi in her hands.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉回家時,安妮從果園芬芳嘅暮色中走出嚟,手裡攞住一束白水仙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉回家時,安妮從果園芬芳的暮色中走出來,手裡拿著一束白水仙。

passages.original: “I apologized pretty well, didn’t I?” she said proudly as they went down the lane.
passages.vernacular: 「我道歉道得挺好,係唔係?」佢哋走下小巷時,佢自豪地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我道歉道得挺好,是不是?」她們走下小巷時,她自豪地說。

passages.original: “I thought since I had to do it I might as well do it thoroughly.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想既然非做不可,不如做徹底。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想既然非做不可,不如做徹底。」

passages.original: “You did it thoroughly, all right enough,” was Marilla’s comment.
passages.vernacular: 「你做得夠徹底嘅,啲不假,」呢個係瑪麗拉嘅評語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你做得夠徹底的,一點不假,」這是瑪麗拉的評語。

passages.original: Marilla was dismayed at finding herself inclined to laugh over the recollection.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉驚恐地發現自己想起嗰一幕就忍不住想笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉驚恐地發現自己想起那一幕就忍不住想笑。

passages.original: She had also an uneasy feeling that she ought to scold Anne for apologizing so well; but then, that was ridiculous!
passages.vernacular: 佢仲有一種不安嘅感覺,覺得應該責備安妮道歉道得太好;不過,嗰太荒唐喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她還有一種不安的感覺,覺得應該責備安妮道歉道得太好;不過,那太荒唐了!

passages.original: She compromised with her conscience by saying severely:
passages.vernacular: 佢對良心作出咗妥協,嚴厲地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她對良心作出了妥協,嚴厲地說:

passages.original: “I hope you won’t have occasion to make many more such apologies.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望你冇機會再做好多咁樣嘅道歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望你沒有機會再做很多這樣的道歉。

passages.original: I hope you’ll try to control your temper now, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望你而家努力控制自己嘅脾氣,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你現在努力控制自己的脾氣,安妮。」

passages.original: “That wouldn’t be so hard if people wouldn’t twit me about my looks,” said Anne with a sigh.
passages.vernacular: 「如果人哋不嘲笑我嘅長相,嗰就不難喇,」安妮嘆咗口氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果人們不嘲笑我的長相,那就不難了,」安妮嘆了口氣說。

passages.original: “I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over.
passages.vernacular: 「別嘅事我唔會發火;但我已經厭倦咗人哋攞我嘅頭髮嘲笑我,佢讓我一下子就沸騰起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別的事我不會發火;但我已經厭倦了人們拿我的頭髮嘲笑我,它讓我一下子就沸騰起來。

passages.original: Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?”
passages.vernacular: 您覺得我長大後頭髮真嘅會係漂亮嘅赤褐色嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您覺得我長大後頭髮真的會是漂亮的赤褐色嗎?」

passages.original: “You shouldn’t think so much about your looks, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「你不該咁在意你嘅長相,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不該那麼在意你的長相,安妮。

passages.original: I’m afraid you are a very vain little girl.”
passages.vernacular: 我怕你係個好愛慕虛榮嘅小女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕你是個很愛慕虛榮的小女孩。」

passages.original: “How can I be vain when I know I’m homely?” protested Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我明知道自己難睇,點能愛慕虛榮呢?」安妮抗議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我明知道自己難看,怎麼能愛慕虛榮呢?」安妮抗議。

passages.original: “I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn’t pretty.
passages.vernacular: 「我愛漂亮嘅嘢;我討厭照鏡子睇到不漂亮嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我愛漂亮的東西;我討厭照鏡子看到不漂亮的東西。

passages.original: It makes me feel so sorrowful--just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓我感到好悲傷——就像我睇到任何醜陋嘅嘢時嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它讓我感到非常悲傷——就像我看到任何醜陋的東西時那樣。

passages.original: I pity it because it isn’t beautiful.”
passages.vernacular: 我可憐佢,因為佢不美麗。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可憐它,因為它不美麗。」

passages.original: “Handsome is as handsome does,” quoted Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「行得美才係真美,」瑪麗拉引用道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「行得美才是真美,」瑪麗拉引用道。

passages.original: “I’ve had that said to me before, but I have my doubts about it,” remarked skeptical Anne, sniffing at her narcissi.
passages.vernacular: 「以前都有人對我咁講過,不過我對此有懷疑,」懷疑嘅安妮講,嗅住佢嘅水仙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「以前也有人對我這麼說過,不過我對此有懷疑,」懷疑的安妮說,嗅著她的水仙。

passages.original: “Oh, aren’t these flowers sweet!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,呢啲花多香啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,這些花多香啊!

passages.original: It was lovely of Mrs. Lynde to give them to me.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太畀咗我呢啲,真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太給了我這些,真好。

passages.original: I have no hard feelings against Mrs. Lynde now.
passages.vernacular: 我而家對林德太太冇啲怨恨喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在對林德太太沒有一點怨恨了。

passages.original: It gives you a lovely, comfortable feeling to apologize and be forgiven, doesn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 道歉同被原諒畀人一種美好、舒適嘅感覺,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 道歉和被原諒給人一種美好、舒適的感覺,是不是?

passages.original: Aren’t the stars bright tonight?
passages.vernacular: 今晚嘅星星多亮啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚的星星多亮啊!

passages.original: If you could live in a star, which one would you pick?
passages.vernacular: 如果您能住喺一顆星星上,您會選邊顆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您能住在一顆星星上,您會選哪顆?

passages.original: I’d like that lovely clear big one away over there above that dark hill.”
passages.vernacular: 我想要遠處嗰座黑山上面嗰顆可愛、清亮嘅大星星。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想要遠處那座黑山上面那顆可愛、清亮的大星星。」

passages.original: “Anne, do hold your tongue,” said Marilla, thoroughly worn out trying to follow the gyrations of Anne’s thoughts.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,閉嘴吧,」瑪麗拉講,佢已被安妮思路嘅盤旋弄得筋疲力盡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,閉嘴吧,」瑪麗拉說,她已被安妮思路的盤旋弄得筋疲力盡。

passages.original: Anne said no more until they turned into their own lane.
passages.vernacular: 安妮唔再講話,直到佢哋拐進自家嘅小巷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮不再說話,直到她們拐進自家的小巷。

passages.original: A little gypsy wind came down it to meet them, laden with the spicy perfume of young dew-wet ferns.
passages.vernacular: 一陣小小嘅吉普賽風順住小巷迎面吹嚟,滿載住沾咗露水嘅嫩蕨類嘅辛香氣息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣小小的吉普賽風順著小巷迎面吹來,滿載著沾了露水的嫩蕨類的辛香氣息。

passages.original: Far up in the shadows a cheerful light gleamed out through the trees from the kitchen at Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 遠遠嘅暗影深處,綠色屋頂廚房嘅一盞歡快嘅燈火透過樹木閃爍出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遠遠的暗影深處,綠色屋頂廚房的一盞歡快的燈火透過樹木閃爍出來。

passages.original: Anne suddenly came close to Marilla and slipped her hand into the older woman’s hard palm.
passages.vernacular: 安妮突然靠近瑪麗拉,把手滑進呢位年長女人粗糙嘅手掌裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮突然靠近瑪麗拉,把手滑進這位年長女人粗糙的手掌裡。

passages.original: “It’s lovely to be going home and know it’s home,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「回家真好,知道嗰個係家,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「回家真好,知道那是家,」她說。

passages.original: “I love Green Gables already, and I never loved any place before.
passages.vernacular: 「我已經愛上綠色屋頂喇,而我以前從冇愛過任何地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我已經愛上綠色屋頂了,而我以前從沒愛過任何地方。

passages.original: No place ever seemed like home.
passages.vernacular: 冇邊個地方像家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有哪個地方像家。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, I’m so happy.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,我太幸福喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,我太幸福了。

passages.original: I could pray right now and not find it a bit hard.”
passages.vernacular: 我而家就能禱告,啲都不覺得困難。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在就能禱告,一點也不覺得困難。」

passages.original: Something warm and pleasant welled up in Marilla’s heart at touch of that thin little hand in her own--a throb of the maternity she had missed, perhaps.
passages.vernacular: 嗰隻瘦小嘅手放喺自己手裡嘅觸感,使某種溫暖愉悅嘅嘢湧上瑪麗拉嘅心頭——或者係佢錯過嘅母性嘅悸動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那隻瘦小的手放在自己手裡的觸感,使某種溫暖愉悅的東西湧上瑪麗拉的心頭——也許是她錯過的母性的悸動。

passages.original: Its very unaccustomedness and sweetness disturbed her.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅陌生同甜蜜本身就使佢不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的陌生和甜蜜本身就使她不安。

passages.original: She hastened to restore her sensations to their normal calm by inculcating a moral.
passages.vernacular: 佢趕緊通過灌輸一條道理嚟恢復佢感覺嘅平常平靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她趕緊通過灌輸一條道理來恢復她感覺的平常平靜。

passages.original: “If you’ll be a good girl you’ll always be happy, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「只要你做個好女孩,你就永遠幸福,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只要你做個好女孩,你就永遠幸福,安妮。

passages.original: And you should never find it hard to say your prayers.”
passages.vernacular: 而且你永遠不該覺得做禱告困難。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且你永遠不該覺得做禱告困難。」

passages.original: “Saying one’s prayers isn’t exactly the same thing as praying,” said Anne meditatively.
passages.vernacular: 「做禱告同禱告不完全係一回事,」安妮若有所思地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「做禱告和禱告不完全是一回事,」安妮若有所思地說。

passages.original: “But I’m going to imagine that I’m the wind that is blowing up there in those tree tops.
passages.vernacular: 「但我要去想像我係嗰邊樹梢上吹過嘅風。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我要去想像我是那邊樹梢上吹過的風。

passages.original: When I get tired of the trees I’ll imagine I’m gently waving down here in the ferns--and then I’ll fly over to Mrs. Lynde’s garden and set the flowers dancing--and then I’ll go with one great swoop over the clover field--and then I’ll blow over the Lake of Shining Waters and ripple it all up into little sparkling waves.
passages.vernacular: 等我對樹梢厭倦喇,我就想像我喺呢下面蕨叢中輕輕搖擺——然後我飛到林德太太嘅花園,讓花朵跳舞——然後我一下子掠過三葉草田——然後我吹過閃亮湖水,把佢吹成一片閃爍嘅小浪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我對樹梢厭倦了,我就想像我在這下面蕨叢中輕輕搖擺——然後我飛到林德太太的花園,讓花朵跳舞——然後我一下子掠過三葉草田——然後我吹過閃亮湖水,把它吹成一片閃爍的小浪。

passages.original: Oh, there’s so much scope for imagination in a wind!
passages.vernacular: 哦,風裡有咁多想像嘅餘地!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,風裡有這麼多想像的餘地!

passages.original: So I’ll not talk any more just now, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我而家唔再講話喇,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我現在不再說話了,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: “Thanks be to goodness for that,” breathed Marilla in devout relief.
passages.vernacular: 「謝天謝地,」瑪麗拉虔誠地鬆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝天謝地,」瑪麗拉虔誠地鬆了口氣。

chapters.title: Ch. XI Anne's Impressions of Sunday-school 第十一章:安妮對主日學校的印象

passages.original: CH WELL, how do you like them?” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你覺得佢哋點樣?」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你覺得它們怎麼樣?」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: Anne was standing in the gable room, looking solemnly at three new dresses spread out on the bed.
passages.vernacular: 安妮站喺山牆房間裡,神情嚴肅地睇住攤喺床上嘅三件新裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮站在山牆房間裡,神情嚴肅地看著攤在床上的三件新裙子。

passages.original: One was of snuffy colored gingham which Marilla had been tempted to buy from a peddler the preceding summer because it looked so serviceable; one was of black-and-white checkered sateen which she had picked up at a bargain counter in the winter; and one was a stiff print of an ugly blue shade which she had purchased that week at a Carmody store.
passages.vernacular: 一件係鼻煙色嘅格子布,瑪麗拉去年夏天因為睇住好耐穿,忍不住從小販手裡買下嘅;一件係黑白方格嘅緞面棉布,冬天喺減價櫃檯撿到嘅;仲有一件係一種難睇嘅藍色硬印花布,係呢周喺卡莫迪嘅一家店買嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一件是鼻煙色的格子布,瑪麗拉去年夏天因為看著很耐穿,忍不住從小販手裡買下的;一件是黑白方格的緞面棉布,冬天在減價櫃檯撿到的;還有一件是一種難看的藍色硬印花布,是這周在卡莫迪的一家店買的。

passages.original: She had made them up herself, and they were all made alike--plain skirts fulled tightly to plain waists, with sleeves as plain as waist and skirt and tight as sleeves could be.
passages.vernacular: 裙子都係佢自己縫嘅,做得都一樣——樸素嘅裙子緊緊地打褶縫喺樸素嘅上衣上,袖子跟上衣同裙子一樣樸素,又盡可能地緊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 裙子都是她自己縫的,做得都一樣——樸素的裙子緊緊地打褶縫在樸素的上衣上,袖子跟上衣和裙子一樣樸素,又盡可能地緊。

passages.original: “I’ll imagine that I like them,” said Anne soberly.
passages.vernacular: 「我要想像我鍾意佢哋,」安妮嚴肅地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要想像我喜歡它們,」安妮嚴肅地說。

passages.original: “I don’t want you to imagine it,” said Marilla, offended.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔好你想像,」瑪麗拉被冒犯喇,講道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不要你想像,」瑪麗拉被冒犯了,說道。

passages.original: “Oh, I can see you don’t like the dresses!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我睇得出您不鍾意呢啲裙子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我看得出您不喜歡這些裙子!

passages.original: What is the matter with them?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋有乜嘢問題?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們有什麼問題?

passages.original: Aren’t they neat and clean and new?”
passages.vernacular: 唔係整潔、乾淨、全新嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是整潔、乾淨、全新的嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
“Then why don’t you like them?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰您點解不鍾意佢哋呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那您為什麼不喜歡它們呢?」

passages.original: “They’re--they’re not--pretty,” said Anne reluctantly.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋——佢哋不——漂亮,」安妮勉強地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們——它們不——漂亮,」安妮勉強地說。

passages.original: “Pretty!”
passages.vernacular: 「漂亮!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「漂亮!」

passages.original: Marilla sniffed.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉嗤之以鼻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉嗤之以鼻。

passages.original: “I didn’t trouble my head about getting pretty dresses for you.
passages.vernacular: 「我才不費心思去畀你弄漂亮裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我才不費心思去給你弄漂亮裙子。

passages.original: I don’t believe in pampering vanity, Anne, I’ll tell you that right off.
passages.vernacular: 我不贊成縱容虛榮,安妮,我一開始就告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不贊成縱容虛榮,安妮,我一開始就告訴你。

passages.original: Those dresses are good, sensible, serviceable dresses, without any frills or furbelows about them, and they’re all you’ll get this summer.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲裙子係好嘅、實用嘅、耐穿嘅裙子,冇任何荷葉邊或褶飾,呢個夏天你就只有呢啲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些裙子是好的、實用的、耐穿的裙子,沒有任何荷葉邊或褶飾,這個夏天你就只有這些了。

passages.original: The brown gingham and the blue print will do you for school when you begin to go.
passages.vernacular: 褐色格子布同藍色印花布等你開始上學時穿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 褐色格子布和藍色印花布等你開始上學時穿。

passages.original: The sateen is for church and Sunday-school.
passages.vernacular: 緞面嘅係去教堂同主日學校穿嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 緞面的是去教堂和主日學校穿的。

passages.original: I’ll expect you to keep them neat and clean and not to tear them.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你保持整潔乾淨,唔好撕破。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你保持整潔乾淨,不要撕破。

passages.original: I should think you’d be grateful to get most anything after those skimpy wincey things you’ve been wearing.”
passages.vernacular: 我想你穿過嗰啲窄小嘅棉毛混紡之後,得到乜嘢都該感激喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你穿過那些窄小的棉毛混紡之後,得到什麼都該感激了。」

passages.original: “Oh, I am grateful,” protested Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我感激,」安妮抗議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我感激,」安妮抗議。

passages.original: “But I’d be ever so much gratefuller if--if you’d made just one of them with puffed sleeves.
passages.vernacular: 「不過如果——如果您至少做一件帶泡泡袖嘅,我會感激得多得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過如果——如果您至少做一件帶泡泡袖的,我會感激得多得多。

passages.original: Puffed sleeves are so fashionable now.
passages.vernacular: 泡泡袖而家特別時髦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 泡泡袖現在特別時髦。

passages.original: It would give me such a thrill, Marilla, just to wear a dress with puffed sleeves.”
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉,光係穿上一件帶泡泡袖嘅裙子,就會讓我激動不已。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉,光是穿上一件帶泡泡袖的裙子,就會讓我激動不已。」

passages.original: “Well, you’ll have to do without your thrill.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你只好冇你嘅激動喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你只好沒有你的激動了。

passages.original: I hadn’t any material to waste on puffed sleeves.
passages.vernacular: 我冇多餘嘅料子浪費喺泡泡袖上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有多餘的料子浪費在泡泡袖上。

passages.original: I think they are ridiculous-looking things anyhow.
passages.vernacular: 反正我覺得佢哋睇起嚟滑稽可笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 反正我覺得它們看起來滑稽可笑。

passages.original: I prefer the plain, sensible ones.”
passages.vernacular: 我更鍾意樸素、實用嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我更喜歡樸素、實用的。」

passages.original: “But I’d rather look ridiculous when everybody else does than plain and sensible all by myself,” persisted Anne mournfully.
passages.vernacular: 「但係,大家都滑稽可笑嘅時候,我寧願跟大家一樣滑稽可笑,都唔好獨自一人樸素實用,」安妮悲傷地堅持。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,大家都滑稽可笑的時候,我寧願跟大家一樣滑稽可笑,也不要獨自一人樸素實用,」安妮悲傷地堅持。

passages.original: “Trust you for that!
passages.vernacular: 「真虧你想得出嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真虧你想得出來!

passages.original: Well, hang those dresses carefully up in your closet, and then sit down and learn the Sunday-school lesson.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,把呢啲裙子小心地掛進你嘅壁櫥,然後坐下嚟學主日學校嘅功課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,把這些裙子小心地掛進你的壁櫥,然後坐下來學主日學校的功課。

passages.original: I got a quarterly from Mr. Bell for you and you’ll go to Sunday-school tomorrow,” said Marilla, disappearing downstairs in high dudgeon.
passages.vernacular: 我從貝爾先生嗰兒替你攞咗一本季刊,聽日你去主日學校,」瑪麗拉講,氣沖沖地下樓去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從貝爾先生那兒替你拿了一本季刊,明天你去主日學校,」瑪麗拉說,氣沖沖地下樓去了。

passages.original: Anne clasped her hands and looked at the dresses.
passages.vernacular: 安妮雙手合十,睇住嗰啲裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮雙手合十,看著那些裙子。

passages.original: “I did hope there would be a white one with puffed sleeves,” she whispered disconsolately.
passages.vernacular: 「我本來希望有一件帶泡泡袖嘅白裙子,」佢悶悶不樂地低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我本來希望有一件帶泡泡袖的白裙子,」她悶悶不樂地低聲說。

passages.original: “I prayed for one, but I didn’t much expect it on that account.
passages.vernacular: 「我為此禱告過,但我並冇指望呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我為此禱告過,但我並沒有指望這個。

passages.original: I didn’t suppose God would have time to bother about a little orphan girl’s dress.
passages.vernacular: 我想上帝冇空為一個小孤女嘅裙子操心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想上帝沒有空為一個小孤女的裙子操心。

passages.original: I knew I’d just have to depend on Marilla for it.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我只能指望瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我只能指望瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Well, fortunately I can imagine that one of them is of snow-white muslin with lovely lace frills and three-puffed sleeves.”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,幸好我可以想像其中一件係雪白嘅細棉布,帶住可愛嘅蕾絲褶邊同三層泡泡袖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,幸好我可以想像其中一件是雪白的細棉布,帶著可愛的蕾絲褶邊和三層泡泡袖。」

passages.original: The next morning warnings of a sick headache prevented Marilla from going to Sunday-school with Anne.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨,偏頭痛嘅預兆使瑪麗拉冇法陪安妮去主日學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨,偏頭痛的預兆使瑪麗拉沒法陪安妮去主日學校。

passages.original: “You’ll have to go down and call for Mrs. Lynde, Anne,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「你得下去找林德太太,安妮,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你得下去找林德太太,安妮,」她說。

passages.original: “She’ll see that you get into the right class.
passages.vernacular: 「佢會睇住你進對班級。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她會看著你進對班級。

passages.original: Now, mind you behave yourself properly.
passages.vernacular: 而家,注意你要規規矩矩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,注意你要規規矩矩。

passages.original: Stay to preaching afterwards and ask Mrs. Lynde to show you our pew.
passages.vernacular: 之後留下嚟聽講道,請林德太太指畀你睇我哋嘅長椅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後留下來聽講道,請林德太太指給你看我們的長椅。

passages.original: Here’s a cent for collection.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一分錢,捐獻用嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一分錢,捐獻用的。

passages.original: Don’t stare at people and don’t fidget.
passages.vernacular: 別盯住人睇,都別坐立不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別盯著人看,也別坐立不安。

passages.original: I shall expect you to tell me the text when you come home.”
passages.vernacular: 我等你回家告訴我經文。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我等你回家告訴我經文。」

passages.original: Anne started off irreproachable, arrayed in the stiff black-and-white sateen, which, while decent as regards length and certainly not open to the charge of skimpiness, contrived to emphasize every corner and angle of her thin figure.
passages.vernacular: 安妮出發時無可指責,穿住硬挺嘅黑白緞面棉布裙,嗰裙子長度得體,當然唔會有人指責佢窄小,卻偏偏把佢瘦削身材嘅每個角落同稜角都突出咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮出發時無可指責,穿著硬挺的黑白緞面棉布裙,那裙子長度得體,當然不會有人指責它窄小,卻偏偏把她瘦削身材的每個角落和稜角都突出了出來。

passages.original: Her hat was a little, flat, glossy, new sailor, the extreme plainness of which had likewise much disappointed Anne, who had permitted herself secret visions of ribbon and flowers.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅帽子係一頂小小嘅、平嘅、有光澤嘅新水手帽,佢極度嘅樸素同樣令安妮大失所望,佢曾暗自幻想過絲帶同花朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的帽子是一頂小小的、平的、有光澤的新水手帽,它極度的樸素同樣令安妮大失所望,她曾暗自幻想過絲帶和花朵。

passages.original: The latter, however, were supplied before Anne reached the main road, for being confronted halfway down the lane with a golden frenzy of wind-stirred buttercups and a glory of wild roses, Anne promptly and liberally garlanded her hat with a heavy wreath of them.
passages.vernacular: 不過,喺安妮走到大路之前,後者就補上喇,因為喺小巷半路,面對住風吹動嘅毛茛嗰一片金色嘅狂熱同野玫瑰嘅絢爛,安妮即刻慷慨地用一大圈花環裝飾咗佢嘅帽子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,在安妮走到大路之前,後者就補上了,因為在小巷半路,面對著風吹動的毛茛那一片金色的狂熱和野玫瑰的絢爛,安妮立刻慷慨地用一大圈花環裝飾了她的帽子。

passages.original: Whatever other people might have thought of the result it satisfied Anne, and she tripped gaily down the road, holding her ruddy head with its decoration of pink and yellow very proudly.
passages.vernacular: 不管別人對效果點睇,安妮自己好滿意,佢歡快地沿住路蹦蹦跳跳,好自豪地昂住佢嗰紅頭,上面裝飾住粉紅同黃色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管別人對效果怎麼看,安妮自己很滿意,她歡快地沿著路蹦蹦跳跳,非常自豪地昂著她那紅頭,上面裝飾著粉紅和黃色。

passages.original: When she had reached Mrs. Lynde’s house she found that lady gone.
passages.vernacular: 佢走到林德太太家時,發現嗰位太太已經出門喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她走到林德太太家時,發現那位太太已經出門了。

passages.original: Nothing daunted, Anne proceeded onward to the church alone.
passages.vernacular: 安妮毫不氣餒,獨自繼續往教堂走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮毫不氣餒,獨自繼續往教堂走。

passages.original: In the porch she found a crowd of little girls, all more or less gaily attired in whites and blues and pinks, and all staring with curious eyes at this stranger in their midst, with her extraordinary head adornment.
passages.vernacular: 喺門廊裡,佢發現一群小女孩,打扮得或多或少都好鮮亮,穿住白嘅、藍嘅、粉紅嘅,全都用好奇嘅眼睛盯住佢哋中間呢個陌生人,同佢嗰非同尋常嘅頭飾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在門廊裡,她發現一群小女孩,打扮得或多或少都很鮮亮,穿著白的、藍的、粉紅的,全都用好奇的眼睛盯著她們中間這個陌生人,和她那非同尋常的頭飾。

passages.original: Avonlea little girls had already heard queer stories about Anne.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利嘅小女孩哋已經聽過關於安妮嘅怪故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利的小女孩們已經聽過關於安妮的怪故事。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde said she had an awful temper; Jerry Buote, the hired boy at Green Gables, said she talked all the time to herself or to the trees and flowers like a crazy girl.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講佢脾氣壞得可怕;綠色屋頂雇嘅小伙子傑里·布特講,佢整天自言自語,或者對住樹同花講話,像個瘋女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說她脾氣壞得可怕;綠色屋頂雇的小伙子傑里·布特說,她整天自言自語,或者對著樹和花說話,像個瘋女孩。

passages.original: They looked at her and whispered to each other behind their quarterlies.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋睇住佢,喺季刊後面互相竊竊私語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們看著她,在季刊後面互相竊竊私語。

passages.original: Nobody made any friendly advances, then or later on when the opening exercises were over and Anne found herself in Miss Rogerson’s class.
passages.vernacular: 冇人做出友好嘅表示,嗰時冇,後來開場儀式結束,安妮發現自己喺羅傑森小姐班上時都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人做出友好的表示,那時沒有,後來開場儀式結束,安妮發現自己在羅傑森小姐班上時也沒有。

passages.original: Miss Rogerson was a middle-aged lady who had taught a Sunday-school class for twenty years.
passages.vernacular: 羅傑森小姐係個中年女士,教主日學校嘅班已有二十年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅傑森小姐是個中年女士,教主日學校的班已有二十年。

passages.original: Her method of teaching was to ask the printed questions from the quarterly and look sternly over its edge at the particular little girl she thought ought to answer the question.
passages.vernacular: 佢教學嘅方法係從季刊上問印好嘅問題,然後嚴厲地隔住佢嘅邊緣睇住佢認為該回答嘅嗰個小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她教學的方法是從季刊上問印好的問題,然後嚴厲地隔著它的邊緣看著她認為該回答的那個小女孩。

passages.original: She looked very often at Anne, and Anne, thanks to Marilla’s drilling, answered promptly; but it may be questioned if she understood very much about either question or answer.
passages.vernacular: 佢經常睇安妮,安妮多虧瑪麗拉嘅訓練,回答得好快;但佢係咪真嘅理解問題同回答,就好難講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她經常看安妮,安妮多虧瑪麗拉的訓練,回答得很快;但她是否真的理解問題和回答,就很難說了。

passages.original: She did not think she liked Miss Rogerson, and she felt very miserable; every other little girl in the class had puffed sleeves.
passages.vernacular: 佢不認為自己鍾意羅傑森小姐,佢感到好痛苦;班上其他每個小女孩都有泡泡袖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不認為自己喜歡羅傑森小姐,她感到非常痛苦;班上其他每個小女孩都有泡泡袖。

passages.original: Anne felt that life was really not worth living without puffed sleeves.
passages.vernacular: 安妮覺得冇泡泡袖,生活真嘅不值得過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮覺得沒有泡泡袖,生活真的不值得過。

passages.original: “Well, how did you like Sunday-school?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你覺得主日學校點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你覺得主日學校怎麼樣?」

passages.original: Marilla wanted to know when Anne came home.
passages.vernacular: 安妮回到家,瑪麗拉想知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮回到家,瑪麗拉想知道。

passages.original: Her wreath having faded, Anne had discarded it in the lane, so Marilla was spared the knowledge of that for a time.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅花環已經凋謝喇,安妮把佢丟棄喺小巷裡,所以瑪麗拉暫時冇被呢事煩擾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的花環已經凋謝了,安妮把它丟棄在小巷裡,所以瑪麗拉暫時沒被這事煩擾。

passages.original: “I didn’t like it a bit.
passages.vernacular: 「我啲都不鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一點也不喜歡。

passages.original: It was horrid.”
passages.vernacular: 太可怕喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太可怕了。」

passages.original: “Anne Shirley!” said Marilla rebukingly.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉!」瑪麗拉責備地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉!」瑪麗拉責備地說。

passages.original: Anne sat down on the rocker with a long sigh, kissed one of Bonny’s leaves, and waved her hand to a blossoming fuchsia.
passages.vernacular: 安妮坐喺搖椅上,長嘆一聲,親吻咗邦妮嘅一片葉子,向一株盛開嘅倒掛金鐘揮咗揮手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮坐在搖椅上,長嘆一聲,親吻了邦妮的一片葉子,向一株盛開的倒掛金鐘揮了揮手。

passages.original: “They might have been lonesome while I was away,” she explained.
passages.vernacular: 「我不喺嘅時候,佢哋可能好孤單,」佢解釋道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不在的時候,它們可能很孤單,」她解釋道。

passages.original: “And now about the Sunday-school.
passages.vernacular: 「而家講講主日學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在說說主日學校。

passages.original: I behaved well, just as you told me.
passages.vernacular: 我表現得好好,就像您告訴我嘅嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我表現得很好,就像您告訴我的那樣。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde was gone, but I went right on myself.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太已經走喇,但我自己繼續往前走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太已經走了,但我自己繼續往前走。

passages.original: I went into the church, with a lot of other little girls, and I sat in the corner of a pew by the window while the opening exercises went on.
passages.vernacular: 我同許多別嘅小女孩一起走進教堂,喺開場儀式進行嘅時候,我坐喺窗邊長椅嘅角落裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我和許多別的小女孩一起走進教堂,在開場儀式進行的時候,我坐在窗邊長椅的角落裡。

passages.original: Mr. Bell made an awfully long prayer.
passages.vernacular: 貝爾先生做咗一個極其長嘅禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝爾先生做了一個極其長的禱告。

passages.original: I would have been dreadfully tired before he got through if I hadn’t been sitting by that window.
passages.vernacular: 要唔係我坐喺嗰扇窗邊,喺佢結束之前我一定累極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是我坐在那扇窗邊,在他結束之前我一定累極了。

passages.original: But it looked right out on the Lake of Shining Waters, so I just gazed at that and imagined all sorts of splendid things.”
passages.vernacular: 但窗子正對住閃亮湖水,所以我就一直望住佢,想像各種壯觀嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但窗子正對著閃亮湖水,所以我就一直望著它,想像各種壯觀的東西。」

passages.original: “You shouldn’t have done anything of the sort.
passages.vernacular: 「你不該做嗰種事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不該做那種事。

passages.original: You should have listened to Mr. Bell.”
passages.vernacular: 你應該聽貝爾先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你應該聽貝爾先生。」

passages.original: “But he wasn’t talking to me,” protested Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「可佢唔係喺跟我講話呀,」安妮抗議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可他不是在跟我說話呀,」安妮抗議。

passages.original: “He was talking to God and he didn’t seem to be very much interested in it, either.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係喺對上帝講話,而且佢似乎對此都不太感興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是在對上帝說話,而且他似乎對此也不太感興趣。

passages.original: I think he thought God was too far off though.
passages.vernacular: 不過我想佢認為上帝太遠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我想他認為上帝太遠了。

passages.original: There was a long row of white birches hanging over the lake and the sunshine fell down through them, ‘way, ‘way down, deep into the water.
passages.vernacular: 有一長排白樺樹懸喺湖面上,陽光透過佢哋灑下去,遠遠地,遠遠地,深入水底。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一長排白樺樹懸在湖面上,陽光透過它們灑下去,遠遠地,遠遠地,深入水底。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, it was like a beautiful dream!
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,嗰就像一場美麗嘅夢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,那就像一場美麗的夢!

passages.original: It gave me a thrill and I just said, ‘Thank you for it, God,’ two or three times.”
passages.vernacular: 佢讓我心頭一顫,我就講咗兩三遍『謝謝祢賜畀我呢個,上帝』。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它讓我心頭一顫,我就說了兩三遍『謝謝祢賜給我這個,上帝』。」

passages.original: “Not out loud, I hope,” said Marilla anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望唔係大聲講嘅,」瑪麗拉焦急地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望不是大聲說的,」瑪麗拉焦急地說。

passages.original: “Oh, no, just under my breath.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不,只係壓低聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不,只是壓低聲音。

passages.original: Well, Mr. Bell did get through at last and they told me to go into the classroom with Miss Rogerson’s class.
passages.vernacular: 後來貝爾先生終於結束喇,佢哋叫我跟羅傑森小姐嘅班進教室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後來貝爾先生終於結束了,他們叫我跟羅傑森小姐的班進教室。

passages.original: There were nine other girls in it.
passages.vernacular: 班上仲有九個女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班上還有九個女孩。

passages.original: They all had puffed sleeves.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都有泡泡袖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們都有泡泡袖。

passages.original: I tried to imagine mine were puffed, too, but I couldn’t.
passages.vernacular: 我試著想像我嘅都係泡泡袖,但不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我試著想像我的也是泡泡袖,但不行。

passages.original: Why couldn’t I?
passages.vernacular: 點解我不行?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼我不行?

passages.original: It was as easy as could be to imagine they were puffed when I was alone in the east gable, but it was awfully hard there among the others who had really truly puffs.”
passages.vernacular: 我獨自在東山牆房間嘅時候,想像佢哋係泡泡袖輕而易舉,但喺嗰啲真正有泡泡袖嘅人中間就難極喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我獨自在東山牆房間的時候,想像它們是泡泡袖輕而易舉,但在那些真正有泡泡袖的人中間就難極了。」

passages.original: “You shouldn’t have been thinking about your sleeves in Sunday-school.
passages.vernacular: 「你喺主日學校不該想你嘅袖子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你在主日學校不該想你的袖子。

passages.original: You should have been attending to the lesson.
passages.vernacular: 你應該專心聽課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你應該專心聽課。

passages.original: I hope you knew it.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望你懂喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你懂了。」

passages.original: “Oh, yes; and I answered a lot of questions.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,懂喇;我仲回答咗好多問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,懂了;我還回答了很多問題。

passages.original: Miss Rogerson asked ever so many.
passages.vernacular: 羅傑森小姐問咗好多好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅傑森小姐問了好多好多。

passages.original: I don’t think it was fair for her to do all the asking.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得全由佢一個人問不公平。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得全由她一個人問不公平。

passages.original: There were lots I wanted to ask her, but I didn’t like to because I didn’t think she was a kindred spirit.
passages.vernacular: 有好多我想問佢嘅,但我唔想問,因為我覺得佢唔係志同道合嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有很多我想問她的,但我不想問,因為我覺得她不是志同道合的人。

passages.original: Then all the other little girls recited a paraphrase.
passages.vernacular: 後來所有別嘅小女孩都背誦咗一篇聖詩釋義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後來所有別的小女孩都背誦了一篇聖詩釋義。

passages.original: She asked me if I knew any.
passages.vernacular: 佢問我知道唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她問我知道不知道。

passages.original: I told her I didn’t, but I could recite, ‘The Dog at His Master’s Grave’ if she liked.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴佢我唔知道,但如果佢鍾意,我可以背《狗喺主人墳前》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴她我不知道,但如果她喜歡,我可以背《狗在主人墳前》。

passages.original: That’s in the Third Royal Reader.
passages.vernacular: 嗰喺《皇家第三讀本》裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那在《皇家第三讀本》裡。

passages.original: It isn’t a really truly religious piece of poetry, but it’s so sad and melancholy that it might as well be.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係真正嘅宗教詩,但佢咁悲傷憂鬱,簡直可以算係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不是真正的宗教詩,但它那麼悲傷憂鬱,簡直可以算是。

passages.original: She said it wouldn’t do and she told me to learn the nineteenth paraphrase for next Sunday.
passages.vernacular: 佢講不行,讓我下個星期天前學會第十九首釋義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說不行,讓我下個星期天前學會第十九首釋義。

passages.original: I read it over in church afterwards and it’s splendid.
passages.vernacular: 後來喺教堂裡我讀咗一遍,太棒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後來在教堂裡我讀了一遍,太棒了。

passages.original: There are two lines in particular that just thrill me.
passages.vernacular: 有兩行特唔好畀我心潮澎湃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有兩行特別讓我心潮澎湃。

passages.original: “‘Quick as the slaughtered squadrons fell In Midian’s evil day.’
passages.vernacular: 「『如被屠戮嘅軍團倒下一般迅疾,喺米甸遭難嘅嗰一天。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『如被屠戮的軍團倒下一般迅疾,在米甸遭難的那一天。』

passages.original: “I don’t know what ‘squadrons’ means nor ‘Midian,’ either, but it sounds so tragical.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道『軍團』係乜嘢意思,都唔知道『米甸』,不過聽起嚟咁悲壯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道『軍團』是什麼意思,也不知道『米甸』,可是聽起來那麼悲壯。

passages.original: I can hardly wait until next Sunday to recite it.
passages.vernacular: 我幾乎等不及到下個星期天去背誦佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我幾乎等不及到下個星期天去背誦它。

passages.original: I’ll practice it all the week.
passages.vernacular: 我要整個星期都練習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要整個星期都練習。

passages.original: After Sunday-school I asked Miss Rogerson--because Mrs. Lynde was too far away--to show me your pew.
passages.vernacular: 主日學校之後我請羅傑森小姐——因為林德太太離得太遠喇——指畀我睇您嘅長椅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 主日學校之後我請羅傑森小姐——因為林德太太離得太遠了——指給我看您的長椅。

passages.original: I sat just as still as I could and the text was Revelations, third chapter, second and third verses.
passages.vernacular: 我儘可能一動不動地坐住,經文係啟示錄,第三章,第二節同第三節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我儘可能一動不動地坐著,經文是啟示錄,第三章,第二節和第三節。

passages.original: It was a very long text.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一段好長嘅經文。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一段非常長的經文。

passages.original: If I was a minister I’d pick the short, snappy ones.
passages.vernacular: 如果我係牧師,我會選嗰啲短而有力嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我是牧師,我會選那些短而有力的。

passages.original: The sermon was awfully long, too.
passages.vernacular: 講道都特別長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 講道也特別長。

passages.original: I suppose the minister had to match it to the text.
passages.vernacular: 我想牧師必須使佢同經文相配。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想牧師必須使它與經文相配。

passages.original: I didn’t think he was a bit interesting.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得佢啲都不有趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得他一點也不有趣。

passages.original: The trouble with him seems to be that he hasn’t enough imagination.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅問題似乎係想像力唔夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的問題似乎是想像力不夠。

passages.original: I didn’t listen to him very much.
passages.vernacular: 我不點聽佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不怎麼聽他講。

passages.original: I just let my thoughts run and I thought of the most surprising things.”
passages.vernacular: 我只係讓思緒馳騁,想到咗最令人驚奇嘅事情。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是讓思緒馳騁,想到了最令人驚奇的事情。」

passages.original: Marilla felt helplessly that all this should be sternly reproved, but she was hampered by the undeniable fact that some of the things Anne had said, especially about the minister’s sermons and Mr. Bell’s prayers, were what she herself had really thought deep down in her heart for years, but had never given expression to.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉無助地覺得,所有呢啲都應該受到嚴厲嘅責備,但佢被一個無可否認嘅事實所牽制:安妮講嘅有些話,尤其係關於牧師講道同貝爾先生禱告嘅,恰恰係佢自己多年嚟內心深處真正想過、卻從未表達過嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉無助地覺得,所有這些都應該受到嚴厲的責備,但她被一個無可否認的事實所牽制:安妮說的有些話,尤其是關於牧師講道和貝爾先生禱告的,恰恰是她自己多年來內心深處真正想過、卻從未表達過的。

passages.original: It almost seemed to her that those secret, unuttered, critical thoughts had suddenly taken visible and accusing shape and form in the person of this outspoken morsel of neglected humanity.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢睇來,呢啲祕密嘅、未講出口嘅批評想法,似乎突然喺呢個直言不諱嘅、被忽視嘅小人類身上,有咗可見嘅、指控性嘅形狀同面目。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她看來,這些祕密的、未說出口的批評想法,似乎突然在這個直言不諱的、被忽視的小人類身上,有了可見的、指控性的形狀和面目。

chapters.title: Ch. XII A Solemn Vow and Promise 第十二章:莊嚴的誓言與承諾

passages.original: CH IT was not until the next Friday that Marilla heard the story of the flower-wreathed hat.
passages.vernacular: 直到下個星期五,瑪麗拉才聽講咗嗰頂鮮花帽嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到下個星期五,瑪麗拉才聽說了那頂鮮花帽的事。

passages.original: She came home from Mrs. Lynde’s and called Anne to account.
passages.vernacular: 佢從林德太太家回嚟,把安妮叫嚟問話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她從林德太太家回來,把安妮叫來問話。

passages.original: “Anne, Mrs. Rachel says you went to church last Sunday with your hat rigged out ridiculous with roses and buttercups.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,雷切爾太太講你上星期天去教堂,帽子上滑稽地插滿咗玫瑰同毛茛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,雷切爾太太說你上星期天去教堂,帽子上滑稽地插滿了玫瑰和毛茛。

passages.original: What on earth put you up to such a caper?
passages.vernacular: 到底係乜嘢讓你搞出呢種花樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到底是什麼讓你搞出這種花樣?

passages.original: A pretty-looking object you must have been!”
passages.vernacular: 你當時一定係個好睇嘅樣子!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你當時一定是個好看的樣子!」

passages.original: “Oh.
I know pink and yellow aren’t becoming to me,” began Anne.
passages.vernacular: 我知道粉紅色同黃色不配我,」安妮開口講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道粉紅色和黃色不配我,」安妮開口說。

passages.original: “Becoming fiddlesticks!
passages.vernacular: 「配乜嘢不配!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「配什麼不配!

passages.original: It was putting flowers on your hat at all, no matter what color they were, that was ridiculous.
passages.vernacular: 根本係喺帽子上插花呢件事本身滑稽,不管係乜嘢顏色嘅花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 根本是在帽子上插花這件事本身滑稽,不管是什麼顏色的花。

passages.original: You are the most aggravating child!”
passages.vernacular: 你真係最氣人嘅細路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你真是最氣人的孩子!」

passages.original: “I don’t see why it’s any more ridiculous to wear flowers on your hat than on your dress,” protested Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白點解喺帽子上戴花,比喺裙子上戴花更滑稽,」安妮抗議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白為什麼在帽子上戴花,比在裙子上戴花更滑稽,」安妮抗議。

passages.original: “Lots of little girls there had bouquets pinned on their dresses.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰兒有好多小女孩喺裙子上別住花束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那兒有好多小女孩在裙子上別著花束。

passages.original: What’s the difference?”
passages.vernacular: 有乜嘢區別?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有什麼區別?」

passages.original: Marilla was not to be drawn from the safe concrete into dubious paths of the abstract.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉唔肯從安全嘅具體事物被拉進模稜兩可嘅抽象嘅小道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉不肯從安全的具體事物被拉進模稜兩可的抽象的小道。

passages.original: “Don’t answer me back like that, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「別嗰樣頂嘴,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別那樣頂嘴,安妮。

passages.original: It was very silly of you to do such a thing.
passages.vernacular: 你做嗰種事太傻喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你做那種事太傻了。

passages.original: Never let me catch you at such a trick again.
passages.vernacular: 再讓我睇到你耍嗰種花招。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再讓我看到你耍那種花招。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel says she thought she would sink through the floor when she saw you come in all rigged out like that.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太講,佢睇見你打扮成嗰樣進嚟,恨唔得地上有個洞鑽下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太說,她看見你打扮成那樣進來,恨不得地上有個洞鑽下去。

passages.original: She couldn’t get near enough to tell you to take them off till it was too late.
passages.vernacular: 佢離得唔夠近,等能走過去叫你摘下嚟時,已經太晚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她離得不夠近,等能走過去叫你摘下來時,已經太晚了。

passages.original: She says people talked about it something dreadful.
passages.vernacular: 佢講人哋議論得特別厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說人們議論得特別厲害。

passages.original: Of course they would think I had no better sense than to let you go decked out like that.”
passages.vernacular: 當然佢哋會認為我冇啲頭腦,才會讓你打扮成嗰樣出去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然他們會認為我沒有一點頭腦,才會讓你打扮成那樣出去。」

passages.original: “Oh, I’m so sorry,” said Anne, tears welling into her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我好抱歉,」安妮講,眼淚湧上咗眼眶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我非常抱歉,」安妮說,眼淚湧上了眼眶。

passages.original: “I never thought you’d mind.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇想過您會介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒想過您會介意。

passages.original: The roses and buttercups were so sweet and pretty I thought they’d look lovely on my hat.
passages.vernacular: 玫瑰同毛茛咁甜美漂亮,我覺得戴喺我帽子上一定好好睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 玫瑰和毛茛那麼甜美漂亮,我覺得戴在我帽子上一定很好看。

passages.original: Lots of the little girls had artificial flowers on their hats.
passages.vernacular: 好多小女孩帽子上都戴住假花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好多小女孩帽子上都戴著假花。

passages.original: I’m afraid I’m going to be a dreadful trial to you.
passages.vernacular: 我怕我會成為您嘅大麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕我會成為您的大麻煩。

passages.original: Maybe you’d better send me back to the asylum.
passages.vernacular: 或者您最好把我送回孤兒院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許您最好把我送回孤兒院。

passages.original: That would be terrible; I don’t think I could endure it; most likely I would go into consumption; I’m so thin as it is, you see.
passages.vernacular: 嗰會好可怕;我想我受不喇;我好可能會得肺癆;您瞧,我已經咁瘦喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那會很可怕;我想我受不了;我很可能會得肺癆;您瞧,我已經這麼瘦了。

passages.original: But that would be better than being a trial to you.”
passages.vernacular: 但嗰比成為您嘅麻煩要好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那比成為您的麻煩要好。」

passages.original: “Nonsense,” said Marilla, vexed at herself for having made the child cry.
passages.vernacular: 「胡講,」瑪麗拉講,為自己讓細路哭咗而惱火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說,」瑪麗拉說,為自己讓孩子哭了而惱火。

passages.original: “I don’t want to send you back to the asylum, I’m sure.
passages.vernacular: 「我當然唔想把你送回孤兒院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我當然不想把你送回孤兒院。

passages.original: All I want is that you should behave like other little girls and not make yourself ridiculous.
passages.vernacular: 我只希望你像別嘅小女孩一樣行事,唔好讓自己出洋相。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只希望你像別的小女孩一樣行事,不要讓自己出洋相。

passages.original: Don’t cry any more.
passages.vernacular: 唔好再哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別再哭了。

passages.original: I’ve got some news for you.
passages.vernacular: 我有個消息要告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有個消息要告訴你。

passages.original: Diana Barry came home this afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜·巴里今日下午回家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜·巴里今天下午回家了。

passages.original: I’m going up to see if I can borrow a skirt pattern from Mrs. Barry, and if you like you can come with me and get acquainted with Diana.”
passages.vernacular: 我要上去睇睇能唔能夠從巴里太太嗰兒借一個裙子紙樣,你要係願意,可以跟我一起去,認識認識黛安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要上去看看能不能從巴里太太那兒借一個裙子紙樣,你要是願意,可以跟我一起去,認識認識黛安娜。」

passages.original: Anne rose to her feet, with clasped hands, the tears still glistening on her cheeks; the dish towel she had been hemming slipped unheeded to the floor.
passages.vernacular: 安妮站起身嚟,雙手緊握,眼淚仲喺臉頰上閃住光;佢正在縫邊嘅洗碗巾無人理會地滑落到地板上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮站起身來,雙手緊握,眼淚還在臉頰上閃著光;她正在縫邊的洗碗巾無人理會地滑落到地板上。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened--now that it has come I’m actually frightened.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我害怕喇——而家佢真嘅嚟喇,我真嘅害怕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我害怕了——現在它真的來了,我真的害怕了。

passages.original: What if she shouldn’t like me!
passages.vernacular: 要係佢不鍾意我點算!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是她不喜歡我怎麼辦!

passages.original: It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰將係我一生中最悲慘嘅失望。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那將是我一生中最悲慘的失望。」

passages.original: “Now, don’t get into a fluster.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,別慌張。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,別慌張。

passages.original: And I do wish you wouldn’t use such long words.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望你唔好用咁長嘅詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望你不要用那麼長的詞。

passages.original: It sounds so funny in a little girl.
passages.vernacular: 從一個小女孩嘴裡講出嚟,聽起嚟太滑稽喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從一個小女孩嘴裡說出來,聽起來太滑稽了。

passages.original: I guess Diana ‘ll like you well enough.
passages.vernacular: 我想黛安娜會足夠鍾意你嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想黛安娜會足夠喜歡你的。

passages.original: It’s her mother you’ve got to reckon with.
passages.vernacular: 你要對付嘅係佢母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要對付的是她母親。

passages.original: If she doesn’t like you it won’t matter how much Diana does.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢不鍾意你,黛安娜再鍾意你都冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她不喜歡你,黛安娜再喜歡你也沒用。

passages.original: If she has heard about your outburst to Mrs. Lynde and going to church with buttercups round your hat I don’t know what she’ll think of you.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢聽講咗你對林德太太嘅發作,仲有你戴住毛茛帽子去教堂,我唔知道佢會點睇你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她聽說了你對林德太太的發作,還有你戴著毛茛帽子去教堂,我不知道她會怎麼看你。

passages.original: You must be polite and well behaved, and don’t make any of your startling speeches.
passages.vernacular: 你一定要有禮貌,舉止得體,唔好講乜嘢驚人嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一定要有禮貌,舉止得體,別說什麼驚人的話。

passages.original: For pity’s sake, if the child isn’t actually trembling!”
passages.vernacular: 天呀,呢細路居然真嘅喺發抖!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,這孩子居然真的在發抖!」

passages.original: Anne was trembling.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在發抖。

passages.original: Her face was pale and tense.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉色蒼白而緊繃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉色蒼白而緊繃。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, you’d be excited, too, if you were going to meet a little girl you hoped to be your bosom friend and whose mother mightn’t like you,” she said as she hastened to get her hat.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,如果您要去見一個您希望成為知心朋友嘅小女孩,而佢嘅母親可能不鍾意您,您都會激動嘅,」佢一邊匆忙去攞帽子,一邊講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,如果您要去見一個您希望成為知心朋友的小女孩,而她的母親可能不喜歡您,您也會激動的,」她一邊匆忙去拿帽子,一邊說。

passages.original: They went over to Orchard Slope by the short cut across the brook and up the firry hill grove.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋走小路穿過小溪,爬上杉樹林嘅山坡,去咗果園坡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們走小路穿過小溪,爬上杉樹林的山坡,去了果園坡。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry came to the kitchen door in answer to Marilla’s knock.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉敲咗敲門,巴里太太嚟到廚房門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉敲了敲門,巴里太太來到廚房門口。

passages.original: She was a tall black-eyed, black-haired woman, with a very resolute mouth.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個高個子、黑眼睛、黑頭髮嘅女人,嘴巴好堅決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個高個子、黑眼睛、黑頭髮的女人,嘴巴很堅決。

passages.original: She had the reputation of being very strict with her children.
passages.vernacular: 佢以對細路管教嚴格而出名。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她以對孩子管教嚴格而出名。

passages.original: “How do you do, Marilla?” she said cordially.
passages.vernacular: 「你好,瑪麗拉?」佢熱情地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你好,瑪麗拉?」她熱情地說。

passages.original: “Come in.
passages.vernacular: 「請進。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請進。

passages.original: And this is the little girl you have adopted, I suppose?”
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係你領養嘅嗰個小女孩吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是你領養的那個小女孩吧?」

passages.original: “Yes, this is Anne Shirley,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,呢個係安妮·雪莉,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,這是安妮·雪莉,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “Spelled with an E,” gasped Anne, who, tremulous and excited as she was, was determined there should be no misunderstanding on that important point.
passages.vernacular: 「末尾帶E嘅,」安妮氣喘住講,雖然佢顫抖又興奮,但佢決心喺呢個重要嘅問題上絕唔能夠有誤解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「末尾帶E的,」安妮氣喘著說,雖然她顫抖又興奮,但她決心在這個重要的問題上絕不能有誤解。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry, not hearing or not comprehending, merely shook hands and said kindly:
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太冇聽見或者冇聽明白,只係握咗握手,和藹地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太沒聽見或者沒聽明白,只是握了握手,和藹地說:

passages.original: “How are you?”
passages.vernacular: 「你好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你好嗎?」

passages.original: “I am well in body although considerable rumpled up in spirit, thank you ma’am,” said Anne gravely.
passages.vernacular: 「我身體好好,不過精神上相當凌亂,謝謝您,太太,」安妮嚴肅地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我身體很好,不過精神上相當凌亂,謝謝您,太太,」安妮嚴肅地說。

passages.original: Then aside to Marilla in an audible whisper, “There wasn’t anything startling in that, was there, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 然後佢對瑪麗拉用清晰可聞嘅耳語講:「嗰度面冇乜嘢驚人嘅話,係唔係,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她對瑪麗拉用清晰可聞的耳語說:「那裡面沒什麼驚人的話,是不是,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: Diana was sitting on the sofa, reading a book which she dropped when the callers entered.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜坐喺沙發上睇書,客人進嚟時,佢把書放下喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜坐在沙發上看書,客人進來時,她把書放下了。

passages.original: She was a very pretty little girl, with her mother’s black eyes and hair, and rosy cheeks, and the merry expression which was her inheritance from her father.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個好漂亮嘅小女孩,有住母親嘅黑眼睛同黑頭髮、紅潤嘅臉頰,以及繼承自父親嘅歡快表情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個非常漂亮的小女孩,有著母親的黑眼睛和黑頭髮、紅潤的臉頰,以及繼承自父親的歡快表情。

passages.original: “This is my little girl Diana,” said Mrs. Barry.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我嘅小女兒黛安娜,」巴里太太講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我的小女兒黛安娜,」巴里太太說。

passages.original: “Diana, you might take Anne out into the garden and show her your flowers.
passages.vernacular: 「黛安娜,你可以帶安妮去花園,畀佢睇睇你嘅花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黛安娜,你可以帶安妮去花園,給她看看你的花。

passages.original: It will be better for you than straining your eyes over that book.
passages.vernacular: 呢對你比累眼睛睇嗰本書強。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這對你比累眼睛看那本書強。

passages.original: She reads entirely too much--” this to Marilla as the little girls went out--“and I can’t prevent her, for her father aids and abets her.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇書太多喇——」呢個係喺小女孩哋出去時對瑪麗拉講嘅——「我又冇法阻止佢,因為佢父親支持縱容佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看書太多了——」這是在小女孩們出去時對瑪麗拉說的——「我又沒法阻止她,因為她父親支持縱容她。

passages.original: She’s always poring over a book.
passages.vernacular: 佢總是埋頭睇書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她總是埋頭看書。

passages.original: I’m glad she has the prospect of a playmate--perhaps it will take her more out-of-doors.”
passages.vernacular: 我好高興佢有機會有個玩伴——或者呢會讓佢更多地去戶外。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興她有機會有個玩伴——也許這會讓她更多地去戶外。」

passages.original: Outside in the garden, which was full of mellow sunset light streaming through the dark old firs to the west of it, stood Anne and Diana, gazing bashfully at each other over a clump of gorgeous tiger lilies.
passages.vernacular: 外面花園裡,柔和嘅夕陽光穿過西邊黑壓壓嘅老杉樹傾瀉進嚟,安妮同黛安娜站喺一叢華麗嘅虎皮百合上方,羞怯地互相望住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 外面花園裡,柔和的夕陽光穿過西邊黑壓壓的老杉樹傾瀉進來,安妮和黛安娜站在一叢華麗的虎皮百合上方,羞怯地互相望著。

passages.original: The Barry garden was a bowery wilderness of flowers which would have delighted Anne’s heart at any time less fraught with destiny.
passages.vernacular: 巴里家嘅花園係一片濃蔭覆蓋嘅花叢荒野,要係喺不咁關乎命運嘅時刻,一定會令安妮心花怒放。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里家的花園是一片濃蔭覆蓋的花叢荒野,要是在不那麼關乎命運的時刻,一定會令安妮心花怒放。

passages.original: It was encircled by huge old willows and tall firs, beneath which flourished flowers that loved the shade.
passages.vernacular: 佢被巨大嘅老柳樹同高大嘅杉樹環繞,樹下盛開住鍾意陰涼嘅花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它被巨大的老柳樹和高大的杉樹環繞,樹下盛開著喜歡陰涼的花。

passages.original: Prim, right-angled paths neatly bordered with clamshells, intersected it like moist red ribbons and in the beds between old-fashioned flowers ran riot.
passages.vernacular: 規規矩矩、成直角嘅小徑整齊地鑲住蛤殼邊,像濕潤嘅紅絲帶一樣縱橫交錯,小徑之間嘅花壇裡,老式嘅花朵肆意瘋長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 規規矩矩、成直角的小徑整齊地鑲著蛤殼邊,像濕潤的紅絲帶一樣縱橫交錯,小徑之間的花壇裡,老式的花朵肆意瘋長。

passages.original: There were rosy bleeding-hearts and great splendid crimson peonies; white, fragrant narcissi and thorny, sweet Scotch roses; pink and blue and white columbines and lilac-tinted Bouncing Bets; clumps of southernwood and ribbon grass and mint; purple Adam-and-Eve, daffodils, and masses of sweet clover white with its delicate, fragrant, feathery sprays; scarlet lightning that shot its fiery lances over prim white musk-flowers; a garden it was where sunshine lingered and bees hummed, and winds, beguiled into loitering, purred and rustled.
passages.vernacular: 有粉紅嘅荷包牡丹同碩大壯麗嘅深紅芍藥;潔白芬芳嘅水仙同多刺而甜美嘅蘇格蘭薔薇;粉紅、藍色同白色嘅耬斗菜,以及淡紫色嘅肥皂草;一叢叢青蒿、絲帶草同薄荷;紫色嘅亞當夏娃花、黃水仙,仲有一大片甜三葉草,白色嘅嫩穗芳香而羽毛般輕盈;猩紅嘅閃電花,把佢火焰般嘅長矛射向規規矩矩嘅白麝香花;呢個係一個陽光流連、蜜蜂嗡鳴嘅花園,風都被誘得逗留不去,發出咕嚕同沙沙嘅聲響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有粉紅的荷包牡丹和碩大壯麗的深紅芍藥;潔白芬芳的水仙和多刺而甜美的蘇格蘭薔薇;粉紅、藍色和白色的耬斗菜,以及淡紫色的肥皂草;一叢叢青蒿、絲帶草和薄荷;紫色的亞當夏娃花、黃水仙,還有一大片甜三葉草,白色的嫩穗芳香而羽毛般輕盈;猩紅的閃電花,把它火焰般的長矛射向規規矩矩的白麝香花;這是一個陽光流連、蜜蜂嗡鳴的花園,風也被誘得逗留不去,發出咕嚕和沙沙的聲響。

passages.original: “Oh, Diana,” said Anne at last, clasping her hands and speaking almost in a whisper, “oh, do you think you can like me a little--enough to be my bosom friend?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,黛安娜,」安妮終於雙手緊握、幾乎低語地講,「哦,你覺得你能有點鍾意我嗎——鍾意到能做我嘅知心朋友?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,黛安娜,」安妮終於雙手緊握、幾乎低語地說,「哦,你覺得你能有點喜歡我嗎——喜歡到能做我的知心朋友?」

passages.original: Diana laughed.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜笑了。

passages.original: Diana always laughed before she spoke.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜總是先笑再講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜總是先笑再說話。

passages.original: “Why, I guess so,” she said frankly.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我想可以,」佢坦率地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我想可以,」她坦率地說。

passages.original: “I’m awfully glad you’ve come to live at Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 「我好高興你嚟綠色屋頂住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我非常高興你來綠色屋頂住了。

passages.original: It will be jolly to have somebody to play with.
passages.vernacular: 有個一起玩嘅人太好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有個一起玩的人太好了。

passages.original: There isn’t any other girl who lives near enough to play with, and I’ve no sisters big enough.”
passages.vernacular: 附近冇別嘅女孩近得能一起玩,我嘅姐妹又都唔夠大。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 附近沒有別的女孩近得能一起玩,我的姐妹又都不夠大。」

passages.original: “Will you swear to be my friend forever and ever?” demanded Anne eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「你願意發誓永遠永遠做我嘅朋友嗎?」安妮急切地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你願意發誓永遠永遠做我的朋友嗎?」安妮急切地問。

passages.original: Diana looked shocked.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜顯得震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜顯得震驚。

passages.original: “Why it’s dreadfully wicked to swear,” she said rebukingly.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,發誓係好邪惡嘅,」佢責備地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,發誓是非常邪惡的,」她責備地說。

passages.original: “Oh no, not my kind of swearing.
passages.vernacular: 「哦不,唔係我講嘅嗰種發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦不,不是我說的那種發誓。

passages.original: There are two kinds, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道,有兩種。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,有兩種。」

passages.original: “I never heard of but one kind,” said Diana doubtfully.
passages.vernacular: 「我只聽講過一種,」黛安娜懷疑地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只聽說過一種,」黛安娜懷疑地說。

passages.original: “There really is another.
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅仲有另一種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的還有另一種。

passages.original: Oh, it isn’t wicked at all.
passages.vernacular: 哦,佢啲都不邪惡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,它一點也不邪惡。

passages.original: It just means vowing and promising solemnly.”
passages.vernacular: 佢只係意味住莊嚴地立誓同承諾。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它只是意味著莊嚴地立誓和承諾。」

passages.original: “Well, I don’t mind doing that,” agreed Diana, relieved.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我不介意做呢個,」黛安娜如釋重負地同意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不介意做這個,」黛安娜如釋重負地同意。

passages.original: “How do you do it?”
passages.vernacular: 「點做?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼做?」

passages.original: “We must join hands--so,” said Anne gravely.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋必須手拉手——像咁樣,」安妮嚴肅地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們必須手拉手——像這樣,」安妮嚴肅地說。

passages.original: “It ought to be over running water.
passages.vernacular: 「應該喺流水上方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「應該在流水上方。

passages.original: We’ll just imagine this path is running water.
passages.vernacular: 我哋就想像呢條小路係流水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們就想像這條小路是流水。

passages.original: I’ll repeat the oath first.
passages.vernacular: 我先念誓詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我先念誓詞。

passages.original: I solemnly swear to be faithful to my bosom friend, Diana Barry, as long as the sun and moon shall endure.
passages.vernacular: 我鄭重發誓,只要日月長存,就對我嘅知心朋友黛安娜·巴里忠誠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我鄭重發誓,只要日月長存,就對我的知心朋友黛安娜·巴里忠誠。

passages.original: Now you say it and put my name in.”
passages.vernacular: 而家你講,把我嘅名字放進去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你說,把我的名字放進去。」

passages.original: Diana repeated the “oath” with a laugh fore and aft.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜笑著重複咗呢個「誓言」,前前後後都喺笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜笑著重複了這個「誓言」,前前後後都在笑。

passages.original: Then she said:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她說:

passages.original: “You’re a queer girl, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「你係個古怪嘅女孩,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是個古怪的女孩,安妮。

passages.original: I heard before that you were queer.
passages.vernacular: 我早就聽講過你古怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我早就聽說過你古怪。

passages.original: But I believe I’m going to like you real well.”
passages.vernacular: 但我相信我會好鍾意你嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我相信我會很喜歡你的。」

passages.original: When Marilla and Anne went home Diana went with them as far as the log bridge.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉同安妮回家時,黛安娜陪佢哋一直走到原木橋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉和安妮回家時,黛安娜陪她們一直走到原木橋。

passages.original: The two little girls walked with their arms about each other.
passages.vernacular: 兩個小女孩摟住對方嘅腰走住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個小女孩摟著對方的腰走著。

passages.original: At the brook they parted with many promises to spend the next afternoon together.
passages.vernacular: 喺小溪邊佢哋分手喇,許下許多諾言,要喺第二天下午一起度過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在小溪邊她們分手了,許下許多諾言,要在第二天下午一起度過。

passages.original: “Well, did you find Diana a kindred spirit?” asked Marilla as they went up through the garden of Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你發現黛安娜係個志同道合嘅人嗎?」佢哋穿過綠色屋頂嘅花園時,瑪麗拉問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你發現黛安娜是個志同道合的人嗎?」她們穿過綠色屋頂的花園時,瑪麗拉問。

passages.original: “Oh yes,” sighed Anne, blissfully unconscious of any sarcasm on Marilla’s part.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,」安妮嘆道,絲毫冇意識到瑪麗拉話裡嘅諷刺,沉浸喺幸福中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,」安妮嘆道,絲毫沒意識到瑪麗拉話裡的諷刺,沉浸在幸福中。

passages.original: “Oh Marilla, I’m the happiest girl on Prince Edward Island this very moment.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,此刻我係愛德華王子島上最幸福嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,此刻我是愛德華王子島上最幸福的女孩。

passages.original: I assure you I’ll say my prayers with a right good-will tonight.
passages.vernacular: 我向您保證,今晚我會心甘情願地做禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向您保證,今晚我會心甘情願地做禱告。

passages.original: Diana and I are going to build a playhouse in Mr. William Bell’s birch grove tomorrow.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜同我聽日要喺威廉·貝爾先生嘅白樺林裡建一座遊戲屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜和我明天要在威廉·貝爾先生的白樺林裡建一座遊戲屋。

passages.original: Can I have those broken pieces of china that are out in the woodshed?
passages.vernacular: 我能要柴棚裡嗰啲碎瓷器嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能要柴棚裡那些碎瓷器嗎?

passages.original: Diana’s birthday is in February and mine is in March.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜嘅生日喺二月,我嘅喺三月。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜的生日在二月,我的在三月。

passages.original: Don’t you think that is a very strange coincidence?
passages.vernacular: 您不覺得呢個係個好奇怪嘅巧合嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不覺得這是個非常奇怪的巧合嗎?

passages.original: Diana is going to lend me a book to read.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜要借我一本書睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜要借我一本書看。

passages.original: She says it’s perfectly splendid and tremendously exciting.
passages.vernacular: 佢講呢書特別精彩,特別刺激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說這書特別精彩,特別刺激。

passages.original: She’s going to show me a place back in the woods where rice lilies grow.
passages.vernacular: 佢要帶我去睇樹林深處長住稻花百合嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她要帶我去看樹林深處長著稻花百合的地方。

passages.original: Don’t you think Diana has got very soulful eyes?
passages.vernacular: 您不覺得黛安娜有一雙好有靈性嘅眼睛嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不覺得黛安娜有一雙非常有靈性的眼睛嗎?

passages.original: I wish I had soulful eyes.
passages.vernacular: 我希望我有一雙有靈性嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我有一雙有靈性的眼睛。

passages.original: Diana is going to teach me to sing a song called ‘Nelly in the Hazel Dell.’
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜要教我唱一首叫《榛樹谷中嘅內莉》嘅歌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜要教我唱一首叫《榛樹谷中的內莉》的歌。

passages.original: She’s going to give me a picture to put up in my room; it’s a perfectly beautiful picture, she says--a lovely lady in a pale blue silk dress.
passages.vernacular: 佢要送我一張畫掛喺房間裡;佢講呢畫特別美——一位穿淡藍色絲綢裙子嘅可愛女士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她要送我一張畫掛在房間裡;她說這畫特別美——一位穿淡藍色絲綢裙子的可愛女士。

passages.original: A sewing-machine agent gave it to her.
passages.vernacular: 係一個縫紉機推銷員送畀佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是一個縫紉機推銷員送給她的。

passages.original: I wish I had something to give Diana.
passages.vernacular: 我希望我有乜嘢嘢可以送畀黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我有什麼東西可以送給黛安娜。

passages.original: I’m an inch taller than Diana, but she is ever so much fatter; she says she’d like to be thin because it’s so much more graceful, but I’m afraid she only said it to soothe my feelings.
passages.vernacular: 我比黛安娜高一寸,不過佢胖得多;佢講佢想瘦,因為瘦幾咁優雅,但我怕佢只係為了安慰我嘅感情才咁講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我比黛安娜高一寸,不過她胖得多;她說她想瘦,因為瘦多麼優雅,但我怕她只是為了安慰我的感情才這麼說的。

passages.original: We’re going to the shore some day to gather shells.
passages.vernacular: 有一天我哋要去海邊撿貝殼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天我們要去海邊撿貝殼。

passages.original: We have agreed to call the spring down by the log bridge the Dryad’s Bubble.
passages.vernacular: 我哋已經商定把原木橋旁嘅嗰眼泉叫做林中仙子泉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們已經商定把原木橋旁的那眼泉叫做林中仙子泉。

passages.original: Isn’t that a perfectly elegant name?
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係一個特別高雅嘅名字嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是一個特別高雅的名字嗎?

passages.original: I read a story once about a spring called that.
passages.vernacular: 我曾讀過一個故事,有一眼泉就叫呢個名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我曾讀過一個故事,有一眼泉就叫這個名字。

passages.original: A dryad is sort of a grown-up fairy, I think.”
passages.vernacular: 我想林中仙子係一種長大咗嘅小仙女。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想林中仙子是一種長大了的小仙女。」

passages.original: “Well, all I hope is you won’t talk Diana to death,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我只希望你別把黛安娜講死喇,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我只希望你別把黛安娜說死了,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “But remember this in all your planning, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「但你所有嘅計劃裡都要記住呢啲,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你所有的計劃裡都要記住這一點,安妮。

passages.original: You’re not going to play all the time nor most of it.
passages.vernacular: 你唔係整天玩,都唔係大部分時間玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不是整天玩,也不是大部分時間玩。

passages.original: You’ll have your work to do and it’ll have to be done first.”
passages.vernacular: 你有你嘅活兒要做,必須先做完。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有你的活兒要做,必須先做完。」

passages.original: Anne’s cup of happiness was full, and Matthew caused it to overflow.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅幸福之杯已滿,馬修又讓佢溢咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的幸福之杯已滿,馬修又讓它溢了出來。

passages.original: He had just got home from a trip to the store at Carmody, and he sheepishly produced a small parcel from his pocket and handed it to Anne, with a deprecatory look at Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 佢剛從卡莫迪嘅店裡回嚟,不好意思地從口袋裡掏出一個小包裹,遞畀安妮,同時帶住歉疚嘅神色睇咗睇瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他剛從卡莫迪的店裡回來,不好意思地從口袋裡掏出一個小包裹,遞給安妮,同時帶著歉疚的神色看了看瑪麗拉。

passages.original: “I heard you say you liked chocolate sweeties, so I got you some,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「我聽你講過你鍾意巧克力糖,所以畀你買咗啲,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我聽你說過你喜歡巧克力糖,所以給你買了一些,」他說。

passages.original: “Humph,” sniffed Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「哼,」瑪麗拉嗤之以鼻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,」瑪麗拉嗤之以鼻。

passages.original: “It’ll ruin her teeth and stomach.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰會毀咗佢嘅牙同胃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那會毀了她的牙和胃。

passages.original: There, there, child, don’t look so dismal.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,好喇,細路,別咁憂鬱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,好了,孩子,別那麼憂鬱。

passages.original: You can eat those, since Matthew has gone and got them.
passages.vernacular: 你可以食呢啲,既然馬修已經去買喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以吃這些,既然馬修已經去買了。

passages.original: He’d better have brought you peppermints.
passages.vernacular: 佢最好畀你買薄荷糖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他最好給你買薄荷糖。

passages.original: They’re wholesomer.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋更有益健康。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們更有益健康。

passages.original: Don’t sicken yourself eating all them at once now.”
passages.vernacular: 而家別一下子都食光咗讓自己生病。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在別一下子都吃光了讓自己生病。」

passages.original: “Oh, no, indeed, I won’t,” said Anne eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不,真嘅,我唔會,」安妮急切地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不,真的,我不會,」安妮急切地說。

passages.original: “I’ll just eat one tonight, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我今晚只食一顆,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我今晚只吃一顆,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: And I can give Diana half of them, can’t I?
passages.vernacular: 而且我可以把一半畀黛安娜,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我可以把一半給黛安娜,是不是?

passages.original: The other half will taste twice as sweet to me if I give some to her.
passages.vernacular: 如果我分畀佢啲,另一半嚐起嚟對我會甜一倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我分給她一些,另一半嚐起來對我會甜一倍。

passages.original: It’s delightful to think I have something to give her.”
passages.vernacular: 想到我有嘢可以畀佢,真係太愉快喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到我有東西可以給她,真是太愉快了。」

passages.original: “I will say it for the child,” said Marilla when Anne had gone to her gable, “she isn’t stingy.
passages.vernacular: 「呢啲我得替呢細路講句公道話,」安妮回山牆房間後,瑪麗拉講,「佢不小氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這一點我得替這孩子說句公道話,」安妮回山牆房間後,瑪麗拉說,「她不小氣。

passages.original: I’m glad, for of all faults I detest stinginess in a child.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興,因為喺所有缺點裡,我最討厭細路小氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興,因為在所有缺點裡,我最討厭孩子小氣。

passages.original: Dear me, it’s only three weeks since she came, and it seems as if she’d been here always.
passages.vernacular: 天呀,佢才嚟咗三個星期,好像佢一直就喺呢兒似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,她才來了三個星期,好像她一直就在這兒似的。

passages.original: I can’t imagine the place without her.
passages.vernacular: 我無法想像冇佢嘅呢個地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我無法想像沒有她的這個地方。

passages.original: Now, don’t be looking I told-you-so, Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 而家,別擺出嗰副『我早講過』嘅樣子,馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,別擺出那副『我早說過』的樣子,馬修。

passages.original: That’s bad enough in a woman, but it isn’t to be endured in a man.
passages.vernacular: 呢喺女人身上就夠糟喇,喺男人身上更讓人受不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這在女人身上就夠糟了,在男人身上更讓人受不了。

passages.original: I’m perfectly willing to own up that I’m glad I consented to keep the child and that I’m getting fond of her, but don’t you rub it in, Matthew Cuthbert.”
passages.vernacular: 我完全願意承認我好高興我同意留下呢細路,我都越嚟越鍾意佢,但你別借題發揮,馬修·卡思伯特。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我完全願意承認我很高興我同意留下這孩子,我也越來越喜歡她,但你別借題發揮,馬修·卡思伯特。」

chapters.title: Ch. XIII The Delights of Anticipation 第十三章:期待的樂趣

passages.original: CH IT’S time Anne was in to do her sewing,” said Marilla, glancing at the clock and then out into the yellow August afternoon where everything drowsed in the heat.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮該進嚟做針線活喇,」瑪麗拉講,睇咗一眼時鐘,然後望向悶熱中萬物昏昏欲瞓嘅八月金色午後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮該進來做針線活了,」瑪麗拉說,看了一眼時鐘,然後望向悶熱中萬物昏昏欲睡的八月金色午後。

passages.original: “She stayed playing with Diana more than half an hour more ‘n I gave her leave to; and now she’s perched out there on the woodpile talking to Matthew, nineteen to the dozen, when she knows perfectly well she ought to be at her work.
passages.vernacular: 「佢同黛安娜玩咗比我准許嘅多半個多小時;而家又棲喺外面柴堆上,跟馬修滔滔不絕地講住話,明明知道自己該喺幹活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她和黛安娜玩了比我准許的多半個多小時;現在又棲在外面柴堆上,跟馬修滔滔不絕地說著話,明明知道自己該在幹活。

passages.original: And of course he’s listening to her like a perfect ninny.
