passages.vernacular: 而且佢當然像個十足嘅傻瓜似嘅喺聽佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且他當然像個十足的傻瓜似的在聽她說。

passages.original: I never saw such an infatuated man.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過咁痴迷嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過這麼痴迷的人。

passages.original: The more she talks and the odder the things she says, the more he’s delighted evidently.
passages.vernacular: 佢講得越多、講得越古怪,佢顯然就越高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說得越多、說得越古怪,他顯然就越高興。

passages.original: Anne Shirley, you come right in here this minute, do you hear me!”
passages.vernacular: 安妮·雪莉,即刻畀我進嚟,聽見冇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮·雪莉,立刻給我進來,聽見沒有!」

passages.original: A series of staccato taps on the west window brought Anne flying in from the yard, eyes shining, cheeks faintly flushed with pink, unbraided hair streaming behind her in a torrent of brightness.
passages.vernacular: 西窗上一連串短促嘅敲擊聲,把安妮從院子裡引咗進嚟,佢眼睛閃亮,臉頰泛住淡淡嘅粉紅,冇編辮子嘅頭髮喺佢身後如一股明亮嘅急流飄揚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 西窗上一連串短促的敲擊聲,把安妮從院子裡引了進來,她眼睛閃亮,臉頰泛著淡淡的粉紅,沒編辮子的頭髮在她身後如一股明亮的急流飄揚。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla,” she exclaimed breathlessly, “there’s going to be a Sunday-school picnic next week--in Mr. Harmon Andrews’s field, right near the lake of Shining Waters.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」佢氣喘吁吁地叫道,「下星期有主日學校野餐——喺哈蒙·安德魯斯先生嘅田地裡,離閃亮湖水好近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」她氣喘吁吁地叫道,「下星期有主日學校野餐——在哈蒙·安德魯斯先生的田地裡,離閃亮湖水很近。

passages.original: And Mrs. Superintendent Bell and Mrs. Rachel Lynde are going to make ice cream--think of it, Marilla--ice cream!
passages.vernacular: 仲有主日學校校長貝爾太太同雷切爾·林德太太要做冰淇淋——您想想,瑪麗拉——冰淇淋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有主日學校校長貝爾太太和雷切爾·林德太太要做冰淇淋——您想想,瑪麗拉——冰淇淋!

passages.original: And, oh, Marilla, can I go to it?”
passages.vernacular: 而且,哦,瑪麗拉,我能去嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,哦,瑪麗拉,我能去嗎?」

passages.original: “Just look at the clock, if you please, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「請睇睇時鐘,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請看看時鐘,安妮。

passages.original: What time did I tell you to come in?”
passages.vernacular: 我叫你幾點進嚟?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫你幾點進來?」

passages.original: “Two o’clock--but isn’t it splendid about the picnic, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 「兩點——但係野餐多棒啊,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「兩點——但是野餐多棒啊,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: Please can I go?
passages.vernacular: 求求您讓我去吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求求您讓我去吧?

passages.original: Oh, I’ve never been to a picnic--I’ve dreamed of picnics, but I’ve never--”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我從冇參加過野餐——我夢想過野餐,但從冇——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我從沒參加過野餐——我夢想過野餐,但從沒——」

passages.original: “Yes, I told you to come at two o’clock.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我叫你兩點進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我叫你兩點進來。

passages.original: And it’s a quarter to three.
passages.vernacular: 而家係兩點三刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在是兩點三刻。

passages.original: I’d like to know why you didn’t obey me, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 我倒想知道你點解不服從我,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我倒想知道你為什麼不服從我,安妮。」

passages.original: “Why, I meant to, Marilla, as much as could be.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我本來係要服從嘅,瑪麗拉,盡可能地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我本來是要服從的,瑪麗拉,盡可能地。

passages.original: But you have no idea how fascinating Idlewild is.
passages.vernacular: 但您唔知道閒遊林幾咁迷人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但您不知道閒遊林多麼迷人。

passages.original: And then, of course, I had to tell Matthew about the picnic.
passages.vernacular: 而且,當然,我得把野餐嘅事告訴馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,當然,我得把野餐的事告訴馬修。

passages.original: Matthew is such a sympathetic listener.
passages.vernacular: 馬修係個好富有同情心嘅傾聽者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修是個非常富有同情心的傾聽者。

passages.original: Please can I go?”
passages.vernacular: 求求您讓我去吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求求您讓我去吧?」

passages.original: “You’ll have to learn to resist the fascination of Idle-whatever-you-call-it.
passages.vernacular: 「你得學會抵抗嗰個叫閒遊乜嘢嘅地方嘅魅力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你得學會抵抗那個叫閒遊什麼的地方的魅力。

passages.original: When I tell you to come in at a certain time I mean that time and not half an hour later.
passages.vernacular: 我叫你某個時間進嚟,就係嗰個時間,而唔係晚半個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫你某個時間進來,就是那個時間,而不是晚半個小時。

passages.original: And you needn’t stop to discourse with sympathetic listeners on your way, either.
passages.vernacular: 而且你路上都用不住停下嚟跟富有同情心嘅傾聽者長篇大論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且你路上也用不著停下來跟富有同情心的傾聽者長篇大論。

passages.original: As for the picnic, of course you can go.
passages.vernacular: 至於野餐,當然你可以去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於野餐,當然你可以去。

passages.original: You’re a Sunday-school scholar, and it’s not likely I’d refuse to let you go when all the other little girls are going.”
passages.vernacular: 你係主日學校嘅學生,所有別嘅小女孩都去,我不大可能不讓你去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是主日學校的學生,所有別的小女孩都去,我不大可能不讓你去。」

passages.original: “But--but,” faltered Anne, “Diana says that everybody must take a basket of things to eat.
passages.vernacular: 「不過——不過,」安妮吞吞吐吐地講,「黛安娜講每個人都得帶一籃子食嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是——可是,」安妮吞吞吐吐地說,「黛安娜說每個人都得帶一籃子吃的。

passages.original: I can’t cook, as you know, Marilla, and--and--I don’t mind going to a picnic without puffed sleeves so much, but I’d feel terribly humiliated if I had to go without a basket.
passages.vernacular: 您知道我唔會做飯,瑪麗拉,而且——而且——我不太介意冇泡泡袖去野餐,但如果冇籃子去,我會覺得極其丟臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道我不會做飯,瑪麗拉,而且——而且——我不太介意沒有泡泡袖去野餐,但如果沒有籃子去,我會覺得極其丟臉。

passages.original: It’s been preying on my mind ever since Diana told me.”
passages.vernacular: 自從黛安娜告訴我以後,呢件事一直壓喺我心上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從黛安娜告訴我以後,這件事一直壓在我心上。」

passages.original: “Well, it needn’t prey any longer.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,唔使再壓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,不必再壓著了。

passages.original: I’ll bake you a basket.”
passages.vernacular: 我畀你烤一籃子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給你烤一籃子。」

passages.original: “Oh, you dear good Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,您呢親愛嘅好瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,您這親愛的好瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Oh, you are so kind to me.
passages.vernacular: 哦,您對我真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,您對我真好。

passages.original: Oh, I’m so much obliged to you.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我太感激您喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我太感激您了。」

passages.original: Getting through with her “ohs” Anne cast herself into Marilla’s arms and rapturously kissed her sallow cheek.
passages.vernacular: 講完佢嘅「哦」,安妮撲進瑪麗拉嘅懷裡,狂喜地親吻佢蠟黃嘅臉頰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說完她的「哦」,安妮撲進瑪麗拉的懷裡,狂喜地親吻她蠟黃的臉頰。

passages.original: It was the first time in her whole life that childish lips had voluntarily touched Marilla’s face.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係佢一生中第一次有細路嘅嘴唇主動碰佢嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是她一生中第一次有孩子的嘴唇主動碰她的臉。

passages.original: Again that sudden sensation of startling sweetness thrilled her.
passages.vernacular: 又係嗰種突然襲嚟嘅驚人嘅甜蜜感使佢顫慄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又是那種突然襲來的驚人的甜蜜感使她顫慄。

passages.original: She was secretly vastly pleased at Anne’s impulsive caress, which was probably the reason why she said brusquely:
passages.vernacular: 佢暗地裡對安妮衝動嘅親吻極為高興,呢大概就係佢粗聲講嘅原因:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她暗地裡對安妮衝動的親吻極為高興,這大概就是她粗聲說的原因:

passages.original: “There, there, never mind your kissing nonsense.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,別管你嗰啲親吻嘅胡鬧喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,別管你那些親吻的胡鬧了。

passages.original: I’d sooner see you doing strictly as you’re told.
passages.vernacular: 我寧願睇到你嚴格照吩咐辦事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願看到你嚴格照吩咐辦事。

passages.original: As for cooking, I mean to begin giving you lessons in that some of these days.
passages.vernacular: 至於做飯,我打算呢幾天就開始畀你上課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於做飯,我打算這幾天就開始給你上課。

passages.original: But you’re so featherbrained, Anne, I’ve been waiting to see if you’d sober down a little and learn to be steady before I begin.
passages.vernacular: 但你太輕浮喇,安妮,我一直喺等住睇你係咪會穩重啲,學會沉得住氣,然後再開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你太輕浮了,安妮,我一直在等著看你是否會穩重一些,學會沉得住氣,然後再開始。

passages.original: You’ve got to keep your wits about you in cooking and not stop in the middle of things to let your thoughts rove all over creation.
passages.vernacular: 做飯得保持頭腦清醒,唔能夠做到一半停下嚟讓思緒飛遍天下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 做飯得保持頭腦清醒,不能做到一半停下來讓思緒飛遍天下。

passages.original: Now, get out your patchwork and have your square done before teatime.”
passages.vernacular: 而家,把你嘅拼布攞出嚟,喺飲茶前把你呢一塊做完。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,把你的拼布拿出來,在喝茶前把你這一塊做完。」

passages.original: “I do not like patchwork,” said Anne dolefully, hunting out her workbasket and sitting down before a little heap of red and white diamonds with a sigh.
passages.vernacular: 「我不鍾意拼布,」安妮悲傷地講,翻出針線籃,嘆住氣坐喺一小堆紅白菱形布片前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不喜歡拼布,」安妮悲傷地說,翻出針線籃,嘆著氣坐在一小堆紅白菱形布片前。

passages.original: “I think some kinds of sewing would be nice; but there’s no scope for imagination in patchwork.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得有些針線活挺好嘅;但拼布裡冇想像嘅餘地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得有些針線活挺好的;但拼布裡沒有想像的餘地。

passages.original: It’s just one little seam after another and you never seem to be getting anywhere.
passages.vernacular: 佢只係一道接一道嘅小縫,你好像永遠冇進展。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它只是一道接一道的小縫,你好像永遠沒有進展。

passages.original: But of course I’d rather be Anne of Green Gables sewing patchwork than Anne of any other place with nothing to do but play.
passages.vernacular: 不過當然,我寧願做縫拼布嘅綠色屋頂嘅安妮,都唔願做無所事事、只會玩耍嘅別處嘅安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過當然,我寧願做縫拼布的綠色屋頂的安妮,也不願做無所事事、只會玩耍的別處的安妮。

passages.original: I wish time went as quick sewing patches as it does when I’m playing with Diana, though.
passages.vernacular: 但我希望縫拼布時時間能像我同黛安娜玩耍時過得咁快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我希望縫拼布時時間能像我和黛安娜玩耍時過得那麼快。

passages.original: Oh, we do have such elegant times, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,我哋過得真高雅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,我們過得真高雅。

passages.original: I have to furnish most of the imagination, but I’m well able to do that.
passages.vernacular: 大部分嘅想像得由我嚟提供,但我完全做得嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大部分的想像得由我來提供,但我完全做得來。

passages.original: Diana is simply perfect in every other way.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜喺其他各方面都簡直完美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜在其他各方面都簡直完美。

passages.original: You know that little piece of land across the brook that runs up between our farm and Mr. Barry’s.
passages.vernacular: 您知道溪對面嗰塊小地,伸喺我哋農場同巴里先生嘅農場之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道溪對面那塊小地,伸在我們農場和巴里先生的農場之間。

passages.original: It belongs to Mr. William Bell, and right in the corner there is a little ring of white birch trees--the most romantic spot, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 佢屬於威廉·貝爾先生,喺佢嘅角落裡有一小圈白樺樹——係最浪漫嘅地方,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它屬於威廉·貝爾先生,在它的角落裡有一小圈白樺樹——是最浪漫的地方,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Diana and I have our playhouse there.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜同我嘅遊戲屋就喺嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜和我的遊戲屋就在那兒。

passages.original: We call it Idlewild.
passages.vernacular: 我哋叫佢閒遊林。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們叫它閒遊林。

passages.original: Isn’t that a poetical name?
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係個好富詩意嘅名字嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是個很富詩意的名字嗎?

passages.original: I assure you it took me some time to think it out.
passages.vernacular: 我向您保證,我費咗好一陣工夫才想出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向您保證,我費了好一陣工夫才想出來。

passages.original: I stayed awake nearly a whole night before I invented it.
passages.vernacular: 我差不多整晚冇瞓才發明了佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我差不多整晚沒睡才發明了它。

passages.original: Then, just as I was dropping off to sleep, it came like an inspiration.
passages.vernacular: 然後,就喺我快瞓住嘅時候,佢像靈感一樣嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,就在我快睡著的時候,它像靈感一樣來了。

passages.original: Diana was enraptured when she heard it.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜聽到時欣喜若狂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜聽到時欣喜若狂。

passages.original: We have got our house fixed up elegantly.
passages.vernacular: 我哋把房子佈置得好高雅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們把房子佈置得很高雅。

passages.original: You must come and see it, Marilla--won’t you?
passages.vernacular: 您一定要嚟睇睇,瑪麗拉——您會嚟嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您一定要來看看,瑪麗拉——您會來嗎?

passages.original: We have great big stones, all covered with moss, for seats, and boards from tree to tree for shelves.
passages.vernacular: 我哋有大塊大塊嘅石頭,上面長滿青苔,當座位,樹同樹之間架住木板當架子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們有大塊大塊的石頭,上面長滿青苔,當座位,樹與樹之間架著木板當架子。

passages.original: And we have all our dishes on them.
passages.vernacular: 我哋所有嘅碗碟都放喺上面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們所有的碗碟都放在上面。

passages.original: Of course, they’re all broken but it’s the easiest thing in the world to imagine that they are whole.
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢哋都係破嘅,但想像佢哋係完整嘅,係世上最容易嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,它們都是破的,但想像它們是完整的,是世上最容易的事。

passages.original: There’s a piece of a plate with a spray of red and yellow ivy on it that is especially beautiful.
passages.vernacular: 有一塊盤子嘅碎片,上面有一枝紅黃相間嘅常春藤,特別漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一塊盤子的碎片,上面有一枝紅黃相間的常春藤,特別漂亮。

passages.original: We keep it in the parlor and we have the fairy glass there, too.
passages.vernacular: 我哋把佢放喺客廳裡,嗰兒仲有仙子玻璃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們把它放在客廳裡,那兒還有仙子玻璃。

passages.original: The fairy glass is as lovely as a dream.
passages.vernacular: 仙子玻璃像夢一樣可愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仙子玻璃像夢一樣可愛。

passages.original: Diana found it out in the woods behind their chicken house.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜喺佢哋家雞舍後面嘅樹林裡發現嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜在他們家雞舍後面的樹林裡發現的。

passages.original: It’s all full of rainbows--just little young rainbows that haven’t grown big yet--and Diana’s mother told her it was broken off a hanging lamp they once had.
passages.vernacular: 佢裡面全係彩虹——只係仲冇長大嘅年幼嘅小彩虹——黛安娜嘅母親告訴佢,嗰個係從佢哋家以前嘅一盞吊燈上掉下嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它裡面全是彩虹——只是還沒長大的年幼的小彩虹——黛安娜的母親告訴她,那是從他們家以前的一盞吊燈上掉下來的。

passages.original: But it’s nice to imagine the fairies lost it one night when they had a ball, so we call it the fairy glass.
passages.vernacular: 但係想像仙子哋有天晚上開舞會時把佢弄丟喇,嗰多好啊,所以我哋叫佢仙子玻璃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是想像仙子們有天晚上開舞會時把它弄丟了,那多好啊,所以我們叫它仙子玻璃。

passages.original: Matthew is going to make us a table.
passages.vernacular: 馬修要畀我哋做一張桌子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修要給我們做一張桌子。

passages.original: Oh, we have named that little round pool over in Mr. Barry’s field Willowmere.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我哋還畀巴里先生田裡嗰個小圓池塘起名叫柳塘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我們還給巴里先生田裡那個小圓池塘起名叫柳塘。

passages.original: I got that name out of the book Diana lent me.
passages.vernacular: 我從黛安娜借畀我嘅書裡取嚟嘅呢個名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從黛安娜借給我的書裡取來的這個名字。

passages.original: That was a thrilling book, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係本讓人激動嘅書,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是本讓人激動的書,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: The heroine had five lovers.
passages.vernacular: 女主角有五個情人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女主角有五個情人。

passages.original: I’d be satisfied with one, wouldn’t you?
passages.vernacular: 我有一個就滿足喇,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一個就滿足了,您說呢?

passages.original: She was very handsome and she went through great tribulations.
passages.vernacular: 佢長得好漂亮,經歷咗許多苦難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她長得很漂亮,經歷了許多苦難。

passages.original: She could faint as easy as anything.
passages.vernacular: 佢輕而易舉就能暈倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她輕而易舉就能暈倒。

passages.original: I’d love to be able to faint, wouldn’t you, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 我真想能暈倒,您講呢,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真想能暈倒,您說呢,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: It’s so romantic.
passages.vernacular: 嗰多浪漫啊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那多浪漫啊。

passages.original: But I’m really very healthy for all I’m so thin.
passages.vernacular: 不過儘管我咁瘦,我其實好健康。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過儘管我這麼瘦,我其實很健康。

passages.original: I believe I’m getting fatter, though.
passages.vernacular: 不過我想我喺變胖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我想我在變胖。

passages.original: Don’t you think I am?
passages.vernacular: 您不覺得係咁樣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不覺得是這樣嗎?

passages.original: I look at my elbows every morning when I get up to see if any dimples are coming.
passages.vernacular: 每天早晨起床時,我都睇睇自己嘅胳膊肘,睇有冇酒窩冒出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每天早晨起床時,我都看看自己的胳膊肘,看有沒有酒窩冒出來。

passages.original: Diana is having a new dress made with elbow sleeves.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜喺做一件帶肘袖嘅新裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜在做一件帶肘袖的新裙子。

passages.original: She is going to wear it to the picnic.
passages.vernacular: 佢要穿住去野餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她要穿著去野餐。

passages.original: Oh, I do hope it will be fine next Wednesday.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我真希望下星期三天氣晴朗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我真希望下星期三天氣晴朗。

passages.original: I don’t feel that I could endure the disappointment if anything happened to prevent me from getting to the picnic.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得如果出咗乜嘢事阻止我去野餐,我係無法忍受呢種失望嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得如果出了什麼事阻止我去野餐,我是無法忍受這種失望的。

passages.original: I suppose I’d live through it, but I’m certain it would be a lifelong sorrow.
passages.vernacular: 我想我能活下嚟,但我肯定嗰會成為終生嘅悲哀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我能活下來,但我肯定那會成為終生的悲哀。

passages.original: It wouldn’t matter if I got to a hundred picnics in after years; they wouldn’t make up for missing this one.
passages.vernacular: 即使以後我去一百次野餐,都彌補不咗錯過呢一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使以後我去一百次野餐,也彌補不了錯過這一次。

passages.original: They’re going to have boats on the Lake of Shining Waters--and ice cream, as I told you.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺閃亮湖水上要有船——仲有冰淇淋,就像我告訴您嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在閃亮湖水上要有船——還有冰淇淋,就像我告訴您的。

passages.original: I have never tasted ice cream.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇嘗過冰淇淋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒嘗過冰淇淋。

passages.original: Diana tried to explain what it was like, but I guess ice cream is one of those things that are beyond imagination.”
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜試住解釋佢係乜嘢樣嘅,但我想冰淇淋係嗰種超出想像力嘅嘢之一。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜試著解釋它是什麼樣的,但我想冰淇淋是那種超出想像力的東西之一。」

passages.original: “Anne, you have talked even on for ten minutes by the clock,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,你已經連住講咗好鐘,有鐘為證,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,你已經連著說了十分鐘,有鐘為證,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “Now, just for curiosity’s sake, see if you can hold your tongue for the same length of time.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家,單單為了好奇,睇睇你能唔能夠閉嘴同樣長嘅時間。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,單單為了好奇,看看你能不能閉嘴同樣長的時間。」

passages.original: Anne held her tongue as desired.
passages.vernacular: 安妮按要求閉上咗嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮按要求閉上了嘴。

passages.original: But for the rest of the week she talked picnic and thought picnic and dreamed picnic.
passages.vernacular: 但接下嚟嗰一星期,佢談野餐、想野餐、夢野餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但接下來那一星期,她談野餐、想野餐、夢野餐。

passages.original: On Saturday it rained and she worked herself up into such a frantic state lest it should keep on raining until and over Wednesday that Marilla made her sew an extra patchwork square by way of steadying her nerves.
passages.vernacular: 星期六下雨喇,佢緊張得不行,生怕雨一直下到星期三仲不停,瑪麗拉讓佢多縫一塊拼布,作為穩定佢神經嘅辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期六下雨了,她緊張得不行,生怕雨一直下到星期三還不停,瑪麗拉讓她多縫一塊拼布,作為穩定她神經的辦法。

passages.original: On Sunday Anne confided to Marilla on the way home from church that she grew actually cold all over with excitement when the minister announced the picnic from the pulpit.
passages.vernacular: 星期天從教堂回家嘅路上,安妮向瑪麗拉吐露,牧師喺講壇上宣布野餐嘅時候,佢激動得全身真嘅發涼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期天從教堂回家的路上,安妮向瑪麗拉吐露,牧師在講壇上宣布野餐的時候,她激動得全身真的發涼。

passages.original: “Such a thrill as went up and down my back, Marilla!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰種顫慄喺我背上一上一下,瑪麗拉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那種顫慄在我背上一上一下,瑪麗拉!

passages.original: I don’t think I’d ever really believed until then that there was honestly going to be a picnic.
passages.vernacular: 我想直到嗰時,我才真正相信真嘅會有野餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想直到那時,我才真正相信真的會有野餐。

passages.original: I couldn’t help fearing I’d only imagined it.
passages.vernacular: 我忍不住擔心嗰只係我想像出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忍不住擔心那只是我想像出來的。

passages.original: But when a minister says a thing in the pulpit you just have to believe it.”
passages.vernacular: 不過當牧師喺講壇上講一件事,你就唔得不相信喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是當牧師在講壇上說一件事,你就不得不相信了。」

passages.original: “You set your heart too much on things, Anne,” said Marilla, with a sigh.
passages.vernacular: 「你對事情太用心喇,安妮,」瑪麗拉嘆息住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你對事情太用心了,安妮,」瑪麗拉嘆息著說。

passages.original: “I’m afraid there’ll be a great many disappointments in store for you through life.”
passages.vernacular: 「我怕你呢一生會遇到好多失望。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我怕你這一生會遇到很多失望。」

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, looking forward to things is half the pleasure of them,” exclaimed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,盼望事情本身就係一半嘅樂趣,」安妮叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,盼望事情本身就是一半的樂趣,」安妮叫道。

passages.original: “You mayn’t get the things themselves; but nothing can prevent you from having the fun of looking forward to them.
passages.vernacular: 「你或者得唔到嗰啲事情本身;但冇乜嘢能阻止你享受盼望佢哋嘅樂趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你也許得不到那些事情本身;但沒什麼能阻止你享受盼望它們的樂趣。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says, ‘Blessed are they who expect nothing for they shall not be disappointed.’
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講:『一無所求嘅人有福喇,因為佢哋唔會失望。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說:『一無所求的人有福了,因為他們不會失望。』

passages.original: But I think it would be worse to expect nothing than to be disappointed.”
passages.vernacular: 但我覺得一無所求比失望更糟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我覺得一無所求比失望更糟。」

passages.original: Marilla wore her amethyst brooch to church that day as usual.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天瑪麗拉像往常一樣戴住佢嘅紫水晶胸針去教堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天瑪麗拉像往常一樣戴著她的紫水晶胸針去教堂。

passages.original: Marilla always wore her amethyst brooch to church.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉去教堂總是戴佢嘅紫水晶胸針。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉去教堂總是戴她的紫水晶胸針。

passages.original: She would have thought it rather sacrilegious to leave it off--as bad as forgetting her Bible or her collection dime.
passages.vernacular: 佢會覺得不戴佢相當褻瀆——同忘記帶聖經或捐獻嘅錢一樣糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會覺得不戴它相當褻瀆——和忘記帶聖經或捐獻的錢一樣糟。

passages.original: That amethyst brooch was Marilla’s most treasured possession.
passages.vernacular: 嗰枚紫水晶胸針係瑪麗拉最珍愛嘅財產。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那枚紫水晶胸針是瑪麗拉最珍愛的財產。

passages.original: A seafaring uncle had given it to her mother who in turn had bequeathed it to Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 一位當水手嘅叔叔把佢送畀佢母親,佢母親又留畀咗瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一位當水手的叔叔把它送給她母親,她母親又留給了瑪麗拉。

passages.original: It was an old-fashioned oval, containing a braid of her mother’s hair, surrounded by a border of very fine amethysts.
passages.vernacular: 佢係一枚老式嘅橢圓形,裡面裝住佢母親嘅一縷編起嚟嘅頭髮,周圍鑲住一圈好精緻嘅紫水晶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是一枚老式的橢圓形,裡面裝著她母親的一縷編起來的頭髮,周圍鑲著一圈非常精緻的紫水晶。

passages.original: Marilla knew too little about precious stones to realize how fine the amethysts actually were; but she thought them very beautiful and was always pleasantly conscious of their violet shimmer at her throat, above her good brown satin dress, even although she could not see it.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉對寶石知道得太少,唔知道呢啲紫水晶實際上有多精美;但佢覺得佢哋好漂亮,總是愉快地意識到佢哋喺佢喉嚨處、佢嗰件好嘅棕色緞子衣服上方閃爍嘅紫羅蘭色微光,儘管佢睇唔到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉對寶石知道得太少,不知道這些紫水晶實際上有多精美;但她覺得它們非常漂亮,總是愉快地意識到它們在她喉嚨處、她那件好的棕色緞子衣服上方閃爍的紫羅蘭色微光,儘管她看不到它。

passages.original: Anne had been smitten with delighted admiration when she first saw that brooch.
passages.vernacular: 安妮第一次睇到嗰枚胸針時,就被迷住喇,滿心歡喜地讚嘆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮第一次看到那枚胸針時,就被迷住了,滿心歡喜地讚嘆。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, it’s a perfectly elegant brooch.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,呢個係一枚特別高雅嘅胸針。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,這是一枚特別高雅的胸針。

passages.original: I don’t know how you can pay attention to the sermon or the prayers when you have it on.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道您戴住佢點仲能專心聽講道同禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道您戴著它怎麼還能專心聽講道和禱告。

passages.original: I couldn’t, I know.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我做唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我做不到。

passages.original: I think amethysts are just sweet.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得紫水晶太可愛喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得紫水晶太可愛了。

passages.original: They are what I used to think diamonds were like.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋就係我以前以為嘅鑽石嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們就是我以前以為的鑽石的樣子。

passages.original: Long ago, before I had ever seen a diamond, I read about them and I tried to imagine what they would be like.
passages.vernacular: 好久以前,喺我見過鑽石之前,我讀到過佢哋,我試著想像佢哋會係乜嘢樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很久以前,在我見過鑽石之前,我讀到過它們,我試著想像它們會是什麼樣子。

passages.original: I thought they would be lovely glimmering purple stones.
passages.vernacular: 我以為佢哋係閃爍住微光嘅可愛嘅紫色石頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以為它們是閃爍著微光的可愛的紫色石頭。

passages.original: When I saw a real diamond in a lady’s ring one day I was so disappointed I cried.
passages.vernacular: 有一天我喺一位女士嘅戒指上睇到真正嘅鑽石時,我失望得哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天我在一位女士的戒指上看到真正的鑽石時,我失望得哭了。

passages.original: Of course, it was very lovely but it wasn’t my idea of a diamond.
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢好美,但唔係我心目中鑽石嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,它很美,但不是我心目中鑽石的樣子。

passages.original: Will you let me hold the brooch for one minute, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 您能讓我攞一分鐘呢枚胸針嗎,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您能讓我拿一分鐘這枚胸針嗎,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: Do you think amethysts can be the souls of good violets?”
passages.vernacular: 您覺得紫水晶會係善良紫羅蘭嘅靈魂嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您覺得紫水晶會是善良紫羅蘭的靈魂嗎?」

chapters.title: Ch. XIV Anne's Confession 第十四章:安妮的坦白

passages.original: CH ON the Monday evening before the picnic Marilla came down from her room with a troubled face.
passages.vernacular: 野餐前嘅星期一傍晚,瑪麗拉帶住憂慮嘅神情從佢嘅房間下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 野餐前的星期一傍晚,瑪麗拉帶著憂慮的神情從她的房間下來。

passages.original: “Anne,” she said to that small personage, who was shelling peas by the spotless table and singing, “Nelly of the Hazel Dell” with a vigor and expression that did credit to Diana’s teaching, “did you see anything of my amethyst brooch?
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,」佢對嗰個坐喺一塵不染嘅桌邊剝豌豆、並以不辜負黛安娜教導嘅力度同表情唱住《榛樹谷嘅內莉》嘅小人兒講,「你有冇睇見我嘅紫水晶胸針?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,」她對那個坐在一塵不染的桌邊剝豌豆、並以不辜負黛安娜教導的力度和表情唱著《榛樹谷的內莉》的小人兒說,「你有沒有看見我的紫水晶胸針?

passages.original: I thought I stuck it in my pincushion when I came home from church yesterday evening, but I can’t find it anywhere.”
passages.vernacular: 我以為尋日傍晚從教堂回家時,我把佢別喺針墊上喇,不過我到處都找唔到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以為昨天傍晚從教堂回家時,我把它別在針墊上了,可是我到處都找不到。」

passages.original: “I--I saw it this afternoon when you were away at the Aid Society,” said Anne, a little slowly.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我今日下午您去互助會嘅時候睇見過佢,」安妮講,講得有點慢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我今天下午您去互助會的時候看見過它,」安妮說,說得有點慢。

passages.original: “I was passing your door when I saw it on the cushion, so I went in to look at it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我路過您嘅門口,睇見佢喺墊子上,就進去睇咗睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我路過您的門口,看見它在墊子上,就進去看了看。」

passages.original: “Did you touch it?” said Marilla sternly.
passages.vernacular: 「你碰佢咗嗎?」瑪麗拉嚴厲地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你碰它了嗎?」瑪麗拉嚴厲地問。

passages.original: “Y-e-e-s,” admitted Anne, “I took it up and I pinned it on my breast just to see how it would look.”
passages.vernacular: 「係——係嘅,」安妮承認,「我把佢攞起嚟,別喺胸前,只係想睇睇佢係乜嘢樣子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是——是的,」安妮承認,「我把它拿起來,別在胸前,只是想看看它是什麼樣子。」

passages.original: “You had no business to do anything of the sort.
passages.vernacular: 「你冇任何權利做嗰樣嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你沒有任何權利做那樣的事。

passages.original: It’s very wrong in a little girl to meddle.
passages.vernacular: 一個小女孩亂動嘢係好不對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個小女孩亂動東西是很不對的。

passages.original: You shouldn’t have gone into my room in the first place and you shouldn’t have touched a brooch that didn’t belong to you in the second.
passages.vernacular: 首先你就不該進我嘅房間,其次你更不該碰不屬於你嘅胸針。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先你就不該進我的房間,其次你更不該碰不屬於你的胸針。

passages.original: Where did you put it?”
passages.vernacular: 你把佢放喺邊兒喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把它放在哪兒了?」

passages.original: “Oh, I put it back on the bureau.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我把佢放回咗梳妝臺上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我把它放回了梳妝臺上。

passages.original: I hadn’t it on a minute.
passages.vernacular: 我戴咗仲唔到一分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我戴了還不到一分鐘。

passages.original: Truly, I didn’t mean to meddle, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 真嘅,我唔係故意要亂動嘢嘅,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的,我不是故意要亂動東西的,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I didn’t think about its being wrong to go in and try on the brooch; but I see now that it was and I’ll never do it again.
passages.vernacular: 我冇想到進去試戴胸針係不對嘅;但而家我明白喇,係不對嘅,我再都唔會嗰樣做喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒想到進去試戴胸針是不對的;但現在我明白了,是不對的,我再也不會那樣做了。

passages.original: That’s one good thing about me.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我嘅一個優點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我的一個優點。

passages.original: I never do the same naughty thing twice.”
passages.vernacular: 我從不兩次犯同樣嘅錯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從不兩次犯同樣的錯。」

passages.original: “You didn’t put it back,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「你冇放回去,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你沒放回去,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “That brooch isn’t anywhere on the bureau.
passages.vernacular: 「梳妝臺上邊兒都冇嗰枚胸針。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「梳妝臺上哪兒也沒有那枚胸針。

passages.original: You’ve taken it out or something, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 你把佢攞走咗或者點喇,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把它拿走了或者怎麼了,安妮。」

passages.original: “I did put it back,” said Anne quickly--pertly, Marilla thought.
passages.vernacular: 「我確實放回去喇,」安妮飛快地講——瑪麗拉覺得係無禮地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確實放回去了,」安妮飛快地說——瑪麗拉覺得是無禮地說。

passages.original: “I don’t just remember whether I stuck it on the pincushion or laid it in the china tray.
passages.vernacular: 「我不太記得係別喺針墊上咗定係放喺瓷托盤裡喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不太記得是別在針墊上了還是放在瓷托盤裡了。

passages.original: But I’m perfectly certain I put it back.”
passages.vernacular: 但我完全肯定我放回去喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我完全肯定我放回去了。」

passages.original: “I’ll go and have another look,” said Marilla, determining to be just.
passages.vernacular: 「我再去睇一睇,」瑪麗拉講,決心做到公正。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再去看一看,」瑪麗拉說,決心做到公正。

passages.original: “If you put that brooch back it’s there still.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你把嗰胸針放回去喇,佢仲喺嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你把那胸針放回去了,它還在那兒。

passages.original: If it isn’t I’ll know you didn’t, that’s all!”
passages.vernacular: 如果不喺,我就知道你冇放回去,就咁樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果不在,我就知道你沒有放回去,就這樣!」

passages.original: Marilla went to her room and made a thorough search, not only over the bureau but in every other place she thought the brooch might possibly be.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉去咗佢嘅房間,徹底搜尋咗一遍,不僅係梳妝臺上,仲有佢認為胸針可能喺嘅所有其他地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉去了她的房間,徹底搜尋了一遍,不僅是梳妝臺上,還有她認為胸針可能在的所有其他地方。

passages.original: It was not to be found and she returned to the kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 冇找到,佢回到咗廚房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有找到,她回到了廚房。

passages.original: “Anne, the brooch is gone.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,胸針唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,胸針不見了。

passages.original: By your own admission you were the last person to handle it.
passages.vernacular: 按你自己嘅承認,你係最後一個碰過佢嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 按你自己的承認,你是最後一個碰過它的人。

passages.original: Now, what have you done with it?
passages.vernacular: 而家,你把佢點喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,你把它怎麼了?

passages.original: Tell me the truth at once.
passages.vernacular: 即刻告訴我實話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上告訴我實話。

passages.original: Did you take it out and lose it?”
passages.vernacular: 你係唔係把佢攞出去弄丟喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是不是把它拿出去弄丟了?」

passages.original: “No, I didn’t,” said Anne solemnly, meeting Marilla’s angry gaze squarely.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我冇,」安妮鄭重地講,直直地迎住瑪麗拉憤怒嘅目光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我沒有,」安妮鄭重地說,直直地迎著瑪麗拉憤怒的目光。

passages.original: “I never took the brooch out of your room and that is the truth, if I was to be led to the block for it--although I’m not very certain what a block is.
passages.vernacular: 「我從來冇把胸針攞出過您嘅房間,呢個係真嘅,就係為此被拉去砍頭,雖然我不太確定斷頭臺係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從來沒把胸針拿出過您的房間,這是真的,就是為此被拉去砍頭,雖然我不太確定斷頭臺是什麼。

passages.original: So there, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 就係咁樣,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這樣,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: Anne’s “so there” was only intended to emphasize her assertion, but Marilla took it as a display of defiance.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅「就係咁樣」只係為了強調佢嘅斷言,但瑪麗拉把佢當作挑釁嘅表示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的「就是這樣」只是為了強調她的斷言,但瑪麗拉把它當作挑釁的表示。

passages.original: “I believe you are telling me a falsehood, Anne,” she said sharply.
passages.vernacular: 「我相信你喺對我講謊,安妮,」佢厲聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我相信你在對我說謊,安妮,」她厲聲說。

passages.original: “I know you are.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道你喺講謊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道你在說謊。

passages.original: There now, don’t say anything more unless you are prepared to tell the whole truth.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,除非你準備講出全部實話,否則唔好再講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,除非你準備說出全部實話,否則別再說什麼。

passages.original: Go to your room and stay there until you are ready to confess.”
passages.vernacular: 回你嘅房間去,待喺嗰兒,直到你準備好坦白。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回你的房間去,待在那兒,直到你準備好坦白。」

passages.original: “Will I take the peas with me?” said Anne meekly.
passages.vernacular: 「我把豌豆帶上去嗎?」安妮溫順地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我把豌豆帶上去嗎?」安妮溫順地問。

passages.original: “No, I’ll finish shelling them myself.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我自己剝完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我自己剝完。

passages.original: Do as I bid you.”
passages.vernacular: 照我吩咐嘅做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 照我吩咐的做。」

passages.original: When Anne had gone Marilla went about her evening tasks in a very disturbed state of mind.
passages.vernacular: 安妮走後,瑪麗拉心情好煩亂地做住晚上嘅活兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮走後,瑪麗拉心情十分煩亂地做著晚上的活兒。

passages.original: She was worried about her valuable brooch.
passages.vernacular: 佢為佢貴重嘅胸針擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她為她貴重的胸針擔心。

passages.original: What if Anne had lost it?
passages.vernacular: 萬一安妮把佢弄丟咗呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 萬一安妮把它弄丟了呢?

passages.original: And how wicked of the child to deny having taken it, when anybody could see she must have!
passages.vernacular: 而且呢細路否認攞過佢,幾咁邪惡,明明邊個都睇得出佢一定攞喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且這孩子否認拿過它,多麼邪惡,明明誰都看得出她一定拿了!

passages.original: With such an innocent face, too!
passages.vernacular: 仲帶住咁一張天真嘅臉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還帶著那麼一張天真的臉!

passages.original: “I don’t know what I wouldn’t sooner have had happen,” thought Marilla, as she nervously shelled the peas.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道仲有乜嘢我寧可發生都唔願呢件事發生,」瑪麗拉一邊緊張地剝住豌豆,一邊想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道還有什麼我寧可發生也不願這件事發生,」瑪麗拉一邊緊張地剝著豌豆,一邊想。

passages.original: “Of course, I don’t suppose she meant to steal it or anything like that.
passages.vernacular: 「當然,我想佢唔係有意要偷佢,或者嗰一類。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,我想她不是有意要偷它,或者那一類。

passages.original: She’s just taken it to play with or help along that imagination of hers.
passages.vernacular: 佢只係攞去玩,或者幫助佢嗰想像力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她只是拿去玩,或者幫助她那想像力。

passages.original: She must have taken it, that’s clear, for there hasn’t been a soul in that room since she was in it, by her own story, until I went up tonight.
passages.vernacular: 一定係佢攞嘅,呢個好清楚,因為按佢自己嘅講法,自從佢進去之後,直到今晚我上樓,嗰個房間裡再冇一個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一定是她拿的,這很清楚,因為按她自己的說法,自從她進去之後,直到今晚我上樓,那個房間裡再沒有一個人。

passages.original: And the brooch is gone, there’s nothing surer.
passages.vernacular: 而胸針唔見喇,呢再肯定不過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而胸針不見了,這再肯定不過。

passages.original: I suppose she has lost it and is afraid to own up for fear she’ll be punished.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢把佢弄丟喇,怕受罰唔敢承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想她把它弄丟了,怕受罰不敢承認。

passages.original: It’s a dreadful thing to think she tells falsehoods.
passages.vernacular: 想到佢撒謊,真係可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到她撒謊,真是可怕。

passages.original: It’s a far worse thing than her fit of temper.
passages.vernacular: 呢比佢發脾氣糟糕得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這比她發脾氣糟糕得多。

passages.original: It’s a fearful responsibility to have a child in your house you can’t trust.
passages.vernacular: 家裡有個你唔能夠信任嘅細路,係個可怕嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 家裡有個你不能信任的孩子,是個可怕的責任。

passages.original: Slyness and untruthfulness--that’s what she has displayed.
passages.vernacular: 狡猾同不誠實——呢個就係佢表現出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狡猾和不誠實——這就是她表現出來的。

passages.original: I declare I feel worse about that than about the brooch.
passages.vernacular: 我敢講我為此比為胸針更難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢說我為此比為胸針更難受。

passages.original: If she’d only have told the truth about it I wouldn’t mind so much.”
passages.vernacular: 如果佢只肯講實話,我就唔會咁介意喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她只肯說實話,我就不會這麼介意了。」

passages.original: Marilla went to her room at intervals all through the evening and searched for the brooch, without finding it.
passages.vernacular: 整個晚上,瑪麗拉不時到佢嘅房間去找胸針,一無所獲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個晚上,瑪麗拉不時到她的房間去找胸針,一無所獲。

passages.original: A bedtime visit to the east gable produced no result.
passages.vernacular: 瞓前到東山牆房間去睇咗一趟,都冇結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 睡前到東山牆房間去看了一趟,也沒有結果。

passages.original: Anne persisted in denying that she knew anything about the brooch but Marilla was only the more firmly convinced that she did.
passages.vernacular: 安妮堅持否認知道胸針嘅任何事,但瑪麗拉卻愈發堅信佢知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮堅持否認知道胸針的任何事,但瑪麗拉卻愈發堅信她知道。

passages.original: She told Matthew the story the next morning.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨佢把呢件事告訴咗馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨她把這件事告訴了馬修。

passages.original: Matthew was confounded and puzzled; he could not so quickly lose faith in Anne but he had to admit that circumstances were against her.
passages.vernacular: 馬修又驚又迷惑;佢唔能夠咁快就對安妮失去信心,但佢唔得不承認情況對佢不利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修又驚又迷惑;他不能這麼快就對安妮失去信心,但他不得不承認情況對她不利。

passages.original: “You’re sure it hasn’t fell down behind the bureau?” was the only suggestion he could offer.
passages.vernacular: 「你肯定佢冇掉到梳妝臺後面去嗎?」係佢唯一能提出嘅建議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你肯定它沒有掉到梳妝臺後面去嗎?」是他唯一能提出的建議。

passages.original: “I’ve moved the bureau and I’ve taken out the drawers and I’ve looked in every crack and cranny” was Marilla’s positive answer.
passages.vernacular: 「我把梳妝臺挪開喇,把抽屜都攞咗出嚟,每條縫隙每個角落都睇過喇,」呢個係瑪麗拉肯定嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我把梳妝臺挪開了,把抽屜都拿了出來,每條縫隙每個角落都看過了,」這是瑪麗拉肯定的回答。

passages.original: “The brooch is gone and that child has taken it and lied about it.
passages.vernacular: 「胸針唔見喇,係嗰細路攞嘅,而且仲撒咗謊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胸針不見了,是那孩子拿的,而且還撒了謊。

passages.original: That’s the plain, ugly truth, Matthew Cuthbert, and we might as well look it in the face.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係赤裸裸、難睇嘅事實,馬修·卡思伯特,我哋不如直面佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是赤裸裸、難看的事實,馬修·卡思伯特,我們不如直面它。」

passages.original: “Well now, what are you going to do about it?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰你打算點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那你打算怎麼辦?」

passages.original: Matthew asked forlornly, feeling secretly thankful that Marilla and not he had to deal with the situation.
passages.vernacular: 馬修無助地問,暗自慶幸應付呢種局面嘅係瑪麗拉而唔係佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修無助地問,暗自慶幸應付這種局面的是瑪麗拉而不是他。

passages.original: He felt no desire to put his oar in this time.
passages.vernacular: 呢一次佢唔想插手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一次他不想插手。

passages.original: “She’ll stay in her room until she confesses,” said Marilla grimly, remembering the success of this method in the former case.
passages.vernacular: 「佢得待喺房間裡,直到佢坦白,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地講,記起咗呢個方法喺上一次嘅成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她得待在房間裡,直到她坦白,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地說,記起了這個方法在上一次的成功。

passages.original: “Then we’ll see.
passages.vernacular: 「然後再睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後再看。

passages.original: Perhaps we’ll be able to find the brooch if she’ll only tell where she took it; but in any case she’ll have to be severely punished, Matthew.”
passages.vernacular: 只要佢肯講喺邊兒攞嘅,或者我哋能找到胸針;但無論如何佢都要受到嚴厲嘅懲罰,馬修。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要她肯說在哪兒拿的,也許我們能找到胸針;但無論如何她都要受到嚴厲的懲罰,馬修。」

passages.original: “Well now, you’ll have to punish her,” said Matthew, reaching for his hat.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你得懲罰佢,」馬修伸手去攞帽子,講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你得懲罰她,」馬修伸手去拿帽子,說。

passages.original: “I’ve nothing to do with it, remember.
passages.vernacular: 「我可不參與,記住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可不參與,記住。

passages.original: You warned me off yourself.”
passages.vernacular: 係你自己警告過我別插手嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是你自己警告過我別插手的。」

passages.original: Marilla felt deserted by everyone.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉覺得被所有人拋棄喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉覺得被所有人拋棄了。

passages.original: She could not even go to Mrs. Lynde for advice.
passages.vernacular: 佢甚至唔能夠去找林德太太商量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她甚至不能去找林德太太商量。

passages.original: She went up to the east gable with a very serious face and left it with a face more serious still.
passages.vernacular: 佢帶住一張好嚴肅嘅臉走上東山牆房間,離開時臉更嚴肅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她帶著一張非常嚴肅的臉走上東山牆房間,離開時臉更嚴肅了。

passages.original: Anne steadfastly refused to confess.
passages.vernacular: 安妮堅決拒絕坦白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮堅決拒絕坦白。

passages.original: She persisted in asserting that she had not taken the brooch.
passages.vernacular: 佢堅持講佢冇攞過胸針。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她堅持說她沒拿過胸針。

passages.original: The child had evidently been crying and Marilla felt a pang of pity which she sternly repressed.
passages.vernacular: 細路顯然哭過,瑪麗拉感到一陣憐憫嘅刺痛,但佢嚴厲地壓制咗下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子顯然哭過,瑪麗拉感到一陣憐憫的刺痛,但她嚴厲地壓制了下去。

passages.original: By night she was, as she expressed it, “beat out.”
passages.vernacular: 到咗晚上,佢,用佢自己嘅話來講,「筋疲力盡」喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到了晚上,她,用她自己的話來說,「筋疲力盡」了。

passages.original: “You’ll stay in this room until you confess, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「你要待喺呢個房間裡,直到你坦白,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要待在這個房間裡,直到你坦白,安妮。

passages.original: You can make up your mind to that,” she said firmly.
passages.vernacular: 你可以打定呢個主意,」佢堅定地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以打定這個主意,」她堅定地說。

passages.original: “But the picnic is tomorrow, Marilla,” cried Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「不過野餐就喺聽日,瑪麗拉,」安妮叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是野餐就在明天,瑪麗拉,」安妮叫道。

passages.original: “You won’t keep me from going to that, will you?
passages.vernacular: 「您唔會不讓我去吧,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您不會不讓我去吧,是不是?

passages.original: You’ll just let me out for the afternoon, won’t you?
passages.vernacular: 您只讓我出去一個下午,好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您只讓我出去一個下午,好嗎?

passages.original: Then I’ll stay here as long as you like afterwards cheerfully.
passages.vernacular: 之後您想讓我待多久,我都高高興興地待喺呢兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後您想讓我待多久,我都高高興興地待在這兒。

passages.original: But I must go to the picnic.”
passages.vernacular: 但我必須去野餐。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我必須去野餐。」

passages.original: “You’ll not go to picnics nor anywhere else until you’ve confessed, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 「你坦白之前,唔能夠去野餐,都唔能夠去任何地方,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你坦白之前,不能去野餐,也不能去任何地方,安妮。」

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla,” gasped Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」安妮喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」安妮喘著氣說。

passages.original: But Marilla had gone out and shut the door.
passages.vernacular: 但瑪麗拉已經出去,關上咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但瑪麗拉已經出去,關上了門。

passages.original: Wednesday morning dawned as bright and fair as if expressly made to order for the picnic.
passages.vernacular: 星期三早晨,天色破曉,晴朗美好,好像專門為野餐訂做嘅一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期三早晨,天色破曉,晴朗美好,好像專門為野餐訂做的一樣。

passages.original: Birds sang around Green Gables; the Madonna lilies in the garden sent out whiffs of perfume that entered in on viewless winds at every door and window, and wandered through halls and rooms like spirits of benediction.
passages.vernacular: 綠色屋頂周圍鳥兒歌唱;花園裡嘅聖母百合散發出陣陣香氣,隨住睇唔見嘅風從每一道門窗飄進嚟,像祝福嘅精靈一樣喺廊廳同房間裡遊蕩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 綠色屋頂周圍鳥兒歌唱;花園裡的聖母百合散發出陣陣香氣,隨著看不見的風從每一道門窗飄進來,像祝福的精靈一樣在廊廳和房間裡遊蕩。

passages.original: The birches in the hollow waved joyful hands as if watching for Anne’s usual morning greeting from the east gable.
passages.vernacular: 窪地裡嘅白樺揮動住歡樂嘅手,好像喺等待安妮平日從東山牆房間發出嘅早晨問候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窪地裡的白樺揮動著歡樂的手,好像在等待安妮平日從東山牆房間發出的早晨問候。

passages.original: But Anne was not at her window.
passages.vernacular: 但安妮不喺佢嘅窗前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安妮不在她的窗前。

passages.original: When Marilla took her breakfast up to her she found the child sitting primly on her bed, pale and resolute, with tight-shut lips and gleaming eyes.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉把早飯端上去時,發現細路端端正正地坐喺床上,臉色蒼白而堅決,嘴唇緊閉,眼睛閃亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉把早飯端上去時,發現孩子端端正正地坐在床上,臉色蒼白而堅決,嘴唇緊閉,眼睛閃亮。

passages.original: “Marilla, I’m ready to confess.”
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉,我準備好坦白喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉,我準備好坦白了。」

passages.original: “Ah!”
Marilla laid down her tray.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉把托盤放下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉把托盤放下。

passages.original: Once again her method had succeeded; but her success was very bitter to her.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅方法又一次成功喇;但呢成功對佢來講好苦澀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的方法又一次成功了;但這成功對她來說非常苦澀。

passages.original: “Let me hear what you have to say then, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁讓我聽聽你有乜嘢要講嘅,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼讓我聽聽你有什麼要說的,安妮。」

passages.original: “I took the amethyst brooch,” said Anne, as if repeating a lesson she had learned.
passages.vernacular: 「我攞咗紫水晶胸針,」安妮講,像背誦學過嘅功課一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我拿了紫水晶胸針,」安妮說,像背誦學過的功課一樣。

passages.original: “I took it just as you said.
passages.vernacular: 「我攞喇,正像您講嘅嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我拿了,正像您說的那樣。

passages.original: I didn’t mean to take it when I went in.
passages.vernacular: 我進去時並不打算攞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我進去時並不打算拿。

passages.original: But it did look so beautiful, Marilla, when I pinned it on my breast that I was overcome by an irresistible temptation.
passages.vernacular: 但係當我把佢別喺胸前時,佢真嘅好漂亮,瑪麗拉,我被一種無法抗拒嘅誘惑壓倒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是當我把它別在胸前時,它真的非常漂亮,瑪麗拉,我被一種無法抗拒的誘惑壓倒了。

passages.original: I imagined how perfectly thrilling it would be to take it to Idlewild and play I was the Lady Cordelia Fitzgerald.
passages.vernacular: 我想像如果把佢帶到閒遊林,扮成科黛莉亞·菲茨傑拉德夫人,嗰會幾咁刺激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想像如果把它帶到閒遊林,扮成科黛莉亞·菲茨傑拉德夫人,那會多麼刺激。

passages.original: It would be so much easier to imagine I was the Lady Cordelia if I had a real amethyst brooch on.
passages.vernacular: 如果戴住一枚真正嘅紫水晶胸針,想像自己係科黛莉亞夫人就容易多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果戴著一枚真正的紫水晶胸針,想像自己是科黛莉亞夫人就容易多了。

passages.original: Diana and I make necklaces of roseberries but what are roseberries compared to amethysts?
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜同我用玫瑰果串項鍊,但玫瑰果點能跟紫水晶相比呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜和我用玫瑰果串項鍊,但玫瑰果怎麼能跟紫水晶相比呢?

passages.original: So I took the brooch.
passages.vernacular: 所以我就攞咗胸針。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我就拿了胸針。

passages.original: I thought I could put it back before you came home.
passages.vernacular: 我以為我能喺您回家前放回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以為我能在您回家前放回去。

passages.original: I went all the way around by the road to lengthen out the time.
passages.vernacular: 我走路繞咗一大圈,為了拖長時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我走路繞了一大圈,為了拖長時間。

passages.original: When I was going over the bridge across the Lake of Shining Waters I took the brooch off to have another look at it.
passages.vernacular: 我走過閃亮湖水上嘅橋時,把胸針取下嚟再睇一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我走過閃亮湖水上的橋時,把胸針取下來再看一眼。

passages.original: Oh, how it did shine in the sunlight!
passages.vernacular: 哦,佢喺陽光下幾咁閃亮啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,它在陽光下多麼閃亮啊!

passages.original: And then, when I was leaning over the bridge, it just slipped through my fingers--so--and went down--down--down, all purply-sparkling, and sank forevermore beneath the Lake of Shining Waters.
passages.vernacular: 然後,我正趴喺橋欄杆上,佢就從我嘅手指間滑咗出去——就咁樣——掉咗下去——下去——下去,全係紫色嘅閃光,永遠沉入咗閃亮湖水之下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,我正趴在橋欄杆上,它就從我的手指間滑了出去——就這樣——掉了下去——下去——下去,全是紫色的閃光,永遠沉入了閃亮湖水之下。

passages.original: And that’s the best I can do at confessing, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係我能做到嘅最好嘅坦白喇,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是我能做到的最好的坦白了,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: Marilla felt hot anger surge up into her heart again.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉感到一股熾熱嘅憤怒又湧上心頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉感到一股熾熱的憤怒又湧上心頭。

passages.original: This child had taken and lost her treasured amethyst brooch and now sat there calmly reciting the details thereof without the least apparent compunction or repentance.
passages.vernacular: 呢細路攞咗佢珍愛嘅紫水晶胸針,仲弄丟喇,而家卻平靜地坐喺嗰兒敘述佢嘅細節,絲毫冇悔恨或悔改嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這孩子拿了她珍愛的紫水晶胸針,還弄丟了,現在卻平靜地坐在那兒敘述它的細節,絲毫沒有悔恨或悔改的樣子。

passages.original: “Anne, this is terrible,” she said, trying to speak calmly.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,呢太可怕喇,」佢講,盡力平靜地講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,這太可怕了,」她說,盡力平靜地說話。

passages.original: “You are the very wickedest girl I ever heard of.”
passages.vernacular: 「你係我聽講過嘅最邪惡嘅女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是我聽說過的最邪惡的女孩。」

passages.original: “Yes, I suppose I am,” agreed Anne tranquilly.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我想我係,」安妮平靜地同意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我想我是,」安妮平靜地同意。

passages.original: “And I know I’ll have to be punished.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道我必須受罰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道我必須受罰。

passages.original: It’ll be your duty to punish me, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 懲罰我係您嘅責任,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懲罰我是您的責任,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Won’t you please get it over right off because I’d like to go to the picnic with nothing on my mind.”
passages.vernacular: 您能唔能夠請而家就把呢事了結,因為我想心裡冇任何負擔地去野餐。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您能不能請現在就把這事了結,因為我想心裡沒有任何負擔地去野餐。」

passages.original: “Picnic, indeed!
passages.vernacular: 「仲想住野餐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還想著野餐!

passages.original: You’ll go to no picnic today, Anne Shirley.
passages.vernacular: 你今日邊個野餐都不許去,安妮·雪莉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你今天哪個野餐也不許去,安妮·雪莉。

passages.original: That shall be your punishment.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係你嘅懲罰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是你的懲罰。

passages.original: And it isn’t half severe enough either for what you’ve done!”
passages.vernacular: 而且就你做嘅事來講,連一半嚴厲都唔到!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且就你做的事來說,連一半嚴厲都不到!」

passages.original: “Not go to the picnic!”
passages.vernacular: 「不去野餐!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不去野餐!」

passages.original: Anne sprang to her feet and clutched Marilla’s hand.
passages.vernacular: 安妮跳起嚟,抓住瑪麗拉嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮跳起來,抓住瑪麗拉的手。

passages.original: “But you promised me I might!
passages.vernacular: 「不過您答應過我可以去嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是您答應過我可以去的!

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, I must go to the picnic.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,我必須去野餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,我必須去野餐。

passages.original: That was why I confessed.
passages.vernacular: 我就係為了呢個才坦白嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是為了這個才坦白的。

passages.original: Punish me any way you like but that.
passages.vernacular: 除咗呢個,您想點罰我都行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了這個,您想怎麼罰我都行。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, please, please, let me go to the picnic.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,求求您,求求您讓我去野餐吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,求求您,求求您讓我去野餐吧。

passages.original: Think of the ice cream!
passages.vernacular: 想想冰淇淋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想想冰淇淋!

passages.original: For anything you know I may never have a chance to taste ice cream again.”
passages.vernacular: 就您所知,我或者再都冇機會嘗冰淇淋喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就您所知,我也許再也沒有機會嘗冰淇淋了。」

passages.original: Marilla disengaged Anne’s clinging hands stonily.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉冷酷地掰開安妮緊抓嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉冷酷地掰開安妮緊抓的手。

passages.original: “You needn’t plead, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「你唔使求,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不用求,安妮。

passages.original: You are not going to the picnic and that’s final.
passages.vernacular: 你不去野餐,呢個係定咗嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不去野餐,這是定了的。

passages.original: No, not a word.”
passages.vernacular: 不,一個字都唔好講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,一個字也別說。」

passages.original: Anne realized that Marilla was not to be moved.
passages.vernacular: 安妮明白咗瑪麗拉係唔會動搖嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮明白了瑪麗拉是不會動搖的。

passages.original: She clasped her hands together, gave a piercing shriek, and then flung herself face downward on the bed, crying and writhing in an utter abandonment of disappointment and despair.
passages.vernacular: 佢雙手緊握,發出一聲刺耳嘅尖叫,然後一頭撲倒喺床上,臉朝下哭泣、扭動,完全沉浸喺失望同絕望之中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她雙手緊握,發出一聲刺耳的尖叫,然後一頭撲倒在床上,臉朝下哭泣、扭動,完全沉浸在失望與絕望之中。

passages.original: “For the land’s sake!” gasped Marilla, hastening from the room.
passages.vernacular: 「老天爺!」瑪麗拉喘息住講,匆匆走出房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「老天爺!」瑪麗拉喘息著說,匆匆走出房間。

passages.original: “I believe the child is crazy.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇呢細路瘋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看這孩子瘋了。

passages.original: No child in her senses would behave as she does.
passages.vernacular: 冇一個頭腦正常嘅細路會像佢咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有一個頭腦正常的孩子會像她這樣做。

passages.original: If she isn’t she’s utterly bad.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢冇瘋,嗰個就係壞透喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她沒瘋,那就是壞透了。

passages.original: Oh dear, I’m afraid Rachel was right from the first.
passages.vernacular: 哦天呀,我怕雷切爾從一開始就係對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦天哪,我怕雷切爾從一開始就是對的。

passages.original: But I’ve put my hand to the plow and I won’t look back.”
passages.vernacular: 但我既然已經扶上咗犁,就唔會回頭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我既然已經扶上了犁,就不會回頭。」

passages.original: That was a dismal morning.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個悶悶不樂嘅上午。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個悶悶不樂的上午。

passages.original: Marilla worked fiercely and scrubbed the porch floor and the dairy shelves when she could find nothing else to do.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉兇猛地幹活,找唔到別嘅事做時就擦洗門廊地板同奶房嘅架子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉兇猛地幹活,找不到別的事做時就擦洗門廊地板和奶房的架子。

passages.original: Neither the shelves nor the porch needed it--but Marilla did.
passages.vernacular: 架子同門廊都不需要擦——但瑪麗拉需要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 架子和門廊都不需要擦——但瑪麗拉需要。

passages.original: Then she went out and raked the yard.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢出去耙院子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她出去耙院子。

passages.original: When dinner was ready she went to the stairs and called Anne.
passages.vernacular: 午飯準備好喇,佢走到樓梯口叫安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 午飯準備好了,她走到樓梯口叫安妮。

passages.original: A tear-stained face appeared, looking tragically over the banisters.
passages.vernacular: 一張淚痕斑斑嘅臉出現喇,悲慘地隔住欄杆往下睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一張淚痕斑斑的臉出現了,悲慘地隔著欄杆往下看。

passages.original: “Come down to your dinner, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 「下嚟食午飯,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「下來吃午飯,安妮。」

passages.original: “I don’t want any dinner, Marilla,” said Anne, sobbingly.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔想食午飯,瑪麗拉,」安妮抽泣住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不想吃午飯,瑪麗拉,」安妮抽泣著說。

passages.original: “I couldn’t eat anything.
passages.vernacular: 「我乜嘢都食不下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我什麼也吃不下。

passages.original: My heart is broken.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅心碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的心碎了。

passages.original: You’ll feel remorse of conscience someday, I expect, for breaking it, Marilla, but I forgive you.
passages.vernacular: 您總有一天會因為弄碎佢而良心不安嘅,我想,瑪麗拉,但我原諒您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您總有一天會因為弄碎它而良心不安的,我想,瑪麗拉,但我原諒您。

passages.original: Remember when the time comes that I forgive you.
passages.vernacular: 請記住,到嗰時候我原諒您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請記住,到那時候我原諒您。

passages.original: But please don’t ask me to eat anything, especially boiled pork and greens.
passages.vernacular: 但請別叫我食任何嘢,特別係煮豬肉同青菜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但請別叫我吃任何東西,特別是煮豬肉和青菜。

passages.original: Boiled pork and greens are so unromantic when one is in affliction.”
passages.vernacular: 當一個人喺痛苦中,煮豬肉同青菜係咁冇浪漫情調。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當一個人在痛苦中,煮豬肉和青菜是那麼沒有浪漫情調。」

passages.original: Exasperated, Marilla returned to the kitchen and poured out her tale of woe to Matthew, who, between his sense of justice and his unlawful sympathy with Anne, was a miserable man.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉惱怒地回到廚房,向馬修傾訴佢嘅苦惱,馬修喺正義感同對安妮不該有嘅同情之間,成咗個可憐嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉惱怒地回到廚房,向馬修傾訴她的苦惱,馬修在正義感與對安妮不該有的同情之間,成了個可憐的人。

passages.original: “Well now, she shouldn’t have taken the brooch, Marilla, or told stories about it,” he admitted, mournfully surveying his plateful of unromantic pork and greens as if he, like Anne, thought it a food unsuited to crises of feeling, “but she’s such a little thing--such an interesting little thing.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢不該攞嗰枚胸針,瑪麗拉,都不該就此撒謊,」佢承認,憂傷地打量住盤子裡冇浪漫情調嘅豬肉同青菜,好像佢同安妮一樣,認為呢個係一種不適合情感危機嘅食物,「但佢係咁小嘅一個小嘢——咁有趣嘅一個小嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,她不該拿那枚胸針,瑪麗拉,也不該就此撒謊,」他承認,憂傷地打量著盤子裡沒有浪漫情調的豬肉和青菜,好像他和安妮一樣,認為這是一種不適合情感危機的食物,「但她是那麼小的一個小東西——那麼有趣的一個小東西。

passages.original: Don’t you think it’s pretty rough not to let her go to the picnic when she’s so set on it?”
passages.vernacular: 佢咁一心想去,你不覺得不讓佢去野餐太狠咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她那麼一心想去,你不覺得不讓她去野餐太狠了嗎?」

passages.original: “Matthew Cuthbert, I’m amazed at you.
passages.vernacular: 「馬修·卡思伯特,我真食驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修·卡思伯特,我真吃驚。

passages.original: I think I’ve let her off entirely too easy.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我已經對佢太輕饒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我已經對她太輕饒了。

passages.original: And she doesn’t appear to realize how wicked she’s been at all--that’s what worries me most.
passages.vernacular: 而且佢似乎啲都冇意識到自己有多邪惡——呢個係最讓我擔心嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且她似乎一點也沒意識到自己有多邪惡——這是最讓我擔心的。

passages.original: If she’d really felt sorry it wouldn’t be so bad.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢真嘅感到抱歉,事情就不咁糟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她真的感到抱歉,事情就不那麼糟了。

passages.original: And you don’t seem to realize it, neither; you’re making excuses for her all the time to yourself--I can see that.”
passages.vernacular: 而你似乎都冇意識到,你一直喺心裡為佢找藉口——我睇得出嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而你似乎也沒意識到,你一直在心裡為她找藉口——我看得出來。」

passages.original: “Well now, she’s such a little thing,” feebly reiterated Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢係咁小嘅一個小嘢,」馬修無力地重複道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,她是那麼小的一個小東西,」馬修無力地重複道。

passages.original: “And there should be allowances made, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「應該畀佢留些餘地,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「應該給她留些餘地,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: You know she’s never had any bringing up.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道佢從冇受過管教。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道她從沒受過管教。」

passages.original: “Well, she’s having it now” retorted Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢而家正在受管教,」瑪麗拉反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,她現在正在受管教,」瑪麗拉反駁。

passages.original: The retort silenced Matthew if it did not convince him.
passages.vernacular: 呢一反駁即使冇講服馬修,都讓佢閉咗嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一反駁即使沒有說服馬修,也讓他閉了嘴。

passages.original: That dinner was a very dismal meal.
passages.vernacular: 嗰頓午飯好沉悶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那頓午飯非常沉悶。

passages.original: The only cheerful thing about it was Jerry Buote, the hired boy, and Marilla resented his cheerfulness as a personal insult.
passages.vernacular: 唯一令人高興嘅係雇工小伙子傑里·布特,而瑪麗拉把佢嘅高興當作對自己嘅人身侮辱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唯一令人高興的是雇工小伙子傑里·布特,而瑪麗拉把他的高興當作對自己的人身侮辱。

passages.original: When her dishes were washed and her bread sponge set and her hens fed Marilla remembered that she had noticed a small rent in her best black lace shawl when she had taken it off on Monday afternoon on returning from the Ladies’ Aid.
passages.vernacular: 等佢把碗碟洗完、麵團發好、母雞餵過,瑪麗拉想起星期一下午從互助會回嚟脫下佢最好嘅黑蕾絲披肩時,曾注意到上面有一個小小嘅破洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等她把碗碟洗完、麵團發好、母雞餵過,瑪麗拉想起星期一下午從互助會回來脫下她最好的黑蕾絲披肩時,曾注意到上面有一個小小的破洞。

passages.original: She would go and mend it.
passages.vernacular: 佢要去補一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她要去補一下。

passages.original: The shawl was in a box in her trunk.
passages.vernacular: 披肩放喺佢箱子嘅一個盒子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 披肩放在她箱子的一個盒子裡。

passages.original: As Marilla lifted it out, the sunlight, falling through the vines that clustered thickly about the window, struck upon something caught in the shawl--something that glittered and sparkled in facets of violet light.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉把佢提起嚟時,透過窗邊濃密嘅藤蔓灑下嚟嘅陽光,照喺披肩上卡住嘅乜嘢嘢上——嗰嘢閃閃發亮,折射出紫羅蘭色嘅光芒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉把它提起來時,透過窗邊濃密的藤蔓灑下來的陽光,照在披肩上卡著的什麼東西上——那東西閃閃發亮,折射出紫羅蘭色的光芒。

passages.original: Marilla snatched at it with a gasp.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉喘住氣一把抓住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉喘著氣一把抓住它。

passages.original: It was the amethyst brooch, hanging to a thread of the lace by its catch!
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係紫水晶胸針,佢嘅搭扣掛喺蕾絲嘅一根線上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是紫水晶胸針,它的搭扣掛在蕾絲的一根線上!

passages.original: “Dear life and heart,” said Marilla blankly, “what does this mean?
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,我嘅老天,」瑪麗拉茫然地講,「呢個係點回事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,我的老天,」瑪麗拉茫然地說,「這是怎麼回事?

passages.original: Here’s my brooch safe and sound that I thought was at the bottom of Barry’s pond.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅胸針好好地喺呢兒,我仲以為佢喺巴里池塘嘅底部呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的胸針好好地在這兒,我還以為它在巴里池塘的底部呢。

passages.original: Whatever did that girl mean by saying she took it and lost it?
passages.vernacular: 嗰個女孩講佢攞咗佢仲弄丟喇,究竟係乜嘢意思?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個女孩說她拿了它還弄丟了,究竟是什麼意思?

passages.original: I declare I believe Green Gables is bewitched.
passages.vernacular: 我敢講,我相信綠色屋頂被施咗魔法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢說,我相信綠色屋頂被施了魔法。

passages.original: I remember now that when I took off my shawl Monday afternoon I laid it on the bureau for a minute.
passages.vernacular: 我而家想起嚟喇,星期一下午我脫下披肩時,喺梳妝臺上放咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在想起來了,星期一下午我脫下披肩時,在梳妝臺上放了一會兒。

passages.original: I suppose the brooch got caught in it somehow.
passages.vernacular: 我想胸針係唔知點勾喺咗上面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想胸針是不知怎麼勾在了上面。

passages.original: Well!”
Marilla betook herself to the east gable, brooch in hand.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉手裡攞住胸針,走向東山牆房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉手裡拿著胸針,走向東山牆房間。

passages.original: Anne had cried herself out and was sitting dejectedly by the window.
passages.vernacular: 安妮已經哭夠喇,沮喪地坐喺窗邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮已經哭夠了,沮喪地坐在窗邊。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley,” said Marilla solemnly, “I’ve just found my brooch hanging to my black lace shawl.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,」瑪麗拉鄭重地講,「我啱啱喺我嘅黑蕾絲披肩上找到咗我嘅胸針,佢掛喺上面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,」瑪麗拉鄭重地說,「我剛剛在我的黑蕾絲披肩上找到了我的胸針,它掛在上面。

passages.original: Now I want to know what that rigmarole you told me this morning meant.”
passages.vernacular: 而家我想知道你今日朝早對我講嘅嗰一大套廢話係乜嘢意思。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我想知道你今天早上對我說的那一大套廢話是什麼意思。」

passages.original: “Why, you said you’d keep me here until I confessed,” returned Anne wearily, “and so I decided to confess because I was bound to get to the picnic.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,您講您要把我關喺呢兒,直到我坦白,」安妮無精打采地回答,「所以我決定坦白,因為我一定要去野餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,您說您要把我關在這兒,直到我坦白,」安妮無精打采地回答,「所以我決定坦白,因為我一定要去野餐。

passages.original: I thought out a confession last night after I went to bed and made it as interesting as I could.
passages.vernacular: 琴晚上床後,我想出咗一個坦白,並儘量把佢編得有趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨晚上床後,我想出了一個坦白,並儘量把它編得有趣。

passages.original: And I said it over and over so that I wouldn’t forget it.
passages.vernacular: 我一遍又一遍地念,怕忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一遍又一遍地念,怕忘了。

passages.original: But you wouldn’t let me go to the picnic after all, so all my trouble was wasted.”
passages.vernacular: 不過您終究定係不讓我去野餐,所以我所有嘅苦心都白費喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是您終究還是不讓我去野餐,所以我所有的苦心都白費了。」

passages.original: Marilla had to laugh in spite of herself.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉不由自主地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉不由自主地笑了。

passages.original: But her conscience pricked her.
passages.vernacular: 但佢嘅良心刺痛咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她的良心刺痛了她。

passages.original: “Anne, you do beat all!
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,你真係無人能及!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,你真是無人能及!

passages.original: But I was wrong--I see that now.
passages.vernacular: 但係我錯喇——我而家明白喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是我錯了——我現在明白了。

passages.original: I shouldn’t have doubted your word when I’d never known you to tell a story.
passages.vernacular: 我不該懷疑你嘅話,我從冇見你講過謊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不該懷疑你的話,我從沒見你說過謊。

passages.original: Of course, it wasn’t right for you to confess to a thing you hadn’t done--it was very wrong to do so.
passages.vernacular: 當然,你坦白一件你冇做過嘅事係不對嘅——嗰樣做好不對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,你坦白一件你沒做過的事是不對的——那樣做非常不對。

passages.original: But I drove you to it.
passages.vernacular: 但係係我逼你嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是是我逼你的。

passages.original: So if you’ll forgive me, Anne, I’ll forgive you and we’ll start square again.
passages.vernacular: 所以如果你原諒我,安妮,我就原諒你,我哋重新開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以如果你原諒我,安妮,我就原諒你,我們重新開始。

passages.original: And now get yourself ready for the picnic.”
passages.vernacular: 而家去準備野餐吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在去準備野餐吧。」

passages.original: Anne flew up like a rocket.
passages.vernacular: 安妮像火箭一樣跳咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮像火箭一樣跳了起來。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, isn’t it too late?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,係唔係太晚喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,是不是太晚了?」

passages.original: “No, it’s only two o’clock.
passages.vernacular: 「不,才兩點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,才兩點。

passages.original: They won’t be more than well gathered yet and it’ll be an hour before they have tea.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋仲冇到齊呢,仲要一個鐘頭才飲茶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們還沒到齊呢,還要一個鐘頭才喝茶。

passages.original: Wash your face and comb your hair and put on your gingham.
passages.vernacular: 洗洗臉,梳梳頭,穿上你嘅格子布裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 洗洗臉,梳梳頭,穿上你的格子布裙子。

passages.original: I’ll fill a basket for you.
passages.vernacular: 我畀你裝一籃子嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給你裝一籃子東西。

passages.original: There’s plenty of stuff baked in the house.
passages.vernacular: 家裡烤嘅嘢有好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 家裡烤的東西有很多。

passages.original: And I’ll get Jerry to hitch up the sorrel and drive you down to the picnic ground.”
passages.vernacular: 我讓傑里把栗色馬套上,送你到野餐嘅地方去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讓傑里把栗色馬套上,送你到野餐的地方去。」

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla,” exclaimed Anne, flying to the wash-stand.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」安妮叫道,飛奔到洗臉架前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」安妮叫道,飛奔到洗臉架前。

passages.original: “Five minutes ago I was so miserable I was wishing I’d never been born and now I wouldn’t change places with an angel!”
passages.vernacular: 「五分鐘前我仲咁痛苦,真希望從冇出生過,而而家我連跟天使換位置都唔肯!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「五分鐘前我還那麼痛苦,真希望從沒出生過,而現在我連跟天使換位置都不肯!」

passages.original: That night a thoroughly happy, completely tired-out Anne returned to Green Gables in a state of beatification impossible to describe.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,一個徹頭徹尾快樂、精疲力竭嘅安妮回到綠色屋頂,處於一種無法形容嘅極樂狀態。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,一個徹頭徹尾快樂、精疲力竭的安妮回到綠色屋頂,處於一種無法形容的極樂狀態。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, I’ve had a perfectly scrumptious time.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我度過咗一段特別絕妙嘅時光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我度過了一段特別絕妙的時光。

passages.original: Scrumptious is a new word I learned today.
passages.vernacular: 絕妙係我今日學到嘅一個新詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 絕妙是我今天學到的一個新詞。

passages.original: I heard Mary Alice Bell use it.
passages.vernacular: 我聽瑪麗·艾麗斯·貝爾用過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽瑪麗·艾麗斯·貝爾用過。

passages.original: Isn’t it very expressive?
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係好有表現力嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不是很有表現力嗎?

passages.original: Everything was lovely.
passages.vernacular: 一切都太可愛喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切都太可愛了。

passages.original: We had a splendid tea and then Mr. Harmon Andrews took us all for a row on the Lake of Shining Waters--six of us at a time.
passages.vernacular: 我哋有一頓豐盛嘅茶點,然後哈蒙·安德魯斯先生帶我哋全都喺閃亮湖水上划船——一次六個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們有一頓豐盛的茶點,然後哈蒙·安德魯斯先生帶我們全都在閃亮湖水上划船——一次六個人。

passages.original: And Jane Andrews nearly fell overboard.
passages.vernacular: 簡·安德魯斯差點掉到船外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡·安德魯斯差點掉到船外。

passages.original: She was leaning out to pick water lilies and if Mr. Andrews hadn’t caught her by her sash just in the nick of time she’d fallen in and prob’ly been drowned.
passages.vernacular: 佢正探身摘瞓蓮,要唔係安德魯斯先生喺千鈞一髮之際抓住佢嘅腰帶,佢就掉下去喇,大概會淹死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她正探身摘睡蓮,要不是安德魯斯先生在千鈞一髮之際抓住她的腰帶,她就掉下去了,大概會淹死。

passages.original: I wish it had been me.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望嗰個係我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望那是我。

passages.original: It would have been such a romantic experience to have been nearly drowned.
passages.vernacular: 差點被淹死會係幾咁浪漫嘅經歷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 差點被淹死會是多麼浪漫的經歷。

passages.original: It would be such a thrilling tale to tell.
passages.vernacular: 嗰將係一個幾咁驚心動魄嘅故事可以講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那將是一個多麼驚心動魄的故事可以講。

passages.original: And we had the ice cream.
passages.vernacular: 我哋仲食咗冰淇淋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們還吃了冰淇淋。

passages.original: Words fail me to describe that ice cream.
passages.vernacular: 我簡直找唔到詞嚟形容嗰冰淇淋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我簡直找不到詞來形容那冰淇淋。

passages.original: Marilla, I assure you it was sublime.”
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉,我向您保證,佢係崇高嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉,我向您保證,它是崇高的。」

passages.original: That evening Marilla told the whole story to Matthew over her stocking basket.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,瑪麗拉喺佢嘅襪子籃邊把整個故事講畀咗馬修聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,瑪麗拉在她的襪子籃邊把整個故事講給了馬修聽。

passages.original: “I’m willing to own up that I made a mistake,” she concluded candidly, “but I’ve learned a lesson.
passages.vernacular: 「我願意承認我弄錯喇,」佢坦率地總結道,「但我學到咗一課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我願意承認我弄錯了,」她坦率地總結道,「但我學到了一課。

passages.original: I have to laugh when I think of Anne’s ‘confession,’ although I suppose I shouldn’t for it really was a falsehood.
passages.vernacular: 想起安妮嘅『坦白』我就忍不住要笑,雖然我想我不該笑,因為嗰確實係謊話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想起安妮的『坦白』我就忍不住要笑,雖然我想我不該笑,因為那確實是謊話。

passages.original: But it doesn’t seem as bad as the other would have been, somehow, and anyhow I’m responsible for it.
passages.vernacular: 但唔知點嘅,佢不像另一種咁糟,不管點樣我要對此負責。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但不知怎麼的,它不像另一種那麼糟,不管怎樣我要對此負責。

passages.original: That child is hard to understand in some respects.
passages.vernacular: 嗰細路喺某些方面好難理解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那孩子在某些方面很難理解。

passages.original: But I believe she’ll turn out all right yet.
passages.vernacular: 但我相信佢終究會變好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我相信她終究會變好的。

passages.original: And there’s one thing certain, no house will ever be dull that she’s in.”
passages.vernacular: 仲有一件事係肯定嘅,只要佢喺,任何房子都唔會沉悶。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有一件事是肯定的,只要她在,任何房子都不會沉悶。」

chapters.title: Ch. XV A Tempest in the School Teapot 第十五章:學校裏的一場茶壺風暴

passages.original: CH WHAT a splendid day!” said Anne, drawing a long breath.
passages.vernacular: 「幾咁美好嘅一天啊!」安妮深深吸咗口氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多麼美好的一天啊!」安妮深深吸了口氣說。

passages.original: “Isn’t it good just to be alive on a day like this?
passages.vernacular: 「喺咁樣嘅日子裡活住唔係太好咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在這樣的日子裡活著不是太好了嗎?

passages.original: I pity the people who aren’t born yet for missing it.
passages.vernacular: 我可憐嗰啲仲冇出生嘅人,佢哋錯過咗呢一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可憐那些還沒出生的人,他們錯過了這一天。

passages.original: They may have good days, of course, but they can never have this one.
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢哋或者會有好日子,但佢哋永遠唔會有呢一天喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,他們也許會有好日子,但他們永遠不會有這一天了。

passages.original: And it’s splendider still to have such a lovely way to go to school by, isn’t it?”
passages.vernacular: 而且有咁可愛嘅上學路走,就更美妙喇,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且有這麼可愛的上學路走,就更美妙了,是不是?」

passages.original: “It’s a lot nicer than going round by the road; that is so dusty and hot,” said Diana practically, peeping into her dinner basket and mentally calculating if the three juicy, toothsome, raspberry tarts reposing there were divided among ten girls how many bites each girl would have.
passages.vernacular: 「呢比繞大路走好得多;嗰條路又髒又熱,」黛安娜務實地講,偷睇住佢嘅午飯籃子,喺心裡盤算住,放喺裡面嘅三塊多汁、可口嘅覆盆子餡餅要係分畀十個女孩,每個女孩能咬幾口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這比繞大路走好得多;那條路又髒又熱,」黛安娜務實地說,偷看著她的午飯籃子,在心裡盤算著,放在裡面的三塊多汁、可口的覆盆子餡餅要是分給十個女孩,每個女孩能咬幾口。

passages.original: The little girls of Avonlea school always pooled their lunches, and to eat three raspberry tarts all alone or even to share them only with one’s best chum would have forever and ever branded as “awful mean” the girl who did it.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利學校嘅小女孩哋總是把午飯湊喺一起,如果邊個獨自食三塊覆盆子餡餅,甚至只同自己最好嘅朋友分享,嗰佢就會永永遠遠被貼上「小氣透頂」嘅標籤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利學校的小女孩們總是把午飯湊在一起,如果誰獨自吃三塊覆盆子餡餅,甚至只和自己最好的朋友分享,那她就會永永遠遠被貼上「小氣透頂」的標籤。

passages.original: And yet, when the tarts were divided among ten girls you just got enough to tantalize you.
passages.vernacular: 不過,當餡餅分畀十個女孩時,你得到嘅剛好只夠讓你饞得慌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是,當餡餅分給十個女孩時,你得到的剛好只夠讓你饞得慌。

passages.original: The way Anne and Diana went to school was a pretty one.
passages.vernacular: 安妮同黛安娜上學嘅路好漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮和黛安娜上學的路很漂亮。

passages.original: Anne thought those walks to and from school with Diana couldn’t be improved upon even by imagination.
passages.vernacular: 安妮覺得,同黛安娜一起上學放學嘅呢段路,連想像力都改進不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮覺得,和黛安娜一起上學放學的這段路,連想像力都改進不了。

passages.original: Going around by the main road would have been so unromantic; but to go by Lover’s Lane and Willowmere and Violet Vale and the Birch Path was romantic, if ever anything was.
passages.vernacular: 走大路會係幾咁冇浪漫情調;而走情人小徑、柳塘、紫羅蘭谷同白樺小徑,如果講有乜嘢係浪漫嘅,嗰個就係呢條路喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走大路會是多麼沒有浪漫情調;而走情人小徑、柳塘、紫羅蘭谷和白樺小徑,如果說有什麼是浪漫的,那就是這條路了。

passages.original: Lover’s Lane opened out below the orchard at Green Gables and stretched far up into the woods to the end of the Cuthbert farm.
passages.vernacular: 情人小徑從綠色屋頂嘅果園下面開始,向上延伸進樹林,一直到卡思伯特農場嘅盡頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 情人小徑從綠色屋頂的果園下面開始,向上延伸進樹林,一直到卡思伯特農場的盡頭。

passages.original: It was the way by which the cows were taken to the back pasture and the wood hauled home in winter.
passages.vernacular: 牛群就係沿住呢條路被趕到後面牧場去嘅,冬天柴火都係從呢條路拉回家嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牛群就是沿著這條路被趕到後面牧場去的,冬天柴火也是從這條路拉回家的。

passages.original: Anne had named it Lover’s Lane before she had been a month at Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 安妮到綠色屋頂唔到一個月,就把佢命名為情人小徑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮到綠色屋頂不到一個月,就把它命名為情人小徑。

passages.original: “Not that lovers ever really walk there,” she explained to Marilla, “but Diana and I are reading a perfectly magnificent book and there’s a Lover’s Lane in it.
passages.vernacular: 「並唔係真嘅有情人喺嗰兒散步,」佢向瑪麗拉解釋,「但係黛安娜同我正在讀一本好了不起嘅書,裡面有個情人小徑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「並不是真的有情人在那兒散步,」她向瑪麗拉解釋,「但是黛安娜和我正在讀一本非常了不起的書,裡面有個情人小徑。

passages.original: So we want to have one, too.
passages.vernacular: 所以我哋都想有一條。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我們也想有一條。

passages.original: And it’s a very pretty name, don’t you think?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個好美嘅名字,您不覺得嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個很美的名字,您不覺得嗎?

passages.original: So romantic!
passages.vernacular: 多浪漫啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多浪漫啊!

passages.original: We can’t imagine the lovers into it, you know.
passages.vernacular: 你知道,我哋冇法把情人想像進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,我們沒法把情人想像進去。

passages.original: I like that lane because you can think out loud there without people calling you crazy.”
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意嗰條小徑,因為喺嗰兒你可以大聲想事情,而唔會被人叫做瘋子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡那條小徑,因為在那兒你可以大聲想事情,而不會被人叫做瘋子。」

passages.original: Anne, starting out alone in the morning, went down Lover’s Lane as far as the brook.
passages.vernacular: 朝早安妮獨自出發,沿住情人小徑走到小溪邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早上安妮獨自出發,沿著情人小徑走到小溪邊。

passages.original: Here Diana met her, and the two little girls went on up the lane under the leafy arch of maples--“maples are such sociable trees,” said Anne; “they’re always rustling and whispering to you”--until they came to a rustic bridge.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜喺呢兒同佢會合,兩個小女孩繼續順住小徑,喺楓樹嘅綠葉拱頂下往上走——「楓樹係幾咁合群嘅樹,」安妮講;「佢哋總是沙沙地、低語地對你講話」——直到走到一座鄉村小橋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜在這兒與她會合,兩個小女孩繼續順著小徑,在楓樹的綠葉拱頂下往上走——「楓樹是多麼合群的樹,」安妮說;「它們總是沙沙地、低語地對你說話」——直到走到一座鄉村小橋。

passages.original: Then they left the lane and walked through Mr. Barry’s back field and past Willowmere.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋離開小徑,穿過巴里先生嘅後田,經過柳塘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她們離開小徑,穿過巴里先生的後田,經過柳塘。

passages.original: Beyond Willowmere came Violet Vale--a little green dimple in the shadow of Mr. Andrew Bell’s big woods.
passages.vernacular: 越過柳塘就係紫羅蘭谷——安德魯·貝爾先生嗰片大樹林陰影裡嘅一個小小嘅綠色酒窩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 越過柳塘就是紫羅蘭谷——安德魯·貝爾先生那片大樹林陰影裡的一個小小的綠色酒窩。

passages.original: “Of course there are no violets there now,” Anne told Marilla, “but Diana says there are millions of them in spring.
passages.vernacular: 「當然,而家嗰度冇紫羅蘭,」安妮告訴瑪麗拉,「但黛安娜講春天有幾百萬朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,現在那裡沒有紫羅蘭,」安妮告訴瑪麗拉,「但黛安娜說春天有幾百萬朵。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, can’t you just imagine you see them?
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,您難道唔能夠想像睇見佢哋嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,您難道不能想像看見它們嗎?

passages.original: It actually takes away my breath.
passages.vernacular: 佢真嘅讓我屏住呼吸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它真的讓我屏住呼吸。

passages.original: I named it Violet Vale.
passages.vernacular: 我把佢命名為紫羅蘭谷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把它命名為紫羅蘭谷。

passages.original: Diana says she never saw the beat of me for hitting on fancy names for places.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜講佢從冇見過比我更會畀地方起花哨名字嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜說她從沒見過比我更會給地方起花哨名字的人。

passages.original: It’s nice to be clever at something, isn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 擅長某樣嘢,真好,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 擅長某樣東西,真好,是不是?

passages.original: But Diana named the Birch Path.
passages.vernacular: 但白樺小徑係黛安娜起嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但白樺小徑是黛安娜起的名字。

passages.original: She wanted to, so I let her; but I’m sure I could have found something more poetical than plain Birch Path.
passages.vernacular: 佢想起,所以我就讓佢起;但我肯定我本可以找出比平淡嘅白樺小徑更有詩意嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她想起,所以我就讓她起;但我肯定我本可以找出比平淡的白樺小徑更有詩意的名字。

passages.original: Anybody can think of a name like that.
passages.vernacular: 邊個都能想出嗰樣嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰都能想出那樣的名字。

passages.original: But the Birch Path is one of the prettiest places in the world, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 但白樺小徑係世上最美嘅地方之一,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但白樺小徑是世上最美的地方之一,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: It was.
passages.vernacular: 確實如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實如此。

passages.original: Other people besides Anne thought so when they stumbled on it.
passages.vernacular: 除咗安妮,別人偶然走到嗰度,都咁認為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了安妮,別人偶然走到那裡,也這麼認為。

passages.original: It was a little narrow, twisting path, winding down over a long hill straight through Mr. Bell’s woods, where the light came down sifted through so many emerald screens that it was as flawless as the heart of a diamond.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一條彎彎曲曲嘅小窄路,蜿蜒向下穿過一座長長嘅山丘,直接穿過貝爾先生嘅樹林,光線透過咁多層翠綠嘅屏障篩下嚟,純淨得像鑽石嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一條彎彎曲曲的小窄路,蜿蜒向下穿過一座長長的山丘,直接穿過貝爾先生的樹林,光線透過那麼多層翠綠的屏障篩下來,純淨得像鑽石的心。

passages.original: It was fringed in all its length with slim young birches, white stemmed and lissom boughed; ferns and starflowers and wild lilies-of-the-valley and scarlet tufts of pigeonberries grew thickly along it; and always there was a delightful spiciness in the air and music of bird calls and the murmur and laugh of wood winds in the trees overhead.
passages.vernacular: 佢全程都鑲住纖細嘅年輕白樺,白色嘅樹幹,柔軟嘅枝條;蕨類、星花、野鈴蘭同鴿莓嘅猩紅小簇,沿路長得茂密;空氣中總有一種愉快嘅辛香,鳥鳴如音樂,頭頂樹上嘅林風低語同笑聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它全程都鑲著纖細的年輕白樺,白色的樹幹,柔軟的枝條;蕨類、星花、野鈴蘭和鴿莓的猩紅小簇,沿路長得茂密;空氣中總有一種愉快的辛香,鳥鳴如音樂,頭頂樹上的林風低語和笑聲。

passages.original: Now and then you might see a rabbit skipping across the road if you were quiet--which, with Anne and Diana, happened about once in a blue moon.
passages.vernacular: 如果你安靜,偶爾可以睇見一隻兔子從路上蹦過——可呢喺安妮同黛安娜身上,大概係百年難遇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你安靜,偶爾可以看見一隻兔子從路上蹦過——可這在安妮和黛安娜身上,大概是百年難遇。

passages.original: Down in the valley the path came out to the main road and then it was just up the spruce hill to the school.
passages.vernacular: 喺山谷中,小路通向大路,然後只需爬上雲杉山就到學校喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在山谷中,小路通向大路,然後只需爬上雲杉山就到學校了。

passages.original: The Avonlea school was a whitewashed building, low in the eaves and wide in the windows, furnished inside with comfortable substantial old-fashioned desks that opened and shut, and were carved all over their lids with the initials and hieroglyphics of three generations of school children.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利學校係一座刷白嘅房子,屋簷低矮,窗戶寬大,裡面擺住舒適結實嘅老式桌子,可以開合,桌蓋上刻滿咗三代學童嘅姓名縮寫同象形文字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利學校是一座刷白的房子,屋簷低矮,窗戶寬大,裡面擺著舒適結實的老式桌子,可以開合,桌蓋上刻滿了三代學童的姓名縮寫和象形文字。

passages.original: The schoolhouse was set back from the road and behind it was a dusky fir wood and a brook where all the children put their bottles of milk in the morning to keep cool and sweet until dinner hour.
passages.vernacular: 校舍位於離路稍遠嘅地方,後面係一片昏暗嘅杉樹林同一條小溪,所有細路早晨都把牛奶瓶放喺溪裡,讓佢保持涼爽同新鮮,直到午飯時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 校舍位於離路稍遠的地方,後面是一片昏暗的杉樹林和一條小溪,所有孩子早晨都把牛奶瓶放在溪裡,讓它保持涼爽和新鮮,直到午飯時間。

passages.original: Marilla had seen Anne start off to school on the first day of September with many secret misgivings.
passages.vernacular: 九月一日安妮開始上學時,瑪麗拉帶住許多暗暗嘅憂慮目送佢出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 九月一日安妮開始上學時,瑪麗拉帶著許多暗暗的憂慮目送她出發。

passages.original: Anne was such an odd girl.
passages.vernacular: 安妮係個咁古怪嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮是個那麼古怪的女孩。

passages.original: How would she get on with the other children?
passages.vernacular: 佢點同別嘅細路相處呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她怎麼和別的孩子相處呢?

passages.original: And how on earth would she ever manage to hold her tongue during school hours?
passages.vernacular: 而且佢究竟點能喺上課時間管住自己嘅舌頭呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且她究竟怎麼能在上課時間管住自己的舌頭呢?

passages.original: Things went better than Marilla feared, however.
passages.vernacular: 不過,事情比瑪麗拉擔心嘅要順利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,事情比瑪麗拉擔心的要順利。

passages.original: Anne came home that evening in high spirits.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天傍晚,安妮興高采烈地回到家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天傍晚,安妮興高采烈地回到家。

passages.original: “I think I’m going to like school here,” she announced.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我會鍾意呢度嘅學校,」佢宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我會喜歡這裡的學校,」她宣布。
