passages.original: “I don’t think much of the master, though.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我對老師評價不高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過我對老師評價不高。

passages.original: He’s all the time curling his mustache and making eyes at Prissy Andrews.
passages.vernacular: 佢總是捲佢嘅鬍子,對普麗茜·安德魯斯拋媚眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他總是捲他的鬍子,對普麗茜·安德魯斯拋媚眼。

passages.original: Prissy is grown up, you know.
passages.vernacular: 您知道,普麗茜已經長大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道,普麗茜已經長大了。

passages.original: She’s sixteen and she’s studying for the entrance examination into Queen’s Academy at Charlottetown next year.
passages.vernacular: 佢十六歲,正在準備明年進夏洛特敦女王學院嘅入學考試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她十六歲,正在準備明年進夏洛特敦女王學院的入學考試。

passages.original: Tillie Boulter says the master is dead gone on her.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莉·博爾特講老師迷死佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莉·博爾特說老師迷死她了。

passages.original: She’s got a beautiful complexion and curly brown hair and she does it up so elegantly.
passages.vernacular: 佢有美麗嘅膚色同棕色嘅捲髮,梳得特別優雅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有美麗的膚色和棕色的捲髮,梳得特別優雅。

passages.original: She sits in the long seat at the back and he sits there, too, most of the time--to explain her lessons, he says.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐喺後面嘅長凳上,佢大部分時間都坐喺嗰兒——佢講係畀佢講解功課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她坐在後面的長凳上,他大部分時間也坐在那兒——他說是給她講解功課。

passages.original: But Ruby Gillis says she saw him writing something on her slate and when Prissy read it she blushed as red as a beet and giggled; and Ruby Gillis says she doesn’t believe it had anything to do with the lesson.”
passages.vernacular: 但露比·吉利斯講,佢睇見佢喺佢嘅石板上寫咗乜嘢,普麗茜讀咗之後臉紅得像甜菜,仲咯咯笑;露比·吉利斯講佢不相信嗰跟功課有任何關係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但露比·吉利斯說,她看見他在她的石板上寫了什麼,普麗茜讀了之後臉紅得像甜菜,還咯咯笑;露比·吉利斯說她不相信那跟功課有任何關係。」

passages.original: “Anne Shirley, don’t let me hear you talking about your teacher in that way again,” said Marilla sharply.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,唔好畀我再聽見你嗰樣談論你嘅老師,」瑪麗拉厲聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,別讓我再聽見你那樣談論你的老師,」瑪麗拉厲聲說。

passages.original: “You don’t go to school to criticize the master.
passages.vernacular: 「你去學校唔係為了批評老師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你去學校不是為了批評老師。

passages.original: I guess he can teach you something, and it’s your business to learn.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢能教你啲嘢,你嘅任務係學。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他能教你一些東西,你的任務是學。

passages.original: And I want you to understand right off that you are not to come home telling tales about him.
passages.vernacular: 我要你即刻明白,不許回家嚟搬弄佢嘅係非。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要你馬上明白,不許回家來搬弄他的是非。

passages.original: That is something I won’t encourage.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係我唔會鼓勵嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是我不會鼓勵的事。

passages.original: I hope you were a good girl.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望你做咗個好細路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你做了個好孩子。」

passages.original: “Indeed I was,” said Anne comfortably.
passages.vernacular: 「當然,」安妮舒服地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,」安妮舒服地說。

passages.original: “It wasn’t so hard as you might imagine, either.
passages.vernacular: 「都冇像您想像嘅咁難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也沒像您想像的那麼難。

passages.original: I sit with Diana.
passages.vernacular: 我同黛安娜坐一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我和黛安娜坐一起。

passages.original: Our seat is right by the window and we can look down to the Lake of Shining Waters.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅座位就喺窗邊,可以俯瞰閃亮湖水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的座位就在窗邊,可以俯瞰閃亮湖水。

passages.original: There are a lot of nice girls in school and we had scrumptious fun playing at dinnertime.
passages.vernacular: 學校里有好多好女孩,午飯時我哋玩得特別痛快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學校里有很多好女孩,午飯時我們玩得特別痛快。

passages.original: It’s so nice to have a lot of little girls to play with.
passages.vernacular: 有好多小女孩一起玩真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有很多小女孩一起玩真好。

passages.original: But of course I like Diana best and always will.
passages.vernacular: 不過當然我最鍾意黛安娜,並且永遠如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過當然我最喜歡黛安娜,並且永遠如此。

passages.original: I adore Diana.
passages.vernacular: 我崇拜黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我崇拜黛安娜。

passages.original: I’m dreadfully far behind the others.
passages.vernacular: 我比別人落後好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我比別人落後很多。

passages.original: They’re all in the fifth book and I’m only in the fourth.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都念第五冊,我只念第四冊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們都念第五冊,我只念第四冊。

passages.original: I feel that it’s kind of a disgrace.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得有點丟臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得有點丟臉。

passages.original: But there’s not one of them has such an imagination as I have and I soon found that out.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋邊個都冇我咁樣嘅想像力,我好快就發現咗呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她們誰都沒有我這樣的想像力,我很快就發現了這一點。

passages.original: We had reading and geography and Canadian history and dictation today.
passages.vernacular: 今日我哋上咗閱讀、地理、加攞大歷史同聽寫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天我們上了閱讀、地理、加拿大歷史和聽寫。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips said my spelling was disgraceful and he held up my slate so that everybody could see it, all marked over.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生講我嘅拼寫好丟人,佢舉起我嘅石板讓大家都睇到,上面全係記號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生說我的拼寫很丟人,他舉起我的石板讓大家都看到,上面全是記號。

passages.original: I felt so mortified, Marilla; he might have been politer to a stranger, I think.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得太羞辱喇,瑪麗拉;我覺得佢對一個陌生人本可以客氣些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得太羞辱了,瑪麗拉;我覺得他對一個陌生人本可以客氣些。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis gave me an apple and Sophia Sloane lent me a lovely pink card with ‘May I see you home?’ on it.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯畀咗我一個蘋果,蘇菲亞·斯隆借畀我一張可愛嘅粉紅卡片,上面寫住『可以送你回家嗎?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯給了我一個蘋果,蘇菲亞·斯隆借給我一張可愛的粉紅卡片,上面寫著『可以送你回家嗎?』

passages.original: I’m to give it back to her tomorrow.
passages.vernacular: 我聽日要還畀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我明天要還給她。

passages.original: And Tillie Boulter let me wear her bead ring all the afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莉·博爾特讓我整個下午都戴佢嘅珠子戒指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莉·博爾特讓我整個下午都戴她的珠子戒指。

passages.original: Can I have some of those pearl beads off the old pincushion in the garret to make myself a ring?
passages.vernacular: 我可以要閣樓上嗰個舊針墊上嘅珍珠珠子,畀自己做一個戒指嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以要閣樓上那個舊針墊上的珍珠珠子,給自己做一個戒指嗎?

passages.original: And oh, Marilla, Jane Andrews told me that Minnie MacPherson told her that she heard Prissy Andrews tell Sara Gillis that I had a very pretty nose.
passages.vernacular: 仲有,哦,瑪麗拉,簡·安德魯斯告訴我,明妮·麥克弗森告訴佢,佢聽見普麗茜·安德魯斯告訴莎拉·吉利斯講我有一個好漂亮嘅鼻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,哦,瑪麗拉,簡·安德魯斯告訴我,明妮·麥克弗森告訴她,她聽見普麗茜·安德魯斯告訴莎拉·吉利斯說我有一個很漂亮的鼻子。

passages.original: Marilla, that is the first compliment I have ever had in my life and you can’t imagine what a strange feeling it gave me.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉,呢個係我一生中得到嘅第一個恭維,您無法想像佢畀咗我幾咁奇怪嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉,這是我一生中得到的第一個恭維,您無法想像它給了我多麼奇怪的感覺。

passages.original: Marilla, have I really a pretty nose?
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉,我真嘅有一個漂亮嘅鼻子嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉,我真的有一個漂亮的鼻子嗎?

passages.original: I know you’ll tell me the truth.”
passages.vernacular: 我知道您會告訴我實話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道您會告訴我實話。」

passages.original: “Your nose is well enough,” said Marilla shortly.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅鼻子仲不錯,」瑪麗拉簡短地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的鼻子還不錯,」瑪麗拉簡短地說。

passages.original: Secretly she thought Anne’s nose was a remarkable pretty one; but she had no intention of telling her so.
passages.vernacular: 佢暗地裡覺得安妮嘅鼻子好漂亮,但佢無意告訴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她暗地裡覺得安妮的鼻子非常漂亮,但她無意告訴她。

passages.original: That was three weeks ago and all had gone smoothly so far.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係三個星期以前嘅事,到目前為止一切都好順利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是三個星期以前的事,到目前為止一切都很順利。

passages.original: And now, this crisp September morning, Anne and Diana were tripping blithely down the Birch Path, two of the happiest little girls in Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 而而家,喺呢個清爽嘅九月早晨,安妮同黛安娜正愉快地沿住白樺小徑蹦蹦跳跳,係阿文利最快樂嘅兩個小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而現在,在這個清爽的九月早晨,安妮和黛安娜正愉快地沿著白樺小徑蹦蹦跳跳,是阿文利最快樂的兩個小女孩。

passages.original: “I guess Gilbert Blythe will be in school today,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我想吉爾伯特·布萊斯今日會嚟學校,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想吉爾伯特·布萊斯今天會來學校,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “He’s been visiting his cousins over in New Brunswick all summer and he only came home Saturday night.
passages.vernacular: 「佢整個夏天都喺新不倫瑞克佢表兄弟家做客,星期六晚上才回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他整個夏天都在新不倫瑞克他表兄弟家做客,星期六晚上才回家。

passages.original: He’s aw’fly handsome, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 佢特別帥,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他特別帥,安妮。

passages.original: And he teases the girls something terrible.
passages.vernacular: 而且佢可愛捉弄女孩,厲害極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且他可愛捉弄女孩,厲害極了。

passages.original: He just torments our lives out.”
passages.vernacular: 佢簡直把我哋折磨死喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他簡直把我們折磨死了。」

passages.original: Diana’s voice indicated that she rather liked having her life tormented out than not.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜嘅聲音表明,佢其實相當鍾意被折磨死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜的聲音表明,她其實相當喜歡被折磨死。

passages.original: “Gilbert Blythe?” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯?」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯?」安妮說。

passages.original: “Isn’t his name that’s written up on the porch wall with Julia Bell’s and a big ‘Take Notice’ over them?”
passages.vernacular: 「門廊牆上同朱莉婭·貝爾嘅名字寫喺一起、上面有個大大嘅『請注意』嘅,不就係佢嘅名字嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「門廊牆上和朱莉婭·貝爾的名字寫在一起、上面有個大大的『請注意』的,不就是他的名字嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes,” said Diana, tossing her head, “but I’m sure he doesn’t like Julia Bell so very much.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」黛安娜甩住頭講,「但我肯定佢不點鍾意朱莉婭·貝爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」黛安娜甩著頭說,「但我肯定他不怎麼喜歡朱莉婭·貝爾。

passages.original: I’ve heard him say he studied the multiplication table by her freckles.”
passages.vernacular: 我聽佢講過,佢係靠數佢嘅雀斑嚟背乘法表嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽他說過,他是靠數她的雀斑來背乘法表的。」

passages.original: “Oh, don’t speak about freckles to me,” implored Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,別跟我提雀斑,」安妮懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,別跟我提雀斑,」安妮懇求道。

passages.original: “It isn’t delicate when I’ve got so many.
passages.vernacular: 「我有咁多,提呢個不太雅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有那麼多,提這個不太雅。

passages.original: But I do think that writing take-notices up on the wall about the boys and girls is the silliest ever.
passages.vernacular: 不過我確實覺得,喺牆上寫男孩女孩嘅『請注意』係最愚蠢嘅事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我確實覺得,在牆上寫男孩女孩的『請注意』是最愚蠢的事了。

passages.original: I should just like to see anybody dare to write my name up with a boy’s.
passages.vernacular: 我真想睇睇有邊個敢把我嘅名字同一個男孩嘅寫喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真想看看有誰敢把我的名字和一個男孩的寫在一起。

passages.original: Not, of course,” she hastened to add, “that anybody would.”
passages.vernacular: 當然,」佢連忙補充,「唔會有人寫嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,」她連忙補充,「不會有人寫的。」

passages.original: Anne sighed.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮嘆了口氣。

passages.original: She didn’t want her name written up.
passages.vernacular: 佢並唔想讓自己嘅名字被寫上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她並不想讓自己的名字被寫上去。

passages.original: But it was a little humiliating to know that there was no danger of it.
passages.vernacular: 但知道根本冇呢種危險,又有點丟臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但知道根本沒有這種危險,又有點丟臉。

passages.original: “Nonsense,” said Diana, whose black eyes and glossy tresses had played such havoc with the hearts of Avonlea schoolboys that her name figured on the porch walls in half a dozen take-notices.
passages.vernacular: 「胡講,」黛安娜講,佢嗰雙黑眼睛同光亮嘅鬈髮,把阿文利嘅男學生哋迷得神魂顛倒,佢嘅名字喺門廊牆上嘅六個『請注意』裡出現過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說,」黛安娜說,她那雙黑眼睛和光亮的鬈髮,把阿文利的男學生們迷得神魂顛倒,她的名字在門廊牆上的六個『請注意』裡出現過。

passages.original: “It’s only meant as a joke.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰只係開玩笑嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那只是開玩笑的。

passages.original: And don’t you be too sure your name won’t ever be written up.
passages.vernacular: 你別太肯定你嘅名字永遠唔會被寫上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你別太肯定你的名字永遠不會被寫上去。

passages.original: Charlie Sloane is dead gone on you.
passages.vernacular: 查理·斯隆迷死你喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 查理·斯隆迷死你了。

passages.original: He told his mother--his mother, mind you--that you were the smartest girl in school.
passages.vernacular: 佢對佢母親講——佢母親,你注意——你係學校裡最聰明嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對他母親說——他母親,你注意——你是學校裡最聰明的女孩。

passages.original: That’s better than being good-looking.”
passages.vernacular: 呢比長得好睇仲好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這比長得好看還好。」

passages.original: “No, it isn’t,” said Anne, feminine to the core.
passages.vernacular: 「不,唔係,」安妮講,徹頭徹尾係個女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不是,」安妮說,徹頭徹尾是個女孩。

passages.original: “I’d rather be pretty than clever.
passages.vernacular: 「我寧願漂亮都唔好聰明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我寧願漂亮也不要聰明。

passages.original: And I hate Charlie Sloane, I can’t bear a boy with goggle eyes.
passages.vernacular: 而且我討厭查理·斯隆,我受不了金魚眼嘅男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我討厭查理·斯隆,我受不了金魚眼的男孩。

passages.original: If anyone wrote my name up with his I’d never get over it, Diana Barry.
passages.vernacular: 如果有邊個把我嘅名字同佢嘅寫喺一起,我永遠唔會緩過嚟嘅,黛安娜·巴里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果有誰把我的名字和他的寫在一起,我永遠不會緩過來的,黛安娜·巴里。

passages.original: But it is nice to keep head of your class.”
passages.vernacular: 不過保持班上第一名係好不錯嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過保持班上第一名是很不錯的。」

passages.original: “You’ll have Gilbert in your class after this,” said Diana, “and he’s used to being head of his class, I can tell you.
passages.vernacular: 「從今以後吉爾伯特會跟你同班,」黛安娜講,「我告訴你,佢習慣咗做班上第一名。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從今以後吉爾伯特會跟你同班,」黛安娜說,「我告訴你,他習慣了做班上第一名。

passages.original: He’s only in the fourth book although he’s nearly fourteen.
passages.vernacular: 佢才讀第四冊,雖然佢快十四歲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他才讀第四冊,雖然他快十四歲了。

passages.original: Four years ago his father was sick and had to go out to Alberta for his health and Gilbert went with him.
passages.vernacular: 四年前佢父親生病喇,得到艾伯塔去養病,吉爾伯特都跟住去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四年前他父親生病了,得到艾伯塔去養病,吉爾伯特也跟著去了。

passages.original: They were there three years and Gil didn’t go to school hardly any until they came back.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺嗰兒待咗三年,吉爾直到回嚟之前幾乎冇上過學。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在那兒待了三年,吉爾直到回來之前幾乎沒上過學。

passages.original: You won’t find it so easy to keep head after this, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 從今以後你要保持第一名就冇咁容易喇,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從今以後你要保持第一名就沒那麼容易了,安妮。」

passages.original: “I’m glad,” said Anne quickly.
passages.vernacular: 「我好高興,」安妮好快地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很高興,」安妮很快地說。

passages.original: “I couldn’t really feel proud of keeping head of little boys and girls of just nine or ten.
passages.vernacular: 「我保持班上只有九、十歲嘅小男孩小女孩嘅第一名,心裡真不覺得自豪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我保持班上只有九、十歲的小男孩小女孩的第一名,心裡真不覺得自豪。

passages.original: I got up yesterday spelling ‘ebullition.’
passages.vernacular: 尋日我站起嚟拼寫『ebullition』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨天我站起來拼寫『ebullition』。

passages.original: Josie Pye was head and, mind you, she peeped in her book.
passages.vernacular: 喬西·派伊係第一名,你注意,佢偷睇咗書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西·派伊是第一名,你注意,她偷看了書。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips didn’t see her--he was looking at Prissy Andrews--but I did.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生冇睇見佢——佢喺睇普麗茜·安德魯斯——但我睇見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生沒看見她——他在看普麗茜·安德魯斯——但我看見了。

passages.original: I just swept her a look of freezing scorn and she got as red as a beet and spelled it wrong after all.”
passages.vernacular: 我只係朝佢投去冰冷嘅輕蔑一瞥,佢就臉紅得像甜菜,結果定係拼錯喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是朝她投去冰冷的輕蔑一瞥,她就臉紅得像甜菜,結果還是拼錯了。」

passages.original: “Those Pye girls are cheats all round,” said Diana indignantly, as they climbed the fence of the main road.
passages.vernacular: 「派伊家嘅女孩哋全都係騙子,」黛安娜憤慨地講,佢哋爬過通往大路嘅柵欄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「派伊家的女孩們全都是騙子,」黛安娜憤慨地說,她們爬過通往大路的柵欄。

passages.original: “Gertie Pye actually went and put her milk bottle in my place in the brook yesterday.
passages.vernacular: 「格蒂·派伊尋日竟然把佢嘅牛奶瓶放喺我喺小溪裡嘅位置上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「格蒂·派伊昨天竟然把她的牛奶瓶放在我在小溪裡的位置上。

passages.original: Did you ever?
passages.vernacular: 你聽講過呢種事嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你聽說過這種事嗎?

passages.original: I don’t speak to her now.”
passages.vernacular: 我而家不跟佢講話喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在不跟她說話了。」

passages.original: When Mr. Phillips was in the back of the room hearing Prissy Andrews’s Latin, Diana whispered to Anne, “That’s Gilbert Blythe sitting right across the aisle from you, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生喺教室後面聽普麗茜·安德魯斯背拉丁文時,黛安娜悄悄對安妮講:「嗰個就係吉爾伯特·布萊斯,坐喺過道對面,正對住你,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生在教室後面聽普麗茜·安德魯斯背拉丁文時,黛安娜悄悄對安妮說:「那就是吉爾伯特·布萊斯,坐在過道對面,正對著你,安妮。

passages.original: Just look at him and see if you don’t think he’s handsome.”
passages.vernacular: 睇睇佢,你覺得佢係唔係好帥。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看看他,你覺得他是不是很帥。」

passages.original: Anne looked accordingly.
passages.vernacular: 安妮於是睇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮於是看了。

passages.original: She had a good chance to do so, for the said Gilbert Blythe was absorbed in stealthily pinning the long yellow braid of Ruby Gillis, who sat in front of him, to the back of her seat.
passages.vernacular: 佢有個好機會,因為嗰位吉爾伯特·布萊斯正全神貫注地偷偷把坐喺佢前面嘅露比·吉利斯嘅黃色長辮子別喺佢嘅椅背上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有個好機會,因為那位吉爾伯特·布萊斯正全神貫注地偷偷把坐在他前面的露比·吉利斯的黃色長辮子別在她的椅背上。

passages.original: He was a tall boy, with curly brown hair, roguish hazel eyes, and a mouth twisted into a teasing smile.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個高個子嘅男孩,有一頭棕色嘅鬈髮,淘氣嘅榛色眼睛,嘴角扭成一個逗弄人嘅微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個高個子的男孩,有一頭棕色的鬈髮,淘氣的榛色眼睛,嘴角扭成一個逗弄人的微笑。

passages.original: Presently Ruby Gillis started up to take a sum to the master; she fell back into her seat with a little shriek, believing that her hair was pulled out by the roots.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒,露比·吉利斯站起嚟把一道算術題交畀老師;佢尖叫一聲跌回座位,以為頭髮被連根拔掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒,露比·吉利斯站起來把一道算術題交給老師;她尖叫一聲跌回座位,以為頭髮被連根拔掉了。

passages.original: Everybody looked at her and Mr. Phillips glared so sternly that Ruby began to cry.
passages.vernacular: 每個人都睇住佢,菲利普斯先生嚴厲地瞪住,露比就哭咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個人都看著她,菲利普斯先生嚴厲地瞪著,露比就哭了起來。

passages.original: Gilbert had whisked the pin out of sight and was studying his history with the soberest face in the world; but when the commotion subsided he looked at Anne and winked with inexpressible drollery.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特已經把別針藏咗起嚟,正以世上最嚴肅嘅面孔研究佢嘅歷史;但等騷動平息,佢就睇住安妮,無法形容地滑稽地眨咗眨眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特已經把別針藏了起來,正以世上最嚴肅的面孔研究他的歷史;但等騷動平息,他就看著安妮,無法形容地滑稽地眨了眨眼。

passages.original: “I think your Gilbert Blythe is handsome,” confided Anne to Diana, “but I think he’s very bold.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得你嘅吉爾伯特·布萊斯好帥,」安妮悄悄對黛安娜講,「但我覺得佢好放肆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得你的吉爾伯特·布萊斯很帥,」安妮悄悄對黛安娜說,「但我覺得他非常放肆。

passages.original: It isn’t good manners to wink at a strange girl.”
passages.vernacular: 對一個陌生女孩眨眼不禮貌。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對一個陌生女孩眨眼不禮貌。」

passages.original: But it was not until the afternoon that things really began to happen.
passages.vernacular: 但直到下午,事情才真正開始發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但直到下午,事情才真正開始發生。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips was back in the corner explaining a problem in algebra to Prissy Andrews and the rest of the scholars were doing pretty much as they pleased eating green apples, whispering, drawing pictures on their slates, and driving crickets harnessed to strings, up and down aisle.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生喺角落裡畀普麗茜·安德魯斯講解一道代數題,其餘學生差不多各行其係:食青蘋果、竊竊私語、喺石板上畫畫,以及把拴住線嘅蟋蟀趕住喺過道上跑嚟跑去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生在角落裡給普麗茜·安德魯斯講解一道代數題,其餘學生差不多各行其是:吃青蘋果、竊竊私語、在石板上畫畫,以及把拴著線的蟋蟀趕著在過道上跑來跑去。

passages.original: Gilbert Blythe was trying to make Anne Shirley look at him and failing utterly, because Anne was at that moment totally oblivious not only to the very existence of Gilbert Blythe, but of every other scholar in Avonlea school itself.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯想讓安妮·雪莉睇佢,卻徹底失敗喇,因為此刻安妮不僅完全忘咗吉爾伯特·布萊斯嘅存在,而且忘咗阿文利學校里所有其他學生嘅存在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯想讓安妮·雪莉看他,卻徹底失敗了,因為此刻安妮不僅完全忘了吉爾伯特·布萊斯的存在,而且忘了阿文利學校里所有其他學生的存在。

passages.original: With her chin propped on her hands and her eyes fixed on the blue glimpse of the Lake of Shining Waters that the west window afforded, she was far away in a gorgeous dreamland hearing and seeing nothing save her own wonderful visions.
passages.vernacular: 佢雙手托住下巴,眼睛盯住西窗外嗰一小片藍色嘅閃亮湖水,神遊喺一個絢麗嘅夢境裡,除咗佢自己奇妙嘅幻象,乜嘢都聽唔見、睇唔見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她雙手托著下巴,眼睛盯著西窗外那一小片藍色的閃亮湖水,神遊在一個絢麗的夢境裡,除了她自己奇妙的幻象,什麼也聽不見、看不見。

passages.original: Gilbert Blythe wasn’t used to putting himself out to make a girl look at him and meeting with failure.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯不習慣為讓一個女孩睇佢而費心,仲遭到失敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯不習慣為讓一個女孩看他而費心,還遭到失敗。

passages.original: She should look at him, that red-haired Shirley girl with the little pointed chin and the big eyes that weren’t like the eyes of any other girl in Avonlea school.
passages.vernacular: 佢應該睇佢,嗰個長住尖尖小下巴同大眼睛嘅紅頭髮雪莉女孩,嗰雙眼睛不像阿文利學校里任何別嘅女孩嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她應該看他,那個長著尖尖小下巴和大眼睛的紅頭髮雪莉女孩,那雙眼睛不像阿文利學校里任何別的女孩的眼睛。

passages.original: Gilbert reached across the aisle, picked up the end of Anne’s long red braid, held it out at arm’s length and said in a piercing whisper:
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特越過過道,攞起安妮嗰條長長嘅紅辮子嘅末梢,伸直手臂舉住,尖聲低語:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特越過過道,拿起安妮那條長長的紅辮子的末梢,伸直手臂舉著,尖聲低語:

passages.original: “Carrots!
passages.vernacular: 「胡蘿蔔!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡蘿蔔!

passages.original: Carrots!”
passages.vernacular: 胡蘿蔔!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 胡蘿蔔!」

passages.original: Then Anne looked at him with a vengeance!
passages.vernacular: 於是安妮狠狠地睇咗佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是安妮狠狠地看了他!

passages.original: She did more than look.
passages.vernacular: 佢做嘅不止係睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她做的不止是看。

passages.original: She sprang to her feet, her bright fancies fallen into cureless ruin.
passages.vernacular: 佢跳咗起嚟,佢明亮嘅幻想已無可挽回地毀滅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她跳了起來,她明亮的幻想已無可挽回地毀滅。

passages.original: She flashed one indignant glance at Gilbert from eyes whose angry sparkle was swiftly quenched in equally angry tears.
passages.vernacular: 佢向吉爾伯特投去憤怒嘅一瞥,嗰雙眼睛裡憤怒嘅光芒好快被同樣憤怒嘅淚水澆滅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她向吉爾伯特投去憤怒的一瞥,那雙眼睛裡憤怒的光芒很快被同樣憤怒的淚水澆滅了。

passages.original: “You mean, hateful boy!” she exclaimed passionately.
passages.vernacular: 「你呢個卑鄙、可恨嘅男孩!」佢激烈地叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你這個卑鄙、可恨的男孩!」她激烈地叫道。

passages.original: “How dare you!”
passages.vernacular: 「你點敢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼敢!」

passages.original: And then--thwack!
passages.vernacular: 接住——啪!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著——啪!

passages.original: Anne had brought her slate down on Gilbert’s head and cracked it--slate not head--clear across.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把佢嘅石板砸喺吉爾伯特嘅頭上,把佢砸裂喇——係石板,唔係頭——一直裂到底。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把她的石板砸在吉爾伯特的頭上,把它砸裂了——是石板,不是頭——一直裂到底。

passages.original: Avonlea school always enjoyed a scene.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利學校總是鍾意睇熱鬧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利學校總是喜歡看熱鬧。

passages.original: This was an especially enjoyable one.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一場特別好睇嘅熱鬧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一場特別好看的熱鬧。

passages.original: Everybody said “Oh” in horrified delight.
passages.vernacular: 每個人都帶住驚駭嘅喜悅講「哦」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個人都帶著驚駭的喜悅說「哦」。

passages.original: Diana gasped.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜倒抽咗一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜倒抽了一口氣。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis, who was inclined to be hysterical, began to cry.
passages.vernacular: 容易歇斯底里嘅露比·吉利斯哭咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 容易歇斯底里的露比·吉利斯哭了起來。

passages.original: Tommy Sloane let his team of crickets escape him altogether while he stared open-mouthed at the tableau.
passages.vernacular: 湯米·斯隆讓佢嘅嗰隊蟋蟀徹底逃脫喇,佢張住嘴盯住呢幅活生生嘅場景。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯米·斯隆讓他的那隊蟋蟀徹底逃脫了,他張著嘴盯著這幅活生生的場景。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips stalked down the aisle and laid his hand heavily on Anne’s shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生大步走下過道,沉重地把手放喺安妮嘅肩上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生大步走下過道,沉重地把手放在安妮的肩上。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley, what does this mean?” he said angrily.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,呢個係乜嘢意思?」佢憤怒地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,這是什麼意思?」他憤怒地說。

passages.original: Anne returned no answer.
passages.vernacular: 安妮冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮沒有回答。

passages.original: It was asking too much of flesh and blood to expect her to tell before the whole school that she had been called “carrots.”
passages.vernacular: 要求佢當住全校嘅面講出佢被叫咗「胡蘿蔔」,呢對血肉之軀來講未免太過分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要求她當著全校的面說出她被叫了「胡蘿蔔」,這對血肉之軀來說未免太過分。

passages.original: Gilbert it was who spoke up stoutly.
passages.vernacular: 係吉爾伯特堅決地開咗口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是吉爾伯特堅決地開了口。

passages.original: “It was my fault Mr. Phillips.
passages.vernacular: 「係我嘅錯,菲利普斯先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是我的錯,菲利普斯先生。

passages.original: I teased her.”
passages.vernacular: 我逗佢嚟住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我逗她來著。」

passages.original: Mr. Phillips paid no heed to Gilbert.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生不理會吉爾伯特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生不理會吉爾伯特。

passages.original: “I am sorry to see a pupil of mine displaying such a temper and such a vindictive spirit,” he said in a solemn tone, as if the mere fact of being a pupil of his ought to root out all evil passions from the hearts of small imperfect mortals.
passages.vernacular: 「我好遺憾睇到我嘅學生表現出咁樣嘅脾氣同咁樣報復嘅心理,」佢用莊重嘅語氣講,好像單憑做佢嘅學生呢個事實,就應該把所有邪惡嘅激情從不完美嘅小凡人心裡根除掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很遺憾看到我的學生表現出這樣的脾氣和這樣報復的心理,」他用莊重的語氣說,好像單憑做他的學生這個事實,就應該把所有邪惡的激情從不完美的小凡人心裡根除掉。

passages.original: “Anne, go and stand on the platform in front of the blackboard for the rest of the afternoon.”
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,到黑板前面嘅講臺上去站住,站到下午結束。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,到黑板前面的講臺上去站著,站到下午結束。」

passages.original: Anne would have infinitely preferred a whipping to this punishment under which her sensitive spirit quivered as from a whiplash.
passages.vernacular: 安妮寧可挨一頓鞭子,都唔願受呢種懲罰,佢敏感嘅心靈喺呢種懲罰下像被鞭子抽打般顫抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮寧可挨一頓鞭子,也不願受這種懲罰,她敏感的心靈在這種懲罰下像被鞭子抽打般顫抖。

passages.original: With a white, set face she obeyed.
passages.vernacular: 佢面色蒼白,神情凝固,服從喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她面色蒼白,神情凝固,服從了。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips took a chalk crayon and wrote on the blackboard above her head.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生攞起一支粉筆,喺佢頭上方嘅黑板上寫道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生拿起一支粉筆,在她頭上方的黑板上寫道:

passages.original: “Ann Shirley has a very bad temper.
passages.vernacular: 「Ann Shirley脾氣好壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「Ann Shirley脾氣很壞。

passages.original: Ann Shirley must learn to control her temper,” and then read it out loud so that even the primer class, who couldn’t read writing, should understand it.
passages.vernacular: Ann Shirley必須學會控制自己嘅脾氣。」然後大聲念出嚟,讓連睇不懂字嘅初級班嘅細路都能聽懂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: Ann Shirley必須學會控制自己的脾氣。」然後大聲念出來,讓連看不懂字的初級班的孩子也能聽懂。

passages.original: Anne stood there the rest of the afternoon with that legend above her.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺嗰兒站咗整個下午,頭頂上就係嗰行字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在那兒站了整個下午,頭頂上就是那行字。

passages.original: She did not cry or hang her head.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇哭,都冇低頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她沒有哭,也沒有低頭。

passages.original: Anger was still too hot in her heart for that and it sustained her amid all her agony of humiliation.
passages.vernacular: 憤怒喺佢心裡依然太熾熱,不允許佢嗰樣,佢支撐住佢度過所有屈辱嘅痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憤怒在她心裡依然太熾熱,不允許她那樣,它支撐著她度過所有屈辱的痛苦。

passages.original: With resentful eyes and passion-red cheeks she confronted alike Diana’s sympathetic gaze and Charlie Sloane’s indignant nods and Josie Pye’s malicious smiles.
passages.vernacular: 佢用怨恨嘅眼睛、激憤得通紅嘅臉頰,同樣面對住黛安娜同情嘅目光、查理·斯隆憤慨嘅點頭,以及喬西·派伊惡意嘅微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她用怨恨的眼睛、激憤得通紅的臉頰,同樣面對著黛安娜同情的目光、查理·斯隆憤慨的點頭,以及喬西·派伊惡意的微笑。

passages.original: As for Gilbert Blythe, she would not even look at him.
passages.vernacular: 至於吉爾伯特·布萊斯,佢連睇都不睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於吉爾伯特·布萊斯,她連看都不看他。

passages.original: She would never look at him again!
passages.vernacular: 佢再都唔會睇佢喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她再也不會看他了!

passages.original: She would never speak to him!!
passages.vernacular: 佢再都唔會跟佢講話喇!!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她再也不會跟他說話了!!

passages.original: When school was dismissed Anne marched out with her red head held high.
passages.vernacular: 放學時,安妮昂住紅頭走咗出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 放學時,安妮昂著紅頭走了出去。

passages.original: Gilbert Blythe tried to intercept her at the porch door.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯試圖喺門廊門口攔住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯試圖在門廊門口攔住她。

passages.original: “I’m awfully sorry I made fun of your hair, Anne,” he whispered contritely.
passages.vernacular: 「我真嘅好抱歉我取笑你嘅頭髮,安妮,」佢悔恨地低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真的很抱歉我取笑你的頭髮,安妮,」他悔恨地低聲說。

passages.original: “Honest I am.
passages.vernacular: 「我真嘅好抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真的很抱歉。

passages.original: Don’t be mad for keeps, now.”
passages.vernacular: 別永遠生我嘅氣,好嗎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別永遠生我的氣,好嗎。」

passages.original: Anne swept by disdainfully, without look or sign of hearing.
passages.vernacular: 安妮輕蔑地從佢身邊走過,睇都不睇,都裝作冇聽見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮輕蔑地從他身邊走過,看也不看,也裝作沒聽見。

passages.original: “Oh how could you, Anne?” breathed Diana as they went down the road half reproachfully, half admiringly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你點能咁樣,安妮?」佢哋走喺路上,黛安娜喘住氣講,半係責備,半係欽佩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你怎麼能這樣,安妮?」她們走在路上,黛安娜喘著氣說,半是責備,半是欽佩。

passages.original: Diana felt that she could never have resisted Gilbert’s plea.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜覺得佢自己係絕對抵擋不咗吉爾伯特嘅懇求嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜覺得她自己是絕對抵擋不了吉爾伯特的懇求的。

passages.original: “I shall never forgive Gilbert Blythe,” said Anne firmly.
passages.vernacular: 「我永遠唔會原諒吉爾伯特·布萊斯,」安妮堅定地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我永遠不會原諒吉爾伯特·布萊斯,」安妮堅定地說。

passages.original: “And Mr. Phillips spelled my name without an e, too.
passages.vernacular: 「而且菲利普斯先生拼我嘅名字都冇E。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且菲利普斯先生拼我的名字也沒有E。

passages.original: The iron has entered into my soul, Diana.”
passages.vernacular: 鐵已經刺進咗我嘅靈魂,黛安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鐵已經刺進了我的靈魂,黛安娜。」

passages.original: Diana hadn’t the least idea what Anne meant but she understood it was something terrible.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜完全不明白安妮係乜嘢意思,但佢明白嗰個係好可怕嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜完全不明白安妮是什麼意思,但她明白那是很可怕的事。

passages.original: “You mustn’t mind Gilbert making fun of your hair,” she said soothingly.
passages.vernacular: 「你別在意吉爾伯特取笑你嘅頭髮,」佢安慰地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你別在意吉爾伯特取笑你的頭髮,」她安慰地說。

passages.original: “Why, he makes fun of all the girls.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,佢取笑所有嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,他取笑所有的女孩。

passages.original: He laughs at mine because it’s so black.
passages.vernacular: 佢笑我嘅頭髮,因為太黑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他笑我的頭髮,因為太黑了。

passages.original: He’s called me a crow a dozen times; and I never heard him apologize for anything before, either.”
passages.vernacular: 佢叫我烏鴉叫咗十幾次;而且我以前都從冇聽佢為任何事道過歉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他叫我烏鴉叫了十幾次;而且我以前也從沒聽他為任何事道過歉。」

passages.original: “There’s a great deal of difference between being called a crow and being called carrots,” said Anne with dignity.
passages.vernacular: 「被叫烏鴉同被叫胡蘿蔔有好大嘅區別,」安妮威嚴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「被叫烏鴉和被叫胡蘿蔔有很大的區別,」安妮威嚴地說。

passages.original: “Gilbert Blythe has hurt my feelings excruciatingly, Diana.”
passages.vernacular: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯極其痛苦地傷咗我嘅感情,黛安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯極其痛苦地傷了我的感情,黛安娜。」

passages.original: It is possible the matter might have blown over without more excruciation if nothing else had happened.
passages.vernacular: 如果冇再發生別嘅事,呢件事或者唔會再引起痛苦就過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果沒有再發生別的事,這件事也許不會再引起痛苦就過去了。

passages.original: But when things begin to happen they are apt to keep on.
passages.vernacular: 但事情一旦開始發生,往往會接二連三。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但事情一旦開始發生,往往會接二連三。

passages.original: Avonlea scholars often spent noon hour picking gum in Mr. Bell’s spruce grove over the hill and across his big pasture field.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利嘅學生經常利用午休時間,喺貝爾先生翻過山、穿過佢大牧場嘅杉樹林裡採樹脂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利的學生經常利用午休時間,在貝爾先生翻過山、穿過他大牧場的杉樹林裡採樹脂。

passages.original: From there they could keep an eye on Eben Wright’s house, where the master boarded.
passages.vernacular: 從嗰兒可以睇住埃本·賴特嘅家,老師喺嗰兒寄宿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那兒可以看著埃本·賴特的家,老師在那兒寄宿。

passages.original: When they saw Mr. Phillips emerging therefrom they ran for the schoolhouse; but the distance being about three times longer than Mr. Wright’s lane they were very apt to arrive there, breathless and gasping, some three minutes too late.
passages.vernacular: 當佢哋睇到菲利普斯先生從嗰兒出嚟時,就向校舍跑去;不過距離大約係賴特先生小巷嘅三倍長,佢哋往往氣喘吁吁地遲到三分鐘左右。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他們看到菲利普斯先生從那兒出來時,就向校舍跑去;可是距離大約是賴特先生小巷的三倍長,他們往往氣喘吁吁地遲到三分鐘左右。

passages.original: On the following day Mr. Phillips was seized with one of his spasmodic fits of reform and announced before going home to dinner, that he should expect to find all the scholars in their seats when he returned.
passages.vernacular: 第二天,菲利普斯先生犯咗佢嗰陣發嘅改革症,回家食午飯前宣布,佢回嚟時要睇到所有學生都在座位上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天,菲利普斯先生犯了他那陣發的改革症,回家吃午飯前宣布,他回來時要看到所有學生都在座位上。

passages.original: Anyone who came in late would be punished.
passages.vernacular: 遲到嘅人要受罰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遲到的人要受罰。

passages.original: All the boys and some of the girls went to Mr. Bell’s spruce grove as usual, fully intending to stay only long enough to “pick a chew.”
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅男孩同啲女孩像往常一樣去咗貝爾先生嘅杉樹林,完全打算只待足夠「採一塊嚼」嘅時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的男孩和一些女孩像往常一樣去了貝爾先生的杉樹林,完全打算只待足夠「採一塊嚼」的時間。

passages.original: But spruce groves are seductive and yellow nuts of gum beguiling; they picked and loitered and strayed; and as usual the first thing that recalled them to a sense of the flight of time was Jimmy Glover shouting from the top of a patriarchal old spruce “Master’s coming.”
passages.vernacular: 但杉樹林係誘人嘅,黃色嘅樹脂塊好迷人;佢哋採住,逗留住,游蕩住;像往常一樣,首先喚醒佢哋意識到時間流逝嘅,係吉米·格洛弗從一棵古老嘅杉樹頂上喊嘅「老師嚟喇」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但杉樹林是誘人的,黃色的樹脂塊很迷人;他們採著,逗留著,游蕩著;像往常一樣,首先喚醒他們意識到時間流逝的,是吉米·格洛弗從一棵古老的杉樹頂上喊的「老師來了」。

passages.original: The girls who were on the ground, started first and managed to reach the schoolhouse in time but without a second to spare.
passages.vernacular: 喺地上嘅女孩哋先出發,設法剛好及時趕到校舍,但一秒鐘都不富餘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在地上的女孩們先出發,設法剛好及時趕到校舍,但一秒鐘也不富餘。

passages.original: The boys, who had to wriggle hastily down from the trees, were later; and Anne, who had not been picking gum at all but was wandering happily in the far end of the grove, waist deep among the bracken, singing softly to herself, with a wreath of rice lilies on her hair as if she were some wild divinity of the shadowy places, was latest of all.
passages.vernacular: 得急匆匆從樹上滑下嚟嘅男孩哋更晚;而安妮根本冇喺採樹脂,而係快樂地漫遊喺樹林嘅遠端,蕨叢冇到腰際,輕聲地自言自語,頭髮上戴住稻花百合花環,仿佛係陰暗之地嘅某位野生神靈,佢係最後一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 得急匆匆從樹上滑下來的男孩們更晚;而安妮根本沒在採樹脂,而是快樂地漫遊在樹林的遠端,蕨叢沒到腰際,輕聲地自言自語,頭髮上戴著稻花百合花環,仿佛是陰暗之地的某位野生神靈,她是最後一個。

passages.original: Anne could run like a deer, however; run she did with the impish result that she overtook the boys at the door and was swept into the schoolhouse among them just as Mr. Phillips was in the act of hanging up his hat.
passages.vernacular: 不過安妮跑起嚟像鹿一樣;佢跑喇,結果淘氣地喺門口追上咗男孩哋,同佢哋一起被捲進咗校舍,正好係菲利普斯先生喺掛帽子嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過安妮跑起來像鹿一樣;她跑了,結果淘氣地在門口追上了男孩們,與他們一起被捲進了校舍,正好是菲利普斯先生在掛帽子的時候。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips’s brief reforming energy was over; he didn’t want the bother of punishing a dozen pupils; but it was necessary to do something to save his word, so he looked about for a scapegoat and found it in Anne, who had dropped into her seat, gasping for breath, with a forgotten lily wreath hanging askew over one ear and giving her a particularly rakish and disheveled appearance.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生短暫嘅改革勁頭已經過去;佢唔想費事去懲罰十幾個學生;但為了保全佢嘅話必須做點乜嘢,於是佢四下尋找替罪羊,喺安妮身上找到喇,佢跌坐在座位上,氣喘吁吁,一個被遺忘嘅百合花環歪掛喺一隻耳朵上,使佢顯得格外放蕩凌亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生短暫的改革勁頭已經過去;他不想費事去懲罰十幾個學生;但為了保全他的話必須做點什麼,於是他四下尋找替罪羊,在安妮身上找到了,她跌坐在座位上,氣喘吁吁,一個被遺忘的百合花環歪掛在一隻耳朵上,使她顯得格外放蕩凌亂。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley, since you seem to be so fond of the boys’ company we shall indulge your taste for it this afternoon,” he said sarcastically.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,既然你似乎咁鍾意男孩哋嘅陪伴,今日下午我哋就滿足你呢個愛好,」佢諷刺地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,既然你似乎這麼喜歡男孩們的陪伴,今天下午我們就滿足你這個愛好,」他諷刺地說。

passages.original: “Take those flowers out of your hair and sit with Gilbert Blythe.”
passages.vernacular: 「把頭上嘅花攞下嚟,去同吉爾伯特·布萊斯坐。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把頭上的花拿下來,去和吉爾伯特·布萊斯坐。」

passages.original: The other boys snickered.
passages.vernacular: 其他男孩竊笑起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他男孩竊笑起來。

passages.original: Diana, turning pale with pity, plucked the wreath from Anne’s hair and squeezed her hand.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜因同情而臉色發白,從安妮嘅頭髮上摘下花環,握咗握佢嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜因同情而臉色發白,從安妮的頭髮上摘下花環,握了握她的手。

passages.original: Anne stared at the master as if turned to stone.
passages.vernacular: 安妮像變成石頭一樣盯住老師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮像變成石頭一樣盯著老師。

passages.original: “Did you hear what I said, Anne?” queried Mr. Phillips sternly.
passages.vernacular: 「你聽見我講嘅話咗嗎,安妮?」菲利普斯先生嚴厲地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你聽見我說的話了嗎,安妮?」菲利普斯先生嚴厲地問。

passages.original: “Yes, sir,” said Anne slowly “but I didn’t suppose you really meant it.”
passages.vernacular: 「聽見喇,先生,」安妮慢慢地講,「但我冇想到您真係呢個意思。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽見了,先生,」安妮慢慢地說,「但我沒想到您真是這個意思。」

passages.original: “I assure you I did”--still with the sarcastic inflection which all the children, and Anne especially, hated.
passages.vernacular: 「我向你保證我係——」仍帶住所有細路,尤其係安妮,最恨嘅嗰種諷刺嘅語調。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我向你保證我是——」仍帶著所有孩子,尤其是安妮,最恨的那種諷刺的語調。

passages.original: It flicked on the raw.
passages.vernacular: 呢戳到咗痛處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這戳到了痛處。

passages.original: “Obey me at once.”
passages.vernacular: 「即刻服從我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬上服從我。」

passages.original: For a moment Anne looked as if she meant to disobey.
passages.vernacular: 有咁一會兒,安妮睇上去像係要違抗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有那麼一會兒,安妮看上去像是要違抗。

passages.original: Then, realizing that there was no help for it, she rose haughtily, stepped across the aisle, sat down beside Gilbert Blythe, and buried her face in her arms on the desk.
passages.vernacular: 然後,意識到冇辦法,佢傲慢地站起身,走過過道,喺吉爾伯特·布萊斯旁邊坐下,把臉埋喺桌上嘅臂彎裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,意識到沒有辦法,她傲慢地站起身,走過過道,在吉爾伯特·布萊斯旁邊坐下,把臉埋在桌上的臂彎裡。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis, who got a glimpse of it as it went down, told the others going home from school that she’d “acksually never seen anything like it--it was so white, with awful little red spots in it.”
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯喺佢埋下去嘅時候瞥見咗一眼,放學回家路上告訴別人,佢「真嘅從冇見過嗰樣嘅臉——咁白,上面仲有可怕嘅小紅點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯在它埋下去的時候瞥見了一眼,放學回家路上告訴別人,她「真的從沒見過那樣的臉——那麼白,上面還有可怕的小紅點。」

passages.original: To Anne, this was as the end of all things.
passages.vernacular: 對安妮來講,呢個係一切嘅終結。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對安妮來說,這是一切的終結。

passages.original: It was bad enough to be singled out for punishment from among a dozen equally guilty ones; it was worse still to be sent to sit with a boy, but that that boy should be Gilbert Blythe was heaping insult on injury to a degree utterly unbearable.
passages.vernacular: 從十幾個同樣有罪嘅人中被單單挑出嚟受罰,已經夠糟嘅喇;被派去同一個男孩坐,更糟;但嗰個男孩偏偏係吉爾伯特·布萊斯,呢個係雪上加霜、侮辱到咗完全無法忍受嘅程度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從十幾個同樣有罪的人中被單單挑出來受罰,已經夠糟的了;被派去和一個男孩坐,更糟;但那個男孩偏偏是吉爾伯特·布萊斯,這是雪上加霜、侮辱到了完全無法忍受的程度。

passages.original: Anne felt that she could not bear it and it would be of no use to try.
passages.vernacular: 安妮覺得佢受不喇,試都冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮覺得她受不了,試也沒用。

passages.original: Her whole being seethed with shame and anger and humiliation.
passages.vernacular: 佢整個人都因羞愧、憤怒同屈辱而沸騰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她整個人都因羞愧、憤怒和屈辱而沸騰。

passages.original: At first the other scholars looked and whispered and giggled and nudged.
passages.vernacular: 起初其他學生睇住、竊竊私語、咯咯笑、推搡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初其他學生看著、竊竊私語、咯咯笑、推搡。

passages.original: But as Anne never lifted her head and as Gilbert worked fractions as if his whole soul was absorbed in them and them only, they soon returned to their own tasks and Anne was forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 但因為安妮始終冇抬頭,而吉爾伯特做分數題時,好像佢整個靈魂都完全沉浸喺其中,佢哋好快就回去做自己嘅事,安妮被忘記喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但因為安妮始終沒有抬頭,而吉爾伯特做分數題時,好像他整個靈魂都完全沉浸在其中,他們很快就回去做自己的事,安妮被忘記了。

passages.original: When Mr. Phillips called the history class out Anne should have gone, but Anne did not move, and Mr. Phillips, who had been writing some verses “To Priscilla” before he called the class, was thinking about an obstinate rhyme still and never missed her.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生叫歷史班出列嘅時候,安妮本應該去,但安妮冇動,而菲利普斯先生喺叫班之前一直喺寫啲「獻畀普麗西拉」嘅詩句,仲喺想住一個頑固嘅韻腳,根本冇想起佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生叫歷史班出列的時候,安妮本應該去,但安妮沒有動,而菲利普斯先生在叫班之前一直在寫一些「獻給普麗西拉」的詩句,還在想著一個頑固的韻腳,根本沒有想起她。

passages.original: Once, when nobody was looking, Gilbert took from his desk a little pink candy heart with a gold motto on it, “You are sweet,” and slipped it under the curve of Anne’s arm.
passages.vernacular: 有一次,喺冇人睇嘅時候,吉爾伯特從佢嘅桌子裡攞出一顆粉紅色嘅小糖心,上面有金色嘅格言「你真甜」,把佢滑到安妮嘅臂彎下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一次,在沒人看的時候,吉爾伯特從他的桌子裡拿出一顆粉紅色的小糖心,上面有金色的格言「你真甜」,把它滑到安妮的臂彎下。

passages.original: Whereupon Anne arose, took the pink heart gingerly between the tips of her fingers, dropped it on the floor, ground it to powder beneath her heel, and resumed her position without deigning to bestow a glance on Gilbert.
passages.vernacular: 於是安妮站起嚟,用指尖小心地捏起粉紅嘅心,把佢丟喺地上,用腳跟把佢碾成粉末,然後回到座位上,不屑睇吉爾伯特一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是安妮站起來,用指尖小心地捏起粉紅的心,把它丟在地上,用腳跟把它碾成粉末,然後回到座位上,不屑看吉爾伯特一眼。

passages.original: When school went out Anne marched to her desk, ostentatiously took out everything therein, books and writing tablet, pen and ink, testament and arithmetic, and piled them neatly on her cracked slate.
passages.vernacular: 放學時,安妮走到自己嘅桌前,故意地把裡面嘅嘢都攞咗出嚟,書同寫字本、鋼筆同墨水、新約聖經同算術書,整整齊齊地堆喺佢嗰塊裂咗嘅石板上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 放學時,安妮走到自己的桌前,故意地把裡面的東西都拿了出來,書和寫字本、鋼筆和墨水、新約聖經和算術書,整整齊齊地堆在她那塊裂了的石板上。

passages.original: “What are you taking all those things home for, Anne?”
passages.vernacular: 「你把呢啲嘢都帶回家幹乜嘢,安妮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你把這些東西都帶回家幹什麼,安妮?」

passages.original: Diana wanted to know, as soon as they were out on the road.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜一到路上就想知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜一到路上就想知道。

passages.original: She had not dared to ask the question before.
passages.vernacular: 佢以前唔敢問呢個問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她以前不敢問這個問題。

passages.original: “I am not coming back to school any more,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔再回學校喇,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不再回學校了,」安妮說。

passages.original: Diana gasped and stared at Anne to see if she meant it.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜倒抽一口氣,盯住安妮睇佢係唔係認真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜倒抽一口氣,盯著安妮看她是不是認真的。

passages.original: “Will Marilla let you stay home?” she asked.
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉會讓你待喺家嗎?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉會讓你待在家嗎?」她問。

passages.original: “She’ll have to,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「佢必須讓,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她必須讓,」安妮說。

passages.original: “I’ll never go to school to that man again.”
passages.vernacular: 「我再都唔到嗰個人嗰兒上學喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再也不到那個人那兒上學了。」

passages.original: “Oh, Anne!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,安妮!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,安妮!」

passages.original: Diana looked as if she were ready to cry.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜睇上去像要哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜看上去像要哭了。

passages.original: “I do think you’re mean.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得你太狠心喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得你太狠心了。

passages.original: What shall I do?
passages.vernacular: 我該點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我該怎麼辦?

passages.original: Mr. Phillips will make me sit with that horrid Gertie Pye--I know he will because she is sitting alone.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生會讓我同嗰個可怕嘅格蒂·派伊坐——我知道佢會嘅,因為佢一個人坐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生會讓我和那個可怕的格蒂·派伊坐——我知道他會的,因為她一個人坐。

passages.original: Do come back, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 回嚟吧,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回來吧,安妮。」

passages.original: “I’d do almost anything in the world for you, Diana,” said Anne sadly.
passages.vernacular: 「我為你幾乎乜嘢都肯做,黛安娜,」安妮悲傷地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我為你幾乎什麼都肯做,黛安娜,」安妮悲傷地說。

passages.original: “I’d let myself be torn limb from limb if it would do you any good.
passages.vernacular: 「只要對你有好處,我會讓自己被碎屍萬段。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只要對你有好處,我會讓自己被碎屍萬段。

passages.original: But I can’t do this, so please don’t ask it.
passages.vernacular: 但呢件事我做唔到,所以請別要求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這件事我做不到,所以請別要求。

passages.original: You harrow up my very soul.”
passages.vernacular: 你呢個係喺撕裂我嘅靈魂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這是在撕裂我的靈魂。」

passages.original: “Just think of all the fun you will miss,” mourned Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「想想你將錯過嘅所有樂趣吧,」黛安娜哀嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「想想你將錯過的所有樂趣吧,」黛安娜哀嘆道。

passages.original: “We are going to build the loveliest new house down by the brook; and we’ll be playing ball next week and you’ve never played ball, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋要喺小溪邊建一座最可愛嘅新房子;下個星期我哋要打球,你從冇打過球,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們要在小溪邊建一座最可愛的新房子;下個星期我們要打球,你從沒打過球,安妮。

passages.original: It’s tremendously exciting.
passages.vernacular: 嗰特別刺激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那特別刺激。

passages.original: And we’re going to learn a new song--Jane Andrews is practicing it up now; and Alice Andrews is going to bring a new Pansy book next week and we’re all going to read it out loud, chapter about, down by the brook.
passages.vernacular: 而且我哋要學一首新歌——簡·安德魯斯而家正在練;愛麗絲·安德魯斯下星期要帶一本新嘅《三色堇》叢書,我哋都要喺小溪邊一章一章輪流大聲朗讀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我們要學一首新歌——簡·安德魯斯現在正在練;愛麗絲·安德魯斯下星期要帶一本新的《三色堇》叢書,我們都要在小溪邊一章一章輪流大聲朗讀。

passages.original: And you know you are so fond of reading out loud, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道你幾咁鍾意大聲朗讀,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道你多麼喜歡大聲朗讀,安妮。」

passages.original: Nothing moved Anne in the least.
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢都冇絲毫打動安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼也沒有絲毫打動安妮。

passages.original: Her mind was made up.
passages.vernacular: 佢已經打定咗主意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她已經打定了主意。

passages.original: She would not go to school to Mr. Phillips again; she told Marilla so when she got home.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔再到菲利普斯先生嗰兒上學;佢回到家就告訴咗瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不再到菲利普斯先生那兒上學;她回到家就告訴了瑪麗拉。

passages.original: “Nonsense,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「胡講,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “It isn’t nonsense at all,” said Anne, gazing at Marilla with solemn, reproachful eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「呢根本唔係胡講,」安妮講,用嚴肅、責備嘅眼睛睇住瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這根本不是胡說,」安妮說,用嚴肅、責備的眼睛看著瑪麗拉。

passages.original: “Don’t you understand, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 「您不明白嗎,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您不明白嗎,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: I’ve been insulted.”
passages.vernacular: 我被侮辱喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被侮辱了。」

passages.original: “Insulted fiddlesticks!
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢侮辱不侮辱嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼侮辱不侮辱的!

passages.original: You’ll go to school tomorrow as usual.”
passages.vernacular: 聽日你照常去上學。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天你照常去上學。」

passages.original: “Oh, no.”
Anne shook her head gently.
passages.vernacular: 安妮輕輕地搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮輕輕地搖搖頭。

passages.original: “I’m not going back, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我不回去喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不回去了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I’ll learn my lessons at home and I’ll be as good as I can be and hold my tongue all the time if it’s possible at all.
passages.vernacular: 我喺家學功課,我會盡量乖,而且只要有可能,我會一直不講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在家學功課,我會盡量乖,而且只要有可能,我會一直不說話。

passages.original: But I will not go back to school, I assure you.”
passages.vernacular: 但我唔會回學校喇,我向您保證。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不會回學校了,我向您保證。」

passages.original: Marilla saw something remarkably like unyielding stubbornness looking out of Anne’s small face.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉睇到一種好像不屈不撓嘅固執嘅嘢,從安妮嘅小臉上顯露出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉看到一種非常像不屈不撓的固執的東西,從安妮的小臉上顯露出來。

passages.original: She understood that she would have trouble in overcoming it; but she resolved wisely to say nothing more just then.
passages.vernacular: 佢明白要克服佢會有麻煩;但佢明智地決定此刻唔再多講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她明白要克服它會有麻煩;但她明智地決定此刻不再多說什麼。

passages.original: “I’ll run down and see Rachel about it this evening,” she thought.
passages.vernacular: 「今晚我去找雷切爾談談呢件事,」佢想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚我去找雷切爾談談這件事,」她想。

passages.original: “There’s no use reasoning with Anne now.
passages.vernacular: 「而家跟安妮講理冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在跟安妮講理沒用。

passages.original: She’s too worked up and I’ve an idea she can be awful stubborn if she takes the notion.
passages.vernacular: 佢太激動喇,我覺得佢要係打定主意,可以固執得好可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她太激動了,我覺得她要是打定主意,可以固執得很可怕。

passages.original: Far as I can make out from her story, Mr. Phillips has been carrying matters with a rather high hand.
passages.vernacular: 據我從佢嘅敘述所能睇出嘅,菲利普斯先生處理問題相當專橫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據我從她的敘述所能看出的,菲利普斯先生處理問題相當專橫。

passages.original: But it would never do to say so to her.
passages.vernacular: 但呢決唔能夠對佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這決不能對她說。

passages.original: I’ll just talk it over with Rachel.
passages.vernacular: 我就同雷切爾商量一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就和雷切爾商量一下。

passages.original: She’s sent ten children to school and she ought to know something about it.
passages.vernacular: 佢送過十個細路上學,應該懂啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她送過十個孩子上學,應該懂一些。

passages.original: She’ll have heard the whole story, too, by this time.”
passages.vernacular: 到呢陣候佢都一定聽講咗整個故事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到這時候她也一定聽說了整個故事。」

passages.original: Marilla found Mrs. Lynde knitting quilts as industriously and cheerfully as usual.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉發現林德太太像往常一樣勤快愉快地織住被子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉發現林德太太像往常一樣勤快愉快地織著被子。

passages.original: “I suppose you know what I’ve come about,” she said, a little shamefacedly.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你知道我係點解嚟嘅,」佢講,有點不好意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你知道我是為什麼來的,」她說,有點不好意思。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel nodded.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太點點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太點點頭。

passages.original: “About Anne’s fuss in school, I reckon,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「係為了安妮喺學校惹嘅事,我猜,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是為了安妮在學校惹的事,我猜,」她說。

passages.original: “Tillie Boulter was in on her way home from school and told me about it.”
passages.vernacular: 「蒂莉·博爾特放學回家路上順道進嚟,跟我講喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蒂莉·博爾特放學回家路上順道進來,跟我說了。」

passages.original: “I don’t know what to do with her,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道攞佢點算,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道拿她怎麼辦,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “She declares she won’t go back to school.
passages.vernacular: 「佢宣布佢不回學校喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她宣布她不回學校了。

passages.original: I never saw a child so worked up.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過咁激動嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過這麼激動的孩子。

passages.original: I’ve been expecting trouble ever since she started to school.
passages.vernacular: 自從佢上學以來,我一直喺預料會有麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從她上學以來,我一直在預料會有麻煩。

passages.original: I knew things were going too smooth to last.
passages.vernacular: 我知道事情太順利喇,唔會長久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道事情太順利了,不會長久。

passages.original: She’s so high strung.
passages.vernacular: 佢太神經緊張喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她太神經緊張了。

passages.original: What would you advise, Rachel?”
passages.vernacular: 你有乜嘢建議,雷切爾?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有什麼建議,雷切爾?」

passages.original: “Well, since you’ve asked my advice, Marilla,” said Mrs. Lynde amiably--Mrs. Lynde dearly loved to be asked for advice--“I’d just humor her a little at first, that’s what I’d do.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,既然你問我嘅建議,瑪麗拉,」林德太太和藹地講——林德太太最鍾意別人問佢建議——「一開始我就稍微順住佢啲,我會咁做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,既然你問我的建議,瑪麗拉,」林德太太和藹地說——林德太太最喜歡別人問她建議——「一開始我就稍微順著她一點,我會這麼做。

passages.original: It’s my belief that Mr. Phillips was in the wrong.
passages.vernacular: 我認為菲利普斯先生錯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我認為菲利普斯先生錯了。

passages.original: Of course, it doesn’t do to say so to the children, you know.
passages.vernacular: 當然,不該對細路哋咁講,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,不該對孩子們這麼說,你知道。

passages.original: And of course he did right to punish her yesterday for giving way to temper.
passages.vernacular: 而且當然佢尋日因為佢發脾氣而處罰佢係對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且當然他昨天因為她發脾氣而處罰她是對的。

passages.original: But today it was different.
passages.vernacular: 但今日就不同喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但今天就不同了。

passages.original: The others who were late should have been punished as well as Anne, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 其他遲到嘅人都應該像安妮一樣受罰,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他遲到的人也應該像安妮一樣受罰,就是這樣。

passages.original: And I don’t believe in making the girls sit with the boys for punishment.
passages.vernacular: 而且我不贊成把女細路罰去同男細路坐喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我不贊成把女孩子罰去和男孩子坐在一起。

passages.original: It isn’t modest.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔得體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不得體。

passages.original: Tillie Boulter was real indignant.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莉·博爾特好憤慨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莉·博爾特很憤慨。

passages.original: She took Anne’s part right through and said all the scholars did too.
passages.vernacular: 佢自始至終站喺安妮一邊,佢講所有嘅學生都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她自始至終站在安妮一邊,她說所有的學生也是。

passages.original: Anne seems real popular among them, somehow.
passages.vernacular: 唔知怎嘅,安妮喺佢哋中間似乎挺受歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知怎的,安妮在他們中間似乎挺受歡迎。

passages.original: I never thought she’d take with them so well.”
passages.vernacular: 我從冇想過佢會咁討佢哋鍾意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒想過她會這麼討他們喜歡。」

passages.original: “Then you really think I’d better let her stay home,” said Marilla in amazement.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你真嘅認為我最好讓佢待喺家裡,」瑪麗拉驚訝地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你真的認為我最好讓她待在家裡,」瑪麗拉驚訝地說。

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: That is I wouldn’t say school to her again until she said it herself.
passages.vernacular: 就係講,喺佢自己講要去之前,我唔會再跟佢提學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是說,在她自己說要去之前,我不會再跟她提學校。

passages.original: Depend upon it, Marilla, she’ll cool off in a week or so and be ready enough to go back of her own accord, that’s what, while, if you were to make her go back right off, dear knows what freak or tantrum she’d take next and make more trouble than ever.
passages.vernacular: 相信我,瑪麗拉,佢過一個星期左右就會冷靜下嚟,好願意自己回去,就係咁樣,而如果你而家逼佢回去,天知道佢接下嚟會發乜嘢怪脾氣、鬧乜嘢彆扭,比以往惹出更多麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我,瑪麗拉,她過一個星期左右就會冷靜下來,很願意自己回去,就是這樣,而如果你現在逼她回去,天知道她接下來會發什麼怪脾氣、鬧什麼彆扭,比以往惹出更多麻煩。

passages.original: The less fuss made the better, in my opinion.
passages.vernacular: 依我嘅睇法,越少大驚小怪越好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 依我的看法,越少大驚小怪越好。

passages.original: She won’t miss much by not going to school, as far as that goes.
passages.vernacular: 就呢點而言,佢不去上學都冇損失多少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這點而言,她不去上學也沒損失多少。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips isn’t any good at all as a teacher.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生當老師啲都不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生當老師一點都不行。

passages.original: The order he keeps is scandalous, that’s what, and he neglects the young fry and puts all his time on those big scholars he’s getting ready for Queen’s.
passages.vernacular: 佢維持嘅秩序太糟糕喇,就係咁樣,佢忽視小細路,把所有時間都花喺佢為女王學院預備嘅嗰啲大學生身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他維持的秩序太糟糕了,就是這樣,他忽視小孩子,把所有時間都花在他為女王學院預備的那些大學生身上。

passages.original: He’d never have got the school for another year if his uncle hadn’t been a trustee--the trustee, for he just leads the other two around by the nose, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 要唔係佢叔叔係校董——係嗰個校董,因為佢把另外兩個牽住鼻子走,就係咁樣——佢明年根本得唔到呢所學校嘅職位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是他叔叔是校董——是那個校董,因為他把另外兩個牽著鼻子走,就是這樣——他明年根本得不到這所學校的職位。

passages.original: I declare, I don’t know what education in this Island is coming to.”
passages.vernacular: 我敢講,我唔知道呢島上嘅教育會變成乜嘢樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢說,我不知道這島上的教育會變成什麼樣。」

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel shook her head, as much as to say if she were only at the head of the educational system of the Province things would be much better managed.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太搖咗搖頭,好像係講,如果佢嚟掌管全省嘅教育系統,管理一定會好得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太搖了搖頭,好像是說,如果她來掌管全省的教育系統,管理一定會好得多。

passages.original: Marilla took Mrs. Rachel’s advice and not another word was said to Anne about going back to school.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉接受咗雷切爾太太嘅建議,唔再對安妮提回學校嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉接受了雷切爾太太的建議,不再對安妮提回學校的事。

passages.original: She learned her lessons at home, did her chores, and played with Diana in the chilly purple autumn twilights; but when she met Gilbert Blythe on the road or encountered him in Sunday-school she passed him by with an icy contempt that was no whit thawed by his evident desire to appease her.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺家學功課,做家務,喺寒冷嘅紫色秋日暮色裡同黛安娜玩;但喺路上遇見吉爾伯特·布萊斯或喺主日學校碰上佢時,佢用冰冷嘅蔑視從佢身邊走過,佢明顯想平息佢嘅願望都冇讓佢有絲毫融化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在家學功課,做家務,在寒冷的紫色秋日暮色裡和黛安娜玩;但在路上遇見吉爾伯特·布萊斯或在主日學校碰上他時,她用冰冷的蔑視從他身邊走過,他明顯想平息她的願望也沒讓它有絲毫融化。

passages.original: Even Diana’s efforts as a peacemaker were of no avail.
passages.vernacular: 甚至黛安娜作為同事佬嘅努力都無濟於事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 甚至黛安娜作為和事佬的努力也無濟於事。

passages.original: Anne had evidently made up her mind to hate Gilbert Blythe to the end of life.
passages.vernacular: 安妮顯然已經打定主意要恨吉爾伯特·布萊斯到生命嘅盡頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮顯然已經打定主意要恨吉爾伯特·布萊斯到生命的盡頭。

passages.original: As much as she hated Gilbert, however, did she love Diana, with all the love of her passionate little heart, equally intense in its likes and dislikes.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢恨吉爾伯特有多深,就愛黛安娜有多深,用佢嗰顆熱情嘅小心靈嘅全部愛,愛同恨同樣強烈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,她恨吉爾伯特有多深,就愛黛安娜有多深,用她那顆熱情的小心靈的全部愛,愛與恨同樣強烈。

passages.original: One evening Marilla, coming in from the orchard with a basket of apples, found Anne sitting along by the east window in the twilight, crying bitterly.
passages.vernacular: 一天傍晚,瑪麗拉提住一籃蘋果從果園裡進嚟,發現安妮獨自坐喺東窗邊嘅暮色裡,哭得好傷心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天傍晚,瑪麗拉提著一籃蘋果從果園裡進來,發現安妮獨自坐在東窗邊的暮色裡,哭得很傷心。

passages.original: “Whatever’s the matter now, Anne?” she asked.
passages.vernacular: 「而家又點喇,安妮?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在又怎麼了,安妮?」她問。

passages.original: “It’s about Diana,” sobbed Anne luxuriously.
passages.vernacular: 「係為了黛安娜,」安妮盡情地抽泣住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是為了黛安娜,」安妮盡情地抽泣著說。

passages.original: “I love Diana so, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我咁愛黛安娜,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我那麼愛黛安娜,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I cannot ever live without her.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠無法冇佢而生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠無法沒有她而生活。

passages.original: But I know very well when we grow up that Diana will get married and go away and leave me.
passages.vernacular: 不過我好清楚,等我哋長大喇,黛安娜會結婚,離開我走掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我很清楚,等我們長大了,黛安娜會結婚,離開我走掉。

passages.original: And oh, what shall I do?
passages.vernacular: 哦,我該點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我該怎麼辦?

passages.original: I hate her husband--I just hate him furiously.
passages.vernacular: 我恨佢嘅丈夫——我就係狠狠地恨佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我恨她的丈夫——我就是狠狠地恨他。

passages.original: I’ve been imagining it all out--the wedding and everything--Diana dressed in snowy garments, with a veil, and looking as beautiful and regal as a queen; and me the bridesmaid, with a lovely dress too, and puffed sleeves, but with a breaking heart hid beneath my smiling face.
passages.vernacular: 我一直喺把呢一切想像出嚟——婚禮同所有嘅一切——黛安娜穿住雪白嘅衣裳,戴住面紗,睇上去美麗高貴得像女王;而我係伴娘,都穿住可愛嘅裙子,有泡泡袖,但微笑嘅臉龐下藏住一顆破碎嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直在把這一切想像出來——婚禮和所有的一切——黛安娜穿著雪白的衣裳,戴著面紗,看上去美麗高貴得像女王;而我是伴娘,也穿著可愛的裙子,有泡泡袖,但微笑的臉龐下藏著一顆破碎的心。

passages.original: And then bidding Diana goodbye-e-e--” Here Anne broke down entirely and wept with increasing bitterness.
passages.vernacular: 然後同黛安娜告別——別——別——」講到呢度,安妮完全崩潰喇,越嚟越痛苦地哭泣起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後同黛安娜告別——別——別——」說到這裡,安妮完全崩潰了,越來越痛苦地哭泣起來。

passages.original: Marilla turned quickly away to hide her twitching face; but it was no use; she collapsed on the nearest chair and burst into such a hearty and unusual peal of laughter that Matthew, crossing the yard outside, halted in amazement.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉急忙轉過身去,隱藏佢抽動嘅臉;但冇用;佢癱倒喺最近嘅椅子上,爆發出如此響亮、罕見嘅笑聲,以至於正穿過外面院子嘅馬修驚訝地停咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉急忙轉過身去,隱藏她抽動的臉;但沒用;她癱倒在最近的椅子上,爆發出如此響亮、罕見的笑聲,以至於正穿過外面院子的馬修驚訝地停了下來。

passages.original: When had he heard Marilla laugh like that before?
passages.vernacular: 佢以前乜嘢時候聽過瑪麗拉咁樣笑?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他以前什麼時候聽過瑪麗拉這樣笑?

passages.original: “Well, Anne Shirley,” said Marilla as soon as she could speak, “if you must borrow trouble, for pity’s sake borrow it handier home.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,安妮·雪莉,」瑪麗拉一能講話就講,「如果你一定要自找煩惱,睇喺老天嘅份上,找離家近啲嘅煩惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,安妮·雪莉,」瑪麗拉一能說話就說,「如果你一定要自找煩惱,看在老天的份上,找離家近一點的煩惱。

passages.original: I should think you had an imagination, sure enough.”
passages.vernacular: 我睇你嘅想像力係真嘅有喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看你的想像力是真的有了。」

chapters.title: Ch. XVI Diana Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results 第十六章:黛安娜受邀喝茶,結果悲慘

passages.original: CH OCTOBER was a beautiful month at Green Gables, when the birches in the hollow turned as golden as sunshine and the maples behind the orchard were royal crimson and the wild cherry-trees along the lane put on the loveliest shades of dark red and bronzy green, while the fields sunned themselves in aftermaths.
passages.vernacular: 十月喺綠色屋頂係個美麗嘅月份,窪地裡嘅白樺樹變得像陽光一樣金黃,果園後面嘅楓樹係皇家嘅深紅,小巷邊嘅野櫻桃樹換上咗最可愛嘅暗紅同古銅綠嘅色調,而田野喺二茬草裡曬住太陽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十月在綠色屋頂是個美麗的月份,窪地裡的白樺樹變得像陽光一樣金黃,果園後面的楓樹是皇家的深紅,小巷邊的野櫻桃樹換上了最可愛的暗紅與古銅綠的色調,而田野在二茬草裡曬著太陽。

passages.original: Anne reveled in the world of color about her.
passages.vernacular: 安妮陶醉喺佢周圍呢個色彩嘅世界裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮陶醉在她周圍這個色彩的世界裡。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla,” she exclaimed one Saturday morning, coming dancing in with her arms full of gorgeous boughs, “I’m so glad I live in a world where there are Octobers.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」一個星期六早晨,佢抱住滿懷絢爛嘅樹枝跳住舞走進嚟,喊道,「我太高興我住喺有十月嘅世界裡喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」一個星期六早晨,她抱著滿懷絢爛的樹枝跳著舞走進來,喊道,「我太高興我住在有十月的世界裡了。

passages.original: It would be terrible if we just skipped from September to November, wouldn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋直接從九月跳到十一月,嗰就太可怕喇,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們直接從九月跳到十一月,那就太可怕了,是不是?

passages.original: Look at these maple branches.
passages.vernacular: 睇睇呢啲楓樹枝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看看這些楓樹枝。

passages.original: Don’t they give you a thrill--several thrills?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔係讓您心頭顫動——顫動好多次嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們不是讓您心頭顫動——顫動好多次嗎?

passages.original: I’m going to decorate my room with them.”
passages.vernacular: 我要用佢哋裝飾我嘅房間。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要用它們裝飾我的房間。」

passages.original: “Messy things,” said Marilla, whose aesthetic sense was not noticeably developed.
passages.vernacular: 「亂糟糟嘅嘢,」瑪麗拉講,佢嘅審美感覺顯然不發達。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「亂糟糟的東西,」瑪麗拉說,她的審美感覺顯然不發達。

passages.original: “You clutter up your room entirely too much with out-of-doors stuff, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「你往房間裡堆戶外嘅嘢堆得太多喇,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你往房間裡堆戶外的東西堆得太多了,安妮。

passages.original: Bedrooms were made to sleep in.”
passages.vernacular: 臥室係用嚟瞓覺嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 臥室是用來睡覺的。」

passages.original: “Oh, and dream in too, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,都係用嚟做夢嘅,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,也是用來做夢的,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: And you know one can dream so much better in a room where there are pretty things.
passages.vernacular: 您知道喺有漂亮嘢嘅房間裡,人做夢好得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道在有漂亮東西的房間裡,人做夢好得多。

passages.original: I’m going to put these boughs in the old blue jug and set them on my table.”
passages.vernacular: 我要把呢啲枝子插進舊藍壺裡,擺喺我嘅桌子上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把這些枝子插進舊藍壺裡,擺在我的桌子上。」

passages.original: “Mind you don’t drop leaves all over the stairs then.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你小心別把葉子掉得滿樓梯都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你小心別把葉子掉得滿樓梯都是。

passages.original: I’m going on a meeting of the Aid Society at Carmody this afternoon, Anne, and I won’t likely be home before dark.
passages.vernacular: 今日下午我要去卡莫迪參加互助會嘅會議,安妮,我可能天黑前回不嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天下午我要去卡莫迪參加互助會的會議,安妮,我可能天黑前回不來。

passages.original: You’ll have to get Matthew and Jerry their supper, so mind you don’t forget to put the tea to draw until you sit down at the table as you did last time.”
passages.vernacular: 你得畀馬修同傑里準備晚飯,所以記住別忘咗喺坐到桌邊之前把茶泡上,像上次嗰樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你得給馬修和傑里準備晚飯,所以記著別忘了在坐到桌邊之前把茶泡上,像上次那樣。」

passages.original: “It was dreadful of me to forget,” said Anne apologetically, “but that was the afternoon I was trying to think of a name for Violet Vale and it crowded other things out.
passages.vernacular: 「我忘咗真係太糟糕喇,」安妮道歉講,「不過嗰個下午我正在畀紫羅蘭谷想名字,佢把別嘅事都擠掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我忘了真是太糟糕了,」安妮道歉說,「可是那個下午我正在給紫羅蘭谷想名字,它把別的事都擠掉了。

passages.original: Matthew was so good.
passages.vernacular: 馬修真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修真好。

passages.original: He never scolded a bit.
passages.vernacular: 佢啲都冇責備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一點也沒責備。

passages.original: He put the tea down himself and said we could wait awhile as well as not.
passages.vernacular: 佢自己把茶泡上,講我哋等一會兒都無妨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他自己把茶泡上,說我們等一會兒也無妨。

passages.original: And I told him a lovely fairy story while we were waiting, so he didn’t find the time long at all.
passages.vernacular: 我哋等嘅時候我畀佢講咗一個可愛嘅童話,所以佢根本不覺得時間長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們等的時候我給他講了一個可愛的童話,所以他根本不覺得時間長。

passages.original: It was a beautiful fairy story, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個美麗嘅童話,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個美麗的童話,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I forgot the end of it, so I made up an end for it myself and Matthew said he couldn’t tell where the join came in.”
passages.vernacular: 我忘了結尾,就自己編咗一個結尾,馬修講佢分不出接縫喺邊兒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忘了結尾,就自己編了一個結尾,馬修說他分不出接縫在哪兒。」

passages.original: “Matthew would think it all right, Anne, if you took a notion to get up and have dinner in the middle of the night.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,就係你突發奇想要喺半夜起嚟食午飯,馬修都會覺得冇問題嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,就是你突發奇想要在半夜起來吃午飯,馬修也會覺得沒問題的。

passages.original: But you keep your wits about you this time.
passages.vernacular: 不過呢次你可要保持頭腦清醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過這次你可要保持頭腦清醒。

passages.original: And--I don’t really know if I’m doing right--it may make you more addlepated than ever--but you can ask Diana to come over and spend the afternoon with you and have tea here.”
passages.vernacular: 仲有——我真唔知道我咁樣做對不對——呢可能讓你比以往更加糊塗——但你可以請黛安娜過嚟,陪你度過下午,喺呢兒飲茶。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有——我真不知道我這樣做對不對——這可能讓你比以往更加糊塗——但你可以請黛安娜過來,陪你度過下午,在這兒喝茶。」

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉!」

passages.original: Anne clasped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 安妮雙手合十。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮雙手合十。

passages.original: “How perfectly lovely!
passages.vernacular: 「太可愛喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太可愛了!

passages.original: You are able to imagine things after all or else you’d never have understood how I’ve longed for that very thing.
passages.vernacular: 您終究定係能想像事情嘅,否則您決唔會明白我幾咁渴望呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您終究還是能想像事情的,否則您決不會明白我多麼渴望這件事。

passages.original: It will seem so nice and grown-uppish.
passages.vernacular: 嗰會顯得咁好、咁像大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那會顯得那麼好、那麼像大人。

passages.original: No fear of my forgetting to put the tea to draw when I have company.
passages.vernacular: 有客人嚟我絕不怕忘咗泡茶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有客人來我絕不怕忘了泡茶。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, can I use the rosebud spray tea set?”
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,我可以用嗰套玫瑰花蕾圖案嘅茶具嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,我可以用那套玫瑰花蕾圖案的茶具嗎?」

passages.original: “No, indeed!
passages.vernacular: 「當然不行!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不行!

passages.original: The rosebud tea set!
passages.vernacular: 玫瑰花蕾茶具!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 玫瑰花蕾茶具!

passages.original: Well, what next?
passages.vernacular: 嗬,仲要乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗬,還要什麼?

passages.original: You know I never use that except for the minister or the Aids.
passages.vernacular: 你知道我除咗牧師或者互助會,從唔使嗰套。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道我除了牧師或者互助會,從不用那套。

passages.original: You’ll put down the old brown tea set.
passages.vernacular: 你把舊嘅棕色茶具攞出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把舊的棕色茶具拿出來。

passages.original: But you can open the little yellow crock of cherry preserves.
passages.vernacular: 不過你可以打開嗰一小罐黃色嘅櫻桃蜜餞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過你可以打開那一小罐黃色的櫻桃蜜餞。

passages.original: It’s time it was being used anyhow--I believe it’s beginning to work.
passages.vernacular: 反正都到該食嘅時候喇——我想佢開始發酵喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 反正也到該吃的時候了——我想它開始發酵了。

passages.original: And you can cut some fruit cake and have some of the cookies and snaps.”
passages.vernacular: 仲可以切啲水果蛋糕,再攞些餅乾同薑餅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還可以切一些水果蛋糕,再拿些餅乾和薑餅。」

passages.original: “I can just imagine myself sitting down at the head of the table and pouring out the tea,” said Anne, shutting her eyes ecstatically.
passages.vernacular: 「我完全能想像自己坐喺桌子上首倒茶嘅樣子,」安妮講,狂喜地閉上眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我完全能想像自己坐在桌子上首倒茶的樣子,」安妮說,狂喜地閉上眼睛。

passages.original: “And asking Diana if she takes sugar!
passages.vernacular: 「仲問黛安娜加不加糖!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還問黛安娜加不加糖!

passages.original: I know she doesn’t but of course I’ll ask her just as if I didn’t know.
passages.vernacular: 我知道佢不加,但當然我會像唔知道一樣問佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道她不加,但當然我會像不知道一樣問她。

passages.original: And then pressing her to take another piece of fruit cake and another helping of preserves.
passages.vernacular: 然後勸佢再食一塊水果蛋糕,再多添啲蜜餞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後勸她再吃一塊水果蛋糕,再多添一點蜜餞。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, it’s a wonderful sensation just to think of it.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,光係想一想就係一種奇妙嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,光是想一想就是一種奇妙的感覺。

passages.original: Can I take her into the spare room to lay off her hat when she comes?
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟嘅時候,我可以帶佢到備用客房放帽子嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她來的時候,我可以帶她到備用客房放帽子嗎?

passages.original: And then into the parlor to sit?”
passages.vernacular: 然後再去客廳坐?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後再去客廳坐?」

passages.original: “No. The sitting room will do for you and your company.
passages.vernacular: 「不行。起居室對你同你嘅客人就夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不行。起居室對你和你的客人就夠了。

passages.original: But there’s a bottle half full of raspberry cordial that was left over from the church social the other night.
passages.vernacular: 不過有半瓶覆盆子果露,係嗰天晚上教堂聯歡會剩下嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過有半瓶覆盆子果露,是那天晚上教堂聯歡會剩下的。

passages.original: It’s on the second shelf of the sitting-room closet and you and Diana can have it if you like, and a cooky to eat with it along in the afternoon, for I daresay Matthew ‘ll be late coming in to tea since he’s hauling potatoes to the vessel.”
passages.vernacular: 佢喺起居室櫥櫃嘅第二層架子上,你同黛安娜要係鍾意可以飲,下午再配一塊餅乾食,因為我想馬修會晚點回嚟飲茶,佢喺往船上運土豆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它在起居室櫥櫃的第二層架子上,你和黛安娜要是喜歡可以喝,下午再配一塊餅乾吃,因為我想馬修會晚點回來喝茶,他在往船上運土豆。」

passages.original: Anne flew down to the hollow, past the Dryad’s Bubble and up the spruce path to Orchard Slope, to ask Diana to tea.
passages.vernacular: 安妮飛奔到窪地,經過林中仙子泉,沿住杉樹小徑上到果園坡,去請黛安娜嚟飲茶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮飛奔到窪地,經過林中仙子泉,沿著杉樹小徑上到果園坡,去請黛安娜來喝茶。

passages.original: As a result just after Marilla had driven off to Carmody, Diana came over, dressed in her second-best dress and looking exactly as it is proper to look when asked out to tea.
passages.vernacular: 結果,瑪麗拉剛趕車去卡莫迪,黛安娜就嚟喇,穿住佢第二好嘅裙子,睇上去恰係被邀請飲茶時應有嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果,瑪麗拉剛趕車去卡莫迪,黛安娜就來了,穿著她第二好的裙子,看上去恰是被邀請喝茶時應有的樣子。

passages.original: At other times she was wont to run into the kitchen without knocking; but now she knocked primly at the front door.
passages.vernacular: 平時佢習慣不敲門就跑進廚房;但而家佢一本正經地敲咗前門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 平時她習慣不敲門就跑進廚房;但現在她一本正經地敲了前門。

passages.original: And when Anne, dressed in her second best, as primly opened it, both little girls shook hands as gravely as if they had never met before.
passages.vernacular: 而當同樣穿住第二好嘅衣服嘅安妮都一本正經地開咗門,兩個小女孩莊重地握咗握手,好像從冇見過面似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而當同樣穿著第二好的衣服的安妮也一本正經地開了門,兩個小女孩莊重地握了握手,好像從沒見過面似的。

passages.original: This unnatural solemnity lasted until after Diana had been taken to the east gable to lay off her hat and then had sat for ten minutes in the sitting room, toes in position.
passages.vernacular: 呢種不自然嘅嚴肅一直持續到黛安娜被帶到東山牆房間放帽子,然後喺起居室坐咗好鐘,腳尖擺得規規矩矩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種不自然的嚴肅一直持續到黛安娜被帶到東山牆房間放帽子,然後在起居室坐了十分鐘,腳尖擺得規規矩矩。

passages.original: “How is your mother?” inquired Anne politely, just as if she had not seen Mrs. Barry picking apples that morning in excellent health and spirits.
passages.vernacular: 「你母親好嗎?」安妮禮貌地問,好像佢今日早晨冇睇到巴里太太喺採蘋果,身體同精神都極好似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你母親好嗎?」安妮禮貌地問,好像她今天早晨沒看到巴里太太在採蘋果,身體和精神都極好似的。

passages.original: “She is very well, thank you.
passages.vernacular: 「佢好好,謝謝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她很好,謝謝。

passages.original: I suppose Mr. Cuthbert is hauling potatoes to the lily sands this afternoon, is he?” said Diana, who had ridden down to Mr. Harmon Andrews’s that morning in Matthew’s cart.
passages.vernacular: 我想卡思伯特先生今日下午喺往百合沙灘運土豆,係嗎?」黛安娜講,佢今日早晨坐馬修嘅馬車到咗哈蒙·安德魯斯先生家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想卡思伯特先生今天下午在往百合沙灘運土豆,是嗎?」黛安娜說,她今天早晨坐馬修的馬車到了哈蒙·安德魯斯先生家。

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: Our potato crop is very good this year.
passages.vernacular: 今年我哋嘅土豆收成好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今年我們的土豆收成很好。

passages.original: I hope your father’s crop is good too.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望你父親嘅收成都好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你父親的收成也好。」

passages.original: “It is fairly good, thank you.
passages.vernacular: 「仲算好,謝謝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還算好,謝謝。

passages.original: Have you picked many of your apples yet?”
passages.vernacular: 你哋嘅蘋果摘咗好多咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們的蘋果摘了很多了嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, ever so many,” said Anne forgetting to be dignified and jumping up quickly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,好多好多喇,」安妮講,忘咗保持端莊,急忙跳起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,很多很多了,」安妮說,忘了保持端莊,急忙跳起來。

passages.original: “Let’s go out to the orchard and get some of the Red Sweetings, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋到果園去摘啲紅甜蘋果吧,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們到果園去摘一些紅甜蘋果吧,黛安娜。

passages.original: Marilla says we can have all that are left on the tree.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉講樹上剩下嘅都可以畀我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉說樹上剩下的都可以給我們。

passages.original: Marilla is a very generous woman.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉係個好慷慨嘅女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉是個很慷慨的女人。

passages.original: She said we could have fruit cake and cherry preserves for tea.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我哋飲茶時可以有水果蛋糕同櫻桃蜜餞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我們喝茶時可以有水果蛋糕和櫻桃蜜餞。

passages.original: But it isn’t good manners to tell your company what you are going to give them to eat, so I won’t tell you what she said we could have to drink.
passages.vernacular: 但係告訴客人你要畀佢哋食乜嘢不禮貌,所以我不告訴你佢講我哋可以飲乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是告訴客人你要給她們吃什麼不禮貌,所以我不告訴你她說我們可以喝什麼。

passages.original: Only it begins with an R and a C and it’s bright red color.
passages.vernacular: 只係佢以R同C開頭,而且係鮮紅色嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是它以R和C開頭,而且是鮮紅色的。

passages.original: I love bright red drinks, don’t you?
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意鮮紅色嘅飲料,你呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡鮮紅色的飲料,你呢?

passages.original: They taste twice as good as any other color.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋比任何其他顏色嘅味道好一倍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們比任何其他顏色的味道好一倍。」

passages.original: The orchard, with its great sweeping boughs that bent to the ground with fruit, proved so delightful that the little girls spent most of the afternoon in it, sitting in a grassy corner where the frost had spared the green and the mellow autumn sunshine lingered warmly, eating apples and talking as hard as they could.
passages.vernacular: 果園裡,大樹枝向下彎垂住結滿咗果子,實在迷人,兩個小女孩下午大部分時間都待喺裡面,坐喺霜冇傷到綠色嘅草角落裡,溫暖嘅秋日陽光喺嗰兒流連,佢哋食住蘋果,盡力地講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 果園裡,大樹枝向下彎垂著結滿了果子,實在迷人,兩個小女孩下午大部分時間都待在裡面,坐在霜沒有傷到綠色的草角落裡,溫暖的秋日陽光在那兒流連,她們吃著蘋果,盡力地說話。

passages.original: Diana had much to tell Anne of what went on in school.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜有好多學校嘅事要告訴安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜有很多學校的事要告訴安妮。

passages.original: She had to sit with Gertie Pye and she hated it; Gertie squeaked her pencil all the time and it just made her--Diana’s--blood run cold; Ruby Gillis had charmed all her warts away, true’s you live, with a magic pebble that old Mary Joe from the Creek gave her.
passages.vernacular: 佢得同格蒂·派伊坐,佢討厭咁樣;格蒂不停地把鉛筆弄得吱吱響,呢讓佢——黛安娜——血都涼喇;露比·吉利斯用溪邊嘅老瑪麗·喬畀佢嘅一顆魔法小石子,把佢所有嘅疣都變冇喇,千真萬確。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她得和格蒂·派伊坐,她討厭這樣;格蒂不停地把鉛筆弄得吱吱響,這讓她——黛安娜——血都涼了;露比·吉利斯用溪邊的老瑪麗·喬給她的一顆魔法小石子,把她所有的疣都變沒了,千真萬確。

passages.original: You had to rub the warts with the pebble and then throw it away over your left shoulder at the time of the new moon and the warts would all go.
passages.vernacular: 你得用小石子擦疣,然後喺新月嘅時候,把佢從你嘅左肩頭上扔掉,疣就全冇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你得用小石子擦疣,然後在新月的時候,把它從你的左肩頭上扔掉,疣就全沒了。

passages.original: Charlie Sloane’s name was written up with Em White’s on the porch wall and Em White was awful mad about it; Sam Boulter had “sassed” Mr. Phillips in class and Mr. Phillips whipped him and Sam’s father came down to the school and dared Mr. Phillips to lay a hand on one of his children again; and Mattie Andrews had a new red hood and a blue crossover with tassels on it and the airs she put on about it were perfectly sickening; and Lizzie Wright didn’t speak to Mamie Wilson because Mamie Wilson’s grown-up sister had cut out Lizzie Wright’s grown-up sister with her beau; and everybody missed Anne so and wished she’s come to school again; and Gilbert Blythe--
passages.vernacular: 查理·斯隆嘅名字同艾姆·懷特嘅名字一起寫喺門廊牆上,艾姆·懷特為此氣瘋喇;山姆·博爾特喺課堂上「頂撞」咗菲利普斯先生,菲利普斯先生鞭打咗佢,山姆嘅父親嚟到學校,向菲利普斯先生挑戰,睇佢敢唔敢再碰佢嘅任何一個細路一下;瑪蒂·安德魯斯有一頂新嘅紅兜帽同一件帶流蘇嘅藍色交叉披肩,佢為此擺嘅架子簡直讓人噁心;莉齊·賴特不跟梅米·威爾遜講話,因為梅米·威爾遜嘅姐姐把莉齊·賴特嘅姐姐嘅情郎搶走喇;大家都咁想念安妮,希望佢再嚟上學;仲有吉爾伯特·布萊斯——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 查理·斯隆的名字和艾姆·懷特的名字一起寫在門廊牆上,艾姆·懷特為此氣瘋了;山姆·博爾特在課堂上「頂撞」了菲利普斯先生,菲利普斯先生鞭打了他,山姆的父親來到學校,向菲利普斯先生挑戰,看他敢不敢再碰他的任何一個孩子一下;瑪蒂·安德魯斯有一頂新的紅兜帽和一件帶流蘇的藍色交叉披肩,她為此擺的架子簡直讓人噁心;莉齊·賴特不跟梅米·威爾遜說話,因為梅米·威爾遜的姐姐把莉齊·賴特的姐姐的情郎搶走了;大家都那麼想念安妮,希望她再來上學;還有吉爾伯特·布萊斯——

passages.original: But Anne didn’t want to hear about Gilbert Blythe.
passages.vernacular: 但安妮唔想聽關於吉爾伯特·布萊斯嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安妮不想聽關於吉爾伯特·布萊斯的事。

passages.original: She jumped up hurriedly and said suppose they go in and have some raspberry cordial.
passages.vernacular: 佢急忙跳起嚟,講不如進去飲些覆盆子果露吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她急忙跳起來,說不如進去喝些覆盆子果露吧。

passages.original: Anne looked on the second shelf of the room pantry but there was no bottle of raspberry cordial there.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺起居室食品櫃嘅第二層架子上找咗找,可嗰兒冇覆盆子果露瓶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在起居室食品櫃的第二層架子上找了找,可那兒沒有覆盆子果露瓶。

passages.original: Search revealed it away back on the top shelf.
passages.vernacular: 找咗一通,發現佢喺最裡面嘅頂層架子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 找了一通,發現它在最裡面的頂層架子上。

passages.original: Anne put it on a tray and set it on the table with a tumbler.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把佢放喺托盤上,連同一個玻璃杯擺到桌上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把它放在托盤上,連同一個玻璃杯擺到桌上。

passages.original: “Now, please help yourself, Diana,” she said politely.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,請隨便飲,黛安娜,」佢禮貌地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,請隨便喝,黛安娜,」她禮貌地說。

passages.original: “I don’t believe I’ll have any just now.
passages.vernacular: 「我而家唔想飲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在不想喝。

passages.original: I don’t feel as if I wanted any after all those apples.”
passages.vernacular: 食咗咁多蘋果,我覺得啲都唔想飲喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吃了那麼多蘋果,我覺得一點也不想喝了。」

passages.original: Diana poured herself out a tumblerful, looked at its bright-red hue admiringly, and then sipped it daintily.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜畀自己倒咗滿滿一杯,欣賞地睇住佢鮮紅嘅色澤,然後優雅地啜咗一口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜給自己倒了滿滿一杯,欣賞地看著它鮮紅的色澤,然後優雅地啜了一口。

passages.original: “That’s awfully nice raspberry cordial, Anne,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「呢覆盆子果露真好飲,安妮,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這覆盆子果露真好喝,安妮,」她說。

passages.original: “I didn’t know raspberry cordial was so nice.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道覆盆子果露咁好飲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道覆盆子果露這麼好喝。」

passages.original: “I’m real glad you like it.
passages.vernacular: 「你鍾意我真高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你喜歡我真高興。

passages.original: Take as much as you want.
passages.vernacular: 想飲多少飲多少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想喝多少喝多少。

passages.original: I’m going to run out and stir the fire up.
passages.vernacular: 我要跑出去把火捅旺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要跑出去把火捅旺。

passages.original: There are so many responsibilities on a person’s mind when they’re keeping house, isn’t there?”
passages.vernacular: 一個人管家嘅時候,心裡有咁多責任,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個人管家的時候,心裡有這麼多責任,是不是?」

passages.original: When Anne came back from the kitchen Diana was drinking her second glassful of cordial; and, being entreated thereto by Anne, she offered no particular objection to the drinking of a third.
passages.vernacular: 安妮從廚房回嚟時,黛安娜正在飲佢嘅第二杯果露;喺安妮嘅勸講下,佢對於飲第三杯都冇特別嘅反對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮從廚房回來時,黛安娜正在喝她的第二杯果露;在安妮的勸說下,她對於喝第三杯也沒有特別的反對。
