passages.original: The tumblerfuls were generous ones and the raspberry cordial was certainly very nice.
passages.vernacular: 杯子都係大杯,而覆盆子果露確實好好飲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 杯子都是大杯,而覆盆子果露確實很好喝。

passages.original: “The nicest I ever drank,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我飲過嘅最好飲嘅,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我喝過的最好喝的,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “It’s ever so much nicer than Mrs. Lynde’s, although she brags of hers so much.
passages.vernacular: 「比林德太太做嘅好飲多喇,雖然佢咁吹噓佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「比林德太太做的好喝多了,雖然她那麼吹噓她的。

passages.original: It doesn’t taste a bit like hers.”
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅味道同佢嘅啲都不像。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的味道和她的一點也不像。」

passages.original: “I should think Marilla’s raspberry cordial would prob’ly be much nicer than Mrs. Lynde’s,” said Anne loyally.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得瑪麗拉嘅覆盆子果露大概比林德太太嘅好飲得多,」安妮忠誠地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得瑪麗拉的覆盆子果露大概比林德太太的好喝得多,」安妮忠誠地說。

passages.original: “Marilla is a famous cook.
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉係個有名嘅廚師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉是個有名的廚師。

passages.original: She is trying to teach me to cook but I assure you, Diana, it is uphill work.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺努力教我做飯,但我向您保證,黛安娜,呢個係食力不討好嘅活兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在努力教我做飯,但我向您保證,黛安娜,這是吃力不討好的活兒。

passages.original: There’s so little scope for imagination in cookery.
passages.vernacular: 烹飪裡想像嘅餘地太少喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 烹飪裡想像的餘地太少了。

passages.original: You just have to go by rules.
passages.vernacular: 你只能按規則做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只能按規則做。

passages.original: The last time I made a cake I forgot to put the flour in.
passages.vernacular: 我上次做蛋糕時忘咗放麵粉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我上次做蛋糕時忘了放麵粉。

passages.original: I was thinking the loveliest story about you and me, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 我當時正在想一個關於你同我嘅最可愛嘅故事,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我當時正在想一個關於你和我的最可愛的故事,黛安娜。

passages.original: I thought you were desperately ill with smallpox and everybody deserted you, but I went boldly to your bedside and nursed you back to life; and then I took the smallpox and died and I was buried under those poplar trees in the graveyard and you planted a rosebush by my grave and watered it with your tears; and you never, never forgot the friend of your youth who sacrificed her life for you.
passages.vernacular: 我想你得咗天花,病得好重,每個人都拋棄咗你,不過我勇敢地走到你嘅床邊,把你護理得起死回生;然後我得咗天花死喇,被埋喺墓地嗰啲白楊樹下,你喺我墳上種咗一棵玫瑰樹,用你嘅眼淚澆灌佢;你永遠永遠唔會忘記為你犧牲生命嘅少年朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你得了天花,病得很重,每個人都拋棄了你,可是我勇敢地走到你的床邊,把你護理得起死回生;然後我得了天花死了,被埋在墓地那些白楊樹下,你在我墳上種了一棵玫瑰樹,用你的眼淚澆灌它;你永遠永遠不會忘記為你犧牲生命的少年朋友。

passages.original: Oh, it was such a pathetic tale, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 哦,嗰個係個幾咁悲慘嘅故事,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,那是個多麼悲慘的故事,黛安娜。

passages.original: The tears just rained down over my cheeks while I mixed the cake.
passages.vernacular: 我同蛋糕麵糊嘅時候,眼淚簡直像雨一樣淌下臉頰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我和蛋糕麵糊的時候,眼淚簡直像雨一樣淌下臉頰。

passages.original: But I forgot the flour and the cake was a dismal failure.
passages.vernacular: 但我忘咗放麵粉,蛋糕徹底失敗喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我忘了放麵粉,蛋糕徹底失敗了。

passages.original: Flour is so essential to cakes, you know.
passages.vernacular: 麵粉對蛋糕太重要喇,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麵粉對蛋糕太重要了,你知道。

passages.original: Marilla was very cross and I don’t wonder.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉好生氣,我都不奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉很生氣,我也不奇怪。

passages.original: I’m a great trial to her.
passages.vernacular: 我對佢係個大麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對她是個大麻煩。

passages.original: She was terribly mortified about the pudding sauce last week.
passages.vernacular: 上個星期布丁醬嘅事,佢特別丟臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上個星期布丁醬的事,她特別丟臉。

passages.original: We had a plum pudding for dinner on Tuesday and there was half the pudding and a pitcherful of sauce left over.
passages.vernacular: 星期二我哋午飯食咗李子布丁,剩下半個布丁同一壺醬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期二我們午飯吃了李子布丁,剩下半個布丁和一壺醬。

passages.original: Marilla said there was enough for another dinner and told me to set it on the pantry shelf and cover it.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉講剩下嘅夠再食一頓午飯,叫我把佢放喺食品櫃架子上蓋好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉說剩下的夠再吃一頓午飯,叫我把它放在食品櫃架子上蓋好。

passages.original: I meant to cover it just as much as could be, Diana, but when I carried it in I was imagining I was a nun--of course I’m a Protestant but I imagined I was a Catholic--taking the veil to bury a broken heart in cloistered seclusion; and I forgot all about covering the pudding sauce.
passages.vernacular: 我係盡可能想蓋好嘅,黛安娜,不過我端進去嘅時候,我喺想像自己係一個修女——當然我係新教徒,但我想像我係天主教徒——戴上面紗,要把一顆破碎嘅心埋葬喺修道院嘅隱居生活裡;我就把蓋布丁醬嘅事全忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是盡可能想蓋好的,黛安娜,可是我端進去的時候,我在想像自己是一個修女——當然我是新教徒,但我想像我是天主教徒——戴上面紗,要把一顆破碎的心埋葬在修道院的隱居生活裡;我就把蓋布丁醬的事全忘了。

passages.original: I thought of it next morning and ran to the pantry.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨我想起嚟,跑到食品櫃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨我想起來,跑到食品櫃。

passages.original: Diana, fancy if you can my extreme horror at finding a mouse drowned in that pudding sauce!
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜,你想像一下吧,如果你能,我發現嗰布丁醬裡淹死咗一隻老鼠時有幾咁極度嘅恐懼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜,你想像一下吧,如果你能,我發現那布丁醬裡淹死了一隻老鼠時有多麼極度的恐懼!

passages.original: I lifted the mouse out with a spoon and threw it out in the yard and then I washed the spoon in three waters.
passages.vernacular: 我用勺子把老鼠舀出嚟,扔到院子裡,然後把勺子洗咗三遍水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我用勺子把老鼠舀出來,扔到院子裡,然後把勺子洗了三遍水。

passages.original: Marilla was out milking and I fully intended to ask her when she came in if I’d give the sauce to the pigs; but when she did come in I was imagining that I was a frost fairy going through the woods turning the trees red and yellow, whichever they wanted to be, so I never thought about the pudding sauce again and Marilla sent me out to pick apples.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉出去擠奶喇,我完全打算等佢回嚟問佢要唔好把醬畀豬食;可佢回嚟嘅時候,我喺想像我係一個霜凍仙子,穿過樹林,把樹染紅染黃,隨佢哋想變成邊種顏色,所以我就再都冇想起布丁醬,瑪麗拉打發我出去摘蘋果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉出去擠奶了,我完全打算等她回來問她要不要把醬給豬吃;可她回來的時候,我在想像我是一個霜凍仙子,穿過樹林,把樹染紅染黃,隨它們想變成哪種顏色,所以我就再也沒想起布丁醬,瑪麗拉打發我出去摘蘋果。

passages.original: Well, Mr. and Mrs. Chester Ross from Spencervale came here that morning.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,嗰天早晨斯潘塞韋爾嘅切斯特·羅斯夫婦嚟到我哋家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,那天早晨斯潘塞韋爾的切斯特·羅斯夫婦來到我們家。

passages.original: You know they are very stylish people, especially Mrs. Chester Ross.
passages.vernacular: 你知道佢哋係好時髦嘅人,尤其係切斯特·羅斯太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道他們是很時髦的人,尤其是切斯特·羅斯太太。

passages.original: When Marilla called me in dinner was all ready and everybody was at the table.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉叫我進去嘅時候,午飯已經準備好喇,每個人都坐喺桌邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉叫我進去的時候,午飯已經準備好了,每個人都坐在桌邊。

passages.original: I tried to be as polite and dignified as I could be, for I wanted Mrs. Chester Ross to think I was a ladylike little girl even if I wasn’t pretty.
passages.vernacular: 我盡可能表現得有禮貌、端莊,因為我想讓切斯特·羅斯太太覺得我係個淑女般嘅小女孩,即使我不漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我盡可能表現得有禮貌、端莊,因為我想讓切斯特·羅斯太太覺得我是個淑女般的小女孩,即使我不漂亮。

passages.original: Everything went right until I saw Marilla coming with the plum pudding in one hand and the pitcher of pudding sauce warmed up, in the other.
passages.vernacular: 一切都好順利,直到我睇見瑪麗拉一手端住李子布丁,另一手端住熱過嘅一壺布丁醬走嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切都很順利,直到我看見瑪麗拉一手端著李子布丁,另一手端著熱過的一壺布丁醬走來。

passages.original: Diana, that was a terrible moment.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜,嗰個係個可怕嘅時刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜,那是個可怕的時刻。

passages.original: I remembered everything and I just stood up in my place and shrieked out ‘Marilla, you mustn’t use that pudding sauce.
passages.vernacular: 我想起咗一切,我就站喺自己嘅位子上尖叫起嚟:『瑪麗拉,您唔能夠用嗰個布丁醬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想起了一切,我就站在自己的位子上尖叫起來:『瑪麗拉,您不能用那個布丁醬。

passages.original: There was a mouse drowned in it.
passages.vernacular: 裡面淹死咗一隻老鼠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 裡面淹死了一隻老鼠。

passages.original: I forgot to tell you before.’
passages.vernacular: 我忘咗早點告訴您。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忘了早點告訴您。』

passages.original: Oh, Diana, I shall never forget that awful moment if I live to be a hundred.
passages.vernacular: 哦,黛安娜,即使我活到一百歲,都永遠忘不咗嗰個可怕嘅時刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,黛安娜,即使我活到一百歲,也永遠忘不了那個可怕的時刻。

passages.original: Mrs. Chester Ross just looked at me and I thought I would sink through the floor with mortification.
passages.vernacular: 切斯特·羅斯太太只係睇住我,我覺得我羞愧得要鑽到地板下面去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 切斯特·羅斯太太只是看著我,我覺得我羞愧得要鑽到地板下面去。

passages.original: She is such a perfect housekeeper and fancy what she must have thought of us.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個咁完美嘅主婦,你想想佢會點睇我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個那麼完美的主婦,你想想她會怎麼看我們。

passages.original: Marilla turned red as fire but she never said a word--then.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉臉紅得像火,但佢一個字都冇講——當時冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉臉紅得像火,但她一個字也沒說——當時沒說。

passages.original: She just carried that sauce and pudding out and brought in some strawberry preserves.
passages.vernacular: 佢只係把嗰醬同布丁端咗出去,攞嚟啲草莓蜜餞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她只是把那醬和布丁端了出去,拿來一些草莓蜜餞。

passages.original: She even offered me some, but I couldn’t swallow a mouthful.
passages.vernacular: 佢甚至還畀我食,但我一口都咽不下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她甚至還給我吃,但我一口也咽不下去。

passages.original: It was like heaping coals of fire on my head.
passages.vernacular: 嗰就像喺我頭上堆燃燒嘅炭火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就像在我頭上堆燃燒的炭火。

passages.original: After Mrs. Chester Ross went away, Marilla gave me a dreadful scolding.
passages.vernacular: 切斯特·羅斯太太走後,瑪麗拉狠狠地訓咗我一頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 切斯特·羅斯太太走後,瑪麗拉狠狠地訓了我一頓。

passages.original: Why, Diana, what is the matter?”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,黛安娜,點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,黛安娜,怎麼了?」

passages.original: Diana had stood up very unsteadily; then she sat down again, putting her hands to her head.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜好不穩地站咗起嚟;然後又坐咗下去,雙手捧住頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜非常不穩地站了起來;然後又坐了下去,雙手捧著頭。

passages.original: “I’m--I’m awful sick,” she said, a little thickly.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我難受極喇,」佢講,舌頭有點發僵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我難受極了,」她說,舌頭有點發僵。

passages.original: “I--I--must go right home.”
passages.vernacular: 「我——我——必須即刻回家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我——必須馬上回家。」

passages.original: “Oh, you mustn’t dream of going home without your tea,” cried Anne in distress.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你可唔能夠想飲完茶才回家,」安妮苦惱地叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你可不能想喝完茶才回家,」安妮苦惱地叫道。

passages.original: “I’ll get it right off--I’ll go and put the tea down this very minute.”
passages.vernacular: 「我即刻就去——我呢就去泡茶。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我馬上就去——我這就去泡茶。」

passages.original: “I must go home,” repeated Diana, stupidly but determinedly.
passages.vernacular: 「我必須回家,」黛安娜呆呆地、但堅決地重複。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須回家,」黛安娜呆呆地、但堅決地重複。

passages.original: “Let me get you a lunch anyhow,” implored Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「無論如何讓我畀你攞點點心,」安妮懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「無論如何讓我給你拿點點心,」安妮懇求道。

passages.original: “Let me give you a bit of fruit cake and some of the cherry preserves.
passages.vernacular: 「讓我畀你啲水果蛋糕同啲櫻桃蜜餞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我給你一點水果蛋糕和一些櫻桃蜜餞。

passages.original: Lie down on the sofa for a little while and you’ll be better.
passages.vernacular: 喺沙發上躺一會兒,你就會好些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在沙發上躺一會兒,你就會好些。

passages.original: Where do you feel bad?”
passages.vernacular: 你邊度不舒服?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你哪裡不舒服?」

passages.original: “I must go home,” said Diana, and that was all she would say.
passages.vernacular: 「我必須回家,」黛安娜講,佢就只講咗呢句。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須回家,」黛安娜說,她就只說了這句。

passages.original: In vain Anne pleaded.
passages.vernacular: 安妮徒勞地懇求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮徒勞地懇求。

passages.original: “I never heard of company going home without tea,” she mourned.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇聽講客人不飲茶就回家嘅,」佢悲傷地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒聽說客人不喝茶就回家的,」她悲傷地說。

passages.original: “Oh, Diana, do you suppose that it’s possible you’re really taking the smallpox?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,黛安娜,你覺得有冇可能你真嘅得咗天花?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,黛安娜,你覺得有沒有可能你真的得了天花?

passages.original: If you are I’ll go and nurse you, you can depend on that.
passages.vernacular: 如果係,我會去護理你嘅,你可以放心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是,我會去護理你的,你可以放心。

passages.original: I’ll never forsake you.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠唔會拋棄你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠不會拋棄你。

passages.original: But I do wish you’d stay till after tea.
passages.vernacular: 但我真希望你飲完茶再走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我真希望你喝完茶再走。

passages.original: Where do you feel bad?”
passages.vernacular: 你邊度不舒服?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你哪裡不舒服?」

passages.original: “I’m awful dizzy,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我頭暈得厲害,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我頭暈得厲害,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: And indeed, she walked very dizzily.
passages.vernacular: 佢走起路嚟確實暈暈乎乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她走起路來確實暈暈乎乎。

passages.original: Anne, with tears of disappointment in her eyes, got Diana’s hat and went with her as far as the Barry yard fence.
passages.vernacular: 安妮含住失望嘅淚水,攞嚟黛安娜嘅帽子,陪佢一直走到巴里家院子嘅柵欄邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮含著失望的淚水,拿來黛安娜的帽子,陪她一直走到巴里家院子的柵欄邊。

passages.original: Then she wept all the way back to Green Gables, where she sorrowfully put the remainder of the raspberry cordial back into the pantry and got tea ready for Matthew and Jerry, with all the zest gone out of the performance.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哭住一路走回綠色屋頂,傷心地把剩下嘅覆盆子果露放回食品櫃,畀馬修同傑里準備茶點,整個過程嘅所有興致都消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她哭著一路走回綠色屋頂,傷心地把剩下的覆盆子果露放回食品櫃,給馬修和傑里準備茶點,整個過程的所有興致都消失了。

passages.original: The next day was Sunday and as the rain poured down in torrents from dawn till dusk Anne did not stir abroad from Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 第二天係星期天,從黎明到黃昏大雨傾盆,安妮冇離開綠色屋頂出門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天是星期天,從黎明到黃昏大雨傾盆,安妮沒有離開綠色屋頂出門。

passages.original: Monday afternoon Marilla sent her down to Mrs. Lynde’s on an errand.
passages.vernacular: 星期一下午,瑪麗拉派佢去林德太太家辦件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期一下午,瑪麗拉派她去林德太太家辦件事。

passages.original: In a very short space of time Anne came flying back up the lane with tears rolling down her cheeks.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒,安妮沿住小巷飛奔回嚟,淚水順住臉頰滾落。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒,安妮沿著小巷飛奔回來,淚水順著臉頰滾落。

passages.original: Into the kitchen she dashed and flung herself face downward on the sofa in an agony.
passages.vernacular: 佢衝進廚房,痛苦地撲倒喺沙發上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她衝進廚房,痛苦地撲倒在沙發上。

passages.original: “Whatever has gone wrong now, Anne?” queried Marilla in doubt and dismay.
passages.vernacular: 「而家又出咗乜嘢事,安妮?」瑪麗拉疑惑又驚慌地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在又出了什麼事,安妮?」瑪麗拉疑惑又驚慌地問。

passages.original: “I do hope you haven’t gone and been saucy to Mrs. Lynde again.”
passages.vernacular: 「我真希望你冇又去對林德太太無禮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真希望你沒有又去對林德太太無禮。」

passages.original: No answer from Anne save more tears and stormier sobs!
passages.vernacular: 安妮冇回答,只有更多嘅淚水同更猛烈嘅啜泣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮沒有回答,只有更多的淚水和更猛烈的啜泣!

passages.original: “Anne Shirley, when I ask you a question I want to be answered.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,我問你問題,我要你回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,我問你問題,我要你回答。

passages.original: Sit right up this very minute and tell me what you are crying about.”
passages.vernacular: 即刻坐起嚟,告訴我你喺哭乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上坐起來,告訴我你在哭什麼。」

passages.original: Anne sat up, tragedy personified.
passages.vernacular: 安妮坐起嚟,係悲劇嘅化身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮坐起來,是悲劇的化身。

passages.original: “Mrs. Lynde was up to see Mrs. Barry today and Mrs. Barry was in an awful state,” she wailed.
passages.vernacular: 「林德太太今日去睇巴里太太,巴里太太處於可怕嘅狀態,」佢哀號住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「林德太太今天去看巴里太太,巴里太太處於可怕的狀態,」她哀號著說。

passages.original: “She says that I set Diana drunk Saturday and sent her home in a disgraceful condition.
passages.vernacular: 「佢講我星期六把黛安娜灌醉喇,讓佢以一副丟人嘅樣子回咗家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她說我星期六把黛安娜灌醉了,讓她以一副丟人的樣子回了家。

passages.original: And she says I must be a thoroughly bad, wicked little girl and she’s never, never going to let Diana play with me again.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我一定係個徹頭徹尾嘅壞蛋、惡毒嘅小女孩,佢永遠永遠唔會再讓黛安娜跟我玩喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我一定是個徹頭徹尾的壞蛋、惡毒的小女孩,她永遠永遠不會再讓黛安娜跟我玩了。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, I’m just overcome with woe.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,我真係被悲痛壓垮喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,我真是被悲痛壓垮了。」

passages.original: Marilla stared in blank amazement.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉茫然地驚訝地瞪住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉茫然地驚訝地瞪著她。

passages.original: “Set Diana drunk!” she said when she found her voice.
passages.vernacular: 「把黛安娜灌醉喇!」佢找回聲音後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把黛安娜灌醉了!」她找回聲音後說。

passages.original: “Anne are you or Mrs. Barry crazy?
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,係你瘋咗定係巴里太太瘋喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,是你瘋了還是巴里太太瘋了?

passages.original: What on earth did you give her?”
passages.vernacular: 你到底畀佢食咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你到底給她吃了什麼?」

passages.original: “Not a thing but raspberry cordial,” sobbed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「只有覆盆子果露,」安妮抽泣住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只有覆盆子果露,」安妮抽泣著說。

passages.original: “I never thought raspberry cordial would set people drunk, Marilla--not even if they drank three big tumblerfuls as Diana did.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇想過覆盆子果露會讓人飲醉,瑪麗拉——即使像黛安娜嗰樣飲咗三大杯都唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒想過覆盆子果露會讓人喝醉,瑪麗拉——即使像黛安娜那樣喝了三大杯也不會。

passages.original: Oh, it sounds so--so--like Mrs. Thomas’s husband!
passages.vernacular: 哦,呢聽起嚟咁——咁——像托馬斯太太嘅丈夫!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,這聽起來那麼——那麼——像托馬斯太太的丈夫!

passages.original: But I didn’t mean to set her drunk.”
passages.vernacular: 但我唔係想灌醉佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不是想灌醉她。」

passages.original: “Drunk fiddlesticks!” said Marilla, marching to the sitting-room pantry.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢醉不醉嘅!」瑪麗拉講,大步走向起居室嘅食品櫃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼醉不醉的!」瑪麗拉說,大步走向起居室的食品櫃。

passages.original: There on the shelf was a bottle which she at once recognized as one containing some of her three-year-old homemade currant wine for which she was celebrated in Avonlea, although certain of the stricter sort, Mrs. Barry among them, disapproved strongly of it.
passages.vernacular: 架子上有一瓶酒,佢即刻認出嗰個係佢自製嘅三年陳醋栗酒,佢喺阿文利因此出名,儘管某些更嚴格嘅人,其中包括巴里太太,強烈反對佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 架子上有一瓶酒,她立刻認出那是她自製的三年陳醋栗酒,她在阿文利因此出名,儘管某些更嚴格的人,其中包括巴里太太,強烈反對它。

passages.original: And at the same time Marilla recollected that she had put the bottle of raspberry cordial down in the cellar instead of in the pantry as she had told Anne.
passages.vernacular: 同時,瑪麗拉想起佢把覆盆子果露瓶放喺咗地窖裡,而唔係像佢告訴安妮嘅嗰樣放喺食品櫃裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時,瑪麗拉想起她把覆盆子果露瓶放在了地窖裡,而不是像她告訴安妮的那樣放在食品櫃裡。

passages.original: She went back to the kitchen with the wine bottle in her hand.
passages.vernacular: 佢手裡攞住酒瓶回到廚房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她手裡拿著酒瓶回到廚房。

passages.original: Her face was twitching in spite of herself.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉不由自主地抽動住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉不由自主地抽動著。

passages.original: “Anne, you certainly have a genius for getting into trouble.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,你確實有惹麻煩嘅天才。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,你確實有惹麻煩的天才。

passages.original: You went and gave Diana currant wine instead of raspberry cordial.
passages.vernacular: 你畀黛安娜飲嘅係醋栗酒,而唔係覆盆子果露。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你給黛安娜喝的是醋栗酒,而不是覆盆子果露。

passages.original: Didn’t you know the difference yourself?”
passages.vernacular: 你自己難道分不出區別嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你自己難道分不出區別嗎?」

passages.original: “I never tasted it,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇嘗過佢,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒嘗過它,」安妮說。

passages.original: “I thought it was the cordial.
passages.vernacular: 「我以為嗰個係果露。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以為那是果露。

passages.original: I meant to be so--so--hospitable.
passages.vernacular: 我想咁——咁——好客。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想那麼——那麼——好客。

passages.original: Diana got awfully sick and had to go home.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜難受極喇,唔得不回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜難受極了,不得不回家。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry told Mrs. Lynde she was simply dead drunk.
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太對林德太太講,佢簡直係爛醉如泥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太對林德太太說,她簡直是爛醉如泥。

passages.original: She just laughed silly-like when her mother asked her what was the matter and went to sleep and slept for hours.
passages.vernacular: 佢母親問佢點喇,佢只係傻笑,然後去瞓覺,瞓咗好幾個鐘頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她母親問她怎麼了,她只是傻笑,然後去睡覺,睡了好幾個鐘頭。

passages.original: Her mother smelled her breath and knew she was drunk.
passages.vernacular: 佢母親聞佢嘅呼吸,就知道佢醉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她母親聞她的呼吸,就知道她醉了。

passages.original: She had a fearful headache all day yesterday.
passages.vernacular: 尋日一整天佢頭疼得厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨天一整天她頭疼得厲害。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry is so indignant.
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太氣憤極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太氣憤極了。

passages.original: She will never believe but what I did it on purpose.”
passages.vernacular: 佢永遠唔會相信嗰唔係我故意做嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她永遠不會相信那不是我故意做的。」

passages.original: “I should think she would better punish Diana for being so greedy as to drink three glassfuls of anything,” said Marilla shortly.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得佢倒不如去罰黛安娜,貪心到飲三杯乜嘢嘢,」瑪麗拉簡短地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得她倒不如去罰黛安娜,貪心到喝三杯什麼東西,」瑪麗拉簡短地說。

passages.original: “Why, three of those big glasses would have made her sick even if it had only been cordial.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,就係只飲果露,三個咁大嘅杯子都會讓佢生病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,就是只喝果露,三個那麼大的杯子也會讓她生病。

passages.original: Well, this story will be a nice handle for those folks who are so down on me for making currant wine, although I haven’t made any for three years ever since I found out that the minister didn’t approve.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,呢個故事將成為嗰啲對我釀醋栗酒咁反感嘅人嘅好把柄,雖然我已經三年冇釀喇,自從我發現牧師不贊成就冇釀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,這個故事將成為那些對我釀醋栗酒那麼反感的人的好把柄,雖然我已經三年沒釀了,自從我發現牧師不贊成就沒釀。

passages.original: I just kept that bottle for sickness.
passages.vernacular: 我只係留住嗰瓶以備生病時用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是留著那瓶以備生病時用。

passages.original: There, there, child, don’t cry.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,好喇,細路,別哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,好了,孩子,別哭了。

passages.original: I can’t see as you were to blame although I’m sorry it happened so.”
passages.vernacular: 我睇不出你有乜嘢過錯,雖然我好遺憾發生咗呢件事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看不出你有什麼過錯,雖然我很遺憾發生了這件事。」

passages.original: “I must cry,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我必須哭,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須哭,」安妮說。

passages.original: “My heart is broken.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅心碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的心碎了。

passages.original: The stars in their courses fight against me, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 星辰喺軌道上同我作對,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星辰在軌道上與我作對,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Diana and I are parted forever.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜同我永遠分開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜和我永遠分開了。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, I little dreamed of this when first we swore our vows of friendship.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,當初我哋發誓結下友誼時,我做夢都冇想到會咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,當初我們發誓結下友誼時,我做夢也沒想到會這樣。」

passages.original: “Don’t be foolish, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「別傻喇,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別傻了,安妮。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry will think better of it when she finds you’re not to blame.
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太發現你冇責任時,會改變想法嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太發現你沒有責任時,會改變想法的。

passages.original: I suppose she thinks you’ve done it for a silly joke or something of that sort.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢認為你係因為愚蠢嘅玩笑或嗰一類嘅事才做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想她認為你是因為愚蠢的玩笑或那一類的事才做的。

passages.original: You’d best go up this evening and tell her how it was.”
passages.vernacular: 你最好今晚上去,告訴佢係點回事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你最好今晚上去,告訴她是怎麼回事。」

passages.original: “My courage fails me at the thought of facing Diana’s injured mother,” sighed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「一想到要面對黛安娜受傷嘅母親,我就失去咗勇氣,」安妮嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一想到要面對黛安娜受傷的母親,我就失去了勇氣,」安妮嘆道。

passages.original: “I wish you’d go, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望您去,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望您去,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: You’re so much more dignified than I am.
passages.vernacular: 您比我莊重得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您比我莊重得多。

passages.original: Likely she’d listen to you quicker than to me.”
passages.vernacular: 佢好可能比聽我嘅更快聽您嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她很可能比聽我的更快聽您的。」

passages.original: “Well, I will,” said Marilla, reflecting that it would probably be the wiser course.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,我去,」瑪麗拉講,想住呢或者係更明智嘅做法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,我去,」瑪麗拉說,想著這也許是更明智的做法。

passages.original: “Don’t cry any more, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「唔好再哭喇,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別再哭了,安妮。

passages.original: It will be all right.”
passages.vernacular: 會好嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 會好的。」

passages.original: Marilla had changed her mind about it being all right by the time she got back from Orchard Slope.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉從果園坡回嚟時,已經改變咗對會好嘅想法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉從果園坡回來時,已經改變了對會好的想法。

passages.original: Anne was watching for her coming and flew to the porch door to meet her.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺盼住佢嚟,飛奔到門廊門口迎接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在盼著她來,飛奔到門廊門口迎接她。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, I know by your face that it’s been no use,” she said sorrowfully.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我從您嘅臉上睇出嚟冇用,」佢悲傷地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我從您的臉上看出來沒用,」她悲傷地說。

passages.original: “Mrs. Barry won’t forgive me?”
passages.vernacular: 「巴里太太不原諒我嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴里太太不原諒我嗎?」

passages.original: “Mrs. Barry indeed!” snapped Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「巴里太太!」瑪麗拉厲聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴里太太!」瑪麗拉厲聲說。

passages.original: “Of all the unreasonable women I ever saw she’s the worst.
passages.vernacular: 「我見過嘅所有不講理嘅女人裡,佢係最糟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我見過的所有不講理的女人裡,她是最糟的。

passages.original: I told her it was all a mistake and you weren’t to blame, but she just simply didn’t believe me.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴佢呢完全係個誤會,你冇責任,可佢就係不相信我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴她這完全是個誤會,你沒有責任,可她就是不相信我。

passages.original: And she rubbed it well in about my currant wine and how I’d always said it couldn’t have the least effect on anybody.
passages.vernacular: 而且佢把我嘅醋栗酒狠狠地數落咗一番,講我總講佢唔會對任何人有啲影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且她把我的醋栗酒狠狠地數落了一番,說我總說它不會對任何人有一點影響。

passages.original: I just told her plainly that currant wine wasn’t meant to be drunk three tumblerfuls at a time and that if a child I had to do with was so greedy I’d sober her up with a right good spanking.”
passages.vernacular: 我只係直截咗當地告訴佢,醋栗酒唔係一次飲三大杯嘅,而且如果我管嘅細路咁貪心,我會狠狠揍佢一頓讓佢清醒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是直截了當地告訴她,醋栗酒不是一次喝三大杯的,而且如果我管的孩子這麼貪心,我會狠狠揍她一頓讓她清醒。」

passages.original: Marilla whisked into the kitchen, grievously disturbed, leaving a very much distracted little soul in the porch behind her.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉風風火火地衝進廚房,心煩意亂,把一個心神極度不安嘅小靈魂留喺咗門廊上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉風風火火地衝進廚房,心煩意亂,把一個心神極度不安的小靈魂留在了門廊上。

passages.original: Presently Anne stepped out bareheaded into the chill autumn dusk; very determinedly and steadily she took her way down through the sere clover field over the log bridge and up through the spruce grove, lighted by a pale little moon hanging low over the western woods.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒,安妮光住頭走進寒冷嘅秋日暮色裡;佢好堅決而穩健地走下去,穿過枯萎嘅三葉草地,過咗原木橋,上咗杉樹林,一彎蒼白嘅小月亮低低地掛喺西邊嘅樹林上,照亮咗佢嘅路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒,安妮光著頭走進寒冷的秋日暮色裡;她非常堅決而穩健地走下去,穿過枯萎的三葉草地,過了原木橋,上了杉樹林,一彎蒼白的小月亮低低地掛在西邊的樹林上,照亮了她的路。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry, coming to the door in answer to a timid knock, found a white-lipped eager-eyed suppliant on the doorstep.
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太聽見一聲怯生生嘅敲門,嚟到門口,發現門階上有一個嘴唇發白、眼神急切嘅懇求者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太聽見一聲怯生生的敲門,來到門口,發現門階上有一個嘴唇發白、眼神急切的懇求者。

passages.original: Her face hardened.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉變硬喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉變硬了。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry was a woman of strong prejudices and dislikes, and her anger was of the cold, sullen sort which is always hardest to overcome.
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太係個有強烈偏見同厭惡嘅女人,佢嘅怒氣係嗰種冷漠、陰沉嘅,永遠最難消除。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太是個有強烈偏見和厭惡的女人,她的怒氣是那種冷漠、陰沉的,永遠最難消除。

passages.original: To do her justice, she really believed Anne had made Diana drunk out of sheer malice prepense, and she was honestly anxious to preserve her little daughter from the contamination of further intimacy with such a child.
passages.vernacular: 講句公道話,佢確實相信安妮係出於純粹嘅預謀惡意把黛安娜灌醉嘅,佢誠心地急於保護佢嘅小女兒,唔再同咁樣一個細路進一步親密而受到玷污。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說句公道話,她確實相信安妮是出於純粹的預謀惡意把黛安娜灌醉的,她誠心地急於保護她的小女兒,不再與這樣一個孩子進一步親密而受到玷污。

passages.original: “What do you want?” she said stiffly.
passages.vernacular: 「你要乜嘢?」佢生硬地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要什麼?」她生硬地問。

passages.original: Anne clasped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 安妮雙手合十。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮雙手合十。

passages.original: “Oh, Mrs. Barry, please forgive me.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,巴里太太,請原諒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,巴里太太,請原諒我。

passages.original: I did not mean to--to--intoxicate Diana.
passages.vernacular: 我唔係想要——要——灌醉黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是想要——要——灌醉黛安娜。

passages.original: How could I?
passages.vernacular: 我點會呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怎麼會呢?

passages.original: Just imagine if you were a poor little orphan girl that kind people had adopted and you had just one bosom friend in all the world.
passages.vernacular: 請您想像一下,如果您係一個被好心人收養嘅可憐小孤女,喺呢世上只有一個知心朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請您想像一下,如果您是一個被好心人收養的可憐小孤女,在這世上只有一個知心朋友。

passages.original: Do you think you would intoxicate her on purpose?
passages.vernacular: 您覺得您會故意灌醉佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您覺得您會故意灌醉她嗎?

passages.original: I thought it was only raspberry cordial.
passages.vernacular: 我以為嗰只係覆盆子果露。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以為那只是覆盆子果露。

passages.original: I was firmly convinced it was raspberry cordial.
passages.vernacular: 我堅信嗰個係覆盆子果露。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我堅信那是覆盆子果露。

passages.original: Oh, please don’t say that you won’t let Diana play with me any more.
passages.vernacular: 哦,請唔好講您唔再讓黛安娜跟我玩喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,請不要說您不再讓黛安娜跟我玩了。

passages.original: If you do you will cover my life with a dark cloud of woe.”
passages.vernacular: 如果您嗰樣講,您就會畀我嘅生活蓋上一片悲痛嘅烏雲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您那樣說,您就會給我的生活蓋上一片悲痛的烏雲。」

passages.original: This speech which would have softened good Mrs. Lynde’s heart in a twinkling, had no effect on Mrs. Barry except to irritate her still more.
passages.vernacular: 呢番話,本來會即刻軟化善良嘅林德太太嘅心,對巴里太太卻冇任何作用,只係更激怒咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這番話,本來會立刻軟化善良的林德太太的心,對巴里太太卻沒有任何作用,只是更激怒了她。

passages.original: She was suspicious of Anne’s big words and dramatic gestures and imagined that the child was making fun of her.
passages.vernacular: 佢懷疑安妮嘅大詞同戲劇性嘅手勢,想像呢細路係喺嘲笑佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她懷疑安妮的大詞和戲劇性的手勢,想像這孩子是在嘲笑她。

passages.original: So she said, coldly and cruelly:
passages.vernacular: 所以佢冷冷地、殘酷地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以她冷冷地、殘酷地說:

passages.original: “I don’t think you are a fit little girl for Diana to associate with.
passages.vernacular: 「我不認為你係適合黛安娜交往嘅小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不認為你是適合黛安娜交往的小女孩。

passages.original: You’d better go home and behave yourself.”
passages.vernacular: 你最好回家去,規矩啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你最好回家去,規矩一點。」

passages.original: Anne’s lips quivered.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅嘴唇顫抖住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的嘴唇顫抖著。

passages.original: “Won’t you let me see Diana just once to say farewell?” she implored.
passages.vernacular: 「您能讓我見黛安娜一次,跟佢告別嗎?」佢懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您能讓我見黛安娜一次,跟她告別嗎?」她懇求道。

passages.original: “Diana has gone over to Carmody with her father,” said Mrs. Barry, going in and shutting the door.
passages.vernacular: 「黛安娜同佢父親去卡莫迪喇,」巴里太太講,走進去關上咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黛安娜和她父親去卡莫迪了,」巴里太太說,走進去關上了門。

passages.original: Anne went back to Green Gables calm with despair.
passages.vernacular: 安妮帶住絕望嘅平靜回到綠色屋頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮帶著絕望的平靜回到綠色屋頂。

passages.original: “My last hope is gone,” she told Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我最後嘅希望冇喇,」佢對瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我最後的希望沒有了,」她對瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “I went up and saw Mrs. Barry myself and she treated me very insultingly.
passages.vernacular: 「我親自上去見咗巴里太太,佢對我極其侮辱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我親自上去見了巴里太太,她對我極其侮辱。

passages.original: Marilla, I do not think she is a well-bred woman.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉,我認為佢唔係一個有教養嘅女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉,我認為她不是一個有教養的女人。

passages.original: There is nothing more to do except to pray and I haven’t much hope that that’ll do much good because, Marilla, I do not believe that God Himself can do very much with such an obstinate person as Mrs. Barry.”
passages.vernacular: 除咗禱告,冇別嘅可做喇,可我對此不抱乜嘢希望,因為,瑪麗拉,我不相信上帝本人對像巴里太太咁樣固執嘅人能有多大辦法。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了禱告,沒有別的可做了,可我對此不抱什麼希望,因為,瑪麗拉,我不相信上帝本人對像巴里太太這樣固執的人能有多大辦法。」

passages.original: “Anne, you shouldn’t say such things” rebuked Marilla, striving to overcome that unholy tendency to laughter which she was dismayed to find growing upon her.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,你不該講呢種話,」瑪麗拉責備道,努力克制嗰種不虔誠嘅想笑嘅傾向,佢驚慌地發現呢種傾向越嚟越強喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,你不該說這種話,」瑪麗拉責備道,努力克制那種不虔誠的想笑的傾向,她驚慌地發現這種傾向越來越強了。

passages.original: And indeed, when she told the whole story to Matthew that night, she did laugh heartily over Anne’s tribulations.
passages.vernacular: 確實,嗰天晚上佢把整個故事告訴馬修時,佢對安妮嘅苦難笑得好開心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,那天晚上她把整個故事告訴馬修時,她對安妮的苦難笑得很開心。

passages.original: But when she slipped into the east gable before going to bed and found that Anne had cried herself to sleep an unaccustomed softness crept into her face.
passages.vernacular: 但係瞓覺前佢悄悄走進東山牆房間,發現安妮哭住瞓住喇,一種不尋常嘅柔和爬上咗佢嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是睡覺前她悄悄走進東山牆房間,發現安妮哭著睡著了,一種不尋常的柔和爬上了她的臉。

passages.original: “Poor little soul,” she murmured, lifting a loose curl of hair from the child’s tear-stained face.
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅小靈魂,」佢喃喃道,撩起細路淚痕斑斑嘅臉上一縷散落嘅鬈髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的小靈魂,」她喃喃道,撩起孩子淚痕斑斑的臉上一縷散落的鬈髮。

passages.original: Then she bent down and kissed the flushed cheek on the pillow.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢俯下身,親吻枕頭上嗰泛紅嘅臉頰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她俯下身,親吻枕頭上那泛紅的臉頰。

chapters.title: Ch. XVII A New Interest in Life 第十七章:生活中的新興趣

passages.original: CH THE next afternoon Anne, bending over her patchwork at the kitchen window, happened to glance out and beheld Diana down by the Dryad’s Bubble beckoning mysteriously.
passages.vernacular: 第二天下午,安妮正在廚房窗邊埋頭做拼布,偶然朝外一瞥,睇見黛安娜喺林中仙子泉邊,神祕地招手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天下午,安妮正在廚房窗邊埋頭做拼布,偶然朝外一瞥,看見黛安娜在林中仙子泉邊,神祕地招手。

passages.original: In a trice Anne was out of the house and flying down to the hollow, astonishment and hope struggling in her expressive eyes.
passages.vernacular: 轉眼間,安妮就衝出屋子,飛奔到窪地,富於表情嘅眼睛裡驚訝同希望交織。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轉眼間,安妮就衝出屋子,飛奔到窪地,富於表情的眼睛裡驚訝和希望交織。

passages.original: But the hope faded when she saw Diana’s dejected countenance.
passages.vernacular: 但當佢睇到黛安娜沮喪嘅臉色時,希望消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但當她看到黛安娜沮喪的臉色時,希望消失了。

passages.original: “Your mother hasn’t relented?” she gasped.
passages.vernacular: 「你媽媽冇消氣?」佢喘住氣問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你媽媽沒有消氣?」她喘著氣問。

passages.original: Diana shook her head mournfully.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜悲傷地搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜悲傷地搖搖頭。

passages.original: “No; and oh, Anne, she says I’m never to play with you again.
passages.vernacular: 「冇;哦,安妮,佢講我再都不許跟你玩喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有;哦,安妮,她說我再也不許跟你玩了。

passages.original: I’ve cried and cried and I told her it wasn’t your fault, but it wasn’t any use.
passages.vernacular: 我哭咗又哭,告訴佢嗰唔係你嘅錯,不過冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我哭了又哭,告訴她那不是你的錯,可是沒用。

passages.original: I had ever such a time coaxing her to let me come down and say good-bye to you.
passages.vernacular: 我好唔容易才哄得佢讓我下嚟跟你講再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我好不容易才哄得她讓我下來跟你說再見。

passages.original: She said I was only to stay ten minutes and she’s timing me by the clock.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講我只能待好鐘,佢喺按鐘計時呢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我只能待十分鐘,她在按鐘計時呢。」

passages.original: “Ten minutes isn’t very long to say an eternal farewell in,” said Anne tearfully.
passages.vernacular: 「好鐘用來講永別,時間不太長,」安妮含淚講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「十分鐘用來說永別,時間不太長,」安妮含淚說。

passages.original: “Oh, Diana, will you promise faithfully never to forget me, the friend of your youth, no matter what dearer friends may caress thee?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,黛安娜,你能唔能夠忠實地答應我,永遠不忘記我,你少年時嘅朋友,無論多少更親嘅朋友愛撫住你?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,黛安娜,你能不能忠實地答應我,永遠不忘記我,你少年時的朋友,無論多少更親的朋友愛撫著你?」

passages.original: “Indeed I will,” sobbed Diana, “and I’ll never have another bosom friend--I don’t want to have.
passages.vernacular: 「我一定,」黛安娜抽泣住講,「我再都唔會有別嘅知心朋友喇——我唔想有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一定,」黛安娜抽泣著說,「我再也不會有別的知心朋友了——我不想有。

passages.original: I couldn’t love anybody as I love you.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔可能像愛你嗰樣愛任何人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不可能像愛你那樣愛任何人。」

passages.original: “Oh, Diana,” cried Anne, clasping her hands, “do you love me?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,黛安娜,」安妮雙手合十叫道,「你愛我嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,黛安娜,」安妮雙手合十叫道,「你愛我嗎?」

passages.original: “Why, of course I do.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,當然愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,當然愛。

passages.original: Didn’t you know that?”
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道嗎?」

passages.original: “No.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不知道。」

passages.original: Anne drew a long breath.
passages.vernacular: 安妮深深吸咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮深深吸了口氣。

passages.original: “I thought you liked me of course but I never hoped you loved me.
passages.vernacular: 「我當然以為你鍾意我,但我從冇敢希望你愛我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我當然以為你喜歡我,但我從沒敢希望你愛我。

passages.original: Why, Diana, I didn’t think anybody could love me.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,黛安娜,我冇想過會有人愛我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,黛安娜,我沒想過會有人愛我。

passages.original: Nobody ever has loved me since I can remember.
passages.vernacular: 從我記事起,從冇人愛過我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從我記事起,從沒有人愛過我。

passages.original: Oh, this is wonderful!
passages.vernacular: 哦,太奇妙喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,太奇妙了!

passages.original: It’s a ray of light which will forever shine on the darkness of a path severed from thee, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一道光,將永遠照亮同你分離嘅黑暗之路,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一道光,將永遠照亮與你分離的黑暗之路,黛安娜。

passages.original: Oh, just say it once again.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,再講一遍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,再說一遍。」

passages.original: “I love you devotedly, Anne,” said Diana stanchly, “and I always will, you may be sure of that.”
passages.vernacular: 「我全心全意地愛你,安妮,」黛安娜堅定地講,「我永遠愛你,你可以肯定。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我全心全意地愛你,安妮,」黛安娜堅定地說,「我永遠愛你,你可以肯定。」

passages.original: “And I will always love thee, Diana,” said Anne, solemnly extending her hand.
passages.vernacular: 「我都將永遠愛你,黛安娜,」安妮莊嚴地伸出手講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也將永遠愛你,黛安娜,」安妮莊嚴地伸出手說。

passages.original: “In the years to come thy memory will shine like a star over my lonely life, as that last story we read together says.
passages.vernacular: 「喺未來嘅歲月,你嘅記憶將像星星一樣照耀我孤獨嘅生命,就像我哋一起讀嘅最後嗰個故事講嘅嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在未來的歲月,你的記憶將像星星一樣照耀我孤獨的生命,就像我們一起讀的最後那個故事說的那樣。

passages.original: Diana, wilt thou give me a lock of thy jet-black tresses in parting to treasure forevermore?”
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜,臨別之際,你能唔能夠畀我一縷你烏黑嘅髮絲,讓我永遠珍藏?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜,臨別之際,你能不能給我一縷你烏黑的髮絲,讓我永遠珍藏?」

passages.original: “Have you got anything to cut it with?” queried Diana, wiping away the tears which Anne’s affecting accents had caused to flow afresh, and returning to practicalities.
passages.vernacular: 「你有乜嘢可以剪佢嘅嗎?」黛安娜問,擦去被安妮動人嘅語調又引出嘅淚水,回到咗實際問題上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有什麼可以剪它的嗎?」黛安娜問,擦去被安妮動人的語調又引出的淚水,回到了實際問題上。

passages.original: “Yes.
I’ve got my patchwork scissors in my apron pocket fortunately,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 幸好我圍裙口袋裡有拼布剪刀,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸好我圍裙口袋裡有拼布剪刀,」安妮說。

passages.original: She solemnly clipped one of Diana’s curls.
passages.vernacular: 佢鄭重地剪下黛安娜嘅一縷鬈髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她鄭重地剪下黛安娜的一縷鬈髮。

passages.original: “Fare thee well, my beloved friend.
passages.vernacular: 「別喇,我親愛嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別了,我親愛的朋友。

passages.original: Henceforth we must be as strangers though living side by side.
passages.vernacular: 從此我哋必須像陌生人一樣,雖然近喺咫尺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從此我們必須像陌生人一樣,雖然近在咫尺。

passages.original: But my heart will ever be faithful to thee.”
passages.vernacular: 但我嘅心永遠對你忠誠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我的心永遠對你忠誠。」

passages.original: Anne stood and watched Diana out of sight, mournfully waving her hand to the latter whenever she turned to look back.
passages.vernacular: 安妮站住目送黛安娜走遠,每當後者回頭睇,就悲傷地向佢揮手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮站著目送黛安娜走遠,每當後者回頭看,就悲傷地向她揮手。

passages.original: Then she returned to the house, not a little consoled for the time being by this romantic parting.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢回到屋裡,呢浪漫嘅離別使佢暫時得到不小嘅安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她回到屋裡,這浪漫的離別使她暫時得到不小的安慰。

passages.original: “It is all over,” she informed Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「一切都結束喇,」佢告訴瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一切都結束了,」她告訴瑪麗拉。

passages.original: “I shall never have another friend.
passages.vernacular: 「我再都唔會有別嘅朋友喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再也不會有別的朋友了。

passages.original: I’m really worse off than ever before, for I haven’t Katie Maurice and Violetta now.
passages.vernacular: 我真嘅比以往任何時候都更糟,因為我而家冇凱蒂·莫里斯同維奧萊塔喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真的比以往任何時候都更糟,因為我現在沒有凱蒂·莫里斯和維奧萊塔了。

passages.original: And even if I had it wouldn’t be the same.
passages.vernacular: 而且即使有都不一樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且即使有也不一樣了。

passages.original: Somehow, little dream girls are not satisfying after a real friend.
passages.vernacular: 唔知怎嘅,有咗真正嘅朋友之後,夢中嘅小女孩唔能夠令人滿足喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知怎的,有了真正的朋友之後,夢中的小女孩不能令人滿足了。

passages.original: Diana and I had such an affecting farewell down by the spring.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜同我喺泉邊有一個咁動人嘅告別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜和我在泉邊有一個那麼動人的告別。

passages.original: It will be sacred in my memory forever.
passages.vernacular: 佢將永遠神聖地留喺我嘅記憶裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它將永遠神聖地留在我的記憶裡。

passages.original: I used the most pathetic language I could think of and said ‘thou’ and ‘thee.’
passages.vernacular: 我用咗我所能想到嘅最悲壯嘅語言,講『你』同『汝』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我用了我所能想到的最悲壯的語言,說『你』和『汝』。

passages.original: ‘Thou’ and ‘thee’ seem so much more romantic than ‘you.’
passages.vernacular: 『汝』比『你』顯得浪漫得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『汝』比『你』顯得浪漫得多。

passages.original: Diana gave me a lock of her hair and I’m going to sew it up in a little bag and wear it around my neck all my life.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜畀咗我一縷佢嘅頭髮,我要把佢縫進一個小袋子裡,終生掛喺脖子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜給了我一縷她的頭髮,我要把它縫進一個小袋子裡,終生掛在脖子上。

passages.original: Please see that it is buried with me, for I don’t believe I’ll live very long.
passages.vernacular: 請您務必讓佢隨我一起下葬,因為我不相信我能活多久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請您務必讓它隨我一起下葬,因為我不相信我能活多久。

passages.original: Perhaps when she sees me lying cold and dead before her Mrs. Barry may feel remorse for what she has done and will let Diana come to my funeral.”
passages.vernacular: 或者佢睇見我冰冷地死去躺喺佢面前嘅時候,巴里太太會為佢所做嘅事感到悔恨,讓黛安娜嚟參加我嘅葬禮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許她看見我冰冷地死去躺在她面前的時候,巴里太太會為她所做的事感到悔恨,讓黛安娜來參加我的葬禮。」

passages.original: “I don’t think there is much fear of your dying of grief as long as you can talk, Anne,” said Marilla unsympathetically.
passages.vernacular: 「只要你仲能講話,我想你仲不至於因悲傷而死,安妮,」瑪麗拉毫不同情地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只要你還能說話,我想你還不至於因悲傷而死,安妮,」瑪麗拉毫不同情地說。

passages.original: The following Monday Anne surprised Marilla by coming down from her room with her basket of books on her arm and hip and her lips primmed up into a line of determination.
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟嘅星期一,安妮讓瑪麗拉食咗一驚:佢挎住書籃從房間下嚟,嘴唇抿成一條決心嘅線。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來的星期一,安妮讓瑪麗拉吃了一驚:她挎著書籃從房間下來,嘴唇抿成一條決心的線。

passages.original: “I’m going back to school,” she announced.
passages.vernacular: 「我要回學校,」佢宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要回學校,」她宣布。

passages.original: “That is all there is left in life for me, now that my friend has been ruthlessly torn from me.
passages.vernacular: 「而家我嘅朋友被無情地從我身邊奪走,生活中剩下嘅就只有呢個喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我的朋友被無情地從我身邊奪走,生活中剩下的就只有這個了。

passages.original: In school I can look at her and muse over days departed.”
passages.vernacular: 喺學校里我可以睇住佢,回想逝去嘅日子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在學校里我可以看著她,回想逝去的日子。」

passages.original: “You’d better muse over your lessons and sums,” said Marilla, concealing her delight at this development of the situation.
passages.vernacular: 「你最好去回想你嘅功課同算術,」瑪麗拉講,掩飾佢對事態呢個發展嘅高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你最好去回想你的功課和算術,」瑪麗拉說,掩飾她對事態這個發展的高興。

passages.original: “If you’re going back to school I hope we’ll hear no more of breaking slates over people’s heads and such carryings on.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你要回學校,我希望唔好再聽到有人被石板砸頭之類嘅胡鬧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你要回學校,我希望不要再聽到有人被石板砸頭之類的胡鬧。

passages.original: Behave yourself and do just what your teacher tells you.”
passages.vernacular: 規矩點,老師叫你做乜嘢就做乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 規矩點,老師叫你做什麼就做什麼。」

passages.original: “I’ll try to be a model pupil,” agreed Anne dolefully.
passages.vernacular: 「我努力做個模範學生,」安妮悲傷地同意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我努力做個模範學生,」安妮悲傷地同意。

passages.original: “There won’t be much fun in it, I expect.
passages.vernacular: 「我想唔會有多少樂趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想不會有多少樂趣。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips said Minnie Andrews was a model pupil and there isn’t a spark of imagination or life in her.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生講明妮·安德魯斯係個模範學生,可佢身上啲想像力或生氣都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生說明妮·安德魯斯是個模範學生,可她身上一點想像力或生氣都沒有。

passages.original: She is just dull and poky and never seems to have a good time.
passages.vernacular: 佢就係遲鈍、呆板,好像永遠玩不痛快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她就是遲鈍、呆板,好像永遠玩不痛快。

passages.original: But I feel so depressed that perhaps it will come easy to me now.
passages.vernacular: 不過我而家咁沮喪,或者呢對我來講會好容易。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我現在這麼沮喪,也許這對我來說會很容易。

passages.original: I’m going round by the road.
passages.vernacular: 我要走大路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要走大路。

passages.original: I couldn’t bear to go by the Birch Path all alone.
passages.vernacular: 我受不了一個人走白樺小徑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我受不了一個人走白樺小徑。

passages.original: I should weep bitter tears if I did.”
passages.vernacular: 如果我走,我會流下苦澀嘅淚水。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我走,我會流下苦澀的淚水。」

passages.original: Anne was welcomed back to school with open arms.
passages.vernacular: 安妮回到學校,受到熱烈歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮回到學校,受到熱烈歡迎。

passages.original: Her imagination had been sorely missed in games, her voice in the singing and her dramatic ability in the perusal aloud of books at dinner hour.
passages.vernacular: 遊戲中好想念佢嘅想像力,唱歌時想念佢嘅聲音,午休時大聲朗讀書嘅時候,想念佢嘅戲劇才能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遊戲中非常想念她的想像力,唱歌時想念她的聲音,午休時大聲朗讀書的時候,想念她的戲劇才能。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis smuggled three blue plums over to her during testament reading; Ella May MacPherson gave her an enormous yellow pansy cut from the covers of a floral catalogue--a species of desk decoration much prized in Avonlea school.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯喺讀新約時偷偷遞畀佢三個藍李子;艾拉·梅·麥克弗森送畀佢一朵從花卉目錄封面上剪下嚟嘅巨大嘅黃色三色堇——呢個係阿文利學校桌上好珍貴嘅一種裝飾;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯在讀新約時偷偷遞給她三個藍李子;艾拉·梅·麥克弗森送給她一朵從花卉目錄封面上剪下來的巨大的黃色三色堇——這是阿文利學校桌上非常珍貴的一種裝飾;

passages.original: Sophia Sloane offered to teach her a perfectly elegant new pattern of knit lace, so nice for trimming aprons.
passages.vernacular: 蘇菲亞·斯隆提出要教佢一種特別高雅嘅新編織蕾絲花樣,最適合畀圍裙滾邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蘇菲亞·斯隆提出要教她一種特別高雅的新編織蕾絲花樣,最適合給圍裙滾邊。

passages.original: Katie Boulter gave her a perfume bottle to keep slate water in, and Julia Bell copied carefully on a piece of pale pink paper scalloped on the edges the following effusion:
passages.vernacular: 凱蒂·博爾特畀咗佢一個香水瓶,用嚟裝擦石板嘅水,朱莉婭·貝爾喺一張邊緣呈扇形嘅淡粉紅紙上仔細抄咗下面呢首詩:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱蒂·博爾特給了她一個香水瓶,用來裝擦石板的水,朱莉婭·貝爾在一張邊緣呈扇形的淡粉紅紙上仔細抄了下面這首詩:

passages.original: “TO ANNE
passages.vernacular: 「獻畀安妮
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「獻給安妮

passages.original: “When twilight drops her curtain down And pins it with a star Remember that you have a friend Though she may wander far.”
passages.vernacular: 「當暮色放下佢嘅簾子,用一顆星星別住,請記住你有一個朋友,雖然佢可能漂泊遠方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當暮色放下她的簾子,用一顆星星別住,請記住你有一個朋友,雖然她可能漂泊遠方。」

passages.original: “It’s so nice to be appreciated,” sighed Anne rapturously to Marilla that night.
passages.vernacular: 「被人重視真好,」嗰天晚上,安妮欣喜地對瑪麗拉嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「被人重視真好,」那天晚上,安妮欣喜地對瑪麗拉嘆道。

passages.original: The girls were not the only scholars who “appreciated” her.
passages.vernacular: 「重視」佢嘅不僅僅係女孩哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「重視」她的不僅僅是女孩們。

passages.original: When Anne went to her seat after dinner hour--she had been told by Mr. Phillips to sit with the model Minnie Andrews--she found on her desk a big luscious “strawberry apple.”
passages.vernacular: 午休後安妮走回自己嘅座位——菲利普斯先生叫佢跟模範生明妮·安德魯斯坐——發現桌上放住一個又大又多汁嘅「草莓蘋果」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 午休後安妮走回自己的座位——菲利普斯先生叫她跟模範生明妮·安德魯斯坐——發現桌上放著一個又大又多汁的「草莓蘋果」。

passages.original: Anne caught it up all ready to take a bite when she remembered that the only place in Avonlea where strawberry apples grew was in the old Blythe orchard on the other side of the Lake of Shining Waters.
passages.vernacular: 安妮攞起佢正要咬時,想起阿文利唯一長草莓蘋果嘅地方,係閃亮湖水另一邊布萊斯家嘅老果園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮拿起它正要咬時,想起阿文利唯一長草莓蘋果的地方,是閃亮湖水另一邊布萊斯家的老果園。

passages.original: Anne dropped the apple as if it were a red-hot coal and ostentatiously wiped her fingers on her handkerchief.
passages.vernacular: 安妮像扔掉燒紅嘅煤塊一樣扔下咗蘋果,故意喺手帕上擦手指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮像扔掉燒紅的煤塊一樣扔下了蘋果,故意在手帕上擦手指。

passages.original: The apple lay untouched on her desk until the next morning, when little Timothy Andrews, who swept the school and kindled the fire, annexed it as one of his perquisites.
passages.vernacular: 嗰蘋果原封不動地躺喺佢桌上,直到第二天早晨,打掃學校、生火嘅小蒂莫西·安德魯斯把佢據為己有,算作佢嘅額外收入之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那蘋果原封不動地躺在她桌上,直到第二天早晨,打掃學校、生火的小蒂莫西·安德魯斯把它據為己有,算作他的額外收入之一。

passages.original: Charlie Sloane’s slate pencil, gorgeously bedizened with striped red and yellow paper, costing two cents where ordinary pencils cost only one, which he sent up to her after dinner hour, met with a more favorable reception.
passages.vernacular: 查理·斯隆嘅石筆就受到咗更友好嘅接待:石筆裹住紅黃條紋嘅紙,裝飾得富麗堂皇,普通石筆一分錢,佢要兩分錢,係佢午休後讓人送畀佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 查理·斯隆的石筆就受到了更友好的接待:石筆裹著紅黃條紋的紙,裝飾得富麗堂皇,普通石筆一分錢,它要兩分錢,是他午休後讓人送給她的。

passages.original: Anne was graciously pleased to accept it and rewarded the donor with a smile which exalted that infatuated youth straightway into the seventh heaven of delight and caused him to make such fearful errors in his dictation that Mr. Phillips kept him in after school to rewrite it.
passages.vernacular: 安妮親切愉快地接受喇,並以微笑報答送禮人,呢使嗰個痴心嘅少年即刻飛上咗喜悅嘅第七重天,並使佢聽寫時犯咗可怕嘅錯誤,菲利普斯先生放學後留佢重寫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮親切愉快地接受了,並以微笑報答送禮人,這使那個痴心的少年立刻飛上了喜悅的第七重天,並使他聽寫時犯了可怕的錯誤,菲利普斯先生放學後留他重寫。

passages.original: But as,
passages.vernacular: 但正如
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但正如

passages.original: The Cæsar’s pageant shorn of Brutus’ bust Did but of Rome’s best son remind her more,
passages.vernacular: 「凱撒嘅儀仗少咗布魯圖斯嘅半身像,反而更讓佢想起羅馬最優秀嘅兒子,」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「凱撒的儀仗少了布魯圖斯的半身像,反而更讓她想起羅馬最優秀的兒子,」

passages.original: so the marked absence of any tribute or recognition from Diana Barry who was sitting with Gertie Pye embittered Anne’s little triumph.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜·巴里同格蒂·派伊同坐,對安妮冇任何表示或認可,呢使安妮嘅小小勝利變得苦澀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜·巴里與格蒂·派伊同坐,對安妮沒有任何表示或認可,這使安妮的小小勝利變得苦澀。

passages.original: “Diana might just have smiled at me once, I think,” she mourned to Marilla that night.
passages.vernacular: 「我想黛安娜至少可以對我笑一笑,」嗰天晚上佢哀傷地對瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想黛安娜至少可以對我笑一笑,」那天晚上她哀傷地對瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: But the next morning a note most fearfully and wonderfully twisted and folded, and a small parcel were passed across to Anne.
passages.vernacular: 但第二天早晨,一張折得極其可怕又奇妙嘅紙條同一個小包裹傳到咗安妮手裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但第二天早晨,一張折得極其可怕又奇妙的紙條和一個小包裹傳到了安妮手裡。

passages.original: “Dear Anne, ran the former, “Mother says I’m not to play with you or talk to you even in school.
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅安妮,」前者寫道,「媽媽講我不許跟你玩,連喺學校都不許跟你講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的安妮,」前者寫道,「媽媽說我不許跟你玩,連在學校也不許跟你說話。

passages.original: It isn’t my fault and don’t be cross at me, because I love you as much as ever.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係我嘅錯,請別生我嘅氣,因為我一如既往地愛你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是我的錯,請別生我的氣,因為我一如既往地愛你。

passages.original: I miss you awfully to tell all my secrets to and I don’t like Gertie Pye one bit.
passages.vernacular: 我特別想念你,冇人可以訴講我所有嘅祕密,而且我啲都不鍾意格蒂·派伊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我特別想念你,沒人可以訴說我所有的祕密,而且我一點也不喜歡格蒂·派伊。

passages.original: I made you one of the new bookmarkers out of red tissue paper.
passages.vernacular: 我用紅色薄紙畀你做咗一個新式書籤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我用紅色薄紙給你做了一個新式書籤。

passages.original: They are awfully fashionable now and only three girls in school know how to make them.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋而家特別時髦,學校里只有三個女孩會做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們現在特別時髦,學校里只有三個女孩會做。

passages.original: When you look at it remember
passages.vernacular: 當你睇住佢嘅時候,請記住
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你看著它的時候,請記住

passages.original: Your true friend, Diana Barry.
passages.vernacular: 你真心嘅朋友,黛安娜·巴里。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你真心的朋友,黛安娜·巴里。」

passages.original: Anne read the note, kissed the bookmark, and dispatched a prompt reply back to the other side of the school.
passages.vernacular: 安妮讀完紙條,親吻咗書籤,迅速回咗一封信,傳到學校嘅另一邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮讀完紙條,親吻了書籤,迅速回了一封信,傳到學校的另一邊。

passages.original: My own darling Diana:--
passages.vernacular: 「我親愛嘅黛安娜:——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我親愛的黛安娜:——

passages.original: Of course I am not cross at you because you have to obey your mother.
passages.vernacular: 我當然不生你嘅氣,因為你必須服從你媽媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我當然不生你的氣,因為你必須服從你媽媽。

passages.original: Our spirits can commune.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅心靈可以交流。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的心靈可以交流。

passages.original: I shall keep your lovely present forever.
passages.vernacular: 我會永遠保存你可愛嘅禮物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會永遠保存你可愛的禮物。

passages.original: Minnie Andrews is a very nice little girl--although she has no imagination--but after having been Diana’s busum friend I cannot be Minnie’s.
passages.vernacular: 明妮·安德魯斯係個好好嘅小女孩——雖然佢冇想像力——但喺做過黛安娜嘅知心朋友之後,我唔能夠做明妮嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明妮·安德魯斯是個很好的小女孩——雖然她沒有想像力——但在做過黛安娜的知心朋友之後,我不能做明妮的。

passages.original: Please excuse mistakes because my spelling isn’t very good yet, although much improoved.
passages.vernacular: 請原諒錯誤,因為我嘅拼寫仲不太好,雖然已經進步咗好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒錯誤,因為我的拼寫還不太好,雖然已經進步了很多。

passages.original: Yours until death us do part Anne or Cordelia Shirley.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅,直到死亡將我哋分開,安妮,或科黛莉亞·雪莉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的,直到死亡將我們分開,安妮,或科黛莉亞·雪莉。

passages.original: P.S. I shall sleep with your letter under my pillow tonight.
passages.vernacular: 又及:今晚我要把你嘅信放喺枕頭下面瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又及:今晚我要把你的信放在枕頭下面睡覺。

passages.original: A. or C.S.
passages.vernacular: A. 或 C. S.」
passages.vernacularMandarin: A. 或 C. S.」

passages.original: Marilla pessimistically expected more trouble since Anne had again begun to go to school.
passages.vernacular: 自從安妮又開始上學,瑪麗拉悲觀地預料仲會有更多麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從安妮又開始上學,瑪麗拉悲觀地預料還會有更多麻煩。

passages.original: But none developed.
passages.vernacular: 但冇出現麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但沒有出現麻煩。

passages.original: Perhaps Anne caught something of the “model” spirit from Minnie Andrews; at least she got on very well with Mr. Phillips thenceforth.
passages.vernacular: 或者安妮從明妮·安德魯斯身上染上咗啲「模範」精神;至少從嗰以後佢同菲利普斯先生相處得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許安妮從明妮·安德魯斯身上染上了一點「模範」精神;至少從那以後她和菲利普斯先生相處得很好。

passages.original: She flung herself into her studies heart and soul, determined not to be outdone in any class by Gilbert Blythe.
passages.vernacular: 佢全心全意地投入學習,決心喺任何一門功課上都不輸畀吉爾伯特·布萊斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她全心全意地投入學習,決心在任何一門功課上都不輸給吉爾伯特·布萊斯。

passages.original: The rivalry between them was soon apparent; it was entirely good natured on Gilbert’s side; but it is much to be feared that the same thing cannot be said of Anne, who had certainly an unpraiseworthy tenacity for holding grudges.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋之間嘅競爭好快就變得明顯喇;喺吉爾伯特呢邊完全係友好嘅;但恐怕安妮就唔能夠咁講喇,佢確實有一種不值得稱讚嘅記仇嘅頑固。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們之間的競爭很快就變得明顯了;在吉爾伯特這邊完全是友好的;但恐怕安妮就不能這麼說了,她確實有一種不值得稱讚的記仇的頑固。

passages.original: She was as intense in her hatreds as in her loves.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅恨同佢嘅愛一樣強烈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的恨和她的愛一樣強烈。

passages.original: She would not stoop to admit that she meant to rival Gilbert in schoolwork, because that would have been to acknowledge his existence which Anne persistently ignored; but the rivalry was there and honors fluctuated between them.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔肯屈尊承認佢打算喺功課上同吉爾伯特較量,因為嗰就等於承認佢嘅存在,而安妮一直堅持無視佢;但競爭係存在嘅,榮譽喺佢哋之間起伏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不肯屈尊承認她打算在功課上與吉爾伯特較量,因為那就等於承認他的存在,而安妮一直堅持無視他;但競爭是存在的,榮譽在他們之間起伏。

passages.original: Now Gilbert was head of the spelling class; now Anne, with a toss of her long red braids, spelled him down.
passages.vernacular: 一會兒吉爾伯特係拼寫班第一;一會兒安妮甩一甩佢長長嘅紅辮子,把佢拼寫贏下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一會兒吉爾伯特是拼寫班第一;一會兒安妮甩一甩她長長的紅辮子,把他拼寫贏下去。

passages.original: One morning Gilbert had all his sums done correctly and had his name written on the blackboard on the roll of honor; the next morning Anne, having wrestled wildly with decimals the entire evening before, would be first.
passages.vernacular: 有一天早晨,吉爾伯特嘅算術全做對喇,佢嘅名字被寫喺黑板嘅榮譽榜上;第二天早晨,安妮喺前一晚瘋狂地同小數搏鬥咗一整晚,就會係第一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天早晨,吉爾伯特的算術全做對了,他的名字被寫在黑板的榮譽榜上;第二天早晨,安妮在前一晚瘋狂地與小數搏鬥了一整晚,就會是第一。

passages.original: One awful day they were ties and their names were written up together.
passages.vernacular: 有可怕嘅一天,佢哋打成平手,佢哋嘅名字被寫喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有可怕的一天,他們打成平手,他們的名字被寫在一起。

passages.original: It was almost as bad as a take-notice and Anne’s mortification was as evident as Gilbert’s satisfaction.
passages.vernacular: 嗰幾乎同『請注意』一樣糟,安妮嘅羞辱同吉爾伯特嘅滿意一樣明顯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那幾乎和『請注意』一樣糟,安妮的羞辱和吉爾伯特的滿意一樣明顯。

passages.original: When the written examinations at the end of each month were held the suspense was terrible.
passages.vernacular: 每個月底舉行筆試時,懸念係可怕嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個月底舉行筆試時,懸念是可怕的。

passages.original: The first month Gilbert came out three marks ahead.
passages.vernacular: 第一個月吉爾伯特領先三分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一個月吉爾伯特領先三分。

passages.original: The second Anne beat him by five.
passages.vernacular: 第二個月安妮領先五分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二個月安妮領先五分。

passages.original: But her triumph was marred by the fact that Gilbert congratulated her heartily before the whole school.
passages.vernacular: 但佢嘅勝利因為吉爾伯特當住全校嘅面熱情地祝賀佢而大打折扣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她的勝利因為吉爾伯特當著全校的面熱情地祝賀她而大打折扣。

passages.original: It would have been ever so much sweeter to her if he had felt the sting of his defeat.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢感受到咗失敗嘅刺痛,對佢來講會甜蜜得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他感受到了失敗的刺痛,對她來說會甜蜜得多。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips might not be a very good teacher; but a pupil so inflexibly determined on learning as Anne was could hardly escape making progress under any kind of teacher.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生或者唔係個好好嘅老師;但像安妮咁樣不屈不撓地決心學習嘅學生,不管遇到乜嘢樣嘅老師,都好難不取得進步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生也許不是個很好的老師;但像安妮這樣不屈不撓地決心學習的學生,不管遇到什麼樣的老師,都很難不取得進步。

passages.original: By the end of the term Anne and Gilbert were both promoted into the fifth class and allowed to begin studying the elements of “the branches”--by which Latin, geometry, French, and algebra were meant.
passages.vernacular: 到學期末,安妮同吉爾伯特都升到咗第五班,獲准開始學習「各門學科」嘅基礎——指嘅係拉丁文、幾何、法語同代數。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到學期末,安妮和吉爾伯特都升到了第五班,獲准開始學習「各門學科」的基礎——指的是拉丁文、幾何、法語和代數。

passages.original: In geometry Anne met her Waterloo.
passages.vernacular: 喺幾何上安妮遭遇咗佢嘅滑鐵盧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在幾何上安妮遭遇了她的滑鐵盧。

passages.original: “It’s perfectly awful stuff, Marilla,” she groaned.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係特別可怕嘅嘢,瑪麗拉,」佢呻吟道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是特別可怕的東西,瑪麗拉,」她呻吟道。

passages.original: “I’m sure I’ll never be able to make head or tail of it.
passages.vernacular: 「我肯定我永遠都弄不明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我肯定我永遠也弄不明白。

passages.original: There is no scope for imagination in it at all.
passages.vernacular: 裡面根本冇想像嘅餘地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 裡面根本沒有想像的餘地。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips says I’m the worst dunce he ever saw at it.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生講我係佢見過嘅喺呢方面最笨嘅蠢材。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生說我是他見過的在這方面最笨的蠢材。

passages.original: And Gil--I mean some of the others are so smart at it.
passages.vernacular: 而吉爾——我係講有些別嘅人,呢方面特別聰明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而吉爾——我是說有些別的人,這方面特別聰明。

passages.original: It is extremely mortifying, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 呢太丟人喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這太丟人了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: “Even Diana gets along better than I do.
passages.vernacular: 「連黛安娜都比我學得好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「連黛安娜都比我學得好。

passages.original: But I don’t mind being beaten by Diana.
passages.vernacular: 但我不介意被黛安娜打敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不介意被黛安娜打敗。

passages.original: Even although we meet as strangers now I still love her with an inextinguishable love.
passages.vernacular: 雖然我哋而家像陌生人一樣相遇,我仍然用不可磨滅嘅愛愛住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然我們現在像陌生人一樣相遇,我仍然用不可磨滅的愛愛著她。

passages.original: It makes me very sad at times to think about her.
passages.vernacular: 想到佢,有時我會好傷心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到她,有時我會很傷心。

passages.original: But really, Marilla, one can’t stay sad very long in such an interesting world, can one?”
passages.vernacular: 不過真嘅,瑪麗拉,人喺咁有趣嘅世界裡,唔可能傷心好久,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是真的,瑪麗拉,人在這麼有趣的世界裡,不可能傷心很久,是不是?」

chapters.title: Ch. XVIII Anne to the Rescue 第十八章:安妮來救援

passages.original: CH ALL things great are wound up with all things little.
passages.vernacular: 一切偉大嘅事都同一切渺小嘅事緊密相連。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切偉大的事都和一切渺小的事緊密相連。

passages.original: At first glance it might not seem that the decision of a certain Canadian Premier to include Prince Edward Island in a political tour could have much or anything to do with the fortunes of little Anne Shirley at Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 乍一睇,似乎加攞大某位總理決定把愛德華王子島列入一次政治巡迴訪問,跟綠色屋頂嘅小安妮·雪莉嘅命運唔會有多大關係,甚至毫無關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 乍一看,似乎加拿大某位總理決定把愛德華王子島列入一次政治巡迴訪問,跟綠色屋頂的小安妮·雪莉的命運不會有多大關係,甚至毫無關係。

passages.original: But it had.
passages.vernacular: 但佢確有關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它確有關係。

passages.original: It was a January the Premier came, to address his loyal supporters and such of his nonsupporters as chose to be present at the monster mass meeting held in Charlottetown.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一月,總理嚟到呢度,向佢忠實嘅支持者以及選擇出席嘅少數非支持者演講,喺夏洛特敦召開咗盛大嘅群眾集會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一月,總理來到這裡,向他忠實的支持者以及選擇出席的少數非支持者演說,在夏洛特敦召開了盛大的群眾集會。

passages.original: Most of the Avonlea people were on Premier’s side of politics; hence on the night of the meeting nearly all the men and a goodly proportion of the women had gone to town thirty miles away.
passages.vernacular: 大多數阿文利人都站喺總理一邊嘅政治立場;因此集會嘅嗰天晚上,幾乎所有男人同相當多嘅女人,都到咗三十英里外嘅城裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大多數阿文利人都站在總理一邊的政治立場;因此集會的那天晚上,幾乎所有男人和相當多的女人,都到了三十英里外的城裡。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel Lynde had gone too.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾·林德太太都去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾·林德太太也去了。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel Lynde was a red-hot politician and couldn’t have believed that the political rally could be carried through without her, although she was on the opposite side of politics.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾·林德太太係個熱烈嘅政治迷,儘管佢站喺對立嘅政治一邊,佢都不相信呢場政治集會冇佢能辦成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾·林德太太是個熱烈的政治迷,儘管她站在對立的政治一邊,她也不相信這場政治集會沒有她能辦成。

passages.original: So she went to town and took her husband--Thomas would be useful in looking after the horse--and Marilla Cuthbert with her.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢進城去喇,帶上咗佢嘅丈夫——托馬斯照睇馬會有用——仲有瑪麗拉·卡思伯特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以她進城去了,帶上了她的丈夫——托馬斯照看馬會有用——還有瑪麗拉·卡思伯特。

passages.original: Marilla had a sneaking interest in politics herself, and as she thought it might be her only chance to see a real live Premier, she promptly took it, leaving Anne and Matthew to keep house until her return the following day.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉自己都暗暗對政治感興趣,而且佢想呢或者係佢睇到一位活生生嘅總理嘅唯一機會,於是立即抓住喇,讓安妮同馬修睇家,直到第二天佢回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉自己也暗暗對政治感興趣,而且她想這也許是她看到一位活生生的總理的唯一機會,於是立即抓住了,讓安妮和馬修看家,直到第二天她回來。

passages.original: Hence, while Marilla and Mrs. Rachel were enjoying themselves hugely at the mass meeting, Anne and Matthew had the cheerful kitchen at Green Gables all to themselves.
passages.vernacular: 因此,瑪麗拉同雷切爾太太喺群眾集會上痛快地享受時,安妮同馬修獨自擁有綠色屋頂嗰間歡快嘅廚房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此,瑪麗拉和雷切爾太太在群眾集會上痛快地享受時,安妮和馬修獨自擁有綠色屋頂那間歡快的廚房。

passages.original: A bright fire was glowing in the old-fashioned Waterloo stove and blue-white frost crystals were shining on the windowpanes.
passages.vernacular: 老式嘅滑鐵盧爐子裡明亮嘅火喺燃燒,窗玻璃上閃住藍白色嘅霜花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老式的滑鐵盧爐子裡明亮的火在燃燒,窗玻璃上閃著藍白色的霜花。

passages.original: Matthew nodded over a Farmers’ Advocate on the sofa and Anne at the table studied her lessons with grim determination, despite sundry wistful glances at the clock shelf, where lay a new book that Jane Andrews had lent her that day.
passages.vernacular: 馬修喺沙發上對住一份《農民倡導者報》打盹,安妮喺桌邊以嚴峻嘅決心學習功課,儘管佢時不時惆悵地朝鐘架瞥一眼,嗰兒放住簡·安德魯斯嗰天借畀佢嘅一本新書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修在沙發上對著一份《農民倡導者報》打盹,安妮在桌邊以嚴峻的決心學習功課,儘管她時不時惆悵地朝鐘架瞥一眼,那兒放著簡·安德魯斯那天借給她的一本新書。

passages.original: Jane had assured her that it was warranted to produce any number of thrills, or words to that effect, and Anne’s fingers tingled to reach out for it.
passages.vernacular: 簡向佢保證,呢本書保證能產生任意多嘅顫慄,或類似嘅意思,安妮嘅手指發癢,好想伸手去攞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡向她保證,這本書保證能產生任意多的顫慄,或類似的意思,安妮的手指發癢,很想伸手去拿。

passages.original: But that would mean Gilbert Blythe’s triumph on the morrow.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰將意味住聽日吉爾伯特·布萊斯嘅勝利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那將意味著明天吉爾伯特·布萊斯的勝利。

passages.original: Anne turned her back on the clock shelf and tried to imagine it wasn’t there.
passages.vernacular: 安妮背對鐘架,試著想像佢不喺嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮背對鐘架,試著想像它不在那兒。

passages.original: “Matthew, did you ever study geometry when you went to school?”
passages.vernacular: 「馬修,您上學嘅時候學過幾何嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修,您上學的時候學過幾何嗎?」

passages.original: “Well now, no, I didn’t,” said Matthew, coming out of his doze with a start.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,冇,我冇學過,」馬修講,猛然從打盹中醒嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,沒有,我沒學過,」馬修說,猛然從打盹中醒來。

passages.original: “I wish you had,” sighed Anne, “because then you’d be able to sympathize with me.
passages.vernacular: 「我真希望您學過,」安妮嘆道,「因為嗰樣您就能同情我喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真希望您學過,」安妮嘆道,「因為那樣您就能同情我了。

passages.original: You can’t sympathize properly if you’ve never studied it.
passages.vernacular: 你要係從冇學過,就唔能夠恰當地同情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要是從沒學過,就不能恰當地同情。

passages.original: It is casting a cloud over my whole life.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀我整個生活蒙上咗一層陰影。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它給我整個生活蒙上了一層陰影。

passages.original: I’m such a dunce at it, Matthew.”
passages.vernacular: 我喺呢方面係個笨蛋,馬修。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在這方面是個笨蛋,馬修。」

passages.original: “Well now, I dunno,” said Matthew soothingly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔知道,」馬修安慰地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不知道,」馬修安慰地說。

passages.original: “I guess you’re all right at anything.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇你乜嘢都行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看你什麼都行。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips told me last week in Blair’s store at Carmody that you was the smartest scholar in school and was making rapid progress.
passages.vernacular: 上星期菲利普斯先生喺卡莫迪嘅布萊爾店裡告訴我,你係學校裡最聰明嘅學生,進步好快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上星期菲利普斯先生在卡莫迪的布萊爾店裡告訴我,你是學校裡最聰明的學生,進步很快。

passages.original: ‘Rapid progress’ was his very words.
passages.vernacular: 『進步好快』係佢嘅原話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『進步很快』是他的原話。

passages.original: There’s them as runs down Teddy Phillips and says he ain’t much of a teacher, but I guess he’s all right.”
passages.vernacular: 有人貶低泰迪·菲利普斯,講佢算不上乜嘢老師,但我睇佢挺好嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人貶低泰迪·菲利普斯,說他算不上什麼老師,但我看他挺好的。」

passages.original: Matthew would have thought anyone who praised Anne was “all right.”
passages.vernacular: 馬修會認為任何稱讚安妮嘅人都「挺好」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修會認為任何稱讚安妮的人都「挺好」。

passages.original: “I’m sure I’d get on better with geometry if only he wouldn’t change the letters,” complained Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我肯定只要佢不改字母,我就能更好地學幾何,」安妮抱怨道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我肯定只要他不改字母,我就能更好地學幾何,」安妮抱怨道。

passages.original: “I learn the proposition off by heart and then he draws it on the blackboard and puts different letters from what are in the book and I get all mixed up.
passages.vernacular: 「我把命題背得滾瓜爛熟,然後佢喺黑板上畫出嚟,字母同書上嘅不一樣,我就全搞亂喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我把命題背得滾瓜爛熟,然後他在黑板上畫出來,字母和書上的不一樣,我就全搞亂了。

passages.original: I don’t think a teacher should take such a mean advantage, do you?
passages.vernacular: 我覺得老師不該咁樣卑鄙地占便宜,您講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得老師不該這樣卑鄙地占便宜,您說呢?

passages.original: We’re studying agriculture now and I’ve found out at last what makes the roads red.
passages.vernacular: 我哋而家喺學農業,我終於弄明白咗係乜嘢讓路變紅嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們現在在學農業,我終於弄明白了是什麼讓路變紅的。

passages.original: It’s a great comfort.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個好大嘅安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個很大的安慰。

passages.original: I wonder how Marilla and Mrs. Lynde are enjoying themselves.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道瑪麗拉同林德太太玩得點樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道瑪麗拉和林德太太玩得怎麼樣。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says Canada is going to the dogs the way things are being run at Ottawa and that it’s an awful warning to the electors.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講,渥太華嗰邊嘅事咁樣管下去,加攞大就要完蛋喇,呢對選民係一個可怕嘅警告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說,渥太華那邊的事這樣管下去,加拿大就要完蛋了,這對選民是一個可怕的警告。

passages.original: She says if women were allowed to vote we would soon see a blessed change.
passages.vernacular: 佢講如果允許婦女投票,我哋好快就會睇到可喜嘅改變。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說如果允許婦女投票,我們很快就會看到可喜的改變。

passages.original: What way do you vote, Matthew?”
passages.vernacular: 您投邊一黨,馬修?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您投哪一黨,馬修?」

passages.original: “Conservative,” said Matthew promptly.
passages.vernacular: 「保守黨,」馬修即刻講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「保守黨,」馬修立刻說。

passages.original: To vote Conservative was part of Matthew’s religion.
passages.vernacular: 投保守黨係馬修宗教信仰嘅一部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 投保守黨是馬修宗教信仰的一部分。

passages.original: “Then I’m Conservative too,” said Anne decidedly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我都係保守黨,」安妮堅決地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我也是保守黨,」安妮堅決地說。

passages.original: “I’m glad because Gil--because some of the boys in school are Grits.
passages.vernacular: 「我好高興,因為吉爾——因為學校里有些男孩係自由黨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很高興,因為吉爾——因為學校里有些男孩是自由黨。

passages.original: I guess Mr. Phillips is a Grit too because Prissy Andrews’s father is one, and Ruby Gillis says that when a man is courting he always has to agree with the girl’s mother in religion and her father in politics.
passages.vernacular: 我猜菲利普斯先生都係自由黨,因為普麗茜·安德魯斯嘅父親係,而露比·吉利斯講,一個男人追求女孩時,總得喺宗教上同意佢母親,喺政治上同意佢父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我猜菲利普斯先生也是自由黨,因為普麗茜·安德魯斯的父親是,而露比·吉利斯說,一個男人追求女孩時,總得在宗教上同意她母親,在政治上同意她父親。

passages.original: Is that true, Matthew?”
passages.vernacular: 係真嘅嗎,馬修?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是真的嗎,馬修?」

passages.original: “Well now, I dunno,” said Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔知道,」馬修講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不知道,」馬修說。

passages.original: “Did you ever go courting, Matthew?”
passages.vernacular: 「您追求過人嗎,馬修?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您追求過人嗎,馬修?」

passages.original: “Well now, no, I dunno’s I ever did,” said Matthew, who had certainly never thought of such a thing in his whole existence.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,冇,我唔知道我追求過冇,」馬修講,佢呢輩子當然從冇想過呢種事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,沒有,我不知道我追求過沒有,」馬修說,他這輩子當然從沒想過這種事。

passages.original: Anne reflected with her chin in her hands.
passages.vernacular: 安妮雙手托住下巴沉思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮雙手托著下巴沉思。

passages.original: “It must be rather interesting, don’t you think, Matthew?
passages.vernacular: 「嗰一定相當有趣,您不覺得嗎,馬修?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那一定相當有趣,您不覺得嗎,馬修?

passages.original: Ruby Gillis says when she grows up she’s going to have ever so many beaus on the string and have them all crazy about her; but I think that would be too exciting.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯講佢長大後要有好多好多追求者圍住佢團團轉,讓佢哋都為佢著迷;但我覺得嗰太刺激喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯說她長大後要有好多好多追求者圍著她團團轉,讓他們都為她著迷;但我覺得那太刺激了。

passages.original: I’d rather have just one in his right mind.
passages.vernacular: 我寧可只有一個頭腦清醒嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧可只有一個頭腦清醒的。

passages.original: But Ruby Gillis knows a great deal about such matters because she has so many big sisters, and Mrs. Lynde says the Gillis girls have gone off like hot cakes.
passages.vernacular: 但係露比·吉利斯對呢類事情知道得好多,因為佢有咁多大姐姐,林德太太講吉利斯家嘅女孩哋都像熱蛋糕一樣被搶走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是露比·吉利斯對這類事情知道得很多,因為她有那麼多大姐姐,林德太太說吉利斯家的女孩們都像熱蛋糕一樣被搶走了。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips goes up to see Prissy Andrews nearly every evening.
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生幾乎每天晚上都去睇普麗茜·安德魯斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生幾乎每天晚上都去看普麗茜·安德魯斯。

passages.original: He says it is to help her with her lessons but Miranda Sloane is studying for Queen’s too, and I should think she needed help a lot more than Prissy because she’s ever so much stupider, but he never goes to help her in the evenings at all.
passages.vernacular: 佢講係去幫佢做功課,不過米蘭達·斯隆都喺準備考女王學院,我覺得佢比普麗茜更需要幫助,因為佢笨得多,但佢晚上從不去幫佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說是去幫她做功課,可是米蘭達·斯隆也在準備考女王學院,我覺得她比普麗茜更需要幫助,因為她笨得多,但他晚上從不去幫她。

passages.original: There are a great many things in this world that I can’t understand very well, Matthew.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個世界上有好多事情我不太明白,馬修。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個世界上有很多事情我不太明白,馬修。」

passages.original: “Well now, I dunno as I comprehend them all myself,” acknowledged Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔知道我自己係唔係全都懂,」馬修承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不知道我自己是不是全都懂,」馬修承認。

passages.original: “Well, I suppose I must finish up my lessons.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,我想我得把功課做完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,我想我得把功課做完。

passages.original: I won’t allow myself to open that new book Jane lent me until I’m through.
passages.vernacular: 做完之前,我不許自己翻開簡借畀我嘅嗰本新書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 做完之前,我不許自己翻開簡借給我的那本新書。

passages.original: But it’s a terrible temptation, Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 但呢個係個可怕嘅誘惑,馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這是個可怕的誘惑,馬修。

passages.original: Even when I turn my back on it I can see it there just as plain.
passages.vernacular: 即使我背對住佢,都能清清楚楚地睇到佢喺嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使我背對著它,也能清清楚楚地看到它在那兒。

passages.original: Jane said she cried herself sick over it.
passages.vernacular: 簡講佢睇得哭到生病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡說她看得哭到生病。

passages.original: I love a book that makes me cry.
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意讓我哭嘅書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡讓我哭的書。

passages.original: But I think I’ll carry that book into the sitting room and lock it in the jam closet and give you the key.
passages.vernacular: 不過我想我要把嗰本書攞到起居室去,鎖喺果醬櫃裡,把鑰匙畀您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我想我要把那本書拿到起居室去,鎖在果醬櫃裡,把鑰匙給您。

passages.original: And you must not give it to me, Matthew, until my lessons are done, not even if I implore you on my bended knees.
passages.vernacular: 您決唔能夠把佢畀我,馬修,直到我嘅功課做完,即使我跪下嚟求您都不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您決不能把它給我,馬修,直到我的功課做完,即使我跪下來求您也不行。

passages.original: It’s all very well to say resist temptation, but it’s ever so much easier to resist it if you can’t get the key.
passages.vernacular: 講要抵禦誘惑固然好,但如果你攞唔到鑰匙,抵禦起嚟就容易得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說要抵禦誘惑固然好,但如果你拿不到鑰匙,抵禦起來就容易得多。

passages.original: And then shall I run down the cellar and get some russets, Matthew?
passages.vernacular: 然後我跑下地窖去攞些褐皮蘋果,好嗎,馬修?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我跑下地窖去拿些褐皮蘋果,好嗎,馬修?

passages.original: Wouldn’t you like some russets?”
passages.vernacular: 您想唔想食些褐皮蘋果?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您想不想吃些褐皮蘋果?」

passages.original: “Well now, I dunno but what I would,” said Matthew, who never ate russets but knew Anne’s weakness for them.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我講不定想,」馬修講,佢從不食褐皮蘋果,但知道安妮愛食。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我說不定想,」馬修說,他從不吃褐皮蘋果,但知道安妮愛吃。

passages.original: Just as Anne emerged triumphantly from the cellar with her plateful of russets came the sound of flying footsteps on the icy board walk outside and the next moment the kitchen door was flung open and in rushed Diana Barry, white faced and breathless, with a shawl wrapped hastily around her head.
passages.vernacular: 就喺安妮端住一盤褐皮蘋果得意洋洋地從地窖裡出嚟時,外面結冰嘅木板人行道上傳嚟飛奔嘅腳步聲,接住廚房門被猛地推開,黛安娜·巴里衝咗進嚟,臉色蒼白,氣喘吁吁,頭上匆忙裹住一條披巾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在安妮端著一盤褐皮蘋果得意洋洋地從地窖裡出來時,外面結冰的木板人行道上傳來飛奔的腳步聲,接著廚房門被猛地推開,黛安娜·巴里衝了進來,臉色蒼白,氣喘吁吁,頭上匆忙裹著一條披巾。

passages.original: Anne promptly let go of her candle and plate in her surprise, and plate, candle, and apples crashed together down the cellar ladder and were found at the bottom embedded in melted grease, the next day, by Marilla, who gathered them up and thanked mercy the house hadn’t been set on fire.
passages.vernacular: 安妮一驚,即刻放開咗蠟燭同盤子,盤子、蠟燭同蘋果一起摔下地窖梯子,第二天被瑪麗拉發現,佢哋嵌喺融化嘅油脂裡,佢把佢哋撿起嚟,謝天謝地冇把房子燒住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮一驚,立刻放開了蠟燭和盤子,盤子、蠟燭和蘋果一起摔下地窖梯子,第二天被瑪麗拉發現,它們嵌在融化的油脂裡,她把它們撿起來,謝天謝地沒有把房子燒著。

passages.original: “Whatever is the matter, Diana?” cried Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「到底點喇,黛安娜?」安妮喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「到底怎麼了,黛安娜?」安妮喊道。

passages.original: “Has your mother relented at last?”
passages.vernacular: 「你媽媽終於消氣咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你媽媽終於消氣了嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, Anne, do come quick,” implored Diana nervously.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,安妮,快嚟,」黛安娜緊張地懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,安妮,快來,」黛安娜緊張地懇求道。

passages.original: “Minnie May is awful sick--she’s got croup.
passages.vernacular: 「明妮·梅病得好重——佢得咗哮吼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「明妮·梅病得很重——她得了哮吼。

passages.original: Young Mary Joe says--and Father and Mother are away to town and there’s nobody to go for the doctor.
passages.vernacular: 小瑪麗·喬講——而爸爸媽媽進城去喇,冇人去請醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小瑪麗·喬說——而爸爸媽媽進城去了,沒人去請醫生。

passages.original: Minnie May is awful bad and Young Mary Joe doesn’t know what to do--and oh, Anne, I’m so scared!”
passages.vernacular: 明妮·梅好嚴重,小瑪麗·喬唔知道點算——哦,安妮,我好害怕!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明妮·梅很嚴重,小瑪麗·喬不知道怎麼辦——哦,安妮,我好害怕!」

passages.original: Matthew, without a word, reached out for cap and coat, slipped past Diana and away into the darkness of the yard.
passages.vernacular: 馬修一言不發,伸手攞咗帽子同外套,從黛安娜身邊溜過,消失喺院子嘅黑暗中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修一言不發,伸手拿了帽子和外套,從黛安娜身邊溜過,消失在院子的黑暗中。

passages.original: “He’s gone to harness the sorrel mare to go to Carmody for the doctor,” said Anne, who was hurrying on hood and jacket.
passages.vernacular: 「佢去畀栗色母馬套車,去卡莫迪請醫生喇,」安妮講,佢正匆忙戴上風帽、穿上夾克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他去給栗色母馬套車,去卡莫迪請醫生了,」安妮說,她正匆忙戴上風帽、穿上夾克。

passages.original: “I know it as well as if he’d said so.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,就像佢講咗一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,就像他說了一樣。

passages.original: Matthew and I are such kindred spirits I can read his thoughts without words at all.”
passages.vernacular: 馬修同我係咁樣志同道合,我完全唔使言語就能讀懂佢嘅想法。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修和我是這樣志同道合,我完全不用言語就能讀懂他的想法。」

passages.original: “I don’t believe he’ll find the doctor at Carmody,” sobbed Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我不相信佢能喺卡莫迪找到醫生,」黛安娜抽泣道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不相信他能在卡莫迪找到醫生,」黛安娜抽泣道。

passages.original: “I know that Dr. Blair went to town and I guess Dr. Spencer would go too.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道布萊爾醫生進城去喇,我想斯潘塞醫生都去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道布萊爾醫生進城去了,我想斯潘塞醫生也去了。

passages.original: Young Mary Joe never saw anybody with croup and Mrs. Lynde is away.
passages.vernacular: 小瑪麗·喬從冇見過邊個得哮吼,林德太太又不喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小瑪麗·喬從沒見過誰得哮吼,林德太太又不在。

passages.original: Oh, Anne!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,安妮!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,安妮!」

passages.original: “Don’t cry, Di,” said Anne cheerily.
passages.vernacular: 「別哭,迪,」安妮愉快地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別哭,迪,」安妮愉快地說。

passages.original: “I know exactly what to do for croup.
passages.vernacular: 「我確切知道哮吼該點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確切知道哮吼該怎麼辦。

passages.original: You forget that Mrs. Hammond had twins three times.
passages.vernacular: 你忘咗哈蒙德太太生咗三次雙胞胎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你忘了哈蒙德太太生了三次雙胞胎。

passages.original: When you look after three pairs of twins you naturally get a lot of experience.
passages.vernacular: 你照睇三對雙胞胎,自然會有好多經驗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你照看三對雙胞胎,自然會有很多經驗。

passages.original: They all had croup regularly.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都定期得哮吼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們都定期得哮吼。

passages.original: Just wait till I get the ipecac bottle--you mayn’t have any at your house.
passages.vernacular: 等我攞吐根瓶——你哋家可能冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我拿吐根瓶——你們家可能沒有。

passages.original: Come on now.”
passages.vernacular: 而家嚟吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在來吧。」
