passages.original: The two little girls hastened out hand in hand and hurried through Lover’s Lane and across the crusted field beyond, for the snow was too deep to go by the shorter wood way.
passages.vernacular: 兩個小女孩手拉手匆匆跑出去,穿過情人小徑,越過嗰邊結咗硬殼嘅田野,因為雪太深,唔能夠走更近嘅林間小路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個小女孩手拉手匆匆跑出去,穿過情人小徑,越過那邊結了硬殼的田野,因為雪太深,不能走更近的林間小路。

passages.original: Anne, although sincerely sorry for Minnie May, was far from being insensible to the romance of the situation and to the sweetness of once more sharing that romance with a kindred spirit.
passages.vernacular: 安妮雖然真心為明妮·梅擔憂,但對呢情景嘅浪漫並非無動於衷,並且為能再次同知心朋友分享呢浪漫而感到甜蜜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮雖然真心為明妮·梅擔憂,但對這情景的浪漫並非無動於衷,並且為能再次與知心朋友分享這浪漫而感到甜蜜。

passages.original: The night was clear and frosty, all ebony of shadow and silver of snowy slope; big stars were shining over the silent fields; here and there the dark pointed firs stood up with snow powdering their branches and the wind whistling through them.
passages.vernacular: 夜色晴朗而寒冷,陰影係烏木般嘅黑,雪坡係銀白;大星星喺寂靜嘅田野上閃亮;呢度嗰度,黑色尖頂嘅冷杉挺立住,枝上落住粉末般嘅雪,風從中呼嘯而過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜色晴朗而寒冷,陰影是烏木般的黑,雪坡是銀白;大星星在寂靜的田野上閃亮;這裡那裡,黑色尖頂的冷杉挺立著,枝上落著粉末般的雪,風從中呼嘯而過。

passages.original: Anne thought it was truly delightful to go skimming through all this mystery and loveliness with your bosom friend who had been so long estranged.
passages.vernacular: 安妮覺得,同久已疏遠嘅知心朋友一起,輕快地穿過呢一切神祕同美麗,真係太愉快喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮覺得,與久已疏遠的知心朋友一起,輕快地穿過這一切神祕與美麗,真是太愉快了。

passages.original: Minnie May, aged three, was really very sick.
passages.vernacular: 三歲嘅明妮·梅真嘅病得好重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三歲的明妮·梅真的病得很重。

passages.original: She lay on the kitchen sofa feverish and restless, while her hoarse breathing could be heard all over the house.
passages.vernacular: 佢躺喺廚房沙發上,發住燒,躁動不安,佢嘶啞嘅呼吸聲喺整個房子裡都能聽見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她躺在廚房沙發上,發著燒,躁動不安,她嘶啞的呼吸聲在整個房子裡都能聽見。

passages.original: Young Mary Joe, a buxom, broad-faced French girl from the creek, whom Mrs. Barry had engaged to stay with the children during her absence, was helpless and bewildered, quite incapable of thinking what to do, or doing it if she thought of it.
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太雇嚟喺佢外出期間照睇細路嘅,係小瑪麗·喬,一個從溪邊嚟嘅胖壯、寬臉盤嘅法國女孩,佢無助而驚慌,完全唔能夠想該點算,即使想到咗都做不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太雇來在她外出期間照看孩子的,是小瑪麗·喬,一個從溪邊來的胖壯、寬臉盤的法國女孩,她無助而驚慌,完全不能想該怎麼辦,即使想到了也做不了。

passages.original: Anne went to work with skill and promptness.
passages.vernacular: 安妮熟練而迅速地動手喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮熟練而迅速地動手了。

passages.original: “Minnie May has croup all right; she’s pretty bad, but I’ve seen them worse.
passages.vernacular: 「明妮·梅確實係哮吼;佢病得好重,不過我見過更重嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「明妮·梅確實是哮吼;她病得很重,不過我見過更重的。

passages.original: First we must have lots of hot water.
passages.vernacular: 首先我哋必須有好多熱水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先我們必須有很多熱水。

passages.original: I declare, Diana, there isn’t more than a cupful in the kettle!
passages.vernacular: 我敢講,黛安娜,水壺裡連一杯都冇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢說,黛安娜,水壺裡連一杯都沒有!

passages.original: There, I’ve filled it up, and, Mary Joe, you may put some wood in the stove.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,我已經灌滿喇,瑪麗·喬,你可以往爐子里添些柴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,我已經灌滿了,瑪麗·喬,你可以往爐子里添些柴。

passages.original: I don’t want to hurt your feelings but it seems to me you might have thought of this before if you’d any imagination.
passages.vernacular: 我唔想傷你嘅感情,但我覺得,如果你有想像力,你本可以早點想到呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不想傷你的感情,但我覺得,如果你有想像力,你本可以早點想到這一點。

passages.original: Now, I’ll undress Minnie May and put her to bed and you try to find some soft flannel cloths, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 而家,我畀明妮·梅脫衣服,讓佢上床,黛安娜你去找些柔軟嘅法蘭絨布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,我給明妮·梅脫衣服,讓她上床,黛安娜你去找些柔軟的法蘭絨布。

passages.original: I’m going to give her a dose of ipecac first of all.”
passages.vernacular: 我首先要畀佢一劑吐根。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我首先要給她一劑吐根。」

passages.original: Minnie May did not take kindly to the ipecac but Anne had not brought up three pairs of twins for nothing.
passages.vernacular: 明妮·梅不太願意食吐根,但安妮帶三對雙胞胎可唔係白帶嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明妮·梅不太願意吃吐根,但安妮帶三對雙胞胎可不是白帶的。

passages.original: Down that ipecac went, not only once, but many times during the long, anxious night when the two little girls worked patiently over the suffering Minnie May, and Young Mary Joe, honestly anxious to do all she could, kept up a roaring fire and heated more water than would have been needed for a hospital of croupy babies.
passages.vernacular: 嗰吐根被灌咗下去,不止一次,而係喺漫長焦急嘅夜裡灌咗許多次,兩個小女孩耐心地照料住受苦嘅明妮·梅,而小瑪麗·喬真誠地急於盡力幫忙,把火燒得熊熊旺旺,燒嘅熱水比一所收治哮吼嬰兒嘅醫院需要嘅仲多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那吐根被灌了下去,不止一次,而是在漫長焦急的夜裡灌了許多次,兩個小女孩耐心地照料著受苦的明妮·梅,而小瑪麗·喬真誠地急於盡力幫忙,把火燒得熊熊旺旺,燒的熱水比一所收治哮吼嬰兒的醫院需要的還多。

passages.original: It was three o’clock when Matthew came with a doctor, for he had been obliged to go all the way to Spencervale for one.
passages.vernacular: 馬修帶住一位醫生來到時已係凌晨三點,因為佢唔得不一直到斯潘塞韋爾去請。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修帶著一位醫生來到時已是凌晨三點,因為他不得不一直到斯潘塞韋爾去請。

passages.original: But the pressing need for assistance was past.
passages.vernacular: 但急需幫助嘅時刻已經過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但急需幫助的時刻已經過去了。

passages.original: Minnie May was much better and was sleeping soundly.
passages.vernacular: 明妮·梅好多喇,瞓得好沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明妮·梅好多了,睡得很沉。

passages.original: “I was awfully near giving up in despair,” explained Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我差點就絕望地放棄喇,」安妮解釋道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我差點就絕望地放棄了,」安妮解釋道。

passages.original: “She got worse and worse until she was sicker than ever the Hammond twins were, even the last pair.
passages.vernacular: 「佢越嚟越重,直到比哈蒙德家嘅雙胞胎病得仲重,連最後嗰一對都不如。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她越來越重,直到比哈蒙德家的雙胞胎病得還重,連最後那一對也不如。

passages.original: I actually thought she was going to choke to death.
passages.vernacular: 我真嘅以為佢要窒息而死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真的以為她要窒息而死了。

passages.original: I gave her every drop of ipecac in that bottle and when the last dose went down I said to myself--not to Diana or Young Mary Joe, because I didn’t want to worry them any more than they were worried, but I had to say it to myself just to relieve my feelings--‘This is the last lingering hope and I fear, tis a vain one.’
passages.vernacular: 我把嗰瓶裡嘅吐根一滴不剩地畀佢灌咗下去,最後一劑下去嘅時候我對自己講——唔係對黛安娜或小瑪麗·喬,因為我唔想讓佢哋比已經有嘅擔心更擔心,但我必須對自己講講以舒緩感情——『呢個係最後嘅苟延殘喘嘅希望,我恐怕係徒勞嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把那瓶裡的吐根一滴不剩地給她灌了下去,最後一劑下去的時候我對自己說——不是對黛安娜或小瑪麗·喬,因為我不想讓她們比已經有的擔心更擔心,但我必須對自己說說以舒緩感情——『這是最後的苟延殘喘的希望,我恐怕是徒勞的。』

passages.original: But in about three minutes she coughed up the phlegm and began to get better right away.
passages.vernacular: 但大約三分鐘後,佢咳出咗痰,即刻開始好轉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但大約三分鐘後,她咳出了痰,馬上開始好轉。

passages.original: You must just imagine my relief, doctor, because I can’t express it in words.
passages.vernacular: 您得想像一下我嘅寬慰,醫生,因為我無法用言語表達。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您得想像一下我的寬慰,醫生,因為我無法用言語表達。

passages.original: You know there are some things that cannot be expressed in words.”
passages.vernacular: 您知道,有些事係無法用言語表達嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道,有些事是無法用言語表達的。」

passages.original: “Yes, I know,” nodded the doctor.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我知道,」醫生點頭講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我知道,」醫生點頭說。

passages.original: He looked at Anne as if he were thinking some things about her that couldn’t be expressed in words.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇住安妮,好像喺想關於佢嘅啲無法用言語表達嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看著安妮,好像在想關於她的一些無法用言語表達的事。

passages.original: Later on, however, he expressed them to Mr. and Mrs. Barry.
passages.vernacular: 不過,後來佢向巴里夫婦表達咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,後來他向巴里夫婦表達了出來。

passages.original: “That little redheaded girl they have over at Cuthbert’s is as smart as they make ‘em.
passages.vernacular: 「卡思伯特家嗰個紅頭髮小女孩聰明絕頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「卡思伯特家那個紅頭髮小女孩聰明絕頂。

passages.original: I tell you she saved that baby’s life, for it would have been too late by the time I got there.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你哋,佢救咗嗰個嬰兒嘅命,因為等我趕到就太晚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你們,她救了那個嬰兒的命,因為等我趕到就太晚了。

passages.original: She seems to have a skill and presence of mind perfectly wonderful in a child of her age.
passages.vernacular: 佢似乎有一種對佢嗰個年齡嘅細路來講完全令人驚歎嘅技能同鎮定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她似乎有一種對她那個年齡的孩子來說完全令人驚歎的技能和鎮定。

passages.original: I never saw anything like the eyes of her when she was explaining the case to me.”
passages.vernacular: 佢向我講明病情時,佢嗰雙眼睛我從冇見過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她向我說明病情時,她那雙眼睛我從沒見過。」

passages.original: Anne had gone home in the wonderful, white-frosted winter morning, heavy eyed from loss of sleep, but still talking unweariedly to Matthew as they crossed the long white field and walked under the glittering fairy arch of the Lover’s Lane maples.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺神奇嘅、白霜覆蓋嘅冬日早晨回家,眼睛因缺覺而沉重,但仍不倦地對馬修講住話,佢哋穿過長長嘅白色田野,走喺情人小徑楓樹閃亮嘅仙境拱門下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在神奇的、白霜覆蓋的冬日早晨回家,眼睛因缺覺而沉重,但仍不倦地對馬修說著話,他們穿過長長的白色田野,走在情人小徑楓樹閃亮的仙境拱門下。

passages.original: “Oh, Matthew, isn’t it a wonderful morning?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,馬修,呢唔係個奇妙嘅早晨嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,馬修,這不是個奇妙的早晨嗎?

passages.original: The world looks like something God had just imagined for His own pleasure, doesn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 世界睇上去像係上帝為了自己嘅愉悅而啱啱想像出嚟嘅嘢,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 世界看上去像是上帝為了自己的愉悅而剛剛想像出來的東西,是不是?

passages.original: Those trees look as if I could blow them away with a breath--pouf!
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲樹睇起嚟好像我吹口氣就能把佢哋吹走——噗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些樹看起來好像我吹口氣就能把它們吹走——噗!

passages.original: I’m so glad I live in a world where there are white frosts, aren’t you?
passages.vernacular: 我太高興我生活喺有白霜嘅世界裡喇,您呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興我生活在有白霜的世界裡了,您呢?

passages.original: And I’m so glad Mrs. Hammond had three pairs of twins after all.
passages.vernacular: 我都太高興哈蒙德太太終究生咗三對雙胞胎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也太高興哈蒙德太太終究生了三對雙胞胎。

passages.original: If she hadn’t I mightn’t have known what to do for Minnie May.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢冇,我可能就唔知道該點救明妮·梅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她沒有,我可能就不知道該怎麼救明妮·梅。

passages.original: I’m real sorry I was ever cross with Mrs. Hammond for having twins.
passages.vernacular: 我真為當初因哈蒙德太太生雙胞胎而對佢生氣感到抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真為當初因哈蒙德太太生雙胞胎而對她生氣感到抱歉。

passages.original: But, oh, Matthew, I’m so sleepy.
passages.vernacular: 不過,哦,馬修,我好困。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,哦,馬修,我好困。

passages.original: I can’t go to school.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠去上學喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能去上學了。

passages.original: I just know I couldn’t keep my eyes open and I’d be so stupid.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我肯定睜不開眼睛,會變得好蠢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我肯定睜不開眼睛,會變得很蠢。

passages.original: But I hate to stay home, for Gil--some of the others will get head of the class, and it’s so hard to get up again--although of course the harder it is the more satisfaction you have when you do get up, haven’t you?”
passages.vernacular: 但我討厭待喺家裡,因為吉爾——別嘅有些人會攞到班上第一名,而要再爬起嚟係咁難——雖然當然越難,爬上去時就越有成就感,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我討厭待在家裡,因為吉爾——別的有些人會拿到班上第一名,而要再爬起來是那麼難——雖然當然越難,爬上去時就越有成就感,是不是?」

passages.original: “Well now, I guess you’ll manage all right,” said Matthew, looking at Anne’s white little face and the dark shadows under her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想你會應付得嚟嘅,」馬修講,睇住安妮蒼白嘅小臉同眼睛下嘅黑影。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想你會應付得來的,」馬修說,看著安妮蒼白的小臉和眼睛下的黑影。

passages.original: “You just go right to bed and have a good sleep.
passages.vernacular: 「你就直接去瞓一覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你就直接去睡一覺。

passages.original: I’ll do all the chores.”
passages.vernacular: 我嚟做所有雜活。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我來做所有雜活。」

passages.original: Anne accordingly went to bed and slept so long and soundly that it was well on in the white and rosy winter afternoon when she awoke and descended to the kitchen where Marilla, who had arrived home in the meantime, was sitting knitting.
passages.vernacular: 於是安妮上床瞓喇,瞓得又長又沉,等佢醒嚟走下樓到廚房時,已係白色同玫瑰色相間嘅冬日下午好晚嘅時候,瑪麗拉已經回嚟喇,正坐住織毛線。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是安妮上床睡了,睡得又長又沉,等她醒來走下樓到廚房時,已是白色與玫瑰色相間的冬日下午很晚的時候,瑪麗拉已經回來了,正坐著織毛線。

passages.original: “Oh, did you see the Premier?” exclaimed Anne at once.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,您睇到總理咗嗎?」安妮即刻喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,您看到總理了嗎?」安妮馬上喊道。

passages.original: “What did he look like Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢長乜嘢樣,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他長什麼樣,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: “Well, he never got to be Premier on account of his looks,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢做上總理可唔係靠長相,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,他做上總理可不是靠長相,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “Such a nose as that man had!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰人嘅鼻子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那人的鼻子!

passages.original: But he can speak.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢會演講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過他會演講。

passages.original: I was proud of being a Conservative.
passages.vernacular: 我為自己係保守黨而自豪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為自己是保守黨而自豪。

passages.original: Rachel Lynde, of course, being a Liberal, had no use for him.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾·林德當然係自由黨,不鍾意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾·林德當然是自由黨,不喜歡他。

passages.original: Your dinner is in the oven, Anne, and you can get yourself some blue plum preserve out of the pantry.
passages.vernacular: 安妮,你嘅午飯喺烤箱裡,你可以從食品櫃裡攞些藍李子蜜餞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮,你的午飯在烤箱裡,你可以從食品櫃裡拿些藍李子蜜餞。

passages.original: I guess you’re hungry.
passages.vernacular: 我想你餓喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你餓了。

passages.original: Matthew has been telling me about last night.
passages.vernacular: 馬修一直喺跟我講琴晚嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修一直在跟我說昨晚的事。

passages.original: I must say it was fortunate you knew what to do.
passages.vernacular: 我必須講,你知道該點算,真係幸運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須說,你知道該怎麼辦,真是幸運。

passages.original: I wouldn’t have had any idea myself, for I never saw a case of croup.
passages.vernacular: 我自己係啲辦法都冇,因為我從冇見過哮吼嘅病例。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己是一點辦法也沒有,因為我從沒見過哮吼的病例。

passages.original: There now, never mind talking till you’ve had your dinner.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,食完午飯再講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,吃完午飯再說話。

passages.original: I can tell by the look of you that you’re just full up with speeches, but they’ll keep.”
passages.vernacular: 我從你嘅樣子睇得出,你滿肚子都係話,但佢哋唔會跑嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從你的樣子看得出,你滿肚子都是話,但它們不會跑的。」

passages.original: Marilla had something to tell Anne, but she did not tell it just then for she knew if she did Anne’s consequent excitement would lift her clear out of the region of such material matters as appetite or dinner.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉有事要告訴安妮,但佢冇即刻講,因為佢知道如果講喇,安妮隨之而嚟嘅興奮會把佢從食慾或午飯呢類物質問題嘅領域完全托出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉有事要告訴安妮,但她沒有馬上說,因為她知道如果說了,安妮隨之而來的興奮會把她從食慾或午飯這類物質問題的領域完全托出去。

passages.original: Not until Anne had finished her saucer of blue plums did Marilla say:
passages.vernacular: 直到安妮食完佢嗰碟藍李子,瑪麗拉才講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到安妮吃完她那碟藍李子,瑪麗拉才說:

passages.original: “Mrs. Barry was here this afternoon, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「巴里太太今日下午嚟過,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴里太太今天下午來過,安妮。

passages.original: She wanted to see you, but I wouldn’t wake you up.
passages.vernacular: 佢想見你,但我唔願叫醒你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她想見你,但我不願叫醒你。

passages.original: She says you saved Minnie May’s life, and she is very sorry she acted as she did in that affair of the currant wine.
passages.vernacular: 佢講你救咗明妮·梅嘅命,佢好抱歉喺醋栗酒嗰件事上嗰樣對待你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說你救了明妮·梅的命,她很抱歉在醋栗酒那件事上那樣對待你。

passages.original: She says she knows now you didn’t mean to set Diana drunk, and she hopes you’ll forgive her and be good friends with Diana again.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢而家知道你唔係有意灌醉黛安娜嘅,佢希望你原諒佢,並再次同黛安娜做好朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她現在知道你不是有意灌醉黛安娜的,她希望你原諒她,並再次和黛安娜做好朋友。

passages.original: You’re to go over this evening if you like for Diana can’t stir outside the door on account of a bad cold she caught last night.
passages.vernacular: 你要係願意,今晚可以過去,因為黛安娜琴晚得咗重感冒,出不咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要是願意,今晚可以過去,因為黛安娜昨晚得了重感冒,出不了門。

passages.original: Now, Anne Shirley, for pity’s sake don’t fly up into the air.”
passages.vernacular: 而家,安妮·雪莉,睇喺老天嘅份上,別高興得飛上天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,安妮·雪莉,看在老天的份上,別高興得飛上天。」

passages.original: The warning seemed not unnecessary, so uplifted and aerial was Anne’s expression and attitude as she sprang to her feet, her face irradiated with the flame of her spirit.
passages.vernacular: 呢個警告似乎唔係冇必要嘅,因為安妮跳起嚟時,佢嘅表情同姿態如此高揚、輕盈,臉上被佢精神之火照得通亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個警告似乎不是沒必要的,因為安妮跳起來時,她的表情和姿態如此高揚、輕盈,臉上被她精神之火照得通亮。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, can I go right now--without washing my dishes?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我而家就能去嗎——不洗碗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我現在就能去嗎——不洗碗?

passages.original: I’ll wash them when I come back, but I cannot tie myself down to anything so unromantic as dishwashing at this thrilling moment.”
passages.vernacular: 我回嚟再洗,但喺呢激動人心嘅時刻,我無法讓自己被洗碗咁冇浪漫情調嘅事束縛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我回來再洗,但在這激動人心的時刻,我無法讓自己被洗碗這麼沒有浪漫情調的事束縛。」

passages.original: “Yes, yes, run along,” said Marilla indulgently.
passages.vernacular: 「好,好,去吧,」瑪麗拉縱容地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,好,去吧,」瑪麗拉縱容地說。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley--are you crazy?
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉——你瘋咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉——你瘋了嗎?

passages.original: Come back this instant and put something on you.
passages.vernacular: 即刻回嚟,穿件嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上回來,穿件東西。

passages.original: I might as well call to the wind.
passages.vernacular: 我仲不如對風講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還不如對風說話。

passages.original: She’s gone without a cap or wrap.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇戴帽子冇披外衣就走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她沒戴帽子沒披外衣就走了。

passages.original: Look at her tearing through the orchard with her hair streaming.
passages.vernacular: 睇佢披散住頭髮從果園裡飛奔而過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看她披散著頭髮從果園裡飛奔而過。

passages.original: It’ll be a mercy if she doesn’t catch her death of cold.”
passages.vernacular: 要係佢冇凍死就係萬幸喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是她沒凍死就是萬幸了。」

passages.original: Anne came dancing home in the purple winter twilight across the snowy places.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺紫色嘅冬日暮色中,穿過積雪嘅地方,翩翩跳舞住回到家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在紫色的冬日暮色中,穿過積雪的地方,翩翩跳舞著回到家。

passages.original: Afar in the southwest was the great shimmering, pearl-like sparkle of an evening star in a sky that was pale golden and ethereal rose over gleaming white spaces and dark glens of spruce.
passages.vernacular: 遠遠嘅西南天空中,一顆閃爍嘅、珍珠般嘅晚星巨大地發住光,天空係淡金色同空靈嘅玫瑰色,映照住閃亮嘅白色空地同雲杉嘅黑色峽谷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遠遠的西南天空中,一顆閃爍的、珍珠般的晚星巨大地發著光,天空是淡金色和空靈的玫瑰色,映照著閃亮的白色空地和雲杉的黑色峽谷。

passages.original: The tinkles of sleigh bells among the snowy hills came like elfin chimes through the frosty air, but their music was not sweeter than the song in Anne’s heart and on her lips.
passages.vernacular: 雪橇鈴鐺嘅叮噹聲從雪山間傳嚟,像精靈嘅鐘聲穿過寒冷嘅空氣,但佢哋嘅音樂比不上安妮心裡同嘴上嘅歌更甜美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪橇鈴鐺的叮噹聲從雪山間傳來,像精靈的鐘聲穿過寒冷的空氣,但它們的音樂比不上安妮心裡和嘴上的歌更甜美。

passages.original: “You see before you a perfectly happy person, Marilla,” she announced.
passages.vernacular: 「你面前係一個完全幸福嘅人,瑪麗拉,」佢宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你面前是一個完全幸福的人,瑪麗拉,」她宣布。

passages.original: “I’m perfectly happy--yes, in spite of my red hair.
passages.vernacular: 「我完全幸福——係嘅,儘管我係紅頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我完全幸福——是的,儘管我是紅頭髮。

passages.original: Just at present I have a soul above red hair.
passages.vernacular: 此刻我嘅靈魂超越咗紅頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此刻我的靈魂超越了紅頭髮。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry kissed me and cried and said she was so sorry and she could never repay me.
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太吻咗我,哭喇,講佢好抱歉,講佢永遠無法報答我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太吻了我,哭了,說她很抱歉,說她永遠無法報答我。

passages.original: I felt fearfully embarrassed, Marilla, but I just said as politely as I could, ‘I have no hard feelings for you, Mrs. Barry.
passages.vernacular: 我感到極其尷尬,瑪麗拉,但我只係盡可能禮貌地講:『我對您冇怨恨,巴里太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感到極其尷尬,瑪麗拉,但我只是盡可能禮貌地說:『我對您沒有怨恨,巴里太太。

passages.original: I assure you once for all that I did not mean to intoxicate Diana and henceforth I shall cover the past with the mantle of oblivion.’
passages.vernacular: 我向您一次性保證,我並唔係想灌醉黛安娜,從此我將用遺忘嘅斗篷掩蓋過去。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向您一次性保證,我並不是想灌醉黛安娜,從此我將用遺忘的斗篷掩蓋過去。』

passages.original: That was a pretty dignified way of speaking wasn’t it, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係挺有尊嚴嘅講話方式,係唔係,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是挺有尊嚴的說話方式,是不是,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: “I felt that I was heaping coals of fire on Mrs. Barry’s head.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得我係喺往巴里太太頭上堆燃燒嘅炭火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得我是在往巴里太太頭上堆燃燒的炭火。

passages.original: And Diana and I had a lovely afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 我同黛安娜度過咗一個美妙嘅下午。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我和黛安娜度過了一個美妙的下午。

passages.original: Diana showed me a new fancy crochet stitch her aunt over at Carmody taught her.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜教咗我一種佢卡莫迪嘅姨媽教佢嘅新式花式鉤針針法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜教了我一種她卡莫迪的姨媽教她的新式花式鉤針針法。

passages.original: Not a soul in Avonlea knows it but us, and we pledged a solemn vow never to reveal it to anyone else.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利除咗我哋邊個都唔會,我哋鄭重發誓永不告訴任何別人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利除了我們誰也不會,我們鄭重發誓永不告訴任何別人。

passages.original: Diana gave me a beautiful card with a wreath of roses on it and a verse of poetry:”
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜畀咗我一張漂亮嘅卡片,上面有玫瑰花環同一句詩:」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜給了我一張漂亮的卡片,上面有玫瑰花環和一句詩:」

passages.original: “If you love me as I love you Nothing but death can part us two.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你愛我如我愛你,除咗死亡,冇乜嘢能把我哋分離。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你愛我如我愛你,除了死亡,沒有什麼能把我們分離。」

passages.original: “And that is true, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係真嘅,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是真的,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: We’re going to ask Mr. Phillips to let us sit together in school again, and Gertie Pye can go with Minnie Andrews.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要請菲利普斯先生讓我哋喺學校里再坐一起,格蒂·派伊可以跟明妮·安德魯斯一起坐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要請菲利普斯先生讓我們在學校里再坐一起,格蒂·派伊可以跟明妮·安德魯斯一起坐。

passages.original: We had an elegant tea.
passages.vernacular: 我哋飲咗一頓高雅嘅茶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們喝了一頓高雅的茶。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry had the very best china set out, Marilla, just as if I was real company.
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太把最好嘅瓷器都擺咗出嚟,瑪麗拉,就好像我係真正嘅客人一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太把最好的瓷器都擺了出來,瑪麗拉,就好像我是真正的客人一樣。

passages.original: I can’t tell you what a thrill it gave me.
passages.vernacular: 我無法告訴您佢帶畀我多大嘅激動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我無法告訴您它帶給我多大的激動。

passages.original: Nobody ever used their very best china on my account before.
passages.vernacular: 以前從冇人為了我而使用佢哋最好嘅瓷器。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以前從沒有人為了我而使用他們最好的瓷器。

passages.original: And we had fruit cake and pound cake and doughnuts and two kinds of preserves, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我哋仲食咗水果蛋糕、磅蛋糕、甜甜圈同兩種蜜餞,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們還吃了水果蛋糕、磅蛋糕、甜甜圈和兩種蜜餞,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: And Mrs. Barry asked me if I took tea and said ‘Pa, why don’t you pass the biscuits to Anne?’
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太問我飲不飲茶,仲講『爸爸,你點解不把餅乾遞畀安妮?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太問我喝不喝茶,還說『爸爸,你為什麼不把餅乾遞給安妮?』

passages.original: It must be lovely to be grown up, Marilla, when just being treated as if you were is so nice.”
passages.vernacular: 長大一定好美,瑪麗拉,光係被當作大人對待就咁好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 長大一定很美,瑪麗拉,光是被當作大人對待就這麼好。」

passages.original: “I don’t know about that,” said Marilla, with a brief sigh.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個我唔知道,」瑪麗拉輕輕嘆咗口氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個我不知道,」瑪麗拉輕輕嘆了口氣說。

passages.original: “Well, anyway, when I am grown up,” said Anne decidedly, “I’m always going to talk to little girls as if they were too, and I’ll never laugh when they use big words.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,不管點樣,等我長大喇,」安妮堅決地講,「我永遠要像對大人一樣同小女孩哋講話,佢哋用大詞嘅時候我永遠唔會笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,不管怎樣,等我長大了,」安妮堅決地說,「我永遠要像對大人一樣和小女孩們說話,她們用大詞的時候我永遠不會笑。

passages.original: I know from sorrowful experience how that hurts one’s feelings.
passages.vernacular: 我從痛苦嘅經驗中知道嗰有多傷人嘅感情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從痛苦的經驗中知道那有多傷人的感情。

passages.original: After tea Diana and I made taffy.
passages.vernacular: 茶後黛安娜同我做咗太妃糖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 茶後黛安娜和我做了太妃糖。

passages.original: The taffy wasn’t very good, I suppose because neither Diana nor I had ever made any before.
passages.vernacular: 太妃糖不太好食,我想係因為黛安娜同我以前都冇做過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太妃糖不太好吃,我想是因為黛安娜和我以前都沒做過。

passages.original: Diana left me to stir it while she buttered the plates and I forgot and let it burn; and then when we set it out on the platform to cool the cat walked over one plate and that had to be thrown away.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜讓我攪拌佢,佢去畀盤子抹黃油,我忘喇,讓佢糊喇;然後我哋把佢放喺平臺上晾涼時,貓從一個盤子上走過去,嗰盤就得扔掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜讓我攪拌它,她去給盤子抹黃油,我忘了,讓它糊了;然後我們把它放在平臺上晾涼時,貓從一個盤子上走過去,那盤就得扔掉了。

passages.original: But the making of it was splendid fun.
passages.vernacular: 但做佢係絕妙嘅樂趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但做它是絕妙的樂趣。

passages.original: Then when I came home Mrs. Barry asked me to come over as often as I could and Diana stood at the window and threw kisses to me all the way down to Lover’s Lane.
passages.vernacular: 然後我回家嘅時候,巴里太太叫我盡可能常去,黛安娜站喺窗邊,一路畀我飛吻直到情人小徑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我回家的時候,巴里太太叫我盡可能常去,黛安娜站在窗邊,一路給我飛吻直到情人小徑。

passages.original: I assure you, Marilla, that I feel like praying tonight and I’m going to think out a special brand-new prayer in honor of the occasion.”
passages.vernacular: 我向您保證,瑪麗拉,今晚我好想禱告,我要想出一篇特別嘅、全新嘅禱詞嚟紀念呢個場合。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向您保證,瑪麗拉,今晚我很想禱告,我要想出一篇特別的、全新的禱詞來紀念這個場合。」

chapters.title: Ch. XIX A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession 第十九章:一場音樂會、一場災難和一次坦白

passages.original: CH MARILLA, can I go over to see Diana just for a minute?” asked Anne, running breathlessly down from the east gable one February evening.
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉,我能過去睇黛安娜一小會兒嗎?」二月嘅一個晚上,安妮氣喘吁吁地從東山牆房間跑下嚟問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉,我能過去看黛安娜一小會兒嗎?」二月的一個晚上,安妮氣喘吁吁地從東山牆房間跑下來問。

passages.original: “I don’t see what you want to be traipsing about after dark for,” said Marilla shortly.
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白你天黑咗仲想到處亂跑幹乜嘢,」瑪麗拉簡短地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白你天黑了還想到處亂跑幹什麼,」瑪麗拉簡短地說。

passages.original: “You and Diana walked home from school together and then stood down there in the snow for half an hour more, your tongues going the whole blessed time, clickety-clack.
passages.vernacular: 「你同黛安娜一起從學校走回家,然後又喺下面嘅雪地裡站咗半個多鐘頭,舌頭一直哢嗒哢嗒地講個不停。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你和黛安娜一起從學校走回家,然後又在下面的雪地裡站了半個多鐘頭,舌頭一直哢嗒哢嗒地說個不停。

passages.original: So I don’t think you’re very badly off to see her again.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我不覺得你再見佢有多大必要。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我不覺得你再見她有多大必要。」

passages.original: “But she wants to see me,” pleaded Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「但係佢想見我,」安妮懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是她想見我,」安妮懇求道。

passages.original: “She has something very important to tell me.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢有好重要嘅事要告訴我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她有非常重要的事要告訴我。」

passages.original: “How do you know she has?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點知道?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼知道?」

passages.original: “Because she just signaled to me from her window.
passages.vernacular: 「因為佢頭先從窗子畀我發咗信號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為她剛才從窗子給我發了信號。

passages.original: We have arranged a way to signal with our candles and cardboard.
passages.vernacular: 我哋想出咗用蠟燭同硬紙板發信號嘅辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們想出了用蠟燭和硬紙板發信號的辦法。

passages.original: We set the candle on the window sill and make flashes by passing the cardboard back and forth.
passages.vernacular: 我哋把蠟燭放喺窗臺上,用硬紙板嚟回擋住,讓佢閃光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們把蠟燭放在窗臺上,用硬紙板來回擋住,讓它閃光。

passages.original: So many flashes mean a certain thing.
passages.vernacular: 閃幾下代表某個意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 閃幾下代表某個意思。

passages.original: It was my idea, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我嘅主意,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我的主意,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: “I’ll warrant you it was,” said Marilla emphatically.
passages.vernacular: 「我敢講係你嘅主意,」瑪麗拉強調地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢說是你的主意,」瑪麗拉強調地說。

passages.original: “And the next thing you’ll be setting fire to the curtains with your signaling nonsense.”
passages.vernacular: 「接下嚟你就會因為你嗰信號嘅胡鬧把窗簾點住喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「接下來你就會因為你那信號的胡鬧把窗簾點著了。」

passages.original: “Oh, we’re very careful, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我哋好小心嘅,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我們很小心的,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: And it’s so interesting.
passages.vernacular: 而且特別有趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且特別有趣。

passages.original: Two flashes mean, ‘Are you there?’
passages.vernacular: 閃兩下表示『你喺嗎?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 閃兩下表示『你在嗎?』

passages.original: Three mean ‘yes’ and four ‘no.’
passages.vernacular: 三下表示『喺』,四下表示『不喺』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三下表示『在』,四下表示『不在』。

passages.original: Five mean, ‘Come over as soon as possible, because I have something important to reveal.’
passages.vernacular: 五下表示『儘快過嚟,因為我有重要嘅事要透露』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 五下表示『儘快過來,因為我有重要的事要透露』。

passages.original: Diana has just signaled five flashes, and I’m really suffering to know what it is.”
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜啱啱發咗五下信號,我真想知道係乜嘢,簡直係受折磨。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜剛剛發了五下信號,我真想知道是什麼,簡直是受折磨。」

passages.original: “Well, you needn’t suffer any longer,” said Marilla sarcastically.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你唔使再受折磨喇,」瑪麗拉諷刺地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你不必再受折磨了,」瑪麗拉諷刺地說。

passages.original: “You can go, but you’re to be back here in just ten minutes, remember that.”
passages.vernacular: 「你可以去,但你必須好鐘後就回到呢兒,記住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你可以去,但你必須十分鐘後就回到這兒,記住。」

passages.original: Anne did remember it and was back in the stipulated time, although probably no mortal will ever know just what it cost her to confine the discussion of Diana’s important communication within the limits of ten minutes.
passages.vernacular: 安妮記住喇,喺規定嘅時間內回嚟喇,儘管大概冇邊個凡人會知道,佢把討論黛安娜嘅重要消息限制喺好鐘之內,花咗佢多大代價。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮記住了,在規定的時間內回來了,儘管大概沒有哪個凡人會知道,她把討論黛安娜的重要消息限制在十分鐘之內,花了她多大代價。

passages.original: But at least she had made good use of them.
passages.vernacular: 但至少佢充分利用咗呢個好鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但至少她充分利用了這十分鐘。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, what do you think?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,您猜點住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,您猜怎麼著?

passages.original: You know tomorrow is Diana’s birthday.
passages.vernacular: 您知道聽日係黛安娜嘅生日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道明天是黛安娜的生日。

passages.original: Well, her mother told her she could ask me to go home with her from school and stay all night with her.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,佢母親告訴佢,佢可以邀請我放學後跟佢回家,喺佢家過夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,她母親告訴她,她可以邀請我放學後跟她回家,在她家過夜。

passages.original: And her cousins are coming over from Newbridge in a big pung sleigh to go to the Debating Club concert at the hall tomorrow night.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅表親哋聽日晚上要從新橋乘一輛大雪橇過嚟,去大廳參加辯論社嘅音樂會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的表親們明天晚上要從新橋乘一輛大雪橇過來,去大廳參加辯論社的音樂會。

passages.original: And they are going to take Diana and me to the concert--if you’ll let me go, that is.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋要帶黛安娜同我去音樂會——如果您讓我去嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們要帶黛安娜和我去音樂會——如果您讓我去的話。

passages.original: You will, won’t you, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 您會嘅,係唔係,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您會的,是不是,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: Oh, I feel so excited.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我太興奮喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我太興奮了。」

passages.original: “You can calm down then, because you’re not going.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你可以平靜下嚟喇,因為你不去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你可以平靜下來了,因為你不去。

passages.original: You’re better at home in your own bed, and as for that club concert, it’s all nonsense, and little girls should not be allowed to go out to such places at all.”
passages.vernacular: 你待喺家裡自己嘅床上更好,至於嗰個社團嘅音樂會,全係胡鬧,小女孩哋根本不該被允許去嗰種地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你待在家裡自己的床上更好,至於那個社團的音樂會,全是胡鬧,小女孩們根本不該被允許去那種地方。」

passages.original: “I’m sure the Debating Club is a most respectable affair,” pleaded Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我肯定辯論社係個最體面嘅組織,」安妮懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我肯定辯論社是個最體面的組織,」安妮懇求道。

passages.original: “I’m not saying it isn’t.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇講佢唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒說它不是。

passages.original: But you’re not going to begin gadding about to concerts and staying out all hours of the night.
passages.vernacular: 但係你唔能夠開始四處閒逛去音樂會,深更半夜仲喺外頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是你不能開始四處閒逛去音樂會,深更半夜還在外頭。

passages.original: Pretty doings for children.
passages.vernacular: 畀細路哋幹嘅好事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給孩子們幹的好事。

passages.original: I’m surprised at Mrs. Barry’s letting Diana go.”
passages.vernacular: 我好驚訝巴里太太竟然讓黛安娜去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很驚訝巴里太太竟然讓黛安娜去。」

passages.original: “But it’s such a very special occasion,” mourned Anne, on the verge of tears.
passages.vernacular: 「但呢個係一個好特別嘅場合,」安妮哀嘆道,幾乎要哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但這是一個非常特別的場合,」安妮哀嘆道,幾乎要哭了。

passages.original: “Diana has only one birthday in a year.
passages.vernacular: 「黛安娜一年只有一個生日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黛安娜一年只有一個生日。

passages.original: It isn’t as if birthdays were common things, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 生日唔係普通嘅事,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 生日不是普通的事,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Prissy Andrews is going to recite ‘Curfew Must Not Ring Tonight.’
passages.vernacular: 普麗茜·安德魯斯要朗誦《今夜不可敲晚鐘》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 普麗茜·安德魯斯要朗誦《今夜不可敲晚鐘》。

passages.original: That is such a good moral piece, Marilla, I’m sure it would do me lots of good to hear it.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一首幾咁好嘅道德詩篇,瑪麗拉,我肯定聽咗對我大有好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一首多麼好的道德詩篇,瑪麗拉,我肯定聽了對我大有好處。

passages.original: And the choir are going to sing four lovely pathetic songs that are pretty near as good as hymns.
passages.vernacular: 唱詩班要唱四首悲壯嘅好歌,幾乎同聖詩一樣好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唱詩班要唱四首悲壯的好歌,幾乎和聖詩一樣好。

passages.original: And oh, Marilla, the minister is going to take part; yes, indeed, he is; he’s going to give an address.
passages.vernacular: 仲有,哦,瑪麗拉,牧師要參加;係嘅,真嘅,佢要發表講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,哦,瑪麗拉,牧師要參加;是的,真的,他要發表講話。

passages.original: That will be just about the same thing as a sermon.
passages.vernacular: 嗰差不多就跟講道一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那差不多就跟講道一樣。

passages.original: Please, mayn’t I go, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 求求您,我唔能夠去嗎,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求求您,我不能去嗎,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: “You heard what I said, Anne, didn’t you?
passages.vernacular: 「你聽見我講嘅話喇,安妮,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你聽見我說的話了,安妮,是不是?

passages.original: Take off your boots now and go to bed.
passages.vernacular: 而家把靴子脫喇,上床瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在把靴子脫了,上床睡覺。

passages.original: It’s past eight.”
passages.vernacular: 已經過八點喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 已經過八點了。」

passages.original: “There’s just one more thing, Marilla,” said Anne, with the air of producing the last shot in her locker.
passages.vernacular: 「仲有最後一件事,瑪麗拉,」安妮講,帶住攞出最後一顆子彈嘅神氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還有最後一件事,瑪麗拉,」安妮說,帶著拿出最後一顆子彈的神氣。

passages.original: “Mrs. Barry told Diana that we might sleep in the spare-room bed.
passages.vernacular: 「巴里太太對黛安娜講,我哋可以瞓喺備用客房嘅床上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴里太太對黛安娜說,我們可以睡在備用客房的床上。

passages.original: Think of the honor of your little Anne being put in the spare-room bed.”
passages.vernacular: 想想您嘅小安妮瞓喺備用客房嘅床上係幾咁榮耀。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想想您的小安妮睡在備用客房的床上是多麼榮耀。」

passages.original: “It’s an honor you’ll have to get along without.
passages.vernacular: 「呢份榮耀你只好冇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這份榮耀你只好沒有了。

passages.original: Go to bed, Anne, and don’t let me hear another word out of you.”
passages.vernacular: 去瞓覺,安妮,唔好畀我再聽到你講一個字。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去睡覺,安妮,別讓我再聽到你說一個字。」

passages.original: When Anne, with tears rolling over her cheeks, had gone sorrowfully upstairs, Matthew, who had been apparently sound asleep on the lounge during the whole dialogue, opened his eyes and said decidedly:
passages.vernacular: 安妮淚水滾過臉頰,傷心地上樓去喇,喺整個對話過程中似乎一直喺長沙發上酣瞓嘅馬修,睜開眼睛,堅決地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮淚水滾過臉頰,傷心地上樓去了,在整個對話過程中似乎一直在長沙發上酣睡的馬修,睜開眼睛,堅決地說:

passages.original: “Well now, Marilla, I think you ought to let Anne go.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,瑪麗拉,我覺得你應該讓安妮去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,瑪麗拉,我覺得你應該讓安妮去。」

passages.original: “I don’t then,” retorted Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我不覺得,」瑪麗拉反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不覺得,」瑪麗拉反駁。

passages.original: “Who’s bringing this child up, Matthew, you or me?”
passages.vernacular: 「係邊個喺養呢細路,馬修,你定係我?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是誰在養這孩子,馬修,你還是我?」

passages.original: “Well now, you,” admitted Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,係你,」馬修承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,是你,」馬修承認。

passages.original: “Don’t interfere then.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就別干涉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就別干涉。」

passages.original: “Well now, I ain’t interfering.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我冇干涉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我沒有干涉。

passages.original: It ain’t interfering to have your own opinion.
passages.vernacular: 有自己嘅意見不算干涉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有自己的意見不算干涉。

passages.original: And my opinion is that you ought to let Anne go.”
passages.vernacular: 而我嘅意見係你應該讓安妮去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我的意見是你應該讓安妮去。」

passages.original: “You’d think I ought to let Anne go to the moon if she took the notion, I’ve no doubt,” was Marilla’s amiable rejoinder.
passages.vernacular: 「我毫不懷疑,只要安妮動咗念頭,你就會認為我該讓佢去月球,」呢個係瑪麗拉嘅客氣回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我毫不懷疑,只要安妮動了念頭,你就會認為我該讓她去月球,」這是瑪麗拉的客氣回答。

passages.original: “I might have let her spend the night with Diana, if that was all.
passages.vernacular: 「如果只係讓佢喺黛安娜家過夜,我或許可以讓佢去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果只是讓她在黛安娜家過夜,我或許可以讓她去。

passages.original: But I don’t approve of this concert plan.
passages.vernacular: 但我不贊成呢個音樂會計劃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不贊成這個音樂會計劃。

passages.original: She’d go there and catch cold like as not, and have her head filled up with nonsense and excitement.
passages.vernacular: 佢到嗰兒大概會感冒,腦子裡仲會裝滿胡鬧同興奮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她到那兒大概會感冒,腦子裡還會裝滿胡鬧和興奮。

passages.original: It would unsettle her for a week.
passages.vernacular: 呢會讓佢一個星期靜不下心嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這會讓她一個星期靜不下心來。

passages.original: I understand that child’s disposition and what’s good for it better than you, Matthew.”
passages.vernacular: 我比你更了解嗰細路嘅性情同對佢有益嘅嘢,馬修。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我比你更了解那孩子的性情和對她有益的東西,馬修。」

passages.original: “I think you ought to let Anne go,” repeated Matthew firmly.
passages.vernacular: 「我認為你應該讓安妮去,」馬修堅定地重複。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我認為你應該讓安妮去,」馬修堅定地重複。

passages.original: Argument was not his strong point, but holding fast to his opinion certainly was.
passages.vernacular: 爭論唔係佢嘅強項,但堅持己見肯定係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爭論不是他的強項,但堅持己見肯定是。

passages.original: Marilla gave a gasp of helplessness and took refuge in silence.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉無助地喘咗口氣,躲進咗沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉無助地喘了口氣,躲進了沉默。

passages.original: The next morning, when Anne was washing the breakfast dishes in the pantry, Matthew paused on his way out to the barn to say to Marilla again:
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨,安妮喺食品櫃裡洗早餐嘅碗碟時,馬修喺去穀倉嘅路上停下嚟,又對瑪麗拉講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨,安妮在食品櫃裡洗早餐的碗碟時,馬修在去穀倉的路上停下來,又對瑪麗拉說:

passages.original: “I think you ought to let Anne go, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 「我認為你應該讓安妮去,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我認為你應該讓安妮去,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: For a moment Marilla looked things not lawful to be uttered.
passages.vernacular: 有一會兒,瑪麗拉嘅眼神裡講住不可言講嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一會兒,瑪麗拉的眼神裡說著不可言說的話。

passages.original: Then she yielded to the inevitable and said tartly:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢向不可避免嘅事屈服喇,尖刻地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她向不可避免的事屈服了,尖刻地說:

passages.original: “Very well, she can go, since nothing else ‘ll please you.”
passages.vernacular: 「好好,佢可以去,既然冇別嘅能讓你滿意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好,她可以去,既然沒有別的能讓你滿意。」

passages.original: Anne flew out of the pantry, dripping dishcloth in hand.
passages.vernacular: 安妮從食品櫃裡飛咗出嚟,手裡攞住滴水嘅抹布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮從食品櫃裡飛了出來,手裡拿著滴水的抹布。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, Marilla, say those blessed words again.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,瑪麗拉,把嗰啲神聖嘅話再講一遍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,瑪麗拉,把那些神聖的話再說一遍。」

passages.original: “I guess once is enough to say them.
passages.vernacular: 「我想講一遍就夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想說一遍就夠了。

passages.original: This is Matthew’s doings and I wash my hands of it.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係馬修搞嘅,我概不負責。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是馬修搞的,我概不負責。

passages.original: If you catch pneumonia sleeping in a strange bed or coming out of that hot hall in the middle of the night, don’t blame me, blame Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 如果你瞓喺陌生嘅床上,或者半夜從嗰個悶熱嘅大廳出嚟得咗肺炎,別怪我,怪馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你睡在陌生的床上,或者半夜從那個悶熱的大廳出來得了肺炎,別怪我,怪馬修。

passages.original: Anne Shirley, you’re dripping greasy water all over the floor.
passages.vernacular: 安妮·雪莉,你把油膩嘅水滴得滿地都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮·雪莉,你把油膩的水滴得滿地都是。

passages.original: I never saw such a careless child.”
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過咁粗心嘅細路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過這麼粗心的孩子。」

passages.original: “Oh, I know I’m a great trial to you, Marilla,” said Anne repentantly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我知道我係您嘅大麻煩,瑪麗拉,」安妮悔恨地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我知道我是您的大麻煩,瑪麗拉,」安妮悔恨地說。

passages.original: “I make so many mistakes.
passages.vernacular: 「我犯咗咁多錯誤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我犯了那麼多錯誤。

passages.original: But then just think of all the mistakes I don’t make, although I might.
passages.vernacular: 但您想想所有我可能犯卻冇犯嘅錯誤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但您想想所有我可能犯卻沒犯的錯誤。

passages.original: I’ll get some sand and scrub up the spots before I go to school.
passages.vernacular: 我去上學前攞些沙子把呢啲污點擦乾淨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去上學前拿些沙子把這些污點擦乾淨。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, my heart was just set on going to that concert.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,我嘅心一直就想去嗰個音樂會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,我的心一直就想去那個音樂會。

passages.original: I never was to a concert in my life, and when the other girls talk about them in school I feel so out of it.
passages.vernacular: 我呢輩子從冇去過音樂會,別嘅女孩喺學校里談論佢哋時,我覺得好被排除喺外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這輩子從沒去過音樂會,別的女孩在學校里談論它們時,我覺得好被排除在外。

passages.original: You didn’t know just how I felt about it, but you see Matthew did.
passages.vernacular: 您唔知道我對此嘅感受,但您瞧,馬修知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不知道我對此的感受,但您瞧,馬修知道。

passages.original: Matthew understands me, and it’s so nice to be understood, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 馬修理解我,被人理解真好,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修理解我,被人理解真好,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: Anne was too excited to do herself justice as to lessons that morning in school.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天早晨喺學校,安妮太興奮,功課表現不好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天早晨在學校,安妮太興奮,功課表現不好。

passages.original: Gilbert Blythe spelled her down in class and left her clear out of sight in mental arithmetic.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯喺課堂上把佢拼寫贏咗下去,喺心算上把佢遠遠甩喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯在課堂上把她拼寫贏了下去,在心算上把她遠遠甩在後面。

passages.original: Anne’s consequent humiliation was less than it might have been, however, in view of the concert and the spare-room bed.
passages.vernacular: 不過,考慮到音樂會同備用客房嘅床,安妮因此受嘅羞辱比本來要少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,考慮到音樂會和備用客房的床,安妮因此受的羞辱比本來要少。

passages.original: She and Diana talked so constantly about it all day that with a stricter teacher than Mr. Phillips dire disgrace must inevitably have been their portion.
passages.vernacular: 佢同黛安娜整天不停地談論呢件事,要係遇到比菲利普斯先生更嚴格嘅老師,佢哋肯定要遭受可怕嘅恥辱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她和黛安娜整天不停地談論這件事,要是遇到比菲利普斯先生更嚴格的老師,她們肯定要遭受可怕的恥辱。

passages.original: Anne felt that she could not have borne it if she had not been going to the concert, for nothing else was discussed that day in school.
passages.vernacular: 安妮覺得,如果佢唔係要去參加音樂會,佢根本無法忍受,因為嗰天學校里別嘅乜嘢都冇討論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮覺得,如果她不是要去參加音樂會,她根本無法忍受,因為那天學校里別的什麼也沒討論。

passages.original: The Avonlea Debating Club, which met fortnightly all winter, had had several smaller free entertainments; but this was to be a big affair, admission ten cents, in aid of the library.
passages.vernacular: 整個冬天每兩週聚會一次嘅阿文利辯論社,舉辦過幾次較小嘅免費娛樂活動;但呢次係個大活動,入場費好錢,資助圖書館。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個冬天每兩週聚會一次的阿文利辯論社,舉辦過幾次較小的免費娛樂活動;但這次是個大活動,入場費十分錢,資助圖書館。

passages.original: The Avonlea young people had been practicing for weeks, and all the scholars were especially interested in it by reason of older brothers and sisters who were going to take part.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利嘅年輕人已經練習咗好幾個星期,所有學生都特別感興趣,因為有些哥哥姐姐要參加。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利的年輕人已經練習了好幾個星期,所有學生都特別感興趣,因為有些哥哥姐姐要參加。

passages.original: Everybody in school over nine years of age expected to go, except Carrie Sloane, whose father shared Marilla’s opinions about small girls going out to night concerts.
passages.vernacular: 學校里九歲以上嘅人都指望去,除咗嘉莉·斯隆,佢父親同瑪麗拉對小女孩去夜間音樂會持相同睇法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學校里九歲以上的人都指望去,除了嘉莉·斯隆,她父親與瑪麗拉對小女孩去夜間音樂會持相同看法。

passages.original: Carrie Sloane cried into her grammar all the afternoon and felt that life was not worth living.
passages.vernacular: 嘉莉·斯隆整個下午對住佢嘅語法書哭泣,覺得生活不值得過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘉莉·斯隆整個下午對著她的語法書哭泣,覺得生活不值得過。

passages.original: For Anne the real excitement began with the dismissal of school and increased therefrom in crescendo until it reached to a crash of positive ecstasy in the concert itself.
passages.vernacular: 對安妮來講,真正嘅興奮從放學開始,從嗰以後漸強漸增,直到喺音樂會本身達到一種實實在喺嘅狂喜嘅轟響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對安妮來說,真正的興奮從放學開始,從那以後漸強漸增,直到在音樂會本身達到一種實實在在的狂喜的轟響。

passages.original: They had a “perfectly elegant tea;” and then came the delicious occupation of dressing in Diana’s little room upstairs.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋食咗一頓「特別高雅嘅茶點」;然後係美妙嘅活動:喺黛安娜樓上嘅小房間裡打扮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們吃了一頓「特別高雅的茶點」;然後是美妙的活動:在黛安娜樓上的小房間裡打扮。

passages.original: Diana did Anne’s front hair in the new pompadour style and Anne tied Diana’s bows with the especial knack she possessed; and they experimented with at least half a dozen different ways of arranging their back hair.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜為安妮梳咗新式嘅蓬帕杜髮型嘅劉海,安妮用佢特有嘅手法為黛安娜繫蝴蝶結;佢哋至少試驗咗六七種不同嘅後髮梳法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜為安妮梳了新式的蓬帕杜髮型的劉海,安妮用她特有的手法為黛安娜繫蝴蝶結;她們至少試驗了六七種不同的後髮梳法。

passages.original: At last they were ready, cheeks scarlet and eyes glowing with excitement.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢哋準備好喇,臉頰通紅,眼睛因興奮而閃亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後她們準備好了,臉頰通紅,眼睛因興奮而閃亮。

passages.original: True, Anne could not help a little pang when she contrasted her plain black tam and shapeless, tight-sleeved, homemade gray-cloth coat with Diana’s jaunty fur cap and smart little jacket.
passages.vernacular: 確實,當佢把自己樸素嘅黑色蘇格蘭帽同寬鬆、袖子緊窄、自家做嘅灰布外套,同黛安娜俏皮嘅皮帽同漂亮嘅小夾克對比時,安妮不禁感到一絲痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,當她把自己樸素的黑色蘇格蘭帽和寬鬆、袖子緊窄、自家做的灰布外套,與黛安娜俏皮的皮帽和漂亮的小夾克對比時,安妮不禁感到一絲痛苦。

passages.original: But she remembered in time that she had an imagination and could use it.
passages.vernacular: 但佢及時想起自己有想像力,而且可以運用佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她及時想起自己有想像力,而且可以運用它。

passages.original: Then Diana’s cousins, the Murrays from Newbridge, came; they all crowded into the big pung sleigh, among straw and furry robes.
passages.vernacular: 然後黛安娜嘅表親哋,新橋嘅默里家人,嚟喇;佢哋都擠進大雪橇,坐喺稻草同毛皮毯子中間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後黛安娜的表親們,新橋的默里家人,來了;他們都擠進大雪橇,坐在稻草和毛皮毯子中間。

passages.original: Anne reveled in the drive to the hall, slipping along over the satin-smooth roads with the snow crisping under the runners.
passages.vernacular: 安妮陶醉喺去大廳嘅路上,喺像緞子一樣光滑嘅路上滑行,雪喺雪橇滑板下發出脆響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮陶醉在去大廳的路上,在像緞子一樣光滑的路上滑行,雪在雪橇滑板下發出脆響。

passages.original: There was a magnificent sunset, and the snowy hills and deep-blue water of the St. Lawrence Gulf seemed to rim in the splendor like a huge bowl of pearl and sapphire brimmed with wine and fire.
passages.vernacular: 有一個壯麗嘅日落,白雪覆蓋嘅山丘同聖勞倫斯灣深藍色嘅水,似乎把呢片輝煌圍喺其中,像一個巨大嘅珍珠同藍寶石嘅碗,盛滿美酒同火焰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一個壯麗的日落,白雪覆蓋的山丘和聖勞倫斯灣深藍色的水,似乎把這片輝煌圍在其中,像一個巨大的珍珠和藍寶石的碗,盛滿美酒與火焰。

passages.original: Tinkles of sleigh bells and distant laughter, that seemed like the mirth of wood elves, came from every quarter.
passages.vernacular: 雪橇鈴鐺嘅叮噹聲同遠處嘅笑聲,像林中小精靈嘅歡笑,從四面八方傳嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪橇鈴鐺的叮噹聲和遠處的笑聲,像林中小精靈的歡笑,從四面八方傳來。

passages.original: “Oh, Diana,” breathed Anne, squeezing Diana’s mittened hand under the fur robe, “isn’t it all like a beautiful dream?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,黛安娜,」安妮講,喺毛皮毯子下捏住黛安娜戴著手套嘅手,「呢一切唔係像一場美麗嘅夢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,黛安娜,」安妮說,在毛皮毯子下捏著黛安娜戴著手套的手,「這一切不是像一場美麗的夢嗎?

passages.original: Do I really look the same as usual?
passages.vernacular: 我真嘅和平常一樣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真的和平常一樣嗎?

passages.original: I feel so different that it seems to me it must show in my looks.”
passages.vernacular: 我覺得自己咁不同,似乎一定會表而家我嘅外貌上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得自己那麼不同,似乎一定會表現在我的外貌上。」

passages.original: “You look awfully nice,” said Diana, who having just received a compliment from one of her cousins, felt that she ought to pass it on.
passages.vernacular: 「你睇上去特別好睇,」黛安娜講,佢剛從一位表兄嗰兒得到咗恭維,覺得應該傳下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看上去特別好看,」黛安娜說,她剛從一位表兄那兒得到了恭維,覺得應該傳下去。

passages.original: “You’ve got the loveliest color.”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅氣色最好睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的氣色最好看。」

passages.original: The program that night was a series of “thrills” for at least one listener in the audience, and, as Anne assured Diana, every succeeding thrill was thrillier than the last.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上嘅節目,至少對觀眾中嘅一位聽眾來講,係一系列嘅「顫慄」,正如安妮向黛安娜保證嘅,每一個接下嚟嘅顫慄都比上一個更顫慄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上的節目,至少對觀眾中的一位聽眾來說,是一系列的「顫慄」,正如安妮向黛安娜保證的,每一個接下來的顫慄都比上一個更顫慄。

passages.original: When Prissy Andrews, attired in a new pink-silk waist with a string of pearls about her smooth white throat and real carnations in her hair--rumor whispered that the master had sent all the way to town for them for her--“climbed the slimy ladder, dark without one ray of light,” Anne shivered in luxurious sympathy; when the choir sang “Far Above the Gentle Daisies” Anne gazed at the ceiling as if it were frescoed with angels; when Sam Sloane proceeded to explain and illustrate “How Sockery Set a Hen” Anne laughed until people sitting near her laughed too, more out of sympathy with her than with amusement at a selection that was rather threadbare even in Avonlea; and when Mr. Phillips gave Mark Antony’s oration over the dead body of Cæsar in the most heart-stirring tones--looking at Prissy Andrews at the end of every sentence--Anne felt that she could rise and mutiny on the spot if but one Roman citizen led the way.
passages.vernacular: 當普麗茜·安德魯斯穿住一件新嘅粉紅絲綢上衣,光滑嘅白皙脖頸上戴住一串珍珠,頭髮裡插住真正嘅康乃馨——傳言講老師特地派人去城裡為佢買嘅——「爬上黏滑嘅梯子,黑暗中冇一絲光亮」時,安妮奢華地同情地顫慄;當唱詩班唱《遠高於溫柔嘅雛菊》時,安妮凝視住天花板,好像上面畫滿咗天使壁畫;當山姆·斯隆接住解釋並演示《索克里如何孵蛋》時,安妮笑得周圍嘅人都笑喇,同其講係被呢個即使喺阿文利都相當陳舊嘅節目逗樂,不如講係被佢嘅笑聲感染;當菲利普斯先生以最激動人心嘅語調朗誦馬克·安東尼喺凱撒屍體旁嘅演講——喺每句話嘅末尾都睇住普麗茜·安德魯斯——時,安妮覺得只要有一個羅馬公民帶頭,佢當場就能站起嚟造反。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當普麗茜·安德魯斯穿著一件新的粉紅絲綢上衣,光滑的白皙脖頸上戴著一串珍珠,頭髮裡插著真正的康乃馨——傳言說老師特地派人去城裡為她買的——「爬上黏滑的梯子,黑暗中沒有一絲光亮」時,安妮奢華地同情地顫慄;當唱詩班唱《遠高於溫柔的雛菊》時,安妮凝視著天花板,好像上面畫滿了天使壁畫;當山姆·斯隆接著解釋並演示《索克里如何孵蛋》時,安妮笑得周圍的人也笑了,與其說是被這個即使在阿文利也相當陳舊的節目逗樂,不如說是被她的笑聲感染;當菲利普斯先生以最激動人心的語調朗誦馬克·安東尼在凱撒屍體旁的演說——在每句話的末尾都看著普麗茜·安德魯斯——時,安妮覺得只要有一個羅馬公民帶頭,她當場就能站起來造反。

passages.original: Only one number on the program failed to interest her.
passages.vernacular: 節目單上只有一個節目冇引起佢嘅興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 節目單上只有一個節目沒引起她的興趣。

passages.original: When Gilbert Blythe recited “Bingen on the Rhine” Anne picked up Rhoda Murray’s library book and read it until he had finished, when she sat rigidly stiff and motionless while Diana clapped her hands until they tingled.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯朗誦《萊茵河畔嘅賓根》時,安妮攞起羅達·默里嘅圖書館借嘅書,一直讀到佢結束,佢僵直地一動不動地坐住,而黛安娜拍手拍得手心發麻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯朗誦《萊茵河畔的賓根》時,安妮拿起羅達·默里的圖書館借的書,一直讀到他結束,她僵直地一動不動地坐著,而黛安娜拍手拍得手心發麻。

passages.original: It was eleven when they got home, sated with dissipation, but with the exceeding sweet pleasure of talking it all over still to come.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋回到家時係十啲,沉溺於放縱,但仲有極其甜美嘅樂趣——把呢一切談個夠——喺等住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們回到家時是十一點,沉溺於放縱,但還有極其甜美的樂趣——把這一切談個夠——在等著。

passages.original: Everybody seemed asleep and the house was dark and silent.
passages.vernacular: 每個人似乎都瞓喇,房子裡一片漆黑寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個人似乎都睡了,房子裡一片漆黑寂靜。

passages.original: Anne and Diana tiptoed into the parlor, a long narrow room out of which the spare room opened.
passages.vernacular: 安妮同黛安娜踮住腳走進客廳,嗰個係一個狹長嘅房間,備用客房就開喺呢房間外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮和黛安娜踮著腳走進客廳,那是一個狹長的房間,備用客房就開在這房間外。

passages.original: It was pleasantly warm and dimly lighted by the embers of a fire in the grate.
passages.vernacular: 嗰度暖洋洋嘅,爐柵裡嘅餘燼發出微弱嘅光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡暖洋洋的,爐柵裡的餘燼發出微弱的光。

passages.original: “Let’s undress here,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋喺呢兒脫衣服吧,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們在這兒脫衣服吧,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “It’s so nice and warm.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢兒又好又暖同。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這兒又好又暖和。」

passages.original: “Hasn’t it been a delightful time?” sighed Anne rapturously.
passages.vernacular: 「呢唔係一個愉快嘅時光嗎?」安妮欣喜地嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這不是一個愉快的時光嗎?」安妮欣喜地嘆道。

passages.original: “It must be splendid to get up and recite there.
passages.vernacular: 「站起嚟喺嗰兒朗誦一定好棒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「站起來在那兒朗誦一定很棒。

passages.original: Do you suppose we will ever be asked to do it, Diana?”
passages.vernacular: 你覺得我哋以後會被邀請做呢個嗎,黛安娜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你覺得我們以後會被邀請做這個嗎,黛安娜?」

passages.original: “Yes, of course, someday.
passages.vernacular: 「會嘅,當然,有一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「會的,當然,有一天。

passages.original: They’re always wanting the big scholars to recite.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋總是想要大啲嘅學生朗誦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們總是想要大一點的學生朗誦。

passages.original: Gilbert Blythe does often and he’s only two years older than us.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯經常朗誦,佢只比我哋大兩歲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯經常朗誦,他只比我們大兩歲。

passages.original: Oh, Anne, how could you pretend not to listen to him?
passages.vernacular: 哦,安妮,你點能假裝不聽佢嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,安妮,你怎麼能假裝不聽他的?

passages.original: When he came to the line,
passages.vernacular: 當佢讀到嗰一句,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他讀到那一句,

passages.original: ‘There’s Another, not a sister,’
passages.vernacular: 『仲有另一個,唔係姐妹,』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『還有另一個,不是姐妹,』

passages.original: he looked right down at you.”
passages.vernacular: 佢直直地睇住你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他直直地看著你。」

passages.original: “Diana,” said Anne with dignity, “you are my bosom friend, but I cannot allow even you to speak to me of that person.
passages.vernacular: 「黛安娜,」安妮威嚴地講,「你係我嘅知心朋友,但我唔能夠允許連你都跟我談起嗰個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黛安娜,」安妮威嚴地說,「你是我的知心朋友,但我不能允許連你都跟我談起那個人。

passages.original: Are you ready for bed?
passages.vernacular: 你準備好瞓覺咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你準備好睡覺了嗎?

passages.original: Let’s run a race and see who’ll get to the bed first.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋賽跑,睇邊個先到床上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們賽跑,看誰先到床上。」

passages.original: The suggestion appealed to Diana.
passages.vernacular: 呢個建議對黛安娜有吸引力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個建議對黛安娜有吸引力。

passages.original: The two little white-clad figures flew down the long room, through the spare-room door, and bounded on the bed at the same moment.
passages.vernacular: 兩個穿白衣嘅小身影飛奔過長房間,穿過備用客房嘅門,同時跳到床上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個穿白衣的小身影飛奔過長房間,穿過備用客房的門,同時跳到床上。

passages.original: And then--something--moved beneath them, there was a gasp and a cry--and somebody said in muffled accents:
passages.vernacular: 然後——有乜嘢嘢——喺佢哋身下動喇,有人喘咗口氣,尖叫一聲——有人用悶悶嘅口音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後——有什麼東西——在她們身下動了,有人喘了口氣,尖叫一聲——有人用悶悶的口音說:

passages.original: “Merciful goodness!”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!」

passages.original: Anne and Diana were never able to tell just how they got off that bed and out of the room.
passages.vernacular: 安妮同黛安娜永遠講不清佢哋係點從嗰張床上下嚟、離開嗰個房間嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮和黛安娜永遠說不清她們是怎麼從那張床上下來、離開那個房間的。

passages.original: They only knew that after one frantic rush they found themselves tiptoeing shiveringly upstairs.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋只知道,一陣瘋狂嘅衝刺之後,發現自己正哆嗦住踮腳上樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們只知道,一陣瘋狂的衝刺之後,發現自己正哆嗦著踮腳上樓。

passages.original: “Oh, who was it--what was it?” whispered Anne, her teeth chattering with cold and fright.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係邊個——係乜嘢?」安妮低聲講,冷得又怕得牙齒打戰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是誰——是什麼?」安妮低聲說,冷得又怕得牙齒打戰。

passages.original: “It was Aunt Josephine,” said Diana, gasping with laughter.
passages.vernacular: 「係約瑟芬姑婆,」黛安娜講,笑得喘不過氣嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是約瑟芬姑婆,」黛安娜說,笑得喘不過氣來。

passages.original: “Oh, Anne, it was Aunt Josephine, however she came to be there.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,安妮,係約瑟芬姑婆,唔知佢點會喺嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,安妮,是約瑟芬姑婆,不知她怎麼會在那兒。

passages.original: Oh, and I know she will be furious.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我知道佢會氣瘋嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我知道她會氣瘋的。

passages.original: It’s dreadful--it’s really dreadful--but did you ever know anything so funny, Anne?”
passages.vernacular: 呢太可怕喇——真嘅太可怕喇——不過你聽講過仲有比呢更可笑嘅事嗎,安妮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這太可怕了——真的太可怕了——可是你聽說過還有比這更可笑的事嗎,安妮?」

passages.original: “Who is your Aunt Josephine?”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅約瑟芬姑婆係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的約瑟芬姑婆是誰?」

passages.original: “She’s father’s aunt and she lives in Charlottetown.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係爸爸嘅姑媽,住喺夏洛特敦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是爸爸的姑媽,住在夏洛特敦。

passages.original: She’s awfully old--seventy anyhow--and I don’t believe she was ever a little girl.
passages.vernacular: 佢老極喇——至少七十歲——我不相信佢曾經係個小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她老極了——至少七十歲——我不相信她曾經是個小女孩。

passages.original: We were expecting her out for a visit, but not so soon.
passages.vernacular: 我哋正期待佢嚟做客,但冇想到咁快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們正期待她來做客,但沒想到這麼快。

passages.original: She’s awfully prim and proper and she’ll scold dreadfully about this, I know.
passages.vernacular: 佢特別拘謹刻板,我知道佢會為此大罵一頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她特別拘謹刻板,我知道她會為此大罵一頓。

passages.original: Well, we’ll have to sleep with Minnie May--and you can’t think how she kicks.”
passages.vernacular: 好喇,我哋得同明妮·梅瞓喇——你想唔到佢踢得有多厲害。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,我們得和明妮·梅睡了——你想不到她踢得有多厲害。」

passages.original: Miss Josephine Barry did not appear at the early breakfast the next morning.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨嘅早餐桌上冇出現約瑟芬·巴里小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨的早餐桌上沒有出現約瑟芬·巴里小姐。

passages.original: Mrs. Barry smiled kindly at the two little girls.
passages.vernacular: 巴里太太和藹地對兩個小女孩笑咗笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里太太和藹地對兩個小女孩笑了笑。

passages.original: “Did you have a good time last night?
passages.vernacular: 「琴晚玩得開心嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「昨晚玩得開心嗎?

passages.original: I tried to stay awake until you came home, for I wanted to tell you Aunt Josephine had come and that you would have to go upstairs after all, but I was so tired I fell asleep.
passages.vernacular: 我努力撐著想等你哋回家,因為我想告訴你哋約瑟芬姑婆嚟喇,你哋終究得上樓瞓,可我太累喇,瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我努力撐著想等你們回家,因為我想告訴你們約瑟芬姑婆來了,你們終究得上樓睡,可我太累了,睡著了。

passages.original: I hope you didn’t disturb your aunt, Diana.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望你哋冇打擾你哋嘅姑婆,黛安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你們沒有打擾你們的姑婆,黛安娜。」

passages.original: Diana preserved a discreet silence, but she and Anne exchanged furtive smiles of guilty amusement across the table.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜謹慎地保持沉默,但佢同安妮隔住桌子交換住心虛嘅、覺得好笑嘅隱祕笑容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜謹慎地保持沉默,但她和安妮隔著桌子交換著心虛的、覺得好笑的隱祕笑容。

passages.original: Anne hurried home after breakfast and so remained in blissful ignorance of the disturbance which presently resulted in the Barry household until the late afternoon, when she went down to Mrs. Lynde’s on an errand for Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 早餐後安妮匆匆回咗家,因此對巴里家不久後發生嘅騷亂一無所知,一直到傍晚,佢替瑪麗拉去林德太太家辦件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早餐後安妮匆匆回了家,因此對巴里家不久後發生的騷亂一無所知,一直到傍晚,她替瑪麗拉去林德太太家辦件事。

passages.original: “So you and Diana nearly frightened poor old Miss Barry to death last night?” said Mrs. Lynde severely, but with a twinkle in her eye.
passages.vernacular: 「咁講你同黛安娜琴晚差點把可憐嘅老巴里小姐嚇死喇?」林德太太嚴厲地講,但眼裡有一絲閃爍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這麼說你和黛安娜昨晚差點把可憐的老巴里小姐嚇死了?」林德太太嚴厲地說,但眼裡有一絲閃爍。

passages.original: “Mrs. Barry was here a few minutes ago on her way to Carmody.
passages.vernacular: 「巴里太太幾分鐘前去卡莫迪嘅路上嚟過呢兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴里太太幾分鐘前去卡莫迪的路上來過這兒。

passages.original: She’s feeling real worried over it.
passages.vernacular: 佢為此真嘅好擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她為此真的很擔心。

passages.original: Old Miss Barry was in a terrible temper when she got up this morning--and Josephine Barry’s temper is no joke, I can tell you that.
passages.vernacular: 老巴里小姐今日早晨起床時脾氣可怕——約瑟芬·巴里嘅脾氣可唔係鬧住玩嘅,我告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老巴里小姐今天早晨起床時脾氣可怕——約瑟芬·巴里的脾氣可不是鬧著玩的,我告訴你。

passages.original: She wouldn’t speak to Diana at all.”
passages.vernacular: 佢完全唔肯跟黛安娜講話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她完全不肯跟黛安娜說話。」

passages.original: “It wasn’t Diana’s fault,” said Anne contritely.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰唔係黛安娜嘅錯,」安妮悔恨地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那不是黛安娜的錯,」安妮悔恨地說。

passages.original: “It was mine.
passages.vernacular: 「係我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是我的。

passages.original: I suggested racing to see who would get into bed first.”
passages.vernacular: 係我提議賽跑,睇邊個先到床上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是我提議賽跑,看誰先到床上。」

passages.original: “I knew it!” said Mrs. Lynde, with the exultation of a correct guesser.
passages.vernacular: 「我就知道!」林德太太講,帶住猜對嘅得意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就知道!」林德太太說,帶著猜對的得意。

passages.original: “I knew that idea came out of your head.
passages.vernacular: 「我就知道嗰主意係從你腦袋裡出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就知道那主意是從你腦袋裡出來的。

passages.original: Well, it’s made a nice lot of trouble, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,闖咗一大堆麻煩,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,闖了一大堆麻煩,就是這樣。

passages.original: Old Miss Barry came out to stay for a month, but she declares she won’t stay another day and is going right back to town tomorrow, Sunday and all as it is.
passages.vernacular: 老巴里小姐係嚟住一個月嘅,可佢聲稱一天都不多待喇,聽日就回城,雖然係星期天乜嘢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老巴里小姐是來住一個月的,可她聲稱一天也不多待了,明天就回城,雖然是星期天什麼的。

passages.original: She’d have gone today if they could have taken her.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋能送佢,佢今日就走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他們能送她,她今天就走了。

passages.original: She had promised to pay for a quarter’s music lessons for Diana, but now she is determined to do nothing at all for such a tomboy.
passages.vernacular: 佢答應過付一個季度嘅音樂課學費畀黛安娜,但而家佢決心為咁樣一個假小子乜嘢都不做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她答應過付一個季度的音樂課學費給黛安娜,但現在她決心為這樣一個假小子什麼也不做。

passages.original: Oh, I guess they had a lively time of it there this morning.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我猜今日早晨佢哋嗰兒鬧得夠熱鬧嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我猜今天早晨他們那兒鬧得夠熱鬧的。

passages.original: The Barrys must feel cut up.
passages.vernacular: 巴里家一定好難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里家一定很難受。

passages.original: Old Miss Barry is rich and they’d like to keep on the good side of her.
passages.vernacular: 老巴里小姐好有錢,佢哋想一直討佢嘅歡心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老巴里小姐很有錢,他們想一直討她的歡心。

passages.original: Of course, Mrs. Barry didn’t say just that to me, but I’m a pretty good judge of human nature, that’s what.”
passages.vernacular: 當然,巴里太太冇對我咁講,但我好會睇人,就係咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,巴里太太沒有對我這麼說,但我很會看人,就是這樣。」

passages.original: “I’m such an unlucky girl,” mourned Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我係咁不幸嘅女孩,」安妮哀嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是這麼不幸的女孩,」安妮哀嘆道。

passages.original: “I’m always getting into scrapes myself and getting my best friends--people I’d shed my heart’s blood for--into them too.
passages.vernacular: 「我自己總是惹麻煩,而且把我最好嘅朋友——我願意為佢哋流盡心血嘅人——都拖進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我自己總是惹麻煩,而且把我最好的朋友——我願意為他們流盡心血的人——也拖進去。

passages.original: Can you tell me why it is so, Mrs. Lynde?”
passages.vernacular: 您能告訴我點解會咁樣嗎,林德太太?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您能告訴我為什麼會這樣嗎,林德太太?」

passages.original: “It’s because you’re too heedless and impulsive, child, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 「因為你太粗心大意、太衝動喇,細路,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為你太粗心大意、太衝動了,孩子,就是這樣。

passages.original: You never stop to think--whatever comes into your head to say or do you say or do it without a moment’s reflection.”
passages.vernacular: 你從不停下嚟想一想——不管心裡冒出乜嘢要講或要做嘅,你不加思索地就講就做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你從不停下來想一想——不管心裡冒出什麼要說或要做的,你不加思索地就說就做。」

passages.original: “Oh, but that’s the best of it,” protested Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,但嗰恰恰係最好嘅地方,」安妮抗議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,但那恰恰是最好的地方,」安妮抗議。

passages.original: “Something just flashes into your mind, so exciting, and you must out with it.
passages.vernacular: 「有乜嘢嘢閃過你嘅腦海,幾咁刺激,你必須講出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有什麼東西閃過你的腦海,多麼刺激,你必須說出來。

passages.original: If you stop to think it over you spoil it all.
passages.vernacular: 如果你停下嚟想,就全毀喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你停下來想,就全毀了。

passages.original: Haven’t you never felt that yourself, Mrs. Lynde?”
passages.vernacular: 您自己從冇過呢種感覺嗎,林德太太?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您自己從沒有過這種感覺嗎,林德太太?」

passages.original: No, Mrs. Lynde had not.
passages.vernacular: 冇,林德太太冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,林德太太沒有。

passages.original: She shook her head sagely.
passages.vernacular: 佢明智地搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她明智地搖搖頭。

passages.original: “You must learn to think a little, Anne, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 「你得學會稍微想一想,安妮,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你得學會稍微想一想,安妮,就是這樣。

passages.original: The proverb you need to go by is ‘Look before you leap’--especially into spare-room beds.”
passages.vernacular: 你需要遵循嘅格言係『三思而後行』——尤其係跳進備用客房嘅床之前。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你需要遵循的格言是『三思而後行』——尤其是跳進備用客房的床之前。」

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde laughed comfortably over her mild joke, but Anne remained pensive.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太為自己呢個溫和嘅玩笑舒服地笑喇,但安妮仍然若有所思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太為自己這個溫和的玩笑舒服地笑了,但安妮仍然若有所思。

passages.original: She saw nothing to laugh at in the situation, which to her eyes appeared very serious.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇不出呢種情形有乜嘢好笑嘅,喺佢眼裡佢顯得好嚴重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看不出這種情形有什麼好笑的,在她眼裡它顯得非常嚴重。

passages.original: When she left Mrs. Lynde’s she took her way across the crusted fields to Orchard Slope.
passages.vernacular: 離開林德太太家時,佢穿過結咗殼嘅田野,朝果園坡走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離開林德太太家時,她穿過結了殼的田野,朝果園坡走去。

passages.original: Diana met her at the kitchen door.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜喺廚房門口迎接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜在廚房門口迎接她。

passages.original: “Your Aunt Josephine was very cross about it, wasn’t she?” whispered Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅約瑟芬姑婆為此好生氣,係唔係?」安妮悄悄問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的約瑟芬姑婆為此非常生氣,是不是?」安妮悄悄問。

passages.original: “Yes,” answered Diana, stifling a giggle with an apprehensive glance over her shoulder at the closed sitting-room door.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」黛安娜回答,憋住咯咯嘅笑聲,擔心地回頭睇咗一眼緊閉嘅起居室門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」黛安娜回答,憋住咯咯的笑聲,擔心地回頭看了一眼緊閉的起居室門。

passages.original: “She was fairly dancing with rage, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「佢氣得簡直喺跳腳,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她氣得簡直在跳腳,安妮。

passages.original: Oh, how she scolded.
passages.vernacular: 哦,佢罵得多厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,她罵得多厲害。

passages.original: She said I was the worst-behaved girl she ever saw and that my parents ought to be ashamed of the way they had brought me up.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我係佢見過嘅最冇規矩嘅女孩,我父母應該為佢哋咁樣教養我而感到羞愧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我是她見過的最沒規矩的女孩,我父母應該為他們這樣教養我而感到羞愧。

passages.original: She says she won’t stay and I’m sure I don’t care.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢不待喇,我肯定我不在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她不待了,我肯定我不在乎。

passages.original: But Father and Mother do.”
passages.vernacular: 但爸爸媽媽在乎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但爸爸媽媽在乎。」

passages.original: “Why didn’t you tell them it was my fault?” demanded Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「你點解不告訴佢哋係我嘅錯?」安妮質問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼不告訴他們是我的錯?」安妮質問。

passages.original: “It’s likely I’d do such a thing, isn’t it?” said Diana with just scorn.
passages.vernacular: 「我大概會做呢種事,對不對?」黛安娜講,帶住正當嘅不屑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我大概會做這種事,對不對?」黛安娜說,帶著正當的不屑。

passages.original: “I’m no telltale, Anne Shirley, and anyhow I was just as much to blame as you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我可唔係告密嘅人,安妮·雪莉,而且不管點樣,我嘅過錯同你一樣大。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可不是告密的人,安妮·雪莉,而且不管怎樣,我的過錯和你一樣大。」

passages.original: “Well, I’m going in to tell her myself,” said Anne resolutely.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我要進去親自告訴佢,」安妮堅決地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我要進去親自告訴她,」安妮堅決地說。

passages.original: Diana stared.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜盯住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜盯著她。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley, you’d never! why--she’ll eat you alive!”
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,你絕唔能夠!哎呀——佢會把你活吞咗嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,你絕不能!哎呀——她會把你活吞了的!」

passages.original: “Don’t frighten me any more than I am frightened,” implored Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「唔好再嚇我喇,我已經夠害怕嘅喇,」安妮懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別再嚇我了,我已經夠害怕的了,」安妮懇求道。

passages.original: “I’d rather walk up to a cannon’s mouth.
passages.vernacular: 「我寧願走到炮口前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我寧願走到炮口前。

passages.original: But I’ve got to do it, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 但我必須做,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我必須做,黛安娜。

passages.original: It was my fault and I’ve got to confess.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我嘅錯,我必須坦白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我的錯,我必須坦白。

passages.original: I’ve had practice in confessing, fortunately.”
passages.vernacular: 幸好我有坦白嘅經驗。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸好我有坦白的經驗。」

passages.original: “Well, she’s in the room,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,佢喺嗰個房間裡,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,她在那個房間裡,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “You can go in if you want to.
passages.vernacular: 「你要係想進去,可以進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要是想進去,可以進去。

passages.original: I wouldn’t dare.
passages.vernacular: 我唔敢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不敢。

passages.original: And I don’t believe you’ll do a bit of good.”
passages.vernacular: 而且我不相信你會有啲好處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我不相信你會有一點好處。」

passages.original: With this encouragement Anne bearded the lion in its den--that is to say, walked resolutely up to the sitting-room door and knocked faintly.
passages.vernacular: 有咗呢番鼓勵,安妮就虎穴捋鬚——都就係講,堅決地走向起居室嘅門,輕輕敲咗敲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有了這番鼓勵,安妮就虎穴捋鬚——也就是說,堅決地走向起居室的門,輕輕敲了敲。

passages.original: A sharp “Come in” followed.
passages.vernacular: 一聲尖銳嘅「進嚟」隨之而嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一聲尖銳的「進來」隨之而來。

passages.original: Miss Josephine Barry, thin, prim, and rigid, was knitting fiercely by the fire, her wrath quite unappeased and her eyes snapping through her gold-rimmed glasses.
passages.vernacular: 約瑟芬·巴里小姐,瘦削、拘謹、僵硬,正在爐火邊猛烈地織住毛線,怒氣根本冇消,眼睛透過金邊眼鏡劈啪閃爍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約瑟芬·巴里小姐,瘦削、拘謹、僵硬,正在爐火邊猛烈地織著毛線,怒氣根本沒消,眼睛透過金邊眼鏡劈啪閃爍。

passages.original: She wheeled around in her chair, expecting to see Diana, and beheld a white-faced girl whose great eyes were brimmed up with a mixture of desperate courage and shrinking terror.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺椅子裡轉過身嚟,以為會睇到黛安娜,卻睇到一個臉色蒼白嘅女孩,大眼睛裡充滿咗絕望嘅勇氣同畏縮嘅恐懼嘅混合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在椅子裡轉過身來,以為會看到黛安娜,卻看到一個臉色蒼白的女孩,大眼睛裡充滿了絕望的勇氣和畏縮的恐懼的混合。

passages.original: “Who are you?” demanded Miss Josephine Barry, without ceremony.
passages.vernacular: 「你係邊個?」約瑟芬·巴里小姐毫不客氣地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是誰?」約瑟芬·巴里小姐毫不客氣地問。

passages.original: “I’m Anne of Green Gables,” said the small visitor tremulously, clasping her hands with her characteristic gesture, “and I’ve come to confess, if you please.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係綠色屋頂嘅安妮,」小訪客顫抖住講,以佢特有嘅姿勢雙手緊握,「我係嚟坦白嘅,如果您允許嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是綠色屋頂的安妮,」小訪客顫抖著說,以她特有的姿勢雙手緊握,「我是來坦白的,如果您允許的話。」

passages.original: “Confess what?”
passages.vernacular: 「坦白乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「坦白什麼?」

passages.original: “That it was all my fault about jumping into bed on you last night.
passages.vernacular: 「琴晚跳到您身上嘅事全係我嘅錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「昨晚跳到您身上的事全是我的錯。

passages.original: I suggested it.
passages.vernacular: 係我提議嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是我提議的。

passages.original: Diana would never have thought of such a thing, I am sure.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜決唔會想到呢種事,我肯定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜決不會想到這種事,我肯定。

passages.original: Diana is a very ladylike girl, Miss Barry.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜係個好有教養嘅女孩,巴里小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜是個非常有教養的女孩,巴里小姐。

passages.original: So you must see how unjust it is to blame her.”
passages.vernacular: 所以您必須明白怪佢幾咁不公平。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以您必須明白怪她多麼不公平。」

passages.original: “Oh, I must, hey?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我必須明白,係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我必須明白,是嗎?

passages.original: I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least.
passages.vernacular: 我倒覺得至少跳嘅部分黛安娜都有份。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我倒覺得至少跳的部分黛安娜也有份。

passages.original: Such carryings on in a respectable house!”
passages.vernacular: 喺一個體面嘅人家裡咁樣胡鬧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一個體面的人家裡這樣胡鬧!」

passages.original: “But we were only in fun,” persisted Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「但我哋只係鬧住玩,」安妮堅持。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我們只是鬧著玩,」安妮堅持。

passages.original: “I think you ought to forgive us, Miss Barry, now that we’ve apologized.
passages.vernacular: 「我想您應該原諒我哋,巴里小姐,既然我哋已經道歉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想您應該原諒我們,巴里小姐,既然我們已經道歉了。

passages.original: And anyhow, please forgive Diana and let her have her music lessons.
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,請原諒黛安娜,讓佢上音樂課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,請原諒黛安娜,讓她上音樂課。

passages.original: Diana’s heart is set on her music lessons, Miss Barry, and I know too well what it is to set your heart on a thing and not get it.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜嘅心就喺佢嘅音樂課上,巴里小姐,而我太清楚乜嘢叫心就喺一件事上卻得唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜的心就在她的音樂課上,巴里小姐,而我太清楚什麼叫心就在一件事上卻得不到。

passages.original: If you must be cross with anyone, be cross with me.
passages.vernacular: 如果您一定要對邊個生氣,就對我生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您一定要對誰生氣,就對我生氣。

passages.original: I’ve been so used in my early days to having people cross at me that I can endure it much better than Diana can.”
passages.vernacular: 我早年已習慣咗人哋對我生氣,所以我比黛安娜更能忍受。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我早年已習慣了人們對我生氣,所以我比黛安娜更能忍受。」

passages.original: Much of the snap had gone out of the old lady’s eyes by this time and was replaced by a twinkle of amused interest.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣老太太眼睛里嘅銳氣已消去許多,代之以一絲覺得有趣嘅興趣嘅閃爍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時老太太眼睛里的銳氣已消去許多,代之以一絲覺得有趣的興趣的閃爍。

passages.original: But she still said severely:
passages.vernacular: 但佢仍然嚴厲地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她仍然嚴厲地說:

passages.original: “I don’t think it is any excuse for you that you were only in fun.
passages.vernacular: 「我不覺得你哋只係鬧住玩就能算藉口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不覺得你們只是鬧著玩就能算藉口。

passages.original: Little girls never indulged in that kind of fun when I was young.
passages.vernacular: 我年輕嘅時候,小女孩從不放縱嗰種玩樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我年輕的時候,小女孩從不放縱那種玩樂。

passages.original: You don’t know what it is to be awakened out of a sound sleep, after a long and arduous journey, by two great girls coming bounce down on you.”
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道喺長途艱苦嘅旅行之後,從酣瞓中被兩個大女孩蹦蹦跳跳地壓上嚟驚醒係乜嘢滋味。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道在長途艱苦的旅行之後,從酣睡中被兩個大女孩蹦蹦跳跳地壓上來驚醒是什麼滋味。」

passages.original: “I don’t know, but I can imagine,” said Anne eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,但我能想像,」安妮急切地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,但我能想像,」安妮急切地說。

passages.original: “I’m sure it must have been very disturbing.
passages.vernacular: 「我肯定嗰一定好令人不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我肯定那一定非常令人不安。

passages.original: But then, there is our side of it too.
passages.vernacular: 但係,我哋呢邊都有道理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,我們這邊也有道理。

passages.original: Have you any imagination, Miss Barry?
passages.vernacular: 您有想像力嗎,巴里小姐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您有想像力嗎,巴里小姐?

passages.original: If you have, just put yourself in our place.
passages.vernacular: 如果有,請把自己放喺我哋嘅位置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果有,請把自己放在我們的位置。

passages.original: We didn’t know there was anybody in that bed and you nearly scared us to death.
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔知道嗰張床上有人,您差點把我哋嚇死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不知道那張床上有人,您差點把我們嚇死。

passages.original: It was simply awful the way we felt.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅感覺簡直可怕極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的感覺簡直可怕極了。

passages.original: And then we couldn’t sleep in the spare room after being promised.
passages.vernacular: 而且之後,答應我哋嘅備用客房都冇能瞓成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且之後,答應我們的備用客房也沒能睡成。

passages.original: I suppose you are used to sleeping in spare rooms.
passages.vernacular: 我想您習慣瞓備用客房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想您習慣睡備用客房。

passages.original: But just imagine what you would feel like if you were a little orphan girl who had never had such an honor.”
passages.vernacular: 但請想像一下,如果您係個從冇享有過呢種榮耀嘅小孤女,您會係乜嘢感覺。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但請想像一下,如果您是個從沒享有過這種榮耀的小孤女,您會是什麼感覺。」

passages.original: All the snap had gone by this time.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣所有嘅銳氣都消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時所有的銳氣都消失了。

passages.original: Miss Barry actually laughed--a sound which caused Diana, waiting in speechless anxiety in the kitchen outside, to give a great gasp of relief.
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐竟然笑喇——呢聲音讓喺外面廚房裡無言焦急地等待嘅黛安娜,大大地鬆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐竟然笑了——這聲音讓在外面廚房裡無言焦急地等待的黛安娜,大大地鬆了口氣。

passages.original: “I’m afraid my imagination is a little rusty--it’s so long since I used it,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「我恐怕我嘅想像力有點生銹喇——我太久冇用喇,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我恐怕我的想像力有點生銹了——我太久沒用了,」她說。

passages.original: “I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine.
passages.vernacular: 「我敢講你要求同情嘅理由同我嘅一樣有力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢說你要求同情的理由和我的一樣有力。

passages.original: It all depends on the way we look at it.
passages.vernacular: 呢都取決於我哋點睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這都取決於我們怎麼看。

passages.original: Sit down here and tell me about yourself.”
passages.vernacular: 坐喺呢兒,跟我講講你自己嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 坐在這兒,跟我說說你自己的事。」

passages.original: “I am very sorry I can’t,” said Anne firmly.
passages.vernacular: 「好抱歉我唔能夠,」安妮堅定地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很抱歉我不能,」安妮堅定地說。

passages.original: “I would like to, because you seem like an interesting lady, and you might even be a kindred spirit although you don’t look very much like it.
passages.vernacular: 「我好想,因為您睇上去像一位有趣嘅女士,甚至可能係志同道合嘅人,儘管您睇上去不太像。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很想,因為您看上去像一位有趣的女士,甚至可能是志同道合的人,儘管您看上去不太像。

passages.original: But it is my duty to go home to Miss Marilla Cuthbert.
passages.vernacular: 但我嘅責任係回家去瑪麗拉·卡思伯特小姐嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我的責任是回家去瑪麗拉·卡思伯特小姐那兒。

passages.original: Miss Marilla Cuthbert is a very kind lady who has taken me to bring up properly.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉·卡思伯特小姐係一位好善良嘅女士,佢收養咗我好好撫養。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉·卡思伯特小姐是一位非常善良的女士,她收養了我好好撫養。

passages.original: She is doing her best, but it is very discouraging work.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺盡最大努力,但呢個係令人好洩氣嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在盡最大努力,但這是令人非常洩氣的工作。

passages.original: You must not blame her because I jumped on the bed.
passages.vernacular: 您不該因為我跳到床上而責怪佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不該因為我跳到床上而責怪她。

passages.original: But before I go I do wish you would tell me if you will forgive Diana and stay just as long as you meant to in Avonlea.”
passages.vernacular: 但喺我走之前,我真希望您告訴我,您係咪原諒黛安娜,並按原計劃喺阿文利住多久就住多久。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在我走之前,我真希望您告訴我,您是否原諒黛安娜,並按原計劃在阿文利住多久就住多久。」

passages.original: “I think perhaps I will if you will come over and talk to me occasionally,” said Miss Barry.
passages.vernacular: 「我想或者我會,只要你偶爾過嚟跟我聊聊,」巴里小姐講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想也許我會,只要你偶爾過來跟我聊聊,」巴里小姐說。

passages.original: That evening Miss Barry gave Diana a silver bangle bracelet and told the senior members of the household that she had unpacked her valise.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天傍晚,巴里小姐送畀黛安娜一隻銀手鐲,並對家裡嘅長輩講,佢已經把行李箱打開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天傍晚,巴里小姐送給黛安娜一隻銀手鐲,並對家裡的長輩說,她已經把行李箱打開了。

passages.original: “I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,” she said frankly.
passages.vernacular: 「我決定留下嚟,純粹為了更好地認識嗰個安妮丫頭,」佢坦率地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我決定留下來,純粹為了更好地認識那個安妮丫頭,」她坦率地說。

passages.original: “She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢逗我開心,喺我呢個年紀,有趣嘅人係難得嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她逗我開心,在我這個年紀,有趣的人是難得的。」

passages.original: Marilla’s only comment when she heard the story was, “I told you so.”
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉聽咗呢個故事後唯一嘅評論係:「我早講過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉聽了這個故事後唯一的評論是:「我早說過。」

passages.original: This was for Matthew’s benefit.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係講畀馬修聽嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是說給馬修聽的。

passages.original: Miss Barry stayed her month out and over.
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐住滿咗一個月仲多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐住滿了一個月還多。

passages.original: She was a more agreeable guest than usual, for Anne kept her in good humor.
passages.vernacular: 佢比平常更係個令人愉快嘅客人,因為安妮讓佢保持好心情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她比平常更是個令人愉快的客人,因為安妮讓她保持好心情。

passages.original: They became firm friends.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋成咗牢固嘅朋友。
