passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們成了牢固的朋友。

passages.original: When Miss Barry went away she said:
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐離開時講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐離開時說:

passages.original: “Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep.”
passages.vernacular: 「記住,你呢個安妮丫頭,你進城時要嚟睇我,我會讓你瞓喺我最最備用嘅備用客房嘅床上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「記住,你這個安妮丫頭,你進城時要來看我,我會讓你睡在我最最備用的備用客房的床上。」

passages.original: “Miss Barry was a kindred spirit, after all,” Anne confided to Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「巴里小姐終究係個志同道合嘅人,」安妮向瑪麗拉吐露。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴里小姐終究是個志同道合的人,」安妮向瑪麗拉吐露。

passages.original: “You wouldn’t think so to look at her, but she is.
passages.vernacular: 「睇佢嘅樣子您唔會咁認為,但佢確實係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看她的樣子您不會這麼認為,但她確實是。

passages.original: You don’t find it right out at first, as in Matthew’s case, but after a while you come to see it.
passages.vernacular: 你一開始唔會直接發現,像馬修嗰樣,但過一陣子你就會睇出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一開始不會直接發現,像馬修那樣,但過一陣子你就會看出來。

passages.original: Kindred spirits are not so scarce as I used to think.
passages.vernacular: 志同道合嘅人冇我以前想嘅咁少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 志同道合的人沒有我以前想的那麼少。

passages.original: It’s splendid to find out there are so many of them in the world.”
passages.vernacular: 發現世上有咁多咁樣嘅人,真係太棒喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 發現世上有這麼多這樣的人,真是太棒了。」

chapters.title: Ch. XX A Good Imagination Gone Wrong 第二十章:好想像力走歪了

passages.original: CH SPRING had come once more to Green Gables--the beautiful capricious, reluctant Canadian spring, lingering along through April and May in a succession of sweet, fresh, chilly days, with pink sunsets and miracles of resurrection and growth.
passages.vernacular: 春天又回到咗綠色屋頂——嗰美麗、變幻無常、遲遲唔肯嚟嘅加攞大嘅春天,喺四月同五月間斷斷續續地逗留,係一連串甜美、清新、微寒嘅日子,有粉紅嘅落日,以及復甦同生長嘅奇蹟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 春天又回到了綠色屋頂——那美麗、變幻無常、遲遲不肯來的加拿大的春天,在四月和五月間斷斷續續地逗留,是一連串甜美、清新、微寒的日子,有粉紅的落日,以及復甦和生長的奇蹟。

passages.original: The maples in Lover’s Lane were red budded and little curly ferns pushed up around the Dryad’s Bubble.
passages.vernacular: 情人小徑嘅楓樹冒出咗紅色嘅花苞,小小嘅捲曲嘅蕨類喺林中仙子泉周圍鑽咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 情人小徑的楓樹冒出了紅色的花苞,小小的捲曲的蕨類在林中仙子泉周圍鑽了出來。

passages.original: Away up in the barrens, behind Mr. Silas Sloane’s place, the Mayflowers blossomed out, pink and white stars of sweetness under their brown leaves.
passages.vernacular: 遠喺荒原上,賽拉斯·斯隆先生家後面,五月花開喇,喺棕色嘅葉子下係粉紅同白色嘅甜美星星。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遠在荒原上,賽拉斯·斯隆先生家後面,五月花開了,在棕色的葉子下是粉紅和白色的甜美星星。

passages.original: All the school girls and boys had one golden afternoon gathering them, coming home in the clear, echoing twilight with arms and baskets full of flowery spoil.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅男學生女學生都有一個金色嘅下午去採佢哋,喺清澈、迴響嘅暮色中回家,手臂上同籃子裡滿係鮮花嘅戰利品。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的男學生女學生都有一個金色的下午去採它們,在清澈、迴響的暮色中回家,手臂上和籃子裡滿是鮮花的戰利品。

passages.original: “I’m so sorry for people who live in lands where there are no Mayflowers,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我真為住喺冇五月花嘅地方嘅人哋難過,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真為住在沒有五月花的地方的人們難過,」安妮說。

passages.original: “Diana says perhaps they have something better, but there couldn’t be anything better than Mayflowers, could there, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 「黛安娜講或者佢哋有更好嘅嘢,但唔可能有比五月花更好嘅嘢喇,係唔係,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黛安娜說也許他們有更好的東西,但不可能有比五月花更好的東西了,是不是,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: And Diana says if they don’t know what they are like they don’t miss them.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜仲講,如果佢哋唔知道佢哋係乜嘢樣子,就唔會想念佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜還說,如果他們不知道它們是什麼樣子,就不會想念它們。

passages.original: But I think that is the saddest thing of all.
passages.vernacular: 但我覺得呢個係最悲哀嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我覺得這是最悲哀的事。

passages.original: I think it would be tragic, Marilla, not to know what Mayflowers are like and not to miss them.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得,唔知道五月花係乜嘢樣子,而且唔想念佢哋,瑪麗拉,係好悲劇嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得,不知道五月花是什麼樣子,而且不想念它們,瑪麗拉,是很悲劇的。

passages.original: Do you know what I think Mayflowers are, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 您知道我覺得五月花係乜嘢嗎,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道我覺得五月花是什麼嗎,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: I think they must be the souls of the flowers that died last summer and this is their heaven.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得佢哋一定係去年夏天死去嘅花嘅靈魂,呢度係佢哋嘅天堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得它們一定是去年夏天死去的花的靈魂,這裡是它們的天堂。

passages.original: But we had a splendid time today, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 不過今日我哋玩得好痛快,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過今天我們玩得非常痛快,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: We had our lunch down in a big mossy hollow by an old well--such a romantic spot.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺一口老井旁一個長滿青苔嘅大窪地裡食嘅午飯——咁浪漫嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在一口老井旁一個長滿青苔的大窪地裡吃的午飯——那麼浪漫的地方。

passages.original: Charlie Sloane dared Arty Gillis to jump over it, and Arty did because he wouldn’t take a dare.
passages.vernacular: 查理·斯隆向阿蒂·吉利斯挑戰,讓佢跳過去,阿蒂就跳喇,因為佢唔肯接受挑戰被激將。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 查理·斯隆向阿蒂·吉利斯挑戰,讓他跳過去,阿蒂就跳了,因為他不肯接受挑戰被激將。

passages.original: Nobody would in school.
passages.vernacular: 喺學校,邊個都唔會接受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在學校,誰也不會接受。

passages.original: It is very fashionable to dare.
passages.vernacular: 挑戰好時髦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 挑戰很時髦。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips gave all the Mayflowers he found to Prissy Andrews and I heard him to say ‘sweets to the sweet.’
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生把佢找到嘅所有五月花都畀咗普麗茜·安德魯斯,我聽見佢講『甜美獻畀甜美』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生把他找到的所有五月花都給了普麗茜·安德魯斯,我聽見他說『甜美獻給甜美』。

passages.original: He got that out of a book, I know; but it shows he has some imagination.
passages.vernacular: 我知道佢係從書里攞嚟嘅;但呢表明佢有啲想像力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道他是從書里拿來的;但這表明他有一點想像力。

passages.original: I was offered some Mayflowers too, but I rejected them with scorn.
passages.vernacular: 都有人要送我啲五月花,但我輕蔑地拒絕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也有人要送我一些五月花,但我輕蔑地拒絕了。

passages.original: I can’t tell you the person’s name because I have vowed never to let it cross my lips.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠告訴您嗰個人嘅名字,因為我發過誓永遠不讓佢從我嘴裡講出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能告訴您那個人的名字,因為我發過誓永遠不讓它從我嘴裡說出來。

passages.original: We made wreaths of the Mayflowers and put them on our hats; and when the time came to go home we marched in procession down the road, two by two, with our bouquets and wreaths, singing ‘My Home on the Hill.’
passages.vernacular: 我哋用五月花編成花環戴喺帽子上;到咗回家嘅時候,我哋捧住花束、戴住花環,排成兩人一排嘅隊伍,沿住路遊行,唱住《山上嘅家》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們用五月花編成花環戴在帽子上;到了回家的時候,我們捧著花束、戴著花環,排成兩人一排的隊伍,沿著路遊行,唱著《山上的家》。

passages.original: Oh, it was so thrilling, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 哦,太激動人心喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,太激動人心了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: All Mr. Silas Sloane’s folks rushed out to see us and everybody we met on the road stopped and stared after us.
passages.vernacular: 賽拉斯·斯隆先生一家人都衝出嚟睇我哋,我哋喺路上遇見嘅每個人都停下嚟盯住我哋睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 賽拉斯·斯隆先生一家人都衝出來看我們,我們在路上遇見的每個人都停下來盯著我們看。

passages.original: We made a real sensation.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋引起咗真正嘅轟動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們引起了真正的轟動。」

passages.original: “Not much wonder!
passages.vernacular: 「呢都不奇怪!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這也不奇怪!

passages.original: Such silly doings!” was Marilla’s response.
passages.vernacular: 做咁傻嘅事!」瑪麗拉回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 做這麼傻的事!」瑪麗拉回答。

passages.original: After the Mayflowers came the violets, and Violet Vale was empurpled with them.
passages.vernacular: 五月花之後係紫羅蘭,紫羅蘭谷被佢哋染成咗紫色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 五月花之後是紫羅蘭,紫羅蘭谷被它們染成了紫色。

passages.original: Anne walked through it on her way to school with reverent steps and worshiping eyes, as if she trod on holy ground.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺上學嘅路上穿過嗰度,腳步恭敬,眼神崇拜,好像佢踩喺神聖嘅土地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在上學的路上穿過那裡,腳步恭敬,眼神崇拜,好像她踩在神聖的土地上。

passages.original: “Somehow,” she told Diana, “when I’m going through here I don’t really care whether Gil--whether anybody gets ahead of me in class or not.
passages.vernacular: 「唔知怎嘅,」佢對黛安娜講,「我走過呢度嘅時候,並不真嘅在乎吉爾——係咪有人喺班上超過我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不知怎的,」她對黛安娜說,「我走過這裡的時候,並不真的在乎吉爾——是否有人在班上超過我。

passages.original: But when I’m up in school it’s all different and I care as much as ever.
passages.vernacular: 但係我到咗學校,一切都不同喇,我跟以前一樣在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是我到了學校,一切都不同了,我跟以前一樣在乎。

passages.original: There’s such a lot of different Annes in me.
passages.vernacular: 我身上有咁多不同嘅安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我身上有那麼多不同的安妮。

passages.original: I sometimes think that is why I’m such a troublesome person.
passages.vernacular: 我有時想,呢個就係點解我係個咁麻煩嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有時想,這就是為什麼我是個這麼麻煩的人。

passages.original: If I was just the one Anne it would be ever so much more comfortable, but then it wouldn’t be half so interesting.”
passages.vernacular: 如果只有一個安妮,會舒服得多,但嗰就一半都冇咁有趣喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果只有一個安妮,會舒服得多,但那就一半也沒這麼有趣了。」

passages.original: One June evening, when the orchards were pink blossomed again, when the frogs were singing silverly sweet in the marshes about the head of the Lake of Shining Waters, and the air was full of the savor of clover fields and balsamic fir woods, Anne was sitting by her gable window.
passages.vernacular: 六月嘅一個傍晚,果園又開滿咗粉紅色嘅花,青蛙喺閃亮湖水上游沼澤裡唱住銀鈴般甜美嘅歌,空氣中充滿咗三葉草田同香脂冷杉林嘅氣味,安妮坐喺佢嘅山牆窗邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 六月的一個傍晚,果園又開滿了粉紅色的花,青蛙在閃亮湖水上游沼澤裡唱著銀鈴般甜美的歌,空氣中充滿了三葉草田和香脂冷杉林的氣味,安妮坐在她的山牆窗邊。

passages.original: She had been studying her lessons, but it had grown too dark to see the book, so she had fallen into wide-eyed reverie, looking out past the boughs of the Snow Queen, once more bestarred with its tufts of blossom.
passages.vernacular: 佢一直喺學習功課,但天色太暗,睇不清書喇,於是佢睜大眼睛陷入遐想,望住窗外雪之女王嘅枝條,上面又繁星般綴滿咗簇簇花朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一直在學習功課,但天色太暗,看不清書了,於是她睜大眼睛陷入遐想,望著窗外雪之女王的枝條,上面又繁星般綴滿了簇簇花朵。

passages.original: In all essential respects the little gable chamber was unchanged.
passages.vernacular: 呢間小山牆房間喺所有主要方面都冇變。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這間小山牆房間在所有主要方面都沒有變。

passages.original: The walls were as white, the pincushion as hard, the chairs as stiffly and yellowly upright as ever.
passages.vernacular: 牆壁依然咁白,針墊依然咁硬,椅子依然咁僵硬、黃黃地直立住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牆壁依然那麼白,針墊依然那麼硬,椅子依然那麼僵硬、黃黃地直立著。

passages.original: Yet the whole character of the room was altered.
passages.vernacular: 然而房間整個嘅性質變喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而房間整個的性質變了。

passages.original: It was full of a new vital, pulsing personality that seemed to pervade it and to be quite independent of schoolgirl books and dresses and ribbons, and even of the cracked blue jug full of apple blossoms on the table.
passages.vernacular: 佢充滿咗一種新嘅有生命嘅、搏動嘅個性,似乎瀰漫咗整個房間,完全獨立於女學生嘅書本同裙子同絲帶,甚至獨立於桌上嗰只插滿蘋果花嘅裂咗嘅藍壺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它充滿了一種新的有生命的、搏動的個性,似乎瀰漫了整個房間,完全獨立於女學生的書本和裙子和絲帶,甚至獨立於桌上那只插滿蘋果花的裂了的藍壺。

passages.original: It was as if all the dreams, sleeping and waking, of its vivid occupant had taken a visible although unmaterial form and had tapestried the bare room with splendid filmy tissues of rainbow and moonshine.
passages.vernacular: 就好像佢生動嘅主人嘅所有夢想,無論瞓住定係醒住,都採取咗一種可見但無形嘅形態,用彩虹同月光嘅華麗輕紗,畀呢光禿禿嘅房間掛上咗掛毯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就好像它生動的主人的所有夢想,無論睡著還是醒著,都採取了一種可見但無形的形態,用彩虹和月光的華麗輕紗,給這光禿禿的房間掛上了掛毯。

passages.original: Presently Marilla came briskly in with some of Anne’s freshly ironed school aprons.
passages.vernacular: 不久瑪麗拉輕快地走進嚟,攞住幾件安妮剛燙好嘅上學圍裙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久瑪麗拉輕快地走進來,拿著幾件安妮剛燙好的上學圍裙。

passages.original: She hung them over a chair and sat down with a short sigh.
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢哋掛喺椅子上,短嘆一聲坐咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把它們掛在椅子上,短嘆一聲坐了下來。

passages.original: She had had one of her headaches that afternoon, and although the pain had gone she felt weak and “tuckered out,” as she expressed it.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天下午佢頭疼發作喇,儘管疼痛已經過去,佢仍然感到虛弱同「筋疲力盡」,用佢嘅話講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天下午她頭疼發作了,儘管疼痛已經過去,她仍然感到虛弱和「筋疲力盡」,用她的話說。

passages.original: Anne looked at her with eyes limpid with sympathy.
passages.vernacular: 安妮用充滿同情嘅清澈眼睛睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮用充滿同情的清澈眼睛看著她。

passages.original: “I do truly wish I could have had the headache in your place, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我真希望能替您頭疼,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真希望能替您頭疼,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I would have endured it joyfully for your sake.”
passages.vernacular: 為了您,我會高高興興地忍受佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了您,我會高高興興地忍受它。」

passages.original: “I guess you did your part in attending to the work and letting me rest,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你已經盡咗你嘅一份力,料理活兒,讓我休息,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你已經盡了你的一份力,料理活兒,讓我休息,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “You seem to have got on fairly well and made fewer mistakes than usual.
passages.vernacular: 「你好像處理得相當好,比平時錯誤少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你好像處理得相當好,比平時錯誤少。

passages.original: Of course it wasn’t exactly necessary to starch Matthew’s handkerchiefs!
passages.vernacular: 當然,畀馬修嘅手帕上漿並唔係完全必要嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,給馬修的手帕上漿並不是完全必要的!

passages.original: And most people when they put a pie in the oven to warm up for dinner take it out and eat it when it gets hot instead of leaving it to be burned to a crisp.
passages.vernacular: 而且大多數人把餡餅放進烤箱熱住準備午飯時,等佢熱咗就會攞出嚟食,而唔係讓佢烤成焦炭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且大多數人把餡餅放進烤箱熱著準備午飯時,等它熱了就會拿出來吃,而不是讓它烤成焦炭。

passages.original: But that doesn’t seem to be your way evidently.”
passages.vernacular: 但顯然呢唔係你嘅作風。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但顯然這不是你的作風。」

passages.original: Headaches always left Marilla somewhat sarcastic.
passages.vernacular: 頭疼總讓瑪麗拉有點愛諷刺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭疼總讓瑪麗拉有點愛諷刺。

passages.original: “Oh, I’m so sorry,” said Anne penitently.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我真抱歉,」安妮悔恨地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我真抱歉,」安妮悔恨地說。

passages.original: “I never thought about that pie from the moment I put it in the oven till now, although I felt instinctively that there was something missing on the dinner table.
passages.vernacular: 「從我把佢放進烤箱到而家,我再冇想過嗰個餡餅,雖然我本能地覺得午飯桌上少咗點乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從我把它放進烤箱到現在,我再沒想過那個餡餅,雖然我本能地覺得午飯桌上少了點什麼。

passages.original: I was firmly resolved, when you left me in charge this morning, not to imagine anything, but keep my thoughts on facts.
passages.vernacular: 今日早晨您把家交畀我管嘅時候,我下定決心唔想像任何嘢,把思想放喺事實上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天早晨您把家交給我管的時候,我下定決心不想像任何東西,把思想放在事實上。

passages.original: I did pretty well until I put the pie in, and then an irresistible temptation came to me to imagine I was an enchanted princess shut up in a lonely tower with a handsome knight riding to my rescue on a coal-black steed.
passages.vernacular: 喺我把餡餅放進去之前我做得相當好,然後一個無法抗拒嘅誘惑襲嚟,讓我想像自己係被關喺孤塔裡嘅魔法公主,一位英俊嘅騎士騎住一匹烏黑嘅駿馬嚟救我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我把餡餅放進去之前我做得相當好,然後一個無法抗拒的誘惑襲來,讓我想像自己是被關在孤塔裡的魔法公主,一位英俊的騎士騎著一匹烏黑的駿馬來救我。

passages.original: So that is how I came to forget the pie.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係我忘咗餡餅嘅原因。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是我忘了餡餅的原因。

passages.original: I didn’t know I starched the handkerchiefs.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道我畀手帕上咗漿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道我給手帕上了漿。

passages.original: All the time I was ironing I was trying to think of a name for a new island Diana and I have discovered up the brook.
passages.vernacular: 熨燙嘅整個過程中,我都喺想畀黛安娜同我喺小溪上游發現嘅新島起個名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 熨燙的整個過程中,我都在想給黛安娜和我在小溪上游發現的新島起個名字。

passages.original: It’s the most ravishing spot, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係最迷人嘅地方,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是最迷人的地方,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: There are two maple trees on it and the brook flows right around it.
passages.vernacular: 上面有兩棵楓樹,小溪從四周流過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面有兩棵楓樹,小溪從四周流過。

passages.original: At last it struck me that it would be splendid to call it Victoria Island because we found it on the Queen’s birthday.
passages.vernacular: 最後我想到,叫佢維多利亞島會好棒,因為我哋係喺女王生日嗰天發現佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後我想到,叫它維多利亞島會很棒,因為我們是在女王生日那天發現它的。

passages.original: Both Diana and I are very loyal.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜同我都好忠誠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜和我都非常忠誠。

passages.original: But I’m sorry about that pie and the handkerchiefs.
passages.vernacular: 但我為嗰個餡餅同手帕感到抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我為那個餡餅和手帕感到抱歉。

passages.original: I wanted to be extra good today because it’s an anniversary.
passages.vernacular: 我今日想特別乖,因為呢個係個紀念日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我今天想特別乖,因為這是個紀念日。

passages.original: Do you remember what happened this day last year, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 您仲記得去年呢一天發生咗乜嘢嗎,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您還記得去年這一天發生了什麼嗎,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: “No, I can’t think of anything special.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,我想不出有乜嘢特別嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我想不出有什麼特別的。」

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, it was the day I came to Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,係我到綠色屋頂嘅嗰一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,是我到綠色屋頂的那一天。

passages.original: I shall never forget it.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠唔會忘記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠不會忘記。

passages.original: It was the turning point in my life.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係我生命中嘅轉折點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是我生命中的轉折點。

passages.original: Of course it wouldn’t seem so important to you.
passages.vernacular: 當然對您來講唔會顯得咁重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然對您來說不會顯得那麼重要。

passages.original: I’ve been here for a year and I’ve been so happy.
passages.vernacular: 我喺呢兒已經一年喇,我過得咁幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在這兒已經一年了,我過得那麼幸福。

passages.original: Of course, I’ve had my troubles, but one can live down troubles.
passages.vernacular: 當然,我有過我嘅煩惱,但人可以把煩惱熬過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,我有過我的煩惱,但人可以把煩惱熬過去。

passages.original: Are you sorry you kept me, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 您後悔留下我嗎,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您後悔留下我嗎,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: “No, I can’t say I’m sorry,” said Marilla, who sometimes wondered how she could have lived before Anne came to Green Gables, “no, not exactly sorry.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我唔能夠講後悔,」瑪麗拉講,佢有時納悶喺安妮嚟到綠色屋頂之前,自己係點生活過嚟嘅,「不,不完全後悔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我不能說後悔,」瑪麗拉說,她有時納悶在安妮來到綠色屋頂之前,自己是怎麼生活過來的,「不,不完全後悔。

passages.original: If you’ve finished your lessons, Anne, I want you to run over and ask Mrs. Barry if she’ll lend me Diana’s apron pattern.”
passages.vernacular: 如果你功課做完喇,安妮,我要你跑過去問問巴里太太,能唔能夠把黛安娜嘅圍裙紙樣借畀我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你功課做完了,安妮,我要你跑過去問問巴里太太,能不能把黛安娜的圍裙紙樣借給我。」

passages.original: “Oh--it’s--it’s too dark,” cried Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦——呢——呢太暗喇,」安妮叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦——這——這太暗了,」安妮叫道。

passages.original: “Too dark?
passages.vernacular: 「太暗喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太暗了?

passages.original: Why, it’s only twilight.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,才剛暮色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,才剛暮色。

passages.original: And goodness knows you’ve gone over often enough after dark.”
passages.vernacular: 而且天知道你天黑後去過多少次喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且天知道你天黑後去過多少次了。」

passages.original: “I’ll go over early in the morning,” said Anne eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「我聽日一早去,」安妮急切地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我明天一早去,」安妮急切地說。

passages.original: “I’ll get up at sunrise and go over, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 「我日出時起床就去,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我日出時起床就去,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: “What has got into your head now, Anne Shirley?
passages.vernacular: 「你而家腦子裡又係點回事,安妮·雪莉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你現在腦子裡又是怎麼回事,安妮·雪莉?

passages.original: I want that pattern to cut out your new apron this evening.
passages.vernacular: 我要嗰個紙樣今晚裁你嘅新圍裙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要那個紙樣今晚裁你的新圍裙。

passages.original: Go at once and be smart too.”
passages.vernacular: 即刻去,都要快。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 立刻去,也要快。」

passages.original: “I’ll have to go around by the road, then,” said Anne, taking up her hat reluctantly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我只好繞大路喇,」安妮不情願地攞起帽子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我只好繞大路了,」安妮不情願地拿起帽子說。

passages.original: “Go by the road and waste half an hour!
passages.vernacular: 「走大路浪費半個鐘頭!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「走大路浪費半個鐘頭!

passages.original: I’d like to catch you!”
passages.vernacular: 我倒想睇睇你敢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我倒想看看你敢!」

passages.original: “I can’t go through the Haunted Wood, Marilla,” cried Anne desperately.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔能夠穿過鬧鬼林,瑪麗拉,」安妮絕望地叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不能穿過鬧鬼林,瑪麗拉,」安妮絕望地叫道。

passages.original: Marilla stared.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉瞪住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉瞪著她。

passages.original: “The Haunted Wood!
passages.vernacular: 「鬧鬼林!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「鬧鬼林!

passages.original: Are you crazy?
passages.vernacular: 你瘋咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你瘋了嗎?

passages.original: What under the canopy is the Haunted Wood?”
passages.vernacular: 鬧鬼林到底係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鬧鬼林到底是什麼?」

passages.original: “The spruce wood over the brook,” said Anne in a whisper.
passages.vernacular: 「溪對面嘅杉樹林,」安妮低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溪對面的杉樹林,」安妮低聲說。

passages.original: “Fiddlesticks!
passages.vernacular: 「胡講八道!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說八道!

passages.original: There is no such thing as a haunted wood anywhere.
passages.vernacular: 任何地方都冇鬧鬼林呢種嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何地方都沒有鬧鬼林這種東西。

passages.original: Who has been telling you such stuff?”
passages.vernacular: 邊個跟你講呢種話嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰跟你說這種話的?」

passages.original: “Nobody,” confessed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「冇人講,」安妮承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒人說,」安妮承認。

passages.original: “Diana and I just imagined the wood was haunted.
passages.vernacular: 「黛安娜同我只係想像嗰片林子鬧鬼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黛安娜和我只是想像那片林子鬧鬼。

passages.original: All the places around here are so--so--commonplace.
passages.vernacular: 呢附近所有嘅地方都咁——咁——平庸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這附近所有的地方都這麼——這麼——平庸。

passages.original: We just got this up for our own amusement.
passages.vernacular: 我哋只係為了自己取樂編出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們只是為了自己取樂編出來的。

passages.original: We began it in April.
passages.vernacular: 我哋四月就開始喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們四月就開始了。

passages.original: A haunted wood is so very romantic, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 鬧鬼林好浪漫,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鬧鬼林非常浪漫,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: We chose the spruce grove because it’s so gloomy.
passages.vernacular: 我哋選咗杉樹林,因為佢咁陰森。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們選了杉樹林,因為它那麼陰森。

passages.original: Oh, we have imagined the most harrowing things.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我哋想像出咗最揪心嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我們想像出了最揪心的事。

passages.original: There’s a white lady walks along the brook just about this time of the night and wrings her hands and utters wailing cries.
passages.vernacular: 有一位白衣女士,差不多呢個時辰沿住小溪走,絞著手,發出哀號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一位白衣女士,差不多這個時辰沿著小溪走,絞著手,發出哀號。

passages.original: She appears when there is to be a death in the family.
passages.vernacular: 佢出現就意味住家裡要死人喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她出現就意味著家裡要死人了。

passages.original: And the ghost of a little murdered child haunts the corner up by Idlewild; it creeps up behind you and lays its cold fingers on your hand--so.
passages.vernacular: 仲有一個被謀殺嘅小孩嘅鬼魂,出沒喺閒遊林上面嘅角落;佢悄悄爬到你身後,用冰冷嘅手指搭喺你手上——像咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有一個被謀殺的小孩的鬼魂,出沒在閒遊林上面的角落;它悄悄爬到你身後,用冰冷的手指搭在你手上——像這樣。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, it gives me a shudder to think of it.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,想到佢我就打冷顫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,想到它我就打冷顫。

passages.original: And there’s a headless man stalks up and down the path and skeletons glower at you between the boughs.
passages.vernacular: 仲有一個無頭人喺小路上大步嚟回走,骷髏從樹枝間瞪住你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有一個無頭人在小路上大步來回走,骷髏從樹枝間瞪著你。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, I wouldn’t go through the Haunted Wood after dark now for anything.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,而家天黑後我講乜嘢都唔會穿過鬧鬼林。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,現在天黑後我說什麼也不會穿過鬧鬼林。

passages.original: I’d be sure that white things would reach out from behind the trees and grab me.”
passages.vernacular: 我肯定白色嘅嘢會從樹後伸出嚟抓住我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我肯定白色的東西會從樹後伸出來抓住我。」

passages.original: “Did ever anyone hear the like!” ejaculated Marilla, who had listened in dumb amazement.
passages.vernacular: 「有邊個聽過呢種事!」瑪麗拉驚呼,佢一直目瞪口呆地聽住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有誰聽過這種事!」瑪麗拉驚呼,她一直目瞪口呆地聽著。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley, do you mean to tell me you believe all that wicked nonsense of your own imagination?”
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,你係想告訴我,你相信你自己想像出嚟嘅嗰啲邪惡嘅胡講八道嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,你是想告訴我,你相信你自己想像出來的那些邪惡的胡說八道嗎?」

passages.original: “Not believe exactly,” faltered Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「不完全係相信,」安妮吞吞吐吐地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不完全是相信,」安妮吞吞吐吐地說。

passages.original: “At least, I don’t believe it in daylight.
passages.vernacular: 「至少,白天我不相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「至少,白天我不相信。

passages.original: But after dark, Marilla, it’s different.
passages.vernacular: 但天黑以後,瑪麗拉,就不一樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但天黑以後,瑪麗拉,就不一樣了。

passages.original: That is when ghosts walk.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係鬼魂走動嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是鬼魂走動的時候。」

passages.original: “There are no such things as ghosts, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 「根本冇鬼魂呢種嘢,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「根本沒有鬼魂這種東西,安妮。」

passages.original: “Oh, but there are, Marilla,” cried Anne eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,但係有嘅,瑪麗拉,」安妮急切地叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,但是有的,瑪麗拉,」安妮急切地叫道。

passages.original: “I know people who have seen them.
passages.vernacular: 「我認識見過佢哋嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我認識見過它們的人。

passages.original: And they are respectable people.
passages.vernacular: 而且佢哋係體面嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且他們是體面的人。

passages.original: Charlie Sloane says that his grandmother saw his grandfather driving home the cows one night after he’d been buried for a year.
passages.vernacular: 查理·斯隆講佢祖母有天晚上睇見佢祖父喺趕牛回家,而佢祖父已經死去埋葬咗一年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 查理·斯隆說他祖母有天晚上看見他祖父在趕牛回家,而他祖父已經死去埋葬了一年。

passages.original: You know Charlie Sloane’s grandmother wouldn’t tell a story for anything.
passages.vernacular: 您知道查理·斯隆嘅祖母決唔會為任何事撒謊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道查理·斯隆的祖母決不會為任何事撒謊。

passages.original: She’s a very religious woman.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個好虔誠嘅女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個很虔誠的女人。

passages.original: And Mrs. Thomas’s father was pursued home one night by a lamb of fire with its head cut off hanging by a strip of skin.
passages.vernacular: 仲有托馬斯太太嘅父親,有天晚上被一隻燃火嘅羔羊追住回家,佢嘅頭被砍下嚟,只靠一條皮掛住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有托馬斯太太的父親,有天晚上被一隻燃火的羔羊追著回家,它的頭被砍下來,只靠一條皮掛著。

passages.original: He said he knew it was the spirit of his brother and that it was a warning he would die within nine days.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢知道嗰個係佢兄弟嘅靈魂,呢個係佢九天內會死嘅警告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他知道那是他兄弟的靈魂,這是他九天內會死的警告。

passages.original: He didn’t, but he died two years after, so you see it was really true.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇死,但兩年後死喇,所以您睇呢個係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒死,但兩年後死了,所以您看這是真的。

passages.original: And Ruby Gillis says--”
passages.vernacular: 而露比·吉利斯講——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而露比·吉利斯說——」

passages.original: “Anne Shirley,” interrupted Marilla firmly, “I never want to hear you talking in this fashion again.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,」瑪麗拉堅決地打斷道,「我再都唔想聽到你咁樣講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,」瑪麗拉堅決地打斷道,「我再也不想聽到你這樣說話。

passages.original: I’ve had my doubts about that imagination of yours right along, and if this is going to be the outcome of it, I won’t countenance any such doings.
passages.vernacular: 我一直都對你嗰想像力有疑慮,如果呢個就係佢嘅結果,我決不縱容任何呢類行為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直都對你那想像力有疑慮,如果這就是它的結果,我決不縱容任何這類行為。

passages.original: You’ll go right over to Barry’s, and you’ll go through that spruce grove, just for a lesson and a warning to you.
passages.vernacular: 你即刻到巴里家去,你要穿過嗰片杉樹林,就當係畀你嘅一個教訓同警告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你馬上到巴里家去,你要穿過那片杉樹林,就當是給你的一個教訓和警告。

passages.original: And never let me hear a word out of your head about haunted woods again.”
passages.vernacular: 再都唔好畀我從你嘴裡聽到一句鬧鬼林嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再也別讓我從你嘴裡聽到一句鬧鬼林的話。」

passages.original: Anne might plead and cry as she liked--and did, for her terror was very real.
passages.vernacular: 安妮可以隨意懇求同哭泣——佢都確實咁樣做喇,因為佢嘅恐懼係真實嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮可以隨意懇求和哭泣——她也確實這樣做了,因為她的恐懼是真實的。

passages.original: Her imagination had run away with her and she held the spruce grove in mortal dread after nightfall.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅想像力失控喇,天黑後佢對嗰片杉樹林怕得要死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的想像力失控了,天黑後她對那片杉樹林怕得要死。

passages.original: But Marilla was inexorable.
passages.vernacular: 但瑪麗拉毫不通融。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但瑪麗拉毫不通融。

passages.original: She marched the shrinking ghost-seer down to the spring and ordered her to proceed straightway over the bridge and into the dusky retreats of wailing ladies and headless specters beyond.
passages.vernacular: 佢把畏縮嘅見鬼者帶到泉邊,命令佢即刻過橋,進入嗰邊哀號嘅女士同無頭幽靈出沒嘅昏暗退隱之處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把畏縮的見鬼者帶到泉邊,命令她立刻過橋,進入那邊哀號的女士和無頭幽靈出沒的昏暗退隱之處。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, how can you be so cruel?” sobbed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,您點能咁殘忍?」安妮抽泣住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,您怎麼能這麼殘忍?」安妮抽泣著說。

passages.original: “What would you feel like if a white thing did snatch me up and carry me off?”
passages.vernacular: 「如果真有白色嘅嘢把我抓走帶走,您會係乜嘢感覺?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果真有白色的東西把我抓走帶走,您會是什麼感覺?」

passages.original: “I’ll risk it,” said Marilla unfeelingly.
passages.vernacular: 「我冒呢個險,」瑪麗拉毫不留情地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我冒這個險,」瑪麗拉毫不留情地說。

passages.original: “You know I always mean what I say.
passages.vernacular: 「你知道我講話總是算數嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道我說話總是算數的。

passages.original: I’ll cure you of imagining ghosts into places.
passages.vernacular: 我要治好你往地方裡想像出鬼魂嘅毛病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要治好你往地方裡想像出鬼魂的毛病。

passages.original: March, now.”
passages.vernacular: 而家,走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,走。」

passages.original: Anne marched.
passages.vernacular: 安妮走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮走了。

passages.original: That is, she stumbled over the bridge and went shuddering up the horrible dim path beyond.
passages.vernacular: 都就係講,佢跌跌撞撞地過咗橋,哆嗦住走上嗰邊可怕昏暗嘅小路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也就是說,她跌跌撞撞地過了橋,哆嗦著走上那邊可怕昏暗的小路。

passages.original: Anne never forgot that walk.
passages.vernacular: 安妮永遠忘不咗嗰次行走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮永遠忘不了那次行走。

passages.original: Bitterly did she repent the license she had given to her imagination.
passages.vernacular: 佢痛苦地後悔曾讓自己嘅想像力嗰樣放縱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她痛苦地後悔曾讓自己的想像力那樣放縱。

passages.original: The goblins of her fancy lurked in every shadow about her, reaching out their cold, fleshless hands to grasp the terrified small girl who had called them into being.
passages.vernacular: 佢幻想出嘅妖怪潛伏喺佢周圍嘅每一個陰影裡,伸出冰冷嘅、冇血肉嘅手,要抓住嗰個召喚佢哋出世嘅受驚嘅小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她幻想出的妖怪潛伏在她周圍的每一個陰影裡,伸出冰冷的、沒有血肉的手,要抓住那個召喚它們出世的受驚的小女孩。

passages.original: A white strip of birch bark blowing up from the hollow over the brown floor of the grove made her heart stand still.
passages.vernacular: 一片白色嘅樺樹皮從窪地吹過樹林嘅棕色地面,讓佢嘅心停止咗跳動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一片白色的樺樹皮從窪地吹過樹林的棕色地面,讓她的心停止了跳動。

passages.original: The long-drawn wail of two old boughs rubbing against each other brought out the perspiration in beads on her forehead.
passages.vernacular: 兩根老樹枝互相摩擦發出嘅長長嘅哀鳴,讓佢額頭上冒出一粒粒汗珠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩根老樹枝互相摩擦發出的長長的哀鳴,讓她額頭上冒出一粒粒汗珠。

passages.original: The swoop of bats in the darkness over her was as the wings of unearthly creatures.
passages.vernacular: 蝙蝠喺佢頭頂黑暗中嘅俯衝,像係非人間生物嘅翅膀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蝙蝠在她頭頂黑暗中的俯衝,像是非人間生物的翅膀。

passages.original: When she reached Mr. William Bell’s field she fled across it as if pursued by an army of white things, and arrived at the Barry kitchen door so out of breath that she could hardly gasp out her request for the apron pattern.
passages.vernacular: 佢走到威廉·貝爾先生嘅田野時,佢穿過佢飛逃,好像被一支白色嘢嘅軍隊追趕,到達巴里家廚房門口時,上氣不接下氣,幾乎講不出要圍裙紙樣嘅請求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她走到威廉·貝爾先生的田野時,她穿過它飛逃,好像被一支白色東西的軍隊追趕,到達巴里家廚房門口時,上氣不接下氣,幾乎說不出要圍裙紙樣的請求。

passages.original: Diana was away so that she had no excuse to linger.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜不喺,所以佢冇藉口逗留。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜不在,所以她沒有藉口逗留。

passages.original: The dreadful return journey had to be faced.
passages.vernacular: 可怕嘅回程唔得不面對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可怕的回程不得不面對。

passages.original: Anne went back over it with shut eyes, preferring to take the risk of dashing her brains out among the boughs to that of seeing a white thing.
passages.vernacular: 安妮閉住眼睛走回去,寧願冒喺樹枝間撞破腦袋嘅危險,都唔願冒睇到白色嘢嘅危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮閉著眼睛走回去,寧願冒在樹枝間撞破腦袋的危險,也不願冒看到白色東西的危險。

passages.original: When she finally stumbled over the log bridge she drew one long shivering breath of relief.
passages.vernacular: 當佢終於跌跌撞撞地過咗原木橋時,佢長長地、顫抖地鬆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當她終於跌跌撞撞地過了原木橋時,她長長地、顫抖地鬆了口氣。

passages.original: “Well, so nothing caught you?” said Marilla unsympathetically.
passages.vernacular: 「點樣,所以冇嘢抓住你?」瑪麗拉毫不同情地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼樣,所以沒有東西抓住你?」瑪麗拉毫不同情地說。

passages.original: “Oh, Mar--Marilla,” chattered Anne, “I’ll b-b-be contt-tented with c-c-commonplace places after this.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪——瑪麗拉,」安妮牙齒打戰地講,「以後我會滿——滿足於平——平庸嘅地方喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪——瑪麗拉,」安妮牙齒打戰地說,「以後我會滿——滿足於平——平庸的地方了。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXI A New Departure in Flavorings 第二十一章:調味的新嘗試

passages.original: CH DEAR me, there is nothing but meetings and partings in this world, as Mrs. Lynde says,” remarked Anne plaintively, putting her slate and books down on the kitchen table on the last day of June and wiping her red eyes with a very damp handkerchief.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,呢世界上除咗相聚就係別離,就像林德太太講嘅,」六月最後一天,安妮哀怨地講,把石板同書放喺廚房桌子上,用一塊濕透咗嘅手帕擦佢紅紅嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,這世界上除了相聚就是別離,就像林德太太說的,」六月最後一天,安妮哀怨地說,把石板和書放在廚房桌子上,用一塊濕透了的手帕擦她紅紅的眼睛。

passages.original: “Wasn’t it fortunate, Marilla, that I took an extra handkerchief to school today?
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉,我今日多帶咗一塊手帕去學校,係唔係好幸運?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉,我今天多帶了一塊手帕去學校,是不是很幸運?

passages.original: I had a presentiment that it would be needed.”
passages.vernacular: 我有預感會用得住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有預感會用得著。」

passages.original: “I never thought you were so fond of Mr. Phillips that you’d require two handkerchiefs to dry your tears just because he was going away,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇想過你咁鍾意菲利普斯先生,佢一走你就要兩塊手帕嚟擦眼淚,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒想過你那麼喜歡菲利普斯先生,他一走你就要兩塊手帕來擦眼淚,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “I don’t think I was crying because I was really so very fond of him,” reflected Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我哭唔係因為真嘅咁鍾意佢,」安妮思量住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我哭不是因為真的那麼喜歡他,」安妮思量著說。

passages.original: “I just cried because all the others did.
passages.vernacular: 「我只係因為別人都哭才哭嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只是因為別人都哭才哭的。

passages.original: It was Ruby Gillis started it.
passages.vernacular: 係露比·吉利斯起嘅頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是露比·吉利斯起的頭。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis has always declared she hated Mr. Phillips, but just as soon as he got up to make his farewell speech she burst into tears.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯一直宣稱佢恨菲利普斯先生,但佢一站起嚟作告別演講,佢就哭咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯一直宣稱她恨菲利普斯先生,但他一站起來作告別演說,她就哭了起來。

passages.original: Then all the girls began to cry, one after the other.
passages.vernacular: 然後所有嘅女孩一個接一個都哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後所有的女孩一個接一個都哭了。

passages.original: I tried to hold out, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我試住忍住,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我試著忍住,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I tried to remember the time Mr. Phillips made me sit with Gil--with a boy; and the time he spelled my name without an ‘e’ on the blackboard; and how he said I was the worst dunce he ever saw at geometry and laughed at my spelling; and all the times he had been so horrid and sarcastic; but somehow I couldn’t, Marilla, and I just had to cry too.
passages.vernacular: 我試住回想菲利普斯先生讓我同吉爾——同一個男孩坐嘅嗰次;仲有佢喺黑板上拼寫我嘅名字冇『e』嘅嗰次;仲有佢講我係佢見過嘅最笨嘅幾何蠢材,仲笑我拼寫嘅時候;仲有所有佢咁可怕、咁諷刺嘅時候;但唔知怎嘅我不行,瑪麗拉,我都只好哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我試著回想菲利普斯先生讓我和吉爾——和一個男孩坐的那次;還有他在黑板上拼寫我的名字沒有『e』的那次;還有他說我是他見過的最笨的幾何蠢材,還笑我拼寫的時候;還有所有他那麼可怕、那麼諷刺的時候;但不知怎的我不行,瑪麗拉,我也只好哭了。

passages.original: Jane Andrews has been talking for a month about how glad she’d be when Mr. Phillips went away and she declared she’d never shed a tear.
passages.vernacular: 簡·安德魯斯一個月嚟一直喺講菲利普斯先生走咗佢有多高興,佢聲稱佢決唔會掉一滴淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡·安德魯斯一個月來一直在說菲利普斯先生走了她有多高興,她聲稱她決不會掉一滴淚。

passages.original: Well, she was worse than any of us and had to borrow a handkerchief from her brother--of course the boys didn’t cry--because she hadn’t brought one of her own, not expecting to need it.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,佢比我哋邊個都糟,唔得不向佢哥哥借手帕——當然男孩哋不哭——因為佢冇帶自己嘅,冇想到會用到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,她比我們誰都糟,不得不向她哥哥借手帕——當然男孩們不哭——因為她沒帶自己的,沒想到會用到。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, it was heartrending.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,太讓人心碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,太讓人心碎了。

passages.original: Mr. Phillips made such a beautiful farewell speech beginning, ‘The time has come for us to part.’
passages.vernacular: 菲利普斯先生作咗一個咁美嘅告別演講,開頭係『我哋分別嘅時刻到喇』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菲利普斯先生作了一個那麼美的告別演說,開頭是『我們分別的時刻到了』。

passages.original: It was very affecting.
passages.vernacular: 太動人喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太動人了。

passages.original: And he had tears in his eyes too, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 佢眼裡都有淚水,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他眼裡也有淚水,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Oh, I felt dreadfully sorry and remorseful for all the times I’d talked in school and drawn pictures of him on my slate and made fun of him and Prissy.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我為所有我喺學校里講話、喺石板上畫佢像、取笑佢同普麗茜嘅時候,感到好難過同悔恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我為所有我在學校里說話、在石板上畫他像、取笑他和普麗茜的時候,感到非常難過和悔恨。

passages.original: I can tell you I wished I’d been a model pupil like Minnie Andrews.
passages.vernacular: 我可以告訴您,我真希望我係像明妮·安德魯斯嗰樣嘅模範學生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以告訴您,我真希望我是像明妮·安德魯斯那樣的模範學生。

passages.original: She hadn’t anything on her conscience.
passages.vernacular: 佢良心上乜嘢都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她良心上什麼也沒有。

passages.original: The girls cried all the way home from school.
passages.vernacular: 女孩哋一路從學校哭住回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩們一路從學校哭著回家。

passages.original: Carrie Sloane kept saying every few minutes, ‘The time has come for us to part,’ and that would start us off again whenever we were in any danger of cheering up.
passages.vernacular: 嘉莉·斯隆每隔幾分鐘就講一句『我哋分別嘅時刻到喇』,每當我哋有點要高興起嚟嘅危險時,呢句話就讓我哋再次哭起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘉莉·斯隆每隔幾分鐘就說一句『我們分別的時刻到了』,每當我們有點要高興起來的危險時,這句話就讓我們再次哭起來。

passages.original: I do feel dreadfully sad, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我確實好傷心,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確實非常傷心,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: But one can’t feel quite in the depths of despair with two months’ vacation before them, can they, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 但係面對兩個月嘅假期,人唔可能完全處喺絕望嘅深淵,係唔係,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是面對兩個月的假期,人不可能完全處在絕望的深淵,是不是,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: And besides, we met the new minister and his wife coming from the station.
passages.vernacular: 而且,我哋喺從車站回嚟嘅路上遇見咗新牧師同佢嘅妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,我們在從車站回來的路上遇見了新牧師和他的妻子。

passages.original: For all I was feeling so bad about Mr. Phillips going away I couldn’t help taking a little interest in a new minister, could I?
passages.vernacular: 儘管我為菲利普斯先生走咗咁難過,我都忍不住對新牧師有啲興趣,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管我為菲利普斯先生走了那麼難過,我也忍不住對新牧師有一點興趣,是不是?

passages.original: His wife is very pretty.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅妻子好漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的妻子很漂亮。

passages.original: Not exactly regally lovely, of course--it wouldn’t do, I suppose, for a minister to have a regally lovely wife, because it might set a bad example.
passages.vernacular: 當然不完全係帝王般嘅可愛——我想牧師有個帝王般可愛嘅妻子係不合適嘅,因為嗰可能樹立壞榜樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然不完全是帝王般的可愛——我想牧師有個帝王般可愛的妻子是不合適的,因為那可能樹立壞榜樣。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says the minister’s wife over at Newbridge sets a very bad example because she dresses so fashionably.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講新橋嗰邊牧師嘅妻子樹立咗好壞嘅榜樣,因為佢穿得太時髦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說新橋那邊牧師的妻子樹立了很壞的榜樣,因為她穿得太時髦。

passages.original: Our new minister’s wife was dressed in blue muslin with lovely puffed sleeves and a hat trimmed with roses.
passages.vernacular: 我哋新牧師嘅妻子穿住藍色細棉布裙,帶住可愛嘅泡泡袖,戴住一頂飾有玫瑰嘅帽子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們新牧師的妻子穿著藍色細棉布裙,帶著可愛的泡泡袖,戴著一頂飾有玫瑰的帽子。

passages.original: Jane Andrews said she thought puffed sleeves were too worldly for a minister’s wife, but I didn’t make any such uncharitable remark, Marilla, because I know what it is to long for puffed sleeves.
passages.vernacular: 簡·安德魯斯講佢覺得泡泡袖對牧師嘅妻子來講太世俗喇,但我冇講呢種不仁慈嘅話,瑪麗拉,因為我知道渴望泡泡袖係乜嘢滋味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡·安德魯斯說她覺得泡泡袖對牧師的妻子來說太世俗了,但我沒有說這種不仁慈的話,瑪麗拉,因為我知道渴望泡泡袖是什麼滋味。

passages.original: Besides, she’s only been a minister’s wife for a little while, so one should make allowances, shouldn’t they?
passages.vernacular: 再講,佢才做咗短短一陣子牧師嘅妻子,所以應該體諒,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再說,她才做了短短一陣子牧師的妻子,所以應該體諒,是不是?

passages.original: They are going to board with Mrs. Lynde until the manse is ready.”
passages.vernacular: 牧場住宅準備好之前,佢哋要喺林德太太家寄宿。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧場住宅準備好之前,他們要在林德太太家寄宿。」

passages.original: If Marilla, in going down to Mrs. Lynde’s that evening, was actuated by any motive save her avowed one of returning the quilting frames she had borrowed the preceding winter, it was an amiable weakness shared by most of the Avonlea people.
passages.vernacular: 如果嗰天傍晚瑪麗拉去林德太太家,除咗佢公開宣稱嘅仲去年冬天借嘅被子繃架之外,仲有別嘅動機,嗰都係大多數阿文利人都有嘅可愛嘅弱點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果那天傍晚瑪麗拉去林德太太家,除了她公開宣稱的還去年冬天借的被子繃架之外,還有別的動機,那也是大多數阿文利人都有的可愛的弱點。

passages.original: Many a thing Mrs. Lynde had lent, sometimes never expecting to see it again, came home that night in charge of the borrowers thereof.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太借出嘅許多嘢,有時從冇指望能再見到,嗰天晚上都由借用人帶回家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太借出的許多東西,有時從沒指望能再見到,那天晚上都由借用人帶回家了。

passages.original: A new minister, and moreover a minister with a wife, was a lawful object of curiosity in a quiet little country settlement where sensations were few and far between.
passages.vernacular: 新牧師,而且係有妻子嘅牧師,喺一個新鮮事寥寥無幾嘅安靜鄉村小聚居地,係個合情合理嘅好奇對象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 新牧師,而且是有妻子的牧師,在一個新鮮事寥寥無幾的安靜鄉村小聚居地,是個合情合理的好奇對象。

passages.original: Old Mr. Bentley, the minister whom Anne had found lacking in imagination, had been pastor of Avonlea for eighteen years.
passages.vernacular: 老本特利先生,就係安妮覺得缺乏想像力嘅嗰位牧師,喺阿文利做咗十八年牧師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老本特利先生,就是安妮覺得缺乏想像力的那位牧師,在阿文利做了十八年牧師。

passages.original: He was a widower when he came, and a widower he remained, despite the fact that gossip regularly married him to this, that, or the other one, every year of his sojourn.
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟時係個鰥夫,儘管閒話每年都定期把佢跟呢個、嗰個或另一個人配成對,佢始終係個鰥夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他來時是個鰥夫,儘管閒話每年都定期把他跟這個、那個或另一個人配成對,他始終是個鰥夫。

passages.original: In the preceding February he had resigned his charge and departed amid the regrets of his people, most of whom had the affection born of long intercourse for their good old minister in spite of his shortcomings as an orator.
passages.vernacular: 去年二月佢辭去咗職務,喺教友哋嘅惋惜聲中離去喇,佢哋大多數人對佢哋呢位好老牧師有住長期相處產生嘅感情,儘管佢作為演講家有缺點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去年二月他辭去了職務,在教友們的惋惜聲中離去了,他們大多數人對他們這位好老牧師有著長期相處產生的感情,儘管他作為演說家有缺點。

passages.original: Since then the Avonlea church had enjoyed a variety of religious dissipation in listening to the many and various candidates and “supplies” who came Sunday after Sunday to preach on trial.
passages.vernacular: 從嗰以後,阿文利教會因為聽咗許多形形色色嘅候選人同「代理牧師」,而享受到各種宗教放縱,佢哋一個星期天接一個星期天地嚟試講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那以後,阿文利教會因為聽了許多形形色色的候選人和「代理牧師」,而享受到各種宗教放縱,他們一個星期天接一個星期天地來試講。

passages.original: These stood or fell by the judgment of the fathers and mothers in Israel; but a certain small, red-haired girl who sat meekly in the corner of the old Cuthbert pew also had her opinions about them and discussed the same in full with Matthew, Marilla always declining from principle to criticize ministers in any shape or form.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲人嘅成敗全睇以色列嘅父親母親嘅判斷;但坐喺卡思伯特家老長椅角落裡溫順地嘅某個紅頭髮小女孩,都有佢對佢哋嘅睇法,並同馬修詳細討論,而瑪麗拉出於原則總是唔肯以任何形式批評牧師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些人的成敗全看以色列的父親母親的判斷;但坐在卡思伯特家老長椅角落裡溫順地的某個紅頭髮小女孩,也有她對他們的看法,並與馬修詳細討論,而瑪麗拉出於原則總是不肯以任何形式批評牧師。

passages.original: “I don’t think Mr. Smith would have done, Matthew” was Anne’s final summing up.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得史密斯先生不行,馬修,」呢個係安妮最後嘅總結。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得史密斯先生不行,馬修,」這是安妮最後的總結。

passages.original: “Mrs. Lynde says his delivery was so poor, but I think his worst fault was just like Mr. Bentley’s--he had no imagination.
passages.vernacular: 「林德太太講佢嘅講道太差,但我覺得佢最大嘅缺點就像本特利先生一樣——佢冇想像力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「林德太太說他的講道太差,但我覺得他最大的缺點就像本特利先生一樣——他沒有想像力。

passages.original: And Mr. Terry had too much; he let it run away with him just as I did mine in the matter of the Haunted Wood.
passages.vernacular: 而特里先生想像力太多;佢讓佢失控喇,就像我喺鬧鬼林嗰件事上讓我嘅想像力失控一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而特里先生想像力太多;他讓它失控了,就像我在鬧鬼林那件事上讓我的想像力失控一樣。

passages.original: Besides, Mrs. Lynde says his theology wasn’t sound.
passages.vernacular: 再講,林德太太講佢嘅神學不健全。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再說,林德太太說他的神學不健全。

passages.original: Mr. Gresham was a very good man and a very religious man, but he told too many funny stories and made the people laugh in church; he was undignified, and you must have some dignity about a minister, mustn’t you, Matthew?
passages.vernacular: 格雷沙姆先生係個好好嘅人,好虔誠嘅人,但佢講嘅有趣故事太多,喺教堂裡惹人笑;佢唔夠莊重,而牧師必須有啲莊重,係唔係,馬修?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 格雷沙姆先生是個很好的人,很虔誠的人,但他講的有趣故事太多,在教堂裡惹人笑;他不夠莊重,而牧師必須有一點莊重,是不是,馬修?

passages.original: I thought Mr. Marshall was decidedly attractive; but Mrs. Lynde says he isn’t married, or even engaged, because she made special inquiries about him, and she says it would never do to have a young unmarried minister in Avonlea, because he might marry in the congregation and that would make trouble.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得馬歇爾先生特別有魅力;但林德太太講佢冇結婚,甚至冇訂婚,因為佢專門打聽過佢,佢講讓一個未婚嘅年輕牧師嚟阿文利決不行,因為佢可能同教友結婚,嗰就會惹麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得馬歇爾先生特別有魅力;但林德太太說他沒有結婚,甚至沒有訂婚,因為她專門打聽過他,她說讓一個未婚的年輕牧師來阿文利決不行,因為他可能和教友結婚,那就會惹麻煩。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde is a very farseeing woman, isn’t she, Matthew?
passages.vernacular: 林德太太係個好有遠見嘅女人,係唔係,馬修?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太是個很有遠見的女人,是不是,馬修?

passages.original: I’m very glad they’ve called Mr. Allan.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興佢哋請咗艾倫先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興他們請了艾倫先生。

passages.original: I liked him because his sermon was interesting and he prayed as if he meant it and not just as if he did it because he was in the habit of it.
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意佢,因為佢嘅講道有趣,佢禱告好像係真心嘅,而不只係因為習慣咗才做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡他,因為他的講道有趣,他禱告好像是真心的,而不只是因為習慣了才做的。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says he isn’t perfect, but she says she supposes we couldn’t expect a perfect minister for seven hundred and fifty dollars a year, and anyhow his theology is sound because she questioned him thoroughly on all the points of doctrine.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講佢不完美,但佢講佢想我哋唔能夠指望一年七百五十元能請到完美嘅牧師,而且無論如何佢嘅神學係健全嘅,因為佢就教義嘅所有要點徹底盤問過佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說他不完美,但她說她想我們不能指望一年七百五十元能請到完美的牧師,而且無論如何他的神學是健全的,因為她就教義的所有要點徹底盤問過他。

passages.original: And she knows his wife’s people and they are most respectable and the women are all good housekeepers.
passages.vernacular: 佢仲認識佢妻子嘅娘家人,佢哋好體面,嗰啲婦女都係好主婦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她還認識他妻子的娘家人,他們非常體面,那些婦女都是好主婦。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says that sound doctrine in the man and good housekeeping in the woman make an ideal combination for a minister’s family.”
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講,男人教義健全、女人持家有方,係牧師家庭嘅理想組合。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說,男人教義健全、女人持家有方,是牧師家庭的理想組合。」

passages.original: The new minister and his wife were a young, pleasant-faced couple, still on their honeymoon, and full of all good and beautiful enthusiasms for their chosen lifework.
passages.vernacular: 新牧師夫婦係一對年輕、面容愉快嘅夫婦,仍喺蜜月中,對佢哋選擇嘅終身事業充滿咗一切美好嘅熱情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 新牧師夫婦是一對年輕、面容愉快的夫婦,仍在蜜月中,對他們選擇的終身事業充滿了一切美好的熱情。

passages.original: Avonlea opened its heart to them from the start.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利從一開始就向佢哋敞開咗心扉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利從一開始就向他們敞開了心扉。

passages.original: Old and young liked the frank, cheerful young man with his high ideals, and the bright, gentle little lady who assumed the mistress-ship of the manse.
passages.vernacular: 老老少少都鍾意呢位坦率、開朗、懷有崇高理想嘅年輕人,同接任牧師住宅女主人嘅聰明、溫柔嘅小女士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老老少少都喜歡這位坦率、開朗、懷有崇高理想的年輕人,和接任牧師住宅女主人的聰明、溫柔的小女士。

passages.original: With Mrs. Allan Anne fell promptly and wholeheartedly in love.
passages.vernacular: 安妮即刻全心全意地愛上咗艾倫太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮立刻全心全意地愛上了艾倫太太。

passages.original: She had discovered another kindred spirit.
passages.vernacular: 佢又發現咗一個志同道合嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她又發現了一個志同道合的人。

passages.original: “Mrs. Allan is perfectly lovely,” she announced one Sunday afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 「艾倫太太特別可愛,」一個星期天下午佢宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「艾倫太太特別可愛,」一個星期天下午她宣布。

passages.original: “She’s taken our class and she’s a splendid teacher.
passages.vernacular: 「佢接咗我哋呢個班,係個好棒嘅老師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她接了我們這個班,是個很棒的老師。

passages.original: She said right away she didn’t think it was fair for the teacher to ask all the questions, and you know, Marilla, that is exactly what I’ve always thought.
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻講佢覺得由老師問所有嘅問題不公平,您知道,瑪麗拉,呢正是我一直以來嘅想法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她馬上說她覺得由老師問所有的問題不公平,您知道,瑪麗拉,這正是我一直以來的想法。

passages.original: She said we could ask her any question we liked and I asked ever so many.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我哋可以問佢任何我哋鍾意嘅問題,我問咗好多好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我們可以問她任何我們喜歡的問題,我問了好多好多。

passages.original: I’m good at asking questions, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 我好擅長問問題,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很擅長問問題,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: “I believe you,” was Marilla’s emphatic comment.
passages.vernacular: 「我相信,」呢個係瑪麗拉強調嘅評語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我相信,」這是瑪麗拉強調的評語。

passages.original: “Nobody else asked any except Ruby Gillis, and she asked if there was to be a Sunday-school picnic this summer.
passages.vernacular: 「除咗露比·吉利斯,冇別人問,佢問今年夏天有冇主日學校野餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「除了露比·吉利斯,沒有別人問,她問今年夏天有沒有主日學校野餐。

passages.original: I didn’t think that was a very proper question to ask because it hadn’t any connection with the lesson--the lesson was about Daniel in the lions’ den--but Mrs. Allan just smiled and said she thought there would be.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得呢問題問得不太合適,因為跟課冇任何關係——課係關於但以理喺獅子坑裡——但艾倫太太只係微笑,講佢想會有嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得這問題問得不太合適,因為跟課沒有任何關係——課是關於但以理在獅子坑裡——但艾倫太太只是微笑,說她想會有的。

passages.original: Mrs. Allan has a lovely smile; she has such exquisite dimples in her cheeks.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太有可愛嘅笑容;佢臉頰上有精緻嘅酒窩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太有可愛的笑容;她臉頰上有精緻的酒窩。

passages.original: I wish I had dimples in my cheeks, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我希望我臉頰上有酒窩,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我臉頰上有酒窩,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I’m not half so skinny as I was when I came here, but I have no dimples yet.
passages.vernacular: 我已經不像剛嚟時咁瘦喇,一半都唔到,但我仲冇酒窩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經不像剛來時那麼瘦了,一半也不到,但我還沒有酒窩。

passages.original: If I had perhaps I could influence people for good.
passages.vernacular: 如果有,或者我就能對人產生好影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果有,也許我就能對人產生好影響。

passages.original: Mrs. Allan said we ought always to try to influence other people for good.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太講我哋應該始終努力對別人產生好影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太說我們應該始終努力對別人產生好影響。

passages.original: She talked so nice about everything.
passages.vernacular: 佢談論一切都咁好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她談論一切都那麼好。

passages.original: I never knew before that religion was such a cheerful thing.
passages.vernacular: 我以前唔知道宗教係咁愉快嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以前不知道宗教是這麼愉快的東西。

passages.original: I always thought it was kind of melancholy, but Mrs. Allan’s isn’t, and I’d like to be a Christian if I could be one like her.
passages.vernacular: 我一直以為佢有點憂鬱,但艾倫太太嘅就唔係,如果能成為像佢嗰樣嘅基督徒,我願意成為基督徒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直以為它有點憂鬱,但艾倫太太的就不是,如果能成為像她那樣的基督徒,我願意成為基督徒。

passages.original: I wouldn’t want to be one like Mr. Superintendent Bell.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔想成為貝爾督導先生嗰樣嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不想成為貝爾督導先生那樣的。」

passages.original: “It’s very naughty of you to speak so about Mr. Bell,” said Marilla severely.
passages.vernacular: 「你咁樣講貝爾先生好淘氣,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你這樣說貝爾先生非常淘氣,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地說。

passages.original: “Mr. Bell is a real good man.”
passages.vernacular: 「貝爾先生係個真正嘅好人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「貝爾先生是個真正的好人。」

passages.original: “Oh, of course he’s good,” agreed Anne, “but he doesn’t seem to get any comfort out of it.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,當然佢係好人,」安妮同意,「但佢似乎並冇從中得到安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,當然他是好人,」安妮同意,「但他似乎並沒有從中得到安慰。

passages.original: If I could be good I’d dance and sing all day because I was glad of it.
passages.vernacular: 如果我能做好人,我會整天又跳舞又唱歌,因為我高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我能做好人,我會整天又跳舞又唱歌,因為我高興。

passages.original: I suppose Mrs. Allan is too old to dance and sing and of course it wouldn’t be dignified in a minister’s wife.
passages.vernacular: 我想艾倫太太年紀太大喇,唔能夠跳舞唱歌,而且當然,呢對牧師嘅妻子來講都唔夠莊重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想艾倫太太年紀太大了,不能跳舞唱歌,而且當然,這對牧師的妻子來說也不夠莊重。

passages.original: But I can just feel she’s glad she’s a Christian and that she’d be one even if she could get to heaven without it.”
passages.vernacular: 但我就係感覺得到佢為自己係基督徒而高興,即使不做基督徒都能上天堂,佢都會做嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我就是感覺得到她為自己是基督徒而高興,即使不做基督徒也能上天堂,她也會做的。」

passages.original: “I suppose we must have Mr. and Mrs. Allan up to tea someday soon,” said Marilla reflectively.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我哋得喺近期請艾倫夫婦嚟家裡飲茶,」瑪麗拉若有所思地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我們得在近期請艾倫夫婦來家裡喝茶,」瑪麗拉若有所思地說。

passages.original: “They’ve been most everywhere but here.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋幾乎去過所有地方,就係冇嚟過呢兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們幾乎去過所有地方,就是沒來過這兒。

passages.original: Let me see.
passages.vernacular: 讓我想想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我想想。

passages.original: Next Wednesday would be a good time to have them.
passages.vernacular: 下星期三係個合適嘅日子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下星期三是個合適的日子。

passages.original: But don’t say a word to Matthew about it, for if he knew they were coming he’d find some excuse to be away that day.
passages.vernacular: 但別對馬修講一個字,因為如果佢知道佢哋要嚟,佢會找藉口嗰天不喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但別對馬修說一個字,因為如果他知道他們要來,他會找藉口那天不在。

passages.original: He’d got so used to Mr. Bentley he didn’t mind him, but he’s going to find it hard to get acquainted with a new minister, and a new minister’s wife will frighten him to death.”
passages.vernacular: 佢習慣咗本特利先生,不介意佢,但佢要認識新牧師會好難,而新牧師嘅妻子會把佢嚇死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他習慣了本特利先生,不介意他,但他要認識新牧師會很難,而新牧師的妻子會把他嚇死。」

passages.original: “I’ll be as secret as the dead,” assured Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我會像死人一樣保密,」安妮保證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會像死人一樣保密,」安妮保證。

passages.original: “But oh, Marilla, will you let me make a cake for the occasion?
passages.vernacular: 「但係,哦,瑪麗拉,您能讓我為呢個場合做一個蛋糕嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,哦,瑪麗拉,您能讓我為這個場合做一個蛋糕嗎?

passages.original: I’d love to do something for Mrs. Allan, and you know I can make a pretty good cake by this time.”
passages.vernacular: 我好想為艾倫太太做點乜嘢,您知道我到而家已經能做相當不錯嘅蛋糕喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很想為艾倫太太做點什麼,您知道我到現在已經能做相當不錯的蛋糕了。」

passages.original: “You can make a layer cake,” promised Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「你可以做夾層蛋糕,」瑪麗拉答應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你可以做夾層蛋糕,」瑪麗拉答應。

passages.original: Monday and Tuesday great preparations went on at Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 星期一同星期二,綠色屋頂喺進行大規模準備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期一和星期二,綠色屋頂在進行大規模準備。

passages.original: Having the minister and his wife to tea was a serious and important undertaking, and Marilla was determined not to be eclipsed by any of the Avonlea housekeepers.
passages.vernacular: 請牧師夫婦飲茶係件嚴肅而重要嘅事,瑪麗拉決心不被任何一個阿文利嘅主婦比下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請牧師夫婦喝茶是件嚴肅而重要的事,瑪麗拉決心不被任何一個阿文利的主婦比下去。

passages.original: Anne was wild with excitement and delight.
passages.vernacular: 安妮興奮得發狂,欣喜萬分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮興奮得發狂,欣喜萬分。

passages.original: She talked it all over with Diana Tuesday night in the twilight, as they sat on the big red stones by the Dryad’s Bubble and made rainbows in the water with little twigs dipped in fir balsam.
passages.vernacular: 星期二晚上暮色中,佢同黛安娜坐喺林中仙子泉邊嘅大紅石頭上,用蘸咗冷杉香脂嘅小樹枝喺水裡製造彩虹,把呢一切談咗個遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期二晚上暮色中,她和黛安娜坐在林中仙子泉邊的大紅石頭上,用蘸了冷杉香脂的小樹枝在水裡製造彩虹,把這一切談了個遍。

passages.original: “Everything is ready, Diana, except my cake which I’m to make in the morning, and the baking-powder biscuits which Marilla will make just before teatime.
passages.vernacular: 「一切都準備好喇,黛安娜,除咗我聽日早晨要做嘅蛋糕,同瑪麗拉喺飲茶前要做嘅發酵粉餅乾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一切都準備好了,黛安娜,除了我明天早晨要做的蛋糕,和瑪麗拉在喝茶前要做的發酵粉餅乾。

passages.original: I assure you, Diana, that Marilla and I have had a busy two days of it.
passages.vernacular: 我向你保證,黛安娜,瑪麗拉同我呢兩天忙得不可開交。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向你保證,黛安娜,瑪麗拉和我這兩天忙得不可開交。

passages.original: It’s such a responsibility having a minister’s family to tea.
passages.vernacular: 請牧師一家飲茶係咁大嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請牧師一家喝茶是這麼大的責任。

passages.original: I never went through such an experience before.
passages.vernacular: 我以前從冇過咁樣嘅經歷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以前從沒有過這樣的經歷。

passages.original: You should just see our pantry.
passages.vernacular: 你真該睇睇我哋嘅食品櫃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你真該看看我們的食品櫃。

passages.original: It’s a sight to behold.
passages.vernacular: 嗰景象好壯觀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那景象很壯觀。

passages.original: We’re going to have jellied chicken and cold tongue.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要有凍雞同冷舌頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要有凍雞和冷舌頭。

passages.original: We’re to have two kinds of jelly, red and yellow, and whipped cream and lemon pie, and cherry pie, and three kinds of cookies, and fruit cake, and Marilla’s famous yellow plum preserves that she keeps especially for ministers, and pound cake and layer cake, and biscuits as aforesaid; and new bread and old both, in case the minister is dyspeptic and can’t eat new.
passages.vernacular: 仲要有兩種果凍,紅色同黃色,以及鮮奶油同檸檬餡餅,櫻桃餡餅,三種餅乾,水果蛋糕,瑪麗拉專門留畀牧師嘅有名嘅黃李子蜜餞,磅蛋糕同夾層蛋糕,以及前面講過嘅餅乾;新麵包同陳麵包都要,萬一牧師消化不良唔能夠食新麵包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還要有兩種果凍,紅色和黃色,以及鮮奶油和檸檬餡餅,櫻桃餡餅,三種餅乾,水果蛋糕,瑪麗拉專門留給牧師的有名的黃李子蜜餞,磅蛋糕和夾層蛋糕,以及前面說過的餅乾;新麵包和陳麵包都要,萬一牧師消化不良不能吃新麵包。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says ministers are dyspeptic, but I don’t think Mr. Allan has been a minister long enough for it to have had a bad effect on him.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講牧師都消化不良,但我覺得艾倫先生做牧師嘅時間仲冇長到對佢有不好嘅影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說牧師都消化不良,但我覺得艾倫先生做牧師的時間還沒長到對他有不好的影響。

passages.original: I just grow cold when I think of my layer cake.
passages.vernacular: 一想到我嘅夾層蛋糕我就渾身發冷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一想到我的夾層蛋糕我就渾身發冷。

passages.original: Oh, Diana, what if it shouldn’t be good!
passages.vernacular: 哦,黛安娜,萬一佢不好食點算!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,黛安娜,萬一它不好吃怎麼辦!

passages.original: I dreamed last night that I was chased all around by a fearful goblin with a big layer cake for a head.”
passages.vernacular: 琴晚我夢見一個可怕嘅妖怪追住我到處跑,佢嘅頭係一個大夾層蛋糕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨晚我夢見一個可怕的妖怪追著我到處跑,它的頭是一個大夾層蛋糕。」

passages.original: “It’ll be good, all right,” assured Diana, who was a very comfortable sort of friend.
passages.vernacular: 「會好食嘅,啲不錯,」黛安娜保證,佢係個好讓人舒心嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「會好吃的,一點不錯,」黛安娜保證,她是個很讓人舒心的朋友。

passages.original: “I’m sure that piece of the one you made that we had for lunch in Idlewild two weeks ago was perfectly elegant.”
passages.vernacular: 「我肯定兩個星期前我哋喺閒遊林食午飯嘅時候食嘅你做嘅嗰塊,特別高雅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我肯定兩個星期前我們在閒遊林吃午飯的時候吃的你做的那塊,特別高雅。」

passages.original: “Yes; but cakes have such a terrible habit of turning out bad just when you especially want them to be good,” sighed Anne, setting a particularly well-balsamed twig afloat.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅;但蛋糕有個可怕嘅習慣,恰恰喺你特別希望佢好嘅時候做壞,」安妮嘆咗口氣講,放下一根特別沾滿香脂嘅小樹枝漂浮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的;但蛋糕有個可怕的習慣,恰恰在你特別希望它好的時候做壞,」安妮嘆了口氣說,放下一根特別沾滿香脂的小樹枝漂浮。

passages.original: “However, I suppose I shall just have to trust to Providence and be careful to put in the flour.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,我想我只好依靠上天,並且小心記得放麵粉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過,我想我只好依靠上天,並且小心記得放麵粉了。

passages.original: Oh, look, Diana, what a lovely rainbow!
passages.vernacular: 哦,睇,黛安娜,多美嘅彩虹!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,看,黛安娜,多美的彩虹!

passages.original: Do you suppose the dryad will come out after we go away and take it for a scarf?”
passages.vernacular: 你覺得我哋走咗以後林中仙子會唔會出嚟,把佢當圍巾?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你覺得我們走了以後林中仙子會不會出來,把它當圍巾?」

passages.original: “You know there is no such thing as a dryad,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「你知道根本冇林中仙子呢種嘢,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道根本沒有林中仙子這種東西,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: Diana’s mother had found out about the Haunted Wood and had been decidedly angry over it.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜嘅母親發現咗鬧鬼林嘅事,對此好生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜的母親發現了鬧鬼林的事,對此非常生氣。

passages.original: As a result Diana had abstained from any further imitative flights of imagination and did not think it prudent to cultivate a spirit of belief even in harmless dryads.
passages.vernacular: 結果黛安娜唔再有任何進一步模仿嘅想像力飛翔,都不覺得即使培養對無害嘅林中仙子嘅信仰係明智嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果黛安娜不再有任何進一步模仿的想像力飛翔,也不覺得即使培養對無害的林中仙子的信仰是明智的。

passages.original: “But it’s so easy to imagine there is,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「但係想像有一個太容易喇,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是想像有一個太容易了,」安妮說。

passages.original: “Every night before I go to bed, I look out of my window and wonder if the dryad is really sitting here, combing her locks with the spring for a mirror.
passages.vernacular: 「每天晚上瞓覺前,我都從窗戶往外睇,想知道林中仙子係唔係真嘅坐喺呢兒,以泉水為鏡子梳理佢嘅頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「每天晚上睡覺前,我都從窗戶往外看,想知道林中仙子是不是真的坐在這兒,以泉水為鏡子梳理她的頭髮。

passages.original: Sometimes I look for her footprints in the dew in the morning.
passages.vernacular: 有時早晨我喺露水裡尋找佢嘅腳印。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時早晨我在露水裡尋找她的腳印。

passages.original: Oh, Diana, don’t give up your faith in the dryad!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,黛安娜,唔好放棄你對林中仙子嘅信念!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,黛安娜,不要放棄你對林中仙子的信念!」

passages.original: Wednesday morning came.
passages.vernacular: 星期三早晨到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期三早晨到了。

passages.original: Anne got up at sunrise because she was too excited to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 安妮日出時起床,因為佢太興奮瞓不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮日出時起床,因為她太興奮睡不著。

passages.original: She had caught a severe cold in the head by reason of her dabbling in the spring on the preceding evening; but nothing short of absolute pneumonia could have quenched her interest in culinary matters that morning.
passages.vernacular: 由於前一晚佢喺泉水裡玩水,佢得咗嚴重嘅頭部感冒;但除咗真正嘅肺炎,乜嘢都澆不滅佢嗰天早晨對烹飪事務嘅興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 由於前一晚她在泉水裡玩水,她得了嚴重的頭部感冒;但除了真正的肺炎,什麼也澆不滅她那天早晨對烹飪事務的興趣。

passages.original: After breakfast she proceeded to make her cake.
passages.vernacular: 早飯後佢開始做蛋糕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早飯後她開始做蛋糕。

passages.original: When she finally shut the oven door upon it she drew a long breath.
passages.vernacular: 佢終於關上烤箱門時,長長地吸咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她終於關上烤箱門時,長長地吸了口氣。

passages.original: “I’m sure I haven’t forgotten anything this time, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我肯定呢次我乜嘢都冇忘,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我肯定這次我什麼也沒忘,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: But do you think it will rise?
passages.vernacular: 但您覺得佢會發起嚟嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但您覺得它會發起來嗎?

passages.original: Just suppose perhaps the baking powder isn’t good?
passages.vernacular: 萬一發酵粉不好呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 萬一發酵粉不好呢?

passages.original: I used it out of the new can.
passages.vernacular: 我用嘅係新罐子里嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我用的是新罐子里的。

passages.original: And Mrs. Lynde says you can never be sure of getting good baking powder nowadays when everything is so adulterated.
passages.vernacular: 而林德太太講,而家乜嘢嘢都摻假,你永遠唔能夠肯定買到嘅係好發酵粉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而林德太太說,現在什麼東西都摻假,你永遠不能肯定買到的是好發酵粉。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says the Government ought to take the matter up, but she says we’ll never see the day when a Tory Government will do it.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講政府應該管呢件事,但佢講我哋永遠睇唔到保守黨政府會做呢件事嘅嗰一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說政府應該管這件事,但她說我們永遠看不到保守黨政府會做這件事的那一天。

passages.original: Marilla, what if that cake doesn’t rise?”
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉,萬一蛋糕發不起嚟點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉,萬一蛋糕發不起來怎麼辦?」

passages.original: “We’ll have plenty without it” was Marilla’s unimpassioned way of looking at the subject.
passages.vernacular: 「冇佢我哋都有好多食嘅,」呢個係瑪麗拉對呢個問題不動感情嘅睇法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有它我們也有很多吃的,」這是瑪麗拉對這個問題不動感情的看法。

passages.original: The cake did rise, however, and came out of the oven as light and feathery as golden foam.
passages.vernacular: 然而蛋糕發起嚟喇,從烤箱裡攞出嚟,像金色嘅泡沫一樣輕盈如羽毛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而蛋糕發起來了,從烤箱裡拿出來,像金色的泡沫一樣輕盈如羽毛。

passages.original: Anne, flushed with delight, clapped it together with layers of ruby jelly and, in imagination, saw Mrs. Allan eating it and possibly asking for another piece!
passages.vernacular: 安妮欣喜得臉通紅,用紅寶石般嘅果凍把佢夾層合喺一起,喺想像中睇到艾倫太太食住佢,可能仲要再嚟一塊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮欣喜得臉通紅,用紅寶石般的果凍把它夾層合在一起,在想像中看到艾倫太太吃著它,可能還要再來一塊!

passages.original: “You’ll be using the best tea set, of course, Marilla,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「您當然要用最好嘅茶具,瑪麗拉,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您當然要用最好的茶具,瑪麗拉,」她說。

passages.original: “Can I fix the table with ferns and wild roses?”
passages.vernacular: 「我能用蕨類同野玫瑰裝飾桌子嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我能用蕨類和野玫瑰裝飾桌子嗎?」

passages.original: “I think that’s all nonsense,” sniffed Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得嗰全係胡鬧,」瑪麗拉哼咗一聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得那全是胡鬧,」瑪麗拉哼了一聲說。

passages.original: “In my opinion it’s the eatables that matter and not flummery decorations.”
passages.vernacular: 「依我睇,要緊嘅係食嘅嘢,而唔係華而不實嘅裝飾。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「依我看,要緊的是吃的東西,而不是華而不實的裝飾。」

passages.original: “Mrs. Barry had her table decorated,” said Anne, who was not entirely guiltless of the wisdom of the serpent, “and the minister paid her an elegant compliment.
passages.vernacular: 「巴里太太裝飾咗佢嘅桌子,」安妮講,佢並不完全冇蛇嘅智慧,「牧師還畀咗佢一個高雅嘅讚美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴里太太裝飾了她的桌子,」安妮說,她並不完全沒有蛇的智慧,「牧師還給了她一個高雅的讚美。

passages.original: He said it was a feast for the eye as well as the palate.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講呢個係一場畀眼睛都畀味覺嘅盛宴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說這是一場給眼睛也給味覺的盛宴。」

passages.original: “Well, do as you like,” said Marilla, who was quite determined not to be surpassed by Mrs. Barry or anybody else.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,隨你鍾意,」瑪麗拉講,佢完全決心不被巴里太太或任何人超過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,隨你喜歡,」瑪麗拉說,她完全決心不被巴里太太或任何人超過。

passages.original: “Only mind you leave enough room for the dishes and the food.”
passages.vernacular: 「只要記得畀碗碟同食物留夠地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只要記得給碗碟和食物留夠地方。」

passages.original: Anne laid herself out to decorate in a manner and after a fashion that should leave Mrs. Barry’s nowhere.
passages.vernacular: 安妮竭盡全力用一種方式同風格嚟裝飾,要讓巴里太太嘅無地自容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮竭盡全力用一種方式和風格來裝飾,要讓巴里太太的無地自容。

passages.original: Having abundance of roses and ferns and a very artistic taste of her own, she made that tea table such a thing of beauty that when the minister and his wife sat down to it they exclaimed in chorus over it loveliness.
passages.vernacular: 有大量嘅玫瑰同蕨類,又有佢自己好藝術嘅品味,佢把嗰張茶桌弄成咗一件美麗嘅嘢,牧師同佢嘅妻子坐到桌邊時,不約而同地驚嘆佢嘅可愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有大量的玫瑰和蕨類,又有她自己非常藝術的品味,她把那張茶桌弄成了一件美麗的東西,牧師和他的妻子坐到桌邊時,不約而同地驚嘆它的可愛。

passages.original: “It’s Anne’s doings,” said Marilla, grimly just; and Anne felt that Mrs. Allan’s approving smile was almost too much happiness for this world.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係安妮嘅功勞,」瑪麗拉嚴厲但公正地講;安妮覺得艾倫太太讚許嘅笑容,幾乎係呢世界上太多嘅幸福喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是安妮的功勞,」瑪麗拉嚴厲但公正地說;安妮覺得艾倫太太讚許的笑容,幾乎是這世界上太多的幸福了。

passages.original: Matthew was there, having been inveigled into the party only goodness and Anne knew how.
passages.vernacular: 馬修都喺,只有天曉得同安妮知道,佢係點被哄嚟參加聚會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修也在,只有天曉得和安妮知道,他是怎麼被哄來參加聚會的。

passages.original: He had been in such a state of shyness and nervousness that Marilla had given him up in despair, but Anne took him in hand so successfully that he now sat at the table in his best clothes and white collar and talked to the minister not uninterestingly.
passages.vernacular: 佢羞怯又緊張到呢個地步,瑪麗拉已經絕望地放棄咗佢,但安妮咁成功地把佢接管喇,以至於佢而家穿住最好嘅衣服、戴住白領子坐喺桌邊,並同牧師談話,而且談得不算無趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他羞怯又緊張到這個地步,瑪麗拉已經絕望地放棄了他,但安妮那麼成功地把他接管了,以至於他現在穿著最好的衣服、戴著白領子坐在桌邊,並與牧師談話,而且談得不算無趣。

passages.original: He never said a word to Mrs. Allan, but that perhaps was not to be expected.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇對艾倫太太講一個字,但呢或者係無需期望嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有對艾倫太太說一個字,但這也許是無需期望的。

passages.original: All went merry as a marriage bell until Anne’s layer cake was passed.
passages.vernacular: 一切都像婚禮嘅鈴聲一樣歡快,直到安妮嘅夾層蛋糕傳上嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切都像婚禮的鈴聲一樣歡快,直到安妮的夾層蛋糕傳上來。

passages.original: Mrs. Allan, having already been helped to a bewildering variety, declined it.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太已經被畀咗眼花繚亂嘅各種點心,謝絕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太已經被給了眼花繚亂的各種點心,謝絕了。

passages.original: But Marilla, seeing the disappointment on Anne’s face, said smilingly:
passages.vernacular: 但瑪麗拉睇到安妮臉上嘅失望,笑住講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但瑪麗拉看到安妮臉上的失望,笑著說:

passages.original: “Oh, you must take a piece of this, Mrs. Allan.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你必須食一塊呢個,艾倫太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你必須吃一塊這個,艾倫太太。

passages.original: Anne made it on purpose for you.”
passages.vernacular: 安妮專門為你做嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮專門為你做的。」

passages.original: “In that case I must sample it,” laughed Mrs. Allan, helping herself to a plump triangle, as did also the minister and Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰樣嘅話我必須嘗嘗,」艾倫太太笑住講,畀自己攞咗一塊飽滿嘅三角形,牧師同瑪麗拉都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那樣的話我必須嘗嘗,」艾倫太太笑著說,給自己拿了一塊飽滿的三角形,牧師和瑪麗拉也是。

passages.original: Mrs. Allan took a mouthful of hers and a most peculiar expression crossed her face; not a word did she say, however, but steadily ate away at it.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太咬咗一口,一個極其奇特嘅表情掠過佢嘅臉;然而佢一個字都冇講,只係穩穩地食下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太咬了一口,一個極其奇特的表情掠過她的臉;然而她一個字也沒說,只是穩穩地吃下去。

passages.original: Marilla saw the expression and hastened to taste the cake.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉睇到咗呢個表情,連忙嘗咗嘗蛋糕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉看到了這個表情,連忙嘗了嘗蛋糕。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley!” she exclaimed, “what on earth did you put into that cake?”
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉!」佢叫道,「你到底往嗰蛋糕裡放咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉!」她叫道,「你到底往那蛋糕裡放了什麼?」

passages.original: “Nothing but what the recipe said, Marilla,” cried Anne with a look of anguish.
passages.vernacular: 「只放咗食譜上講嘅,瑪麗拉,」安妮帶住痛苦嘅神情叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只放了食譜上說的,瑪麗拉,」安妮帶著痛苦的神情叫道。

passages.original: “Oh, isn’t it all right?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不好食嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不好吃嗎?」

passages.original: “All right!
passages.vernacular: 「好食!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吃!

passages.original: It’s simply horrible.
passages.vernacular: 簡直可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡直可怕。

passages.original: Mr. Allan, don’t try to eat it.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫先生,別試住食佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫先生,別試著吃它。

passages.original: Anne, taste it yourself.
passages.vernacular: 安妮,你自己嘗嘗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮,你自己嘗嘗。

passages.original: What flavoring did you use?”
passages.vernacular: 你用咗乜嘢香料?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你用了什麼香料?」

passages.original: “Vanilla,” said Anne, her face scarlet with mortification after tasting the cake.
passages.vernacular: 「香草,」安妮講,嘗過蛋糕後佢羞愧得滿臉通紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「香草,」安妮說,嘗過蛋糕後她羞愧得滿臉通紅。

passages.original: “Only vanilla.
passages.vernacular: 「只有香草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只有香草。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, it must have been the baking powder.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,一定係發酵粉嘅問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,一定是發酵粉的問題。

passages.original: I had my suspicions of that bak--”
passages.vernacular: 我對嗰發酵——有過懷疑——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對那發酵——有過懷疑——」

passages.original: “Baking powder fiddlesticks!
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢發酵粉不發酵粉嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼發酵粉不發酵粉的!

passages.original: Go and bring me the bottle of vanilla you used.”
passages.vernacular: 去把你用嘅嗰瓶香草攞嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去把你用的那瓶香草拿來。」

passages.original: Anne fled to the pantry and returned with a small bottle partially filled with a brown liquid and labeled yellowly, “Best Vanilla.”
passages.vernacular: 安妮飛奔到食品櫃,攞回一個小瓶子,裡面裝咗一部分棕色液體,標籤發黃地寫住「上等香草精」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮飛奔到食品櫃,拿回一個小瓶子,裡面裝了一部分棕色液體,標籤發黃地寫著「上等香草精」。

passages.original: Marilla took it, uncorked it, smelled it.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉接過嚟,打開塞子,聞咗聞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉接過來,打開塞子,聞了聞。

passages.original: “Mercy on us, Anne, you’ve flavored that cake with Anodyne Liniment.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,安妮,你用止痛擦劑畀蛋糕調咗味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,安妮,你用止痛擦劑給蛋糕調了味。

passages.original: I broke the liniment bottle last week and poured what was left into an old empty vanilla bottle.
passages.vernacular: 上星期我打碎咗擦劑瓶子,把剩下嘅倒進咗一個舊嘅空香草精瓶子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上星期我打碎了擦劑瓶子,把剩下的倒進了一個舊的空香草精瓶子裡。

passages.original: I suppose it’s partly my fault--I should have warned you--but for pity’s sake why couldn’t you have smelled it?”
passages.vernacular: 我想一部分係我嘅錯——我該警告你——但睇喺老天嘅份上,你點就冇聞出嚟呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想一部分是我的錯——我該警告你——但看在老天的份上,你怎麼就沒聞出來呢?」

passages.original: Anne dissolved into tears under this double disgrace.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢雙重恥辱下,安妮哭成咗淚人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這雙重恥辱下,安妮哭成了淚人。

passages.original: “I couldn’t--I had such a cold!” and with this she fairly fled to the gable chamber, where she cast herself on the bed and wept as one who refuses to be comforted.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔能夠——我感冒得咁厲害!」講完佢簡直逃進咗山牆房間,撲倒喺床上,哭得像唔肯被安慰嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不能——我感冒得這麼厲害!」說完她簡直逃進了山牆房間,撲倒在床上,哭得像不肯被安慰的人。

passages.original: Presently a light step sounded on the stairs and somebody entered the room.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒,樓梯上響起輕輕嘅腳步聲,有人走進咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒,樓梯上響起輕輕的腳步聲,有人走進了房間。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla,” sobbed Anne, without looking up, “I’m disgraced forever.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」安妮抽泣住講,冇抬頭,「我永遠丟臉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」安妮抽泣著說,沒有抬頭,「我永遠丟臉了。

passages.original: I shall never be able to live this down.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠無法擺脫呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠無法擺脫這個。

passages.original: It will get out--things always do get out in Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 佢會傳出去嘅——事情喺阿文利總會傳出去嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它會傳出去的——事情在阿文利總會傳出去的。

passages.original: Diana will ask me how my cake turned out and I shall have to tell her the truth.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜會問我蛋糕做得點樣,我將唔得不告訴佢實話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜會問我蛋糕做得怎麼樣,我將不得不告訴她實話。

passages.original: I shall always be pointed at as the girl who flavored a cake with anodyne liniment.
passages.vernacular: 我將永遠被人指指點點,講係嗰個用止痛擦劑畀蛋糕調味嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我將永遠被人指指點點,說是那個用止痛擦劑給蛋糕調味的女孩。

passages.original: Gil--the boys in school will never get over laughing at it.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾——學校嘅男孩哋會永遠笑個冇完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾——學校的男孩們會永遠笑個沒完。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, if you have a spark of Christian pity don’t tell me that I must go down and wash the dishes after this.
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,如果您有一絲基督徒嘅憐憫心,別告訴我我仲得下去洗碗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,如果您有一絲基督徒的憐憫心,別告訴我我還得下去洗碗。

passages.original: I’ll wash them when the minister and his wife are gone, but I cannot ever look Mrs. Allan in the face again.
passages.vernacular: 牧師夫婦走咗以後我再洗,但我再都唔能夠正視艾倫太太嘅臉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師夫婦走了以後我再洗,但我再也不能正視艾倫太太的臉了。

passages.original: Perhaps she’ll think I tried to poison her.
passages.vernacular: 或者佢會以為我想毒死佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許她會以為我想毒死她。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says she knows an orphan girl who tried to poison her benefactor.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講佢認識一個孤女,想毒死佢嘅恩人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說她認識一個孤女,想毒死她的恩人。

passages.original: But the liniment isn’t poisonous.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰擦劑唔係有毒嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那擦劑不是有毒的。

passages.original: It’s meant to be taken internally--although not in cakes.
passages.vernacular: 佢係要內服嘅——雖然唔係放喺蛋糕里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是要內服的——雖然不是放在蛋糕里。

passages.original: Won’t you tell Mrs. Allan so, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 您能唔能夠告訴艾倫太太呢啲,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您能不能告訴艾倫太太這一點,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: “Suppose you jump up and tell her so yourself,” said a merry voice.
passages.vernacular: 「不如你跳起來自己告訴佢吧,」一個歡快嘅聲音講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不如你跳起來自己告訴她吧,」一個歡快的聲音說。

passages.original: Anne flew up, to find Mrs. Allan standing by her bed, surveying her with laughing eyes.
passages.vernacular: 安妮一躍而起,發現艾倫太太站喺佢嘅床邊,帶住笑盈盈嘅眼睛睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮一躍而起,發現艾倫太太站在她的床邊,帶著笑盈盈的眼睛看著她。

passages.original: “My dear little girl, you mustn’t cry like this,” she said, genuinely disturbed by Anne’s tragic face.
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅小姑娘,你不該咁樣哭,」佢講,被安妮悲劇般嘅臉真嘅弄得不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的小姑娘,你不該這樣哭,」她說,被安妮悲劇般的臉真的弄得不安。

passages.original: “Why, it’s all just a funny mistake that anybody might make.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,呢只係任何人都可能犯嘅有趣嘅錯誤。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,這只是任何人都可能犯的有趣的錯誤。」

passages.original: “Oh, no, it takes me to make such a mistake,” said Anne forlornly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不,只有我會犯咁樣嘅錯誤,」安妮淒涼地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不,只有我會犯這樣的錯誤,」安妮淒涼地說。

passages.original: “And I wanted to have that cake so nice for you, Mrs. Allan.”
passages.vernacular: 「而我本想把嗰個蛋糕為您做得咁好,艾倫太太。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而我本想把那個蛋糕為您做得那麼好,艾倫太太。」

passages.original: “Yes, I know, dear.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我知道,親愛嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我知道,親愛的。

passages.original: And I assure you I appreciate your kindness and thoughtfulness just as much as if it had turned out all right.
passages.vernacular: 我向你保證,我感謝你嘅好意同周到,就像佢做成功咗一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向你保證,我感謝你的好意和周到,就像它做成功了一樣。

passages.original: Now, you mustn’t cry any more, but come down with me and show me your flower garden.
passages.vernacular: 而家,你不許再哭喇,跟我下去,帶我睇睇你嘅花園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,你不許再哭了,跟我下去,帶我看看你的花園。

passages.original: Miss Cuthbert tells me you have a little plot all your own.
passages.vernacular: 卡思伯特小姐告訴我你有一小塊自己嘅地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卡思伯特小姐告訴我你有一小塊自己的地。

passages.original: I want to see it, for I’m very much interested in flowers.”
passages.vernacular: 我想睇睇,因為我對花好感興趣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想看看,因為我對花很感興趣。」

passages.original: Anne permitted herself to be led down and comforted, reflecting that it was really providential that Mrs. Allan was a kindred spirit.
passages.vernacular: 安妮任由自己被領下去、被安慰,心想艾倫太太係個志同道合嘅人,真係天意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮任由自己被領下去、被安慰,心想艾倫太太是個志同道合的人,真是天意。

passages.original: Nothing more was said about the liniment cake, and when the guests went away Anne found that she had enjoyed the evening more than could have been expected, considering that terrible incident.
passages.vernacular: 關於止痛擦劑蛋糕,再冇人提過,客人哋走時,安妮發現,考慮到嗰可怕嘅事件,佢呢個晚上過得比預料嘅愉快得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 關於止痛擦劑蛋糕,再沒有人提過,客人們走時,安妮發現,考慮到那可怕的事件,她這個晚上過得比預料的愉快得多。

passages.original: Nevertheless, she sighed deeply.
passages.vernacular: 儘管如此,佢定係深深嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管如此,她還是深深嘆了口氣。

passages.original: “Marilla, isn’t it nice to think that tomorrow is a new day with no mistakes in it yet?”
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉,想到聽日係新嘅一天,仲冇任何錯誤,唔係好好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉,想到明天是新的一天,還沒有任何錯誤,不是很好嗎?」

passages.original: “I’ll warrant you’ll make plenty in it,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我敢講你會喺裡面犯好多,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢說你會在裡面犯很多,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “I never saw your beat for making mistakes, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇見過比你更會犯錯嘅人,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒見過比你更會犯錯的人,安妮。」

passages.original: “Yes, and well I know it,” admitted Anne mournfully.
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,我自己好清楚,」安妮悲傷地承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,我自己很清楚,」安妮悲傷地承認。

passages.original: “But have you ever noticed one encouraging thing about me, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 「不過您有冇注意到我一個令人鼓舞嘅地方,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過您有沒有注意到我一個令人鼓舞的地方,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: I never make the same mistake twice.”
passages.vernacular: 我從不兩次犯同樣嘅錯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從不兩次犯同樣的錯。」

passages.original: “I don’t know as that’s much benefit when you’re always making new ones.”
passages.vernacular: 「你總是喺犯新嘅,我唔知道呢有多大好處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你總是在犯新的,我不知道這有多大好處。」

passages.original: “Oh, don’t you see, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,您不明白嗎,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,您不明白嗎,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: There must be a limit to the mistakes one person can make, and when I get to the end of them, then I’ll be through with them.
passages.vernacular: 一個人能犯嘅錯誤總有個限度,等我犯到頭喇,我就冇錯可犯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個人能犯的錯誤總有個限度,等我犯到頭了,我就沒有錯可犯了。

passages.original: That’s a very comforting thought.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個好令人安慰嘅想法。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個很令人安慰的想法。」
