passages.original: “Well, you’d better go and give that cake to the pigs,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你最好去把嗰個蛋糕攞去喂豬,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你最好去把那個蛋糕拿去喂豬,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “It isn’t fit for any human to eat, not even Jerry Boute.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢不適合任何人食,連傑里·布特都不行。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它不適合任何人吃,連傑里·布特也不行。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXII Anne Is Invited Out to Tea 第二十二章:安妮受邀外出喝茶

passages.original: CH AND what are your eyes popping out of your head about.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅眼睛瞪得快要蹦出頭嚟喇,呢個係為了乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的眼睛瞪得快要蹦出頭來了,這是為了什麼。

passages.original: Now?” asked Marilla, when Anne had just come in from a run to the post office.
passages.vernacular: 而家又點喇?」安妮剛從郵局跑回嚟,瑪麗拉問道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在又怎麼了?」安妮剛從郵局跑回來,瑪麗拉問道。

passages.original: “Have you discovered another kindred spirit?”
passages.vernacular: 「你又發現咗另一個志同道合嘅人嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你又發現了另一個志同道合的人嗎?」

passages.original: Excitement hung around Anne like a garment, shone in her eyes, kindled in every feature.
passages.vernacular: 興奮像一件衣服一樣罩喺安妮身上,喺佢眼裡閃耀,喺佢每一個神態裡燃燒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 興奮像一件衣服一樣罩在安妮身上,在她眼裡閃耀,在她每一個神態裡燃燒。

passages.original: She had come dancing up the lane, like a wind-blown sprite, through the mellow sunshine and lazy shadows of the August evening.
passages.vernacular: 佢像一個被風吹嚟嘅小精靈,穿過八月傍晚柔和嘅陽光同懶洋洋嘅陰影,舞動住跑上小巷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她像一個被風吹來的小精靈,穿過八月傍晚柔和的陽光和懶洋洋的陰影,舞動著跑上小巷。

passages.original: “No, Marilla, but oh, what do you think?
passages.vernacular: 「唔係,瑪麗拉,但係,哦,您猜點住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是,瑪麗拉,但是,哦,您猜怎麼著?

passages.original: I am invited to tea at the manse tomorrow afternoon!
passages.vernacular: 我被邀請聽日下午去牧師住宅飲茶喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被邀請明天下午去牧師住宅喝茶了!

passages.original: Mrs. Allan left the letter for me at the post office.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太把信留喺郵局畀我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太把信留在郵局給我的。

passages.original: Just look at it, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 您睇睇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看看,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: ‘Miss Anne Shirley, Green Gables.’
passages.vernacular: 『安妮·雪莉小姐,綠色屋頂。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『安妮·雪莉小姐,綠色屋頂。』

passages.original: That is the first time I was ever called ‘Miss.’
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我第一次被稱作『小姐』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我第一次被稱作『小姐』。

passages.original: Such a thrill as it gave me!
passages.vernacular: 我激動得發顫!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我激動得發顫!

passages.original: I shall cherish it forever among my choicest treasures.”
passages.vernacular: 我要永遠把佢當作我最珍貴嘅寶貝珍藏。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要永遠把它當作我最珍貴的寶貝珍藏。」

passages.original: “Mrs. Allan told me she meant to have all the members of her Sunday-school class to tea in turn,” said Marilla, regarding the wonderful event very coolly.
passages.vernacular: 「艾倫太太跟我講過,佢打算輪流請佢主日學校班上嘅所有成員去飲茶,」瑪麗拉講,對呢件奇妙嘅大事睇得好冷靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「艾倫太太跟我說過,她打算輪流請她主日學校班上的所有成員去喝茶,」瑪麗拉說,對這件奇妙的大事看得很冷靜。

passages.original: “You needn’t get in such a fever over it.
passages.vernacular: 「你唔使為此發熱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不必為此發熱。

passages.original: Do learn to take things calmly, child.”
passages.vernacular: 細路,學會平靜地睇待事情吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子,學會平靜地看待事情吧。」

passages.original: For Anne to take things calmly would have been to change her nature.
passages.vernacular: 讓安妮平靜地對待事情,就等於要改變佢嘅天性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓安妮平靜地對待事情,就等於要改變她的天性。

passages.original: All “spirit and fire and dew,” as she was, the pleasures and pains of life came to her with trebled intensity.
passages.vernacular: 佢整個就係「精神、火焰同露珠」,生活嘅喜悅同痛苦臨到佢身上,強度要放大三倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她整個就是「精神、火焰與露珠」,生活的喜悅和痛苦臨到她身上,強度要放大三倍。

passages.original: Marilla felt this and was vaguely troubled over it, realizing that the ups and downs of existence would probably bear hardly on this impulsive soul and not sufficiently understanding that the equally great capacity for delight might more than compensate.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉感覺到咗呢啲,為此隱隱不安,意識到生存嘅起伏好可能會讓呢個衝動嘅靈魂食盡苦頭,卻冇充分理解,同樣巨大嘅喜悅嘅能力或許能超額補償。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉感覺到了這一點,為此隱隱不安,意識到生存的起伏很可能會讓這個衝動的靈魂吃盡苦頭,卻沒有充分理解,同樣巨大的喜悅的能力或許能超額補償。

passages.original: Therefore Marilla conceived it to be her duty to drill Anne into a tranquil uniformity of disposition as impossible and alien to her as to a dancing sunbeam in one of the brook shallows.
passages.vernacular: 因此瑪麗拉認為佢嘅責任係把安妮訓練成一種平靜劃一嘅性情,而呢對安妮來講,就像小溪淺灘裡一道舞動嘅陽光一樣唔可能、一樣格格不入。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此瑪麗拉認為她的責任是把安妮訓練成一種平靜劃一的性情,而這對安妮來說,就像小溪淺灘裡一道舞動的陽光一樣不可能、一樣格格不入。

passages.original: She did not make much headway, as she sorrowfully admitted to herself.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇取得多大進展,佢悲傷地對自己承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她沒有取得多大進展,她悲傷地對自己承認。

passages.original: The downfall of some dear hope or plan plunged Anne into “deeps of affliction.”
passages.vernacular: 某個親愛嘅希望或計劃嘅破滅,會把安妮投入「苦難嘅深淵」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 某個親愛的希望或計劃的破滅,會把安妮投入「苦難的深淵」。

passages.original: The fulfillment thereof exalted her to dizzy realms of delight.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅實現又會把佢捧到令人暈眩嘅歡樂境界。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的實現又會把她捧到令人暈眩的歡樂境界。

passages.original: Marilla had almost begun to despair of ever fashioning this waif of the world into her model little girl of demure manners and prim deportment.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉幾乎開始絕望,覺得永遠唔能夠把呢個世界上嘅小流浪兒塑造成佢心目中舉止端莊、儀態拘謹嘅模範小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉幾乎開始絕望,覺得永遠不能把這個世界上的小流浪兒塑造成她心目中舉止端莊、儀態拘謹的模範小女孩。

passages.original: Neither would she have believed that she really liked Anne much better as she was.
passages.vernacular: 佢都唔會相信,自己其實更鍾意安妮而家嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也不會相信,自己其實更喜歡安妮現在的樣子。

passages.original: Anne went to bed that night speechless with misery because Matthew had said the wind was round northeast and he feared it would be a rainy day tomorrow.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上安妮上床時悲痛得講不出話,因為馬修講風轉到東北喇,佢怕聽日會下雨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上安妮上床時悲痛得說不出話,因為馬修說風轉到東北了,他怕明天會下雨。

passages.original: The rustle of the poplar leaves about the house worried her, it sounded so like pattering raindrops, and the full, faraway roar of the gulf, to which she listened delightedly at other times, loving its strange, sonorous, haunting rhythm, now seemed like a prophecy of storm and disaster to a small maiden who particularly wanted a fine day.
passages.vernacular: 房子四周白楊樹葉嘅沙沙聲讓佢擔心,聽上去咁像雨滴嘅噠噠聲,而海灣遙遠嘅、飽滿嘅轟鳴,佢別嘅時候愛聽,鍾意佢奇異、洪亮、縈繞嘅節奏,而家對一個特別想要好天氣嘅小姑娘來講,像係風暴同災難嘅預言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房子四周白楊樹葉的沙沙聲讓她擔心,聽上去那麼像雨滴的噠噠聲,而海灣遙遠的、飽滿的轟鳴,她別的時候愛聽,喜歡它奇異、洪亮、縈繞的節奏,現在對一個特別想要好天氣的小姑娘來說,像是風暴與災難的預言。

passages.original: Anne thought that the morning would never come.
passages.vernacular: 安妮覺得早晨永遠唔會嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮覺得早晨永遠不會來了。

passages.original: But all things have an end, even nights before the day on which you are invited to take tea at the manse.
passages.vernacular: 但係萬物都有盡頭,即使係你被邀請去牧師住宅飲茶嗰天嘅前一夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是萬物都有盡頭,即使是你被邀請去牧師住宅喝茶那天的前一夜。

passages.original: The morning, in spite of Matthew’s predictions, was fine and Anne’s spirits soared to their highest.
passages.vernacular: 早晨,不顧馬修嘅預言,係晴天,安妮嘅情緒飛升到最高點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨,不顧馬修的預言,是晴天,安妮的情緒飛升到最高點。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, there is something in me today that makes me just love everybody I see,” she exclaimed as she washed the breakfast dishes.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,今日我心裡有種嘢,讓我簡直愛睇見嘅每一個人,」佢洗早飯碗碟時叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,今天我心裡有種東西,讓我簡直愛看見的每一個人,」她洗早飯碗碟時叫道。

passages.original: “You don’t know how good I feel!
passages.vernacular: 「您唔知道我感覺多好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您不知道我感覺多好!

passages.original: Wouldn’t it be nice if it could last?
passages.vernacular: 要係能持續下去唔係好好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是能持續下去不是很好嗎?

passages.original: I believe I could be a model child if I were just invited out to tea every day.
passages.vernacular: 我相信,如果每天都被邀請出去飲茶,我能成為模範細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信,如果每天都被邀請出去喝茶,我能成為模範孩子。

passages.original: But oh, Marilla, it’s a solemn occasion too.
passages.vernacular: 但係哦,瑪麗拉,呢都係個莊重嘅場合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是哦,瑪麗拉,這也是個莊重的場合。

passages.original: I feel so anxious.
passages.vernacular: 我好焦慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我好焦慮。

passages.original: What if I shouldn’t behave properly?
passages.vernacular: 萬一我舉止唔得體點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 萬一我舉止不得體怎麼辦?

passages.original: You know I never had tea at a manse before, and I’m not sure that I know all the rules of etiquette, although I’ve been studying the rules given in the Etiquette Department of the Family Herald ever since I came here.
passages.vernacular: 您知道我以前從冇喺牧師住宅飲過茶,我不確定我係咪知道所有嘅禮儀規則,雖然自從我嚟呢兒以來,我一直喺學習《家庭先驅報》禮儀欄裡畀出嘅規則。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道我以前從沒在牧師住宅喝過茶,我不確定我是否知道所有的禮儀規則,雖然自從我來這兒以來,我一直在學習《家庭先驅報》禮儀欄裡給出的規則。

passages.original: I’m so afraid I’ll do something silly or forget to do something I should do.
passages.vernacular: 我好怕我會做傻事,或者忘咗做該做嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很怕我會做傻事,或者忘了做該做的事。

passages.original: Would it be good manners to take a second helping of anything if you wanted to very much?”
passages.vernacular: 如果你好想要,再要一份任何食物,係咪合乎禮貌?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你非常想要,再要一份任何食物,是否合乎禮貌?」

passages.original: “The trouble with you, Anne, is that you’re thinking too much about yourself.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅毛病,安妮,係你太多地想住你自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的毛病,安妮,是你太多地想著你自己。

passages.original: You should just think of Mrs. Allan and what would be nicest and most agreeable to her,” said Marilla, hitting for once in her life on a very sound and pithy piece of advice.
passages.vernacular: 你應該只想住艾倫太太,想乜嘢對佢最好、最合佢意,」瑪麗拉講,一生中第一次講出咗好合理而簡明扼要嘅建議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你應該只想著艾倫太太,想什麼對她最好、最合她意,」瑪麗拉說,一生中第一次說出了非常合理而簡明扼要的建議。

passages.original: Anne instantly realized this.
passages.vernacular: 安妮立即領會喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮立即領會了。

passages.original: “You are right, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「您講得對,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您說得對,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I’ll try not to think about myself at all.”
passages.vernacular: 我會努力完全不去想自己。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會努力完全不去想自己。」

passages.original: Anne evidently got through her visit without any serious breach of “etiquette,” for she came home through the twilight, under a great, high-sprung sky gloried over with trails of saffron and rosy cloud, in a beatified state of mind and told Marilla all about it happily, sitting on the big red-sandstone slab at the kitchen door with her tired curly head in Marilla’s gingham lap.
passages.vernacular: 安妮顯然拜訪過程冇任何嚴重違反「禮儀」嘅地方,因為佢喺暮色中回家,喺一片高高拱起、被一縷縷藏紅花色同玫瑰色嘅雲霞映照得榮耀嘅天空下,處於極樂嘅心境,坐喺廚房門口嘅大紅砂岩板上,把疲倦嘅鬈髮腦袋枕喺瑪麗拉嘅格子布圍裙上,高高興興地把一切告訴咗瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮顯然拜訪過程沒有任何嚴重違反「禮儀」的地方,因為她在暮色中回家,在一片高高拱起、被一縷縷藏紅花色和玫瑰色的雲霞映照得榮耀的天空下,處於極樂的心境,坐在廚房門口的大紅砂岩板上,把疲倦的鬈髮腦袋枕在瑪麗拉的格子布圍裙上,高高興興地把一切告訴了瑪麗拉。

passages.original: A cool wind was blowing down over the long harvest fields from the rims of firry western hills and whistling through the poplars.
passages.vernacular: 一陣涼風從西邊杉樹山丘嘅邊緣,吹過長長嘅收穫後嘅田野,喺白楊樹間呼嘯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣涼風從西邊杉樹山丘的邊緣,吹過長長的收穫後的田野,在白楊樹間呼嘯。

passages.original: One clear star hung over the orchard and the fireflies were flitting over in Lover’s Lane, in and out among the ferns and rustling boughs.
passages.vernacular: 一顆明亮嘅星星懸喺果園上方,螢火蟲喺情人小徑裡飛舞,穿梭喺蕨叢同沙沙作響嘅樹枝間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一顆明亮的星星懸在果園上方,螢火蟲在情人小徑裡飛舞,穿梭在蕨叢和沙沙作響的樹枝間。

passages.original: Anne watched them as she talked and somehow felt that wind and stars and fireflies were all tangled up together into something unutterably sweet and enchanting.
passages.vernacular: 安妮一邊講話一邊睇住佢哋,唔知怎嘅覺得風、星星同螢火蟲全都糾纏喺一起,成咗某種難以言表嘅甜美迷人嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮一邊說話一邊看著它們,不知怎的覺得風、星星和螢火蟲全都糾纏在一起,成了某種難以言表的甜美迷人的東西。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, I’ve had a most fascinating time.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我度過咗最迷人嘅時光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我度過了最迷人的時光。

passages.original: I feel that I have not lived in vain and I shall always feel like that even if I should never be invited to tea at a manse again.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我冇白活,即使我再都不被邀請去牧師住宅飲茶,我都永遠會咁樣覺得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我沒有白活,即使我再也不被邀請去牧師住宅喝茶,我也永遠會這樣覺得。

passages.original: When I got there Mrs. Allan met me at the door.
passages.vernacular: 我到嗰度時艾倫太太喺門口迎接我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我到那裡時艾倫太太在門口迎接我。

passages.original: She was dressed in the sweetest dress of pale-pink organdy, with dozens of frills and elbow sleeves, and she looked just like a seraph.
passages.vernacular: 佢穿住最可愛嘅淡粉紅色薄紗裙,有幾十道荷葉邊同肘袖,佢睇起嚟就像一位六翼天使。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她穿著最可愛的淡粉紅色薄紗裙,有幾十道荷葉邊和肘袖,她看起來就像一位六翼天使。

passages.original: I really think I’d like to be a minister’s wife when I grow up, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我真覺得我長大後想做牧師嘅妻子,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真覺得我長大後想做牧師的妻子,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: A minister mightn’t mind my red hair because he wouldn’t be thinking of such worldly things.
passages.vernacular: 牧師或者唔會介意我嘅紅頭髮,因為佢唔會想呢種世俗嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師也許不會介意我的紅頭髮,因為他不會想這種世俗的事。

passages.original: But then of course one would have to be naturally good and I’ll never be that, so I suppose there’s no use in thinking about it.
passages.vernacular: 不過當然人得天生善良,而我永遠唔會係,所以我想想都冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過當然人得天生善良,而我永遠不會是,所以我想想也沒用。

passages.original: Some people are naturally good, you know, and others are not.
passages.vernacular: 有些人天生善良,您知道,而有些人唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人天生善良,您知道,而有些人不是。

passages.original: I’m one of the others.
passages.vernacular: 我係屬於其他人嘅一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是屬於其他人的一個。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says I’m full of original sin.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講我充滿咗原罪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說我充滿了原罪。

passages.original: No matter how hard I try to be good I can never make such a success of it as those who are naturally good.
passages.vernacular: 無論我幾咁努力做個好人,都永遠唔可能像嗰啲天生善良嘅人嗰樣成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論我多麼努力做個好人,都永遠不可能像那些天生善良的人那樣成功。

passages.original: It’s a good deal like geometry, I expect.
passages.vernacular: 我想呢個好像幾何。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想這很像幾何。

passages.original: But don’t you think the trying so hard ought to count for something?
passages.vernacular: 但您不覺得咁努力地嘗試,應該算點乜嘢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但您不覺得這麼努力地嘗試,應該算點什麼嗎?

passages.original: Mrs. Allan is one of the naturally good people.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太係天生善良嘅人之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太是天生善良的人之一。

passages.original: I love her passionately.
passages.vernacular: 我熱烈地愛佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我熱烈地愛她。

passages.original: You know there are some people, like Matthew and Mrs. Allan that you can love right off without any trouble.
passages.vernacular: 您知道有些人,像馬修同艾倫太太,你可以一下子毫不費力地愛上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道有些人,像馬修和艾倫太太,你可以一下子毫不費力地愛上。

passages.original: And there are others, like Mrs. Lynde, that you have to try very hard to love.
passages.vernacular: 仲有別嘅人,像林德太太,你得好努力去愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有別的人,像林德太太,你得非常努力去愛。

passages.original: You know you ought to love them because they know so much and are such active workers in the church, but you have to keep reminding yourself of it all the time or else you forget.
passages.vernacular: 你知道你應該愛佢哋,因為佢哋知道咁多,係教會咁積極嘅工作者,但你得一直不停地提醒自己,否則就忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道你應該愛他們,因為他們知道那麼多,是教會那麼積極的工作者,但你得一直不停地提醒自己,否則就忘了。

passages.original: There was another little girl at the manse to tea, from the White Sands Sunday-school.
passages.vernacular: 牧師住宅仲有另一個小女孩嚟飲茶,係白沙主日學校嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師住宅還有另一個小女孩來喝茶,是白沙主日學校的。

passages.original: Her name was Laurette Bradley, and she was a very nice little girl.
passages.vernacular: 佢叫勞蕾特·布拉德利,係個好好嘅小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她叫勞蕾特·布拉德利,是個很好的小女孩。

passages.original: Not exactly a kindred spirit, you know, but still very nice.
passages.vernacular: 不完全係志同道合嘅人,您知道,但定係好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不完全是志同道合的人,您知道,但還是很好。

passages.original: We had an elegant tea, and I think I kept all the rules of etiquette pretty well.
passages.vernacular: 我哋飲咗一頓高雅嘅茶,我想我把所有禮儀規則都遵守得相當好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們喝了一頓高雅的茶,我想我把所有禮儀規則都遵守得相當好。

passages.original: After tea Mrs. Allan played and sang and she got Lauretta and me to sing too.
passages.vernacular: 茶後艾倫太太彈琴唱歌,仲讓勞蕾特同我都唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 茶後艾倫太太彈琴唱歌,還讓勞蕾特和我也唱。

passages.original: Mrs. Allan says I have a good voice and she says I must sing in the Sunday-school choir after this.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太講我嗓子好,佢講從今以後我必須喺主日學校唱詩班唱歌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太說我嗓子好,她說從今以後我必須在主日學校唱詩班唱歌。

passages.original: You can’t think how I was thrilled at the mere thought.
passages.vernacular: 您想唔到我光係想想就幾咁激動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您想不到我光是想想就多麼激動。

passages.original: I’ve longed so to sing in the Sunday-school choir, as Diana does, but I feared it was an honor I could never aspire to.
passages.vernacular: 我一直咁渴望像黛安娜嗰樣喺主日學校唱詩班唱歌,但我怕呢個係我永遠唔敢企及嘅榮譽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直那麼渴望像黛安娜那樣在主日學校唱詩班唱歌,但我怕這是我永遠不敢企及的榮譽。

passages.original: Lauretta had to go home early because there is a big concert in the White Sands Hotel tonight and her sister is to recite at it.
passages.vernacular: 勞蕾特得早點回家,因為今晚白沙旅館有一場大型音樂會,佢姐姐要喺嗰度朗誦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勞蕾特得早點回家,因為今晚白沙旅館有一場大型音樂會,她姐姐要在那裡朗誦。

passages.original: Lauretta says that the Americans at the hotel give a concert every fortnight in aid of the Charlottetown hospital, and they ask lots of the White Sands people to recite.
passages.vernacular: 勞蕾特講旅館里嘅美國人每兩個星期舉辦一次音樂會,資助夏洛特敦醫院,佢哋邀請許多白沙人去朗誦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勞蕾特說旅館里的美國人每兩個星期舉辦一次音樂會,資助夏洛特敦醫院,他們邀請許多白沙人去朗誦。

passages.original: Lauretta said she expected to be asked herself someday.
passages.vernacular: 勞蕾特講佢期待有一天自己都被邀請。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勞蕾特說她期待有一天自己也被邀請。

passages.original: I just gazed at her in awe.
passages.vernacular: 我只係敬畏地盯住佢睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是敬畏地盯著她看。

passages.original: After she had gone Mrs. Allan and I had a heart-to-heart talk.
passages.vernacular: 佢走後,艾倫太太同我進行咗一次推心置腹嘅談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她走後,艾倫太太和我進行了一次推心置腹的談話。

passages.original: I told her everything--about Mrs. Thomas and the twins and Katie Maurice and Violetta and coming to Green Gables and my troubles over geometry.
passages.vernacular: 我把一切都告訴咗佢——關於托馬斯太太同雙胞胎、凱蒂·莫里斯同維奧萊塔、嚟到綠色屋頂,仲有我喺幾何上嘅煩惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把一切都告訴了她——關於托馬斯太太和雙胞胎、凱蒂·莫里斯和維奧萊塔、來到綠色屋頂,還有我在幾何上的煩惱。

passages.original: And would you believe it, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 您信嗎,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您信嗎,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: Mrs. Allan told me she was a dunce at geometry too.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太告訴我,佢喺幾何上都係個蠢材。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太告訴我,她在幾何上也是個蠢材。

passages.original: You don’t know how that encouraged me.
passages.vernacular: 您唔知道呢對我係多大嘅鼓勵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不知道這對我是多大的鼓勵。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde came to the manse just before I left, and what do you think, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 我離開前,林德太太嚟到牧師住宅,您猜點住,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我離開前,林德太太來到牧師住宅,您猜怎麼著,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: The trustees have hired a new teacher and it’s a lady.
passages.vernacular: 校董哋聘咗一位新老師,係位女士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 校董們聘了一位新老師,是位女士。

passages.original: Her name is Miss Muriel Stacy.
passages.vernacular: 佢叫繆麗爾·斯泰西小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她叫繆麗爾·斯泰西小姐。

passages.original: Isn’t that a romantic name?
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係個浪漫嘅名字嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是個浪漫的名字嗎?

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says they’ve never had a female teacher in Avonlea before and she thinks it is a dangerous innovation.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講,阿文利以前從冇過女老師,佢認為呢個係個危險嘅創新。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說,阿文利以前從沒有過女老師,她認為這是個危險的創新。

passages.original: But I think it will be splendid to have a lady teacher, and I really don’t see how I’m going to live through the two weeks before school begins.
passages.vernacular: 但我覺得有位女老師會好棒,我真唔知道我點熬過開學前呢兩個星期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我覺得有位女老師會很棒,我真不知道我怎麼熬過開學前這兩個星期。

passages.original: I’m so impatient to see her.”
passages.vernacular: 我太迫不及待想見佢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太迫不及待想見她了。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXIII Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor 第二十三章:安妮在一場榮譽之爭中吃了苦頭

passages.original: CH ANNE had to live through more than two weeks, as it happened.
passages.vernacular: 碰巧,安妮要熬嘅不止兩個星期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 碰巧,安妮要熬的不止兩個星期。

passages.original: Almost a month having elapsed since the liniment cake episode, it was high time for her to get into fresh trouble of some sort, little mistakes, such as absentmindedly emptying a pan of skim milk into a basket of yarn balls in the pantry instead of into the pigs’ bucket, and walking clean over the edge of the log bridge into the brook while wrapped in imaginative reverie, not really being worth counting.
passages.vernacular: 自從止痛擦劑蛋糕事件以來已將近一個月,而家佢該惹新麻煩喇,小錯誤,比如心不喺焉地把一盆脫脂牛奶倒進食品櫃裡嘅一籃子毛線球裡,而唔係倒進豬桶裡,以及沉浸喺想像嘅遐思中,徑直從原木橋邊上走進咗小溪,真嘅不值得數。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從止痛擦劑蛋糕事件以來已將近一個月,現在她該惹新麻煩了,小錯誤,比如心不在焉地把一盆脫脂牛奶倒進食品櫃裡的一籃子毛線球裡,而不是倒進豬桶裡,以及沉浸在想像的遐思中,徑直從原木橋邊上走進了小溪,真的不值得數。

passages.original: A week after the tea at the manse Diana Barry gave a party.
passages.vernacular: 牧師住宅飲茶嘅一周後,黛安娜·巴里舉行咗一個聚會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師住宅喝茶的一周後,黛安娜·巴里舉行了一個聚會。

passages.original: “Small and select,” Anne assured Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「小型而精選嘅,」安妮向瑪麗拉保證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小型而精選的,」安妮向瑪麗拉保證。

passages.original: “Just the girls in our class.”
passages.vernacular: 「只有我哋班上嘅女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只有我們班上的女孩。」

passages.original: They had a very good time and nothing untoward happened until after tea, when they found themselves in the Barry garden, a little tired of all their games and ripe for any enticing form of mischief which might present itself.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋玩得好開心,直到茶點後,乜嘢不愉快嘅事都冇發生,佢哋發現自己喺巴里家嘅花園裡,對所有遊戲有點厭倦,正好適合任何誘人嘅惡作劇形式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們玩得非常開心,直到茶點後,什麼不愉快的事也沒發生,她們發現自己在巴里家的花園裡,對所有遊戲有點厭倦,正好適合任何誘人的惡作劇形式。

passages.original: This presently took the form of “daring.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個好快就採取咗「挑戰」嘅形式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這很快就採取了「挑戰」的形式。

passages.original: Daring was the fashionable amusement among the Avonlea small fry just then.
passages.vernacular: 挑戰係當時阿文利小孩中間時髦嘅消遣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 挑戰是當時阿文利小孩中間時髦的消遣。

passages.original: It had begun among the boys, but soon spread to the girls, and all the silly things that were done in Avonlea that summer because the doers thereof were “dared” to do them would fill a book by themselves.
passages.vernacular: 佢始於男孩,但好快蔓延到女孩,嗰個夏天阿文利做嘅所有蠢事,都係因為做嘅人被「挑戰」,足夠寫成一本書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它始於男孩,但很快蔓延到女孩,那個夏天阿文利做的所有蠢事,都是因為做的人被「挑戰」,足夠寫成一本書。

passages.original: First of all Carrie Sloane dared Ruby Gillis to climb to a certain point in the huge old willow tree before the front door; which Ruby Gillis, albeit in mortal dread of the fat green caterpillars with which said tree was infested and with the fear of her mother before her eyes if she should tear her new muslin dress, nimbly did, to the discomfiture of the aforesaid Carrie Sloane.
passages.vernacular: 首先嘉莉·斯隆向露比·吉利斯挑戰,爬到前門嗰棵巨大古老嘅柳樹嘅某個高度;露比·吉利斯雖然好害怕嗰樹上爬滿嘅肥綠毛毛蟲,而且眼前浮現住如果佢撕破新細棉布裙子母親嘅恐怖,但定係敏捷地做到喇,令前面講嘅嘉莉·斯隆大為沮喪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先嘉莉·斯隆向露比·吉利斯挑戰,爬到前門那棵巨大古老的柳樹的某個高度;露比·吉利斯雖然非常害怕那樹上爬滿的肥綠毛毛蟲,而且眼前浮現著如果她撕破新細棉布裙子母親的恐怖,但還是敏捷地做到了,令前面說的嘉莉·斯隆大為沮喪。

passages.original: Then Josie Pye dared Jane Andrews to hop on her left leg around the garden without stopping once or putting her right foot to the ground; which Jane Andrews gamely tried to do, but gave out at the third corner and had to confess herself defeated.
passages.vernacular: 然後喬西·派伊向簡·安德魯斯挑戰,用左腿單腳跳住繞花園一圈,中途不停,右腳不住地;簡·安德魯斯勇敢地試住做,但喺第三個拐角處不行喇,唔得不承認失敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後喬西·派伊向簡·安德魯斯挑戰,用左腿單腳跳著繞花園一圈,中途不停,右腳不著地;簡·安德魯斯勇敢地試著做,但在第三個拐角處不行了,不得不承認失敗。

passages.original: Josie’s triumph being rather more pronounced than good taste permitted, Anne Shirley dared her to walk along the top of the board fence which bounded the garden to the east.
passages.vernacular: 喬西嘅勝利比好品味所允許嘅更為明顯,安妮·雪莉便向佢挑戰,走過花園東邊嘅木板柵欄頂上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西的勝利比好品味所允許的更為明顯,安妮·雪莉便向她挑戰,走過花園東邊的木板柵欄頂上。

passages.original: Now, to “walk” board fences requires more skill and steadiness of head and heel than one might suppose who has never tried it.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,「走」木板柵欄需要嘅技巧、頭腦同腳跟嘅穩定性,比冇試過嘅人想像嘅要多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,「走」木板柵欄需要的技巧、頭腦和腳跟的穩定性,比沒試過的人想像的要多。

passages.original: But Josie Pye, if deficient in some qualities that make for popularity, had at least a natural and inborn gift, duly cultivated, for walking board fences.
passages.vernacular: 但喬西·派伊,雖然缺少某些讓人受歡迎嘅品質,至少有一種天生嘅、同生俱嚟並已適當培養嘅走木板柵欄嘅天賦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但喬西·派伊,雖然缺少某些讓人受歡迎的品質,至少有一種天生的、與生俱來並已適當培養的走木板柵欄的天賦。

passages.original: Josie walked the Barry fence with an airy unconcern which seemed to imply that a little thing like that wasn’t worth a “dare.”
passages.vernacular: 喬西走巴里家嘅柵欄時輕鬆無憂,好像暗示咁樣嘅小事不值得「挑戰」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西走巴里家的柵欄時輕鬆無憂,好像暗示這樣的小事不值得「挑戰」。

passages.original: Reluctant admiration greeted her exploit, for most of the other girls could appreciate it, having suffered many things themselves in their efforts to walk fences.
passages.vernacular: 勉強嘅欽佩迎接住佢嘅功績,因為大多數其他女孩都能理解,佢哋自己喺努力走柵欄時食過許多苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勉強的欽佩迎接著她的功績,因為大多數其他女孩都能理解,她們自己在努力走柵欄時吃過許多苦。

passages.original: Josie descended from her perch, flushed with victory, and darted a defiant glance at Anne.
passages.vernacular: 喬西從佢嘅高處下嚟,因勝利而面色通紅,向安妮投去挑釁嘅一瞥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西從她的高處下來,因勝利而面色通紅,向安妮投去挑釁的一瞥。

passages.original: Anne tossed her red braids.
passages.vernacular: 安妮甩咗甩紅辮子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮甩了甩紅辮子。

passages.original: “I don’t think it’s such a very wonderful thing to walk a little, low, board fence,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「我不覺得走一道矮矮嘅木板柵欄有乜嘢了不起,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不覺得走一道矮矮的木板柵欄有什麼了不起,」她說。

passages.original: “I knew a girl in Marysville who could walk the ridgepole of a roof.”
passages.vernacular: 「我喺馬里斯維爾認識一個女孩,能走屋頂嘅脊樑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在馬里斯維爾認識一個女孩,能走屋頂的脊樑。」

passages.original: “I don’t believe it,” said Josie flatly.
passages.vernacular: 「我不信,」喬西乾脆地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不信,」喬西乾脆地說。

passages.original: “I don’t believe anybody could walk a ridgepole.
passages.vernacular: 「我不相信有邊個能走屋脊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不相信有誰能走屋脊。

passages.original: You couldn’t, anyhow.”
passages.vernacular: 反正你不行。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 反正你不行。」

passages.original: “Couldn’t I?” cried Anne rashly.
passages.vernacular: 「我不行嗎?」安妮魯莽地叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不行嗎?」安妮魯莽地叫道。

passages.original: “Then I dare you to do it,” said Josie defiantly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我挑戰你做,」喬西挑釁地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我挑戰你做,」喬西挑釁地說。

passages.original: “I dare you to climb up there and walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry’s kitchen roof.”
passages.vernacular: 「我挑戰你爬上去,走巴里先生廚房嘅屋脊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我挑戰你爬上去,走巴里先生廚房的屋脊。」

passages.original: Anne turned pale, but there was clearly only one thing to be done.
passages.vernacular: 安妮臉色發白,但顯然只有一件事可做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮臉色發白,但顯然只有一件事可做。

passages.original: She walked toward the house, where a ladder was leaning against the kitchen roof.
passages.vernacular: 佢朝房子走去,嗰度有一把梯子靠喺廚房嘅屋頂上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她朝房子走去,那裡有一把梯子靠在廚房的屋頂上。

passages.original: All the fifth-class girls said, “Oh!” partly in excitement, partly in dismay.
passages.vernacular: 所有五年級嘅女孩都講「哦!」,一半係興奮,一半係驚慌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有五年級的女孩都說「哦!」,一半是興奮,一半是驚慌。

passages.original: “Don’t you do it, Anne,” entreated Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「你別咁做,安妮,」黛安娜懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你別這麼做,安妮,」黛安娜懇求道。

passages.original: “You’ll fall off and be killed.
passages.vernacular: 「你會掉下嚟摔死嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會掉下來摔死的。

passages.original: Never mind Josie Pye.
passages.vernacular: 別理喬西·派伊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別理喬西·派伊。

passages.original: It isn’t fair to dare anybody to do anything so dangerous.”
passages.vernacular: 挑戰別人做咁危險嘅事不公平。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 挑戰別人做這麼危險的事不公平。」

passages.original: “I must do it.
passages.vernacular: 「我必須做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須做。

passages.original: My honor is at stake,” said Anne solemnly.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅榮譽岌岌可危,」安妮莊嚴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的榮譽岌岌可危,」安妮莊嚴地說。

passages.original: “I shall walk that ridgepole, Diana, or perish in the attempt.
passages.vernacular: 「我要走完嗰個屋脊,黛安娜,否則就死喺嘗試中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要走完那個屋脊,黛安娜,否則就死在嘗試中。

passages.original: If I am killed you are to have my pearl bead ring.”
passages.vernacular: 如果我死喇,我嘅珍珠戒指畀你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我死了,我的珍珠戒指給你。」

passages.original: Anne climbed the ladder amid breathless silence, gained the ridgepole, balanced herself uprightly on that precarious footing, and started to walk along it, dizzily conscious that she was uncomfortably high up in the world and that walking ridgepoles was not a thing in which your imagination helped you out much.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺屏息嘅寂靜中爬上梯子,到達屋脊,喺嗰危險嘅立足點上筆直地平衡住自己,開始沿住走,頭暈目眩地意識到自己高得令人不安,而且走屋脊呢事,你嘅想像力幫不上多大忙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在屏息的寂靜中爬上梯子,到達屋脊,在那危險的立足點上筆直地平衡著自己,開始沿著走,頭暈目眩地意識到自己高得令人不安,而且走屋脊這事,你的想像力幫不上多大忙。

passages.original: Nevertheless, she managed to take several steps before the catastrophe came.
passages.vernacular: 儘管如此,佢定係設法走咗幾步,災難才來臨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管如此,她還是設法走了幾步,災難才來臨。

passages.original: Then she swayed, lost her balance, stumbled, staggered, and fell, sliding down over the sun-baked roof and crashing off it through the tangle of Virginia creeper beneath--all before the dismayed circle below could give a simultaneous, terrified shriek.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢搖晃起嚟,失去平衡,絆咗一下,踉蹌住摔咗下去,滑過被太陽曬烤嘅屋頂,穿過下面纏結嘅爬山虎重重摔下——所有呢一切發生喺下面驚慌嘅圈子同時發出一聲恐怖嘅尖叫之前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她搖晃起來,失去平衡,絆了一下,踉蹌著摔了下去,滑過被太陽曬烤的屋頂,穿過下面纏結的爬山虎重重摔下——所有這一切發生在下面驚慌的圈子同時發出一聲恐怖的尖叫之前。

passages.original: If Anne had tumbled off the roof on the side up which she had ascended Diana would probably have fallen heir to the pearl bead ring then and there.
passages.vernacular: 如果安妮係從佢爬上去嘅嗰一邊摔下屋頂,黛安娜大概就會當場繼承嗰枚珍珠戒指喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果安妮是從她爬上去的那一邊摔下屋頂,黛安娜大概就會當場繼承那枚珍珠戒指了。

passages.original: Fortunately she fell on the other side, where the roof extended down over the porch so nearly to the ground that a fall therefrom was a much less serious thing.
passages.vernacular: 幸運嘅係佢摔喺咗另一邊,嗰邊屋頂向下延伸到門廊,離地面咁近,從嗰兒摔下係嚴重得多嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸運的是她摔在了另一邊,那邊屋頂向下延伸到門廊,離地面那麼近,從那兒摔下是嚴重得多的事。

passages.original: Nevertheless, when Diana and the other girls had rushed frantically around the house--except Ruby Gillis, who remained as if rooted to the ground and went into hysterics--they found Anne lying all white and limp among the wreck and ruin of the Virginia creeper.
passages.vernacular: 儘管如此,當黛安娜同其他女孩瘋狂地繞到房子另一側——除咗露比·吉利斯,佢像生咗根似嘅待喺原地,歇斯底里起嚟——佢哋發現安妮蒼白無力地躺喺爬山虎嘅殘骸中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管如此,當黛安娜和其他女孩瘋狂地繞到房子另一側——除了露比·吉利斯,她像生了根似的待在原地,歇斯底里起來——她們發現安妮蒼白無力地躺在爬山虎的殘骸中。

passages.original: “Anne, are you killed?” shrieked Diana, throwing herself on her knees beside her friend.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,你死咗嗎?」黛安娜尖叫,撲跪喺朋友身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,你死了嗎?」黛安娜尖叫,撲跪在朋友身邊。

passages.original: “Oh, Anne, dear Anne, speak just one word to me and tell me if you’re killed.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,安妮,親愛嘅安妮,對我講一個字,告訴我你係唔係死喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,安妮,親愛的安妮,對我說一個字,告訴我你是不是死了。」

passages.original: To the immense relief of all the girls, and especially of Josie Pye, who, in spite of lack of imagination, had been seized with horrible visions of a future branded as the girl who was the cause of Anne Shirley’s early and tragic death, Anne sat dizzily up and answered uncertainly:
passages.vernacular: 所有女孩都鬆咗口氣,尤其係喬西·派伊,佢雖然缺乏想像力,卻被可怕嘅幻象攫住,想像自己將來被打上烙印,成為造成安妮·雪莉早逝悲劇嘅女孩,安妮頭暈地坐咗起嚟,不確定地回答:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有女孩都鬆了口氣,尤其是喬西·派伊,她雖然缺乏想像力,卻被可怕的幻象攫住,想像自己將來被打上烙印,成為造成安妮·雪莉早逝悲劇的女孩,安妮頭暈地坐了起來,不確定地回答:

passages.original: “No, Diana, I am not killed, but I think I am rendered unconscious.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,黛安娜,我冇死,但我想我失去咗知覺。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,黛安娜,我沒死,但我想我失去了知覺。」

passages.original: “Where?” sobbed Carrie Sloane.
passages.vernacular: 「邊兒?」嘉莉·斯隆抽泣住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哪兒?」嘉莉·斯隆抽泣著說。

passages.original: “Oh, where, Anne?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,邊兒,安妮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,哪兒,安妮?」

passages.original: Before Anne could answer Mrs. Barry appeared on the scene.
passages.vernacular: 安妮仲冇嚟得及回答,巴里太太就出而家現場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮還沒來得及回答,巴里太太就出現在現場。

passages.original: At sight of her Anne tried to scramble to her feet, but sank back again with a sharp little cry of pain.
passages.vernacular: 一睇到佢,安妮試圖爬起嚟,但又跌倒,發出一聲尖銳嘅痛叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一看到她,安妮試圖爬起來,但又跌倒,發出一聲尖銳的痛叫。

passages.original: “What’s the matter?
passages.vernacular: 「點喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了?

passages.original: Where have you hurt yourself?” demanded Mrs. Barry.
passages.vernacular: 你傷到邊兒喇?」巴里太太問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你傷到哪兒了?」巴里太太問。

passages.original: “My ankle,” gasped Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅腳踝,」安妮喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的腳踝,」安妮喘著氣說。

passages.original: “Oh, Diana, please find your father and ask him to take me home.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,黛安娜,請去找你父親,請佢送我回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,黛安娜,請去找你父親,請他送我回家。

passages.original: I know I can never walk there.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我永遠走不回去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我永遠走不回去了。

passages.original: And I’m sure I couldn’t hop so far on one foot when Jane couldn’t even hop around the garden.”
passages.vernacular: 而我肯定唔能夠單腳蹦咁遠,簡連繞花園都蹦不喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我肯定不能單腳蹦那麼遠,簡連繞花園都蹦不了。」

passages.original: Marilla was out in the orchard picking a panful of summer apples when she saw Mr. Barry coming over the log bridge and up the slope, with Mrs. Barry beside him and a whole procession of little girls trailing after him.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉喺果園裡摘滿滿一盆夏蘋果,睇見巴里先生過咗原木橋走上斜坡,巴里太太喺佢旁邊,一整隊小女孩跟喺佢後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉在果園裡摘滿滿一盆夏蘋果,看見巴里先生過了原木橋走上斜坡,巴里太太在他旁邊,一整隊小女孩跟在他後面。

passages.original: In his arms he carried Anne, whose head lay limply against his shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 佢懷裡抱住安妮,佢嘅頭軟軟地靠喺佢嘅肩上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他懷裡抱著安妮,她的頭軟軟地靠在他的肩上。

passages.original: At that moment Marilla had a revelation.
passages.vernacular: 就喺嗰一刻,瑪麗拉恍然大悟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在那一刻,瑪麗拉恍然大悟。

passages.original: In the sudden stab of fear that pierced her very heart she realized what Anne had come to mean to her.
passages.vernacular: 喺刺穿佢心臟嘅突然嘅恐懼刺痛中,佢意識到安妮對佢意味住乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在刺穿她心臟的突然的恐懼刺痛中,她意識到安妮對她意味著什麼。

passages.original: She would have admitted that she liked Anne--nay, that she was very fond of Anne.
passages.vernacular: 佢會承認佢鍾意安妮——不,佢好鍾意安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會承認她喜歡安妮——不,她非常喜歡安妮。

passages.original: But now she knew as she hurried wildly down the slope that Anne was dearer to her than anything else on earth.
passages.vernacular: 但此刻佢瘋狂地跑下斜坡,知道咗安妮比世上任何其他嘢都更珍貴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但此刻她瘋狂地跑下斜坡,知道了安妮比世上任何其他東西都更珍貴。

passages.original: “Mr. Barry, what has happened to her?” she gasped, more white and shaken than the self-contained, sensible Marilla had been for many years.
passages.vernacular: 「巴里先生,佢點喇?」佢喘息住問,比呢位沉穩理智嘅瑪麗拉多年嚟更蒼白、更顫抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴里先生,她怎麼了?」她喘息著問,比這位沉穩理智的瑪麗拉多年來更蒼白、更顫抖。

passages.original: Anne herself answered, lifting her head.
passages.vernacular: 安妮自己回答喇,抬起頭嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮自己回答了,抬起頭來。

passages.original: “Don’t be very frightened, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「別太害怕,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別太害怕,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I was walking the ridgepole and I fell off.
passages.vernacular: 我喺走屋脊,摔下嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在走屋脊,摔下來了。

passages.original: I expect I have sprained my ankle.
passages.vernacular: 我想我扭傷咗腳踝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我扭傷了腳踝。

passages.original: But, Marilla, I might have broken my neck.
passages.vernacular: 但係,瑪麗拉,我本可能摔斷脖子嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,瑪麗拉,我本可能摔斷脖子的。

passages.original: Let us look on the bright side of things.”
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋睇事情光明嘅一面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們看事情光明的一面。」

passages.original: “I might have known you’d go and do something of the sort when I let you go to that party,” said Marilla, sharp and shrewish in her very relief.
passages.vernacular: 「我早該知道,我讓你去嗰個聚會,你就會去做呢種事,」瑪麗拉講,佢喺如釋重負中尖刻而潑辣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我早該知道,我讓你去那個聚會,你就會去做這種事,」瑪麗拉說,她在如釋重負中尖刻而潑辣。

passages.original: “Bring her in here, Mr. Barry, and lay her on the sofa.
passages.vernacular: 「把佢帶進呢兒,巴里先生,放喺沙發上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把她帶進這兒,巴里先生,放在沙發上。

passages.original: Mercy me, the child has gone and fainted!”
passages.vernacular: 天呀,呢細路昏過去喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,這孩子昏過去了!」

passages.original: It was quite true.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係千真萬確嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是千真萬確的。

passages.original: Overcome by the pain of her injury, Anne had one more of her wishes granted to her.
passages.vernacular: 被傷痛壓倒,安妮嘅又一個願望實現喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被傷痛壓倒,安妮的又一個願望實現了。

passages.original: She had fainted dead away.
passages.vernacular: 佢徹底昏咗過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她徹底昏了過去。

passages.original: Matthew, hastily summoned from the harvest field, was straightway dispatched for the doctor, who in due time came, to discover that the injury was more serious than they had supposed.
passages.vernacular: 從收割嘅田裡被匆忙叫嚟嘅馬修,即刻被派去請醫生,醫生及時嚟喇,發現傷勢比佢哋想嘅更嚴重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從收割的田裡被匆忙叫來的馬修,立刻被派去請醫生,醫生及時來了,發現傷勢比他們想的更嚴重。

passages.original: Anne’s ankle was broken.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅腳踝斷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的腳踝斷了。

passages.original: That night, when Marilla went up to the east gable, where a white-faced girl was lying, a plaintive voice greeted her from the bed.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,瑪麗拉走上東山牆房間,一個臉色蒼白嘅女孩躺喺嗰度,一個哀怨嘅聲音從床上迎接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,瑪麗拉走上東山牆房間,一個臉色蒼白的女孩躺在那裡,一個哀怨的聲音從床上迎接她。

passages.original: “Aren’t you very sorry for me, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 「您不為我難過嗎,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您不為我難過嗎,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: “It was your own fault,” said Marilla, twitching down the blind and lighting a lamp.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係你自己嘅過錯,」瑪麗拉講,一邊拉下百葉窗,點上一盞燈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是你自己的過錯,」瑪麗拉說,一邊拉下百葉窗,點上一盞燈。

passages.original: “And that is just why you should be sorry for me,” said Anne, “because the thought that it is all my own fault is what makes it so hard.
passages.vernacular: 「正因如此您才應該為我難過,」安妮講,「因為想到呢全係我自己嘅過錯,才讓佢咁難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「正因如此您才應該為我難過,」安妮說,「因為想到這全是我自己的過錯,才讓它這麼難受。

passages.original: If I could blame it on anybody I would feel so much better.
passages.vernacular: 如果我能怪邊個,我會好受得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我能怪誰,我會好受得多。

passages.original: But what would you have done, Marilla, if you had been dared to walk a ridgepole?”
passages.vernacular: 但如果有人挑戰您走屋脊,瑪麗拉,您會點做?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果有人挑戰您走屋脊,瑪麗拉,您會怎麼做?」

passages.original: “I’d have stayed on good firm ground and let them dare away.
passages.vernacular: 「我會待喺堅實嘅地上,讓佢哋隨便挑戰去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會待在堅實的地上,讓他們隨便挑戰去。

passages.original: Such absurdity!” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 幾咁荒唐!」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多麼荒唐!」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: Anne sighed.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮嘆了口氣。

passages.original: “But you have such strength of mind, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「但係您有咁堅強嘅意志,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是您有那麼堅強的意志,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I haven’t.
passages.vernacular: 我冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有。

passages.original: I just felt that I couldn’t bear Josie Pye’s scorn.
passages.vernacular: 我就係覺得我受不了喬西·派伊嘅蔑視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是覺得我受不了喬西·派伊的蔑視。

passages.original: She would have crowed over me all my life.
passages.vernacular: 佢會一輩子喺我面前得意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會一輩子在我面前得意。

passages.original: And I think I have been punished so much that you needn’t be very cross with me, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我已經受咗咁多懲罰,您唔使再對我好生氣喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我已經受了這麼多懲罰,您不必再對我很生氣了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: It’s not a bit nice to faint, after all.
passages.vernacular: 昏過去終究啲都不好受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昏過去終究一點也不好受。

passages.original: And the doctor hurt me dreadfully when he was setting my ankle.
passages.vernacular: 而且醫生畀我接腳踝時疼得我要命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且醫生給我接腳踝時疼得我要命。

passages.original: I won’t be able to go around for six or seven weeks and I’ll miss the new lady teacher.
passages.vernacular: 我六七個星期唔能夠到處走喇,會錯過新嚟嘅女老師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我六七個星期不能到處走了,會錯過新來的女老師。

passages.original: She won’t be new any more by the time I’m able to go to school.
passages.vernacular: 等我能去上學時,佢就唔再新喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我能去上學時,她就不再新了。

passages.original: And Gil--everybody will get ahead of me in class.
passages.vernacular: 仲有吉爾——每個人都會喺班上超過我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有吉爾——每個人都會在班上超過我。

passages.original: Oh, I am an afflicted mortal.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我真係個受苦嘅凡人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我真是個受苦的凡人。

passages.original: But I’ll try to bear it all bravely if only you won’t be cross with me, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 但如果您不生我嘅氣,瑪麗拉,我會盡量勇敢地承受呢一切。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果您不生我的氣,瑪麗拉,我會盡量勇敢地承受這一切。」

passages.original: “There, there, I’m not cross,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,我不生氣,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,我不生氣,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “You’re an unlucky child, there’s no doubt about that; but as you say, you’ll have the suffering of it.
passages.vernacular: 「你係個不幸嘅細路,呢個係毫無疑問嘅;但正如你講嘅,你要承受佢嘅苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是個不幸的孩子,這是毫無疑問的;但正如你說的,你要承受它的苦。

passages.original: Here now, try and eat some supper.”
passages.vernacular: 嚟,試住食點晚飯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,試著吃點晚飯。」

passages.original: “Isn’t it fortunate I’ve got such an imagination?” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我有想像力,唔係好幸運嗎?」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有想像力,不是很幸運嗎?」安妮說。

passages.original: “It will help me through splendidly, I expect.
passages.vernacular: 「我想佢會讓我順利地熬過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想它會讓我順利地熬過去。

passages.original: What do people who haven’t any imagination do when they break their bones, do you suppose, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 您覺得冇想像力嘅人摔斷骨頭時點算,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您覺得沒有想像力的人摔斷骨頭時怎麼辦,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: Anne had good reason to bless her imagination many a time and oft during the tedious seven weeks that followed.
passages.vernacular: 喺接下嚟冗長嘅七個星期里,安妮有充分嘅理由一次又一次地感謝佢嘅想像力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在接下來冗長的七個星期里,安妮有充分的理由一次又一次地感謝她的想像力。

passages.original: But she was not solely dependent on it.
passages.vernacular: 但佢並非完全依賴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她並非完全依賴它。

passages.original: She had many visitors and not a day passed without one or more of the schoolgirls dropping in to bring her flowers and books and tell her all the happenings in the juvenile world of Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 佢有許多訪客,冇一天冇一個或更多嘅女學生順道嚟,帶嚟花同書,告訴佢阿文利兒童世界嘅所有大事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有許多訪客,沒有一天沒有一個或更多的女學生順道來,帶來花和書,告訴她阿文利兒童世界的所有大事。

passages.original: “Everybody has been so good and kind, Marilla,” sighed Anne happily, on the day when she could first limp across the floor.
passages.vernacular: 「大家都咁好咁親切,瑪麗拉,」安妮幸福地嘆道,喺佢第一次能一瘸一拐地走過地板嘅嗰天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「大家都那麼好那麼親切,瑪麗拉,」安妮幸福地嘆道,在她第一次能一瘸一拐地走過地板的那天。

passages.original: “It isn’t very pleasant to be laid up; but there is a bright side to it, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「臥床唔係好愉快;但佢有光明嘅一面,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「臥床不是很愉快;但它有光明的一面,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: You find out how many friends you have.
passages.vernacular: 你發現你有多少朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你發現你有多少朋友。

passages.original: Why, even Superintendent Bell came to see me, and he’s really a very fine man.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,連貝爾督導都嚟睇我,佢真係一位好好嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,連貝爾督導都來看我,他真是一位很好的人。

passages.original: Not a kindred spirit, of course; but still I like him and I’m awfully sorry I ever criticized his prayers.
passages.vernacular: 當然唔係志同道合嘅人;但我定係鍾意佢,我好抱歉我曾批評過佢嘅禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然不是志同道合的人;但我還是喜歡他,我非常抱歉我曾批評過他的禱告。

passages.original: I believe now he really does mean them, only he has got into the habit of saying them as if he didn’t.
passages.vernacular: 我而家相信佢確實係真心嘅,只係佢養成咗講得好像唔係嘅習慣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在相信他確實是真心的,只是他養成了說得好像不是的習慣。

passages.original: He could get over that if he’d take a little trouble.
passages.vernacular: 佢只要費點心就能改掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他只要費點心就能改掉。

passages.original: I gave him a good broad hint.
passages.vernacular: 我畀咗佢一個好廣嘅暗示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給了他一個很廣的暗示。

passages.original: I told him how hard I tried to make my own little private prayers interesting.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴佢我幾咁努力地讓自己私下嘅小禱告變得有趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴他我多麼努力地讓自己私下的小禱告變得有趣。

passages.original: He told me all about the time he broke his ankle when he was a boy.
passages.vernacular: 佢跟我講咗佢小時候摔斷腳踝嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他跟我說了他小時候摔斷腳踝的事。

passages.original: It does seem so strange to think of Superintendent Bell ever being a boy.
passages.vernacular: 想到貝爾督導曾經係個男孩,真嘅好奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到貝爾督導曾經是個男孩,真的好奇怪。

passages.original: Even my imagination has its limits, for I can’t imagine that.
passages.vernacular: 連我嘅想像力都有極限,因為我想像不出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連我的想像力都有極限,因為我想像不出來。

passages.original: When I try to imagine him as a boy I see him with gray whiskers and spectacles, just as he looks in Sunday-school, only small.
passages.vernacular: 當我試著想像佢係個男孩,我睇到佢長住灰鬍鬚,戴住眼鏡,就像佢喺主日學校嘅樣子,只係小嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我試著想像他是個男孩,我看到他長著灰鬍鬚,戴著眼鏡,就像他在主日學校的樣子,只是小的。

passages.original: Now, it’s so easy to imagine Mrs. Allan as a little girl.
passages.vernacular: 而家,想像艾倫太太係個小女孩就太容易喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,想像艾倫太太是個小女孩就太容易了。

passages.original: Mrs. Allan has been to see me fourteen times.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太已經嚟睇咗我十四次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太已經來看了我十四次。

passages.original: Isn’t that something to be proud of, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係值得自豪嘅事嗎,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是值得自豪的事嗎,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: When a minister’s wife has so many claims on her time!
passages.vernacular: 一個牧師嘅妻子有咁多事占用佢嘅時間!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個牧師的妻子有這麼多事占用她的時間!

passages.original: She is such a cheerful person to have visit you, too.
passages.vernacular: 佢都係個嚟睇望你時讓人如此愉快嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也是個來看望你時讓人如此愉快的人。

passages.original: She never tells you it’s your own fault and she hopes you’ll be a better girl on account of it.
passages.vernacular: 佢從不跟你講呢個係你自己嘅過錯,佢希望你因此變成更好嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她從不跟你說這是你自己的過錯,她希望你因此變成更好的女孩。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde always told me that when she came to see me; and she said it in a kind of way that made me feel she might hope I’d be a better girl but didn’t really believe I would.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太嚟睇我時總是咁講;佢講呢話嘅方式,讓我覺得佢或者希望我變成更好嘅女孩,但並不真嘅相信我會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太來看我時總是這麼說;她說這話的方式,讓我覺得她也許希望我變成更好的女孩,但並不真的相信我會。

passages.original: Even Josie Pye came to see me.
passages.vernacular: 連喬西·派伊都嚟睇我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連喬西·派伊也來看我。

passages.original: I received her as politely as I could, because I think she was sorry she dared me to walk a ridgepole.
passages.vernacular: 我儘可能禮貌地接待咗佢,因為我想佢為挑戰我走屋脊感到抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我儘可能禮貌地接待了她,因為我想她為挑戰我走屋脊感到抱歉。

passages.original: If I had been killed she would had to carry a dark burden of remorse all her life.
passages.vernacular: 如果我死喇,佢將一輩子背負悔恨嘅沉重負擔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我死了,她將一輩子背負悔恨的沉重負擔。

passages.original: Diana has been a faithful friend.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜一直係忠實嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜一直是忠實的朋友。

passages.original: She’s been over every day to cheer my lonely pillow.
passages.vernacular: 佢每天都過嚟,安慰我孤獨嘅枕頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她每天都過來,安慰我孤獨的枕頭。

passages.original: But oh, I shall be so glad when I can go to school for I’ve heard such exciting things about the new teacher.
passages.vernacular: 但係,哦,等我能去上學時我會多高興,因為我聽到咗關於新老師咁多令人興奮嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,哦,等我能去上學時我會多高興,因為我聽到了關於新老師那麼多令人興奮的事。

passages.original: The girls all think she is perfectly sweet.
passages.vernacular: 女孩哋都認為佢可愛極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩們都認為她可愛極了。

passages.original: Diana says she has the loveliest fair curly hair and such fascinating eyes.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜講佢有最可愛嘅金色鬈髮同迷人嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜說她有最可愛的金色鬈髮和迷人的眼睛。

passages.original: She dresses beautifully, and her sleeve puffs are bigger than anybody else’s in Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 佢穿得好漂亮,佢嘅泡泡袖比阿文利任何人嘅都大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她穿得很漂亮,她的泡泡袖比阿文利任何人的都大。

passages.original: Every other Friday afternoon she has recitations and everybody has to say a piece or take part in a dialogue.
passages.vernacular: 每隔一個星期五下午佢都有朗誦會,每個人都得背誦一篇或參加一個對話劇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每隔一個星期五下午她都有朗誦會,每個人都得背誦一篇或參加一個對話劇。

passages.original: Oh, it’s just glorious to think of it.
passages.vernacular: 哦,想想都太棒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,想想都太棒了。

passages.original: Josie Pye says she hates it but that is just because Josie has so little imagination.
passages.vernacular: 喬西·派伊講佢恨佢,但嗰只係因為喬西想像力太少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西·派伊說她恨它,但那只是因為喬西想像力太少。

passages.original: Diana and Ruby Gillis and Jane Andrews are preparing a dialogue, called ‘A Morning Visit,’ for next Friday.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜、露比·吉利斯同簡·安德魯斯喺為下週五準備一個叫《晨訪》嘅對話劇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜、露比·吉利斯和簡·安德魯斯在為下週五準備一個叫《晨訪》的對話劇。

passages.original: And the Friday afternoons they don’t have recitations Miss Stacy takes them all to the woods for a ‘field’ day and they study ferns and flowers and birds.
passages.vernacular: 冇朗誦會嘅星期五下午,斯泰西小姐帶佢哋全體去樹林里搞「野外」活動日,佢哋學習蕨類、花同鳥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有朗誦會的星期五下午,斯泰西小姐帶他們全體去樹林里搞「野外」活動日,他們學習蕨類、花和鳥。

passages.original: And they have physical culture exercises every morning and evening.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋每天早晚都有體育鍛煉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們每天早晚都有體育鍛煉。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says she never heard of such goings on and it all comes of having a lady teacher.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講佢從冇聽講過咁樣嘅事,呢都係因為有位女老師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說她從沒聽說過這樣的事,這都是因為有位女老師。

passages.original: But I think it must be splendid and I believe I shall find that Miss Stacy is a kindred spirit.”
passages.vernacular: 但我覺得一定好棒,我相信我會發現斯泰西小姐係志同道合嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我覺得一定很棒,我相信我會發現斯泰西小姐是志同道合的人。」

passages.original: “There’s one thing plain to be seen, Anne,” said Marilla, “and that is that your fall off the Barry roof hasn’t injured your tongue at all.”
passages.vernacular: 「有一件事顯而易見,安妮,」瑪麗拉講,「就係你從巴里家屋頂上摔下嚟,根本冇傷到你嘅舌頭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一件事顯而易見,安妮,」瑪麗拉說,「就是你從巴里家屋頂上摔下來,根本沒傷到你的舌頭。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXIV Miss Stacy and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert 第二十四章:斯泰西小姐和學生們籌辦音樂會

passages.original: CH IT was October again when Anne was ready to go back to school--a glorious October, all red and gold, with mellow mornings when the valleys were filled with delicate mists as if the spirit of autumn had poured them in for the sun to drain--amethyst, pearl, silver, rose, and smoke-blue.
passages.vernacular: 安妮準備好回學校時又係十月喇——一個光輝嘅十月,滿係紅色同金色,晨光柔和,山谷里滿係精緻嘅薄霧,仿佛秋天嘅精靈把佢哋倒進去讓太陽嚟飲乾——紫水晶色、珍珠色、銀色、玫瑰色同煙藍色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮準備好回學校時又是十月了——一個光輝的十月,滿是紅色和金色,晨光柔和,山谷里滿是精緻的薄霧,仿佛秋天的精靈把它們倒進去讓太陽來喝乾——紫水晶色、珍珠色、銀色、玫瑰色和煙藍色。

passages.original: The dews were so heavy that the fields glistened like cloth of silver and there were such heaps of rustling leaves in the hollows of many-stemmed woods to run crisply through.
passages.vernacular: 露水咁重,田野像銀布一樣閃閃發光,多枝幹嘅樹林窪地里有咁多堆沙沙作響嘅樹葉,可以脆生生地跑過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露水那麼重,田野像銀布一樣閃閃發光,多枝幹的樹林窪地里有那麼多堆沙沙作響的樹葉,可以脆生生地跑過去。

passages.original: The Birch Path was a canopy of yellow and the ferns were sear and brown all along it.
passages.vernacular: 白樺小徑係一頂黃色嘅華蓋,沿路嘅蕨類乾枯變成咗棕色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白樺小徑是一頂黃色的華蓋,沿路的蕨類乾枯變成了棕色。

passages.original: There was a tang in the very air that inspired the hearts of small maidens tripping, unlike snails, swiftly and willingly to school; and it was jolly to be back again at the little brown desk beside Diana, with Ruby Gillis nodding across the aisle and Carrie Sloane sending up notes and Julia Bell passing a “chew” of gum down from the back seat.
passages.vernacular: 空氣中就有一種辛辣,激勵住同蝸牛不同嘅、輕快而樂意地去學校嘅小姑娘哋嘅心;回到黛安娜旁邊嘅小棕色桌子前真愉快,露比·吉利斯隔住過道點頭,嘉莉·斯隆傳遞紙條,朱莉婭·貝爾從後座傳下嚟一塊「嚼」嘅口香糖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 空氣中就有一種辛辣,激勵著與蝸牛不同的、輕快而樂意地去學校的小姑娘們的心;回到黛安娜旁邊的小棕色桌子前真愉快,露比·吉利斯隔著過道點頭,嘉莉·斯隆傳遞紙條,朱莉婭·貝爾從後座傳下來一塊「嚼」的口香糖。

passages.original: Anne drew a long breath of happiness as she sharpened her pencil and arranged her picture cards in her desk.
passages.vernacular: 安妮一邊削鉛筆,一邊把圖畫卡片整理進桌子,長長地吸咗口幸福嘅氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮一邊削鉛筆,一邊把圖畫卡片整理進桌子,長長地吸了口幸福的氣。

passages.original: Life was certainly very interesting.
passages.vernacular: 生活確實好有趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 生活確實非常有趣。

passages.original: In the new teacher she found another true and helpful friend.
passages.vernacular: 喺新老師身上佢又找到咗一位真誠而有益嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在新老師身上她又找到了一位真誠而有益的朋友。

passages.original: Miss Stacy was a bright, sympathetic young woman with the happy gift of winning and holding the affections of her pupils and bringing out the best that was in them mentally and morally.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐係個聰明、富有同情心嘅年輕女士,有贏得並保持學生嘅愛、激發佢哋喺智力同道德上最好嘅一面嘅幸福天賦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐是個聰明、富有同情心的年輕女士,有贏得並保持學生的愛、激發他們在智力和道德上最好的一面的幸福天賦。

passages.original: Anne expanded like a flower under this wholesome influence and carried home to the admiring Matthew and the critical Marilla glowing accounts of schoolwork and aims.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺呢種健康嘅影響下像花一樣綻放,把關於功課同目標嘅熱情洋溢嘅敘述帶回家,講畀欽佩嘅馬修同挑剔嘅瑪麗拉聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在這種健康的影響下像花一樣綻放,把關於功課和目標的熱情洋溢的敘述帶回家,說給欽佩的馬修和挑剔的瑪麗拉聽。

passages.original: “I love Miss Stacy with my whole heart, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我全心全意地愛斯泰西小姐,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我全心全意地愛斯泰西小姐,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: She is so ladylike and she has such a sweet voice.
passages.vernacular: 佢係咁有淑女風度,有咁甜美嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是那麼有淑女風度,有那麼甜美的聲音。

passages.original: When she pronounces my name I feel instinctively that she’s spelling it with an E. We had recitations this afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 當佢念我嘅名字時,我本能地覺得佢係帶E拼嘅。今日下午我哋有朗誦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當她念我的名字時,我本能地覺得她是帶E拼的。今天下午我們有朗誦。

passages.original: I just wish you could have been there to hear me recite ‘Mary, Queen of Scots.’
passages.vernacular: 我真希望您當時在場,聽我背誦《蘇格蘭女王瑪麗》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望您當時在場,聽我背誦《蘇格蘭女王瑪麗》。

passages.original: I just put my whole soul into it.
passages.vernacular: 我把整個靈魂都投進去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把整個靈魂都投進去了。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis told me coming home that the way I said the line, ‘Now for my father’s arm,’ she said, ‘my woman’s heart farewell,’ just made her blood run cold.”
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯回家路上告訴我,我講『而家為了父親嘅臂膀,』佢講,『我女人嘅心,永別喇』呢一句嘅方式,讓佢嘅血都涼喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯回家路上告訴我,我說『現在為了父親的臂膀,』她說,『我女人的心,永別了』這一句的方式,讓她的血都涼了。」

passages.original: “Well now, you might recite it for me some of these days, out in the barn,” suggested Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,邊天你可以喺穀倉裡畀我背一背,」馬修建議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,哪天你可以在穀倉裡給我背一背,」馬修建議。

passages.original: “Of course I will,” said Anne meditatively, “but I won’t be able to do it so well, I know.
passages.vernacular: 「當然會,」安妮沉思地講,「但我知道,我唔會背得咁好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然會,」安妮沉思地說,「但我知道,我不會背得那麼好。

passages.original: It won’t be so exciting as it is when you have a whole schoolful before you hanging breathlessly on your words.
passages.vernacular: 唔會像你面前有整個學校嘅人屏息凝神地聽你講話時嗰樣令人激動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不會像你面前有整個學校的人屏息凝神地聽你說話時那樣令人激動。

passages.original: I know I won’t be able to make your blood run cold.”
passages.vernacular: 我知道我唔能夠讓您嘅血變涼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我不能讓您的血變涼。」

passages.original: “Mrs. Lynde says it made her blood run cold to see the boys climbing to the very tops of those big trees on Bell’s hill after crows’ nests last Friday,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「林德太太講上星期五睇到男孩哋爬到貝爾山上嗰啲大樹嘅樹頂去掏烏鴉窩,佢嘅血都涼喇,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「林德太太說上星期五看到男孩們爬到貝爾山上那些大樹的樹頂去掏烏鴉窩,她的血都涼了,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “I wonder at Miss Stacy for encouraging it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我真奇怪斯泰西小姐竟然鼓勵呢種事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真奇怪斯泰西小姐竟然鼓勵這種事。」

passages.original: “But we wanted a crow’s nest for nature study,” explained Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我哋要一個烏鴉窩做自然課研究,」安妮解釋講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我們要一個烏鴉窩做自然課研究,」安妮解釋說。

passages.original: “That was on our field afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係我哋野外活動嘅下午。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是我們野外活動的下午。

passages.original: Field afternoons are splendid, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 野外活動嘅下午太棒喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 野外活動的下午太棒了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: And Miss Stacy explains everything so beautifully.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐把一切講解得咁好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐把一切講解得那麼好。

passages.original: We have to write compositions on our field afternoons and I write the best ones.”
passages.vernacular: 野外活動嘅下午我哋要寫作文,我寫得最好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 野外活動的下午我們要寫作文,我寫得最好。」

passages.original: “It’s very vain of you to say so then.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你咁講就好自負喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你這麼說就很自負了。

passages.original: You’d better let your teacher say it.”
passages.vernacular: 你最好讓你嘅老師去講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你最好讓你的老師去說。」

passages.original: “But she did say it, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「可佢講喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可她說了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: And indeed I’m not vain about it.
passages.vernacular: 而且我真嘅不為此自負。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我真的不為此自負。

passages.original: How can I be, when I’m such a dunce at geometry?
passages.vernacular: 我點可能,我喺幾何上係咁笨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怎麼可能,我在幾何上是那麼笨。

passages.original: Although I’m really beginning to see through it a little, too.
passages.vernacular: 雖然我真嘅都開始稍微睇得透啲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然我真的也開始稍微看得透一點了。

passages.original: Miss Stacy makes it so clear.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐講得咁清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐講得那麼清楚。

passages.original: Still, I’ll never be good at it and I assure you it is a humbling reflection.
passages.vernacular: 不過,我永遠學不好佢,我向您保證,呢個係一個讓人謙卑嘅思考。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,我永遠學不好它,我向您保證,這是一個讓人謙卑的思考。

passages.original: But I love writing compositions.
passages.vernacular: 但我鍾意寫作文。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我喜歡寫作文。

passages.original: Mostly Miss Stacy lets us choose our own subjects; but next week we are to write a composition on some remarkable person.
passages.vernacular: 大多數時候斯泰西小姐讓我哋自己選題目;但下星期我哋要寫一篇關於某位傑出人物嘅作文。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大多數時候斯泰西小姐讓我們自己選題目;但下星期我們要寫一篇關於某位傑出人物的作文。

passages.original: It’s hard to choose among so many remarkable people who have lived.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁多曾經生活過嘅傑出人物中選一個好難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那麼多曾經生活過的傑出人物中選一個很難。

passages.original: Mustn’t it be splendid to be remarkable and have compositions written about you after you’re dead?
passages.vernacular: 做一個傑出嘅人,死後有人寫關於你嘅作文,唔係好棒嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 做一個傑出的人,死後有人寫關於你的作文,不是很棒嗎?

passages.original: Oh, I would dearly love to be remarkable.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我特別想成為傑出嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我特別想成為傑出的人。

passages.original: I think when I grow up I’ll be a trained nurse and go with the Red Crosses to the field of battle as a messenger of mercy.
passages.vernacular: 我想長大後我要當一名受過訓練嘅護士,作為慈悲嘅使者隨紅十字會上戰場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想長大後我要當一名受過訓練的護士,作為慈悲的使者隨紅十字會上戰場。

passages.original: That is, if I don’t go out as a foreign missionary.
passages.vernacular: 都就係講,如果我不去國外做傳教士嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也就是說,如果我不去國外做傳教士的話。

passages.original: That would be very romantic, but one would have to be very good to be a missionary, and that would be a stumbling block.
passages.vernacular: 嗰會好浪漫,但做傳教士必須好善良,而呢個係個絆腳石。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那會很浪漫,但做傳教士必須非常善良,而這是個絆腳石。

passages.original: We have physical culture exercises every day, too.
passages.vernacular: 我哋每天都有體育鍛煉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們每天也有體育鍛煉。

passages.original: They make you graceful and promote digestion.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋讓你姿態優美,促進消化。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們讓你姿態優美,促進消化。」

passages.original: “Promote fiddlesticks!” said Marilla, who honestly thought it was all nonsense.
passages.vernacular: 「促進乜嘢消化!」瑪麗拉講,佢真心認為呢全係胡鬧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「促進什麼消化!」瑪麗拉說,她真心認為這全是胡鬧。

passages.original: But all the field afternoons and recitation Fridays and physical culture contortions paled before a project which Miss Stacy brought forward in November.
passages.vernacular: 但所有嘅野外活動下午、朗誦星期五同體育鍛煉嘅扭曲動作,都因為斯泰西小姐十一月提出嘅一個計劃而黯然失色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但所有的野外活動下午、朗誦星期五和體育鍛煉的扭曲動作,都因為斯泰西小姐十一月提出的一個計劃而黯然失色。

passages.original: This was that the scholars of Avonlea school should get up a concert and hold it in the hall on Christmas Night, for the laudable purpose of helping to pay for a schoolhouse flag.
passages.vernacular: 呢個計劃係:阿文利學校嘅學生要搞一場音樂會,喺聖誕之夜喺大廳舉行,為了值得稱讚嘅目的——幫助支付校舍嘅一面旗幟嘅費用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個計劃是:阿文利學校的學生要搞一場音樂會,在聖誕之夜在大廳舉行,為了值得稱讚的目的——幫助支付校舍的一面旗幟的費用。

passages.original: The pupils one and all taking graciously to this plan, the preparations for a program were begun at once.
passages.vernacular: 學生哋一致欣然接受呢個計劃,節目單嘅籌備即刻開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學生們一致欣然接受這個計劃,節目單的籌備立刻開始。

passages.original: And of all the excited performers-elect none was so excited as Anne Shirley, who threw herself into the undertaking heart and soul, hampered as she was by Marilla’s disapproval.
passages.vernacular: 喺所有興奮嘅當選演員中,冇邊個比安妮·雪莉更興奮,佢全心全意地投入呢項工作,儘管受到瑪麗拉反對嘅牽制。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在所有興奮的當選演員中,沒有誰比安妮·雪莉更興奮,她全心全意地投入這項工作,儘管受到瑪麗拉反對的牽制。

passages.original: Marilla thought it all rank foolishness.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉認為呢全係徹頭徹尾嘅愚蠢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉認為這全是徹頭徹尾的愚蠢。

passages.original: “It’s just filling your heads up with nonsense and taking time that ought to be put on your lessons,” she grumbled.
passages.vernacular: 「呢只係把你哋嘅腦袋塞滿胡鬧,占用本該用喺功課上嘅時間,」佢嘟囔道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這只是把你們的腦袋塞滿胡鬧,占用本該用在功課上的時間,」她嘟囔道。

passages.original: “I don’t approve of children’s getting up concerts and racing about to practices.
passages.vernacular: 「我不贊成細路哋搞音樂會,到處奔波去排練。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不贊成孩子們搞音樂會,到處奔波去排練。

passages.original: It makes them vain and forward and fond of gadding.”
passages.vernacular: 呢會讓佢哋虛榮、冒失、愛到處閒逛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這會讓他們虛榮、冒失、愛到處閒逛。」

passages.original: “But think of the worthy object,” pleaded Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「但想想呢值得嘅目標,」安妮懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但想想這值得的目標,」安妮懇求道。

passages.original: “A flag will cultivate a spirit of patriotism, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 「旗幟能培養愛國精神,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「旗幟能培養愛國精神,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: “Fudge!
passages.vernacular: 「胡講!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說!

passages.original: There’s precious little patriotism in the thoughts of any of you.
passages.vernacular: 你哋任何一個人嘅思想裡都冇多少愛國精神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們任何一個人的思想裡都沒有多少愛國精神。

passages.original: All you want is a good time.”
passages.vernacular: 你哋想要嘅只係玩得開心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們想要的只是玩得開心。」

passages.original: “Well, when you can combine patriotism and fun, isn’t it all right?
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,當你能把愛國同快樂結合起嚟時,唔係挺好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,當你能把愛國和快樂結合起來時,不是挺好嗎?

passages.original: Of course it’s real nice to be getting up a concert.
passages.vernacular: 當然,搞音樂會真嘅好棒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,搞音樂會真的很棒。

passages.original: We’re going to have six choruses and Diana is to sing a solo.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要有六個合唱,黛安娜要獨唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要有六個合唱,黛安娜要獨唱。

passages.original: I’m in two dialogues--‘The Society for the Suppression of Gossip’ and ‘The Fairy Queen.’
passages.vernacular: 我參加兩個對話劇——《禁止閒話協會》同《仙后》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我參加兩個對話劇——《禁止閒話協會》和《仙后》。

passages.original: The boys are going to have a dialogue too.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋都要有一個對話劇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們也要有一個對話劇。

passages.original: And I’m to have two recitations, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我仲要有兩篇朗誦,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還要有兩篇朗誦,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I just tremble when I think of it, but it’s a nice thrilly kind of tremble.
passages.vernacular: 想到佢我就發抖,但嗰個係一種美好嘅、令人興奮嘅發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到它我就發抖,但那是一種美好的、令人興奮的發抖。

passages.original: And we’re to have a tableau at the last--‘Faith, Hope and Charity.’
passages.vernacular: 最後我哋仲要有一個靜態造型劇——《信、望、愛》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後我們還要有一個靜態造型劇——《信、望、愛》。

passages.original: Diana and Ruby and I are to be in it, all draped in white with flowing hair.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜、露比同我參加,都披住白紗、長髮飄飄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜、露比和我參加,都披著白紗、長髮飄飄。

passages.original: I’m to be Hope, with my hands clasped--so--and my eyes uplifted.
passages.vernacular: 我演望,雙手合十——像咁樣——眼睛向上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我演望,雙手合十——像這樣——眼睛向上。

passages.original: I’m going to practice my recitations in the garret.
passages.vernacular: 我要喺閣樓上練習我嘅朗誦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要在閣樓上練習我的朗誦。

passages.original: Don’t be alarmed if you hear me groaning.
passages.vernacular: 如果您聽到我呻吟,別害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您聽到我呻吟,別害怕。

passages.original: I have to groan heartrendingly in one of them, and it’s really hard to get up a good artistic groan, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我喺其中一篇里得撕心裂肺地呻吟,要發出一聲好嘅藝術呻吟真嘅好難,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在其中一篇里得撕心裂肺地呻吟,要發出一聲好的藝術呻吟真的很難,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Josie Pye is sulky because she didn’t get the part she wanted in the dialogue.
passages.vernacular: 喬西·派伊喺生悶氣,因為佢冇得到佢想要嘅對話劇角色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西·派伊在生悶氣,因為她沒得到她想要的對話劇角色。

passages.original: She wanted to be the fairy queen.
passages.vernacular: 佢想演仙后。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她想演仙后。

passages.original: That would have been ridiculous, for who ever heard of a fairy queen as fat as Josie?
passages.vernacular: 嗰會好可笑,因為邊個聽講過像喬西咁胖嘅仙后?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那會很可笑,因為誰聽說過像喬西這麼胖的仙后?

passages.original: Fairy queens must be slender.
passages.vernacular: 仙后必須苗條。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仙后必須苗條。

passages.original: Jane Andrews is to be the queen and I am to be one of her maids of honor.
passages.vernacular: 簡·安德魯斯演女王,我演佢嘅一名宮女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡·安德魯斯演女王,我演她的一名宮女。

passages.original: Josie says she thinks a red-haired fairy is just as ridiculous as a fat one, but I do not let myself mind what Josie says.
passages.vernacular: 喬西講佢覺得紅頭髮嘅小仙女同胖仙女一樣可笑,但我不讓自己在意喬西講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西說她覺得紅頭髮的小仙女和胖仙女一樣可笑,但我不讓自己在意喬西說什麼。

passages.original: I’m to have a wreath of white roses on my hair and Ruby Gillis is going to lend me her slippers because I haven’t any of my own.
passages.vernacular: 我頭上要戴白玫瑰花環,露比·吉利斯要把佢嘅拖鞋借畀我,因為我冇自己嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我頭上要戴白玫瑰花環,露比·吉利斯要把她的拖鞋借給我,因為我沒有自己的。

passages.original: It’s necessary for fairies to have slippers, you know.
passages.vernacular: 仙女必須有拖鞋,您知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仙女必須有拖鞋,您知道。

passages.original: You couldn’t imagine a fairy wearing boots, could you?
passages.vernacular: 您想像不出仙女穿靴子,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您想像不出仙女穿靴子,是不是?

passages.original: Especially with copper toes?
passages.vernacular: 尤其係銅頭嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尤其是銅頭的?

passages.original: We are going to decorate the hall with creeping spruce and fir mottoes with pink tissue-paper roses in them.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要用匍匐嘅杉枝同裡面有粉紅薄紙玫瑰嘅冷杉格言裝飾大廳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要用匍匐的杉枝和裡面有粉紅薄紙玫瑰的冷杉格言裝飾大廳。

passages.original: And we are all to march in two by two after the audience is seated, while Emma White plays a march on the organ.
passages.vernacular: 觀眾坐好後我哋全體要兩人一排列隊入場,艾瑪·懷特喺風琴上彈進行曲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 觀眾坐好後我們全體要兩人一排列隊入場,艾瑪·懷特在風琴上彈進行曲。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, I know you are not so enthusiastic about it as I am, but don’t you hope your little Anne will distinguish herself?”
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,我知道您冇我咁熱衷,但您難道不希望您嘅小安妮脫穎而出嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,我知道您沒有我那麼熱衷,但您難道不希望您的小安妮脫穎而出嗎?」

passages.original: “All I hope is that you’ll behave yourself.
passages.vernacular: 「我只希望你規矩些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只希望你規矩些。

passages.original: I’ll be heartily glad when all this fuss is over and you’ll be able to settle down.
passages.vernacular: 等呢一切忙亂結束,你能安下心嚟時,我會打心眼里高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等這一切忙亂結束,你能安下心來時,我會打心眼里高興。

passages.original: You are simply good for nothing just now with your head stuffed full of dialogues and groans and tableaus.
passages.vernacular: 你而家腦子裡塞滿咗對話劇、呻吟同靜態造型,簡直一無係處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你現在腦子裡塞滿了對話劇、呻吟和靜態造型,簡直一無是處。

passages.original: As for your tongue, it’s a marvel it’s not clean worn out.”
passages.vernacular: 至於你嘅舌頭,冇完全磨壞,真係奇蹟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於你的舌頭,沒有完全磨壞,真是奇蹟。」

passages.original: Anne sighed and betook herself to the back yard, over which a young new moon was shining through the leafless poplar boughs from an apple-green western sky, and where Matthew was splitting wood.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘆咗口氣,走到後院,一彎年輕嘅新月透過光禿禿嘅白楊樹枝,從蘋果綠嘅西邊天空照下嚟,馬修正在嗰度劈柴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮嘆了口氣,走到後院,一彎年輕的新月透過光禿禿的白楊樹枝,從蘋果綠的西邊天空照下來,馬修正在那裡劈柴。

passages.original: Anne perched herself on a block and talked the concert over with him, sure of an appreciative and sympathetic listener in this instance at least.
passages.vernacular: 安妮坐喺一個木墩上,同佢談論音樂會,確信至少喺呢個人身上有一個欣賞而同情嘅聽眾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮坐在一個木墩上,與他談論音樂會,確信至少在這個人身上有一個欣賞而同情的聽眾。

passages.original: “Well now, I reckon it’s going to be a pretty good concert.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想呢會係一場相當不錯嘅音樂會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想這會是一場相當不錯的音樂會。

passages.original: And I expect you’ll do your part fine,” he said, smiling down into her eager, vivacious little face.
passages.vernacular: 我想你會把你嘅部分做得好好,」佢講,微笑住低頭睇佢嗰張熱切、活潑嘅小臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你會把你的部分做得很好,」他說,微笑著低頭看她那張熱切、活潑的小臉。

passages.original: Anne smiled back at him.
passages.vernacular: 安妮向佢回以微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮向他回以微笑。

passages.original: Those two were the best of friends and Matthew thanked his stars many a time and oft that he had nothing to do with bringing her up.
passages.vernacular: 呢兩人係最好嘅朋友,馬修多次感謝老天,讓佢唔使參與撫養佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這兩人是最好的朋友,馬修多次感謝老天,讓他不必參與撫養她。

passages.original: That was Marilla’s exclusive duty; if it had been his he would have been worried over frequent conflicts between inclination and said duty.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係瑪麗拉專屬嘅責任;如果係佢嘅,佢會因傾向同責任之間嘅頻繁衝突而擔憂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是瑪麗拉專屬的責任;如果是他的,他會因傾向與責任之間的頻繁衝突而擔憂。

passages.original: As it was, he was free to, “spoil Anne”--Marilla’s phrasing--as much as he liked.
passages.vernacular: 事實上,佢可以隨心所欲地「寵壞安妮」——呢個係瑪麗拉嘅講法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實上,他可以隨心所欲地「寵壞安妮」——這是瑪麗拉的說法。

passages.original: But it was not such a bad arrangement after all; a little “appreciation” sometimes does quite as much good as all the conscientious “bringing up” in the world.
passages.vernacular: 但呢終究唔係個壞安排;有時啲「欣賞」所起嘅作用,同世上所有認真負責嘅「撫養」一樣大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這終究不是個壞安排;有時一點「欣賞」所起的作用,和世上所有認真負責的「撫養」一樣大。

chapters.title: Ch. XXV Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves 第二十五章:馬修堅持要泡泡袖

passages.original: CH MATTHEW was having a bad ten minutes of it.
passages.vernacular: 馬修正度過難熬嘅好鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修正度過難熬的十分鐘。

passages.original: He had come into the kitchen, in the twilight of a cold, gray December evening, and had sat down in the woodbox corner to take off his heavy boots, unconscious of the fact that Anne and a bevy of her schoolmates were having a practice of “The Fairy Queen” in the sitting room.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺一個寒冷陰沉嘅十二月傍晚嘅暮色中走進廚房,喺柴箱嘅角落裡坐下脫佢嘅厚靴子,冇意識到安妮同一群同學正在起居室裡排練《仙后》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在一個寒冷陰沉的十二月傍晚的暮色中走進廚房,在柴箱的角落裡坐下脫他的厚靴子,沒意識到安妮和一群同學正在起居室裡排練《仙后》。

passages.original: Presently they came trooping through the hall and out into the kitchen, laughing and chattering gaily.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋成群結隊地穿過門廳,走進廚房,歡笑嬉鬧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久她們成群結隊地穿過門廳,走進廚房,歡笑嬉鬧。

passages.original: They did not see Matthew, who shrank bashfully back into the shadows beyond the woodbox with a boot in one hand and a bootjack in the other, and he watched them shyly for the aforesaid ten minutes as they put on caps and jackets and talked about the dialogue and the concert.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋冇睇見馬修,佢害羞地縮回到柴箱後面嘅陰影裡,一隻手攞住一隻靴子,另一隻手攞住脫靴器,上述嘅好鐘里,佢羞怯地睇住佢哋戴上帽子、穿上夾克,談論對話劇同音樂會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們沒看見馬修,他害羞地縮回到柴箱後面的陰影裡,一隻手拿著一隻靴子,另一隻手拿著脫靴器,上述的十分鐘里,他羞怯地看著她們戴上帽子、穿上夾克,談論對話劇和音樂會。

passages.original: Anne stood among them, bright eyed and animated as they; but Matthew suddenly became conscious that there was something about her different from her mates.
passages.vernacular: 安妮站喺佢哋中間,眼睛明亮,神采飛揚,同佢哋一樣;但馬修突然意識到佢身上有某種同同學不同嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮站在她們中間,眼睛明亮,神采飛揚,和她們一樣;但馬修突然意識到她身上有某種與同學不同的東西。

passages.original: And what worried Matthew was that the difference impressed him as being something that should not exist.
passages.vernacular: 讓馬修擔憂嘅係,呢種不同畀佢嘅印象係不該存在嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓馬修擔憂的是,這種不同給他的印象是不該存在的東西。

passages.original: Anne had a brighter face, and bigger, starrier eyes, and more delicate features than the other; even shy, unobservant Matthew had learned to take note of these things; but the difference that disturbed him did not consist in any of these respects.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅臉更明亮,眼睛更大、更像星星,五官比別人更精緻;就連害羞、不善觀察嘅馬修都學會咗注意呢啲;但令佢不安嘅不同並不喺呢啲方面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的臉更明亮,眼睛更大、更像星星,五官比別人更精緻;就連害羞、不善觀察的馬修也學會了注意這些;但令他不安的不同並不在這些方面。

passages.original: Then in what did it consist?
passages.vernacular: 咁喺邊度呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼在哪裡呢?

passages.original: Matthew was haunted by this question long after the girls had gone, arm in arm, down the long, hard-frozen lane and Anne had betaken herself to her books.
passages.vernacular: 女孩哋手挽手沿住長長嘅凍硬嘅小巷離去,安妮回去睇書之後好久,馬修依然被呢個問題縈繞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩們手挽手沿著長長的凍硬的小巷離去,安妮回去看書之後很久,馬修依然被這個問題縈繞。

passages.original: He could not refer it to Marilla, who, he felt, would be quite sure to sniff scornfully and remark that the only difference she saw between Anne and the other girls was that they sometimes kept their tongues quiet while Anne never did.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔能夠問瑪麗拉,佢覺得佢肯定會輕蔑地哼一聲,講佢睇到嘅安妮同其他女孩嘅唯一區別,係佢哋有時仲會安靜一下,而安妮從不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不能問瑪麗拉,他覺得她肯定會輕蔑地哼一聲,說她看到的安妮和其他女孩的唯一區別,是她們有時還會安靜一下,而安妮從不。

passages.original: This, Matthew felt, would be no great help.
passages.vernacular: 馬修覺得呢個冇多大幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修覺得這沒有多大幫助。

passages.original: He had recourse to his pipe that evening to help him study it out, much to Marilla’s disgust.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上佢求助於煙斗嚟幫佢琢磨出嚟,瑪麗拉好討厭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上他求助於煙斗來幫他琢磨出來,瑪麗拉很討厭。

passages.original: After two hours of smoking and hard reflection Matthew arrived at a solution of his problem.
passages.vernacular: 經過兩個小時嘅吸煙同苦思,馬修找到咗問題嘅答案。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 經過兩個小時的吸煙和苦思,馬修找到了問題的答案。

passages.original: Anne was not dressed like the other girls!
passages.vernacular: 安妮穿得同別嘅女孩不一樣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮穿得和別的女孩不一樣!

passages.original: The more Matthew thought about the matter the more he was convinced that Anne never had been dressed like the other girls--never since she had come to Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 馬修越想越確信,安妮從來冇穿得跟別嘅女孩一樣——自從佢嚟到綠色屋頂以來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修越想越確信,安妮從來沒有穿得跟別的女孩一樣——自從她來到綠色屋頂以來。

passages.original: Marilla kept her clothed in plain, dark dresses, all made after the same unvarying pattern.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉讓佢穿樸素嘅深色裙子,全按同一個一成不變嘅樣式做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉讓她穿樸素的深色裙子,全按同一個一成不變的樣式做的。

passages.original: If Matthew knew there was such a thing as fashion in dress it was as much as he did; but he was quite sure that Anne’s sleeves did not look at all like the sleeves the other girls wore.
passages.vernacular: 馬修若知道衣服仲有時尚呢回事,嗰已經算係了不起;但佢好肯定,安妮嘅袖子啲都不像別嘅女孩穿嘅袖子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修若知道衣服還有時尚這回事,那已經算是了不起;但他十分肯定,安妮的袖子一點也不像別的女孩穿的袖子。

passages.original: He recalled the cluster of little girls he had seen around her that evening--all gay in waists of red and blue and pink and white--and he wondered why Marilla always kept her so plainly and soberly gowned.
passages.vernacular: 佢回想起嗰天傍晚佢睇到嘅圍繞喺佢身邊嘅嗰群小女孩——都穿住鮮豔嘅紅、藍、粉紅同白色嘅上衣——佢納悶瑪麗拉點解總讓佢穿得咁樸素、咁肅穆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他回想起那天傍晚他看到的圍繞在她身邊的那群小女孩——都穿著鮮豔的紅、藍、粉紅和白色的上衣——他納悶瑪麗拉為什麼總讓她穿得那麼樸素、那麼肅穆。

passages.original: Of course, it must be all right.
passages.vernacular: 當然,一定係冇問題嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,一定是沒問題的。

passages.original: Marilla knew best and Marilla was bringing her up.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉最懂,瑪麗拉喺撫養佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉最懂,瑪麗拉在撫養她。

passages.original: Probably some wise, inscrutable motive was to be served thereby.
passages.vernacular: 或者咁樣做有某種英明、深不可測嘅動機。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許這樣做有某種英明、深不可測的動機。

passages.original: But surely it would do no harm to let the child have one pretty dress--something like Diana Barry always wore.
passages.vernacular: 但讓細路有一件漂亮裙子——像黛安娜·巴里總穿嘅嗰種——肯定冇壞處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但讓孩子有一件漂亮裙子——像黛安娜·巴里總穿的那種——肯定沒有壞處。

passages.original: Matthew decided that he would give her one; that surely could not be objected to as an unwarranted putting in of his oar.
passages.vernacular: 馬修決定佢要畀佢買一件;呢肯定唔會被反對為無理地插手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修決定他要給她買一件;這肯定不會被反對為無理地插手。

passages.original: Christmas was only a fortnight off.
passages.vernacular: 離聖誕節只有兩個星期喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離聖誕節只有兩個星期了。

passages.original: A nice new dress would be the very thing for a present.
passages.vernacular: 一件漂亮嘅新裙子正是合適嘅禮物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一件漂亮的新裙子正是合適的禮物。

passages.original: Matthew, with a sigh of satisfaction, put away his pipe and went to bed, while Marilla opened all the doors and aired the house.
passages.vernacular: 馬修滿意地嘆咗口氣,收起煙斗上床瞓覺,瑪麗拉則打開所有嘅門畀房子通風。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修滿意地嘆了口氣,收起煙斗上床睡覺,瑪麗拉則打開所有的門給房子通風。

passages.original: The very next evening Matthew betook himself to Carmody to buy the dress, determined to get the worst over and have done with it.
passages.vernacular: 第二天晚上,馬修就去咗卡莫迪買裙子,決心把最壞嘅事了結掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天晚上,馬修就去了卡莫迪買裙子,決心把最壞的事了結掉。

passages.original: It would be, he felt assured, no trifling ordeal.
passages.vernacular: 佢確信呢唔會係件小小嘅考驗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他確信這不會是件小小的考驗。

passages.original: There were some things Matthew could buy and prove himself no mean bargainer; but he knew he would be at the mercy of shopkeepers when it came to buying a girl’s dress.
passages.vernacular: 有些嘢馬修能買,並證明自己係個不差嘅討價仲價者;但佢知道,講到買女孩嘅裙子,佢就會任憑店主擺布喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些東西馬修能買,並證明自己是個不差的討價還價者;但他知道,說到買女孩的裙子,他就會任憑店主擺布了。

passages.original: After much cogitation Matthew resolved to go to Samuel Lawson’s store instead of William Blair’s.
passages.vernacular: 經過一番深思,馬修決定去塞繆爾·勞森嘅店,而唔係威廉·布萊爾嘅店。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 經過一番深思,馬修決定去塞繆爾·勞森的店,而不是威廉·布萊爾的店。

passages.original: To be sure, the Cuthberts always had gone to William Blair’s; it was almost as much a matter of conscience with them as to attend the Presbyterian church and vote Conservative.
passages.vernacular: 誠然,卡思伯特家一向去威廉·布萊爾嘅店;呢幾乎同去長老會教堂、投票畀保守黨一樣,係個良心問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠然,卡思伯特家一向去威廉·布萊爾的店;這幾乎和去長老會教堂、投票給保守黨一樣,是個良心問題。

passages.original: But William Blair’s two daughters frequently waited on customers there and Matthew held them in absolute dread.
passages.vernacular: 但威廉·布萊爾嘅兩個女兒經常喺嗰度接待顧客,馬修對佢哋怕得要死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但威廉·布萊爾的兩個女兒經常在那裡接待顧客,馬修對她們怕得要死。

passages.original: He could contrive to deal with them when he knew exactly what he wanted and could point it out; but in such a matter as this, requiring explanation and consultation, Matthew felt that he must be sure of a man behind the counter.
passages.vernacular: 當佢確切知道自己要乜嘢並能指出嚟時,佢可以設法應付佢哋;但喺咁樣需要解釋同商量嘅事情上,馬修覺得佢必須確保櫃檯後面係個男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他確切知道自己要什麼並能指出來時,他可以設法應付她們;但在這樣需要解釋和商量的事情上,馬修覺得他必須確保櫃檯後面是個男人。

passages.original: So he would go to Lawson’s, where Samuel or his son would wait on him.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢要去勞森嘅店,嗰度塞繆爾或佢兒子會接待佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他要去勞森的店,那裡塞繆爾或他兒子會接待他。

passages.original: Alas!
passages.vernacular: 唉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉!
