passages.original: Matthew did not know that Samuel, in the recent expansion of his business, had set up a lady clerk also; she was a niece of his wife’s and a very dashing young person indeed, with a huge, drooping pompadour, big, rolling brown eyes, and a most extensive and bewildering smile.
passages.vernacular: 馬修唔知道塞繆爾喺最近擴大生意時,都僱咗一位女店員;佢係佢妻子嘅外甥女,一個好時髦嘅年輕人,頭上梳住巨大垂落嘅蓬帕杜髮型,有一雙滴溜溜轉嘅大棕眼睛,臉上帶住最寬廣、最令人困惑嘅笑容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修不知道塞繆爾在最近擴大生意時,也僱了一位女店員;她是他妻子的外甥女,一個非常時髦的年輕人,頭上梳著巨大垂落的蓬帕杜髮型,有一雙滴溜溜轉的大棕眼睛,臉上帶著最寬廣、最令人困惑的笑容。

passages.original: She was dressed with exceeding smartness and wore several bangle bracelets that glittered and rattled and tinkled with every movement of her hands.
passages.vernacular: 佢穿得特別時髦,戴住幾隻手鐲,每次手一動都閃光、嘩啦、叮噹作響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她穿得特別時髦,戴著幾隻手鐲,每次手一動都閃光、嘩啦、叮噹作響。

passages.original: Matthew was covered with confusion at finding her there at all; and those bangles completely wrecked his wits at one fell swoop.
passages.vernacular: 馬修睇到佢喺嗰度就已經窘迫不堪;嗰啲手鐲一下子徹底搞亂咗佢嘅頭腦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修看到她在那裡就已經窘迫不堪;那些手鐲一下子徹底搞亂了他的頭腦。

passages.original: “What can I do for you this evening, Mr. Cuthbert?”
passages.vernacular: 「今晚我能為您做乜嘢,卡思伯特先生?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚我能為您做什麼,卡思伯特先生?」

passages.original: Miss Lucilla Harris inquired, briskly and ingratiatingly, tapping the counter with both hands.
passages.vernacular: 盧西拉·哈里斯小姐輕快而討好地問,雙手拍住櫃檯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 盧西拉·哈里斯小姐輕快而討好地問,雙手拍著櫃檯。

passages.original: “Have you any--any--any--well now, say any garden rakes?” stammered Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋有冇——有冇——有冇——嗯,比如講,有冇花園耙子?」馬修結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們有沒有——有沒有——有沒有——嗯,比如說,有沒有花園耙子?」馬修結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: Miss Harris looked somewhat surprised, as well she might, to hear a man inquiring for garden rakes in the middle of December.
passages.vernacular: 哈里斯小姐顯得有些驚訝,都難怪,十二月中旬居然有個男人嚟問花園耙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈里斯小姐顯得有些驚訝,也難怪,十二月中旬居然有個男人來問花園耙子。

passages.original: “I believe we have one or two left over,” she said, “but they’re upstairs in the lumber room.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我哋仲剩一兩把,」佢講,「不過佢哋喺樓上嘅雜物間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我們還剩一兩把,」她說,「不過它們在樓上的雜物間。

passages.original: I’ll go and see.”
passages.vernacular: 我去睇睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去看看。」

passages.original: During her absence Matthew collected his scattered senses for another effort.
passages.vernacular: 佢不喺嘅時候,馬修把散亂嘅神志收攏起嚟,準備再作一次努力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不在的時候,馬修把散亂的神志收攏起來,準備再作一次努力。

passages.original: When Miss Harris returned with the rake and cheerfully inquired: “Anything else tonight, Mr. Cuthbert?”
passages.vernacular: 哈里斯小姐攞住耙子回嚟,愉快地問:「今晚仲要別嘅嗎,卡思伯特先生?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈里斯小姐拿著耙子回來,愉快地問:「今晚還要別的嗎,卡思伯特先生?」

passages.original: Matthew took his courage in both hands and replied: “Well now, since you suggest it, I might as well--take--that is--look at--buy some--some hayseed.”
passages.vernacular: 馬修鼓起全部勇氣回答:「嗯,既然你建議喇,我不妨——攞——就係講——睇睇——買些——些乾草籽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修鼓起全部勇氣回答:「嗯,既然你建議了,我不妨——拿——就是說——看看——買些——些乾草籽。」

passages.original: Miss Harris had heard Matthew Cuthbert called odd.
passages.vernacular: 哈里斯小姐聽講過馬修·卡思伯特古怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈里斯小姐聽說過馬修·卡思伯特古怪。

passages.original: She now concluded that he was entirely crazy.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家斷定佢完全瘋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在斷定他完全瘋了。

passages.original: “We only keep hayseed in the spring,” she explained loftily.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋只有春天才賣乾草籽,」佢傲慢地解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們只有春天才賣乾草籽,」她傲慢地解釋。

passages.original: “We’ve none on hand just now.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家手頭冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在手頭沒有。」

passages.original: “Oh, certainly--certainly--just as you say,” stammered unhappy Matthew, seizing the rake and making for the door.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,當然——當然——您講得對,」不幸嘅馬修結巴地講,抓起耙子往門口走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,當然——當然——您說得對,」不幸的馬修結巴地說,抓起耙子往門口走。

passages.original: At the threshold he recollected that he had not paid for it and he turned miserably back.
passages.vernacular: 走到門口佢想起冇付錢,又痛苦地折咗回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走到門口他想起沒付錢,又痛苦地折了回來。

passages.original: While Miss Harris was counting out his change he rallied his powers for a final desperate attempt.
passages.vernacular: 哈里斯小姐數找零嘅時候,佢重整旗鼓作最後嘅孤注一擲嘅嘗試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈里斯小姐數找零的時候,他重整旗鼓作最後的孤注一擲的嘗試。

passages.original: “Well now--if it isn’t too much trouble--I might as well--that is--I’d like to look at--at--some sugar.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯——如果不太麻煩——我不妨——就係講——我想睇睇——睇睇——啲糖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯——如果不太麻煩——我不妨——就是說——我想看看——看看——一些糖。」

passages.original: “White or brown?” queried Miss Harris patiently.
passages.vernacular: 「白糖定係紅糖?」哈里斯小姐耐心地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「白糖還是紅糖?」哈里斯小姐耐心地問。

passages.original: “Oh--well now--brown,” said Matthew feebly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦——嗯——紅糖,」馬修虛弱地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦——嗯——紅糖,」馬修虛弱地說。

passages.original: “There’s a barrel of it over there,” said Miss Harris, shaking her bangles at it.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰邊有一桶,」哈里斯小姐講,朝佢搖咗搖手鐲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那邊有一桶,」哈里斯小姐說,朝它搖了搖手鐲。

passages.original: “It’s the only kind we have.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我哋唯一有嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我們唯一有的。」

passages.original: “I’ll--I’ll take twenty pounds of it,” said Matthew, with beads of perspiration standing on his forehead.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我要二十磅,」馬修講,額頭上豆大嘅汗珠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我要二十磅,」馬修說,額頭上豆大的汗珠。

passages.original: Matthew had driven halfway home before he was his own man again.
passages.vernacular: 馬修趕車走咗一半嘅路才恢復自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修趕車走了一半的路才恢復自己。

passages.original: It had been a gruesome experience, but it served him right, he thought, for committing the heresy of going to a strange store.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一次可怕嘅經歷,但佢想,呢個係佢活該,因為犯咗去陌生店嘅異端行為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一次可怕的經歷,但他想,這是他活該,因為犯了去陌生店的異端行為。

passages.original: When he reached home he hid the rake in the tool house, but the sugar he carried in to Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 回到家,佢把耙子藏喺工具房,但把糖帶進去畀咗瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回到家,他把耙子藏在工具房,但把糖帶進去給了瑪麗拉。

passages.original: “Brown sugar!” exclaimed Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「紅糖!」瑪麗拉叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「紅糖!」瑪麗拉叫道。

passages.original: “Whatever possessed you to get so much?
passages.vernacular: 「你到底點想起買咁多?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你到底怎麼想起買這麼多?

passages.original: You know I never use it except for the hired man’s porridge or black fruit cake.
passages.vernacular: 你知道我除咗畀雇工煮粥或做黑水果蛋糕,從唔使佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道我除了給雇工煮粥或做黑水果蛋糕,從不用它。

passages.original: Jerry’s gone and I’ve made my cake long ago.
passages.vernacular: 傑里走喇,我嘅蛋糕早就做好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑里走了,我的蛋糕早就做好了。

passages.original: It’s not good sugar, either--it’s coarse and dark--William Blair doesn’t usually keep sugar like that.”
passages.vernacular: 而且呢糖都不好——又粗又黑——威廉·布萊爾通常不賣呢種糖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且這糖也不好——又粗又黑——威廉·布萊爾通常不賣這種糖。」

passages.original: “I--I thought it might come in handy sometime,” said Matthew, making good his escape.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我想佢邊天可能用得上,」馬修講,趁機溜走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我想它哪天可能用得上,」馬修說,趁機溜走了。

passages.original: When Matthew came to think the matter over he decided that a woman was required to cope with the situation.
passages.vernacular: 馬修回頭琢磨呢件事時,斷定需要一個女人嚟應付呢種局面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修回頭琢磨這件事時,斷定需要一個女人來應付這種局面。

passages.original: Marilla was out of the question.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉係唔可能嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉是不可能的。

passages.original: Matthew felt sure she would throw cold water on his project at once.
passages.vernacular: 馬修確信佢即刻會畀佢嘅計劃潑冷水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修確信她馬上會給他的計劃潑冷水。

passages.original: Remained only Mrs. Lynde; for of no other woman in Avonlea would Matthew have dared to ask advice.
passages.vernacular: 剩下嘅只有林德太太;因為阿文利嘅其他女人,馬修都唔敢請教。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 剩下的只有林德太太;因為阿文利的其他女人,馬修都不敢請教。

passages.original: To Mrs. Lynde he went accordingly, and that good lady promptly took the matter out of the harassed man’s hands.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢去找林德太太,嗰位好太太即刻把事情從呢個焦頭爛額嘅男人手裡接咗過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他去找林德太太,那位好太太立刻把事情從這個焦頭爛額的男人手裡接了過去。

passages.original: “Pick out a dress for you to give Anne?
passages.vernacular: 「挑一件裙子讓你送畀安妮?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「挑一件裙子讓你送給安妮?

passages.original: To be sure I will.
passages.vernacular: 我當然會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我當然會。

passages.original: I’m going to Carmody tomorrow and I’ll attend to it.
passages.vernacular: 我聽日要去卡莫迪,我會辦嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我明天要去卡莫迪,我會辦的。

passages.original: Have you something particular in mind?
passages.vernacular: 你有乜嘢特別嘅想法嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有什麼特別的想法嗎?

passages.original: No?
passages.vernacular: 冇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有?

passages.original: Well, I’ll just go by my own judgment then.
passages.vernacular: 嗰我就憑我自己嘅判斷吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我就憑我自己的判斷吧。

passages.original: I believe a nice rich brown would just suit Anne, and William Blair has some new gloria in that’s real pretty.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得一種漂亮嘅深棕色正適合安妮,威廉·布萊爾有啲剛到嘅格洛麗亞綢,真嘅好漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得一種漂亮的深棕色正適合安妮,威廉·布萊爾有一些剛到的格洛麗亞綢,真的很漂亮。

passages.original: Perhaps you’d like me to make it up for her, too, seeing that if Marilla was to make it Anne would probably get wind of it before the time and spoil the surprise?
passages.vernacular: 或者你想讓我畀佢做出嚟,因為如果瑪麗拉做,安妮好可能提前聽到風聲,破壞驚喜?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許你想讓我給她做出來,因為如果瑪麗拉做,安妮很可能提前聽到風聲,破壞驚喜?

passages.original: Well, I’ll do it.
passages.vernacular: 好,我嚟做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我來做。

passages.original: No, it isn’t a mite of trouble.
passages.vernacular: 不,啲都不麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,一點也不麻煩。

passages.original: I like sewing.
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意縫紉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡縫紉。

passages.original: I’ll make it to fit my niece, Jenny Gillis, for she and Anne are as like as two peas as far as figure goes.”
passages.vernacular: 我照我外甥女珍妮·吉利斯嘅尺寸做,因為論身材,佢同安妮像兩顆豌豆一樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我照我外甥女珍妮·吉利斯的尺寸做,因為論身材,她和安妮像兩顆豌豆一樣。」

passages.original: “Well now, I’m much obliged,” said Matthew, “and--and--I dunno--but I’d like--I think they make the sleeves different nowadays to what they used to be.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我好感謝,」馬修講,「仲有——仲有——我唔知道——但我想——我覺得而家袖子嘅做法同以前不一樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我非常感謝,」馬修說,「還有——還有——我不知道——但我想——我覺得現在袖子的做法和以前不一樣了。

passages.original: If it wouldn’t be asking too much I--I’d like them made in the new way.”
passages.vernacular: 如果不算要求太多,我——我想做成新式嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果不算要求太多,我——我想做成新式的。」

passages.original: “Puffs?
passages.vernacular: 「泡泡袖?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「泡泡袖?

passages.original: Of course.
passages.vernacular: 當然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然。

passages.original: You needn’t worry a speck more about it, Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 你唔使再為此擔心喇,馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不必再為此擔心了,馬修。

passages.original: I’ll make it up in the very latest fashion,” said Mrs. Lynde.
passages.vernacular: 我會按最新嘅款式做出嚟,」林德太太講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會按最新的款式做出來,」林德太太說。

passages.original: To herself she added when Matthew had gone:
passages.vernacular: 馬修走後,佢對自己補充道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修走後,她對自己補充道:

passages.original: “It’ll be a real satisfaction to see that poor child wearing something decent for once.
passages.vernacular: 「睇到嗰個可憐嘅細路穿一回像樣嘅衣服,真係個滿足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看到那個可憐的孩子穿一回像樣的衣服,真是個滿足。

passages.original: The way Marilla dresses her is positively ridiculous, that’s what, and I’ve ached to tell her so plainly a dozen times.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉畀佢穿嘅方式簡直荒唐,就係咁樣,我有十幾次急住要直白地告訴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉給她穿的方式簡直荒唐,就是這樣,我有十幾次急著要直白地告訴她。

passages.original: I’ve held my tongue though, for I can see Marilla doesn’t want advice and she thinks she knows more about bringing children up than I do for all she’s an old maid.
passages.vernacular: 不過我一直冇開口,因為我睇得出瑪麗拉唔想要建議,佢以為自己比我更懂得點養細路,儘管佢係個老處女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我一直沒開口,因為我看得出瑪麗拉不想要建議,她以為自己比我更懂得怎麼養孩子,儘管她是個老處女。

passages.original: But that’s always the way.
passages.vernacular: 但向來如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但向來如此。

passages.original: Folks that has brought up children know that there’s no hard and fast method in the world that’ll suit every child.
passages.vernacular: 養過細路嘅人都知道,世上冇一種硬性嘅方法適合每一個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 養過孩子的人都知道,世上沒有一種硬性的方法適合每一個孩子。

passages.original: But them as never have think it’s all as plain and easy as Rule of Three--just set your three terms down so fashion, and the sum ‘ll work out correct.
passages.vernacular: 但從冇養過嘅人,以為呢一切都像三率法一樣簡單明瞭——只要把三項數字咁樣一擺,算式就能算對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但從沒養過的人,以為這一切都像三率法一樣簡單明瞭——只要把三項數字這樣一擺,算式就能算對。

passages.original: But flesh and blood don’t come under the head of arithmetic and that’s where Marilla Cuthbert makes her mistake.
passages.vernacular: 但血肉之軀不屬於算術範疇,而呢個就係瑪麗拉·卡思伯特嘅錯誤所在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但血肉之軀不屬於算術範疇,而這就是瑪麗拉·卡思伯特的錯誤所在。

passages.original: I suppose she’s trying to cultivate a spirit of humility in Anne by dressing her as she does; but it’s more likely to cultivate envy and discontent.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢係想通過咁樣畀安妮穿衣,培養佢謙卑嘅精神;但更可能培養嘅係嫉妒同不滿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想她是想通過這樣給安妮穿衣,培養她謙卑的精神;但更可能培養的是嫉妒和不滿。

passages.original: I’m sure the child must feel the difference between her clothes and the other girls’.
passages.vernacular: 我肯定嗰細路一定感覺得到佢嘅衣服同別嘅女孩嘅衣服嘅差別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我肯定那孩子一定感覺得到她的衣服和別的女孩的衣服的差別。

passages.original: But to think of Matthew taking notice of it!
passages.vernacular: 不過想唔到馬修竟注意到喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是想不到馬修竟注意到了!

passages.original: That man is waking up after being asleep for over sixty years.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個人瞓咗六十多年之後正在醒嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個人睡了六十多年之後正在醒來。」

passages.original: Marilla knew all the following fortnight that Matthew had something on his mind, but what it was she could not guess, until Christmas Eve, when Mrs. Lynde brought up the new dress.
passages.vernacular: 喺接下嚟嘅兩個星期里,瑪麗拉都知道馬修心裡有事,但佢猜不出係乜嘢,直到平安夜,林德太太把新裙子攞嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在接下來的兩個星期里,瑪麗拉都知道馬修心裡有事,但她猜不出是什麼,直到平安夜,林德太太把新裙子拿來了。

passages.original: Marilla behaved pretty well on the whole, although it is very likely she distrusted Mrs. Lynde’s diplomatic explanation that she had made the dress because Matthew was afraid Anne would find out about it too soon if Marilla made it.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉總嘅來講表現得相當好,儘管佢好可能不相信林德太太嗰番圓滑嘅解釋:佢做呢條裙子係因為馬修怕如果瑪麗拉做,安妮太早發現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉總的來說表現得相當好,儘管她很可能不相信林德太太那番圓滑的解釋:她做這條裙子是因為馬修怕如果瑪麗拉做,安妮太早發現。

passages.original: “So this is what Matthew has been looking so mysterious over and grinning about to himself for two weeks, is it?” she said a little stiffly but tolerantly.
passages.vernacular: 「所以馬修兩個星期嚟一直神祕兮兮、獨自傻笑,就係為了呢個,係嗎?」佢略帶生硬但寬容地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所以馬修兩個星期來一直神祕兮兮、獨自傻笑,就是為了這個,是嗎?」她略帶生硬但寬容地說。

passages.original: “I knew he was up to some foolishness.
passages.vernacular: 「我就知道佢喺搞乜嘢蠢事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就知道他在搞什麼蠢事。

passages.original: Well, I must say I don’t think Anne needed any more dresses.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我必須講我不覺得安妮仲需要裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我必須說我不覺得安妮還需要裙子。

passages.original: I made her three good, warm, serviceable ones this fall, and anything more is sheer extravagance.
passages.vernacular: 今年秋天我畀佢做咗三件好嘅、暖同嘅、耐穿嘅,再多就純屬浪費喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今年秋天我給她做了三件好的、暖和的、耐穿的,再多就純屬浪費了。

passages.original: There’s enough material in those sleeves alone to make a waist, I declare there is.
passages.vernacular: 光嗰兩個袖子嘅料子,就夠做一件上衣喇,我敢講係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 光那兩個袖子的料子,就夠做一件上衣了,我敢說是的。

passages.original: You’ll just pamper Anne’s vanity, Matthew, and she’s as vain as a peacock now.
passages.vernacular: 你會寵壞安妮嘅虛榮,馬修,佢而家已經像孔雀一樣愛慕虛榮喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會寵壞安妮的虛榮,馬修,她現在已經像孔雀一樣愛慕虛榮了。

passages.original: Well, I hope she’ll be satisfied at last, for I know she’s been hankering after those silly sleeves ever since they came in, although she never said a word after the first.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我希望佢終於能滿意,因為我知道自從嗰種愚蠢嘅袖子流行以來,佢一直喺渴望,雖然第一次之後佢一個字都冇再提。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我希望她終於能滿意,因為我知道自從那種愚蠢的袖子流行以來,她一直在渴望,雖然第一次之後她一個字也沒再提。

passages.original: The puffs have been getting bigger and more ridiculous right along; they’re as big as balloons now.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲泡泡一直越嚟越大、越嚟越可笑;而家已經像氣球一樣大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些泡泡一直越來越大、越來越可笑;現在已經像氣球一樣大了。

passages.original: Next year anybody who wears them will have to go through a door sideways.”
passages.vernacular: 明年邊個要係戴上佢哋,就得側住身子過門喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明年誰要是戴上它們,就得側著身子過門了。」

passages.original: Christmas morning broke on a beautiful white world.
passages.vernacular: 聖誕節早晨,喺一個美麗嘅白色世界中破曉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖誕節早晨,在一個美麗的白色世界中破曉。

passages.original: It had been a very mild December and people had looked forward to a green Christmas; but just enough snow fell softly in the night to transfigure Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 十二月好溫和,人哋一直期待一個綠色嘅聖誕節;但夜裡輕輕落下嘅雪,剛好足以讓阿文利變咗模樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十二月非常溫和,人們一直期待一個綠色的聖誕節;但夜裡輕輕落下的雪,剛好足以讓阿文利變了模樣。

passages.original: Anne peeped out from her frosted gable window with delighted eyes.
passages.vernacular: 安妮從結咗霜花嘅山牆窗子向外窺視,眼裡滿係喜悅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮從結了霜花的山牆窗子向外窺視,眼裡滿是喜悅。

passages.original: The firs in the Haunted Wood were all feathery and wonderful; the birches and wild cherry-trees were outlined in pearl; the plowed fields were stretches of snowy dimples; and there was a crisp tang in the air that was glorious.
passages.vernacular: 鬧鬼林里嘅冷杉都係羽毛般嘅,奇妙無比;白樺同野櫻桃樹被珍珠勾勒出輪廓;耕過嘅田野係一片片雪白嘅酒窩;空氣中有一種令人暢快嘅清冽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鬧鬼林里的冷杉都是羽毛般的,奇妙無比;白樺和野櫻桃樹被珍珠勾勒出輪廓;耕過的田野是一片片雪白的酒窩;空氣中有一種令人暢快的清冽。

passages.original: Anne ran downstairs singing until her voice reechoed through Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 安妮跑下樓,唱住歌,歌聲喺整個綠色屋頂迴響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮跑下樓,唱著歌,歌聲在整個綠色屋頂迴響。

passages.original: “Merry Christmas, Marilla!
passages.vernacular: 「聖誕快樂,瑪麗拉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聖誕快樂,瑪麗拉!

passages.original: Merry Christmas, Matthew!
passages.vernacular: 聖誕快樂,馬修!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖誕快樂,馬修!

passages.original: Isn’t it a lovely Christmas?
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係個可愛嘅聖誕節嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是個可愛的聖誕節嗎?

passages.original: I’m so glad it’s white.
passages.vernacular: 我真高興佢係白色嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真高興它是白色的。

passages.original: Any other kind of Christmas doesn’t seem real, does it?
passages.vernacular: 任何其他樣子嘅聖誕節似乎都不真實,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何其他樣子的聖誕節似乎都不真實,是不是?

passages.original: I don’t like green Christmases.
passages.vernacular: 我不鍾意綠色嘅聖誕節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不喜歡綠色的聖誕節。

passages.original: They’re not green--they’re just nasty faded browns and grays.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋根本唔係綠嘅——只係難睇嘅褪色嘅棕色同灰色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們根本不是綠的——只是難看的褪色的棕色和灰色。

passages.original: What makes people call them green?
passages.vernacular: 點解人哋叫佢哋綠色嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼人們叫它們綠色的?

passages.original: Why--why--Matthew, is that for me?
passages.vernacular: 哎呀——哎呀——馬修,嗰個係畀我嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀——哎呀——馬修,那是給我的嗎?

passages.original: Oh, Matthew!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,馬修!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,馬修!」

passages.original: Matthew had sheepishly unfolded the dress from its paper swathings and held it out with a deprecatory glance at Marilla, who feigned to be contemptuously filling the teapot, but nevertheless watched the scene out of the corner of her eye with a rather interested air.
passages.vernacular: 馬修害羞地從紙包裹中把裙子展開,帶住歉疚嘅目光睇咗一眼瑪麗拉,瑪麗拉假裝輕蔑地往茶壺裡倒水,但仍用眼角餘光帶住相當感興趣嘅神氣睇住呢一幕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修害羞地從紙包裹中把裙子展開,帶著歉疚的目光看了一眼瑪麗拉,瑪麗拉假裝輕蔑地往茶壺裡倒水,但仍用眼角餘光帶著相當感興趣的神氣看著這一幕。

passages.original: Anne took the dress and looked at it in reverent silence.
passages.vernacular: 安妮接過裙子,恭敬地沉默住睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮接過裙子,恭敬地沉默著看著它。

passages.original: Oh, how pretty it was--a lovely soft brown gloria with all the gloss of silk; a skirt with dainty frills and shirrings; a waist elaborately pintucked in the most fashionable way, with a little ruffle of filmy lace at the neck.
passages.vernacular: 哦,多漂亮啊——一件可愛嘅柔軟棕色格洛麗亞綢,有絲綢般嘅所有光澤;裙子帶有精緻嘅荷葉邊同抽褶;上衣用最時髦嘅方式精心打住細褶,領口有一圈輕薄蕾絲嘅小褶邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,多漂亮啊——一件可愛的柔軟棕色格洛麗亞綢,有絲綢般的所有光澤;裙子帶有精緻的荷葉邊和抽褶;上衣用最時髦的方式精心打著細褶,領口有一圈輕薄蕾絲的小褶邊。

passages.original: But the sleeves--they were the crowning glory!
passages.vernacular: 但袖子——佢哋係點睛之筆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但袖子——它們是點睛之筆!

passages.original: Long elbow cuffs, and above them two beautiful puffs divided by rows of shirring and bows of brown-silk ribbon.
passages.vernacular: 長長嘅肘袖口,上面係兩個美麗嘅泡泡,中間由一排排抽褶同棕色絲帶蝴蝶結隔開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 長長的肘袖口,上面是兩個美麗的泡泡,中間由一排排抽褶和棕色絲帶蝴蝶結隔開。

passages.original: “That’s a Christmas present for you, Anne,” said Matthew shyly.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係畀你嘅聖誕禮物,安妮,」馬修害羞地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是給你的聖誕禮物,安妮,」馬修害羞地說。

passages.original: “Why--why--Anne, don’t you like it?
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀——哎呀——安妮,你不鍾意嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀——哎呀——安妮,你不喜歡嗎?

passages.original: Well now--well now.”
For Anne’s eyes had suddenly filled with tears.
passages.vernacular: 因為安妮嘅眼睛裡突然充滿咗淚水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為安妮的眼睛裡突然充滿了淚水。

passages.original: “Like it!
passages.vernacular: 「鍾意!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喜歡!

passages.original: Oh, Matthew!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,馬修!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,馬修!」

passages.original: Anne laid the dress over a chair and clasped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把裙子放喺椅子上,雙手合十。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把裙子放在椅子上,雙手合十。

passages.original: “Matthew, it’s perfectly exquisite.
passages.vernacular: 「馬修,佢精緻極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修,它精緻極了。

passages.original: Oh, I can never thank you enough.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我永遠感謝唔夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我永遠感謝不夠。

passages.original: Look at those sleeves!
passages.vernacular: 睇嗰啲袖子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看那些袖子!

passages.original: Oh, it seems to me this must be a happy dream.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我覺得呢一定係個幸福嘅夢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我覺得這一定是個幸福的夢。」

passages.original: “Well, well, let us have breakfast,” interrupted Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,我哋食早飯吧,」瑪麗拉打斷道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,我們吃早飯吧,」瑪麗拉打斷道。

passages.original: “I must say, Anne, I don’t think you needed the dress; but since Matthew has got it for you, see that you take good care of it.
passages.vernacular: 「我必須講,安妮,我不覺得你需要呢條裙子;不過既然馬修畀你買喇,你要好好愛護佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須說,安妮,我不覺得你需要這條裙子;不過既然馬修給你買了,你要好好愛護它。

passages.original: There’s a hair ribbon Mrs. Lynde left for you.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太留畀你一條髮帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太留給你一條髮帶。

passages.original: It’s brown, to match the dress.
passages.vernacular: 係棕色嘅,配裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是棕色的,配裙子。

passages.original: Come now, sit in.”
passages.vernacular: 好喇,坐下吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,坐下吧。」

passages.original: “I don’t see how I’m going to eat breakfast,” said Anne rapturously.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道我點食得下早飯,」安妮狂喜地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道我怎麼吃得下早飯,」安妮狂喜地說。

passages.original: “Breakfast seems so commonplace at such an exciting moment.
passages.vernacular: 「喺咁令人激動嘅時刻,早飯似乎太平凡喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在這麼令人激動的時刻,早飯似乎太平凡了。

passages.original: I’d rather feast my eyes on that dress.
passages.vernacular: 我寧願用眼睛嚟享受嗰條裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願用眼睛來享受那條裙子。

passages.original: I’m so glad that puffed sleeves are still fashionable.
passages.vernacular: 我太高興泡泡袖仲時髦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興泡泡袖還時髦。

passages.original: It did seem to me that I’d never get over it if they went out before I had a dress with them.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得,如果喺我有一條帶泡泡袖嘅裙子之前佢哋就過時喇,我會永遠緩不過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得,如果在我有一條帶泡泡袖的裙子之前它們就過時了,我會永遠緩不過來。

passages.original: I’d never have felt quite satisfied, you see.
passages.vernacular: 您瞧,我永遠唔會完全滿足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您瞧,我永遠不會完全滿足。

passages.original: It was lovely of Mrs. Lynde to give me the ribbon too.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太還畀我髮帶,真係太好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太還給我髮帶,真是太好了。

passages.original: I feel that I ought to be a very good girl indeed.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得我真嘅應該做一個好好嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得我真的應該做一個非常好的女孩。

passages.original: It’s at times like this I’m sorry I’m not a model little girl; and I always resolve that I will be in future.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅時刻,我為自己唔係模範小女孩而抱歉;我總是決心將來要做到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的時刻,我為自己不是模範小女孩而抱歉;我總是決心將來要做到。

passages.original: But somehow it’s hard to carry out your resolutions when irresistible temptations come.
passages.vernacular: 但係唔知怎嘅,當無法抗拒嘅誘惑來臨時,好難實現你嘅決心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是不知怎的,當無法抗拒的誘惑來臨時,很難實現你的決心。

passages.original: Still, I really will make an extra effort after this.”
passages.vernacular: 不過,我今後真嘅會格外努力。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,我今後真的會格外努力。」

passages.original: When the commonplace breakfast was over Diana appeared, crossing the white log bridge in the hollow, a gay little figure in her crimson ulster.
passages.vernacular: 平凡嘅早飯結束後,黛安娜出現喇,穿過窪地里白色嘅原木橋,係一個穿住深紅色長大衣嘅歡快小身影。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 平凡的早飯結束後,黛安娜出現了,穿過窪地里白色的原木橋,是一個穿著深紅色長大衣的歡快小身影。

passages.original: Anne flew down the slope to meet her.
passages.vernacular: 安妮飛奔下斜坡去迎接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮飛奔下斜坡去迎接她。

passages.original: “Merry Christmas, Diana!
passages.vernacular: 「聖誕快樂,黛安娜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聖誕快樂,黛安娜!

passages.original: And oh, it’s a wonderful Christmas.
passages.vernacular: 哦,呢個係個奇妙嘅聖誕節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,這是個奇妙的聖誕節。

passages.original: I’ve something splendid to show you.
passages.vernacular: 我有好棒嘅嘢畀你睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有很棒的東西給你看。

passages.original: Matthew has given me the loveliest dress, with such sleeves.
passages.vernacular: 馬修畀咗我最可愛嘅裙子,嗰袖子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修給了我最可愛的裙子,那袖子。

passages.original: I couldn’t even imagine any nicer.”
passages.vernacular: 我甚至想像不出更好嘅喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我甚至想像不出更好的了。」

passages.original: “I’ve got something more for you,” said Diana breathlessly.
passages.vernacular: 「我仲有更好嘅嘢畀你,」黛安娜氣喘吁吁地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我還有更好的東西給你,」黛安娜氣喘吁吁地說。

passages.original: “Here--this box.
passages.vernacular: 「畀——呢個盒子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「給——這個盒子。

passages.original: Aunt Josephine sent us out a big box with ever so many things in it--and this is for you.
passages.vernacular: 約瑟芬姑婆畀我哋寄嚟一個大盒子,裡面有好多嘢——呢個係畀你嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約瑟芬姑婆給我們寄來一個大盒子,裡面有好多東西——這是給你的。

passages.original: I’d have brought it over last night, but it didn’t come until after dark, and I never feel very comfortable coming through the Haunted Wood in the dark now.”
passages.vernacular: 我琴晚就想送過嚟,但佢天黑後才到,而我而家天黑後穿過鬧鬼林從來不太舒服。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我昨晚就想送過來,但它天黑後才到,而我現在天黑後穿過鬧鬼林從來不太舒服。」

passages.original: Anne opened the box and peeped in.
passages.vernacular: 安妮打開盒子,向裡面窺視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮打開盒子,向裡面窺視。

passages.original: First a card with “For the Anne-girl and Merry Christmas,” written on it; and then, a pair of the daintiest little kid slippers, with beaded toes and satin bows and glistening buckles.
passages.vernacular: 首先係一張卡片,上面寫住「畀安妮丫頭,聖誕快樂」;然後係一雙最精緻嘅小山羊皮拖鞋,鞋尖有珠飾,綴住緞帶蝴蝶結同閃亮嘅搭扣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先是一張卡片,上面寫著「給安妮丫頭,聖誕快樂」;然後是一雙最精緻的小山羊皮拖鞋,鞋尖有珠飾,綴著緞帶蝴蝶結和閃亮的搭扣。

passages.original: “Oh,” said Anne, “Diana, this is too much.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,」安妮講,「黛安娜,呢太過分喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,」安妮說,「黛安娜,這太過分了。

passages.original: I must be dreaming.”
passages.vernacular: 我一定係喺做夢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一定是在做夢。」

passages.original: “I call it providential,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我講呢個係天意,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說這是天意,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “You won’t have to borrow Ruby’s slippers now, and that’s a blessing, for they’re two sizes too big for you, and it would be awful to hear a fairy shuffling.
passages.vernacular: 「你而家唔使借露比嘅拖鞋喇,呢個係福氣,因為嗰雙大你兩碼,聽見仙女拖住腳走路多可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你現在不必借露比的拖鞋了,這是福氣,因為那雙大你兩碼,聽見仙女拖著腳走路多可怕。

passages.original: Josie Pye would be delighted.
passages.vernacular: 喬西·派伊會高興死嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西·派伊會高興死的。

passages.original: Mind you, Rob Wright went home with Gertie Pye from the practice night before last.
passages.vernacular: 你注意,前天晚上排練完,羅伯·賴特送格蒂·派伊回家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你注意,前天晚上排練完,羅伯·賴特送格蒂·派伊回家了。

passages.original: Did you ever hear anything equal to that?”
passages.vernacular: 你聽講過比呢更離奇嘅事嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你聽說過比這更離奇的事嗎?」

passages.original: All the Avonlea scholars were in a fever of excitement that day, for the hall had to be decorated and a last grand rehearsal held.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天阿文利所有學生都處喺狂熱嘅興奮中,因為大廳必須裝飾,仲要舉行最後一次盛大排練。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天阿文利所有學生都處在狂熱的興奮中,因為大廳必須裝飾,還要舉行最後一次盛大排練。

passages.original: The concert came off in the evening and was a pronounced success.
passages.vernacular: 音樂會喺晚上舉行,獲得咗公認嘅成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 音樂會在晚上舉行,獲得了公認的成功。

passages.original: The little hall was crowded; all the performers did excellently well, but Anne was the bright particular star of the occasion, as even envy, in the shape of Josie Pye, dared not deny.
passages.vernacular: 小禮堂擠滿咗人;所有表演者都出色極喇,但安妮係呢個場合最耀眼嘅明星,連喬西·派伊所代表嘅嫉妒都唔敢否認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小禮堂擠滿了人;所有表演者都出色極了,但安妮是這個場合最耀眼的明星,連喬西·派伊所代表的嫉妒也不敢否認。

passages.original: “Oh, hasn’t it been a brilliant evening?” sighed Anne, when it was all over and she and Diana were walking home together under a dark, starry sky.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,呢唔係個精彩嘅夜晚嗎?」安妮嘆道,一切結束後,佢同黛安娜一起走喺黑暗滿天星斗嘅天空下回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,這不是個精彩的夜晚嗎?」安妮嘆道,一切結束後,她和黛安娜一起走在黑暗滿天星斗的天空下回家。

passages.original: “Everything went off very well,” said Diana practically.
passages.vernacular: 「一切都好順利,」黛安娜務實地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一切都很順利,」黛安娜務實地說。

passages.original: “I guess we must have made as much as ten dollars.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我哋大概賺咗十塊錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我們大概賺了十塊錢。

passages.original: Mind you, Mr. Allan is going to send an account of it to the Charlottetown papers.”
passages.vernacular: 你注意,艾倫先生要把呢件事嘅報道寄畀夏洛特敦嘅報紙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你注意,艾倫先生要把這件事的報道寄給夏洛特敦的報紙。」

passages.original: “Oh, Diana, will we really see our names in print?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,黛安娜,我哋真嘅會喺報上睇到我哋嘅名字嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,黛安娜,我們真的會在報上看到我們的名字嗎?

passages.original: It makes me thrill to think of it.
passages.vernacular: 想到呢個我就激動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到這個我就激動。

passages.original: Your solo was perfectly elegant, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅獨唱特別高雅,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的獨唱特別高雅,黛安娜。

passages.original: I felt prouder than you did when it was encored.
passages.vernacular: 你被要求再唱一次嘅時候,我比你仲自豪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你被要求再唱一次的時候,我比你還自豪。

passages.original: I just said to myself, ‘It is my dear bosom friend who is so honored.’”
passages.vernacular: 我只係對自己講:『被咁樣榮耀嘅係我親愛嘅知心朋友。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是對自己說:『被這樣榮耀的是我親愛的知心朋友。』」

passages.original: “Well, your recitations just brought down the house, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你嘅朗誦真讓全場轟動,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你的朗誦真讓全場轟動,安妮。

passages.original: That sad one was simply splendid.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰首悲傷嘅簡直棒極喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那首悲傷的簡直棒極了。」

passages.original: “Oh, I was so nervous, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我太緊張喇,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我太緊張了,黛安娜。

passages.original: When Mr. Allan called out my name I really cannot tell how I ever got up on that platform.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫先生喊我嘅名字時,我真講不出我係點上嘅嗰個講臺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫先生喊我的名字時,我真說不出我是怎麼上的那個講臺。

passages.original: I felt as if a million eyes were looking at me and through me, and for one dreadful moment I was sure I couldn’t begin at all.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得有一百萬隻眼睛喺睇住我、睇穿我,有咁可怕嘅一刻,我確信我根本開不咗口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得有一百萬隻眼睛在看著我、看穿我,有那麼可怕的一刻,我確信我根本開不了口。

passages.original: Then I thought of my lovely puffed sleeves and took courage.
passages.vernacular: 然後我想起咗我可愛嘅泡泡袖,鼓起咗勇氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我想起了我可愛的泡泡袖,鼓起了勇氣。

passages.original: I knew that I must live up to those sleeves, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我必須配得上嗰兩隻袖子,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我必須配得上那兩隻袖子,黛安娜。

passages.original: So I started in, and my voice seemed to be coming from ever so far away.
passages.vernacular: 所以我開始喇,我嘅聲音似乎來自好遠好遠嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我開始了,我的聲音似乎來自很遠很遠的地方。

passages.original: I just felt like a parrot.
passages.vernacular: 我感覺自己像一隻鸚鵡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感覺自己像一隻鸚鵡。

passages.original: It’s providential that I practiced those recitations so often up in the garret, or I’d never have been able to get through.
passages.vernacular: 幸好我喺閣樓上咁多次練習呢啲朗誦,否則我永遠熬不過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸好我在閣樓上那麼多次練習這些朗誦,否則我永遠熬不過去。

passages.original: Did I groan all right?”
passages.vernacular: 我呻吟得對嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我呻吟得對嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, indeed, you groaned lovely,” assured Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「對,真嘅,你呻吟得好好聽,」黛安娜保證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,真的,你呻吟得很好聽,」黛安娜保證。

passages.original: “I saw old Mrs. Sloane wiping away tears when I sat down.
passages.vernacular: 「我坐下時睇見老斯隆太太喺擦眼淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我坐下時看見老斯隆太太在擦眼淚。

passages.original: It was splendid to think I had touched somebody’s heart.
passages.vernacular: 想到我感動咗某個人嘅心,真棒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到我感動了某個人的心,真棒。

passages.original: It’s so romantic to take part in a concert, isn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 參加音樂會好浪漫,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 參加音樂會很浪漫,是不是?

passages.original: Oh, it’s been a very memorable occasion indeed.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,呢確實係個好難忘嘅場合。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,這確實是個非常難忘的場合。」

passages.original: “Wasn’t the boys’ dialogue fine?” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「男孩哋嘅對話劇唔係好好嗎?」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「男孩們的對話劇不是很好嗎?」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “Gilbert Blythe was just splendid.
passages.vernacular: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯棒極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯棒極了。

passages.original: Anne, I do think it’s awful mean the way you treat Gil.
passages.vernacular: 安妮,我真覺得你對待吉爾嘅方式太卑鄙喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮,我真覺得你對待吉爾的方式太卑鄙了。

passages.original: Wait till I tell you.
passages.vernacular: 等我告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我告訴你。

passages.original: When you ran off the platform after the fairy dialogue one of your roses fell out of your hair.
passages.vernacular: 你演完仙女對話劇跑下講臺時,你頭髮上嘅一朵玫瑰掉咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你演完仙女對話劇跑下講臺時,你頭髮上的一朵玫瑰掉了下來。

passages.original: I saw Gil pick it up and put it in his breast pocket.
passages.vernacular: 我睇到吉爾把佢撿起嚟,放進咗佢嘅胸前口袋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看到吉爾把它撿起來,放進了他的胸前口袋。

passages.original: There now.
passages.vernacular: 就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這樣。

passages.original: You’re so romantic that I’m sure you ought to be pleased at that.”
passages.vernacular: 你咁浪漫,我肯定你該為此高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這麼浪漫,我肯定你該為此高興。」

passages.original: “It’s nothing to me what that person does,” said Anne loftily.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個人做乜嘢同我無關,」安妮傲慢地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那個人做什麼與我無關,」安妮傲慢地說。

passages.original: “I simply never waste a thought on him, Diana.”
passages.vernacular: 「我啲都不喺佢身上浪費心思,黛安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一點也不在他身上浪費心思,黛安娜。」

passages.original: That night Marilla and Matthew, who had been out to a concert for the first time in twenty years, sat for a while by the kitchen fire after Anne had gone to bed.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,二十年嚟頭一次出去聽音樂會嘅瑪麗拉同馬修,喺安妮上床後,喺廚房爐火邊坐咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,二十年來頭一次出去聽音樂會的瑪麗拉和馬修,在安妮上床後,在廚房爐火邊坐了一會兒。

passages.original: “Well now, I guess our Anne did as well as any of them,” said Matthew proudly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想我哋嘅安妮做得同佢哋任何人一樣好,」馬修自豪地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想我們的安妮做得和他們任何人一樣好,」馬修自豪地說。

passages.original: “Yes, she did,” admitted Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,佢做得好,」瑪麗拉承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,她做得好,」瑪麗拉承認。

passages.original: “She’s a bright child, Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係個聰明嘅細路,馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是個聰明的孩子,馬修。

passages.original: And she looked real nice too.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇上去都真漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看上去也真漂亮。

passages.original: I’ve been kind of opposed to this concert scheme, but I suppose there’s no real harm in it after all.
passages.vernacular: 我有點反對呢次音樂會計劃,但我想終究冇乜嘢真正嘅害處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有點反對這次音樂會計劃,但我想終究沒有什麼真正的害處。

passages.original: Anyhow, I was proud of Anne tonight, although I’m not going to tell her so.”
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,今晚我為安妮自豪,雖然我不打算告訴佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,今晚我為安妮自豪,雖然我不打算告訴她。」

passages.original: “Well now, I was proud of her and I did tell her so ‘fore she went upstairs,” said Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我為佢自豪,而且佢上樓前我告訴佢喇,」馬修講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我為她自豪,而且她上樓前我告訴她了,」馬修說。

passages.original: “We must see what we can do for her some of these days, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋得睇睇邊天能為佢做些乜嘢,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們得看看哪天能為她做些什麼,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I guess she’ll need something more than Avonlea school by and by.”
passages.vernacular: 我想佢遲早會需要比阿文利學校更多嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想她遲早會需要比阿文利學校更多的東西。」

passages.original: “There’s time enough to think of that,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「有嘅係時間想呢個,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有的是時間想這個,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “She’s only thirteen in March.
passages.vernacular: 「佢三月才十三歲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她三月才十三歲。

passages.original: Though tonight it struck me she was growing quite a big girl.
passages.vernacular: 不過今晚我感覺佢正變成大姑娘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過今晚我感覺她正變成大姑娘了。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde made that dress a mite too long, and it makes Anne look so tall.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太把嗰條裙子做得有點太長,讓安妮睇起嚟咁高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太把那條裙子做得有點太長,讓安妮看起來那麼高。

passages.original: She’s quick to learn and I guess the best thing we can do for her will be to send her to Queen’s after a spell.
passages.vernacular: 佢學得快,我想我哋能為佢做嘅最好嘅事,就係過一陣子送佢去女王學院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她學得快,我想我們能為她做的最好的事,就是過一陣子送她去女王學院。

passages.original: But nothing need be said about that for a year or two yet.”
passages.vernacular: 但呢件事一兩年內唔使提。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這件事一兩年內不必提。」

passages.original: “Well now, it’ll do no harm to be thinking it over off and on,” said Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,時不時地考慮一下冇壞處,」馬修講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,時不時地考慮一下沒有壞處,」馬修說。

passages.original: “Things like that are all the better for lots of thinking over.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢類事多想想總是更好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這類事多想想總是更好。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXVI The Story Club Is Formed 第二十六章:故事俱樂部成立

passages.original: CH JUNIOR Avonlea found it hard to settle down to humdrum existence again.
passages.vernacular: 阿文利嘅小學生哋發現好難重新適應平淡嘅生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利的小學生們發現很難重新適應平淡的生活。

passages.original: To Anne in particular things seemed fearfully flat, stale, and unprofitable after the goblet of excitement she had been sipping for weeks.
passages.vernacular: 尤其係對安妮來講,喺啜飲咗幾個星期嘅興奮之杯後,一切似乎可怕地乏味、陳腐、無益。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尤其是對安妮來說,在啜飲了幾個星期的興奮之杯後,一切似乎可怕地乏味、陳腐、無益。

passages.original: Could she go back to the former quiet pleasures of those faraway days before the concert?
passages.vernacular: 佢能回到音樂會之前嗰啲遙遠日子裡以前嗰種安靜嘅樂趣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她能回到音樂會之前那些遙遠日子裡以前那種安靜的樂趣嗎?

passages.original: At first, as she told Diana, she did not really think she could.
passages.vernacular: 起初,正如佢對黛安娜講嘅,佢真不認為自己能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初,正如她對黛安娜說的,她真不認為自己能。

passages.original: “I’m positively certain, Diana, that life can never be quite the same again as it was in those olden days,” she said mournfully, as if referring to a period of at least fifty years back.
passages.vernacular: 「我肯定地確信,黛安娜,生活再都唔可能像從前嗰啲古老嘅日子喇,」佢悲傷地講,好像喺談論至少五十年前嘅一個時代。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我肯定地確信,黛安娜,生活再也不可能像從前那些古老的日子了,」她悲傷地說,好像在談論至少五十年前的一個時代。

passages.original: “Perhaps after a while I’ll get used to it, but I’m afraid concerts spoil people for everyday life.
passages.vernacular: 「或者過一陣子我會習慣,但恐怕音樂會讓人無法再過日常生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許過一陣子我會習慣,但恐怕音樂會讓人無法再過日常生活。

passages.original: I suppose that is why Marilla disapproves of them.
passages.vernacular: 我想呢個就係瑪麗拉不贊成佢哋嘅原因。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想這就是瑪麗拉不贊成它們的原因。

passages.original: Marilla is such a sensible woman.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉係個咁明智嘅女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉是個那麼明智的女人。

passages.original: It must be a great deal better to be sensible; but still, I don’t believe I’d really want to be a sensible person, because they are so unromantic.
passages.vernacular: 明智一定好得多;但我定係不相信我真想做一個明智嘅人,因為佢哋太冇浪漫情調喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明智一定好得多;但我還是不相信我真想做一個明智的人,因為他們太沒有浪漫情調了。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says there is no danger of my ever being one, but you can never tell.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講我永遠唔可能成為明智嘅人,但你永遠講不準。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說我永遠不可能成為明智的人,但你永遠說不準。

passages.original: I feel just now that I may grow up to be sensible yet.
passages.vernacular: 我而家覺得我長大後仍可能變得明智。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在覺得我長大後仍可能變得明智。

passages.original: But perhaps that is only because I’m tired.
passages.vernacular: 但或者只係因為我累喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但也許只是因為我累了。

passages.original: I simply couldn’t sleep last night for ever so long.
passages.vernacular: 琴晚我好久好久都瞓不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨晚我很久很久都睡不著。

passages.original: I just lay awake and imagined the concert over and over again.
passages.vernacular: 我只係醒住躺喺嗰兒,一遍又一遍地想像音樂會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是醒著躺在那兒,一遍又一遍地想像音樂會。

passages.original: That’s one splendid thing about such affairs--it’s so lovely to look back to them.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係呢類事情嘅一個棒處——回顧起嚟太愉快喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是這類事情的一個棒處——回顧起來太愉快了。」

passages.original: Eventually, however, Avonlea school slipped back into its old groove and took up its old interests.
passages.vernacular: 然而,最終,阿文利學校又滑回咗老軌道,重新有咗舊嘅興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,最終,阿文利學校又滑回了老軌道,重新有了舊的興趣。

passages.original: To be sure, the concert left traces.
passages.vernacular: 誠然,音樂會留下咗痕跡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠然,音樂會留下了痕跡。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis and Emma White, who had quarreled over a point of precedence in their platform seats, no longer sat at the same desk, and a promising friendship of three years was broken up.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯同艾瑪·懷特,為喺講臺上座位嘅先後次序爭吵過,唔再坐同一張桌子,一段持續三年嘅、好有前途嘅友誼破裂喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯和艾瑪·懷特,為在講臺上座位的先後次序爭吵過,不再坐同一張桌子,一段持續三年的、很有前途的友誼破裂了。

passages.original: Josie Pye and Julia Bell did not “speak” for three months, because Josie Pye had told Bessie Wright that Julia Bell’s bow when she got up to recite made her think of a chicken jerking its head, and Bessie told Julia.
passages.vernacular: 喬西·派伊同朱莉婭·貝爾三個月不「講話」,因為喬西·派伊對貝西·賴特講,朱莉婭·貝爾起身朗誦時嘅鞠躬讓佢想起一隻雞甩住頭,貝西告訴咗朱莉婭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西·派伊和朱莉婭·貝爾三個月不「說話」,因為喬西·派伊對貝西·賴特說,朱莉婭·貝爾起身朗誦時的鞠躬讓她想起一隻雞甩著頭,貝西告訴了朱莉婭。

passages.original: None of the Sloanes would have any dealings with the Bells, because the Bells had declared that the Sloanes had too much to do in the program, and the Sloanes had retorted that the Bells were not capable of doing the little they had to do properly.
passages.vernacular: 斯隆家嘅人都唔肯同貝爾家嘅人打交道,因為貝爾家宣稱斯隆家喺節目單里戲份太多,而斯隆家反駁講貝爾家嘅人連自己嗰點戲份都做不好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯隆家的人都不肯和貝爾家的人打交道,因為貝爾家宣稱斯隆家在節目單里戲份太多,而斯隆家反駁說貝爾家的人連自己那點戲份都做不好。

passages.original: Finally, Charlie Sloane fought Moody Spurgeon MacPherson, because Moody Spurgeon had said that Anne Shirley put on airs about her recitations, and Moody Spurgeon was “licked”; consequently Moody Spurgeon’s sister, Ella May, would not “speak” to Anne Shirley all the rest of the winter.
passages.vernacular: 最後,查理·斯隆同穆迪·斯珀吉翁·麥克弗森打咗一架,因為穆迪·斯珀吉翁講安妮·雪莉朗誦時裝腔作勢,結果穆迪·斯珀吉翁被「揍」喇;因此穆迪·斯珀吉翁嘅姐姐艾拉·梅喺整個冬天都不跟安妮·雪莉「講話」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後,查理·斯隆和穆迪·斯珀吉翁·麥克弗森打了一架,因為穆迪·斯珀吉翁說安妮·雪莉朗誦時裝腔作勢,結果穆迪·斯珀吉翁被「揍」了;因此穆迪·斯珀吉翁的姐姐艾拉·梅在整個冬天都不跟安妮·雪莉「說話」。

passages.original: With the exception of these trifling frictions, work in Miss Stacy’s little kingdom went on with regularity and smoothness.
passages.vernacular: 除咗呢啲細小嘅摩擦,斯泰西小姐小王國里嘅工作有規律地、順利地進行住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了這些細小的摩擦,斯泰西小姐小王國里的工作有規律地、順利地進行著。

passages.original: The winter weeks slipped by.
passages.vernacular: 冬天嘅幾個星期滑過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冬天的幾個星期滑過。

passages.original: It was an unusually mild winter, with so little snow that Anne and Diana could go to school nearly every day by way of the Birch Path.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個異乎尋常溫和嘅冬天,雪咁少,安妮同黛安娜幾乎每天都能走白樺小徑去學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個異乎尋常溫和的冬天,雪那麼少,安妮和黛安娜幾乎每天都能走白樺小徑去學校。

passages.original: On Anne’s birthday they were tripping lightly down it, keeping eyes and ears alert amid all their chatter, for Miss Stacy had told them that they must soon write a composition on “A Winter’s Walk in the Woods,” and it behooved them to be observant.
passages.vernacular: 安妮生日嗰天,佢哋輕快地沿住佢走下去,喺所有嘅閒聊中保持眼耳警覺,因為斯泰西小姐告訴佢哋,佢哋好快要寫一篇關於《冬日林中散步》嘅作文,佢哋必須善於觀察。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮生日那天,她們輕快地沿著它走下去,在所有的閒聊中保持眼耳警覺,因為斯泰西小姐告訴她們,她們很快要寫一篇關於《冬日林中散步》的作文,她們必須善於觀察。

passages.original: “Just think, Diana, I’m thirteen years old today,” remarked Anne in an awed voice.
passages.vernacular: 「想想,黛安娜,我今日十三歲喇,」安妮用敬畏嘅聲音講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「想想,黛安娜,我今天十三歲了,」安妮用敬畏的聲音說。

passages.original: “I can scarcely realize that I’m in my teens.
passages.vernacular: 「我幾乎唔能夠意識到我進入十幾歲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我幾乎不能意識到我進入十幾歲了。

passages.original: When I woke this morning it seemed to me that everything must be different.
passages.vernacular: 今日早晨醒嚟時,我覺得一切一定不同喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天早晨醒來時,我覺得一切一定不同了。

passages.original: You’ve been thirteen for a month, so I suppose it doesn’t seem such a novelty to you as it does to me.
passages.vernacular: 你已經十三歲一個月喇,所以我想對你來講冇對我咁新鮮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你已經十三歲一個月了,所以我想對你來說沒有對我這麼新鮮。

passages.original: It makes life seem so much more interesting.
passages.vernacular: 呢讓生活顯得有趣得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這讓生活顯得有趣得多。

passages.original: In two more years I’ll be really grown up.
passages.vernacular: 再過兩年我就真正長大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再過兩年我就真正長大了。

passages.original: It’s a great comfort to think that I’ll be able to use big words then without being laughed at.”
passages.vernacular: 想到嗰時我可以用大詞而唔會被人嘲笑,真係個好大嘅安慰。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到那時我可以用大詞而不會被人嘲笑,真是個很大的安慰。」

passages.original: “Ruby Gillis says she means to have a beau as soon as she’s fifteen,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「露比·吉利斯講佢打算一滿十五歲就有個情郎,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「露比·吉利斯說她打算一滿十五歲就有個情郎,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “Ruby Gillis thinks of nothing but beaus,” said Anne disdainfully.
passages.vernacular: 「露比·吉利斯滿腦子只想住情郎,」安妮不屑地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「露比·吉利斯滿腦子只想著情郎,」安妮不屑地說。

passages.original: “She’s actually delighted when anyone writes her name up in a take-notice for all she pretends to be so mad.
passages.vernacular: 「別人把佢嘅名字寫進『請注意』時,佢其實好高興,儘管佢假裝咁生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別人把她的名字寫進『請注意』時,她其實很高興,儘管她假裝那麼生氣。

passages.original: But I’m afraid that is an uncharitable speech.
passages.vernacular: 但我怕呢話不仁慈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我怕這話不仁慈。

passages.original: Mrs. Allan says we should never make uncharitable speeches; but they do slip out so often before you think, don’t they?
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太講我哋永遠唔應該該講不仁慈嘅話;但佢哋總是喺你仲冇想到之前就溜出嚟喇,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太說我們永遠不應該說不仁慈的話;但它們總是在你還沒想到之前就溜出來了,是不是?

passages.original: I simply can’t talk about Josie Pye without making an uncharitable speech, so I never mention her at all.
passages.vernacular: 我簡直唔能夠談論喬西·派伊而不講不仁慈嘅話,所以我根本不提佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我簡直不能談論喬西·派伊而不說不仁慈的話,所以我根本不提她。

passages.original: You may have noticed that.
passages.vernacular: 你可能已經注意到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可能已經注意到了。

passages.original: I’m trying to be as much like Mrs. Allan as I possibly can, for I think she’s perfect.
passages.vernacular: 我喺儘量地學艾倫太太,因為我覺得佢完美無缺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在儘量地學艾倫太太,因為我覺得她完美無缺。

passages.original: Mr. Allan thinks so too.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫先生都咁想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫先生也這麼想。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says he just worships the ground she treads on and she doesn’t really think it right for a minister to set his affections so much on a mortal being.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講佢簡直崇拜佢踩過嘅地面,佢真不覺得牧師把咁多感情放喺一個凡人身上係對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說他簡直崇拜她踩過的地面,她真不覺得牧師把這麼多感情放在一個凡人身上是對的。

passages.original: But then, Diana, even ministers are human and have their besetting sins just like everybody else.
passages.vernacular: 但係,黛安娜,牧師都係人,都有像每個人一樣嘅纏身之罪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,黛安娜,牧師也是人,也有像每個人一樣的纏身之罪。

passages.original: I had such an interesting talk with Mrs. Allan about besetting sins last Sunday afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 上個星期天下午我同艾倫太太就纏身之罪進行咗一次好有趣嘅談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上個星期天下午我和艾倫太太就纏身之罪進行了一次很有趣的談話。

passages.original: There are just a few things it’s proper to talk about on Sundays and that is one of them.
passages.vernacular: 星期天只有少數幾件事係適合談論嘅,呢個係其中之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期天只有少數幾件事是適合談論的,這是其中之一。

passages.original: My besetting sin is imagining too much and forgetting my duties.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅纏身之罪係想像太多同忘記我嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的纏身之罪是想像太多和忘記我的責任。

passages.original: I’m striving very hard to overcome it and now that I’m really thirteen perhaps I’ll get on better.”
passages.vernacular: 我正在好努力地克服佢,而家我真嘅十三歲喇,或者我會做得更好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我正在非常努力地克服它,現在我真的十三歲了,也許我會做得更好。」

passages.original: “In four more years we’ll be able to put our hair up,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「再過四年我哋就能把頭髮盤起嚟喇,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再過四年我們就能把頭髮盤起來了,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “Alice Bell is only sixteen and she is wearing hers up, but I think that’s ridiculous.
passages.vernacular: 「艾麗斯·貝爾才十六歲就盤起咗頭髮,但我覺得嗰好可笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「艾麗斯·貝爾才十六歲就盤起了頭髮,但我覺得那很可笑。

passages.original: I shall wait until I’m seventeen.”
passages.vernacular: 我要等到十七歲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要等到十七歲。」

passages.original: “If I had Alice Bell’s crooked nose,” said Anne decidedly, “I wouldn’t--but there!
passages.vernacular: 「如果我有艾麗斯·貝爾嗰彎彎嘅鼻子,」安妮堅決地講,「我唔會——不過!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我有艾麗斯·貝爾那彎彎的鼻子,」安妮堅決地說,「我不會——不過!

passages.original: I won’t say what I was going to because it was extremely uncharitable.
passages.vernacular: 我不講我原本要講嘅,因為嗰極不仁慈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不說我原本要說的,因為那極不仁慈。

passages.original: Besides, I was comparing it with my own nose and that’s vanity.
passages.vernacular: 再講,我係喺攞佢跟我自己嘅鼻子比較,嗰個係虛榮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再說,我是在拿它跟我自己的鼻子比較,那是虛榮。

passages.original: I’m afraid I think too much about my nose ever since I heard that compliment about it long ago.
passages.vernacular: 自從好久以前聽到對我鼻子嘅恭維,我恐怕太常想我嘅鼻子喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從很久以前聽到對我鼻子的恭維,我恐怕太常想我的鼻子了。

passages.original: It really is a great comfort to me.
passages.vernacular: 佢真嘅對我係一個好大嘅安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它真的對我是一個很大的安慰。

passages.original: Oh, Diana, look, there’s a rabbit.
passages.vernacular: 哦,黛安娜,睇,有一隻兔子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,黛安娜,看,有一隻兔子。

passages.original: That’s something to remember for our woods composition.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係可以記住寫我哋樹林作文嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是可以記住寫我們樹林作文的東西。

passages.original: I really think the woods are just as lovely in winter as in summer.
passages.vernacular: 我真覺得樹林喺冬天同夏天一樣可愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真覺得樹林在冬天和夏天一樣可愛。

passages.original: They’re so white and still, as if they were asleep and dreaming pretty dreams.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋咁白、咁靜,好像瞓住喇,做住美麗嘅夢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們那麼白、那麼靜,好像睡著了,做著美麗的夢。」

passages.original: “I won’t mind writing that composition when its time comes,” sighed Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「到時候寫嗰篇作文我唔會介意,」黛安娜嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「到時候寫那篇作文我不會介意,」黛安娜嘆道。

passages.original: “I can manage to write about the woods, but the one we’re to hand in Monday is terrible.
passages.vernacular: 「我能設法寫樹林,但我哋下週一要交嘅嗰篇太可怕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我能設法寫樹林,但我們下週一要交的那篇太可怕了。

passages.original: The idea of Miss Stacy telling us to write a story out of our own heads!”
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐居然叫我哋從自己腦子裡編一個故事寫出嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐居然叫我們從自己腦子裡編一個故事寫出來!」

passages.original: “Why, it’s as easy as wink,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,呢跟眨眼一樣容易,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,這跟眨眼一樣容易,」安妮說。

passages.original: “It’s easy for you because you have an imagination,” retorted Diana, “but what would you do if you had been born without one?
passages.vernacular: 「對你容易,因為你有想像力,」黛安娜反駁,「但如果你生下嚟冇想像力,你點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對你容易,因為你有想像力,」黛安娜反駁,「但如果你生下來沒有想像力,你怎麼辦?

passages.original: I suppose you have your composition all done?”
passages.vernacular: 我想你嘅作文都寫完咗吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你的作文都寫完了吧?」

passages.original: Anne nodded, trying hard not to look virtuously complacent and failing miserably.
passages.vernacular: 安妮點點頭,努力不顯出道貌岸然嘅自滿,卻慘敗喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮點點頭,努力不顯出道貌岸然的自滿,卻慘敗了。

passages.original: “I wrote it last Monday evening.
passages.vernacular: 「我上週一晚上寫嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我上週一晚上寫的。

passages.original: It’s called ‘The Jealous Rival; or In Death Not Divided.’
passages.vernacular: 佢叫《嫉妒嘅情敵;或,死亦不分離》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它叫《嫉妒的情敵;或,死亦不分離》。

passages.original: I read it to Marilla and she said it was stuff and nonsense.
passages.vernacular: 我讀畀瑪麗拉聽,佢講係胡講八道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讀給瑪麗拉聽,她說是胡說八道。

passages.original: Then I read it to Matthew and he said it was fine.
passages.vernacular: 然後我讀畀馬修聽,佢講好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我讀給馬修聽,他說很好。

passages.original: That is the kind of critic I like.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係我鍾意嘅嗰種批評家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是我喜歡的那種批評家。

passages.original: It’s a sad, sweet story.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個悲傷、甜蜜嘅故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個悲傷、甜蜜的故事。

passages.original: I just cried like a child while I was writing it.
passages.vernacular: 我寫嘅時候哭得像個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寫的時候哭得像個孩子。

passages.original: It’s about two beautiful maidens called Cordelia Montmorency and Geraldine Seymour who lived in the same village and were devotedly attached to each other.
passages.vernacular: 故事講嘅係兩個美麗嘅少女,叫科黛莉亞·蒙莫朗西同傑拉爾丁·西摩,佢哋住喺同一個村子,彼此深深依戀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 故事講的是兩個美麗的少女,叫科黛莉亞·蒙莫朗西和傑拉爾丁·西摩,她們住在同一個村子,彼此深深依戀。

passages.original: Cordelia was a regal brunette with a coronet of midnight hair and duskly flashing eyes.
passages.vernacular: 科黛莉亞係個高貴嘅黑髮女子,頭戴一圈午夜般嘅烏髮,眼睛閃住幽暗嘅光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 科黛莉亞是個高貴的黑髮女子,頭戴一圈午夜般的烏髮,眼睛閃著幽暗的光。

passages.original: Geraldine was a queenly blonde with hair like spun gold and velvety purple eyes.”
passages.vernacular: 傑拉爾丁係個女王般嘅金髮女子,頭髮像紡出嘅金絲,眼睛係天鵝絨般嘅紫色。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑拉爾丁是個女王般的金髮女子,頭髮像紡出的金絲,眼睛是天鵝絨般的紫色。」

passages.original: “I never saw anybody with purple eyes,” said Diana dubiously.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇見過邊個有紫色眼睛,」黛安娜懷疑地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒見過誰有紫色眼睛,」黛安娜懷疑地說。

passages.original: “Neither did I. I just imagined them.
passages.vernacular: 「我都冇。我只係想像出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也沒有。我只是想像出來的。

passages.original: I wanted something out of the common.
passages.vernacular: 我想要點不平常嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想要點不平常的東西。

passages.original: Geraldine had an alabaster brow too.
passages.vernacular: 傑拉爾丁仲有雪花石膏般嘅額頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑拉爾丁還有雪花石膏般的額頭。

passages.original: I’ve found out what an alabaster brow is.
passages.vernacular: 我已經弄明白咗乜嘢係雪花石膏般嘅額頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經弄明白了什麼是雪花石膏般的額頭。

passages.original: That is one of the advantages of being thirteen.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係十三歲嘅好處之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是十三歲的好處之一。

passages.original: You know so much more than you did when you were only twelve.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道嘅比十二歲時多得多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道的比十二歲時多得多。」

passages.original: “Well, what became of Cordelia and Geraldine?” asked Diana, who was beginning to feel rather interested in their fate.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,科黛莉亞同傑拉爾丁後來點樣喇?」黛安娜問,佢開始對佢哋嘅命運相當感興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,科黛莉亞和傑拉爾丁後來怎麼樣了?」黛安娜問,她開始對她們的命運相當感興趣。

passages.original: “They grew in beauty side by side until they were sixteen.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋肩並肩地美麗地成長,直到十六歲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她們肩並肩地美麗地成長,直到十六歲。

passages.original: Then Bertram DeVere came to their native village and fell in love with the fair Geraldine.
passages.vernacular: 然後伯特倫·德維爾嚟到佢哋嘅家鄉村子,愛上咗美麗嘅傑拉爾丁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後伯特倫·德維爾來到她們的家鄉村子,愛上了美麗的傑拉爾丁。

passages.original: He saved her life when her horse ran away with her in a carriage, and she fainted in his arms and he carried her home three miles; because, you understand, the carriage was all smashed up.
passages.vernacular: 佢乘馬車時馬狂奔,佢救咗佢嘅命,佢喺佢懷裡暈咗過去,佢把佢抱回家走咗三英里;因為,你懂嘅,馬車撞得粉碎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她乘馬車時馬狂奔,他救了她的命,她在他懷裡暈了過去,他把她抱回家走了三英里;因為,你懂的,馬車撞得粉碎。

passages.original: I found it rather hard to imagine the proposal because I had no experience to go by.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得好難想像求婚嘅情景,因為我冇經驗可依。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得很難想像求婚的情景,因為我沒有經驗可依。

passages.original: I asked Ruby Gillis if she knew anything about how men proposed because I thought she’d likely be an authority on the subject, having so many sisters married.
passages.vernacular: 我問露比·吉利斯佢知唔知道男人係點求婚嘅,因為我想佢有咁多姐姐都結咗婚,大概係呢方面嘅權威。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我問露比·吉利斯她知不知道男人是怎麼求婚的,因為我想她有那麼多姐姐都結了婚,大概是這方面的權威。

passages.original: Ruby told me she was hid in the hall pantry when Malcolm Andres proposed to her sister Susan.
passages.vernacular: 露比告訴我,馬爾科姆·安德烈斯向佢姐姐蘇珊求婚時,佢就藏喺門廳嘅食品櫃裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比告訴我,馬爾科姆·安德烈斯向她姐姐蘇珊求婚時,她就藏在門廳的食品櫃裡。

passages.original: She said Malcolm told Susan that his dad had given him the farm in his own name and then said, ‘What do you say, darling pet, if we get hitched this fall?’
passages.vernacular: 佢講馬爾科姆告訴蘇珊,佢爸爸已經把農場以佢自己嘅名義畀咗佢,然後講:『你點講,親愛嘅寶貝,我哋今年秋天結婚好不好?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說馬爾科姆告訴蘇珊,他爸爸已經把農場以他自己的名義給了他,然後說:『你怎麼說,親愛的寶貝,我們今年秋天結婚好不好?』

passages.original: And Susan said, ‘Yes--no--I don’t know--let me see’--and there they were, engaged as quick as that.
passages.vernacular: 蘇珊講:『好——不——我唔知道——讓我想想』——然後佢哋就咁快地訂婚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蘇珊說:『好——不——我不知道——讓我想想』——然後他們就那麼快地訂婚了。

passages.original: But I didn’t think that sort of a proposal was a very romantic one, so in the end I had to imagine it out as well as I could.
passages.vernacular: 但我不覺得嗰種求婚好浪漫,所以最後我只好盡量把佢想像出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不覺得那種求婚很浪漫,所以最後我只好盡量把它想像出來。

passages.original: I made it very flowery and poetical and Bertram went on his knees, although Ruby Gillis says it isn’t done nowadays.
passages.vernacular: 我把佢寫得好華麗而富有詩意,伯特倫仲跪下喇,雖然露比·吉利斯講而家不興呢個喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把它寫得非常華麗而富有詩意,伯特倫還跪下了,雖然露比·吉利斯說現在不興這個了。

passages.original: Geraldine accepted him in a speech a page long.
passages.vernacular: 傑拉爾丁以一頁長嘅一篇演講接受咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑拉爾丁以一頁長的一篇演說接受了他。

passages.original: I can tell you I took a lot of trouble with that speech.
passages.vernacular: 我可以告訴您,我喺嗰篇演講上費咗好多功夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以告訴您,我在那篇演說上費了很多功夫。

passages.original: I rewrote it five times and I look upon it as my masterpiece.
passages.vernacular: 我重寫咗五遍,把佢睇作我嘅傑作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我重寫了五遍,把它看作我的傑作。

passages.original: Bertram gave her a diamond ring and a ruby necklace and told her they would go to Europe for a wedding tour, for he was immensely wealthy.
passages.vernacular: 伯特倫畀咗佢一枚鑽石戒指同一條紅寶石項鍊,告訴佢佢哋要去歐洲度蜜月,因為佢極其富有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伯特倫給了她一枚鑽石戒指和一條紅寶石項鍊,告訴她他們要去歐洲度蜜月,因為他極其富有。

passages.original: But then, alas, shadows began to darken over their path.
passages.vernacular: 但接住,唉,陰影開始籠罩佢哋嘅道路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但接著,唉,陰影開始籠罩他們的道路。

passages.original: Cordelia was secretly in love with Bertram herself and when Geraldine told her about the engagement she was simply furious, especially when she saw the necklace and the diamond ring.
passages.vernacular: 科黛莉亞自己暗暗愛住伯特倫,傑拉爾丁告訴佢訂婚嘅事時,佢簡直氣瘋喇,特別係睇到項鍊同鑽石戒指嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 科黛莉亞自己暗暗愛著伯特倫,傑拉爾丁告訴她訂婚的事時,她簡直氣瘋了,特別是看到項鍊和鑽石戒指的時候。

passages.original: All her affection for Geraldine turned to bitter hate and she vowed that she should never marry Bertram.
passages.vernacular: 佢對傑拉爾丁所有嘅感情都變成咗苦澀嘅恨,佢發誓傑拉爾丁決唔能夠嫁畀伯特倫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她對傑拉爾丁所有的感情都變成了苦澀的恨,她發誓傑拉爾丁決不能嫁給伯特倫。

passages.original: But she pretended to be Geraldine’s friend the same as ever.
passages.vernacular: 但佢假裝仍係傑拉爾丁嘅朋友,同往常一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她假裝仍是傑拉爾丁的朋友,和往常一樣。

passages.original: One evening they were standing on the bridge over a rushing turbulent stream and Cordelia, thinking they were alone, pushed Geraldine over the brink with a wild, mocking, ‘Ha, ha, ha.’
passages.vernacular: 一天晚上,佢哋站喺一條湍急洶湧嘅溪流上嘅橋上,科黛莉亞以為只有佢哋兩個人,就用狂野嘅、嘲弄嘅『哈,哈,哈』把傑拉爾丁推下咗橋邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天晚上,她們站在一條湍急洶湧的溪流上的橋上,科黛莉亞以為只有她們兩個人,就用狂野的、嘲弄的『哈,哈,哈』把傑拉爾丁推下了橋邊。

passages.original: But Bertram saw it all and he at once plunged into the current, exclaiming, ‘I will save thee, my peerless Geraldine.’
passages.vernacular: 但伯特倫睇到咗一切,佢即刻跳進急流,喊道:『我嚟救你,我無同倫比嘅傑拉爾丁。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但伯特倫看到了一切,他立刻跳進急流,喊道:『我來救你,我無與倫比的傑拉爾丁。』

passages.original: But alas, he had forgotten he couldn’t swim, and they were both drowned, clasped in each other’s arms.
passages.vernacular: 但係,唉,佢忘咗佢唔會游泳,兩人都被淹死喇,緊緊抱喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,唉,他忘了他不會游泳,兩人都被淹死了,緊緊抱在一起。

passages.original: Their bodies were washed ashore soon afterwards.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋嘅屍體被沖上岸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他們的屍體被沖上岸。

passages.original: They were buried in the one grave and their funeral was most imposing, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋被葬喺同一座墳墓裡,佢哋嘅葬禮極為隆重,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們被葬在同一座墳墓裡,他們的葬禮極為隆重,黛安娜。

passages.original: It’s so much more romantic to end a story up with a funeral than a wedding.
passages.vernacular: 用葬禮而唔係婚禮嚟結束一個故事浪漫得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用葬禮而不是婚禮來結束一個故事浪漫得多。

passages.original: As for Cordelia, she went insane with remorse and was shut up in a lunatic asylum.
passages.vernacular: 至於科黛莉亞,佢因悔恨而發咗瘋,被關進咗瘋人院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於科黛莉亞,她因悔恨而發了瘋,被關進了瘋人院。

passages.original: I thought that was a poetical retribution for her crime.”
passages.vernacular: 我覺得呢個係對佢罪行嘅富有詩意嘅報應。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得這是對她罪行的富有詩意的報應。」

passages.original: “How perfectly lovely!” sighed Diana, who belonged to Matthew’s school of critics.
passages.vernacular: 「太可愛喇!」黛安娜嘆道,佢屬於馬修嗰一派嘅批評家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太可愛了!」黛安娜嘆道,她屬於馬修那一派的批評家。

passages.original: “I don’t see how you can make up such thrilling things out of your own head, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白你點能從自己嘅腦子里編出咁驚險嘅嘢,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白你怎麼能從自己的腦子里編出這麼驚險的東西,安妮。

passages.original: I wish my imagination was as good as yours.”
passages.vernacular: 我真希望我嘅想像力同你嘅一樣好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望我的想像力和你的一樣好。」

passages.original: “It would be if you’d only cultivate it,” said Anne cheeringly.
passages.vernacular: 「只要你肯培養佢,就會嘅,」安妮鼓勵地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只要你肯培養它,就會的,」安妮鼓勵地說。

passages.original: “I’ve just thought of a plan, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我剛想到一個計劃,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我剛想到一個計劃,黛安娜。

passages.original: Let you and me have a story club all our own and write stories for practice.
passages.vernacular: 讓你同我有一個我哋自己嘅故事俱樂部,寫故事練習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓你和我有一個我們自己的故事俱樂部,寫故事練習。

passages.original: I’ll help you along until you can do them by yourself.
passages.vernacular: 我會幫你,直到你能自己寫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會幫你,直到你能自己寫。

passages.original: You ought to cultivate your imagination, you know.
passages.vernacular: 你應該培養你嘅想像力,您知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你應該培養你的想像力,您知道。

passages.original: Miss Stacy says so.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐這麼說。

passages.original: Only we must take the right way.
passages.vernacular: 只係我哋必須走正確嘅路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是我們必須走正確的路。

passages.original: I told her about the Haunted Wood, but she said we went the wrong way about it in that.”
passages.vernacular: 我跟佢講咗鬧鬼林嘅事,但佢講我哋喺嗰件事上走錯咗路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跟她說了鬧鬼林的事,但她說我們在那件事上走錯了路。」

passages.original: This was how the story club came into existence.
passages.vernacular: 故事俱樂部就咁樣誕生喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 故事俱樂部就這樣誕生了。

passages.original: It was limited to Diana and Anne at first, but soon it was extended to include Jane Andrews and Ruby Gillis and one or two others who felt that their imaginations needed cultivating.
passages.vernacular: 起初佢只限於黛安娜同安妮,但好快擴大到包括簡·安德魯斯同露比·吉利斯,以及一兩位覺得自己想像力需要培養嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初它只限於黛安娜和安妮,但很快擴大到包括簡·安德魯斯和露比·吉利斯,以及一兩位覺得自己想像力需要培養的人。

passages.original: No boys were allowed in it--although Ruby Gillis opined that their admission would make it more exciting--and each member had to produce one story a week.
passages.vernacular: 不許男孩加入——雖然露比·吉利斯認為佢哋嘅加入會更刺激——每個成員每星期必須交一篇故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不許男孩加入——雖然露比·吉利斯認為他們的加入會更刺激——每個成員每星期必須交一篇故事。

passages.original: “It’s extremely interesting,” Anne told Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「特別有意思,」安妮對瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「特別有意思,」安妮對瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “Each girl has to read her story out loud and then we talk it over.
passages.vernacular: 「每個女孩必須大聲讀自己嘅故事,然後我哋討論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「每個女孩必須大聲讀自己的故事,然後我們討論。

passages.original: We are going to keep them all sacredly and have them to read to our descendants.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要把佢哋全部神聖地保存起嚟,讀畀我哋嘅後代聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要把它們全部神聖地保存起來,讀給我們的後代聽。

passages.original: We each write under a nom-de-plume.
passages.vernacular: 我哋每個人都用筆名寫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們每個人都用筆名寫。

passages.original: Mine is Rosamond Montmorency.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅係羅莎蒙德·蒙莫朗西。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的是羅莎蒙德·蒙莫朗西。

passages.original: All the girls do pretty well.
passages.vernacular: 所有女孩都做得相當好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有女孩都做得相當好。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis is rather sentimental.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯相當多愁善感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯相當多愁善感。

passages.original: She puts too much lovemaking into her stories and you know too much is worse than too little.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅故事里談情講愛太多,您知道太多比太少更糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的故事里談情說愛太多,您知道太多比太少更糟。

passages.original: Jane never puts any because she says it makes her feel so silly when she had to read it out loud.
passages.vernacular: 簡從來不寫,因為佢講大聲讀出嚟時讓佢覺得太傻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡從來不寫,因為她說大聲讀出來時讓她覺得太傻。

passages.original: Jane’s stories are extremely sensible.
passages.vernacular: 簡嘅故事極其明智。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡的故事極其明智。

passages.original: Then Diana puts too many murders into hers.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜嘅故事里謀殺太多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜的故事里謀殺太多。

passages.original: She says most of the time she doesn’t know what to do with the people so she kills them off to get rid of them.
passages.vernacular: 佢講大多數時候佢唔知道該攞嗰啲人點算,所以就把佢哋殺掉擺脫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說大多數時候她不知道該拿那些人怎麼辦,所以就把他們殺掉擺脫。

passages.original: I mostly always have to tell them what to write about, but that isn’t hard for I’ve millions of ideas.”
passages.vernacular: 我幾乎總是得告訴佢哋寫乜嘢,但呢不難,因為我有上百萬個點子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我幾乎總是得告訴她們寫什麼,但這不難,因為我有上百萬個點子。」

passages.original: “I think this story-writing business is the foolishest yet,” scoffed Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得呢寫故事嘅事係最愚蠢嘅,」瑪麗拉譏諷道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得這寫故事的事是最愚蠢的,」瑪麗拉譏諷道。

passages.original: “You’ll get a pack of nonsense into your heads and waste time that should be put on your lessons.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋腦子里會塞滿一堆胡講八道,浪費本該用喺功課上嘅時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們腦子里會塞滿一堆胡說八道,浪費本該用在功課上的時間。

passages.original: Reading stories is bad enough but writing them is worse.”
passages.vernacular: 讀故事已經夠糟喇,寫故事更糟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讀故事已經夠糟了,寫故事更糟。」

passages.original: “But we’re so careful to put a moral into them all, Marilla,” explained Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「可我哋好小心地喺每一個故事里都放進寓意,瑪麗拉,」安妮解釋道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可我們很小心地在每一個故事里都放進寓意,瑪麗拉,」安妮解釋道。

passages.original: “I insist upon that.
passages.vernacular: 「我堅持呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我堅持這一點。

passages.original: All the good people are rewarded and all the bad ones are suitably punished.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅好人都得到獎賞,所有嘅壞人都受到適當嘅懲罰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的好人都得到獎賞,所有的壞人都受到適當的懲罰。

passages.original: I’m sure that must have a wholesome effect.
passages.vernacular: 我肯定嗰一定會有有益嘅效果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我肯定那一定會有有益的效果。

passages.original: The moral is the great thing.
passages.vernacular: 寓意係最重要嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寓意是最重要的。

passages.original: Mr. Allan says so.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫先生咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫先生這麼說。

passages.original: I read one of my stories to him and Mrs. Allan and they both agreed that the moral was excellent.
passages.vernacular: 我畀佢同艾倫太太讀咗我嘅一篇故事,佢哋都同意寓意極好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給他和艾倫太太讀了我的一篇故事,他們都同意寓意極好。

passages.original: Only they laughed in the wrong places.
passages.vernacular: 只係佢哋喺不該笑嘅地方笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是他們在不該笑的地方笑了。

passages.original: I like it better when people cry.
passages.vernacular: 我更鍾意人哋哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我更喜歡人們哭。

passages.original: Jane and Ruby almost always cry when I come to the pathetic parts.
passages.vernacular: 我讀到悲傷嘅部分時,簡同露比幾乎總是哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讀到悲傷的部分時,簡和露比幾乎總是哭。

passages.original: Diana wrote her Aunt Josephine about our club and her Aunt Josephine wrote back that we were to send her some of our stories.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜寫信畀佢嘅約瑟芬姑婆講咗我哋嘅俱樂部,佢嘅約瑟芬姑婆回信講我哋應該畀佢寄幾篇我哋嘅故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜寫信給她的約瑟芬姑婆說了我們的俱樂部,她的約瑟芬姑婆回信說我們應該給她寄幾篇我們的故事。

passages.original: So we copied out four of our very best and sent them.
passages.vernacular: 所以我哋抄咗四篇我哋最好嘅寄去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我們抄了四篇我們最好的寄去了。

passages.original: Miss Josephine Barry wrote back that she had never read anything so amusing in her life.
passages.vernacular: 約瑟芬·巴里小姐回信講佢一生中從冇讀過咁有趣嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約瑟芬·巴里小姐回信說她一生中從沒讀過這麼有趣的東西。

passages.original: That kind of puzzled us because the stories were all very pathetic and almost everybody died.
passages.vernacular: 呢讓我哋有點困惑,因為故事都好悲壯,幾乎每個人都死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這讓我們有點困惑,因為故事都很悲壯,幾乎每個人都死了。

passages.original: But I’m glad Miss Barry liked them.
passages.vernacular: 但我好高興巴里小姐鍾意佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我很高興巴里小姐喜歡它們。

passages.original: It shows our club is doing some good in the world.
passages.vernacular: 呢表明我哋嘅俱樂部在世上做咗啲好事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這表明我們的俱樂部在世上做了一些好事。

passages.original: Mrs. Allan says that ought to be our object in everything.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太講呢應該係我哋一切行動嘅目標。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太說這應該是我們一切行動的目標。

passages.original: I do really try to make it my object but I forget so often when I’m having fun.
passages.vernacular: 我真嘅努力讓佢成為我嘅目標,但喺玩樂嘅時候我常常忘記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真的努力讓它成為我的目標,但在玩樂的時候我常常忘記。

passages.original: I hope I shall be a little like Mrs. Allan when I grow up.
passages.vernacular: 我希望我長大後會有點像艾倫太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我長大後會有點像艾倫太太。

passages.original: Do you think there is any prospect of it, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 您覺得有可能嗎,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您覺得有可能嗎,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: “I shouldn’t say there was a great deal” was Marilla’s encouraging answer.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔會講可能性好大,」呢個係瑪麗拉鼓勵嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不會說可能性很大,」這是瑪麗拉鼓勵的回答。

passages.original: “I’m sure Mrs. Allan was never such a silly, forgetful little girl as you are.”
passages.vernacular: 「我敢肯定艾倫太太從來冇像你咁樣傻乎乎、健忘嘅小女孩嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢肯定艾倫太太從來沒有像你這樣傻乎乎、健忘的小女孩的時候。」

passages.original: “No; but she wasn’t always so good as she is now either,” said Anne seriously.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,但佢都唔係一直像而家咁好,」安妮認真地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,但她也不是一直像現在這麼好,」安妮認真地說。

passages.original: “She told me so herself--that is, she said she was a dreadful mischief when she was a girl and was always getting into scrapes.
passages.vernacular: 「佢自己告訴我嘅——就係講,佢講佢做女孩時係個可怕嘅淘氣鬼,總是惹禍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她自己告訴我的——就是說,她說她做女孩時是個可怕的淘氣鬼,總是惹禍。

passages.original: I felt so encouraged when I heard that.
passages.vernacular: 聽到呢個我感到好受鼓舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到這個我感到很受鼓舞。

passages.original: Is it very wicked of me, Marilla, to feel encouraged when I hear that other people have been bad and mischievous?
passages.vernacular: 聽講別人曾經壞過、淘氣過,我就受到鼓舞,呢個係唔係好邪惡,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽說別人曾經壞過、淘氣過,我就受到鼓舞,這是不是非常邪惡,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says it is.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說是。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says she always feels shocked when she hears of anyone ever having been naughty, no matter how small they were.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講,每當佢聽講有人曾經淘氣過,不管幾咁小,佢總是感到震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說,每當她聽說有人曾經淘氣過,不管多麼小,她總是感到震驚。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says she once heard a minister confess that when he was a boy he stole a strawberry tart out of his aunt’s pantry and she never had any respect for that minister again.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講佢曾聽一位牧師坦白,佢小時候從佢姨媽嘅食品櫃偷過一塊草莓餡餅,佢從此再都冇尊敬過嗰位牧師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說她曾聽一位牧師坦白,他小時候從他姨媽的食品櫃偷過一塊草莓餡餅,她從此再也沒尊敬過那位牧師。

passages.original: Now, I wouldn’t have felt that way.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我就唔會嗰樣感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我就不會那樣感覺。

passages.original: I’d have thought that it was real noble of him to confess it, and I’d have thought what an encouraging thing it would be for small boys nowadays who do naughty things and are sorry for them to know that perhaps they may grow up to be ministers in spite of it.
passages.vernacular: 我會認為佢坦白出嚟真高貴,我會認為對而家嗰啲做咗淘氣事並為此後悔嘅小男孩來講,知道或者佢哋儘管如此長大後都能成為牧師,係幾咁令人鼓舞嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會認為他坦白出來真高貴,我會認為對現在那些做了淘氣事並為此後悔的小男孩來說,知道也許他們儘管如此長大後也能成為牧師,是多麼令人鼓舞的事。

passages.original: That’s how I’d feel, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係我嘅感覺,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是我的感覺,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: “The way I feel at present, Anne,” said Marilla, “is that it’s high time you had those dishes washed.
passages.vernacular: 「我而家嘅感覺,安妮,」瑪麗拉講,「係你早該把嗰啲碗碟洗好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在的感覺,安妮,」瑪麗拉說,「是你早該把那些碗碟洗好了。

passages.original: You’ve taken half an hour longer than you should with all your chattering.
passages.vernacular: 你聊咗呢一大堆,比應該嘅多花咗半個鐘頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你聊了這一大堆,比應該的多花了半個鐘頭。

passages.original: Learn to work first and talk afterwards.”
passages.vernacular: 先學會幹活,然後再講話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先學會幹活,然後再說話。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXVII Vanity and Vexation of Spirit 第二十七章:虛榮與心靈的煩惱

passages.original: CH MARILLA, walking home one late April evening from an Aid meeting, realized that the winter was over and gone with the thrill of delight that spring never fails to bring to the oldest and saddest as well as to the youngest and merriest.
passages.vernacular: 四月下旬嘅一個傍晚,瑪麗拉從互助會嘅會議走路回家,春天從來冇不畀最老最悲傷嘅人,以及最年輕最歡快嘅人帶嚟嘅嗰種喜悅嘅顫慄,讓佢意識到冬天已經過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四月下旬的一個傍晚,瑪麗拉從互助會的會議走路回家,春天從來沒有不給最老最悲傷的人,以及最年輕最歡快的人帶來的那種喜悅的顫慄,讓她意識到冬天已經過去了。

passages.original: Marilla was not given to subjective analysis of her thoughts and feelings.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉不習慣對自己嘅想法同感受進行主觀分析。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉不習慣對自己的想法和感受進行主觀分析。

passages.original: She probably imagined that she was thinking about the Aids and their missionary box and the new carpet for the vestry room, but under these reflections was a harmonious consciousness of red fields smoking into pale-purply mists in the declining sun, of long, sharp-pointed fir shadows falling over the meadow beyond the brook, of still, crimson-budded maples around a mirrorlike wood pool, of a wakening in the world and a stir of hidden pulses under the gray sod.
passages.vernacular: 佢大概以為自己喺想互助會同佢哋嘅傳教士箱子,以及聖器室嘅新地毯,但喺呢啲思緒之下,係一種和諧嘅意識:紅色嘅田野喺西沉嘅太陽下冒住淡紫色嘅薄霧,冷杉長長嘅尖形影子投喺溪對岸嘅草地上,寂靜嘅、長住深紅花苞嘅楓樹圍住一眼鏡子般嘅林中水池,世界喺甦醒,灰色草皮下隱藏嘅脈搏喺躁動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她大概以為自己在想互助會和它們的傳教士箱子,以及聖器室的新地毯,但在這些思緒之下,是一種和諧的意識:紅色的田野在西沉的太陽下冒著淡紫色的薄霧,冷杉長長的尖形影子投在溪對岸的草地上,寂靜的、長著深紅花苞的楓樹圍著一眼鏡子般的林中水池,世界在甦醒,灰色草皮下隱藏的脈搏在躁動。

passages.original: The spring was abroad in the land and Marilla’s sober, middle-aged step was lighter and swifter because of its deep, primal gladness.
passages.vernacular: 春天嚟到咗大地,瑪麗拉嗰沉穩嘅、中年嘅腳步,因佢深沉、原始嘅喜悅而更輕快喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 春天來到了大地,瑪麗拉那沉穩的、中年的腳步,因它深沉、原始的喜悅而更輕快了。

passages.original: Her eyes dwelt affectionately on Green Gables, peering through its network of trees and reflecting the sunlight back from its windows in several little coruscations of glory.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅目光深情地停留喺綠色屋頂上,佢從樹木嘅網絡中探出頭嚟,從窗戶把陽光反射成幾道榮耀嘅小火花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的目光深情地停留在綠色屋頂上,它從樹木的網絡中探出頭來,從窗戶把陽光反射成幾道榮耀的小火花。

passages.original: Marilla, as she picked her steps along the damp lane, thought that it was really a satisfaction to know that she was going home to a briskly snapping wood fire and a table nicely spread for tea, instead of to the cold comfort of old Aid meeting evenings before Anne had come to Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉喺潮濕嘅小巷里一步步挑住走,覺得知道自己係回家去,迎接嘅係一爐噼啪作響嘅明火同擺得整整齊齊等住飲茶嘅桌子,而唔係安妮嚟綠色屋頂之前嗰啲互助會之夜冷冰冰嘅慰藉,實在係個滿足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉在潮濕的小巷里一步步挑著走,覺得知道自己是回家去,迎接的是一爐噼啪作響的明火和擺得整整齊齊等著喝茶的桌子,而不是安妮來綠色屋頂之前那些互助會之夜冷冰冰的慰藉,實在是個滿足。

passages.original: Consequently, when Marilla entered her kitchen and found the fire black out, with no sign of Anne anywhere, she felt justly disappointed and irritated.
passages.vernacular: 因此,當瑪麗拉走進廚房,發現爐火全熄喇,邊兒都唔見安妮嘅蹤影時,佢感到理所當然嘅失望同惱火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此,當瑪麗拉走進廚房,發現爐火全熄了,哪兒也不見安妮的蹤影時,她感到理所當然的失望和惱火。

passages.original: She had told Anne to be sure and have tea ready at five o’clock, but now she must hurry to take off her second-best dress and prepare the meal herself against Matthew’s return from plowing.
passages.vernacular: 佢告訴過安妮務必喺五點鐘準備好茶點,但而家佢必須趕緊脫下佢第二好嘅裙子,喺馬修耕地回嚟之前自己準備飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她告訴過安妮務必在五點鐘準備好茶點,但現在她必須趕緊脫下她第二好的裙子,在馬修耕地回來之前自己準備飯。

passages.original: “I’ll settle Miss Anne when she comes home,” said Marilla grimly, as she shaved up kindlings with a carving knife and with more vim than was strictly necessary.
passages.vernacular: 「等安妮小姐回嚟,我要跟佢算帳,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地講,用雕刻刀削引火柴,比嚴格需要嘅更用力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等安妮小姐回來,我要跟她算帳,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地說,用雕刻刀削引火柴,比嚴格需要的更用力。

passages.original: Matthew had come in and was waiting patiently for his tea in his corner.
passages.vernacular: 馬修已經進嚟,喺佢嘅角落裡耐心地等住飲茶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修已經進來,在他的角落裡耐心地等著喝茶。

passages.original: “She’s gadding off somewhere with Diana, writing stories or practicing dialogues or some such tomfoolery, and never thinking once about the time or her duties.
passages.vernacular: 「佢肯定又跟黛安娜喺邊兒閒逛,寫故事或者排練對話劇,或者諸如此類嘅胡鬧,一次都冇想過時間或佢嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她肯定又跟黛安娜在哪兒閒逛,寫故事或者排練對話劇,或者諸如此類的胡鬧,一次也沒想過時間或她的責任。

passages.original: She’s just got to be pulled up short and sudden on this sort of thing.
passages.vernacular: 必須對呢類事情當頭飲止佢,而且要突然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 必須對這類事情當頭喝止她,而且要突然。

passages.original: I don’t care if Mrs. Allan does say she’s the brightest and sweetest child she ever knew.
passages.vernacular: 我不在乎艾倫太太係唔係講佢係佢所認識嘅最聰明最可愛嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不在乎艾倫太太是不是說她是她所認識的最聰明最可愛的孩子。

passages.original: She may be bright and sweet enough, but her head is full of nonsense and there’s never any knowing what shape it’ll break out in next.
passages.vernacular: 佢或者足夠聰明可愛,但佢腦袋里滿係胡鬧,永遠唔知道下次會以乜嘢形式爆發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也許足夠聰明可愛,但她腦袋里滿是胡鬧,永遠不知道下次會以什麼形式爆發。

passages.original: Just as soon as she grows out of one freak she takes up with another.
passages.vernacular: 佢剛一改掉一個怪癖,又迷上另一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她剛一改掉一個怪癖,又迷上另一個。

passages.original: But there!
passages.vernacular: 不過!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過!

passages.original: Here I am saying the very thing I was so riled with Rachel Lynde for saying at the Aid today.
passages.vernacular: 我而家講嘅,正是我今日喺互助會上聽雷切爾·林德講時氣得要死嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在說的,正是我今天在互助會上聽雷切爾·林德說時氣得要死的話。

passages.original: I was real glad when Mrs. Allan spoke up for Anne, for if she hadn’t I know I’d have said something too sharp to Rachel before everybody.
