passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太替安妮講話時,我真嘅好高興,因為要唔係咁樣,我知道我會當住大家嘅面對雷切爾講出太尖刻嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太替安妮說話時,我真的很高興,因為要不是這樣,我知道我會當著大家的面對雷切爾說出太尖刻的話。

passages.original: Anne’s got plenty of faults, goodness knows, and far be it from me to deny it.
passages.vernacular: 安妮有好多缺點,天知道,我決不否認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮有很多缺點,天知道,我決不否認。

passages.original: But I’m bringing her up and not Rachel Lynde, who’d pick faults in the Angel Gabriel himself if he lived in Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 但係撫養佢嘅係我,唔係雷切爾·林德,佢就係大天使加百列住喺阿文利,都要挑佢嘅毛病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是撫養她的是我,不是雷切爾·林德,她就是大天使加百列住在阿文利,也要挑他的毛病。

passages.original: Just the same, Anne has no business to leave the house like this when I told her she was to stay home this afternoon and look after things.
passages.vernacular: 即便如此,我告訴佢今日下午要待喺家裡照睇,安妮都冇權利咁樣離開房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即便如此,我告訴她今天下午要待在家裡照看,安妮也沒權利這樣離開房子。

passages.original: I must say, with all her faults, I never found her disobedient or untrustworthy before and I’m real sorry to find her so now.”
passages.vernacular: 我必須講,佢雖然有咁多缺點,但我以前從冇發現佢不服從或不可靠,我而家發現佢咁樣,真嘅好難過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須說,她雖然有那麼多缺點,但我以前從沒發現她不服從或不可靠,我現在發現她這樣,真的很難過。」

passages.original: “Well now, I dunno,” said Matthew, who, being patient and wise and, above all, hungry, had deemed it best to let Marilla talk her wrath out unhindered, having learned by experience that she got through with whatever work was on hand much quicker if not delayed by untimely argument.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔知道,」馬修講,佢耐心、明智,尤其係餓喇,認為最好讓瑪麗拉不受阻撓地把怒氣發完,從經驗中得知,如果不被不合時宜嘅爭論耽誤,佢完成手頭嘅活快得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不知道,」馬修說,他耐心、明智,尤其是餓了,認為最好讓瑪麗拉不受阻撓地把怒氣發完,從經驗中得知,如果不被不合時宜的爭論耽誤,她完成手頭的活快得多。

passages.original: “Perhaps you’re judging her too hasty, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「或者你判斷得太匆忙喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許你判斷得太匆忙了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Don’t call her untrustworthy until you’re sure she has disobeyed you.
passages.vernacular: 喺你確定佢不服從你之前,別叫佢不可靠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在你確定她不服從你之前,別叫她不可靠。

passages.original: Mebbe it can all be explained--Anne’s a great hand at explaining.”
passages.vernacular: 講不定都能解釋——安妮係解釋嘅好手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說不定都能解釋——安妮是解釋的好手。」

passages.original: “She’s not here when I told her to stay,” retorted Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我叫佢待住嘅時候佢不喺,」瑪麗拉反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我叫她待著的時候她不在,」瑪麗拉反駁。

passages.original: “I reckon she’ll find it hard to explain that to my satisfaction.
passages.vernacular: 「我想佢好難解釋到讓我滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想她很難解釋到讓我滿意。

passages.original: Of course I knew you’d take her part, Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 當然我知道你會偏袒佢,馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然我知道你會偏袒她,馬修。

passages.original: But I’m bringing her up, not you.”
passages.vernacular: 但係撫養佢嘅係我,唔係你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是撫養她的是我,不是你。」

passages.original: It was dark when supper was ready, and still no sign of Anne, coming hurriedly over the log bridge or up Lover’s Lane, breathless and repentant with a sense of neglected duties.
passages.vernacular: 晚飯準備好時天黑喇,仍唔見安妮匆匆過原木橋或上情人小徑回嚟,氣喘吁吁、為被忽視嘅責任而悔恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚飯準備好時天黑了,仍不見安妮匆匆過原木橋或上情人小徑回來,氣喘吁吁、為被忽視的責任而悔恨。

passages.original: Marilla washed and put away the dishes grimly.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉嚴厲地洗咗碗碟收起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉嚴厲地洗了碗碟收起來。

passages.original: Then, wanting a candle to light her way down the cellar, she went up to the east gable for the one that generally stood on Anne’s table.
passages.vernacular: 然後,佢要一根蠟燭下地窖照路,就上東山牆房間去攞通常放喺安妮桌上嘅嗰根。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,她要一根蠟燭下地窖照路,就上東山牆房間去拿通常放在安妮桌上的那根。

passages.original: Lighting it, she turned around to see Anne herself lying on the bed, face downward among the pillows.
passages.vernacular: 點住佢,佢轉過身,睇到安妮本人臉朝下趴喺床上嘅枕頭中間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 點著它,她轉過身,看到安妮本人臉朝下趴在床上的枕頭中間。

passages.original: “Mercy on us,” said astonished Marilla, “have you been asleep, Anne?”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,」食驚嘅瑪麗拉講,「你瞓住咗嗎,安妮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,」吃驚的瑪麗拉說,「你睡著了嗎,安妮?」

passages.original: “No,” was the muffled reply.
passages.vernacular: 「冇,」悶悶嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,」悶悶的回答。

passages.original: “Are you sick then?” demanded Marilla anxiously, going over to the bed.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你病咗嗎?」瑪麗拉焦急地問,走到床邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你病了嗎?」瑪麗拉焦急地問,走到床邊。

passages.original: Anne cowered deeper into her pillows as if desirous of hiding herself forever from mortal eyes.
passages.vernacular: 安妮更深地縮進枕頭裡,仿佛想永遠躲開凡人嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮更深地縮進枕頭裡,仿佛想永遠躲開凡人的眼睛。

passages.original: “No. But please, Marilla, go away and don’t look at me.
passages.vernacular: 「冇。但係請您,瑪麗拉,走開,別睇我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有。但是請您,瑪麗拉,走開,別看我。

passages.original: I’m in the depths of despair and I don’t care who gets head in class or writes the best composition or sings in the Sunday-school choir any more.
passages.vernacular: 我處喺絕望嘅深淵裡,我再都不在乎邊個喺班上第一、邊個寫嘅作文最好、邊個喺主日學校唱詩班唱歌喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我處在絕望的深淵裡,我再也不在乎誰在班上第一、誰寫的作文最好、誰在主日學校唱詩班唱歌了。

passages.original: Little things like that are of no importance now because I don’t suppose I’ll ever be able to go anywhere again.
passages.vernacular: 像嗰樣嘅小事而家已經不重要喇,因為我想我再都唔能夠去任何地方喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像那樣的小事現在已經不重要了,因為我想我再也不能去任何地方了。

passages.original: My career is closed.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅前途結束喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的前途結束了。

passages.original: Please, Marilla, go away and don’t look at me.”
passages.vernacular: 請您,瑪麗拉,走開,別睇我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請您,瑪麗拉,走開,別看我。」

passages.original: “Did anyone ever hear the like?” the mystified Marilla wanted to know.
passages.vernacular: 「有邊個聽講過呢種事?」迷惑不解嘅瑪麗拉想知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有誰聽說過這種事?」迷惑不解的瑪麗拉想知道。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley, whatever is the matter with you?
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,你到底點喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,你到底怎麼了?

passages.original: What have you done?
passages.vernacular: 你做咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你做了什麼?

passages.original: Get right up this minute and tell me.
passages.vernacular: 即刻起嚟,告訴我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上起來,告訴我。

passages.original: This minute, I say.
passages.vernacular: 即刻,我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上,我說。

passages.original: There now, what is it?”
passages.vernacular: 好喇,係乜嘢事?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,是什麼事?」

passages.original: Anne had slid to the floor in despairing obedience.
passages.vernacular: 安妮絕望地服從,從床上滑到咗地板上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮絕望地服從,從床上滑到了地板上。

passages.original: “Look at my hair, Marilla,” she whispered.
passages.vernacular: 「睇睇我嘅頭髮,瑪麗拉,」佢低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看看我的頭髮,瑪麗拉,」她低聲說。

passages.original: Accordingly, Marilla lifted her candle and looked scrutinizingly at Anne’s hair, flowing in heavy masses down her back.
passages.vernacular: 於是,瑪麗拉舉起蠟燭,仔細地睇咗睇安妮嘅頭髮,佢哋濃密地披喺佢背後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是,瑪麗拉舉起蠟燭,仔細地看了看安妮的頭髮,它們濃密地披在她背後。

passages.original: It certainly had a very strange appearance.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅樣子確實好奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的樣子確實非常奇怪。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley, what have you done to your hair?
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,你對你嘅頭髮做咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,你對你的頭髮做了什麼?

passages.original: Why, it’s green!”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,係綠嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,是綠的!」

passages.original: Green it might be called, if it were any earthly color--a queer, dull, bronzy green, with streaks here and there of the original red to heighten the ghastly effect.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢係人間任何一種顏色嘅話,可以稱佢為綠色——一種奇怪嘅、暗淡嘅、古銅色嘅綠,呢度嗰度仲有幾縷原來嘅紅色,增添咗可怕嘅效果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果它是人間任何一種顏色的話,可以稱它為綠色——一種奇怪的、暗淡的、古銅色的綠,這裡那裡還有幾縷原來的紅色,增添了可怕的效果。

passages.original: Never in all her life had Marilla seen anything so grotesque as Anne’s hair at that moment.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉呢輩子從冇見過比此刻安妮嘅頭髮更怪異嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉這輩子從沒見過比此刻安妮的頭髮更怪異的東西。

passages.original: “Yes, it’s green,” moaned Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係綠嘅,」安妮呻吟道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是綠的,」安妮呻吟道。

passages.original: “I thought nothing could be as bad as red hair.
passages.vernacular: 「我以為冇乜嘢比紅頭髮更糟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以為沒什麼比紅頭髮更糟了。

passages.original: But now I know it’s ten times worse to have green hair.
passages.vernacular: 但而家我知道綠頭髮糟十倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在我知道綠頭髮糟十倍。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, you little know how utterly wretched I am.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,您唔知道我有多徹底嘅悲慘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,您不知道我有多徹底的悲慘。」

passages.original: “I little know how you got into this fix, but I mean to find out,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道你係點弄成咁樣嘅,但我打算弄明白,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道你是怎麼弄成這樣的,但我打算弄明白,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “Come right down to the kitchen--it’s too cold up here--and tell me just what you’ve done.
passages.vernacular: 「即刻下到廚房嚟——呢上面太冷喇——告訴我你到底做咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬上下到廚房來——這上面太冷了——告訴我你到底做了什麼。

passages.original: I’ve been expecting something queer for some time.
passages.vernacular: 我一直喺預料有乜嘢古怪嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直在預料有什麼古怪的事。

passages.original: You haven’t got into any scrape for over two months, and I was sure another one was due.
passages.vernacular: 你已經兩個多月冇惹乜嘢麻煩喇,我確信另一件係該嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你已經兩個多月沒有惹什麼麻煩了,我確信另一件是該來了。

passages.original: Now, then, what did you do to your hair?”
passages.vernacular: 好喇,咁,你對你嘅頭髮做咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,那麼,你對你的頭髮做了什麼?」

passages.original: “I dyed it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我染咗佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我染了它。」

passages.original: “Dyed it!
passages.vernacular: 「染喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「染了!

passages.original: Dyed your hair!
passages.vernacular: 染咗你嘅頭髮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 染了你的頭髮!

passages.original: Anne Shirley, didn’t you know it was a wicked thing to do?”
passages.vernacular: 安妮·雪莉,你難道唔知道呢個係邪惡嘅事嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮·雪莉,你難道不知道這是邪惡的事嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, I knew it was a little wicked,” admitted Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我知道有點邪惡,」安妮承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我知道有點邪惡,」安妮承認。

passages.original: “But I thought it was worth while to be a little wicked to get rid of red hair.
passages.vernacular: 「但我覺得為了擺脫紅頭髮,做啲邪惡係值得嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我覺得為了擺脫紅頭髮,做一點邪惡是值得的。

passages.original: I counted the cost, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我算過代價喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我算過代價了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Besides, I meant to be extra good in other ways to make up for it.”
passages.vernacular: 而且,我打算喺別嘅方面格外乖嚟彌補。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,我打算在別的方面格外乖來彌補。」

passages.original: “Well,” said Marilla sarcastically, “if I’d decided it was worth while to dye my hair I’d have dyed it a decent color at least.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」瑪麗拉諷刺地講,「如果我決定染頭髮值得,我至少會染成一個像樣嘅顏色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」瑪麗拉諷刺地說,「如果我決定染頭髮值得,我至少會染成一個像樣的顏色。

passages.original: I wouldn’t have dyed it green.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔會染成綠色。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會染成綠色。」

passages.original: “But I didn’t mean to dye it green, Marilla,” protested Anne dejectedly.
passages.vernacular: 「可我冇打算染成綠色,瑪麗拉,」安妮沮喪地抗議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可我沒打算染成綠色,瑪麗拉,」安妮沮喪地抗議。

passages.original: “If I was wicked I meant to be wicked to some purpose.
passages.vernacular: 「如果我要邪惡,我都要邪惡得有目的。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我要邪惡,我也要邪惡得有目的。

passages.original: He said it would turn my hair a beautiful raven black--he positively assured me that it would.
passages.vernacular: 佢講會把我嘅頭髮染成美麗嘅烏鴉黑——佢明確地向我保證會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說會把我的頭髮染成美麗的烏鴉黑——他明確地向我保證會的。

passages.original: How could I doubt his word, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 我點能懷疑佢嘅話,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怎麼能懷疑他的話,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: I know what it feels like to have your word doubted.
passages.vernacular: 我知道話被人懷疑係乜嘢滋味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道話被人懷疑是什麼滋味。

passages.original: And Mrs. Allan says we should never suspect anyone of not telling us the truth unless we have proof that they’re not.
passages.vernacular: 而且艾倫太太講我哋永遠不該懷疑任何人不講實話,除非我哋有證據證明佢哋唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且艾倫太太說我們永遠不該懷疑任何人不說實話,除非我們有證據證明他們不是。

passages.original: I have proof now--green hair is proof enough for anybody.
passages.vernacular: 我而家有證據喇——綠頭髮對任何人來講都係足夠嘅證據。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在有證據了——綠頭髮對任何人來說都是足夠的證據。

passages.original: But I hadn’t then and I believed every word he said implicitly.”
passages.vernacular: 但我當時冇,我完全相信佢講嘅每一個字。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我當時沒有,我完全相信他說的每一個字。」

passages.original: “Who said?
passages.vernacular: 「邊個講嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰說的?

passages.original: Who are you talking about?”
passages.vernacular: 你講嘅係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說的是誰?」

passages.original: “The peddler that was here this afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 「今日下午喺呢兒嘅嗰個小販。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今天下午在這兒的那個小販。

passages.original: I bought the dye from him.”
passages.vernacular: 我從佢嗰兒買嘅染髮劑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從他那兒買的染髮劑。」

passages.original: “Anne Shirley, how often have I told you never to let one of those Italians in the house!
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,我告訴過你多少次,決唔好讓嗰啲意大利人進屋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,我告訴過你多少次,決不要讓那些意大利人進屋!

passages.original: I don’t believe in encouraging them to come around at all.”
passages.vernacular: 我根本不贊成鼓勵佢哋嚟呢兒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我根本不贊成鼓勵他們來這兒。」

passages.original: “Oh, I didn’t let him in the house.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我冇讓佢進屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我沒讓他進屋。

passages.original: I remembered what you told me, and I went out, carefully shut the door, and looked at his things on the step.
passages.vernacular: 我記得您跟我講過,我就出去,小心地關上門,喺台階上睇佢嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記得您跟我說過,我就出去,小心地關上門,在台階上看他的東西。

passages.original: Besides, he wasn’t an Italian--he was a German Jew.
passages.vernacular: 再講,佢唔係意大利人——佢係個德國猶太人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再說,他不是意大利人——他是個德國猶太人。

passages.original: He had a big box full of very interesting things and he told me he was working hard to make enough money to bring his wife and children out from Germany.
passages.vernacular: 佢有一個大箱子,裡面裝滿咗好有趣嘅嘢,佢告訴我佢喺拼命賺足夠嘅錢,把佢嘅妻子同細路從德國接嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有一個大箱子,裡面裝滿了非常有趣的東西,他告訴我他在拼命賺足夠的錢,把他的妻子和孩子從德國接來。

passages.original: He spoke so feelingly about them that it touched my heart.
passages.vernacular: 佢講到佢哋時咁動情,觸動咗我嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他講到他們時那麼動情,觸動了我的心。

passages.original: I wanted to buy something from him to help him in such a worthy object.
passages.vernacular: 我想從佢嗰兒買點嘢,幫助佢實現咁值得嘅目標。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想從他那兒買點東西,幫助他實現這麼值得的目標。

passages.original: Then all at once I saw the bottle of hair dye.
passages.vernacular: 然後我忽然睇到嗰瓶染髮劑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我忽然看到那瓶染髮劑。

passages.original: The peddler said it was warranted to dye any hair a beautiful raven black and wouldn’t wash off.
passages.vernacular: 小販講保證能把任何頭髮染成美麗嘅烏鴉黑,而且洗不掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小販說保證能把任何頭髮染成美麗的烏鴉黑,而且洗不掉。

passages.original: In a trice I saw myself with beautiful raven-black hair and the temptation was irresistible.
passages.vernacular: 轉眼間我就睇到咗自己有美麗嘅烏黑頭髮,誘惑無法抗拒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轉眼間我就看到了自己有美麗的烏黑頭髮,誘惑無法抗拒。

passages.original: But the price of the bottle was seventy-five cents and I had only fifty cents left out of my chicken money.
passages.vernacular: 但係嗰瓶嘅價錢係七十五分,我從養雞嘅錢里只剩五好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是那瓶的價錢是七十五分,我從養雞的錢里只剩五十分。

passages.original: I think the peddler had a very kind heart, for he said that, seeing it was me, he’d sell it for fifty cents and that was just giving it away.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得嗰個小販心腸好好,因為佢講,睇喺係我嘅份上,佢五好賣畀我,嗰簡直係白送。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得那個小販心腸很好,因為他說,看在是我的份上,他五十分賣給我,那簡直是白送。

passages.original: So I bought it, and as soon as he had gone I came up here and applied it with an old hairbrush as the directions said.
passages.vernacular: 所以我買喇,佢一走我就上樓嚟,按講明書用一把舊髮刷塗上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我買了,他一走我就上樓來,按說明書用一把舊髮刷塗上。

passages.original: I used up the whole bottle, and oh, Marilla, when I saw the dreadful color it turned my hair I repented of being wicked, I can tell you.
passages.vernacular: 我把一整瓶都用光喇,哦,瑪麗拉,當我睇到佢把我嘅頭髮染成咗嗰種可怕嘅顏色時,我為自己嘅邪惡後悔喇,我可以告訴您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把一整瓶都用光了,哦,瑪麗拉,當我看到它把我的頭髮染成了那種可怕的顏色時,我為自己的邪惡後悔了,我可以告訴您。

passages.original: And I’ve been repenting ever since.”
passages.vernacular: 而且我從嗰以後一直喺後悔。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我從那以後一直在後悔。」

passages.original: “Well, I hope you’ll repent to good purpose,” said Marilla severely, “and that you’ve got your eyes opened to where your vanity has led you, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我希望你嘅悔改有好嘅結果,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地講,「都希望你睜開咗眼睛,睇到你嘅虛榮把你引到咗乜嘢地步,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我希望你的悔改有好的結果,」瑪麗拉嚴厲地說,「也希望你睜開了眼睛,看到你的虛榮把你引到了什麼地步,安妮。

passages.original: Goodness knows what’s to be done.
passages.vernacular: 天曉得該點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天曉得該怎麼辦。

passages.original: I suppose the first thing is to give your hair a good washing and see if that will do any good.”
passages.vernacular: 我想第一件事係把你嘅頭髮好好洗一洗,睇睇有冇用。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想第一件事是把你的頭髮好好洗一洗,看看有沒有用。」

passages.original: Accordingly, Anne washed her hair, scrubbing it vigorously with soap and water, but for all the difference it made she might as well have been scouring its original red.
passages.vernacular: 於是安妮洗咗頭髮,用肥皂同水用力擦洗,但係毫無變化,佢簡直好像係喺擦洗佢原來嘅紅色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是安妮洗了頭髮,用肥皂和水用力擦洗,但是毫無變化,她簡直好像是在擦洗它原來的紅色。

passages.original: The peddler had certainly spoken the truth when he declared that the dye wouldn’t wash off, however his veracity might be impeached in other respects.
passages.vernacular: 小販講染髮劑洗不掉,呢確實係實話,不管佢嘅誠實在其他方面係咪值得懷疑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小販說染髮劑洗不掉,這確實是實話,不管他的誠實在其他方面是否值得懷疑。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, what shall I do?” questioned Anne in tears.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我該點算?」安妮含淚問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,我該怎麼辦?」安妮含淚問。

passages.original: “I can never live this down.
passages.vernacular: 「我永遠無法擺脫呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我永遠無法擺脫這件事。

passages.original: People have pretty well forgotten my other mistakes--the liniment cake and setting Diana drunk and flying into a temper with Mrs. Lynde.
passages.vernacular: 人哋已經差不多忘咗我嘅其他錯誤——止痛擦劑蛋糕、灌醉黛安娜同對林德太太發脾氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們已經差不多忘了我的其他錯誤——止痛擦劑蛋糕、灌醉黛安娜和對林德太太發脾氣。

passages.original: But they’ll never forget this.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋永遠唔會忘記呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們永遠不會忘記這個。

passages.original: They will think I am not respectable.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋會認為我不體面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們會認為我不體面。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, ‘what a tangled web we weave when first we practice to deceive.’
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,『當我哋初次練習欺騙,編織出嘅網幾咁糾纏。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,『當我們初次練習欺騙,編織出的網多麼糾纏。』

passages.original: That is poetry, but it is true.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係詩,但佢係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是詩,但它是真的。

passages.original: And oh, how Josie Pye will laugh!
passages.vernacular: 哦,喬西·派伊會笑成乜嘢樣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,喬西·派伊會笑成什麼樣!

passages.original: Marilla, I cannot face Josie Pye.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉,我唔能夠面對喬西·派伊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉,我不能面對喬西·派伊。

passages.original: I am the unhappiest girl in Prince Edward Island.”
passages.vernacular: 我係愛德華王子島上最不幸嘅女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是愛德華王子島上最不幸的女孩。」

passages.original: Anne’s unhappiness continued for a week.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅不幸持續咗一個星期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的不幸持續了一個星期。

passages.original: During that time she went nowhere and shampooed her hair every day.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢期間,佢邊兒都冇去,每天洗頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這期間,她哪兒也沒去,每天洗頭。

passages.original: Diana alone of outsiders knew the fatal secret, but she promised solemnly never to tell, and it may be stated here and now that she kept her word.
passages.vernacular: 局外人當中只有黛安娜知道呢個致命嘅祕密,但佢鄭重地承諾永不洩露,可以喺此講明,佢信守咗諾言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 局外人當中只有黛安娜知道這個致命的祕密,但她鄭重地承諾永不洩露,可以在此說明,她信守了諾言。

passages.original: At the end of the week Marilla said decidedly:
passages.vernacular: 一個星期結束時,瑪麗拉斷然講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個星期結束時,瑪麗拉斷然說:

passages.original: “It’s no use, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「冇用喇,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒用了,安妮。

passages.original: That is fast dye if ever there was any.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我見過最牢固嘅染劑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我見過最牢固的染劑。

passages.original: Your hair must be cut off; there is no other way.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅頭髮必須剪掉;冇別嘅辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的頭髮必須剪掉;沒有別的辦法。

passages.original: You can’t go out with it looking like that.”
passages.vernacular: 你唔能夠頂住咁樣出去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不能頂著這樣出去。」

passages.original: Anne’s lips quivered, but she realized the bitter truth of Marilla’s remarks.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅嘴唇顫抖住,但佢意識到瑪麗拉嘅話係苦澀嘅真理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的嘴唇顫抖著,但她意識到瑪麗拉的話是苦澀的真理。

passages.original: With a dismal sigh she went for the scissors.
passages.vernacular: 佢憂鬱地嘆口氣,去攞剪刀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她憂鬱地嘆口氣,去拿剪刀。

passages.original: “Please cut it off at once, Marilla, and have it over.
passages.vernacular: 「請即刻剪掉,瑪麗拉,把佢了結。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請馬上剪掉,瑪麗拉,把它了結。

passages.original: Oh, I feel that my heart is broken.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我覺得我嘅心碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我覺得我的心碎了。

passages.original: This is such an unromantic affliction.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係咁冇浪漫色彩嘅苦難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是這麼沒有浪漫色彩的苦難。

passages.original: The girls in books lose their hair in fevers or sell it to get money for some good deed, and I’m sure I wouldn’t mind losing my hair in some such fashion half so much.
passages.vernacular: 書裡嘅女孩因發燒掉頭髮,或者為做某件好事賣頭髮換錢,我肯定我以嗰樣嘅方式失去頭髮,連一半都唔會介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 書裡的女孩因發燒掉頭髮,或者為做某件好事賣頭髮換錢,我肯定我以那樣的方式失去頭髮,連一半也不會介意。

passages.original: But there is nothing comforting in having your hair cut off because you’ve dyed it a dreadful color, is there?
passages.vernacular: 但係因為把頭髮染成可怕嘅顏色而被剪掉,冇任何安慰,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是因為把頭髮染成可怕的顏色而被剪掉,沒有任何安慰,是不是?

passages.original: I’m going to weep all the time you’re cutting it off, if it won’t interfere.
passages.vernacular: 您剪嘅時候我要一直哭,如果不妨礙嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您剪的時候我要一直哭,如果不妨礙的話。

passages.original: It seems such a tragic thing.”
passages.vernacular: 呢似乎係一件咁悲劇嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這似乎是一件這麼悲劇的事。」

passages.original: Anne wept then, but later on, when she went upstairs and looked in the glass, she was calm with despair.
passages.vernacular: 安妮於是哭喇,但後來,佢上樓照鏡子時,已經因絕望而平靜喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮於是哭了,但後來,她上樓照鏡子時,已經因絕望而平靜了。

passages.original: Marilla had done her work thoroughly and it had been necessary to shingle the hair as closely as possible.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉做得好徹底,唔得不把頭髮剪得貼住頭皮,像瓦片一樣短。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉做得很徹底,不得不把頭髮剪得貼著頭皮,像瓦片一樣短。

passages.original: The result was not becoming, to state the case as mildly as may be.
passages.vernacular: 結果並不好睇,講得再委婉都係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果並不好看,說得再委婉也是這樣。

passages.original: Anne promptly turned her glass to the wall.
passages.vernacular: 安妮即刻把鏡子轉向牆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮立刻把鏡子轉向牆。

passages.original: “I’ll never, never look at myself again until my hair grows,” she exclaimed passionately.
passages.vernacular: 「我再都,再都不睇自己,直到我嘅頭髮長出嚟,」佢激烈地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再也,再也不看自己,直到我的頭髮長出來,」她激烈地喊道。

passages.original: Then she suddenly righted the glass.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢突然又把鏡子扶正。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她突然又把鏡子扶正。

passages.original: “Yes, I will, too.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我要睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我要看。

passages.original: I’d do penance for being wicked that way.
passages.vernacular: 我要為邪惡而用嗰種方式贖罪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要為邪惡而用那種方式贖罪。

passages.original: I’ll look at myself every time I come to my room and see how ugly I am.
passages.vernacular: 每次我回房間,我都要睇自己,睇睇我有多醜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每次我回房間,我都要看自己,看看我有多醜。

passages.original: And I won’t try to imagine it away, either.
passages.vernacular: 而且我都唔會試圖把佢想像掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我也不會試圖把它想像掉。

passages.original: I never thought I was vain about my hair, of all things, but now I know I was, in spite of its being red, because it was so long and thick and curly.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇想過我竟然為頭髮而虛榮,但而家我知道我係,儘管佢係紅色嘅,因為佢咁長、咁密、咁捲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒想過我竟然為頭髮而虛榮,但現在我知道我是,儘管它是紅色的,因為它那麼長、那麼密、那麼捲。

passages.original: I expect something will happen to my nose next.”
passages.vernacular: 我想接下嚟我嘅鼻子要出事喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想接下來我的鼻子要出事了。」

passages.original: Anne’s clipped head made a sensation in school on the following Monday, but to her relief nobody guessed the real reason for it, not even Josie Pye, who, however, did not fail to inform Anne that she looked like a perfect scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 下個星期一,安妮剪短咗嘅頭喺學校引起咗轟動,但令佢寬慰嘅係,邊個都冇猜到真正嘅原因,連喬西·派伊都冇,不過佢冇忘咗告訴安妮,佢睇起嚟像個十足嘅稻草人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下個星期一,安妮剪短了的頭在學校引起了轟動,但令她寬慰的是,誰也沒猜到真正的原因,連喬西·派伊也沒有,不過她沒忘了告訴安妮,她看起來像個十足的稻草人。

passages.original: “I didn’t say anything when Josie said that to me,” Anne confided that evening to Marilla, who was lying on the sofa after one of her headaches, “because I thought it was part of my punishment and I ought to bear it patiently.
passages.vernacular: 「喬西對我咁講時,我乜嘢都冇講,」嗰天傍晚,安妮向躺喺沙發上、剛頭疼完嘅瑪麗拉吐露,「因為我覺得呢個係我懲罰嘅一部分,我應該耐心地承受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喬西對我這麼說時,我什麼也沒說,」那天傍晚,安妮向躺在沙發上、剛頭疼完的瑪麗拉吐露,「因為我覺得這是我懲罰的一部分,我應該耐心地承受。

passages.original: It’s hard to be told you look like a scarecrow and I wanted to say something back.
passages.vernacular: 被講成像稻草人好難受,我想回嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被說成像稻草人很難受,我想回嘴。

passages.original: But I didn’t.
passages.vernacular: 但我冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我沒有。

passages.original: I just swept her one scornful look and then I forgave her.
passages.vernacular: 我只係掃咗佢一眼輕蔑嘅目光,然後我原諒咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是掃了她一眼輕蔑的目光,然後我原諒了她。

passages.original: It makes you feel very virtuous when you forgive people, doesn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 原諒別人會讓你覺得好有道德,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 原諒別人會讓你覺得非常有道德,是不是?

passages.original: I mean to devote all my energies to being good after this and I shall never try to be beautiful again.
passages.vernacular: 我打算此後把我全部嘅精力都用嚟做個好人,我決唔再試圖美麗喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我打算此後把我全部的精力都用來做個好人,我決不再試圖美麗了。

passages.original: Of course it’s better to be good.
passages.vernacular: 當然,做好人更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,做好人更好。

passages.original: I know it is, but it’s sometimes so hard to believe a thing even when you know it.
passages.vernacular: 我知道係咁樣,但有時就算你知道,都好難相信一件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道是這樣,但有時就算你知道,也很難相信一件事。

passages.original: I do really want to be good, Marilla, like you and Mrs. Allan and Miss Stacy, and grow up to be a credit to you.
passages.vernacular: 我真嘅想做個好人,瑪麗拉,像您、艾倫太太同斯泰西小姐嗰樣,長大後成為你哋嘅光榮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真的想做個好人,瑪麗拉,像您、艾倫太太和斯泰西小姐那樣,長大後成為你們的光榮。

passages.original: Diana says when my hair begins to grow to tie a black velvet ribbon around my head with a bow at one side.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜講,等我嘅頭髮開始長嘅時候,用一條黑天鵝絨緞帶繞住頭,喺一側打個蝴蝶結。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜說,等我的頭髮開始長的時候,用一條黑天鵝絨緞帶繞著頭,在一側打個蝴蝶結。

passages.original: She says she thinks it will be very becoming.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢覺得會好好睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她覺得會很好看。

passages.original: I will call it a snood--that sounds so romantic.
passages.vernacular: 我要叫佢髮網——呢聽起嚟好浪漫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要叫它髮網——這聽起來很浪漫。

passages.original: But am I talking too much, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 但我係唔係講得太多喇,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我是不是說得太多了,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: Does it hurt your head?”
passages.vernacular: 會唔會讓您頭疼?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 會不會讓您頭疼?」

passages.original: “My head is better now.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅頭而家好些喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的頭現在好些了。

passages.original: It was terrible bad this afternoon, though.
passages.vernacular: 不過今日下午疼得可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過今天下午疼得可怕。

passages.original: These headaches of mine are getting worse and worse.
passages.vernacular: 我呢啲頭疼越嚟越嚴重喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這些頭疼越來越嚴重了。

passages.original: I’ll have to see a doctor about them.
passages.vernacular: 我得去睇醫生喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得去看醫生了。

passages.original: As for your chatter, I don’t know that I mind it--I’ve got so used to it.”
passages.vernacular: 至於你嘅嘮叨,我唔知道我係唔係介意——我已經習慣喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於你的嘮叨,我不知道我是不是介意——我已經習慣了。」

passages.original: Which was Marilla’s way of saying that she liked to hear it.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係瑪麗拉講佢鍾意聽嘅方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是瑪麗拉說她喜歡聽的方式。

chapters.title: Ch. XXVIII An Unfortunate Lily Maid 第二十八章:不幸的百合少女

passages.original: CH OF course you must be Elaine, Anne,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「當然你必須做艾蓮,安妮,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然你必須做艾蓮,安妮,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “I could never have the courage to float down there.”
passages.vernacular: 「我永遠冇勇氣漂到嗰度去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我永遠沒有勇氣漂到那裡去。」

passages.original: “Nor I,” said Ruby Gillis, with a shiver.
passages.vernacular: 「我都冇,」露比·吉利斯打住寒顫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也沒有,」露比·吉利斯打著寒顫說。

passages.original: “I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋兩三個人喺平底船里能坐直嘅時候,我不介意漂下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們兩三個人在平底船里能坐直的時候,我不介意漂下去。

passages.original: It’s fun then.
passages.vernacular: 嗰時挺好玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時挺好玩。

passages.original: But to lie down and pretend I was dead--I just couldn’t.
passages.vernacular: 但係躺下假裝我死喇——我就係做唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是躺下假裝我死了——我就是做不到。

passages.original: I’d die really of fright.”
passages.vernacular: 我真嘅會嚇死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真的會嚇死。」

passages.original: “Of course it would be romantic,” conceded Jane Andrews, “but I know I couldn’t keep still.
passages.vernacular: 「當然嗰會好浪漫,」簡·安德魯斯承認,「但我知道我唔可能一動不動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然那會很浪漫,」簡·安德魯斯承認,「但我知道我不可能一動不動。

passages.original: I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out.
passages.vernacular: 我每隔一分鐘就會蹦起嚟睇睇我喺邊兒,有冇漂得太遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我每隔一分鐘就會蹦起來看看我在哪兒,有沒有漂得太遠。

passages.original: And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道,安妮,嗰會破壞效果。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,安妮,那會破壞效果。」

passages.original: “But it’s so ridiculous to have a redheaded Elaine,” mourned Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「但係讓紅頭髮嘅人做艾蓮太可笑喇,」安妮哀嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是讓紅頭髮的人做艾蓮太可笑了,」安妮哀嘆道。

passages.original: “I’m not afraid to float down and I’d love to be Elaine.
passages.vernacular: 「我不怕漂下去,我好想做艾蓮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不怕漂下去,我很想做艾蓮。

passages.original: But it’s ridiculous just the same.
passages.vernacular: 但係依然好可笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是依然很可笑。

passages.original: Ruby ought to be Elaine because she is so fair and has such lovely long golden hair--Elaine had ‘all her bright hair streaming down,’ you know.
passages.vernacular: 露比應該做艾蓮,因為佢咁白,有咁可愛嘅金色長髮——艾蓮有『明亮嘅頭髮全飄垂下嚟』,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比應該做艾蓮,因為她那麼白,有那麼可愛的金色長髮——艾蓮有『明亮的頭髮全飄垂下來』,你知道。

passages.original: And Elaine was the lily maid.
passages.vernacular: 而且艾蓮係百合少女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且艾蓮是百合少女。

passages.original: Now, a red-haired person cannot be a lily maid.”
passages.vernacular: 紅頭髮嘅人唔能夠做百合少女。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紅頭髮的人不能做百合少女。」

passages.original: “Your complexion is just as fair as Ruby’s,” said Diana earnestly, “and your hair is ever so much darker than it used to be before you cut it.”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅膚色同露比嘅一樣白,」黛安娜認真地講,「而且你嘅頭髮比剪之前深多喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的膚色和露比的一樣白,」黛安娜認真地說,「而且你的頭髮比剪之前深多了。」

passages.original: “Oh, do you really think so?” exclaimed Anne, flushing sensitively with delight.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你真咁認為嗎?」安妮叫道,敏感地因喜悅而臉紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你真這麼認為嗎?」安妮叫道,敏感地因喜悅而臉紅。

passages.original: “I’ve sometimes thought it was myself--but I never dared to ask anyone for fear she would tell me it wasn’t.
passages.vernacular: 「我有時自己都覺得係——但我從唔敢問別人,怕佢告訴我唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有時自己也覺得是——但我從不敢問別人,怕她告訴我不是。

passages.original: Do you think it could be called auburn now, Diana?”
passages.vernacular: 你覺得而家可以叫赤褐色咗嗎,黛安娜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你覺得現在可以叫赤褐色了嗎,黛安娜?」

passages.original: “Yes, and I think it is real pretty,” said Diana, looking admiringly at the short, silky curls that clustered over Anne’s head and were held in place by a very jaunty black velvet ribbon and bow.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我覺得真嘅好漂亮,」黛安娜講,欣賞地睇住圍繞喺安妮頭上、被一條好俏皮嘅黑天鵝絨緞帶同蝴蝶結固定嘅短而柔滑嘅鬈髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我覺得真的很漂亮,」黛安娜說,欣賞地看著圍繞在安妮頭上、被一條非常俏皮的黑天鵝絨緞帶和蝴蝶結固定的短而柔滑的鬈髮。

passages.original: They were standing on the bank of the pond, below Orchard Slope, where a little headland fringed with birches ran out from the bank; at its tip was a small wooden platform built out into the water for the convenience of fishermen and duck hunters.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋站喺果園坡下面嘅池塘岸邊,嗰度有一個長滿白樺嘅小岬角從岸上伸出去;岬角嘅尖端有一個小木平臺,伸入水中,係為了方便釣魚嘅人同獵鴨嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們站在果園坡下面的池塘岸邊,那裡有一個長滿白樺的小岬角從岸上伸出去;岬角的尖端有一個小木平臺,伸入水中,是為了方便釣魚的人和獵鴨的人。

passages.original: Ruby and Jane were spending the midsummer afternoon with Diana, and Anne had come over to play with them.
passages.vernacular: 露比同簡正同黛安娜一起度過仲夏嘅下午,安妮係過嚟跟佢哋玩嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比和簡正與黛安娜一起度過仲夏的下午,安妮是過來跟她們玩的。

passages.original: Anne and Diana had spent most of their playtime that summer on and about the pond.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個夏天,安妮同黛安娜大部分玩耍時間都喺池塘上同池塘邊度過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個夏天,安妮和黛安娜大部分玩耍時間都在池塘上和池塘邊度過。

passages.original: Idlewild was a thing of the past, Mr. Bell having ruthlessly cut down the little circle of trees in his back pasture in the spring.
passages.vernacular: 閒遊林已成為過去,貝爾先生春天無情地砍倒咗佢後牧場上嗰一小圈樹木。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 閒遊林已成為過去,貝爾先生春天無情地砍倒了他後牧場上那一小圈樹木。

passages.original: Anne had sat among the stumps and wept, not without an eye to the romance of it; but she was speedily consoled, for, after all, as she and Diana said, big girls of thirteen, going on fourteen, were too old for such childish amusements as playhouses, and there were more fascinating sports to be found about the pond.
passages.vernacular: 安妮曾坐喺樹樁間哭泣,唔係冇留意其中嘅浪漫;但佢好快就得到咗安慰,因為講到底,正如佢同黛安娜講嘅,十三歲即將十四歲嘅大女孩,對於遊戲屋咁樣幼稚嘅消遣已經太大喇,池塘邊仲有更迷人嘅遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮曾坐在樹樁間哭泣,不是沒有留意其中的浪漫;但她很快就得到了安慰,因為說到底,正如她和黛安娜說的,十三歲即將十四歲的大女孩,對於遊戲屋這樣幼稚的消遣已經太大了,池塘邊還有更迷人的遊戲。

passages.original: It was splendid to fish for trout over the bridge and the two girls learned to row themselves about in the little flat-bottomed dory Mr. Barry kept for duck shooting.
passages.vernacular: 喺橋上釣鱒魚太棒喇,兩個女孩學會咗划巴里先生為獵鴨留嘅嗰隻小平底漁船。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在橋上釣鱒魚太棒了,兩個女孩學會了划巴里先生為獵鴨留的那隻小平底漁船。

passages.original: It was Anne’s idea that they dramatize Elaine.
passages.vernacular: 把艾蓮戲劇化係安妮嘅主意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把艾蓮戲劇化是安妮的主意。

passages.original: They had studied Tennyson’s poem in school the preceding winter, the Superintendent of Education having prescribed it in the English course for the Prince Edward Island schools.
passages.vernacular: 去年冬天佢哋喺學校學過丁尼生嘅嗰首詩,教育督學規定把佢列入愛德華王子島學校嘅英語課程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去年冬天她們在學校學過丁尼生的那首詩,教育督學規定把它列入愛德華王子島學校的英語課程。

passages.original: They had analyzed and parsed it and torn it to pieces in general until it was a wonder there was any meaning at all left in it for them, but at least the fair lily maid and Lancelot and Guinevere and King Arthur had become very real people to them, and Anne was devoured by secret regret that she had not been born in Camelot.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋分析佢、句法剖析佢、總之把佢撕得粉碎,以至於奇怪佢還畀佢哋留下咗乜嘢意義,但至少美麗嘅百合少女、蘭斯洛特、格尼薇兒同亞瑟王已經成咗佢哋眼中好真實嘅人,安妮被一種暗暗嘅遺憾吞噬住,遺憾自己冇生喺卡米洛特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們分析它、句法剖析它、總之把它撕得粉碎,以至於奇怪它還給她們留下了什麼意義,但至少美麗的百合少女、蘭斯洛特、格尼薇兒和亞瑟王已經成了她們眼中非常真實的人,安妮被一種暗暗的遺憾吞噬著,遺憾自己沒有生在卡米洛特。

passages.original: Those days, she said, were so much more romantic than the present.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,嗰啲日子比而家浪漫得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說,那些日子比現在浪漫得多。

passages.original: Anne’s plan was hailed with enthusiasm.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅計劃受到熱烈歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的計劃受到熱烈歡迎。

passages.original: The girls had discovered that if the flat were pushed off from the landing place it would drift down with the current under the bridge and finally strand itself on another headland lower down which ran out at a curve in the pond.
passages.vernacular: 女孩哋發現,如果把平底船從登陸處推出去,佢會隨水流漂到橋下,最後擱淺喺池塘彎道處更下游嘅另一個岬角上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩們發現,如果把平底船從登陸處推出去,它會隨水流漂到橋下,最後擱淺在池塘彎道處更下游的另一個岬角上。

passages.original: They had often gone down like this and nothing could be more convenient for playing Elaine.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋經常咁樣漂下去,再冇比呢更方便演艾蓮喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們經常這樣漂下去,再沒有比這更方便演艾蓮了。

passages.original: “Well, I’ll be Elaine,” said Anne, yielding reluctantly, for, although she would have been delighted to play the principal character, yet her artistic sense demanded fitness for it and this, she felt, her limitations made impossible.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,我嚟演艾蓮,」安妮不情願地讓步,因為雖然佢好樂意演主角,但佢嘅藝術感要求同角色相稱,而佢覺得自己嘅局限使呢唔可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,我來演艾蓮,」安妮不情願地讓步,因為雖然她很樂意演主角,但她的藝術感要求與角色相稱,而她覺得自己的局限使這不可能。

passages.original: “Ruby, you must be King Arthur and Jane will be Guinevere and Diana must be Lancelot.
passages.vernacular: 「露比,你演亞瑟王,簡演格尼薇兒,黛安娜演蘭斯洛特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「露比,你演亞瑟王,簡演格尼薇兒,黛安娜演蘭斯洛特。

passages.original: But first you must be the brothers and the father.
passages.vernacular: 但係首先你哋得演兄弟同父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是首先你們得演兄弟和父親。

passages.original: We can’t have the old dumb servitor because there isn’t room for two in the flat when one is lying down.
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔能夠有嗰個老啞僕,因為一個人躺住嘅時候,平底船上容不下兩個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不能有那個老啞僕,因為一個人躺著的時候,平底船上容不下兩個人。

passages.original: We must pall the barge all its length in blackest samite.
passages.vernacular: 我哋必須用最黑嘅錦緞把整條駁船全長罩住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們必須用最黑的錦緞把整條駁船全長罩住。

passages.original: That old black shawl of your mother’s will be just the thing, Diana.”
passages.vernacular: 你母親嗰條舊黑披肩正合適,黛安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你母親那條舊黑披肩正合適,黛安娜。」

passages.original: The black shawl having been procured, Anne spread it over the flat and then lay down on the bottom, with closed eyes and hands folded over her breast.
passages.vernacular: 黑披肩攞嚟喇,安妮把佢鋪喺平底船上,然後躺喺船底,閉住眼睛,雙手交疊喺胸前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黑披肩拿來了,安妮把它鋪在平底船上,然後躺在船底,閉著眼睛,雙手交疊在胸前。

passages.original: “Oh, she does look really dead,” whispered Ruby Gillis nervously, watching the still, white little face under the flickering shadows of the birches.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢睇起嚟真嘅死喇,」露比·吉利斯緊張地低聲講,睇住白樺閃爍嘅陰影下嗰張靜止蒼白嘅小臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,她看起來真的死了,」露比·吉利斯緊張地低聲說,看著白樺閃爍的陰影下那張靜止蒼白的小臉。

passages.original: “It makes me feel frightened, girls.
passages.vernacular: 「呢讓我害怕,女孩哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這讓我害怕,女孩們。

passages.original: Do you suppose it’s really right to act like this?
passages.vernacular: 你哋覺得咁樣演真嘅對嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們覺得這樣演真的對嗎?

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says that all play-acting is abominably wicked.”
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講,所有嘅扮演都係極度邪惡嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說,所有的扮演都是極度邪惡的。」

passages.original: “Ruby, you shouldn’t talk about Mrs. Lynde,” said Anne severely.
passages.vernacular: 「露比,你不該談林德太太,」安妮嚴厲地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「露比,你不該談林德太太,」安妮嚴厲地說。

passages.original: “It spoils the effect because this is hundreds of years before Mrs. Lynde was born.
passages.vernacular: 「呢破壞效果,因為呢個係林德太太出生前幾百年嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這破壞效果,因為這是林德太太出生前幾百年的事。

passages.original: Jane, you arrange this.
passages.vernacular: 簡,你嚟佈置呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡,你來佈置這個。

passages.original: It’s silly for Elaine to be talking when she’s dead.”
passages.vernacular: 艾蓮死咗仲講話好傻。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾蓮死了還說話很傻。」

passages.original: Jane rose to the occasion.
passages.vernacular: 簡臨危不亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡臨危不亂。

passages.original: Cloth of gold for coverlet there was none, but an old piano scarf of yellow Japanese crepe was an excellent substitute.
passages.vernacular: 金線布做嘅被子係冇嘅,但一條舊嘅黃色日本縐紗鋼琴罩係極好嘅替代品。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 金線布做的被子是沒有的,但一條舊的黃色日本縐紗鋼琴罩是極好的替代品。

passages.original: A white lily was not obtainable just then, but the effect of a tall blue iris placed in one of Anne’s folded hands was all that could be desired.
passages.vernacular: 白百合當時弄唔到,但把一朵高高嘅藍鳶尾花放喺安妮交疊嘅手裡,效果好得唔能夠再好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白百合當時弄不到,但把一朵高高的藍鳶尾花放在安妮交疊的手裡,效果好得不能再好。

passages.original: “Now, she’s all ready,” said Jane.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,佢準備好喇,」簡講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,她準備好了,」簡說。

passages.original: “We must kiss her quiet brows and, Diana, you say, ‘Sister, farewell forever,’ and Ruby, you say, ‘Farewell, sweet sister,’ both of you as sorrowfully as you possibly can.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋必須親吻佢安靜嘅眉頭,黛安娜,你講:『姐妹,永別喇』,露比,你講:『再見,親愛嘅姐妹』,你哋倆要儘可能悲傷地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們必須親吻她安靜的眉頭,黛安娜,你說:『姐妹,永別了』,露比,你說:『再見,親愛的姐妹』,你們倆要儘可能悲傷地說。

passages.original: Anne, for goodness sake smile a little.
passages.vernacular: 安妮,睇喺老天嘅份上,微笑啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮,看在老天的份上,微笑一點。

passages.original: You know Elaine ‘lay as though she smiled.’
passages.vernacular: 你知道艾蓮『躺住,彷彿帶住微笑』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道艾蓮『躺著,彷彿帶著微笑』。

passages.original: That’s better.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣好多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣好多了。

passages.original: Now push the flat off.”
passages.vernacular: 而家把平底船推出去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在把平底船推出去。」

passages.original: The flat was accordingly pushed off, scraping roughly over an old embedded stake in the process.
passages.vernacular: 於是平底船被推咗出去,喺呢個過程中,粗糙地刮過一根埋喺水里嘅舊木樁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是平底船被推了出去,在這個過程中,粗糙地刮過一根埋在水里的舊木樁。

passages.original: Diana and Jane and Ruby only waited long enough to see it caught in the current and headed for the bridge before scampering up through the woods, across the road, and down to the lower headland where, as Lancelot and Guinevere and the King, they were to be in readiness to receive the lily maid.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜、簡同露比只等咗足夠睇到佢被水流捉住、朝橋嘅方向漂去嘅時間,就奔跑住穿過樹林、橫過馬路,下到下游嘅岬角,喺嗰度,作為蘭斯洛特、格尼薇兒同國王,佢哋要準備好迎接百合少女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜、簡和露比只等了足夠看到它被水流捉住、朝橋的方向漂去的時間,就奔跑著穿過樹林、橫過馬路,下到下游的岬角,在那裡,作為蘭斯洛特、格尼薇兒和國王,她們要準備好迎接百合少女。

passages.original: For a few minutes Anne, drifting slowly down, enjoyed the romance of her situation to the full.
passages.vernacular: 有幾分鐘,安妮慢慢地漂下嚟,充分享受住佢處境嘅浪漫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有幾分鐘,安妮慢慢地漂下來,充分享受著她處境的浪漫。

passages.original: Then something happened not at all romantic.
passages.vernacular: 然後發生咗一件完全不浪漫嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後發生了一件完全不浪漫的事。

passages.original: The flat began to leak.
passages.vernacular: 平底船開始漏水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 平底船開始漏水。

passages.original: In a very few moments it was necessary for Elaine to scramble to her feet, pick up her cloth of gold coverlet and pall of blackest samite and gaze blankly at a big crack in the bottom of her barge through which the water was literally pouring.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒,艾蓮就唔得不爬起嚟,攞起佢嘅金線布被子同最黑嘅錦緞罩單,茫然地凝視住佢駁船底部嘅一道大裂縫,水正真嘅湧進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒,艾蓮就不得不爬起來,拿起她的金線布被子和最黑的錦緞罩單,茫然地凝視著她駁船底部的一道大裂縫,水正真的湧進來。

passages.original: That sharp stake at the landing had torn off the strip of batting nailed on the flat.
passages.vernacular: 登陸處嗰根尖尖嘅木樁,把釘喺平底船上嘅嗰條襯料撕掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 登陸處那根尖尖的木樁,把釘在平底船上的那條襯料撕掉了。

passages.original: Anne did not know this, but it did not take her long to realize that she was in a dangerous plight.
passages.vernacular: 安妮唔知道呢啲,但佢冇多久就意識到自己處境危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮不知道這一點,但她沒多久就意識到自己處境危險。

passages.original: At this rate the flat would fill and sink long before it could drift to the lower headland.
passages.vernacular: 照呢個速度,平底船會喺漂到下游岬角之前好久就灌滿水沉沒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 照這個速度,平底船會在漂到下游岬角之前很久就灌滿水沉沒。

passages.original: Where were the oars?
passages.vernacular: 槳喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 槳在哪裡?

passages.original: Left behind at the landing!
passages.vernacular: 留喺登陸處喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留在登陸處了!

passages.original: Anne gave one gasping little scream which nobody ever heard; she was white to the lips, but she did not lose her self-possession.
passages.vernacular: 安妮發出一聲喘息般嘅小小尖叫,冇人聽見;佢嘴唇都白喇,但冇失去鎮定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮發出一聲喘息般的小小尖叫,沒人聽見;她嘴唇都白了,但沒有失去鎮定。

passages.original: There was one chance--just one.
passages.vernacular: 有一個機會——只有一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一個機會——只有一個。

passages.original: “I was horribly frightened,” she told Mrs. Allan the next day, “and it seemed like years while the flat was drifting down to the bridge and the water rising in it every moment.
passages.vernacular: 「我嚇壞喇,」第二天佢對艾倫太太講,「平底船漂向橋嘅時候,水每時每刻都喺往上漲,感覺像過咗好多年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我嚇壞了,」第二天她對艾倫太太說,「平底船漂向橋的時候,水每時每刻都在往上漲,感覺像過了好多年。

passages.original: I prayed, Mrs. Allan, most earnestly, but I didn’t shut my eyes to pray, for I knew the only way God could save me was to let the flat float close enough to one of the bridge piles for me to climb up on it.
passages.vernacular: 我禱告喇,艾倫太太,好懇切,但我禱告時冇閉眼睛,因為我知道上帝能救我嘅唯一辦法係,讓平底船漂得離橋墩足夠近,讓我爬上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我禱告了,艾倫太太,非常懇切,但我禱告時沒有閉眼睛,因為我知道上帝能救我的唯一辦法是,讓平底船漂得離橋墩足夠近,讓我爬上去。

passages.original: You know the piles are just old tree trunks and there are lots of knots and old branch stubs on them.
passages.vernacular: 您知道橋墩只係舊樹幹,上面有好多節疤同舊樹枝樁子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道橋墩只是舊樹幹,上面有很多節疤和舊樹枝樁子。

passages.original: It was proper to pray, but I had to do my part by watching out and right well I knew it.
passages.vernacular: 禱告係對嘅,但我必須通過留神觀察嚟盡我嘅一份力,而且我好清楚呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 禱告是對的,但我必須通過留神觀察來盡我的一份力,而且我很清楚這一點。

passages.original: I just said, ‘Dear God, please take the flat close to a pile and I’ll do the rest,’ over and over again.
passages.vernacular: 我只係一遍又一遍地講:『親愛嘅上帝,請把平底船帶到橋墩旁,剩下嘅我嚟。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是一遍又一遍地說:『親愛的上帝,請把平底船帶到橋墩旁,剩下的我來。』

passages.original: Under such circumstances you don’t think much about making a flowery prayer.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢種情況下,你唔會想住做華麗嘅禱詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這種情況下,你不會想著做華麗的禱詞。

passages.original: But mine was answered, for the flat bumped right into a pile for a minute and I flung the scarf and the shawl over my shoulder and scrambled up on a big providential stub.
passages.vernacular: 但係我嘅禱告得到咗回應,因為平底船正好撞上咗一個橋墩有一會兒,我把披肩同被子甩到肩上,爬上咗一個巨大而合時嘅樁子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是我的禱告得到了回應,因為平底船正好撞上了一個橋墩有一會兒,我把披肩和被子甩到肩上,爬上了一個巨大而合時的樁子。

passages.original: And there I was, Mrs. Allan, clinging to that slippery old pile with no way of getting up or down.
passages.vernacular: 我就喺嗰兒,艾倫太太,抱住嗰根濕滑嘅舊橋墩,上不去都下不嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就在那兒,艾倫太太,抱著那根濕滑的舊橋墩,上不去也下不來。

passages.original: It was a very unromantic position, but I didn’t think about that at the time.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個好冇浪漫情調嘅位置,但我當時冇想嗰個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個非常沒有浪漫情調的位置,但我當時沒想那個。

passages.original: You don’t think much about romance when you have just escaped from a watery grave.
passages.vernacular: 你剛逃脫水中嘅墳墓時,唔會多想浪漫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你剛逃脫水中的墳墓時,不會多想浪漫。

passages.original: I said a grateful prayer at once and then I gave all my attention to holding on tight, for I knew I should probably have to depend on human aid to get back to dry land.”
passages.vernacular: 我即刻做咗一個感恩嘅禱告,然後我把全部注意力都放喺抓緊上,因為我知道我大概得依靠人嘅幫助才能回到乾地上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我立刻做了一個感恩的禱告,然後我把全部注意力都放在抓緊上,因為我知道我大概得依靠人的幫助才能回到乾地上。」

passages.original: The flat drifted under the bridge and then promptly sank in midstream.
passages.vernacular: 平底船漂到咗橋下,然後即刻喺河中心沉沒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 平底船漂到了橋下,然後立刻在河中心沉沒了。

passages.original: Ruby, Jane, and Diana, already awaiting it on the lower headland, saw it disappear before their very eyes and had not a doubt but that Anne had gone down with it.
passages.vernacular: 露比、簡同黛安娜已經喺下游岬角上等住,眼睜睜睇住佢消失,毫不懷疑安妮隨佢一起沉下去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比、簡和黛安娜已經在下游岬角上等著,眼睜睜看著它消失,毫不懷疑安妮隨它一起沉下去了。

passages.original: For a moment they stood still, white as sheets, frozen with horror at the tragedy; then, shrieking at the tops of their voices, they started on a frantic run up through the woods, never pausing as they crossed the main road to glance the way of the bridge.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋靜靜地站咗一會兒,臉色慘白,被悲劇嚇得僵住;然後佢哋扯住嗓子尖叫,開始瘋狂地向樹林上跑,過大路時都冇停下往橋嘅方向睇一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們靜靜地站了一會兒,臉色慘白,被悲劇嚇得僵住;然後她們扯著嗓子尖叫,開始瘋狂地向樹林上跑,過大路時也沒停下往橋的方向看一眼。

passages.original: Anne, clinging desperately to her precarious foothold, saw their flying forms and heard their shrieks.
passages.vernacular: 安妮拼命抓住佢危險嘅立足點,睇見佢哋飛奔嘅身影,聽到佢哋嘅尖叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮拼命抓著她危險的立足點,看見她們飛奔的身影,聽到她們的尖叫。

passages.original: Help would soon come, but meanwhile her position was a very uncomfortable one.
passages.vernacular: 幫助好快就會嚟,但同時佢嘅處境好不舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幫助很快就會來,但同時她的處境非常不舒服。

passages.original: The minutes passed by, each seeming an hour to the unfortunate lily maid.
passages.vernacular: 分分秒秒過去,對呢位不幸嘅百合少女來講,每一分鐘都像一個鐘頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 分分秒秒過去,對這位不幸的百合少女來說,每一分鐘都像一個鐘頭。

passages.original: Why didn’t somebody come?
passages.vernacular: 點解冇人嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼沒人來?

passages.original: Where had the girls gone?
passages.vernacular: 女孩哋去邊兒喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩們去哪兒了?

passages.original: Suppose they had fainted, one and all!
passages.vernacular: 假如佢哋全都昏過去咗呢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假如她們全都昏過去了呢!

passages.original: Suppose nobody ever came!
passages.vernacular: 假如永遠冇人嚟呢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假如永遠沒人來呢!

passages.original: Suppose she grew so tired and cramped that she could hold on no longer!
passages.vernacular: 假如佢累得抽筋,再都抓不住咗呢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假如她累得抽筋,再也抓不住了呢!

passages.original: Anne looked at the wicked green depths below her, wavering with long, oily shadows, and shivered.
passages.vernacular: 安妮睇住下面邪惡嘅綠色深處,搖晃住長長嘅油亮嘅影子,不禁打咗個寒顫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮看著下面邪惡的綠色深處,搖晃著長長的油亮的影子,不禁打了個寒顫。

passages.original: Her imagination began to suggest all manner of gruesome possibilities to her.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅想像力開始向佢暗示種種可怕嘅可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的想像力開始向她暗示種種可怕的可能。

passages.original: Then, just as she thought she really could not endure the ache in her arms and wrists another moment, Gilbert Blythe came rowing under the bridge in Harmon Andrews’s dory!
passages.vernacular: 然後,就喺佢覺得佢嘅手臂同手腕嘅疼痛真嘅再都忍受不了一分鐘時,吉爾伯特·布萊斯划住哈蒙·安德魯斯嘅小漁船從橋下過嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,就在她覺得她的手臂和手腕的疼痛真的再也忍受不了一分鐘時,吉爾伯特·布萊斯划著哈蒙·安德魯斯的小漁船從橋下過來了!

passages.original: Gilbert glanced up and, much to his amazement, beheld a little white scornful face looking down upon him with big, frightened but also scornful gray eyes.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特抬頭一睇,令佢大為食驚嘅係,睇到一張蒼白輕蔑嘅小臉喺低頭睇佢,一雙大大嘅、驚恐卻都輕蔑嘅灰眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特抬頭一看,令他大為吃驚的是,看到一張蒼白輕蔑的小臉在低頭看他,一雙大大的、驚恐卻也輕蔑的灰眼睛。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley!
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉!

passages.original: How on earth did you get there?” he exclaimed.
passages.vernacular: 你到底點到嗰兒嘅?」佢叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你到底怎麼到那兒的?」他叫道。

passages.original: Without waiting for an answer he pulled close to the pile and extended his hand.
passages.vernacular: 冇等回答,佢划近橋墩,伸出手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒等回答,他划近橋墩,伸出手。

passages.original: There was no help for it; Anne, clinging to Gilbert Blythe’s hand, scrambled down into the dory, where she sat, drabbled and furious, in the stern with her arms full of dripping shawl and wet crepe.
passages.vernacular: 冇辦法;安妮抓住吉爾伯特·布萊斯嘅手,爬下進咗小漁船,佢濕漉漉地、怒氣沖沖地坐喺船尾,懷裡抱住滴水嘅披肩同濕透嘅縐紗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有辦法;安妮抓著吉爾伯特·布萊斯的手,爬下進了小漁船,她濕漉漉地、怒氣沖沖地坐在船尾,懷裡抱著滴水的披肩和濕透的縐紗。

passages.original: It was certainly extremely difficult to be dignified under the circumstances!
passages.vernacular: 喺呢種情況下保持尊嚴確實極其困難!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這種情況下保持尊嚴確實極其困難!

passages.original: “What has happened, Anne?” asked Gilbert, taking up his oars.
passages.vernacular: 「發生咗乜嘢事,安妮?」吉爾伯特問,攞起咗槳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「發生了什麼事,安妮?」吉爾伯特問,拿起了槳。

passages.original: “We were playing Elaine,” explained Anne frigidly, without even looking at her rescuer, “and I had to drift down to Camelot in the barge--I mean the flat.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋喺演艾蓮,」安妮冷冰冰地解釋,甚至冇睇佢嘅救助者,「我得乘駁船——我係講平底船——漂到卡米洛特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們在演艾蓮,」安妮冷冰冰地解釋,甚至沒看她的救助者,「我得乘駁船——我是說平底船——漂到卡米洛特。

passages.original: The flat began to leak and I climbed out on the pile.
passages.vernacular: 平底船開始漏水,我爬上咗橋墩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 平底船開始漏水,我爬上了橋墩。

passages.original: The girls went for help.
passages.vernacular: 女孩哋去找人幫忙喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩們去找人幫忙了。

passages.original: Will you be kind enough to row me to the landing?”
passages.vernacular: 你能好心把我划到登陸處嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能好心把我划到登陸處嗎?」

passages.original: Gilbert obligingly rowed to the landing and Anne, disdaining assistance, sprang nimbly on shore.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特樂意地划到登陸處,安妮不屑被幫助,敏捷地跳上咗岸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特樂意地划到登陸處,安妮不屑被幫助,敏捷地跳上了岸。

passages.original: “I’m very much obliged to you,” she said haughtily as she turned away.
passages.vernacular: 「我好感謝你,」佢傲慢地講,轉身要走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我非常感謝你,」她傲慢地說,轉身要走。

passages.original: But Gilbert had also sprung from the boat and now laid a detaining hand on her arm.
passages.vernacular: 但吉爾伯特都從船上跳咗下嚟,而家把一隻手搭喺佢手臂上,留住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但吉爾伯特也從船上跳了下來,現在把一隻手搭在她手臂上,留住她。

passages.original: “Anne,” he said hurriedly, “look here.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,」佢匆忙地講,「聽住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,」他匆忙地說,「聽著。

passages.original: Can’t we be good friends?
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔能夠做好朋友嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不能做好朋友嗎?

passages.original: I’m awfully sorry I made fun of your hair that time.
passages.vernacular: 我為嗰次取笑你嘅頭髮好抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為那次取笑你的頭髮非常抱歉。

passages.original: I didn’t mean to vex you and I only meant it for a joke.
passages.vernacular: 我唔係故意惹你生氣,我只係開個玩笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是故意惹你生氣,我只是開個玩笑。

passages.original: Besides, it’s so long ago.
passages.vernacular: 再講,嗰個係好久以前嘅事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再說,那是很久以前的事了。

passages.original: I think your hair is awfully pretty now--honest I do.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得你嘅頭髮而家特別漂亮——真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得你的頭髮現在特別漂亮——真的。

passages.original: Let’s be friends.”
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋做朋友吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們做朋友吧。」

passages.original: For a moment Anne hesitated.
passages.vernacular: 有咁一會兒,安妮猶豫喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有那麼一會兒,安妮猶豫了。

passages.original: She had an odd, newly awakened consciousness under all her outraged dignity that the half-shy, half-eager expression in Gilbert’s hazel eyes was something that was very good to see.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢全部被冒犯嘅尊嚴之下,佢有一種奇怪嘅、新覺醒嘅意識:吉爾伯特榛色眼睛里嗰半羞怯半急切嘅神情,係一種睇起嚟好好嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她全部被冒犯的尊嚴之下,她有一種奇怪的、新覺醒的意識:吉爾伯特榛色眼睛里那半羞怯半急切的神情,是一種看起來非常好的東西。

passages.original: Her heart gave a quick, queer little beat.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅心好快地、奇怪地跳咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的心很快地、奇怪地跳了一下。

passages.original: But the bitterness of her old grievance promptly stiffened up her wavering determination.
passages.vernacular: 但舊怨嘅苦澀即刻讓佢動搖嘅決心變硬喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但舊怨的苦澀立刻讓她動搖的決心變硬了。

passages.original: That scene of two years before flashed back into her recollection as vividly as if it had taken place yesterday.
passages.vernacular: 兩年前嘅嗰一幕閃回到佢嘅記憶中,鮮明得好像係尋日發生嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩年前的那一幕閃回到她的記憶中,鮮明得好像是昨天發生的。

passages.original: Gilbert had called her “carrots” and had brought about her disgrace before the whole school.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特叫佢「胡蘿蔔」,並使佢喺全校面前丟咗臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特叫她「胡蘿蔔」,並使她在全校面前丟了臉。

passages.original: Her resentment, which to other and older people might be as laughable as its cause, was in no whit allayed and softened by time seemingly.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅怨恨,對其他更年長嘅人來講或者同佢嘅起因一樣可笑,似乎啲都冇被時間緩和同軟化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的怨恨,對其他更年長的人來說也許和它的起因一樣可笑,似乎一點也沒有被時間緩和與軟化。

passages.original: She hated Gilbert Blythe!
passages.vernacular: 佢恨吉爾伯特·布萊斯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她恨吉爾伯特·布萊斯!

passages.original: She would never forgive him!
passages.vernacular: 佢永遠唔會原諒佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她永遠不會原諒他!

passages.original: “No,” she said coldly, “I shall never be friends with you, Gilbert Blythe; and I don’t want to be!”
passages.vernacular: 「不,」佢冷冷地講,「我永遠唔會跟你做朋友,吉爾伯特·布萊斯;我都唔想!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」她冷冷地說,「我永遠不會跟你做朋友,吉爾伯特·布萊斯;我也不想!」

passages.original: “All right!”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧!」

passages.original: Gilbert sprang into his skiff with an angry color in his cheeks.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特跳進佢嘅小艇,臉頰上帶住憤怒嘅紅暈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特跳進他的小艇,臉頰上帶著憤怒的紅暈。

passages.original: “I’ll never ask you to be friends again, Anne Shirley.
passages.vernacular: 「我再都唔會要求你做朋友喇,安妮·雪莉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再也不會要求你做朋友了,安妮·雪莉。

passages.original: And I don’t care either!”
passages.vernacular: 我都不在乎!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不在乎!」

passages.original: He pulled away with swift defiant strokes, and Anne went up the steep, ferny little path under the maples.
passages.vernacular: 佢用迅疾而挑釁嘅划動遠去喇,安妮走上楓樹下陡峭嘅、長滿蕨類嘅小路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他用迅疾而挑釁的划動遠去了,安妮走上楓樹下陡峭的、長滿蕨類的小路。

passages.original: She held her head very high, but she was conscious of an odd feeling of regret.
passages.vernacular: 佢把頭抬得好高,但意識到一種奇怪嘅遺憾感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把頭抬得很高,但意識到一種奇怪的遺憾感。

passages.original: She almost wished she had answered Gilbert differently.
passages.vernacular: 佢幾乎希望自己對吉爾伯特嘅回答唔係嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她幾乎希望自己對吉爾伯特的回答不是那樣。

passages.original: Of course, he had insulted her terribly, but still--!
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢曾經嚴重地侮辱過佢,但定係——!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,他曾經嚴重地侮辱過她,但還是——!

passages.original: Altogether, Anne rather thought it would be a relief to sit down and have a good cry.
passages.vernacular: 總嘅來講,安妮覺得坐下嚟痛痛快快哭一場會係種寬慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總的來說,安妮覺得坐下來痛痛快快哭一場會是種寬慰。

passages.original: She was really quite unstrung, for the reaction from her fright and cramped clinging was making itself felt.
passages.vernacular: 佢真嘅好緊張,因為從恐懼同抽筋地緊抱中產生嘅反應正在顯現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她真的很緊張,因為從恐懼和抽筋地緊抱中產生的反應正在顯現。

passages.original: Halfway up the path she met Jane and Diana rushing back to the pond in a state narrowly removed from positive frenzy.
passages.vernacular: 走到小路一半,佢遇見咗簡同黛安娜,佢哋幾乎瘋狂地跑回池塘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走到小路一半,她遇見了簡和黛安娜,她們幾乎瘋狂地跑回池塘。

passages.original: They had found nobody at Orchard Slope, both Mr. and Mrs. Barry being away.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺果園坡冇找到人,巴里先生同太太都不喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們在果園坡沒找到人,巴里先生和太太都不在。

passages.original: Here Ruby Gillis had succumbed to hysterics, and was left to recover from them as best she might, while Jane and Diana flew through the Haunted Wood and across the brook to Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯喺呢度歇斯底里發作喇,被留下讓佢自己盡量恢復,而簡同黛安娜飛奔穿過鬧鬼林同小溪,到咗綠色屋頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯在這裡歇斯底里發作了,被留下讓她自己盡量恢復,而簡和黛安娜飛奔穿過鬧鬼林和小溪,到了綠色屋頂。

passages.original: There they had found nobody either, for Marilla had gone to Carmody and Matthew was making hay in the back field.
passages.vernacular: 嗰兒都冇找到人,因為瑪麗拉去咗卡莫迪,馬修喺後田裡割乾草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那兒也沒找到人,因為瑪麗拉去了卡莫迪,馬修在後田裡割乾草。

passages.original: “Oh, Anne,” gasped Diana, fairly falling on the former’s neck and weeping with relief and delight, “oh, Anne--we thought--you were--drowned--and we felt like murderers--because we had made--you be--Elaine.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,安妮,」黛安娜喘住氣講,簡直撲到前者嘅脖子上,因寬慰同喜悅而哭泣,「哦,安妮——我哋以為——你——淹死喇——我哋覺得像殺人犯——因為係我哋讓——你——演艾蓮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,安妮,」黛安娜喘著氣說,簡直撲到前者的脖子上,因寬慰和喜悅而哭泣,「哦,安妮——我們以為——你——淹死了——我們覺得像殺人犯——因為是我們讓——你——演艾蓮。

passages.original: And Ruby is in hysterics--oh, Anne, how did you escape?”
passages.vernacular: 露比歇斯底里喇——哦,安妮,你係點逃脫嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比歇斯底里了——哦,安妮,你是怎麼逃脫的?」

passages.original: “I climbed up on one of the piles,” explained Anne wearily, “and Gilbert Blythe came along in Mr. Andrews’s dory and brought me to land.”
passages.vernacular: 「我爬上咗一個橋墩,」安妮疲倦地解釋,「吉爾伯特·布萊斯划住安德魯斯先生嘅小漁船過嚟,把我送上咗岸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我爬上了一個橋墩,」安妮疲倦地解釋,「吉爾伯特·布萊斯划著安德魯斯先生的小漁船過來,把我送上了岸。」

passages.original: “Oh, Anne, how splendid of him!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,安妮,佢真棒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,安妮,他真棒!

passages.original: Why, it’s so romantic!” said Jane, finding breath enough for utterance at last.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,呢太浪漫喇!」簡講,終於喘過氣嚟能講話喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,這太浪漫了!」簡說,終於喘過氣來能說話了。

passages.original: “Of course you’ll speak to him after this.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然你以後要跟佢講話喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然你以後要跟他說話了。」

passages.original: “Of course I won’t,” flashed Anne, with a momentary return of her old spirit.
passages.vernacular: 「當然唔會,」安妮閃電般地講,舊日嘅精神一時回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不會,」安妮閃電般地說,舊日的精神一時回來了。

passages.original: “And I don’t want ever to hear the word ‘romantic’ again, Jane Andrews.
passages.vernacular: 「而且我唔想再聽到『浪漫』呢個詞喇,簡·安德魯斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且我不想再聽到『浪漫』這個詞了,簡·安德魯斯。

passages.original: I’m awfully sorry you were so frightened, girls.
passages.vernacular: 我為你哋嚇成嗰樣,感到好抱歉,女孩哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為你們嚇成那樣,感到非常抱歉,女孩們。

passages.original: It is all my fault.
passages.vernacular: 呢全係我嘅過錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這全是我的過錯。

passages.original: I feel sure I was born under an unlucky star.
passages.vernacular: 我肯定我係喺不吉利嘅星下出生嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我肯定我是在不吉利的星下出生的。

passages.original: Everything I do gets me or my dearest friends into a scrape.
passages.vernacular: 我做嘅每件事都使我或我最親愛嘅朋友惹上麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我做的每件事都使我或我最親愛的朋友惹上麻煩。

passages.original: We’ve gone and lost your father’s flat, Diana, and I have a presentiment that we’ll not be allowed to row on the pond any more.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋把你父親嘅平底船弄丟喇,黛安娜,我有預感,我哋唔會再被允許喺池塘上划船喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們把你父親的平底船弄丟了,黛安娜,我有預感,我們不會再被允許在池塘上划船了。」

passages.original: Anne’s presentiment proved more trustworthy than presentiments are apt to do.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅預感,比預感通常嘅情況準確得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的預感,比預感通常的情況準確得多。

passages.original: Great was the consternation in the Barry and Cuthbert households when the events of the afternoon became known.
passages.vernacular: 下午嘅事一傳開,巴里家同卡思伯特家一片驚慌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下午的事一傳開,巴里家和卡思伯特家一片驚慌。

passages.original: “Will you ever have any sense, Anne?” groaned Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「你乜嘢時候才會有點理智,安妮?」瑪麗拉呻吟道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你什麼時候才會有點理智,安妮?」瑪麗拉呻吟道。

passages.original: “Oh, yes, I think I will, Marilla,” returned Anne optimistically.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,我想我會嘅,瑪麗拉,」安妮樂觀地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,我想我會的,瑪麗拉,」安妮樂觀地回答。

passages.original: A good cry, indulged in the grateful solitude of the east gable, had soothed her nerves and restored her to her wonted cheerfulness.
passages.vernacular: 喺東山牆房間感恩嘅孤獨中好好地哭咗一場,安撫咗佢嘅神經,使佢恢復咗往常嘅快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在東山牆房間感恩的孤獨中好好地哭了一場,安撫了她的神經,使她恢復了往常的快樂。

passages.original: “I think my prospects of becoming sensible are brighter now than ever.”
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得我而家變得理智嘅前景比以往任何時候都更光明。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得我現在變得理智的前景比以往任何時候都更光明。」

passages.original: “I don’t see how,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇不出點會,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看不出怎麼會,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “Well,” explained Anne, “I’ve learned a new and valuable lesson today.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」安妮解釋道,「我今日學到咗新嘅寶貴嘅一課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」安妮解釋道,「我今天學到了新的寶貴的一課。

passages.original: Ever since I came to Green Gables I’ve been making mistakes, and each mistake has helped to cure me of some great shortcoming.
passages.vernacular: 自從我嚟到綠色屋頂,我一直喺犯錯,每一個錯誤都幫助我治好咗一個大缺點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從我來到綠色屋頂,我一直在犯錯,每一個錯誤都幫助我治好了一個大缺點。

passages.original: The affair of the amethyst brooch cured me of meddling with things that didn’t belong to me.
passages.vernacular: 紫水晶胸針嘅事治好咗我亂動不屬於我嘅嘢嘅毛病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紫水晶胸針的事治好了我亂動不屬於我的東西的毛病。

passages.original: The Haunted Wood mistake cured me of letting my imagination run away with me.
passages.vernacular: 鬧鬼林嘅錯誤治好咗我讓想像力失控嘅毛病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鬧鬼林的錯誤治好了我讓想像力失控的毛病。

passages.original: The liniment cake mistake cured me of carelessness in cooking.
passages.vernacular: 止痛擦劑蛋糕嘅錯誤治好咗我烹飪時粗心大意嘅毛病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 止痛擦劑蛋糕的錯誤治好了我烹飪時粗心大意的毛病。

passages.original: Dyeing my hair cured me of vanity.
passages.vernacular: 染頭髮治好咗我嘅虛榮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 染頭髮治好了我的虛榮。

passages.original: I never think about my hair and nose now--at least, very seldom.
passages.vernacular: 我而家唔再想我嘅頭髮同鼻子喇——至少好少想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在不再想我的頭髮和鼻子了——至少很少想。

passages.original: And today’s mistake is going to cure me of being too romantic.
passages.vernacular: 而今日嘅錯誤將治好我太浪漫嘅毛病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而今天的錯誤將治好我太浪漫的毛病。

passages.original: I have come to the conclusion that it is no use trying to be romantic in Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 我得出嘅結論係,喺阿文利試圖浪漫係冇用嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得出的結論是,在阿文利試圖浪漫是沒用的。

passages.original: It was probably easy enough in towered Camelot hundreds of years ago, but romance is not appreciated now.
passages.vernacular: 喺幾百年前有塔樓嘅卡米洛特大概好容易,但而家浪漫不受欣賞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在幾百年前有塔樓的卡米洛特大概很容易,但現在浪漫不受欣賞。

passages.original: I feel quite sure that you will soon see a great improvement in me in this respect, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 我肯定,瑪麗拉,您好快就會睇到我喺呢方面有好大嘅進步。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我肯定,瑪麗拉,您很快就會看到我在這方面有很大的進步。」

passages.original: “I’m sure I hope so,” said Marilla skeptically.
passages.vernacular: 「我當然希望如此,」瑪麗拉懷疑地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我當然希望如此,」瑪麗拉懷疑地說。

passages.original: But Matthew, who had been sitting mutely in his corner, laid a hand on Anne’s shoulder when Marilla had gone out.
passages.vernacular: 但馬修,佢一直默默地坐喺佢嘅角落裡,瑪麗拉出去後,把一隻手放喺安妮肩上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但馬修,他一直默默地坐在他的角落裡,瑪麗拉出去後,把一隻手放在安妮肩上。

passages.original: “Don’t give up all your romance, Anne,” he whispered shyly, “a little of it is a good thing--not too much, of course--but keep a little of it, Anne, keep a little of it.”
passages.vernacular: 「別放棄你所有嘅浪漫,安妮,」佢害羞地低聲講,「啲點係好事——當然唔好太多——但保留啲,安妮,保留啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別放棄你所有的浪漫,安妮,」他害羞地低聲說,「一點點是好事——當然不要太多——但保留一點,安妮,保留一點。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXIX An Epoch in Anne's Life 第二十九章:安妮生命中的新紀元

passages.original: CH ANNE was bringing the cows home from the back pasture by way of Lover’s Lane.
passages.vernacular: 安妮正沿住情人小徑把牛從後牧場趕回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮正沿著情人小徑把牛從後牧場趕回家。

passages.original: It was a September evening and all the gaps and clearings in the woods were brimmed up with ruby sunset light.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係九月嘅一個傍晚,樹林裡所有嘅缺口同空地都盈滿咗紅寶石色嘅落日餘暉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是九月的一個傍晚,樹林裡所有的缺口和空地都盈滿了紅寶石色的落日餘暉。

passages.original: Here and there the lane was splashed with it, but for the most part it was already quite shadowy beneath the maples, and the spaces under the firs were filled with a clear violet dusk like airy wine.
passages.vernacular: 小路呢度嗰度被佢濺染,但大部分地方,楓樹下已經相當陰暗,而冷杉下嘅空間則充滿咗清澈嘅紫羅蘭色暮靄,像空靈嘅美酒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小路這裡那裡被它濺染,但大部分地方,楓樹下已經相當陰暗,而冷杉下的空間則充滿了清澈的紫羅蘭色暮靄,像空靈的美酒。

passages.original: The winds were out in their tops, and there is no sweeter music on earth than that which the wind makes in the fir trees at evening.
passages.vernacular: 風喺樹梢上蕩漾,世上冇比傍晚時風喺冷杉林中演奏嘅音樂更甜美嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風在樹梢上蕩漾,世上沒有比傍晚時風在冷杉林中演奏的音樂更甜美的了。

passages.original: The cows swung placidly down the lane, and Anne followed them dreamily, repeating aloud the battle canto from Marmion--which had also been part of their English course the preceding winter and which Miss Stacy had made them learn off by heart--and exulting in its rushing lines and the clash of spears in its imagery.
passages.vernacular: 牛群平靜地搖擺住走下小巷,安妮夢幻般地跟喺後面,大聲背誦住《馬密恩》中嘅戰鬥詩章——嗰都係去年冬天佢哋英語課程嘅一部分,斯泰西小姐讓佢哋背得滾瓜爛熟——為佢奔湧嘅詩行同意象中長矛嘅撞擊而歡欣鼓舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牛群平靜地搖擺著走下小巷,安妮夢幻般地跟在後面,大聲背誦著《馬密恩》中的戰鬥詩章——那也是去年冬天他們英語課程的一部分,斯泰西小姐讓他們背得滾瓜爛熟——為它奔湧的詩行和意象中長矛的撞擊而歡欣鼓舞。

passages.original: When she came to the lines
passages.vernacular: 當佢念到嗰幾行
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當她念到那幾行

passages.original: The stubborn spearsmen still made good Their dark impenetrable wood,
passages.vernacular: 頑強嘅槍兵依然堅守,佢哋嗰片黑暗不可穿透嘅樹林,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頑強的槍兵依然堅守,他們那片黑暗不可穿透的樹林,

passages.original: she stopped in ecstasy to shut her eyes that she might the better fancy herself one of that heroic ring.
passages.vernacular: 佢狂喜地停下,閉上眼睛,以便更好地幻想自己係嗰英雄圈中嘅一員。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她狂喜地停下,閉上眼睛,以便更好地幻想自己是那英雄圈中的一員。

passages.original: When she opened them again it was to behold Diana coming through the gate that led into the Barry field and looking so important that Anne instantly divined there was news to be told.
passages.vernacular: 佢再睜開眼時,睇見黛安娜正穿過通向巴里家田地嘅柵欄門走嚟,神情咁鄭重其事,安妮即刻猜到有新聞要講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她再睜開眼時,看見黛安娜正穿過通向巴里家田地的柵欄門走來,神情那麼鄭重其事,安妮立刻猜到有新聞要說。

passages.original: But betray too eager curiosity she would not.
passages.vernacular: 但佢唔肯顯得過分急切好奇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她不肯顯得過分急切好奇。

passages.original: “Isn’t this evening just like a purple dream, Diana?
passages.vernacular: 「呢個傍晚唔係像一個紫色嘅夢嗎,黛安娜?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個傍晚不是像一個紫色的夢嗎,黛安娜?

passages.original: It makes me so glad to be alive.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓我活住咁高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它讓我活著這麼高興。

passages.original: In the mornings I always think the mornings are best; but when evening comes I think it’s lovelier still.”
passages.vernacular: 早晨我總是覺得早晨最好;但到咗傍晚,我又覺得佢更可愛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨我總是覺得早晨最好;但到了傍晚,我又覺得它更可愛。」

passages.original: “It’s a very fine evening,” said Diana, “but oh, I have such news, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係個好好嘅傍晚,」黛安娜講,「不過,哦,我有咁樣嘅消息,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是個很好的傍晚,」黛安娜說,「不過,哦,我有這樣的消息,安妮。

passages.original: Guess.
passages.vernacular: 猜猜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猜猜。

passages.original: You can have three guesses.”
passages.vernacular: 你可以猜三次。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以猜三次。」

passages.original: “Charlotte Gillis is going to be married in the church after all and Mrs. Allan wants us to decorate it,” cried Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「夏洛特·吉利斯終究要喺教堂結婚喇,艾倫太太要我哋去裝飾佢,」安妮叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夏洛特·吉利斯終究要在教堂結婚了,艾倫太太要我們去裝飾它,」安妮叫道。

passages.original: “No. Charlotte’s beau won’t agree to that, because nobody ever has been married in the church yet, and he thinks it would seem too much like a funeral.
passages.vernacular: 「不。夏洛特嘅情郎不同意,因為教堂裡仲從冇人結過婚,佢覺得嗰會太像葬禮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不。夏洛特的情郎不同意,因為教堂裡還從沒有人結過婚,他覺得那會太像葬禮。

passages.original: It’s too mean, because it would be such fun.
passages.vernacular: 呢太卑鄙喇,因為嗰樣會好好玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這太卑鄙了,因為那樣會很好玩。

passages.original: Guess again.”
passages.vernacular: 再猜一次。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再猜一次。」

passages.original: “Jane’s mother is going to let her have a birthday party?”
passages.vernacular: 「簡嘅媽媽要讓佢辦生日派對?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「簡的媽媽要讓她辦生日派對?」

passages.original: Diana shook her head, her black eyes dancing with merriment.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜搖搖頭,黑眼睛因歡快而跳動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜搖搖頭,黑眼睛因歡快而跳動。

passages.original: “I can’t think what it can be,” said Anne in despair, “unless it’s that Moody Spurgeon MacPherson saw you home from prayer meeting last night.
passages.vernacular: 「我想不出會係乜嘢,」安妮絕望地講,「除非係穆迪·斯珀吉翁·麥克弗森琴晚祈禱會後送你回家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想不出會是什麼,」安妮絕望地說,「除非是穆迪·斯珀吉翁·麥克弗森昨晚祈禱會後送你回家了。

passages.original: Did he?”
passages.vernacular: 佢送咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他送了嗎?」

passages.original: “I should think not,” exclaimed Diana indignantly.
passages.vernacular: 「我想唔會,」黛安娜憤憤地叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想不會,」黛安娜憤憤地叫道。

passages.original: “I wouldn’t be likely to boast of it if he did, the horrid creature!
passages.vernacular: 「就算佢送喇,我都不大可能誇耀,嗰個討厭嘅傢伙!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就算他送了,我也不大可能誇耀,那個討厭的傢伙!

passages.original: I knew you couldn’t guess it.
passages.vernacular: 我知道你猜不出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道你猜不出。

passages.original: Mother had a letter from Aunt Josephine today, and Aunt Josephine wants you and me to go to town next Tuesday and stop with her for the Exhibition.
passages.vernacular: 媽媽今日收到約瑟芬姑婆嘅一封信,約瑟芬姑婆想讓你同我下星期二進城,喺佢嗰兒住下,去睇博覽會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 媽媽今天收到約瑟芬姑婆的一封信,約瑟芬姑婆想讓你和我下星期二進城,在她那兒住下,去看博覽會。

passages.original: There!”
passages.vernacular: 就係咁樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這樣!」

passages.original: “Oh, Diana,” whispered Anne, finding it necessary to lean up against a maple tree for support, “do you really mean it?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,黛安娜,」安妮低聲講,覺得有必要靠喺楓樹上支撐自己,「你真係認真嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,黛安娜,」安妮低聲說,覺得有必要靠在楓樹上支撐自己,「你真是認真的嗎?

passages.original: But I’m afraid Marilla won’t let me go.
passages.vernacular: 不過我怕瑪麗拉唔會讓我去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我怕瑪麗拉不會讓我去。

passages.original: She will say that she can’t encourage gadding about.
passages.vernacular: 佢會講佢唔能夠鼓勵到處閒逛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會說她不能鼓勵到處閒逛。

passages.original: That was what she said last week when Jane invited me to go with them in their double-seated buggy to the American concert at the White Sands Hotel.
passages.vernacular: 上星期簡邀請我坐佢哋嘅雙座馬車去白沙旅館嘅美國人音樂會,佢就係咁講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上星期簡邀請我坐他們的雙座馬車去白沙旅館的美國人音樂會,她就是這麼說的。

passages.original: I wanted to go, but Marilla said I’d be better at home learning my lessons and so would Jane.
passages.vernacular: 我想去,但瑪麗拉講我待喺家裡學功課更好,簡都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想去,但瑪麗拉說我待在家裡學功課更好,簡也是。

passages.original: I was bitterly disappointed, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 我好失望,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我非常失望,黛安娜。

passages.original: I felt so heartbroken that I wouldn’t say my prayers when I went to bed.
passages.vernacular: 我心都碎喇,上床時都唔肯做禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我心都碎了,上床時都不肯做禱告。

passages.original: But I repented of that and got up in the middle of the night and said them.”
passages.vernacular: 但我後悔喇,半夜起嚟把禱告做喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我後悔了,半夜起來把禱告做了。」

passages.original: “I’ll tell you,” said Diana, “we’ll get Mother to ask Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「我告訴你,」黛安娜講,「我哋讓媽媽去問瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我告訴你,」黛安娜說,「我們讓媽媽去問瑪麗拉。

passages.original: She’ll be more likely to let you go then; and if she does we’ll have the time of our lives, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 嗰樣佢更可能讓你去;如果佢讓,我哋會玩得開心死喇,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那樣她更可能讓你去;如果她讓,我們會玩得開心死了,安妮。

passages.original: I’ve never been to an Exhibition, and it’s so aggravating to hear the other girls talking about their trips.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇去過博覽會,聽別嘅女孩談論佢哋嘅旅行,太氣人喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒去過博覽會,聽別的女孩談論她們的旅行,太氣人了。

passages.original: Jane and Ruby have been twice, and they’re going this year again.”
passages.vernacular: 簡同露比去過兩次,今年仲要去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡和露比去過兩次,今年還要去。」

passages.original: “I’m not going to think about it at all until I know whether I can go or not,” said Anne resolutely.
passages.vernacular: 「喺知道我能唔能夠去之前,我完全不去想佢,」安妮堅決地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在知道我能不能去之前,我完全不去想它,」安妮堅決地說。

passages.original: “If I did and then was disappointed, it would be more than I could bear.
passages.vernacular: 「如果我想咗然後又失望,我承受不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我想了然後又失望,我承受不了。

passages.original: But in case I do go I’m very glad my new coat will be ready by that time.
passages.vernacular: 但萬一我去嘅話,我好高興嗰時我嘅新外套會做好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但萬一我去的話,我很高興那時我的新外套會做好。

passages.original: Marilla didn’t think I needed a new coat.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉不認為我需要新外套。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉不認為我需要新外套。

passages.original: She said my old one would do very well for another winter and that I ought to be satisfied with having a new dress.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我嘅舊外套再穿一個冬天都冇問題,我應該滿足於有咗一條新裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我的舊外套再穿一個冬天也沒問題,我應該滿足於有了一條新裙子。

passages.original: The dress is very pretty, Diana--navy blue and made so fashionably.
passages.vernacular: 嗰條裙子好漂亮,黛安娜——藏青色,做得咁時髦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那條裙子很漂亮,黛安娜——藏青色,做得那麼時髦。

passages.original: Marilla always makes my dresses fashionably now, because she says she doesn’t intend to have Matthew going to Mrs. Lynde to make them.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉而家總是把我嘅裙子做得時髦,因為佢講佢不打算讓馬修去找林德太太做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉現在總是把我的裙子做得時髦,因為她說她不打算讓馬修去找林德太太做。

passages.original: I’m so glad.
passages.vernacular: 我太高興喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興了。

passages.original: It is ever so much easier to be good if your clothes are fashionable.
passages.vernacular: 如果你嘅衣服時髦,做好人容易多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你的衣服時髦,做好人容易多了。

passages.original: At least, it is easier for me.
passages.vernacular: 至少對我來講容易多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少對我來說容易多了。

passages.original: I suppose it doesn’t make such a difference to naturally good people.
passages.vernacular: 我想對天生善良嘅人冇咁大嘅差別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想對天生善良的人沒有那麼大的差別。

passages.original: But Matthew said I must have a new coat, so Marilla bought a lovely piece of blue broadcloth, and it’s being made by a real dressmaker over at Carmody.
passages.vernacular: 但馬修講我必須有一件新外套,所以瑪麗拉買咗一塊可愛嘅藍色闊幅呢,由卡莫迪嘅一位真正嘅裁縫喺做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但馬修說我必須有一件新外套,所以瑪麗拉買了一塊可愛的藍色闊幅呢,由卡莫迪的一位真正的裁縫在做。

passages.original: It’s to be done Saturday night, and I’m trying not to imagine myself walking up the church aisle on Sunday in my new suit and cap, because I’m afraid it isn’t right to imagine such things.
passages.vernacular: 星期六晚上做好,我努力不去想像自己星期天穿住新套裝戴住帽子走喺教堂過道上,因為我怕想像呢種事不對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期六晚上做好,我努力不去想像自己星期天穿著新套裝戴著帽子走在教堂過道上,因為我怕想像這種事不對。

passages.original: But it just slips into my mind in spite of me.
passages.vernacular: 但佢不由自主地鑽進我嘅腦子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它不由自主地鑽進我的腦子。

passages.original: My cap is so pretty.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅帽子咁漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的帽子那麼漂亮。

passages.original: Matthew bought it for me the day we were over at Carmody.
passages.vernacular: 係馬修喺我哋去卡莫迪嗰天畀我買嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是馬修在我們去卡莫迪那天給我買的。

passages.original: It is one of those little blue velvet ones that are all the rage, with gold cord and tassels.
passages.vernacular: 係嗰種而家特別流行嘅藍色天鵝絨小帽,帶金色飾繩同流蘇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是那種現在特別流行的藍色天鵝絨小帽,帶金色飾繩和流蘇。

passages.original: Your new hat is elegant, Diana, and so becoming.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅新帽子好高雅,黛安娜,特別合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的新帽子很高雅,黛安娜,特別合適。

passages.original: When I saw you come into church last Sunday my heart swelled with pride to think you were my dearest friend.
passages.vernacular: 上個星期天我睇你走進教堂時,想到你係我最親愛嘅朋友,我嘅心充滿咗自豪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上個星期天我看你走進教堂時,想到你是我最親愛的朋友,我的心充滿了自豪。

passages.original: Do you suppose it’s wrong for us to think so much about our clothes?
passages.vernacular: 你覺得我哋咁多地想我哋嘅衣服係唔係錯嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你覺得我們這麼多地想我們的衣服是不是錯的?

passages.original: Marilla says it is very sinful.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉講嗰好有罪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉說那非常有罪。

passages.original: But it is such an interesting subject, isn’t it?”
passages.vernacular: 但呢個係個咁有趣嘅話題,唔係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這是個這麼有趣的話題,不是嗎?」

passages.original: Marilla agreed to let Anne go to town, and it was arranged that Mr. Barry should take the girls in on the following Tuesday.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉同意讓安妮進城,並安排巴里先生下週二帶女孩哋進城。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉同意讓安妮進城,並安排巴里先生下週二帶女孩們進城。

passages.original: As Charlottetown was thirty miles away and Mr. Barry wished to go and return the same day, it was necessary to make a very early start.
passages.vernacular: 因為夏洛特敦喺三十英里外,巴里先生希望當天嚟回,所以必須好早出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為夏洛特敦在三十英里外,巴里先生希望當天來回,所以必須很早出發。

passages.original: But Anne counted it all joy, and was up before sunrise on Tuesday morning.
passages.vernacular: 但安妮把一切都算作快樂,星期二早晨日出前就起咗床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安妮把一切都算作快樂,星期二早晨日出前就起了床。

passages.original: A glance from her window assured her that the day would be fine, for the eastern sky behind the firs of the Haunted Wood was all silvery and cloudless.
passages.vernacular: 從窗口睇咗一眼,佢確信嗰天天氣會好好,因為鬧鬼林冷杉後面嘅東方天空一片銀色,萬里無雲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從窗口看了一眼,她確信那天天氣會很好,因為鬧鬼林冷杉後面的東方天空一片銀色,萬里無雲。

passages.original: Through the gap in the trees a light was shining in the western gable of Orchard Slope, a token that Diana was also up.
passages.vernacular: 穿過樹林嘅缺口,果園坡西山牆里亮住一盞燈,表明黛安娜都起嚟喇。
