passages.vernacularMandarin: 穿過樹林的缺口,果園坡西山牆里亮著一盞燈,表明黛安娜也起來了。

passages.original: Anne was dressed by the time Matthew had the fire on and had the breakfast ready when Marilla came down, but for her own part was much too excited to eat.
passages.vernacular: 馬修生火、瑪麗拉下樓時,安妮已經穿好衣服,早飯準備好喇,但佢自己太興奮,食不下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修生火、瑪麗拉下樓時,安妮已經穿好衣服,早飯準備好了,但她自己太興奮,吃不下。

passages.original: After breakfast the jaunty new cap and jacket were donned, and Anne hastened over the brook and up through the firs to Orchard Slope.
passages.vernacular: 早飯後穿上咗俏皮嘅新帽子同夾克,安妮匆匆越過小溪,穿過冷杉林,上咗果園坡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早飯後穿上了俏皮的新帽子和夾克,安妮匆匆越過小溪,穿過冷杉林,上了果園坡。

passages.original: Mr. Barry and Diana were waiting for her, and they were soon on the road.
passages.vernacular: 巴里先生同黛安娜喺等住佢,佢哋好快就上路喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里先生和黛安娜在等著她,他們很快就上路了。

passages.original: It was a long drive, but Anne and Diana enjoyed every minute of it.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一段漫長嘅路程,但安妮同黛安娜享受每一分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一段漫長的路程,但安妮和黛安娜享受每一分鐘。

passages.original: It was delightful to rattle along over the moist roads in the early red sunlight that was creeping across the shorn harvest fields.
passages.vernacular: 喺潮濕嘅路上轔轔前行,爬過收割後嘅田野嘅紅色早晨陽光中,真係愉快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在潮濕的路上轔轔前行,爬過收割後的田野的紅色早晨陽光中,真是愉快。

passages.original: The air was fresh and crisp, and little smoke-blue mists curled through the valleys and floated off from the hills.
passages.vernacular: 空氣新鮮而清爽,小片煙藍色嘅薄霧喺山谷間盤繞,從山上飄走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 空氣新鮮而清爽,小片煙藍色的薄霧在山谷間盤繞,從山上飄走。

passages.original: Sometimes the road went through woods where maples were beginning to hang out scarlet banners; sometimes it crossed rivers on bridges that made Anne’s flesh cringe with the old, half-delightful fear; sometimes it wound along a harbor shore and passed by a little cluster of weather-gray fishing huts; again it mounted to hills whence a far sweep of curving upland or misty-blue sky could be seen; but wherever it went there was much of interest to discuss.
passages.vernacular: 有時路穿過楓樹開始掛出猩紅旗幟嘅樹林;有時佢跨過河流上嘅橋,讓安妮因舊日嗰種半係愉快嘅恐懼而起雞皮疙瘩;有時佢沿住港灣岸邊蜿蜒,經過一小群風化成灰色嘅漁棚;又一次佢爬上山丘,從嗰度可以睇到遠處彎曲嘅高地或蔚藍嘅薄霧天空;但無論佢到邊兒,都有好多有趣嘅事可談。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時路穿過楓樹開始掛出猩紅旗幟的樹林;有時它跨過河流上的橋,讓安妮因舊日那種半是愉快的恐懼而起雞皮疙瘩;有時它沿著港灣岸邊蜿蜒,經過一小群風化成灰色的漁棚;又一次它爬上山丘,從那裡可以看到遠處彎曲的高地或蔚藍的薄霧天空;但無論它到哪兒,都有很多有趣的事可談。

passages.original: It was almost noon when they reached town and found their way to “Beechwood.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋到達城裡找到「山毛櫸莊」時,已近中午。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們到達城裡找到「山毛櫸莊」時,已近中午。

passages.original: It was quite a fine old mansion, set back from the street in a seclusion of green elms and branching beeches.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一座相當漂亮嘅老宅,退喺街後面,隱蔽喺綠色榆樹同分叉嘅山毛櫸中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一座相當漂亮的老宅,退在街後面,隱蔽在綠色榆樹和分叉的山毛櫸中。

passages.original: Miss Barry met them at the door with a twinkle in her sharp black eyes.
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐喺門口迎接佢哋,尖銳嘅黑眼睛裡閃爍住光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐在門口迎接他們,尖銳的黑眼睛裡閃爍著光。

passages.original: “So you’ve come to see me at last, you Anne-girl,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋終於嚟睇我喇,你呢個安妮丫頭,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們終於來看我了,你這個安妮丫頭,」她說。

passages.original: “Mercy, child, how you have grown!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,細路,你長高咗多少!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,孩子,你長高了多少!

passages.original: You’re taller than I am, I declare.
passages.vernacular: 我敢講你比我仲高喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢說你比我還高了。

passages.original: And you’re ever so much better-looking than you used to be, too.
passages.vernacular: 而且你都比以前好睇多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且你也比以前好看多了。

passages.original: But I dare say you know that without being told.”
passages.vernacular: 但我敢講唔使別人告訴你,你自己都知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我敢說不用別人告訴你,你自己也知道。」

passages.original: “Indeed I didn’t,” said Anne radiantly.
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅唔知道,」安妮容光煥發地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的不知道,」安妮容光煥發地說。

passages.original: “I know I’m not so freckled as I used to be, so I’ve much to be thankful for, but I really hadn’t dared to hope there was any other improvement.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道我不像以前咁長雀斑喇,所以我有許多該感恩嘅,但我真嘅唔敢希望仲有其他嘅改善。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道我不像以前那麼長雀斑了,所以我有許多該感恩的,但我真的不敢希望還有其他的改善。

passages.original: I’m so glad you think there is, Miss Barry.”
passages.vernacular: 您認為有,我太高興喇,巴里小姐。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您認為有,我太高興了,巴里小姐。」

passages.original: Miss Barry’s house was furnished with “great magnificence,” as Anne told Marilla afterward.
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐嘅房子布置得「極其華麗」,安妮後來對瑪麗拉咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐的房子布置得「極其華麗」,安妮後來對瑪麗拉這麼說。

passages.original: The two little country girls were rather abashed by the splendor of the parlor where Miss Barry left them when she went to see about dinner.
passages.vernacular: 兩個鄉下小女孩被客廳嘅輝煌弄得有點窘,巴里小姐去睇晚飯時把佢哋留喺嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個鄉下小女孩被客廳的輝煌弄得有點窘,巴里小姐去看晚飯時把她們留在那兒。

passages.original: “Isn’t it just like a palace?” whispered Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「呢唔係就像宮殿嗎?」黛安娜低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這不是就像宮殿嗎?」黛安娜低聲說。

passages.original: “I never was in Aunt Josephine’s house before, and I’d no idea it was so grand.
passages.vernacular: 「我以前從冇到過約瑟芬姑婆嘅家,都唔知道咁氣派。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以前從沒到過約瑟芬姑婆的家,也不知道這麼氣派。

passages.original: I just wish Julia Bell could see this--she puts on such airs about her mother’s parlor.”
passages.vernacular: 我真希望朱莉婭·貝爾能睇到呢個——佢對佢媽媽嘅客廳擺咁大架子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望朱莉婭·貝爾能看到這個——她對她媽媽的客廳擺那麼大架子。」

passages.original: “Velvet carpet,” sighed Anne luxuriously, “and silk curtains!
passages.vernacular: 「天鵝絨地毯,」安妮奢華地嘆道,「仲有絲綢窗簾!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天鵝絨地毯,」安妮奢華地嘆道,「還有絲綢窗簾!

passages.original: I’ve dreamed of such things, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 我夢想過咁樣嘅嘢,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我夢想過這樣的東西,黛安娜。

passages.original: But do you know I don’t believe I feel very comfortable with them after all.
passages.vernacular: 但你知道嗎,我覺得終究不太舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你知道嗎,我覺得終究不太舒服。

passages.original: There are so many things in this room and all so splendid that there is no scope for imagination.
passages.vernacular: 呢房間里有咁多嘢,都咁華麗,冇想像嘅餘地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這房間里有那麼多東西,都那麼華麗,沒有想像的餘地。

passages.original: That is one consolation when you are poor--there are so many more things you can imagine about.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係窮嘅時候嘅一個安慰——有咁多更多嘅嘢可以去想像。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是窮的時候的一個安慰——有那麼多更多的東西可以去想像。」

passages.original: Their sojourn in town was something that Anne and Diana dated from for years.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺城裡嘅逗留,安妮同黛安娜以後多年都攞佢嚟紀年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們在城裡的逗留,安妮和黛安娜以後多年都拿它來紀年。

passages.original: From first to last it was crowded with delights.
passages.vernacular: 從頭到尾佢都充滿咗歡樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從頭到尾它都充滿了歡樂。

passages.original: On Wednesday Miss Barry took them to the Exhibition grounds and kept them there all day.
passages.vernacular: 星期三,巴里小姐帶佢哋去博覽會場地,整天待喺嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期三,巴里小姐帶她們去博覽會場地,整天待在那兒。

passages.original: “It was splendid,” Anne related to Marilla later on.
passages.vernacular: 「太棒喇,」後來安妮對瑪麗拉講述。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太棒了,」後來安妮對瑪麗拉講述。

passages.original: “I never imagined anything so interesting.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇想像過有咁有趣嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒想像過有這麼有趣的東西。

passages.original: I don’t really know which department was the most interesting.
passages.vernacular: 我真唔知道邊個展區最有趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真不知道哪個展區最有趣。

passages.original: I think I liked the horses and the flowers and the fancywork best.
passages.vernacular: 我想我最鍾意馬、花同手工藝品。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我最喜歡馬、花和手工藝品。

passages.original: Josie Pye took first prize for knitted lace.
passages.vernacular: 喬西·派伊獲得咗編織蕾絲嘅一等獎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西·派伊獲得了編織蕾絲的一等獎。

passages.original: I was real glad she did.
passages.vernacular: 我真高興佢得獎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真高興她得獎了。

passages.original: And I was glad that I felt glad, for it shows I’m improving, don’t you think, Marilla, when I can rejoice in Josie’s success?
passages.vernacular: 而且我好高興我感到高興,因為呢講明我喺進步,您講呢,瑪麗拉,我能為喬西嘅成功而高興?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我很高興我感到高興,因為這說明我在進步,您說呢,瑪麗拉,我能為喬西的成功而高興?

passages.original: Mr. Harmon Andrews took second prize for Gravenstein apples and Mr. Bell took first prize for a pig.
passages.vernacular: 哈蒙·安德魯斯先生獲得咗格拉文斯坦蘋果嘅二等獎,貝爾先生獲得咗豬嘅一等獎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈蒙·安德魯斯先生獲得了格拉文斯坦蘋果的二等獎,貝爾先生獲得了豬的一等獎。

passages.original: Diana said she thought it was ridiculous for a Sunday-school superintendent to take a prize in pigs, but I don’t see why.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜講佢覺得一個主日學校督導得豬嘅獎好可笑,但我不明白點解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜說她覺得一個主日學校督導得豬的獎很可笑,但我不明白為什麼。

passages.original: Do you?
passages.vernacular: 您明白嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您明白嗎?

passages.original: She said she would always think of it after this when he was praying so solemnly.
passages.vernacular: 佢講以後佢咁嚴肅地禱告時,佢總會想到呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說以後他那麼嚴肅地禱告時,她總會想到這個。

passages.original: Clara Louise MacPherson took a prize for painting, and Mrs. Lynde got first prize for homemade butter and cheese.
passages.vernacular: 克拉拉·路易絲·麥克弗森獲得咗繪畫獎,林德太太獲得咗自製黃油同乳酪嘅一等獎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 克拉拉·路易絲·麥克弗森獲得了繪畫獎,林德太太獲得了自製黃油和乳酪的一等獎。

passages.original: So Avonlea was pretty well represented, wasn’t it?
passages.vernacular: 所以阿文利有相當好嘅代表,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以阿文利有相當好的代表,是不是?

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde was there that day, and I never knew how much I really liked her until I saw her familiar face among all those strangers.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太嗰天喺嗰兒,我直到喺所有嗰啲陌生人中睇到佢熟悉嘅臉,才知道我有多鍾意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太那天在那兒,我直到在所有那些陌生人中看到她熟悉的臉,才知道我有多喜歡她。

passages.original: There were thousands of people there, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 嗰兒有成千上萬嘅人,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那兒有成千上萬的人,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: It made me feel dreadfully insignificant.
passages.vernacular: 呢讓我覺得自己渺小得可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這讓我覺得自己渺小得可怕。

passages.original: And Miss Barry took us up to the grandstand to see the horse races.
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐仲帶我哋上咗睇臺睇賽馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐還帶我們上了看臺看賽馬。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde wouldn’t go; she said horse racing was an abomination and, she being a church member, thought it her bounden duty to set a good example by staying away.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太唔肯去;佢講賽馬係可憎嘅,佢作為教會成員,覺得佢有不可推卸嘅責任不去,以樹立好榜樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太不肯去;她說賽馬是可憎的,她作為教會成員,覺得她有不可推卸的責任不去,以樹立好榜樣。

passages.original: But there were so many there I don’t believe Mrs. Lynde’s absence would ever be noticed.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰兒有咁多人,我相信林德太太不喺永遠唔會被注意到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那兒有那麼多人,我相信林德太太不在永遠不會被注意到。

passages.original: I don’t think, though, that I ought to go very often to horse races, because they are awfully fascinating.
passages.vernacular: 不過我不覺得我應該常去睇賽馬,因為佢哋太吸引人喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我不覺得我應該常去看賽馬,因為它們太吸引人了。

passages.original: Diana got so excited that she offered to bet me ten cents that the red horse would win.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜激動得提議跟我打賭好錢,賭紅馬會贏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜激動得提議跟我打賭十分錢,賭紅馬會贏。

passages.original: I didn’t believe he would, but I refused to bet, because I wanted to tell Mrs. Allan all about everything, and I felt sure it wouldn’t do to tell her that.
passages.vernacular: 我不相信佢會贏,但我拒絕打賭,因為我想把一切都告訴艾倫太太,而我確信把嗰個告訴佢不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不相信它會贏,但我拒絕打賭,因為我想把一切都告訴艾倫太太,而我確信把那個告訴她不行。

passages.original: It’s always wrong to do anything you can’t tell the minister’s wife.
passages.vernacular: 做任何你唔能夠告訴牧師妻子嘅事總是錯嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 做任何你不能告訴牧師妻子的事總是錯的。

passages.original: It’s as good as an extra conscience to have a minister’s wife for your friend.
passages.vernacular: 有個牧師嘅妻子做朋友,就像多咗一個良心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有個牧師的妻子做朋友,就像多了一個良心。

passages.original: And I was very glad I didn’t bet, because the red horse did win, and I would have lost ten cents.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興我冇打賭,因為紅馬真嘅贏喇,我會輸掉好錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興我沒打賭,因為紅馬真的贏了,我會輸掉十分錢。

passages.original: So you see that virtue was its own reward.
passages.vernacular: 所以您睇美德本身就係回報。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以您看美德本身就是回報。

passages.original: We saw a man go up in a balloon.
passages.vernacular: 我哋睇到一個人乘氣球升空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們看到一個人乘氣球升空。

passages.original: I’d love to go up in a balloon, Marilla; it would be simply thrilling; and we saw a man selling fortunes.
passages.vernacular: 我真想乘氣球上去,瑪麗拉;嗰簡直太刺激喇;我哋仲睇到一個人喺賣算命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真想乘氣球上去,瑪麗拉;那簡直太刺激了;我們還看到一個人在賣算命。

passages.original: You paid him ten cents and a little bird picked out your fortune for you.
passages.vernacular: 你付佢好錢,一隻小鳥替你叼出你嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你付他十分錢,一隻小鳥替你叼出你的命運。

passages.original: Miss Barry gave Diana and me ten cents each to have our fortunes told.
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐畀咗黛安娜同我每人好錢去算命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐給了黛安娜和我每人十分錢去算命。

passages.original: Mine was that I would marry a dark-complected man who was very wealthy, and I would go across water to live.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅係我會嫁畀一個好有錢嘅黑皮膚男人,並渡海去生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的是我會嫁給一個很有錢的黑皮膚男人,並渡海去生活。

passages.original: I looked carefully at all the dark men I saw after that, but I didn’t care much for any of them, and anyhow I suppose it’s too early to be looking out for him yet.
passages.vernacular: 嗰以後我仔細睇咗我睇到嘅所有黑皮膚嘅男人,但我一個都不點鍾意,不管點樣,我想而家去物色佢仲太早喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那以後我仔細看了我看到的所有黑皮膚的男人,但我一個也不怎麼喜歡,不管怎樣,我想現在去物色他還太早了。

passages.original: Oh, it was a never-to-be-forgotten day, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 哦,嗰個係難忘嘅一天,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,那是難忘的一天,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I was so tired I couldn’t sleep at night.
passages.vernacular: 我累得晚上瞓不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我累得晚上睡不著。

passages.original: Miss Barry put us in the spare room, according to promise.
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐按照承諾,讓我哋瞓喺備用客房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐按照承諾,讓我們睡在備用客房。

passages.original: It was an elegant room, Marilla, but somehow sleeping in a spare room isn’t what I used to think it was.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個高雅嘅房間,瑪麗拉,但唔知怎嘅,瞓備用客房並不像我以前想嘅嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個高雅的房間,瑪麗拉,但不知怎的,睡備用客房並不像我以前想的那樣。

passages.original: That’s the worst of growing up, and I’m beginning to realize it.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係長大最糟嘅地方,我開始意識到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是長大最糟的地方,我開始意識到了。

passages.original: The things you wanted so much when you were a child don’t seem half so wonderful to you when you get them.”
passages.vernacular: 你小時候咁想要嘅嘢,得到之後,覺得連一半都冇咁奇妙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你小時候那麼想要的東西,得到之後,覺得連一半也沒那麼奇妙。」

passages.original: Thursday the girls had a drive in the park, and in the evening Miss Barry took them to a concert in the Academy of Music, where a noted prima donna was to sing.
passages.vernacular: 星期四,女孩哋喺公園裡乘車兜風,晚上巴里小姐帶佢哋去音樂學院嘅音樂會,一位著名嘅首席女高音要喺嗰兒演唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期四,女孩們在公園裡乘車兜風,晚上巴里小姐帶她們去音樂學院的音樂會,一位著名的首席女高音要在那兒演唱。

passages.original: To Anne the evening was a glittering vision of delight.
passages.vernacular: 對安妮來講,嗰個晚上係一幅閃耀嘅喜悅幻景。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對安妮來說,那個晚上是一幅閃耀的喜悅幻景。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, it was beyond description.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,簡直無法形容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,簡直無法形容。

passages.original: I was so excited I couldn’t even talk, so you may know what it was like.
passages.vernacular: 我興奮得連話都講不出嚟,所以你可以想像係乜嘢樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我興奮得連話都說不出來,所以你可以想像是什麼樣子。

passages.original: I just sat in enraptured silence.
passages.vernacular: 我只係狂喜地沉默地坐住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是狂喜地沉默地坐著。

passages.original: Madame Selitsky was perfectly beautiful, and wore white satin and diamonds.
passages.vernacular: 謝利茨基夫人美極喇,穿住白緞子同鑽石。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝利茨基夫人美極了,穿著白緞子和鑽石。

passages.original: But when she began to sing I never thought about anything else.
passages.vernacular: 但佢一開始唱歌,我就唔再想別嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她一開始唱歌,我就不再想別的了。

passages.original: Oh, I can’t tell you how I felt.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我無法告訴您我嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我無法告訴您我的感覺。

passages.original: But it seemed to me that it could never be hard to be good any more.
passages.vernacular: 但我似乎覺得再都唔會覺得做好人難喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我似乎覺得再也不會覺得做好人難了。

passages.original: I felt like I do when I look up to the stars.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅感覺就像我仰望星星時一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的感覺就像我仰望星星時一樣。

passages.original: Tears came into my eyes, but, oh, they were such happy tears.
passages.vernacular: 眼淚湧進咗眼眶,但係,哦,嗰個係咁幸福嘅眼淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 眼淚湧進了眼眶,但是,哦,那是那麼幸福的眼淚。

passages.original: I was so sorry when it was all over, and I told Miss Barry I didn’t see how I was ever to return to common life again.
passages.vernacular: 一切結束時我好難過,我告訴巴里小姐,我睇不出我點才能回到平凡嘅生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切結束時我好難過,我告訴巴里小姐,我看不出我怎麼才能回到平凡的生活。

passages.original: She said she thought if we went over to the restaurant across the street and had an ice cream it might help me.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢覺得,如果我哋到街對面嘅餐館食一份冰淇淋,或者會有幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她覺得,如果我們到街對面的餐館吃一份冰淇淋,也許會有幫助。

passages.original: That sounded so prosaic; but to my surprise I found it true.
passages.vernacular: 呢聽起嚟咁平淡;但令我驚奇嘅係我發現呢個係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這聽起來那麼平淡;但令我驚奇的是我發現這是真的。

passages.original: The ice cream was delicious, Marilla, and it was so lovely and dissipated to be sitting there eating it at eleven o’clock at night.
passages.vernacular: 冰淇淋美味極喇,瑪麗拉,深夜十啲坐喺嗰兒食佢,真係美妙又放縱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冰淇淋美味極了,瑪麗拉,深夜十一點坐在那兒吃它,真是美妙又放縱。

passages.original: Diana said she believed she was born for city life.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜講佢相信自己天生適合城市生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜說她相信自己天生適合城市生活。

passages.original: Miss Barry asked me what my opinion was, but I said I would have to think it over very seriously before I could tell her what I really thought.
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐問我嘅睇法,但我講我必須好認真地考慮之後才能告訴佢我真正嘅想法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐問我的看法,但我說我必須非常認真地考慮之後才能告訴她我真正的想法。

passages.original: So I thought it over after I went to bed.
passages.vernacular: 所以我上床後想咗想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我上床後想了想。

passages.original: That is the best time to think things out.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係想清楚事情嘅最佳時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是想清楚事情的最佳時間。

passages.original: And I came to the conclusion, Marilla, that I wasn’t born for city life and that I was glad of it.
passages.vernacular: 我得出嘅結論,瑪麗拉,係我唔係天生適合城市生活,而且我為此高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得出的結論,瑪麗拉,是我不是天生適合城市生活,而且我為此高興。

passages.original: It’s nice to be eating ice cream at brilliant restaurants at eleven o’clock at night once in a while; but as a regular thing I’d rather be in the east gable at eleven, sound asleep, but kind of knowing even in my sleep that the stars were shining outside and that the wind was blowing in the firs across the brook.
passages.vernacular: 偶爾喺晚上十啲喺燦爛輝煌嘅餐館食冰淇淋係好嘅;但作為常態,我寧願十啲喺東山牆房間裡,瞓得正香,但即使喺夢中都隱隱知道外面星星喺閃,風喺小溪嗰邊嘅冷杉林中吹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 偶爾在晚上十一點在燦爛輝煌的餐館吃冰淇淋是好的;但作為常態,我寧願十一點在東山牆房間裡,睡得正香,但即使在夢中也隱隱知道外面星星在閃,風在小溪那邊的冷杉林中吹。

passages.original: I told Miss Barry so at breakfast the next morning and she laughed.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早飯時我咁告訴咗巴里小姐,佢笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早飯時我這麼告訴了巴里小姐,她笑了。

passages.original: Miss Barry generally laughed at anything I said, even when I said the most solemn things.
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐通常對我講嘅任何話都笑,即使我講最嚴肅嘅話時都笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐通常對我說的任何話都笑,即使我說最嚴肅的話時也笑。

passages.original: I don’t think I liked it, Marilla, because I wasn’t trying to be funny.
passages.vernacular: 我想我不鍾意咁樣,瑪麗拉,因為我並唔想講得有趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我不喜歡這樣,瑪麗拉,因為我並不想說得有趣。

passages.original: But she is a most hospitable lady and treated us royally.”
passages.vernacular: 但佢係最好客嘅女士,像王室一樣款待我哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她是最好客的女士,像王室一樣款待我們。」

passages.original: Friday brought going-home time, and Mr. Barry drove in for the girls.
passages.vernacular: 星期五到咗回家嘅時間,巴里先生駕車進城接女孩哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期五到了回家的時間,巴里先生駕車進城接女孩們。

passages.original: “Well, I hope you’ve enjoyed yourselves,” said Miss Barry, as she bade them good-bye.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我希望你哋玩得開心,」巴里小姐喺向佢哋告別時講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我希望你們玩得開心,」巴里小姐在向她們告別時說。

passages.original: “Indeed we have,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅好開心,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的很開心,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “And you, Anne-girl?”
passages.vernacular: 「你呢,安妮丫頭?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你呢,安妮丫頭?」

passages.original: “I’ve enjoyed every minute of the time,” said Anne, throwing her arms impulsively about the old woman’s neck and kissing her wrinkled cheek.
passages.vernacular: 「我享受咗每一分鐘,」安妮講,衝動地用雙臂摟住老太太嘅脖子,吻咗佢布滿皺紋嘅臉頰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我享受了每一分鐘,」安妮說,衝動地用雙臂摟住老太太的脖子,吻了她布滿皺紋的臉頰。

passages.original: Diana would never have dared to do such a thing and felt rather aghast at Anne’s freedom.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜永遠唔敢做咁樣嘅事,對安妮嘅隨意感到有點驚愕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜永遠不敢做這樣的事,對安妮的隨意感到有點驚愕。

passages.original: But Miss Barry was pleased, and she stood on her veranda and watched the buggy out of sight.
passages.vernacular: 但巴里小姐好高興,佢站喺陽臺上目送馬車消失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但巴里小姐很高興,她站在陽臺上目送馬車消失。

passages.original: Then she went back into her big house with a sigh.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢嘆咗口氣,回到佢嘅大房子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她嘆了口氣,回到她的大房子裡。

passages.original: It seemed very lonely, lacking those fresh young lives.
passages.vernacular: 缺少咗嗰啲鮮活嘅年輕生命,顯得好孤獨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 缺少了那些鮮活的年輕生命,顯得非常孤獨。

passages.original: Miss Barry was a rather selfish old lady, if the truth must be told, and had never cared much for anybody but herself.
passages.vernacular: 巴里小姐實話實講係個相當自私嘅老太太,除咗自己從不太在乎別人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里小姐實話實說是個相當自私的老太太,除了自己從不太在乎別人。

passages.original: She valued people only as they were of service to her or amused her.
passages.vernacular: 佢只重視別人對佢有用或讓佢開心嘅方面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她只重視別人對她有用或讓她開心的方面。

passages.original: Anne had amused her, and consequently stood high in the old lady’s good graces.
passages.vernacular: 安妮讓佢開心,因此喺老太太嘅好感中地位好高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮讓她開心,因此在老太太的好感中地位很高。

passages.original: But Miss Barry found herself thinking less about Anne’s quaint speeches than of her fresh enthusiasms, her transparent emotions, her little winning ways, and the sweetness of her eyes and lips.
passages.vernacular: 但巴里小姐發現自己想嘅,同其講係安妮古怪嘅話,不如講係佢新鮮嘅熱情、佢透明嘅情感、佢可愛嘅小小魅力,以及佢眼睛同嘴唇嘅甜美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但巴里小姐發現自己想的,與其說是安妮古怪的話,不如說是她新鮮的熱情、她透明的情感、她可愛的小小魅力,以及她眼睛和嘴唇的甜美。

passages.original: “I thought Marilla Cuthbert was an old fool when I heard she’d adopted a girl out of an orphan asylum,” she said to herself, “but I guess she didn’t make much of a mistake after all.
passages.vernacular: 「我聽講瑪麗拉·卡思伯特從孤兒院領養咗一個女孩時,我以為佢係個老傻瓜,」佢對自己講,「但我想佢終究冇犯多大錯誤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我聽說瑪麗拉·卡思伯特從孤兒院領養了一個女孩時,我以為她是個老傻瓜,」她對自己說,「但我想她終究沒有犯多大錯誤。

passages.original: If I’d a child like Anne in the house all the time I’d be a better and happier woman.”
passages.vernacular: 如果我家裡一直有一個安妮咁樣嘅細路,我會係個更好更快樂嘅女人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我家裡一直有一個安妮這樣的孩子,我會是個更好更快樂的女人。」

passages.original: Anne and Diana found the drive home as pleasant as the drive in--pleasanter, indeed, since there was the delightful consciousness of home waiting at the end of it.
passages.vernacular: 安妮同黛安娜發現回家嘅路同嚟時一樣愉快——其實更愉快,因為有回家喺盡頭等住嘅美妙意識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮和黛安娜發現回家的路和來時一樣愉快——其實更愉快,因為有回家在盡頭等著的美妙意識。

passages.original: It was sunset when they passed through White Sands and turned into the shore road.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋穿過白沙拐進海岸路時,正是日落。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們穿過白沙拐進海岸路時,正是日落。

passages.original: Beyond, the Avonlea hills came out darkly against the saffron sky.
passages.vernacular: 遠處,阿文利嘅山丘喺藏紅花色嘅天空下黑黑地顯露出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遠處,阿文利的山丘在藏紅花色的天空下黑黑地顯露出來。

passages.original: Behind them the moon was rising out of the sea that grew all radiant and transfigured in her light.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋身後,月亮從海中升起,海喺佢嘅光輝下變得一片燦爛同轉變。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們身後,月亮從海中升起,海在她的光輝下變得一片燦爛和轉變。

passages.original: Every little cove along the curving road was a marvel of dancing ripples.
passages.vernacular: 蜿蜒道路沿途嘅每個小海灣都係舞動漣漪嘅奇蹟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蜿蜒道路沿途的每個小海灣都是舞動漣漪的奇蹟。

passages.original: The waves broke with a soft swish on the rocks below them, and the tang of the sea was in the strong, fresh air.
passages.vernacular: 浪花喺下面岩石上輕輕沙沙地破碎,強勁、清新嘅空氣中有海嘅氣息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 浪花在下面岩石上輕輕沙沙地破碎,強勁、清新的空氣中有海的氣息。

passages.original: “Oh, but it’s good to be alive and to be going home,” breathed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,活住並正在回家,真好,」安妮輕聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,活著並正在回家,真好,」安妮輕聲說。

passages.original: When she crossed the log bridge over the brook the kitchen light of Green Gables winked her a friendly welcome back, and through the open door shone the hearth fire, sending out its warm red glow athwart the chilly autumn night.
passages.vernacular: 當佢過小溪上嘅原木橋時,綠色屋頂嘅廚房燈光向佢眨眼,友好地歡迎佢回嚟,敞開嘅門裡爐火喺發光,把溫暖嘅紅光投向寒冷嘅秋夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當她過小溪上的原木橋時,綠色屋頂的廚房燈光向她眨眼,友好地歡迎她回來,敞開的門裡爐火在發光,把溫暖的紅光投向寒冷的秋夜。

passages.original: Anne ran blithely up the hill and into the kitchen, where a hot supper was waiting on the table.
passages.vernacular: 安妮快活地跑上山,進咗廚房,嗰度熱騰騰嘅晚飯已擺喺桌上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮快活地跑上山,進了廚房,那裡熱騰騰的晚飯已擺在桌上。

passages.original: “So you’ve got back?” said Marilla, folding up her knitting.
passages.vernacular: 「你回嚟喇?」瑪麗拉折起佢嘅針線活,講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你回來了?」瑪麗拉折起她的針線活,說。

passages.original: “Yes, and oh, it’s so good to be back,” said Anne joyously.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,哦,回嚟真好,」安妮歡快地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,哦,回來真好,」安妮歡快地說。

passages.original: “I could kiss everything, even to the clock.
passages.vernacular: 「我想親吻一切,連鐘都要吻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想親吻一切,連鐘也要吻。

passages.original: Marilla, a broiled chicken!
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉,烤雞!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉,烤雞!

passages.original: You don’t mean to say you cooked that for me!”
passages.vernacular: 您唔係講您為我做嘅吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不是說您為我做的吧!」

passages.original: “Yes, I did,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我做嘅,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我做的,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “I thought you’d be hungry after such a drive and need something real appetizing.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你走咗咁遠嘅路會餓,需要點真正開胃嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你走了那麼遠的路會餓,需要點真正開胃的東西。

passages.original: Hurry and take off your things, and we’ll have supper as soon as Matthew comes in.
passages.vernacular: 快把嘢脫喇,馬修一進嚟我哋就食晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快把東西脫了,馬修一進來我們就吃晚飯。

passages.original: I’m glad you’ve got back, I must say.
passages.vernacular: 我必須講,我好高興你回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須說,我很高興你回來了。

passages.original: It’s been fearful lonesome here without you, and I never put in four longer days.”
passages.vernacular: 冇你呢度可孤單喇,我從冇度過更長嘅四天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有你這裡可孤單了,我從沒度過更長的四天。」

passages.original: After supper Anne sat before the fire between Matthew and Marilla, and gave them a full account of her visit.
passages.vernacular: 晚飯後,安妮坐喺爐火前,喺馬修同瑪麗拉之間,把佢嘅訪問原原本本地講畀佢哋聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚飯後,安妮坐在爐火前,在馬修和瑪麗拉之間,把她的訪問原原本本地講給他們聽。

passages.original: “I’ve had a splendid time,” she concluded happily, “and I feel that it marks an epoch in my life.
passages.vernacular: 「我度過咗美好嘅時光,」佢幸福地總結道,「我覺得佢標誌住我生命中嘅一個新紀元。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我度過了美好的時光,」她幸福地總結道,「我覺得它標誌著我生命中的一個新紀元。

passages.original: But the best of it all was the coming home.”
passages.vernacular: 但最好嘅係回家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但最好的是回家。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXX The Queen's Class Is Organized 第三十章:女王學院班成立

passages.original: CH MARILLA laid her knitting on her lap and leaned back in her chair.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉把針線活放喺膝上,往椅背上靠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉把針線活放在膝上,往椅背上靠。

passages.original: Her eyes were tired, and she thought vaguely that she must see about having her glasses changed the next time she went to town, for her eyes had grown tired very often of late.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛累喇,佢隱約想到,下次進城時必須睇睇換眼鏡嘅事,因為最近佢嘅眼睛常常累。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛累了,她隱約想到,下次進城時必須看看換眼鏡的事,因為最近她的眼睛常常累。

passages.original: It was nearly dark, for the full November twilight had fallen around Green Gables, and the only light in the kitchen came from the dancing red flames in the stove.
passages.vernacular: 天快黑喇,因為十一月嘅黃昏已經完全降臨綠色屋頂周圍,廚房裡唯一嘅光亮來自爐子裡跳動嘅紅色火焰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天快黑了,因為十一月的黃昏已經完全降臨綠色屋頂周圍,廚房裡唯一的光亮來自爐子裡跳動的紅色火焰。

passages.original: Anne was curled up Turk-fashion on the hearthrug, gazing into that joyous glow where the sunshine of a hundred summers was being distilled from the maple cordwood.
passages.vernacular: 安妮盤腿蜷坐喺壁爐地毯上,凝視住嗰歡快嘅光輝,嗰度,一百個夏天嘅陽光正從楓木柴裡被蒸餾出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮盤腿蜷坐在壁爐地毯上,凝視著那歡快的光輝,那裡,一百個夏天的陽光正從楓木柴裡被蒸餾出來。

passages.original: She had been reading, but her book had slipped to the floor, and now she was dreaming, with a smile on her parted lips.
passages.vernacular: 佢本喺睇書,但書滑到咗地上,佢而家喺做夢,微張嘅嘴唇上帶住微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她本在看書,但書滑到了地上,她現在在做夢,微張的嘴唇上帶著微笑。

passages.original: Glittering castles in Spain were shaping themselves out of the mists and rainbows of her lively fancy; adventures wonderful and enthralling were happening to her in cloudland--adventures that always turned out triumphantly and never involved her in scrapes like those of actual life.
passages.vernacular: 閃亮嘅空中樓閣正從佢活躍幻想嘅薄霧同彩虹中成形;奇妙而迷人嘅冒險正發生喺佢雲中嘅世界裡——呢啲冒險總是勝利地結束,從不像現實生活嗰樣使佢惹上麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 閃亮的空中樓閣正從她活躍幻想的薄霧和彩虹中成形;奇妙而迷人的冒險正發生在她雲中的世界裡——這些冒險總是勝利地結束,從不像現實生活那樣使她惹上麻煩。

passages.original: Marilla looked at her with a tenderness that would never have been suffered to reveal itself in any clearer light than that soft mingling of fireshine and shadow.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉睇住佢,帶住一種溫柔,呢種溫柔喺比爐火同陰影柔和交織更明亮嘅光線下,係永唔容許顯露出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉看著她,帶著一種溫柔,這種溫柔在比爐火與陰影柔和交織更明亮的光線下,是永不容許顯露出來的。

passages.original: The lesson of a love that should display itself easily in spoken word and open look was one Marilla could never learn.
passages.vernacular: 愛能輕易地用言語同坦率嘅眼神表現出嚟,呢一課係瑪麗拉永遠學唔會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛能輕易地用言語和坦率的眼神表現出來,這一課是瑪麗拉永遠學不會的。

passages.original: But she had learned to love this slim, gray-eyed girl with an affection all the deeper and stronger from its very undemonstrativeness.
passages.vernacular: 但佢已學會咗愛呢個苗條嘅、灰眼睛嘅女孩,呢份感情因其恰恰不外露而更深更強。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她已學會了愛這個苗條的、灰眼睛的女孩,這份感情因其恰恰不外露而更深更強。

passages.original: Her love made her afraid of being unduly indulgent, indeed.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅愛確實使佢害怕過分縱容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的愛確實使她害怕過分縱容。

passages.original: She had an uneasy feeling that it was rather sinful to set one’s heart so intensely on any human creature as she had set hers on Anne, and perhaps she performed a sort of unconscious penance for this by being stricter and more critical than if the girl had been less dear to her.
passages.vernacular: 佢有種不安嘅感覺,覺得像佢把心如此強烈地放喺安妮身上嗰樣,把心放喺任何一個人身上,係相當有罪嘅,或者佢就通過比女孩不咁親近時更嚴厲、更挑剔,做一種無意識嘅贖罪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有種不安的感覺,覺得像她把心如此強烈地放在安妮身上那樣,把心放在任何一個人身上,是相當有罪的,也許她就通過比女孩不那麼親近時更嚴厲、更挑剔,做一種無意識的贖罪。

passages.original: Certainly Anne herself had no idea how Marilla loved her.
passages.vernacular: 當然,安妮自己唔知道瑪麗拉幾咁愛佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,安妮自己不知道瑪麗拉多麼愛她。

passages.original: She sometimes thought wistfully that Marilla was very hard to please and distinctly lacking in sympathy and understanding.
passages.vernacular: 佢有時悵然地想,瑪麗拉好難討好,而且明顯缺乏同情同理解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有時悵然地想,瑪麗拉很難討好,而且明顯缺乏同情和理解。

passages.original: But she always checked the thought reproachfully, remembering what she owed to Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 但佢總是自責地制止呢個想法,記起自己欠瑪麗拉嘅一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她總是自責地制止這個想法,記起自己欠瑪麗拉的一切。

passages.original: “Anne,” said Marilla abruptly, “Miss Stacy was here this afternoon when you were out with Diana.”
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,」瑪麗拉突然講,「你同黛安娜出去嘅時候,斯泰西小姐今日下午嚟過呢兒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,」瑪麗拉突然說,「你和黛安娜出去的時候,斯泰西小姐今天下午來過這兒。」

passages.original: Anne came back from her other world with a start and a sigh.
passages.vernacular: 安妮帶住驚跳同嘆息從佢嘅另一個世界回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮帶著驚跳和嘆息從她的另一個世界回來。

passages.original: “Was she?
passages.vernacular: 「係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是嗎?

passages.original: Oh, I’m so sorry I wasn’t in.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我太抱歉我不喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我太抱歉我不在。

passages.original: Why didn’t you call me, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 您點解不叫我,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您為什麼不叫我,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: Diana and I were only over in the Haunted Wood.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜同我只係喺鬧鬼林。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜和我只是在鬧鬼林。

passages.original: It’s lovely in the woods now.
passages.vernacular: 而家樹林里太可愛喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在樹林里太可愛了。

passages.original: All the little wood things--the ferns and the satin leaves and the crackerberries--have gone to sleep, just as if somebody had tucked them away until spring under a blanket of leaves.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅林中小嘢——蕨類、緞葉同爆漿莓——都瞓住喇,好像有人把佢哋用一條樹葉嘅毯子裹起嚟,直到春天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的林中小東西——蕨類、緞葉和爆漿莓——都睡著了,好像有人把它們用一條樹葉的毯子裹起來,直到春天。

passages.original: I think it was a little gray fairy with a rainbow scarf that came tiptoeing along the last moonlight night and did it.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得係一個圍住彩虹圍巾嘅灰色小仙女,喺上次月夜裡踮住腳尖走嚟咁做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得是一個圍著彩虹圍巾的灰色小仙女,在上次月夜裡踮著腳尖走來這麼做的。

passages.original: Diana wouldn’t say much about that, though.
passages.vernacular: 不過黛安娜對此講得不多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過黛安娜對此說得不多。

passages.original: Diana has never forgotten the scolding her mother gave her about imagining ghosts into the Haunted Wood.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜從冇忘記佢母親因為佢把鬼魂想像進鬧鬼林而罵佢嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜從沒忘記她母親因為她把鬼魂想像進鬧鬼林而罵她的事。

passages.original: It had a very bad effect on Diana’s imagination.
passages.vernacular: 呢對黛安娜嘅想像力有好不好嘅影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這對黛安娜的想像力有非常不好的影響。

passages.original: It blighted it.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓佢枯萎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它讓它枯萎了。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says Myrtle Bell is a blighted being.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講默特爾·貝爾係個枯萎嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說默特爾·貝爾是個枯萎的人。

passages.original: I asked Ruby Gillis why Myrtle was blighted, and Ruby said she guessed it was because her young man had gone back on her.
passages.vernacular: 我問露比·吉利斯點解默特爾枯萎喇,露比講佢猜係因為佢嘅情郎拋棄咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我問露比·吉利斯為什麼默特爾枯萎了,露比說她猜是因為她的情郎拋棄了她。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis thinks of nothing but young men, and the older she gets the worse she is.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯除咗情郎乜嘢都唔想,而且佢越大越糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯除了情郎什麼也不想,而且她越大越糟。

passages.original: Young men are all very well in their place, but it doesn’t do to drag them into everything, does it?
passages.vernacular: 年輕男人喺佢哋嘅位置上係挺好嘅,但唔使把佢哋拖進一切事情里,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 年輕男人在他們的位置上是挺好的,但不必把他們拖進一切事情里,是不是?

passages.original: Diana and I are thinking seriously of promising each other that we will never marry but be nice old maids and live together forever.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜同我正認真考慮互相許諾永不結婚,做可愛嘅老處女,永遠住喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜和我正認真考慮互相許諾永不結婚,做可愛的老處女,永遠住在一起。

passages.original: Diana hasn’t quite made up her mind though, because she thinks perhaps it would be nobler to marry some wild, dashing, wicked young man and reform him.
passages.vernacular: 不過黛安娜仲冇完全攞定主意,因為佢覺得嫁畀某個狂野嘅、俊俏嘅、邪惡嘅年輕人並改造佢,或者更高尚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過黛安娜還沒完全拿定主意,因為她覺得嫁給某個狂野的、俊俏的、邪惡的年輕人並改造他,也許更高尚。

passages.original: Diana and I talk a great deal about serious subjects now, you know.
passages.vernacular: 您知道,黛安娜同我而家經常談論嚴肅嘅話題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道,黛安娜和我現在經常談論嚴肅的話題。

passages.original: We feel that we are so much older than we used to be that it isn’t becoming to talk of childish matters.
passages.vernacular: 我哋覺得自己比從前大得多,談論幼稚嘅事不合適喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們覺得自己比從前大得多,談論幼稚的事不合適了。

passages.original: It’s such a solemn thing to be almost fourteen, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 差不多十四歲係咁莊重嘅事,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 差不多十四歲是這麼莊重的事,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Miss Stacy took all us girls who are in our teens down to the brook last Wednesday, and talked to us about it.
passages.vernacular: 上星期三斯泰西小姐把我哋所有十幾歲嘅女孩帶到小溪邊,跟我哋談呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上星期三斯泰西小姐把我們所有十幾歲的女孩帶到小溪邊,跟我們談這個。

passages.original: She said we couldn’t be too careful what habits we formed and what ideals we acquired in our teens, because by the time we were twenty our characters would be developed and the foundation laid for our whole future life.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我哋喺十幾歲時,養成乜嘢習慣、樹立乜嘢理想,點小心都不為過,因為到我哋二十歲時,我哋嘅性格就成形喇,整個未來生活嘅基礎就奠定喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我們在十幾歲時,養成什麼習慣、樹立什麼理想,怎麼小心都不為過,因為到我們二十歲時,我們的性格就成形了,整個未來生活的基礎就奠定了。

passages.original: And she said if the foundation was shaky we could never build anything really worth while on it.
passages.vernacular: 佢講如果基礎不穩,我哋永遠無法喺上面建造任何真正有價值嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說如果基礎不穩,我們永遠無法在上面建造任何真正有價值的東西。

passages.original: Diana and I talked the matter over coming home from school.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜同我喺放學回家嘅路上談咗呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜和我在放學回家的路上談了這件事。

passages.original: We felt extremely solemn, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我哋感到極其莊重,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們感到極其莊重,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: And we decided that we would try to be very careful indeed and form respectable habits and learn all we could and be as sensible as possible, so that by the time we were twenty our characters would be properly developed.
passages.vernacular: 我哋決定我哋要好小心,養成可敬嘅習慣,盡量多學,盡可能明智,咁樣到二十歲時,我哋嘅性格就能得到恰當嘅發展。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們決定我們要非常小心,養成可敬的習慣,盡量多學,盡可能明智,這樣到二十歲時,我們的性格就能得到恰當的發展。

passages.original: It’s perfectly appalling to think of being twenty, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 想到二十歲簡直太可怕喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到二十歲簡直太可怕了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: It sounds so fearfully old and grown up.
passages.vernacular: 聽起嚟咁老、咁成熟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽起來那麼老、那麼成熟。

passages.original: But why was Miss Stacy here this afternoon?”
passages.vernacular: 不過斯泰西小姐今日下午點解嚟呢兒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過斯泰西小姐今天下午為什麼來這兒?」

passages.original: “That is what I want to tell you, Anne, if you’ll ever give me a chance to get a word in edgewise.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個就係我要告訴你嘅,安妮,如果你肯畀我插話嘅機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就是我要告訴你的,安妮,如果你肯給我插話的機會。

passages.original: She was talking about you.”
passages.vernacular: 佢喺談你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在談你。」

passages.original: “About me?”
passages.vernacular: 「談我?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「談我?」

passages.original: Anne looked rather scared.
passages.vernacular: 安妮顯得相當害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮顯得相當害怕。

passages.original: Then she flushed and exclaimed:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢臉紅喇,叫道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她臉紅了,叫道:

passages.original: “Oh, I know what she was saying.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我知道佢講乜嘢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我知道她說什麼了。

passages.original: I meant to tell you, Marilla, honestly I did, but I forgot.
passages.vernacular: 我本想告訴您嘅,瑪麗拉,真嘅,但我忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我本想告訴您的,瑪麗拉,真的,但我忘了。

passages.original: Miss Stacy caught me reading Ben Hur in school yesterday afternoon when I should have been studying my Canadian history.
passages.vernacular: 尋日下午斯泰西小姐抓到我喺學校里睇《賓虛》,而我本該喺學習加攞大歷史。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨天下午斯泰西小姐抓到我在學校里看《賓虛》,而我本該在學習加拿大歷史。

passages.original: Jane Andrews lent it to me.
passages.vernacular: 係簡·安德魯斯借畀我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是簡·安德魯斯借給我的。

passages.original: I was reading it at dinner hour, and I had just got to the chariot race when school went in.
passages.vernacular: 我喺午休時睇,正讀到戰車比賽,上課鈴就響喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在午休時看,正讀到戰車比賽,上課鈴就響了。

passages.original: I was simply wild to know how it turned out--although I felt sure Ben Hur must win, because it wouldn’t be poetical justice if he didn’t--so I spread the history open on my desk lid and then tucked Ben Hur between the desk and my knee.
passages.vernacular: 我簡直瘋狂地想知道結果如何——雖然我肯定賓虛一定會贏,因為佢要係不贏就不合詩意嘅公正——所以我把歷史書攤開喺桌蓋上,然後把《賓虛》塞喺桌子同我嘅膝蓋之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我簡直瘋狂地想知道結果如何——雖然我肯定賓虛一定會贏,因為他要是不贏就不合詩意的公正——所以我把歷史書攤開在桌蓋上,然後把《賓虛》塞在桌子和我的膝蓋之間。

passages.original: I just looked as if I were studying Canadian history, you know, while all the while I was reveling in Ben Hur.
passages.vernacular: 我睇起嚟就像喺學加攞大歷史,您知道,而我一直陶醉喺《賓虛》裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看起來就像在學加拿大歷史,您知道,而我一直陶醉在《賓虛》裡。

passages.original: I was so interested in it that I never noticed Miss Stacy coming down the aisle until all at once I just looked up and there she was looking down at me, so reproachful-like.
passages.vernacular: 我太投入喇,直到突然抬頭,才發現斯泰西小姐已走到過道上,站喺嗰兒低頭睇住我,咁責備嘅樣子,我才注意到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太投入了,直到突然抬頭,才發現斯泰西小姐已走到過道上,站在那兒低頭看著我,那麼責備的樣子,我才注意到。

passages.original: I can’t tell you how ashamed I felt, Marilla, especially when I heard Josie Pye giggling.
passages.vernacular: 我無法告訴您我有多羞愧,瑪麗拉,特別係聽到喬西·派伊喺咯咯笑嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我無法告訴您我有多羞愧,瑪麗拉,特別是聽到喬西·派伊在咯咯笑的時候。

passages.original: Miss Stacy took Ben Hur away, but she never said a word then.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐把《賓虛》攞走喇,但當時一個字都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐把《賓虛》拿走了,但當時一個字也沒說。

passages.original: She kept me in at recess and talked to me.
passages.vernacular: 課間休息時佢把我留下嚟跟我談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 課間休息時她把我留下來跟我談話。

passages.original: She said I had done very wrong in two respects.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我喺兩方面做得好不對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我在兩方面做得很不對。

passages.original: First, I was wasting the time I ought to have put on my studies; and secondly, I was deceiving my teacher in trying to make it appear I was reading a history when it was a storybook instead.
passages.vernacular: 第一,我喺浪費本該用喺學習上嘅時間;第二,我喺欺騙老師,試圖讓佢以為我喺睇歷史書,而實際上嗰個係一本故事書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一,我在浪費本該用在學習上的時間;第二,我在欺騙老師,試圖讓她以為我在看歷史書,而實際上那是一本故事書。

passages.original: I had never realized until that moment, Marilla, that what I was doing was deceitful.
passages.vernacular: 直到嗰一刻我才意識到,瑪麗拉,我所做嘅係欺騙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到那一刻我才意識到,瑪麗拉,我所做的是欺騙。

passages.original: I was shocked.
passages.vernacular: 我震驚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我震驚了。

passages.original: I cried bitterly, and asked Miss Stacy to forgive me and I’d never do such a thing again; and I offered to do penance by never so much as looking at Ben Hur for a whole week, not even to see how the chariot race turned out.
passages.vernacular: 我痛哭起嚟,請求斯泰西小姐原諒我,我再都唔會做咁樣嘅事;我仲提出要通過整整一個星期連睇都不睇《賓虛》一眼嚟贖罪,甚至不睇戰車比賽嘅結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我痛哭起來,請求斯泰西小姐原諒我,我再也不會做這樣的事;我還提出要通過整整一個星期連看都不看《賓虛》一眼來贖罪,甚至不看戰車比賽的結果。

passages.original: But Miss Stacy said she wouldn’t require that, and she forgave me freely.
passages.vernacular: 但斯泰西小姐講佢唔好求呢個,佢好慷慨地原諒咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但斯泰西小姐說她不要求這個,她很慷慨地原諒了我。

passages.original: So I think it wasn’t very kind of her to come up here to you about it after all.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我覺得佢跑上嚟跟您講呢件事,終究不太好心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我覺得她跑上來跟您說這件事,終究不太好心。」

passages.original: “Miss Stacy never mentioned such a thing to me, Anne, and its only your guilty conscience that’s the matter with you.
passages.vernacular: 「斯泰西小姐從冇跟我提過呢種事,安妮,你嘅毛病只係你嘅負罪感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「斯泰西小姐從沒跟我提過這種事,安妮,你的毛病只是你的負罪感。

passages.original: You have no business to be taking storybooks to school.
passages.vernacular: 你冇權利把故事書帶到學校去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒有權利把故事書帶到學校去。

passages.original: You read too many novels anyhow.
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣你讀小講太多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣你讀小說太多了。

passages.original: When I was a girl I wasn’t so much as allowed to look at a novel.”
passages.vernacular: 我小時候連睇小講一眼都不被允許。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我小時候連看小說一眼都不被允許。」

passages.original: “Oh, how can you call Ben Hur a novel when it’s really such a religious book?” protested Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,《賓虛》真嘅係一本咁宗教嘅書,您點能叫佢小講?」安妮抗議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,《賓虛》真的是一本這麼宗教的書,您怎麼能叫它小說?」安妮抗議。

passages.original: “Of course it’s a little too exciting to be proper reading for Sunday, and I only read it on weekdays.
passages.vernacular: 「當然佢有點太刺激,不適合喺星期天讀,我只喺平日讀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然它有點太刺激,不適合在星期天讀,我只在平日讀。

passages.original: And I never read any book now unless either Miss Stacy or Mrs. Allan thinks it is a proper book for a girl thirteen and three-quarters to read.
passages.vernacular: 而且而家我從不讀任何書,除非斯泰西小姐或艾倫太太認為對一個十三歲又四分之三嘅女孩來講係合適嘅書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且現在我從不讀任何書,除非斯泰西小姐或艾倫太太認為對一個十三歲又四分之三的女孩來說是合適的書。

passages.original: Miss Stacy made me promise that.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐讓我保證呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐讓我保證這一點。

passages.original: She found me reading a book one day called, The Lurid Mystery of the Haunted Hall.
passages.vernacular: 有一天佢發現我喺讀一本書,叫《鬼屋嘅可怕之謎》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天她發現我在讀一本書,叫《鬼屋的可怕之謎》。

passages.original: It was one Ruby Gillis had lent me, and, oh, Marilla, it was so fascinating and creepy.
passages.vernacular: 係露比·吉利斯借畀我嘅,哦,瑪麗拉,佢係咁迷人而令人毛骨悚然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是露比·吉利斯借給我的,哦,瑪麗拉,它是那麼迷人而令人毛骨悚然。

passages.original: It just curdled the blood in my veins.
passages.vernacular: 佢簡直讓我血管里嘅血都凝固喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它簡直讓我血管里的血都凝固了。

passages.original: But Miss Stacy said it was a very silly, unwholesome book, and she asked me not to read any more of it or any like it.
passages.vernacular: 但斯泰西小姐講嗰個係本好愚蠢、不健康嘅書,佢要我唔好再讀佢或任何類似嘅書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但斯泰西小姐說那是本非常愚蠢、不健康的書,她要我不要再讀它或任何類似的書。

passages.original: I didn’t mind promising not to read any more like it, but it was agonizing to give back that book without knowing how it turned out.
passages.vernacular: 我不介意保證唔再讀類似嘅,但仲嗰本書卻唔知道結局係點樣,真係痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不介意保證不再讀類似的,但還那本書卻不知道結局是怎麼樣,真是痛苦。

passages.original: But my love for Miss Stacy stood the test and I did.
passages.vernacular: 但我對斯泰西小姐嘅愛經受住咗考驗,我仲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我對斯泰西小姐的愛經受住了考驗,我還了。

passages.original: It’s really wonderful, Marilla, what you can do when you’re truly anxious to please a certain person.”
passages.vernacular: 真嘅好奇妙,瑪麗拉,當你真心想討某個人鍾意時,你乜嘢都能做到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的很奇妙,瑪麗拉,當你真心想討某個人喜歡時,你什麼都能做到。」

passages.original: “Well, I guess I’ll light the lamp and get to work,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「好,我想我該點燈幹活喇,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,我想我該點燈幹活了,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “I see plainly that you don’t want to hear what Miss Stacy had to say.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇得好清楚,你唔想聽斯泰西小姐講咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看得很清楚,你不想聽斯泰西小姐說了什麼。

passages.original: You’re more interested in the sound of your own tongue than in anything else.”
passages.vernacular: 你對你自己舌頭嘅聲音比對別嘅都更感興趣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你對你自己舌頭的聲音比對別的都更感興趣。」

passages.original: “Oh, indeed, Marilla, I do want to hear it,” cried Anne contritely.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,真嘅,瑪麗拉,我想聽,」安妮悔恨地叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,真的,瑪麗拉,我想聽,」安妮悔恨地叫道。

passages.original: “I won’t say another word--not one.
passages.vernacular: 「我再都不多講一個字——一個都不講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再也不多說一個字——一個也不說。

passages.original: I know I talk too much, but I am really trying to overcome it, and although I say far too much, yet if you only knew how many things I want to say and don’t, you’d give me some credit for it.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我講得太多,但我真嘅喺努力克服,雖然我講得太多,但係如果您知道有多少事我想講卻冇講,您會因此畀我啲功勞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我說得太多,但我真的在努力克服,雖然我說得太多,但是如果您知道有多少事我想說卻沒說,您會因此給我一些功勞。

passages.original: Please tell me, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 請告訴我,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請告訴我,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: “Well, Miss Stacy wants to organize a class among her advanced students who mean to study for the entrance examination into Queen’s.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,斯泰西小姐想組織一個班,由佢嘅高年級學生組成,佢哋打算準備考女王學院嘅入學考試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,斯泰西小姐想組織一個班,由她的高年級學生組成,她們打算準備考女王學院的入學考試。

passages.original: She intends to give them extra lessons for an hour after school.
passages.vernacular: 佢打算放學後畀佢哋額外上一個鐘頭嘅課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她打算放學後給他們額外上一個鐘頭的課。

passages.original: And she came to ask Matthew and me if we would like to have you join it.
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟問馬修同我,願唔願意讓你參加。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她來問馬修和我,願不願意讓你參加。

passages.original: What do you think about it yourself, Anne?
passages.vernacular: 你自己點想,安妮?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你自己怎麼想,安妮?

passages.original: Would you like to go to Queen’s and pass for a teacher?”
passages.vernacular: 你願唔願意去女王學院,通過考試做教師?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你願不願意去女王學院,通過考試做教師?」

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉!」

passages.original: Anne straightened to her knees and clasped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 安妮直起身跪住,雙手緊握。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮直起身跪著,雙手緊握。

passages.original: “It’s been the dream of my life--that is, for the last six months, ever since Ruby and Jane began to talk of studying for the Entrance.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我一生嘅夢想——就係講,過去六個月嚟,自從露比同簡開始談論準備入學考試以後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我一生的夢想——就是說,過去六個月來,自從露比和簡開始談論準備入學考試以後。

passages.original: But I didn’t say anything about it, because I supposed it would be perfectly useless.
passages.vernacular: 但我乜嘢都冇講,因為我以為嗰完全冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我什麼也沒說,因為我以為那完全沒用。

passages.original: I’d love to be a teacher.
passages.vernacular: 我好想做老師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很想做老師。

passages.original: But won’t it be dreadfully expensive?
passages.vernacular: 但係唔會好昂貴嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是不會非常昂貴嗎?

passages.original: Mr. Andrews says it cost him one hundred and fifty dollars to put Prissy through, and Prissy wasn’t a dunce in geometry.”
passages.vernacular: 安德魯斯先生講送普麗茜上學花咗佢一百五十元,而普麗茜喺幾何上唔係笨蛋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安德魯斯先生說送普麗茜上學花了他一百五十元,而普麗茜在幾何上不是笨蛋。」

passages.original: “I guess you needn’t worry about that part of it.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你唔使擔心嗰一部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你不必擔心那一部分。

passages.original: When Matthew and I took you to bring up we resolved we would do the best we could for you and give you a good education.
passages.vernacular: 馬修同我領你嚟撫養嘅時候,我哋決心盡我哋所能為你做到最好,畀你良好嘅教育。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修和我領你來撫養的時候,我們決心盡我們所能為你做到最好,給你良好的教育。

passages.original: I believe in a girl being fitted to earn her own living whether she ever has to or not.
passages.vernacular: 我相信女孩應該具備養活自己嘅能力,不管佢將來係咪需要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信女孩應該具備養活自己的能力,不管她將來是否需要。

passages.original: You’ll always have a home at Green Gables as long as Matthew and I are here, but nobody knows what is going to happen in this uncertain world, and it’s just as well to be prepared.
passages.vernacular: 只要馬修同我喺,你總有一個家喺綠色屋頂,但邊個都唔知道呢個不確定嘅世界會發生乜嘢,做好準備都好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要馬修和我在,你總有一個家在綠色屋頂,但誰也不知道這個不確定的世界會發生什麼,做好準備也好。

passages.original: So you can join the Queen’s class if you like, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 所以如果你願意,安妮,你可以加入女王學院班。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以如果你願意,安妮,你可以加入女王學院班。」

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, thank you.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,謝謝您。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,謝謝您。」

passages.original: Anne flung her arms about Marilla’s waist and looked up earnestly into her face.
passages.vernacular: 安妮用雙臂摟住瑪麗拉嘅腰,認真地抬頭睇住佢嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮用雙臂摟住瑪麗拉的腰,認真地抬頭看著她的臉。

passages.original: “I’m extremely grateful to you and Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 「我極其感激您同馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我極其感激您和馬修。

passages.original: And I’ll study as hard as I can and do my very best to be a credit to you.
passages.vernacular: 我會盡我所能努力學習,盡我最大努力為你哋增光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會盡我所能努力學習,盡我最大努力為你們增光。

passages.original: I warn you not to expect much in geometry, but I think I can hold my own in anything else if I work hard.”
passages.vernacular: 我警告您別喺幾何上指望太多,但我想,只要我努力,我能喺別嘅任何事上不輸畀別人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我警告您別在幾何上指望太多,但我想,只要我努力,我能在別的任何事上不輸給別人。」

passages.original: “I dare say you’ll get along well enough.
passages.vernacular: 「我敢講你會做得足夠好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢說你會做得足夠好。

passages.original: Miss Stacy says you are bright and diligent.”
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐講你聰明又勤奮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐說你聰明又勤奮。」

passages.original: Not for worlds would Marilla have told Anne just what Miss Stacy had said about her; that would have been to pamper vanity.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉講乜嘢都唔會把斯泰西小姐對佢的確切評價告訴安妮;嗰會係縱容虛榮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉說什麼也不會把斯泰西小姐對她的確切評價告訴安妮;那會是縱容虛榮。

passages.original: “You needn’t rush to any extreme of killing yourself over your books.
passages.vernacular: 「你唔使急住走向極端,為書本把自己累死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不必急著走向極端,為書本把自己累死。

passages.original: There is no hurry.
passages.vernacular: 不住急。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不著急。

passages.original: You won’t be ready to try the Entrance for a year and a half yet.
passages.vernacular: 你仲有一年半才能準備好去考入學考試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你還有一年半才能準備好去考入學考試。

passages.original: But it’s well to begin in time and be thoroughly grounded, Miss Stacy says.”
passages.vernacular: 但斯泰西小姐講,及時開始、打好牢固基礎係好嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但斯泰西小姐說,及時開始、打好牢固基礎是好的。」

passages.original: “I shall take more interest than ever in my studies now,” said Anne blissfully, “because I have a purpose in life.
passages.vernacular: 「我而家會比任何時候都更感興趣地學習,」安妮幸福地講,「因為我有生活嘅目標喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在會比任何時候都更感興趣地學習,」安妮幸福地說,「因為我有生活的目標了。

passages.original: Mr. Allan says everybody should have a purpose in life and pursue it faithfully.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫先生講每個人都應該有生活嘅目標,並忠實地追求佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫先生說每個人都應該有生活的目標,並忠實地追求它。

passages.original: Only he says we must first make sure that it is a worthy purpose.
passages.vernacular: 只係佢講我哋必須首先確定佢係個有價值嘅目標。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是他說我們必須首先確定它是個有價值的目標。

passages.original: I would call it a worthy purpose to want to be a teacher like Miss Stacy, wouldn’t you, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 我會把想做像斯泰西小姐嗰樣嘅老師稱為有價值嘅目標,您講呢,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會把想做像斯泰西小姐那樣的老師稱為有價值的目標,您說呢,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: I think it’s a very noble profession.”
passages.vernacular: 我覺得呢個係一個好高尚嘅職業。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得這是一個非常高尚的職業。」

passages.original: The Queen’s class was organized in due time.
passages.vernacular: 女王學院班及時組織起嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女王學院班及時組織起來了。

passages.original: Gilbert Blythe, Anne Shirley, Ruby Gillis, Jane Andrews, Josie Pye, Charlie Sloane, and Moody Spurgeon MacPherson joined it.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯、安妮·雪莉、露比·吉利斯、簡·安德魯斯、喬西·派伊、查理·斯隆同穆迪·斯珀吉翁·麥克弗森加入喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯、安妮·雪莉、露比·吉利斯、簡·安德魯斯、喬西·派伊、查理·斯隆和穆迪·斯珀吉翁·麥克弗森加入了。

passages.original: Diana Barry did not, as her parents did not intend to send her to Queen’s.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜·巴里冇,因為佢父母不打算送佢去女王學院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜·巴里沒有,因為她父母不打算送她去女王學院。

passages.original: This seemed nothing short of a calamity to Anne.
passages.vernacular: 呢喺安妮睇來簡直係一場災難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這在安妮看來簡直是一場災難。

passages.original: Never, since the night on which Minnie May had had the croup, had she and Diana been separated in anything.
passages.vernacular: 自從明妮·梅得哮吼嘅嗰天晚上以來,佢同黛安娜從冇喺任何事上分開過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從明妮·梅得哮吼的那天晚上以來,她和黛安娜從沒有在任何事上分開過。

passages.original: On the evening when the Queen’s class first remained in school for the extra lessons and Anne saw Diana go slowly out with the others, to walk home alone through the Birch Path and Violet Vale, it was all the former could do to keep her seat and refrain from rushing impulsively after her chum.
passages.vernacular: 女王學院班第一次留喺學校上額外課程嘅嗰天晚上,安妮睇住黛安娜隨其他人慢慢走出去,獨自穿過白樺小徑同紫羅蘭谷回家,前者幾乎要忍不住衝動地追趕佢嘅好友,才坐在座位上不動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女王學院班第一次留在學校上額外課程的那天晚上,安妮看著黛安娜隨其他人慢慢走出去,獨自穿過白樺小徑和紫羅蘭谷回家,前者幾乎要忍不住衝動地追趕她的好友,才坐在座位上不動。

passages.original: A lump came into her throat, and she hastily retired behind the pages of her uplifted Latin grammar to hide the tears in her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢喉嚨裡湧上一個硬塊,佢連忙躲到舉起嘅拉丁語法書後面,藏起眼中嘅淚水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她喉嚨裡湧上一個硬塊,她連忙躲到舉起的拉丁語法書後面,藏起眼中的淚水。

passages.original: Not for worlds would Anne have had Gilbert Blythe or Josie Pye see those tears.
passages.vernacular: 講乜嘢安妮都唔願讓吉爾伯特·布萊斯或喬西·派伊睇到嗰啲眼淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說什麼安妮也不願讓吉爾伯特·布萊斯或喬西·派伊看到那些眼淚。

passages.original: “But, oh, Marilla, I really felt that I had tasted the bitterness of death, as Mr. Allan said in his sermon last Sunday, when I saw Diana go out alone,” she said mournfully that night.
passages.vernacular: 「但係,哦,瑪麗拉,我睇到黛安娜獨自出去嘅時候,我真嘅覺得自己嘗到咗死亡嘅苦澀,就像艾倫先生上個星期天嘅講道里講嘅,」嗰天晚上佢悲傷地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,哦,瑪麗拉,我看到黛安娜獨自出去的時候,我真的覺得自己嘗到了死亡的苦澀,就像艾倫先生上個星期天的講道里說的,」那天晚上她悲傷地說。

passages.original: “I thought how splendid it would have been if Diana had only been going to study for the Entrance, too.
passages.vernacular: 「我想,要係黛安娜都要準備入學考試該多好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想,要是黛安娜也要準備入學考試該多好。

passages.original: But we can’t have things perfect in this imperfect world, as Mrs. Lynde says.
passages.vernacular: 但我哋唔能夠喺呢個不完美嘅世界里事事完美,就像林德太太講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們不能在這個不完美的世界里事事完美,就像林德太太說的。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde isn’t exactly a comforting person sometimes, but there’s no doubt she says a great many very true things.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太有時不完全係個令人安慰嘅人,但毫無疑問佢講咗許多好真實嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太有時不完全是個令人安慰的人,但毫無疑問她說了許多非常真實的話。

passages.original: And I think the Queen’s class is going to be extremely interesting.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得女王學院班將會極其有趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得女王學院班將會極其有趣。

passages.original: Jane and Ruby are just going to study to be teachers.
passages.vernacular: 簡同露比只打算學做老師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡和露比只打算學做老師。

passages.original: That is the height of their ambition.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係佢哋志向嘅頂點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是她們志向的頂點。

passages.original: Ruby says she will only teach for two years after she gets through, and then she intends to be married.
passages.vernacular: 露比講佢畢業後只教兩年書,然後打算結婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比說她畢業後只教兩年書,然後打算結婚。

passages.original: Jane says she will devote her whole life to teaching, and never, never marry, because you are paid a salary for teaching, but a husband won’t pay you anything, and growls if you ask for a share in the egg and butter money.
passages.vernacular: 簡講佢要把全部生命獻畀教學,而且永遠,永遠不結婚,因為教書有薪水,而丈夫乜嘢都不畀你,如果你要求分享雞蛋同黃油錢,佢仲會咆哮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡說她要把全部生命獻給教學,而且永遠,永遠不結婚,因為教書有薪水,而丈夫什麼也不給你,如果你要求分享雞蛋和黃油錢,他還會咆哮。

passages.original: I expect Jane speaks from mournful experience, for Mrs. Lynde says that her father is a perfect old crank, and meaner than second skimmings.
passages.vernacular: 我想簡係喺講佢悲慘嘅經驗,因為林德太太講佢父親係個十足嘅怪脾氣老頭,比第二次撇嘅奶油仲小氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想簡是在說她悲慘的經驗,因為林德太太說她父親是個十足的怪脾氣老頭,比第二次撇的奶油還小氣。

passages.original: Josie Pye says she is just going to college for education’s sake, because she won’t have to earn her own living; she says of course it is different with orphans who are living on charity--they have to hustle.
passages.vernacular: 喬西·派伊講佢只係為了教育本身去上大學,因為佢唔使養活自己;佢講當然靠慈善生活嘅孤兒不一樣——佢哋必須奔波。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西·派伊說她只是為了教育本身去上大學,因為她不必養活自己;她說當然靠慈善生活的孤兒不一樣——他們必須奔波。

passages.original: Moody Spurgeon is going to be a minister.
passages.vernacular: 穆迪·斯珀吉翁要當牧師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 穆迪·斯珀吉翁要當牧師。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says he couldn’t be anything else with a name like that to live up to.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講有嗰樣嘅名字要配得上,佢唔可能做別嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說有那樣的名字要配得上,他不可能做別的。

passages.original: I hope it isn’t wicked of me, Marilla, but really the thought of Moody Spurgeon being a minister makes me laugh.
passages.vernacular: 我希望呢唔係邪惡嘅,瑪麗拉,但真嘅,穆迪·斯珀吉翁做牧師嘅想法讓我發笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望這不是邪惡的,瑪麗拉,但真的,穆迪·斯珀吉翁做牧師的想法讓我發笑。

passages.original: He’s such a funny-looking boy with that big fat face, and his little blue eyes, and his ears sticking out like flaps.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個長相咁滑稽嘅男孩,嗰張大胖臉,嗰雙藍色嘅小眼睛,仲有像蓋子一樣支楞住嘅耳朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個長相那麼滑稽的男孩,那張大胖臉,那雙藍色的小眼睛,還有像蓋子一樣支楞著的耳朵。

passages.original: But perhaps he will be more intellectual-looking when he grows up.
passages.vernacular: 但或者佢長大後會顯得更有學問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但也許他長大後會顯得更有學問。

passages.original: Charlie Sloane says he’s going to go into politics and be a member of Parliament, but Mrs. Lynde says he’ll never succeed at that, because the Sloanes are all honest people, and it’s only rascals that get on in politics nowadays.”
passages.vernacular: 查理·斯隆講佢要從政,做國會議員,但林德太太講佢喺嗰方面永遠唔會成功,因為斯隆家嘅人都係誠實嘅人,而家只有無賴才能喺政界混得好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 查理·斯隆說他要從政,做國會議員,但林德太太說他在那方面永遠不會成功,因為斯隆家的人都是誠實的人,現在只有無賴才能在政界混得好。」

passages.original: “What is Gilbert Blythe going to be?” queried Marilla, seeing that Anne was opening her Cæsar.
passages.vernacular: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯打算做乜嘢?」瑪麗拉問,睇見安妮喺翻開佢嘅《凱撒》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯打算做什麼?」瑪麗拉問,看見安妮在翻開她的《凱撒》。

passages.original: “I don’t happen to know what Gilbert Blythe’s ambition in life is--if he has any,” said Anne scornfully.
passages.vernacular: 「我碰巧唔知道吉爾伯特·布萊斯嘅人生志向係乜嘢——如果佢有嘅話,」安妮輕蔑地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我碰巧不知道吉爾伯特·布萊斯的人生志向是什麼——如果他有的話,」安妮輕蔑地說。

passages.original: There was open rivalry between Gilbert and Anne now.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特同安妮而家有公開嘅競爭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特和安妮現在有公開的競爭了。

passages.original: Previously the rivalry had been rather one-sided, but there was no longer any doubt that Gilbert was as determined to be first in class as Anne was.
passages.vernacular: 以前競爭相當單方面,但而家毫無疑問,吉爾伯特同安妮一樣決心要當班上第一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以前競爭相當單方面,但現在毫無疑問,吉爾伯特和安妮一樣決心要當班上第一。

passages.original: He was a foeman worthy of her steel.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個值得佢較量嘅對手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個值得她較量的對手。

passages.original: The other members of the class tacitly acknowledged their superiority, and never dreamed of trying to compete with them.
passages.vernacular: 班上嘅其他成員默默地承認佢哋嘅優越,從冇想過要同佢哋競爭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 班上的其他成員默默地承認他們的優越,從沒想過要和他們競爭。

passages.original: Since the day by the pond when she had refused to listen to his plea for forgiveness, Gilbert, save for the aforesaid determined rivalry, had evinced no recognition whatever of the existence of Anne Shirley.
passages.vernacular: 自從池塘邊嗰天佢拒絕聽佢求原諒以來,吉爾伯特除咗前面講嘅決心嘅競爭外,絲毫不承認安妮·雪莉嘅存在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從池塘邊那天她拒絕聽他求原諒以來,吉爾伯特除了前面說的決心的競爭外,絲毫不承認安妮·雪莉的存在。

passages.original: He talked and jested with the other girls, exchanged books and puzzles with them, discussed lessons and plans, sometimes walked home with one or the other of them from prayer meeting or Debating Club.
passages.vernacular: 佢同其他女孩講話、開玩笑,同佢哋交換書同謎語,討論功課同計劃,有時從祈禱會或辯論社同佢哋中嘅某一個一起走回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他和其他女孩說話、開玩笑,與她們交換書和謎語,討論功課和計劃,有時從祈禱會或辯論社與她們中的某一個一起走回家。

passages.original: But Anne Shirley he simply ignored, and Anne found out that it is not pleasant to be ignored.
passages.vernacular: 但安妮·雪莉佢就係不理,安妮發現被忽視係不愉快嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安妮·雪莉他就是不理,安妮發現被忽視是不愉快的。

passages.original: It was in vain that she told herself with a toss of her head that she did not care.
passages.vernacular: 佢甩甩頭,告訴自己佢不在乎,但徒勞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她甩甩頭,告訴自己她不在乎,但徒勞。

passages.original: Deep down in her wayward, feminine little heart she knew that she did care, and that if she had that chance of the Lake of Shining Waters again she would answer very differently.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢任性嘅、女細路氣嘅小心靈深處,佢知道自己在乎,如果佢再有閃亮湖水嗰樣嘅機會,佢會回答得好不同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她任性的、女孩子氣的小心靈深處,她知道自己在乎,如果她再有閃亮湖水那樣的機會,她會回答得非常不同。

passages.original: All at once, as it seemed, and to her secret dismay, she found that the old resentment she had cherished against him was gone--gone just when she most needed its sustaining power.
passages.vernacular: 似乎突然間,令佢暗暗驚慌嘅係,佢發現自己對佢懷有嘅舊怨消失喇——恰恰喺佢最需要佢嘅支撐力量嘅時候消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 似乎突然間,令她暗暗驚慌的是,她發現自己對他懷有的舊怨消失了——恰恰在她最需要它的支撐力量的時候消失了。

passages.original: It was in vain that she recalled every incident and emotion of that memorable occasion and tried to feel the old satisfying anger.
passages.vernacular: 佢徒勞地回想嗰個難忘嘅場合嘅每一個細節同情緒,試圖感到從前嗰種令人滿足嘅憤怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她徒勞地回想那個難忘的場合的每一個細節和情緒,試圖感到從前那種令人滿足的憤怒。

passages.original: That day by the pond had witnessed its last spasmodic flicker.
passages.vernacular: 池塘邊嗰天見證咗佢最後嘅痙攣閃爍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 池塘邊那天見證了它最後的痙攣閃爍。

passages.original: Anne realized that she had forgiven and forgotten without knowing it.
passages.vernacular: 安妮意識到佢喺唔知不覺中原諒並忘記喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮意識到她在不知不覺中原諒並忘記了。

passages.original: But it was too late.
passages.vernacular: 但太遲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但太遲了。

passages.original: And at least neither Gilbert nor anybody else, not even Diana, should ever suspect how sorry she was and how much she wished she hadn’t been so proud and horrid!
passages.vernacular: 至少吉爾伯特或任何人,甚至黛安娜,都唔應該懷疑佢有多抱歉,多希望自己當時冇咁驕傲同討厭!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少吉爾伯特或任何人,甚至黛安娜,都不應懷疑她有多抱歉,多希望自己當時沒有那麼驕傲和討厭!

passages.original: She determined to “shroud her feelings in deepest oblivion,” and it may be stated here and now that she did it, so successfully that Gilbert, who possibly was not quite so indifferent as he seemed, could not console himself with any belief that Anne felt his retaliatory scorn.
passages.vernacular: 佢決定「把佢嘅感情掩藏喺最深嘅遺忘中」,可以喺此講明,佢做到喇,而且咁成功,以至於吉爾伯特,佢可能並不像睇上去咁無動於衷,無法安慰自己相信安妮感受到咗佢報復性嘅蔑視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她決定「把她的感情掩藏在最深的遺忘中」,可以在此說明,她做到了,而且那麼成功,以至於吉爾伯特,他可能並不像看上去那麼無動於衷,無法安慰自己相信安妮感受到了他報復性的蔑視。

passages.original: The only poor comfort he had was that she snubbed Charlie Sloane, unmercifully, continually, and undeservedly.
passages.vernacular: 佢僅有嘅可憐嘅安慰係,佢殘酷地、不停地、無緣無故地冷落查理·斯隆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他僅有的可憐的安慰是,她殘酷地、不停地、無緣無故地冷落查理·斯隆。

passages.original: Otherwise the winter passed away in a round of pleasant duties and studies.
passages.vernacular: 除此之外,冬天喺一連串愉快嘅職責同學習中過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除此之外,冬天在一連串愉快的職責和學習中過去了。

passages.original: For Anne the days slipped by like golden beads on the necklace of the year.
passages.vernacular: 對安妮來講,日子像金色嘅珠子一樣從一年嘅項鍊上滑過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對安妮來說,日子像金色的珠子一樣從一年的項鍊上滑過。

passages.original: She was happy, eager, interested; there were lessons to be learned and honor to be won; delightful books to read; new pieces to be practiced for the Sunday-school choir; pleasant Saturday afternoons at the manse with Mrs. Allan; and then, almost before Anne realized it, spring had come again to Green Gables and all the world was abloom once more.
passages.vernacular: 佢快樂、熱切、有興趣;有功課要學,有榮譽要贏;有美妙嘅書要讀;有新曲子要為主日學校唱詩班練習;有喺牧師住宅同艾倫太太共度嘅愉快嘅星期六下午;然後,幾乎喺安妮意識到之前,春天又回到咗綠色屋頂,整個世界再次開滿咗花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她快樂、熱切、有興趣;有功課要學,有榮譽要贏;有美妙的書要讀;有新曲子要為主日學校唱詩班練習;有在牧師住宅與艾倫太太共度的愉快的星期六下午;然後,幾乎在安妮意識到之前,春天又回到了綠色屋頂,整個世界再次開滿了花。

passages.original: Studies palled just a wee bit then; the Queen’s class, left behind in school while the others scattered to green lanes and leafy wood cuts and meadow byways, looked wistfully out of the windows and discovered that Latin verbs and French exercises had somehow lost the tang and zest they had possessed in the crisp winter months.
passages.vernacular: 嗰時學習有點乏味咗啲點;女王學院班被留喺學校里,而其他人散去到綠色嘅小巷、樹葉茂密嘅伐木小徑同草地岔路,佢哋悵然地望住窗外,發現拉丁語動詞同法語練習,唔知怎嘅已失去咗佢哋喺清爽嘅冬月中曾有嘅辛辣同興味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時學習有點乏味了一點點;女王學院班被留在學校里,而其他人散去到綠色的小巷、樹葉茂密的伐木小徑和草地岔路,她們悵然地望著窗外,發現拉丁語動詞和法語練習,不知怎的已失去了它們在清爽的冬月中曾有的辛辣和興味。

passages.original: Even Anne and Gilbert lagged and grew indifferent.
passages.vernacular: 連安妮同吉爾伯特都落後喇,變得無精打采。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連安妮和吉爾伯特也落後了,變得無精打采。

passages.original: Teacher and taught were alike glad when the term was ended and the glad vacation days stretched rosily before them.
passages.vernacular: 學期結束時,師生同樣高興,快樂嘅假期玫瑰色地展而家佢哋面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學期結束時,師生同樣高興,快樂的假期玫瑰色地展現在他們面前。

passages.original: “But you’ve done good work this past year,” Miss Stacy told them on the last evening, “and you deserve a good, jolly vacation.
passages.vernacular: 「但你哋過去呢一年做得好好,」斯泰西小姐喺最後一個晚上對佢哋講,「你哋理應有一個美好、快樂嘅假期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你們過去這一年做得很好,」斯泰西小姐在最後一個晚上對他們說,「你們理應有一個美好、快樂的假期。

passages.original: Have the best time you can in the out-of-door world and lay in a good stock of health and vitality and ambition to carry you through next year.
passages.vernacular: 儘可能喺戶外世界里過得最開心,積蓄足夠嘅健康、活力同志向,帶你哋度過明年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘可能在戶外世界里過得最開心,積蓄足夠的健康、活力和志向,帶你們度過明年。

passages.original: It will be the tug of war, you know--the last year before the Entrance.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰將係拔河比賽,你哋知道——入學考試前嘅最後一年。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那將是拔河比賽,你們知道——入學考試前的最後一年。」

passages.original: “Are you going to be back next year, Miss Stacy?” asked Josie Pye.
passages.vernacular: 「您明年仲回嚟嗎,斯泰西小姐?」喬西·派伊問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您明年還回來嗎,斯泰西小姐?」喬西·派伊問。

passages.original: Josie Pye never scrupled to ask questions; in this instance the rest of the class felt grateful to her; none of them would have dared to ask it of Miss Stacy, but all wanted to, for there had been alarming rumors running at large through the school for some time that Miss Stacy was not coming back the next year--that she had been offered a position in the grade school of her own home district and meant to accept.
passages.vernacular: 喬西·派伊從不猶豫提問;呢次班上其他人都感激佢;佢哋中冇人敢問斯泰西小姐,但都想問,因為學校里已經流傳咗一陣令人不安嘅謠言,講斯泰西小姐明年不回嚟喇——講佢被提供咗佢自己家鄉學區小學嘅一個職位,打算接受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西·派伊從不猶豫提問;這次班上其他人都感激她;他們中沒有人敢問斯泰西小姐,但都想問,因為學校里已經流傳了一陣令人不安的謠言,說斯泰西小姐明年不回來了——說她被提供了她自己家鄉學區小學的一個職位,打算接受。

passages.original: The Queen’s class listened in breathless suspense for her answer.
passages.vernacular: 女王學院班屏息懸念地等待佢嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女王學院班屏息懸念地等待她的回答。

passages.original: “Yes, I think I will,” said Miss Stacy.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我想我會,」斯泰西小姐講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我想我會,」斯泰西小姐說。

passages.original: “I thought of taking another school, but I have decided to come back to Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 「我考慮過去另一所學校,但我決定回阿文利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我考慮過去另一所學校,但我決定回阿文利。

passages.original: To tell the truth, I’ve grown so interested in my pupils here that I found I couldn’t leave them.
passages.vernacular: 講實話,我對呢度嘅學生越嚟越感興趣,發現自己離不開佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說實話,我對這裡的學生越來越感興趣,發現自己離不開他們。

passages.original: So I’ll stay and see you through.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我留下嚟,陪你哋走完。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我留下來,陪你們走完。」

passages.original: “Hurrah!” said Moody Spurgeon.
passages.vernacular: 「萬歲!」穆迪·斯珀吉翁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「萬歲!」穆迪·斯珀吉翁說。

passages.original: Moody Spurgeon had never been so carried away by his feelings before, and he blushed uncomfortably every time he thought about it for a week.
passages.vernacular: 穆迪·斯珀吉翁以前從冇咁樣被感情沖昏過頭,接下嚟一個星期里,每次想到呢件事佢都不舒服地臉紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 穆迪·斯珀吉翁以前從沒這樣被感情沖昏過頭,接下來一個星期里,每次想到這件事他都不舒服地臉紅。

passages.original: “Oh, I’m so glad,” said Anne, with shining eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我太高興喇,」安妮眼睛閃亮地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我太高興了,」安妮眼睛閃亮地說。

passages.original: “Dear Stacy, it would be perfectly dreadful if you didn’t come back.
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅斯泰西,要係您不回嚟,嗰會係完全可怕嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的斯泰西,要是您不回來,那會是完全可怕的。

passages.original: I don’t believe I could have the heart to go on with my studies at all if another teacher came here.”
passages.vernacular: 我相信如果有另一位老師嚟呢兒,我根本冇心情繼續學習。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信如果有另一位老師來這兒,我根本沒心情繼續學習。」

passages.original: When Anne got home that night she stacked all her textbooks away in an old trunk in the attic, locked it, and threw the key into the blanket box.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上安妮回到家,把所有課本堆放喺閣樓嘅一個舊箱子里,鎖上,把鑰匙扔進咗被褥箱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上安妮回到家,把所有課本堆放在閣樓的一個舊箱子里,鎖上,把鑰匙扔進了被褥箱。

passages.original: “I’m not even going to look at a schoolbook in vacation,” she told Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「假期里我連一本課本都唔想睇,」佢告訴瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「假期里我連一本課本都不想看,」她告訴瑪麗拉。

passages.original: “I’ve studied as hard all the term as I possibly could and I’ve pored over that geometry until I know every proposition in the first book off by heart, even when the letters are changed.
passages.vernacular: 「整個學期我盡可能地努力學習,啃嗰本幾何,直到我把第一冊里嘅每個命題都背得滾瓜爛熟,連字母換咗都一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「整個學期我盡可能地努力學習,啃那本幾何,直到我把第一冊里的每個命題都背得滾瓜爛熟,連字母換了也一樣。

passages.original: I just feel tired of everything sensible and I’m going to let my imagination run riot for the summer.
passages.vernacular: 我只係對一切明智嘅嘢感到厭倦,我打算整個夏天讓我嘅想像力放縱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是對一切明智的東西感到厭倦,我打算整個夏天讓我的想像力放縱。

passages.original: Oh, you needn’t be alarmed, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 哦,您唔使驚慌,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,您不必驚慌,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I’ll only let it run riot within reasonable limits.
passages.vernacular: 我只會喺合理嘅範圍內讓佢放縱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只會在合理的範圍內讓它放縱。

passages.original: But I want to have a real good jolly time this summer, for maybe it’s the last summer I’ll be a little girl.
passages.vernacular: 但我想有一個真正美好快樂嘅夏天,因為呢或者係我做小女孩嘅最後一個夏天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我想有一個真正美好快樂的夏天,因為這也許是我做小女孩的最後一個夏天。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says that if I keep stretching out next year as I’ve done this I’ll have to put on longer skirts.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講,如果明年我繼續像今年咁樣長高,我就得穿更長嘅裙子喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說,如果明年我繼續像今年這樣長高,我就得穿更長的裙子了。

passages.original: She says I’m all running to legs and eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我全長喺腿同眼睛上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我全長在腿和眼睛上了。

passages.original: And when I put on longer skirts I shall feel that I have to live up to them and be very dignified.
passages.vernacular: 當我穿上更長嘅裙子,我會覺得必須配得上佢哋,要好莊重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我穿上更長的裙子,我會覺得必須配得上它們,要非常莊重。

passages.original: It won’t even do to believe in fairies then, I’m afraid; so I’m going to believe in them with all my whole heart this summer.
passages.vernacular: 我恐怕嗰時連相信仙女都不行喇;所以呢個夏天我要全心全意地相信佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我恐怕那時連相信仙女都不行了;所以這個夏天我要全心全意地相信它們。

passages.original: I think we’re going to have a very gay vacation.
passages.vernacular: 我想我哋會有一個好歡樂嘅假期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我們會有一個非常歡樂的假期。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis is going to have a birthday party soon and there’s the Sunday-school picnic and the missionary concert next month.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯不久要辦生日派對,仲有下個月嘅主日學校野餐同傳教士音樂會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯不久要辦生日派對,還有下個月的主日學校野餐和傳教士音樂會。

passages.original: And Mr. Barry says that some evening he’ll take Diana and me over to the White Sands Hotel and have dinner there.
passages.vernacular: 巴里先生講有天晚上佢會帶黛安娜同我去白沙旅館食晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里先生說有天晚上他會帶黛安娜和我去白沙旅館吃晚飯。

passages.original: They have dinner there in the evening, you know.
passages.vernacular: 您知道,佢哋嗰度晚上有正餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道,他們那裡晚上有正餐。

passages.original: Jane Andrews was over once last summer and she says it was a dazzling sight to see the electric lights and the flowers and all the lady guests in such beautiful dresses.
passages.vernacular: 簡·安德魯斯去年夏天去過一次,佢講睇到電燈同花,以及所有穿住咁美嘅裙子嘅女客人,係令人眼花繚亂嘅景象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡·安德魯斯去年夏天去過一次,她說看到電燈和花,以及所有穿著那麼美的裙子的女客人,是令人眼花繚亂的景象。

passages.original: Jane says it was her first glimpse into high life and she’ll never forget it to her dying day.”
passages.vernacular: 簡講嗰個係佢第一次窺見上流社會,佢至死都唔會忘記。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡說那是她第一次窺見上流社會,她至死都不會忘記。」

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde came up the next afternoon to find out why Marilla had not been at the Aid meeting on Thursday.
passages.vernacular: 第二天下午林德太太上嚟,想知道瑪麗拉星期四點解冇去互助會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天下午林德太太上來,想知道瑪麗拉星期四為什麼沒去互助會。

passages.original: When Marilla was not at Aid meeting people knew there was something wrong at Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉冇去互助會時,人哋就知道綠色屋頂出事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉沒去互助會時,人們就知道綠色屋頂出事了。

passages.original: “Matthew had a bad spell with his heart Thursday,” Marilla explained, “and I didn’t feel like leaving him.
passages.vernacular: 「馬修星期四心臟病發作得厲害,」瑪麗拉解釋,「我唔想離開佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修星期四心臟病發作得厲害,」瑪麗拉解釋,「我不想離開他。

passages.original: Oh, yes, he’s all right again now, but he takes them spells oftener than he used to and I’m anxious about him.
passages.vernacular: 哦,係嘅,佢而家又好喇,但佢發呢種病比以前頻繁喇,我為佢擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,是的,他現在又好了,但他發這種病比以前頻繁了,我為他擔心。

passages.original: The doctor says he must be careful to avoid excitement.
passages.vernacular: 醫生講佢必須小心避免激動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生說他必須小心避免激動。

passages.original: That’s easy enough, for Matthew doesn’t go about looking for excitement by any means and never did, but he’s not to do any very heavy work either and you might as well tell Matthew not to breathe as not to work.
passages.vernacular: 呢個好容易,因為馬修根本唔到處找刺激,從來冇,但佢都唔能夠做任何好重嘅活,你不如叫馬修別呼吸,都別叫佢別幹活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這很容易,因為馬修根本不到處找刺激,從來沒有,但他也不能做任何很重的活,你不如叫馬修別呼吸,也別叫他別幹活。

passages.original: Come and lay off your things, Rachel.
passages.vernacular: 過嚟把嘢脫喇,雷切爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過來把東西脫了,雷切爾。

passages.original: You’ll stay to tea?”
passages.vernacular: 你留下飲茶嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你留下喝茶嗎?」

passages.original: “Well, seeing you’re so pressing, perhaps I might as well, stay” said Mrs. Rachel, who had not the slightest intention of doing anything else.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,既然你咁懇切,或者我不妨留下,」雷切爾太太講,佢絲毫冇打算做別嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,既然你這麼懇切,也許我不妨留下,」雷切爾太太說,她絲毫沒有打算做別的。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel and Marilla sat comfortably in the parlor while Anne got the tea and made hot biscuits that were light and white enough to defy even Mrs. Rachel’s criticism.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太同瑪麗拉舒舒服服地坐喺客廳里,而安妮準備咗茶,做咗熱餅乾,輕而白,足以抵禦連雷切爾太太嘅批評。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太和瑪麗拉舒舒服服地坐在客廳里,而安妮準備了茶,做了熱餅乾,輕而白,足以抵禦連雷切爾太太的批評。

passages.original: “I must say Anne has turned out a real smart girl,” admitted Mrs. Rachel, as Marilla accompanied her to the end of the lane at sunset.
passages.vernacular: 「我必須講安妮成咗一個真正聰明嘅女孩,」日落時瑪麗拉陪雷切爾太太到小巷盡頭,雷切爾太太承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須說安妮成了一個真正聰明的女孩,」日落時瑪麗拉陪雷切爾太太到小巷盡頭,雷切爾太太承認。

passages.original: “She must be a great help to you.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢一定係你嘅大幫手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她一定是你的大幫手。」

passages.original: “She is,” said Marilla, “and she’s real steady and reliable now.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」瑪麗拉講,「佢而家真嘅好穩重可靠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」瑪麗拉說,「她現在真的很穩重可靠。

passages.original: I used to be afraid she’d never get over her featherbrained ways, but she has and I wouldn’t be afraid to trust her in anything now.”
passages.vernacular: 我過去擔心佢永遠改不掉佢輕浮嘅作風,但佢改喇,而家我乜嘢都敢信任佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我過去擔心她永遠改不掉她輕浮的作風,但她改了,現在我什麼都敢信任她。」

passages.original: “I never would have thought she’d have turned out so well that first day I was here three years ago,” said Mrs. Rachel.
passages.vernacular: 「三年前我第一天嚟呢兒,我點都冇想到佢會長得咁好,」雷切爾太太講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「三年前我第一天來這兒,我怎麼也沒想到她會長得這麼好,」雷切爾太太說。

passages.original: “Lawful heart, shall I ever forget that tantrum of hers!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,我能忘記佢嗰次發脾氣嗎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,我能忘記她那次發脾氣嗎!

passages.original: When I went home that night I says to Thomas, says I, ‘Mark my words, Thomas, Marilla Cuthbert ‘ll live to rue the step she’s took.’
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上我回家對托馬斯講,我講:『記住我嘅話,托馬斯,瑪麗拉·卡思伯特會為佢邁出嘅呢一步後悔嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上我回家對托馬斯說,我說:『記住我的話,托馬斯,瑪麗拉·卡思伯特會為她邁出的這一步後悔的。』

passages.original: But I was mistaken and I’m real glad of it.
passages.vernacular: 但我錯喇,我真嘅好高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我錯了,我真的很高興。

passages.original: I ain’t one of those kind of people, Marilla, as can never be brought to own up that they’ve made a mistake.
passages.vernacular: 我唔係嗰種永遠唔肯承認自己犯咗錯誤嘅人,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是那種永遠不肯承認自己犯了錯誤的人,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: No, that never was my way, thank goodness.
passages.vernacular: 不,我從來唔係嗰樣,謝天謝地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我從來不是那樣,謝天謝地。

passages.original: I did make a mistake in judging Anne, but it weren’t no wonder, for an odder, unexpecteder witch of a child there never was in this world, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 我評價安妮時確實錯喇,但呢不奇怪,因為世上再冇比呢更古怪、更意想唔到嘅小妖精細路喇,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我評價安妮時確實錯了,但這不奇怪,因為世上再沒有比這更古怪、更意想不到的小妖精孩子了,就是這樣。

passages.original: There was no ciphering her out by the rules that worked with other children.
passages.vernacular: 唔能夠用對別嘅細路管用嘅規則嚟琢磨佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不能用對別的孩子管用的規則來琢磨她。

passages.original: It’s nothing short of wonderful how she’s improved these three years, but especially in looks.
passages.vernacular: 呢三年佢進步之大簡直係奇蹟,尤其係容貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這三年她進步之大簡直是奇蹟,尤其是容貌。

passages.original: She’s a real pretty girl got to be, though I can’t say I’m overly partial to that pale, big-eyed style myself.
