passages.vernacular: 佢變成咗一個真正漂亮嘅女孩,雖然我自己不太偏愛嗰種蒼白、大眼睛嘅類型。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她變成了一個真正漂亮的女孩,雖然我自己不太偏愛那種蒼白、大眼睛的類型。

passages.original: I like more snap and color, like Diana Barry has or Ruby Gillis.
passages.vernacular: 我更鍾意有活力同顏色嘅,像黛安娜·巴里或露比·吉利斯嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我更喜歡有活力和顏色的,像黛安娜·巴里或露比·吉利斯那樣。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis’s looks are real showy.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯嘅長相真係顯眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯的長相真是顯眼。

passages.original: But somehow--I don’t know how it is but when Anne and them are together, though she ain’t half as handsome, she makes them look kind of common and overdone--something like them white June lilies she calls narcissus alongside of the big, red peonies, that’s what.”
passages.vernacular: 但唔知怎嘅——我唔知道係點回事,但係當安妮同佢哋喺一起時,儘管佢連一半都冇咁漂亮,佢卻讓佢哋顯得有點平庸同俗氣——有點像佢叫水仙花嘅嗰啲白色六月百合,放喺大紅芍藥旁邊,就係咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但不知怎的——我不知道是怎麼回事,但是當安妮和她們在一起時,儘管她連一半都沒有那麼漂亮,她卻讓她們顯得有點平庸和俗氣——有點像她叫水仙花的那些白色六月百合,放在大紅芍藥旁邊,就是這樣。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXXI Where the Brook and River Meet 第三十一章:小溪與大河交匯處

passages.original: CH ANNE had her “good” summer and enjoyed it wholeheartedly.
passages.vernacular: 安妮度過咗佢「好」嘅夏天,並全心全意地享受佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮度過了她「好」的夏天,並全心全意地享受它。

passages.original: She and Diana fairly lived outdoors, reveling in all the delights that Lover’s Lane and the Dryad’s Bubble and Willowmere and Victoria Island afforded.
passages.vernacular: 佢同黛安娜簡直生活喺戶外,陶醉於情人小徑、林中仙子泉、柳塘同維多利亞島所提供嘅一切樂趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她和黛安娜簡直生活在戶外,陶醉於情人小徑、林中仙子泉、柳塘和維多利亞島所提供的一切樂趣。

passages.original: Marilla offered no objections to Anne’s gypsyings.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉對安妮嘅吉普賽式流浪冇提出任何反對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉對安妮的吉普賽式流浪沒有提出任何反對。

passages.original: The Spencervale doctor who had come the night Minnie May had the croup met Anne at the house of a patient one afternoon early in vacation, looked her over sharply, screwed up his mouth, shook his head, and sent a message to Marilla Cuthbert by another person.
passages.vernacular: 明妮·梅得哮吼嗰晚嚟過嘅斯潘塞韋爾醫生,喺假期初嘅一個下午,喺一位病人家裡遇到咗安妮,佢銳利地打量咗佢一番,撇住嘴,搖搖頭,通過另一個人畀瑪麗拉·卡思伯特捎咗口信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明妮·梅得哮吼那晚來過的斯潘塞韋爾醫生,在假期初的一個下午,在一位病人家裡遇到了安妮,他銳利地打量了她一番,撇著嘴,搖搖頭,通過另一個人給瑪麗拉·卡思伯特捎了口信。

passages.original: It was:
passages.vernacular: 口信係:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 口信是:

passages.original: “Keep that redheaded girl of yours in the open air all summer and don’t let her read books until she gets more spring into her step.”
passages.vernacular: 「整個夏天讓你嗰紅頭髮女孩待喺戶外,唔好畀佢睇書,直到佢嘅腳步多啲彈性。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「整個夏天讓你那紅頭髮女孩待在戶外,別讓她看書,直到她的腳步多一點彈性。」

passages.original: This message frightened Marilla wholesomely.
passages.vernacular: 呢個口信有益地嚇壞咗瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個口信有益地嚇壞了瑪麗拉。

passages.original: She read Anne’s death warrant by consumption in it unless it was scrupulously obeyed.
passages.vernacular: 佢從中讀出咗安妮嘅肺癆死亡判決書,除非嚴格服從。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她從中讀出了安妮的肺癆死亡判決書,除非嚴格服從。

passages.original: As a result, Anne had the golden summer of her life as far as freedom and frolic went.
passages.vernacular: 結果,就自由同嬉戲而言,安妮度過咗佢一生中嘅黃金夏天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果,就自由和嬉戲而言,安妮度過了她一生中的黃金夏天。

passages.original: She walked, rowed, berried, and dreamed to her heart’s content; and when September came she was bright-eyed and alert, with a step that would have satisfied the Spencervale doctor and a heart full of ambition and zest once more.
passages.vernacular: 佢隨心所欲地走路、划船、採漿果、做夢;九月來臨時,佢眼睛明亮、機警,腳步會讓斯潘塞韋爾醫生滿意,心裡又充滿咗雄心同熱情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她隨心所欲地走路、划船、採漿果、做夢;九月來臨時,她眼睛明亮、機警,腳步會讓斯潘塞韋爾醫生滿意,心裡又充滿了雄心和熱情。

passages.original: “I feel just like studying with might and main,” she declared as she brought her books down from the attic.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得自己就想拼命學習,」佢宣布,一邊把書從閣樓上攞下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得自己就想拼命學習,」她宣布,一邊把書從閣樓上拿下來。

passages.original: “Oh, you good old friends, I’m glad to see your honest faces once more--yes, even you, geometry.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你哋呢啲親愛嘅老朋友,再次睇到你哋誠實嘅臉,我真高興——係嘅,連你,幾何都一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你們這些親愛的老朋友,再次看到你們誠實的臉,我真高興——是的,連你,幾何也一樣。

passages.original: I’ve had a perfectly beautiful summer, Marilla, and now I’m rejoicing as a strong man to run a race, as Mr. Allan said last Sunday.
passages.vernacular: 我度過咗一個極其美麗嘅夏天,瑪麗拉,而家我像個強壯嘅人一樣,為賽跑而歡喜,就像艾倫先生上星期天講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我度過了一個極其美麗的夏天,瑪麗拉,現在我像個強壯的人一樣,為賽跑而歡喜,就像艾倫先生上星期天說的。

passages.original: Doesn’t Mr. Allan preach magnificent sermons?
passages.vernacular: 艾倫先生唔係講道講得好精彩嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫先生不是講道講得很精彩嗎?

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde says he is improving every day and the first thing we know some city church will gobble him up and then we’ll be left and have to turn to and break in another green preacher.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太講佢每天都喺進步,我哋仲冇反應過嚟,某個城裡嘅教堂就會把佢吞掉,然後我哋就被撇下喇,唔得不動手調教另一個稚嫩嘅牧師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太說他每天都在進步,我們還沒反應過來,某個城裡的教堂就會把他吞掉,然後我們就被撇下了,不得不動手調教另一個稚嫩的牧師。

passages.original: But I don’t see the use of meeting trouble halfway, do you, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 但係我睇不出提前迎接麻煩有乜嘢用,您講呢,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是我看不出提前迎接麻煩有什麼用,您說呢,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: I think it would be better just to enjoy Mr. Allan while we have him.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得最好係趁我哋仲擁有艾倫先生嘅時候享受佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得最好是趁我們還擁有艾倫先生的時候享受他。

passages.original: If I were a man I think I’d be a minister.
passages.vernacular: 如果我係男人,我想我會做牧師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我是男人,我想我會做牧師。

passages.original: They can have such an influence for good, if their theology is sound; and it must be thrilling to preach splendid sermons and stir your hearers’ hearts.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋能產生咁大嘅好影響,如果佢哋嘅神學係健全嘅;而且講精彩嘅道、激動聽眾嘅心,一定令人激動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們能產生這麼大的好影響,如果他們的神學是健全的;而且講精彩的道、激動聽眾的心,一定令人激動。

passages.original: Why can’t women be ministers, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 點解女人唔能夠做牧師,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼女人不能做牧師,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: I asked Mrs. Lynde that and she was shocked and said it would be a scandalous thing.
passages.vernacular: 我問過林德太太,佢震驚喇,講嗰會係醜聞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我問過林德太太,她震驚了,說那會是醜聞。

passages.original: She said there might be female ministers in the States and she believed there was, but thank goodness we hadn’t got to that stage in Canada yet and she hoped we never would.
passages.vernacular: 佢講美國可能有女牧師,佢相信有,但謝天謝地我哋加攞大仲冇到嗰個階段,佢希望永遠唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說美國可能有女牧師,她相信有,但謝天謝地我們加拿大還沒到那個階段,她希望永遠不會。

passages.original: But I don’t see why.
passages.vernacular: 但我睇不出點解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我看不出為什麼。

passages.original: I think women would make splendid ministers.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得女人會成為出色嘅牧師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得女人會成為出色的牧師。

passages.original: When there is a social to be got up or a church tea or anything else to raise money the women have to turn to and do the work.
passages.vernacular: 要辦聯誼會或教堂茶會,或任何別嘅籌款活動時,都係女人動手幹活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要辦聯誼會或教堂茶會,或任何別的籌款活動時,都是女人動手幹活。

passages.original: I’m sure Mrs. Lynde can pray every bit as well as Superintendent Bell and I’ve no doubt she could preach too with a little practice.”
passages.vernacular: 我肯定林德太太禱告起嚟同貝爾督導一樣好,我都毫不懷疑,只要稍加練習,佢都能講道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我肯定林德太太禱告起來和貝爾督導一樣好,我也毫不懷疑,只要稍加練習,她也能講道。」

passages.original: “Yes, I believe she could,” said Marilla dryly.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我相信佢能,」瑪麗拉乾巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我相信她能,」瑪麗拉乾巴巴地說。

passages.original: “She does plenty of unofficial preaching as it is.
passages.vernacular: 「佢而家就做咗大量非官方嘅講道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她現在就做了大量非官方的講道。

passages.original: Nobody has much of a chance to go wrong in Avonlea with Rachel to oversee them.”
passages.vernacular: 有雷切爾監督住,阿文利冇人有多大嘅機會走上歪路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有雷切爾監督著,阿文利沒有人有多大的機會走上歪路。」

passages.original: “Marilla,” said Anne in a burst of confidence, “I want to tell you something and ask you what you think about it.
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉,」安妮突然傾吐地講,「我想告訴您一件事,問問您點睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉,」安妮突然傾吐地說,「我想告訴您一件事,問問您怎麼看。

passages.original: It has worried me terribly--on Sunday afternoons, that is, when I think specially about such matters.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓我特別苦惱——喺星期天下午,都就係我特別思考呢類事情嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它讓我特別苦惱——在星期天下午,也就是我特別思考這類事情的時候。

passages.original: I do really want to be good; and when I’m with you or Mrs. Allan or Miss Stacy I want it more than ever and I want to do just what would please you and what you would approve of.
passages.vernacular: 我真嘅想做個好人;同您、艾倫太太或斯泰西小姐喺一起時,我想得比任何時候都強烈,我想做讓你哋高興、讓你哋贊成嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真的想做個好人;和您、艾倫太太或斯泰西小姐在一起時,我想得比任何時候都強烈,我想做讓你們高興、讓你們贊成的事。

passages.original: But mostly when I’m with Mrs. Lynde I feel desperately wicked and as if I wanted to go and do the very thing she tells me I oughtn’t to do.
passages.vernacular: 但大部分時候,同林德太太喺一起時,我覺得自己壞透喇,好像想去做佢告訴我不該做嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但大部分時候,和林德太太在一起時,我覺得自己壞透了,好像想去做她告訴我不該做的事。

passages.original: I feel irresistibly tempted to do it.
passages.vernacular: 我感到有一種無法抗拒嘅誘惑要去做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感到有一種無法抗拒的誘惑要去做。

passages.original: Now, what do you think is the reason I feel like that?
passages.vernacular: 而家,您覺得我有呢種感覺嘅原因係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,您覺得我有這種感覺的原因是什麼?

passages.original: Do you think it’s because I’m really bad and unregenerate?”
passages.vernacular: 您覺得係唔係因為我真嘅係壞嘅、未得重生嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您覺得是不是因為我真的是壞的、未得重生的?」

passages.original: Marilla looked dubious for a moment.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉遲疑咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉遲疑了一會兒。

passages.original: Then she laughed.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她笑了。

passages.original: “If you are I guess I am too, Anne, for Rachel often has that very effect on me.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你係,我想我都係,安妮,因為雷切爾常常對我有呢種影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你是,我想我也是,安妮,因為雷切爾常常對我有這種影響。

passages.original: I sometimes think she’d have more of an influence for good, as you say yourself, if she didn’t keep nagging people to do right.
passages.vernacular: 我有時想,如果佢不老係嘮叨人家行善,佢對人嘅好影響會更大,就像你自己講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有時想,如果她不老是嘮叨人家行善,她對人的好影響會更大,就像你自己說的。

passages.original: There should have been a special commandment against nagging.
passages.vernacular: 本應該有一條專門反對嘮叨嘅誡命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 本應該有一條專門反對嘮叨的誡命。

passages.original: But there, I shouldn’t talk so.
passages.vernacular: 不過,我不該咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,我不該這麼說。

passages.original: Rachel is a good Christian woman and she means well.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾係個好基督徒婦女,佢心眼好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾是個好基督徒婦女,她心眼好。

passages.original: There isn’t a kinder soul in Avonlea and she never shirks her share of work.”
passages.vernacular: 阿文利冇比佢更善良嘅人,而且佢從不逃避自己嗰份工作。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿文利沒有比她更善良的人,而且她從不逃避自己那份工作。」

passages.original: “I’m very glad you feel the same,” said Anne decidedly.
passages.vernacular: 「您嘅感覺同我一樣,我太高興喇,」安妮堅決地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您的感覺和我一樣,我太高興了,」安妮堅決地說。

passages.original: “It’s so encouraging.
passages.vernacular: 「呢太令人鼓舞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這太令人鼓舞了。

passages.original: I shan’t worry so much over that after this.
passages.vernacular: 從今以後我唔會再為此咁擔心喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從今以後我不會再為此那麼擔心了。

passages.original: But I dare say there’ll be other things to worry me.
passages.vernacular: 但我敢講仲會有別嘅事讓我擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我敢說還會有別的事讓我擔心。

passages.original: They keep coming up new all the time--things to perplex you, you know.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不停地冒出嚟,新嘅——讓你困惑嘅事,您知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們不停地冒出來,新的——讓你困惑的事,您知道。

passages.original: You settle one question and there’s another right after.
passages.vernacular: 你解決咗一個問題,緊接住又有一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你解決了一個問題,緊接著又有一個。

passages.original: There are so many things to be thought over and decided when you’re beginning to grow up.
passages.vernacular: 當你開始長大,有咁多事情要思考同決定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你開始長大,有這麼多事情要思考和決定。

passages.original: It keeps me busy all the time thinking them over and deciding what is right.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓我整天忙住思考佢哋,決定乜嘢係對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它讓我整天忙著思考它們,決定什麼是對的。

passages.original: It’s a serious thing to grow up, isn’t it, Marilla?
passages.vernacular: 長大係件嚴肅嘅事,係唔係,瑪麗拉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 長大是件嚴肅的事,是不是,瑪麗拉?

passages.original: But when I have such good friends as you and Matthew and Mrs. Allan and Miss Stacy I ought to grow up successfully, and I’m sure it will be my own fault if I don’t.
passages.vernacular: 但係,既然我有您、馬修、艾倫太太同斯泰西小姐咁好嘅朋友,我應該能成功地長大,而且我肯定如果不成功,嗰將係我自己嘅錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,既然我有您、馬修、艾倫太太和斯泰西小姐這麼好的朋友,我應該能成功地長大,而且我肯定如果不成功,那將是我自己的錯。

passages.original: I feel it’s a great responsibility because I have only the one chance.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得呢個係一個好大嘅責任,因為我只有一次機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得這是一個很大的責任,因為我只有一次機會。

passages.original: If I don’t grow up right I can’t go back and begin over again.
passages.vernacular: 如果我冇長好,我唔能夠回頭重新開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我沒長好,我不能回頭重新開始。

passages.original: I’ve grown two inches this summer, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 呢個夏天我長高咗兩寸,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個夏天我長高了兩寸,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Mr. Gillis measured me at Ruby’s party.
passages.vernacular: 吉利斯先生喺露比嘅派對上畀我量嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉利斯先生在露比的派對上給我量的。

passages.original: I’m so glad you made my new dresses longer.
passages.vernacular: 我太高興您把我嘅新裙子做長喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興您把我的新裙子做長了。

passages.original: That dark-green one is so pretty and it was sweet of you to put on the flounce.
passages.vernacular: 嗰條深綠色嘅好漂亮,您畀佢加荷葉邊真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那條深綠色的好漂亮,您給它加荷葉邊真好。

passages.original: Of course I know it wasn’t really necessary, but flounces are so stylish this fall and Josie Pye has flounces on all her dresses.
passages.vernacular: 當然我知道呢並不真嘅必要,但荷葉邊今年秋天好時髦,喬西·派伊所有嘅裙子上都有荷葉邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然我知道這並不真的必要,但荷葉邊今年秋天很時髦,喬西·派伊所有的裙子上都有荷葉邊。

passages.original: I know I’ll be able to study better because of mine.
passages.vernacular: 我知道因為我嘅荷葉邊,我能學得更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道因為我的荷葉邊,我能學得更好。

passages.original: I shall have such a comfortable feeling deep down in my mind about that flounce.”
passages.vernacular: 我會喺心底深處對嗰道荷葉邊有種舒適嘅感覺。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會在心底深處對那道荷葉邊有種舒適的感覺。」

passages.original: “It’s worth something to have that,” admitted Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「有呢個都算有點價值,」瑪麗拉承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有這個也算有點價值,」瑪麗拉承認。

passages.original: Miss Stacy came back to Avonlea school and found all her pupils eager for work once more.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐回到阿文利學校,發現佢所有嘅學生又渴望學習喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐回到阿文利學校,發現她所有的學生又渴望學習了。

passages.original: Especially did the Queen’s class gird up their loins for the fray, for at the end of the coming year, dimly shadowing their pathway already, loomed up that fateful thing known as “the Entrance,” at the thought of which one and all felt their hearts sink into their very shoes.
passages.vernacular: 女王學院班尤其振作起嚟迎接戰鬥,因為喺即將到來嘅一年末尾,已隱隱把陰影投喺佢哋嘅路上嘅,隱約出現咗嗰件命運攸關嘅事,被稱為「入學考試」,一想到佢,佢哋每個人都覺得心沉到咗鞋底。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女王學院班尤其振作起來迎接戰鬥,因為在即將到來的一年末尾,已隱隱把陰影投在他們的路上的,隱約出現了那件命運攸關的事,被稱為「入學考試」,一想到它,他們每個人都覺得心沉到了鞋底。

passages.original: Suppose they did not pass!
passages.vernacular: 假如佢哋冇通過呢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假如他們沒通過呢!

passages.original: That thought was doomed to haunt Anne through the waking hours of that winter, Sunday afternoons inclusive, to the almost entire exclusion of moral and theological problems.
passages.vernacular: 呢個念頭注定要喺嗰個冬天安妮清醒嘅時間裡纏住佢,包括星期天下午,幾乎完全排擠咗道德同神學問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個念頭注定要在那個冬天安妮清醒的時間裡纏著她,包括星期天下午,幾乎完全排擠了道德和神學問題。

passages.original: When Anne had bad dreams she found herself staring miserably at pass lists of the Entrance exams, where Gilbert Blythe’s name was blazoned at the top and in which hers did not appear at all.
passages.vernacular: 安妮做噩夢時,發現自己痛苦地盯住入學考試嘅及格名單,吉爾伯特·布萊斯嘅名字赫然列喺頂端,而佢嘅名字根本冇出現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮做噩夢時,發現自己痛苦地盯著入學考試的及格名單,吉爾伯特·布萊斯的名字赫然列在頂端,而她的名字根本沒有出現。

passages.original: But it was a jolly, busy, happy swift-flying winter.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰個係個快樂、忙碌、幸福、飛逝嘅冬天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那是個快樂、忙碌、幸福、飛逝的冬天。

passages.original: Schoolwork was as interesting, class rivalry as absorbing, as of yore.
passages.vernacular: 功課同往昔一樣有趣,班級競爭同往昔一樣吸引人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 功課和往昔一樣有趣,班級競爭和往昔一樣吸引人。

passages.original: New worlds of thought, feeling, and ambition, fresh, fascinating fields of unexplored knowledge seemed to be opening out before Anne’s eager eyes.
passages.vernacular: 思想、感情同志向嘅新世界,新鮮、迷人嘅未探索嘅知識領域,似乎喺安妮熱切嘅眼前展開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 思想、感情和志向的新世界,新鮮、迷人的未探索的知識領域,似乎在安妮熱切的眼前展開。

passages.original: “Hills peeped o’er hill and Alps on Alps arose.”
passages.vernacular: 「山後有山,阿爾卑斯山上更有阿爾卑斯山。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「山後有山,阿爾卑斯山上更有阿爾卑斯山。」

passages.original: Much of all this was due to Miss Stacy’s tactful, careful, broadminded guidance.
passages.vernacular: 呢一切喺好大程度上歸功於斯泰西小姐機智、細心、胸襟開闊嘅指導。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切在很大程度上歸功於斯泰西小姐機智、細心、胸襟開闊的指導。

passages.original: She led her class to think and explore and discover for themselves and encouraged straying from the old beaten paths to a degree that quite shocked Mrs. Lynde and the school trustees, who viewed all innovations on established methods rather dubiously.
passages.vernacular: 佢領住佢嘅班思考、探索、自己發現,並鼓勵離開老路,達到相當令林德太太同校董哋震驚嘅程度,佢哋對一切改變既有方法嘅革新都持相當懷疑態度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她領著她的班思考、探索、自己發現,並鼓勵離開老路,達到相當令林德太太和校董們震驚的程度,他們對一切改變既有方法的革新都持相當懷疑態度。

passages.original: Apart from her studies Anne expanded socially, for Marilla, mindful of the Spencervale doctor’s dictum, no longer vetoed occasional outings.
passages.vernacular: 除咗學業,安妮嘅社交都擴大喇,因為瑪麗拉牢記斯潘塞韋爾醫生嘅箴言,唔再否決偶爾嘅外出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了學業,安妮的社交也擴大了,因為瑪麗拉牢記斯潘塞韋爾醫生的箴言,不再否決偶爾的外出。

passages.original: The Debating Club flourished and gave several concerts; there were one or two parties almost verging on grown-up affairs; there were sleigh drives and skating frolics galore.
passages.vernacular: 辯論社興旺發達,舉辦咗幾次音樂會;有一兩次聚會幾乎係成人嘅活動;仲有大量嘅雪橇出遊同溜冰嬉戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 辯論社興旺發達,舉辦了幾次音樂會;有一兩次聚會幾乎是成人的活動;還有大量的雪橇出遊和溜冰嬉戲。

passages.original: Between times Anne grew, shooting up so rapidly that Marilla was astonished one day, when they were standing side by side, to find the girl was taller than herself.
passages.vernacular: 其間安妮喺長高,長得咁快,有一天佢同瑪麗拉並肩站住時,瑪麗拉驚訝地發現女孩比佢自己仲高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其間安妮在長高,長得那麼快,有一天她和瑪麗拉並肩站著時,瑪麗拉驚訝地發現女孩比她自己還高。

passages.original: “Why, Anne, how you’ve grown!” she said, almost unbelievingly.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,安妮,你長高咗多少!」佢幾乎唔敢相信地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,安妮,你長高了多少!」她幾乎不敢相信地說。

passages.original: A sigh followed on the words.
passages.vernacular: 話後跟住一聲嘆息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 話後跟著一聲嘆息。

passages.original: Marilla felt a queer regret over Anne’s inches.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉為安妮嘅身高感到一種奇怪嘅遺憾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉為安妮的身高感到一種奇怪的遺憾。

passages.original: The child she had learned to love had vanished somehow and here was this tall, serious-eyed girl of fifteen, with the thoughtful brows and the proudly poised little head, in her place.
passages.vernacular: 佢學會愛嘅嗰個細路唔知怎嘅消失喇,取而代之嘅係呢個高個子、眼神嚴肅嘅十五歲女孩,有一雙深思嘅眉毛同傲然昂起嘅小腦袋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她學會愛的那個孩子不知怎的消失了,取而代之的是這個高個子、眼神嚴肅的十五歲女孩,有一雙深思的眉毛和傲然昂起的小腦袋。

passages.original: Marilla loved the girl as much as she had loved the child, but she was conscious of a queer sorrowful sense of loss.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉愛呢女孩,就像佢愛嗰個細路一樣,但佢意識到一種奇怪悲傷嘅失落感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉愛這女孩,就像她愛那個孩子一樣,但她意識到一種奇怪悲傷的失落感。

passages.original: And that night, when Anne had gone to prayer meeting with Diana, Marilla sat alone in the wintry twilight and indulged in the weakness of a cry.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,安妮同黛安娜去祈禱會之後,瑪麗拉獨自坐喺寒冷嘅暮色中,放縱咗哭一場嘅軟弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,安妮和黛安娜去祈禱會之後,瑪麗拉獨自坐在寒冷的暮色中,放縱了哭一場的軟弱。

passages.original: Matthew, coming in with a lantern, caught her at it and gazed at her in such consternation that Marilla had to laugh through her tears.
passages.vernacular: 馬修提住燈籠進嚟,撞見佢喺哭,驚愕地望住佢,瑪麗拉唔得不含住淚笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修提著燈籠進來,撞見她在哭,驚愕地望著她,瑪麗拉不得不含著淚笑了。

passages.original: “I was thinking about Anne,” she explained.
passages.vernacular: 「我喺想安妮,」佢解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在想安妮,」她解釋。

passages.original: “She’s got to be such a big girl--and she’ll probably be away from us next winter.
passages.vernacular: 「佢成咗咁大嘅女孩——明年冬天佢大概就要離開我哋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她成了這麼大的女孩——明年冬天她大概就要離開我們了。

passages.original: I’ll miss her terrible.”
passages.vernacular: 我會特別想佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會特別想她。」

passages.original: “She’ll be able to come home often,” comforted Matthew, to whom Anne was as yet and always would be the little, eager girl he had brought home from Bright River on that June evening four years before.
passages.vernacular: 「佢能常回家嘅,」馬修安慰道,喺佢睇來,安妮至今以及永遠都係四年前嗰個六月傍晚佢從明河接回家嘅嗰個小小嘅、熱切嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她能常回家的,」馬修安慰道,在他看來,安妮至今以及永遠都是四年前那個六月傍晚他從明河接回家的那個小小的、熱切的女孩。

passages.original: “The branch railroad will be built to Carmody by that time.”
passages.vernacular: 「到嗰時支線鐵路會修到卡莫迪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「到那時支線鐵路會修到卡莫迪。」

passages.original: “It won’t be the same thing as having her here all the time,” sighed Marilla gloomily, determined to enjoy her luxury of grief uncomforted.
passages.vernacular: 「呢跟佢一直喺呢兒唔係一回事,」瑪麗拉憂鬱地嘆息,決心享受佢不被安慰嘅悲傷嘅奢侈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這跟她一直在這兒不是一回事,」瑪麗拉憂鬱地嘆息,決心享受她不被安慰的悲傷的奢侈。

passages.original: “But there--men can’t understand these things!”
passages.vernacular: 「不過算喇——男人不懂呢啲事!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過算了——男人不懂這些事!」

passages.original: There were other changes in Anne no less real than the physical change.
passages.vernacular: 安妮身上仲有別嘅變化,同身體嘅變化同樣真實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮身上還有別的變化,和身體的變化同樣真實。

passages.original: For one thing, she became much quieter.
passages.vernacular: 一方面,佢變得安靜得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一方面,她變得安靜得多。

passages.original: Perhaps she thought all the more and dreamed as much as ever, but she certainly talked less.
passages.vernacular: 或者佢想得更多,夢想得同以前一樣多,但佢確實講得少喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許她想得更多,夢想得和以前一樣多,但她確實說得少了。

passages.original: Marilla noticed and commented on this also.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉都注意到並評論咗呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉也注意到並評論了這一點。

passages.original: “You don’t chatter half as much as you used to, Anne, nor use half as many big words.
passages.vernacular: 「你講話連一半都不像以前咁嘮叨喇,安妮,都唔使一半咁多嘅大詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說話連一半也不像以前那麼嘮叨了,安妮,也不用一半那麼多的大詞。

passages.original: What has come over you?”
passages.vernacular: 你點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼了?」

passages.original: Anne colored and laughed a little, as she dropped her book and looked dreamily out of the window, where big fat red buds were bursting out on the creeper in response to the lure of the spring sunshine.
passages.vernacular: 安妮臉紅喇,微微一笑,放下書,夢幻般地望向窗外,嗰度,大而肥嘅紅色花苞正在爬藤上綻開,響應春天陽光嘅誘惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮臉紅了,微微一笑,放下書,夢幻般地望向窗外,那裡,大而肥的紅色花苞正在爬藤上綻開,響應春天陽光的誘惑。

passages.original: “I don’t know--I don’t want to talk as much,” she said, denting her chin thoughtfully with her forefinger.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道——我唔想講咁多喇,」佢講,用食指若有所思地戳住下巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道——我不想說那麼多了,」她說,用食指若有所思地戳著下巴。

passages.original: “It’s nicer to think dear, pretty thoughts and keep them in one’s heart, like treasures.
passages.vernacular: 「想親愛嘅、美好嘅想法,把佢哋藏喺心裡,像寶貝一樣,更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「想親愛的、美好的想法,把它們藏在心裡,像寶貝一樣,更好。

passages.original: I don’t like to have them laughed at or wondered over.
passages.vernacular: 我不鍾意佢哋被人嘲笑或驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不喜歡它們被人嘲笑或驚訝。

passages.original: And somehow I don’t want to use big words any more.
passages.vernacular: 而且唔知怎嘅,我唔想再用大詞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且不知怎的,我不想再用大詞了。

passages.original: It’s almost a pity, isn’t it, now that I’m really growing big enough to say them if I did want to.
passages.vernacular: 而家我真嘅長大到可以講佢哋喇,如果我想講嘅話,呢幾乎係個遺憾,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我真的長大到可以說它們了,如果我想說的話,這幾乎是個遺憾,是不是?

passages.original: It’s fun to be almost grown up in some ways, but it’s not the kind of fun I expected, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 喺某些方面差不多長大咗好有趣,但唔係我預期嘅嗰種有趣,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在某些方面差不多長大了很有趣,但不是我預期的那種有趣,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: There’s so much to learn and do and think that there isn’t time for big words.
passages.vernacular: 要學嘅、要做嘅、要想嘅咁多,冇時間用大詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要學的、要做的、要想的那麼多,沒有時間用大詞。

passages.original: Besides, Miss Stacy says the short ones are much stronger and better.
passages.vernacular: 再講,斯泰西小姐講短詞更有力、更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再說,斯泰西小姐說短詞更有力、更好。

passages.original: She makes us write all our essays as simply as possible.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓我哋把所有嘅文章都寫得儘可能簡單。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她讓我們把所有的文章都寫得儘可能簡單。

passages.original: It was hard at first.
passages.vernacular: 起初好難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初很難。

passages.original: I was so used to crowding in all the fine big words I could think of--and I thought of any number of them.
passages.vernacular: 我過去習慣把我能想到嘅所有漂亮嘅大詞都塞進去——我能想到任意多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我過去習慣把我能想到的所有漂亮的大詞都塞進去——我能想到任意多。

passages.original: But I’ve got used to it now and I see it’s so much better.”
passages.vernacular: 但我而家習慣喇,我明白嗰樣好得多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我現在習慣了,我明白那樣好得多。」

passages.original: “What has become of your story club?
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅故事俱樂部點樣喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的故事俱樂部怎麼樣了?

passages.original: I haven’t heard you speak of it for a long time.”
passages.vernacular: 我好久冇聽你提起佢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我好久沒聽你提起它了。」

passages.original: “The story club isn’t in existence any longer.
passages.vernacular: 「故事俱樂部唔再存在喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「故事俱樂部不再存在了。

passages.original: We hadn’t time for it--and anyhow I think we had got tired of it.
passages.vernacular: 我哋冇時間——不管點樣,我想我哋已經厭倦喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們沒時間——不管怎樣,我想我們已經厭倦了。

passages.original: It was silly to be writing about love and murder and elopements and mysteries.
passages.vernacular: 寫愛情、謀殺、私奔同神祕好傻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寫愛情、謀殺、私奔和神祕很傻。

passages.original: Miss Stacy sometimes has us write a story for training in composition, but she won’t let us write anything but what might happen in Avonlea in our own lives, and she criticizes it very sharply and makes us criticize our own too.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐有時讓我哋寫一個故事嚟訓練作文,但佢只許我哋寫喺阿文利我哋自己生活中可能發生嘅事,佢批評得好尖銳,都讓我哋批評自己嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐有時讓我們寫一個故事來訓練作文,但她只許我們寫在阿文利我們自己生活中可能發生的事,她批評得非常尖銳,也讓我們批評自己的。

passages.original: I never thought my compositions had so many faults until I began to look for them myself.
passages.vernacular: 直到我自己開始找,我才想唔到我嘅作文有咁多毛病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到我自己開始找,我才想不到我的作文有那麼多毛病。

passages.original: I felt so ashamed I wanted to give up altogether, but Miss Stacy said I could learn to write well if I only trained myself to be my own severest critic.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得太羞愧,想完全放棄,但斯泰西小姐講,只要我訓練自己做自己最嚴厲嘅批評家,我就能學會寫好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得太羞愧,想完全放棄,但斯泰西小姐說,只要我訓練自己做自己最嚴厲的批評家,我就能學會寫好。

passages.original: And so I am trying to.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我喺努力。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我在努力。」

passages.original: “You’ve only two more months before the Entrance,” said Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「距離入學考試你只剩兩個月喇,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「距離入學考試你只剩兩個月了,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “Do you think you’ll be able to get through?”
passages.vernacular: 「你覺得你能通過嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你覺得你能通過嗎?」

passages.original: Anne shivered.
passages.vernacular: 安妮打咗個寒顫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮打了個寒顫。

passages.original: “I don’t know.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: Sometimes I think I’ll be all right--and then I get horribly afraid.
passages.vernacular: 有時我覺得會冇事——然後我又可怕地害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時我覺得會沒事——然後我又可怕地害怕。

passages.original: We’ve studied hard and Miss Stacy has drilled us thoroughly, but we mayn’t get through for all that.
passages.vernacular: 我哋學習好努力,斯泰西小姐徹底地訓練咗我哋,但我哋都未必就能通過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們學習很努力,斯泰西小姐徹底地訓練了我們,但我們也未必就能通過。

passages.original: We’ve each got a stumbling block.
passages.vernacular: 我哋每個人都有絆腳石。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們每個人都有絆腳石。

passages.original: Mine is geometry of course, and Jane’s is Latin, and Ruby and Charlie’s is algebra, and Josie’s is arithmetic.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅當然係幾何,簡嘅係拉丁文,露比同查理嘅係代數,喬西嘅係算術。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的當然是幾何,簡的是拉丁文,露比和查理的是代數,喬西的是算術。

passages.original: Moody Spurgeon says he feels it in his bones that he is going to fail in English history.
passages.vernacular: 穆迪·斯珀吉翁講佢骨子裡感覺到自己英國歷史會不及格。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 穆迪·斯珀吉翁說他骨子裡感覺到自己英國歷史會不及格。

passages.original: Miss Stacy is going to give us examinations in June just as hard as we’ll have at the Entrance and mark us just as strictly, so we’ll have some idea.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐六月要畀我哋考試,跟入學考試一樣難,打分跟入學考試一樣嚴格,咁樣我哋就會有些概念。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐六月要給我們考試,跟入學考試一樣難,打分跟入學考試一樣嚴格,這樣我們就會有些概念。

passages.original: I wish it was all over, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我希望一切都結束喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望一切都結束了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: It haunts me.
passages.vernacular: 佢纏住我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它纏著我。

passages.original: Sometimes I wake up in the night and wonder what I’ll do if I don’t pass.”
passages.vernacular: 有時我半夜醒嚟,想如果我冇通過我該點算。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時我半夜醒來,想如果我沒通過我該怎麼辦。」

passages.original: “Why, go to school next year and try again,” said Marilla unconcernedly.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,明年上學再試一次,」瑪麗拉不在意地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,明年上學再試一次,」瑪麗拉不在意地說。

passages.original: “Oh, I don’t believe I’d have the heart for it.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我覺得我冇嗰個心情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我覺得我沒有那個心情。

passages.original: It would be such a disgrace to fail, especially if Gil--if the others passed.
passages.vernacular: 不及格太丟人喇,尤其係如果吉爾——如果別人通過喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不及格太丟人了,尤其是如果吉爾——如果別人通過了。

passages.original: And I get so nervous in an examination that I’m likely to make a mess of it.
passages.vernacular: 而且我考試時太緊張,可能會搞砸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我考試時太緊張,可能會搞砸。

passages.original: I wish I had nerves like Jane Andrews.
passages.vernacular: 我希望我有簡·安德魯斯嗰樣嘅神經。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我有簡·安德魯斯那樣的神經。

passages.original: Nothing rattles her.”
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢都嚇不住佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼也嚇不住她。」

passages.original: Anne sighed and, dragging her eyes from the witcheries of the spring world, the beckoning day of breeze and blue, and the green things upspringing in the garden, buried herself resolutely in her book.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘆咗口氣,把眼睛從春天世界嘅魅力、招手嘅有微風同蔚藍嘅日子、花園裡冒出嘅綠色事物上拉回嚟,堅決地埋頭睇書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮嘆了口氣,把眼睛從春天世界的魅力、招手的有微風和蔚藍的日子、花園裡冒出的綠色事物上拉回來,堅決地埋頭看書。

passages.original: There would be other springs, but if she did not succeed in passing the Entrance, Anne felt convinced that she would never recover sufficiently to enjoy them.
passages.vernacular: 仲會有別嘅春天,但如果佢冇能通過入學考試,安妮確信自己永遠唔能夠恢復到足以享受佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還會有別的春天,但如果她沒能通過入學考試,安妮確信自己永遠不能恢復到足以享受它們。

chapters.title: Ch. XXXII The Pass List Is Out 第三十二章:及格名單公佈

passages.original: CH WITH the end of June came the close of the term and the close of Miss Stacy’s rule in Avonlea school.
passages.vernacular: 六月底學期結束,斯泰西小姐喺阿文利學校嘅任期都結束喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 六月底學期結束,斯泰西小姐在阿文利學校的任期也結束了。

passages.original: Anne and Diana walked home that evening feeling very sober indeed.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天傍晚安妮同黛安娜走路回家,心情確實好沉重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天傍晚安妮和黛安娜走路回家,心情確實非常沉重。

passages.original: Red eyes and damp handkerchiefs bore convincing testimony to the fact that Miss Stacy’s farewell words must have been quite as touching as Mr. Phillips’s had been under similar circumstances three years before.
passages.vernacular: 紅紅嘅眼睛同濕透嘅手帕令人信服地證明,斯泰西小姐嘅告別語,一定同三年前菲利普斯先生喺類似情況下嘅一樣感人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紅紅的眼睛和濕透的手帕令人信服地證明,斯泰西小姐的告別語,一定和三年前菲利普斯先生在類似情況下的一樣感人。

passages.original: Diana looked back at the schoolhouse from the foot of the spruce hill and sighed deeply.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜喺杉樹山腳回頭望住校舍,深深地嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜在杉樹山腳回頭望著校舍,深深地嘆了口氣。

passages.original: “It does seem as if it was the end of everything, doesn’t it?” she said dismally.
passages.vernacular: 「呢真像係一切嘅終結,係唔係?」佢沮喪地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這真像是一切的終結,是不是?」她沮喪地說。

passages.original: “You oughtn’t to feel half as badly as I do,” said Anne, hunting vainly for a dry spot on her handkerchief.
passages.vernacular: 「你不該有我一半咁難過,」安妮講,喺手帕上徒勞地尋找乾嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不該有我一半那麼難過,」安妮說,在手帕上徒勞地尋找乾的地方。

passages.original: “You’ll be back again next winter, but I suppose I’ve left the dear old school forever--if I have good luck, that is.”
passages.vernacular: 「你明年冬天仲會回嚟,而我想我永遠離開咗親愛嘅老學校喇——如果我運氣好嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你明年冬天還會回來,而我想我永遠離開了親愛的老學校了——如果我運氣好的話。」

passages.original: “It won’t be a bit the same.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰絕對不一樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那絕對不一樣了。

passages.original: Miss Stacy won’t be there, nor you nor Jane nor Ruby probably.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐唔會喺嗰兒,你、簡或露比大概都不喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐不會在那兒,你、簡或露比大概也不在。

passages.original: I shall have to sit all alone, for I couldn’t bear to have another deskmate after you.
passages.vernacular: 我只能獨自坐住,因為我受不了喺你之後再有另一個同桌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只能獨自坐著,因為我受不了在你之後再有另一個同桌。

passages.original: Oh, we have had jolly times, haven’t we, Anne?
passages.vernacular: 哦,我哋有過愉快嘅時光,係唔係,安妮?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我們有過愉快的時光,是不是,安妮?

passages.original: It’s dreadful to think they’re all over.”
passages.vernacular: 想到佢哋都結束咗真可怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到它們都結束了真可怕。」

passages.original: Two big tears rolled down by Diana’s nose.
passages.vernacular: 兩顆大淚珠沿住黛安娜嘅鼻子滾落。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩顆大淚珠沿著黛安娜的鼻子滾落。

passages.original: “If you would stop crying I could,” said Anne imploringly.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你不哭喇,我就能不哭,」安妮懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你不哭了,我就能不哭,」安妮懇求道。

passages.original: “Just as soon as I put away my hanky I see you brimming up and that starts me off again.
passages.vernacular: 「我剛把手帕收起嚟,睇到你眼淚汪汪,就又開始喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我剛把手帕收起來,看到你眼淚汪汪,就又開始了。

passages.original: As Mrs. Lynde says, ‘If you can’t be cheerful, be as cheerful as you can.’
passages.vernacular: 就像林德太太講嘅:『如果你唔能夠快樂,就儘量快樂。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就像林德太太說的:『如果你不能快樂,就儘量快樂。』

passages.original: After all, I dare say I’ll be back next year.
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,我敢講我明年會回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,我敢說我明年會回來。

passages.original: This is one of the times I know I’m not going to pass.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我知道我唔會通過嘅時刻之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我知道我不會通過的時刻之一。

passages.original: They’re getting alarmingly frequent.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋變得令人驚恐地頻繁。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們變得令人驚恐地頻繁。」

passages.original: “Why, you came out splendidly in the exams Miss Stacy gave.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,斯泰西小姐畀嘅考試你考得棒極喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,斯泰西小姐給的考試你考得棒極了。」

passages.original: “Yes, but those exams didn’t make me nervous.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,但嗰啲考試冇讓我緊張。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,但那些考試沒讓我緊張。

passages.original: When I think of the real thing you can’t imagine what a horrid cold fluttery feeling comes round my heart.
passages.vernacular: 你想像不出,我想到真考時,心裡湧起一種幾咁可怕嘅冰冷顫抖嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想像不出,我想到真考時,心裡湧起一種多麼可怕的冰冷顫抖的感覺。

passages.original: And then my number is thirteen and Josie Pye says it’s so unlucky.
passages.vernacular: 而且我嘅號碼係十三,喬西·派伊講嗰好不吉利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我的號碼是十三,喬西·派伊說那很不吉利。

passages.original: I am not superstitious and I know it can make no difference.
passages.vernacular: 我不迷信,我知道呢唔會有任何差別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不迷信,我知道這不會有任何差別。

passages.original: But still I wish it wasn’t thirteen.”
passages.vernacular: 但我定係希望佢唔係十三。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我還是希望它不是十三。」

passages.original: “I do wish I was going in with you,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我真希望我跟你一起去,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真希望我跟你一起去,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “Wouldn’t we have a perfectly elegant time?
passages.vernacular: 「我哋唔係會度過極其高雅嘅時光嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們不是會度過極其高雅的時光嗎?

passages.original: But I suppose you’ll have to cram in the evenings.”
passages.vernacular: 不過我想你得晚上突擊複習。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我想你得晚上突擊複習。」

passages.original: “No; Miss Stacy has made us promise not to open a book at all.
passages.vernacular: 「不;斯泰西小姐讓我哋保證完全不翻書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不;斯泰西小姐讓我們保證完全不翻書。

passages.original: She says it would only tire and confuse us and we are to go out walking and not think about the exams at all and go to bed early.
passages.vernacular: 佢講嗰隻會讓我哋疲倦同混亂,我哋應該出去散步,完全不去想考試,並早朝早床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說那隻會讓我們疲倦和混亂,我們應該出去散步,完全不去想考試,並早早上床。

passages.original: It’s good advice, but I expect it will be hard to follow; good advice is apt to be, I think.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係好建議,但我預料佢好難遵循;我想,好建議往往如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是好建議,但我預料它很難遵循;我想,好建議往往如此。

passages.original: Prissy Andrews told me that she sat up half the night every night of her Entrance week and crammed for dear life; and I had determined to sit up at least as long as she did.
passages.vernacular: 普麗茜·安德魯斯告訴我,佢喺入學考試嗰週,每天晚上熬夜到半夜,拼命突擊複習;我已經決心至少熬得跟佢一樣久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 普麗茜·安德魯斯告訴我,她在入學考試那週,每天晚上熬夜到半夜,拼命突擊複習;我已經決心至少熬得跟她一樣久。

passages.original: It was so kind of your Aunt Josephine to ask me to stay at Beechwood while I’m in town.”
passages.vernacular: 你嘅約瑟芬姑婆邀請我喺城裡時住喺山毛櫸莊,佢真好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的約瑟芬姑婆邀請我在城裡時住在山毛櫸莊,她真好。」

passages.original: “You’ll write to me while you’re in, won’t you?”
passages.vernacular: 「你喺城裡時會畀我寫信吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你在城裡時會給我寫信吧?」

passages.original: “I’ll write Tuesday night and tell you how the first day goes,” promised Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我星期二晚上寫,告訴你第一天點樣,」安妮保證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我星期二晚上寫,告訴你第一天怎麼樣,」安妮保證。

passages.original: “I’ll be haunting the post office Wednesday,” vowed Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我星期三會喺郵局出沒,」黛安娜發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我星期三會在郵局出沒,」黛安娜發誓。

passages.original: Anne went to town the following Monday and on Wednesday Diana haunted the post office, as agreed, and got her letter.
passages.vernacular: 安妮下週一進咗城,星期三黛安娜按約定喺郵局出沒,收到咗佢嘅信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮下週一進了城,星期三黛安娜按約定在郵局出沒,收到了她的信。

passages.original: “Dearest Diana” [wrote Anne],
passages.vernacular: 「最親愛嘅黛安娜」[安妮寫道],
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最親愛的黛安娜」[安妮寫道],

passages.original: “Here it is Tuesday night and I’m writing this in the library at Beechwood.
passages.vernacular: 「而家係星期二晚上,我喺山毛櫸莊嘅圖書室寫呢封信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在是星期二晚上,我在山毛櫸莊的圖書室寫這封信。

passages.original: Last night I was horribly lonesome all alone in my room and wished so much you were with me.
passages.vernacular: 琴晚我一個人喺房間里可怕地孤獨,多希望你喺我身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨晚我一個人在房間里可怕地孤獨,多希望你在我身邊。

passages.original: I couldn’t ‘cram’ because I’d promised Miss Stacy not to, but it was as hard to keep from opening my history as it used to be to keep from reading a story before my lessons were learned.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠『突擊複習』,因為我向斯泰西小姐保證過不睇,但要忍住不翻開我嘅歷史書,就像過去忍住不喺功課學完之前先睇故事一樣難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能『突擊複習』,因為我向斯泰西小姐保證過不看,但要忍住不翻開我的歷史書,就像過去忍住不在功課學完之前先看故事一樣難。

passages.original: “This morning Miss Stacy came for me and we went to the Academy, calling for Jane and Ruby and Josie on our way.
passages.vernacular: 「今日朝早斯泰西小姐嚟接我,我哋去咗學院,路上順道叫咗簡、露比同喬西。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今天早上斯泰西小姐來接我,我們去了學院,路上順道叫了簡、露比和喬西。

passages.original: Ruby asked me to feel her hands and they were as cold as ice.
passages.vernacular: 露比叫我摸佢嘅手,冰冷得像冰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比叫我摸她的手,冰冷得像冰。

passages.original: Josie said I looked as if I hadn’t slept a wink and she didn’t believe I was strong enough to stand the grind of the teacher’s course even if I did get through.
passages.vernacular: 喬西講我睇上去像一夜冇合眼,佢不相信我即使通過喇,身體都強壯到能承受師範課程嘅辛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西說我看上去像一夜沒合眼,她不相信我即使通過了,身體也強壯到能承受師範課程的辛苦。

passages.original: There are times and seasons even yet when I don’t feel that I’ve made any great headway in learning to like Josie Pye!
passages.vernacular: 甚至到而家,有些時候我定係覺得,喺學會鍾意喬西·派伊呢方面,我冇取得多大進展!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 甚至到現在,有些時候我還是覺得,在學會喜歡喬西·派伊這方面,我沒有取得多大進展!

passages.original: “When we reached the Academy there were scores of students there from all over the Island.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋到學院時,嗰度有幾十個來自全島各地嘅學生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們到學院時,那裡有幾十個來自全島各地的學生。

passages.original: The first person we saw was Moody Spurgeon sitting on the steps and muttering away to himself.
passages.vernacular: 我哋睇到嘅第一個人係穆迪·斯珀吉翁,坐喺台階上,嘴裡喃喃自語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們看到的第一個人是穆迪·斯珀吉翁,坐在台階上,嘴裡喃喃自語。

passages.original: Jane asked him what on earth he was doing and he said he was repeating the multiplication table over and over to steady his nerves and for pity’s sake not to interrupt him, because if he stopped for a moment he got frightened and forgot everything he ever knew, but the multiplication table kept all his facts firmly in their proper place!
passages.vernacular: 簡問佢到底喺幹乜嘢,佢講佢喺一遍又一遍地背乘法表嚟穩定神經,睇喺老天嘅份上別打斷佢,因為如果佢停一會兒,佢就害怕,忘記佢知道嘅所有嘢,但乘法表讓佢所有嘅知識牢牢地待喺恰當嘅位置!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡問他到底在幹什麼,他說他在一遍又一遍地背乘法表來穩定神經,看在老天的份上別打斷他,因為如果他停一會兒,他就害怕,忘記他知道的所有東西,但乘法表讓他所有的知識牢牢地待在恰當的位置!

passages.original: “When we were assigned to our rooms Miss Stacy had to leave us.
passages.vernacular: 「分配我哋到教室時,斯泰西小姐唔得不離開我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「分配我們到教室時,斯泰西小姐不得不離開我們。

passages.original: Jane and I sat together and Jane was so composed that I envied her.
passages.vernacular: 簡同我坐喺一起,簡咁鎮定,我羨慕佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡和我坐在一起,簡那麼鎮定,我羨慕她。

passages.original: No need of the multiplication table for good, steady, sensible Jane!
passages.vernacular: 善良、穩重、明智嘅簡用不住乘法表!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 善良、穩重、明智的簡用不著乘法表!

passages.original: I wondered if I looked as I felt and if they could hear my heart thumping clear across the room.
passages.vernacular: 我想知道我睇起嚟係咪同我感覺嘅一樣,佢哋能否聽見我嘅心砰砰地跳,一直響遍整個房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想知道我看起來是否和我感覺的一樣,他們能否聽見我的心砰砰地跳,一直響遍整個房間。

passages.original: Then a man came in and began distributing the English examination sheets.
passages.vernacular: 然後一個男人進嚟,開始分發英語考卷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後一個男人進來,開始分發英語考卷。

passages.original: My hands grew cold then and my head fairly whirled around as I picked it up.
passages.vernacular: 攞起佢嘅時候我嘅手變冷喇,我嘅頭簡直喺旋轉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿起它的時候我的手變冷了,我的頭簡直在旋轉。

passages.original: Just one awful moment--Diana, I felt exactly as I did four years ago when I asked Marilla if I might stay at Green Gables--and then everything cleared up in my mind and my heart began beating again--I forgot to say that it had stopped altogether!--for I knew I could do something with that paper anyhow.
passages.vernacular: 就一個可怕嘅瞬間——黛安娜,我感覺同四年前我問瑪麗拉我係咪可以留喺綠色屋頂時一模一樣——然後我腦子里一切都清楚喇,我嘅心又開始跳動——我忘咗講佢曾完全停止!——因為我知道我無論如何能對嗰份試卷做點乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就一個可怕的瞬間——黛安娜,我感覺和四年前我問瑪麗拉我是否可以留在綠色屋頂時一模一樣——然後我腦子里一切都清楚了,我的心又開始跳動——我忘了說它曾完全停止!——因為我知道我無論如何能對那份試卷做點什麼。

passages.original: “At noon we went home for dinner and then back again for history in the afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 「中午我哋回家食飯,下午又回去考歷史。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「中午我們回家吃飯,下午又回去考歷史。

passages.original: The history was a pretty hard paper and I got dreadfully mixed up in the dates.
passages.vernacular: 歷史卷子相當難,我把日期弄得一團糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歷史卷子相當難,我把日期弄得一團糟。

passages.original: Still, I think I did fairly well today.
passages.vernacular: 不過,我想我今日考得仲算不錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,我想我今天考得還算不錯。

passages.original: But oh, Diana, tomorrow the geometry exam comes off and when I think of it it takes every bit of determination I possess to keep from opening my Euclid.
passages.vernacular: 但係哦,黛安娜,聽日考幾何,一想到佢,我就得用上我全部嘅決心,才忍住不去翻我嘅歐幾里得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是哦,黛安娜,明天考幾何,一想到它,我就得用上我全部的決心,才忍住不去翻我的歐幾里得。

passages.original: If I thought the multiplication table would help me any I would recite it from now till tomorrow morning.
passages.vernacular: 如果我覺得背乘法表對我有任何幫助,我會從而家背到聽日早晨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我覺得背乘法表對我有任何幫助,我會從現在背到明天早晨。

passages.original: “I went down to see the other girls this evening.
passages.vernacular: 「今晚我下去睇咗其他女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚我下去看了其他女孩。

passages.original: On my way I met Moody Spurgeon wandering distractedly around.
passages.vernacular: 路上我遇到穆迪·斯珀吉翁魂不守舍地到處遊蕩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 路上我遇到穆迪·斯珀吉翁魂不守舍地到處遊蕩。

passages.original: He said he knew he had failed in history and he was born to be a disappointment to his parents and he was going home on the morning train; and it would be easier to be a carpenter than a minister, anyhow.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢知道佢歷史不及格喇,佢生來就係讓佢父母失望嘅,佢要乘早班火車回家;而且不管點樣,做木匠比做牧師容易。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他知道他歷史不及格了,他生來就是讓他父母失望的,他要乘早班火車回家;而且不管怎樣,做木匠比做牧師容易。

passages.original: I cheered him up and persuaded him to stay to the end because it would be unfair to Miss Stacy if he didn’t.
passages.vernacular: 我鼓勵咗佢,講服佢留到最後,因為如果佢不咁樣,對斯泰西小姐不公平。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我鼓勵了他,說服他留到最後,因為如果他不這樣,對斯泰西小姐不公平。

passages.original: Sometimes I have wished I was born a boy, but when I see Moody Spurgeon I’m always glad I’m a girl and not his sister.
passages.vernacular: 有時我希望我生來係男孩,但睇到穆迪·斯珀吉翁時,我總是好高興我係女孩,唔係佢嘅姐妹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時我希望我生來是男孩,但看到穆迪·斯珀吉翁時,我總是很高興我是女孩,不是他的姐妹。

passages.original: “Ruby was in hysterics when I reached their boardinghouse; she had just discovered a fearful mistake she had made in her English paper.
passages.vernacular: 「我到佢哋寄宿嘅地方時,露比喺歇斯底里;佢剛發現佢英語卷子里犯咗一個可怕嘅錯誤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我到她們寄宿的地方時,露比在歇斯底里;她剛發現她英語卷子里犯了一個可怕的錯誤。

passages.original: When she recovered we went uptown and had an ice cream.
passages.vernacular: 佢恢復後我哋去咗市區,食咗冰淇淋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她恢復後我們去了市區,吃了冰淇淋。

passages.original: How we wished you had been with us.
passages.vernacular: 我哋多希望你同我哋喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們多希望你和我們在一起。

passages.original: “Oh, Diana, if only the geometry examination were over!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,黛安娜,要係幾何考試結束咗該多好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,黛安娜,要是幾何考試結束了該多好!

passages.original: But there, as Mrs. Lynde would say, the sun will go on rising and setting whether I fail in geometry or not.
passages.vernacular: 不過,就像林德太太會講嘅,不管我幾何不及格定係及格,太陽照樣升起落下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,就像林德太太會說的,不管我幾何不及格還是及格,太陽照樣升起落下。

passages.original: That is true but not especially comforting.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係真嘅,但並不特別令人安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是真的,但並不特別令人安慰。

passages.original: I think I’d rather it didn’t go on if I failed!
passages.vernacular: 我想如果我不及格,我寧願佢唔好繼續!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想如果我不及格,我寧願它不要繼續!

passages.original: “Yours devotedly, “Anne”
passages.vernacular: 「你忠實嘅,安妮」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你忠實的,安妮」

passages.original: The geometry examination and all the others were over in due time and Anne arrived home on Friday evening, rather tired but with an air of chastened triumph about her.
passages.vernacular: 幾何考試同所有其他考試及時結束喇,安妮星期五晚上回到家,相當疲倦,但帶住一種受過磨練嘅勝利嘅神氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾何考試和所有其他考試及時結束了,安妮星期五晚上回到家,相當疲倦,但帶著一種受過磨練的勝利的神氣。

passages.original: Diana was over at Green Gables when she arrived and they met as if they had been parted for years.
passages.vernacular: 佢到達時黛安娜正在綠色屋頂,佢哋像分別咗多年一樣相見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她到達時黛安娜正在綠色屋頂,她們像分別了多年一樣相見。

passages.original: “You old darling, it’s perfectly splendid to see you back again.
passages.vernacular: 「你呢個親愛嘅老寶貝,睇到你回嚟真係太棒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你這個親愛的老寶貝,看到你回來真是太棒了。

passages.original: It seems like an age since you went to town and oh, Anne, how did you get along?”
passages.vernacular: 你進城以來好像過咗一個世紀,哦,安妮,你考得點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你進城以來好像過了一個世紀,哦,安妮,你考得怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “Pretty well, I think, in everything but the geometry.
passages.vernacular: 「我想相當不錯,除咗幾何。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想相當不錯,除了幾何。

passages.original: I don’t know whether I passed in it or not and I have a creepy, crawly presentiment that I didn’t.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道我幾何係咪通過喇,我有毛骨悚然嘅預感我冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道我幾何是否通過了,我有毛骨悚然的預感我沒有。

passages.original: Oh, how good it is to be back!
passages.vernacular: 哦,回嚟真好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,回來真好!

passages.original: Green Gables is the dearest, loveliest spot in the world.”
passages.vernacular: 綠色屋頂係世界上最親愛、最可愛嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 綠色屋頂是世界上最親愛、最可愛的地方。」

passages.original: “How did the others do?”
passages.vernacular: 「別人考得點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別人考得怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “The girls say they know they didn’t pass, but I think they did pretty well.
passages.vernacular: 「女孩哋講佢哋知道自己冇通過,但我認為佢哋考得相當好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「女孩們說她們知道自己沒通過,但我認為她們考得相當好。

passages.original: Josie says the geometry was so easy a child of ten could do it!
passages.vernacular: 喬西講幾何太容易喇,十歲嘅細路都能做!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西說幾何太容易了,十歲的孩子都能做!

passages.original: Moody Spurgeon still thinks he failed in history and Charlie says he failed in algebra.
passages.vernacular: 穆迪·斯珀吉翁仍然覺得歷史不及格,查理講佢代數不及格。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 穆迪·斯珀吉翁仍然覺得歷史不及格,查理說他代數不及格。

passages.original: But we don’t really know anything about it and won’t until the pass list is out.
passages.vernacular: 但我哋其實啲都唔知道,喺及格名單公布前都唔會知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們其實一點也不知道,在及格名單公布前也不會知道。

passages.original: That won’t be for a fortnight.
passages.vernacular: 嗰要兩個星期後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那要兩個星期後。

passages.original: Fancy living a fortnight in such suspense!
passages.vernacular: 想想喺呢種懸念中生活兩個星期!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想想在這種懸念中生活兩個星期!

passages.original: I wish I could go to sleep and never wake up until it is over.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望我能瞓住,直到一切結束才醒嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我能睡著,直到一切結束才醒來。」

passages.original: Diana knew it would be useless to ask how Gilbert Blythe had fared, so she merely said:
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜知道問吉爾伯特·布萊斯考得點樣冇用,所以佢只講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜知道問吉爾伯特·布萊斯考得怎麼樣沒有用,所以她只說:

passages.original: “Oh, you’ll pass all right.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你肯定通過喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你肯定通過了。

passages.original: Don’t worry.”
passages.vernacular: 別擔心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別擔心。」

passages.original: “I’d rather not pass at all than not come out pretty well up on the list,” flashed Anne, by which she meant--and Diana knew she meant--that success would be incomplete and bitter if she did not come out ahead of Gilbert Blythe.
passages.vernacular: 「我寧可根本不通過,都唔願名單上排名不高,」安妮激烈地講,佢嘅意思係——黛安娜知道佢嘅意思——如果佢冇超過吉爾伯特·布萊斯,成功將係不完整同苦澀嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我寧可根本不通過,也不願名單上排名不高,」安妮激烈地說,她的意思是——黛安娜知道她的意思——如果她沒超過吉爾伯特·布萊斯,成功將是不完整和苦澀的。

passages.original: With this end in view Anne had strained every nerve during the examinations.
passages.vernacular: 為了呢個目標,安妮喺考試期間繃緊咗每一根神經。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了這個目標,安妮在考試期間繃緊了每一根神經。

passages.original: So had Gilbert.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特都一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特也一樣。

passages.original: They had met and passed each other on the street a dozen times without any sign of recognition and every time Anne had held her head a little higher and wished a little more earnestly that she had made friends with Gilbert when he asked her, and vowed a little more determinedly to surpass him in the examination.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺街上相遇並擦肩而過十幾次,冇任何認識嘅表示,每一次安妮都把頭抬得更高啲,更熱切地希望當吉爾伯特要求時佢同佢成咗朋友,更堅決地發誓要喺考試中超過佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在街上相遇並擦肩而過十幾次,沒有任何認識的表示,每一次安妮都把頭抬得更高一點,更熱切地希望當吉爾伯特要求時她與他成了朋友,更堅決地發誓要在考試中超過他。

passages.original: She knew that all Avonlea junior was wondering which would come out first; she even knew that Jimmy Glover and Ned Wright had a bet on the question and that Josie Pye had said there was no doubt in the world that Gilbert would be first; and she felt that her humiliation would be unbearable if she failed.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道整個阿文利嘅年輕一代都喺想知道邊個會排第一;佢甚至知道吉米·格洛弗同內德·賴特就呢個問題打咗賭,喬西·派伊講世上毫無疑問吉爾伯特會係第一;佢覺得如果佢失敗,佢嘅屈辱將無法忍受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她知道整個阿文利的年輕一代都在想知道誰會排第一;她甚至知道吉米·格洛弗和內德·賴特就這個問題打了賭,喬西·派伊說世上毫無疑問吉爾伯特會是第一;她覺得如果她失敗,她的屈辱將無法忍受。

passages.original: But she had another and nobler motive for wishing to do well.
passages.vernacular: 但佢有另一個更高尚嘅動機希望考好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她有另一個更高尚的動機希望考好。

passages.original: She wanted to “pass high” for the sake of Matthew and Marilla--especially Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 佢想為了馬修同瑪麗拉——尤其係馬修——「高分通過」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她想為了馬修和瑪麗拉——尤其是馬修——「高分通過」。

passages.original: Matthew had declared to her his conviction that she “would beat the whole Island.”
passages.vernacular: 馬修向佢宣告咗佢嘅信念,佢「會打敗全島」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修向她宣告了他的信念,她「會打敗全島」。

passages.original: That, Anne felt, was something it would be foolish to hope for even in the wildest dreams.
passages.vernacular: 安妮覺得,嗰個係即使喺最狂野嘅夢里都愚蠢去希望嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮覺得,那是即使在最狂野的夢里也愚蠢去希望的東西。

passages.original: But she did hope fervently that she would be among the first ten at least, so that she might see Matthew’s kindly brown eyes gleam with pride in her achievement.
passages.vernacular: 但佢確實熱切地希望自己至少進入前十名,咁樣佢就能睇到馬修慈祥嘅棕色眼睛為佢嘅成就閃耀自豪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她確實熱切地希望自己至少進入前十名,這樣她就能看到馬修慈祥的棕色眼睛為她的成就閃耀自豪。

passages.original: That, she felt, would be a sweet reward indeed for all her hard work and patient grubbing among unimaginative equations and conjugations.
passages.vernacular: 佢覺得,對於佢所有嘅努力同耐心地鑽研嗰啲缺乏想像力嘅方程同動詞變位,嗰將係甜蜜嘅回報。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她覺得,對於她所有的努力和耐心地鑽研那些缺乏想像力的方程和動詞變位,那將是甜蜜的回報。

passages.original: At the end of the fortnight Anne took to “haunting” the post office also, in the distracted company of Jane, Ruby, and Josie, opening the Charlottetown dailies with shaking hands and cold, sinkaway feelings as bad as any experienced during the Entrance week.
passages.vernacular: 兩周結束時,安妮都開始喺郵局「出沒」喇,同簡、露比同喬西心神不寧地喺一起,用顫抖嘅手打開夏洛特敦嘅日報,嗰種冰冷嘅、沉沒嘅感覺,同入學考試週里經歷嘅一樣糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩周結束時,安妮也開始在郵局「出沒」了,與簡、露比和喬西心神不寧地在一起,用顫抖的手打開夏洛特敦的日報,那種冰冷的、沉沒的感覺,和入學考試週里經歷的一樣糟。

passages.original: Charlie and Gilbert were not above doing this too, but Moody Spurgeon stayed resolutely away.
passages.vernacular: 查理同吉爾伯特都不甘落後咁樣做,但穆迪·斯珀吉翁堅決不去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 查理和吉爾伯特也不甘落後這樣做,但穆迪·斯珀吉翁堅決不去。

passages.original: “I haven’t got the grit to go there and look at a paper in cold blood,” he told Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇勇氣去嗰兒冷靜地睇報紙,」佢對安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒有勇氣去那兒冷靜地看報紙,」他對安妮說。

passages.original: “I’m just going to wait until somebody comes and tells me suddenly whether I’ve passed or not.”
passages.vernacular: 「我只打算等住有人嚟,突然告訴我我係咪通過喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只打算等著有人來,突然告訴我我是否通過了。」

passages.original: When three weeks had gone by without the pass list appearing Anne began to feel that she really couldn’t stand the strain much longer.
passages.vernacular: 三個星期過去喇,及格名單仲冇出現,安妮開始覺得佢真嘅無法再忍受呢種壓力喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三個星期過去了,及格名單還沒出現,安妮開始覺得她真的無法再忍受這種壓力了。

passages.original: Her appetite failed and her interest in Avonlea doings languished.
passages.vernacular: 佢食慾不振,對阿文利嘅事情興趣萎縮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她食慾不振,對阿文利的事情興趣萎縮。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde wanted to know what else you could expect with a Tory superintendent of education at the head of affairs, and Matthew, noting Anne’s paleness and indifference and the lagging steps that bore her home from the post office every afternoon, began seriously to wonder if he hadn’t better vote Grit at the next election.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太想知道,喺一個保守黨嘅教育督學當家嘅情況下,你仲能指望乜嘢;馬修注意到安妮嘅蒼白同冷淡,以及佢每天下午從郵局走回家時沉重嘅腳步,開始認真地納悶,佢下次選舉係唔係最好投自由黨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太想知道,在一個保守黨的教育督學當家的情況下,你還能指望什麼;馬修注意到安妮的蒼白和冷淡,以及她每天下午從郵局走回家時沉重的腳步,開始認真地納悶,他下次選舉是不是最好投自由黨。

passages.original: But one evening the news came.
passages.vernacular: 但有天傍晚消息嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但有天傍晚消息來了。

passages.original: Anne was sitting at her open window, for the time forgetful of the woes of examinations and the cares of the world, as she drank in the beauty of the summer dusk, sweet-scented with flower breaths from the garden below and sibilant and rustling from the stir of poplars.
passages.vernacular: 安妮坐喺敞開嘅窗邊,暫時忘咗考試嘅苦惱同世間嘅煩憂,陶醉喺夏日暮色嘅美麗中,花園裡嘅花香飄嚟,白楊樹嘅搖動發出沙沙聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮坐在敞開的窗邊,暫時忘了考試的苦惱和世間的煩憂,陶醉在夏日暮色的美麗中,花園裡的花香飄來,白楊樹的搖動發出沙沙聲。

passages.original: The eastern sky above the firs was flushed faintly pink from the reflection of the west, and Anne was wondering dreamily if the spirit of color looked like that, when she saw Diana come flying down through the firs, over the log bridge, and up the slope, with a fluttering newspaper in her hand.
passages.vernacular: 冷杉上方嘅東邊天空被西邊嘅倒影映成淡淡嘅粉紅,安妮正夢幻般地想,色彩嘅精靈係唔係長呢個樣子,呢陣佢睇見黛安娜從冷杉林中飛奔而下,過咗原木橋,跑上斜坡,手裡攞住一張飄動嘅報紙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冷杉上方的東邊天空被西邊的倒影映成淡淡的粉紅,安妮正夢幻般地想,色彩的精靈是不是長這個樣子,這時她看見黛安娜從冷杉林中飛奔而下,過了原木橋,跑上斜坡,手裡拿著一張飄動的報紙。

passages.original: Anne sprang to her feet, knowing at once what that paper contained.
passages.vernacular: 安妮一躍而起,即刻知道嗰報紙上係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮一躍而起,立刻知道那報紙上是什麼。

passages.original: The pass list was out!
passages.vernacular: 及格名單出嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 及格名單出來了!

passages.original: Her head whirled and her heart beat until it hurt her.
passages.vernacular: 佢頭暈目眩,心跳得發痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她頭暈目眩,心跳得發痛。

passages.original: She could not move a step.
passages.vernacular: 佢一步都動不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一步也動不了。

passages.original: It seemed an hour to her before Diana came rushing along the hall and burst into the room without even knocking, so great was her excitement.
passages.vernacular: 佢覺得過咗一個鐘頭,黛安娜才沿住走廊衝進嚟,連門都冇敲就闖進房間,佢咁激動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她覺得過了一個鐘頭,黛安娜才沿著走廊衝進來,連門都沒敲就闖進房間,她那麼激動。

passages.original: “Anne, you’ve passed,” she cried, “passed the very first--you and Gilbert both--you’re ties--but your name is first.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,你通過喇,」佢叫道,「第一名通過——你同吉爾伯特都——你哋並列——但你嘅名字排第一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,你通過了,」她叫道,「第一名通過——你和吉爾伯特都——你們並列——但你的名字排第一。

passages.original: Oh, I’m so proud!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我太自豪喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我太自豪了!」

passages.original: Diana flung the paper on the table and herself on Anne’s bed, utterly breathless and incapable of further speech.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜把報紙扔喺桌上,自己撲到安妮嘅床上,完全喘不過氣嚟,講不出話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜把報紙扔在桌上,自己撲到安妮的床上,完全喘不過氣來,說不出話。

passages.original: Anne lighted the lamp, oversetting the match safe and using up half a dozen matches before her shaking hands could accomplish the task.
passages.vernacular: 安妮點燈,打翻咗火柴盒,用掉咗半打火柴,顫抖嘅手才完成咗呢個任務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮點燈,打翻了火柴盒,用掉了半打火柴,顫抖的手才完成了這個任務。

passages.original: Then she snatched up the paper.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢一把抓起報紙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她一把抓起報紙。

passages.original: Yes, she had passed--there was her name at the very top of a list of two hundred!
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,佢通過喇——佢嘅名字就喺兩百人名單嘅最頂端!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,她通過了——她的名字就在兩百人名單的最頂端!

passages.original: That moment was worth living for.
passages.vernacular: 呢一刻值得活住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一刻值得活著。

passages.original: “You did just splendidly, Anne,” puffed Diana, recovering sufficiently to sit up and speak, for Anne, starry eyed and rapt, had not uttered a word.
passages.vernacular: 「你做得太棒喇,安妮,」黛安娜喘住氣講,恢復得足以坐起來講話,因為眼睛星光閃閃、陶醉出神嘅安妮一個字都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你做得太棒了,安妮,」黛安娜喘著氣說,恢復得足以坐起來說話,因為眼睛星光閃閃、陶醉出神的安妮一個字也沒說。

passages.original: “Father brought the paper home from Bright River not ten minutes ago--it came out on the afternoon train, you know, and won’t be here till tomorrow by mail--and when I saw the pass list I just rushed over like a wild thing.
passages.vernacular: 「爸爸好鐘前剛從明河把報紙帶回嚟——佢係乘下午嘅火車出嚟嘅,郵寄要聽日才到——我一睇到及格名單,就像個野丫頭一樣跑過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「爸爸十分鐘前剛從明河把報紙帶回來——它是乘下午的火車出來的,郵寄要明天才到——我一看到及格名單,就像個野丫頭一樣跑過來。

passages.original: You’ve all passed, every one of you, Moody Spurgeon and all, although he’s conditioned in history.
passages.vernacular: 你哋都通過喇,每一個人,連穆迪·斯珀吉翁都係,雖然佢歷史要補考。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們都通過了,每一個人,連穆迪·斯珀吉翁也是,雖然他歷史要補考。

passages.original: Jane and Ruby did pretty well--they’re halfway up--and so did Charlie.
passages.vernacular: 簡同露比考得相當好——喺中間——查理都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡和露比考得相當好——在中間——查理也是。

passages.original: Josie just scraped through with three marks to spare, but you’ll see she’ll put on as many airs as if she’d led.
passages.vernacular: 喬西剛好擦邊通過,多出三分,但你睇佢會擺出同得第一一樣嘅架子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西剛好擦邊通過,多出三分,但你看她會擺出和得第一一樣的架子。

passages.original: Won’t Miss Stacy be delighted?
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐唔係會高興嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐不是會高興嗎?

passages.original: Oh, Anne, what does it feel like to see your name at the head of a pass list like that?
passages.vernacular: 哦,安妮,睇到你嘅名字喺咁樣嘅及格名單頂端係乜嘢感覺?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,安妮,看到你的名字在這樣的及格名單頂端是什麼感覺?

passages.original: If it were me I know I’d go crazy with joy.
passages.vernacular: 如果係我,我知道我會高興瘋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是我,我知道我會高興瘋了。

passages.original: I am pretty near crazy as it is, but you’re as calm and cool as a spring evening.”
passages.vernacular: 我而家就快瘋喇,但你卻像春天嘅傍晚一樣平靜同冷靜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在就快瘋了,但你卻像春天的傍晚一樣平靜和冷靜。」

passages.original: “I’m just dazzled inside,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我只係內心炫目,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只是內心炫目,」安妮說。

passages.original: “I want to say a hundred things, and I can’t find words to say them in.
passages.vernacular: 「我想講一百件事,卻找唔到詞語來講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想說一百件事,卻找不到詞語來說。

passages.original: I never dreamed of this--yes, I did too, just once!
passages.vernacular: 我從冇夢想過呢個——不,我夢想過,就一次!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒夢想過這個——不,我夢想過,就一次!

passages.original: I let myself think once, ‘What if I should come out first?’ quakingly, you know, for it seemed so vain and presumptuous to think I could lead the Island.
passages.vernacular: 我讓自己想過一次:『如果我得第一點算?』顫抖住,您知道,因為覺得想領先全島似乎太虛榮同自大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讓自己想過一次:『如果我得第一怎麼辦?』顫抖著,您知道,因為覺得想領先全島似乎太虛榮和自大。

passages.original: Excuse me a minute, Diana.
passages.vernacular: 請原諒我一會兒,黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒我一會兒,黛安娜。

passages.original: I must run right out to the field to tell Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 我必須跑到田里去告訴馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須跑到田里去告訴馬修。

passages.original: Then we’ll go up the road and tell the good news to the others.”
passages.vernacular: 然後我哋沿路去把好消息告訴其他人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我們沿路去把好消息告訴其他人。」

passages.original: They hurried to the hayfield below the barn where Matthew was coiling hay, and, as luck would have it, Mrs. Lynde was talking to Marilla at the lane fence.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋匆匆趕到穀倉下面嘅乾草地,馬修正在嗰兒捲乾草,碰巧林德太太正在小巷柵欄邊同瑪麗拉講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們匆匆趕到穀倉下面的乾草地,馬修正在那兒捲乾草,碰巧林德太太正在小巷柵欄邊和瑪麗拉說話。

passages.original: “Oh, Matthew,” exclaimed Anne, “I’ve passed and I’m first--or one of the first!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,馬修,」安妮喊道,「我通過喇,我係第一名——或者之一!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,馬修,」安妮喊道,「我通過了,我是第一名——或者之一!

passages.original: I’m not vain, but I’m thankful.”
passages.vernacular: 我不虛榮,但我感恩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不虛榮,但我感恩。」

passages.original: “Well now, I always said it,” said Matthew, gazing at the pass list delightedly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我一直講呢,」馬修講,高興地睇住及格名單。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我一直說呢,」馬修說,高興地看著及格名單。

passages.original: “I knew you could beat them all easy.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道你能輕鬆打敗佢哋所有人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道你能輕鬆打敗他們所有人。」

passages.original: “You’ve done pretty well, I must say, Anne,” said Marilla, trying to hide her extreme pride in Anne from Mrs. Rachel’s critical eye.
passages.vernacular: 「你做得相當不錯,我必須講,安妮,」瑪麗拉講,試圖向雷切爾太太挑剔嘅目光隱藏佢對安妮嘅極大自豪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你做得相當不錯,我必須說,安妮,」瑪麗拉說,試圖向雷切爾太太挑剔的目光隱藏她對安妮的極大自豪。

passages.original: But that good soul said heartily:
passages.vernacular: 但嗰位好心人熱情地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那位好心人熱情地說:

passages.original: “I just guess she has done well, and far be it from me to be backward in saying it.
passages.vernacular: 「我就猜佢做得好好,我絕唔願喺講呢個上落後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就猜她做得很好,我絕不願在說這個上落後。

passages.original: You’re a credit to your friends, Anne, that’s what, and we’re all proud of you.”
passages.vernacular: 你係你朋友哋嘅光榮,安妮,就係咁樣,我哋都為你自豪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是你朋友們的光榮,安妮,就是這樣,我們都為你自豪。」

passages.original: That night Anne, who had wound up the delightful evening with a serious little talk with Mrs. Allan at the manse, knelt sweetly by her open window in a great sheen of moonshine and murmured a prayer of gratitude and aspiration that came straight from her heart.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,安妮喺牧師住宅同艾倫太太進行咗一次認真嘅小談話,結束咗愉快嘅夜晚,甜蜜地跪喺敞開嘅窗邊,滿身月光,喃喃地做咗一個直接發自內心嘅感恩同嚮往嘅禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,安妮在牧師住宅與艾倫太太進行了一次認真的小談話,結束了愉快的夜晚,甜蜜地跪在敞開的窗邊,滿身月光,喃喃地做了一個直接發自內心的感恩和嚮往的禱告。

passages.original: There was in it thankfulness for the past and reverent petition for the future; and when she slept on her white pillow her dreams were as fair and bright and beautiful as maidenhood might desire.
passages.vernacular: 禱告里有對過去嘅感恩,有對未來嘅虔敬祈求;當佢瞓喺白色嘅枕頭上時,佢嘅夢像少女期所能希望嘅嗰樣,美好、光明、美麗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 禱告里有對過去的感恩,有對未來的虔敬祈求;當她睡在白色的枕頭上時,她的夢像少女期所能希望的那樣,美好、光明、美麗。

chapters.title: Ch. XXXIII The Hotel Concert 第三十三章:旅館音樂會

passages.original: CH PUT on your white organdy, by all means, Anne,” advised Diana decidedly.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,你一定要穿嗰件白色細麻紗裙,」黛安娜斷然建議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,你一定要穿那件白色細麻紗裙,」黛安娜斷然建議。

passages.original: They were together in the east gable chamber; outside it was only twilight--a lovely yellowish-green twilight with a clear-blue cloudless sky.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋一起喺東山牆房間里;外面只係暮色——可愛嘅淡黃綠色暮色,天空係清澈嘅藍色,萬里無雲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們一起在東山牆房間里;外面只是暮色——可愛的淡黃綠色暮色,天空是清澈的藍色,萬里無雲。

passages.original: A big round moon, slowly deepening from her pallid luster into burnished silver, hung over the Haunted Wood; the air was full of sweet summer sounds--sleepy birds twittering, freakish breezes, faraway voices and laughter.
passages.vernacular: 一輪大圓月,慢慢地從蒼白嘅光澤加深成磨亮嘅銀色,懸喺鬧鬼林上空;空氣中充滿甜美嘅夏日聲音——昏昏欲瞓嘅鳥兒啁啾,任性嘅微風,遠處嘅聲音同笑聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一輪大圓月,慢慢地從蒼白的光澤加深成磨亮的銀色,懸在鬧鬼林上空;空氣中充滿甜美的夏日聲音——昏昏欲睡的鳥兒啁啾,任性的微風,遠處的聲音和笑聲。

passages.original: But in Anne’s room the blind was drawn and the lamp lighted, for an important toilet was being made.
passages.vernacular: 但安妮房間里,窗簾拉上喇,燈點亮喇,因為正在進行一次重要嘅梳妝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安妮房間里,窗簾拉上了,燈點亮了,因為正在進行一次重要的梳妝。

passages.original: The east gable was a very different place from what it had been on that night four years before, when Anne had felt its bareness penetrate to the marrow of her spirit with its inhospitable chill.
passages.vernacular: 東山牆房間同四年前嗰個夜晚大不相同,當時安妮覺得佢嘅光禿用佢不友好嘅寒意滲透進咗佢靈魂嘅骨髓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 東山牆房間與四年前那個夜晚大不相同,當時安妮覺得它的光禿用它不友好的寒意滲透進了她靈魂的骨髓。

passages.original: Changes had crept in, Marilla conniving at them resignedly, until it was as sweet and dainty a nest as a young girl could desire.
passages.vernacular: 變化悄悄地潛入,瑪麗拉順從地默許,直到佢成為一個少女所能希望嘅最甜美、最雅致嘅小窩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 變化悄悄地潛入,瑪麗拉順從地默許,直到它成為一個少女所能希望的最甜美、最雅致的小窩。

passages.original: The velvet carpet with the pink roses and the pink silk curtains of Anne’s early visions had certainly never materialized; but her dreams had kept pace with her growth, and it is not probable she lamented them.
passages.vernacular: 安妮早年幻想嘅帶粉紅玫瑰嘅天鵝絨地毯同粉紅絲綢窗簾,確實從未實現;但佢嘅夢想隨住佢嘅成長而改變,佢大概都不為佢哋惋惜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮早年幻想的帶粉紅玫瑰的天鵝絨地毯和粉紅絲綢窗簾,確實從未實現;但她的夢想隨著她的成長而改變,她大概也不為它們惋惜。

passages.original: The floor was covered with a pretty matting, and the curtains that softened the high window and fluttered in the vagrant breezes were of pale-green art muslin.
passages.vernacular: 地板上鋪住漂亮嘅蓆子,柔化高窗並喺漂泊嘅微風中飄動嘅窗簾,係淡綠色嘅藝術細棉布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 地板上鋪著漂亮的蓆子,柔化高窗並在漂泊的微風中飄動的窗簾,是淡綠色的藝術細棉布。

passages.original: The walls, hung not with gold and silver brocade tapestry, but with a dainty apple-blossom paper, were adorned with a few good pictures given Anne by Mrs. Allan.
passages.vernacular: 牆壁上冇掛金銀錦緞掛毯,而係貼住雅致嘅蘋果花壁紙,掛住艾倫太太送畀安妮嘅幾幅好畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牆壁上沒有掛金銀錦緞掛毯,而是貼著雅致的蘋果花壁紙,掛著艾倫太太送給安妮的幾幅好畫。

passages.original: Miss Stacy’s photograph occupied the place of honor, and Anne made a sentimental point of keeping fresh flowers on the bracket under it.
passages.vernacular: 斯泰西小姐嘅照片佔據住榮譽嘅位置,安妮多愁善感地堅持喺佢下面嘅托架上永遠放住鮮花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯泰西小姐的照片佔據著榮譽的位置,安妮多愁善感地堅持在它下面的托架上永遠放著鮮花。

passages.original: Tonight a spike of white lilies faintly perfumed the room like the dream of a fragrance.
passages.vernacular: 今晚一枝白百合,像一個香味嘅夢一樣,淡淡地薰住房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚一枝白百合,像一個香味的夢一樣,淡淡地薰著房間。

passages.original: There was no “mahogany furniture,” but there was a white-painted bookcase filled with books, a cushioned wicker rocker, a toilet table befrilled with white muslin, a quaint, gilt-framed mirror with chubby pink Cupids and purple grapes painted over its arched top, that used to hang in the spare room, and a low white bed.
passages.vernacular: 冇「桃花心木傢俱」,但有一個漆成白色嘅書櫃,裡面塞滿書;一把有墊子嘅藤搖椅;一張綴滿白細棉布褶邊嘅梳妝桌;一面古雅嘅、鍍金邊框嘅鏡子,拱形頂上畫住胖嘟嘟嘅粉紅丘比特同紫葡萄,過去掛喺備用客房里;仲有一張低矮嘅白色床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有「桃花心木傢俱」,但有一個漆成白色的書櫃,裡面塞滿書;一把有墊子的藤搖椅;一張綴滿白細棉布褶邊的梳妝桌;一面古雅的、鍍金邊框的鏡子,拱形頂上畫著胖嘟嘟的粉紅丘比特和紫葡萄,過去掛在備用客房里;還有一張低矮的白色床。

passages.original: Anne was dressing for a concert at the White Sands Hotel.
passages.vernacular: 安妮正在打扮,要去參加白沙旅館嘅音樂會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮正在打扮,要去參加白沙旅館的音樂會。

passages.original: The guests had got it up in aid of the Charlottetown hospital, and had hunted out all the available amateur talent in the surrounding districts to help it along.
passages.vernacular: 客人哋為資助夏洛特敦醫院而舉辦,並搜羅咗周邊地區所有可用嘅業餘才藝嚟幫忙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 客人們為資助夏洛特敦醫院而舉辦,並搜羅了周邊地區所有可用的業餘才藝來幫忙。

passages.original: Bertha Sampson and Pearl Clay of the White Sands Baptist choir had been asked to sing a duet; Milton Clark of Newbridge was to give a violin solo; Winnie Adella Blair of Carmody was to sing a Scotch ballad; and Laura Spencer of Spencervale and Anne Shirley of Avonlea were to recite.
passages.vernacular: 白沙浸信會唱詩班嘅伯莎·桑普森同珀爾·克萊被請去合唱二重唱;新橋嘅米爾頓·克拉克要拉小提琴獨奏;卡莫迪嘅溫妮·阿德拉·布萊爾要唱一首蘇格蘭民謠;斯潘塞韋爾嘅勞拉·斯潘塞同阿文利嘅安妮·雪莉要朗誦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白沙浸信會唱詩班的伯莎·桑普森和珀爾·克萊被請去合唱二重唱;新橋的米爾頓·克拉克要拉小提琴獨奏;卡莫迪的溫妮·阿德拉·布萊爾要唱一首蘇格蘭民謠;斯潘塞韋爾的勞拉·斯潘塞和阿文利的安妮·雪莉要朗誦。

passages.original: As Anne would have said at one time, it was “an epoch in her life,” and she was deliciously athrill with the excitement of it.
passages.vernacular: 正如安妮曾經會講嘅,呢個係「佢生命中嘅一個新紀元」,佢為呢次激動而美妙地顫慄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正如安妮曾經會說的,這是「她生命中的一個新紀元」,她為這次激動而美妙地顫慄。

passages.original: Matthew was in the seventh heaven of gratified pride over the honor conferred on his Anne and Marilla was not far behind, although she would have died rather than admit it, and said she didn’t think it was very proper for a lot of young folks to be gadding over to the hotel without any responsible person with them.
passages.vernacular: 馬修為授予佢嘅安妮嘅榮譽而自豪得上咗七重天,瑪麗拉都不甚落後,儘管佢寧死都不承認,仲講佢覺得一大群年輕人冇負責任嘅人陪同就到旅館閒逛,不太合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修為授予他的安妮的榮譽而自豪得上了七重天,瑪麗拉也不甚落後,儘管她寧死也不承認,還說她覺得一大群年輕人沒有負責任的人陪同就到旅館閒逛,不太合適。

passages.original: Anne and Diana were to drive over with Jane Andrews and her brother Billy in their double-seated buggy; and several other Avonlea girls and boys were going too.
passages.vernacular: 安妮同黛安娜要坐簡·安德魯斯同佢哥哥比利嘅雙座馬車去;仲有幾個阿文利嘅男孩女孩都去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮和黛安娜要坐簡·安德魯斯和她哥哥比利的雙座馬車去;還有幾個阿文利的男孩女孩也去。

passages.original: There was a party of visitors expected out from town, and after the concert a supper was to be given to the performers.
passages.vernacular: 有一批訪客預計從城里嚟,音樂會後要為表演者舉辦晚宴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一批訪客預計從城里來,音樂會後要為表演者舉辦晚宴。

passages.original: “Do you really think the organdy will be best?” queried Anne anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 「你真覺得細麻紗裙最好嗎?」安妮焦急地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真覺得細麻紗裙最好嗎?」安妮焦急地問。

passages.original: “I don’t think it’s as pretty as my blue-flowered muslin--and it certainly isn’t so fashionable.”
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得佢不如我嘅藍花細棉布好睇——而且肯定冇咁時髦。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得它不如我的藍花細棉布好看——而且肯定沒那麼時髦。」

passages.original: “But it suits you ever so much better,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「但佢更適合你得多,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但它更適合你得多,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “It’s so soft and frilly and clinging.
passages.vernacular: 「佢咁柔軟、帶褶邊、服帖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它那麼柔軟、帶褶邊、服帖。

passages.original: The muslin is stiff, and makes you look too dressed up.
passages.vernacular: 細棉布硬挺,讓你顯得太刻意打扮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 細棉布硬挺,讓你顯得太刻意打扮。

passages.original: But the organdy seems as if it grew on you.”
passages.vernacular: 但細麻紗裙好像長喺你身上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但細麻紗裙好像長在你身上。」

passages.original: Anne sighed and yielded.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘆咗口氣,讓步喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮嘆了口氣,讓步了。

passages.original: Diana was beginning to have a reputation for notable taste in dressing, and her advice on such subjects was much sought after.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜開始有咗住裝品味卓越嘅名聲,人哋好睇重佢喺呢類事上嘅意見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜開始有了著裝品味卓越的名聲,人們很看重她在這類事上的意見。

passages.original: She was looking very pretty herself on this particular night in a dress of the lovely wild-rose pink, from which Anne was forever debarred; but she was not to take any part in the concert, so her appearance was of minor importance.
passages.vernacular: 呢個特別嘅夜晚,佢自己穿住可愛嘅野玫瑰粉紅色裙子,睇上去好漂亮,呢種顏色安妮永遠唔能夠穿;但佢不參加音樂會表演,所以佢嘅外表次要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個特別的夜晚,她自己穿著可愛的野玫瑰粉紅色裙子,看上去很漂亮,這種顏色安妮永遠不能穿;但她不參加音樂會表演,所以她的外表次要。

passages.original: All her pains were bestowed upon Anne, who, she vowed, must, for the credit of Avonlea, be dressed and combed and adorned to the Queen’s taste.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅全部心思都用喺安妮身上,佢發誓,為了阿文利嘅榮譽,安妮必須被打扮、梳理、裝點得合女王嘅口味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的全部心思都用在安妮身上,她發誓,為了阿文利的榮譽,安妮必須被打扮、梳理、裝點得合女王的口味。

passages.original: “Pull out that frill a little more--so; here, let me tie your sash; now for your slippers.
passages.vernacular: 「再把嗰道褶邊抽出嚟啲——咁樣;嚟,讓我畀你繫腰帶;而家穿拖鞋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再把那道褶邊抽出來一點——這樣;來,讓我給你繫腰帶;現在穿拖鞋。

passages.original: I’m going to braid your hair in two thick braids, and tie them halfway up with big white bows--no, don’t pull out a single curl over your forehead--just have the soft part.
passages.vernacular: 我要把你嘅頭髮編成兩條粗辮子,用大白蝴蝶結綁喺半腰——不,別把額前嘅鬈髮拉出嚟一縷——就留柔和嘅部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把你的頭髮編成兩條粗辮子,用大白蝴蝶結綁在半腰——不,別把額前的鬈髮拉出來一縷——就留柔和的部分。

passages.original: There is no way you do your hair suits you so well, Anne, and Mrs. Allan says you look like a Madonna when you part it so.
passages.vernacular: 你冇邊種梳法比呢更適合你喇,安妮,艾倫太太講你咁樣分頭髮像聖母。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒有哪種梳法比這更適合你了,安妮,艾倫太太說你這樣分頭髮像聖母。

passages.original: I shall fasten this little white house rose just behind your ear.
passages.vernacular: 我要把呢朵小白家薔薇別喺你耳朵後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把這朵小白家薔薇別在你耳朵後面。

passages.original: There was just one on my bush, and I saved it for you.”
passages.vernacular: 我嘅樹叢上只有一朵,我畀你留住喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的樹叢上只有一朵,我給你留著了。」

passages.original: “Shall I put my pearl beads on?” asked Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我戴上我嘅珍珠項鍊嗎?」安妮問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我戴上我的珍珠項鍊嗎?」安妮問。

passages.original: “Matthew brought me a string from town last week, and I know he’d like to see them on me.”
passages.vernacular: 「馬修上星期從城里畀我帶嚟一串,我知道佢想睇我戴上佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修上星期從城里給我帶來一串,我知道他想看我戴上它們。」

passages.original: Diana pursed up her lips, put her black head on one side critically, and finally pronounced in favor of the beads, which were thereupon tied around Anne’s slim milk-white throat.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜噘起嘴唇,把黑髮腦袋歪向一邊,挑剔地端詳,最後宣布贊成戴珠子,於是佢哋被繫喺安妮纖細乳白嘅脖子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜噘起嘴唇,把黑髮腦袋歪向一邊,挑剔地端詳,最後宣布贊成戴珠子,於是它們被繫在安妮纖細乳白的脖子上。

passages.original: “There’s something so stylish about you, Anne,” said Diana, with unenvious admiration.
passages.vernacular: 「你身上有一種咁時髦嘅嘢,安妮,」黛安娜講,帶住不嫉妒嘅欽佩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你身上有一種那麼時髦的東西,安妮,」黛安娜說,帶著不嫉妒的欽佩。

passages.original: “You hold your head with such an air.
passages.vernacular: 「你昂住頭嘅樣子咁有氣派。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你昂著頭的樣子那麼有氣派。

passages.original: I suppose it’s your figure.
passages.vernacular: 我想係你嘅身材。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想是你的身材。

passages.original: I am just a dumpling.
passages.vernacular: 我只係個湯圓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是個湯圓。

passages.original: I’ve always been afraid of it, and now I know it is so.
passages.vernacular: 我一直擔心呢啲,而家我知道係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直擔心這一點,現在我知道是真的。

passages.original: Well, I suppose I shall just have to resign myself to it.”
passages.vernacular: 好吧,我想我只好順從喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,我想我只好順從了。」

passages.original: “But you have such dimples,” said Anne, smiling affectionately into the pretty, vivacious face so near her own.
passages.vernacular: 「但你有咁好嘅酒窩,」安妮講,深情地對住近喺咫尺嘅漂亮、活潑嘅臉微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你有那麼好的酒窩,」安妮說,深情地對著近在咫尺的漂亮、活潑的臉微笑。

passages.original: “Lovely dimples, like little dents in cream.
passages.vernacular: 「可愛嘅酒窩,像奶油里嘅小凹痕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可愛的酒窩,像奶油里的小凹痕。

passages.original: I have given up all hope of dimples.
passages.vernacular: 我已經放棄酒窩嘅希望喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經放棄酒窩的希望了。

passages.original: My dimple-dream will never come true; but so many of my dreams have that I mustn’t complain.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅酒窩夢永遠唔會實現;但我有咁多夢實現喇,不該抱怨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的酒窩夢永遠不會實現;但我有這麼多夢實現了,不該抱怨。

passages.original: Am I all ready now?”
passages.vernacular: 我而家全都準備好咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在全都準備好了嗎?」

passages.original: “All ready,” assured Diana, as Marilla appeared in the doorway, a gaunt figure with grayer hair than of yore and no fewer angles, but with a much softer face.
passages.vernacular: 「全準備好喇,」黛安娜保證,呢陣瑪麗拉出而家門口,一個消瘦嘅身影,頭髮比往昔更灰,稜角啲冇少,但臉龐柔和得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「全準備好了,」黛安娜保證,這時瑪麗拉出現在門口,一個消瘦的身影,頭髮比往昔更灰,稜角一點沒少,但臉龐柔和得多。

passages.original: “Come right in and look at our elocutionist, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「進嚟睇睇我哋嘅朗誦家,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「進來看看我們的朗誦家,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: Doesn’t she look lovely?”
passages.vernacular: 佢睇上去唔係好可愛嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看上去不是很可愛嗎?」

passages.original: Marilla emitted a sound between a sniff and a grunt.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉發出介於哼鼻同咕噥之間嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉發出介於哼鼻和咕噥之間的聲音。

passages.original: “She looks neat and proper.
passages.vernacular: 「佢睇上去整潔得體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她看上去整潔得體。

passages.original: I like that way of fixing her hair.
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意咁樣梳頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡這樣梳頭髮。

passages.original: But I expect she’ll ruin that dress driving over there in the dust and dew with it, and it looks most too thin for these damp nights.
passages.vernacular: 但我想佢坐車去嗰兒,喺灰塵同露水里,會毀咗嗰條裙子,而且對呢啲潮濕嘅夜晚來講,佢睇上去太薄喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我想她坐車去那兒,在灰塵和露水里,會毀了那條裙子,而且對這些潮濕的夜晚來說,它看上去太薄了。

passages.original: Organdy’s the most unserviceable stuff in the world anyhow, and I told Matthew so when he got it.
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,細麻紗係世上最不耐用嘅料子,馬修買嘅時候我就咁告訴過佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,細麻紗是世上最不耐用的料子,馬修買的時候我就這麼告訴過他。

passages.original: But there is no use in saying anything to Matthew nowadays.
passages.vernacular: 但如今跟馬修講乜嘢都冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如今跟馬修說什麼都沒用。

passages.original: Time was when he would take my advice, but now he just buys things for Anne regardless, and the clerks at Carmody know they can palm anything off on him.
passages.vernacular: 曾經佢聽我嘅勸告,但而家佢畀安妮買嘢乜嘢都不顧喇,卡莫迪嘅店員都知道佢哋可以把任何嘢塞畀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 曾經他聽我的勸告,但現在他給安妮買東西什麼都不顧了,卡莫迪的店員都知道他們可以把任何東西塞給他。

passages.original: Just let them tell him a thing is pretty and fashionable, and Matthew plunks his money down for it.
passages.vernacular: 只要佢哋告訴佢某樣嘢漂亮時髦,馬修就把錢扔出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要他們告訴他某樣東西漂亮時髦,馬修就把錢扔出去。

passages.original: Mind you keep your skirt clear of the wheel, Anne, and put your warm jacket on.”
passages.vernacular: 注意讓你嘅裙子別碰到輪子,安妮,穿上你嘅暖夾克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 注意讓你的裙子別碰到輪子,安妮,穿上你的暖夾克。」

passages.original: Then Marilla stalked downstairs, thinking proudly how sweet Anne looked, with that
passages.vernacular: 然後瑪麗拉大步走下樓,自豪地想住安妮睇上去幾咁可愛,嗰
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後瑪麗拉大步走下樓,自豪地想著安妮看上去多麼可愛,那

passages.original: “One moonbeam from the forehead to the crown”
passages.vernacular: 「一道月光從額頭到頭頂」
