passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一道月光從額頭到頭頂」

passages.original: and regretting that she could not go to the concert herself to hear her girl recite.
passages.vernacular: 並遺憾自己唔能夠去音樂會聽佢嘅女孩朗誦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並遺憾自己不能去音樂會聽她的女孩朗誦。

passages.original: “I wonder if it is too damp for my dress,” said Anne anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道對我嘅裙子來講係唔係太潮濕喇,」安妮焦急地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道對我的裙子來說是不是太潮濕了,」安妮焦急地說。

passages.original: “Not a bit of it,” said Diana, pulling up the window blind.
passages.vernacular: 「啲都不,」黛安娜講,拉起窗簾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一點也不,」黛安娜說,拉起窗簾。

passages.original: “It’s a perfect night, and there won’t be any dew.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係個完美嘅夜晚,唔會有露水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是個完美的夜晚,不會有露水。

passages.original: Look at the moonlight.”
passages.vernacular: 睇月光。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看月光。」

passages.original: “I’m so glad my window looks east into the sun rising,” said Anne, going over to Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我真高興我嘅窗子朝東,睇得到太陽升起,」安妮講,走到黛安娜身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真高興我的窗子朝東,看得到太陽升起,」安妮說,走到黛安娜身邊。

passages.original: “It’s so splendid to see the morning coming up over those long hills and glowing through those sharp fir tops.
passages.vernacular: 「睇到早晨從嗰啲長長嘅山丘上升起,透過嗰啲尖尖嘅冷杉頂閃耀,太棒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看到早晨從那些長長的山丘上升起,透過那些尖尖的冷杉頂閃耀,太棒了。

passages.original: It’s new every morning, and I feel as if I washed my very soul in that bath of earliest sunshine.
passages.vernacular: 每天早晨都係新嘅,我覺得好像喺嗰最早嘅陽光浴里洗滌咗我嘅靈魂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每天早晨都是新的,我覺得好像在那最早的陽光浴里洗滌了我的靈魂。

passages.original: Oh, Diana, I love this little room so dearly.
passages.vernacular: 哦,黛安娜,我咁深愛呢間小屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,黛安娜,我那麼深愛這間小屋。

passages.original: I don’t know how I’ll get along without it when I go to town next month.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道下個月去城裡後,冇佢我點過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道下個月去城裡後,沒有它我怎麼過。」

passages.original: “Don’t speak of your going away tonight,” begged Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「今晚別談你要走嘅事,」黛安娜央求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚別談你要走的事,」黛安娜央求道。

passages.original: “I don’t want to think of it, it makes me so miserable, and I do want to have a good time this evening.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔想想佢,佢讓我咁難受,而我想今晚好好玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不想想它,它讓我那麼難受,而我想今晚好好玩。

passages.original: What are you going to recite, Anne?
passages.vernacular: 你要朗誦乜嘢,安妮?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要朗誦什麼,安妮?

passages.original: And are you nervous?”
passages.vernacular: 你緊張嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你緊張嗎?」

passages.original: “Not a bit.
passages.vernacular: 「啲都不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一點也不。

passages.original: I’ve recited so often in public I don’t mind at all now.
passages.vernacular: 我喺公眾場合朗誦咁多次,而家啲都不介意喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在公眾場合朗誦那麼多次,現在一點也不介意了。

passages.original: I’ve decided to give ‘The Maiden’s Vow.’
passages.vernacular: 我決定朗誦《少女嘅誓言》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我決定朗誦《少女的誓言》。

passages.original: It’s so pathetic.
passages.vernacular: 佢咁悲壯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它那麼悲壯。

passages.original: Laura Spencer is going to give a comic recitation, but I’d rather make people cry than laugh.”
passages.vernacular: 勞拉·斯潘塞要朗誦一篇滑稽嘅,但我寧願讓人哭而唔係讓人笑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勞拉·斯潘塞要朗誦一篇滑稽的,但我寧願讓人哭而不是讓人笑。」

passages.original: “What will you recite if they encore you?”
passages.vernacular: 「如果佢哋要你再嚟一個,你朗誦乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果他們要你再來一個,你朗誦什麼?」

passages.original: “They won’t dream of encoring me,” scoffed Anne, who was not without her own secret hopes that they would, and already visioned herself telling Matthew all about it at the next morning’s breakfast table.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋做夢都唔會要我再嚟一個,」安妮嗤之以鼻,佢並非冇自己嘅暗暗希望,希望佢哋會要,並且已經喺想像自己第二天朝早喺早餐桌上把呢一切告訴馬修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們做夢也不會要我再來一個,」安妮嗤之以鼻,她並非沒有自己的暗暗希望,希望他們會要,並且已經在想像自己第二天早上在早餐桌上把這一切告訴馬修。

passages.original: “There are Billy and Jane now--I hear the wheels.
passages.vernacular: 「比利同簡嚟喇——我聽見輪子聲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「比利和簡來了——我聽見輪子聲了。

passages.original: Come on.”
passages.vernacular: 走吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走吧。」

passages.original: Billy Andrews insisted that Anne should ride on the front seat with him, so she unwillingly climbed up.
passages.vernacular: 比利·安德魯斯堅持安妮應該跟佢坐喺前座,所以佢不情願地爬咗上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比利·安德魯斯堅持安妮應該跟他坐在前座,所以她不情願地爬了上去。

passages.original: She would have much preferred to sit back with the girls, where she could have laughed and chattered to her heart’s content.
passages.vernacular: 佢本寧願坐喺後面同女孩哋喺一起,喺嗰兒佢可以盡情地笑同聊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她本寧願坐在後面和女孩們在一起,在那兒她可以盡情地笑和聊。

passages.original: There was not much of either laughter or chatter in Billy.
passages.vernacular: 比利身上冇多少笑同聊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比利身上沒有多少笑和聊。

passages.original: He was a big, fat, stolid youth of twenty, with a round, expressionless face, and a painful lack of conversational gifts.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個高大、肥胖、遲鈍嘅二十歲青年,圓圓嘅、冇表情嘅臉,痛苦地缺乏談話嘅天賦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個高大、肥胖、遲鈍的二十歲青年,圓圓的、沒有表情的臉,痛苦地缺乏談話的天賦。

passages.original: But he admired Anne immensely, and was puffed up with pride over the prospect of driving to White Sands with that slim, upright figure beside him.
passages.vernacular: 但佢極其欽佩安妮,一想到要同嗰苗條挺直嘅身影坐喺身邊駕車去白沙,佢就得意洋洋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他極其欽佩安妮,一想到要和那苗條挺直的身影坐在身邊駕車去白沙,他就得意洋洋。

passages.original: Anne, by dint of talking over her shoulder to the girls and occasionally passing a sop of civility to Billy--who grinned and chuckled and never could think of any reply until it was too late--contrived to enjoy the drive in spite of all.
passages.vernacular: 安妮一邊扭頭跟女孩哋講話,偶爾畀比利扔一句客套嘅安慰話——佢咧嘴笑住、呵呵笑住,總是等到太晚咗才想出回答——設法喺所有呢啲情況下享受咗呢趟旅程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮一邊扭頭跟女孩們說話,偶爾給比利扔一句客套的安慰話——他咧嘴笑著、呵呵笑著,總是等到太晚了才想出回答——設法在所有這些情況下享受了這趟旅程。

passages.original: It was a night for enjoyment.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個適合享受嘅夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個適合享受的夜晚。

passages.original: The road was full of buggies, all bound for the hotel, and laughter, silver clear, echoed and reechoed along it.
passages.vernacular: 路上擠滿咗馬車,全都駛向旅館,銀鈴般清脆嘅笑聲,沿路回響不絕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 路上擠滿了馬車,全都駛向旅館,銀鈴般清脆的笑聲,沿路回響不絕。

passages.original: When they reached the hotel it was a blaze of light from top to bottom.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋到達旅館時,佢從上到下燈火通明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們到達旅館時,它從上到下燈火通明。

passages.original: They were met by the ladies of the concert committee, one of whom took Anne off to the performers’ dressing room which was filled with the members of a Charlottetown Symphony Club, among whom Anne felt suddenly shy and frightened and countrified.
passages.vernacular: 音樂會委員會嘅女士哋迎接咗佢哋,其中一位把安妮帶到表演者更衣室,嗰度擠滿咗夏洛特敦交響樂團嘅成員,喺佢哋中間安妮突然感到羞怯、驚恐同土氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 音樂會委員會的女士們迎接了他們,其中一位把安妮帶到表演者更衣室,那裡擠滿了夏洛特敦交響樂團的成員,在他們中間安妮突然感到羞怯、驚恐和土氣。

passages.original: Her dress, which, in the east gable, had seemed so dainty and pretty, now seemed simple and plain--too simple and plain, she thought, among all the silks and laces that glistened and rustled around her.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅裙子,喺東山牆房間里似乎咁雅致漂亮,而家似乎樸素平淡——喺佢周圍閃耀、沙沙作響嘅所有綢緞同蕾絲中間,太樸素平淡喇,佢想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的裙子,在東山牆房間里似乎那麼雅致漂亮,現在似乎樸素平淡——在她周圍閃耀、沙沙作響的所有綢緞和蕾絲中間,太樸素平淡了,她想。

passages.original: What were her pearl beads compared to the diamonds of the big, handsome lady near her?
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅珍珠項鍊比起旁邊嗰位高大漂亮嘅女士嘅鑽石算乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的珍珠項鍊比起旁邊那位高大漂亮的女士的鑽石算什麼?

passages.original: And how poor her one wee white rose must look beside all the hothouse flowers the others wore!
passages.vernacular: 佢嗰一朵小白玫瑰,喺別人戴嘅所有溫室花旁邊,一定顯得幾咁寒酸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她那一朵小白玫瑰,在別人戴的所有溫室花旁邊,一定顯得多麼寒酸!

passages.original: Anne laid her hat and jacket away, and shrank miserably into a corner.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把帽子同夾克放好,痛苦地縮進一個角落。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把帽子和夾克放好,痛苦地縮進一個角落。

passages.original: She wished herself back in the white room at Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 佢希望自己回到綠色屋頂嗰間白色嘅房間里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她希望自己回到綠色屋頂那間白色的房間里。

passages.original: It was still worse on the platform of the big concert hall of the hotel, where she presently found herself.
passages.vernacular: 佢隨即發現自己喺旅館大音樂廳嘅臺上,更糟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她隨即發現自己在旅館大音樂廳的臺上,更糟了。

passages.original: The electric lights dazzled her eyes, the perfume and hum bewildered her.
passages.vernacular: 電燈晃得佢眼花,香水味同嗡嗡聲令佢迷惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 電燈晃得她眼花,香水味和嗡嗡聲令她迷惑。

passages.original: She wished she were sitting down in the audience with Diana and Jane, who seemed to be having a splendid time away at the back.
passages.vernacular: 佢希望自己坐喺觀眾席里同黛安娜、簡喺一起,佢哋喺遠遠嘅後面似乎玩得好開心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她希望自己坐在觀眾席里和黛安娜、簡在一起,她們在遠遠的後面似乎玩得很開心。

passages.original: She was wedged in between a stout lady in pink silk and a tall, scornful-looking girl in a white-lace dress.
passages.vernacular: 佢被夾喺一位穿粉紅絲綢嘅胖女士同一位穿白蕾絲裙、顯得高傲嘅瘦高女孩之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她被夾在一位穿粉紅絲綢的胖女士和一位穿白蕾絲裙、顯得高傲的瘦高女孩之間。

passages.original: The stout lady occasionally turned her head squarely around and surveyed Anne through her eyeglasses until Anne, acutely sensitive of being so scrutinized, felt that she must scream aloud; and the white-lace girl kept talking audibly to her next neighbor about the “country bumpkins” and “rustic belles” in the audience, languidly anticipating “such fun” from the displays of local talent on the program.
passages.vernacular: 胖女士偶爾把頭方方正正地轉過嚟,透過眼鏡打量安妮,直到對被咁樣審視極度敏感嘅安妮覺得自己必須大聲尖叫;而穿白蕾絲嘅女孩一直對佢旁邊嘅鄰居大聲談論觀眾里嘅「鄉巴佬」同「鄉下美人」,懶洋洋地期待節目單上本地才藝嘅表演「會有多好玩」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 胖女士偶爾把頭方方正正地轉過來,透過眼鏡打量安妮,直到對被這樣審視極度敏感的安妮覺得自己必須大聲尖叫;而穿白蕾絲的女孩一直對她旁邊的鄰居大聲談論觀眾里的「鄉巴佬」和「鄉下美人」,懶洋洋地期待節目單上本地才藝的表演「會有多好玩」。

passages.original: Anne believed that she would hate that white-lace girl to the end of life.
passages.vernacular: 安妮相信自己會恨嗰個穿白蕾絲嘅女孩直到生命嘅盡頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮相信自己會恨那個穿白蕾絲的女孩直到生命的盡頭。

passages.original: Unfortunately for Anne, a professional elocutionist was staying at the hotel and had consented to recite.
passages.vernacular: 對安妮不幸嘅係,一位專業朗誦家住喺旅館里,並答應朗誦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對安妮不幸的是,一位專業朗誦家住在旅館里,並答應朗誦。

passages.original: She was a lithe, dark-eyed woman in a wonderful gown of shimmering gray stuff like woven moonbeams, with gems on her neck and in her dark hair.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個柔韌、黑眼睛嘅女人,穿住一件奇妙嘅閃爍灰色禮服,像編織嘅月光,脖子上同黑髮上戴住寶石。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個柔韌、黑眼睛的女人,穿著一件奇妙的閃爍灰色禮服,像編織的月光,脖子上和黑髮上戴著寶石。

passages.original: She had a marvelously flexible voice and wonderful power of expression; the audience went wild over her selection.
passages.vernacular: 佢有好靈活嘅嗓音同奇妙嘅表現力;觀眾對佢嘅選段狂熱起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有非常靈活的嗓音和奇妙的表現力;觀眾對她的選段狂熱起來。

passages.original: Anne, forgetting all about herself and her troubles for the time, listened with rapt and shining eyes; but when the recitation ended she suddenly put her hands over her face.
passages.vernacular: 安妮暫時忘咗自己同佢嘅煩惱,眼睛入神發亮地聽住;但朗誦結束時,佢突然用雙手捂住咗臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮暫時忘了自己和她的煩惱,眼睛入神發亮地聽著;但朗誦結束時,她突然用雙手捂住了臉。

passages.original: She could never get up and recite after that--never.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢之後佢永遠唔可能站起嚟朗誦喇——永遠唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這之後她永遠不可能站起來朗誦了——永遠不能。

passages.original: Had she ever thought she could recite?
passages.vernacular: 佢曾經以為自己能朗誦嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她曾經以為自己能朗誦嗎?

passages.original: Oh, if she were only back at Green Gables!
passages.vernacular: 哦,要係佢回到綠色屋頂就好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,要是她回到綠色屋頂就好了!

passages.original: At this unpropitious moment her name was called.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢個不祥嘅時刻,佢嘅名字被叫到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這個不祥的時刻,她的名字被叫到了。

passages.original: Somehow Anne--who did not notice the rather guilty little start of surprise the white-lace girl gave, and would not have understood the subtle compliment implied therein if she had--got on her feet, and moved dizzily out to the front.
passages.vernacular: 安妮——佢冇注意到穿白蕾絲嘅女孩帶住相當內疚嘅小小驚訝一抖,就算注意到,都不懂其中隱含嘅微妙讚美——唔知怎嘅站咗起嚟,頭暈目眩地走向前面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮——她沒注意到穿白蕾絲的女孩帶著相當內疚的小小驚訝一抖,就算注意到,也不懂其中隱含的微妙讚美——不知怎的站了起來,頭暈目眩地走向前面。

passages.original: She was so pale that Diana and Jane, down in the audience, clasped each other’s hands in nervous sympathy.
passages.vernacular: 佢臉色咁蒼白,觀眾席里嘅黛安娜同簡緊張地握緊咗彼此嘅手表示同情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她臉色那麼蒼白,觀眾席里的黛安娜和簡緊張地握緊了彼此的手表示同情。

passages.original: Anne was the victim of an overwhelming attack of stage fright.
passages.vernacular: 安妮成咗一場壓倒性嘅怯場嘅受害者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮成了一場壓倒性的怯場的受害者。

passages.original: Often as she had recited in public, she had never before faced such an audience as this, and the sight of it paralyzed her energies completely.
passages.vernacular: 儘管佢經常喺公眾場合朗誦,佢以前從未面對過咁樣嘅觀眾,睇到佢,佢嘅精力完全麻痺喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管她經常在公眾場合朗誦,她以前從未面對過這樣的觀眾,看到它,她的精力完全麻痺了。

passages.original: Everything was so strange, so brilliant, so bewildering--the rows of ladies in evening dress, the critical faces, the whole atmosphere of wealth and culture about her.
passages.vernacular: 一切都咁陌生、咁輝煌、咁令人迷惑——一排排穿晚禮服嘅女士,挑剔嘅臉,佢周圍嗰種財富同文化嘅整個氛圍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切都那麼陌生、那麼輝煌、那麼令人迷惑——一排排穿晚禮服的女士,挑剔的臉,她周圍那種財富與文化的整個氛圍。

passages.original: Very different this from the plain benches at the Debating Club, filled with the homely, sympathetic faces of friends and neighbors.
passages.vernacular: 呢同辯論社嗰啲樸素嘅長凳大不相同,嗰度坐滿咗朋友同鄰居樸實而同情嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這與辯論社那些樸素的長凳大不相同,那裡坐滿了朋友和鄰居樸實而同情的臉。

passages.original: These people, she thought, would be merciless critics.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲人,佢想,會係無情嘅批評家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些人,她想,會是無情的批評家。

passages.original: Perhaps, like the white-lace girl, they anticipated amusement from her “rustic” efforts.
passages.vernacular: 或者,像穿白蕾絲嘅女孩一樣,佢哋期待從佢「鄉下嘅」努力中得到樂趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許,像穿白蕾絲的女孩一樣,他們期待從她「鄉下的」努力中得到樂趣。

passages.original: She felt hopelessly, helplessly ashamed and miserable.
passages.vernacular: 佢感到絕望地、無助地羞愧同痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她感到絕望地、無助地羞愧和痛苦。

passages.original: Her knees trembled, her heart fluttered, a horrible faintness came over her; not a word could she utter, and the next moment she would have fled from the platform despite the humiliation which, she felt, must ever after be her portion if she did so.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅膝蓋顫抖,心怦怦亂跳,一陣可怕嘅暈眩襲嚟;佢一個字都講不出嚟,下一刻佢就會逃離講臺,儘管佢覺得,如果嗰樣做,屈辱將永遠成為佢嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的膝蓋顫抖,心怦怦亂跳,一陣可怕的暈眩襲來;她一個字也說不出來,下一刻她就會逃離講臺,儘管她覺得,如果那樣做,屈辱將永遠成為她的命運。

passages.original: But suddenly, as her dilated, frightened eyes gazed out over the audience, she saw Gilbert Blythe away at the back of the room, bending forward with a smile on his face--a smile which seemed to Anne at once triumphant and taunting.
passages.vernacular: 但忽然,佢睜大嘅、驚恐嘅眼睛望過觀眾席時,睇見吉爾伯特·布萊斯遠喺房間後面,身子前傾,臉上帶住微笑——嗰微笑喺安妮睇來既得意又嘲諷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但忽然,她睜大的、驚恐的眼睛望過觀眾席時,看見吉爾伯特·布萊斯遠在房間後面,身子前傾,臉上帶著微笑——那微笑在安妮看來既得意又嘲諷。

passages.original: In reality it was nothing of the kind.
passages.vernacular: 實際上完全唔係嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 實際上完全不是那樣。

passages.original: Gilbert was merely smiling with appreciation of the whole affair in general and of the effect produced by Anne’s slender white form and spiritual face against a background of palms in particular.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特只係為整個場面,尤其係為安妮纖細嘅白色身影同佢靈性嘅臉龐喺棕櫚背景襯托下產生嘅效果,而帶住欣賞地微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特只是為整個場面,尤其是為安妮纖細的白色身影和她靈性的臉龐在棕櫚背景襯托下產生的效果,而帶著欣賞地微笑。

passages.original: Josie Pye, whom he had driven over, sat beside him, and her face certainly was both triumphant and taunting.
passages.vernacular: 被佢駕車載嚟嘅喬西·派伊坐喺佢旁邊,佢嘅臉確實既得意又嘲諷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被他駕車載來的喬西·派伊坐在他旁邊,她的臉確實既得意又嘲諷。

passages.original: But Anne did not see Josie, and would not have cared if she had.
passages.vernacular: 但安妮冇睇見喬西,就算睇見都唔會在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安妮沒看見喬西,就算看見也不會在乎。

passages.original: She drew a long breath and flung her head up proudly, courage and determination tingling over her like an electric shock.
passages.vernacular: 佢深吸一口氣,驕傲地昂起頭,勇氣同決心像電擊一樣喺佢全身刺痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她深吸一口氣,驕傲地昂起頭,勇氣和決心像電擊一樣在她全身刺痛。

passages.original: She would not fail before Gilbert Blythe--he should never be able to laugh at her, never, never!
passages.vernacular: 佢唔會喺吉爾伯特·布萊斯面前失敗——佢永遠唔能夠嘲笑佢,永遠,永遠唔能夠!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不會在吉爾伯特·布萊斯面前失敗——他永遠不能嘲笑她,永遠,永遠不能!

passages.original: Her fright and nervousness vanished; and she began her recitation, her clear, sweet voice reaching to the farthest corner of the room without a tremor or a break.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅恐懼同緊張消失喇;佢開始朗誦,佢清脆甜美嘅聲音傳到房間最遠嘅角落,冇顫抖,冇中斷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的恐懼和緊張消失了;她開始朗誦,她清脆甜美的聲音傳到房間最遠的角落,沒有顫抖,沒有中斷。

passages.original: Self-possession was fully restored to her, and in the reaction from that horrible moment of powerlessness she recited as she had never done before.
passages.vernacular: 鎮定完全恢復喇,喺從嗰個可怕嘅無力時刻嘅反彈中,佢朗誦得前所未有地好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鎮定完全恢復了,在從那個可怕的無力時刻的反彈中,她朗誦得前所未有地好。

passages.original: When she finished there were bursts of honest applause.
passages.vernacular: 佢結束時,響起咗真誠嘅掌聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她結束時,響起了真誠的掌聲。

passages.original: Anne, stepping back to her seat, blushing with shyness and delight, found her hand vigorously clasped and shaken by the stout lady in pink silk.
passages.vernacular: 安妮退回座位,羞澀同喜悅得臉紅,發現佢嘅手被穿粉紅絲綢嘅胖女士用力握住搖晃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮退回座位,羞澀和喜悅得臉紅,發現她的手被穿粉紅絲綢的胖女士用力握住搖晃。

passages.original: “My dear, you did splendidly,” she puffed.
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅,你做得太棒喇,」佢喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的,你做得太棒了,」她喘著氣說。

passages.original: “I’ve been crying like a baby, actually I have.
passages.vernacular: 「我一直哭得像個嬰兒,真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一直哭得像個嬰兒,真的。

passages.original: There, they’re encoring you--they’re bound to have you back!”
passages.vernacular: 瞧,佢哋要你再嚟一個——佢哋一定要你回去!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瞧,他們要你再來一個——他們一定要你回去!」

passages.original: “Oh, I can’t go,” said Anne confusedly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我唔能夠去,」安妮慌亂地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我不能去,」安妮慌亂地說。

passages.original: “But yet--I must, or Matthew will be disappointed.
passages.vernacular: 「但係——我必須,否則馬修會失望嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是——我必須,否則馬修會失望的。

passages.original: He said they would encore me.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢哋會要我再嚟一個嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他們會要我再來一個的。」

passages.original: “Then don’t disappoint Matthew,” said the pink lady, laughing.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就唔好畀馬修失望,」粉紅女士笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就別讓馬修失望,」粉紅女士笑著說。

passages.original: Smiling, blushing, limpid eyed, Anne tripped back and gave a quaint, funny little selection that captivated her audience still further.
passages.vernacular: 微笑住,臉紅住,眼睛清澈,安妮輕快地走回去,朗誦咗一個古雅有趣嘅小選段,更加迷住咗觀眾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 微笑著,臉紅著,眼睛清澈,安妮輕快地走回去,朗誦了一個古雅有趣的小選段,更加迷住了觀眾。

passages.original: The rest of the evening was quite a little triumph for her.
passages.vernacular: 晚上剩下嘅時間對佢來講完全係個小小嘅勝利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚上剩下的時間對她來說完全是個小小的勝利。

passages.original: When the concert was over, the stout, pink lady--who was the wife of an American millionaire--took her under her wing, and introduced her to everybody; and everybody was very nice to her.
passages.vernacular: 音樂會結束後,嗰位胖胖嘅粉紅女士——美國一位百萬富翁嘅妻子——把佢置於羽翼之下,把佢介紹畀所有人;每個人都對佢好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 音樂會結束後,那位胖胖的粉紅女士——美國一位百萬富翁的妻子——把她置於羽翼之下,把她介紹給所有人;每個人都對她很好。

passages.original: The professional elocutionist, Mrs. Evans, came and chatted with her, telling her that she had a charming voice and “interpreted” her selections beautifully.
passages.vernacular: 專業朗誦家埃文斯太太過嚟同佢聊天,告訴佢佢嘅嗓音迷人,「詮釋」佢嘅選段好出色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 專業朗誦家埃文斯太太過來和她聊天,告訴她她的嗓音迷人,「詮釋」她的選段非常出色。

passages.original: Even the white-lace girl paid her a languid little compliment.
passages.vernacular: 連穿白蕾絲嘅女孩都畀咗佢一個懶洋洋嘅小小恭維。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連穿白蕾絲的女孩也給了她一個懶洋洋的小小恭維。

passages.original: They had supper in the big, beautifully decorated dining room; Diana and Jane were invited to partake of this, also, since they had come with Anne, but Billy was nowhere to be found, having decamped in mortal fear of some such invitation.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺裝飾華麗嘅大餐廳食咗晚餐;黛安娜同簡因為係同安妮一起嚟嘅,都被邀請參加,但比利唔見喇,佢喺對呢類邀請嘅極度恐懼中溜走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在裝飾華麗的大餐廳吃了晚餐;黛安娜和簡因為是和安妮一起來的,也被邀請參加,但比利不見了,他在對這類邀請的極度恐懼中溜走了。

passages.original: He was in waiting for them, with the team, however, when it was all over, and the three girls came merrily out into the calm, white moonshine radiance.
passages.vernacular: 不過一切結束後,三個女孩快樂地走出到寧靜、白色嘅月光里時,佢已帶住馬車喺等待佢哋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過一切結束後,三個女孩快樂地走出到寧靜、白色的月光里時,他已帶著馬車在等待她們了。

passages.original: Anne breathed deeply, and looked into the clear sky beyond the dark boughs of the firs.
passages.vernacular: 安妮深深地呼吸,望住冷杉黑色枝條之外澄澈嘅天空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮深深地呼吸,望著冷杉黑色枝條之外澄澈的天空。

passages.original: Oh, it was good to be out again in the purity and silence of the night!
passages.vernacular: 哦,再次嚟到純潔寂靜嘅夜晚真好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,再次來到純潔寂靜的夜晚真好!

passages.original: How great and still and wonderful everything was, with the murmur of the sea sounding through it and the darkling cliffs beyond like grim giants guarding enchanted coasts.
passages.vernacular: 一切係幾咁偉大、寂靜、奇妙,大海嘅低語穿過其中,遠處昏暗嘅懸崖像睇守魔法海岸嘅嚴厲巨人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切是多麼偉大、寂靜、奇妙,大海的低語穿過其中,遠處昏暗的懸崖像看守魔法海岸的嚴厲巨人。

passages.original: “Hasn’t it been a perfectly splendid time?” sighed Jane, as they drove away.
passages.vernacular: 「呢唔係一段絕妙嘅時光嗎?」簡嘆息道,佢哋駛離時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這不是一段絕妙的時光嗎?」簡嘆息道,他們駛離時。

passages.original: “I just wish I was a rich American and could spend my summer at a hotel and wear jewels and low-necked dresses and have ice cream and chicken salad every blessed day.
passages.vernacular: 「我真希望我係個富有嘅美國人,可以喺旅館過夏天,戴珠寶,穿低領裙,天天食冰淇淋同雞肉沙拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真希望我是個富有的美國人,可以在旅館過夏天,戴珠寶,穿低領裙,天天吃冰淇淋和雞肉沙拉。

passages.original: I’m sure it would be ever so much more fun than teaching school.
passages.vernacular: 我肯定比教書有趣得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我肯定比教書有趣得多。

passages.original: Anne, your recitation was simply great, although I thought at first you were never going to begin.
passages.vernacular: 安妮,你嘅朗誦簡直太棒喇,雖然起初我以為你永遠開不咗頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮,你的朗誦簡直太棒了,雖然起初我以為你永遠開不了頭。

passages.original: I think it was better than Mrs. Evans’s.”
passages.vernacular: 我覺得比埃文斯太太嘅仲好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得比埃文斯太太的還好。」

passages.original: “Oh, no, don’t say things like that, Jane,” said Anne quickly, “because it sounds silly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不,唔好講咁樣嘅話,簡,」安妮好快地講,「因為聽起嚟好傻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不,別說這樣的話,簡,」安妮很快地說,「因為聽起來很傻。

passages.original: It couldn’t be better than Mrs. Evans’s, you know, for she is a professional, and I’m only a schoolgirl, with a little knack of reciting.
passages.vernacular: 唔可能比埃文斯太太嘅好,你知道,因為佢係專業嘅,而我只係個有啲朗誦技巧嘅女學生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不可能比埃文斯太太的好,你知道,因為她是專業的,而我只是個有一點朗誦技巧的女學生。

passages.original: I’m quite satisfied if the people just liked mine pretty well.”
passages.vernacular: 如果人哋只係相當鍾意我嘅,我就好滿意喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果人們只是相當喜歡我的,我就很滿意了。」

passages.original: “I’ve a compliment for you, Anne,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「我有一個恭維要畀你,安妮,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有一個恭維要給你,安妮,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “At least I think it must be a compliment because of the tone he said it in.
passages.vernacular: 「至少我覺得一定係恭維,從佢講話嘅語氣判斷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「至少我覺得一定是恭維,從他說話的語氣判斷。

passages.original: Part of it was anyhow.
passages.vernacular: 至少有一部分係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少有一部分是。

passages.original: There was an American sitting behind Jane and me--such a romantic-looking man, with coal-black hair and eyes.
passages.vernacular: 有一個美國人坐喺簡同我後面——一個長相好浪漫嘅男人,烏黑嘅頭髮同眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一個美國人坐在簡和我後面——一個長相很浪漫的男人,烏黑的頭髮和眼睛。

passages.original: Josie Pye says he is a distinguished artist, and that her mother’s cousin in Boston is married to a man that used to go to school with him.
passages.vernacular: 喬西·派伊講佢係個著名嘅藝術家,佢母親喺波士頓嘅表親嫁嘅男人過去同佢同學。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西·派伊說他是個著名的藝術家,她母親在波士頓的表親嫁的男人過去和他同學。

passages.original: Well, we heard him say--didn’t we, Jane?--‘Who is that girl on the platform with the splendid Titian hair?
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我哋聽到佢講——係唔係,簡?——『臺上嗰個有住壯麗提香紅髮嘅女孩係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我們聽到他說——是不是,簡?——『臺上那個有著壯麗提香紅髮的女孩是誰?

passages.original: She has a face I should like to paint.’
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉我想畫下嚟。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉我想畫下來。』

passages.original: There now, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 就係咁樣,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這樣,安妮。

passages.original: But what does Titian hair mean?”
passages.vernacular: 但提香紅髮係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但提香紅髮是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “Being interpreted it means plain red, I guess,” laughed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「翻譯過嚟,我想就係普通嘅紅色,」安妮笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「翻譯過來,我想就是普通的紅色,」安妮笑著說。

passages.original: “Titian was a very famous artist who liked to paint red-haired women.”
passages.vernacular: 「提香係個好著名嘅藝術家,鍾意畫紅髮女人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「提香是個非常著名的藝術家,喜歡畫紅髮女人。」

passages.original: “Did you see all the diamonds those ladies wore?” sighed Jane.
passages.vernacular: 「你睇到嗰啲女士戴嘅所有鑽石咗嗎?」簡嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看到那些女士戴的所有鑽石了嗎?」簡嘆道。

passages.original: “They were simply dazzling.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋簡直耀眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們簡直耀眼。

passages.original: Wouldn’t you just love to be rich, girls?”
passages.vernacular: 你哋唔係好想富有嗎,女孩哋?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們不是很想富有嗎,女孩們?」

passages.original: “We are rich,” said Anne staunchly.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋好富有,」安妮堅定地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們很富有,」安妮堅定地說。

passages.original: “Why, we have sixteen years to our credit, and we’re happy as queens, and we’ve all got imaginations, more or less.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我哋有十六年嘅歲月喺賬上,我哋像女王一樣快樂,我哋都或多或少有想像力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我們有十六年的歲月在賬上,我們像女王一樣快樂,我們都或多或少有想像力。

passages.original: Look at that sea, girls--all silver and shadow and vision of things not seen.
passages.vernacular: 睇嗰片海,女孩哋——全係銀色、陰影同未見之物嘅幻象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看那片海,女孩們——全是銀色、陰影和未見之物的幻象。

passages.original: We couldn’t enjoy its loveliness any more if we had millions of dollars and ropes of diamonds.
passages.vernacular: 即使我哋有幾百萬美元同成串嘅鑽石,都唔能夠更享受佢嘅可愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使我們有幾百萬美元和成串的鑽石,也不能更享受它的可愛。

passages.original: You wouldn’t change into any of those women if you could.
passages.vernacular: 即使你能,你都唔會變成嗰啲女人中嘅任何一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使你能,你也不會變成那些女人中的任何一個。

passages.original: Would you want to be that white-lace girl and wear a sour look all your life, as if you’d been born turning up your nose at the world?
passages.vernacular: 你想變成嗰個穿白蕾絲嘅女孩,一輩子板住臉,好像生來就對世界翹鼻子嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想變成那個穿白蕾絲的女孩,一輩子板著臉,好像生來就對世界翹鼻子嗎?

passages.original: Or the pink lady, kind and nice as she is, so stout and short that you’d really no figure at all?
passages.vernacular: 或者嗰位粉紅女士,雖然和善可親,但又胖又矮,幾乎冇身材?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者那位粉紅女士,雖然和善可親,但又胖又矮,幾乎沒有身材?

passages.original: Or even Mrs. Evans, with that sad, sad look in her eyes?
passages.vernacular: 或者甚至埃文斯太太,眼睛里帶住嗰種悲傷悲傷嘅神情?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者甚至埃文斯太太,眼睛里帶著那種悲傷悲傷的神情?

passages.original: She must have been dreadfully unhappy sometime to have such a look.
passages.vernacular: 佢一定曾經好不幸,才有嗰種神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一定曾經非常不幸,才有那種神情。

passages.original: You know you wouldn’t, Jane Andrews!”
passages.vernacular: 你知道你唔想嘅,簡·安德魯斯!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道你不想的,簡·安德魯斯!」

passages.original: “I don’t know--exactly,” said Jane unconvinced.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道——不確切,」簡不服氣地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道——不確切,」簡不服氣地說。

passages.original: “I think diamonds would comfort a person for a good deal.”
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得鑽石能安慰一個人好多事情。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得鑽石能安慰一個人很多事情。」

passages.original: “Well, I don’t want to be anyone but myself, even if I go uncomforted by diamonds all my life,” declared Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔想做任何人,只做我自己,即使我一生中冇鑽石嘅安慰,」安妮宣稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不想做任何人,只做我自己,即使我一生中沒有鑽石的安慰,」安妮宣稱。

passages.original: “I’m quite content to be Anne of Green Gables, with my string of pearl beads.
passages.vernacular: 「我完全滿足於做綠色屋頂嘅安妮,有我嘅珍珠項鍊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我完全滿足於做綠色屋頂的安妮,有我的珍珠項鍊。

passages.original: I know Matthew gave me as much love with them as ever went with Madame the Pink Lady’s jewels.”
passages.vernacular: 我知道馬修畀我佢哋時帶住嘅愛,同粉紅女士嘅珠寶上帶嘅一樣多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道馬修給我它們時帶著的愛,和粉紅女士的珠寶上帶的一樣多。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXXIV A Queen's Girl 第三十四章:女王學院的女孩

passages.original: CH THE next three weeks were busy ones at Green Gables, for Anne was getting ready to go to Queen’s, and there was much sewing to be done, and many things to be talked over and arranged.
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟嘅三個星期,綠色屋頂好忙碌,因為安妮正在準備去女王學院,有許多針線活要做,有許多事要談論同安排。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來的三個星期,綠色屋頂很忙碌,因為安妮正在準備去女王學院,有許多針線活要做,有許多事要談論和安排。

passages.original: Anne’s outfit was ample and pretty, for Matthew saw to that, and Marilla for once made no objections whatever to anything he purchased or suggested.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅行頭既充足又漂亮,因為馬修操心咗呢件事,而瑪麗拉呢回對佢買嘅或建議嘅任何嘢都冇提出反對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的行頭既充足又漂亮,因為馬修操心了這件事,而瑪麗拉這回對他買的或建議的任何東西都沒有提出反對。

passages.original: More--one evening she went up to the east gable with her arms full of a delicate pale green material.
passages.vernacular: 而且——一天晚上佢抱住滿懷嘅淡綠色輕薄料子上咗東山牆房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且——一天晚上她抱著滿懷的淡綠色輕薄料子上了東山牆房間。

passages.original: “Anne, here’s something for a nice light dress for you.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,呢個係畀你做一件漂亮輕便裙子嘅料子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,這是給你做一件漂亮輕便裙子的料子。

passages.original: I don’t suppose you really need it; you’ve plenty of pretty waists; but I thought maybe you’d like something real dressy to wear if you were asked out anywhere of an evening in town, to a party or anything like that.
passages.vernacular: 我想你並不真嘅需要;你有好多漂亮嘅上衣;但我想,如果你晚上喺城里被請去乜嘢地方,參加派對之類,或者你想要一件真正體面嘅衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你並不真的需要;你有很多漂亮的上衣;但我想,如果你晚上在城里被請去什麼地方,參加派對之類,也許你想要一件真正體面的衣服。

passages.original: I hear that Jane and Ruby and Josie have got ‘evening dresses,’ as they call them, and I don’t mean you shall be behind them.
passages.vernacular: 我聽講簡、露比同喬西有『晚禮服』,佢哋咁叫,我唔會讓你落喺佢哋後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽說簡、露比和喬西有『晚禮服』,她們這麼叫,我不會讓你落在她們後面。

passages.original: I got Mrs. Allan to help me pick it in town last week, and we’ll get Emily Gillis to make it for you.
passages.vernacular: 上星期我請艾倫太太幫我喺城里挑嘅,我哋請艾米麗·吉利斯畀你做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上星期我請艾倫太太幫我在城里挑的,我們請艾米麗·吉利斯給你做。

passages.original: Emily has got taste, and her fits aren’t to be equaled.”
passages.vernacular: 艾米麗有品味,佢做嘅剪裁無人能比。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾米麗有品味,她做的剪裁無人能比。」

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, it’s just lovely,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,太可愛喇,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,太可愛了,」安妮說。

passages.original: “Thank you so much.
passages.vernacular: 「好謝謝您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「非常謝謝您。

passages.original: I don’t believe you ought to be so kind to me--it’s making it harder every day for me to go away.”
passages.vernacular: 我覺得您唔應該該對我咁好——呢使我每天離開都更難喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得您不應該對我這麼好——這使我每天離開都更難了。」

passages.original: The green dress was made up with as many tucks and frills and shirrings as Emily’s taste permitted.
passages.vernacular: 綠裙子被做出咗艾米麗嘅品味所允許嘅盡可能多嘅褶襉、荷葉邊同抽褶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 綠裙子被做出了艾米麗的品味所允許的盡可能多的褶襉、荷葉邊和抽褶。

passages.original: Anne put it on one evening for Matthew’s and Marilla’s benefit, and recited “The Maiden’s Vow” for them in the kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 一天晚上安妮穿上佢,畀馬修同瑪麗拉睇,並喺廚房里為佢哋朗誦咗《少女嘅誓言》。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天晚上安妮穿上它,給馬修和瑪麗拉看,並在廚房里為他們朗誦了《少女的誓言》。

passages.original: As Marilla watched the bright, animated face and graceful motions her thoughts went back to the evening Anne had arrived at Green Gables, and memory recalled a vivid picture of the odd, frightened child in her preposterous yellowish-brown wincey dress, the heartbreak looking out of her tearful eyes.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉睇住嗰張明亮、生動嘅臉同優雅嘅動作,佢嘅思緒回到安妮到達綠色屋頂嘅嗰個晚上,記憶重現咗一幅鮮明嘅畫面:嗰個古怪、受驚嘅細路,穿住荒唐嘅黃褐色棉毛混紡裙,含淚嘅眼睛里流露出心碎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉看著那張明亮、生動的臉和優雅的動作,她的思緒回到安妮到達綠色屋頂的那個晚上,記憶重現了一幅鮮明的畫面:那個古怪、受驚的孩子,穿著荒唐的黃褐色棉毛混紡裙,含淚的眼睛里流露出心碎。

passages.original: Something in the memory brought tears to Marilla’s own eyes.
passages.vernacular: 記憶中嘅某樣嘢使瑪麗拉自己嘅眼里都湧上咗淚水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 記憶中的某樣東西使瑪麗拉自己的眼里也湧上了淚水。

passages.original: “I declare, my recitation has made you cry, Marilla,” said Anne gaily stooping over Marilla’s chair to drop a butterfly kiss on that lady’s cheek.
passages.vernacular: 「我敢講,我嘅朗誦讓您哭喇,瑪麗拉,」安妮快活地講,俯身喺瑪麗拉嘅椅子上,畀嗰位太太嘅臉頰留下一個蝴蝶般嘅吻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢說,我的朗誦讓您哭了,瑪麗拉,」安妮快活地說,俯身在瑪麗拉的椅子上,給那位太太的臉頰留下一個蝴蝶般的吻。

passages.original: “Now, I call that a positive triumph.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢我可稱為實實在喺嘅勝利。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這我可稱為實實在在的勝利。」

passages.original: “No, I wasn’t crying over your piece,” said Marilla, who would have scorned to be betrayed into such weakness by any poetry stuff.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我唔係為你嘅朗誦哭,」瑪麗拉講,佢絕不屑被任何詩歌之類嘅嘢引發呢種軟弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我不是為你的朗誦哭,」瑪麗拉說,她絕不屑被任何詩歌之類的東西引發這種軟弱。

passages.original: “I just couldn’t help thinking of the little girl you used to be, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我只係忍不住想起你曾經係嘅嗰個小女孩,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只是忍不住想起你曾經是的那個小女孩,安妮。

passages.original: And I was wishing you could have stayed a little girl, even with all your queer ways.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你能一直做個小女孩,即使有你嗰所有古怪嘅毛病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你能一直做個小女孩,即使有你那所有古怪的毛病。

passages.original: You’ve grown up now and you’re going away; and you look so tall and stylish and so--so--different altogether in that dress--as if you didn’t belong in Avonlea at all--and I just got lonesome thinking it all over.”
passages.vernacular: 你而家長大喇,你要走喇;你睇上去穿住嗰條裙子咁高、咁時髦、咁——咁——完全不同——好像你根本不屬於阿文利——我想住呢一切,就孤單喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你現在長大了,你要走了;你看上去穿著那條裙子那麼高、那麼時髦、那麼——那麼——完全不同——好像你根本不屬於阿文利——我想著這一切,就孤單了。」

passages.original: “Marilla!”
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉!」

passages.original: Anne sat down on Marilla’s gingham lap, took Marilla’s lined face between her hands, and looked gravely and tenderly into Marilla’s eyes.
passages.vernacular: 安妮坐喺瑪麗拉嘅格子布圍裙上,雙手捧住瑪麗拉布滿皺紋嘅臉,嚴肅而溫柔地睇住瑪麗拉嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮坐在瑪麗拉的格子布圍裙上,雙手捧著瑪麗拉布滿皺紋的臉,嚴肅而溫柔地看著瑪麗拉的眼睛。

passages.original: “I’m not a bit changed--not really.
passages.vernacular: 「我啲冇變——真嘅冇變。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一點沒變——真的沒變。

passages.original: I’m only just pruned down and branched out.
passages.vernacular: 我只係被修剪咗、分出咗枝杈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是被修剪了、分出了枝杈。

passages.original: The real me--back here--is just the same.
passages.vernacular: 真正嘅我——呢度面——完全一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真正的我——這裡面——完全一樣。

passages.original: It won’t make a bit of difference where I go or how much I change outwardly; at heart I shall always be your little Anne, who will love you and Matthew and dear Green Gables more and better every day of her life.”
passages.vernacular: 不管我去邊兒、外表點變,都唔會有任何差別;喺心裡,我永遠係您嘅小安妮,佢將一生中一天比一天更愛您、馬修同親愛嘅綠色屋頂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管我去哪兒、外表怎麼變,都不會有任何差別;在心裡,我永遠是您的小安妮,她將一生中一天比一天更愛您、馬修和親愛的綠色屋頂。」

passages.original: Anne laid her fresh young cheek against Marilla’s faded one, and reached out a hand to pat Matthew’s shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把佢鮮嫩年輕嘅臉頰貼喺瑪麗拉凋謝嘅臉頰上,伸手拍拍馬修嘅肩膀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把她鮮嫩年輕的臉頰貼在瑪麗拉凋謝的臉頰上,伸手拍拍馬修的肩膀。

passages.original: Marilla would have given much just then to have possessed Anne’s power of putting her feelings into words; but nature and habit had willed it otherwise, and she could only put her arms close about her girl and hold her tenderly to her heart, wishing that she need never let her go.
passages.vernacular: 嗰一刻瑪麗拉願意付出好多,只為擁有安妮把感情化為言語嘅能力;但天性同習慣另有所願,佢只能用雙臂緊緊摟住佢嘅女孩,溫柔地抱喺心口,希望永唔使放佢走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那一刻瑪麗拉願意付出很多,只為擁有安妮把感情化為言語的能力;但天性和習慣另有所願,她只能用雙臂緊緊摟住她的女孩,溫柔地抱在心口,希望永不必放她走。

passages.original: Matthew, with a suspicious moisture in his eyes, got up and went out-of-doors.
passages.vernacular: 馬修眼裡含住可疑嘅濕意,站起嚟走到門外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修眼裡含著可疑的濕意,站起來走到門外。

passages.original: Under the stars of the blue summer night he walked agitatedly across the yard to the gate under the poplars.
passages.vernacular: 喺藍色夏夜嘅星空下,佢激動地穿過院子,走到白楊樹下嘅大門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在藍色夏夜的星空下,他激動地穿過院子,走到白楊樹下的大門。

passages.original: “Well now, I guess she ain’t been much spoiled,” he muttered, proudly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想佢冇被點寵壞,」佢自豪地喃喃道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想她沒被怎麼寵壞,」他自豪地喃喃道。

passages.original: “I guess my putting in my oar occasional never did much harm after all.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我偶爾插手終究冇造成乜嘢害處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我偶爾插手終究沒造成什麼害處。

passages.original: She’s smart and pretty, and loving, too, which is better than all the rest.
passages.vernacular: 佢聰明,漂亮,又有愛心,呢比其他一切都好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她聰明,漂亮,又有愛心,這比其他一切都好。

passages.original: She’s been a blessing to us, and there never was a luckier mistake than what Mrs. Spencer made--if it was luck.
passages.vernacular: 佢係我哋嘅福氣,冇比斯潘塞太太犯嘅錯誤更幸運嘅錯誤喇——如果嗰個係運氣嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是我們的福氣,沒有比斯潘塞太太犯的錯誤更幸運的錯誤了——如果那是運氣的話。

passages.original: I don’t believe it was any such thing.
passages.vernacular: 我不相信嗰個係乜嘢運氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不相信那是什麼運氣。

passages.original: It was Providence, because the Almighty saw we needed her, I reckon.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係天意,因為全能嘅上帝睇出我哋需要佢,我想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是天意,因為全能的上帝看出我們需要她,我想。」

passages.original: The day finally came when Anne must go to town.
passages.vernacular: 終於到咗安妮必須進城嘅日子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於到了安妮必須進城的日子。

passages.original: She and Matthew drove in one fine September morning, after a tearful parting with Diana and an untearful practical one--on Marilla’s side at least--with Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 九月一個晴朗嘅早晨,佢同馬修駕車進城,同黛安娜含淚分別,同瑪麗拉——至少瑪麗拉嗰邊——冇眼淚、實事求係地分別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 九月一個晴朗的早晨,她和馬修駕車進城,與黛安娜含淚分別,與瑪麗拉——至少瑪麗拉那邊——沒有眼淚、實事求是地分別。

passages.original: But when Anne had gone Diana dried her tears and went to a beach picnic at White Sands with some of her Carmody cousins, where she contrived to enjoy herself tolerably well; while Marilla plunged fiercely into unnecessary work and kept at it all day long with the bitterest kind of heartache--the ache that burns and gnaws and cannot wash itself away in ready tears.
passages.vernacular: 但安妮走後,黛安娜擦乾眼淚,同佢嘅啲卡莫迪表親去咗白沙海灘野餐,喺嗰度佢設法玩得仲算不錯;而瑪麗拉猛烈地投入唔使要嘅工作,整天不停,帶住最苦澀嘅心痛——嗰種燒灼、啃噬、唔能夠喺現成嘅眼淚中沖掉嘅痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安妮走後,黛安娜擦乾眼淚,和她的一些卡莫迪表親去了白沙海灘野餐,在那裡她設法玩得還算不錯;而瑪麗拉猛烈地投入不必要的工作,整天不停,帶著最苦澀的心痛——那種燒灼、啃噬、不能在現成的眼淚中沖掉的痛。

passages.original: But that night, when Marilla went to bed, acutely and miserably conscious that the little gable room at the end of the hall was untenanted by any vivid young life and unstirred by any soft breathing, she buried her face in her pillow, and wept for her girl in a passion of sobs that appalled her when she grew calm enough to reflect how very wicked it must be to take on so about a sinful fellow creature.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰天晚上,瑪麗拉上床時,尖銳而痛苦地意識到走廊盡頭嗰間山牆小屋冇任何鮮活嘅年輕生命入住,都冇輕柔嘅呼吸聲擾動,佢把臉埋進枕頭,為佢嘅女孩哭泣,啜泣得咁激烈,當佢平靜到能反思時,佢被驚呆喇:為一個有罪嘅同類咁樣放縱自己,一定係幾咁邪惡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那天晚上,瑪麗拉上床時,尖銳而痛苦地意識到走廊盡頭那間山牆小屋沒有任何鮮活的年輕生命入住,也沒有輕柔的呼吸聲擾動,她把臉埋進枕頭,為她的女孩哭泣,啜泣得那麼激烈,當她平靜到能反思時,她被驚呆了:為一個有罪的同類這樣放縱自己,一定是多麼邪惡。

passages.original: Anne and the rest of the Avonlea scholars reached town just in time to hurry off to the Academy.
passages.vernacular: 安妮同其餘嘅阿文利學生到達城裡,正好趕得及匆忙去學院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮和其餘的阿文利學生到達城裡,正好趕得及匆忙去學院。

passages.original: That first day passed pleasantly enough in a whirl of excitement, meeting all the new students, learning to know the professors by sight and being assorted and organized into classes.
passages.vernacular: 嗰第一天喺一陣興奮嘅旋風中相當愉快地過去喇,認識所有新同學,認識教授嘅長相,被分類組織成班級。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那第一天在一陣興奮的旋風中相當愉快地過去了,認識所有新同學,認識教授的長相,被分類組織成班級。

passages.original: Anne intended taking up the Second Year work being advised to do so by Miss Stacy; Gilbert Blythe elected to do the same.
passages.vernacular: 安妮打算修第二年嘅課程,係斯泰西小姐建議嘅;吉爾伯特·布萊斯選擇都咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮打算修第二年的課程,是斯泰西小姐建議的;吉爾伯特·布萊斯選擇也這樣做。

passages.original: This meant getting a First Class teacher’s license in one year instead of two, if they were successful; but it also meant much more and harder work.
passages.vernacular: 呢意味住如果成功,一年而唔係兩年就能獲得一級教師執照;但都意味住多得多、難得多嘅功課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這意味著如果成功,一年而不是兩年就能獲得一級教師執照;但也意味著多得多、難得多的功課。

passages.original: Jane, Ruby, Josie, Charlie, and Moody Spurgeon, not being troubled with the stirrings of ambition, were content to take up the Second Class work.
passages.vernacular: 簡、露比、喬西、查理同穆迪·斯珀吉翁,因為冇被雄心嘅騷動所困擾,滿足於修二級課程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡、露比、喬西、查理和穆迪·斯珀吉翁,因為沒有被雄心的騷動所困擾,滿足於修二級課程。

passages.original: Anne was conscious of a pang of loneliness when she found herself in a room with fifty other students, not one of whom she knew, except the tall, brown-haired boy across the room; and knowing him in the fashion she did, did not help her much, as she reflected pessimistically.
passages.vernacular: 安妮發現自己喺一個有五十名其他學生嘅房間里,其中一個都不認識,除咗房間另一頭嗰個棕色頭髮嘅高個子男孩時,佢意識到一陣孤獨嘅刺痛;而佢悲觀地反思,以佢認識佢嘅嗰種方式,對佢都冇多大幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮發現自己在一個有五十名其他學生的房間里,其中一個也不認識,除了房間另一頭那個棕色頭髮的高個子男孩時,她意識到一陣孤獨的刺痛;而她悲觀地反思,以她認識他的那種方式,對她也沒多大幫助。

passages.original: Yet she was undeniably glad that they were in the same class; the old rivalry could still be carried on, and Anne would hardly have known what to do if it had been lacking.
passages.vernacular: 然而,佢無可否認地高興佢哋喺同一個班;舊日嘅競爭仲可以繼續,如果缺少佢,安妮幾乎唔知道該點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,她無可否認地高興他們在同一個班;舊日的競爭還可以繼續,如果缺少它,安妮幾乎不知道該怎麼辦。

passages.original: “I wouldn’t feel comfortable without it,” she thought.
passages.vernacular: 「冇佢我會覺得不舒服,」佢想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有它我會覺得不舒服,」她想。

passages.original: “Gilbert looks awfully determined.
passages.vernacular: 「吉爾伯特睇起嚟好堅決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉爾伯特看起來非常堅決。

passages.original: I suppose he’s making up his mind, here and now, to win the medal.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢此時此地就下定決心要贏得獎牌喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他此時此地就下定決心要贏得獎牌了。

passages.original: What a splendid chin he has!
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅下巴幾咁棒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的下巴多麼棒!

passages.original: I never noticed it before.
passages.vernacular: 我以前從冇注意到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以前從沒注意到。

passages.original: I do wish Jane and Ruby had gone in for First Class, too.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望簡同露比都報咗一級班。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望簡和露比也報了一級班。

passages.original: I suppose I won’t feel so much like a cat in a strange garret when I get acquainted, though.
passages.vernacular: 不過我想等我熟悉喇,我就唔會咁覺得像一隻貓喺陌生嘅閣樓里喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我想等我熟悉了,我就不會那麼覺得像一隻貓在陌生的閣樓里了。

passages.original: I wonder which of the girls here are going to be my friends.
passages.vernacular: 我想知道呢度嘅女孩邊個會成為我嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想知道這裡的女孩誰會成為我的朋友。

passages.original: It’s really an interesting speculation.
passages.vernacular: 呢真係個有趣嘅推測。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這真是個有趣的推測。

passages.original: Of course I promised Diana that no Queen’s girl, no matter how much I liked her, should ever be as dear to me as she is; but I’ve lots of second-best affections to bestow.
passages.vernacular: 當然,我向黛安娜保證過,冇邊個女王學院嘅女孩,不管我多鍾意佢,會像佢嗰樣對我親愛;但我有好多次好嘅感情可以畀予。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,我向黛安娜保證過,沒有哪個女王學院的女孩,不管我多喜歡她,會像她那樣對我親愛;但我有很多次好的感情可以給予。

passages.original: I like the look of that girl with the brown eyes and the crimson waist.
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意嗰個棕色眼睛、穿深紅上衣嘅女孩嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡那個棕色眼睛、穿深紅上衣的女孩的樣子。

passages.original: She looks vivid and red-rosy; there’s that pale, fair one gazing out of the window.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇上去鮮豔、紅玫瑰色;仲有嗰個望住窗外嘅蒼白、白皙嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看上去鮮豔、紅玫瑰色;還有那個望著窗外的蒼白、白皙的女孩。

passages.original: She has lovely hair, and looks as if she knew a thing or two about dreams.
passages.vernacular: 佢有可愛嘅頭髮,睇上去像係對夢知道一二。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有可愛的頭髮,看上去像是對夢知道一二。

passages.original: I’d like to know them both--know them well--well enough to walk with my arm about their waists, and call them nicknames.
passages.vernacular: 我想認識佢哋倆——好好認識——認識到能摟住佢哋嘅腰一起散步,叫佢哋嘅綽號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想認識她們倆——好好認識——認識到能摟著她們的腰一起散步,叫她們的綽號。

passages.original: But just now I don’t know them and they don’t know me, and probably don’t want to know me particularly.
passages.vernacular: 但而家我不認識佢哋,佢哋都不認識我,大概特別唔想認識我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在我不認識她們,她們也不認識我,大概特別不想認識我。

passages.original: Oh, it’s lonesome!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,太孤單喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,太孤單了!」

passages.original: It was lonesomer still when Anne found herself alone in her hall bedroom that night at twilight.
passages.vernacular: 當天傍晚暮色中,安妮獨自在佢嘅大廳臥室里時,更孤單喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當天傍晚暮色中,安妮獨自在她的大廳臥室里時,更孤單了。

passages.original: She was not to board with the other girls, who all had relatives in town to take pity on them.
passages.vernacular: 佢不同別嘅女孩一起寄宿,佢哋都有城里嘅親戚可憐佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不和別的女孩一起寄宿,她們都有城里的親戚可憐她們。

passages.original: Miss Josephine Barry would have liked to board her, but Beechwood was so far from the Academy that it was out of the question; so Miss Barry hunted up a boarding-house, assuring Matthew and Marilla that it was the very place for Anne.
passages.vernacular: 約瑟芬·巴里小姐本想讓佢住喺佢嗰兒,但山毛櫸莊離學院太遠,唔可能;所以巴里小姐找咗一個寄宿公寓,向馬修同瑪麗拉保證嗰正是適合安妮嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約瑟芬·巴里小姐本想讓她住在她那兒,但山毛櫸莊離學院太遠,不可能;所以巴里小姐找了一個寄宿公寓,向馬修和瑪麗拉保證那正是適合安妮的地方。

passages.original: “The lady who keeps it is a reduced gentlewoman,” explained Miss Barry.
passages.vernacular: 「經營佢嘅女士係個家道中落嘅貴婦,」巴里小姐解釋道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「經營它的女士是個家道中落的貴婦,」巴里小姐解釋道。

passages.original: “Her husband was a British officer, and she is very careful what sort of boarders she takes.
passages.vernacular: 「佢丈夫係英國軍官,佢對收乜嘢樣嘅寄宿者好小心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她丈夫是英國軍官,她對收什麼樣的寄宿者非常小心。

passages.original: Anne will not meet with any objectionable persons under her roof.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺佢屋簷下唔會遇到任何令人討厭嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在她屋簷下不會遇到任何令人討厭的人。

passages.original: The table is good, and the house is near the Academy, in a quiet neighborhood.”
passages.vernacular: 飯菜好好,房子離學院近,喺一個安靜嘅街區。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 飯菜很好,房子離學院近,在一個安靜的街區。」

passages.original: All this might be quite true, and indeed, proved to be so, but it did not materially help Anne in the first agony of homesickness that seized upon her.
passages.vernacular: 所有呢啲可能完全係真嘅,事實上都證明如此,但喺襲向佢嘅第一陣思鄉嘅痛苦中,呢對安妮冇實質性嘅幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有這些可能完全是真的,事實上也證明如此,但在襲向她的第一陣思鄉的痛苦中,這對安妮沒有實質性的幫助。

passages.original: She looked dismally about her narrow little room, with its dull-papered, pictureless walls, its small iron bedstead and empty bookcase; and a horrible choke came into her throat as she thought of her own white room at Green Gables, where she would have the pleasant consciousness of a great green still outdoors, of sweet peas growing in the garden, and moonlight falling on the orchard, of the brook below the slope and the spruce boughs tossing in the night wind beyond it, of a vast starry sky, and the light from Diana’s window shining out through the gap in the trees.
passages.vernacular: 佢沮喪地環顧佢狹小嘅房間,佢嘅牆紙暗淡、冇畫,有小小嘅鐵床架同空書櫃;佢想到自己喺綠色屋頂嘅白色房間,喺嗰度佢會有對外面廣闊寧靜嘅綠色嘅愉快意識,花園里生長嘅香豌豆,月光灑喺果園上,斜坡下嘅小溪同溪嗰邊夜風中搖擺嘅杉樹枝,廣闊嘅星空,以及穿過樹木缺口閃耀出嚟嘅黛安娜窗子嘅燈光,一陣可怕嘅哽咽湧上佢嘅喉嚨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她沮喪地環顧她狹小的房間,它的牆紙暗淡、沒有畫,有小小的鐵床架和空書櫃;她想到自己在綠色屋頂的白色房間,在那裡她會有對外面廣闊寧靜的綠色的愉快意識,花園里生長的香豌豆,月光灑在果園上,斜坡下的小溪和溪那邊夜風中搖擺的杉樹枝,廣闊的星空,以及穿過樹木缺口閃耀出來的黛安娜窗子的燈光,一陣可怕的哽咽湧上她的喉嚨。

passages.original: Here there was nothing of this; Anne knew that outside of her window was a hard street, with a network of telephone wires shutting out the sky, the tramp of alien feet, and a thousand lights gleaming on stranger faces.
passages.vernacular: 呢度冇呢啲;安妮知道佢窗外係一條堅硬嘅街道,電話線嘅網絡遮住咗天空,陌生腳步嘅踏步聲,千盞燈光閃爍喺陌生人嘅臉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡沒有這些;安妮知道她窗外是一條堅硬的街道,電話線的網絡遮住了天空,陌生腳步的踏步聲,千盞燈光閃爍在陌生人的臉上。

passages.original: She knew that she was going to cry, and fought against it.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道自己要哭喇,於是抵抗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她知道自己要哭了,於是抵抗。

passages.original: “I won’t cry.
passages.vernacular: 「我不哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不哭。

passages.original: It’s silly--and weak--there’s the third tear splashing down by my nose.
passages.vernacular: 太傻喇——太軟弱喇——第三滴眼淚啪嗒落喺我鼻子旁邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太傻了——太軟弱了——第三滴眼淚啪嗒落在我鼻子旁邊。

passages.original: There are more coming!
passages.vernacular: 仲有更多要嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有更多要來了!

passages.original: I must think of something funny to stop them.
passages.vernacular: 我必須想點有趣嘅事嚟阻止佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須想點有趣的事來阻止它們。

passages.original: But there’s nothing funny except what is connected with Avonlea, and that only makes things worse--four--five--I’m going home next Friday, but that seems a hundred years away.
passages.vernacular: 但係除咗同阿文利有關嘅,冇乜嘢有趣嘅,而嗰隻會讓事情更糟——四——五——我下星期五要回家,但嗰似乎仲有一百年——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是除了與阿文利有關的,沒有什麼有趣的,而那隻會讓事情更糟——四——五——我下星期五要回家,但那似乎還有一百年——

passages.original: Oh, Matthew is nearly home by now--and Marilla is at the gate, looking down the lane for him--six--seven--eight--oh, there’s no use in counting them!
passages.vernacular: 哦,馬修而家差不多到家喇——瑪麗拉喺大門口,望住小巷等佢——六——七——八——哦,數佢哋冇用!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,馬修現在差不多到家了——瑪麗拉在大門口,望著小巷等他——六——七——八——哦,數它們沒用!

passages.original: They’re coming in a flood presently.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋好快就要像洪水一樣嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們很快就要像洪水一樣來了。

passages.original: I can’t cheer up--I don’t want to cheer up.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠高興起嚟——我唔想高興起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能高興起來——我不想高興起來。

passages.original: It’s nicer to be miserable!”
passages.vernacular: 痛苦更好!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 痛苦更好!」

passages.original: The flood of tears would have come, no doubt, had not Josie Pye appeared at that moment.
passages.vernacular: 淚水嘅洪流無疑就要嚟喇,如果喬西·派伊冇喺嗰一刻出現嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 淚水的洪流無疑就要來了,如果喬西·派伊沒有在那一刻出現的話。

passages.original: In the joy of seeing a familiar face Anne forgot that there had never been much love lost between her and Josie.
passages.vernacular: 睇到一張熟悉嘅臉嘅喜悅中,安妮忘咗佢同喬西之間從來冇多少情誼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到一張熟悉的臉的喜悅中,安妮忘了她和喬西之間從來沒多少情誼。

passages.original: As a part of Avonlea life even a Pye was welcome.
passages.vernacular: 作為阿文利生活嘅一部分,連一個派伊都受歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 作為阿文利生活的一部分,連一個派伊也受歡迎。

passages.original: “I’m so glad you came up,” Anne said sincerely.
passages.vernacular: 「我好高興你嚟喇,」安妮真誠地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很高興你來了,」安妮真誠地說。

passages.original: “You’ve been crying,” remarked Josie, with aggravating pity.
passages.vernacular: 「你哭喇,」喬西講,帶住惱人嘅憐憫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你哭了,」喬西說,帶著惱人的憐憫。

passages.original: “I suppose you’re homesick--some people have so little self-control in that respect.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你係思鄉喇——有些人喺呢方面自制力咁差。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你是思鄉了——有些人在這方面自制力那麼差。

passages.original: I’ve no intention of being homesick, I can tell you.
passages.vernacular: 我可以告訴你,我根本不打算思鄉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以告訴你,我根本不打算思鄉。

passages.original: Town’s too jolly after that poky old Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰個破舊嘅阿文利之後,城里太好玩喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那個破舊的阿文利之後,城里太好玩了。

passages.original: I wonder how I ever existed there so long.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道我點喺嗰度待咗咁久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道我怎麼在那裡待了那麼久。

passages.original: You shouldn’t cry, Anne; it isn’t becoming, for your nose and eyes get red, and then you seem all red.
passages.vernacular: 你不該哭,安妮;嗰不好睇,因為你嘅鼻子同眼睛會變紅,然後你整個人睇上去都係紅嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不該哭,安妮;那不好看,因為你的鼻子和眼睛會變紅,然後你整個人看上去都是紅的。

passages.original: I’d a perfectly scrumptious time in the Academy today.
passages.vernacular: 今日我喺學院過得特別棒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天我在學院過得特別棒。

passages.original: Our French professor is simply a duck.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅法語教授簡直係個寶貝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的法語教授簡直是個寶貝。

passages.original: His moustache would give you kerwollowps of the heart.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅鬍子會讓你心撲通撲通。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的鬍子會讓你心撲通撲通。

passages.original: Have you anything eatable around, Anne?
passages.vernacular: 你呢兒有乜嘢食嘅嘢嗎,安妮?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這兒有什麼吃的東西嗎,安妮?

passages.original: I’m literally starving.
passages.vernacular: 我簡直餓死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我簡直餓死了。

passages.original: Ah, I guessed likely Marilla ‘d load you up with cake.
passages.vernacular: 啊,我猜瑪麗拉會畀你塞滿蛋糕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我猜瑪麗拉會給你塞滿蛋糕。

passages.original: That’s why I called round.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係我順道嚟嘅原因。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是我順道來的原因。

passages.original: Otherwise I’d have gone to the park to hear the band play with Frank Stockley.
passages.vernacular: 不然我就同弗蘭克·斯托克利去公園聽樂隊演奏喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不然我就和弗蘭克·斯托克利去公園聽樂隊演奏了。

passages.original: He boards same place as I do, and he’s a sport.
passages.vernacular: 佢同我寄宿喺同一個地方,佢係個好棒嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他和我寄宿在同一個地方,他是個很棒的人。

passages.original: He noticed you in class today, and asked me who the red-headed girl was.
passages.vernacular: 佢今日喺班上注意到咗你,問我嗰個紅頭髮嘅女孩係邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他今天在班上注意到了你,問我那個紅頭髮的女孩是誰。

passages.original: I told him you were an orphan that the Cuthberts had adopted, and nobody knew very much about what you’d been before that.”
passages.vernacular: 我告訴佢你係卡思伯特家領養嘅孤兒,冇人知道你以前係乜嘢人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴他你是卡思伯特家領養的孤兒,沒人知道你以前是什麼人。」

passages.original: Anne was wondering if, after all, solitude and tears were not more satisfactory than Josie Pye’s companionship when Jane and Ruby appeared, each with an inch of Queen’s color ribbon--purple and scarlet--pinned proudly to her coat.
passages.vernacular: 安妮正在納悶,終究獨處同眼淚係唔係比喬西·派伊嘅陪伴更令人滿意,呢陣簡同露比出現喇,每人把一寸女王學院嘅顏色絲帶——紫色同猩紅——自豪地別喺外套上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮正在納悶,終究獨處和眼淚是不是比喬西·派伊的陪伴更令人滿意,這時簡和露比出現了,每人把一寸女王學院的顏色絲帶——紫色和猩紅——自豪地別在外套上。

passages.original: As Josie was not “speaking” to Jane just then she had to subside into comparative harmlessness.
passages.vernacular: 由於喬西嗰時不跟簡「講話」,佢唔得不沉默下嚟,相對無害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 由於喬西那時不跟簡「說話」,她不得不沉默下來,相對無害。

passages.original: “Well,” said Jane with a sigh, “I feel as if I’d lived many moons since the morning.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」簡嘆咗口氣講,「我覺得自從早晨以來好像過咗好多個月亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」簡嘆了口氣說,「我覺得自從早晨以來好像過了好多個月亮。

passages.original: I ought to be home studying my Virgil--that horrid old professor gave us twenty lines to start in on tomorrow.
passages.vernacular: 我應該喺家學我嘅維吉爾——嗰個討厭嘅老教授畀我哋二十行,聽日開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我應該在家學我的維吉爾——那個討厭的老教授給我們二十行,明天開始。

passages.original: But I simply couldn’t settle down to study tonight.
passages.vernacular: 但我今晚簡直冇法安下心嚟學習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我今晚簡直沒法安下心來學習。

passages.original: Anne, methinks I see the traces of tears.
passages.vernacular: 安妮,我覺得我睇到咗眼淚嘅痕跡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮,我覺得我看到了眼淚的痕跡。

passages.original: If you’ve been crying do own up.
passages.vernacular: 如果你哭過就承認吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你哭過就承認吧。

passages.original: It will restore my self-respect, for I was shedding tears freely before Ruby came along.
passages.vernacular: 呢會恢復我嘅自尊,因為露比嚟之前我都喺大流眼淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這會恢復我的自尊,因為露比來之前我也在大流眼淚。

passages.original: I don’t mind being a goose so much if somebody else is goosey, too.
passages.vernacular: 如果別人都傻乎乎嘅,我就不咁介意做個傻瓜喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果別人也傻乎乎的,我就不那麼介意做個傻瓜了。

passages.original: Cake?
passages.vernacular: 蛋糕?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蛋糕?

passages.original: You’ll give me a teeny piece, won’t you?
passages.vernacular: 你畀我一小塊,好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你給我一小塊,好嗎?

passages.original: Thank you.
passages.vernacular: 謝謝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝謝。

passages.original: It has the real Avonlea flavor.”
passages.vernacular: 佢有真正嘅阿文利嘅味道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它有真正的阿文利的味道。」

passages.original: Ruby, perceiving the Queen’s calendar lying on the table, wanted to know if Anne meant to try for the gold medal.
passages.vernacular: 露比睇到桌上嘅女王學院日曆,想知道安妮係咪打算爭取金獎牌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比看到桌上的女王學院日曆,想知道安妮是否打算爭取金獎牌。

passages.original: Anne blushed and admitted she was thinking of it.
passages.vernacular: 安妮臉紅喇,承認佢正在考慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮臉紅了,承認她正在考慮。

passages.original: “Oh, that reminds me,” said Josie, “Queen’s is to get one of the Avery scholarships after all.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,呢讓我想起嚟喇,」喬西講,「女王學院終究要得到一個艾弗里獎學金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,這讓我想起來了,」喬西說,「女王學院終究要得到一個艾弗里獎學金。

passages.original: The word came today.
passages.vernacular: 消息今日到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 消息今天到了。

passages.original: Frank Stockley told me--his uncle is one of the board of governors, you know.
passages.vernacular: 弗蘭克·斯托克利告訴我嘅——佢叔叔係校董會成員之一,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗蘭克·斯托克利告訴我的——他叔叔是校董會成員之一,你知道。

passages.original: It will be announced in the Academy tomorrow.”
passages.vernacular: 聽日將喺學院宣布。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天將在學院宣布。」

passages.original: An Avery scholarship!
passages.vernacular: 艾弗里獎學金!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾弗里獎學金!

passages.original: Anne felt her heart beat more quickly, and the horizons of her ambition shifted and broadened as if by magic.
passages.vernacular: 安妮感到佢嘅心跳得更快喇,佢雄心嘅地平線像變魔術一樣移動、拓寬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮感到她的心跳得更快了,她雄心的地平線像變魔術一樣移動、拓寬。

passages.original: Before Josie had told the news Anne’s highest pinnacle of aspiration had been a teacher’s provincial license, First Class, at the end of the year, and perhaps the medal!
passages.vernacular: 喺喬西講呢個消息之前,安妮渴望嘅最高峰,係年底嘅一級教師省執照,或者再加獎牌!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在喬西說這個消息之前,安妮渴望的最高峰,是年底的一級教師省執照,也許再加獎牌!

passages.original: But now in one moment Anne saw herself winning the Avery scholarship, taking an Arts course at Redmond College, and graduating in a gown and mortar board, before the echo of Josie’s words had died away.
passages.vernacular: 但而家,喺喬西嘅話嘅回聲消失之前,安妮喺一瞬間睇見自己贏得艾弗里獎學金,喺雷德蒙學院修文科課程,穿住長袍戴住方帽畢業。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在,在喬西的話的回聲消失之前,安妮在一瞬間看見自己贏得艾弗里獎學金,在雷德蒙學院修文科課程,穿著長袍戴著方帽畢業。

passages.original: For the Avery scholarship was in English, and Anne felt that here her foot was on native heath.
passages.vernacular: 因為艾弗里獎學金係英語嘅,安妮覺得呢度佢嘅腳踩喺熟悉嘅地盤上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為艾弗里獎學金是英語的,安妮覺得這裡她的腳踩在熟悉的地盤上。

passages.original: A wealthy manufacturer of New Brunswick had died and left part of his fortune to endow a large number of scholarships to be distributed among the various high schools and academies of the Maritime Provinces, according to their respective standings.
passages.vernacular: 新不倫瑞克嘅一位富有製造商去世喇,留下部分財產,設立大量獎學金,按照海洋省份各中學同學院各自嘅排名分配。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 新不倫瑞克的一位富有製造商去世了,留下部分財產,設立大量獎學金,按照海洋省份各中學和學院各自的排名分配。

passages.original: There had been much doubt whether one would be allotted to Queen’s, but the matter was settled at last, and at the end of the year the graduate who made the highest mark in English and English Literature would win the scholarship--two hundred and fifty dollars a year for four years at Redmond College.
passages.vernacular: 女王學院係咪會分到一個,一直存在好大疑問,但呢個問題最終解決喇,年底時,英語同英國文學得分最高嘅畢業生將贏得獎學金——喺雷德蒙學院四年,每年兩百五十元。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女王學院是否會分到一個,一直存在很大疑問,但這個問題最終解決了,年底時,英語和英國文學得分最高的畢業生將贏得獎學金——在雷德蒙學院四年,每年兩百五十元。

passages.original: No wonder that Anne went to bed that night with tingling cheeks!
passages.vernacular: 難怪嗰天晚上安妮上床時臉頰發燙!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難怪那天晚上安妮上床時臉頰發燙!

passages.original: “I’ll win that scholarship if hard work can do it,” she resolved.
passages.vernacular: 「如果努力學習能辦到,我就要贏得嗰個獎學金,」佢決心道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果努力學習能辦到,我就要贏得那個獎學金,」她決心道。

passages.original: “Wouldn’t Matthew be proud if I got to be a B.A.?
passages.vernacular: 「如果我成為文學學士,馬修唔係會好自豪嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我成為文學學士,馬修不是會很自豪嗎?

passages.original: Oh, it’s delightful to have ambitions.
passages.vernacular: 哦,有雄心真快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,有雄心真快樂。

passages.original: I’m so glad I have such a lot.
passages.vernacular: 我太高興我有咁多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興我有那麼多。

passages.original: And there never seems to be any end to them--that’s the best of it.
passages.vernacular: 而且佢哋似乎永遠冇盡頭——呢個係最棒嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且它們似乎永遠沒有盡頭——這是最棒的地方。

passages.original: Just as soon as you attain to one ambition you see another one glittering higher up still.
passages.vernacular: 你剛達成一個雄心,就睇到另一個喺更高嘅地方閃閃發光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你剛達成一個雄心,就看到另一個在更高的地方閃閃發光。

passages.original: It does make life so interesting.”
passages.vernacular: 呢確實使生活變得咁有趣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這確實使生活變得那麼有趣。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXXV The Winter at Queen's 第三十五章:女王學院的冬天

passages.original: CH ANNE’S homesickness wore off, greatly helped in the wearing by her weekend visits home.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嘅思鄉病逐漸消退,好大程度上得益於佢週末回家探望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮的思鄉病逐漸消退,很大程度上得益於她週末回家探望。

passages.original: As long as the open weather lasted the Avonlea students went out to Carmody on the new branch railway every Friday night.
passages.vernacular: 只要天氣晴朗,阿文利嘅學生哋每個星期五晚上都乘新支線鐵路去卡莫迪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要天氣晴朗,阿文利的學生們每個星期五晚上都乘新支線鐵路去卡莫迪。

passages.original: Diana and several other Avonlea young folks were generally on hand to meet them and they all walked over to Avonlea in a merry party.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜同其他幾個阿文利嘅年輕人通常喺嗰度迎接佢哋,大家組成一支歡快嘅隊伍步行走回阿文利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜和其他幾個阿文利的年輕人通常在那裡迎接他們,大家組成一支歡快的隊伍步行走回阿文利。

passages.original: Anne thought those Friday evening gypsyings over the autumnal hills in the crisp golden air, with the homelights of Avonlea twinkling beyond, were the best and dearest hours in the whole week.
passages.vernacular: 安妮認為,星期五傍晚喺清脆金黃嘅空氣中漫步越過秋日山丘、遠處阿文利家家戶戶燈火閃爍嘅呢啲吉普賽式漫遊,係整個星期里最美好最親愛嘅時光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮認為,星期五傍晚在清脆金黃的空氣中漫步越過秋日山丘、遠處阿文利家家戶戶燈火閃爍的這些吉普賽式漫遊,是整個星期里最美好最親愛的時光。

passages.original: Gilbert Blythe nearly always walked with Ruby Gillis and carried her satchel for her.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯幾乎總是同露比·吉利斯同行,並替佢提書包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特·布萊斯幾乎總是與露比·吉利斯同行,並替她提書包。

passages.original: Ruby was a very handsome young lady, now thinking herself quite as grown up as she really was; she wore her skirts as long as her mother would let her and did her hair up in town, though she had to take it down when she went home.
passages.vernacular: 露比係一位好漂亮嘅年輕小姐,而家自以為已經完全長大喇;佢嘅裙子穿到母親允許嘅最長度,喺城里把頭髮盤起嚟,儘管回家時唔得不放下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比是一位非常漂亮的年輕小姐,現在自以為已經完全長大了;她的裙子穿到母親允許的最長度,在城里把頭髮盤起來,儘管回家時不得不放下。

passages.original: She had large, bright-blue eyes, a brilliant complexion, and a plump showy figure.
passages.vernacular: 佢有一雙明亮嘅大藍眼睛,光彩照人嘅膚色,豐滿惹眼嘅身材。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有一雙明亮的大藍眼睛,光彩照人的膚色,豐滿惹眼的身材。

passages.original: She laughed a great deal, was cheerful and good-tempered, and enjoyed the pleasant things of life frankly.
passages.vernacular: 佢愛笑,快活又隨同,坦率地享受生活中愉快嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她愛笑,快活又隨和,坦率地享受生活中愉快的事。

passages.original: “But I shouldn’t think she was the sort of girl Gilbert would like,” whispered Jane to Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「但我不覺得佢係吉爾伯特會鍾意嘅嗰種女孩,」簡低聲對安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我不覺得她是吉爾伯特會喜歡的那種女孩,」簡低聲對安妮說。

passages.original: Anne did not think so either, but she would not have said so for the Avery scholarship.
passages.vernacular: 安妮都不咁想,但佢講乜嘢都唔會為了艾弗里獎學金而講出口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮也不這麼想,但她說什麼也不會為了艾弗里獎學金而說出口。

passages.original: She could not help thinking, too, that it would be very pleasant to have such a friend as Gilbert to jest and chatter with and exchange ideas about books and studies and ambitions.
passages.vernacular: 佢都忍不住想,有吉爾伯特咁樣嘅朋友,一起講笑聊天、交流關於書本、學業同雄心嘅想法,一定好愉快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也忍不住想,有吉爾伯特這樣的朋友,一起說笑聊天、交流關於書本、學業和雄心的想法,一定很愉快。

passages.original: Gilbert had ambitions, she knew, and Ruby Gillis did not seem the sort of person with whom such could be profitably discussed.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道吉爾伯特有雄心,而露比·吉利斯似乎唔係能有益地討論呢啲嘅嗰種人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她知道吉爾伯特有雄心,而露比·吉利斯似乎不是能有益地討論這些的那種人。

passages.original: There was no silly sentiment in Anne’s ideas concerning Gilbert.
passages.vernacular: 安妮對吉爾伯特嘅睇法裡,冇愚蠢嘅感傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮對吉爾伯特的看法裡,沒有愚蠢的感傷。

passages.original: Boys were to her, when she thought about them at all, merely possible good comrades.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢偶爾想到男孩時,佢哋對佢只係可能嘅好夥伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她偶爾想到男孩時,他們對她只是可能的好夥伴。

passages.original: If she and Gilbert had been friends she would not have cared how many other friends he had nor with whom he walked.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢同吉爾伯特係朋友,佢唔會在乎佢有多少別嘅朋友,都不在乎佢同邊個同行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她和吉爾伯特是朋友,她不會在乎他有多少別的朋友,也不在乎他和誰同行。

passages.original: She had a genius for friendship; girl friends she had in plenty; but she had a vague consciousness that masculine friendship might also be a good thing to round out one’s conceptions of companionship and furnish broader standpoints of judgment and comparison.
passages.vernacular: 佢有交友嘅天賦;女性朋友佢有好多;但佢隱約意識到,男性嘅友誼可能都係件好事,可以完善一個人對友情嘅概念,提供更廣闊嘅判斷同比較嘅立足點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有交友的天賦;女性朋友她有很多;但她隱約意識到,男性的友誼可能也是件好事,可以完善一個人對友情的概念,提供更廣闊的判斷和比較的立足點。

passages.original: Not that Anne could have put her feelings on the matter into just such clear definition.
passages.vernacular: 並唔係講安妮能把自己對此嘅感受表述得咁清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並不是說安妮能把自己對此的感受表述得這麼清楚。

passages.original: But she thought that if Gilbert had ever walked home with her from the train, over the crisp fields and along the ferny byways, they might have had many and merry and interesting conversations about the new world that was opening around them and their hopes and ambitions therein.
passages.vernacular: 但佢想,如果吉爾伯特曾經從火車站同佢一同走回家,越過清脆嘅田野,沿住長滿蕨類嘅小徑,佢哋或者會有許多愉快有趣嘅談話,談圍繞佢哋展開嘅新世界,以及佢哋喺其中嘅希望同雄心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她想,如果吉爾伯特曾經從火車站與她一同走回家,越過清脆的田野,沿著長滿蕨類的小徑,他們也許會有許多愉快有趣的談話,談圍繞他們展開的新世界,以及他們在其中的希望和雄心。

passages.original: Gilbert was a clever young fellow, with his own thoughts about things and a determination to get the best out of life and put the best into it.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特係個聰明嘅年輕人,對事物有自己嘅想法,決心從生活中得到最好嘅,並把最好嘅投入其中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特是個聰明的年輕人,對事物有自己的想法,決心從生活中得到最好的,並把最好的投入其中。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis told Jane Andrews that she didn’t understand half the things Gilbert Blythe said; he talked just like Anne Shirley did when she had a thoughtful fit on and for her part she didn’t think it any fun to be bothering about books and that sort of thing when you didn’t have to.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯對簡·安德魯斯講,佢聽不懂吉爾伯特·布萊斯講嘅一半嘅話;佢講起話嚟跟安妮·雪莉有深思情緒時一模一樣,就佢而言,唔使要嘅時候為書本同嗰類事情煩惱,啲都不好玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯對簡·安德魯斯說,她聽不懂吉爾伯特·布萊斯說的一半的話;他說起話來跟安妮·雪莉有深思情緒時一模一樣,就她而言,不必要的時候為書本和那類事情煩惱,一點都不好玩。

passages.original: Frank Stockley had lots more dash and go, but then he wasn’t half as good-looking as Gilbert and she really couldn’t decide which she liked best!
passages.vernacular: 弗蘭克·斯托克利有更多嘅衝勁同活力,不過佢冇吉爾伯特一半好睇,佢真嘅無法決定更鍾意邊個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 弗蘭克·斯托克利有更多的衝勁和活力,不過他沒有吉爾伯特一半好看,她真的無法決定更喜歡哪個!

passages.original: In the Academy Anne gradually drew a little circle of friends about her, thoughtful, imaginative, ambitious students like herself.
passages.vernacular: 喺學院里,安妮逐漸喺身邊聚集起一小圈朋友,深思、富有想像力、有雄心嘅學生,同佢自己一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在學院里,安妮逐漸在身邊聚集起一小圈朋友,深思、富有想像力、有雄心的學生,和她自己一樣。

passages.original: With the “rose-red” girl, Stella Maynard, and the “dream girl,” Priscilla Grant, she soon became intimate, finding the latter pale spiritual-looking maiden to be full to the brim of mischief and pranks and fun, while the vivid, black-eyed Stella had a heartful of wistful dreams and fancies, as aerial and rainbow-like as Anne’s own.
passages.vernacular: 佢好快同「玫瑰紅」嘅女孩斯特拉·梅納德同「夢想女孩」普麗西拉·格蘭特成咗知己,發現後者嗰個蒼白、有靈性嘅少女充滿咗淘氣、惡作劇同樂趣,而鮮豔、黑眼睛嘅斯特拉心中充滿咗惆悵嘅夢想同幻想,像安妮自己嘅一樣空靈、如彩虹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她很快和「玫瑰紅」的女孩斯特拉·梅納德和「夢想女孩」普麗西拉·格蘭特成了知己,發現後者那個蒼白、有靈性的少女充滿了淘氣、惡作劇和樂趣,而鮮豔、黑眼睛的斯特拉心中充滿了惆悵的夢想和幻想,像安妮自己的一樣空靈、如彩虹。

passages.original: After the Christmas holidays the Avonlea students gave up going home on Fridays and settled down to hard work.
passages.vernacular: 聖誕假期之後,阿文利嘅學生哋唔再星期五回家,安下心嚟努力學習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖誕假期之後,阿文利的學生們不再星期五回家,安下心來努力學習。

passages.original: By this time all the Queen’s scholars had gravitated into their own places in the ranks and the various classes had assumed distinct and settled shadings of individuality.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣所有女王學院嘅學生都已各歸其位,各班都呈現出鮮明而穩定嘅個性特徵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時所有女王學院的學生都已各歸其位,各班都呈現出鮮明而穩定的個性特徵。

passages.original: Certain facts had become generally accepted.
passages.vernacular: 某些事實已被普遍接受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 某些事實已被普遍接受。

passages.original: It was admitted that the medal contestants had practically narrowed down to three--Gilbert Blythe, Anne Shirley, and Lewis Wilson; the Avery scholarship was more doubtful, any one of a certain six being a possible winner.
passages.vernacular: 大家公認,獎牌嘅競爭者實際上縮小到三個人——吉爾伯特·布萊斯、安妮·雪莉同劉易斯·威爾遜;艾弗里獎學金更不確定,某六個人中嘅任何一個都可能獲勝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家公認,獎牌的競爭者實際上縮小到三個人——吉爾伯特·布萊斯、安妮·雪莉和劉易斯·威爾遜;艾弗里獎學金更不確定,某六個人中的任何一個都可能獲勝。

passages.original: The bronze medal for mathematics was considered as good as won by a fat, funny little up-country boy with a bumpy forehead and a patched coat.
passages.vernacular: 數學銅牌被認為幾乎已被一個胖胖嘅、滑稽嘅、前額凸起、穿打補丁外套嘅鄉下小男孩收入囊中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 數學銅牌被認為幾乎已被一個胖胖的、滑稽的、前額凸起、穿打補丁外套的鄉下小男孩收入囊中。

passages.original: Ruby Gillis was the handsomest girl of the year at the Academy; in the Second Year classes Stella Maynard carried off the palm for beauty, with small but critical minority in favor of Anne Shirley.
passages.vernacular: 露比·吉利斯係學院嗰一年最漂亮嘅女孩;喺二年級班裡,斯特拉·梅納德以美貌奪得桂冠,同時安妮·雪莉都有少數但挑剔嘅支持者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露比·吉利斯是學院那一年最漂亮的女孩;在二年級班裡,斯特拉·梅納德以美貌奪得桂冠,同時安妮·雪莉也有少數但挑剔的支持者。

passages.original: Ethel Marr was admitted by all competent judges to have the most stylish modes of hair-dressing, and Jane Andrews--plain, plodding, conscientious Jane--carried off the honors in the domestic science course.
passages.vernacular: 所有有資格嘅評判都承認埃塞爾·馬爾有最時髦嘅髮型,而簡·安德魯斯——平凡、踏實、認真嘅簡——喺家政科學課程中獲得榮譽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有有資格的評判都承認埃塞爾·馬爾有最時髦的髮型,而簡·安德魯斯——平凡、踏實、認真的簡——在家政科學課程中獲得榮譽。

passages.original: Even Josie Pye attained a certain preeminence as the sharpest-tongued young lady in attendance at Queen’s.
passages.vernacular: 連喬西·派伊都取得咗一定嘅卓越地位:女王學院裡舌頭最毒嘅年輕小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連喬西·派伊也取得了一定的卓越地位:女王學院裡舌頭最毒的年輕小姐。

passages.original: So it may be fairly stated that Miss Stacy’s old pupils held their own in the wider arena of the academical course.
passages.vernacular: 所以可以公正地講,斯泰西小姐嘅老學生哋喺學院課程嘅更廣闊嘅競技場上守住咗陣地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以可以公正地說,斯泰西小姐的老學生們在學院課程的更廣闊的競技場上守住了陣地。

passages.original: Anne worked hard and steadily.
passages.vernacular: 安妮努力而持之以恆地學習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮努力而持之以恆地學習。

passages.original: Her rivalry with Gilbert was as intense as it had ever been in Avonlea school, although it was not known in the class at large, but somehow the bitterness had gone out of it.
passages.vernacular: 佢同吉爾伯特嘅競爭同喺阿文利學校時一樣激烈,儘管班上大多數人唔知道,但唔知怎嘅,其中嘅苦澀已經消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她與吉爾伯特的競爭和在阿文利學校時一樣激烈,儘管班上大多數人不知道,但不知怎的,其中的苦澀已經消失了。

passages.original: Anne no longer wished to win for the sake of defeating Gilbert; rather, for the proud consciousness of a well-won victory over a worthy foeman.
passages.vernacular: 安妮唔再為了打敗吉爾伯特而想贏;而係為了贏得一個值得尊敬嘅對手之後嗰份自豪嘅、贏得光榮嘅意識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮不再為了打敗吉爾伯特而想贏;而是為了贏得一個值得尊敬的對手之後那份自豪的、贏得光榮的意識。

passages.original: It would be worth while to win, but she no longer thought life would be insupportable if she did not.
passages.vernacular: 贏係值得嘅,但佢唔再認為如果贏不咗生活就不可忍受喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 贏是值得的,但她不再認為如果贏不了生活就不可忍受了。

passages.original: In spite of lessons the students found opportunities for pleasant times.
passages.vernacular: 儘管有功課,學生哋定係找機會享受愉快嘅時光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管有功課,學生們還是找機會享受愉快的時光。

passages.original: Anne spent many of her spare hours at Beechwood and generally ate her Sunday dinners there and went to church with Miss Barry.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把許多空閒時間花喺山毛櫸莊,通常喺嗰度食星期天嘅午飯,並同巴里小姐一起去教堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把許多空閒時間花在山毛櫸莊,通常在那裡吃星期天的午飯,並與巴里小姐一起去教堂。

passages.original: The latter was, as she admitted, growing old, but her black eyes were not dim nor the vigor of her tongue in the least abated.
passages.vernacular: 後者,正如佢承認嘅,正在老去,但佢嘅黑眼睛並不昏花,舌頭嘅力量都絲毫未減。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後者,正如她承認的,正在老去,但她的黑眼睛並不昏花,舌頭的力量也絲毫未減。

passages.original: But she never sharpened the latter on Anne, who continued to be a prime favorite with the critical old lady.
passages.vernacular: 但佢從不喺安妮身上磨快佢,安妮繼續係呢位挑剔嘅老太太嘅頭號寵兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她從不在安妮身上磨快它,安妮繼續是這位挑剔的老太太的頭號寵兒。

passages.original: “That Anne-girl improves all the time,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個安妮丫頭一直喺進步,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那個安妮丫頭一直在進步,」她說。

passages.original: “I get tired of other girls--there is such a provoking and eternal sameness about them.
passages.vernacular: 「我對別嘅女孩感到厭倦——佢哋身上有咁令人惱火嘅、永恆嘅千篇一律。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我對別的女孩感到厭倦——她們身上有那麼令人惱火的、永恆的千篇一律。

passages.original: Anne has as many shades as a rainbow and every shade is the prettiest while it lasts.
passages.vernacular: 安妮有彩虹咁多嘅色調,每一種色調喺持續嘅時候都係最漂亮嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮有彩虹那麼多的色調,每一種色調在持續的時候都是最漂亮的。

passages.original: I don’t know that she is as amusing as she was when she was a child, but she makes me love her and I like people who make me love them.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道佢係唔係仲像小時候咁有趣,但佢讓我愛佢,而我鍾意讓我愛佢哋嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道她是不是還像小時候那麼有趣,但她讓我愛她,而我喜歡讓我愛她們的人。

passages.original: It saves me so much trouble in making myself love them.”
passages.vernacular: 呢省咗我好多讓自己愛佢哋嘅麻煩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這省了我好多讓自己愛她們的麻煩。」

passages.original: Then, almost before anybody realized it, spring had come; out in Avonlea the Mayflowers were peeping pinkly out on the sere barrens where snow-wreaths lingered; and the “mist of green” was on the woods and in the valleys.
passages.vernacular: 然後,幾乎喺人哋意識到之前,春天嚟喇;喺阿文利,五月花正粉紅地探出頭嚟,喺積雪嘅花環仲喺逗留嘅枯萎荒原上;「綠色嘅薄霧」籠罩住樹林同山谷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,幾乎在人們意識到之前,春天來了;在阿文利,五月花正粉紅地探出頭來,在積雪的花環還在逗留的枯萎荒原上;「綠色的薄霧」籠罩著樹林和山谷。

passages.original: But in Charlottetown harassed Queen’s students thought and talked only of examinations.
passages.vernacular: 但喺夏洛特敦,焦頭爛額嘅女王學院學生哋只想住、談住考試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在夏洛特敦,焦頭爛額的女王學院學生們只想著、談著考試。

passages.original: “It doesn’t seem possible that the term is nearly over,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「學期快結束似乎唔可能,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「學期快結束似乎不可能,」安妮說。

passages.original: “Why, last fall it seemed so long to look forward to--a whole winter of studies and classes.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,去年秋天,展望佢似乎咁漫長——整整一個冬天嘅學習同上課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,去年秋天,展望它似乎那麼漫長——整整一個冬天的學習和上課。

passages.original: And here we are, with the exams looming up next week.
passages.vernacular: 而而家我哋到喇,考試下個星期就迫近喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而現在我們到了,考試下個星期就迫近了。

passages.original: Girls, sometimes I feel as if those exams meant everything, but when I look at the big buds swelling on those chestnut trees and the misty blue air at the end of the streets they don’t seem half so important.”
passages.vernacular: 女孩哋,有時我覺得嗰啲考試意味住一切,但當我睇嗰啲栗樹上鼓起嘅大花苞,以及街道盡頭藍色嘅薄霧空氣時,佢哋似乎連一半重要都唔係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩們,有時我覺得那些考試意味著一切,但當我看那些栗樹上鼓起的大花苞,以及街道盡頭藍色的薄霧空氣時,它們似乎連一半重要也不是。」

passages.original: Jane and Ruby and Josie, who had dropped in, did not take this view of it.
passages.vernacular: 順道嚟嘅簡、露比同喬西不咁樣睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 順道來的簡、露比和喬西不這樣看。

passages.original: To them the coming examinations were constantly very important indeed--far more important than chestnut buds or Maytime hazes.
passages.vernacular: 對佢哋來講,即將到來嘅考試始終係好重要嘅——比栗樹花苞或五月嘅薄霧重要得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對她們來說,即將到來的考試始終是非常重要的——比栗樹花苞或五月的薄霧重要得多。

passages.original: It was all very well for Anne, who was sure of passing at least, to have her moments of belittling them, but when your whole future depended on them--as the girls truly thought theirs did--you could not regard them philosophically.
passages.vernacular: 對安妮來講,佢至少肯定會通過,偶爾貶低佢哋倒都無妨,但當你嘅整個未來都依賴於佢哋——女孩哋確實認為自己嘅如此——你就唔能夠抱住哲學嘅態度睇待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對安妮來說,她至少肯定會通過,偶爾貶低它們倒也無妨,但當你的整個未來都依賴於它們——女孩們確實認為自己的如此——你就不能抱著哲學的態度看待。

passages.original: “I’ve lost seven pounds in the last two weeks,” sighed Jane.
passages.vernacular: 「過去兩個星期我瘦咗七磅,」簡嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「過去兩個星期我瘦了七磅,」簡嘆道。

passages.original: “It’s no use to say don’t worry.
passages.vernacular: 「講別擔心冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說別擔心沒用。

passages.original: I will worry.
passages.vernacular: 我就係要擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是要擔心。

passages.original: Worrying helps you some--it seems as if you were doing something when you’re worrying.
passages.vernacular: 擔心對你有點幫助——擔心嘅時候似乎你喺做點乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 擔心對你有點幫助——擔心的時候似乎你在做點什麼。

passages.original: It would be dreadful if I failed to get my license after going to Queen’s all winter and spending so much money.”
passages.vernacular: 如果我喺女王學院讀咗一整個冬天、花咗咁多錢,卻攞唔到執照,嗰就太可怕喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我在女王學院讀了一整個冬天、花了這麼多錢,卻拿不到執照,那就太可怕了。」

passages.original: “I don’t care,” said Josie Pye.
passages.vernacular: 「我才不在乎,」喬西·派伊講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我才不在乎,」喬西·派伊說。

passages.original: “If I don’t pass this year I’m coming back next.
passages.vernacular: 「如果我今年冇通過,我明年再嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我今年沒通過,我明年再來。

passages.original: My father can afford to send me.
passages.vernacular: 我父親供得起我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父親供得起我。

passages.original: Anne, Frank Stockley says that Professor Tremaine said Gilbert Blythe was sure to get the medal and that Emily Clay would likely win the Avery scholarship.”
passages.vernacular: 安妮,弗蘭克·斯托克利講特里梅因教授講吉爾伯特·布萊斯肯定能得獎牌,艾米麗·克萊好可能贏得艾弗里獎學金。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮,弗蘭克·斯托克利說特里梅因教授說吉爾伯特·布萊斯肯定能得獎牌,艾米麗·克萊很可能贏得艾弗里獎學金。」

passages.original: “That may make me feel badly tomorrow, Josie,” laughed Anne, “but just now I honestly feel that as long as I know the violets are coming out all purple down in the hollow below Green Gables and that little ferns are poking their heads up in Lovers’ Lane, it’s not a great deal of difference whether I win the Avery or not.
passages.vernacular: 「呢或者聽日會讓我難受,喬西,」安妮笑住講,「但而家我確實覺得,只要我知道綠色屋頂下面窪地里嘅紫羅蘭正在開得一片紫色,小小嘅蕨類喺情人小徑里探出頭嚟,我係咪贏得艾弗里獎學金就冇多大區別喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這也許明天會讓我難受,喬西,」安妮笑著說,「但現在我確實覺得,只要我知道綠色屋頂下面窪地里的紫羅蘭正在開得一片紫色,小小的蕨類在情人小徑里探出頭來,我是否贏得艾弗里獎學金就沒有多大區別了。

passages.original: I’ve done my best and I begin to understand what is meant by the ‘joy of the strife.’
passages.vernacular: 我已經盡力喇,我開始明白『奮鬥之樂』係乜嘢意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經盡力了,我開始明白『奮鬥之樂』是什麼意思。

passages.original: Next to trying and winning, the best thing is trying and failing.
passages.vernacular: 僅次於努力並贏得,最好嘅事情係努力並失敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 僅次於努力並贏得,最好的事情是努力並失敗。

passages.original: Girls, don’t talk about exams!
passages.vernacular: 女孩哋,別談考試!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩們,別談考試!

passages.original: Look at that arch of pale green sky over those houses and picture to yourself what it must look like over the purply-dark beech-woods back of Avonlea.”
passages.vernacular: 睇嗰啲房屋上方淡綠色嘅天空拱頂,想像一下,喺阿文利後面紫黑色嘅山毛櫸林上方,佢會係乜嘢樣子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看那些房屋上方淡綠色的天空拱頂,想像一下,在阿文利後面紫黑色的山毛櫸林上方,它會是什麼樣子。」

passages.original: “What are you going to wear for commencement, Jane?” asked Ruby practically.
passages.vernacular: 「你畢業典禮穿乜嘢,簡?」露比務實地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你畢業典禮穿什麼,簡?」露比務實地問。

passages.original: Jane and Josie both answered at once and the chatter drifted into a side eddy of fashions.
passages.vernacular: 簡同喬西同時回答,閒聊漂流進時尚嘅小旋渦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡和喬西同時回答,閒聊漂流進時尚的小旋渦。

passages.original: But Anne, with her elbows on the window sill, her soft cheek laid against her clasped hands, and her eyes filled with visions, looked out unheedingly across city roof and spire to that glorious dome of sunset sky and wove her dreams of a possible future from the golden tissue of youth’s own optimism.
passages.vernacular: 但安妮,手肘支喺窗臺上,柔軟嘅臉頰貼住交握嘅雙手,眼睛里充滿幻象,不經意地望過城市屋頂同尖塔,望向嗰光輝嘅日落天空穹頂,用青春自己嘅樂觀嘅金色織物編織住對可能嘅未來嘅夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安妮,手肘支在窗臺上,柔軟的臉頰貼著交握的雙手,眼睛里充滿幻象,不經意地望過城市屋頂和尖塔,望向那光輝的日落天空穹頂,用青春自己的樂觀的金色織物編織著對可能的未來的夢。

passages.original: All the Beyond was hers with its possibilities lurking rosily in the oncoming years--each year a rose of promise to be woven into an immortal chaplet.
