passages.vernacular: 整個未來都係佢嘅,可能性玫瑰色地潛伏喺即將到來嘅歲月里——每一年都係一朵承諾之玫瑰,要編進不朽嘅花冠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個未來都是她的,可能性玫瑰色地潛伏在即將到來的歲月里——每一年都是一朵承諾之玫瑰,要編進不朽的花冠。

chapters.title: Ch. XXXVI The Glory and the Dream 第三十六章:榮耀與夢想

passages.original: CH ON the morning when the final results of all the examinations were to be posted on the bulletin board at Queen’s, Anne and Jane walked down the street together.
passages.vernacular: 喺女王學院公告欄上張貼所有考試最終結果嘅嗰天早晨,安妮同簡一起沿街走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在女王學院公告欄上張貼所有考試最終結果的那天早晨,安妮和簡一起沿街走去。

passages.original: Jane was smiling and happy; examinations were over and she was comfortably sure she had made a pass at least; further considerations troubled Jane not at all; she had no soaring ambitions and consequently was not affected with the unrest attendant thereon.
passages.vernacular: 簡微笑住,好高興;考試結束喇,佢舒舒服服地確信自己至少考過喇;更多嘅顧慮根本不困擾簡;佢冇高飛嘅雄心,因此不受隨之而嚟嘅不安嘅影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡微笑著,很高興;考試結束了,她舒舒服服地確信自己至少考過了;更多的顧慮根本不困擾簡;她沒有高飛的雄心,因此不受隨之而來的不安的影響。

passages.original: For we pay a price for everything we get or take in this world; and although ambitions are well worth having, they are not to be cheaply won, but exact their dues of work and self-denial, anxiety and discouragement.
passages.vernacular: 因為我哋喺呢世上得到或攞走嘅一切都要付出代價;雖然雄心好值得擁有,但佢哋唔係廉價獲得嘅,而係要求付出工作同自我克制、焦慮和氣餒嘅代價。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我們在這世上得到或拿走的一切都要付出代價;雖然雄心很值得擁有,但它們不是廉價獲得的,而是要求付出工作和自我克制、焦慮和氣餒的代價。

passages.original: Anne was pale and quiet; in ten more minutes she would know who had won the medal and who the Avery.
passages.vernacular: 安妮臉色蒼白,默不作聲;再過好鐘佢就會知道邊個贏得咗獎牌,邊個贏得咗艾弗里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮臉色蒼白,默不作聲;再過十分鐘她就會知道誰贏得了獎牌,誰贏得了艾弗里。

passages.original: Beyond those ten minutes there did not seem, just then, to be anything worth being called Time.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰好鐘之外,嗰時似乎冇任何值得稱為時間嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那十分鐘之外,那時似乎沒有任何值得稱為時間的東西。

passages.original: “Of course you’ll win one of them anyhow,” said Jane, who couldn’t understand how the faculty could be so unfair as to order it otherwise.
passages.vernacular: 「不管點樣你肯定會贏其中一個,」簡講,佢唔能夠理解教師團點會不公平到作出別嘅安排。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不管怎樣你肯定會贏其中一個,」簡說,她不能理解教師團怎麼會不公平到作出別的安排。

passages.original: “I have not hope of the Avery,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我對艾弗里不抱希望,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我對艾弗里不抱希望,」安妮說。

passages.original: “Everybody says Emily Clay will win it.
passages.vernacular: 「大家都講艾米麗·克萊會贏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「大家都說艾米麗·克萊會贏。

passages.original: And I’m not going to march up to that bulletin board and look at it before everybody.
passages.vernacular: 而且我不打算喺大家面前走到嗰個公告欄前去睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我不打算在大家面前走到那個公告欄前去看。

passages.original: I haven’t the moral courage.
passages.vernacular: 我冇嗰個精神勇氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有那個精神勇氣。

passages.original: I’m going straight to the girls’ dressing room.
passages.vernacular: 我直接去女生更衣室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我直接去女生更衣室。

passages.original: You must read the announcements and then come and tell me, Jane.
passages.vernacular: 你必須讀公告,然後來告訴我,簡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你必須讀公告,然後來告訴我,簡。

passages.original: And I implore you in the name of our old friendship to do it as quickly as possible.
passages.vernacular: 我以我哋舊日友誼嘅名義懇求你,儘快辦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以我們舊日友誼的名義懇求你,儘快辦。

passages.original: If I have failed just say so, without trying to break it gently; and whatever you do don’t sympathize with me.
passages.vernacular: 如果我失敗喇,就直講,別試住委婉;不管你做乜嘢,都別同情我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我失敗了,就直說,別試著委婉;不管你做什麼,都別同情我。

passages.original: Promise me this, Jane.”
passages.vernacular: 答應我呢個,簡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 答應我這個,簡。」

passages.original: Jane promised solemnly; but, as it happened, there was no necessity for such a promise.
passages.vernacular: 簡鄭重地答應喇;但事實上,並冇咁樣一個承諾嘅必要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡鄭重地答應了;但事實上,並沒有這樣一個承諾的必要。

passages.original: When they went up the entrance steps of Queen’s they found the hall full of boys who were carrying Gilbert Blythe around on their shoulders and yelling at the tops of their voices, “Hurrah for Blythe, Medalist!”
passages.vernacular: 當佢哋走上女王學院嘅入口台階時,發現大廳里擠滿咗男孩,佢哋正把吉爾伯特·布萊斯扛喺肩上轉圈,扯住嗓子大喊:「布萊斯獲得獎牌,萬歲!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他們走上女王學院的入口台階時,發現大廳里擠滿了男孩,他們正把吉爾伯特·布萊斯扛在肩上轉圈,扯著嗓子大喊:「布萊斯獲得獎牌,萬歲!」

passages.original: For a moment Anne felt one sickening pang of defeat and disappointment.
passages.vernacular: 有咁一會兒,安妮感到一陣令人作嘔嘅失敗同失望嘅刺痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有那麼一會兒,安妮感到一陣令人作嘔的失敗和失望的刺痛。

passages.original: So she had failed and Gilbert had won!
passages.vernacular: 咁講佢失敗喇,吉爾伯特贏喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這麼說她失敗了,吉爾伯特贏了!

passages.original: Well, Matthew would be sorry--he had been so sure she would win.
passages.vernacular: 唉,馬修會難過嘅——佢曾經咁確信佢會贏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,馬修會難過的——他曾經那麼確信她會贏。

passages.original: And then!
passages.vernacular: 然後!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後!

passages.original: Somebody called out:
passages.vernacular: 有人喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人喊道:

passages.original: “Three cheers for Miss Shirley, winner of the Avery!”
passages.vernacular: 「為贏得艾弗里嘅雪莉小姐三呼萬歲!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為贏得艾弗里的雪莉小姐三呼萬歲!」

passages.original: “Oh, Anne,” gasped Jane, as they fled to the girls’ dressing room amid hearty cheers.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,安妮,」簡喘住氣講,佢哋喺熱烈嘅歡呼聲中逃向女生更衣室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,安妮,」簡喘著氣說,他們在熱烈的歡呼聲中逃向女生更衣室。

passages.original: “Oh, Anne I’m so proud!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,安妮,我太自豪喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,安妮,我太自豪了!

passages.original: Isn’t it splendid?”
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係太棒咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是太棒了嗎?」

passages.original: And then the girls were around them and Anne was the center of a laughing, congratulating group.
passages.vernacular: 然後女孩哋圍咗上嚟,安妮成咗一群歡笑、道賀嘅人嘅中心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後女孩們圍了上來,安妮成了一群歡笑、道賀的人的中心。

passages.original: Her shoulders were thumped and her hands shaken vigorously.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅肩膀被拍打,佢嘅手被用力地搖晃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的肩膀被拍打,她的手被用力地搖晃。

passages.original: She was pushed and pulled and hugged and among it all she managed to whisper to Jane:
passages.vernacular: 佢被推、被拉、被擁抱,喺呢一切之中,佢設法對簡低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她被推、被拉、被擁抱,在這一切之中,她設法對簡低聲說:

passages.original: “Oh, won’t Matthew and Marilla be pleased!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,馬修同瑪麗拉唔係會高興嗎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,馬修和瑪麗拉不是會高興嗎!

passages.original: I must write the news home right away.”
passages.vernacular: 我必須即刻把消息寫信寄回家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須立刻把消息寫信寄回家。」

passages.original: Commencement was the next important happening.
passages.vernacular: 畢業典禮係下一個重要事件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 畢業典禮是下一個重要事件。

passages.original: The exercises were held in the big assembly hall of the Academy.
passages.vernacular: 儀式喺學院嘅大禮堂舉行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儀式在學院的大禮堂舉行。

passages.original: Addresses were given, essays read, songs sung, the public award of diplomas, prizes and medals made.
passages.vernacular: 有演講,有宣讀嘅文章,有唱嘅歌,公開頒發文憑、獎品同獎牌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有演講,有宣讀的文章,有唱的歌,公開頒發文憑、獎品和獎牌。

passages.original: Matthew and Marilla were there, with eyes and ears for only one student on the platform--a tall girl in pale green, with faintly flushed cheeks and starry eyes, who read the best essay and was pointed out and whispered about as the Avery winner.
passages.vernacular: 馬修同瑪麗拉喺嗰兒,眼睛同耳朵只為臺上嘅一位學生——一個穿淡綠色衣服、臉頰微紅、眼睛如星嘅高個子女孩,佢讀咗最優秀嘅文章,被指點出嚟,被議論紛紛講係艾弗里獲得者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修和瑪麗拉在那兒,眼睛和耳朵只為臺上的一位學生——一個穿淡綠色衣服、臉頰微紅、眼睛如星的高個子女孩,她讀了最優秀的文章,被指點出來,被議論紛紛說是艾弗里獲得者。

passages.original: “Reckon you’re glad we kept her, Marilla?” whispered Matthew, speaking for the first time since he had entered the hall, when Anne had finished her essay.
passages.vernacular: 「想必你好高興我哋留下咗佢,瑪麗拉?」馬修低聲講,呢個係佢進入大廳以來第一次講話,安妮剛讀完佢嘅文章。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「想必你很高興我們留下了她,瑪麗拉?」馬修低聲說,這是他進入大廳以來第一次說話,安妮剛讀完她的文章。

passages.original: “It’s not the first time I’ve been glad,” retorted Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「呢唔係我第一次高興喇,」瑪麗拉反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這不是我第一次高興了,」瑪麗拉反駁。

passages.original: “You do like to rub things in, Matthew Cuthbert.”
passages.vernacular: 「你就係愛把呢種事挑明,馬修·卡思伯特。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你就是愛把這種事挑明,馬修·卡思伯特。」

passages.original: Miss Barry, who was sitting behind them, leaned forward and poked Marilla in the back with her parasol.
passages.vernacular: 坐喺佢哋後面嘅巴里小姐身子前傾,用佢嘅陽傘戳咗戳瑪麗拉嘅背。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 坐在他們後面的巴里小姐身子前傾,用她的陽傘戳了戳瑪麗拉的背。

passages.original: “Aren’t you proud of that Anne-girl?
passages.vernacular: 「你不為嗰個安妮丫頭自豪嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不為那個安妮丫頭自豪嗎?

passages.original: I am,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 我係,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是,」她說。

passages.original: Anne went home to Avonlea with Matthew and Marilla that evening.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天傍晚,安妮同馬修、瑪麗拉一起回阿文利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天傍晚,安妮和馬修、瑪麗拉一起回阿文利。

passages.original: She had not been home since April and she felt that she could not wait another day.
passages.vernacular: 佢自四月以來冇回過家,佢覺得一天都等不及喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她自四月以來沒回過家,她覺得一天也等不及了。

passages.original: The apple blossoms were out and the world was fresh and young.
passages.vernacular: 蘋果花開喇,世界鮮嫩年輕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蘋果花開了,世界鮮嫩年輕。

passages.original: Diana was at Green Gables to meet her.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜喺綠色屋頂迎接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜在綠色屋頂迎接她。

passages.original: In her own white room, where Marilla had set a flowering house rose on the window sill, Anne looked about her and drew a long breath of happiness.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢自己嘅白色房間里,瑪麗拉喺窗臺上放咗一盆開花嘅家薔薇,安妮環顧四周,深深吸咗一口幸福嘅氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她自己的白色房間里,瑪麗拉在窗臺上放了一盆開花的家薔薇,安妮環顧四周,深深吸了一口幸福的氣。

passages.original: “Oh, Diana, it’s so good to be back again.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,黛安娜,回嚟真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,黛安娜,回來真好。

passages.original: It’s so good to see those pointed firs coming out against the pink sky--and that white orchard and the old Snow Queen.
passages.vernacular: 睇到嗰啲尖尖嘅冷杉映喺粉紅色嘅天空下——仲有嗰白色嘅果園同老雪之女王,真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到那些尖尖的冷杉映在粉紅色的天空下——還有那白色的果園和老雪之女王,真好。

passages.original: Isn’t the breath of the mint delicious?
passages.vernacular: 薄荷嘅氣息唔係好香嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 薄荷的氣息不是很香嗎?

passages.original: And that tea rose--why, it’s a song and a hope and a prayer all in one.
passages.vernacular: 仲有嗰朵茶玫瑰——哎呀,佢係一首歌、一個希望、一個禱告集於一身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有那朵茶玫瑰——哎呀,它是一首歌、一個希望、一個禱告集於一身。

passages.original: And it’s good to see you again, Diana!”
passages.vernacular: 再次見到你真好,黛安娜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再次見到你真好,黛安娜!」

passages.original: “I thought you liked that Stella Maynard better than me,” said Diana reproachfully.
passages.vernacular: 「我以為你鍾意嗰個斯特拉·梅納德勝過鍾意我,」黛安娜責備地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以為你喜歡那個斯特拉·梅納德勝過喜歡我,」黛安娜責備地說。

passages.original: “Josie Pye told me you did.
passages.vernacular: 「喬西·派伊告訴我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喬西·派伊告訴我的。

passages.original: Josie said you were infatuated with her.”
passages.vernacular: 喬西講你迷戀佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西說你迷戀她。」

passages.original: Anne laughed and pelted Diana with the faded “June lilies” of her bouquet.
passages.vernacular: 安妮笑喇,用佢花束中凋謝嘅「六月百合」打黛安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮笑了,用她花束中凋謝的「六月百合」打黛安娜。

passages.original: “Stella Maynard is the dearest girl in the world except one and you are that one, Diana,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「斯特拉·梅納德係世上最親愛嘅女孩,除咗一個,而你就係嗰一個,黛安娜,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「斯特拉·梅納德是世上最親愛的女孩,除了一個,而你就是那一個,黛安娜,」她說。

passages.original: “I love you more than ever--and I’ve so many things to tell you.
passages.vernacular: 「我比以往任何時候都更愛你——我有咁多事要告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我比以往任何時候都更愛你——我有那麼多事要告訴你。

passages.original: But just now I feel as if it were joy enough to sit here and look at you.
passages.vernacular: 但而家我覺得,光係坐喺呢兒睇住你就已經夠快樂嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在我覺得,光是坐在這兒看著你就已經夠快樂的了。

passages.original: I’m tired, I think--tired of being studious and ambitious.
passages.vernacular: 我想我累喇——厭倦咗做學究同有雄心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我累了——厭倦了做學究和有雄心。

passages.original: I mean to spend at least two hours tomorrow lying out in the orchard grass, thinking of absolutely nothing.”
passages.vernacular: 我打算聽日至少花兩個鐘頭躺喺果園草地上,完全乜嘢都唔想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我打算明天至少花兩個鐘頭躺在果園草地上,完全什麼都不想。」

passages.original: “You’ve done splendidly, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「你做得太棒喇,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你做得太棒了,安妮。

passages.original: I suppose you won’t be teaching now that you’ve won the Avery?”
passages.vernacular: 我想你既然贏得咗艾弗里,就唔會去教書咗吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你既然贏得了艾弗里,就不會去教書了吧?」

passages.original: “No. I’m going to Redmond in September.
passages.vernacular: 「不。我九月去雷德蒙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不。我九月去雷德蒙。

passages.original: Doesn’t it seem wonderful?
passages.vernacular: 呢不奇妙嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不奇妙嗎?

passages.original: I’ll have a brand new stock of ambition laid in by that time after three glorious, golden months of vacation.
passages.vernacular: 經過三個光輝嘅、金色嘅假期,到嗰時我會儲備全新嘅雄心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 經過三個光輝的、金色的假期,到那時我會儲備全新的雄心。

passages.original: Jane and Ruby are going to teach.
passages.vernacular: 簡同露比要去教書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡和露比要去教書。

passages.original: Isn’t it splendid to think we all got through even to Moody Spurgeon and Josie Pye?”
passages.vernacular: 想到我哋全都通過喇,連穆迪·斯珀吉翁同喬西·派伊都係,唔係太棒咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到我們全都通過了,連穆迪·斯珀吉翁和喬西·派伊也是,不是太棒了嗎?」

passages.original: “The Newbridge trustees have offered Jane their school already,” said Diana.
passages.vernacular: 「新橋嘅校董哋已經畀簡提供咗佢哋嘅學校,」黛安娜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「新橋的校董們已經給簡提供了他們的學校,」黛安娜說。

passages.original: “Gilbert Blythe is going to teach, too.
passages.vernacular: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯都要去教書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯也要去教書。

passages.original: He has to.
passages.vernacular: 佢必須。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他必須。

passages.original: His father can’t afford to send him to college next year, after all, so he means to earn his own way through.
passages.vernacular: 佢父親終究供不起佢明年上大學,所以佢打算自己賺學費。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他父親終究供不起他明年上大學,所以他打算自己賺學費。

passages.original: I expect he’ll get the school here if Miss Ames decides to leave.”
passages.vernacular: 我想如果艾姆斯小姐決定離開,佢會得到呢兒嘅學校。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想如果艾姆斯小姐決定離開,他會得到這兒的學校。」

passages.original: Anne felt a queer little sensation of dismayed surprise.
passages.vernacular: 安妮感到一種奇怪嘅、驚愕又意外嘅小感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮感到一種奇怪的、驚愕又意外的小感覺。

passages.original: She had not known this; she had expected that Gilbert would be going to Redmond also.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔知道呢啲;佢原本期待吉爾伯特都去雷德蒙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不知道這一點;她原本期待吉爾伯特也去雷德蒙。

passages.original: What would she do without their inspiring rivalry?
passages.vernacular: 冇佢哋嗰種激勵人嘅競爭,佢該點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有他們那種激勵人的競爭,她該怎麼辦?

passages.original: Would not work, even at a coeducational college with a real degree in prospect, be rather flat without her friend the enemy?
passages.vernacular: 冇佢嘅朋友兼對手,即使喺一所男女同校嘅、有真正學位前景嘅大學裡,工作唔會相當乏味嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有她的朋友兼對手,即使在一所男女同校的、有真正學位前景的大學裡,工作不會相當乏味嗎?

passages.original: The next morning at breakfast it suddenly struck Anne that Matthew was not looking well.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨食早飯時,安妮突然覺得馬修氣色不好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨吃早飯時,安妮突然覺得馬修氣色不好。

passages.original: Surely he was much grayer than he had been a year before.
passages.vernacular: 佢肯定比一年前灰白得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他肯定比一年前灰白得多。

passages.original: “Marilla,” she said hesitatingly when he had gone out, “is Matthew quite well?”
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉,」佢出去後佢猶豫地講,「馬修身體好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉,」他出去後她猶豫地說,「馬修身體好嗎?」

passages.original: “No, he isn’t,” said Marilla in a troubled tone.
passages.vernacular: 「不好,」瑪麗拉用憂愁嘅語氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不好,」瑪麗拉用憂愁的語氣說。

passages.original: “He’s had some real bad spells with his heart this spring and he won’t spare himself a mite.
passages.vernacular: 「今年春天佢心臟病發作得好厲害,而佢啲都不愛惜自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今年春天他心臟病發作得很厲害,而他一點也不愛惜自己。

passages.original: I’ve been real worried about him, but he’s some better this while back and we’ve got a good hired man, so I’m hoping he’ll kind of rest and pick up.
passages.vernacular: 我一直好為佢擔心,但前一陣子佢好啲喇,我哋有咗一個好雇工,所以我希望佢能休息一下恢復。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直非常為他擔心,但前一陣子他好一些了,我們有了一個好雇工,所以我希望他能休息一下恢復。

passages.original: Maybe he will now you’re home.
passages.vernacular: 或者你而家回嚟佢會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許你現在回來他會的。

passages.original: You always cheer him up.”
passages.vernacular: 你總能讓佢高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你總能讓他高興。」

passages.original: Anne leaned across the table and took Marilla’s face in her hands.
passages.vernacular: 安妮隔住桌子探過身,雙手捧住瑪麗拉嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮隔著桌子探過身,雙手捧住瑪麗拉的臉。

passages.original: “You are not looking as well yourself as I’d like to see you, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「您自己嘅氣色都冇我希望睇到嘅咁好,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您自己的氣色也沒有我希望看到的那麼好,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: You look tired.
passages.vernacular: 您睇上去累喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看上去累了。

passages.original: I’m afraid you’ve been working too hard.
passages.vernacular: 我怕您工作太辛苦喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕您工作太辛苦了。

passages.original: You must take a rest, now that I’m home.
passages.vernacular: 而家我回家喇,您必須休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我回家了,您必須休息。

passages.original: I’m just going to take this one day off to visit all the dear old spots and hunt up my old dreams, and then it will be your turn to be lazy while I do the work.”
passages.vernacular: 我只打算休息呢一天,去睇睇所有親愛嘅老地方,尋找我嘅舊夢,然後輪到您偷懶,我嚟幹活。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只打算休息這一天,去看看所有親愛的老地方,尋找我的舊夢,然後輪到您偷懶,我來幹活。」

passages.original: Marilla smiled affectionately at her girl.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉深情地對佢嘅女孩微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉深情地對她的女孩微笑。

passages.original: “It’s not the work--it’s my head.
passages.vernacular: 「唔係工作——係我嘅頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是工作——是我的頭。

passages.original: I’ve got a pain so often now--behind my eyes.
passages.vernacular: 我而家經常頭疼——喺眼睛後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在經常頭疼——在眼睛後面。

passages.original: Doctor Spencer’s been fussing with glasses, but they don’t do me any good.
passages.vernacular: 斯潘塞醫生一直喺折騰眼鏡,但對我冇乜嘢用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯潘塞醫生一直在折騰眼鏡,但對我沒什麼用。

passages.original: There is a distinguished oculist coming to the Island the last of June and the doctor says I must see him.
passages.vernacular: 六月底有一位著名嘅眼科醫生要嚟島上,醫生講我必須去見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 六月底有一位著名的眼科醫生要來島上,醫生說我必須去見他。

passages.original: I guess I’ll have to.
passages.vernacular: 我想我得去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我得去。

passages.original: I can’t read or sew with any comfort now.
passages.vernacular: 我而家讀書縫紉都不舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在讀書縫紉都不舒服。

passages.original: Well, Anne, you’ve done real well at Queen’s I must say.
passages.vernacular: 好吧,安妮,我必須講你喺女王學院做得真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,安妮,我必須說你在女王學院做得真好。

passages.original: To take First Class License in one year and win the Avery scholarship--well, well, Mrs. Lynde says pride goes before a fall and she doesn’t believe in the higher education of women at all; she says it unfits them for woman’s true sphere.
passages.vernacular: 一年攞到一級執照並贏得艾弗里獎學金——嗯,嗯,林德太太講驕傲喺跌倒之前,佢根本不相信女人受高等教育;佢講呢使佢哋不適合女人真正嘅領域。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一年拿到一級執照並贏得艾弗里獎學金——嗯,嗯,林德太太說驕傲在跌倒之前,她根本不相信女人受高等教育;她說這使她們不適合女人真正的領域。

passages.original: I don’t believe a word of it.
passages.vernacular: 我一個字都不信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一個字也不信。

passages.original: Speaking of Rachel reminds me--did you hear anything about the Abbey Bank lately, Anne?”
passages.vernacular: 講起雷切爾,我想起嚟喇——最近你聽到乜嘢關於艾比銀行嘅消息嗎,安妮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說起雷切爾,我想起來了——最近你聽到什麼關於艾比銀行的消息嗎,安妮?」

passages.original: “I heard it was shaky,” answered Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我聽講佢不穩,」安妮回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我聽說它不穩,」安妮回答。

passages.original: “Why?”
passages.vernacular: 「點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了?」

passages.original: “That is what Rachel said.
passages.vernacular: 「雷切爾就係咁講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「雷切爾就是這麼說的。

passages.original: She was up here one day last week and said there was some talk about it.
passages.vernacular: 佢上星期有一天嚟呢兒,講有些關於佢嘅議論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她上星期有一天來這兒,說有些關於它的議論。

passages.original: Matthew felt real worried.
passages.vernacular: 馬修好擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修非常擔心。

passages.original: All we have saved is in that bank--every penny.
passages.vernacular: 我哋所有嘅積蓄都喺嗰家銀行——每一分錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們所有的積蓄都在那家銀行——每一分錢。

passages.original: I wanted Matthew to put it in the Savings Bank in the first place, but old Mr. Abbey was a great friend of father’s and he’d always banked with him.
passages.vernacular: 我起初就想讓馬修把佢存進儲蓄銀行,但老艾比先生係我父親嘅好朋友,佢總是存在佢嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我起初就想讓馬修把它存進儲蓄銀行,但老艾比先生是我父親的好朋友,他總是存在他那兒。

passages.original: Matthew said any bank with him at the head of it was good enough for anybody.”
passages.vernacular: 馬修講任何由佢掌管嘅銀行,對任何人都夠好喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修說任何由他掌管的銀行,對任何人都夠好了。」

passages.original: “I think he has only been its nominal head for many years,” said Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我想佢多年嚟只係名義上嘅行長,」安妮講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想他多年來只是名義上的行長,」安妮說。

passages.original: “He is a very old man; his nephews are really at the head of the institution.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係個好老嘅人;佢嘅侄子哋才係呢個機構真正嘅負責人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是個非常老的人;他的侄子們才是這個機構真正的負責人。」

passages.original: “Well, when Rachel told us that, I wanted Matthew to draw our money right out and he said he’d think of it.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,雷切爾告訴我哋嗰件事時,我想讓馬修把我哋嘅錢直接取出嚟,佢講佢會考慮嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,雷切爾告訴我們那件事時,我想讓馬修把我們的錢直接取出來,他說他會考慮的。

passages.original: But Mr. Russell told him yesterday that the bank was all right.”
passages.vernacular: 但係拉塞爾先生尋日告訴佢銀行冇事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是拉塞爾先生昨天告訴他銀行沒事。」

passages.original: Anne had her good day in the companionship of the outdoor world.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺同戶外世界嘅相伴中度過咗佢美好嘅一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在與戶外世界的相伴中度過了她美好的一天。

passages.original: She never forgot that day; it was so bright and golden and fair, so free from shadow and so lavish of blossom.
passages.vernacular: 佢永遠忘不咗嗰一天;佢咁明亮、金黃、美好,咁不帶陰影,咁慷慨地開住花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她永遠忘不了那一天;它那麼明亮、金黃、美好,那麼不帶陰影,那麼慷慨地開著花。

passages.original: Anne spent some of its rich hours in the orchard; she went to the Dryad’s Bubble and Willowmere and Violet Vale; she called at the manse and had a satisfying talk with Mrs. Allan; and finally in the evening she went with Matthew for the cows, through Lovers’ Lane to the back pasture.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺果園裡度過咗佢豐富時光嘅一部分;佢去咗林中仙子泉、柳塘同紫羅蘭谷;佢拜訪咗牧師住宅,同艾倫太太進行咗令人滿意嘅談話;最後晚上佢同馬修去趕牛,穿過情人小徑到後牧場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在果園裡度過了它豐富時光的一部分;她去了林中仙子泉、柳塘和紫羅蘭谷;她拜訪了牧師住宅,與艾倫太太進行了令人滿意的談話;最後晚上她和馬修去趕牛,穿過情人小徑到後牧場。

passages.original: The woods were all gloried through with sunset and the warm splendor of it streamed down through the hill gaps in the west.
passages.vernacular: 樹林里都被日落榮耀地穿透,佢溫暖嘅光輝從西邊嘅山隙傾瀉下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樹林里都被日落榮耀地穿透,它溫暖的光輝從西邊的山隙傾瀉下來。

passages.original: Matthew walked slowly with bent head; Anne, tall and erect, suited her springing step to his.
passages.vernacular: 馬修低住頭緩慢地走;安妮高挑挺直,把佢輕快嘅腳步調整到同佢一致。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修低著頭緩慢地走;安妮高挑挺直,把她輕快的腳步調整到與他一致。

passages.original: “You’ve been working too hard today, Matthew,” she said reproachfully.
passages.vernacular: 「你今日工作太辛苦喇,馬修,」佢責備地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你今天工作太辛苦了,馬修,」她責備地說。

passages.original: “Why won’t you take things easier?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點解不輕鬆啲?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼不輕鬆一點?」

passages.original: “Well now, I can’t seem to,” said Matthew, as he opened the yard gate to let the cows through.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我似乎做唔到,」馬修講,打開院子嘅大門讓牛通過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我似乎做不到,」馬修說,打開院子的大門讓牛通過。

passages.original: “It’s only that I’m getting old, Anne, and keep forgetting it.
passages.vernacular: 「只係我老喇,安妮,老係忘記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是我老了,安妮,老是忘記。

passages.original: Well, well, I’ve always worked pretty hard and I’d rather drop in harness.”
passages.vernacular: 唉,唉,我一向工作相當辛苦,我寧願死喺崗位上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,唉,我一向工作相當辛苦,我寧願死在崗位上。」

passages.original: “If I had been the boy you sent for,” said Anne wistfully, “I’d be able to help you so much now and spare you in a hundred ways.
passages.vernacular: 「如果我係你哋當初要嘅嗰個男孩,」安妮悵然地講,「我而家就能幫你咁多,從一百個方面減輕你嘅負擔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我是你們當初要的那個男孩,」安妮悵然地說,「我現在就能幫你那麼多,從一百個方面減輕你的負擔。

passages.original: I could find it in my heart to wish I had been, just for that.”
passages.vernacular: 我真心地,光係為此,就希望我曾經係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真心地,光是為此,就希望我曾經是。」

passages.original: “Well now, I’d rather have you than a dozen boys, Anne,” said Matthew patting her hand.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我寧願有你而唔係一打男孩,安妮,」馬修拍住佢嘅手講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我寧願有你而不是一打男孩,安妮,」馬修拍著她的手說。

passages.original: “Just mind you that--rather than a dozen boys.
passages.vernacular: 「你要記住呢個——寧願有你而唔係一打男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要記住這個——寧願有你而不是一打男孩。

passages.original: Well now, I guess it wasn’t a boy that took the Avery scholarship, was it?
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我想攞到艾弗里獎學金嘅唔係男孩,對不對?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我想拿到艾弗里獎學金的不是男孩,對不對?

passages.original: It was a girl--my girl--my girl that I’m proud of.”
passages.vernacular: 係個女孩——我嘅女孩——我為之自豪嘅女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是個女孩——我的女孩——我為之自豪的女孩。」

passages.original: He smiled his shy smile at her as he went into the yard.
passages.vernacular: 佢走進院子時,對佢露出佢害羞嘅微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走進院子時,對她露出他害羞的微笑。

passages.original: Anne took the memory of it with her when she went to her room that night and sat for a long while at her open window, thinking of the past and dreaming of the future.
passages.vernacular: 安妮嗰天晚上回到房間,帶住對佢嘅記憶,喺敞開嘅窗邊坐咗好久,想住過去,夢住未來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮那天晚上回到房間,帶著對它的記憶,在敞開的窗邊坐了很久,想著過去,夢著未來。

passages.original: Outside the Snow Queen was mistily white in the moonshine; the frogs were singing in the marsh beyond Orchard Slope.
passages.vernacular: 窗外雪之女王喺月光下白得朦朧;青蛙喺果園坡嗰邊嘅沼澤里歌唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窗外雪之女王在月光下白得朦朧;青蛙在果園坡那邊的沼澤里歌唱。

passages.original: Anne always remembered the silvery, peaceful beauty and fragrant calm of that night.
passages.vernacular: 安妮永遠記得嗰個夜晚銀色寧靜嘅美同芬芳嘅平靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮永遠記得那個夜晚銀色寧靜的美和芬芳的平靜。

passages.original: It was the last night before sorrow touched her life; and no life is ever quite the same again when once that cold, sanctifying touch has been laid upon it.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係悲傷觸及佢嘅生活之前嘅最後一夜;一旦嗰冰冷而神聖嘅觸摸落喺生活上,任何生命都唔再完全一樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是悲傷觸及她的生活之前的最後一夜;一旦那冰冷而神聖的觸摸落在生活上,任何生命都不再完全一樣了。

chapters.title: Ch. XXXVII The Reaper Whose Name Is Death 第三十七章:名叫死亡的收割者

passages.original: CH MATTHEW--Matthew--what is the matter?
passages.vernacular: 「馬修——馬修——點喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修——馬修——怎麼了?

passages.original: Matthew, are you sick?”
passages.vernacular: 馬修,你病咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬修,你病了嗎?」

passages.original: It was Marilla who spoke, alarm in every jerky word.
passages.vernacular: 講話嘅係瑪麗拉,每一個急促嘅字里都帶住驚慌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說話的是瑪麗拉,每一個急促的字里都帶著驚慌。

passages.original: Anne came through the hall, her hands full of white narcissus,--it was long before Anne could love the sight or odor of white narcissus again,--in time to hear her and to see Matthew standing in the porch doorway, a folded paper in his hand, and his face strangely drawn and gray.
passages.vernacular: 安妮手捧白水仙穿過門廳——好久以後安妮才又能愛上白水仙嘅樣子或香氣——正好聽見佢,並睇到馬修站喺門廊門口,手裡攞住一張折起嚟嘅紙,臉色奇怪地憔悴灰白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮手捧白水仙穿過門廳——很久以後安妮才又能愛上白水仙的樣子或香氣——正好聽見她,並看到馬修站在門廊門口,手裡拿著一張折起來的紙,臉色奇怪地憔悴灰白。

passages.original: Anne dropped her flowers and sprang across the kitchen to him at the same moment as Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 安妮扔下花,同瑪麗拉同時跳過廚房向佢奔去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮扔下花,與瑪麗拉同時跳過廚房向他奔去。

passages.original: They were both too late; before they could reach him Matthew had fallen across the threshold.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都太遲喇;喺佢哋趕到佢身邊之前,馬修已經倒喺咗門檻上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們都太遲了;在她們趕到他身邊之前,馬修已經倒在了門檻上。

passages.original: “He’s fainted,” gasped Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「佢暈過去喇,」瑪麗拉喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他暈過去了,」瑪麗拉喘著氣說。

passages.original: “Anne, run for Martin--quick, quick!
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,快去找馬丁——快,快!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,快去找馬丁——快,快!

passages.original: He’s at the barn.”
passages.vernacular: 佢喺穀倉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在穀倉。」

passages.original: Martin, the hired man, who had just driven home from the post office, started at once for the doctor, calling at Orchard Slope on his way to send Mr. and Mrs. Barry over.
passages.vernacular: 雇工馬丁剛從郵局駕車回嚟,即刻動身去請醫生,路上順便去果園坡,叫巴里夫婦過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雇工馬丁剛從郵局駕車回來,立刻動身去請醫生,路上順便去果園坡,叫巴里夫婦過來。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde, who was there on an errand, came too.
passages.vernacular: 碰巧嚟辦事嘅林德太太都嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 碰巧來辦事的林德太太也來了。

passages.original: They found Anne and Marilla distractedly trying to restore Matthew to consciousness.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋發現安妮同瑪麗拉正慌亂地試圖讓馬修恢復知覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們發現安妮和瑪麗拉正慌亂地試圖讓馬修恢復知覺。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde pushed them gently aside, tried his pulse, and then laid her ear over his heart.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太輕輕把佢哋推到一邊,試咗試佢嘅脈搏,然後把耳朵貼喺佢嘅心口上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太輕輕把她們推到一邊,試了試他的脈搏,然後把耳朵貼在他的心口上。

passages.original: She looked at their anxious faces sorrowfully and the tears came into her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢悲傷地睇住佢哋焦急嘅臉,淚水湧上眼眶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她悲傷地看著她們焦急的臉,淚水湧上眼眶。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla,” she said gravely.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」佢莊重地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,」她莊重地說。

passages.original: “I don’t think--we can do anything for him.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想——我哋乜嘢都為佢做不咗喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想——我們什麼也為他做不了了。」

passages.original: “Mrs. Lynde, you don’t think--you can’t think Matthew is--is--” Anne could not say the dreadful word; she turned sick and pallid.
passages.vernacular: 「林德太太,您不覺得——您唔可能認為馬修係——係——」安妮講不出嗰個可怕嘅字;佢感到噁心,面色蒼白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「林德太太,您不覺得——您不可能認為馬修是——是——」安妮說不出那個可怕的字;她感到噁心,面色蒼白。

passages.original: “Child, yes, I’m afraid of it.
passages.vernacular: 「細路,係嘅,我怕係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「孩子,是的,我怕是這樣。

passages.original: Look at his face.
passages.vernacular: 睇睇佢嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看看他的臉。

passages.original: When you’ve seen that look as often as I have you’ll know what it means.”
passages.vernacular: 等你像我見過咁多次呢種神情,你就知道佢意味住乜嘢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等你像我見過那麼多次這種神情,你就知道它意味著什麼了。」

passages.original: Anne looked at the still face and there beheld the seal of the Great Presence.
passages.vernacular: 安妮睇住嗰張靜止嘅臉,喺上面睇到咗偉大存在嘅印記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮看著那張靜止的臉,在上面看到了偉大存在的印記。

passages.original: When the doctor came he said that death had been instantaneous and probably painless, caused in all likelihood by some sudden shock.
passages.vernacular: 醫生來咗後講,死亡係瞬間嘅,可能冇痛苦,好可能係由某種突然嘅衝擊引起嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生來了後說,死亡是瞬間的,可能沒有痛苦,很可能是由某種突然的衝擊引起的。

passages.original: The secret of the shock was discovered to be in the paper Matthew had held and which Martin had brought from the office that morning.
passages.vernacular: 衝擊嘅祕密被發現就喺馬修手裡攞住嘅嗰張紙里,係嗰天早晨馬丁從郵局帶回嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 衝擊的祕密被發現就在馬修手裡拿著的那張紙里,是那天早晨馬丁從郵局帶回來的。

passages.original: It contained an account of the failure of the Abbey Bank.
passages.vernacular: 上面報道咗艾比銀行倒閉嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面報道了艾比銀行倒閉的消息。

passages.original: The news spread quickly through Avonlea, and all day friends and neighbors thronged Green Gables and came and went on errands of kindness for the dead and living.
passages.vernacular: 消息好快傳遍咗阿文利,整天朋友同鄰居擠滿咗綠色屋頂,為死者同生者嚟來往往地辦事,表達好意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 消息很快傳遍了阿文利,整天朋友和鄰居擠滿了綠色屋頂,為死者和生者來來往往地辦事,表達好意。

passages.original: For the first time shy, quiet Matthew Cuthbert was a person of central importance; the white majesty of death had fallen on him and set him apart as one crowned.
passages.vernacular: 害羞、安靜嘅馬修·卡思伯特第一次成咗舉足輕重嘅人物;死亡白色嘅威嚴降臨喺佢身上,把佢區別出嚟,像係被加冕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 害羞、安靜的馬修·卡思伯特第一次成了舉足輕重的人物;死亡白色的威嚴降臨在他身上,把他區別出來,像是被加冕。

passages.original: When the calm night came softly down over Green Gables the old house was hushed and tranquil.
passages.vernacular: 當寧靜嘅夜晚輕輕降臨綠色屋頂,呢座老房子安靜而祥同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當寧靜的夜晚輕輕降臨綠色屋頂,這座老房子安靜而祥和。

passages.original: In the parlor lay Matthew Cuthbert in his coffin, his long gray hair framing his placid face on which there was a little kindly smile as if he but slept, dreaming pleasant dreams.
passages.vernacular: 喺客廳里,馬修·卡思伯特躺喺棺材裡,佢灰色嘅長髮環繞住佢安詳嘅臉,臉上有一絲慈祥嘅微笑,好像佢只係瞓住喇,做住愉快嘅夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在客廳里,馬修·卡思伯特躺在棺材裡,他灰色的長髮環繞著他安詳的臉,臉上有一絲慈祥的微笑,好像他只是睡著了,做著愉快的夢。

passages.original: There were flowers about him--sweet old-fashioned flowers which his mother had planted in the homestead garden in her bridal days and for which Matthew had always had a secret, wordless love.
passages.vernacular: 佢周圍有花——佢母親新婚時喺老宅花園裡種嘅甜美嘅老式花朵,馬修一直對佢哋有一種祕密嘅、無言嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他周圍有花——他母親新婚時在老宅花園裡種的甜美的老式花朵,馬修一直對它們有一種祕密的、無言的愛。

passages.original: Anne had gathered them and brought them to him, her anguished, tearless eyes burning in her white face.
passages.vernacular: 安妮把佢哋採嚟,帶畀佢,佢痛苦而無淚嘅眼睛喺蒼白嘅臉上燃燒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮把它們採來,帶給他,她痛苦而無淚的眼睛在蒼白的臉上燃燒。

passages.original: It was the last thing she could do for him.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係佢能為佢做嘅最後一件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是她能為他做的最後一件事。

passages.original: The Barrys and Mrs. Lynde stayed with them that night.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上巴里夫婦同林德太太留下陪伴佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上巴里夫婦和林德太太留下陪伴他們。

passages.original: Diana, going to the east gable, where Anne was standing at her window, said gently:
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜走到東山牆房間,安妮正站喺窗邊,溫和地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜走到東山牆房間,安妮正站在窗邊,溫和地說:

passages.original: “Anne dear, would you like to have me sleep with you tonight?”
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅安妮,今晚你想讓我跟你瞓嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的安妮,今晚你想讓我跟你睡嗎?」

passages.original: “Thank you, Diana.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,黛安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,黛安娜。」

passages.original: Anne looked earnestly into her friend’s face.
passages.vernacular: 安妮認真地睇住朋友嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮認真地看著朋友的臉。

passages.original: “I think you won’t misunderstand me when I say I want to be alone.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你唔會誤解我,我想一個人待住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你不會誤解我,我想一個人待著。

passages.original: I’m not afraid.
passages.vernacular: 我不害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不害怕。

passages.original: I haven’t been alone one minute since it happened--and I want to be.
passages.vernacular: 自從事情發生以來,我一分鐘都冇獨處過——我想要獨處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從事情發生以來,我一分鐘也沒獨處過——我想要獨處。

passages.original: I want to be quite silent and quiet and try to realize it.
passages.vernacular: 我想完全安靜平靜,試住意識到呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想完全安靜平靜,試著意識到這件事。

passages.original: I can’t realize it.
passages.vernacular: 我意識唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我意識不到。

passages.original: Half the time it seems to me that Matthew can’t be dead; and the other half it seems as if he must have been dead for a long time and I’ve had this horrible dull ache ever since.”
passages.vernacular: 有一半時間我覺得馬修唔可能死喇;另一半時間又似乎佢一定已經死咗好久,我從嗰時起一直有呢種可怕嘅、鈍鈍嘅痛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一半時間我覺得馬修不可能死了;另一半時間又似乎他一定已經死了很久,我從那時起一直有這種可怕的、鈍鈍的痛。」

passages.original: Diana did not quite understand.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜不太理解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜不太理解。

passages.original: Marilla’s impassioned grief, breaking all the bounds of natural reserve and lifelong habit in its stormy rush, she could comprehend better than Anne’s tearless agony.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉激烈嘅悲傷,以風暴般嘅衝力衝破咗天然嘅矜持同終生習慣嘅一切界限,佢比安妮無淚嘅痛苦更能理解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉激烈的悲傷,以風暴般的衝力衝破了天然的矜持和終生習慣的一切界限,她比安妮無淚的痛苦更能理解。

passages.original: But she went away kindly, leaving Anne alone to keep her first vigil with sorrow.
passages.vernacular: 但佢和善地走喇,留安妮一個人守住佢同悲傷嘅第一次守夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她和善地走了,留安妮一個人守著她與悲傷的第一次守夜。

passages.original: Anne hoped that the tears would come in solitude.
passages.vernacular: 安妮希望眼淚會喺孤獨中到來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮希望眼淚會在孤獨中到來。

passages.original: It seemed to her a terrible thing that she could not shed a tear for Matthew, whom she had loved so much and who had been so kind to her, Matthew who had walked with her last evening at sunset and was now lying in the dim room below with that awful peace on his brow.
passages.vernacular: 佢覺得呢個係件可怕嘅事:佢唔能夠為馬修流一滴淚,佢咁愛佢,佢對佢咁好,馬修琴晚日落時仲同佢同行,而家卻躺喺樓下昏暗嘅房間裡,眉頭帶住嗰可怕嘅平靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她覺得這是件可怕的事:她不能為馬修流一滴淚,她那麼愛他,他對她那麼好,馬修昨晚日落時還與她同行,現在卻躺在樓下昏暗的房間裡,眉頭帶著那可怕的平靜。

passages.original: But no tears came at first, even when she knelt by her window in the darkness and prayed, looking up to the stars beyond the hills--no tears, only the same horrible dull ache of misery that kept on aching until she fell asleep, worn out with the day’s pain and excitement.
passages.vernacular: 但起初冇眼淚嚟,即使佢跪喺黑暗中嘅窗邊禱告,仰望山外嘅星星——冇眼淚,只有同樣可怕嘅、鈍鈍嘅痛苦嘅疼痛,一直痛到佢瞓住,被一天嘅痛苦同激動耗盡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但起初沒有眼淚來,即使她跪在黑暗中的窗邊禱告,仰望山外的星星——沒有眼淚,只有同樣可怕的、鈍鈍的痛苦的疼痛,一直痛到她睡著,被一天的痛苦和激動耗盡。

passages.original: In the night she awakened, with the stillness and the darkness about her, and the recollection of the day came over her like a wave of sorrow.
passages.vernacular: 夜里佢醒嚟,寂靜同黑暗環繞住佢,對呢一天嘅回憶像一股悲傷嘅浪潮湧向佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜里她醒來,寂靜和黑暗環繞著她,對這一天的回憶像一股悲傷的浪潮湧向她。

passages.original: She could see Matthew’s face smiling at her as he had smiled when they parted at the gate that last evening--she could hear his voice saying, “My girl--my girl that I’m proud of.”
passages.vernacular: 佢睇到馬修嘅臉對佢微笑,就像上次傍晚佢哋喺大門口分別時佢微笑嗰樣——佢聽到佢嘅聲音講:「我嘅女孩——我為之自豪嘅女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看到馬修的臉對她微笑,就像上次傍晚他們在大門口分別時他微笑那樣——她聽到他的聲音說:「我的女孩——我為之自豪的女孩。」

passages.original: Then the tears came and Anne wept her heart out.
passages.vernacular: 然後眼淚嚟喇,安妮哭得肝腸寸斷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後眼淚來了,安妮哭得肝腸寸斷。

passages.original: Marilla heard her and crept in to comfort her.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉聽見喇,悄悄進嚟安慰佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉聽見了,悄悄進來安慰她。

passages.original: “There--there--don’t cry so, dearie.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇——好喇——別咁哭,親愛嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了——好了——別這麼哭,親愛的。

passages.original: It can’t bring him back.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔能夠把佢帶回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不能把他帶回來。

passages.original: It--it--isn’t right to cry so.
passages.vernacular: 呢——呢——哭成咁樣不對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這——這——哭成這樣不對。

passages.original: I knew that today, but I couldn’t help it then.
passages.vernacular: 我今日就知道呢啲,但當時我忍不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我今天就知道這一點,但當時我忍不住。

passages.original: He’d always been such a good, kind brother to me--but God knows best.”
passages.vernacular: 佢一直係我咁好嘅、善良嘅哥哥——但上帝最清楚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一直是我那麼好的、善良的哥哥——但上帝最清楚。」

passages.original: “Oh, just let me cry, Marilla,” sobbed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,就讓我哭吧,瑪麗拉,」安妮抽泣道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,就讓我哭吧,瑪麗拉,」安妮抽泣道。

passages.original: “The tears don’t hurt me like that ache did.
passages.vernacular: 「眼淚不像嗰種痛嗰樣傷害我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「眼淚不像那種痛那樣傷害我。

passages.original: Stay here for a little while with me and keep your arm round me--so.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢兒陪我一小會兒,用胳膊摟住我——咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這兒陪我一小會兒,用胳膊摟著我——這樣。

passages.original: I couldn’t have Diana stay, she’s good and kind and sweet--but it’s not her sorrow--she’s outside of it and she couldn’t come close enough to my heart to help me.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠讓黛安娜留下,佢善良、和善、甜美——但呢唔係佢嘅悲傷——佢喺外面,佢無法靠近我嘅心嚟幫助我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能讓黛安娜留下,她善良、和善、甜美——但這不是她的悲傷——她在外面,她無法靠近我的心來幫助我。

passages.original: It’s our sorrow--yours and mine.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我哋嘅悲傷——您嘅同我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我們的悲傷——您的和我的。

passages.original: Oh, Marilla, what will we do without him?”
passages.vernacular: 哦,瑪麗拉,冇佢我哋該點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,瑪麗拉,沒有他我們該怎麼辦?」

passages.original: “We’ve got each other, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋有彼此,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們有彼此,安妮。

passages.original: I don’t know what I’d do if you weren’t here--if you’d never come.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道如果你不喺呢兒——如果你從冇嚟過,我會點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道如果你不在這兒——如果你從沒來過,我會怎麼辦。

passages.original: Oh, Anne, I know I’ve been kind of strict and harsh with you maybe--but you mustn’t think I didn’t love you as well as Matthew did, for all that.
passages.vernacular: 哦,安妮,我知道我對你或者有點嚴厲、苛刻——但你唔好因此認為我不像馬修嗰樣愛你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,安妮,我知道我對你也許有點嚴厲、苛刻——但你不要因此認為我不像馬修那樣愛你。

passages.original: I want to tell you now when I can.
passages.vernacular: 我想趁而家能講嘅時候告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想趁現在能說的時候告訴你。

passages.original: It’s never been easy for me to say things out of my heart, but at times like this it’s easier.
passages.vernacular: 從心底講出事情對我從來唔容易,但喺咁樣嘅時刻,容易些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從心底說出事情對我從來不容易,但在這樣的時刻,容易些。

passages.original: I love you as dear as if you were my own flesh and blood and you’ve been my joy and comfort ever since you came to Green Gables.”
passages.vernacular: 我愛你就像愛我自己嘅親骨肉一樣深,自從你嚟到綠色屋頂,你一直係我嘅快樂同安慰。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛你就像愛我自己的親骨肉一樣深,自從你來到綠色屋頂,你一直是我的快樂和安慰。」

passages.original: Two days afterwards they carried Matthew Cuthbert over his homestead threshold and away from the fields he had tilled and the orchards he had loved and the trees he had planted; and then Avonlea settled back to its usual placidity and even at Green Gables affairs slipped into their old groove and work was done and duties fulfilled with regularity as before, although always with the aching sense of “loss in all familiar things.”
passages.vernacular: 兩天後,佢哋把馬修·卡思伯特抬過佢家嘅門檻,離開佢耕種過嘅田野、佢愛過嘅果園同佢種下嘅樹;然後阿文利恢復咗往常嘅平靜,甚至喺綠色屋頂事務都滑回咗舊有嘅軌道,工作照常完成,職責照常履行,儘管總帶住「一切熟悉事物中嘅失落」嘅疼痛感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩天後,他們把馬修·卡思伯特抬過他家的門檻,離開他耕種過的田野、他愛過的果園和他種下的樹;然後阿文利恢復了往常的平靜,甚至在綠色屋頂事務也滑回了舊有的軌道,工作照常完成,職責照常履行,儘管總帶著「一切熟悉事物中的失落」的疼痛感。

passages.original: Anne, new to grief, thought it almost sad that it could be so--that they could go on in the old way without Matthew.
passages.vernacular: 新近遭遇悲傷嘅安妮,幾乎覺得悲哀嘅係竟然可以咁樣——冇馬修,佢哋竟可以照舊生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 新近遭遇悲傷的安妮,幾乎覺得悲哀的是竟然可以這樣——沒有馬修,他們竟可以照舊生活。

passages.original: She felt something like shame and remorse when she discovered that the sunrises behind the firs and the pale pink buds opening in the garden gave her the old inrush of gladness when she saw them--that Diana’s visits were pleasant to her and that Diana’s merry words and ways moved her to laughter and smiles--that, in brief, the beautiful world of blossom and love and friendship had lost none of its power to please her fancy and thrill her heart, that life still called to her with many insistent voices.
passages.vernacular: 佢發現,睇到冷杉後嘅日出同花園裡綻開嘅淡粉紅花蕾,佢仍有舊日湧嚟嘅喜悅——黛安娜嘅嚟訪使佢愉快,黛安娜歡快嘅言語同舉止使佢發笑同微笑——簡而言之,美麗嘅花朵、愛同友誼嘅世界,冇失去任何悅人幻想、使人心潮澎湃嘅力量,生活仍喺用許多堅持嘅聲音向佢呼喚,佢感到類似羞愧同悔恨嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她發現,看到冷杉後的日出和花園裡綻開的淡粉紅花蕾,她仍有舊日湧來的喜悅——黛安娜的來訪使她愉快,黛安娜歡快的言語和舉止使她發笑和微笑——簡而言之,美麗的花朵、愛和友誼的世界,沒有失去任何悅人幻想、使人心潮澎湃的力量,生活仍在用許多堅持的聲音向她呼喚,她感到類似羞愧和悔恨的東西。

passages.original: “It seems like disloyalty to Matthew, somehow, to find pleasure in these things now that he has gone,” she said wistfully to Mrs. Allan one evening when they were together in the manse garden.
passages.vernacular: 「唔知怎嘅,佢走喇,我而家仲為呢啲事感到愉快,好像係對馬修嘅不忠,」一天傍晚佢哋喺牧師住宅花園裡時,佢悵然地對艾倫太太講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不知怎的,他走了,我現在還為這些事感到愉快,好像是對馬修的不忠,」一天傍晚她們在牧師住宅花園裡時,她悵然地對艾倫太太說。

passages.original: “I miss him so much--all the time--and yet, Mrs. Allan, the world and life seem very beautiful and interesting to me for all.
passages.vernacular: 「我時時刻刻都咁想念佢——然而,艾倫太太,世界同生活對我來講,卻依然顯得好美麗有趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我時時刻刻都那麼想念他——然而,艾倫太太,世界和生活對我來說,卻依然顯得非常美麗有趣。

passages.original: Today Diana said something funny and I found myself laughing.
passages.vernacular: 今日黛安娜講咗件好笑嘅事,我發現自己笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天黛安娜說了件好笑的事,我發現自己笑了。

passages.original: I thought when it happened I could never laugh again.
passages.vernacular: 佢發生時我以為我再都笑不出嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它發生時我以為我再也笑不出來了。

passages.original: And it somehow seems as if I oughtn’t to.”
passages.vernacular: 唔知怎嘅,好像我不該笑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不知怎的,好像我不該笑。」

passages.original: “When Matthew was here he liked to hear you laugh and he liked to know that you found pleasure in the pleasant things around you,” said Mrs. Allan gently.
passages.vernacular: 「馬修喺嘅時候,佢鍾意聽你笑,鍾意知道你喺周圍愉快嘅事物中找到樂趣,」艾倫太太溫和地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬修在的時候,他喜歡聽你笑,喜歡知道你在周圍愉快的事物中找到樂趣,」艾倫太太溫和地說。

passages.original: “He is just away now; and he likes to know it just the same.
passages.vernacular: 「佢而家只係離開喇;佢同樣鍾意知道呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他現在只是離開了;他同樣喜歡知道這一點。

passages.original: I am sure we should not shut our hearts against the healing influences that nature offers us.
passages.vernacular: 我確信我哋不該讓心靈抗拒大自然畀我哋嘅治癒影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信我們不該讓心靈抗拒大自然給我們的治癒影響。

passages.original: But I can understand your feeling.
passages.vernacular: 但我能理解你嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我能理解你的感覺。

passages.original: I think we all experience the same thing.
passages.vernacular: 我想我哋都經歷過同樣嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我們都經歷過同樣的事。

passages.original: We resent the thought that anything can please us when someone we love is no longer here to share the pleasure with us, and we almost feel as if we were unfaithful to our sorrow when we find our interest in life returning to us.”
passages.vernacular: 當我哋愛嘅人唔再喺呢兒同我哋分享快樂時,我哋怨恨任何事能使我哋愉快嘅想法,當我哋發現自己對生活嘅興趣回嚟咗時,我哋幾乎覺得係對悲傷嘅不忠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我們愛的人不再在這兒與我們分享快樂時,我們怨恨任何事能使我們愉快的想法,當我們發現自己對生活的興趣回來了時,我們幾乎覺得是對悲傷的不忠。」

passages.original: “I was down to the graveyard to plant a rosebush on Matthew’s grave this afternoon,” said Anne dreamily.
passages.vernacular: 「今日下午我去墳場喺馬修嘅墳上種咗一株玫瑰,」安妮夢幻般地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今天下午我去墳場在馬修的墳上種了一株玫瑰,」安妮夢幻般地說。

passages.original: “I took a slip of the little white Scotch rosebush his mother brought out from Scotland long ago; Matthew always liked those roses the best--they were so small and sweet on their thorny stems.
passages.vernacular: 「我取咗佢母親好久以前從蘇格蘭帶嚟嘅嗰株小白蘇格蘭玫瑰嘅一枝插條;馬修一直最鍾意嗰啲玫瑰——佢哋喺多刺嘅莖上咁小咁甜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我取了他母親很久以前從蘇格蘭帶來的那株小白蘇格蘭玫瑰的一枝插條;馬修一直最喜歡那些玫瑰——它們在多刺的莖上那麼小那麼甜。

passages.original: It made me feel glad that I could plant it by his grave--as if I were doing something that must please him in taking it there to be near him.
passages.vernacular: 我能把佢種喺佢墳邊,讓我感到高興——好像我把佢帶到嗰兒靠近佢,係喺做一件一定會使佢高興嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能把它種在他墳邊,讓我感到高興——好像我把它帶到那兒靠近他,是在做一件一定會使他高興的事。

passages.original: I hope he has roses like them in heaven.
passages.vernacular: 我希望天堂裡有像佢哋一樣嘅玫瑰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望天堂裡有像它們一樣的玫瑰。

passages.original: Perhaps the souls of all those little white roses that he has loved so many summers were all there to meet him.
passages.vernacular: 或者佢咁多個夏天喜愛過嘅所有嗰啲小白玫瑰嘅靈魂,都喺嗰度迎接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許他這麼多個夏天喜愛過的所有那些小白玫瑰的靈魂,都在那裡迎接他。

passages.original: I must go home now.
passages.vernacular: 我而家必須回家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在必須回家了。

passages.original: Marilla is all alone and she gets lonely at twilight.”
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉一個人喺家,黃昏時佢會孤單。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉一個人在家,黃昏時她會孤單。」

passages.original: “She will be lonelier still, I fear, when you go away again to college,” said Mrs. Allan.
passages.vernacular: 「等你再去上大學,我怕佢會更孤單,」艾倫太太講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等你再去上大學,我怕她會更孤單,」艾倫太太說。

passages.original: Anne did not reply; she said good night and went slowly back to Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 安妮冇回答;佢道咗晚安,慢慢走回綠色屋頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮沒有回答;她道了晚安,慢慢走回綠色屋頂。

passages.original: Marilla was sitting on the front door-steps and Anne sat down beside her.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉坐喺前門台階上,安妮喺佢旁邊坐下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉坐在前門台階上,安妮在她旁邊坐下。

passages.original: The door was open behind them, held back by a big pink conch shell with hints of sea sunsets in its smooth inner convolutions.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋身後嘅門開住,由一隻大粉紅海螺殼擋住,光滑嘅內旋裡隱隱帶住海上日落嘅影子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們身後的門開著,由一隻大粉紅海螺殼擋著,光滑的內旋裡隱隱帶著海上日落的影子。

passages.original: Anne gathered some sprays of pale-yellow honeysuckle and put them in her hair.
passages.vernacular: 安妮採咗幾枝淡黃色嘅忍冬,插喺頭髮裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮採了幾枝淡黃色的忍冬,插在頭髮裡。

passages.original: She liked the delicious hint of fragrance, as some aerial benediction, above her every time she moved.
passages.vernacular: 佢鍾意嗰一絲美妙嘅香氣,像某種空靈嘅祝福,每次佢動一下都喺佢頭上方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她喜歡那一絲美妙的香氣,像某種空靈的祝福,每次她動一下都在她頭上方。

passages.original: “Doctor Spencer was here while you were away,” Marilla said.
passages.vernacular: 「你不喺嘅時候斯潘塞醫生來過,」瑪麗拉講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不在的時候斯潘塞醫生來過,」瑪麗拉說。

passages.original: “He says that the specialist will be in town tomorrow and he insists that I must go in and have my eyes examined.
passages.vernacular: 「佢講專家聽日會喺城裡,佢堅持我必須進城去檢查眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他說專家明天會在城裡,他堅持我必須進城去檢查眼睛。

passages.original: I suppose I’d better go and have it over.
passages.vernacular: 我想我最好去,把佢做喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我最好去,把它做了。

passages.original: I’ll be more than thankful if the man can give me the right kind of glasses to suit my eyes.
passages.vernacular: 如果嗰人能畀我配一副適合我眼睛嘅眼鏡,我會好感激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果那人能給我配一副適合我眼睛的眼鏡,我會非常感激。

passages.original: You won’t mind staying here alone while I’m away, will you?
passages.vernacular: 我不喺時你一個人待住不介意吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不在時你一個人待著不介意吧?

passages.original: Martin will have to drive me in and there’s ironing and baking to do.”
passages.vernacular: 馬丁得趕車送我進城,仲有熨燙同烘焙要做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬丁得趕車送我進城,還有熨燙和烘焙要做。」

passages.original: “I shall be all right.
passages.vernacular: 「我會冇事嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會沒事的。

passages.original: Diana will come over for company for me.
passages.vernacular: 黛安娜會過嚟陪我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黛安娜會過來陪我。

passages.original: I shall attend to the ironing and baking beautifully--you needn’t fear that I’ll starch the handkerchiefs or flavor the cake with liniment.”
passages.vernacular: 我會把熨燙同烘焙做得好漂亮——您唔使擔心我會畀手帕上漿或用擦劑畀蛋糕調味。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會把熨燙和烘焙做得很漂亮——您不必擔心我會給手帕上漿或用擦劑給蛋糕調味。」

passages.original: Marilla laughed.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉笑了。

passages.original: “What a girl you were for making mistakes in them days, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,你嗰啲日子多愛犯錯啊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,你那些日子多愛犯錯啊。

passages.original: You were always getting into scrapes.
passages.vernacular: 你總是惹麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你總是惹麻煩。

passages.original: I did use to think you were possessed.
passages.vernacular: 我過去確實以為你被附身喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我過去確實以為你被附身了。

passages.original: Do you mind the time you dyed your hair?”
passages.vernacular: 你仲記得你染頭髮嗰次嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你還記得你染頭髮那次嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, indeed.
passages.vernacular: 「記得,真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「記得,真的。

passages.original: I shall never forget it,” smiled Anne, touching the heavy braid of hair that was wound about her shapely head.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠唔會忘記,」安妮微笑住講,摸住盤喺佢勻稱頭上嘅粗辮子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠不會忘記,」安妮微笑著說,摸著盤在她勻稱頭上的粗辮子。

passages.original: “I laugh a little now sometimes when I think what a worry my hair used to be to me--but I don’t laugh much, because it was a very real trouble then.
passages.vernacular: 「而家想到我嘅頭髮過去畀我造成多大煩惱,我有時有點想笑——但笑得不多,因為嗰時係真正嘅苦惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在想到我的頭髮過去給我造成多大煩惱,我有時有點想笑——但笑得不多,因為那時是真正的苦惱。

passages.original: I did suffer terribly over my hair and my freckles.
passages.vernacular: 我確實為我嘅頭髮同雀斑痛苦得厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確實為我的頭髮和雀斑痛苦得厲害。

passages.original: My freckles are really gone; and people are nice enough to tell me my hair is auburn now--all but Josie Pye.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅雀斑真嘅冇喇;人哋好心地講我嘅頭髮而家係赤褐色——除咗喬西·派伊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的雀斑真的沒了;人們好心地說我的頭髮現在是赤褐色——除了喬西·派伊。

passages.original: She informed me yesterday that she really thought it was redder than ever, or at least my black dress made it look redder, and she asked me if people who had red hair ever got used to having it.
passages.vernacular: 佢尋日告訴我,佢真覺得佢比以往更紅喇,或者至少我嘅黑裙子讓佢顯得更紅,佢問我紅頭髮嘅人係咪終究習慣咗有紅頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她昨天告訴我,她真覺得它比以往更紅了,或者至少我的黑裙子讓它顯得更紅,她問我紅頭髮的人是否終究習慣了有紅頭髮。

passages.original: Marilla, I’ve almost decided to give up trying to like Josie Pye.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉,我差不多決定放棄試住鍾意喬西·派伊喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉,我差不多決定放棄試著喜歡喬西·派伊了。

passages.original: I’ve made what I would once have called a heroic effort to like her, but Josie Pye won’t be liked.”
passages.vernacular: 我曾作出過我以前會稱之為英勇嘅努力去鍾意佢,但喬西·派伊唔肯被人鍾意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我曾作出過我以前會稱之為英勇的努力去喜歡她,但喬西·派伊不肯被人喜歡。」

passages.original: “Josie is a Pye,” said Marilla sharply, “so she can’t help being disagreeable.
passages.vernacular: 「喬西係個派伊,」瑪麗拉尖銳地講,「所以佢免不咗令人討厭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喬西是個派伊,」瑪麗拉尖銳地說,「所以她免不了令人討厭。

passages.original: I suppose people of that kind serve some useful purpose in society, but I must say I don’t know what it is any more than I know the use of thistles.
passages.vernacular: 我想嗰一類嘅人喺社會上有某種用處,但我必須講我唔知道係乜嘢,就像我唔知道薊嘅用處一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想那一類的人在社會上有某種用處,但我必須說我不知道是什麼,就像我不知道薊的用處一樣。

passages.original: Is Josie going to teach?”
passages.vernacular: 喬西要去教書嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西要去教書嗎?」

passages.original: “No, she is going back to Queen’s next year.
passages.vernacular: 「不,佢明年回女王學院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,她明年回女王學院。

passages.original: So are Moody Spurgeon and Charlie Sloane.
passages.vernacular: 穆迪·斯珀吉翁同查理·斯隆都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 穆迪·斯珀吉翁和查理·斯隆也是。

passages.original: Jane and Ruby are going to teach and they have both got schools--Jane at Newbridge and Ruby at some place up west.”
passages.vernacular: 簡同露比要去教書,佢哋都找到咗學校——簡喺新橋,露比喺西部乜嘢地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡和露比要去教書,她們都找到了學校——簡在新橋,露比在西部什麼地方。」

passages.original: “Gilbert Blythe is going to teach too, isn’t he?”
passages.vernacular: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯都要去教書,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯也要去教書,是不是?」

passages.original: “Yes”--briefly.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅」——簡短地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的」——簡短地。

passages.original: “What a nice-looking fellow he is,” said Marilla absently.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係個幾咁好睇嘅小伙子,」瑪麗拉心不喺焉地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是個多麼好看的小伙子,」瑪麗拉心不在焉地說。

passages.original: “I saw him in church last Sunday and he seemed so tall and manly.
passages.vernacular: 「上星期天我喺教堂睇到佢,佢顯得咁高大有男子氣概。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「上星期天我在教堂看到他,他顯得那麼高大有男子氣概。

passages.original: He looks a lot like his father did at the same age.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇上去好像佢父親喺同樣年紀時嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看上去很像他父親在同樣年紀時的樣子。

passages.original: John Blythe was a nice boy.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·布萊斯係個好男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·布萊斯是個好男孩。

passages.original: We used to be real good friends, he and I. People called him my beau.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋過去係真正嘅好朋友,佢同我。人哋叫佢我嘅情郎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們過去是真正的好朋友,他和我。人們叫他我的情郎。」

passages.original: Anne looked up with swift interest.
passages.vernacular: 安妮迅速感興趣地抬起頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮迅速感興趣地抬起頭。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla--and what happened?--why didn’t you--”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉——後來點喇?——您點解冇——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉——後來怎麼了?——您為什麼沒有——」

passages.original: “We had a quarrel.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋吵咗一架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們吵了一架。

passages.original: I wouldn’t forgive him when he asked me to.
passages.vernacular: 佢要求我原諒佢時,我唔肯原諒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他要求我原諒他時,我不肯原諒。

passages.original: I meant to, after awhile--but I was sulky and angry and I wanted to punish him first.
passages.vernacular: 我本打算過一陣子就原諒——但我當時鬧彆扭、生氣,想先懲罰佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我本打算過一陣子就原諒——但我當時鬧彆扭、生氣,想先懲罰他。

passages.original: He never came back--the Blythes were all mighty independent.
passages.vernacular: 佢再都冇回嚟——布萊斯家嘅人都極其獨立。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他再也沒回來——布萊斯家的人都極其獨立。

passages.original: But I always felt--rather sorry.
passages.vernacular: 但我總覺得——相當遺憾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我總覺得——相當遺憾。

passages.original: I’ve always kind of wished I’d forgiven him when I had the chance.”
passages.vernacular: 我總是有點希望當初有機會時原諒咗佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我總是有點希望當初有機會時原諒了他。」

passages.original: “So you’ve had a bit of romance in your life, too,” said Anne softly.
passages.vernacular: 「所以您嘅生活中都有過啲浪漫,」安妮輕聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所以您的生活中也有過一點浪漫,」安妮輕聲說。

passages.original: “Yes, I suppose you might call it that.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我想你可以咁稱呼佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我想你可以這麼稱呼它。

passages.original: You wouldn’t think so to look at me, would you?
passages.vernacular: 睇我嘅樣子你唔會咁想,係吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看我的樣子你不會這麼想,是吧?

passages.original: But you never can tell about people from their outsides.
passages.vernacular: 但係你永遠唔能夠從外表判斷人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是你永遠不能從外表判斷人。

passages.original: Everybody has forgot about me and John.
passages.vernacular: 大家都忘記咗我和約翰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家都忘記了我和約翰。

passages.original: I’d forgotten myself.
passages.vernacular: 我自己都忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己也忘了。

passages.original: But it all came back to me when I saw Gilbert last Sunday.”
passages.vernacular: 但上星期天我睇到吉爾伯特時,一切又都回嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但上星期天我看到吉爾伯特時,一切又都回來了。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXXVIII The Bend in the Road 第三十八章:路上的轉彎處

passages.original: CH MARILLA went to town the next day and returned in the evening.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉第二天進城,傍晚回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉第二天進城,傍晚回來。

passages.original: Anne had gone over to Orchard Slope with Diana and came back to find Marilla in the kitchen, sitting by the table with her head leaning on her hand.
passages.vernacular: 安妮同黛安娜去咗果園坡,回嚟時發現瑪麗拉喺廚房,坐喺桌邊,頭靠喺手上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮和黛安娜去了果園坡,回來時發現瑪麗拉在廚房,坐在桌邊,頭靠在手上。

passages.original: Something in her dejected attitude struck a chill to Anne’s heart.
passages.vernacular: 佢嗰沮喪嘅姿態中有某種嘢使安妮心中一寒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她那沮喪的姿態中有某種東西使安妮心中一寒。

passages.original: She had never seen Marilla sit limply inert like that.
passages.vernacular: 佢從冇見過瑪麗拉咁樣軟綿綿、無精打采地坐住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她從沒見過瑪麗拉這樣軟綿綿、無精打采地坐著。

passages.original: “Are you very tired, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 「您好累嗎,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您很累嗎,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: “Yes--no--I don’t know,” said Marilla wearily, looking up.
passages.vernacular: 「係——唔係——我唔知道,」瑪麗拉疲倦地講,抬起頭嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是——不是——我不知道,」瑪麗拉疲倦地說,抬起頭來。

passages.original: “I suppose I am tired but I haven’t thought about it.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我係累喇,但我冇想過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我是累了,但我沒想過。

passages.original: It’s not that.”
passages.vernacular: 唔係嗰個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是那個。」

passages.original: “Did you see the oculist?
passages.vernacular: 「您見到眼科醫生咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您見到眼科醫生了嗎?

passages.original: What did he say?” asked Anne anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 佢點講?」安妮焦急地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他怎麼說?」安妮焦急地問。

passages.original: “Yes, I saw him.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我見到佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我見到他了。

passages.original: He examined my eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢檢查咗我嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他檢查了我的眼睛。

passages.original: He says that if I give up all reading and sewing entirely and any kind of work that strains the eyes, and if I’m careful not to cry, and if I wear the glasses he’s given me he thinks my eyes may not get any worse and my headaches will be cured.
passages.vernacular: 佢講如果我完全放棄閱讀、縫紉同任何傷眼睛嘅工作,如果我小心不哭,如果我戴佢畀我嘅眼鏡,佢認為我嘅眼睛或者唔會更壞,我嘅頭疼會治好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說如果我完全放棄閱讀、縫紉和任何傷眼睛的工作,如果我小心不哭,如果我戴他給我的眼鏡,他認為我的眼睛也許不會更壞,我的頭疼會治好。

passages.original: But if I don’t he says I’ll certainly be stone-blind in six months.
passages.vernacular: 但係如果我不咁樣,佢講我六個月內肯定會全盲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是如果我不這樣,他說我六個月內肯定會全盲。

passages.original: Blind!
passages.vernacular: 失明!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 失明!

passages.original: Anne, just think of it!”
passages.vernacular: 安妮,你想想睇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮,你想想看!」

passages.original: For a minute Anne, after her first quick exclamation of dismay, was silent.
passages.vernacular: 安妮喺最初嘅一聲驚慌嘅驚呼之後,沉默咗一分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮在最初的一聲驚慌的驚呼之後,沉默了一分鐘。

passages.original: It seemed to her that she could not speak.
passages.vernacular: 佢似乎講不出話嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她似乎說不出話來。

passages.original: Then she said bravely, but with a catch in her voice:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢勇敢地講,但聲音哽咽:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她勇敢地說,但聲音哽咽:

passages.original: “Marilla, don’t think of it.
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉,唔好去想佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉,別去想它。

passages.original: You know he has given you hope.
passages.vernacular: 您知道佢畀咗您希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道他給了您希望。

passages.original: If you are careful you won’t lose your sight altogether; and if his glasses cure your headaches it will be a great thing.”
passages.vernacular: 如果您小心,您唔會完全失去視力;如果佢嘅眼鏡治好咗您嘅頭疼,嗰個係件大好事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您小心,您不會完全失去視力;如果他的眼鏡治好了您的頭疼,那是件大好事。」

passages.original: “I don’t call it much hope,” said Marilla bitterly.
passages.vernacular: 「我不覺得呢算多少希望,」瑪麗拉苦澀地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不覺得這算多少希望,」瑪麗拉苦澀地說。

passages.original: “What am I to live for if I can’t read or sew or do anything like that?
passages.vernacular: 「如果我唔能夠讀書、縫紉或做任何呢類事情,我靠乜嘢活住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我不能讀書、縫紉或做任何這類事情,我靠什麼活著?

passages.original: I might as well be blind--or dead.
passages.vernacular: 我不如瞎喇——或死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不如瞎了——或死了。

passages.original: And as for crying, I can’t help that when I get lonesome.
passages.vernacular: 至於哭,我孤單嘅時候忍不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於哭,我孤單的時候忍不住。

passages.original: But there, it’s no good talking about it.
passages.vernacular: 不過,談論佢冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,談論它沒用。

passages.original: If you’ll get me a cup of tea I’ll be thankful.
passages.vernacular: 你要係畀我倒杯茶,我會好感激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要是給我倒杯茶,我會很感激。

passages.original: I’m about done out.
passages.vernacular: 我快撐不住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我快撐不住了。

passages.original: Don’t say anything about this to any one for a spell yet, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 呢件事,暫時不管點樣,別對任何人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這件事,暫時不管怎樣,別對任何人說。

passages.original: I can’t bear that folks should come here to question and sympathize and talk about it.”
passages.vernacular: 我受不了人哋嚟呢兒詢問、同情、談論佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我受不了人們來這兒詢問、同情、談論它。」

passages.original: When Marilla had eaten her lunch Anne persuaded her to go to bed.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉食完點心,安妮勸佢去瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉吃完點心,安妮勸她去睡覺。

passages.original: Then Anne went herself to the east gable and sat down by her window in the darkness alone with her tears and her heaviness of heart.
passages.vernacular: 然後安妮自己去咗東山牆房間,喺黑暗中坐喺窗邊,獨自同佢嘅眼淚同沉重嘅心喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後安妮自己去了東山牆房間,在黑暗中坐在窗邊,獨自與她的眼淚和沉重的心在一起。

passages.original: How sadly things had changed since she had sat there the night after coming home!
passages.vernacular: 自從回家嘅嗰個晚上佢坐喺嗰兒以來,事情變得幾咁悲哀啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從回家的那個晚上她坐在那兒以來,事情變得多麼悲哀啊!

passages.original: Then she had been full of hope and joy and the future had looked rosy with promise.
passages.vernacular: 嗰時佢充滿希望同喜悅,未來睇上去充滿玫瑰色嘅承諾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時她充滿希望和喜悅,未來看上去充滿玫瑰色的承諾。

passages.original: Anne felt as if she had lived years since then, but before she went to bed there was a smile on her lips and peace in her heart.
passages.vernacular: 安妮覺得自嗰時起彷彿過咗好多年,但喺上床前,佢嘅唇上有微笑,心中有平靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮覺得自那時起彷彿過了好多年,但在上床前,她的唇上有微笑,心中有平靜。

passages.original: She had looked her duty courageously in the face and found it a friend--as duty ever is when we meet it frankly.
passages.vernacular: 佢勇敢地直視咗佢嘅責任,發現佢係一位朋友——當我哋坦率地面對責任時,佢總是如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她勇敢地直視了她的責任,發現它是一位朋友——當我們坦率地面對責任時,它總是如此。

passages.original: One afternoon a few days later Marilla came slowly in from the front yard where she had been talking to a caller--a man whom Anne knew by sight as Sadler from Carmody.
passages.vernacular: 幾天後嘅一個下午,瑪麗拉慢慢從前院走進嚟,佢一直喺嗰兒同一位訪客講話——安妮認得嗰人係卡莫迪嘅賽德勒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾天後的一個下午,瑪麗拉慢慢從前院走進來,她一直在那兒與一位訪客說話——安妮認得那人是卡莫迪的賽德勒。

passages.original: Anne wondered what he could have been saying to bring that look to Marilla’s face.
passages.vernacular: 安妮納悶佢講咗乜嘢才讓瑪麗拉臉上有嗰種神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮納悶他說了什麼才讓瑪麗拉臉上有那種神情。

passages.original: “What did Mr. Sadler want, Marilla?”
passages.vernacular: 「賽德勒先生要乜嘢,瑪麗拉?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「賽德勒先生要什麼,瑪麗拉?」

passages.original: Marilla sat down by the window and looked at Anne.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉喺窗邊坐下,睇住安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉在窗邊坐下,看著安妮。

passages.original: There were tears in her eyes in defiance of the oculist’s prohibition and her voice broke as she said:
passages.vernacular: 佢眼裡含住淚,違背咗眼科醫生嘅禁令,佢嘅聲音哽住喇,講道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她眼裡含著淚,違背了眼科醫生的禁令,她的聲音哽住了,說道:

passages.original: “He heard that I was going to sell Green Gables and he wants to buy it.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢聽講我要賣綠色屋頂,佢想買佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他聽說我要賣綠色屋頂,他想買它。」

passages.original: “Buy it!
passages.vernacular: 「買佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「買它!

passages.original: Buy Green Gables?”
passages.vernacular: 買綠色屋頂?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 買綠色屋頂?」

passages.original: Anne wondered if she had heard aright.
passages.vernacular: 安妮懷疑自己係咪聽對喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮懷疑自己是否聽對了。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, you don’t mean to sell Green Gables!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,您唔係講要賣綠色屋頂吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,您不是說要賣綠色屋頂吧!」

passages.original: “Anne, I don’t know what else is to be done.
passages.vernacular: 「安妮,我唔知道仲有乜嘢別嘅辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮,我不知道還有什麼別的辦法。

passages.original: I’ve thought it all over.
passages.vernacular: 我全都想過喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我全都想過了。

passages.original: If my eyes were strong I could stay here and make out to look after things and manage, with a good hired man.
passages.vernacular: 如果我嘅眼睛好,我可以留喺呢兒,設法照睇,喺一個好嘅雇工幫助下應付。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我的眼睛好,我可以留在這兒,設法照看,在一個好的雇工幫助下應付。

passages.original: But as it is I can’t.
passages.vernacular: 但而家咁樣我做唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在這樣我做不到。

passages.original: I may lose my sight altogether; and anyway I’ll not be fit to run things.
passages.vernacular: 我可能完全失明;不管點樣我都不適合管事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可能完全失明;不管怎樣我都不適合管事了。

passages.original: Oh, I never thought I’d live to see the day when I’d have to sell my home.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我從冇想過我會活到唔得不賣掉家嘅嗰一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我從沒想過我會活到不得不賣掉家的那一天。

passages.original: But things would only go behind worse and worse all the time, till nobody would want to buy it.
passages.vernacular: 但係事情只會越嚟越糟,直到冇人想買佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是事情只會越來越糟,直到沒人想買它。

passages.original: Every cent of our money went in that bank; and there’s some notes Matthew gave last fall to pay.
passages.vernacular: 我哋所有嘅錢都投喺嗰家銀行里喇;仲有馬修去年秋天開嘅啲要付嘅票據。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們所有的錢都投在那家銀行里了;還有馬修去年秋天開的一些要付的票據。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde advises me to sell the farm and board somewhere--with her I suppose.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太建議我賣掉農場,喺乜嘢地方寄宿——我想係同佢住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太建議我賣掉農場,在什麼地方寄宿——我想是和她住。

passages.original: It won’t bring much--it’s small and the buildings are old.
passages.vernacular: 佢賣不咗多少錢——佢小,房子又舊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它賣不了多少錢——它小,房子又舊。

passages.original: But it’ll be enough for me to live on I reckon.
passages.vernacular: 但我想夠我生活喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我想夠我生活了。

passages.original: I’m thankful you’re provided for with that scholarship, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 我感謝你有咗嗰筆獎學金,安妮,生活有保障。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感謝你有了那筆獎學金,安妮,生活有保障。

passages.original: I’m sorry you won’t have a home to come to in your vacations, that’s all, but I suppose you’ll manage somehow.”
passages.vernacular: 我只係難過你放假時冇家可回,就咁樣,但我想你總能想辦法。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是難過你放假時沒有家可回,就這樣,但我想你總能想辦法。」

passages.original: Marilla broke down and wept bitterly.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉崩潰喇,痛哭起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉崩潰了,痛哭起來。

passages.original: “You mustn’t sell Green Gables,” said Anne resolutely.
passages.vernacular: 「您唔能夠賣綠色屋頂,」安妮堅決地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您不能賣綠色屋頂,」安妮堅決地說。

passages.original: “Oh, Anne, I wish I didn’t have to.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,安妮,我都希望唔使賣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,安妮,我也希望不用賣。

passages.original: But you can see for yourself.
passages.vernacular: 但你自己睇得出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你自己看得出。

passages.original: I can’t stay here alone.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠一個人待喺呢兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能一個人待在這兒。

passages.original: I’d go crazy with trouble and loneliness.
passages.vernacular: 我會被煩惱同孤獨逼瘋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會被煩惱和孤獨逼瘋。

passages.original: And my sight would go--I know it would.”
passages.vernacular: 而且我嘅視力會喪失——我知道會嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我的視力會喪失——我知道會的。」

passages.original: “You won’t have to stay here alone, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 「您唔使一個人待喺呢兒,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您不用一個人待在這兒,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I’ll be with you.
passages.vernacular: 我會同您喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會和您在一起。

passages.original: I’m not going to Redmond.”
passages.vernacular: 我不去雷德蒙喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不去雷德蒙了。」

passages.original: “Not going to Redmond!”
passages.vernacular: 「不去雷德蒙!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不去雷德蒙!」

passages.original: Marilla lifted her worn face from her hands and looked at Anne.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉從手中抬起佢憔悴嘅臉,睇住安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉從手中抬起她憔悴的臉,看著安妮。

passages.original: “Why, what do you mean?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,你係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,你是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “Just what I say.
passages.vernacular: 「就係我講嘅意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是我說的意思。

passages.original: I’m not going to take the scholarship.
passages.vernacular: 我不去領嗰個獎學金喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不去領那個獎學金了。

passages.original: I decided so the night after you came home from town.
passages.vernacular: 您從城里回嚟嘅嗰天晚上,我就咁決定喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您從城里回來的那天晚上,我就這麼決定了。

passages.original: You surely don’t think I could leave you alone in your trouble, Marilla, after all you’ve done for me.
passages.vernacular: 您肯定唔會認為喺您遇到困難時,我能撇下您一個人,瑪麗拉,喺您為我做咗呢一切之後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您肯定不會認為在您遇到困難時,我能撇下您一個人,瑪麗拉,在您為我做了這一切之後。

passages.original: I’ve been thinking and planning.
passages.vernacular: 我一直喺思考同計劃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直在思考和計劃。

passages.original: Let me tell you my plans.
passages.vernacular: 讓我告訴您我嘅計劃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我告訴您我的計劃。

passages.original: Mr. Barry wants to rent the farm for next year.
passages.vernacular: 巴里先生想租下農場明年用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里先生想租下農場明年用。

passages.original: So you won’t have any bother over that.
passages.vernacular: 所以您喺呢方面唔使操心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以您在這方面不用操心。

passages.original: And I’m going to teach.
passages.vernacular: 我要去教書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要去教書。

passages.original: I’ve applied for the school here--but I don’t expect to get it for I understand the trustees have promised it to Gilbert Blythe.
passages.vernacular: 我申請咗呢度嘅學校——但我不指望得到,因為我知道校董哋已經答應畀吉爾伯特·布萊斯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我申請了這裡的學校——但我不指望得到,因為我知道校董們已經答應給吉爾伯特·布萊斯了。

passages.original: But I can have the Carmody school--Mr. Blair told me so last night at the store.
passages.vernacular: 但我可以得到卡莫迪嘅學校——布萊爾先生琴晚喺店裡告訴我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我可以得到卡莫迪的學校——布萊爾先生昨晚在店裡告訴我的。

passages.original: Of course that won’t be quite as nice or convenient as if I had the Avonlea school.
passages.vernacular: 當然嗰唔會像我得到阿文利學校咁好或方便。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然那不會像我得到阿文利學校那麼好或方便。

passages.original: But I can board home and drive myself over to Carmody and back, in the warm weather at least.
passages.vernacular: 但係我可以喺家食住,自己駕車去卡莫迪再回嚟,至少喺暖同嘅天氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是我可以在家吃住,自己駕車去卡莫迪再回來,至少在暖和的天氣。

passages.original: And even in winter I can come home Fridays.
passages.vernacular: 甚至冬天我都可以星期五回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 甚至冬天我也可以星期五回家。

passages.original: We’ll keep a horse for that.
passages.vernacular: 我哋為此養一匹馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們為此養一匹馬。

passages.original: Oh, I have it all planned out, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我全都計劃好喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我全都計劃好了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: And I’ll read to you and keep you cheered up.
passages.vernacular: 我仲要讀書畀您聽,讓您保持愉快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還要讀書給您聽,讓您保持愉快。

passages.original: You sha’n’t be dull or lonesome.
passages.vernacular: 您唔會沉悶或孤單。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不會沉悶或孤單。

passages.original: And we’ll be real cozy and happy here together, you and I.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺呢度一起會好舒適、幸福,您同我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在這裡一起會非常舒適、幸福,您和我。」

passages.original: Marilla had listened like a woman in a dream.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗拉像做夢嘅人一樣聽住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拉像做夢的人一樣聽著。

passages.original: “Oh, Anne, I could get on real well if you were here, I know.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,安妮,如果你喺呢兒,我能過得相當好,我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,安妮,如果你在這兒,我能過得相當好,我知道。

passages.original: But I can’t let you sacrifice yourself so for me.
passages.vernacular: 但我唔能夠讓你咁樣為我犧牲自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不能讓你這樣為我犧牲自己。

passages.original: It would be terrible.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰太可怕喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那太可怕了。」

passages.original: “Nonsense!”
passages.vernacular: 「胡講!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說!」

passages.original: Anne laughed merrily.
passages.vernacular: 安妮快活地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮快活地笑了。

passages.original: “There is no sacrifice.
passages.vernacular: 「冇犧牲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有犧牲。

passages.original: Nothing could be worse than giving up Green Gables--nothing could hurt me more.
passages.vernacular: 冇乜嘢比放棄綠色屋頂更糟嘅喇——冇乜嘢比呢更傷我嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有什麼比放棄綠色屋頂更糟的了——沒有什麼比這更傷我的心。

passages.original: We must keep the dear old place.
passages.vernacular: 我哋必須保住呢個親愛嘅老地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們必須保住這個親愛的老地方。

passages.original: My mind is quite made up, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 我已經完全攞定主意喇,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經完全拿定主意了,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I’m not going to Redmond; and I am going to stay here and teach.
passages.vernacular: 我不去雷德蒙喇;我要留喺呢兒教書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不去雷德蒙了;我要留在這兒教書。

passages.original: Don’t you worry about me a bit.”
passages.vernacular: 您別為我擔心啲點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您別為我擔心一點點。」

passages.original: “But your ambitions--and--”
passages.vernacular: 「但係你嘅雄心——仲有——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是你的雄心——還有——」

passages.original: “I’m just as ambitious as ever.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅雄心同以前一樣大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的雄心和以前一樣大。

passages.original: Only, I’ve changed the object of my ambitions.
passages.vernacular: 只係我改變咗雄心嘅對象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是我改變了雄心的對象。

passages.original: I’m going to be a good teacher--and I’m going to save your eyesight.
passages.vernacular: 我要做個好老師——我要保住您嘅視力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要做個好老師——我要保住您的視力。

passages.original: Besides, I mean to study at home here and take a little college course all by myself.
passages.vernacular: 再講,我打算喺呢兒家裡學習,自己學一個小小嘅大學課程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再說,我打算在這兒家裡學習,自己學一個小小的大學課程。

passages.original: Oh, I’ve dozens of plans, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我有幾十個計劃,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我有幾十個計劃,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I’ve been thinking them out for a week.
passages.vernacular: 我已經琢磨咗一個星期喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經琢磨了一個星期了。

passages.original: I shall give life here my best, and I believe it will give its best to me in return.
passages.vernacular: 我要把最好嘅畀予呢度嘅生活,我相信佢都會把最好嘅回報畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把最好的給予這裡的生活,我相信它也會把最好的回報給我。

passages.original: When I left Queen’s my future seemed to stretch out before me like a straight road.
passages.vernacular: 我離開女王學院時,我嘅未來喺我面前似乎像一條筆直嘅路伸展。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我離開女王學院時,我的未來在我面前似乎像一條筆直的路伸展。

passages.original: I thought I could see along it for many a milestone.
passages.vernacular: 我以為我能沿住佢睇到許多里程碑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以為我能沿著它看到許多里程碑。

passages.original: Now there is a bend in it.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢有咗一個轉彎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在它有了一個轉彎。

passages.original: I don’t know what lies around the bend, but I’m going to believe that the best does.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道轉彎處有乜嘢,但我要相信最好嘅就喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道轉彎處有什麼,但我要相信最好的就在那裡。

passages.original: It has a fascination of its own, that bend, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個轉彎有佢自己嘅魅力,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個轉彎有它自己的魅力,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I wonder how the road beyond it goes--what there is of green glory and soft, checkered light and shadows--what new landscapes--what new beauties--what curves and hills and valleys further on.”
passages.vernacular: 我想知道轉彎之後嘅路係點樣嘅——嗰度有乜嘢綠色嘅榮光、柔和嘅斑駁嘅光同影——乜嘢新嘅景色——乜嘢新嘅美——前面仲有乜嘢彎道、山丘同山谷。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想知道轉彎之後的路是怎樣的——那裡有什麼綠色的榮光、柔和的斑駁的光與影——什麼新的景色——什麼新的美——前面還有什麼彎道、山丘和山谷。」

passages.original: “I don’t feel as if I ought to let you give it up,” said Marilla, referring to the scholarship.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得我不該讓你放棄佢,」瑪麗拉講,指獎學金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得我不該讓你放棄它,」瑪麗拉說,指獎學金。

passages.original: “But you can’t prevent me.
passages.vernacular: 「但您阻止不咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但您阻止不了我。

passages.original: I’m sixteen and a half, ‘obstinate as a mule,’ as Mrs. Lynde once told me,” laughed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 我十六歲半喇,『像騾子一樣固執』,林德太太曾咁告訴我,」安妮笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我十六歲半了,『像騾子一樣固執』,林德太太曾這麼告訴我,」安妮笑著說。

passages.original: “Oh, Marilla, don’t you go pitying me.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,瑪麗拉,您別可憐我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,瑪麗拉,您別可憐我。

passages.original: I don’t like to be pitied, and there is no need for it.
passages.vernacular: 我不鍾意被可憐,而且冇必要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不喜歡被可憐,而且沒有必要。

passages.original: I’m heart glad over the very thought of staying at dear Green Gables.
passages.vernacular: 一想到留喺親愛嘅綠色屋頂,我就從心底裡高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一想到留在親愛的綠色屋頂,我就從心底裡高興。

passages.original: Nobody could love it as you and I do--so we must keep it.”
passages.vernacular: 冇人能像您同我一樣愛佢——所以我哋必須保住佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人能像您和我一樣愛它——所以我們必須保住它。」

passages.original: “You blessed girl!” said Marilla, yielding.
passages.vernacular: 「你呢個可愛嘅女孩!」瑪麗拉屈服喇,講道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你這個可愛的女孩!」瑪麗拉屈服了,說道。

passages.original: “I feel as if you’d given me new life.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得你畀咗我新生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得你給了我新生。

passages.original: I guess I ought to stick out and make you go to college--but I know I can’t, so I ain’t going to try.
passages.vernacular: 我想我應該堅持,讓你去上大學——但我知道我做唔到,所以我不打算試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我應該堅持,讓你去上大學——但我知道我做不到,所以我不打算試。

passages.original: I’ll make it up to you though, Anne.”
passages.vernacular: 不過我會補償你,安妮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我會補償你,安妮。」

passages.original: When it became noised abroad in Avonlea that Anne Shirley had given up the idea of going to college and intended to stay home and teach there was a good deal of discussion over it.
passages.vernacular: 安妮·雪莉放棄咗上大學嘅想法、打算留喺家裡教書嘅消息喺阿文利傳開時,引起咗不少議論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮·雪莉放棄了上大學的想法、打算留在家裡教書的消息在阿文利傳開時,引起了不少議論。

passages.original: Most of the good folks, not knowing about Marilla’s eyes, thought she was foolish.
passages.vernacular: 大部分好人,唔知道瑪麗拉嘅眼睛,都認為佢傻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大部分好人,不知道瑪麗拉的眼睛,都認為她傻。

passages.original: Mrs. Allan did not.
passages.vernacular: 艾倫太太不咁樣想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾倫太太不這樣想。

passages.original: She told Anne so in approving words that brought tears of pleasure to the girl’s eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢用讚許嘅話告訴咗安妮,呢啲話使女孩嘅眼里湧出喜悅嘅淚水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她用讚許的話告訴了安妮,這些話使女孩的眼里湧出喜悅的淚水。

passages.original: Neither did good Mrs. Lynde.
passages.vernacular: 好心嘅林德太太都不咁樣想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好心的林德太太也不這樣想。

passages.original: She came up one evening and found Anne and Marilla sitting at the front door in the warm, scented summer dusk.
passages.vernacular: 一天傍晚佢上嚟,發現安妮同瑪麗拉坐喺前門,喺溫暖芬芳嘅夏日暮色中。
