passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天傍晚她上來,發現安妮和瑪麗拉坐在前門,在溫暖芬芳的夏日暮色中。

passages.original: They liked to sit there when the twilight came down and the white moths flew about in the garden and the odor of mint filled the dewy air.
passages.vernacular: 暮色降臨,白蛾喺花園裡飛舞,薄荷嘅氣味充滿露水嘅空氣時,佢哋鍾意坐喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暮色降臨,白蛾在花園裡飛舞,薄荷的氣味充滿露水的空氣時,她們喜歡坐在那裡。

passages.original: Mrs. Rachel deposited her substantial person upon the stone bench by the door, behind which grew a row of tall pink and yellow hollyhocks, with a long breath of mingled weariness and relief.
passages.vernacular: 雷切爾太太把佢結實嘅身軀安放喺門邊嘅石凳上,後面長住一排高大嘅粉紅同黃色蜀葵,佢長長地呼咗口氣,疲倦同寬慰交織。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷切爾太太把她結實的身軀安放在門邊的石凳上,後面長著一排高大的粉紅和黃色蜀葵,她長長地呼了口氣,疲倦與寬慰交織。

passages.original: “I declare I’m getting glad to sit down.
passages.vernacular: 「我敢講我好高興坐下嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢說我很高興坐下來了。

passages.original: I’ve been on my feet all day, and two hundred pounds is a good bit for two feet to carry round.
passages.vernacular: 我整天都站住,兩百磅對兩隻腳來講,搬住到處走可不輕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我整天都站著,兩百磅對兩隻腳來說,搬著到處走可不輕。

passages.original: It’s a great blessing not to be fat, Marilla.
passages.vernacular: 不胖真係個大福氣,瑪麗拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不胖真是個大福氣,瑪麗拉。

passages.original: I hope you appreciate it.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你體會到呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你體會到這一點。

passages.original: Well, Anne, I hear you’ve given up your notion of going to college.
passages.vernacular: 好吧,安妮,我聽講你放棄咗去上大學嘅念頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,安妮,我聽說你放棄了去上大學的念頭。

passages.original: I was real glad to hear it.
passages.vernacular: 聽到呢個我真高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到這個我真高興。

passages.original: You’ve got as much education now as a woman can be comfortable with.
passages.vernacular: 你而家受嘅教育,已經足夠一個女人舒服地用喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你現在受的教育,已經足夠一個女人舒服地用了。

passages.original: I don’t believe in girls going to college with the men and cramming their heads full of Latin and Greek and all that nonsense.”
passages.vernacular: 我不相信女細路同男人一起上大學,把腦袋塞滿拉丁文、希臘文同所有嗰啲胡講八道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不相信女孩子和男人一起上大學,把腦袋塞滿拉丁文、希臘文和所有那些胡說八道。」

passages.original: “But I’m going to study Latin and Greek just the same, Mrs. Lynde,” said Anne laughing.
passages.vernacular: 「但我定係要學拉丁文同希臘文,林德太太,」安妮笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我還是要學拉丁文和希臘文,林德太太,」安妮笑著說。

passages.original: “I’m going to take my Arts course right here at Green Gables, and study everything that I would at college.”
passages.vernacular: 「我要就喺呢兒綠色屋頂修我嘅文科課程,學我喺大學裡會學嘅一切。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要就在這兒綠色屋頂修我的文科課程,學我在大學裡會學的一切。」

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde lifted her hands in holy horror.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太驚恐萬分地舉起雙手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太驚恐萬分地舉起雙手。

passages.original: “Anne Shirley, you’ll kill yourself.”
passages.vernacular: 「安妮·雪莉,你會把自己累死嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安妮·雪莉,你會把自己累死的。」

passages.original: “Not a bit of it.
passages.vernacular: 「啲都唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一點也不會。

passages.original: I shall thrive on it.
passages.vernacular: 我會越學越興旺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會越學越興旺。

passages.original: Oh, I’m not going to overdo things.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我唔會過度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我不會過度。

passages.original: As ‘Josiah Allen’s wife,’ says, I shall be ‘mejum’.
passages.vernacular: 就像《約書亞·艾倫嘅妻子》講嘅,我會『適度』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就像《約書亞·艾倫的妻子》說的,我會『適度』。

passages.original: But I’ll have lots of spare time in the long winter evenings, and I’ve no vocation for fancy work.
passages.vernacular: 但漫長嘅冬夜里我有好多空閒時間,而我又冇做針線活嘅天賦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但漫長的冬夜里我有很多空閒時間,而我又沒有做針線活的天賦。

passages.original: I’m going to teach over at Carmody, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 您知道,我要去卡莫迪教書。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您知道,我要去卡莫迪教書。」

passages.original: “I don’t know it.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: I guess you’re going to teach right here in Avonlea.
passages.vernacular: 我想你要喺阿文利呢兒教書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你要在阿文利這兒教書。

passages.original: The trustees have decided to give you the school.”
passages.vernacular: 校董哋已決定把學校畀你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 校董們已決定把學校給你。」

passages.original: “Mrs. Lynde!” cried Anne, springing to her feet in her surprise.
passages.vernacular: 「林德太太!」安妮驚訝地跳起嚟喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「林德太太!」安妮驚訝地跳起來喊道。

passages.original: “Why, I thought they had promised it to Gilbert Blythe!”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我以為佢哋答應畀吉爾伯特·布萊斯喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我以為他們答應給吉爾伯特·布萊斯了!」

passages.original: “So they did.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋係答應喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們是答應了。

passages.original: But as soon as Gilbert heard that you had applied for it he went to them--they had a business meeting at the school last night, you know--and told them that he withdrew his application, and suggested that they accept yours.
passages.vernacular: 但吉爾伯特一聽講你申請喇,就去找佢哋——你知道,琴晚佢哋喺學校開咗一個業務會議——告訴佢哋佢撤回申請,並建議佢哋接受你嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但吉爾伯特一聽說你申請了,就去找他們——你知道,昨晚他們在學校開了一個業務會議——告訴他們他撤回申請,並建議他們接受你的。

passages.original: He said he was going to teach at White Sands.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢要去白沙教書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他要去白沙教書。

passages.original: Of course he knew how much you wanted to stay with Marilla, and I must say I think it was real kind and thoughtful in him, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 當然佢知道你幾咁想留喺瑪麗拉身邊,我必須講我覺得佢咁樣做真係又好心又周到,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然他知道你多麼想留在瑪麗拉身邊,我必須說我覺得他這樣做真是又好心又周到,就是這樣。

passages.original: Real self-sacrificing, too, for he’ll have his board to pay at White Sands, and everybody knows he’s got to earn his own way through college.
passages.vernacular: 仲真係自我犧牲,因為佢喺白沙要付食宿費,而且人人都知道佢必須自己賺學費上大學。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還真是自我犧牲,因為他在白沙要付食宿費,而且人人都知道他必須自己賺學費上大學。

passages.original: So the trustees decided to take you.
passages.vernacular: 所以校董哋決定聘用你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以校董們決定聘用你。

passages.original: I was tickled to death when Thomas came home and told me.”
passages.vernacular: 托馬斯回家告訴我時,我高興死喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 托馬斯回家告訴我時,我高興死了。」

passages.original: “I don’t feel that I ought to take it,” murmured Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得我不該接受佢,」安妮喃喃講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得我不該接受它,」安妮喃喃說。

passages.original: “I mean--I don’t think I ought to let Gilbert make such a sacrifice for--for me.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係講——我覺得我不該讓吉爾伯特為喇——為了我作出咁樣嘅犧牲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是說——我覺得我不該讓吉爾伯特為了——為了我作出這樣的犧牲。」

passages.original: “I guess you can’t prevent him now.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你而家阻止不咗佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你現在阻止不了他了。

passages.original: He’s signed papers with the White Sands trustees.
passages.vernacular: 佢已經同白沙嘅校董哋簽咗文件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他已經和白沙的校董們簽了文件。

passages.original: So it wouldn’t do him any good now if you were to refuse.
passages.vernacular: 所以你而家拒絕對佢冇任何好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你現在拒絕對他沒有任何好處。

passages.original: Of course you’ll take the school.
passages.vernacular: 當然你要接受呢所學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然你要接受這所學校。

passages.original: You’ll get along all right, now that there are no Pyes going.
passages.vernacular: 你會順利嘅,而家冇派伊家嘅人去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會順利的,現在沒有派伊家的人去了。

passages.original: Josie was the last of them, and a good thing she was, that’s what.
passages.vernacular: 喬西係佢哋中最後一個,謝天謝地,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬西是他們中最後一個,謝天謝地,就是這樣。

passages.original: There’s been some Pye or other going to Avonlea school for the last twenty years, and I guess their mission in life was to keep school teachers reminded that earth isn’t their home.
passages.vernacular: 過去二十年,總有某個派伊去阿文利學校,我想佢哋生命中嘅使命,就係讓學校老師哋記住,塵世唔係佢哋嘅家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過去二十年,總有某個派伊去阿文利學校,我想他們生命中的使命,就是讓學校老師們記住,塵世不是他們的家。

passages.original: Bless my heart!
passages.vernacular: 天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪!

passages.original: What does all that winking and blinking at the Barry gable mean?”
passages.vernacular: 巴里家山牆嗰兒眨眼睛、閃爍係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴里家山牆那兒眨眼睛、閃爍是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “Diana is signaling for me to go over,” laughed Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「黛安娜喺畀我發信號讓我過去,」安妮笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黛安娜在給我發信號讓我過去,」安妮笑著說。

passages.original: “You know we keep up the old custom.
passages.vernacular: 「您知道,我哋仲保持住老習慣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您知道,我們還保持著老習慣。

passages.original: Excuse me while I run over and see what she wants.”
passages.vernacular: 請原諒,讓我跑過去睇佢要乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒,讓我跑過去看她要什麼。」

passages.original: Anne ran down the clover slope like a deer, and disappeared in the firry shadows of the Haunted Wood.
passages.vernacular: 安妮像鹿一樣跑下三葉草斜坡,消失喺鬧鬼林冷杉嘅陰影裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮像鹿一樣跑下三葉草斜坡,消失在鬧鬼林冷杉的陰影裡。

passages.original: Mrs. Lynde looked after her indulgently.
passages.vernacular: 林德太太縱容地目送佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林德太太縱容地目送她。

passages.original: “There’s a good deal of the child about her yet in some ways.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺某些方面佢身上仲有好多細路氣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在某些方面她身上還有很多孩子氣。」

passages.original: “There’s a good deal more of the woman about her in others,” retorted Marilla, with a momentary return of her old crispness.
passages.vernacular: 「喺另啲方面佢身上有更多女人氣,」瑪麗拉反駁,佢往日嘅乾脆片刻間回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在另一些方面她身上有更多女人氣,」瑪麗拉反駁,她往日的乾脆片刻間回來了。

passages.original: But crispness was no longer Marilla’s distinguishing characteristic.
passages.vernacular: 但乾脆唔再係瑪麗拉嘅顯著特徵喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但乾脆不再是瑪麗拉的顯著特徵了。

passages.original: As Mrs. Lynde told her Thomas that night.
passages.vernacular: 正如林德太太嗰天晚上對佢嘅托馬斯講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正如林德太太那天晚上對她的托馬斯說的。

passages.original: “Marilla Cuthbert has got mellow.
passages.vernacular: 「瑪麗拉·卡思伯特變得溫和喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瑪麗拉·卡思伯特變得溫和了。

passages.original: That’s what.”
passages.vernacular: 就係咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這樣。」

passages.original: Anne went to the little Avonlea graveyard the next evening to put fresh flowers on Matthew’s grave and water the Scotch rosebush.
passages.vernacular: 第二天傍晚,安妮去咗阿文利嘅小墳場,喺馬修嘅墳上放上新鮮嘅花,並畀蘇格蘭玫瑰澆水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天傍晚,安妮去了阿文利的小墳場,在馬修的墳上放上新鮮的花,並給蘇格蘭玫瑰澆水。

passages.original: She lingered there until dusk, liking the peace and calm of the little place, with its poplars whose rustle was like low, friendly speech, and its whispering grasses growing at will among the graves.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺嗰兒逗留到黃昏,鍾意呢個小地方嘅平靜同安寧,佢嘅白楊樹沙沙作響像低語嘅友好談話,佢嘅低語嘅青草喺墓碑間隨意生長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在那兒逗留到黃昏,喜歡這個小地方的平靜和安寧,它的白楊樹沙沙作響像低語的友好談話,它的低語的青草在墓碑間隨意生長。

passages.original: When she finally left it and walked down the long hill that sloped to the Lake of Shining Waters it was past sunset and all Avonlea lay before her in a dreamlike afterlight--“a haunt of ancient peace.”
passages.vernacular: 佢最後離開,走下通向閃亮湖水嘅長長山坡時,太陽已經落山,整個阿文利喺夢幻般嘅餘暉中展而家佢面前——「古老和平嘅棲息地」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她最後離開,走下通向閃亮湖水的長長山坡時,太陽已經落山,整個阿文利在夢幻般的餘暉中展現在她面前——「古老和平的棲息地」。

passages.original: There was a freshness in the air as of a wind that had blown over honey-sweet fields of clover.
passages.vernacular: 空氣中有一種清新,好像一陣風吹過蜜一樣甜嘅三葉草田。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 空氣中有一種清新,好像一陣風吹過蜜一樣甜的三葉草田。

passages.original: Home lights twinkled out here and there among the homestead trees.
passages.vernacular: 家家戶戶嘅燈火喺老宅嘅樹木間呢度嗰度閃爍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 家家戶戶的燈火在老宅的樹木間這裡那裡閃爍。

passages.original: Beyond lay the sea, misty and purple, with its haunting, unceasing murmur.
passages.vernacular: 遠處係大海,朦朧而紫色,帶住佢縈繞不去、不停息嘅低語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遠處是大海,朦朧而紫色,帶著它縈繞不去、不停息的低語。

passages.original: The west was a glory of soft mingled hues, and the pond reflected them all in still softer shadings.
passages.vernacular: 西邊係一片柔和交融嘅色彩嘅榮光,池塘把佢哋全都倒映出嚟,色調更加柔和。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 西邊是一片柔和交融的色彩的榮光,池塘把它們全都倒映出來,色調更加柔和。

passages.original: The beauty of it all thrilled Anne’s heart, and she gratefully opened the gates of her soul to it.
passages.vernacular: 呢一切嘅美觸動咗安妮嘅心,佢感激地向佢敞開咗靈魂嘅大門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切的美觸動了安妮的心,她感激地向它敞開了靈魂的大門。

passages.original: “Dear old world,” she murmured, “you are very lovely, and I am glad to be alive in you.”
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅老世界,」佢喃喃講,「你好可愛,我好高興活喺你裡面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的老世界,」她喃喃說,「你非常可愛,我很高興活在你裡面。」

passages.original: Halfway down the hill a tall lad came whistling out of a gate before the Blythe homestead.
passages.vernacular: 走到山坡一半,一個高個子少年吹住口哨從布萊斯家宅前嘅大門裡出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走到山坡一半,一個高個子少年吹著口哨從布萊斯家宅前的大門裡出來。

passages.original: It was Gilbert, and the whistle died on his lips as he recognized Anne.
passages.vernacular: 係吉爾伯特,佢認出安妮時,口哨喺佢唇邊消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是吉爾伯特,他認出安妮時,口哨在他唇邊消失了。

passages.original: He lifted his cap courteously, but he would have passed on in silence, if Anne had not stopped and held out her hand.
passages.vernacular: 佢有禮貌地舉咗舉帽子,但若唔係安妮停下嚟伸出手,佢本會默默走過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有禮貌地舉了舉帽子,但若不是安妮停下來伸出手,他本會默默走過去。

passages.original: “Gilbert,” she said, with scarlet cheeks, “I want to thank you for giving up the school for me.
passages.vernacular: 「吉爾伯特,」佢講,臉頰猩紅,「我想為你為我放棄學校嘅事謝謝你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉爾伯特,」她說,臉頰猩紅,「我想為你為我放棄學校的事謝謝你。

passages.original: It was very good of you--and I want you to know that I appreciate it.”
passages.vernacular: 你太好喇——我想讓你知道我感激。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你太好了——我想讓你知道我感激。」

passages.original: Gilbert took the offered hand eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 吉爾伯特急切地握住伸出嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉爾伯特急切地握住伸出的手。

passages.original: “It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「呢根本唔係特別好,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這根本不是特別好,安妮。

passages.original: I was pleased to be able to do you some small service.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興能為你做啲小事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興能為你做一點小事。

passages.original: Are we going to be friends after this?
passages.vernacular: 從此以後我哋做朋友好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從此以後我們做朋友好嗎?

passages.original: Have you really forgiven me my old fault?”
passages.vernacular: 你真嘅原諒咗我過去嘅過錯嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你真的原諒了我過去的過錯嗎?」

passages.original: Anne laughed and tried unsuccessfully to withdraw her hand.
passages.vernacular: 安妮笑喇,試圖抽回手,冇成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮笑了,試圖抽回手,沒成功。

passages.original: “I forgave you that day by the pond landing, although I didn’t know it.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰天喺池塘碼頭我就原諒你喇,雖然我當時唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那天在池塘碼頭我就原諒你了,雖然我當時不知道。

passages.original: What a stubborn little goose I was.
passages.vernacular: 我嗰時係幾咁固執嘅小傻瓜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我那時是多麼固執的小傻瓜。

passages.original: I’ve been--I may as well make a complete confession--I’ve been sorry ever since.”
passages.vernacular: 我一直——我不妨完全坦白——我從嗰以後就一直後悔。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直——我不妨完全坦白——我從那以後就一直後悔。」

passages.original: “We are going to be the best of friends,” said Gilbert, jubilantly.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋會成為最好嘅朋友,」吉爾伯特歡欣地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們會成為最好的朋友,」吉爾伯特歡欣地說。

passages.original: “We were born to be good friends, Anne.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋生來就係要做好朋友嘅,安妮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們生來就是要做好朋友的,安妮。

passages.original: You’ve thwarted destiny enough.
passages.vernacular: 你對命運嘅阻撓夠多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你對命運的阻撓夠多了。

passages.original: I know we can help each other in many ways.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我哋喺許多方面可以互相幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我們在許多方面可以互相幫助。

passages.original: You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you?
passages.vernacular: 你要繼續學業,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要繼續學業,是不是?

passages.original: So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you.”
passages.vernacular: 我都係。嚟,我送你回家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也是。來,我送你回家。」

passages.original: Marilla looked curiously at Anne when the latter entered the kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 安妮走進廚房時,瑪麗拉好奇地睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安妮走進廚房時,瑪麗拉好奇地看著她。

passages.original: “Who was that came up the lane with you, Anne?”
passages.vernacular: 「跟你一起上小巷嘅人係邊個,安妮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「跟你一起上小巷的人是誰,安妮?」

passages.original: “Gilbert Blythe,” answered Anne, vexed to find herself blushing.
passages.vernacular: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯,」安妮回答,懊惱地發現自己臉紅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉爾伯特·布萊斯,」安妮回答,懊惱地發現自己臉紅了。

passages.original: “I met him on Barry’s hill.”
passages.vernacular: 「我喺巴里家山坡上遇到佢嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在巴里家山坡上遇到他的。」

passages.original: “I didn’t think you and Gilbert Blythe were such good friends that you’d stand for half an hour at the gate talking to him,” said Marilla with a dry smile.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇想到你同吉爾伯特·布萊斯係咁要好嘅朋友,會站喺門口跟佢講半個鐘頭嘅話,」瑪麗拉帶住幹巴巴嘅微笑講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒想到你和吉爾伯特·布萊斯是這麼要好的朋友,會站在門口跟他說半個鐘頭的話,」瑪麗拉帶著幹巴巴的微笑說。

passages.original: “We haven’t been--we’ve been good enemies.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋唔係——我哋係好對手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們不是——我們是好對手。

passages.original: But we have decided that it will be much more sensible to be good friends in the future.
passages.vernacular: 但我哋決定,今後做好朋友要明智得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們決定,今後做好朋友要明智得多。

passages.original: Were we really there half an hour?
passages.vernacular: 我哋真嘅喺嗰兒待咗半個鐘頭嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們真的在那兒待了半個鐘頭嗎?

passages.original: It seemed just a few minutes.
passages.vernacular: 似乎只有幾分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 似乎只有幾分鐘。

passages.original: But, you see, we have five years’ lost conversations to catch up with, Marilla.”
passages.vernacular: 但係,您瞧,我哋有五年落下嘅談話要補上,瑪麗拉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,您瞧,我們有五年落下的談話要補上,瑪麗拉。」

passages.original: Anne sat long at her window that night companioned by a glad content.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,安妮坐喺窗邊好久,有一種快樂嘅滿足陪伴住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,安妮坐在窗邊很久,有一種快樂的滿足陪伴著她。

passages.original: The wind purred softly in the cherry boughs, and the mint breaths came up to her.
passages.vernacular: 風喺櫻桃樹枝間輕輕地咕嚕,薄荷嘅氣息飄上嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風在櫻桃樹枝間輕輕地咕嚕,薄荷的氣息飄上來。

passages.original: The stars twinkled over the pointed firs in the hollow and Diana’s light gleamed through the old gap.
passages.vernacular: 星星喺窪地里尖尖嘅冷杉上空閃爍,黛安娜嘅燈光透過老缺口閃耀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星星在窪地里尖尖的冷杉上空閃爍,黛安娜的燈光透過老缺口閃耀。

passages.original: Anne’s horizons had closed in since the night she had sat there after coming home from Queen’s; but if the path set before her feet was to be narrow she knew that flowers of quiet happiness would bloom along it.
passages.vernacular: 自從佢從女王學院回家嘅嗰個晚上坐喺嗰度以來,安妮嘅地平線縮小喇;但如果擺喺佢腳前嘅路係窄嘅,佢知道平靜幸福嘅花朵將沿路開放。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從她從女王學院回家的那個晚上坐在那裡以來,安妮的地平線縮小了;但如果擺在她腳前的路是窄的,她知道平靜幸福的花朵將沿路開放。

passages.original: The joy of sincere work and worthy aspiration and congenial friendship were to be hers; nothing could rob her of her birthright of fancy or her ideal world of dreams.
passages.vernacular: 真誠工作嘅快樂、值得嘅志向同志趣相投嘅友誼將屬於佢;冇乜嘢能剝奪佢同生俱嚟嘅幻想權,或佢理想嘅夢想世界。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真誠工作的快樂、值得的志向和志趣相投的友誼將屬於她;沒有什麼能剝奪她與生俱來的幻想權,或她理想的夢想世界。

passages.original: And there was always the bend in the road!
passages.vernacular: 而且總有路上嘅轉彎處!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且總有路上的轉彎處!

passages.original: “‘God’s in his heaven, all’s right with the world,’” whispered Anne softly.
passages.vernacular: 「『上帝喺天堂,世間一切安好,』」安妮輕輕地低語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『上帝在天堂,世間一切安好,』」安妮輕輕地低語。
